1 How do the operations of repression structure or inform the work? That is, what unconscious motives are operating in the main character(s); what core issues are thereby illustrated; and how do these core issues structure or inform the piece? (Remember, the unconscious consists of repressed wounds, fears, unresolved conflicts, and guilty desires.)

2这里是否存在俄狄浦斯情结或其他家庭动力？也就是说，能否将故事中人物的成年行为模式与其早期家庭经历联系起来？这些行为模式和家庭动力是如何运作的，它们又揭示了什么？

2 Are there any oedipal dynamics – or any other family dynamics – at work here? That is, is it possible to relate a character’s patterns of adult behavior to early experiences in the family as represented in the story? How do these patterns of behavior and family dynamics operate and what do they reveal?

3如何用各种精神分析概念来解释人物的行为、叙事事件和/或形象（例如，退行、危机、投射、对死亡的恐惧或迷恋、性——包括爱情和浪漫以及性行为——作为心理身份的主要指标，或者自我-本我-超我的运作）？

3 How can characters’ behavior, narrative events, and/or images be explained in terms of psychoanalytic concepts of any kind (for example, regression, crisis, projection, fear of or fascination with death, sexuality – which includes love and romance as well as sexual behavior – as a primary indicator of psychological identity, or the operations of ego-id-superego)?

4我们该如何将文学作品比作梦境？也就是说，反复出现或引人注目的梦境符号如何揭示叙述者或说话者如何将自己潜意识中的欲望、恐惧、创伤或未解决的冲突投射到其他角色、场景或所描绘的事件上？与死亡、性欲和潜意识相关的符号尤其有用。事实上，梦境符号的运用对于解读那些看似不切实际或奇幻的文学作品，或者其中某些段落，也就是那些如梦似幻的作品，非常有帮助。

4 In what ways can we view a literary work as analogous to a dream? That is, how might recurrent or striking dream symbols reveal the ways in which the narrator or speaker is projecting his or her unconscious desires, fears, wounds, or unresolved conflicts onto other characters, onto the setting, or onto the events portrayed? Symbols relevant to death, sexuality, and the unconscious are especially helpful. Indeed, the use of dream symbols can be very useful in interpreting literary works, or passages thereof, that seem unrealistic or fantastic, in other words, that seem dreamlike.

5这部作品对作者的心理状态有何启示？尽管这个问题不再是精神分析批评家们关注的焦点，但仍有一些批评家会探讨它，尤其是那些撰写心理传记（心理传记）的批评家。在这些案例中，文学文本的解读往往如同作者的梦境一般。以这种方式对作者进行精神分析是一项艰巨的任务，我们的分析必须通过仔细考察作者的全部作品，包括信件、日记以及其他任何可用的传记资料而得出。当然，单一的文学作品所能提供的只是非常片面的图景。

5 What does the work suggest about the psychological being of its author? Although this question is no longer the primary question asked by psychoanalytic critics, some critics still address it, especially those who write psychological biographies (psychobiographies). In these cases, the literary text is interpreted much as if it were the author’s dream. Psychoanalyzing an author in this manner is a difficult undertaking, and our analysis must be carefully derived by examining the author’s entire corpus as well as letters, diaries, and any other biographical material available. Certainly, a single literary work can provide but a very incomplete picture.

6对文学作品的特定解读可能暗示读者的心理动机是什么？或者，某种批评趋势可能暗示一群读者的心理动机是什么（例如，文学评论家倾向于将威利·洛曼视为一位忠诚的顾家男人，而忽略或淡化他对家庭功能失调的影响）？

6 What might a given interpretation of a literary work suggest about the psychological motives of the reader? Or what might a critical trend suggest about the psychological motives of a group of readers (for example, the tendency of literary critics to see Willy Loman as a devoted family man and ignore or underplay his contribution to the family dysfunction)?

7文本似乎以何种方式揭示了人物在象征秩序、想象秩序、镜像阶段（或拉康所说的）中的情感投入。文本中是否有任何部分似乎体现了拉康的“实在界”概念？拉康的哪些概念能够解释文本的大部分内容，以至于我们可以说文本是由其中一个或多个概念构建的？

7 In what ways does the text seem to reveal characters’ emotional investments in the Symbolic Order, the Imaginary Order, the Mirror Stage, or what Lacan calls objet petit a? Does any part of the text seem to represent Lacan’s notion of the Real? Do any Lacanian concepts account for so much of the text that we might say the text is structured by one or more of these concepts?

根据具体文学作品，我们可以提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们也可以提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们以富有成效的精神分析方式思考文学作品的一些起点。重要的是要记住，即使关注相同的精神分析概念，并非所有精神分析批评家都会以相同的方式解读同一部作品。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。我们的目标是运用精神分析来丰富我们对文学作品的阅读，帮助我们理解作品中阐述的一些重要思想，而如果没有精神分析的帮助，我们可能无法如此清晰或深刻地领悟这些思想。

Depending on the literary work in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us thinking about literary works in productive psychoanalytic ways. It is important to keep in mind that not all psychoanalytic critics will interpret the same work in the same way, even if they focus on the same psychoanalytic concepts. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use psychoanalysis to help enrich our reading of literary works, to help us see some important ideas they illustrate that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply without psychoanalysis.

以下对菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的心理分析解读，旨在说明心理分析对该小说的诠释可能得出的结果。我将论证，对亲密关系的恐惧构成了一种心理行为模式，这种模式贯穿于小说的所有主要人物，并推动了叙事的诸多发展。因此，从心理分析的角度来看，《了不起的盖茨比》并非令众多读者着迷的伟大爱情故事，而是一部关于功能失调爱情的心理剧。

The following psychoanalytic reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a psychoanalytic interpretation of that novel might yield. I will argue that fear of intimacy forms a pattern of psychological behavior that is common to all of the novel’s main characters and responsible for a good deal of the narrative progression. Through a psychoanalytic lens, then, The Great Gatsby is not the great love story that enthralls so many of its readers, but a psychological drama of dysfunctional love.

《爱与这一切有何干系？》：对《了不起的盖茨比》的精神分析解读

“What’s Love Got to Do with It?”: a psychoanalytic reading of The Great Gatsby

F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）探讨的人类行为领域中，有一个领域对精神分析批评具有重要意义，那就是小说中描绘的浪漫关系。事实上，即使对于不以精神分析视角解读这部小说的读者来说，盖茨比对黛西那份炽烈而持久的爱也是书中最为令人难忘的特质之一。这种情感的魅力，在许多读者心中，使《了不起的盖茨比》成为美国最伟大的爱情故事之一。实际上，对于许多非精神分析文学批评家而言，杰伊·盖茨比是一位近乎传奇的浪漫英雄，与小说中其他人物截然不同。然而，从精神分析的角度来看，盖茨比和黛西的爱情之所以引人入胜，并非在于其表面上的独特性，而在于它如何映射出书中其他不那么吸引人的爱情关系——汤姆和黛西、汤姆和默特尔、默特尔和乔治、尼克和乔丹——从而揭示了一种心理行为模式，而这种模式在很大程度上推动了叙事的发展。正如我们将看到的，这种模式根植于人物对亲密关系的恐惧，即潜意识里认为与他人建立情感联系会导致自己遭受情感上的毁灭。这种心理问题在小说中如此普遍，以至于《了不起的盖茨比》 从精神分析的角度来看，盖茨比的著名爱情故事变成了一出功能失调的爱情剧。为了便于理解，我们先来考察一下最明显建立在对亲密关系的恐惧之上的关系：汤姆和黛西·布坎南的婚姻。

One area of human behavior explored in F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925) that has important implications for psychoanalytic criticism is found in the romantic relationships portrayed in the novel. Indeed, even for readers not viewing the novel through a psychoanalytic lens, one of the most memorable qualities of the book is the force and endurance of Gatsby’s love for Daisy, the emotional magnetism of which, for many fans, renders The Great Gatsby one of the great American love stories. For many nonpsychoanalytic literary critics, in fact, Jay Gatsby is a rather larger-than-life romantic hero,2 quite different from the other characters portrayed in the novel. For a psychoanalytic reading, however, the interest created by the romance between Gatsby and Daisy lies not in its apparent uniqueness but in the ways in which it mirrors all of the less appealing romantic relationships depicted – those between Tom and Daisy, Tom and Myrtle, Myrtle and George, and Nick and Jordan – and thereby reveals a pattern of psychological behavior responsible for a good deal of the narrative progression. As we shall see, this pattern is grounded in the characters’ fear of intimacy, the unconscious conviction that emotional ties to another human being will result in one’s being emotionally devastated. This psychological problem is so pervasive in the novel that The Great Gatsby’s famous love story becomes, through a psychoanalytic lens, a drama of dysfunctional love. For the sake of clarity, let’s begin by examining the relationship most obviously based on fear of intimacy: the marriage of Tom and Daisy Buchanan.

小说中最能体现对亲密关系恐惧的或许是汤姆·布坎南长期的婚外情，乔丹在两人结婚三个月后才得知此事。乔丹告诉尼克：

Perhaps the clearest indication of fear of intimacy in the novel lies in Tom Buchanan’s chronic extramarital affairs, of which Jordan became aware three months after the couple’s wedding. Jordan tells Nick,

我在圣巴巴拉见到了汤姆和黛西，当时他们刚度完蜜月回来。……我离开一周后……一天晚上，汤姆在文图拉路上撞上了一辆马车，前轮被撞掉了。和他同行的女孩也上了报纸，因为她胳膊骨折了——她是圣巴巴拉酒店的一名女服务员。

I saw [Tom and Daisy] in Santa Barbara when they came back [from their honeymoon]. … A week after I left … Tom ran into a wagon on the Ventura road one night and ripped a front wheel off his car. The girl who was with him got into the papers too because her arm was broken – she was one of the chambermaids in the Santa Barbara Hotel.

（81-82；第4章）

(81–82; ch. 4)

我们初次见到汤姆时，他正沉浸在最新的婚外情中，这次的对象是默特尔·威尔逊。将兴趣、时间和精力分散在两个女人身上，让他得以避免与她们中的任何一个建立真正的亲密关系。事实上，汤姆与女性的关系，包括他与妻子的关系，都揭示了他追求的是满足虚荣心，而非情感上的亲密。对汤姆而言，黛西代表着社会地位的优越：她不是那种会被像杰伊·盖茨比这样的“无名小卒”（137；第七章）轻易得到的女人。汤姆占有了默特尔·威尔逊——尼克形容她是一个“性感”、“魅力四射”且“活力四射”的女人（29-30；第二章）——这强化了汤姆对自身男性力量的认知，也正因如此，他才会带她去高档餐厅，让他的男性朋友看到他们，以及在东卵的家中与尼克重逢后不久，就把她介绍给尼克。事实上，汤姆对其他女人的兴趣已经习以为常，黛西也习以为常了。当汤姆告诉她，他想在盖茨比的派对上和一群陌生人一起吃晚饭，而不是和她一起，因为他觉得其中一个男人很有趣时，她立刻意识到丈夫在追求另一个女人：她把自己的“小金铅笔”递给他，以防他想“记下任何地址”，然后“她环顾四周，告诉尼克，那个女孩‘虽然俗气，但很漂亮’”（112；第6章）。

When we meet Tom, he’s engaged in his latest affair, this time with Myrtle Wilson. Dividing his interest, time, and energy between two women protects him from real intimacy with either. Indeed, Tom’s relationships with women, including his wife, reveal his desire for ego gratification rather than for emotional intimacy. For Tom, Daisy represents social superiority: she’s not the kind of woman who can be acquired by a “Mr. Nobody from Nowhere” (137; ch. 7) like Jay Gatsby. Tom’s possession of Myrtle Wilson – whom Nick describes as a “sensu[ous],” “smouldering” woman with “an immediately perceptible vitality” (29–30; ch. 2) – reinforces Tom’s sense of his own masculine power, which is why he brings her to fashionable restaurants where they are seen by his male acquaintances and why he introduces her to Nick so soon after their reunion at his East Egg home. In fact, Tom’s interest in other women is so routine that Daisy has come to expect it. When Tom tells her he wants to eat supper with a group of strangers at Gatsby’s party, rather than with her, because he finds one of the men amusing, she immediately realizes that her husband is pursuing another woman: she offers him her “little gold pencil” in case he wants to “take down any addresses,” and “[s]he looked around after a moment and told [Nick] that the girl was ‘common but pretty’” (112; ch. 6).

黛西对亲密关系的恐惧虽然与汤姆一样强烈，但却不那么显而易见。事实上，在她与盖茨比发生婚外情之前，她对婚姻的忠贞，以及她对汤姆与默特尔交往的痛苦，或许会让一些读者觉得黛西渴望与丈夫建立情感上的亲密关系。乔丹对黛西蜜月后的描写也强化了这种解读：

Daisy’s fear of intimacy, though as intense as Tom’s, is not quite as immediately apparent. Indeed, her marital fidelity, until her affair with Gatsby, and her distress over Tom’s involvement with Myrtle might suggest to some readers that Daisy desires emotional intimacy with her husband. Jordan’s description of Daisy after her honeymoon reinforces this interpretation:

我从未见过哪个女孩像她那样生丈夫的气。他哪怕离开房间一会儿，她也会不安地四处张望，问：“汤姆去哪儿了？”然后一脸茫然，直到看到他进门才回过神来。她以前总是她一连几个小时坐在沙滩上，让他把头枕在她的腿上，用手指轻轻揉搓他的眼睛，用难以言喻的喜悦看着他。

I’d never seen a girl so mad about her husband. If he left the room for a minute she’d look around uneasily and say “Where’s Tom gone?” and wear the most abstracted expression until she saw him coming in the door. She used to sit on the sand with his head in her lap by the hour, rubbing her fingers over his eyes and looking at him with unfathomable delight.

（81-82；第4章）

(81–82; ch. 4)

然而，汤姆和黛西的恋爱史表明，黛西对丈夫的“喜爱”可能另有解释，这其中可能存在心理动机。

However, the history of Tom and Daisy’s relationship suggests psychological motives that point to a different interpretation of Daisy’s “delight” in her husband.

黛西嫁给汤姆时显然并不爱他：婚礼前一天晚上，她收到盖茨比从海外寄来的信后，就试图取消婚礼。事实上，她收到信后的反应表明，她嫁给汤姆是为了让自己不再爱上盖茨比，因为她对盖茨比的依恋已经到了难以承受的地步：她生平第一次喝醉了，“她哭个不停……我们……让她泡在冷水澡里。她不肯放开盖茨比的信……直到看到信像雪一样碎成渣，才让乔丹把它留在肥皂盒里”（81；第四章）。否则，她为什么会嫁给汤姆呢？她显然更喜欢盖茨比，她认为盖茨比“和她出身相仿……而且完全有能力照顾她”（156；第八章）？然而，婚后仅仅三个月，她似乎就对新婚丈夫痴迷不已。究竟是什么让黛西的态度在短短时间内发生了如此巨大的转变？考虑到汤姆对女性的痴迷，很可能在他和黛西抵达圣巴巴拉时，黛西就已经怀疑他不忠了。这可以解释为什么只要汤姆不在身边，她就显得心神不宁。她有充分的理由担心，如果汤姆不在她身边，他可能正在追求其他女人，就像她认为的那样，例如，在她生下帕米后，“从麻醉中醒来，感到彻底被抛弃”，而“汤姆不知身在何处”（21；第一章）。然而，黛西非但没有因为这种冷落而憎恨他，反而深深地爱上了他。虽然这种反应看似不合常理，但可以用心理学来解释。

It is obvious that Daisy didn’t love Tom when she married him: she tried to call off the wedding the evening before when she’d received an overseas letter from Gatsby. In fact, her behavior upon receiving his letter suggests that she married Tom to keep herself from loving Gatsby, to whom she had gotten too attached for her own comfort: she got drunk for the first time in her life, and “she cried and cried. … [W]e … got her into a cold bath. She wouldn’t let go of [Gatsby’s] letter. … [A]nd [she] only let [Jordan] leave it in the soap dish when she saw that it was coming to pieces like snow” (81; ch. 4). Why else would she marry Tom, when she obviously preferred Gatsby, who she believed was “from much the same strata as herself … [and] fully able to take care of her” (156; ch. 8)? Yet just three months after the wedding she seemed obsessively fond of her new husband. What happened in this short time to change Daisy’s attitude so dramatically? Given Tom’s compulsive pursuit of women, it is probable that by the time he and Daisy arrived in Santa Barbara, Daisy already suspected him of infidelity. This would explain why she seemed so distracted whenever Tom was out of sight. She had good reason to fear that, if he wasn’t with her, he might be pursuing another woman, as she believes he was doing, for example, when she “woke up out of the ether with a totally abandoned feeling,” after giving birth to Pammy, “and Tom was God knows where” (21; ch. 1). Rather than hate him for such mistreatment, however, Daisy fell head-over-heels in love with him. Although such a response may not seem to make sense, it can be explained psychologically.

从精神分析的角度来看，一个爱上患有严重亲密恐惧症的男人的女人，很可能自己也害怕亲密关系。如果她害怕亲密关系，没有什么比一个对亲密关系毫无渴望的男人更能让她感到安全。当她发现汤姆的兴趣并非只集中在她身上时，她很可能会深深地爱上他，因为他不会对她的保护壳构成威胁：即使他有能力，他也不会想要突破这层保护。这正是我们在黛西对汤姆态度的转变中所看到的，尽管她肯定不会用这样的语言来描述自己的感受，而且她很可能根本没有意识到自己的这种心理动机。

In psychoanalytic terms, a woman who falls in love with a man suffering from severe fear of intimacy probably fears intimacy herself. If she fears intimacy, nothing can make her feel safer than a man who has no desire for it. Upon learning that Tom’s interest did not focus exclusively on her, such a woman would have become very capable of loving him intensely because he posed no threat to her protective shell: he wouldn’t have wanted to break through it even if he could have. And this is just what we see in Daisy’s changed attitude toward Tom, though she certainly wouldn’t use this language to describe her feelings, and it is very unlikely that she was even aware of her psychological motives.

正如我们在本章前面所学到的，害怕与他人亲密通常是害怕与自己亲密的结果。因为亲密的人际关系会唤起早期家庭冲突的心理创伤，并让我们面对那些我们不愿处理甚至不愿了解的身份层面，所以避免痛苦的自我认知的最佳方法就是避免亲密的人际关系。人际关系，尤其是恋爱关系。为什么不干脆完全避免恋爱关系呢？虽然对于一些害怕亲密关系的人来说，这种做法或许是一种有效的逃避方式，但造成这种恐惧的心理创伤通常需要一个舞台，让他们以伪装的形式重演最初的创伤经历，而恋爱关系恰好提供了一个绝佳的舞台。例如，如果我曾被疏于照顾或虐待的父母伤害过，我就会寻找一个拥有相同特质的伴侣，潜意识里希望填补父母遗留的未满足的心理需求。讽刺的是，选择一个与父母有着相同负面特质的伴侣，几乎可以肯定我未被满足的心理需求将永远得不到满足。然而，到了我人生的这个阶段，由于心理创伤造成的低自尊，我可能觉得自己不配拥有被满足的需求。因为潜意识里存在的假设——如果我是个好人，就不会有这些创伤——一直被压抑着，它的不合逻辑性没有受到挑战，我便继续受其控制。

As we learned earlier in this chapter, fear of intimacy with others is usually a product of fear of intimacy with oneself. Because close interpersonal relationships dredge up the psychological residue of earlier family conflicts and bring into play aspects of our identity we don’t want to deal with or even know about, the best way to avoid painful psychological self-awareness is to avoid close interpersonal relationships, especially romantic relationships. Why not simply avoid romantic relationships altogether? Although this practice may be an effective form of avoidance for some people who fear intimacy, the psychological wounds responsible for that fear usually demand a stage on which to reenact, in disguised form, the original wounding experience, and a romantic relationship provides an excellent stage. For example, if I was hurt by a parent who was neglectful or abusive, I will seek a mate who has these same characteristics, unconsciously hoping to fulfill whatever psychological needs were left unfulfilled by that parent. Ironically, choosing a mate who shares my parent’s negative qualities almost guarantees that my unmet psychological needs will remain unmet. However, by this time in my life, due to the low self-esteem produced by my psychological wounds, I probably feel I don’t deserve to have my needs met. Because the unconscious premise operating here – I wouldn’t have these wounds if I were a good person – remains repressed, its illogic remains unchallenged, and I remain in its grasp.

对汤姆和黛西来说，对亲密关系的恐惧都与低自尊有关。如果汤姆真像他的财富和地位所展现的那样内心安全，他就不会像现在这样费尽心思地用金钱和权力来炫耀自己，比如向尼克吹嘘自己的房子和马厩，在尼克和其他人面前炫耀他的情妇默特尔，贬低那些不属于“统治阶级”的人（17；第一章），以及戏弄乔治·威尔逊，让他不要卖给这位可怜的修车工一辆他或许能转手赚点钱的车。甚至汤姆选择的情妇——全部都来自下层阶级——也表明他需要通过掌控他人来弥补内心的不安全感。

For both Tom and Daisy, fear of intimacy is related to low self-esteem. If Tom were as emotionally secure as his wealth and size make him appear, he wouldn’t work as hard as he does to impress others with his money and power, as he does, for example, when he brags about his house and stables to Nick, when he flaunts Myrtle before Nick and others, when he degrades those who don’t belong to the “dominant race” (17; ch. 1), and when he toys with George Wilson concerning whether or not he will sell George a car that the poor mechanic might be able to resell at a profit. Even Tom’s choice of mistresses – all from the lower class – bespeaks his need to bolster an insecure psyche through power over others.

黛西的低自尊，如同她对亲密关系的恐惧，很大程度上体现在她与汤姆的关系中。她如此深爱一个公然对她不忠的男人，暗示着她潜意识里认为自己不配拥有更好的。此外，黛西的不安全感，如同汤姆一样，常常需要通过给别人留下深刻印象来获得自我满足，这一点在她诸多矫揉造作的行为中可见一斑。尼克注意到她的虚伪，她“声称自己是某个相当显赫的秘密社团的成员，她和汤姆都是其中一员”（22；第一章）：

Daisy’s low self-esteem, like her fear of intimacy, is indicated in large part by her relationship with Tom. Falling so much in love with a man who is openly unfaithful to her suggests an unconscious belief that she doesn’t deserve better. Furthermore, Daisy’s insecurity, like Tom’s, frequently requires the ego reinforcement obtained by impressing others, attempts at which we see in her numerous affectations. Nick notes her artifice when she “assert[s] her membership in a rather distinguished secret society to which she and Tom belon[g]” (22; ch. 1):

“我觉得一切都糟透了……所有人都这么认为——就连那些最前卫的人也这么认为。而且我知道……我去过很多地方，见过很多事，也做过很多事。”她目光挑衅地环视四周，有点像汤姆的眼神，然后带着令人胆寒的轻蔑大笑起来……就在她声音戛然而止的那一刻……我感觉到了她话语中根本的虚伪。

“I think everything’s terrible anyhow. … Everybody thinks so – the most advanced people. And I know. I’ve been everywhere and seen everything and done everything.” Her eyes flashed around her in a defiant way, rather like Tom’s, and she laughed with thrilling scorn. … The instant her voice broke off … I felt the basic insincerity of what she had said.

（22；第1章）

(22; ch. 1)

我们几乎每次在人群中看到黛西时，都能看到她受惊的行为，以下例子便可说明这一点。当尼克第一次和布坎南一家以及乔丹·贝克一起去黛西位于长岛的家时，黛西告诉他：“我……我麻木了。”“幸福。”……她笑了……仿佛说了什么妙语……抬头看着我的脸，承诺说这世上没有谁比我更让她想见。她就是这样的人”（13；第一章）。在盖茨比的派对上，她告诉尼克：“如果你今晚想吻我……告诉我一声，我很乐意为你安排。只要提我的名字就行。或者出示一张绿卡”（111；第六章）。盖茨比带着尼克和乔丹去布坎南家拜访时，黛西把汤姆支开，然后“起身走到盖茨比面前，拉下他的脸吻了他的嘴唇……‘我不在乎！’黛西喊道，然后开始在砖砌壁炉旁扭动”（122-123；第七章）。矫揉造作往往是缺乏安全感的表现，而黛西显然非常缺乏安全感。

We see Daisy’s affected behavior almost every time we see her in a group, as the following examples illustrate. When Nick joins the Buchanans and Jordan Baker for the first time at Daisy’s Long Island home, Daisy tells him, “‘I’m p-paralyzed with happiness.’ … She laughed … as if she said something very witty … looking up into my face, promising that there was no one in the world she so much wanted to see. That was a way she had” (13; ch. 1). At Gatsby’s party she tells Nick, “If you want to kiss me any time during the evening … just let me know and I’ll be glad to arrange it for you. Just mention my name. Or present a green card” (111; ch. 6). When Gatsby visits the Buchanans with Nick and Jordan, Daisy sends Tom out of the room, and then she “got up and went over to Gatsby, and pulled down his face kissing him on the mouth. … ‘I don’t care!’ cried Daisy and began to clog on the brick fireplace” (122–23; ch. 7). Affectation is often a sign of insecurity, of which Daisy clearly has a good deal.

汤姆和黛西对亲密关系的恐惧也体现在他们与他人的关系中。他们俩都不花时间陪伴帕米。他们的女儿由保姆抚养，黛西对孩子虚伪的态度——“‘宝贝，你这受祝福的小天使，’她轻声细语地张开双臂，‘来，到爱你的亲生母亲身边来吧’”（123页；第七章）——一如既往地表明，她更注重的是戏剧化的姿态，而非母性的热情。汤姆和黛西都与尼克和乔丹没有建立起亲密的关系，尽管尼克是黛西的表弟，而乔丹是黛西从小就认识的，并且经常住在他们家。从这个角度来看，这对夫妇频繁的搬迁——正如尼克所说，他们“不安地四处漂泊”（10；第1章）——并不是他们与他人缺乏亲密关系的原因，而是结果：他们不会在一个地方停留太久，因为他们不想与任何人亲近。

Tom and Daisy’s fear of intimacy is apparent in their relationships with others as well. Neither of them spends time with Pammy. Their daughter is being raised by her nurse, and Daisy’s artificial behavior toward the child – “‘Bles-sed pre-cious,’ she crooned, holding out her arms. ‘Come to your own mother that loves you’” (123; ch. 7) – bespeaks, as usual, an eye for the dramatic pose rather than maternal ardor. Neither Tom nor Daisy forms close ties with Nick or Jordan, although the former is Daisy’s cousin and the latter, whom Daisy has known since childhood, spends a good deal of time living under their roof. In this light, the couple’s frequent relocations – as Nick puts it, they “drifted here and there unrestfully” (10; ch. 1) – are not the cause of their lack of intimacy with others, but the result: they don’t stay in one place for any length of time because they don’t want to become close to anyone.

因此，汤姆与默特尔之间缺乏亲密关系也就不足为奇了。他并不想与情妇亲近；她只不过是他逃避与妻子亲近的工具。他对默特尔的态度也表明他并没有投入太多的感情。他只在自己方便的时候才叫她，为了不让黛西提出过分的要求，就谎称黛西因宗教信仰反对离婚，而当她最终还是提出要求时，他却漫不经心地用“一个利落的动作”（41；第二章）打断了她的鼻子。汤姆伤感地描述他最后一次回到那间专门用来幽会的小公寓，在那里他“坐下来像个孩子一样哭泣”（187；第九章），这表明他只是在沉溺于感伤的自我放纵，而非爱情。唯一能与汤姆的冷漠形成对比的，是默特尔对他缺乏真正的关心。

It is no surprise, therefore, that Tom’s relationship with Myrtle lacks intimacy. He has no desire to be close to his mistress; she is merely the means by which he avoids being close to his wife. And his treatment of Myrtle certainly suggests no deep emotional investment. He calls for her when it suits him, lies to her about Daisy’s religious opposition to divorce in order to keep her from becoming inconveniently demanding, and casually breaks her nose with “a short deft movement” (41; ch. 2) when she becomes so anyway. Tom’s maudlin account of his final visit to the small apartment he kept for their rendezvous, where he “sat down and cried like a baby” (187; ch. 9), suggests sentimental self-indulgence, not love. The only counterweight to Tom’s insensitivity to her is Myrtle’s lack of real concern for him.

对默特尔来说，汤姆·布坎南是她逃离乔治·威尔逊车库的通行证。通过汤姆，默特尔希望获得一个永久的归属感，在那里她可以展现她在两人公寓聚会上所表现出的那种“令人印象深刻的傲慢”，在聚会上，“她的笑声、手势和断言都变得越来越夸张”（35；第二章）。虽然小说中给出的默特尔追求汤姆的唯一动机是经济困境，而非对亲密关系的恐惧，但她与其他人的交往也表明她想要逃避情感上的亲密。她嫁给乔治·威尔逊显然并非出于对他的任何个人感情，而是因为她误以为他来自……她认为他比他实际出身的阶层更高贵：她“觉得他是个绅士”，“懂些教养”，当她得知他结婚时穿的那套体面西装是借来的，她“哭了一下午”（39；第二章）。乔治对默特尔的完全情感依赖，就像他坚信T·J·埃克尔伯格医生广告牌上的眼睛是上帝的眼睛一样，这表明他心理迷失，而非情感上的亲密。对于像乔治这样迷失方向的男人，默特尔不必担心他会靠得太近。而她对妹妹和麦基一家（显然是她仅有的朋友）虚伪的态度表明，这些关系为她提供了社交展示的机会，而非亲密关系。

For Myrtle, Tom Buchanan represents a ticket out of George Wilson’s garage. Through Tom, Myrtle hopes to acquire permanent membership in a world where she can display the “impressive hauteur” she enjoys exhibiting at the party in the couple’s apartment, during which “[h]er laughter, her gestures, her assertions became more violently affected moment by moment” (35; ch. 2). While economic desperation, rather than fear of intimacy, is the only motive given in the novel for Myrtle’s pursuit of Tom, her other relationships also suggest that she wants to avoid emotional closeness. She was apparently induced to marry George Wilson not by any personal feeling for him but by her mistaken impression that he was from a higher class than the one to which he belongs: she “thought he was a gentleman” who “knew something about breeding,” and when she learned that the good suit in which he was married was borrowed, she “cried to beat the band all afternoon” (39; ch. 2). George’s complete emotional dependence on Myrtle, like his belief that the billboard eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg are the eyes of God, suggests psychological disorientation rather than emotional intimacy. With a man as lost in space as George, Myrtle need not fear his getting too close. And her artificial behavior toward her sister and the McKees, apparently her only friends, indicates that these relationships provide opportunities for social display, not for intimacy.

尼克和乔丹之间的恋情揭示了他们也同样害怕亲密关系。事实上，尼克最初被乔丹的内敛，以及她所展现出的情感疏离感所吸引。他赞许地提到乔丹表面上的“完全的自给自足”（13；第一章），并用一些词语来描述她和黛西，这些词语都体现了她们情感疏离的吸引力：

The romance between Nick and Jordan reveals that they, too, fear intimacy. Indeed, Nick is first attracted to Jordan by her self-containment, by the image of emotional distance she projects. He refers approvingly to Jordan’s apparent “complete self sufficiency” (13; ch. 1) and describes her, along with Daisy, in terms that denote the appeal of their emotional aloofness:

有时黛西和贝克小姐会同时交谈，她们的谈话不引人注目，带着一种无关紧要的玩笑，但又不像是在闲聊，就像她们的白色连衣裙和她们毫无感情的眼神一样冷漠。

Sometimes [Daisy] and Miss Baker talked at once, unobtrusively and with a bantering inconsequence that was never quite chatter, that was as cool as their white dresses and their impersonal eyes in the absence of all desire.

（16-17；第1章）

(16–17; ch. 1)

他经常用傲慢、冷漠、冷漠和轻蔑等词语来形容他认为乔丹脸上“令人愉悦”（23；第一章）的表情。只要她看起来还属于一个遥远的世界——一个“阿什维尔、温泉城和棕榈滩的体育生活凹版印刷照片”（23；第一章）的世界——一个似乎不受情感现实影响的世界，他就对她保持着兴趣。然而，一旦她与布坎南一家共同居住的家中变得过于“混乱”，尼克便匆匆离去。从默特尔·威尔逊的死亡现场和她一起回来后，他拒绝了乔丹邀请他去布坎南家陪伴她的提议：“我才不会进去呢；我今天已经受够他们了，突然间乔丹也成了我的负担。她一定从我的表情中看出了这一点，因为她突然转身跑上门廊的台阶，进了屋”（150；第7章）。

He frequently uses words such as insolent, impersonal, cool, and contemptuous to describe what he considers the “pleasing” (23; ch. 1) expression on Jordan’s face. And he remains interested in her as long as she seems to belong to a faraway world, the world of “rotogravure pictures of the sporting life at Asheville and Hot Springs and Palm Beach” (23; ch. 1), a world seemingly untouched by emotional realities. However, once the household she shares with the Buchanans becomes too emotionally “untidy,” Nick beats a hasty retreat. After returning with her from the scene of Myrtle Wilson’s death, he declines Jordan’s invitation to keep her company in the Buchanan home: “I’d be damned if I’d go in; I’d had enough of them for one day and suddenly that included Jordan too. She must have seen something of this in my expression for she turned abruptly away and ran up the porch steps into the house” (150; ch. 7).

尼克随后开始躲避乔丹，不久后便以一种让他情感封闭的方式结束了这段关系。他刻意压抑着在默特尔去世第二天通过电话与她分手的记忆——“我不知道我们俩谁挂断了电话”（163页；第八章）——尽管他确实“抛弃了她”（186页；第九章），正如乔丹后来提醒他时我们得知的那样。即使在他与乔丹见面讨论他们之间发生的事情时，他也承认自己“避而不谈”（185页；第九章）了他们共同的过去，暗示着在谈话过程中，他们刻意回避了许多痛苦的问题。

Nick subsequently avoids Jordan and shortly thereafter ends the relationship in a manner that keeps him emotionally insulated. He represses the memory of breaking up with her on the telephone the day after Myrtle’s death – “I don’t know which of us hung up with a sharp click” (163; ch. 8) – although he did “throw [her] over” (186; ch. 9), as we learn when Jordan later reminds him of the event. And even when he meets with her to discuss what had happened between them, he admits that he “talked over and around” (185; ch. 9) their shared past, implying that there was a good deal of avoidance of painful issues during the conversation.

尼克对亲密关系的恐惧并非仅限于他与乔丹的关系，这一点可以从他之前的两段恋情中看出。尽管他声称自己“甚至连和明尼苏达老家的一位老朋友订婚的苗头都没有”（24；第一章），但他承认自己来到东部，部分原因是为了躲避当地关于他订婚的传言。正如他所说，他之所以会被“谣传结婚”（24；第一章），唯一的解释就是那位女士不认为自己只是个“老朋友”。当尼克​​决定在和乔丹交往之前“先彻底摆脱老家的那段纠葛”（64；第三章）时，我们才意识到她对他而言远不止是朋友。显然，这段关系比他愿意承认的要认真得多，而他想要结束这段关系。同样，在纽约，他“和公司会计部门的一个女孩有过一段短暂的恋情”，“但她哥哥开始对他恶语相向，所以当她七月份去度假时，他就悄悄地把这段关系抛诸脑后了”（61；第三章）。换句话说，当这段恋情发展到一定程度时，他就甩了她，而且很可能是为了避免一场情绪化的场面。在与女性的关系中，尼克是个逃避和否认的高手。

That Nick’s fear of intimacy is not limited to his relationship with Jordan is suggested by his two previous romances. Although he claims that he “wasn’t even vaguely engaged” to “an old friend” (24; ch. 1) back home in Minnesota,3 he admits that he came east, in part, to escape local rumors to that effect. The only way he could have been, as he puts it, “rumored into marriage” (24; ch. 1) was if the young lady in question didn’t consider herself just an “old friend.” We learn that she was more than a friend when Nick decides that, before getting involved with Jordan, “first [he] had to get [him]self definitely out of that tangle back home” (64; ch. 3). Clearly, this relationship was more serious than he cares to acknowledge, and he wants out. Similarly, in New York City he “had a short affair with a girl … who worked in the accounting department” at his place of business, “but her brother began throwing mean looks in [his] direction so when she went on her vacation in July [he] let it blow quietly away” (61; ch. 3). In other words, when the affair became somewhat serious, he dropped her, again in the manner most likely to avoid an emotional scene. In his relationships with women, Nick is a master of avoidance and denial.

正如乔丹那“冷漠傲慢的微笑”（63；第三章）所暗示的那样，她和尼克一样渴望保持情感上的孤立，而她的事业和她选择的朋友恰好让她能够做到这一点，这绝非偶然。她的体育生涯为她提供了一个现成的光鲜形象——“她摆在世人面前的那副百无聊赖、傲慢自大的面孔”（62；第三章）——以此来保护她免受与他人亲密关系的伤害。“她是一位高尔夫冠军，人人都知道她的名字”（62；第三章），但她通过各种“诡计”（63；第三章）确保人们对她的了解仅限于此。她选择像布坎南夫妇这样的朋友，他们更注重社交形象而非真正的情感交流，这也保护她免受亲密关系的伤害。他们和她一样，都不想与人亲近。正如尼克所观察到的，乔丹“本能地避开那些精明世故的男人”（63；第三章），因为他们可能会看穿她的伪装。当然，选择像尼克这样的男人，乔丹就能免受情感束缚的威胁。

As Jordan’s “cool insolent smile” (63; ch. 3) suggests, she shares Nick’s desire to remain emotionally insulated, and it is no coincidence that her career and the friends she chooses allow her to do so. Her sporting life provides a ready-made glossy image – “the bored haughty face that she turned to the world” (62; ch.3) – to shield her from intimacy with others. “[S]he was a golf champion and everyone knew her name” (62; ch. 3), but she made sure, through various “subterfuges” (63; ch. 3), that that’s all they knew about her. Her choice of friends like the Buchanans, who prefer the world of social image to that of genuine emotional engagement, also protects her from intimacy. They don’t want to be close any more than she does. And as Nick observes, Jordan “instinctively avoided clever shrewd men” (63; ch. 3) who might see through her charade. Surely, in choosing men like Nick, Jordan is safe from the threat of emotional ties.

尽管盖茨比和黛西之间炽热的婚外情似乎是为了与布坎南夫妇出于心理利益而缔结的婚姻，以及小说中其他所有情感疏离的关系形成对比，但盖茨比和黛西的恋情与其他恋情却有着惊人的相似之处。例如，黛西对盖茨比的亲密渴望并不比她对汤姆的亲密渴望更多。如果她知道盖茨比并非出身于她所在的社会阶层，那么她与盖茨比的婚外情，就像她之前与情人的恋情一样，都不会发生。她对盖茨比的任何感情都需要汤姆所提供的社会地位的巩固。事实上，在纽约酒店房间里，当汤姆揭露盖茨比的社会出身时，黛西立刻选择了疏远他。

Although the intense affair between Gatsby and Daisy seems to be offered as counterpoint to the Buchanans’ marriage of psychological convenience, and to all the other emotionally distant relationships in the novel as well, Gatsby and Daisy’s romance has striking similarities to the others. For example, Daisy has no more desire for intimacy with Gatsby than she has for intimacy with Tom. Her extramarital affair, like her earlier romance with her lover, would not have occurred had she known that Gatsby does not belong to her social class. Whatever she feels for Gatsby requires the reinforcement of the same social status Tom provides. Indeed, Tom’s revelation of Gatsby’s social origin during their confrontation in the New York hotel room results in Daisy’s immediate withdrawal:

盖茨比开始激动地和黛西说话，否认一切，为自己辩护，反驳那些根本没有提出的指控。但她每说一个字，她就更加确信这一点。她越来越沉浸于自己的世界，于是他放弃了，只有死去的梦想在午后悄然流逝中继续挣扎……挣扎着……朝着房间另一头那消失的声音前进。

[Gatsby] began to talk excitedly to Daisy, denying everything, defending his name against accusations that had not been made. But with every word she was drawing further and further into herself, so he gave that up and only the dead dream fought on as the afternoon slipped away … struggling … toward that lost voice across the room.

那声音再次恳求着要离开。

The voice begged again to go.

“求求你，汤姆！我再也受不了了。”

“Please, Tom! I can’t stand this any more.”

她惊恐的眼神表明，她曾经拥有的一切意图和勇气，都已荡然无存。

Her frightened eyes told that whatever intentions, whatever courage she had had, were definitely gone.

（142；第7章）

(142; ch. 7)

当黛西得知盖茨比并非出身名门时，盖茨比多年来对她的深情厚谊，以及她渴望成为他生命一部分的愿望，都烟消云散了。不久之后，黛西也离开了人世。盖茨比去世的第二天，她和汤姆收拾行装，离开了这座城市。

All the years of Gatsby’s devotion, as well as Daisy’s desire to be part of his life, disappear for her when she learns that Gatsby does not come from “the right side of the tracks.” And Daisy herself disappears shortly thereafter, as she and Tom pack their bags and leave town directly after Gatsby’s death the following day.

黛西并未意识到，盖茨比和默特尔对布坎南夫妇的作用几乎相同：他们都是彼此关系中的心理棋子。正如汤姆利用默特尔来逃避婚姻中的情感问题一样，黛西也利用盖茨比。盖茨比的出现恰逢其时，帮助黛西抵御了汤姆婚外情的新动向。执着的默特尔通过反复的电话，侵入了黛西的家。汤姆在黛西视线之外炫耀默特尔，并不像他在家中接听情妇的电话那样侵犯妻子的领地。伴侣的行为虽然能给我们带来心理上的满足——就像汤姆的婚外情给黛西带来满足一样——但这并不意味着这些行为不会给我们带来痛苦。这就是为什么心理问题经常被称为冲突：我们无意识地渴望某种特定的体验，因为它满足了心理需求，但由于这种需求是心理创伤的结果，所以这种体验往往是痛苦的。

Daisy doesn’t realize it, but Gatsby and Myrtle function in much the same capacity for the Buchanans: as psychological pawns in their relationship with each other. Just as Tom uses Myrtle to avoid the emotional problems in his marriage, so Daisy uses Gatsby. Gatsby came along again just in time to buffer Daisy from what seems to be a new development in Tom’s extramarital activities. The insistent Myrtle intrudes herself, by means of repeated telephone calls, right into Daisy’s home. Tom’s flaunting Myrtle out of Daisy’s sight does not invade his wife’s territory as does his accepting his mistress’s telephone calls at home. Just because a mate’s behavior has psychological payoffs for us – as Tom’s affairs do for Daisy – it does not mean that those behaviors do not also give us pain. That’s why psychological problems are so often referred to as conflicts: we unconsciously desire a particular experience because it fulfills a psychological need, but because that need is the result of a psychological wound, the experience is often painful.

黛西的婚姻变得痛苦不堪，而她与盖茨比的婚外情则成了她逃避现实的良方。有了盖茨比，她就可以告诉自己不需要汤姆，甚至不必去想汤姆（或者，更妙的是，她可以想着自己与盖茨比的婚外情是对汤姆的一种惩罚），因此，她才能在盖茨比的派对上对汤姆的拈花惹草表现得如此冷漠。黛西的婚外情由此成为一种心理防御机制，也因此凸显了她那段不幸婚姻在她心中的心理重要性：如果婚姻对她而言并非如此重要，她也就无需为此防御。事实上，正是婚姻在她潜意识中持续存在的重要性，最终让黛西感到足够安全，可以再次与盖茨比在一起。只要她与汤姆保持着心理上的联系，她就不必担心会像婚前那样对盖茨比产生依恋。

Daisy’s marriage has become painful, and her affair with Gatsby provides a welcome distraction. If she has Gatsby, she can tell herself that she doesn’t need Tom, that she doesn’t even have to think about Tom (or, better yet, she can think about how her affair with Gatsby is an appropriate punishment for Tom), and she can therefore afford the blasé attitude toward Tom’s womanizing that she exhibits at Gatsby’s party. Daisy’s affair thus functions as a psychological defense, and as such it underscores the psychological importance of her dysfunctional marriage: if her marriage weren’t a powerful force in her life then she wouldn’t have to defend against it. In fact, it is the continued unconscious importance of her marriage that finally makes Daisy feel safe enough to be with Gatsby again. As long as she remains psychologically involved with Tom, she need not fear that she will develop the kind of attachment she had to Gatsby before her marriage.

鉴于盖茨比和默特尔在布坎南夫妇的婚姻中是心理上的象征，汤姆和黛西实际上杀死了彼此的爱人，这具有重要的象征意义。虽然这表面上是一场意外，但黛西才是肇事司机。默特尔开着盖茨比的车。相比之下，汤姆派乔治·威尔逊带着武器、神志不清地去盖茨比家，这显然算不上什么意外。即便汤姆出于对自身和黛西性命的担忧，觉得必须告诉威尔逊是盖茨比杀了默特尔（至少汤姆是这么认为的），但如果他不是希望威尔逊会杀了妻子的情人，他完全可以打电话警告盖茨比。黛西似乎毫不犹豫地让盖茨比替默特尔的死背黑锅，这既表明她把盖茨比视为自己与外界情感的缓冲，也表明一旦她了解了盖茨比的社会出身，意识到他不再适合做她的情人，她便觉得他可有可无。

Given that Gatsby and Myrtle are psychological tokens in the Buchanans’ marriage, it is symbolically significant that Tom and Daisy, in effect, kill each other’s lover. Although it is apparently a genuine accident, Daisy is the driver who kills Myrtle with Gatsby’s car. Far less of an accident, surely, is Tom’s sending George Wilson, armed and crazed, to Gatsby’s house. Even if, from fear for his and Daisy’s lives, Tom felt he had to tell Wilson that it was Gatsby who killed Myrtle (or so Tom thought), had Tom not hoped Wilson would kill his wife’s lover he could have phoned Gatsby to warn him. That Daisy lets Gatsby take the blame for Myrtle’s death, apparently without a second thought, indicates both her conception of him as an emotional buffer between her and the world and, once her knowledge of his social origin renders him useless as her lover, his expendability.

对许多读者来说，盖茨比的例子或许是最难解释的害怕亲密关系的例子。他如此忠于黛西，如同“追寻圣杯”（156页；第八章），他甚至把所有关于黛西的消息都记录在剪贴簿里，在她漫长的婚姻生活中也始终对她忠贞不渝，而且他在那段时间里积累的所有财富都只是为了赢回黛西的心，我们又怎能说盖茨比害怕亲密关系呢？我们可以通过分析盖茨比忠于黛西的真正原因来论证这一点。

For many readers, perhaps the most difficult case to make for fear of intimacy is the case for Gatsby. How can we say that Gatsby fears intimacy when he is committed to Daisy as to “the following of a grail” (156; ch. 8), when he kept a scrapbook of all news items concerning her, when he remained faithful to her even during the long years of her married life, and when all the money he acquired during that time was acquired only to win Daisy back? We can make the case by examining what it is that Gatsby remains devoted to in remaining devoted to Daisy.

尽管盖茨比认为他最终的目标是拥有黛西——许多读者，以及尼克、乔丹、汤姆和黛西本人似乎也持有这种观点——但黛西仅仅是他实现目标的关键，而非目标本身。早在认识黛西之前，盖茨比就已将目光投向了财富和社会地位。吉米·盖茨（杰伊·盖茨比的法定姓名）的童年“日程表”——这位年轻人效仿本杰明·富兰克林的自我提升理念，将一天的时间分配在体育锻炼、学习电学、工作、运动、练习演讲和仪态举止以及研究必要的发明创造——表明他早已计划过上像约翰·D·洛克菲勒和安德鲁·卡内基那样白手起家、最终成为百万富翁的生活。

Although Gatsby believes that his ultimate goal is the possession of Daisy – a belief that many readers, as well as Nick, Jordan, Tom, and Daisy, seem to share – Daisy is merely the key to his goal rather than the goal itself. Gatsby had set his sights on the attainment of wealth and social status long before he knew Daisy. The boyhood “schedule” of Jimmy Gatz (Jay Gatsby’s legal name) – in which the young man divided his day, in the self-improvement tradition of Ben Franklin, among physical exercise, the study of electricity, work, sports, the practice of elocution and poise, and the study of needed inventions – suggests that he’d long planned to live the “rags-to-riches” life associated with such self-made millionaires as John D. Rockefeller and Andrew Carnegie.

盖茨比渴望跻身上流社会，源于他与贫困的父母——“游手好闲、一事无成的农民”（104页；第六章）——共同生活的不幸。显然，他童年的不幸并非仅仅源于家庭的贫困，正如盖茨先生对尼克所说：“他曾经说我吃得像猪一样，我为此揍了他一顿”（182页；第九章）。无论盖茨比在青年时期遭受了怎样的心理创伤，都足以让他彻底否定与父母的情感关系：“他的想象力从未真正接受过他们是他的父母”（104页；第六章）。因此，从精神分析的角度来看，盖茨比虚构的过去不仅仅是他伪装成上流社会成员的伎俩；它也是一种否认，一种心理防御机制，帮助他压抑对真实过去的记忆。他声称他虚构的家庭“全部去世了，[他]得到了一大笔钱”（70；第 4 章），在这种情况下，这成为他想要在心理上杀死父母的隐喻，因为父母的伤害性影响仍然存在于他的心理中，并且，矛盾的是，他想要从父母那里获得他们从未给予他的心理滋养——“金钱”。

Gatsby’s desire to move up in the world resulted from his unhappy life with his impoverished parents, “shiftless and unsuccessful farm people” (104; ch. 6). And, apparently, the unhappiness of his boyhood resulted from more than his family’s poverty, as is hinted when Mr. Gatz tells Nick, “He told me I et like a hog once and I beat him for it” (182; ch. 9). Whatever psychological traumas Gatsby suffered in his youth, they were sufficient to make him completely reject his emotional relationship with his parents: “his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all” (104; ch. 6). Thus, from a psychoanalytic perspective, Gatsby’s invented past is more than just a ploy to pass himself off as a member of the upper class; it’s also a form of denial, a psychological defense to help him repress the memory of his real past. And his claim that his invented family “all died and [he] came into a good deal of money” (70; ch. 4) becomes, in this context, a metaphor for his desire to psychologically kill the parents whose wounding influence still inhabits his own psyche and, paradoxically, receive from those parents the psychological nourishment – the “money” – they’d never given him.

盖茨比为自己规划的财富成就，直到遇见黛西之后，才最终展现出其心理上的回报。“她是他认识的第一个‘好’女孩……他以前也接触过这样的人，但彼此之间总是隔着一道难以察觉的铁丝网”（155；第八章）。通过黛西，他能够想象自己融入她的世界会是什么感觉，像她一样，“像银子一样闪耀，在穷人的苦苦挣扎之上，安全而骄傲”（157；第八章），而这些苦苦挣扎正是他年轻时经历过的，他不由自主地将它们与那段时期的心理痛苦联系起来。对他而言，黛西并非一个有血有肉的女人，而是他潜意识里渴望的情感隔离的象征：与自我、与詹姆斯·盖茨以及他所属的过去隔绝开来。正如我们在汤姆和黛西的例子中看到的，实现与自我情感隔绝的最佳方法就是避免与他人建立亲密关系。盖茨比对黛西近乎疯狂的理想化——她完美无瑕，不会犯错；她只爱他一人；时间也无法改变她——这无疑表明他试图逃避亲密关系，因为与理想化的对象建立亲密关系是不可能的。事实上，我们甚至无法真正了解我们理想化的对象，因为我们用理想化的形象代替了真实的人，而我们看到的也仅仅是理想化的形象。即使在他只能通过社交版面的新闻了解黛西的那些年里，盖茨比对黛西的痴迷也使他无法与其他女性建立亲密关系。

The financial achievements Gatsby planned for himself revealed their ultimate psychological payoff, however, only upon meeting Daisy. “She was the first ‘nice’ girl he had ever known. … [H]e had come in contact with such people but always with indiscernible barbed wire between” (155; ch. 8). Through Daisy, he could imagine what it would feel like to be part of her world, to be, as he felt she was, “gleaming like silver, safe and proud above the hot struggles of the poor” (157; ch. 8), the struggles he experienced as a youth, which he can’t help but associate with the psychological pain of that period of his life. Daisy is, for him, not a flesh-and-blood woman but an emblem of the emotional insulation he unconsciously desires: emotional insulation from himself, from James Gatz and the past to which he belongs. As we saw in the case of Tom and Daisy, the best way to achieve emotional insulation from oneself is to avoid intimacy with others. Gatsby’s outrageous idealization of Daisy as the perfect woman – she can do no wrong; she can love no one but him; time cannot change her – is a sure sign that he seeks to avoid intimacy, for it is impossible to be intimate with an ideal. In fact, we can’t even know a person we idealize because we substitute the ideal for the real human being, and that’s all we see. Even during the years when his only access to her was through the news items he read in the society pages, Gatsby’s obsession with Daisy protected him from intimacy with other women.

因此，值得注意的是，菲茨杰拉德无法想象盖茨比和黛西在长岛的这段情事中究竟经历了怎样的情感纠葛。正如作者在给埃德蒙·威尔逊的信中所述，他“对盖茨比和黛西从重逢到悲剧发生这段时期的情感关系一无所知，也毫无感觉”（《书信集》341-42页）。我认为，从精神分析的角度来看，菲茨杰拉德无法向我们描述他们的情感关系，是因为根本不存在这样的关系。我并非暗示盖茨比和黛西没有情感，而是说他们彼此之间的任何感觉都只是为了逃避某种更深层次的困扰，例如盖茨比不幸的童年、黛西不幸的婚姻，以及两人对亲密关系的恐惧。

It is significant, then, that Fitzgerald could not imagine what went on emotionally between Gatsby and Daisy during their Long Island affair. As the author notes in a letter to Edmund Wilson, he “had no feeling about or knowledge of … the emotional relations between Gatsby and Daisy from the time of their reunion to the catastrophe” (Letters 341–42). I think it is clear, from a psychoanalytic perspective, that Fitzgerald was unable to provide us with an account of their emotional relationship because there is none. I’m not suggesting that Gatsby and Daisy don’t experience emotions, but that whatever they feel for each other is always a means of avoiding feeling the effects of something else, something profoundly disturbing that they want to keep repressed, for example, Gatsby’s unhappy youth, Daisy’s dysfunctional marriage, and both characters’ fear of intimacy.

显然，精神分析的视角揭示了一个与通常人们所理解的《了不起的盖茨比》截然不同的爱情故事。正如小说所展现的，浪漫爱情是我们所有未解决的心理冲突反复上演的舞台。事实上，正是这种反复，这种破坏性行为的重复，告诉我们，未解决的心理冲突正在潜意识中“操控”着一切。以上讨论的所有人物都体现了这一原则，尽管在盖茨比对黛西的痴迷中，这一原则的运作最为戏剧化，也最为隐蔽——也就是说，最为压抑。因为盖茨比对自身心理动机的压抑程度超过了其他所有人物的总和。他那句名言“过去无法重演？……当然可以！”（116；第六章）在此语境下尤为意义深远，因为它暗示了……的隐含前提。小说的精神分析内容正是基于此：我们对心理创伤的压抑使我们注定要反复遭受同样的创伤。盖茨比孤独地追求黛西，重现了他青年时代的孤独。在他为迎接黛西而购置的豪宅里——他唯一使用或放置个人物品的房间只有卧室——他似乎仍然感到格格不入，就像当年在父母家中一样。黛西的离弃，无论是她嫁给汤姆，还是在默特尔·威尔逊去世当晚他再次失去她，黛西又被他的情敌夺走，都无疑比父母带给他的伤痛更加深刻。因此，无论《了不起的盖茨比》是否有意为之，它都向我们展示了浪漫关系如何有效地助长我们对心理创伤的压抑，从而不可避免地将我们带入过去，正如小说结尾处精辟地指出的那样（189页；第九章）。

Clearly, a psychoanalytic lens reveals a much different love story than the one ordinarily associated with The Great Gatsby. As the novel illustrates, romantic love is the stage on which all of our unresolved psychological conflicts are dramatized, over and over. Indeed, it’s the over-and-over, the repetition of destructive behavior, that tells us an unresolved psychological conflict is “pulling the strings” from the unconscious. All of the characters discussed above illustrate this principle, though its operations are, at once, most dramatic and most camouflaged – that is, most repressed – in Gatsby’s obsession with Daisy. For Gatsby’s repression of his psychological motives outstrips that of all the other characters put together. His famous words “Can’t repeat the past? … Why of course you can!” (116; ch. 6) are especially meaningful in this context because they betoken the implicit premise on which the psychoanalytic content of the novel is based: that our repression of psychological wounds condemns us to repeatedly incur them. Gatsby’s lonely pursuit of Daisy replays the loneliness of his youth, and he seems to feel as much an outsider in the mansion he bought to receive her – the only room he uses or marks with a personal possession is his bedroom – as he must have felt in the home of his parents. Surely, Gatsby could not have been wounded more severely by his parents than he is by Daisy’s abandonment of him, both when she married Tom and when he loses her again to his rival the night of Myrtle Wilson’s death. Thus, whether it intends to do so or not, The Great Gatsby shows us how effectively romantic relationships can facilitate our repression of psychological wounds and thereby inevitably carry us, as the novel’s closing line so aptly puts it, “ceaselessly into the past” (189; ch. 9).

拓展练习题：运用精神分析方法解读其他文学作品

Questions for further practice: psychoanalytic approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用精神分析批评来解读文中提及的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。问题5提供了一种专门针对拉康的文学分析方法。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use psychoanalytic criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice. Question 5 offers a specifically Lacanian approach to literature.

1理解被压抑之物的回归如何能帮助我们理解托妮·莫里森的小说《宠儿》 （1987）中转世的宠儿（她可能被视为前奴隶们难以忍受的过去的化身）与塞丝、保罗·D以及黑人社区之间的关系？

1 How might an understanding of the return of the repressed help us understand the relationship of the reincarnated Beloved (who might be viewed as the embodiment of the former slaves’ unbearable pasts) to Sethe, Paul D, and the black community in Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987)?

2了解死亡工作如何投射到环境中，如何帮助我们理解约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》（1902 年）中的马洛？

2 How might an understanding of the ways in which death work can be projected onto the environment help us interpret Marlow in Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness (1902)?

3理解否认和转移（在这种情况下，将对丈夫的负面情绪转移到孩子身上）如何能帮助我们分析蒂莉·奥尔森 (Tillie Olsen) 的小说《我站在这里熨衣服》(1956) 中叙述者与她问题重重的女儿之间的关系？

3 How might an understanding of denial and displacement (in this case, displacement of negative feelings for one’s husband onto one’s child) help us analyze the narrator’s relationship to her troubled daughter in Tillie Olsen’s “I Stand Here Ironing” (1956)?

4我们如何运用对压抑、超我和梦境象征意义（尤其是水作为情感或性欲的象征）的理解来帮助我们解读艾米莉·狄金森的《我早早出发——带上了我的狗》（1862 年）？

4 How might we use an understanding of repression, the superego, and dream symbolism (especially water as a symbol of the emotions or of sexuality) to help us interpret Emily Dickinson’s “I Started Early – Took My Dog” (1862)?

5我们如何论证玛丽·雪莱的小说《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818）的主人公维克多的经历源于他对想象秩序的怀旧以及他对象征秩序的矛盾关系？我们又如何进一步论证维克多对伊丽莎白和克莱瓦尔的感情，甚至他创造怪物的动机，都是他内心对“小客体a”的渴望的转移？

5 How might we argue that the experiences of Victor, the protagonist in Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818), result from his nostalgia for the Imaginary Order and his conflicted relationship to the Symbolic Order? How might we further argue that Victor’s feelings for Elizabeth and Clerval, and even Victor’s motive for creating the Monster, are all displacements of the desire for his objet petit a?

Notes

1卡尔·荣格（1875-1961）的心理学理论催生了一个心理学文学批评流派，该流派既不同于弗洛伊德的古典精神分析，也不同于拉康的精神分析。本章讨论的是荣格批评。事实上，要充分阐述荣格批评（有时也称为原型批评或神话批评），需要单独成章。本书未涉及荣格批评，是因为其实践目前尚未普及到足以将其纳入教材的程度。无论如何，希望学习荣格批评的学生需要首先对经典精神分析有较为透彻的理解，本章将对此进行介绍。荣格的全集列于“延伸阅读”部分。

1 The psychological theories of Carl G. Jung (1875–1961) have generated a school of psychological literary criticism distinct from both the Freudian, or classical, and Lacanian psychoanalytic criticism discussed in this chapter. Jungian criticism is not covered in this textbook because its practice is not widespread enough at this time to warrant its inclusion. 3. 马克思主义批评

3   Marxist criticism

初涉批判理论的学生常常会问，既然欧洲共产主义阵营已经失败，为何我们还要学习马克思主义批判，这岂不是证明马克思主义并非一种可行的理论？这种问题不仅忽略了世界其他地区共产主义国家的存在，还忽略了两个重要的事实。首先，除了少数规模相对较小、存在时间较短的公社之外，历史上从未出现过完全符合卡尔·马克思（1818-1883）所提出的原则的社会，正如历史上从未出现过完全符合其抽象定义的民主制度一样。其次，即便所有共产主义国家都是真正的马克思主义社会，即便它们全部失败，马克思主义理论仍然能够为我们理解历史和时事提供一种有意义的途径。事实上，我们可以运用马克思主义批判来解读马克思主义社会的失败。然而，在我们尝试用马克思主义视角解读此类政治事件，或任何类型的事件之前，我们首先必须理解马克思主义理论。

Students new to the study of critical theory often ask why we study Marxist criticism now that the Communist Bloc in Europe has failed, thereby proving that Marxism is not a viable theory. In addition to ignoring the existence of communist countries in other parts of the world, such a question overlooks two important facts. First, beyond some relatively small and relatively short-lived communes, there has never been a society completely in keeping with the principles developed by Karl Marx (1818–83), just as there has never been a democracy completely in keeping with its abstract definition. Second, even if all communist countries were true Marxist societies and even if all of them had failed, Marxist theory would still give us a meaningful way to understand history and current events. Indeed, one could use Marxist criticism to interpret the failure of a Marxist society. However, before we can attempt a Marxist interpretation of such political events, or of events of any kind, we must first, of course, understand Marxist theory.

马克思主义的基本前提

The fundamental premises of Marxism

马克思主义理论究竟是什么？让我们先从回答另一个问题入手：马克思主义批评家会如何评价前一章关于精神分析批评的内容？他们会说，精神分析将我们的注意力集中在个体心理及其家庭情结的根源上，从而分散了我们对创造人类经验的真正力量——构建人类社会的经济体系——的关注。事实上，马克思主义批评家对本书讨论的所有其他理论都会提出类似的批评。如果一种理论没有将人类文化的经济现实置于首位，那么它就误解了人类文化。对马克思主义而言，获取和维持经济权力是所有社会和政治活动背后的动机，包括教育、哲学、宗教、政府、艺术、科学、技术、媒体等等。因此，经济是社会/政治/意识形态现实上层建筑的基础。经济权力因此总是包含社会和政治权力，而社会和政治权力正是建立在经济之上的。为什么今天许多马克思主义者在谈论阶级结构时会提到社会经济阶级，而不是经济阶级。

What exactly is Marxist theory? Let’s begin to answer that question by answering another: what would Marxist critics say about the preceding chapter on psychoanalytic criticism? They would say that, by focusing our attention on the individual psyche and its roots in the family complex, psychoanalysis distracts our attention from the real forces that create human experience: the economic systems that structure human societies. Indeed, Marxist critics would have the same complaint, more or less, about all the other theories discussed in this book. If a theory does not foreground the economic realities of human culture, then it misunderstands human culture. For Marxism, getting and keeping economic power is the motive behind all social and political activities, including education, philosophy, religion, government, the arts, science, technology, the media, and so on. Thus, economics is the base on which the superstructure of social/political/ideological realities is built. Economic power therefore always includes social and political power as well, which is why many Marxists today refer to socioeconomic class, rather than economic class, when talking about the class structure.

在马克思主义术语中，经济条件被称为物质条件，而由物质条件产生的社会/政治/意识形态氛围则被称为历史情境。对于马克思主义批评家而言，如果不理解人类事件（无论是政治领域还是个人领域）或人类生产（从核潜艇到电视节目），就无法理解这些事件和生产发生的具体物质/历史情境。也就是说，所有人类事件和生产都有其特定的物质/历史原因。对人类事务的准确理解并非源于对抽象的、永恒的本质或原则的探寻，而是源于对现实世界具体条件的理解。因此，马克思主义对人类事件和生产的分析侧重于社会经济阶级之间的关系，既包括社会内部的关系，也包括社会之间的关系，并从经济权力的分配和动态变化的角度来解释一切人类活动。马克思主义实践，或者说方法论，要求理论思想的价值只能通过其具体应用来判断，也就是说，只能通过其对现实世界的适用性来判断。

In Marxist terminology, economic conditions are referred to as material circumstances, and the social/political/ideological atmosphere generated by material conditions is called the historical situation. For the Marxist critic, neither human events (in the political or personal domain) nor human productions (from nuclear submarines to television shows) can be understood without understanding the specific material/historical circumstances in which those events and productions occur. That is, all human events and productions have specific material/historical causes. An accurate picture of human affairs cannot be obtained by the search for abstract, timeless essences or principles but only by understanding concrete conditions in the world. Therefore, Marxist analysis of human events and productions focuses on relationships among socioeconomic classes, both within a society and among societies, and it explains all human activities in terms of the distribution and dynamics of economic power. And Marxist praxis, or methodology, dictates that theoretical ideas can be judged to have value only in terms of their concrete applications, that is, only in terms of their applicability to the real world.

从马克思主义的视角来看，社会经济阶级的差异比宗教、种族、民族或性别的差异更能造成人与人之间的分裂。简而言之，真正的斗争界限划分在“有产者”和“无产者”之间，划分在资产阶级（控制着世界自然、经济和人力资源的人）和无产阶级（占全球人口绝大多数、生活在恶劣条件下、长期从事体力劳动——采矿、工厂工作、挖沟、修建铁路——为富人敛财的人）之间。不幸的是，无产阶级往往是最后才意识到这一点的人；他们通常允许宗教、种族、民族或性别的差异将他们分裂成相互敌对的派系，而这些派系几乎无法带来任何社会变革。如今，很少有马克思主义者像马克思那样相信，无产阶级终有一天会自发地觉醒阶级意识，从而发动暴力革命反抗压迫者，建立一个无阶级社会。然而，如果任何一个国家的无产阶级能够团结一致，不计彼此间的差异（例如，如果他们都投票给相同的政治候选人，抵制相同的公司，并举行罢工直到他们的需求得到满足），那么当前的权力结构将会发生根本性的改变。

From a Marxist perspective, differences in socioeconomic class divide people in ways that are much more significant than differences in religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. For the real battle lines are drawn, to put the matter simply, between the “haves” and the “have-nots,” between the bourgeoisie – those who control the world’s natural, economic, and human resources – and the proletariat, the majority of the global population who live in substandard conditions and who have always performed the manual labor – the mining, the factory work, the ditch digging, the railroad building – that fills the coffers of the rich. Unfortunately, those in the proletariat are often the last to recognize this fact; they usually permit differences in religion, race, ethnicity, or gender to separate them into warring factions that accomplish little or no social change. Few Marxists today believe, as Marx did, that the proletariat will one day spontaneously develop the class consciousness needed to rise up in violent revolution against their oppressors and create a classless society. However, were the proletariat of any given country to act as a group, regardless of their differences (for example, were they all to vote for the same political candidates, boycott the same companies, and go on strike until their needs were met), the current power structure would be radically altered.

美国阶级制度

The class system in America

在美国，越来越难以将人明确地归类为资产阶级或无产阶级。例如，我们如何定义一个小型家族企业主，他雇佣了多名工人，但其年利润却低于大公司销售人员的年薪？换句话说，至少在这个国家，一些工人的收入高于一些老板。更复杂的是，“资产阶级”（名词）和“资产阶级的”（形容词）这两个词在日常用语中已经泛指中产阶级，不再区分老板和工薪阶层。因此，在当今历史阶段，或许根据社会经济生活方式对美国人进行分类更为有效，而无需考虑他们的收入来源。为了便于理解，我们现在不妨花点时间，简要概述一下当代美国的主要社会经济分化。

It has become increasingly difficult in the United States to clearly place people either in the bourgeoisie or the proletariat. How do we classify, for example, the person who employs several workers in a small, family-owned business but whose yearly profits are less than the annual wages of a salesperson working for a big corporation? In other words, in this country at least, some workers earn more than some owners. To complicate matters further, the words bourgeoisie (noun) and bourgeois (adjective) have come to refer in everyday speech to the middle class in general, with no distinction between owners and wage earners. At this point in history, therefore, it might be more useful to classify Americans according to socioeconomic lifestyle, without reference to the manner in which their income is acquired. For the sake of clarity, let’s take a moment to do so now by drawing a simplified sketch of the major socioeconomic divisions in contemporary America.

无论我们是否认同哪些人属于资产阶级，哪些人属于无产阶级，大多数人都能观察到以下群体在社会经济生活方式上的显著差异：无家可归者，他们几乎没有任何物质财富，也看不到任何改善的希望；贫困者，由于教育和职业机会有限，他们不得不挣扎求生，勉力维持生计，时刻生活在流离失所的恐惧之中；经济条件优越者，他们拥有漂亮的房子和汽车，通常也能负担得起子女的大学教育；富裕者，他们可以拥有两套或更多套豪宅、几辆汽车和各种奢侈品；以及超级富豪，例如大型知名企业的拥有者，对他们来说，金钱（豪宅、豪华轿车、私人飞机、游艇）根本不成问题。我们可以粗略地将这五个群体分别称为美国的底层阶级、下层阶级、中产阶级、上层阶级和“贵族”。

Whether or not we would agree on which individuals belong to the bourgeoisie and which to the proletariat, most of us can observe the striking difference in socioeconomic lifestyle among the following groups: the homeless, who have few, if any, material possessions and little hope of improvement; the poor, whose limited educational and career opportunities keep them struggling to support their families and living in fear of becoming homeless; the financially established, who own nice homes and cars and can usually afford to send their children to college; the well-todo, who can afford two or more expensive homes, several cars, and luxury items; and the extremely wealthy, such as the owners of large, well-established corporations, for whom money (mansions, limousines, personal airplanes, yachts) is no problem whatsoever. We might loosely refer to these five groups as America’s underclass, lower class, middle class, upper class, and “aristocracy.”

显然，底层阶级和下层阶级在经济上受到压迫：他们饱受经济匮乏之苦，受经济衰退的打击最为严重，且改善自身境遇的途径有限。与之形成鲜明对比的是，上层阶级和“贵族”在经济上享有特权：他们享受奢华的生活方式，受经济衰退的影响最小，且拥有相当的经济保障。那么，中产阶级呢？他们是在经济上受到压迫还是享有特权？答案很可能是两者兼而有之。他们的社会经济生活水平无疑优于下层阶级，但他们可能永远无法拥有豪宅；他们的经济状况比下层阶级更加稳定，但他们也常常受到经济衰退的严重冲击，并且通常有充分的理由担忧自己的经济前景；他们受益于制度化的经济保障，例如良好的医疗保险和养老金计划，但相对于他们的收入而言，他们也承担着巨大的（而且许多人认为是不公平的）税负。

Clearly, members of the underclass and the lower class are economically oppressed: they suffer the ills of economic privation, are hardest hit by economic recessions, and have limited means of improving their lot. In sharp contrast, members of the upper class and “aristocracy” are economically privileged: they enjoy luxurious lifestyles, are least affected by economic recessions, and have a great deal of financial security. But what about members of the middle class? Are they economically oppressed or economically privileged? Of course, the answer is probably both. Their socioeconomic lifestyle is certainly better than that of the classes below them, but they’ll probably never own a mansion; they have more financial stability than the lower classes, yet they are often hard hit by economic recessions and usually have good reason to worry about their financial future; they benefit from institutionalized forms of economic security, such as good medical insurance and pension plans, but they shoulder an enormous (and, many would argue, unfair) tax burden relative to their income.

为什么经济上受压迫的人不反抗？是什么让底层阶级“安分守己”，任由富人摆布？至少对于当今美国的穷人和无家可归者来说，生存的挣扎无疑是压抑他们的重要因素。当一个人为了生存和养活孩子而苦苦挣扎时，谁还有时间参与政治活动，甚至还有时间去关注政治？压迫他们的其他因素还包括警察和其他政府强力机构，这些机构奉政府之命，虐待底层阶级和贫困阶层。那些被视为对权力结构构成威胁的人，例如美国工会早期罢工的工人，他们遭到逮捕、殴打甚至杀害；又如几年前纽约中央公园里无家可归的流浪汉，因为他们的棚屋实际上“破坏了”附近豪华公寓富人的视野，而被驱逐出纸箱。然而，穷人遭受的压迫，更多地来自意识形态。

Why don’t the economically oppressed fight back? What keeps the lower classes “in their place” and at the mercy of the wealthy? At least for the poor and homeless in America today, the struggle to survive is certainly a factor in keeping them down. Who has the time to become politically active, or even politically aware, when one is struggling just to stay alive and feed one’s children? Other elements oppressing them are the police and other government strong-arm agencies, who, under government orders, have mistreated the lower-class and underclass poor, who are perceived as a threat to the power structure, such as the striking workers who were arrested, beaten, or killed in the early days of American labor unions or the homeless who were routed from their cardboard boxes in New York’s Central Park some years ago because their shanties, in effect, “ruined the view” from the windows of the wealthy living in posh apartments nearby. The poor are oppressed even more effectively, however, by ideology.

意识形态的作用

The role of ideology

对马克思主义而言，意识形态是一种信仰体系，而所有信仰体系都是文化制约的产物。例如，资本主义、共产主义、马克思主义、爱国主义、宗教、伦理体系、人道主义、环保主义、占星术和空手道都是意识形态。本书将要探讨的批判理论也都是意识形态。甚至我们关于自然遵循科学规律的假设也是一种意识形态。然而，尽管我们能想到的几乎所有经验或研究领域都包含意识形态成分，但并非所有意识形态都同样有效或可取。不良的意识形态会推行压制性的政治议程，为了确保其被民众接受，它们会伪装成看待世界的自然方式，而不是承认自身是意识形态。“男性担任领导职位是自然而然的，因为他们的生理优势使他们在体力、智力和情感上都比女性更胜一筹”是一种性别歧视的意识形态，它将自身包装成自然规律，而非文化信仰的产物。 “每个家庭都想拥有自己的土地和房屋”是一种资本主义意识形态，它通过指出几乎所有美国人都想拥有自己的房产这一事实，将这种想法包装成一种自然而然的观念，却忽略了这种欲望是由我们所处的资本主义文化塑造的。与此相反，许多美洲原住民部落并不认为土地是可以被拥有的。对他们来说，这就像试图拥有我们呼吸的空气一样。

For Marxism, an ideology is a belief system, and all belief systems are products of cultural conditioning. For example, capitalism, communism, Marxism, patriotism, religion, ethical systems, humanism, environmentalism, astrology, and karate are all ideologies. The critical theories we will study in this book are all ideologies. Even our assumption that nature behaves according to the laws of science is an ideology. However, although almost any experience or field of study we can think of has an ideological component, not all ideologies are equally productive or desirable. Undesirable ideologies promote repressive political agendas and, in order to ensure their acceptance among the citizenry, pass themselves off as natural ways of seeing the world instead of acknowledging themselves as ideologies. “It’s natural for men to hold leadership positions because their biological superiority renders them more physically, intellectually, and emotionally capable than women” is a sexist ideology that sells itself as a function of nature, rather than as a product of cultural belief. “Every family wants to own its own home on its own land” is a capitalist ideology that sells itself as natural by pointing, for example, to the fact that almost all Americans want to own their own property, without acknowledging that this desire is created in us by the capitalist culture in which we live. Many Native American nations, in contrast, don’t believe that land is something that can be owned. For them, it’s like trying to own the air we breathe.

压制性意识形态伪装成看待世界的自然方式，阻碍我们理解我们所处的物质/历史条件，因为它们拒绝承认这些条件对我们看待世界的方式有任何影响。马克思主义作为一种非压制性意识形态，承认自身是一种意识形态。马克思主义致力于让我们时刻意识到自身是如何成为物质/历史环境的产物，以及那些压制性意识形态如何蒙蔽我们的双眼，使我们对统治权力体系保持顺从。尽管马克思主义理论家们对我们受意识形态“影响”的程度看法不一，但他们一致认为，最成功的意识形态并非被视为意识形态，而是被信奉者视为看待世界的自然方式。因此，尽管我们可以论证，为了实现更公平的资源分配，美国中产阶级的经济利益最好通过与穷人结成政治联盟来实现，但……美国中下阶层拥有巨额财富，但在政治事务上，中产阶级通常站在富人一边，反对穷人。

By posing as natural ways of seeing the world, repressive ideologies prevent us from understanding the material/historical conditions in which we live because they refuse to acknowledge that those conditions have any bearing on the way we see the world. Marxism, a nonrepressive ideology, acknowledges that it is an ideology. Marxism works to make us constantly aware of all the ways in which we are products of material/historical circumstances and of the repressive ideologies that serve to blind us to this fact in order to keep us subservient to the ruling power system. Although Marxist theorists differ in their estimation of the degree to which we are “programmed” by ideology, all agree that the most successful ideologies are not recognized as ideologies but are thought to be natural ways of seeing the world by the people who subscribe to them. Thus, although we could argue that the economic interests of middle-class America would best be served by a political alliance with the poor in order to attain a more equitable distribution of America’s enormous wealth among the middle and lower classes, in political matters the middle class generally sides with the wealthy against the poor.

举个简单的例子，中产阶级往往对穷人心怀怨恨，因为大量中产阶级的税款被用于政府扶贫项目。然而，中产阶级却忽视了两个重要的社会经济现实：(1) 掌握权力的富人决定谁缴纳最多的税款以及如何使用这些钱（换句话说，是富人让中产阶级去扶贫）；(2) 穷人实际得到的资金少之又少，因为大部分资金通过回扣和“巧妙”的账目运作，流入了控制社会服务的富人以及管理这些服务的中产阶级雇员的口袋。究竟是什么样的意识形态蒙蔽了中产阶级的双眼，让他们看不到当代美国的社会经济不平等？很大程度上，是他们对“美国梦”的盲目信仰。这种信仰告诉他们，经济上的成功仅仅是靠主动性和努力工作就能实现的。因此，如果有人贫穷，那是因为他们游手好闲、懒惰成性。在这个国家，我们认为“出人头地”是人之常情，想要拥有更好的房子，穿更好的衣服，都是人之常情。这里的关键词是“更好”，它不仅指“比我以前拥有的更好”，也指“比别人拥有的更好”。也就是说，在“出人头地”的信念中，蕴含着竞争作为一种自然或必要生存方式的信念。毕竟，我们不是已经从科学中了解到，自然界遵循“适者生存”的法则吗？这种对人类行为的看法，难道不与美国赖以建立的、崇尚个人主义的信念完美契合吗？没有这种个人主义，美国就不会成为今天这样伟大的国家。就此而言，上述所有因素——出人头地、竞争和崇尚个人主义——难道不都是美国梦不可或缺的一部分吗？根据美国梦，我们生而平等，可以凭借自身的努力和进取心去实现人生的无限可能。

To cite one simple example, the middle class tends to resent the poor because so much middle-class tax money goes to government programs to help the poor. However, the middle class fails to realize two important socioeconomic realities: (1) that it is the wealthy in positions of power who decide who pays the most taxes and how the money will be spent (in other words, it is the wealthy who make the middle class support the poor), and (2) that the poor receive but a small portion of the funds earmarked for them because so much of it goes, through kickbacks and “creative” bookkeeping, into the pockets of the wealthy who control our social services and the middle-class employees who administer them. What is the ideology that blinds the middle class to the socioeconomic inequities in contemporary America? In large part, the middle class is blinded by their belief in the American dream, which tells them that financial success is simply the product of initiative and hard work. Therefore, if some people are poor, it is because they are shiftless and lazy. In this country, we believe that it is natural to want to “get ahead,” to want to own a better house and wear better clothes. The key word here is better, which refers not only to “better than I had before” but also to “better than other people have.” That is, embedded within the belief in “getting ahead” is the belief in competition as a natural or necessary mode of being. After all, haven’t we learned from science that nature demands the “survival of the fittest”? And doesn’t this view of human behavior fit perfectly with the belief in rugged individualism upon which America was founded and without which it would not have become the great nation it is today? For that matter, isn’t all of the above – getting ahead, competition, and rugged individualism – part and parcel of the American dream, according to which we are all born equal and are free to advance as far as our own “get-up-and-go” will take us?

虽然这种看待人类奋斗的观点，至少对大多数美国人来说，似乎相当自然合理——我们当然可以举出本杰明·富兰克林和亚伯拉罕·林肯等白手起家的成功案例来佐证其表面上的公平性——但马克思主义分析表明，“美国梦”是一种意识形态，一种信仰体系，而非一种与生俱来或自然而然的世界观。就像所有支持资本主义国家（例如我们这样的国家）社会经济不平等的意识形态一样——也就是说，在这些国家，生产资料（自然资源、金融资源和人力资源）为私人所有，而拥有这些资源的人必然成为统治阶级——“美国梦”使我们对自身过去和现在所犯下的巨大错误视而不见：对美洲原住民的种族灭绝、对非洲人的奴役、对契约劳工的实质奴役、对移民群体的虐待、美国贫富差距的日益扩大、无家可归者和饥饿人口的不断增长、针对妇女和有色人种的长期存在的社会经济障碍等等。换句话说，美国的成功少数人追求富裕生活的梦想，建立在多数人的苦难之上。正是意识形态的力量，正是我们对这个梦想的自然性和公平性的盲目信仰，蒙蔽了我们的双眼，使我们看不到它所掩盖的残酷现实。

While this view of human endeavor may seem, to most Americans at least, quite natural and proper – and we can certainly point to the success of self-made men like Benjamin Franklin and Abraham Lincoln to underscore its apparent fairness – Marxist analysis reveals that the American dream is an ideology, a belief system, not an innate or natural way of seeing the world. And like all ideologies that support the socioeconomic inequities of capitalist countries like ours – that is, countries in which the means of production (natural, financial, and human resources) are privately owned and in which those who own them inevitably become the dominant class – the American dream blinds us to the enormities of its own failure, past and present: the genocide of Native Americans, the enslavement of Africans, the virtual enslavement of indentured servants, the abuses suffered by immigrant populations, the widening economic gulf between America’s rich and poor, the growing ranks of the homeless and hungry, the enduring socioeconomic barriers against women and people of color, and the like. In other words, the success of the American dream – the acquisition of a wealthy lifestyle for a few – rests on the misery of the many. And it is the power of ideology, of our belief in the naturalness and fairness of this dream, that has blinded us to the harsh realities it masks.

此时，我们中的一些人或许会停下来思考：“但美国梦难道不是一种理想吗？即便我们的理想在实践中可能落空，我们难道不应该继续追求它们吗？例如，仅仅因为我们有时无法践行‘人的生命神圣不可侵犯’这一理想，我们就应该放弃它吗？”在马克思主义看来，当一种理想掩盖其自身的失败时，它就是一种虚假的理想，或者说是一种虚假的意识，其真正目的是为了维护当权者的利益。因此，就美国梦而言，马克思主义分析的问题是：“美国梦是如何获得所有美国人的支持，甚至是那些未能实现它的人的支持，从而维护当权者的利益的？”

Some of us might want to pause at this point to ask, “But isn’t the American dream an ideal? Although our ideals may fail in practice, shouldn’t we continue to aspire to them? Should we abandon, for example, the ideal that human life is sacred just because we sometimes fail to live up to it?” For Marxism, when an ideal functions to mask its own failure, it is a false ideal, or false consciousness, whose real purpose is to promote the interests of those in power. In the case of the American dream, then, the question for Marxist analysis is, “How does the American dream enlist the support of all Americans, even of those who fail to achieve it, in promoting the interests of those in power?”

答案至少部分在于，美国梦就像州彩票或它最新化身的巨额奖金抽奖一样，让每个人都有机会获胜，而我们就像赌徒一样，紧紧抓住这种可能性不放。事实上，我们的经济保障越少，就越需要一些希望。美国梦也告诉我们想听的话：我们“和”最富有的人一样优秀。只要我相信这是真的，富人是否认为我和他们一样优秀就无关紧要。而且，“和他们一样优秀”并不意味着享有同样的医疗保健、物质享受或社会特权，包括在必要时聘请顶尖律师的权利，这也无关紧要。为了“自我感觉良好”，尤其是在我的生活充满经济压力时，我会紧紧抓住美国梦所提供的自我满足感。同样地，如果我想避免因积累巨额财富而感到内疚——尤其是在许多同胞勉强糊口的情况下——那么“美国梦”会给我带来安慰，让我相信我理应获得我努力积累的任何财富。事实上，“美国梦”掩盖物质/历史现实的力量如此强大，以至于它可以描绘出一个阶级无关紧要的美国，并将这种意识形态强加于一个阶级体系过于复杂、我无法详尽描绘的美国，除了之前给出的粗略轮廓之外。

The answer, at least in part, is that the American dream, much like the state lotteries or the big-bucks sweepstakes that are its latest incarnation, opens the possibility that anyone can win, and, like gambling addicts, we cling to that possibility. In fact, the less financial security we have, the more we need something to hope for. The American dream also tells us what we want to hear: that we are all “as good as” the wealthiest among us. It’s not supposed to matter that the wealthy don’t think I’m as good as they are as long as I believe it’s true. And it’s not supposed to matter that “as good as” doesn’t mean entitled to the same health care, material comforts, or social privileges, including the privilege of hiring the best lawyers should the need arise. In my need to “feel good about myself,” especially if my life is burdened with financial worries, I will cling to the ego gratification offered by the American dream. Analogously, if I want to avoid the guilt that accompanies my acquisition of a large fortune while so many of my fellow citizens can barely eke out a living, I will be comforted by the assurance I receive from the American dream that I deserve whatever wealth I have the initiative to amass. Indeed, the power of the American dream to mask material/historical reality is such that it can invoke an America for whom class doesn’t matter and plunk that ideology down right in the middle of an America whose class system is too complex for me to map, beyond the rough outline provided earlier.

从马克思主义的视角来看，意识形态在维护权力方面发挥着至关重要的作用，因此我们应该简要考察几个例子，以便了解其运作方式。例如，阶级主义是一种将人的价值与其所属的社会阶级划等号的意识形态：社会阶级越高，人就越被认为优秀，因为品质是“与生俱来的”。从阶级主义的视角来看，处于社会阶梯顶端的人自然优于其下层的人：他们更聪明、更负责、更值得信赖、更有道德等等。由此推断，处于社会阶梯底端的人自然游手好闲、懒惰成性、不负责任。因此，最高社会阶级的人掌握所有权力是理所当然的。阶级主义之所以能使穷人占据权力和领导地位，是因为他们天生适合这些角色，也只有他们才能被信任地胜任这些角色。因此，阶级主义必然会加剧对穷人的社会、经济和政治歧视。

From a Marxist perspective, the role of ideology in maintaining those in power is so important that we should briefly examine a few more examples so that we can see how it works. Classism, for example, is an ideology that equates one’s value as a human being with the social class to which one belongs: the higher one’s social class, the better one is assumed to be because quality is “in the blood,” that is, inborn. From a classist perspective, people at the top of the social scale are naturally superior to those below them: those at the top are more intelligent, more responsible, more trustworthy, more ethical, and so on. People at the bottom of the social scale, it follows, are naturally shiftless, lazy, and irresponsible. Therefore, it is only right and natural that those from the highest social class should hold all the positions of power and leadership because they are naturally suited to such roles and are the only ones who can be trusted to perform them properly. Classism thus inevitably promotes social, economic, and political discrimination against the poor.

爱国主义是一种意识形态，它让穷人互相征战，对抗其他国家的穷人（无论如何，足够的金钱通常可以让人在战时免于服役，或者至少免于进入战斗部队），而交战双方的富人则从战时经济中攫取巨额利润。因为爱国主义使穷人将自己视为一个独立于其他国家的民族成员，而不是一个与包括本国在内的所有特权阶级对抗的全球受压迫阶级，所以它阻碍了穷人团结起来，在全球范围内改善自身处境。

Patriotism is an ideology that keeps poor people fighting wars against poor people from other countries (one way or another, sufficient money can generally keep one out of the armed forces during war time or, at least, out of the combat units) while the rich on both sides rake in the profits of war-time economy. Because patriotism leads the poor to see themselves as members of a nation, separate from other nations, rather than as members of a worldwide oppressed class opposed to all privileged classes including those from their own country, it prevents the poor from banding together to improve their condition globally.

宗教，正如卡尔·马克思所说的“人民的鸦片”，是一种意识形态，它帮助虔诚的穷人安于现状，或者至少容忍现状，其作用如同镇静剂一般。上帝是否存在并非马克思主义分析的根本问题；相反，重点在于人类以上帝之名所做的事情——有组织的宗教。例如，许多基督教宗教团体致力于为世界上的穷人提供食物、衣物、住所，甚至教育，但与食物和衣物一同传播的宗教信条中包含这样一种信念：穷人如果保持非暴力，就能在天堂获得奖赏。显然，占世界人口10%（甚至更少）却拥有世界90%（甚至更多）财富的人，在向穷人推广基督教信仰的这一方面方面有着既得利益，并且历史上他们也正是出于这个目的而利用基督教。事实上，圣经曾被成功地用来为奴役美洲的非洲人以及对妇女和女同性恋、男同性恋、双性恋和跨性别者（LGBT）的压迫辩护和推行。

Religion, which Karl Marx called “the opiate of the masses,” is an ideology that helps to keep the faithful poor satisfied with their lot in life, or at least tolerant of it, much as a tranquilizer might do. The question of God’s existence is not the fundamental issue for Marxist analysis; rather, what human beings do in God’s name – organized religion – is the focus. For example, while many Christian religious groups work to feed, clothe, house, and even educate the world’s poor, the religious tenets that are disseminated along with the food and clothing include the conviction that the poor, if they remain nonviolent, will find their reward in heaven. Obviously, the 10 percent (or less) of the world’s population who own 90 percent (or more) of the world’s wealth have a vested interest in promoting this aspect of Christian belief among the poor and historically have exploited Christianity for just this purpose. Indeed, the Bible has been used successfully to justify and promote the enslavement of Africans in America and the subordination of women and of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) individuals.

正如我们所见，坚韧不拔的个人主义是美国梦的基石，它浪漫化了那些孤身一人追求不易达成的目标的个人，这些目标往往伴随着风险，而且大多数人不会轻易尝试。例如，在过去，这样的目标可能是在美国边疆淘金热潮中，许多人为此冒着生命危险。如今，这样的目标可能是从事高风险的商业活动，冒着血本无归的风险。尽管这听起来像是一种令人钦佩的性格特质，但马克思主义思想家认为坚韧不拔的个人主义是一种压迫性的意识形态，因为它将个人利益置于他人的需求——甚至生存——之上。由于它关注的是“我”而不是“我们”，坚韧不拔的个人主义损害了整个社会的福祉，尤其损害了弱势群体的福祉。强烈的个人主义也让我们产生一种错觉，认为我们可以独立做出决定，而不会受到任何意识形态的显著影响，而事实上，无论我们是否意识到，我们一直都受到各种意识形态的影响。

Rugged individualism, which, as we have seen, is a cornerstone of the American dream, is an ideology that romanticizes the individual who strikes out alone in pursuit of a goal not easily achieved, a goal that often involves risk and one that most people would not readily undertake. In the past, such a goal would have been, for example, the rush for gold and silver on the American frontier, an attempt in which many individuals risked losing their lives. Today, such a goal might be the undertaking of a high-risk business, in which one risks losing all one’s money. Although it may sound like an admirable character trait, Marxist thinkers consider rugged individualism an oppressive ideology because it puts self-interest above the needs – and even above the survival – of other people. By keeping the focus on “me” instead of on “us,” rugged individualism works against the well-being of society as a whole and of underprivileged people in particular. Rugged individualism also gives us the illusion that we make our own decisions without being significantly influenced by ideology of any sort when, in fact, we’re all influenced by various ideologies all the time, whether we realize it or not.

消费主义，或者说“买到筋疲力尽”的消费主义，是美国梦的另一基石。消费主义是一种意识形态，它认为“我的价值取决于我购买的东西”。因此，它同时实现了两个意识形态目的：一方面，它让我产生一种错觉，即如果我能买到富人购买的东西，或者类似的替代品（即使是赊账购买），我就能“和他们一样优秀”；另一方面，它让那些生产和销售我购买的消费品的富人赚得盆满钵满，并从我的信用卡账单中赚取15%到20%的利息。

Consumerism, or shop-’til-you-drop-ism, is another cornerstone of the American dream. Consumerism is an ideology that says “I’m only as good as what I buy.” Thus, it simultaneously fulfills two ideological purposes: it gives me the illusion that I can be “as good as” the wealthy if I can purchase what they purchase or a reasonable facsimile thereof (albeit on credit) and it fills the coffers of the wealthy who manufacture and sell the consumer products I buy and who reap the 15–20 percent interest on my credit-card bills.

当然，我们还可以分析更多资本主义意识形态。这里列举的几个例子仅仅是为了概括性地说明马克思主义对压制性意识形态的看法。作为马克思主义批评家，我们的目标是识别文化产品——文学、电影、绘画、音乐、电视节目、商业广告、教育、大众哲学、宗教、娱乐形式等等——中发挥作用的意识形态，并分析这种意识形态如何支持或破坏文化产品所扮演重要角色的社会经济体系（权力结构）。虽然马克思主义者认为，从育儿实践到环境问题，所有社会现象都是文化产品，而且文化与产生它的社会经济体系密不可分，但许多马克思主义者更关注狭义的文化产品：例如艺术、音乐、电影、戏剧、文学和电视。在这些批评家看来，狭义的文化是意识形态的主要载体，因为它以看似无害的形式——娱乐——触及了众多人群。当我们享受娱乐时，可以说我们的戒备心会降低，我们尤其容易受到意识形态的灌输。

Of course, there are many more capitalist ideologies we could analyze. These few are intended just to illustrate in general terms the Marxist view of repressive ideologies. Our goal as Marxist critics is to identify the ideology at work in cultural productions – literature, films, paintings, music, television programs, commercial advertisements, education, popular philosophy, religion, forms of entertainment, and so on – and to analyze how that ideology supports or undermines the socioeconomic system (the power structure) in which that cultural production plays a significant role. While Marxists believe that all social phenomena, from child-rearing practices to environmental concerns, are cultural productions – and that culture cannot be separated from the socioeconomic system that produced it – many Marxists are interested in cultural productions in the narrower sense of the word: for example, art, music, film, theater, literature, and television. For these critics, culture, in this narrower sense, is the primary bearer of ideology because it reaches so many people in what seems to be an innocent form: entertainment. When we are being entertained, our guard is down, so to speak, and we are especially vulnerable to ideological programming.

例如，我在一部情景喜剧中看到一个无家可归的男人的形象。这个男人每晚都睡在汽车站，而这部情景喜剧的背景就设定在那里。我们看到他坐在一个公用电话亭里打电话，这时一个工作人员打断了他，把邮件递给了他。（笑声不断：这家伙在车站待得太久了，邮局都以为那是他的家！）他查看邮件，漫不经心地抱怨道：“真希望邮局能管管这些垃圾邮件！”（又一个笑声：他没有抱怨——甚至根本没注意到——自己的处境，反而抱怨垃圾邮件！）这一幕看似无伤大雅，但马克思主义批评家会从中解读出一个服务于美国资本主义权力结构的隐含信息：“别担心无家可归的人；他们过得很好。”或者更糟的是，“无家可归的人就喜欢这样生活；对他们来说，这就像我们的生活方式对我们来说一样自然。”

Consider, for example, a representation of a homeless man I saw on a situation comedy on television. The man sleeps every night in a bus station, where the sitcom is set. We see him in a public phone booth, talking on the phone, when he is interrupted by one of the workers, who gives him his mail. (Big laugh: the guy hangs around the station so much that the post office thinks it’s his home!) He inspects his mail and makes a casual comment like, “I wish the post office would do something about all this junk mail!” (Another big laugh: instead of complaining about – or even noticing – the situation he’s in, he’s complaining about junk mail!) The scene may seem innocent enough, but a Marxist critic would see in it an implied message that serves the capitalist power structure in America: “Don’t worry about the homeless; they’re doing all right for themselves” or, worse, “The homeless like to live this way; it’s as natural to them as our lifestyle is to us.”

“美国梦”是如何助长这种对无家可归者的看法的呢？它通过宣扬一种我们之前讨论过的迷思来达到这一目的，即在这个国家，只要有进取心和努力工作就能获得经济上的成功。因此，穷人必然是游手好闲、懒惰的。由此，我们很容易忘记，例如，无家可归的人没有住址就找不到工作，没有工作就找不到住址；大多数人之所以无家可归，是因为经济原因。完全不受他们控制的情况；而且，如今许多人无家可归，是因为他们被里根政府时期关闭的精神病院驱逐出去，因此需要越来越昂贵的药物和/或治疗以及住房。

How does the American dream contribute to just such a view of the homeless? It does so by promoting the myth, which we discussed earlier, that financial success can be achieved in this country merely through initiative and hard work. Therefore, the poor must be shiftless and lazy.
