We are thus encouraged to forget, for example, that a homeless person can’t get a job without an address and can’t get an address without a job; that most homeless people become so due to economic circumstances wholly beyond their control; and that many people are homeless today because they were evicted from the mental health institutions closed during the Reagan administration and are, therefore, in need of increasingly expensive medication and/or therapy as well as homes.

人类行为、商品与家庭

Human behavior, the commodity, and the family

尽管马克思后期的著作侧重于经济学，侧重于整个社会的运作，而​​非个体，但我们仍需记住，他最初是一位研究人类行为的学者——我们甚至可以说是一位社会心理学家。例如，他对十九世纪中期工业化兴起的担忧，源于他对工厂劳动对那些被迫将劳动力出卖给取代独立工匠和农民的工业企业的人们的影响的关注。由于工厂工人生产了大量产品，而这些产品上没有任何他们的名字或其他个人贡献的标记，马克思观察到，他们不仅与他们生产的产品脱节，也与他们自身的劳动脱节。他注意到，这种他称之为异化劳动的现象，对劳动者自身以及整个社会都产生了严重的负面影响。

Although the later works of Karl Marx focus on economics, on the workings of society as a whole, rather than on the individual, it is important to remember that he began as a student of human behavior – we might even say a social psychologist – in his own right. For example, his concern over the rise of industrialism in the mid-nineteenth century was a concern for the effects of factory work on people who were forced to sell their labor to the industries that were replacing independent artisans and farmers. Because factory workers produced such large quantities of products, none of which bore their names or any other mark of their individual contributions, Marx observed that they became disassociated not only from the products they produced but from their own labor as well, and he noted the debilitating effects of what he called alienated labor on the laborer and on the society as a whole.

同样，马克思对资本主义经济兴起的担忧，实际上是对资本主义对人类价值观影响的担忧。在资本主义经济体系中，物品的价值变得非人格化。它的价值被转化为货币“等价物”——“资本”一词本身就意味着货币——并且完全取决于它与货币市场的关系。问题变成了：有多少人会购买这件物品？他们愿意为它支付多少钱？人们是否真的需要这件物品，以及它是否真的值这个价钱，都无关紧要。在盎格鲁-欧洲文化中，资本主义取代了物物交换经济，在物物交换经济中，劳动或商品是根据参与交换的个人的能力和需求进行交换的。因此，许多后来的马克思主义者关注意识形态如何通过大众文化传播并在我们的情感生活中发挥作用，这自然是马克思本人对人类行为和经验兴趣的延伸。

Similarly, Marx’s concern over the rise of a capitalist economy was a concern for the effects of capitalism on human values. In a capitalist economic system, an object’s value becomes impersonal. Its value is translated into a monetary “equivalent” – the word capital means money – and determined solely in terms of its relationship to a monetary market. The question becomes, how many people will buy the object, and how much money will they be willing to pay for it? Whether or not people really need the object in question and whether or not it is really worth its assigned price are irrelevant issues. In Anglo-European culture, capitalism replaced a barter economy in which labor or goods were exchanged for other labor or goods, depending on the abilities and needs of the individuals involved in the exchange. The focus of many later Marxists on the ways in which ideology is transmitted through popular culture and operates in our emotional lives is thus a natural extension of Marx’s own interest in human behavior and experience.

当然，马克思主义对人类行为的许多洞见都涉及资本主义对人类心理的破坏性影响，而这些破坏性影响往往体现在我们与商品的关系中。在马克思主义看来，商品的价值不在于它的功能（使用价值），而在于它可以用来交换的货币或其他商品（交换价值），或者在于它赋予拥有者的社会地位（符号交换价值）。一件物品只有具有交换价值或符号交换价值时才能成为商品，而这两种价值都取决于物品被交换的社会。例如，如果我为了娱乐或获取信息而阅读一本书，甚至只是用它来支撑桌腿，这本书就具有使用价值。如果我卖掉那本书，它就有交换价值。如果我把那本书放在咖啡桌上，想给约会对象留下好印象，它就有符号交换价值。商品化是指根据物品或人的交换价值或符号交换价值来看待它们。当我购买一件艺术品作为金融投资，也就是打算以后卖掉换取更高的价格，或者当我购买它是为了向他人炫耀我的高雅品味时，我就把这件艺术品商品化了。如果我过度购买和展示昂贵的商品或服务，只是为了向他人炫耀我的财富，我就犯了炫耀性消费的错误，比如我买一件白色长款貂皮大衣（或者一副价值100美元的名牌太阳镜），不仅仅是因为这些物品的实用性或美观性，而是为了向世人展示我有多少钱。

Of course, many Marxist insights into human behavior involve the damaging effects of capitalism on human psychology, and those damaging effects often appear in our relationship to the commodity. For Marxism, a commodity’s value lies not in what it can do (use value) but in the money or other commodities for which it can be traded (exchange value) or in the social status it confers on its owner (signexchange value). An object becomes a commodity only when it has exchange value or sign-exchange value, and both forms of value are determined by the society in which the object is exchanged. For example, if I read a book for pleasure or for information, or even if I use it to prop up a table leg, the book has use value. If I sell that same book, it has exchange value. If I leave that book out on my coffee table to impress my date, it has sign-exchange value. Commodification is the act of relating to objects or persons in terms of their exchange value or sign-exchange value. I commodify a work of art when I buy it as a financial investment, that is, with the intention of selling it for more money, or when I buy it to impress other people with my refined tastes. If I purchase and display costly goods or services excessively in order to impress people with my wealth, I am guilty of conspicuous consumption, as when I buy a full-length, white mink coat (or even a pair of $100 designer sunglasses), not just for the object’s usefulness or beauty but in order to show the world how much money I have.

最后，当我为了提升自身经济或社会地位而构建与他人的关系时，我就把人商品化了。我们大多数人都知道把人当作物品（例如，性对象）对待意味着什么。然而，物品只有具备交换价值或符号交换价值时，才能成为商品。我选择约会对象是基于我认为他们会为我花多少钱（他们的交换价值），还是基于我认为他们会给我的朋友留下多深刻的印象（他们的符号交换价值）？如果是这样，那么我就是在把他们商品化。

Finally, I commodify human beings when I structure my relations with them to promote my own advancement financially or socially. Most of us know what it means to treat a person like an object (for example, a sex object). An object becomes a commodity, however, only when it has exchange value or sign-exchange value. Do I choose my dates based on how much money I think they will spend on me (their exchange value) or on how much I think they will impress my friends (their sign-exchange value)? If so, then I’m commodifying them.

从马克思主义视角来看，作为市场经济的资本主义的生存依赖于消费主义，因此它将符号交换价值作为我们与周围世界互动的主要方式。对于资本主义经济而言，还有什么比让其成员只有拥有时尚的“外表”（而这种“外表”只能通过不断购买新衣服、新化妆品和新的美容服务来维持）才能“自我感觉良好”更有利的呢？换句话说，从经济角度来看，资本主义最有利的做法就是刺激任何能促使我们购买消费品的个人不安全感。（我的牙齿不够白吗？我的头发应该更金一些吗？我的肌肉应该更发达一些吗？我的口气够清新吗？）而且，由于促使我们购买消费品的个人不安全感源于与他人的比较（我的牙齿像他一样白吗？我的头发像她一样金吗？），因此，竞争不仅在想要销售产品的公司之间，也在那些觉得自己必须“推销”自己才能受欢迎或成功的人之间被强化。

From a Marxist perspective, because the survival of capitalism, which is a market economy, depends on consumerism, it promotes sign-exchange value as our primary mode of relating to the world around us. What could be better for a capitalist economy than for its members to be unable to “feel good about themselves” unless they acquire a fashionable “look” that can be maintained only by the continual purchase of new clothing, new cosmetic products, and new cosmetic services? In other words, in economic terms, it’s in capitalism’s best interests to promote whatever personal insecurities will motivate us to buy consumer goods. (Are my teeth not white enough? Should my hair be blonder? Should my muscles bulge more? Is my breath fresh enough?) And because the kinds of personal insecurities that make us buy consumer products are produced by comparing ourselves with other people (Are my teeth as white as his? Is my hair as blond as hers?), competition is promoted not just among companies who want to sell products but among people who feel they must “sell” themselves in order to be popular or successful.

资本主义不断需要新的市场来销售商品，以及新的原材料来源来生产商品，这也导致了帝国主义的扩张：一个国家为了自身的经济利益，对另一个国家进行军事、经济和/或文化上的统治，而对被统治者的福祉却漠不关心。西班牙对墨西哥的统治、英国对印度的统治、比利时对非洲刚果地区的剥削，以及美国在北美、中美洲和南美洲对原住民的奴役，都只是帝国主义活动的几个例子。当帝国主义国家在一个“欠发达”国家建立殖民地时，这些殖民地就被称为殖民地。就像美国革命前的美洲殖民地一样，它利用这些殖民地来扩张其经济利益。因为所有帝国主义行径的动机，无论征服国声称对当地居民产生了多么积极的影响，都是为了“宗主国”的经济利益。

Capitalism’s constant need for new markets in which to sell goods and for new sources of raw materials from which to make goods is also responsible for the spread of imperialism: the military, economic, and/or cultural domination of one nation by another for the financial benefit of the dominating nation with little or no concern for the welfare of the dominated. Spain’s rule of Mexico, England’s domination of India, Belgium’s exploitation of the Congo region of Africa, and US efforts to subordinate native populations in North, Central, and South America are but a few examples of imperialist activities. When the imperialist nation establishes communities in an “underdeveloped” country, those communities are called colonies, as were the American Colonies before the American Revolution, and it uses those colonies to extend its economic interests. For the motive of all imperialist endeavor, no matter what positive influence the conquering nation claims to have on the local population, is economic gain for the “mother country.”

或许不那么显而易见，但对于我们理解当今资本主义而言同样重要的一点是，帝国主义政府是如何“殖民”人民的意识的。殖民被统治民族的意识意味着让他们以帝国主义国家希望的方式看待自身处境，例如，让他们相信自己在精神、心灵和文化上都逊于征服者，并且在新领导人的“指导”和“保护”下，他们的命运将会得到改善。例如，南北战争前的奴隶主试图让非洲奴隶相信，他们是未开化的、无神论的野蛮人，如果没有白人主人的持续监视，他们就会重新回到食人习俗。当然，事实上，非洲奴隶来自拥有丰富艺术、音乐、宗教和伦理的古老文明。这种试图以种族界限殖民意识的做法一直延续到二十世纪，并延续至今，例如媒体对非裔美国人的刻板印象、美国历史教科书中对非裔美国人经历的不足描述，以及对盎格鲁-撒克逊式审美理想的推崇。因此，这种试图殖民意识的做法也可能反过来被我们自身的文化所利用。事实上，前文讨论的消费主义盛行正是另一个例证。

Less clear cut, perhaps, but equally important for our understanding of capitalism today, is the way in which consciousness can be “colonized” by imperialist governments. To colonize the consciousness of subordinate peoples means to convince them to see their situation the way the imperialist nation wants them to see it, to convince them, for example, that they are mentally, spiritually, and culturally inferior to their conquerors and that their lot will be improved under the “guidance” and “protection” of their new leaders. Antebellum slave owners, for example, tried to convince African slaves that they were uncivilized, godless savages who would revert to cannibalism without the constant vigilance of their white masters. In reality, of course, African slaves came from ancient cultures that could boast many forms of art, music, religion, and ethics. This same attempt to colonize consciousness along racial lines continued into the twentieth century and endures today through, for example, stereotypes of black Americans in the media, the inadequate representation of African American experience in American history books, and the promotion of an Anglo-Saxon ideal of beauty. Thus, the attempt to colonize consciousness can be practiced against us by our own culture. Indeed, the promotion of consumerism discussed earlier is just such another example.

显然，马克思主义对人类心理学的关注与精神分析存在重叠之处：这两个学科都从心理学的角度研究人类行为和动机。然而，精神分析侧重于个体心理及其在家庭中的形成，而马克思主义则侧重于塑造个体和群体心理体验和行为的物质/历史力量——社会经济体系的政治和意识形态。在马克思主义看来，家庭并非个体心理认同的来源，因为个体和家庭都是物质/历史环境的产物。家庭在养育子女的过程中无意识地执行着文化“程序”，但这一程序是由家庭所处的社会经济文化环境所塑造的。虽然是父母给我们讲睡前故事、带我们看电影，并通过这些以及其他方式塑造我们的道德观，但正是我们的社会体系提供了这些故事、电影和道德观，而所有这些最终都服务于掌控该社会体系者的经济利益。因此，精神分析批评家考察决定个体行为的家庭冲突和心理创伤，而马克思主义批评家则将同样的行为视为意识形态力量的产物，例如电影、时尚、艺术、音乐、教育和法律所承载的意识形态。事实上，马克思主义批评家会向我们展示，家庭功能失调本身就是社会经济体系及其所宣扬的意识形态的产物。

Clearly, Marxism’s concern with human psychology overlaps with that of psychoanalysis: both disciplines study human behavior and motivation in psychological terms. However, while psychoanalysis focuses on the individual psyche and its formation within the family, Marxism focuses on the material/historical forces – the politics and ideologies of socioeconomic systems – that shape the psychological experience and behavior of individuals and groups. For Marxism, the family is not the source of the individual’s psychological identity, for both the individual and the family are products of material/historical circumstances. The family unconsciously carries out the cultural “program” in raising its children, but that program is produced by the socioeconomic culture within which the family operates. While it is our parents who read us bedtime stories, take us to movies, and, in these and other ways, form our morals, it is our social system that provides the stories, movies, and morals, all of which ultimately serve the economic interests of those in control of that social system. Thus, while psychoanalytic critics examine the family conflicts and psychological wounds that determine individual behavior, Marxist critics examine that same behavior as a product of the ideological forces carried, for example, by film, fashion, art, music, education, and law. Indeed, the Marxist critic will show us the ways in which family dysfunctions are themselves products of the socioeconomic system and the ideologies it promotes.

马克思主义与文学

Marxism and literature

当然，家庭是文学中反复出现的主题，因此，让我们从对比马克思主义和精神分析对阿瑟·米勒最伟大的家庭剧《推销员之死》（1949）的解读开始，来探讨马克思主义与文学的关系。精神分析的解读会聚焦于以下几个方面：威利幼年时被父亲和哥哥抛弃；威利的不安全感以及由此产生的对现实的强烈否认；威利将个人需求投射到儿子比夫身上；哈皮与比夫之间的兄弟竞争；家庭动态中存在的俄狄浦斯情结；以及琳达对自身与威利之间问题的回避和转移。这种解读的核心场景是比夫在酒店与威利的对峙，他在那里发现了父亲与另一个女人在一起。精神分析批评家之所以对剧中的这些方面感兴趣，是因为它们关注的是作为家庭产物的个体心理。

Of course, the family is a recurrent theme in literature, so let’s begin our discussion of Marxism and literature by contrasting Marxist and psychoanalytic readings of Arthur Miller’s greatest familial play, Death of a Salesman (1949). A psychoanalytic reading of the play would focus on such elements as Willy’s abandonment at a very young age by his father and older brother; Willy’s insecurity and the massive denial of reality that results; Willy’s projection of his personal needs onto his son Biff; Happy’s sibling rivalry with Biff; the oedipal dimension at work in the family dynamic; and Linda’s avoidance and displacement of her problems with Willy. The central scene for such an interpretation would be Biff’s confrontation with Willy in the hotel, where he discovers his father with another woman. These aspects of the play would be of interest to psychoanalytic critics because they focus on the individual psyche as the product of the family.

相反，马克思主义的解读会着重分析上述心理问题是如何由家庭所处的物质/历史现实造成的：美国梦的意识形态让威利相信，他的自我价值只能通过经济成功来获得，并让他一直仰慕着贪婪的哥哥本；猖獗的消费主义让洛曼一家不得不赊购他们负担不起的东西；商业世界的竞争让威利在同一家公司工作了30年后又回到了纯粹的佣金制工作；社会经济体系中存在的剥削潜力，使得并非所有公司都必须为员工提供充足的养老金保障；以及“适者生存”的资本主义意识形态，使得霍华德可以毫不顾忌威利日益恶化的精神状况而解雇他。这种解读的核心场景是：霍华德（在展现出自己经济成功的迹象后）解雇了威利，并让他去找儿子们寻求经济援助。

A Marxist reading, in contrast, would focus on the ways in which the psychological problems listed above are produced by the material/historical realities within which the family operates: the ideology of the American dream that tells Willy his self-worth is earned only by economic success and that keeps him looking up to his predatory brother Ben; the rampant consumerism that keeps the Lomans buying on credit what they can’t afford; the competitiveness of the business world that puts Willy back on straight commission work after 30 years of employment with the same firm; the exploitative potential of a socioeconomic system that doesn’t require all companies to provide adequate pension coverage for their employees; and the ideology of “survival-of-the-fittest” capitalism that allows Howard to fire Willy with no concern for the latter’s deteriorating mental condition. The central scene for such an interpretation would be that in which Howard (after displaying signs of his own economic success) fires Willy, telling him to turn to his sons for financial help.

显然，如果马克思主义批评家使用精神分析概念，其目的就是服务于马克思主义的解释。例如，威利对现实的否认以及伴随而来的倒退幻觉，会被视为美国梦有害意识形态议程的证据：美国梦固然有利于资本主义经济，但它牺牲了众多未能实现梦想者的福祉。同样地，当你阅读其他马克思主义对文化和文化产品的解释时，你可能会注意到我们正在研究的其他理论中的概念也会出现。例如，你可能会注意到，通过揭示民主党、共和党、社会主义和法西斯主义等不同政治派别在文化和教育资助政策方面微妙而深刻的资本主义相似性，马克思主义批评家实际上是在进行某种结构主义的分析。或者，你可能会注意到，通过揭示文学作品如何暗中强化其所批判的资本主义价值观，马克思主义批评家实际上是在进行一种解构主义的分析。事实上，许多马克思主义批评家同时也是女权主义者、解构主义者、社会心理学家和文化学家。人类学家。然而，在所有情况下，你都会发现，与其他领域重叠或借用的概念都被用来服务于马克思主义的目标。

Clearly, if a Marxist critic uses a psychoanalytic concept, it is used in service of a Marxist interpretation. For example, Willy’s denial of reality, and the regressive hallucinations that accompany it, would be viewed as evidence of the American dream’s debilitating ideological agenda: the American dream is certainly good for capitalist economics, but it sacrifices the well-being of the many individuals who don’t achieve it. Similarly, as you read other Marxist interpretations of culture and cultural productions, you may notice that concepts from other theories we are studying will appear. For example, you may notice that by revealing the subtle but profound capitalist similarities between, say, Democratic, Republican, Socialist, and Fascist cultural and educational funding policies, a Marxist critic is engaged in a kind of structuralist enterprise. Or you may notice that, by revealing the ways in which a literary work covertly reinforces the capitalist values it criticizes, a Marxist critic is engaged in a deconstructive enterprise. Indeed, many Marxist critics are, among other things, feminists, deconstructors, social psychologists, and cultural anthropologists. In every case, however, you will see that concepts overlapping with or borrowed from other fields are put in service of Marxist goals.

当然，以上讨论的马克思主义概念并非涵盖所有领域；还有许多其他概念。正如在任何领域一样，马克思主义理论家和文学批评家之间也存在诸多分歧，例如无产阶级阶级团结的形成和作用、媒体在操纵政治意识中的作用、意识形态与心理学的关系、马克思主义与其他批评理论的兼容性等等。然而，本章提供的概念可以被视为基本原则，是理解马克思主义理论家和文学批评家提出的问题并对其著作有所了解所需掌握的主要思想。在将这些概念扩展到文学阐释领域之前，让我们先来看一下马克思主义对文学的总体看法。

Of course, the Marxist concepts discussed above do not exhaust the field; there are many others. And as in every field, there is a great deal of disagreement among Marxist theorists and literary critics concerning, for example, the formation and role of class solidarity among the proletariat, the role of the media in manipulating our political consciousness, the relationship between ideology and psychology, the compatibility of Marxism with other critical theories, and many other topics. However, the concepts provided in this chapter can be considered the basic principles, the main ideas you need to know in order to read Marxist theorists and literary critics with some understanding of the issues they raise. Before we extend these concepts to the realm of literary interpretation, let’s take a look at Marxism’s view of literature in general.

在马克思主义看来，文学并非存在于某种永恒的审美领域，供人被动地欣赏。相反，如同所有文化表现形式一样，文学是其创作时代和地域的社会经济条件乃至意识形态条件的产物，无论作者是否出于本意。因为人类本身就是其社会经济和意识形态环境的产物，所以人们认为，作者的作品必然会以某种形式体现意识形态。

For Marxism, literature does not exist in some timeless, aesthetic realm as an object to be passively contemplated. Rather, like all cultural manifestations, it is a product of the socioeconomic and hence ideological conditions of the time and place in which it was written, whether or not the author intended it so. Because human beings are themselves products of their socioeconomic and ideological environment, it is assumed that authors cannot help but create works that embody ideology in some form.

文学源于并反映真实的物质/历史条件，这一事实至少为马克思主义批评家提供了两种可能性：(1) 文学作品可能倾向于强化读者对其所体现的意识形态的认同；(2) 它可能引导读者批判其所代表的意识形态。许多文本兼具这两种特性。承载意识形态的不仅是文学作品的内容——“情节”或主题——形式，或者如大多数马克思主义者所言，形式才是最重要的。现实主义、自然主义、超现实主义、象征主义、浪漫主义、现代主义、后现代主义、悲剧、喜剧、讽刺、内心独白、意识流以及其他体裁和文学手法，都是构成形式的手段。如果说内容是文学的“内容”，那么形式就是文学的“方式”。

The fact that literature grows out of and reflects real material/historical conditions creates at least two possibilities of interest to Marxist critics: (1) the literary work might tend to reinforce in the reader the ideologies it embodies, or (2) it might invite the reader to criticize the ideologies it represents. Many texts do both. And it is not merely the content of a literary work – the “action” or the theme – that carries ideology, but the form as well or, as most Marxists would argue, the form primarily. Realism, naturalism, surrealism, symbolism, romanticism, modernism, postmodernism, tragedy, comedy, satire, interior monologue, stream of consciousness, and other genres and literary devices are the means by which form is constituted. If content is the “what” of literature, then form is the “how.”

例如，现实主义作品中的人物和情节，仿佛让我们透过窗户观看眼前正在发生的真实场景。我们的注意力并非集中在文字本身，而是被文字所传达的行动所吸引。事实上，我们常常会忘记正在阅读的文字以及叙事的结构，因为我们会“沉浸”在故事之中。我们之所以不会注意到语言、结构和形式，部分原因在于，作品中呈现的行动遵循着连贯的顺序，让我们能够像看待自己生活中的事件一样去理解它，而且作品中的人物也栩栩如生，就像我们可能遇到的人一样。因此，我们会被“拉入”故事之中。相比之下，许多后现代文学（以及任何类型的非现实主义实验文学）采用碎片化的超现实风格，似乎挑战着我们的理解，并将我们与叙事及其人物拉开距离或产生疏离感。

Realism, for example, gives us characters and plot as if we were looking through a window onto an actual scene taking place before our eyes. Our attention is drawn not to the nature of the words on the page but to the action those words convey. Indeed, we frequently forget about the words we’re reading and the way the narrative is structured as we “get lost” in the story. Part of the reason we don’t notice the language and structure, the form, is because the action represented is ordered in a coherent sequence that invites us to relate to it much as we relate to the events in our own lives, and the characters it portrays are believable, much like people we might meet. So we get “pulled into” the story. In contrast, a good deal of postmodern literature (and nonrealistic, experimental literature of any kind) is written in a fragmented, surreal style that seems to defy our understanding and serves to distance or estrange us from the narrative and the characters it portrays.

对一些马克思主义者而言，现实主义是实现马克思主义目标的最佳形式，因为它清晰准确地展现了真实世界，包括其所有的社会经济不平等和意识形态矛盾，并鼓励读者正视物质/历史现实中令人不快的真相。无论作者是否刻意为之，只要他们准确地描绘了真实世界，就必然会反映出社会经济不平等和意识形态矛盾。马克思主义现实主义小说的拥趸往往倾向于拒绝非现实主义的实验性小说，认为它们晦涩难懂，难以被大多数读者理解，并且过于关注个体内心世界的运作，而​​忽略了个体与社会的关系。然而，许多马克思主义者珍视非现实主义的实验性小说，因为它们所呈现的经验碎片化以及读者常常感受到的疏离感，恰恰是对当今资本主义所造成的支离破碎的世界和异化的人类的一种批判。

For some Marxists, realism is the best form for Marxist purposes because it clearly and accurately represents the real world, with all its socioeconomic inequities and ideological contradictions, and encourages readers to see the unhappy truths about material/historical reality, for whether or not authors intend it they are bound to represent socioeconomic inequities and ideological contradictions if they accurately represent the real world. Marxist fans of realist fiction often have been inclined to reject nonrealistic, experimental fiction for being inaccessible to the majority of readers and for being too exclusively concerned with the inner workings of an individual mind rather than with the individual’s relationship to society. However, many Marxists value nonrealistic, experimental fiction because the fragmentation of experience it represents and the estrangement the reader often experiences constitute a critique of the fragmented world and the alienated human beings produced by capitalism in today’s world.

为了了解形式如何影响我们对内容的理解（或者说形式本身就是一种内容），让我们再简要地看一下《推销员之死》。正如我们所见，这部剧作具有强烈的马克思主义色彩，它促使我们谴责威利遭受雇主剥削的资本主义行径，并揭示了资本主义意识形态固有的矛盾：它以牺牲“小人物”的利益为代价，维护了大企业的利益，而这些小人物却“接受了”资本主义价值观。然而，对许多马克思主义者来说，这部剧作以悲剧的形式写成，这严重削弱了其反资本主义主题。我们应该记得，悲剧描绘的是个人因自身性格缺陷——通常是傲慢或过度骄傲——而走向毁灭的故事。《推销员之死》的悲剧形式促使我们主要关注威利作为个体的性格缺陷，而不是造成这些缺陷的社会，从而导致我们忽略了资本主义意识形态的负面影响，而这种意识形态从根本上说是剧中所有事件的根源。

To see how form affects our understanding of content (or how form is a kind of content), let’s take another brief look at Death of a Salesman. As we have seen, the play has a strong Marxist component in that it invites us to condemn the capitalist exploitation Willy suffers at the hands of his employer, and it shows us the contradictions inherent in capitalist ideology, which promotes the interests of big business at the expense of the “little man” who has “bought into” capitalist values. However, for many Marxists, this anticapitalist theme is severely undermined by the fact that the play is written in the form of a tragedy. You will recall that tragedy portrays the ruin of an individual human being due to some character flaw – usually hubris, or excessive pride – in that individual’s personal makeup. The tragic form of Death of a Salesman thus encourages us to focus primarily on the character flaws in Willy as an individual rather than on the society that helped produce those flaws, and we are thus led to overlook the negative influence of the capitalist ideology that is, at bottom, responsible for all the action in the play.

尽管马克思主义者长期以来对哪些类型的作品最有助于提升社会意识和促进积极的政治变革存在分歧，但如今许多人认为，即使是那些强化资本主义、帝国主义或其他阶级价值观的文学作品也是有用的，因为它们可以揭示这些意识形态是如何诱使我们或胁迫我们与它们压迫性的意识形态议程同流合污的。例如，玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818）在某种程度上强化了阶级价值观，因为它将出身于上层阶级的人——例如阿尔方斯·弗兰肯斯坦、伊丽莎白·拉文扎和德莱西一家——描绘成在道德和智力上都优于社会底层的人。另一方面，处于社会底层的人物往往被描绘成粗鲁、冷漠，并且容易被暴民行为所煽动。与之相反，托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）通过展现20世纪40年代初美国资本主义强加的阶级制度下人们所遭受的不公，瓦解了阶级价值观。此外，它还揭示了宗教和逃避现实的电影如何通过鼓励和助长这种现象而损害穷人的利益。这部小说没有展现出他们面对残酷现实的无视态度，而是组织起来进行政治斗争，争取他们应得的那份利益，可以说它具有马克思主义倾向。

Although Marxists have long disagreed about what kinds of works are most useful in promoting social awareness and positive political change, many today believe that even those literary works that reinforce capitalist, imperialist, or other classist values are useful in that they can show us how these ideologies work to seduce or coerce us into collusion with their repressive ideological agendas. Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818), for example, may be said to reinforce classist values to the extent that it portrays those born into the upper class – for example, Alphonse Frankenstein, Elizabeth Lavenza, and the DeLaceys – as morally and intellectually superior to those below them on the social scale. Characters at the bottom of the social ladder, on the other hand, are often depicted as rude, insensitive, and easily incensed to mob behavior. In contrast, Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) undermines classist values by illustrating the injustices suffered under the class system imposed by American capitalism in the early 1940s. In addition, by revealing the ways in which religion and escapist movies harm the poor by encouraging them to ignore the harsh realities of their lives, rather than organize politically and fight collectively for their fair share of the pie, this novel can be said to have a Marxist agenda.

马克思主义批评家对文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions Marxist critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在概括马克思主义的文学研究方法。

The following questions are offered to summarize Marxist approaches to literature.

1作品是否（有意或无意地）强化了资本主义、帝国主义或阶级主义价值观？如果是，那么可以说作品具有资本主义、帝国主义或阶级主义的倾向，而批评家的职责就是揭露和谴责作品的这一方面。

1 Does the work reinforce (intentionally or not) capitalist, imperialist, or classist values? If so, then the work may be said to have a capitalist, imperialist, or classist agenda, and it is the critic’s job to expose and condemn this aspect of the work.

2如何将这部作品视为对资本主义、帝国主义或阶级主义的批判？也就是说，文本以何种方式揭示并引导我们谴责压迫性的社会经济力量（包括压迫性意识形态）？如果一部作品批判或引导我们批判压迫性的社会经济力量，那么它就可能被认为具有马克思主义倾向。

2 How might the work be seen as a critique of capitalism, imperialism, or classism? That is, in what ways does the text reveal, and invite us to condemn, oppressive socioeconomic forces (including repressive ideologies)? If a work criticizes or invites us to criticize oppressive socioeconomic forces, then it may be said to have a Marxist agenda.

3这部作品是否在某些方面支持马克思主义议程，但在其他方面（或许是无意的）支持资本主义、帝国主义或阶级主义议程？换句话说，这部作品是否存在意识形态上的冲突？

3 Does the work in some ways support a Marxist agenda but in other ways (perhaps unintentionally) support a capitalist, imperialist, or classist agenda? In other words, is the work ideologically conflicted?

4这部文学作品是如何（有意或无意地）反映其创作时期和/或故事背景时期的社会经济状况的？这些状况又揭示了阶级斗争史的哪些方面？

4 How does the literary work reflect (intentionally or not) the socioeconomic conditions of the time in which it was written and/or the time in which it is set, and what do those conditions reveal about the history of class struggle?

5这部作品如何被视为对有组织的宗教的批判？也就是说，在文本中，宗教是如何阻止一个或多个角色认识到并反抗社会经济压迫的？

5 How might the work be seen as a critique of organized religion? That is, how does religion function in the text to keep a character or characters from realizing and resisting socioeconomic oppression?

根据具体文学作品，我们可以提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们也可以提出一些此处未列出的、更有意义的问题。这些只是引导我们以富有成效的马克思主义方式思考文学作品的一些起点。请记住，即使关注相同的马克思主义概念，并非所有马克思主义批评家都会以相同的方式解读同一部作品。一如既往，即使是专家学者也会有分歧。我们的目标是运用马克思主义理论来丰富我们对文学作品的阅读，帮助我们理解作品中阐述的一些重要思想——如果没有马克思主义理论，我们可能无法如此清晰或深刻地领悟这些思想；而且，如果我们以正确的方式运用马克思主义理论，它还能帮助我们认识到意识形态是如何蒙蔽我们，使我们看不到自身参与压迫性社会政治议程的。

Depending on the literary work in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question of our own not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us thinking about literary works in productive Marxist ways. Remember, not all Marxist critics will interpret the same work in the same way, even if they focus on the same Marxist concepts. As always, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use Marxist theory to help enrich our reading of literary works, to help us see some important ideas they illustrate that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply without Marxist theory, and, if we use Marxist theory the way it is intended to be used, to help us see the ways in which ideology blinds us to our own participation in oppressive sociopolitical agendas.

以下对F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的马克思主义解读，旨在展示马克思主义对该小说的诠释可能得出的结果。本文重点探讨小说对美国资本主义的批判，我将论证这一点。意识形态。此外，我将尝试指出这部小说在哪些方面未能充分推进其批判，反而不知不觉地成为了它所批判的资本主义意识形态的牺牲品。

The following Marxist reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a Marxist interpretation of that novel might yield. It focuses on what I will argue is the novel’s critique of American capitalist ideology. In addition, I will try to show the ways in which the novel fails to push its critique far enough, becoming the unwitting prey of the capitalist ideology it attacks.

你拥有什么，你就是什么：马克思主义视角下的《了不起的盖茨比》

You are what you own: a Marxist reading of The Great Gatsby

F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）创作于第一次世界大战后20世纪20年代的经济繁荣时期，故事背景也设定于此。这部小说可以被视为美国梦的编年史，记录了美国历史上资本主义为所有人提供经济机会的承诺似乎达到顶峰的时期。“快速致富”的计划层出不穷，而且许多计划都成功了，因为当时股票交易的保证金只有10%，这意味着可以用10美分赊购价值1美元的股票。因此，即使是“小人物”也能涉足股市，并希望从中发家致富。我们从盖茨比派对宾客们狂热的放纵中，以及盖茨比本人身上，都能看出当时的时代精神——他们坚信主人提供的丰盛食物和饮料，就像国家的资源一样，永远不会枯竭。盖茨比从“游手好闲、一事无成的农民”的儿子（104；第6章）一跃成为长岛“巨大”豪宅的主人，这座豪宅拥有“大理石游泳池和超过40英亩的草坪和花园”（9；第1章），他的飞速崛起似乎体现了美国梦所提供的无限可能。

Written and set during the post-World War I economic boom of the 1920s, F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925) can be seen as a chronicle of the American dream at a point in this nation’s history when capitalism’s promise of economic opportunity for all seemed at its peak of fulfillment. “Get-rich-quick” schemes abounded, and many of them succeeded, for it was a time when stocks could be bought on a 10 percent margin, which means that a dollar’s worth of stocks could be purchased, on credit, for ten cents. So even the “little man” could play the stock market and hope to make his fortune there. We see the tenor of the times in the feverish abandon of Gatsby’s party guests – confident that their host’s abundance of food and drink, like the nation’s resources, will never be depleted – and in Gatsby himself, whose meteoric rise from being the son of “shiftless and unsuccessful farm people” (104; ch. 6) to the proprietor of a “colossal” Long Island mansion with “a marble swimming pool and over forty acres of lawn and garden” (9; ch. 1) seems to embody the infinite possibility offered by the American dream.

然而， 《了不起的盖茨比》并没有歌颂它所描绘的令人陶醉的资本主义文化，而是如马克思主义解读所揭示的那样，揭露了其阴暗的本质。菲茨杰拉德的小说通过对经济顶层人士毫不留情的刻画，以及对美国梦不仅未能兑现承诺，反而导致个人价值观衰落的深刻剖析，对美国资本主义文化及其背后的意识形态进行了尖锐的批判。此外，我们还将看到，马克思主义视角如何揭示了这部小说对资本主义的批判力度不足之处，它最终反而成为了自己试图批判的意识形态的牺牲品。

The Great Gatsby, however, does not celebrate the heady capitalist culture it portrays but, as a Marxist interpretation of the novel makes especially clear, reveals its dark underbelly instead. Through its unflattering characterization of those at the top of the economic heap and its trenchant examination of the ways in which the American dream not only fails to fulfill its promise but also contributes to the decay of personal values, Fitzgerald’s novel stands as a scathing critique of American capitalist culture and the ideology that promotes it. In addition, we will see how a Marxist perspective shows us the ways in which the novel fails to push its critique of capitalism far enough, falling an unwitting prey to the very ideology it tries to undermine.

《了不起的盖茨比》批判资本主义文化最有效的方式之一，在于它展现了资本主义意识形态对那些最成功的“产品”——消费者——造成的破坏性影响，而这种影响正是通过对商品化的刻画实现的。正如你可能记得的，商品的价值，顾名思义，并非取决于它的功能（使用价值），而是取决于它可以交换的金钱或其他商品（交换价值），或是取决于拥有它所带来的社会地位（符号交换价值）。一件物品只有具备交换价值或符号交换价值才能成为商品，而这两种价值并非任何物品固有的。它们都是社会价值：在特定的社会语境中，人们赋予物品这些价值。因此，商品化就是将物品与社会价值联系起来的过程。人或物被定义为具有交换价值或符号交换价值，而忽略了其他因素。当然，商品化是买卖的必然功能，因此也是资本主义的必然功能，因为资本主义的生存依赖于买卖。然而，正如小说所揭示的，商品化，尤其是以符号交换价值形式存在的商品化，并非仅仅是我们下班回家后就能抛诸脑后的市场活动。相反，它是一种心理状态，已经渗透到我们生活的方方面面。

One of the most effective ways The Great Gatsby criticizes capitalist culture is by showing the debilitating effects of capitalist ideology even on those who are its most successful products, and it does so through its representation of commodification. As you may recall, a commodity, by definition, has value not in terms of what it can do (use value) but in terms of the money or other commodities for which it can be traded (exchange value) or in terms of the social status its ownership confers (sign-exchange value). An object becomes a commodity only when it has exchange value or sign-exchange value, and neither form of value is inherent in any object. Both are forms of social value: they are assigned to objects by human beings in a given social context. Commodification, then, is the act of relating to persons or things in terms of their exchange value or sign-exchange value to the exclusion of other considerations. Of course, commodification is a necessary function of buying and selling, and thus it is a necessary function of capitalism, which depends for its survival on buying and selling. However, as the novel illustrates, commodification, especially in the form of sign-exchange value, is not merely a marketplace activity that we can leave at the office when we go home at the end of the day. Rather, it is a psychological attitude that has invaded every domain of our existence.

在《了不起的盖茨比》中，没有哪个角色比汤姆·布坎南更能体现商品化的本质。作为小说中最富有的人，汤姆与世界的关系完全建立在金钱之上：对他而言，万物皆为商品。他与黛西·费的婚姻无疑是用黛西的青春、美貌和社会地位换取汤姆的金钱、权力以及由此赋予他的强大和稳重的形象。恰如其分的是，象征着这笔“交易”的正是汤姆送给未婚妻价值35万美元的珍珠项链。同样，汤姆也利用他的金钱和社会地位“购买”了默特尔·威尔逊以及他与之有染的其他众多底层女性，例如与黛西结婚三个月后就与他有染的女佣，以及他在盖茨比的派对上搭讪的“出身平凡却很漂亮”（112页；第六章）的年轻女子。汤姆一贯选择下层阶级女性，也可以从他对人际交往的商品化看法来理解：他“推销”自己的社会经济地位，以便在最能让他占优势的地方——那些最渴望得到他所兜售的东西，并且最容易被他所迷惑的女性——中获利。

Nowhere in The Great Gatsby is commodification so clearly embodied as in the character of Tom Buchanan. The wealthiest man in the novel, Tom relates to the world only through his money: for him, all things and all people are commodities. His marriage to Daisy Fay was certainly an exchange of Daisy’s youth, beauty, and social standing for Tom’s money and power and the image of strength and stability they imparted to him. Appropriately, the symbol of this “purchase” was the $350,000 string of pearls Tom gave his bride-to-be. Similarly, Tom uses his money and social rank to “purchase” Myrtle Wilson and the numerous other working-class women with whom he has affairs, such as the chambermaid with whom he was involved three months after his marriage to Daisy and the “common but pretty” (112; ch. 6) young woman he picks up at Gatsby’s party. Tom’s consistent choice of lower-class women can also be understood in terms of his commodified view of human interaction: he “markets” his socioeconomic status where it will put him at the greatest advantage – among women who are most desperate for and most easily awed by what he has to sell.

当然，汤姆的商品化行为并不局限于他与女性的关系。因为资本主义宣扬“人如其所有”的观念——即我们作为人的价值取决于我们所拥有的财产的价值——汤姆对昂贵物品的享受很大程度上源于它们的符号交换价值，源于拥有它们所赋予他的社会地位。“我在这儿有个好房子，”他告诉尼克，并补充道，“它以前属于石油大亨德梅恩”（12；第一章），仿佛这栋房子的“出身”就能给他带来某种身份地位。当他戏弄修车工乔治·威尔逊，让他买下自己的车转手牟利时，我们也看到了他这种炫耀社会经济地位的欲望。鉴于汤姆生来就拥有巨额财富，显然多到他一辈子都花不完，他又何必需要这种炫耀来提升自己的社会经济地位呢？

Of course, Tom’s acts of commodification are not limited to his relationships with women. Because capitalism promotes the belief that “you are what you own” – that our value as human beings is only as great as the value of our possessions – much of Tom’s pleasure in his expensive possessions is a product of their sign-exchange value, of the social status their ownership confers on him. “I’ve got a nice place here,” he tells Nick, adding, “It belonged to Demaine, the oil man” (12; ch. 1), as if the house’s “pedigree” could confer a pedigree on him. We see this same desire to flex his socioeconomic muscles, so to speak, when he toys with George Wilson concerning the mechanic’s wish to buy Tom’s car in order to sell it at a profit. Given that Tom was born into enormous wealth, apparently more than he could ever spend, why should he need the socioeconomic ego boost provided by such posturing?

商品化的一大讽刺之处在于，它在满足欲望的同时也创造了欲望。因为它在我们心中滋生的自我价值感总是来源于外部标准，例如时尚潮流，所以我们永远无法对自己的拥有感到安心：总会有更新更好的东西出售，别人可能会买到我们没有的东西，那样的话，他们就会比我们“更好”。对汤姆来说，这种不安全感因为他意识到自己可能拥有某种社会地位而加剧。他永远无法获得：那种因出生于东部而带来的地位。尽管他继承了芝加哥一个显赫家族的财富——因此他的钱并非“新”的，并非是他一生挣来的——但在20世纪20年代的东部，一个显赫的芝加哥家族并不会被视为“老钱”。自英国和荷兰先祖最初移民以来，美国的“贵族”就一直居住在东部。至少在20世纪20年代，对于东部人来说，所谓“老钱”的必要条件之一，就是财富不仅要在过去挣到，而且要在东部挣到。在东部人眼中，来自中西部的人，无论财富规模大小或积累时间长短，都意味着他们是后来者。

One of the ironies of commodification is that it creates desire even as it fulfills it. Because the sense of self-worth it fosters in us is always derived from external standards, such as fashion trends, we can never rest secure in our possessions: something new and better is always being sold, and others may purchase something we don’t have, in which case they will be “better” than we are. In Tom’s case, this kind of insecurity is increased by his awareness of a type of social status he can never acquire: the status that comes from being born in the East. Although he inherited his wealth from an established Chicago family – so his money is not “new” in the sense of having been earned during his lifetime – an established Chicago family in the 1920s would not have been considered “old” in the East, where America’s “bluebloods” had lived since their English and Dutch forebears’ initial immigration. For Easterners, in the 1920s at least, one of the requirements of old money was that it be earned not only in the past but in the East. To be from the Midwest, regardless of the size or age of one’s fortune, was to be a latecomer in the eyes of Easterners.

汤姆曾就读于耶鲁大学，想必和菲​​茨杰拉德在普林斯顿大学时一样，痛苦地意识到自己出身无法满足的东方社会阶层要求。即便他和黛西重返欧洲或中西部，汤姆内心深处依然铭记着自身的社会地位低下。因此，他寻求的是一种与他无法拥有的地位截然不同的身份，一种能够表明他对新旧财富之争漠不关心的身份。所以，他的粗俗——他对默特尔·威尔逊的轻率言行；他喧闹、咄咄逼人的行为；他的无礼——都可以被视为一种自我安慰，试图证明金钱和权力才是最重要的，试图表明他的财富使他免受阶级或教养的束缚。汤姆向尼克推荐一本关于白人文明的书时所表现出的伪科学的“知识分子”姿态——以及他所读到的书中体现的种族主义——也可以从这个角度来解读。他不需要属于旧钱家族，因为他属于一个更庞大、更重要的群体：雅利安人种。正如汤姆所说，“我们已经创造了所有构成文明的东西——哦，科学、艺术等等”（18；第 1 章）。

Having attended Yale, Tom must be, as Fitzgerald was at Princeton, painfully aware of the Eastern social requirement he can never by birth fulfill. Even if he and Daisy return to Europe or the Midwest, Tom carries the knowledge of his social inferiority inside himself. He therefore seeks a status other than the one he can’t have, a status that would declare his indifference to the issue of old money versus new. Thus his vulgarity – his lack of discretion with Myrtle Wilson; his loud, aggressive behavior; his rudeness – can be seen as an attempt to reassure himself that his money and power are all that count, an attempt to show that his wealth insulates him from considerations of class or refinement. The pseudoscientific “intellectualism” Tom adopts in referring Nick to a book he’d read about white civilization – as well as the racism endorsed by his reading – might be seen in this same light. He doesn’t need to belong to old money because he belongs to a larger and more important group: the Aryan race. As Tom puts it, “[W]e’ve produced all the things that go to make civilization – oh, science and art and all that” (18; ch. 1).

汤姆将人商品化的必然结果之一，就是他能够冷酷无情地操纵他人以达到自己的目的。商品化的本质，就是将人物视为商品，视其存在的唯一意义在于对我们自身有利。为了得到默特尔·威尔逊的性服务，他让她以为自己将来可能会娶她，并谎称自己的犹豫是因为黛西信奉天主教，而非自己缺乏性欲。为了除掉争夺黛西芳心的情敌，他牺牲了盖茨比，将乔治·威尔逊交给了他。他故意派乔治·威尔逊带着武器，在精神错乱的情况下前往盖茨比的住所，甚至没有事先打电话警告盖茨比。此外，汤姆的阴险本性也体现在他与黑社会的熟稔上，例如沃尔特·蔡斯就曾与盖茨比一起参与非法活动。

A corollary of Tom’s commodification of people is his ability to manipulate them very cold-bloodedly to get what he wants, for commodification is, by definition, the treatment of objects and people as commodities, as things whose only importance lies in their benefit to ourselves. In order to get Myrtle Wilson’s sexual favors, he lets her think that he may marry her someday, that his hesitation is due to Daisy’s alleged Catholicism rather than to his own lack of desire. And in order to eliminate his rival for Daisy’s affection, he sacrifices Gatsby to George Wilson, whom he deliberately sends, armed and crazed, to Gatsby’s house without even telephoning Gatsby to warn him. In addition, Tom’s sinister capabilities are hinted at through his familiarity with the underworld in the person of Walter Chase, who was involved in illegal activities with Gatsby.

像汤姆·布坎南这样的人物，很容易让我们同情那些依赖他的人，但黛西并非仅仅是她丈夫物化行为的无辜受害者。首先，黛西接受珍珠——以及珍珠所代表的与汤姆的婚姻——当然是一种物化行为：她想要汤姆的象征价值，正如汤姆想要她的一样。而且，黛西也像汤姆一样，能够为了她认为能赋予她的地位而拥护某种理念，例如，她为了给尼克留下深刻印象而将不满商品化。

While a character such as Tom Buchanan is likely to make us sympathize with anyone who is dependent upon him, Daisy is not merely an innocent victim of her husband’s commodification. In the first place, Daisy’s acceptance of the pearls – and of the marriage to Tom they represent – is, of course, an act of commodification: she wanted Tom’s sign-exchange value as much as he wanted hers. And certainly, Daisy is capable, like Tom, of espousing an idea for the status she thinks it confers on her, as when she commodifies disaffection in order to impress Nick:

“你看，我觉得一切都糟透了，”她语气坚定地说。“所有人都这么认为——就连最进步的人也这么认为。而且我知道……我去过很多地方，见过很多事，也做过很多事。”她的目光带着挑衅地环顾四周，有点像汤姆的眼神。

“You see I think everything’s terrible anyhow,” she went on in a convinced way. “Everybody thinks so – the most advanced people. And I know. I’ve been everywhere and seen everything and done everything.” Her eyes flashed around her in a defiant way, rather like Tom’s. …

她声音戛然而止的那一刻……我立刻感受到了她话语中的虚伪。……片刻之后，她那张美丽的脸上浮现出一丝得意的笑容，仿佛在向我宣告她和汤姆都属于某个颇为神秘的组织。

The instant her voice broke off … I felt the basic insincerity of what she had said. … [I]n a moment she looked at me with an absolute smirk on her lovely face as if she had asserted her membership in a rather distinguished secret society to which she and Tom belonged.

（21-22；第1章）

(21–22; ch. 1)

黛西与盖茨比的婚外情，如同她之前与盖茨比的恋情一样，也建立在一种物化的生活观之上。如果她知道盖茨比并非“与她出身相同……[并且]完全有能力照顾她”（156；第八章），她绝不会对他产生兴趣。当她在酒店套房的对峙中得知真相后，她对盖茨比的兴趣迅速消退。她轻而易举地让盖茨比承担默特尔之死的罪责，而自己却与汤姆匆匆离去，这表明她对人的物化，如同她对待丈夫一样，使她能够为了自己的方便而冷酷无情地牺牲他人。

Even Daisy’s extramarital affair with Gatsby, like her earlier romance with him, is based on a commodified view of life. She would never have become interested in him had she known that Gatsby was not from “much the same strata as herself … [and] fully able to take care of her” (156; ch. 8), and when she learns the truth during the confrontation scene in the hotel suite, her interest in him quickly fades. The apparent ease with which she lets Gatsby take the blame for Myrtle’s death, while she beats a hasty retreat with Tom, indicates that her commodification of people, like that of her husband, facilitates the cold-blooded sacrifice of others to her convenience.

布坎南一家将他们的世界商品化，并拥有巨额财富，使他们能够“肆意破坏万物，然后躲回他们的金钱怀抱”（187-88页；第九章）。乔治和默特尔·威尔逊夫妇居住的“灰烬谷”（27页；第二章）与之形成鲜明的社会经济对比，更凸显了布坎南一家的这种行为令人反感。像威尔逊一家这样的人在布坎南一家主宰的世界里毫无生存空间。“灰烬谷”——

The Buchanans’ commodification of their world and the enormous wealth that makes it possible for them to “smas[h] up things and creatures and then retrea[t] back into their money” (187–88; ch. 9) are rendered especially objectionable by the socioeconomic contrast provided by the “valley of ashes” (27; ch. 2) near which George and Myrtle Wilson live. People like the Wilsons don’t stand a chance in a world dominated by people like the Buchanans. The “valley of ashes” –

那是一座奇特的农场，灰烬像小麦一样生长，形成垄沟、山丘和怪诞的花园；灰烬幻化成房屋、烟囱和升腾的烟雾，最终，经过一番超凡的努力，幻化成在粉尘弥漫的空气中模糊移动、摇摇欲坠的人形。

a fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens; where ashes take the forms of houses and chimneys and rising smoke and finally, with a transcendent effort, of men who move dimly and already crumbling through the powdery air

（27；第 2 章）

(27; ch. 2)

——这幅景象令人不寒而栗，生动地描绘了那些缺乏布坎南一家那样社会经济资源的人们的生活。灰烬是物品用尽或浪费后剩下的东西，事实上，这片区域就是一个名副其实的“垃圾场”，“偶尔会有一列灰色的[火车]车厢……停了下来，立刻，一群灰蒙蒙的男人拿着沉重的铁锹蜂拥而至，扬起一片密不透风的尘土”（27；第二章），他们把垃圾从车厢里搬出来。显然，这里也是一个人类的“垃圾场”：除了从火车上清理垃圾的男人们，这里只有“一小块黄砖”（28；第二章）里有一家出租的店铺，“一家通宵营业的餐馆，门口铺着一条灰烬小径”（29；第 2 章），以及乔治·威尔逊的车库，他和默特尔住在车库楼上的一间小公寓里。

– is a powerfully chilling image of the life led by those who do not have the socioeconomic resources of the Buchanans. Ashes are what’s left over after something is used up or wasted, and, indeed, the area is a literal “dumping ground” where “occasionally a line of grey [train] cars … comes to rest, and immediately the ash-grey men swarm up with leaden spades and stir up an impenetrable cloud” (27; ch. 2) as they remove the refuse from the cars. It’s obviously a human “dumping ground” as well: aside from the men who remove the trash from the train, there is only “a small block of yellow brick” (28; ch. 2) containing a shop for rent, “an all-night restaurant approached by a trail of ashes” (29; ch. 2), and George Wilson’s garage above which he and Myrtle occupy a small apartment.

正是在这样的环境中，美国梦才得以萌芽，一个摇摇欲坠却坚持不懈的商业企业，最终应该为自己和子女带来经济保障。然而，用来描述这一场景的语言却清晰地表明，这是一片绝望之地，而非梦想成真的乐土：这是一片“灰蒙蒙的土地”，“难以逾越”，“荒凉的尘土……无休止地飘荡其上”，并且“被一条污浊的小河所环绕”（27-28页；第二章）。这里没有孩子，没有象征美好未来的希望，除了那个“灰白瘦弱的意大利孩子……沿着铁轨一字排开地燃放鞭炮”（30页；第二章），他绝非美好未来的化身。在这人间炼狱中，唯一的生存之道就是任由像汤姆·布坎南这样的人剥削自己，就像乔治那样，为了能低价买下汤姆的车而忍受他的羞辱性玩笑；也像默特尔那样，为了彻底逃离这片苦难之地而忍受汤姆的虐待。但正如乔治和默特尔最终领悟到的，逃离资本主义“垃圾场”的唯一出路，竟是躺进棺材。

It is precisely from settings such as this that the American dream is supposed to emerge, that a shaky but persistent business enterprise is supposed to lead to financial security for oneself and one’s children. But the language used to describe this scene makes it clear that this is a land of hopelessness, not of dreams likely to be fulfilled: it is a “grey land,” “impenetrable,” with “spasms of bleak dust … drift[ing] endlessly over it” and “bounded … by a small foul river” (27–28; ch. 2). And there are no children here, no emblems of hope for a better future, except for the “grey, scrawny Italian child … setting torpedoes [firecrackers] in a row along the railroad track” (30; ch. 2), hardly the embodiment of a promising tomorrow. The only way to survive this hell on earth is to let someone like Tom Buchanan exploit you, as George does when he tolerates Tom’s humiliating banter in the hope of getting a good price on Tom’s car and as Myrtle does when she accepts Tom’s mistreatment in the hope of getting out of the valley of ashes for good. But the only way out of capitalism’s “dumping ground,” as George and Myrtle both finally learn, is in a coffin.

即使是杰伊·盖茨比，这个起初看似体现了美国梦以及资本主义带给所有人的希望的人物，仔细审视之后也会发现这个梦想的空洞本质。盖茨比以典型的白手起家故事，在短短几年内就从极度贫困跃升至极度富有。他童年时期的“日程安排”——效仿本杰明·富兰克林的自我提升传统，将时间分配在诸如“演讲技巧”练习和“必要的发明创造”（181页；第九章）等追求上——与美国梦中白手起家的形象产生了强烈的共鸣。甚至他积累财富的动机似乎也很纯粹：他这样做是为了赢得心爱的女人。然而，如果盖茨比是小说中美国梦的代表，那么这个梦必然是腐败的，因为盖茨比的财富是通过犯罪活动获得的，这严重削弱了美国梦本应塑造的诚实勤奋的形象。虽然盖茨比无疑比汤姆和黛西更有魅力，尼克对他的刻画也更富同情心，但他和他们一样，都将自己的世界商品化了。事实上，有人甚至认为他商品化的程度更甚。

Even Jay Gatsby, the character who seems at first to embody the American dream and the hope capitalism thereby offers to all, reveals, upon closer inspection, the hollowness of that dream. In true rags-to-riches style, Gatsby has risen from extreme poverty to extreme wealth in a very few years. His boyhood “schedule,” in which he divided his time, in the self-improvement tradition of Benjamin Franklin, among such pursuits as the practice of “elocution” and the study of “needed inventions” (181; ch. 9), resonates strongly with the American dream’s image of the self-made man. And even his motive for amassing wealth seems pure: he did it to win the woman he loves. If Gatsby is the novel’s representative of the American dream, however, the dream must be a corrupt one, for Gatsby achieves it only through criminal activities, a fact that severely deflates the image of the honest, hardworking man that the dream is supposed to foster. And although Gatsby is certainly more charming than Tom and Daisy, and more sympathetically portrayed by Nick, he commodifies his world just as they do. In fact, one might argue that he commodifies it more.

布坎南夫妇的财产对他们而言，其象征意义固然重要，但同时也具有使用价值：我们看到这对夫妇斜倚在沙发上，在餐桌旁用餐。相比之下，我们得知盖茨比在他那座装饰华丽的豪宅里，唯一占据的房间是他那间简朴的卧室，而我们唯一一次看到他待在那里，也只是为了带黛西参观。他几乎从不亲自使用他的图书馆、游泳池或水上飞机；他也不喝酒，甚至不认识他那些奢华派对上的大多数宾客。对盖茨比来说，物质财富的唯一功能似乎就是象征意义：他想要的是拥有这些财富所带来的形象，仅此而已。此外，盖茨比的商品几乎所有的符号都是空洞的：他那哥特式的图书馆里摆满了未经切割（因而也从未翻阅）的书籍，他那“仿造的……市政厅”，以及它那“崭新”的塔楼“在稀疏的常春藤下”（9；第一章，斜体为笔者所加），还有他在牛津大学时拍的那张照片，所有这些都只是空洞的表面，没有实质的影像。因此，他之所以拥有这些，似乎也合情合理，因为他最终是为了获得他想要拥有的、具有终极符号交换价值的形象：黛西。

However much the Buchanans’ possessions are important to them in terms of sign-exchange value, they also have use value: we see the couple reclining on their sofas and eating at their tables. In contrast, we are told that the only room Gatsby occupies in his magnificently furnished mansion is his simple bedroom, and during the only time we see him there his purpose is to show it to Daisy. He almost never uses his library, pool, or hydroplane himself; and he doesn’t drink the alcohol or know most of the guests at his lavish parties. It seems that for Gatsby the sole function of material possessions is sign-exchange value: he wants the image their ownership confers on him and nothing more. Furthermore, Gatsby’s commodity signs are almost all empty: his Gothic library filled with uncut (and, therefore, unopened) books, his “imitation … Hôtel de Ville” with its “spanking new” tower “under a thin beard of raw ivy” (9; ch. 1, my italics), and his photo of himself at Oxford are all surfaces without interiors, all images without substance. It seems fitting, then, that he acquired them in order to acquire the ultimate image of sign-exchange value he wants to possess: Daisy.

拥有黛西将给盖茨比他真正想要的：一个永久的标志，表明他属于她那样的社会经济阶层，属于黛西初次见到他时，在他眼中那种明亮、洁净、轻松、无忧无虑的富人世界。对盖茨比来说，她的存在给她居住的房子带来了一种“令人窒息的强烈”感觉。

Possession of Daisy would give Gatsby what he really wants: a permanent sign that he belongs to her socioeconomic class, to the same bright, spotless, airy, carefree world of the very rich that Daisy embodied for him when they first met. For Gatsby, her presence gave the house in which she lived a feeling of “breathless intensity,”

楼上的卧室比其他卧室更漂亮、更凉爽，走廊里传来欢快而光彩照人的活动，还有浪漫的爱情故事……让人联想起今年闪亮的汽车和鲜花尚未凋零的舞会。

a hint of bedrooms upstairs more beautiful and cool than other bedrooms, of gay and radiant activities taking place through its corridors, and of romances that were … redolent of this year’s shining motor cars and of dances whose flowers were scarcely withered.

（155-56；第 8 章）

(155–56; ch. 8)

在盖茨比眼中，拥有黛西——终极的商品象征——就能“洗白”他的“新钱”，让它变成“旧钱”，就能让他那座“崭新”的仿制市政厅变成祖传的宅邸。因此，他为了赢得黛西而积累物质财富，实际上是为了获得另一种商品象征。

Possession of Daisy, the ultimate commodity sign, would, in Gatsby’s eyes, “launder” his “new money” and make it “old,” would make his “spanking new” imitation Hôtel de Ville an ancestral seat. Thus, in accumulating material goods in order to win Daisy, he accumulated one kind of commodity sign in order to acquire another.

盖茨比对世界的商品化，与汤姆一样，都与他冷酷无情地追求欲望的野心密不可分。盖茨比所处的奢华生活并非孤立存在，而是建立在一个充斥着腐败、犯罪和死亡的黑暗险恶的世界之上。他的财富​​来源于非法活动，包括走私私酒和出售伪造债券。这个地下世界属于迈耶·沃尔夫希姆，他拥有无所不在的犯罪关系，甚至能够操纵1919年的世界大赛。而正是这个人，声称是他给了盖茨比成功的机会。

Gatsby’s commodification of his world is linked, like Tom’s, to the cold-blooded aggression with which he pursues what he wants. The lap of luxury in which Gatsby lives does not exist in a vacuum. It is supported by a very dark and sinister world of corruption, crime, and death. The underworld activities from which his wealth derives include bootlegging and the selling of fraudulent bonds. This is the underworld of Meyer Wolfsheim, who has such unlimited criminal connections that he was able to “fix” the 1919 World Series. And this is the man who takes credit for giving Gatsby his start.

沃尔夫希姆派去为盖茨比工作的那些“面目狰狞”的仆人（119页；第七章）以及盖茨比接到的（盖茨比死后，尼克也意外接到的）明显来自犯罪分子的电话，让我们得以窥见这个世界。这是一个捕食者和猎物的世界，非法的——因而往往品质低劣的——酒类被随意出售给任何有钱人，假债券在小镇上流传，落入毫无戒心的投资者手中。一些购买酒类的人可能会因此生病，甚至丧命。所有购买假债券的小投资者都会损失他们根本输不起的钱。而当不可避免的错误发生，法律介入时，总会有人成为牺牲品，就像盖茨比牺牲沃尔特·蔡斯一样。

We get a glimpse of this world in the “villainous” looking servants (119; ch. 7) Wolfsheim sends to work for Gatsby and in the phone calls Gatsby receives (and which, after Gatsby’s death, Nick receives by accident) from obvious criminal sources. This is a world of predators and prey in which illegal – and thus often imperfect – liquor is sold over the counter to anyone with the money to pay for it and in which fake bonds are passed in small towns to unsuspecting investors. Some of the people who buy the liquor may become ill from it; some may die. All of the small investors who buy the fraudulent bonds will lose money that they can’t afford to lose. And when the inevitable mistakes are made and the law steps in, someone will have to be sacrificed as Gatsby sacrifices Walter Chase.

甚至主人公对黛西的渴望也带有黑社会的色彩。盖茨比第一次在路易斯维尔黛西父母家追求她时，他“让她……”她认为他与她出身于大致相同的阶层，而事实上，“他没有舒适的家庭支持，而且他很容易受到冷酷无情的政府的摆布，被送到世界任何地方”（156；第 8 章）：

Even the protagonist’s desire for Daisy is informed by an underworld perspective. When Gatsby first courted Daisy at her parents’ home in Louisville, he “let her believe that he was a person from much the same strata as herself” when, in fact, “he had no comfortable family standing behind him and he was liable at the whim of an impersonal government to be blown anywhere about the world” (156; ch. 8):

然而，无论他的未来多么辉煌……他此刻只是个身无分文、没有过去的年轻士兵，随时都可能失去他那身无形的军装。所以他格外珍惜每一分每一秒。他贪婪而肆无忌惮地攫取一切——最终，在一个静谧的十月夜晚，他掳走了黛西，因为他根本没有权利触碰她的手。

However glorious might be his future … he was at present a penniless young [soldier] without a past, and at any moment the invisible cloak of his uniform might slip from his shoulders. So he made the most of his time. He took what he could get, ravenously and unscrupulously – eventually he took Daisy one still October night, took her because he had no real right to touch her hand.

（156；第 8 章）

(156; ch. 8)

这种语言——“他贪婪无度、肆无忌惮地攫取一切”——绝非爱情的语言。相反，这种语言更像是用来形容流氓的，它强烈地反映了盖茨比在遇见黛西之前与丹·科迪的暧昧关系，以及在与黛西初次交往之后他的犯罪活动。

This language – “he took what he could get, ravenously and unscrupulously” – is hardly the language of love. Rather, it is the kind of language that would be used to describe a hoodlum, the kind of language that resonates strongly with Gatsby’s dubious association with Dan Cody before meeting Daisy and with his criminal activities subsequent to their initial affair.

因此，盖茨比也未能免于小说对富人的不加修饰的刻画。事实上，他的形象表明，美国梦并没有为布坎南夫妇的商品化世界提供道德上的替代方案，反而像汤姆和黛西继承的财富一样，造成了人与物的商品化。《了不起的盖茨比》对美国文化的描绘，揭示了资本主义对汤姆、黛西和盖茨比等社会经济“赢家”以及乔治和默特尔等“输家”的负面影响。

Thus, Gatsby is not exempt from the novel’s unflattering portrait of the wealthy. Indeed, his characterization suggests that the American dream does not offer a moral alternative to the commodified world of the Buchanans but produces the same commodification of people and things as does Tom and Daisy’s inherited wealth. The Great Gatsby’s representation of American culture, then, reveals the debilitating effects of capitalism on socioeconomic “winners” such as Tom, Daisy, and Gatsby, as well as on “losers” such as George and Myrtle.

《了不起的盖茨比》对资本主义的有力批判，与小说中对资本主义压迫性意识形态的微妙强化形成鲜明对比。这种反作用体现在三个方面。首先，对乔治和默特尔·威尔逊夫妇的丑化刻画，转移了我们对他们作为资本主义制度受害者的关注，而他们在这个制度下苦苦挣扎求生。其次，由于尼克被盖茨比所代表的美国梦所吸引，他的叙述将主人公浪漫化，掩盖了吉米·盖茨对美国梦的投入如何造就了道德沦丧的杰伊·盖茨比。第三，小说中用来描绘富人世界的华丽辞藻，即便其中充斥着像布坎南夫妇这样的人，也依然使其充满吸引力。

Operating against The Great Gatsby’s powerful critique of capitalism is the novel’s subtle reinforcement of capitalism’s repressive ideology. This counter-movement operates in three ways. First, the unflattering portraits of George and Myrtle Wilson deflect our attention from their victimization by the capitalist system in which they both struggle to survive. Second, because Nick is seduced by the American dream Gatsby represents, his narrative romanticizes the protagonist, obscuring the ways in which Jimmy Gatz’s investment in the dream produced the amoral Jay Gatsby. Third, the lush language used to describe the world of the wealthy makes it attractive despite the people like the Buchanans who populate it.

从马克思主义视角来看， 《了不起的盖茨比》最明显的缺陷或许在于它对乔治和默特尔·威尔逊夫妇——小说中底层阶级的代表——缺乏同情心的刻画。乔治和默特尔试图用他们唯一知道的方式来改善自己的境遇。乔治苦苦支撑着摇摇欲坠的生意，而默特尔则试图通过出售她唯一拥有的“商品”——将自己的身体“出租”给汤姆·布坎南——来开创自己的事业，希望他有朝一日会通过娶她来“买下”她的身体。他们是资本主义的受害者，因为在资本主义经济中，成功的唯一途径就是在市场上取得成功，而由于乔治和默特尔在他们唯一能够进入的市场中都未能成功，他们注定要坠入“灰烬谷”。然而，人物刻画过于负面，以至于人们很容易忽略控制他们生活的社会经济现实。事实上，有人可能会认为小说对威尔逊夫妇的描写是一种阶级歧视的底层夫妇刻板印象：乔治不太聪明；默特尔聒噪、令人讨厌，而且性欲过强。我们或许会同情乔治，但他的个人缺陷削弱了我们的同情心。也就是说，我们不是因为他是阶级压迫的受害者而感到同情（或对体制感到愤怒），而是因为他没有能力“白手起家”，无法像美国梦告诉我们的那样改善自身境遇而感到同情（或愤怒）：我们责怪的是受害者，而不是压迫他的体制。同样，默特尔对乔治的残酷拒绝和对汤姆的肆意追求，使她很容易成为我们谴责的对象：我们对默特尔极其有限的选择的认知，恰恰因为她竭尽全力地利用这些选择而变得模糊不清。

Perhaps The Great Gatsby’s most obvious flaw, from a Marxist perspective, is its unsympathetic rendering of George and Myrtle Wilson, the novel’s representatives of the lower class. George and Myrtle try to improve their lot the only way they know how. George clings to his foundering business, and Myrtle, in a sense, tries to start one of her own by marketing the only commodity she has in stock: she “rents” her body to Tom Buchanan, hoping he’ll want someday to “purchase” it by marrying her. They are victims of capitalism because the only way to succeed in a capitalist economy is to succeed in a market, and, as neither George nor Myrtle succeed in the only markets open to them, they are condemned to the “valley of ashes.” Their characterizations, however, are so negative that it is easy to overlook the socioeconomic realities that control their lives. Indeed, one might argue that the novel’s portrayal of the Wilsons is a classist stereotype of a lower-class couple: George is not very bright; Myrtle is loud, obnoxious, and overtly sexual. We may feel sorry for George, but our sympathy is undercut by his personal failings. That is, instead of feeling sorry (or angry at the system) that he is a victim of class oppression, we feel sorry (or angry at him) that he doesn’t have what it takes to “pull himself up by his bootstraps” and better himself, as the American dream tells us he should: we blame the victim instead of the system that victimizes him. Similarly, Myrtle’s cruel rejection of George and brazen pursuit of Tom make her an easy target for our disapproval: our awareness of Myrtle’s severely limited options is dimmed by the very fact that she does her best to use them.

从马克思主义视角来看，小说在更微妙的层面上也存在缺陷，那就是尼克对盖茨比的浪漫化。尼克或许自认为不赞同杰伊·盖茨比——因为他知道自己应该赞同他，理由与他反对布坎南夫妇的理由相同——但从一开始就很明显，叙述者被盖茨比深深吸引。正如尼克所说：“他身上有一种迷人的气质，对生活的美好有着格外敏锐的感知……这是一种非凡的希望天赋，一种浪漫的情怀，我从未在其他人身上发现过，而且恐怕以后也很难再找到了”（6；第一章）。

In a more subtle manner, the novel is also flawed, from a Marxist perspective, by Nick’s romanticization of Gatsby. Nick may like to think he disapproves of Jay Gatsby – because he knows he should disapprove of him for the same reasons he disapproves of the Buchanans – but it is clear from the beginning that the narrator is charmed by him. As Nick tells us, “There was something gorgeous about him, some heightened sensitivity to the promises of life. … [I]t was an extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness such as I have never found in any other person and which it is not likely I shall ever find again” (6; ch. 1).

在尼克的叙述中，这种理想化通过他对盖茨比浪漫形象的着重刻画而凸显：叛逆的少年、雄心勃勃的年轻粗犷汉子、理想主义的梦想家、深情的情人、勇敢的士兵、慷慨的主人。盖茨比的犯罪背景虽被提及，但由于尼克对此的反应，这些并未影响他对盖茨比的看法。例如，尼克谈论盖茨比犯罪生活的方式往往有意转移人们对盖茨比地下活动道德层面的关注，就像尼克在盖茨比的一次派对上无意间听到的一段对话：“‘他是个私酒贩子，’年轻的女士们一边说着，一边在他面前的鸡尾酒和鲜花之间穿梭”（65；第四章）。这句话的修辞手法是尼克为盖茨比辩护，反驳批评者时的典型做法，即使批评者是对的：他的声明着重强调盖茨比的慷慨，以及他乐于利用这种慷慨来对付那些议论他的人，从而回避了这样一个事实：“他的鸡尾酒和鲜花”根本不是他自己的：它们是用他犯罪所得的资金购买的。

This idealization is foregrounded in Nick’s narrative through his focus on romantic images of Gatsby: the rebellious boy, the ambitious young roughneck, the idealistic dreamer, the devoted lover, the brave soldier, the lavish host. Gatsby’s criminal connections are acknowledged, but because of Nick’s response to them, they don’t influence his opinion of the man. For example, Nick’s manner of discussing Gatsby’s criminal life tends to deflect attention away from the moral implications of Gatsby’s underworld activities, as when Nick reports the following conversation he overheard at one of Gatsby’s parties: “‘He’s a bootlegger,’ said the young ladies, moving somewhere between his cocktails and his flowers” (65; ch. 4). The rhetoric of this phrase is typical of Nick’s defense of Gatsby against his detractors, even when those detractors are right: his statement focuses on Gatsby’s generosity and on the willingness to abuse it of those who gossip about him, thereby sidestepping the fact that “his cocktails and his flowers” weren’t rightfully his at all: they were purchased with funds obtained from his criminal activities.

同样，尼克对那些展现盖茨比正面形象的事件投入了情感，从而影响了我们对盖茨比的反应。例如，当盖茨比被汤姆质问时，当众承认他在牛津的经历是政府为一战后留在欧洲的美国士兵提供的，尼克“真想站起来拍拍他的背”（136；第七章）。盖茨比对现实的这一小小让步，让尼克重新“完全信任他”（136；第七章）。尽管尼克对黑社会有所了解，但他仍然对盖茨比抱有这种信任。尽管尼克声称他对盖茨比的世界“毫不掩饰地鄙夷”，但盖茨比本人却“不受”尼克的谴责：“盖茨比最终安然无恙；真正令尼克——以及许多读者——感到不满的，是那些吞噬盖茨比的东西，是那些在他梦想破灭后飘散的污秽尘埃”（6；第一章）。尼克的情感如此真挚，以至于很容易影响读者，因为这些情感深深地影响了他所描绘的人物形象。汤姆·伯纳姆也赞同尼克的观点，并代表了许多文学评论家对主人公的典型看法，他认为盖茨比“在周围的腐败环境中幸存下来，保持了健全完整的品格”（105），而罗斯·艾德琳·加洛则认为盖茨比“至死都保持着他的纯真”（43）。

Similarly, Nick influences our reaction to Gatsby by his own emotional investment in those events that show Gatsby in a good light. For example, when Gatsby, confronted by Tom, admits in front of everyone that his Oxford experience was provided by a government arrangement for American soldiers who remained in Europe after World War I, Nick “wanted to get up and slap him on the back” (136; ch. 7). This small concession to reality on Gatsby’s part elicits in Nick a renewal “of complete faith in him” (136; ch. 7). Despite what Nick knows about the underworld sources of Gatsby’s wealth, despite the “unaffected scorn” Nick says he has for Gatsby’s world, Gatsby himself is “exempt” from Nick’s disapprobation: “Gatsby turned out all right at the end; it is what preyed on Gatsby, what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams” (6; ch. 1) that elicits Nick’s disaffection – and that of many readers. It is easy to be influenced by the warmth of Nick’s feelings because these feelings so strongly inform the portrait he paints. Following Nick’s lead, and typical of the response of many literary critics to the title character, Tom Burnam says that Gatsby “survives sound and whole in character, uncorrupted by the corruption which surrounded him” (105), and Rose Adrienne Gallo believes that Gatsby “maintained his innocence” to the end (43).1

尼克为什么要自欺欺人，也为什么要欺骗我们，让我们对盖茨比产生误解？他为什么要极力强调盖茨比性格中所有积极、讨人喜欢的品质，却把那些令人不快的缺点推卸给别人？我认为这是因为叙述者自己也被盖茨比的梦想所迷惑。三十岁的尼克，仍然靠父亲的资助生活，一边摸索着自己的人生方向，一边又渴望相信生活依然充满希望，这并不奇怪，因为他害怕现实并非如此。他害怕自己未来所剩无几，正如他自己所说，“单身男士的名单越来越短，热情也越来越少，头发也越来越稀疏”（143页；第七章）。他在纽约的夏天——他一系列冒险经历中的最新一次——以灾难告终，因此他渴望相信希望的存在。尼克相信盖茨比，因为他想相信盖茨比的梦想也能在自己身上实现：一个迷茫的年轻人也能像盖茨比那样获得惊人的财富，找到梦寐以求的女人，并对未来充满乐观。尼克不愿想起盖茨比光鲜亮丽的世界建立在腐败之上，因为他渴望拥有那样一个充满希望的世界。他与盖茨比的愿望沆瀣一气，而他的叙述也可能引导读者与这种愿望产生共鸣。

Why should Nick deceive himself, and us, about Gatsby? Why should he foreground all the positive, likable qualities in Gatsby’s personality and shift responsibility for the unpleasant ones onto others’ shoulders? I think it is because the narrator is himself seduced by Gatsby’s dream. At the age of 30, and still being financed by his father while he tries to figure out what he should do, it is not surprising that Nick wants to believe life still holds promise because he is afraid that it doesn’t. He fears that all he has to look forward to is, as he puts it, “a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning brief-case of enthusiasm, thinning hair” (143; ch. 7). With his summer in New York – his latest in a series of adventures – having ended in disaster, he wants to believe in the possibility of hope. Nick believes in Gatsby because he wants to believe that Gatsby’s dream can come true for himself: that a young man at loose ends can make the kind of outrageous financial success of himself that Gatsby has made, can find the woman of his dreams, and can be so optimistic about the future. Nick doesn’t want to be reminded that Gatsby’s glittering world rests on corruption because he wants that kind of hopeful world for himself. He is in collusion with Gatsby’s desire, and his narrative can lead readers into collusion with that desire as well.

盖茨比渴望融入富人的魔幻世界——正如安德鲁·狄龙所言，“盖茨比拥有读者也渴望的东西：纵情享乐的当下”（61）——这种渴望对读者来说，也恰恰印证了商品的力量。盖茨比或许没有充分利用他的豪宅、水上飞机、游泳池和藏书，但我们中的许多人或许会觉得，自己肯定会这么做。因此，从马克思主义的视角来看，这部小说的另一个缺陷在于，它用华丽的语言描绘这个休闲奢华的世界，从而有力地强化了商品对读者的吸引力。消费品被赋予了魔力——拥有改变现实的能力——这暗示着商品本身是超越尘世限制的。例如，就连盖茨比派对上的茶点也显得格外迷人：“一盘鸡尾酒在暮色中向我们飘来”（47；第3章，我的斜体字），“自助餐桌上摆满了闪闪发光的开胃菜，香料烤火腿挤在小丑图案的沙拉旁边，还有被施了魔法变成深金色的糕点猪和火鸡”（44；第3章，我的斜体字）。

The appeal to readers of Gatsby’s desire to belong to the magical world of the wealthy – as Andrew Dillon puts it, “Gatsby has possessed what the reader must also desire: the orgiastic present” (61) – is also a testimonial to the power of the commodity. Gatsby may not make the best use of his mansion, his hydroplane, his swimming pool, and his library, but many of us might feel that we certainly would. Thus another flaw in the novel, from a Marxist perspective, is the way in which the commodity’s appeal is powerfully reinforced for the reader by the lush language used to describe this world of leisure and luxury. Consumer goods are invested with magic – with the capacity to transform reality – which suggests that the commodity is itself transcendent, beyond earthly limitation. Even the refreshments at Gatsby’s parties, for example, seem enchanted: a “tray of cocktails floated at us through the twilight” (47; ch. 3, my italics), and on “buffet tables, garnished with glistening hors-d’oeuvre, spiced baked hams crowded against salads of harlequin designs and pastry pigs and turkeys bewitched to a dark gold” (44; ch. 3, my italics).

在对布坎南一家位于东卵的家的以下描述中，这种特质尤其引人注目：

The commodity is especially compelling in the following description of the Buchanans’ home on East Egg:

他们的房子是……一栋欢快的红白相间的乔治亚殖民风格宅邸，俯瞰着海湾。草坪从海滩一直延伸到前门，绵延四分之一英里，越过日晷、砖砌小径和繁茂的花园——最终到达房子时，仿佛凭借奔跑的惯性，沿着房屋侧面蜿蜒而上，长满了鲜艳的藤蔓。正面是一排法式落地窗，此刻在阳光的映照下闪闪发光，敞开着迎接温暖的午后微风。

Their house was … a cheerful red and white Georgian Colonial mansion overlooking the bay. The lawn started at the beach and ran toward the front door for a quarter of a mile, jumping over sun-dials and brick walks and burning gardens – finally when it reached the house drifting up the side in bright vines as though from the momentum of its run. The front was broken by a line of French windows, glowing now with reflected gold, and wide open to the warm windy afternoon. …

前方的景色……包括一座下沉式的意大利花园、半英亩芬芳浓郁的玫瑰花丛，以及一艘船头略短的摩托艇，它在近岸的潮水中颠簸前行。

[T]he front vista … [included] in its sweep a sunken Italian garden, a half acre of deep pungent roses and a snub-nosed motor boat that bumped the tide off shore. …

我们穿过高高的走廊，走进一个明亮、玫瑰色的空间，两端的落地窗将这空间与房屋巧妙地连接起来。……一阵微风吹过房间，将窗帘从一端吹进，又从另一端吹出，如同淡色的旗帜，它们向上盘旋，仿佛要飘向那如同糖霜婚礼蛋糕般光滑的天花板——然后，微风拂过酒红色的地毯，在地毯上投下斑驳的影子，如同风在海面上投下的影子。

We walked through a high hallway into a bright rosy-colored space, fragilely bound into the house by French windows at either end. … A breeze blew through the room, blew curtains in at one end and out the other like pale flags, twisting them up toward the frosted wedding cake of the ceiling – and then rippled over the wine-colored rug, making a shadow on it as wind does on the sea.

（11-12；第1章）

(11–12; ch. 1)

这段文字巧妙地调动了五官，语言如此感性，仿佛房子都拥有了生命。因此，这处场景的存在独立于居住其中的人物：庄园无需汤姆和黛西也能美轮美奂；在汤姆买下它之前，它就已美轮美奂；布坎南一家离开之后，它依然会美不胜收。事实上，我们完全可以欣然想象没有住户的这处地方。也就是说，这处场景比布坎南一家更加宏大——它既包含他们，又超越他们。他们既没有用尽它，也没有耗尽它的可能性。而且，它不受他们的腐蚀：我们不会被引导将这个地方与发生在那里的事件联系起来。因此，它对许多读者有着强大的吸引力。菲茨杰拉德既是资本主义的批判者，也是它的桂冠诗人，他的诗歌能够吸引读者关注小说表面上所谴责的事物。

This passage is a delicious appeal to every one of the five senses, with language so sensual that the house seems to breathe with a life of its own. This setting thus has an existence independent of the characters who inhabit it: the estate doesn’t need Tom and Daisy in order to be gorgeous; it was gorgeous before Tom bought it, and it will be gorgeous after the Buchanans are gone. In fact, we could easily, and happily, imagine this place without its occupants. That is, the setting is bigger than the Buchanans – it contains and exceeds them. They neither use it up nor exhaust its possibilities. And it is impervious to their corruption: we are not led to associate the place with the events that occur there. Therefore, it can exert a magnetic appeal on many readers. As much as Fitzgerald is the critic of capitalism, he is also its poet laureate, and his poetry can attract readers to the very thing that, on a more overt level, the novel condemns.

《了不起的盖茨比》虽然对资本主义意识形态进行了深刻的批判，但同时也对这种意识形态进行了重新包装和兜售。这种文本的双重作用赋予了结尾一句特殊的讽刺意味：如果我们“奋力前行，逆流而上，却不断被推回过去”（189页；第九章），那么这部小说中却存在着某种东西，它强化了这种倒退，不断地将我们拉回资本主义的魔咒之下。最终，盖茨比未能实现美国梦，但正因为这部小说本身也沦为了它所批判的资本主义意识形态的牺牲品，许多读者才会继续沉迷其中。

While The Great Gatsby offers a significant critique of capitalist ideology, it also repackages and markets that ideology anew. This double movement of the text gives the closing line a special irony: if we do “beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past” (189; ch. 9), there is in this novel that which strengthens the backflow, bearing us ceaselessly back under capitalism’s spell. In the end, Gatsby fails to realize the American dream, but because the novel falls prey to the capitalist ideology it condemns, many readers will continue to invest in it.

拓展练习题：马克思主义对其他文学作品的解读

Questions for further practice: Marxist approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用马克思主义批评来解读文中提及的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use Marxist criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1威廉·福克纳的小说《献给艾米丽的玫瑰》（1931）中体现出的森严的阶级结构，是如何推动故事情节发展和塑造人物性格的？你认为这篇小说是否引导我们去批判它所展现的阶级主义？

1 How is the rigid class structure evident in William Faulkner’s “A Rose for Emily” (1931) responsible for much of the story’s action and characterization? Would you say the story does or does not invite us to criticize the classism it represents?

2我们能从托妮·凯德·班巴拉的小说《教训》（1972）中学到关于炫耀性消费和商品化的哪些知识？这部小说是如何利用其对这些资本主义现实的描绘来批判阶级压迫的？

2 What can we learn from Toni Cade Bambara’s “The Lesson” (1972) about conspicuous consumption and commodification? How does the story use its representation of these capitalist realities to criticize class oppression?

3约翰·斯坦贝克的《愤怒的葡萄》（1939）如何能被视为对美国资本主义的马克思主义批判？小说的形式（现实主义）如何支撑了这种批判？电影版的结局（从马克思主义视角来看是有缺陷的）如何削弱了小说更为现实主义的结局？

3 How does John Steinbeck’s The Grapes of Wrath (1939) qualify as a Marxist critique of American capitalism? How does the novel’s form (realism) support that critique? How does the ending of the film version (which is flawed, from a Marxist perspective) undermine the more realistic ending of the novel?

4描述凯特·肖邦的小说《暴风雨》（1898）中人物生活中存在的阶级制度。这篇小说在哪些方面未能批判它所描绘的阶级制度，又在哪些方面未能引导我们去批判这种阶级制度？

4 Describe the class system operating in the lives of the characters in Kate Chopin’s “The Storm” (1898). In what ways does the story fail to criticize, and fail to invite us to criticize, the classism it depicts?

5兰斯顿·休斯的《在路上》（1952）如何能被视为对有组织宗教的马克思主义批判？

5 How does Langston Hughes’ “On the Road” (1952) qualify as a Marxist critique of organized religion?

4. 女性主义批评

4   Feminist criticism

“我不是女权主义者——我喜欢男人！”

“I’m not a feminist – I like men!”

“我不是女权主义者——我认为如果女性愿意，她们就应该能够待在家里养育孩子！”

“I’m not a feminist – I think women should be able to stay at home and raise children if they want to!”

“我不是女权主义者——我穿胸罩！”

“I’m not a feminist – I wear a bra!”

与许多初涉女性主义文学批评的学生的观点相反，许多女性主义者和男性一样，认为女性如果愿意，就应该待在家里抚养孩子，并且应该穿胸罩。广义而言，女性主义批评探讨文学（以及其他文化产品）如何强化或削弱女性在经济、政治、社会和心理层面所受到的压迫。然而，正如所有批评理论的实践者一样，女性主义批评家对于其学科所研究的所有问题也持有许多不同的观点。事实上，一些女性主义者将她们的研究领域称为“多元女性主义”，以强调其拥护者观点的多样性，并提供一种与传统观念（即存在单一最佳观点）相悖的思维方式。然而，我们这些初涉女性主义理论研究的人，无论男女，都事先认定自己不是女性主义者，因为我们不认同我们认为最令人反感的某种女性主义观点。换句话说，在我们进入理论课堂之前，许多人就已经将女权主义简化为我们认为最令人反感的部分，并以此为依据否定了它。我认为，这种态度揭示了当今美国文化中仍然存在的对女权主义的过度简化和负面看法。因为我们正是从更广泛的文化——家庭、工作场所、媒体等等——中吸收了反女权主义偏见，并有时会将其带入课堂。

Contrary to the opinions of many students new to the study of feminist literary criticism, many feminists like men, think that women should be able to stay at home and raise children if they want to do so, and wear bras. Broadly defined, feminist criticism examines the ways in which literature (and other cultural productions) reinforces or undermines the economic, political, social, and psychological oppression of women. However, just as the practitioners of all critical theories do, feminist critics hold many different opinions on all of the issues their discipline examines. In fact, some feminists call their field feminisms in order to underscore the multiplicity of points of view of its adherents and offer ways of thinking that oppose the traditional tendency to believe there is a single best point of view. Yet many of us who are new to the study of feminist theory, both male and female, have decided ahead of time that we are not feminists because we don’t share whatever feminist point of view we have found the most objectionable. In other words, before we even come to the theory classroom, many of us have reduced feminism to whatever we consider its most objectionable element and, on that basis, have rejected it. This attitude reveals, I think, the oversimplified, negative view of feminism that persists in American culture today. For it is from the culture at large – the home, the workplace, the media, and so on – that we have gathered the antifeminist bias we sometimes bring into the classroom.

为了了解这种负面的过度简化是如何让我们忽视女权主义所提出问题的严重性的，让我们简要地审视一下女权主义最受诟病的主张之一：我们不应该用男性代词“他”来指代男性和女性。对许多人来说，这种主张暗示了他们眼中女权主义诉求的琐碎，甚至是幼稚。如果我们继续使用“包容性的他”来指代两性，又能有什么区别呢？我们这样做，并非毫无道理：这只是一种语言惯例，它同时涵盖了男性和女性。这些人认为，女权主义者应该专注于争取女性在经济上获得平等的机会，而应该忽略所有关于代词的无稽之谈！然而，对许多女权主义者来说，使用“他”来指代两性，反映并延续了一种“看待事物的习惯”，一种以男性经验作为评判两性经验标准的看待生活的方式。换句话说，尽管“包容性的他”声称代表男性和女性，但实际上它体现了一种根深蒂固的文化态度，这种态度忽视了女性的经验和观点。这种态度的危害体现在许多方面。

To see how this negative oversimplification works to blind us to the seriousness of the issues feminism raises, let’s briefly examine one of the most maligned feminist claims: that we should not use the masculine pronoun he to represent both men and women. For many people, this claim suggests what they see as the trivial, even infantile, nature of feminist demands. What possible difference could it make if we continue to use the “inclusive he” to refer to members of both sexes? We know what we mean when we do it: it’s simply a convention of language that includes both males and females. Such people believe that feminists should just concentrate on getting women an equal crack at the dough and forget all this nonsense about pronouns! For many feminists, however, the use of the pronoun he to refer to members of both sexes reflects and perpetuates a “habit of seeing,” a way of looking at life, that uses male experience as the standard by which the experience of both sexes is evaluated. In other words, although the “inclusive he” claims to represent both men and women, in reality it is part of a deeply rooted cultural attitude that ignores women’s experiences and women’s points of view. The damaging effects of this attitude can be seen in a number of areas.

例如，在20世纪60年代末女性争取平等的斗争最终在文学研究领域兴起之前，（白人）男性作家以（白人）男性视角描述经历的文学作品被视为普遍性的标准——也就是说，它们代表了所有读者的经历——而普遍性也被视为衡量伟大作品的重要标准。由于（白人）女性作家（以及所有有色人种作家）的作品并非以（白人）男性视角描述经历，因此它们不被认为是普遍性的，因而也没有被纳入文学经典。值得注意的是，作品的受欢迎程度并不一定被视为普遍性的证据，因为许多生前享有盛名的女性作家并没有被文学史“奉为经典”，而文学史主要关注的是男性作家。当然，那些坚持这种伟大标准的人并不认为自己是在进行不公平的歧视；他们只是认为自己是在拒绝那些不具有普遍性、不够伟大的文学作品。即使在 20 世纪 70 年代中期，（白人）女性作家开始更频繁地出现在经典作品和大学课程大纲中，她们的地位也与（白人）男性作家不相上下。

For example, before the centuries-old struggle for women’s equality finally emerged in literary studies in the late 1960s, the literary works of (white) male authors describing experience from a (white) male point of view were considered the standard of universality – that is, representative of the experience of all readers – and universality was considered a major criterion of greatness. Because the works of (white) female authors (and of all authors of color) do not describe experience from a (white) male point of view, they were not considered universal and hence did not become part of the literary canon. It is interesting to note that popularity was not necessarily considered evidence of universality, for many women writers who enjoyed widespread fame during their lives were not “canonized” in literary histories, which focused primarily on male writers. Of course, those holding up this standard of greatness did not believe they were being unfairly discriminatory; they simply believed that they were rejecting literary texts that were not universal, that were not great. Even when (white) women authors began to appear more frequently in the canon and on college syllabi in the mid-1970s, they were not represented on an equal basis with (white) male authors.

即使在今天，除非从女性主义的视角进行批判或历史研究，否则女性作家的贡献往往被低估。例如，马修·J·布鲁科利在《了不起的盖茨比》新版序言中指出，20世纪20年代是“美国文学的成就时代”（x），并列举了12位作家的名字来佐证他的观点。然而，这些作家中只有一位是女性——薇拉·凯瑟。那么艾伦·格拉斯哥、苏珊·格拉斯佩尔、内拉·拉森、埃德娜·圣文森特·米莱、罗拉·林恩·里格斯、格特鲁德·斯坦、朱娜·巴恩斯、伊丽莎白·马多克斯·罗伯茨、H·D（希尔达·杜利特尔）或玛丽安·摩尔呢？许多学生可能只认识其中的几位，这说明文学史对许多女性作家的边缘化，尽管在她们写作的时代，读者未必也如此看待她们。同样，即使在今天，大多数好莱坞电影中，镜头（电影拍摄的视角）仍然是男性的：镜头凝视的对象是女性角色，而不是男性角色，她们常常被赋予情色意味，仿佛是男性的视角在观看她们，仿佛“普遍”的电影观众的视角是男性的。

Even today, unless the critical or historical point of view is feminist, there is a tendency to underrepresent the contribution of women writers. For example, in Matthew J. Bruccoli’s preface to recent editions of The Great Gatsby, he notes that the 1920s was “an age of achievement … in American literature” (x) and lists the names of 12 authors to support his claim. Only one of those authors – Willa Cather – is a woman. What about Ellen Glasgow, Susan Glaspell, Nella Larsen, Edna St. Vincent Millay, Rolla Lynn Riggs, Gertrude Stein, Djuna Barnes, Elizabeth Maddox Roberts, H. D. (Hilda Doolittle), or Marianne Moore? That many students probably recognize only a few of these names illustrates the marginalization of many women writers by literary history, though not necessarily by the reading public at the time these women wrote. Similarly, in most Hollywood films, even today, the camera eye (the point of view from which the film is shot) is male: the female characters, not male, are the objects gazed on by the camera and often eroticized as if a male eye were viewing them, as if the point of view of the “universal” moviegoer were male.

这种“认知习惯”造成的危害，或许最令人不寒而栗的例子就体现在现代医学领域。在现代医学中，许多男女通用的药物，往往只在男性受试者身上进行过测试。换句话说，在药物上市前，为了确定其安全性，实验室测试中经常会使用男性受试者的反应来收集药物疗效和潜在副作用的统计数据。结果，女性可能会出现意想不到的副作用，而男性受试者却不受影响。医学科学家怎么可能没有预料到这个问题呢？毫无疑问，将男性经验视为普遍适用的文化习惯在其中扮演了重要角色。

Perhaps the most chilling example of the damaging effects of this “habit of seeing” is found in the world of modern medicine, where drugs prescribed for both sexes often have been tested on male subjects only. In other words, in laboratory tests to determine the safety of prescription drugs before marketing them, men’s responses frequently have been used to gather statistical data on the medications’ effectiveness and possible side effects. As a result, women may experience unexpected side effects while male users are unaffected. How could medical scientists not have anticipated this problem? Surely, the cultural habit of seeing male experience as universal played a role.

传统性别角色

Traditional gender roles

我之所以先列举以上例子，是因为我认为它们揭示了我们所有人（包括我自己）在哪些方面被潜移默化地影响着（或视而不见）。我自认为是一个正在摆脱父权制束缚的女性。我所说的“父权制女性” ，当然是指那些内化了父权制规范和价值观的女性。简而言之，父权制可以定义为任何通过推崇传统性别角色来赋予男性特权的文化。传统的性别角色将男性塑造为理性、强大、有保护欲且果断；将女性塑造为感性（非理性）、柔弱、善于照顾且顺从。这些性别角色曾被非常成功地用来为各种不平等现象辩护，而这些不平等现象至今仍然存在，例如：女性被剥夺了平等获得领导和决策职位的机会（无论是在家庭、政治、学术界还是企业界）；男性从事同样的工作却比女性获得更高的工资（即便女性能够获得这些工作）；以及让女性相信她们不适合从事数学和工程等领域的工作。如今许多人认为，这种不平等现象已成为过去，因为随着时间的推移，各国纷纷通过反歧视法律，努力保障女性同工同酬。然而，这些法律很容易被削弱，甚至完全被规避。例如，雇主只需给女性不同的职位名称，就可以支付更少的工资，即使她们从事与男性相同的工作（或比男性付出更多劳动）。因此，以美国为例，女性的平均收入仍然只有男性收入的55%到77%——具体比例取决于她们的种族、年龄和居住地。在那些根本没有此类法律的国家，女性劳动者的收入差距自然更大。

I offer the above examples up front because I think they show some of the ways in which all of us have been programmed to see (or to be blind), myself included. I consider myself a recovering patriarchal woman. By patriarchal woman I mean, of course, a woman who has internalized the norms and values of patriarchy, which can be defined, in short, as any culture that privileges men by promoting traditional gender roles. Traditional gender roles cast men as rational, strong, protective, and decisive; they cast women as emotional (irrational), weak, nurturing, and submissive.
