These gender roles have been used very successfully to justify inequities, which still occur today, such as excluding women from equal access to leadership and decision-making positions (in the family as well as in politics, academia, and the corporate world), paying men higher wages than women for doing the same job (if women are even able to obtain the job), and convincing women that they are not fit for careers in such areas as mathematics and engineering. Many people today believe such inequities are a thing of the past because, over time, antidiscriminatory laws have been passed in an effort to guarantee women equal pay for equal work. However, these laws can be readily undermined, if not completely sidestepped. For example, an employer can pay a woman less for performing the same work as a man (or for doing more work than a man) simply by giving her a different job title. So women working in the United States, for instance, still are paid, on average, between 55 and 77 cents – depending on their ethnicity, age, and geographic location – for every dollar earned by men. In countries where such laws don’t exist at all, women workers, of course, generally suffer even greater disparity.1

因此，父权制从定义上来说就是性别歧视，这意味着它宣扬女性天生不如男性的观念。这种认为女性天生低人一等的观念是一种所谓的生物本质主义，因为它基于两性之间的生物差异，而这些差异被认为是男性和女性永恒不变的本质的一部分。一个鲜明的例子是“歇斯底里症” （hysteria）一词，它源于希腊语中表示子宫的词（hystera），指的是被认为女性特有的心理障碍，其特征是情绪过度、极度非理性。行为方面，女权主义者并不否认男女之间的生物学差异；事实上，许多女权主义者甚至赞赏这些差异。但她们并不认为诸如体型、外形和身体化学成分等差异会使男性天生优于女性：例如，更聪明、更理性、更勇敢或更善于领导。因此，许多英美女权主义学者区分了“性别”（sex）和“性别认同”（gender）这两个词。“性别认同”指的是我们生理上的性别，即女性或男性；而“性别认同”指的是我们文化建构的女性化或男性化。换句话说，女性并非生来就是女性，男性也并非生来就是男性。相反，这些性别类别是由社会建构的，因此这种性别观正是所谓的社会建构主义的例证。

Patriarchy is thus, by definition, sexist, which means it promotes the belief that women are innately inferior to men. This belief in the inborn inferiority of women is a form of what is called biological essentialism because it is based on biological differences between the sexes that are considered part of our unchanging essence as men and women. A striking illustration is the word hysteria, which derives from the Greek word for womb (hystera) and refers to psychological disorders deemed peculiar to women and characterized by overemotional, extremely irrational behavior. Feminists don’t deny the biological differences between men and women; in fact, many feminists celebrate those differences. But they don’t agree that such differences as physical size, shape, and body chemistry make men naturally superior to women: for example, more intelligent, more logical, more courageous, or better leaders. Much Anglo-American feminism therefore distinguishes between the word sex, which refers to our biological constitution as female or male, and the word gender, which refers to our cultural programming as feminine or masculine. In other words, women are not born feminine, and men are not born masculine. Rather, these gender categories are constructed by society, which is why this view of gender is an example of what has come to be called social constructionism.

女权主义者指出，男性优于女性的观念被用来为男性垄断经济、政治和社会权力辩护并维持这种垄断地位，换句话说，就是通过剥夺女性获得经济、政治和社会权力的教育和职业途径来使她们处于弱势地位。也就是说，女性在父权社会中长期处于的劣势地位是文化而非生物因素造成的。例如，认为女性比男性更容易患歇斯底里症，这是一种父权制的假设，而非事实。但由于歇斯底里症被定义为女性问题，男性的歇斯底里行为不会被诊断为歇斯底里症。相反，它会被忽视，或者被赋予另一个危害性较小的名称，例如“脾气暴躁”。当然，并非所有男人都接受父权制思想，而那些不接受父权制思想的男人——例如，那些不相信男人天生肌肉更强壮，就意味着他们拥有其他任何自然优势的男人——常常被信奉父权制的男人和女人嘲笑为软弱无能、缺乏男子气概，仿佛成为男人的唯一途径就是成为信奉父权制的男人。

The belief that men are superior to women has been used, feminists have observed, to justify and maintain the male monopoly of positions of economic, political, and social power, in other words, to keep women powerless by denying them the educational and occupational means of acquiring economic, political, and social power. That is, the inferior position long occupied by women in patriarchal society has been culturally, not biologically, produced. For example, it is a patriarchal assumption, rather than a fact, that more women than men suffer from hysteria. But because it has been defined as a female problem, hysterical behavior in men won’t be diagnosed as such. Instead, it will be ignored or given another, less damaging name, for example, shortness of temper. Of course, not all men accept patriarchal ideology, and those who don’t – those who don’t believe, for example, that because men generally have been endowed by nature with stronger muscles, they have been endowed with any other natural superiority – are often derided, by both patriarchal men and women, as weak and unmanly, as if the only way to be a man were to be a patriarchal man.

我称自己为“父权制女性”，因为我和大多数男性女性一样，从小就被社会观念束缚，看不到传统性别角色对女性的压迫。我说我正在“康复”，是因为我学会了识别并反抗这种观念。对我而言，这种识别和反抗始终需要付出努力——我仍在“康复”而非“康复”，这不仅是因为我多年前就内化了父权制观念，还因为这种观念仍在我的生活中持续发挥作用：在电影、电视节目、书籍、杂志和广告中，也体现在销售人员的态度上——他们认为我连简单的机器都学不会操作；体现在维修技师的态度上——他们认为我不会察觉他们的工作是否粗糙；体现在男司机的态度上——他们认为我会对从路过车辆中喊出的性暗示感到受宠若惊（或者更糟的是，他们根本不考虑我的感受；或者更糟糕的是，他们希望我感到害怕，这样他们就能获得权力感）。这里的重点很简单：父权制不断施加各种力量来削弱女性的自信和果断，然后指出女性缺乏这些品质，以此证明女性天生就应该谦逊顺从，因此这种顺从是正确的。

I call myself a patriarchal woman because I was socially programmed, as are most women and men, not to see the ways in which women are oppressed by traditional gender roles. I say that I’m recovering because I learned to recognize and resist that programming. For me, such recognition and resistance will always require effort – I’m recovering rather than recovered – not just because I internalized patriarchal programming years ago but because that program continues to assert itself in my world: in movies, television shows, books, magazines, and advertisements as well as in the attitudes of salespeople who think I can’t learn to operate a simple machine, repair technicians who assume I won’t know if they’ve done a shoddy job, and male drivers who believe I’m flattered by sexual offers shouted from passing cars (or, worse, who don’t give a moment’s thought to how I might feel or, worse yet, who hope I feel intimidated so that they can feel powerful). The point here is fairly simple: patriarchy continually exerts forces that undermine women’s self-confidence and assertiveness, then points to the absence of these qualities as proof that women are naturally, and therefore correctly, self-effacing and submissive.

举一个类似的父权制思维的例子：小女孩在早期教育阶段就被告知（有些女孩至今仍被灌输）她们学不好数学。即使父母、老师或朋友没有明确地用语言告诉她们，她们也会通过成人和同伴的肢体语言、语气和面部表情感受到这一点。由于人们常常认为小女孩学不好数学，而且这种缺陷无关紧要，因为她们中的大多数人在以后的生活中都不需要用到数学，所以老师不会像布置数学作业那样频繁地让女孩做题。事实上，女孩数学不好反而常常会得到“奖励”：她们会因为展现女性特质而获得同情、溺爱和其他一些诱人却又令人沮丧的“好处”。如果女孩克服这些障碍，最终数学成绩优异，她们就会被视为例外（在孩子看来，这通常意味着她们被视为“怪胎”）。简而言之，女孩从小就被灌输了“失败”的观念。父权制思维会以女孩数学成绩较低以及她们未能成为数学专业学生为由，证明她们在生物学上不适合学习数学。鉴于数学与逻辑的密切联系，这又暗示女性的逻辑能力不如男性。换句话说，父权制制造了这种失败，并以此来为其对女性的固有偏见辩护。

To cite a similar example of patriarchal programming, little girls have been (and some still are) told early in their educational careers that they can’t do math. If not told so explicitly in words (by parents, teachers, or friends), they are told so by the body language, tone of voice, and facial expression of adults and peers. Because it is often assumed that little girls can’t do math and, furthermore, that this deficiency doesn’t really matter because most of them won’t need math in later life, girls are not called on by the teacher as frequently as boys to perform mathematical operations. In fact, girls are often “rewarded” for failing at math: they receive ready sympathy, coddling, and other debilitating though enticing payoffs for being feminine. If girls manage to do well in math despite these obstacles, they are considered exceptions to the rule (which, from a child’s point of view, usually means they are considered “freaks”). In short, girls are programmed to fail. Then the patriarchal mind-set points to girls’ lower test scores in math and their failure to become math majors as proof that they are biologically ill-suited to mathematical studies, which, given the close relationship between math and logic, suggests that females are less logical than males. In other words, patriarchy creates the failure that it then uses to justify its assumptions about women.

因为我曾深受父权制观念的影响，所以我深知父权制性别角色对男性和女性都具有破坏性。例如，传统的性别角色要求男性坚强（体魄强健、情感坚忍），因此他们不应该哭泣，因为哭泣被视为软弱的表现，表明一个人被情绪所控制。出于类似的原因，男性表现出恐惧或痛苦，或者表达对其他男性的同情，都被认为是不男子气概的表现。表达对其他男性的同情（或任何爱意）尤其禁忌，因为父权制认为只有最沉默寡言、坚忍克己（或喧闹稚气）的男性情谊才不带有同性恋的意味。此外，男性不允许在任何尝试中失败，因为任何领域的失败都意味着男性尊严的丧失。

Because I’m a recovering patriarchal woman, I am also very aware of the ways in which patriarchal gender roles are destructive for men as well as for women. For example, because traditional gender roles dictate that men are supposed to be strong (physically powerful and emotionally stoic), they are not supposed to cry because crying is considered a sign of weakness, a sign that one has been overpowered by one’s emotions. For similar reasons, it is considered unmanly for men to show fear or pain or to express their sympathy for other men. Expressing sympathy (or any loving feeling) for other men is especially taboo because patriarchy assumes that only the most mute and stoic (or boisterous and boyish) forms of male bonding are free of homosexual overtones. In addition, men are not permitted to fail at anything they try because failure in any domain implies failure in one’s manhood.

无法为家庭提供足够的经济支持被认为是男人所能经历的最屈辱的失败，因为这意味着他辜负了作为养家糊口者的生物本能。在当今美国，男性在经济上取得成功的压力极大，因为社会对男性成功的期望不断提高：要想在这个时代成为一个“真正的”男人，就必须拥有比父亲、兄弟姐妹和朋友更昂贵的房子和车子，并且必须把孩子送进更昂贵的学校。如果男性无法实现当代美国社会为他们设定的不切实际的经济目标，那么他们就必须在其他方面展现自己的男子气概：他们必须性生活最活跃（或者让别人相信他们性生活最活跃），或者酒量最大，或者最容易发怒。在这种背景下，愤怒和其他暴力情绪成为男性唯一被允许甚至被鼓励的情绪也就不足为奇了，因为愤怒是一种……这是一种非常有效的屏蔽恐惧和痛苦的方法，而恐惧和痛苦是不被允许的，愤怒通常会产生与父权制男性气质相关的攻击性行为。

Failure to provide adequate economic support for one’s family is considered the most humiliating failure a man can experience because it means that he has failed at what is considered his biological role as provider. The imperative for men to succeed economically has become an extremely pressurized situation in contemporary America because the degree of success men are expected to achieve keeps increasing: to be a “real” man in this day and age one must have a more expensive house and car than one’s father, siblings, and friends, and one must send one’s children to a more expensive school. If men can’t achieve the unrealistic economic goals set for them in contemporary America, then they must increase the signs of their manhood in some other area: they must be the most sexually active (or make others believe that they are) or be able to hold the most liquor or display the most anger. It is not surprising, in this context, that anger and other violent emotions are the only emotions permitted, even encouraged, in men, for anger is a very effective means of blocking out fear and pain, which are not permitted, and anger usually produces the kind of aggressive behaviors associated with patriarchal manhood.

我在此提及男性思维定式，有两个原因，而这两个原因都反映了我个人的女权主义偏见。我希望阅读本章的男性读者能够从女权主义中看到，他们不仅能从中了解女性，还能从中了解自身。我也希望所有读者，无论男女，都能明白，即便我们自认为在谈论男性，实际上也在谈论女性，因为在父权制社会中，所有与男性相关的事物通常都隐含着对女性的某种（通常是负面的）评价。例如，值得注意的是，前两段中描述的所有行为——男性被禁止的行为——都被认为是“女性化的”，也就是说，低人一等，有损男性尊严。哭泣的男人，甚至小男孩，都会被称作“娘娘腔”。“娘娘腔”听起来很像“姐妹”，它的意思是“胆小”或“女性化”，而这两个词在这个语境中是同义词。显然，对男性而言，最具破坏性的语言攻击之一就是被比作女性。因此，在父权文化中，做一个“真正的”男人意味着要鄙视女性特质。同性恋至少在美国男性眼中被列入了“女性化”行为的范畴，因为尽管有很多非常阳刚的同性恋男性，但美国人对同性恋男性的刻板印象却极其女性化。这种现象意味着，每当父权制想要贬低某种行为时，它就会将其描绘成女性化的。同样重要的是，父权制对女性气质的理解——与柔弱、谦逊和胆怯联系在一起——在现实世界中剥夺了女性的权力：在事业上取得成功、拥有超凡的智慧、赚取丰厚的收入、拥有鲜明的观点、拥有旺盛的食欲（对任何事物都如此）、或者维护自身权益，都不是女性化的特质。

I refer to male programming, at this point, for two reasons, both of which reflect my personal feminist biases. I want the men reading this chapter to see in feminism the potential for learning a good deal about themselves as well as about women. And I want readers of both sexes to see that, even when we think we’re talking about men, we’re also talking about women because, in a patriarchy, everything that concerns men usually implies something (usually negative) about women. For example, it is important to note that all the behaviors described in the preceding two paragraphs – behaviors forbidden to men – are considered “womanish,” that is, inferior, beneath the dignity of manhood. Men, and even little boys, who cry are called “sissies.” Sissy sounds very much like sister, and it means “cowardly” or “feminine,” two words that, in this context, are synonyms. Clearly, one of the most devastating verbal attacks to which a man can be subjected is to be compared to a woman. Thus, being a “real” man in patriarchal culture requires that one hold feminine qualities in contempt. Homosexuality is included on the list of “feminine” behaviors, at least for American men, because despite the plentiful example of very masculine homosexual men, the American stereotype of the homosexual male is an extremely feminine one. This phenomenon implies that whenever patriarchy wants to undermine a behavior, it portrays that behavior as feminine. It is important to note, too, that the patriarchal concept of femininity – which is linked to frailty, modesty, and timidity – disempowers women in the real world: it is not feminine to succeed in business, to be extremely intelligent, to earn big bucks, to have strong opinions, to have a healthy appetite (for anything), or to assert one’s rights.

为了简要说明父权制性别角色对男女双方的负面影响，不妨以“灰姑娘”的故事为例。女权主义者早已意识到，父权制强加给年轻女孩的灰姑娘形象是一种有害的角色，因为它将女性气质等同于顺从，鼓励女性忍受家庭虐待，耐心等待男性的拯救，并将婚姻视为“正确”行为的唯一回报。同样，白马王子的角色——要求男性成为富有的拯救者，负责让女性“从此幸福快乐地生活在一起”——对男性而言也是一种有害的角色，因为它强化了一种观念，即男性必须是不知疲倦的超级供养者，没有情感需求。

To briefly illustrate the debilitating effects of patriarchal gender roles on both women and men, consider the story of “Cinderella.” Feminists have long been aware that the role of Cinderella, which patriarchy imposes on the imagination of young girls, is a destructive role because it equates femininity with submission, encouraging women to tolerate familial abuse, wait patiently to be rescued by a man, and view marriage as the only desirable reward for “right” conduct. By the same token, however, the role of Prince Charming – which requires men to be wealthy rescuers responsible for making their women happy “ever after” – is a destructive role for men because it promotes the belief that men must be unflagging superproviders without emotional needs.

不幸的是，对童话故事进行女性主义批判的想法一直受到社会评论家的嘲讽。他们以荒谬幽默且自诩政治正确的方式解读经典童话，以此来向我们展示女权主义者和其他“不满分子”会把我们引向何等荒谬的极端。然而，事实上，对童话故事的女性主义解读可以提供一种绝佳的途径，来阐明父权制意识形态如何影响我们习以为常的认知。即使是最天真的行为，也难免带有偏见。例如，想想那些经久不衰的童话故事，比如《白雪公主和七个小矮人》、《睡美人》，当然还有《灰姑娘》。在这三个故事中，一位美丽善良的少女（因为在人们眼中，女性必须美丽、善良、年轻才能赢得浪漫的爱慕）被一位英俊潇洒的年轻人从困境中解救出来（因为她无力自救），然后被带走结婚，从此过上了幸福的生活。故事的情节暗示着，嫁给合适的男人是幸福的保证，也是一位正直少女应得的回报。在这三个故事中，女性主角都被刻板地分为两类：要么是“好女孩”（温柔、顺从、纯洁、天使般），要么是“坏女孩”（暴力、好斗、世故、可怕）。这些刻画暗示，如果女性不接受父权制赋予的性别角色，那么她唯一的选择就是成为怪物。在这三个故事中，“坏女孩”——《白雪公主》中的邪恶皇后、《睡美人》中的邪恶仙女以及《灰姑娘》中的邪恶继母和继姐——都虚荣、小气、嫉妒，她们因为不如主角美丽而恼怒，或者像邪恶仙女那样，因为没有被邀请参加皇家庆典而恼怒。这些动机暗示，即使女性作恶，她们的诉求也显得微不足道。在其中两个故事里，年轻的少女被心仪之人的强吻从沉睡中唤醒（毕竟，这吻赋予了她生命）。这样的结局暗示，符合父权制规范的年轻女性在性方面处于休眠状态，直到被声称拥有她的男人“唤醒”。我们可以进一步分析这些故事，也可以分析更多故事，但这里的重点是要了解父权制意识形态的普遍性，以及它如何在我们不知情或未经我们同意的情况下对我们进行洗脑。

Unfortunately, the notion of a feminist critique of fairy tales has been the target of mockery by social commentators who offer absurdly humorous and what they claim are politically correct versions of classic fairy tales in order to show us the allegedly ridiculous extremes to which feminists and other “malcontents” would lead us. However, feminist readings of fairy tales can, in fact, provide a wonderful means for illustrating the ways in which patriarchal ideology informs what appear to be even the most innocent of our activities. Consider, for example, the similarities among the ever popular “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs,” “Sleeping Beauty,” and, of course, “Cinderella.” In all three tales, a beautiful, sweet young girl (for females must be beautiful, sweet, and young if they are to be worthy of romantic admiration) is rescued (for she is incapable of rescuing herself) from a dire situation by a dashing young man who carries her off to marry him and live happily ever after. The plot thus implies that marriage to the right man is a guarantee of happiness and the proper reward for a right-minded young woman. In all three tales, the main female characters are stereotyped as either “good girls” (gentle, submissive, virginal, angelic) or “bad girls” (violent, aggressive, worldly, monstrous). These characterizations imply that if a woman does not accept her patriarchal gender role, then the only role left her is that of a monster. In all three tales, the “bad girls” – the wicked queen in “Snow White,” the wicked fairy in “Sleeping Beauty,” and the wicked stepmother and stepsisters in “Cinderella” – are also vain, petty, and jealous, infuriated because they are not as beautiful as the main character or, in the case of the wicked fairy, because she wasn’t invited to a royal celebration. Such motivations imply that even when women are evil, their concerns are trivial. In two of the stories, the young maiden is awakened from a deathlike slumber by the potent (after all, it brings her to life) kiss of the would-be lover. This ending implies that the proper patriarchal young woman is sexually dormant until “awakened” by the man who claims her. We could analyze these tales further, and we could analyze additional tales, but the point here is to see how pervasive patriarchal ideology is and how it can program us without our knowledge or consent.

我在上文中提到了“好女孩”和“坏女孩”，这个概念值得我们更多关注，因为它体现了性别歧视意识形态持续影响我们的另一种方式。正如我们前面看到的，父权制意识形态认为女性只有两种身份：如果她接受传统的性别角色并遵守父权制规则，她就是“好女孩”；如果她不这样做，她就是“坏女孩”。这两种角色——也被称为“圣母”和“妓女”或“天使”和“泼妇”——仅仅从女性与父权秩序的关系来定义她们。当然，“好女孩”和“坏女孩”的具体定义会随着时代和地域的不同而有所变化。但最终决定性的因素是父权制，因为这两种角色都是父权制男性欲望的投射：例如，渴望拥有适合做妻子和母亲的“有价值”的女性，渴望控制女性的性欲以确保男性的性欲不受任何威胁，以及渴望在所有经济事务中占据主导地位。父权制意识形态完美地满足了最后一种欲望，它认为某些类型的工作不适合“好女孩”。这种意识形态迫使维多利亚时代英国的许多女作家使用男性笔名发表作品，并要求大西洋两岸的女作家都必须调整自己的艺术以迎合父权制的期望，否则将面临后果（就像凯特·肖邦在二十世纪初所做的那样）。由于其女权主义内容，这部作品被埋没，直到 20 世纪 60 年代末才被女权主义者重新发现并再版。

I refer in the above paragraph to “good girls” and “bad girls,” and this concept deserves more attention because it’s another way in which sexist ideology continues to influence us. As we saw above, patriarchal ideology suggests that there are only two identities a woman can have. If she accepts her traditional gender role and obeys the patriarchal rules, she’s a “good girl”; if she doesn’t, she’s a “bad girl.” These two roles – also referred to as “madonna” and “whore” or “angel” and “bitch” – view women only in terms of how they relate to the patriarchal order. Of course, how “good girls” and “bad girls” are specifically defined will alter somewhat according to the time and place in which they live. But it is patriarchy that will do the defining because both roles are projections of patriarchal male desire: for example, the desire to own “valuable” women suited to be wives and mothers, the desire to control women’s sexuality so that men’s sexuality cannot be threatened in any way, and the desire to dominate in all financial matters. This last desire is well served by the patriarchal ideology that deems certain kinds of work improper for “good girls,” an ideology that forced many women writers in Victorian England to publish their work under male pseudonyms and that required women writers on both sides of the Atlantic to accommodate their art to patriarchal expectations or face the consequences (as Kate Chopin did at the turn of the twentieth century when her work was buried due to its feminist content, not to be reprinted until it was rediscovered by feminists in the late 1960s).

在20世纪50年代盛行的父权制意识形态（其某些形式至今仍然存在）中，“坏女孩”以某种方式违反了父权制的性规范：她们外表或行为性感奔放，或者拥有多个性伴侣。男人会和“坏女孩”上床，但不会娶她们。“坏女孩”被利用后便被抛弃，因为她们不配拥有更好的，她们自己可能也不奢望更好的。她们不够好，不配拥有男人的姓氏或合法的子女。只有顺从的“好女孩”才配扮演这样的角色。“好女孩”的行为会得到父权文化的奖赏，被捧上神坛。她被赋予了所有与父权制女性气质和家庭主妇形象相关的美德：谦逊、低调、自我牺牲、善于照顾。她没有自己的需求，因为她通过服侍家庭而获得完全的满足。她有时会为他人的困境感到难过，也常常为她照顾的人担忧——但她从不生气。在维多利亚时代的英国，她堪称“家中的天使”。她把家打造成丈夫的避风港，让他能在重返职场、应对日常挑战之前，在这里获得精神上的慰藉；也为孩子们营造了一个温馨的家，让他们在这里接受必要的道德引导，最终在成人世界中承担起各自的传统角色。

According to a patriarchal ideology in full force through the 1950s, versions of which are still with us today, “bad girls” violate patriarchal sexual norms in some way: they’re sexually forward in appearance or behavior, or they have multiple sexual partners. Men sleep with “bad girls,” but they don’t marry them. “Bad girls” are used and then discarded because they don’t deserve better, and they probably don’t even expect better. They’re not good enough to bear a man’s name or his legitimate children. That role is appropriate only for a properly submissive “good girl.” The “good girl” is rewarded for her behavior by being placed on a pedestal by patriarchal culture. To her are attributed all the virtues associated with patriarchal femininity and domesticity: she’s modest, unassuming, self-sacrificing, and nurturing. She has no needs of her own, for she is completely satisfied by serving her family. At times, she may be sad about the problems of others, and she frequently worries about those in her care – but she is never angry. In Victorian culture in England she was the “angel in the house.” She made the home a safe haven for her husband, where he could spiritually fortify himself before resuming the daily struggles of the workplace, and for her children, where they could receive the moral guidance needed to eventually assume their own traditional roles in the adult world.

被捧上神坛有什么错？首先，神坛狭小，女性除了履行既定角色之外几乎没有其他活动空间。例如，为了保住维多利亚时代的“好女孩”地位，她们必须对性行为保持冷漠，除非是为了合法生育，因为当时人们认为女性有性欲是不自然的。事实上，“好”女人甚至应该对性感到恐惧或厌恶。其次，神坛摇摇欲坠。人很容易从神坛上跌落，而一旦跌落，女性往往会受到惩罚。往好了说，她会因为自己的不足或“不自然”而自责；往坏了说，她会遭受来自社区或丈夫的体罚，这种体罚直到不久前还受到法律和习俗的鼓励，而如今，一个效率低下或沆瀣一气的司法系统仍然常常对此默许纵容。值得注意的是，父权制在这种语境下将“坏女孩”和“好女孩”都物化了。也就是说，无论女性扮演何种角色，父权制都将她们视为物品：在父权制看来，女性的存在就是为了被利用，而无需考虑她们自身的视角、感受或意见。毕竟，从父权制的角度来看，女性的视角、感受和意见只有在符合父权制的价值观时才重要。

What’s wrong with being placed on a pedestal? For one thing, pedestals are small and leave a woman very little room to do anything but fulfill the prescribed role. For example, to remain on her Victorian pedestal, the “good girl” had to remain uninterested in sexual activity, except for the purpose of legitimate procreation, because it was believed unnatural for women to have sexual desire. In fact, “good” women were expected to find sex frightening or disgusting. For another thing, pedestals are shaky. One can easily fall off a pedestal, and when a woman does, she is often punished. At best, she suffers self-recrimination for her inadequacy or “unnaturalness.” At worst, she suffers physical punishment from the community or from her husband, which until relatively recently was encouraged by law and custom and which is still too often tacitly condoned by an ineffectual or complicit justice system. It is interesting to note, in this context, that patriarchy objectifies both “bad girls” and “good girls.” That is, patriarchy treats women, whatever their role, like objects: like objects, women exist, according to patriarchy, to be used without consideration of their own perspectives, feelings, or opinions. After all, from a patriarchal standpoint, women’s perspectives, feelings, and opinions don’t count unless they conform to those of patriarchy.

在当今美国向上流动的中产阶级文化中，备受推崇的女性是那些成功兼顾事业和家庭的女性。这意味着她们在办公室和餐桌旁都光彩照人，下班后也从不疲惫到无暇准备晚餐、打扫房屋、照顾孩子的一切需求，并且取悦他人。她丈夫还在床上。换句话说，即使现代女性进入了男性主导的职场，父权制的性别角色也并未消失，即便其中一些女性现在从事着过去传统上由男性担任的工作。因为很多女性在家中仍然受到父权制性别角色的束缚，她们现在除了要实现职业目标之外，还必须履行这些家庭职责。

In upwardly mobile, middle-class American culture today, the woman on the pedestal is the woman who successfully juggles a career and a family, which means she looks great at the office and over the breakfast table, and she’s never too tired after work to fix dinner, clean house, attend to all her children’s needs, and please her husband in bed. In other words, patriarchal gender roles have not been eliminated by modern women’s entrance into the male-dominated workplace, even if some of those women now hold what used to be traditionally male jobs. For many of those same women are still bound by patriarchal gender roles in the home, which they must now fulfill in addition to their career goals.

此外，对女性性行为的压抑态度至今仍体现在我们的语言中。例如，我们用贬义词“荡妇”（slut）来形容与多名男性发生性关系的女性，而用褒义词“种马” （stud）来形容与多名女性发生性关系的男性。尽管自19世纪以来女性的时尚发生了翻天覆地的变化，但最具“女性气质”的服装仍然强化着父权制意识形态。例如，19世纪女性穿着的极度紧身的束身衣使她们无法获得足够的氧气进行体育活动，也无法体验情感，否则就会出现“喘息”——即呼吸急促或轻微晕厥，这被认为是女性特有的症状，证明女性过于脆弱和情绪化，无法参与男性主导的世界。类似地，当今女性最具“女性气质”的服装风格之一是紧身裙和高跟鞋，这创造了一种“女性化”的步态（同时又限制了奔跑），这在象征意义上既类似于十九世纪女性服装对身体能力的限制，也类似于这种服装所允许男性对女性身体的性侵犯。

Furthermore, the persistence of repressive attitudes toward women’s sexuality is still visible in our language today. For example, we use the negative word slut to describe a woman who sleeps with a number of men while we use the positive word stud to describe a man who sleeps with a number of women. And though women’s fashions have radically changed since the nineteenth century, the most “feminine” clothing still promotes patriarchal ideology. For example, the extremely tight corsets worn by nineteenth-century women prevented them from getting enough oxygen to be physically active or to experience emotion without getting “the vapors”: shortness of breath or slight fits of fainting, which were considered very feminine and proved that women were too fragile and emotional to participate in a man’s world. Analogously, one of the most “feminine” styles of clothing for today’s woman is the tight skirt and high heels, which create a kind of “feminine” walk (while precluding running) symbolically akin both to the restrained physical capability imposed by nineteenth-century women’s clothing and to the male sexual access to women’s bodies such attire allows.

女权主义基本原则概述

A summary of feminist premises

到目前为止，我们已经探讨了父权制意识形态如何运作，使女性和男性固守传统的性别角色，从而维护男性主导地位。所有女权主义者都认同父权制意识形态的这种运作方式，即便她们在其他问题上存在分歧。事实上，大多数女权主义者都持有几个重要的共同假设，这些假设可以概括如下。

So far, we’ve examined how patriarchal ideology works to keep women and men in traditional gender roles and thereby maintain male dominance. That patriarchal ideology functions in this way is a belief shared by all feminists even if they disagree about other issues. In fact, most feminists share several important assumptions, which might be summarized as follows.

1父权制在经济、政治、社会和心理上压迫女性；父权制意识形态是维持这种压迫的主要手段。

1 Women are oppressed by patriarchy economically, politically, socially, and psychologically; patriarchal ideology is the primary means by which they are kept so.

2在父权制盛行的每一个领域，女性都是他者：她被物化和边缘化，仅仅因为她与男性规范和价值观的不同而被定义，仅仅因为她（据称）缺乏什么而男性（据称）拥有什么而被定义。

2 In every domain where patriarchy reigns, woman is other: she is objectified and marginalized, defined only by her difference from male norms and values, defined by what she (allegedly) lacks and that men (allegedly) have.

3整个西方（盎格鲁-欧洲）文明都深深植根于父权制意识形态，例如，我们可以在希腊罗马文学和神话中看到众多父权制女性形象和女性怪物；圣经中对夏娃的父权制解读，认为她是世间罪恶和死亡的起源；传统西方哲学将女性描绘成非理性生物；以及对以男性为中心的男性思维的依赖。（其词汇、逻辑规则和客观知识标准均受教育、政治、法律和商业机构的影响。）正如我们之前所见，即使是西方伟大文学经典（包括传统童话故事）的形成，也是父权制意识形态的产物。

3 All of Western (Anglo-European) civilization is deeply rooted in patriarchal ideology, as we see, for example, in the numerous patriarchal women and female monsters of Greek and Roman literature and mythology; the patriarchal interpretation of the biblical Eve as the origin of sin and death in the world; the representation of woman as a nonrational creature by traditional Western philosophy; and the reliance on phallogocentric thinking (thinking that is male oriented in its vocabulary, rules of logic, and criteria for what is considered objective knowledge) by educational, political, legal, and business institutions. As we saw earlier, even the development of the Western canon of great literature, including traditional fairy tales, was a product of patriarchal ideology.

4生物学决定了我们的生理性别（男性或女性），而文化决定了我们的性别认同（男性化或女性化）。也就是说，至少对大多数英语国家的女权主义者而言，“性别”一词指的并非我们的生理构造，而是我们作为社会塑造的男性和女性的行为。我“像个女人一样”（例如，顺从）的行为并非出于本性，而是因为我被教导要这样做。事实上，所有我们与男性化和女性化行为联系起来的特征都是后天习得的，而非与生俱来的。

4 While biology determines our sex (male or female), culture determines our gender (masculine or feminine). That is, at least for most English-speaking feminists, the word gender refers not to our anatomy but to our behavior as socially programmed men and women. I behave “like a woman” (for example, submissively) not because it is natural for me to do so but because I was taught to do so. In fact, all the traits we associate with masculine and feminine behavior are learned, not inborn.

5所有女权主义活动，包括女权主义理论和文学批评，其最终目标都是通过促进女性平等来改变世界。因此，所有女权主义活动都可以被视为一种行动主义，尽管“行动主义”一词通常用于指那些通过政治活动直接推动社会变革的女权主义活动，例如公众示威、抵制、选民教育和登记、为强奸受害者提供热线以及为受虐妇女提供庇护所等等。尽管女权主义者经常被错误地描绘成与“家庭价值观”对立，但他们仍然在为改善家庭政策而奋斗，例如为母亲和儿童提供营养和医疗保健；育儿假；以及高质量且价格合理的日托服务。

5 All feminist activity, including feminist theory and literary criticism, has as its ultimate goal to change the world by promoting women’s equality. Thus, all feminist activity can be seen as a form of activism, although the word is usually applied to feminist activity that directly promotes social change through political activity such as public demonstrations, boycotts, voter education and registration, the provision of hotlines for rape victims and shelters for abused women, and the like. Although frequently falsely portrayed in opposition to “family values,” feminists continue to lead the struggle for better family policies such as nutrition and health care for mothers and children; parental leave; and high-quality, affordable day care.

6无论我们是否意识到这些问题，性别问题都影响着人类生产和体验的各个方面，包括文学的生产和体验。

6 Gender issues play a part in every aspect of human production and experience, including the production and experience of literature, whether we are consciously aware of these issues or not.

当然，上述假设彼此关联、相互重叠，它们共同表明，父权制意识形态对我们的思考方式、言语表达、自我认知以及对世界的观察都具有根深蒂固的普遍影响。父权制意识形态的普遍性给女性主义理论提出了一些重要问题。例如，如果父权制意识形态对我们的身份认同和生活体验影响如此之大，我们又该如何超越它？如果我们的思维模式和语言都带有父权制色彩，我们又该如何以不同的方式思考或表达？换言之，如果我们存在的本质是父权制的，我们又该如何摆脱父权制的影响？

Of course, the assumptions listed above are related, overlapping ideas, and, together, they imply that patriarchal ideology has a pervasive, deeply rooted influence on the way we think, speak, see ourselves, and view the world in which we live. The pervasiveness of patriarchal ideology raises some important questions for feminist theory. For example, if patriarchal ideology influences our identity and experience so strongly, how can we ever get beyond it? If our modes of thinking and our language are patriarchal, how can we ever think or speak differently? In other words, if the fabric of our existence is patriarchal, how can we ever become nonpatriarchal?

超越父权制

Getting beyond patriarchy

女权主义者长期以来一直苦苦思索如何摆脱父权制思维的束缚，并提出了许多不同的解决方案。例如，应对我们明显陷入父权制意识形态陷阱的一种方法是，考虑这样一种可能性：没有任何一种意识形态能够成功地完全控制所有人。时间。每一种意识形态都存在自相矛盾之处，存在逻辑谬误，这些谬误使我们能够理解其运作方式并削弱其影响。例如，玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特在1792年撰写《女权辩护》时反抗父权制意识形态；弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫在1929年撰写《一间自己的房间》时反抗父权制意识形态；西蒙娜·德·波伏娃在1949年撰写《第二性》时反抗父权制意识形态；而如今，女权主义理论家们仍在继续反抗父权制意识形态。或许，我们难以从理论上摆脱父权制意识形态的原因在于，我们常常将自身身处其中的状态视为一种非此即彼的选择：如果我们不能完全摆脱父权制，那么我们就一定完全被它所塑造。我认为，将我们与父权制意识形态的关系视为一种动态情境或许更有意义：我们必须不断努力理解并抵制父权制支配我们生活的方方面面，尽管我们无法总是看清它施加影响的所有方式。无论个体还是群体，我们都会在某些领域取得进步，即便在其他领域停滞不前甚至倒退，但我们必须继续前进——无论何时何地，都要努力理解并抵制父权制意识形态。

Feminists have long puzzled over the problem of getting beyond patriarchal programming and have offered many different solutions. For example, one way to deal with our apparent entrapment within patriarchal ideology is to consider the possibility that no ideology succeeds in fully programming all of the people all of the time. Every ideology has points of self-contradiction, of illogic, that permit us to understand its operations and decrease its influence, for instance, as Mary Wollstonecraft resisted patriarchal ideology in 1792 when she wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, as Virginia Woolf resisted patriarchal ideology in 1929 when she wrote A Room of One’s Own, as Simone de Beauvoir resisted patriarchal ideology in 1949 when she wrote The Second Sex, and as feminist theorists continue to resist it today. Perhaps the difficulty in theorizing our way out of patriarchal ideology arises when we think of our immersion in it as an all-or-nothing situation: if we’re not completely beyond patriarchy, then we must be completely programmed by it. I think it might be more useful to look at our relationship to patriarchal ideology as a dynamic situation: we must constantly struggle to understand and resist the various ways in which patriarchy dictates our lives, although we can’t always see all the ways in which it does so. Individually and collectively, we will move forward in some areas even as we remain static or backslide in others, but we must continue to move forward – to understand and resist patriarchal ideology – wherever and whenever we can.

鉴于抵制父权制思维的种种困难，许多女性主义理论家和文学批评家认为，我们应该格外谨慎地使用那些本身就带有父权制色彩的理论框架，例如精神分析和马克思主义。这些框架之所以被认为是父权制的，是因为它们体现了父权制意识形态的种种要素。例如，弗洛伊德以男性经验作为衡量女性经验的标准，因此他认为女性患有所谓的“阴茎嫉妒”，并且倾向于将长子视为“阴茎替代品”，以弥补自身男性生殖器的缺失。尽管马克思洞见了经济力量如何决定两性的生活，但他却未能意识到，女性即便身处不同的经济阶层，也依然会受到男性的压迫。

Given the difficulties involved in resisting patriarchal programming, many feminist theorists and literary critics believe we should be especially cautious about using frameworks that are themselves patriarchal, such as psychoanalysis and Marxism. Such frameworks are considered patriarchal because they embody various elements of patriarchal ideology. For example, because he used male experience as the standard against which he measured female experience, Freud believed that women suffer from what he called “penis envy” and that they tend to see their first-born sons as “penis substitutes” to make up for their own lack. Despite Marx’s insights into the ways in which economic forces determine the lives of both sexes, he failed to realize the ways in which women have been oppressed by men despite their economic class.

尽管如此，许多女性主义者仍然借鉴精神分析、马克思主义理论以及其他批判理论的要素，因为她们发现这些理论有助于审视与女性经验相关的问题。例如，精神分析可以帮助我们理解父权制意识形态的心理影响，以及女性和男性如何以及为何内化这种意识形态。马克思主义可以帮助我们理解父权制法律和习俗如何操纵经济力量，使女性在经济、政治和社会层面持续处于压迫之下，沦为底层阶级。结构主义原则可以用来研究不同文化背景下女性经验和作品的潜在相似性，以及她们遭受压迫方式的潜在相似性。解构主义可以用来探究文学作品如何暗中强化其所批判的父权制意识形态——一些女性主义文学批评家在解构主义理论传入美国之前就已经开始这样做了。

Nevertheless, many feminists draw on elements of psychoanalytic and Marxist theory as well as other critical theories because they find them useful in examining issues relevant to women’s experience. For example, psychoanalysis can be used to help us understand the psychological effects of patriarchal ideology as well as how and why women and men internalize it. Marxism can be used to help us understand how economic forces have been manipulated by patriarchal law and custom to keep women economically, politically, and socially oppressed as an underclass. Structuralist principles can be used to study underlying similarities among the experiences and productions of women from various cultures as well as underlying similarities in the ways they are oppressed. And deconstruction can be used to find the ways in which a literary work covertly reinforces the patriarchal ideology it criticizes, which some feminist literary critics were doing in America before the theory of deconstruction reached American shores.

第八章讨论的解构主义，帮助我们认识到，除其他方面外，我们的思维何时建立在错误的对立之上，也就是说，建立在以下信念之上：两种观念、特质或范畴常常被视为截然相反的两极——例如，爱/恨或善/恶——但事实上并非如此。因此，解构主义对女权主义者也大有裨益，它能帮助我们看清父权制意识形态常常建立在虚假对立之上的本质。例如，在反驳“男性天生理性，女性天生感性”这种性别歧视的观点时，女权主义者或许不会仅仅论证女性天生更感性，或者认为这两种范畴同样适用于两性。运用解构主义原则，她或许会指出，将理性和感性截然对立地划分为如此极端的范畴是错误的。我们认同某种哲学观点或理论框架的理性理由，难道不是源于（无论是有意识的还是无意识的）该观点或框架带给我们的感受吗？理性和感性，如果理解正确的话，难道不是常常在我们的生活中协同运作的吗？

Deconstruction, which is discussed in Chapter 8, helps us see, among other things, when our thinking is based on false oppositions, that is, on the belief that two ideas, qualities, or categories are polar opposites – for example, love/hate or good/evil – when, in fact, they are not. So deconstruction is also useful to feminists in helping us see the ways in which patriarchal ideology is often based on false oppositions. For instance, in refuting the sexist belief that men are naturally rational while women are naturally emotional, a feminist might do more than argue, for example, that women have been programmed to be more emotional or that both categories apply equally to both genders. Using deconstructive principles, she might argue that we are mistaken to separate the rational and the emotional into such diametrically opposed categories. Aren’t our rational reasons for subscribing to a particular philosophical view or theoretical framework based, consciously or unconsciously, on how that viewpoint or framework makes us feel? Don’t the rational and the emotional, properly understood, often work in tandem in our lives?

在我看来，女权主义的优势之一在于它能够自由地借鉴其他理论的思想，并将其应用于自身快速发展的需要。这也是我相信女权主义理论永不过时的原因之一：它不断地吸收其他领域的新思想，并探索运用旧思想的新途径。也正因如此，女权主义可以被视为一种跨学科理论，帮助我们建立看似迥异的思想流派之间的联系。尽管本书探讨的所有理论都以各种方式相互重叠，但很少有理论像女权主义那样充分认识到这一点，并利用这一点来拓展或深化自身的理论探索。

To my mind, one of feminism’s strengths is the freedom with which it borrows ideas from other theories and adapts them to its own rapidly evolving needs. This is one reason why I believe that feminist theory will never become stale: it constantly incorporates new ideas from other fields and finds new ways to use old ideas. This is also why feminism can be seen as an interdisciplinary theory that can help us learn to make connections among seemingly divergent schools of thought. While all of the theories addressed in this book overlap with one another in various ways, few acknowledge that fact or use it to broaden or deepen their theoretical explorations to the extent that feminism does.

当然，如何超越任何主导我们思维方式的意识形态，这个问题与任何自诩为新颖的理论都息息相关，这意味着它与所有理论都相关，尽管很少有理论直接探讨这个问题。事实上，许多女性主义思想家持续探讨的无解理论难题，对任何理论而言都是无解的，尽管这些问题要么被相关领域的实践者所忽视，要么被早期思想家认为已经解决。例如，与超越任何主导我们思维方式的意识形态的可能性（或不可能性）相关的问题是，个体的主观性问题：个体的自我意识，个体看待自己和他人的方式，源于个体自身的经验。鉴于我们无法意识到自身主观性决定我们如何诠释世界的所有方式，我们又如何能够确定，我们对人类经验或任何其他事物的推测，并非自身主观性的表达呢？

Of course, the question of how we can get beyond any ideology that dominates the way we think is a question relevant to any theory that purports to be new, which means it’s a question relevant to all theories, though few directly address it. In fact, many of the unsolvable theoretical problems that feminist thinkers continue to engage are unsolvable problems for every theory, though these problems either remain unacknowledged by practitioners in those fields or are considered solved by earlier thinkers. For example, related to the problem of the possibility (or impossibility) of getting beyond any ideology that dominates the way we think is the problem of one’s own subjectivity: one’s own selfhood, the way one views oneself and others, which develops from one’s own individual experiences. Given that we can’t be aware of all the ways in which our own subjectivity determines how we interpret the world, how can we ever know that our speculations about human experience, or about anything else for that matter, are anything but expressions of our own subjectivity?

正如我们将在后续章节中看到的，解构主义和新历史主义都触及了这个问题，但大多数其他理论并未直接探讨它。对于女性主义而言，正如对于解构主义和新历史主义一样，所有感知，以及所有阐释行为，都不可避免地带有主观性。我们在描述所见之物时，无法将自身排除在外，因为我们所见之物正是我们自身的一种产物。包括：我们的性别、政治立场、宗教信仰、种族、社会经济阶层、性取向、教育背景、家庭经历、自身问题、优势、劣势、理论框架等等。声称自己客观，正如父权制鼓励男性所做的那样，只不过是让我们对自身并非客观的种种方面视而不见罢了。

As we’ll see in subsequent chapters, deconstruction and new historicism engage this problem, but most of the other theories do not directly address it. For feminism, as for deconstruction and new historicism, all perceptions, therefore all acts of interpretation, are unavoidably subjective. We cannot leave ourselves out of the picture when describing what we see because what we see is a product of who we are: our gender, our politics, our religion, our race, our socioeconomic class, our sexual orientation, our education, our family background, our problems, our strengths, our weaknesses, our theoretical framework, and so on. To claim that we are objective, as patriarchy encourages men to do, is merely to blind ourselves to the ways in which we are not so.

从女性主义视角来看，当我们解读文本或其他任何事物时，处理自身主观性的方法并非试图回避它，而是尽可能地觉察它，并尽可能地将其充分纳入我们的解读之中，以便他人在评估我们的观点时能够将其考虑在内。正因如此，正如你可能已经注意到的，我在本章中提及自身的经历和偏见显得尤为恰当。我是一位中年、中产阶级、异性恋、白人美国女性，拥有英语博士学位，并来自一个充满爱却又略显不和谐的家庭，我的经历必然会影响我对女性主义的解读，以及我在本章结尾处对《了不起的盖茨比》的女性主义解读。不可避免地，我对某些事物的看法会与其他理论家和文学批评家有所不同，而其中许多差异或许都可以用我上面列举的个人信息差异来解释。希望读者在了解我之后，能够留意到我的观点仅仅是我所处位置所看到的观点。

From a feminist perspective, when we interpret texts or anything else, the way to deal with our subjectivity is not to try to avoid it but to be as aware of it as possible, to include it in our interpretation as fully as possible, so that others will be able to take it into account when evaluating our viewpoints. This is why it’s especially appropriate that I refer in this chapter, as you may have noticed, to my own experience and biases. My experience as a middle-aged, middle-class, heterosexual, white American woman with a Ph.D. in English and a lovingly dysfunctional family is bound to affect my interpretation of feminism as well as the feminist reading of The Great Gatsby I offer at the end of this chapter. Unavoidably, I’ll see some things differently from other theorists and literary critics, and many of those differences can probably be accounted for by differences in the personal data I listed above. By knowing a little bit about me, it is hoped that my readers will be on the lookout for the ways in which my point of view is just that: what I see from where I’m standing.

法国女权主义

French feminism

法国女权主义者提出了超越父权制的其他策略。与美国女权主义一样，法国女权主义也具有多元性，包含多种不同的观点。同样，法国女权主义也相信社会和政治行动主义对于确保女性享有平等机会和获得公正待遇至关重要。然而，我们将法国女权主义作为一个单独的类别进行简要探讨，因为与英国和美国女权主义者相比，法国女权主义者往往更注重女性问题的哲学层面，尽管随着时间的推移，法国女权主义理论在英美女权主义中也日益凸显。

Additional strategies for getting beyond patriarchy have been offered by French feminists. Like American feminism, French feminism is diverse: it consists of many different points of view. Also like American feminism, French feminism believes in the importance of social and political activism in order to ensure equal opportunity and equal access to justice for women. We’re taking a brief look at French feminism as a separate category, however, because French feminists have tended to focus more strongly on the philosophical dimension of women’s issues than have British and American feminists, although French feminist theory has become, over time, an increasingly visible presence in Anglo-American feminism.

总的来说，法国女权主义主要有两种形式：唯物主义女权主义和精神分析女权主义。前者关注女性在社会和经济上遭受的压迫，后者顾名思义，则侧重于女性的心理体验。尽管这两种分析女性在父权制文化中经历的方法往往存在显著差异，但法国女权主义者也同样关注女性的社会/经济经历与心理经历之间的关联。不过，现在我们先分别探讨这两种形式。我认为，如果我们能够对它们各自有一个较为清晰的认识，就能很容易地看出它们之间的互补与差异。

Generally speaking, the focus of French feminism has taken two different forms: materialist feminism and psychoanalytic feminism. The first form is interested in the social and economic oppression of women while the second form, as you might expect, concentrates on women’s psychological experience. Although these two approaches to analyzing women’s experience in patriarchal culture often contrast significantly, French feminists are also concerned with the ways in which women’s social/economic and psychological experience are connected. For now, however, let’s look at these two forms separately. I think that if we can gain a fairly clear idea of each, we will readily see the ways in which they compliment as well as contrast with each other.

法国唯物主义女权主义审视了父权制传统和制度，这些传统和制度控制着社会压迫女性的物质（生理）和经济条件，例如，关于男女差异的父权制观念，以及规范婚姻和母性的法律和习俗。尽管西蒙娜·德·波伏娃并未自称为唯物主义女权主义者，但她开创性的著作《第二性》（1949）为后世数十年的唯物主义女权主义者奠定了理论基础。波伏娃指出，在父权制社会中，男性被视为本质主体（拥有自由意志的独立个体），而女性则被视为偶然存在（受环境控制的依赖者）。男性可以作用于世界，改变世界，赋予世界意义，而女性的意义却只能与男性相关联。因此，女性的定义不仅在于她们与男性的差异，还在于她们相对于男性的不足。因此， “女性”一词与“他者”一词具有相同的含义。女性并非一个独立自主的人。她是男人的“他者”：她不如男人；在男人的世界里，她就像一个异类；她不像男人那样是一个完全成熟的人。

French materialist feminism examines the patriarchal traditions and institutions that control the material (physical) and economic conditions by which society oppresses women, for example, patriarchal beliefs about the difference between men and women and the laws and customs that govern marriage and motherhood. Although Simone de Beauvoir didn’t refer to herself as a materialist feminist, her groundbreaking The Second Sex (1949) created a theoretical basis for materialist feminists for decades to come. In a patriarchal society, Beauvoir observes, men are considered essential subjects (independent selves with free will), while women are considered contingent beings (dependent beings controlled by circumstances). Men can act upon the world, change it, give it meaning, while women have meaning only in relation to men. Thus, women are defined not just in terms of their difference from men, but in terms of their inadequacy in comparison to men. The word woman, therefore, has the same implications as the word other. A woman is not a person in her own right. She is man’s Other: she is less than a man; she is a kind of alien in a man’s world; she is not a fully developed human being the way a man is.

波伏娃是第一个提出女性并非天生具有女性特质，而是被父权制塑造为女性的人。她阐述了如今被称为社会建构主义的观点，正如我们在本章前面所看到的，她那句如今广为人知的名言是：“人不是生来就是女人；人是后天成为女人的”（引自《我》92页）。事实上，波伏娃认为，尽管父权制假定女性天生具有母性本能，但事实并非如此。母性本能是所有物种成员与生俱来的自然生物特征，然而并非所有女性都渴望生育或乐于为人母。但父权制却告诉她们，如果不生育，她们作为女性的人生就不完整，因此，女性承受着巨大的压力，被强迫成为母亲。显然，鉴于我们从未在父权制的社会制约之外看到过“女性”这一形象，我们又如何能够了解“女性的本性”呢？

The first to argue that women are not born feminine but rather conditioned to be feminine by patriarchy, Beauvoir articulated an idea that is now called, as we saw earlier in this chapter, social constructionism in her now-famous words, “One is not born a woman; one becomes one” (cited in Moi 92). Indeed, Beauvoir argues that, despite patriarchy’s assumptions to the contrary, women are not even born with a maternal instinct. An instinct is something all members of a species have as part of their natural biological makeup, whereas not all women want to have children or feel comfortable being mothers. Yet patriarchy tells them that they are unfulfilled as women if they don’t have children, and there is a great deal of pressure brought to bear upon women in order to recruit them for motherhood. Clearly, how can we know what “woman” is “by nature,” given that we never see her outside the social conditioning of patriarchy?

波伏娃认为，女性不应像父权制鼓励的那样，将生命的意义寄托于丈夫和儿子身上。正如詹妮弗·汉森所观察到的，“波伏娃坚信婚姻……束缚并阻碍了女性的智力发展和自由”（2）。波伏娃认为，女性如此全身心地投入到丈夫和儿子的成就中，实际上是在逃避自身实现潜能的自由。这种自由往往令她们感到恐惧，因此她们常常试图逃避：它要求个人承担责任，却无法保证成功，甚至无法保证幸福。“如果女性似乎总是​​无关紧要的，永远无法成为至关重要的存在，”波伏娃指出，“那是因为她自己未能促成这种改变”（10）。

Beauvoir maintains that women should not be content with investing the meaning of their lives in their husbands and sons, as patriarchy encourages them to do. As Jennifer Hansen observes, “Beauvoir strongly believed that marriage … trapped and stunted women’s intellectual growth and freedom” (2). In investing themselves so thoroughly in the accomplishments of their husbands and sons, Beauvoir claims, women are trying to escape their own freedom to fulfill their own potential in the world, a freedom that they often try to avoid because it is frightening: it demands personal responsibility while offering no guarantee of success or even of well-being. “If woman seems to be the inessential [being] which never becomes the essential,” Beauvoir suggests, “it is because she herself fails to bring about this change” (10).

为什么女性如此难以意识到自身所受的压迫，更遑论采取行动？波伏娃指出，与其他受压迫群体——例如受压迫的阶级、受压迫的种族和宗教少数群体——不同，历史上并没有关于女性共享文化、共享传统或共享权利的记录。压迫。从这个意义上讲，她们已被“从”历史中“抹去”，不被认为是一个值得讨论的话题。此外，她还观察到女性

Why is it so difficult for women to recognize their own subjugation, let alone do something about it? Beauvoir points out that, unlike other oppressed groups – for example, oppressed classes and oppressed racial and religious minorities – there is no historical record of women’s shared culture, shared traditions, or shared oppression. They have been, in this sense, “written out” of history, not considered a topic worth covering. Furthermore, she observes that women

她们缺乏组织起来的具体手段……她们没有集体记录的历史……没有自己的宗教信仰……她们分散居住在男性群体中，通过居住、家务、经济状况和社会地位，她们与某些男性——父亲或丈夫——的联系比与其他女性的联系更为紧密。

lack a concrete means for organizing themselves into a unit. … They have no [collective recorded] past … no religion of their own. … They live dispersed among the males, attached through residence, housework, economic condition, and social standing to certain men – fathers or husbands – more firmly than they are to other women.

（11）

(11)

换句话说，女性对同阶层、同种族或同宗教男性的忠诚总是优先于对不同阶层、不同种族或不同宗教女性的忠诚。事实上，女性对男性的忠诚也优先于对同阶层、同种族或同宗教女性的忠诚。

In other words, women’s allegiance to men from their own social class, race, or religion always supersedes their allegiance to women from different classes, races, or religions. In fact, women’s allegiance to men also supersedes their allegiance to women from their own class, race, or religion.

受波伏娃影响的众多思想家之一，克里斯蒂娜·德尔菲（Christine Delphy）基于马克思主义原则，对父权制进行了女性主义批判。德尔菲在20世纪70年代初提出了“唯物主义女性主义”的概念，她将分析的重点放在作为经济单位的家庭上。她解释说，正如社会整体上底层阶级受到上层阶级的压迫一样，女性在家庭中也处于从属地位。因此，女性构成了一个独立的受压迫阶级，这种压迫源于她们作为女性所遭受的压迫，而与她们所属的社会经济阶级无关。在德尔菲看来，婚姻是一种劳动契约，它将女性束缚于无偿的家务劳动，这些劳动通常被轻描淡写地称为“家务”，不被认为足够重要，以至于需要作为一个独立的话题或问题进行严肃的分析。她指出，理解这种情况的含义对于理解女性所受的压迫至关重要。德尔菲指出：

One of many thinkers influenced by Beauvoir, Christine Delphy offers a feminist critique of patriarchy based on Marxist principles. Delphy, who coined the phrase materialist feminism in the early 1970s, focuses her analysis on the family as economic unit. Just as the lower classes are oppressed by the upper classes in society as a whole, she explains, women are the subordinates within families. As such, women constitute a separate oppressed class, based on their oppression as women, regardless of the socioeconomic class to which they belong. For Delphy, marriage is a labor contract that ties women to unpaid domestic labor, commonly trivialized as “housework,” not considered important enough to be seriously analyzed as a topic, or a problem, in its own right. An understanding of the implications of this situation is central, she notes, to an understanding of women’s oppression. Delphy points out that

所有当代“发达”社会……都依赖女性无偿的家务劳动和育儿。这些服务是在与特定个体（丈夫）的特定关系框架内提供的。它们被排除在交换范畴之外[也就是说，这些服务不被视为人们在家庭之外从事的有偿工作]，因此没有价值。它们是无偿的。女性所获得的回报与她们所做的工作无关，因为它不是作为劳动的交换（即作为她们劳动应得的工资），而是作为一种馈赠。丈夫唯一的义务，显然也符合他自身的利益，就是满足妻子的基本需求，换句话说，他维持着妻子的劳动力。

[a]ll contemporary “developed” societies … depend on the unpaid labour of women for domestic services and child-rearing. These services are furnished within the framework of a particular relationship to an individual (the husband). They are excluded from the realm of exchange [i.e., these services are not treated like the jobs people do for money outside their own home] and consequently have no value. They are unpaid. Whatever women receive in return is independent of the work which they perform because it is not handed out in exchange for that work (i.e., as a wage to which their work entitles them), but rather as a gift. The husband’s only obligation, which is obviously in his own interest, is to provide for his wife’s basic needs, in other words he maintains her labour power.

（60）

(60)

此外，德尔菲认为，女性在家中从事的家务劳动之所以没有报酬，并非因为她们的工作不重要，或者耗时或劳动量少于男性。男性在家庭之外从事有偿工作，但由于父权制将女性的家庭角色定义为非劳动者，因此女性在家务劳动中无法获得报酬。当然，非劳动者不应该期望获得报酬。具有讽刺意味的是，德尔菲指出，“所有人类学和社会学证据都表明，统治阶级让其权力阶层从事生产性工作——而占主导地位的性别从事的工作更少”（61）。换句话说，在父权制社会中，女性在家承担男性不愿做的家务劳动，而且她们的工作时间长达24小时。因此，总的来说，女性的工作时间比男性更长，尽管女性的家务劳动不被认为是值得获得报酬的真正劳动。因此，德尔菲认为，为了理解任何关于性和性别的问题，我们首先必须理解，男女之间的关系都建立在权力之上，这也就不足为奇了：父权制下的男性想要掌握所有权力；非父权制下的女性则希望权力得到平等分配。随着越来越多的美国妻子外出工作，同时她们仍然承担着大部分家务劳动和育儿任务，德尔菲的分析似乎与当今美国女性的生活特别相关。

In addition, Delphy contends that women’s domestic work in their own homes is unpaid not because their work is unimportant or involves less time or labor than the paid work performed by men outside the home, but because patriarchy defines women in their domestic roles as nonworkers. And nonworkers, of course, should not expect to be paid. Ironically, “all the anthropological and sociological evidence reveals,” Delphy notes, “that the dominant classes make the classes in their power do the productive work – that the pre-eminent sex does less work” (61). In other words, in a patriarchy women do the domestic labor at home that men don’t want to do, and their work day is 24 hours long. So when you add it all up, women work longer hours than men, though women’s work in the home isn’t recognized as real labor deserving of pay. It should not be surprising, then, that in order to understand anything about sexuality or gender we must first understand, Delphy argues, that all relationships between men and women are based on power: patriarchal men want to keep all of it; nonpatriarchal women want power to be equally distributed. As more and more American wives take jobs outside the home, while they still perform the lion’s share of domestic labor and child-rearing tasks, Delphy’s analysis seems especially relevant to the lives of American women today.

最后，让我们来看科莱特·吉约曼（Colette Guillaumin）的作品，以此作为法国唯物主义女权主义的最后一个例证。吉约曼指出，男性主要根据其所从事的职业来定义和描述，根据他们在社会中作为劳动力参与者、决策者等的价值来评判。而女性则主要根据其性别来定义和描述。正如吉约曼所记录的，在她收集的48小时内的短语中，有人提到“一个小组会议，旨在就某事发表意见”，其成员包括“公司董事、车床操作员、荷官（赌场里负责赌桌的人）和一名女性”（73）。同样，吉约曼还提到，一位世界领导人在谈到他所反对的压迫政权时说：“他们杀害了成千上万的工人、学生和妇女”（73）。换句话说，吉约曼观察到，就她们在社会中的功能而言，“女性人类……首先且根本上是女性”（73）。在吉约曼看来，这意味着她们首先且根本上是财产，例如，在婚姻中可以“交换”或“赠予”（取决于她们所属的文化）的财产。

For our final example of French materialist feminism let’s take a look at the work of Colette Guillaumin. Guillaumin observes that men are defined primarily and referred to primarily in terms of what they do, according to their value in society as participants in the workforce, as decision-makers, and so forth. Women are defined primarily and referred to primarily in terms of their sex. As Guillaumin notes, from phrases she collected within a single 48-hour period, a “group meeting to give their opinion on some matter” was said to consist of a “company director, a lathe-operator, a croupier [a person who runs a gambling table at a casino] and a woman” (73). Similarly, Guillaumin reports, a world leader, discussing a repressive regime to which he was opposed, said, “They killed tens of thousands of workers, students, and women” (73). In other words, Guillaumin observes, in terms of their function in society, “female human beings … [are] … primarily and fundamentally women” (73). And for Guillaumin, this means they are primarily and fundamentally property, for example, property to be “exchanged” or “given away” (depending on the culture to which they belong) in marriage.

吉约曼认为，女性受压迫的主要形式是占有，这也揭示了她们作为财产的功能。正如她解释的那样，女性不仅像众所周知的那样在劳动力市场（例如，同工不同酬）和家庭中遭受剥削（她们的劳动通常得不到任何报酬），而且还受到吉约曼所谓的“直接物质占有”的压迫。她所说的“直接物质占有”是指“将女性贬低为物质对象”（74），并将其比作奴隶制和农奴制。吉约曼将这种针对女性的占有称为“性别占有”（sexage）。她认为，“性别占有”主要有四种形式：（1）对女性时间的占有；（2）对女性身体产物的占有；（3）对女性性器官的占有。（4）妇女有义务照顾那些无法照顾自己的家庭成员，以及照顾健康的男性家庭成员。

The primary form of women’s oppression, Guillaumin argues, which also reveals their function as property, is appropriation. As she explains, it is not merely the case that women are exploited, as everyone knows, in the labor market (for example, paid less than men for the same work) and in the home, where they are generally not paid at all for their labor. Women are also oppressed by what Guillaumin calls “direct physical appropriation,” by which she means “the reduction of women to the state of material objects” (74) and which she compares to slavery and serfdom. In the case of women, Guillaumin calls this appropriation sexage. Sexage occurs, she believes, in four main forms: (1) the appropriation of women’s time, (2) the appropriation of the products of women’s bodies, (3) women’s sexual obligation, and (4) women’s obligation to care for whichever members of the family can’t care for themselves as well as for healthy male family members.

让我们简要地看一下这些性义务的形式。正如吉约曼所观察到的：（1）婚姻契约并未限制妻子（以及家中其他女性，例如女儿、姑姨和祖母）的工作时间，也没有规定她们可以休息的节假日。（2）在某些文化中，女性的头发甚至乳汁都会被男性家庭成员出售；夫妻生育子女的数量由男性决定；子女的法定财产仍然属于丈夫。（3）女性对男性的性义务既存在于婚姻中，也存在于卖淫中。吉约曼认为，两者之间的主要区别在于，男性嫖娼的时间受到限制，并且必须为他想要的特定服务付费。 （4）虽然照料婴儿、儿童、老人和病人有时由有偿工作者（通常是女性）承担，但绝大多数此类工作是由无偿的女性家庭成员完成的，或者在某些文化中，是由无偿的女性宗教工作者（例如修女）完成的。这四个领域的挪用最终导致女性丧失了个性、独立性和自主性。简而言之，正如吉约曼所言，女性成了“被赋予从事男性不愿承担的那些任务的社会工具”（79）。

Let’s take a brief look at each of these forms of sexage. As Guillaumin observes, (1) the marriage contract puts no limits on the time wives (and any other women living in the family, such as daughters, aunts, and grandmothers) will have to work and specifies no holidays on which they won’t have to work. (2) In some cultures, women’s hair and even their milk are sold by male members of the family; the number of children a couple will have is decided by the male; and children are still the legal property of the husband. (3) Women’s sexual obligation to men occurs both in marriage and in prostitution. For Guillaumin, the primary difference between the two is that time limits are placed on a man’s use of prostitutes, and he must pay for the specific acts he wants. (4) Although the caretaking of babies, children, the elderly, and the sick is sometimes carried out by paid workers (who are usually women), the overwhelming majority of it is done by unpaid female family members or, in some cultures, by unpaid female religious workers, such as nuns. The overall effect of all four areas of appropriation is to deprive women of a sense of their individuality as well as of their independence and autonomy. In short, women are, as Guillaumin puts it, “the social tool assigned to those tasks” (79) that men don’t want to do.

与唯物主义女权主义不同，法国女权主义精神分析理论关注父权制对女性心理体验和创造力的影响。它关注的是个体心理，而非群体经验。因为对女性的压迫不仅限于经济、政治和社会领域，也包括女性在潜意识层面的心理压抑。正因为如此，每个女性都必须在自身的心理层面学会解放自己，女性的唯物主义解放才能拥有持久的基础。如果一个女人不知道自己需要解放，她就无法获得任何有意义的解放。对于许多法国精神分析女权主义者来说，女性心理解放的可能性必须在她们遭受心理压迫的场所——语言——进行探究，因为正是语言定义了有害的父权制性别差异观念（父权制认为男女之间存在的本质差异或先天差异），并且这些观念继续发挥着压迫性的影响。

In contrast to materialist feminism, French feminist psychoanalytic theory is interested in patriarchy’s influence on women’s psychological experience and creativity. Its focus is on the individual psyche, not on group experience. For the oppression of women is not limited to the economic, political, and social domains; it includes women’s psychological repression at the level of the unconscious as well. And it is here, in each woman’s personal psychology, that she must learn to liberate herself if women’s materialist liberation is going to have any lasting foundation. For a woman can’t be liberated in any meaningful way if she doesn’t know that she needs to be liberated. And for many French psychoanalytic feminists, the possibilities for women’s psychological liberation must be investigated at the site at which most, if not all, of their psychological subjugation occurs – language – because it is within language that detrimental patriarchal notions of sexual difference (what patriarchy believes are the essential, or inborn, differences between women and men) have been defined and continue to exert their repressive influence.

例如，海伦·西苏认为，语言揭示了她所谓的父权制二元思维，这种思维可以定义为以对立的两极来看待世界，其中一方被认为优于另一方。例如，等级森严的二元对立包括：头脑/心灵、父亲/母亲、文化/自然、可理解的/可感知的（即可以用头脑理解的与可以用身体感受到的）、太阳/月亮以及主动/被动。诸如此类的对立塑造了我们的思维方式，而对于每一种对立，西苏都会提出这样的问题：“（女性）在哪里？”（91）。也就是说，每一种对立的哪一方被认为定义了女性的某些方面。女性？显然，按照父权制思维，女性占据了这些对立概念的右侧，即父权制认为的低等的一侧——心、母亲、自然、可触及的、月亮和被动——而男性则被假定为由这些对立概念的左侧所定义，即父权制认为的优越的一侧：头、父亲、文化、可理解的、太阳和主动。“传统上，”西苏指出，“性别差异问题是通过将其与主动/被动的对立联系起来来处理的”（92）。换句话说，父权制思维认为女性天生被动，男性天生主动，因为两性在这一点上存在差异是自然规律。因此，如果一个女人不被动，她就不是真正的女人。当然，由此可以推断，女性天生顺从男性，男性天生是领导者，等等。

For instance, Hélène Cixous argues that language reveals what she calls patriarchal binary thought, which might be defined as seeing the world in terms of polar opposites, one of which is considered superior to the other. Examples include such hierarchical binary oppositions as head/heart, father/mother, culture/nature, intelligible/palpable (that which can be understood by the mind versus that which can be felt by the body), sun/moon, and activity/passivity. Oppositions like these organize the way we think, and for each opposition Cixous asks, “Where is [the woman]?” (91). That is, which side of each opposition is assumed to define some aspect of the female? Clearly, according to patriarchal thinking, the woman occupies the right side of each of these oppositions, the side that patriarchy considers inferior – heart, mother, nature, palpable, moon, and passivity – while it is assumed that the male is defined by the left side of each opposition, the side that patriarchy considers superior: head, father, culture, intelligible, sun, and activity. “Traditionally,” Cixous notes, “the question of sexual difference is treated by coupling it with the opposition activity/passivity” (92). In other words, patriarchal thinking believes that women are born to be passive while men are born to be active because it is natural for the sexes to be different in this way. Thus, if a woman is not passive, she is not really a woman. Of course, it follows that women are naturally submissive to men, that men are natural leaders, and so forth.

在西苏看来，女性无法通过融入父权制权力结构——即在现有的父权制社会中获得平等地位和平等机会——来学会反抗父权制思维。因为女性在现有的社会政治体系内获得权力并不能从根本上改变这个体系。事实上，其结果反而会使女性变得更像父权制下的男性，因为她们会学会像父权制下的男性那样思考。相反，她认为，作为生命的源泉，女性本身就是力量和能量的源泉。因此，我们需要一种新的、女性化的语言，来瓦解或消除压迫和压制女性的父权制二元思维。西苏认为，这种语言最能通过写作来表达，它被称为“女性写作”（ écriture féminine）。这种语言结构流畅，联想自由。它抵制父权制的思维和写作模式，这些模式通常要求规定“正确”的组织方法、理性主义的逻辑规则（这种逻辑“停留在头脑层面”，依赖于对认知经验的狭隘定义，并否定许多种类的情感和直觉经验），以及线性推理（x 先于 y，y 先于 z）。

For Cixous, women will not learn to resist patriarchal thinking by becoming part of the patriarchal power structure, that is, by obtaining equal status and equal opportunity in current patriarchal society. For women’s acquisition of power within the existing sociopolitical system would not adequately change the system. Indeed, the result would be that women would become more like patriarchal men because they would learn to think as patriarchal men have been trained to think. Instead, she argues that, as the source of life, women are themselves the source of power, of energy. We therefore need a new, feminine language that undermines or eliminates the patriarchal binary thinking that oppresses and silences women. This kind of language, which Cixous believes best expresses itself in writing, is called écriture féminine (feminine writing). It is fluidly organized and freely associative. It resists patriarchal modes of thinking and writing, which generally require prescribed, “correct” methods of organization, rationalist rules of logic (logic that stays “above the neck,” relying on narrow definitions of cognitive experience and discrediting many kinds of emotional and intuitive experience), and linear reasoning (x precedes y, which precedes z).

尽管女性与母亲之间长久的联系，以及她们最初的力量和能量源泉，赋予了她们与女性写作（écriture féminine）之间一种特殊的关系，但能够与自己早期与母亲的联系建立联系的男性也能创作出这种作品。西苏列举了法国作家玛格丽特·杜拉斯、科莱特和让·热内，以及巴西作家克拉丽丝·利斯佩克托的作品作为此类写作的例证。我认为，托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》 、弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《达洛维夫人》、詹姆斯·乔伊斯的《芬尼根守灵夜》和威廉·福克纳的《押沙龙，押沙龙！》等文学作品也可能属于此类。西苏认为，这种写作是一种自发地与女性身体不受束缚、充满活力的生命力建立联系（或重新建立联系）的方式，正如我们之前看到的，她强调这种生命力是生命的源泉。因此，对她而言，写作可以是一种解放的实践。这里设想的放弃父权思想或许确实显得乌托邦式，但正如托里尔·莫伊所观察到的，“乌托邦思想一直是女权主义者的灵感来源”（121）。

Although women’s prolonged bonds with their mothers, with their original source of power and energy, have given them a privileged relationship to écriture féminine, a man who can get in touch with his early bond with his mother can also produce it. As examples of such writing, Cixous names the work of French writers Marguerite Duras, Colette, and Jean (John) Genet as well as that of Brazilian writer Clarice Lispector. I think we can speculate that literary works such as Toni Morrison’s Beloved, Virginia Woolf’s Mrs. Dalloway, James Joyce’s Finnegan’s Wake, and William Faulkner’s Absalom, Absalom! might also serve as examples. Cixous sees this kind of writing as a way to spontaneously connect (or reconnect) to the unfettered, joyous vitality of the female body, which as we saw earlier, she emphasizes as the source of life. Thus, for her, writing can be an enactment of liberation. The abandonment of patriarchal thinking envisioned here may indeed seem utopian, but as Toril Moi observes, “[u]topian thought has always been a source of inspiration for feminists” (121).

同样，露西·伊里加雷指出，在父权制文化中，女性的很多屈从行为都以心理压抑的形式出现，并通过语言媒介得以实现。换句话说，女性生活在一个几乎所有意义都被父权制语言定义的世界里。因此，尽管她们可能没有意识到，但女性并非主动表达自己的想法，而是被动地模仿先前已有的观念。当我们回顾西方父权制思想史时，这种状况并不像最初看起来那么令人惊讶。正如伊里加雷所观察到的，对西方哲学家而言，女性只不过是他们自身男性气质的一面镜子。也就是说，男性根据自身的需要、恐惧和欲望来定义女性气质。例如，她指出，弗洛伊德——尽管她认为他的理论很有用，甚至具有开创性——在假设女性患有“阴茎嫉妒”（即她们觉得自己被阉割了）时，实际上是将男性对阉割的恐惧投射到了女性身上。显然，这种观点假定女性想要的东西与男性想要的相同，假定女性没有专属于她们的情感或欲望。伊里加雷认为，身处父权制之下的女性只有两种选择：（1）保持沉默（因为任何不符合父权制逻辑的言论都会被视为不可理解、毫无意义），或者（2）模仿父权制对女性的刻板印象（即扮演父权制对性别差异的定义所赋予的从属角色，这种定义凸显了男性的优越性）。显然，这根本算不上真正的选择。

Similarly, Luce Irigaray suggests that, in a patriarchal culture, much of women’s subjugation occurs in the form of psychological repression enacted through the medium of language. In other words, women live in a world in which virtually all meaning has been defined by patriarchal language. Therefore, though they may not realize it, women don’t speak as active originators of their own thoughts. Rather, they passively imitate previously spoken ideas. This state of affairs is not as surprising as it initially may seem when we consider the history of Western patriarchal thought. As Irigaray observes, for Western philosophers the woman is just a mirror of their own masculinity. That is, men have defined femininity in terms of their own needs, fears, and desires. For example, she points out that Freud – although she finds his theories useful, even groundbreaking – was projecting the masculine fear of castration onto women when he hypothesized that women suffer from penis envy, that they feel they have been castrated. Clearly, such a viewpoint assumes that women want the same things men want, that women do not have feelings or desires that are theirs alone. Caught within patriarchy, Irigaray posits, women have only two choices: (1) to keep quiet (for anything a woman says that does not fit within the logic of patriarchy will be seen as incomprehensible, meaningless), or (2) to imitate patriarchy’s representation of herself as it wants to see her (that is, to play the inferior role given her by patriarchy’s definition of sexual difference, which foregrounds men’s superiority). Obviously, this is hardly a real choice.

在伊里加雷看来，父权制权力也体现在许多思想家所说的“男性凝视”中：男人观看，女人被观看。而正是观看者掌握着控制权，拥有命名事物、解释世界乃至统治世界的权力。被观看者——女人——仅仅是一个供人观看的对象。因此，在父权制社会中，女性仅仅是男性经济中的象征、标记和商品。换句话说，女性的功能在于展现男性之间的相互关系。举个最简单的例子，一个父权制男性如果觉得自己必须身边有个漂亮女人才能给人留下深刻印象，那么他真正感兴趣的并非如何给别人留下深刻印象，而是如何给其他男性留下深刻印象。简而言之，父权制是一个男人的世界：男人制定游戏规则，他们只与彼此进行游戏，而女人仅仅是奖品中的一种。

Patriarchal power is also evident, for Irigaray, in what many thinkers refer to as the male gaze: the man looks; the woman is looked at. And it is the one who looks who is in control, who holds the power to name things, the power to explain the world and so to rule the world. The one looked at – the woman – is merely an object to be seen. Thus, in a patriarchy, women are merely tokens, markers, commodities in a male economy. In other words, women function to display men’s relations to other men. To cite the simplest example, a patriarchal man who feels he must have a beautiful woman on his arm in order to impress other people isn’t interested in impressing other people. He’s interested in impressing other men. In short, patriarchy is a man’s world: men invent the rules of the game, they play it only with one another, and women are merely to be found among the prizes.

与西苏一样，伊里加雷认为，超越父权制的途径正是通过父权制塑造我们的同一工具：语言。她相信，女性专属群体对于发展非父权制的思维和表达方式至关重要。伊里加雷将她所理解的女性语言称为“女性之语” （womanspeak），并认为其源头在于女性的身体，特别是她所看到的男女性快感的对比。在她看来，女性的性快感“远比人们通常想象的更加多样化、差异更加丰富、更加复杂、更加微妙”（28）。同样，“女性之语”也比父权制语言更加多样化、含义更加丰富、更加复杂、更加微妙。正如伊里加雷所说，当一位女性敢于用自己的方式表达时，“她便开启了全新的篇章”。这些指示让“他”（父权制下的男性）无法理解任何意义的连贯性。她的话语自相矛盾，从理性的角度来看近乎疯狂，对于那些带着现成框架、手握一套完整密码的聆听者来说，根本无法理解”（29）。对于一些女性主义思想家而言，伊里加雷对“女性话语”的定义尤其具有争议性，因为除其他原因外，它似乎强化了父权制对女性不合逻辑甚至不理性的刻板印象。然而，一种富有成效的理解方式或许是，至少在我看来，伊里加雷并非在说女性说话语无伦次，而是说在父权制社会中，女性的语言之所以显得语无伦次，是因为父权制社会的人们习惯于只赋予符合父权制逻辑规则的语言以意义，即线性的、以论点为导向的语言。

Like Cixous, Irigaray argues that the way to get beyond patriarchy is by means of the same vehicle that programmed us within patriarchy: language. And she believes that women-only groups are necessary for the development of nonpatriarchal ways of thinking and speaking. Irigaray calls her notion of woman’s language womanspeak, and she finds its source in the female body, specifically in what she sees as the contrast between female and male sexual pleasure. For her, female sexual pleasure is “far more diversified, more multiple in its differences, more complex, more subtle, than is commonly imagined” (28). And so is womanspeak more diversified, more multiple in its meanings, more complex, and more subtle than patriarchal language. As Irigaray puts it, when a woman dares speak in her own way, “‘she’ sets off in all directions leaving ‘him’ [the patriarchal man] unable to discern the coherence of any meaning. Hers are contradictory words, somewhat mad from the standpoint of reason, inaudible for whoever listens to them with ready-made grids, with a fully elaborated code in hand” (29). For some feminist thinkers, Irigaray’s definition of womanspeak is particularly controversial because, among other things, it seems to reinforce patriarchal stereotypes of women as illogical or even irrational. One productive way to view womanspeak, however, might be to consider what seems to me, at least, to be the very strong possibility that Irigaray is not saying that women speak incoherently but that this is how it seems to patriarchal people, programmed to attribute meaning only to language that conforms to patriarchal rules of logic, that is, to linear, thesis-oriented language.

与此相反，另一位法国精神分析女性主义者朱莉娅·克里斯蒂娃不相信“女性写作”（écriture féminine）或“女性话语”（womanspeak），因为她认为任何将女性本质化的理论（即假定女性具有本质的、与生俱来的、生物学的特征）都歪曲了女性的无限多样性，并使她们容易受到父权制对女性本质化的刻板印象的影响，例如天生顺从、情绪化等等。事实上，在克里斯蒂娃看来，女性气质无法定义，因为女性气质的定义与女性的数量一样多。然而，克里斯蒂娃断言，我们可以了解女性气质的这一特性：它被边缘化、被压迫，正如工人阶级被边缘化和被压迫一样。

In contrast, Julia Kristeva, another French psychoanalytic feminist, doesn’t believe in écriture féminine or womanspeak because she believes that any theory that essentializes women (that is, that posits essential – inborn, biological – characteristics for women) misrepresents their infinite diversity and leaves them vulnerable to the patriarchal essentialization of women as naturally submissive, overly emotional, and so forth. Indeed, for Kristeva, the feminine can’t be defined because there are as many definitions of the feminine as there are women. We can, however, know this about femininity, Kristeva asserts: it is marginalized, oppressed, just as the working class is marginalized and oppressed.

此外，许多女权主义者普遍接受的、使女性成为女性、男性成为男性的生物学差异（而非父权制强加于我们身上、定义我们为女性或男性的社会差异），在克里斯蒂娃看来却是社会差异而非生物学差异，因为这些差异对现实世界中的女性有着切实的影响。正如她所说，“（女性和男性之间）性、生物学、生理和生殖方面的差异反映了……社会契约的差异”（《女性的时代》188页）。换句话说，如果一个人天生具有女性的生物学特征，那么她在社会中享有的权利就更少——尤其是在性方面，包括性关系的类型和数量，以及堕胎和避孕的权利——而如果一个人天生具有男性的生物学特征，她所享有的权利则更少。归根结底，问题的关键不在于如何定义生物学差异；问题在于，无论生物差异本身具有何种意义，都会立即被伴随而来的社会（父权制）意义所吞噬、掩盖和取代。正是这种赋予性别差异的社会意义压迫着女性。因此，对于克里斯蒂娃以及大多数法国女权主义者——包括前文讨论过的唯物主义女权主义者——而言，英美女权主义者所提出的性别与性之间的区别并不存在。父权制定义并控制着我们看待性别（女性）和性（女性特质）的方式，仿佛它们是同一回事。事实上，法语中并没有像英语中那样用来指代“性别”的词汇。

Furthermore, what have been generally accepted by many feminists as the biological differences that make women female and men male (as opposed to the differences socially imposed by patriarchy that define us as feminine or masculine) are seen by Kristeva as social differences rather than biological differences because of their concrete effects on women in the real world. As she puts it, the “sexual, biological, physiological, and reproductive difference [between women and men] reflects a difference in … the social contract” (“Woman’s Time” 188). In other words, if one is born with the biology of a female, one’s place in society is accorded fewer rights – particularly the right to own and control one’s body sexually, both in terms of the kind and number of sexual relationships one will have and in terms of abortion and contraceptive rights – than if one is born with the biology of a male. In the final analysis, the issue is not how biological difference should be defined; rather the issue is that whatever meaning biological difference may have is instantly consumed, overshadowed, displaced by the social (patriarchal) meaning that accompanies it. And it is the social meaning given to sexual difference that oppresses women. Thus for Kristeva, as for most French feminists – including materialist feminists like the ones discussed earlier – the difference between sex and gender posited by Anglo-American feminists does not exist. Patriarchy defines and controls the way we relate to sex (female) and gender (feminine) as if they were the same thing. Indeed, there is no word in French for gender as we use the word in English.

克里斯蒂娃认为，与其拥抱女性写作和女性话语来超越父权压迫，不如通过探索她所谓的语言符号维度（不要与符号学混淆，符号学是对文化符号系统进行分析的研究领域），来超越父权制语言和父权制思维。在克里斯蒂娃看来，语言包含两个维度：符号维度和符号维度。符号维度是词语运作和赋予意义的领域。而她所说的语言符号维度则与之相反，它包含语调（声音、语气、音量，以及音乐性）；节奏；以及说话时产生的肢体语言，这些肢体语言揭示了我们的情感和生理本能（例如，与性、生存等相关的生理本能）。那么，或许我们可以说，符号学包含我们说话的方式，例如我们在说话时通过声音和肢体语言传递出的情感。因此，正如克里斯蒂娃所指出的，“例如，科学话语……倾向于尽可能地减少符号学成分。相反……在诗歌语言中……符号学……往往占据主导地位”（《语言中的欲望》 134页），这并不令人意外。

Instead of embracing écriture féminine and womanspeak as a means to take us beyond patriarchal oppression, Kristeva maintains that women and men can get beyond patriarchal language and patriarchal thinking by seeking access to what she calls the semiotic dimension of language (not to be confused with the field of study called semiotics, which is the analysis of cultural sign systems). For Kristeva, language consists of two dimensions: the symbolic and the semiotic. The symbolic dimension is the domain in which words operate and meanings are attributed to them. What she calls the semiotic dimension of language is that part of language that, in contrast, consists of such elements as intonation (sound, tone of voice, volume, and for lack of a better word, musicality); rhythm; and the body language that occurs as we speak, which reveals our feelings and bodily drives (for example, bodily drives that relate to the sexual, to survival, and so forth). Perhaps we can say, then, that the semiotic consists of the way we speak, for instance the emotions that come across in our voice and body language as we talk. So it is not unexpected that, as Kristeva notes, “Scientific discourse, for example … tends to reduce as much as possible the semiotic component. On the contrary … [in] poetic language … the semiotic … tends to gain the upper hand” (Desire in Language 134).

事实上，符号学是婴儿在习得语言之前所能接触到的最早的“语言”——他们发出的声音和身体动作。他们通过与母亲身体相关的手势、节奏和其他非语言交流方式的接触来学习这种“语言”。因此，正是通过语言的符号学层面，我们才能在无意识中与我们认知前、语言前的经验保持持续的联系：与我们的本能驱力以及我们与母亲最早的联系。值得注意的是，克里斯蒂娃指出，我们的本能驱力和与母亲最早的联系都会在我们进入语言时代后受到压制。因为语言是父权制的统治领域，父权制控制着语言的象征或意义建构维度。然而，符号学却超越了父权制的程序设定，父权制无法直接控制的一切都会被压制。当然，克里斯蒂娃并非建议我们能够或应该回到婴儿时期的符号学状态，而是说我们能够且应该进入我们无意识中符号学所在的领域，例如通过艺术和文学等创造性手段。因为这些途径使我们能够以一种全新的方式与语言建立联系，从而克服父权制对男女思维方式的束缚。

Indeed, the semiotic is the first “speech” infants have available to them – the vocal sounds and bodily movements they produce – before they acquire language. And they learn this “speech” through their contact with the gestures, rhythms, and other nonverbal forms of communication associated with the mother’s body. Thus it is through the semiotic aspect of language that we remain, though unconsciously, in continual contact with our precognitive, preverbal experience: with our instinctual drives and with our earliest connections to our mothers. It is noteworthy, Kristeva observes, that both our instinctual drives and our earliest connections to our mothers are repressed by our entrance into language. For language is the dominion of patriarchy, which controls its symbolic, or meaning-making, dimension. The semiotic, however, remains beyond patriarchal programming, and whatever patriarchy can’t control outright, it represses. Of course, Kristeva is not suggesting that we can or should return to the semiotic state of the infant but that we can and should access that part of our unconscious where the semiotic resides, for example, through such creative means as art and literature. For these are the vehicles that allow us a new way to relate to language and to thereby overcome the stranglehold patriarchy has on the way women and men think.

在结束本节之前，我认为有必要谈谈一个你可能知道也可能不知道的问题。通常，当我们提到“法国女权主义”这个词时，我们想到的是法国精神分析女权主义所涉及的那些议题。对许多美国人来说，法国唯物主义女权主义者的工作并不容易被提及，因为除了西蒙娜·德·波伏娃的著作之外，她们的工作在主流学术界并没有像精神分析女权主义那样受到广泛的关注。当然，法国唯物主义女权主义有很多不同的流派。造成这种不平衡的原因有很多。当然，其中一个原因是，对批判理论传播影响最大的美国学术界分支更习惯于我们在法国精神分析女性主义中看到的那种抽象理论，因此更容易接受它。此外，我不得不注意到，法国精神分析女性主义的抽象倾向具有双重好处：(1) 对新手来说难以理解，从而巩固了那些已经在批判理论领域掌握学术权力的教授、理论家和文学评论家的地位；(2) 使法国女性主义容易受到嘲笑和否定，考虑到许多美国顶尖理论家的作品也常常相当抽象，这颇具讽刺意味。不幸的是，忽视或否定法国女性主义的愿望在美国学术界由来已久，甚至包括一些女性主义者和非女性主义者。

Before we leave this section, I think it’s important to address an issue of which you may or may not be aware. Often, when the phrase French feminism is used, we think of the kinds of topics that fall within the realm of French psychoanalytic feminism. For many Americans, the work done by French materialist feminists doesn’t come readily to mind because that work – with the exception of the writing of Simone de Beauvoir – hasn’t received as much press, so to speak, in mainstream academia as has psychoanalytic feminism. Certainly, there are a variety of reasons for this imbalance. Surely, one reason is the fact that the branch of American academia that has had the most influence over the dissemination of critical theory is more accustomed to the kind of abstract theorizing we find in French psychoanalytic feminism and therefore has welcomed it more readily. In addition, however, I can’t help but notice that French psychoanalytic feminism’s tendency toward abstraction has the double pay-off of (1) being difficult for novices to understand, thereby securing the position of those professors, theorists, and literary critics already holding academic power in the field of critical theory, and (2) rendering French feminism vulnerable to ridicule and dismissal, which is rather ironic given that the work of many leading American theorists is often rather abstract. Unfortunately, the desire to ignore or dismiss French feminism has been a desire of long standing in much of American academia, including among some feminists as well as nonfeminists.

的确，许多法国精神分析女性主义作品似乎主要是为那些具备相应教育背景的人而写的。其中一个原因是，它们大多借鉴、扩展或质疑两位法国思想家的著作，而这两位思想家的作品对于非专业人士来说相当晦涩难懂：一位是雅克·德里达，他提出了被称为解构主义的阐释方法；另一位是雅克·拉康，他对弗洛伊德精神分析的诠释，其逻辑若要充分理解，我认为需要对结构主义和解构主义都有所了解。（如果您有兴趣，可以阅读第二章关于拉康精神分析的内容，以及第七章和第八章分别关于结构主义和解构主义的内容。）事实上，大多数法国女性主义者的作品虽然可能不如上述精神分析女性主义者的作品那样抽象，但它们的写作也根植于一个美国文学专业的学生可能并不熟悉的哲学传统之中。所以，当你第一次阅读法国女权主义者的作品时，不要感到畏惧。无论她们的哲学倾向如何，她们并非有意排斥你。就像她们借鉴并常常与之持不同意见的哲学家一样，她们也在努力开拓新的领域，开启新的思维方式。我希望你也能认同，学习新的思维方式虽然困难，但绝对值得我们付出努力。

It’s true that much French psychoanalytic feminism does seem to have been written primarily for people who have the educational background to comprehend it. Among other factors, most of it draws on, extends, or quarrels with the work of two French thinkers whose work is quite difficult for the uninitiated to understand: Jacques Derrida, who came up with the interpretive approach called deconstruction, and Jacques Lacan, who offers us an interpretation of Freudian psychoanalysis the logic of which, if we are to reap its full benefit, requires, I think, an understanding of both structuralism and deconstruction. (If you wish, you can read about Lacanian psychoanalysis in Chapter 2 and about structuralism and deconstruction in Chapters 7 and 8, respectively.) In fact, most French feminists, though their work may be less abstract than that of the psychoanalytic feminists discussed above, write within a philosophical tradition with which students of literature in America might not be acquainted. So don’t be put off when you first read the work of French feminists for yourself. Whatever their philosophical orientation may be, they’re not trying to exclude you. Like the philosophers upon whom they draw and with whom they often disagree, they’re trying to break new ground and open up new ways of thinking. And I hope you’ll agree that learning to think in new ways is a task that, though difficult, is well worth our effort.

多元文化女权主义

Multicultural feminism

认识到自身的主体性——正如我们之前提到的，这是女权主义的目标之一——变得尤为重要，因为一直以来在美国女性运动中占据最显眼领导地位的白人、中产阶级、异性恋女权主义者，终于意识到她们的政策和实践反映了她们自身的经历，却忽视了有色人种女性、女同性恋者以及贫困、受教育程度低的女性（无论她们身处美国还是世界各地）的经历。虽然所有女性都受到父权制压迫，但每个女性的……具体需求、愿望和问题很大程度上受其种族、社会经济阶层、性取向、教育经历、宗教、国籍和地理位置的影响。
