Awareness of one’s own subjectivity, which as we noted earlier is a feminist goal, has become especially important as white, middle-class, heterosexual feminists, who have always held the most visible positions of leadership in women’s movements in the United States, are finally recognizing the ways in which their policies and practices have reflected their own experiences while ignoring the experiences of women of color, lesbians, and poor, undereducated women both in America and throughout the world. While all women are subject to patriarchal oppression, each woman’s specific needs, desires, and problems are greatly shaped by her race, socioeconomic class, sexual orientation, educational experience, religion, nationality, and geographic location.

首先，父权制在不同国家的运作方式各不相同：美国的父权制与印度、墨西哥或伊朗等国的父权制存在显著差异。此外，即使在同一个国家内部，文化差异也会影响女性对父权制的体验。例如，在美国，有色人种女性对父权制的体验与她们遭受的种族歧视密不可分（参见第十一章）；女同性恋者对父权制的体验与她们遭受的异性恋霸权密不可分（参见第十章）；贫困女性对父权制的体验与她们遭受的阶级歧视密不可分（参见第三章）；等等。你可以想象，如果女性同时属于上述三个或更多类别，她们的生活中将会面临多么复杂的压迫。因此，促进姐妹情谊——即基于对共同经历和目标的认识而建立的女性之间的心理和政治联系——必须包括尊重和关注女性之间的个体差异，以及在女权主义领导层中不同文化群体之间公平分配权力。

For one thing, patriarchy operates differently in different countries: there are significant differences between patriarchy in the United States and patriarchy in, say, India, Mexico, or Iran. Furthermore, even within the borders of a single country, cultural differences affect women’s experience of patriarchy. In the United States, for example, the experience of patriarchy for women of color is inseparable from their experience of racism (see Chapter 11); lesbians’ experience of patriarchy is inseparable from their experience of heterosexism (see Chapter 10); poor women’s experience of patriarchy is inseparable from their experience of classism (see Chapter 3); and so forth. And you can imagine the complex operations of oppression in the lives of women who belong to three or more of these categories. Therefore, the promotion of sisterhood – psychological and political bonding among women based on the recognition of common experiences and goals – must include respect for and attention to individual differences among women as well as an equitable distribution of power among various cultural groups within feminist leadership.

非裔美国女权主义者尤其有助于揭示主流白人女权主义者忽视自身文化经验的政治和理论局限性。例如，黑人女权主义者分析了性别压迫无法脱离种族压迫而得到理解的种种方式。黑人女权主义者指出，黑人女性遭受父权制压迫，不仅因为她是女性，更因为她是黑人女性——在美国历史上，黑人女性这一群体一直被认为不如白人女性有价值。维多利亚时代白人对“真正女性”的理想化定义——顺从、柔弱、性纯洁——至今仍影响着父权制思想，这种定义从根本上排除了黑人女性以及所有种族的贫困女性，因为她们的生存需要艰苦的体力劳动，并且容易遭受强奸和职场性剥削。这种逻辑循环往复，且致命：一个因经济状况被迫外出从事繁重体力劳动、成为性侵犯受害者的女性，被定义为“非女性”，因此不值得受到保护，免受剥削。这种观点在男性中普遍存在，无论白人还是黑人，白人女性也持有这种观点。因此，黑人女性陷入了两难境地。她们既无法指望白人女性给予她们性别上的支持，也无法指望黑人男性给予她们种族上的支持，而这两个群体本应是她们可以依靠的。不幸的是，这种困境至今仍然存在。白人主流女权主义虽然倾向于因为种族原因而边缘化黑人女性，却仍然鼓励她们优先考虑性别问题而非种族问题。有人认为，黑人女性遭受的压迫更多地源于性别歧视而非种族歧视。与此同时，黑人男性群体虽然常常因为性别而边缘化黑人女性，却仍然鼓励她们优先考虑种族问题而非性别问题，并声称黑人女性遭受的压迫更多地源于种族歧视而非性别歧视。正如洛林·贝瑟尔所观察到的，对这种双重压迫的理解构成了非裔美国女性主义批评的基础：

African American feminists have been especially helpful in revealing the political and theoretical limitations inherent in white mainstream feminists’ neglect of cultural experiences different from their own. For example, black feminists have analyzed the ways in which gender oppression cannot be understood apart from racial oppression. A black woman is oppressed by patriarchy, black feminists observe, not just because she’s a woman but because she’s a black woman, a category that has been defined historically in America as less valuable than the category of white woman. The white Victorian ideal of the “true woman” as submissive, fragile, and sexually pure, which still influences patriarchal thinking today, excluded by definition black women and poor women of all races whose survival demanded hard physical labor and who were vulnerable to rape and to sexual exploitation in the workplace. The logic was circular and deadly: a woman whose economic situation forced her into hard labor outside the home and made her the victim of sexual predators was defined as unwomanly and therefore unworthy of protection from those who exploited her. This view was widely held by men, both white and black, and by white women as well. Black women, therefore, were in a double bind. They could expect neither gender solidarity from white women nor racial solidarity from black men, the two groups on whom they should have been able to count for help. Unfortunately, this dilemma persists today. White mainstream feminism, while it has tended to marginalize black women because of their race, nevertheless encourages them to prioritize gender issues over racial issues, arguing that black women are oppressed more by sexism than by racism. At the same time, the black male community, while it has tended to marginalize black women because of their gender, nevertheless encourages them to prioritize racial issues over gender issues, arguing that black women are oppressed more by racism than by sexism. As Lorraine Bethel observes, an understanding of this double oppression forms the basis of African American feminist criticism:

黑人女性主义文学批评提供了一个框架，用于识别那些试图在种族/性别压迫下构建文化认同文学的作家们所面临的共同社会美学问题。它融合了政治分析，使我们能够理解和欣赏黑人女性在建立各种艺术和文学传统方面所取得的卓越成就，并理解她们的特质和感性。这种理解需要我们意识到这些艺术家在充斥着制度化和暴力仇恨的社会中，每天所遭受的压迫，这种仇恨既针对她们的黑皮肤，也针对她们的女性身体。培养和保持这种意识是黑人女性主义的基本原则。

Black feminist literary criticism offers a framework for identifying the common socio-aesthetic problems of authors who attempt to fashion a literature of cultural identity in the midst of racial/sexual oppression. It incorporates a political analysis that enables us to comprehend and appreciate the incredible achievements Black women … made in establishing artistic and literary traditions of any sort, and to understand their qualities and sensibilities. Such understanding requires a consciousness of the oppression these artists faced daily in a society full of institutionalized and violent hatred for both their Black skins and their female bodies. Developing and maintaining this consciousness is a basic tenet of Black feminism.

（178）

(178)

另一方面，一些黑人女性认为女权主义在黑人社区中造成了分裂。因此，她们要么放弃了女权主义，要么寻求将其与黑人社区的关切相调和的方法，例如爱丽丝·沃克（Alice Walker）就称自己为“女性主义者”（womanist）（xi），因为她致力于维护黑人社群（包括男性和女性）的生存和完整，促进对话和社群建设，并重视女性及其从事的各种工作。同样，正如卡罗琳·德纳德（Carolyn Denard）所指出的，许多非裔美国女性“倡导所谓的族裔文化女权主义”（172），这种女权主义“更关注她们自身族群的特定女性文化价值观，而非女性的普遍价值观”（171）。德纳尔以托妮·莫里森的小说为例来阐释这一观点，她解释说，族裔文化女权主义承认性别歧视对有色人种女性造成的伤害，无论是在她们的族裔群体内部还是外部，但它“并不提倡将……使黑人女性与其族群疏离的政治女权主义作为解决她们所受压迫的方案”（172）。此外，族裔文化女权主义“颂扬黑人女性在遭受压迫的情况下，甚至正是因为遭受压迫而发展出的独特女性文化价值观”（172）。

On the other hand, some black women feel that feminism is a divisive force in the black community. As a result, some have either abandoned feminism or sought ways to reconcile it with the concerns of the black community, as Alice Walker did when she called herself a “womanist” (xi) because she works for the survival and wholeness of her people, men and women both, and for the promotion of dialogue and community as well as for the valorization of women and of all the varieties of work women perform. Similarly, as Carolyn Denard points out, many African American women “advocate what may be called ethnic cultural feminism” (172), which is “concerned more with the particular female cultural values of their own ethnic group rather than with those of women in general” (171). Drawing on the novels of Toni Morrison to illustrate this approach, Denard explains that ethnic cultural feminism acknowledges the damaging effects of sexism on women of color, both inside and outside their ethnic community, but it “does not advocate as a solution to their oppression [a] … political feminism that alienates black women from their ethnic group” (172). Furthermore, ethnic cultural feminism “celebrat[es] the unique feminine cultural values that black women have developed in spite of and often because of their oppression” (172).

无论黑人女性主义批评家在文学分析中秉持何种理论偏好，她们的解读往往都体现了在文化语境中理解性别议题的重要性。鉴于某些文化群体拥有其自身的文学批评范畴，而且一些女性的关注点可能在不止一个范畴中得到体现，因此，不妨在此稍作停留，了解一下这些范畴的具体内容。

Whatever theoretical preferences black feminist critics bring to their analyses of literature, their interpretations often demonstrate the importance of understanding gender issues in cultural context. Given that some cultural groups have their own categories of literary criticism and that some women may find their concerns addressed in more than one category, it might be useful to pause here and note what some of those categories are.

根据其理论取向，探讨女性问题的文学批评可能属于一个或多个不同的范畴。其中包括：女性主义批评、非裔美国人批评（研究非裔美国人的作品，并将其置于非裔美国人的经验、历史和文学传统的语境中进行考察）、女同性恋批评、马克思主义批评和后殖民批评（研究在反抗殖民统治的文化背景下发展起来的作品，例如，1947年之前一直被英国统治的印度作家的作品）。当然，任何关注特定族裔女性作家的文学批评都会涉及女性议题：例如，我们未提及的奇卡纳女性、拉丁裔女性、美洲原住民女性和亚裔美国女性。尽管所有这些类别都可能涉及女性的经验，但一般来说，只有当女性主义视角有助于解读时，一篇批评作品才会被称为女性主义批评。显然，这些类别很容易重叠，因此，我们经常会发现一些文学批评家自认为是某种混合型批评家，例如马克思主义女性主义批评家或女同性恋女性主义奇卡纳批评家。

Depending on its theoretical orientation, literary criticism that addresses women’s issues may fall under one or more different headings. Among them are feminist criticism, African American criticism (which studies, among other things, works by African Americans within the context of African American experience, history, and literary traditions), lesbian criticism, Marxist criticism, and postcolonial criticism (which studies, among other things, works that have emerged from cultures that developed in response to colonial domination, for example, works by writers from India, which was controlled by Britain until 1947). Of course, women’s issues will also be addressed in any literary criticism that focuses on women writers from a particular ethnic group: for example, to name a few we haven’t mentioned, Chicanas, Latinas, Native American women, and Asian American women. Although all of these categories may address women’s experience, generally speaking it is only when a feminist perspective helps guide the interpretation that a piece of criticism is referred to as feminist. Clearly, these categories easily overlap, and it is not unusual to find literary critics who consider themselves hybrids of a sort, for example, Marxist-feminist or lesbian-feminist-Chicana critics.

性别研究与女权主义

Gender studies and feminism

正如我们在本章中所看到的，女性主义分析非常关注性别——即社会对女性气质和男性气质的定义——在我们日常生活中所扮演的巨大角色。例如，我们的性别在塑造我们的个人身份认同中起着关键作用：它影响着我们的自我认知以及我们与他人的关系。我们的性别也深刻地影响着他人以及整个社会对待我们的方式，因为它体现在医疗行业、法律、教育体系以及我们文化中的招聘和雇佣实践等机构中。此外，酷儿理论（您可以在第十章“女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评”中阅读到）在过去几年中也引起了人们对性别问题的广泛关注，它质疑了我们社会关于性和性别的异性恋假设，例如，男性“天生具有阳刚之气”，女性“天生具有阴柔之美”。因此，性别研究作为一个独立的学科领域应运而生，专门研究这些以及所有与性别相关的主题，这似乎合乎逻辑。事实上，你可能已经修读过名为“性别研究”或“女性与性别研究”的课程：后者通常用于那些主要关注性别与父权制对女性压迫之间关系的课程。

As we have seen throughout this chapter, feminist analysis focuses a good deal on the enormous role played by gender – that is, by a society’s definitions of femininity and masculinity – in our daily lives. For example, our gender plays a key role in forming our individual identity: both our self-perception and the way we relate to others. And our gender strongly influences how we are treated by others and by society as a whole as it is embodied in such institutions as the medical profession, the law, the educational system, and our culture’s hiring and employment practices. In addition, queer theory, which you can read about in Chapter 10 (“Lesbian, gay, and queer criticism”), has brought a good deal of attention to gender issues over the last several years by raising questions concerning our society’s heterosexual assumptions about sexuality and gender, for example, its assumption that males are “naturally masculine” and that females are “naturally feminine.” It seems logical, then, that gender has emerged as a field of study in its own right devoted to these and to all topics pertaining to gender. Indeed, you may already have taken a course called Gender Studies or Women and Gender Studies: the latter title is often given to courses about gender when their primary focus is the relationship between gender and the patriarchal oppression of women.

就我们的目的而言，理解性别研究探讨的一些主要议题，对于我们理解女权主义关注点如何持续发展和扩展，是十分有益且或许不可或缺的。性别研究中突出的议题包括以下几个相互交织的主题：（1）父权制关于性别和性别角色的假设，这些假设持续压迫着女性；（2）对当前将性别概念化为女性或男性的方式的替代方案；（3）生理性别与社会性别之间的关系（生理性别与社会性别之间的关系）。（4）我们身体的生物学构造方式以及我们被赋予的性别），以及（5）性与性别之间的关系（我们的性取向与我们在性别方面被看待的方式之间的关系）。当然，我们在本章中已经讨论了许多父权制关于性别和性别角色的假设如何继续压迫女性，所以现在让我们来看看剩下的三个方面。

For our purposes, an understanding of some of the major issues addressed by gender studies is a useful and perhaps indispensable part of our understanding of the ways in which feminist concerns are continuing to evolve and expand. Among other issues that figure prominently in gender studies are the following overlapping topics: (1) patriarchal assumptions about gender and gender roles that continue to oppress women, (2) alternatives to the current way we conceptualize gender as either feminine or masculine, (3) the relationship between sex and gender (between the ways our bodies are biologically constructed and the genders to which we are assigned), and (4) the relationship between sexuality and gender (between our sexual orientation and the ways in which we are viewed in terms of gender). Of course, we’ve discussed throughout this chapter many of the ways in which patriarchal assumptions about gender and gender roles continue to oppress women, so let’s take a look now at each of the three remaining areas.

首先，我们需要寻找替代当前性别观念的方案，因为我们现有的性别观念包含诸多谬误。尽管性别研究成果，如同其他领域的研究成果一样，往往复杂且相互矛盾，但它们仍然能够提醒我们，我们曾经将太多广为流传却未经证实的观点和关于性别的迷思奉为事实。让我举两个引人注目的例子，首先是关于睾酮（即“男性激素”）生物学作用的一个观点，我认为我们大多数人都认同这个观点。

To begin, we need alternatives to the current way we think about gender because the current way we think about gender includes so many inaccuracies. Although research findings about gender, just like research findings in every field, often can be complex and contradictory, they can nevertheless alert us to the ways in which we’ve taken as facts too many widely held but unsubstantiated opinions and myths about gender. Let me cite just two striking examples, starting with a belief that I think most of us share about the biological operations of testosterone, or the “male hormone.”

我们常常会说或听到这样的说法：当男性表现出过度或不恰当的攻击性行为时，“哦，他只是睾酮分泌过多。”也就是说，男性的攻击性行为通常被认为是一种本能，而不是成长经历、家庭心理动态、接触危险环境等社会因素的结果。一旦某种行为被认为是本能的，并与性别联系起来，我们中的许多人就很难用其他视角来看待它。然而，罗伯特·M·萨波尔斯基指出，关于男性睾酮水平的研究仅限于表明睾酮水平升高伴随着攻击性增强。也就是说，没有研究表明睾酮水平升高会导致攻击性；这仅仅是人们的臆测。萨波尔斯基的研究表明，事实上，睾酮并不会增强攻击性。相反，“攻击性会促进睾酮分泌”（16）。萨波尔斯基指出，“一定量的睾酮”对于“正常的攻击行为”是必要的（17），但所需量的范围非常广泛。“大约在正常水平的20%到两倍正常水平之间”（17），都能在男性中产生大致相同的正常攻击行为。因此，即使我们知道特定男性群体中每个个体的睾酮水平，也无法预测他们的攻击性，因为正常睾酮水平的范围实在太广了。萨波尔斯基指出，过量的睾酮会“加剧已有的攻击性”（17，萨波尔斯基斜体字），但它本身并不会导致攻击性。换句话说，只有当攻击性是由“攻击行为发生的社会因素和环境”（萨波尔斯基 19）引发时，睾酮才会允许攻击行为的发生。

We’ve often said or heard it said about a male exhibiting overly or inappropriately aggressive behavior, “Oh, he just has too much testosterone.” That is, aggressive behavior in males is generally considered an instinct rather than a product of such social factors as upbringing, psychological dynamics in the home, exposure to a dangerous environment outside the home, and the like. And once a behavior is considered instinctual and linked to gender, it is difficult for many of us to see it in any other light. Robert M. Sapolsky points out, however, that studies of testosterone levels in males have been limited to showing merely that increased testosterone levels accompany increased aggression. That is, there is no research indicating that increased testosterone levels cause aggression; it is merely assumed that they do so. Sapolsky’s research indicates that, in fact, testosterone does not elevate aggression. Rather, “aggression elevates testosterone secretion” (16). Sapolsky observes that “[s]ome testosterone” is necessary for “normal aggressive behavior” (17), but the range of what is necessary is very wide. “[A]nywhere from roughly 20 percent of normal to twice normal” (17) produces roughly the same amount of normal aggressive behavior in males. So even if we know the testosterone level for each individual in a given group of males, we will not be able to predict their aggression because the range of what is considered a normal amount of testosterone is so wide. Excessive amounts of testosterone, Sapolsky notes, can “exaggerat[e] the aggression that’s already there” (17, Sapolsky’s italics), but it doesn’t cause aggression. In other words, testosterone permits aggression to occur only if that aggression is elicited by “the social factors and environment in which [aggression] occurs” (Sapolsky 19).

正如关于睾酮在男性攻击性中所起作用的未经证实的观点被广泛接受为事实一样——对我们许多人来说，这种作用也与男性作为养家糊口者和保护家庭的“本能”联系在一起——关于母性本能对女性的作用的未经证实的观点也被广泛接受为事实。同样，因为照顾，尤其是照顾……对婴儿和幼儿的关爱，一直被认为是女性的本能，因此我们很多人很难从其他角度看待它。然而，正如琳达·布兰农所指出的，“关于……情绪的研究表明，在情绪的内在体验方面，性别差异可能很小。性别差异体现在情绪的表达方式和时间上”（213），而不是情绪的感受方式和时间上。”她观察到，具体来说，布兰农发现，“关于对婴儿反应的性别差异的研究表明，在自我报告中存在差异，但在生理指标上则没有差异”（214）。因此，“女孩和女性对婴儿表现出更多的反应，因为她们认为自己应该这样做，而……男孩和男性出于同样的原因，对婴儿的反应较少”（214）。

Just as unsubstantiated opinion has been widely accepted as fact concerning the role of testosterone in male aggression – a role that is also associated, for many of us, with the male “instinct” to be the breadwinner and to protect the home – so has unsubstantiated opinion been widely accepted as fact concerning the role of the maternal instinct in females. Again, because caregiving, especially caregiving to infants and young children, has been labeled a female instinct, it is difficult for many of us to consider it in any other light. As Linda Brannon notes, however, “research on … emotion has revealed that there may be few gender differences in the inner experience of emotion. Gender differences appear in how and when emotion is displayed” (213), she observes, rather than in how and when emotion is felt. Specifically, Brannon finds that “[r]esearch on gender differences in responsiveness to babies has shown differences in self-reports, but not in physiological measures, of responses to babies” (214). Thus, “girls and women show more responsiveness to babies because they believe they should, and … boys and men show less responsiveness for the same reasons” (214).

当然，女性在育儿方面仍然比男性投入更多，而那些照顾孩子的女性也表示，她们在照顾孩子的过程中既体验到极大的乐趣，也感受到诸多烦恼。然而，值得注意的是，那些花费大量时间照顾孩子的男性也常常表达类似的感受（Brannon 214）。事实上，我们大多数人都看到了父亲越来越多地参与到孩子的生活中这一趋势。此外，Brannon指出，“研究表明……母性本能的概念并没有生物学依据来解释照护行为，而且男性和女性在养育子女方面有着相似的情感”（214）。虽然没有人想说女性不是优秀的照护者，但更准确的说法是，许多女性和男性都是优秀的照护者，并且非常享受这个角色；然而与此同时，如果可以选择的话，许多女性和男性并不会把照顾孩子作为他们在家庭中的主要职责。简而言之，养育子女并非一种与性别有生物学联系的角色，尽管许多人长期以来一直认为它与性别有关。

Of course, women are still much more involved in childcare than men, and women who take care of children report that they experience both a great deal of pleasure and a great deal of irritation in caring for them. It is interesting to note, however, that men who spend a great deal of time caring for children often report similar responses (Brannon 214). Indeed, most of us have seen the growing trend in fathers’ increased involvement in the lives of their children. Moreover, Brannon points out, “research indicates that … the concept of maternal instinct has no support as a biologically based explanation for caregiving, and both men and women have similar emotions related to nurturing” (214). While no one is trying to say that women are not good caregivers to children, a more accurate statement is that many women and men are good caregivers to children and enjoy that role a great deal; at the same time, however, many women and men wouldn’t choose that role as their primary function in the household if they had a choice. In short, nurturing is not a role biologically linked to sex although many people long have believed it to be.

以上两个例子都表明，性别是社会建构的产物，而非生物学上的必然结果：男女通常会按照其被赋予的性别规范行事，这是因为他们受到社会规范的约束，而非出于天性。然而，如果说性别研究中有一个维度更能促使我们重新思考传统的性别观念，那就是跨文化性别研究。正如琼·Z·斯佩德和凯瑟琳·G·瓦伦丁所指出的，“不同文化中性别定义和表达方式的差异和流动性表明，美国的性别体系并非普世通用”（5）。

Both of the examples just given suggest that gender is socially constructed rather than a matter of biology: women and men usually behave in ways associated with their assigned gender because they are socially programmed to do so, not because it is natural for them to do so. However, if there is one dimension of gender studies that is perhaps even more capable of making us rethink our conventional way of viewing gender, it is cross-cultural studies in gender. For as Joan Z. Spade and Catherine G. Valentine point out, “The variations and fluidity in the definitions and expressions of gender across cultures illustrate that the American gender system is not universal” (5).

美国的性别体系被称为二元体系，因为它由男性和女性两种性别构成，这两种性别基于男性和女性两种生理性别，并且这两种性别被认为是截然相反的两极。没有中间地带：你要么是男性，要么是女性，因为你要么是男性，要么是女性；如果你不属于这两种性别中的任何一种，那么你肯定有问题。然而，在许多其他文化中，存在着非二元的性别体系。在过去和现在存在的众多文化中，都存在着非二元的性别体系。对于那些至今仍然存在的性别观念，让我们简要地看一下几个有趣的例子。具体来说，让我们来看看东南亚的两种文化，在这些文化中，男性和女性被认为相似之处远大于差异——以至于他们不被视为我们通常意义上的不同性别——以及美洲原住民文化，在这些文化中，存在两种以上的性别。

The American gender system is referred to as a binary system because it consists of two genders, masculine and feminine, that are based on two sexes, male and female, and because those two genders are considered polar opposites. There is no in-between: you’re either masculine or feminine because you’re either male or female, and if you’re not one or the other of these two genders, then there must by something wrong with you. In numerous other cultures, however, there are gender systems that are not binary. Among the many that have existed in the past and those that still exist today, let’s take a brief look at a few interesting examples. Specifically, let’s take a look at two Southeast Asian cultures in which men and women are considered more alike than different – so much so that they are not considered different genders in our sense of the term – and at Native American cultures in which there are more than two genders.

例如，克里斯汀·赫利韦尔观察到，东南亚许多社会强调男女之间的相似之处而非差异。她以印度尼西亚的格莱族为例，指出那里的人们重视男女之间的相似性而非差异性。

Christine Helliwell, for instance, observes that there are many societies in Southeast Asia that emphasize the similarities between men and women rather than their differences. As one example, she points to the Gerai people of Indonesia, where

在格莱人眼中，不存在二元对立的男性气质和女性气质。相反，男性和女性被认为拥有相同的能力和倾向（尤其是不良行为的倾向）。……就养育这一核心品质而言（这或许是格莱人最珍视的品质），……格莱人认为男性和女性之间没有区别。

there is no sense of a dichotomized [separated into two polar opposites] masculinity and femininity. Rather, men and women are seen to have the same kinds of capacities and proclivities [inclinations, especially toward objectionable behavior]. … [I]n terms of the central quality of nurturance (perhaps the most valued quality in Gerai) … Gerai people see no difference between men and women.

（126）

(126)

事实上，格莱族男女的性器官也被“明确地概念化为相同……它们都具有相同的……圆锥形，底部较窄，顶部较宽”；区别仅仅在于女性的性器官位于“体内​​”，而男性的性器官位于“体外”（Helliwell 127）。如果您难以想象这种相似性，不妨将阴茎比作产道，将睾丸比作卵巢：从整体上看，它们的结构大致相同；只是位置不同而已。

In fact, even the sexual organs of Gerai men and women are “explicitly conceptualized as the same. … [T]hey have the same … conical shape, narrower at the base and wider at the top”; the difference is simply that women’s sexual organs are “inside the body” while men’s are “outside the body” (Helliwell 127). In case you have difficulty visualizing this similarity, you might imagine the penis as analogous to the birth canal and the testicles as analogous to the ovaries: the overall, bird’s-eye-view formation is roughly the same; it’s just the location that’s different.

玛丽亚·亚历山德拉·莱波夫斯基以瓦纳蒂奈岛居民为例，进一步阐释了男女之间的相似之处——这次是从某些文化中存在的权力动态角度来看。瓦纳蒂奈岛位于新几内亚附近，是一个小岛。在那里，“男性优越或凌驾于女性之上的权威观念明显缺失，性别平等的观念则清晰明确”（150）。在这个文化中，男女对自己的劳动及其产出拥有平等的权利，平等地积累物质财富，并平等地获得社会声望。“女性不被视为软弱或低人一等。男女都因其力量、智慧和慷慨等品质而受到赞扬”（莱波夫斯基 158）。正如格莱人和瓦纳蒂奈岛民的文化所表明的那样，我们不能声称男性主导地位是自然的或普遍的——尽管许多美国人确实这样声称——因此，我们也不能声称人类的支配行为在生物学上与性别有关。

Another useful illustration of the similarities between women and men – this time in terms of the power dynamics that can be found in some cultures – is offered by Maria Alexandra Lepowsky’s example of the people of Vanatinai, a small island near New Guinea, where “[i]deologies of male superiority or right of authority over women are notably absent, and ideologies of gender equivalence are clearly articulated” (150). Men and women in this culture have equal rights over their own labor and the products of their labor, equal access to the accumulation of material wealth, and equal access to the acquisition of prestige in the community. “Women are not characterized as weak or inferior. Women and men are valorized for the same qualities of strength, wisdom, and generosity” (Lepowsky 158). As both the cultures of the Gerai and of the Vanatinai Islanders illustrate, we can’t claim that male dominance is natural or universal – although many Americans do claim just that – and therefore we can’t claim that dominant behavior in human beings is biologically linked to sex.

在其他文化中，性别制度既非像当今美国实行的性别制度那样是二元的，也非像前文所述的两种性别制度那样是单一的——即没有显著的性别差异。如上所述。相比之下，一些文化将性别视为一个包含多种可能性的系统。例如，北美一百多个印第安部落就拥有多种性别体系，即包含两种以上性别的体系，尤其是在欧洲殖民者占领美洲之前。北美原住民部落往往以各自文化特有的方式定义性别，在性别观念中，他们对社会生活哪些方面最为重视也各不相同。然而，大多数北美原住民文化都包含以下三种或四种性别：（1）女性；（2）女性变体，或生理女性所扮演的不同性别角色；（3）男性；以及（4）男性变体，或生理男性所扮演的不同性别角色（Nanda 66）。

In other cultures, gender systems are neither binary, like the gender system in force in the United States today, nor what might be called unitary – that is, without significant gender differentiation – like the two gender systems described above. In contrast, some cultures see gender as a system of multiple possibilities. As one example among many, consider the hundred or more North American Indian societies that had multiple gender systems, that is, systems consisting of more than two genders, especially prior to the takeover of the Americas by European colonizers. Native North American societies tended to define gender in ways specific to their own cultures, differing in what aspects of social life were considered primary in their conceptions of gender. Yet most Native North American cultures included three or four of the following genders: (1) women; (2) female variants, or variant gender roles adopted by biological females; (3) men; and (4) male variants, or variant gender roles adopted by biological males (Nanda 66).

在北美原住民社会中，确定一个人的性别时，生理性别和性取向通常都不是主要因素。相反，职业兴趣和追求才是核心。服装有时也起到一定作用，尽管根据其所属文化的不同，那些扮演不同性别角色的人可能会穿着男女服装的任意组合。在一些北美印第安文化中，性别差异者在社群中扮演着重要的角色，例如治疗师或神圣仪式的执行者，因为性别差异与神圣的力量相关联，这在许多文化中都是如此。然而，无论如何，许多社群的成员都可以选择他们希望归属的性别，而无需考虑其生理构成（Nanda 66）。

In determining a person’s gender, neither biological sex nor sexual orientation was generally the primary factor in Native North American societies. Rather, occupational interests and pursuits were of central importance. Clothing sometimes played a role, although persons adopting variant gender roles might have worn, depending on the culture to which they belonged, any combination of men’s and women’s clothes. In some North American Indian cultures, gender variants played valued roles in the community, such as healers or performers of sacred ritual functions, because gender variance was associated, as it is in many cultures, with sacred power. Whatever the case, however, members of many communities could choose, irrespective of biological makeup, the gender to which they wished to belong (Nanda 66).

除了探索当前二元性别观念之外的其他可能性，性别理论家也对生理性别与社会性别之间的关系感兴趣：即我们身体的生物学构造与我们被赋予的性别之间的关系。正如朱迪思·洛伯所说，尽管人们普遍认为，

In addition to exploring alternatives to our current binary conception of gender, gender theorists are also interested in the relationship between sex and gender: between the ways in which our bodies are biologically constructed and the genders to which we are assigned. As Judith Lorber puts it, despite common belief,

性别和性取向都不是纯粹的[分离的、自主的、离散的]范畴。在性别分类（男性或女性）中，不一致的基因、生殖器和激素输入的组合被忽略，正如在性别地位（男性或女性）的社会建构中，不一致的生理、身份、性取向、外貌和行为的组合被忽略一样。

[n]either sex nor gender are pure [separate, autonomous, discrete] categories. Combinations of incongruous genes, genitalia, and hormonal input are ignored in sex categorization [as male or female], just as combinations of incongruous physiology, identity, sexuality, appearance, and behavior are ignored in the social construction of gender statuses [masculine or feminine].

（14）

(14)

简而言之，认为只有两种性别的整个观念都基于只有两种生理性别的观念。然而，来自不同领域的研究人员已经揭示，事实并非如此：生理性别并不能简单地归入两个截然相反的类别。更准确地说，美国社会效仿欧洲模式，强加了二元性别制度，尽管这种制度并不符合相当一部分人的实际情况。换句话说，并非生理性别类别将二元性别制度强加于美国人；而是美国人将二元性别制度强加于生理性别类别之上。

In short, the whole idea that there are only two genders is based on the idea that there are only two sexes. However, researchers from a variety of fields have revealed that such is not the case: biological sex does not fit neatly into two separate, opposite categories. It would be more accurate to say that, following the European model, American society has imposed the two-sex system despite the fact that this system does not fit a significant portion of the population. In other words, biological sex categories have not imposed the two-gender system on Americans; rather, Americans have imposed the two-gender system on biological sex categories.

据安妮·福斯托-斯特林（Anne Fausto-Sterling）所述，虽然完整的频率数据难以获取，但基于大量现有记录的合理估计表明，每年出生的所有儿童中约有1.7%是双性人（51），或者如各种性别理论家所称，是双性人或间性人。也就是说，双性人拥有男性和女性生殖器官、外生殖器、染色体和/或激素构成的某种组合。福斯托-斯特林指出，

According to Anne Fausto-Sterling, although complete frequency data is difficult to find, a reasonable estimate based on numerous available records indicates that approximately 1.7 percent of all children born each year are intersexual (51), or as various gender theorists refer to them, intersexed or intersex. That is, intersex individuals have some combination of male and female reproductive organs, genitals, chromosomal and/or hormonal makeup. Fausto-Sterling observes,

即使我们高估了两倍，也意味着每年有很多双性人出生。例如，按1.7%的比例计算，一个30万人口的城市将有5100名不同程度双性发育的人。相比之下，白化病（白化病患者没有色素，因此头发、皮肤和眼睛都是白色的）虽然在美国也相对少见，但大多数读者可能都见过。

Even if we’ve overestimated by a factor of two, that still means a lot of intersexual children are born each year. At the rate of 1.7 percent, for example, a city of 300,000 people would have 5,100 people with varying degrees of intersexual development. Compare this with albinism [an albino has no pigmentation and therefore has white hair, white skin, and red eyes], another relatively uncommon human trait [in the United States] but one that most readers can probably recall having seen.

（51）

(51)

我们之所以“看不到”福斯托-斯特林所指的众多双性人，并非仅仅因为涉及的身体部位通常位于体内或被衣物遮盖。正如莎伦·普里夫斯所指出的，我们根深蒂固地认为只有两种性别和两种相应的性别认同，以至于双性婴儿经常在父母不知情或未经同意的情况下，被迅速地通过手术改变体型，使其看起来像男性或女性（32）。

The reason we don’t “see” the numerous intersex individuals to whom Fausto-Sterling refers is not simply because the parts of the body involved are usually inside the body or hidden under clothing. Rather, as Sharon Preeves notes, so embedded is our belief that there are only two sexes and two corresponding genders, that intersex infants have been routinely, quickly, and often without their parents’ knowledge or consent, surgically altered to physically resemble either a male or a female (32).

如何给婴儿“确定性别”的决定通常基于外貌因素（孩子看起来是否“正常”？）和社会因素（如果孩子被确定为男孩，他成年后能否站着排尿，阴茎是否足够大以进行性行为？），而不是基于孩子在其他方面——化学、激素、基因——可能具有不同性别或两性特征的可能性。例如，一个双性婴儿可能具有男性基因（XY），但如果负责的医疗团队认为其阴茎部分过小，成年后不太可能被视为“正常”，并且可能无法站着排尿（例如，因为尿道口位于阴茎根部而不是顶端），那么这个婴儿很可能会被通过手术和激素治疗进行性别重建，成为女性。尽管有研究表明，婴儿阴茎或阴蒂的大小与其成年生殖器的大小无关（Preeves 33），但这种做法仍在继续。

The decisions on how to “sex” the infant are usually based on cosmetic factors (will the child look “normal”?) and social factors (if the child is sexed as a boy, will he be able to urinate standing up and will his penis be large enough as an adult to perform sexually?) rather than on the possibility that the child may be in every other respect – chemically, hormonally, genetically – a different sex or a combination of both sexes. For example, an intersex infant may have a male genetic makeup (xy), but if the penis part of its genitals is considered too small by the medical team in charge, unlikely to pass as “normal” when the child matures, and probably unable to urinate from a standing position (for example, because the urethra opens at the base of the penis instead of at the tip), the infant is most likely to be surgically and hormonally reconstructed as a female. This practice has continued despite studies showing that the size of an infant’s penis or clitoris is unrelated to the size of its adult genitals (Preeves 33).

据普里夫斯报道，直到上世纪90年代，跨性别维权人士（跨性别者的性别认同与其生理性别不符）仍然认为，双性人不应被视为异常，而应被视为属于不同性别类别的正常人。事实上，一些维权人士甚至提出，自然界中存在五种性别：（1）女性，（2）女性双性人（双性人）。（3）真性双性人（具有更突出或功能更佳的女性性器官的双性人），（4）男性双性人（具有更突出或功能更佳的男性性器官的双性人），以及（5）男性（Preeves 37）。

As recently as the 1990s, Preeves reports, transgender activists (a transgender person’s gender doesn’t match his or her biological sex) have argued that intersex individuals should not be seen as abnormalities but as normal people belonging to a different sex category. Some activists have, in fact, suggested that there are really five sexes that occur naturally: (1) female, (2) female intersex (an intersex person with more prominent or functional female sex organs), (3) true intersex (an intersex person with equally prominent or functional male and female sex organs), (4) male intersex (an intersex person with more prominent or functional male sex organs), and (5) male (Preeves 37).

或许最值得关注的并非双性人出生的频率（尽管其频率确实会让许多人感到惊讶），而是医疗界对此的反应。除非存在健康问题（例如尿道功能障碍），否则是否一定要如此急于进行手术？为什么不更普遍地先向父母提供教育资料，让他们有机会了解孩子性特征的诸多影响？为什么不立即将父母与双性儿童家长组织联系起来？或者更确切地说，为什么这类组织不存在——或者数量太少？为什么孩子在成长过程中不能选择了解自己的双性特征？如果手术是一种选择，为什么孩子不能在日后做出选择？

Perhaps the most striking point to consider here is not the frequency of intersex births, though their frequency will certainly come as a surprise to many of us, but the reaction of the medical profession to the situation. Unless there were a health consideration at stake (for example, a nonfunctioning urethra), does there have to be such a rush to surgery? Why isn’t it more common to first offer parents educational materials so they can have the opportunity to learn about the many ramifications of their child’s sexual makeup? Why aren’t parents immediately put in touch with an organization of parents with intersex children, or, more to the point, why do such organizations not – or not enough of them – exist? Why doesn’t the child, as it matures, have the option to learn about his or her intersexuality and, if a surgical change is an option, why can’t the child make the choice at a later point in time?

当然，造成这种情况的原因之一，或许可以称之为二元性别体系的专制。而且我认为，至少在某种程度上，社会对医疗行业施加的二元性别专制，与医疗行业对社会施加的专制如出一辙，这种怀疑是合理的。“我的孩子怎么了？”“医生治不好吗？”当许多父母被告知他们的新生儿是双性人时，这些问题肯定会涌上心头，因为我们都被社会灌输了一种二元性别体系的思维模式。然而，对许多性别理论家来说，问题在于父母往往被告知的并非是他们的婴儿是双性人，而是他们通常被告知婴儿患有生殖器先天缺陷，医生需要发现并恢复新生儿的“真实性别”（Fausto-Sterling 30）。这样的措辞又能给父母提供怎样的选择呢？

Surely the reasons why include what might be called the tyranny of the two-sex/two-gender system. And I think it’s reasonable to suspect that, at least to some extent, society practices the same two-sex/two-gender tyranny on the medical profession that the medical profession practices on society. “What’s wrong with my child?” “Can’t the doctor fix it?” Surely these questions leap to the minds of many parents who are told that their newborns are intersex because we’re all socially programmed to think within the confines of our binary sex/gender system. For many gender theorists, however, the problem is that parents too often are not told that their infants are intersex. Rather, they’re generally told that their infants have a genital birth defect and that the doctors need to discover and restore the newborn’s “true sex” (Fausto-Sterling 30). What kind of choice can that language possibly offer parents?

好消息是，医学界的态度正在转变。医生和科学家已经开始意识到，不应该对婴儿进行生殖器改变手术。许多人认为，最好等到孩子自我认同为男孩或女孩，或者等到父母和双性儿童有时间了解他们的选择之后再进行手术。因为一旦手术进行，可能很难甚至不可能逆转。

The good news is that attitudes are changing in the medical profession. Doctors and scientists have begun to realize that genital altering surgery should not be performed on infants. Many believe that it is best to wait, for example, until the child self-identifies as a boy or a girl or until parents and intersex children have time to learn about their options. For once a surgery is performed, it may be difficult or impossible to undo it.2

最后，许多性别理论家对性取向与性别之间的关系很感兴趣，也就是我们的性取向与我们被赋予的性别角色之间的关系。一方面，许多女同性恋、男同性恋、双性恋和跨性别者（LGBT）所遭受的残酷和不公平待遇，很大程度上是因为他们往往不符合传统的性别行为或外貌。事实上，许多性别理论家都认同，“二元对立的女性气质和男性气质的理解塑造了我们对性别的认知……异性恋的假设决定了我们构建女性气质和男性气质的方式”（Cranny-Francis等人，第ix页）。换句话说，对儿童进行性别化（在社会和心理层面上培养儿童以符合其传统的性别角色）始终是异性恋的性别化。因此，“性别/性取向系统不仅决定了身体的性别，也决定了他们可能拥有的欲望类型”（Cranny-Francis等人，第6页）。

Finally, many gender theorists are interested in the relationship between sexuality and gender, that is, between our sexual orientation and the ways in which we are viewed in terms of gender. For one thing, much of the cruel and unfair treatment many lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender (LGBT) individuals endure is due largely to the fact that they often don’t conform to traditional gender behavior or appearance. In fact, many gender theorists agree that while “binaristic understandings of femininity and masculinity shape the ways we perceive gender … the assumption of heterosexuality determines the ways we constitute that femininity and masculinity” (Cranny-Francis et al. ix). In other words, gendering a child (raising a child to conform to his or her traditional gender role both socially and psychologically) is always heterosexual gendering. Thus, “the sex/gender system establishes not only the sex of bodies but also the kinds of desire they can have” (Cranny-Francis et al. 6).

在此背景下，值得关注的是一些西欧文化古代医学和神学著作中揭示的一段重要历史。莎伦·普里夫斯指出，这些著作表明，在过去的几个世纪里，一些西欧文化将双性人视为第三性别，有时被视为正常，有时被视为异常，但无论如何都承认他们属于一个独特的性别（34）。此外，双性人通常被允许选择自己的性别、性别认同和性取向。这听起来不错，但真正有趣的地方在于：双性人被承认为第三性别——既非男性也非女性——但他们仍然必须选择认同自己为男性或女性。一旦做出选择，他们就不能改变主意。因此，这一体系不仅受到至今仍主导我们文化的二元性别/性别认同观念的控制，而且还受到持续困扰我们的恐同症的控制。正如普里夫斯指出的那样，这种选择一种性别并坚持下去的态度，是通过法律强制执行的，其依据是，如果没有这项法律，双性人可以选择成为女人（只使用她的女性生殖器），嫁给一个男人，然后改变主意选择成为男人（使用她的男性生殖器），在这种情况下，一对已婚夫妇将由两个男人组成（36）。

It’s interesting to consider, in this context, a noteworthy piece of history revealed in old medical and theological writings of some Western European cultures. These writings indicate, Sharon Preeves reports, that in centuries past some Western European cultures considered intersex people members of a third sex, sometimes viewed as normal, sometimes viewed as abnormal, but nevertheless acknowledged as belonging to a unique sex (34). In addition, intersex people were usually allowed to choose their sex, gender, and sexuality. Sounds good, but here’s where things really get interesting. Consider it: intersex people were acknowledged as members of a third sex – not male or female – but they nevertheless had to choose to identify themselves as either male or female. And once they made their choice, they were not allowed to change their minds. So not only was this system controlled by the binary sex/gender mind-set that still controls our culture today, but it was also controlled by the homophobia that continues to plague us. For as Preeves points out, this pick-one-sex-and-stick-to-it attitude, which was enforced legally, was based on the fear that, without this law, an intersex person could choose to be a woman (use her female genitals only), marry a man, then change her mind and choose to be a man (use her male genitals), in which case a married couple would consist of two men (36).

在结束这个话题之前，我们必须记住，谈论性和性别，我们实际上是在谈论人以及他们的日常生活。因此，让我们思考一下那些觉得自己无法完全融入我们这种传统的异性恋二元性别体系的人们的经历。尽管在女权主义、性别研究和酷儿理论等领域取得了进步，但我们的社会仍然固守着“性”和“性别”这两个词本质上是同一个意思的观念，认为只有符合传统男性/女性分类的异性恋者才值得关注。这种现状忽略了理论进步，例如，性别认同、雌雄同体以及被称为“性别认同质疑”的性别认同范畴等概念的出现。仅这三个例子就极大地提升了我们对性别概念复杂性的理解。“性别认同”一词意味着一个人的性别认同可能与其生理性别不符——实际上，可能与任何一种生理性别都不符——因为如果两者总是一致，我们就无需“性别认同”这个概念了。“雌雄同体”则告诉我们，无论生理性别如何，一个人的性别认同可能包含女性化和男性化行为的某种组合。最后，“质疑”一词为那些感到迷茫的人打开了一扇门。他们的性取向，以及“性别认同……可能没有现有标签”的人（Perry 和 Ballard-Reisch 30）。

Before we leave this topic, it’s important to remember that, in talking about sex and gender, we’re talking about people and how they live their daily lives. So let’s give some thought to the experience of people who don’t feel they fit neatly into a traditional heterosexual binary sex/gender system like ours. For despite the progress made in such fields as feminism, gender studies, and queer theory, our society persists in thinking that the words sex and gender mean basically the same thing and that the only people worth thinking about are the straight people who fit the traditional masculine-male/feminine-female categories. This state of affairs ignores the theoretical progress that has given us, for example, such concepts as gender identity, androgyny, and the category of sex/gender identification called questioning. Consider the enormous contribution that these three examples alone offer us in terms of our ability to understand the complexity of the concept of gender. The term gender identity implies that one’s gender may not match one’s biological sex – indeed, may not match either primary biological sex – for if it always did, we wouldn’t need the term gender identity. Androgyny tells us that, regardless of one’s sex, one’s gender identity may consist of some combination of feminine and masculine behaviors. Finally, questioning opens the door both for people who feel unsure of their sexual orientation and for people whose “sex and gender identification … may not [have] an existing label” (Perry and Ballard-Reisch 30).

不幸的是，性别歧视如今以多种形式存在，但往往只有那些自身遭受歧视或亲人遭受歧视的人才会意识到它的存在。琳达·A·M·佩里和黛博拉·巴拉德-雷施列举了三个性别歧视的例子，我相信你会从中受益匪浅，并引发思考。我在此简要列举一下，以便你了解人类性别认同的多样性，以及任何被视为“异类”的人常常遭受的压迫。

Unfortunately, gender discrimination exists today in myriad forms, yet too often the only people aware of it are those who must suffer it themselves or whose loved ones must suffer it. Linda A. M. Perry and Deborah Ballard-Reisch report three examples of sex and gender discrimination that I think you will find both instructive and thought-provoking. Let me just list them here briefly to give you an idea of the range of gender identification available to human beings and of the oppression with which anything deemed different is so often met.

在佩里和巴拉德-雷施提供的第一个例子中，一位已婚、育有子女的异性恋男子，有时也会异装——即穿着异性服饰，但行为举止仍符合自身生理性别——曾遭受异性恋和同性恋群体的言语和肢体虐待。作为一名异性恋异装者，他并不符合两个群体所熟悉的同性恋异装者的刻板印象，因此遭到了双方的排斥（21-22）。在另一个例子中，佩里和巴拉德-雷施描述了一位同性恋异装癖者（即穿着异性服饰并模仿异性行为，通常表现得较为夸张），他屡次遭到同性恋群体成员的排斥。这些成员希望提升同性恋群体的政治可见度——赋予同性恋群体在社会和政治议题上更大的话语权——但又担心冒犯异性恋群体。讽刺的是，这种讽刺既显而易见又令人痛心：一个倡导多元化的群体，却因为自身的多元化而遭到排斥，如今又因为其中一位成员的多元化而将其拒之门外（22-23）。在佩里和巴拉德-雷施的最后一个例子中，我们遇到了一位从女性转变为男性的男子，他通过变性手术获得了与自身性别认同相符的身体，而他的性别认同始终是男性。在变性手术之前，他是一位男性化的女同性恋者。如今，作为一名男性，他仍然对女性有性吸引力，所以，他现在当然是一位异性恋男性。他的问题似乎应该已经解决了。然而，由于他的性别/性取向史，他仍然无法获得社会的接纳。他一生都在试图解释自己的性取向和性别认同，并因此遭受骚扰和殴打。作为一名生理女性，他觉得自己无法融入社会，因为他的性别认同是被女性吸引的男性。变性后，他感觉自己无法融入社会，因为他的家人和朋友无法接受他身体上的变化。尽管如此，他仍然坚持公开自己的性取向/性别认同经历，因为他认为“出柜”是必要的，这样社会才能认识到，有很多人并不符合异性恋的“正常”标准（24）。

In the first example offered by Perry and Ballard-Reisch, a heterosexual man who is married, a father, and also at times a cross-dresser – one who adopts the attire of the opposite sex but who behaves in a manner associated with one’s biological sex – has been verbally and physically abused by both straight and gay people. As a heterosexual cross-dresser he doesn’t fit the stereotype of the gay cross-dresser with which both communities are familiar, and he has therefore experienced rejection from both (21–22). In another example, Perry and Ballard-Reisch describe a gay transvestite (one who adopts both the attire and the behavior of the opposite sex, usually in an exaggerated manner) who repeatedly has experienced rejection by members of the gay community wanting to advance gay political visibility – to give gay people a stronger voice in social and political issues – and fearing to offend straight people. The irony is self-evident and painful: a group that advocates diversity, that has been rejected because of its own diversity, rejects one of its members for being diverse (22–23). In Perry and Ballard-Reisch’s final example, we meet a man who has had a biological sex change from female to male in order to have a body that matches his gender identity, which has always been masculine. Before his sex-change procedure, he had been a masculine lesbian. Now, as a man, he is still sexually attracted to women, so, of course, he is now a heterosexual male. His problem, it seems, should be solved. However, he is still unable to find acceptance because of his sex/gender history. He has spent his life trying to explain his sexual and gender identities and being harassed and battered due to his difference. As a biological female, he didn’t feel he fit into society because his gender identity was that of a masculine male attracted to women. After his sex change, he did not feel he fit into society because his family and friends would not accept his physical transformation. Nevertheless, he persists in being open about his sex/gender history because he believes that being “out” is necessary in order for society to recognize that a large number of people do not fit the heterosexual standard of “normality” (24).

显然，女权主义和性别研究密切相关。它们不仅关注一些相同的主题，也都渴望正义，并坚信教育能够改善社会。几个世纪以来，女权主义一直致力于性别平等：致力于消除父权制下的性别角色，而这些角色即使在今天仍然阻碍着人们实现完全平等的努力。女性和男性。性别研究致力于加深我们对性别概念复杂性的理解。

Clearly, feminism and gender studies are intimately related. They share some of the same subject matter as well as a desire for justice and a belief in the power of education to change our society for the better. For centuries feminism has worked for gender equality: for a dissolution of the patriarchal gender roles that, even today, continue to short-circuit efforts to achieve complete equality between women and men. And gender studies is working to broaden our understanding of how complex the concept of gender really is.

当然，女权主义议题远不止本章所讨论的这些。如同其他领域一样，女权主义理论家和文学批评家之间也存在诸多分歧，例如：女性在多大程度上（以及在多大程度上）受到父权制意识形态的影响；是否存在一种可以称之为“女性化”的独特写作方式；女性作家的作品是否应该与男性作家的作品区别对待；各种文化因素如何与性别交织，共同塑造女性的经验；以及正如我们刚才所看到的，性别理论家们为拓展和质疑我们对性别的理解所开辟的新视野。本文的目的仅在于向您介绍一些主要观点和基本原则，以便您能够理解女权主义理论家和文学批评家提出的问题。

Of course, there are many more feminist issues than the ones discussed in this chapter. And as in every field, there is a great deal of disagreement among feminist theorists and literary critics concerning, for example, how (and how much) women are programmed by patriarchal ideology; whether or not there is a distinctive way of writing that might be called feminine; whether or not the work of women writers should be interpreted along different lines than writing by men; the ways in which various cultural factors intersect with sex and gender in creating women’s experience; and as we have just seen, the new horizons offered by the efforts of gender theorists to enlarge and problematize our conception of gender. Our purpose here is merely to introduce you to the main ideas and the general principles you need to know in order to read feminist theorists and literary critics with some understanding of the issues they raise.

女权主义与文学

Feminism and literature

当然，有些文学作品比其他作品更容易进行女性主义分析，或者至少更容易进行某些类型的女性主义分析。对于初学者来说，我认为考察文学文本如何强化父权制很有帮助，因为了解父权制意识形态何时以及如何运作，对于我们在生活中抵制它至关重要。这种方法应用于男性经典文学作品时，是20世纪70年代美国女性主义文学分析的主流模式。它通常需要“反其道而行之”，即不按照文本表面的意图去解读，因为父权制文学通常意识不到其所宣扬的性别歧视意识形态，或者更准确地说，父权制文学并不认为自身的性别歧视有任何不妥之处。

Naturally, some literary works will lend themselves more readily than others to feminist analysis or at least to certain kinds of feminist analyses. For students new to the field, I think it useful to examine the ways in which literary texts reinforce patriarchy because the ability to see when and how patriarchal ideology operates is crucial to our ability to resist it in our own lives. This approach, applied to literary works in the male canon, was the dominant mode of feminist literary analysis in America during the 1970s, and it usually requires reading “against the grain” of the text’s apparent intention, for patriarchal literature is usually unconscious of the sexist ideology it promotes, or perhaps more precisely, patriarchal literature sees nothing wrong with its own sexism.

例如，对阿瑟·米勒的《推销员之死》（1949）中父权制意识形态的女性主义分析，可以从三个相关方面入手：（1）剧中女性角色（比夫和哈皮的各种“猎艳对象”、威利在波士顿酒店房间里遇到的女人以及琳达·洛曼）如何作为男性地位的象征；（2）“好女孩”/“坏女孩”的女性二元论如何强化了洛曼家男人的性别歧视；（3）琳达·洛曼如何内化了父权制意识形态。女性主义解读还会指出，该剧通过对威利的同情刻画以及对琳达支持其父权态度的明显认可，强化了父权制意识形态。这种解读还会将该剧的父权制意识形态与其创作和设定的时代背景——二战后的美国——联系起来。当时，美国父权制试图通过重新确立“（好）女人的位置在家里”的观念，来抵消战时女性承担起丈夫的工作和家庭责任所带来的自由。

A feminist analysis of the patriarchal ideology operating in Arthur Miller’s Death of a Salesman (1949), for example, might examine three related areas: (1) the ways in which the female characters (Biff’s and Happy’s various “conquests,” the woman Willy meets in the Boston hotel room, and Linda Loman) function as tokens of male status; (2) the ways in which the “good-girl”/“bad-girl” view of women validates the Loman men’s sexism; and (3) the ways in which Linda Loman has internalized patriarchal ideology. A feminist reading would also note that the play reinforces patriarchal ideology through its sympathetic portrayal of Willy and apparent approval of Linda’s support for his patriarchal attitude. Such a reading would also relate the play’s patriarchal ideology to the period in which it was written and is set: post-World War II America. This was a time when American patriarchy attempted to counteract the war-time freedom of women who took on the jobs and family responsibilities of their absent men by reestablishing the belief that “the (good) woman’s place is in the home.”

当然，识别文学作品中何时描绘了父权制意识形态也至关重要，这样才能对其进行批判或引导我们去批判它。例如，对托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）进行女性主义解读，可以考察小说如何引导我们批判其中描绘的性别歧视行为和态度。小说对父权制心理的深刻洞察，体现在它将女性描绘成男性痛苦和愤怒的转移对象。一个令人印象深刻的例子是，年轻的乔利憎恨达琳，他将自己对羞辱他们的白人猎人的仇恨转移到了达琳身上。此外，小说对坚强女性——例如吉米阿姨、亲爱的妈妈和麦克蒂尔太太——的赞赏，以及对姐妹情谊对女性生存重要性的强调，也体现了其女性主义倾向。《最蓝的眼睛》也向我们展示了性别问题如何与种族问题交织在一起，因为乔利对达琳的仇恨是黑人少女在白人猎人的种族主义面前无能为力的直接结果，而当女性成为性别歧视和种族主义双重压迫的受害者时，姐妹情谊对女性生存的重要性就显得尤为突出。

Of course, it is also important to be able to recognize when a literary work depicts patriarchal ideology in order to criticize it or invite us to criticize it. For example, a feminist reading of Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) might examine the ways in which the novel invites us to criticize the sexist behaviors and attitudes it portrays. A striking illustration of the novel’s insight into patriarchal psychology is its depiction of women as the site upon which men’s pain and anger are displaced, a memorable example of which we see in the young Cholly’s hatred of Darlene, upon whom he displaces his hatred of the white hunters who humiliate them. In addition, the novel’s feminist agenda is revealed in its appreciation of strong women – such as Aunt Jimmy, M’Dear, and Mrs. MacTeer – and of the importance of sisterhood to women’s survival. The Bluest Eye also shows us how gender issues intersect with race, for Cholly’s hatred of Darlene is a direct result of the black youngster’s powerlessness in the face of the white hunters’ racism, and the importance of sisterhood to women’s survival becomes especially acute when the women are victims of the combined forces of sexism and racism.

最后，许多文学作品对父权制意识形态持矛盾态度，例如玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818）。一方面，这部作品通过展现女性的力量，削弱了父权制对女性软弱的认知：卡罗琳是她破产父亲唯一的经济和精神支柱；朱斯蒂娜勇敢高尚地承受着来自社会的不公正谴责，包括死刑；萨菲不顾父亲的反对，成功地踏上了一段危险的旅程，追求自己的目标。怪物也可以被解读为女性权利的间接倡导者。在许多方面，怪物占据了十八世纪欧洲社会中女性的地位：它被认为不如男性，因此被剥夺了男性享有的权利和舒适的生活。然而，它通过自学获得了知识，显然非常聪明且能言善辩，它只想被接纳为人类大家庭的平等成员，并愿意为之做出自己的贡献（正如我们看到它匿名帮助德莱西一家时所做的那样）。

Finally, many literary works have a conflicted response to patriarchal ideology, as we see, for example, in Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818). On the one hand, the text undermines patriarchy’s belief in female weakness through its portrayal of women’s strength: Caroline is the sole financial and moral support of her ruined father; Justine bears up bravely and nobly under the community’s unjust condemnation of her, which includes the penalty of death; and Safie defies her patriarchal father and successfully undertakes a dangerous journey in pursuit of her own goals. The monster, too, can be read as an indirect advocate for women’s rights. In many ways, the monster occupies the woman’s position in eighteenth-century European society: it is considered inferior to men and therefore denied the rights and comforts men enjoy. Nevertheless, it acquires an education on its own, is clearly very intelligent and articulate, and wants only to be accepted as an equal member of the human family, to which it will willingly contribute its share (as we see it do when it anonymously helps the De Lacey family).

另一方面，小说通过对卡罗琳、贾斯汀、伊丽莎白和阿加莎恪守传统性别角色的赞扬，强化了父权制意识形态。这三位“圣母”全身心投入到照顾他人中，甚至到了为他人牺牲生命的地步，无论她们是否意识到这一点。卡罗琳作为一位尽职尽责的母亲，悉心照料伊丽莎白而死；贾斯汀作为一位尽职尽责的仆人和代理母亲而死，本应死去的是维克多；伊丽莎白作为一位尽职尽责的妻子和代理母亲而死，她信任丈夫的判断，满足他的需求，而本应死去的是维克多。就连萨菲的独立行为，也是为了迎合传统女性渴望找到丈夫的愿望。此外，这部小说似乎并没有引导我们去批判维克多对女性的杀戮狂怒中明显存在的厌女症（仇恨女性）或恐女症（对女性作为性存在和生育能力的恐惧和厌恶）。怪物形象，以及他长期回避伊丽莎白的行为，都更隐晦地暗示了这一点。这种对《弗兰肯斯坦》的解读还可以考察小说对父权制意识形态的矛盾回应，是如何反映在玛丽·雪莱自身关于父权制经历的冲突中的：例如，她热衷于已故母亲玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特的反父权制文章；她与已婚男子珀西·雪莱私奔，违背了父权制价值观；然而，她似乎对丈夫极其依赖，甚至顺从。

On the other hand, the novel reinforces patriarchal ideology through its admiration of the ways in which Caroline, Justine, Elizabeth, and Agatha conform to traditional gender roles. Three of these “madonnas” devote themselves to nurturing others to the point, whether they realize it or not, of sacrificing their lives for them. Caroline dies as a dutiful mother, tending Elizabeth; Justine dies as a dutiful servant and surrogate mother, when it should be Victor who dies; and Elizabeth dies as a dutiful wife and surrogate mother, trusting her husband’s judgment and catering to his needs, when, again, it should be Victor who dies. Even Safie’s independent behavior is in the service of the traditional woman’s desire to secure herself a husband. In addition, the novel does not seem to invite us to criticize the misogyny (hatred of women) or gynophobia (fear and loathing of women as sexual and reproductive beings) clearly evident in Victor’s murderous rage against the female monster and more subtly suggested by his prolonged avoidance of Elizabeth. This reading of Frankenstein might also examine the ways in which the novel’s conflicted response to patriarchal ideology is reflected in Mary Shelley’s own conflicts concerning her personal experience of patriarchy: for example, she was an ardent admirer of the antipatriarchal essays of her late mother, Mary Wollstonecraft; she violated patriarchal values when she eloped with a married man, Percy Shelley; yet she seemed extremely dependent on, even submissive to, her husband.

由于女权主义议题涵盖文化、社会、政治和心理等诸多领域，女权主义文学批评的范围也十分广泛。然而，无论采用何种分析方法，女权主义批评的最终目标都是增进我们对女性过去和现在经历的理解，并提升我们对女性在世界上的价值的认知。

Because feminist issues range so widely across cultural, social, political, and psychological categories, feminist literary criticism is wide ranging, too. Whatever kind of analysis is undertaken, however, the ultimate goal of feminist criticism is to increase our understanding of women’s experience, both in the past and present, and promote our appreciation of women’s value in the world.

女性主义批评家对文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions feminist critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在概括女性主义文学研究方法。试图为分析女性写作构建专门的女性框架的方法（例如问题 6、7 和 8）通常被称为女性批评。

The questions that follow are offered to summarize feminist approaches to literature. Approaches that attempt to develop a specifically female framework for the analysis of women’s writing (such as questions 6, 7, and 8) are often referred to as gynocriticism.

1这部作品揭示了父权制在经济、政治、社会或心理层面上的运作方式？女性形象是如何被塑造的？这些形象与小说创作或设定时期的性别议题有何关联？换言之，这部作品是在强化还是削弱父权制意识形态？（如果是前者，我们可以说这部作品带有父权制倾向；如果是后者，我们可以说这部作品带有女权主义倾向。那些似乎既强化又削弱父权制意识形态的文本，或许可以被认为是意识形态上存在冲突的。）

1 What does the work reveal about the operations (economically, politically, socially, or psychologically) of patriarchy? How are women portrayed? How do these portrayals relate to the gender issues of the period in which the novel was written or is set? In other words, does the work reinforce or undermine patriarchal ideology? (In the first case, we might say that the text has a patriarchal agenda. In the second case, we might say that the text has a feminist agenda. Texts that seem to both reinforce and undermine patriarchal ideology might be said to be ideologically conflicted.)

2这项研究对种族、阶级和/或其他文化因素与性别交织在一起，从而塑造女性的经历，提出了哪些启示？

2 What does the work suggest about the ways in which race, class, and/or other cultural factors intersect with gender in producing women’s experience?

3这部作品是如何体现“性别”的？也就是说，它似乎是如何定义女性气质和男性气质的？人物的行为是否总是符合他们被赋予的性别？这部作品是否暗示存在除女性气质和男性气质之外的其他性别？这部作品对它所描绘的性别持何种态度？例如，这部作品似乎是接受、质疑还是拒绝传统的性别观念？

3 How is the work “gendered”? That is, how does it seem to define femininity and masculinity? Does the characters’ behavior always conform to their assigned genders? Does the work suggest that there are genders other than feminine and masculine? What seems to be the work’s attitude toward the gender(s) it portrays? For example, does the work seem to accept, question, or reject the traditional view of gender?

4这部作品对姐妹情谊作为一种抵抗父权制的方式的可能性有何启示？或者对改善女性在世界上的经济、政治、社会或心理状况的方式有何启示？

4 What does the work imply about the possibilities of sisterhood as a mode of resisting patriarchy and/or about the ways in which women’s situations in the world – economic, political, social, or psychological – might be improved?

5这部作品在公众和评论界的接受史，揭示了父权制运作的哪些方面？这部文学作品是否被忽视了？或者过去被忽视了？为什么？或者，如果过去得到了认可，现在这项工作是否被忽视或冷落了？为什么？

5 What does the history of the work’s reception by the public and by the critics tell us about the operations of patriarchy? Has the literary work been ignored or neglected in the past? Why? Or, if recognized in the past, is the work ignored or neglected now? Why?

6这部作品对女性的创造力有何启示？要回答这个问题，需要了解作者的生平资料以及她所处文化的历史资料。

6 What does the work suggest about women’s creativity? In order to answer this question, biographical data about the author and historical data about the culture in which she lived will be required.

7对作者风格的考察可能会对目前正在进行的界定女性特有的写作形式（例如，女性写作）的努力做出哪些贡献？

7 What might an examination of the author’s style contribute to the ongoing efforts to delineate a specifically feminine form of writing (for example, écriture féminine)?

8这部作品在女性文学史和文学传统中扮演着怎样的角色？

8 What role does the work play in terms of women’s literary history and literary tradition?

根据具体文学作品，我们可以提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们也可以提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们以富有成效的女性主义视角思考文学作品的一些起点。请记住，即使关注相同的女性主义概念，不同的女性主义批评家对同一作品的解读也并非完全相同。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。我们的目标是运用女性主义理论来丰富我们对文学作品的解读；帮助我们理解作品所阐述的一些重要思想，这些思想如果没有女性主义理论的帮助，我们可能无法如此清晰或深刻地领悟；并帮助我们认识到父权制意识形态如何蒙蔽了我们，使我们看不到自身参与或至少是默许了性别歧视议程的事实。

Depending on the literary work in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us thinking about literary works in productive feminist ways. Keep in mind that not all feminist critics will interpret the same work in the same way even if they focus on the same feminist concepts. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use feminist theory to help enrich our reading of literary works; to help us see some important ideas they illustrate that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply without feminist theory; and to help us see the ways in which patriarchal ideology blinds us to our own participation in, or at least complicity with, sexist agendas.

以下对菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的女性主义解读，旨在展示女性主义对该小说的诠释可能带来的成果。本文将着重探讨小说中通过女性角色塑造所揭示的性别歧视倾向，其意识形态内涵想必各位已有所察觉。此外，我将从20世纪20年代美国女性角色变迁的角度来分析小说中的父权制意识形态，因为大多数女性主义者已经意识到，了解特定历史环境如何孕育特定意识形态至关重要。然而，我论证的历史部分并不复杂，而是基于一些大家可能都比较熟悉的历史信息。

The following feminist reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a feminist interpretation of that novel might yield. It focuses on what I will argue is the novel’s sexist agenda as revealed through the text’s characterizations of women, the ideological content of which should be fairly easy for you to see at this point. In addition, I will situate the novel’s patriarchal ideology in terms of the changing role of American women during the 1920s because most feminists have come to realize the importance of seeing how specific historical circumstances foster particular ideologies. The historical component of my argument is not complex, however, but rather draws on historical information with which most of you are probably somewhat familiar.

“……接下来他们会把一切都扔到海里去……”：对《了不起的盖茨比》的女性主义解读

“… next they’ll throw everything overboard …”: a feminist reading of The Great Gatsby

在发现妻子有了情人后，F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的小说《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）中的汤姆·布坎南惊慌失措地喊道：“现在的人先是嘲笑家庭生活和家庭制度，接下来他们就会抛弃一切，让黑白通婚！”（137；第七章）。除了汤姆对自己和妻子的行为持有双重标准（以及他的种族主义）之外，这句话还揭示了汤姆对道德的假设。社会结构建立在父权制家庭的稳定之上，而父权制家庭的稳定又建立在女性对父权制性别角色的顺从之上。当然，通过尼克·卡拉威的叙述，小说显然对汤姆的立场进行了嘲讽：“汤姆满脸热情地胡言乱语，”尼克观察到，“他觉得自己孤身一人站在文明的最后一道防线上”（137；第七章）。然而，我认为可以证明，《了不起的盖茨比》也认同汤姆对父权制性别角色的看法。

In a sudden panic over his discovery that his wife has taken a lover, Tom Buchanan, from F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925), exclaims, “Nowadays people begin by sneering at family life and family institutions and next they’ll throw everything overboard and have intermarriage between black and white” (137; ch. 7). In addition to Tom’s double standard for his own and his wife’s behavior (as well as his racism), this statement reveals Tom’s assumptions that the moral structure of society rests on the stability of the patriarchal family and that the stability of the patriarchal family rests on the conformity of women to patriarchal gender roles. Of course, through the vehicle of Nick Carraway’s narration, the novel clearly ridicules Tom’s position: “Flushed with his impassioned gibberish,” Nick observes, “[Tom] saw himself standing alone on the last barrier of civilization” (137; ch. 7). Nevertheless, I think it can be shown that The Great Gatsby also shares Tom’s view of patriarchal gender roles.

这部小说创作于第一次世界大战结束后的十年间，故事背景也设定在1918年11月结束的那十年。咆哮的二十年代，或称爵士时代（菲茨杰拉德创造的词汇），是美国社会发生巨大变革的时期，尤其是在女性权利方面。第一次世界大战前，美国女性没有普选权。1920年，在战争结束两年后（以及经过72年有组织的政治运动），她们终于获得了投票权。战前，女性的标准着装包括长裙、紧身胸衣、高跟鞋以及端庄地盘在头顶的长发。战后几年，裙子变短了（有些裙子短了很多），束身胸衣开始消失（事实上，最大胆、最不拘一格的年轻女性很少穿，甚至不穿任何束缚性的内衣），现代鞋履经常取代高帮皮鞋，“波波头”（剪短并随意披散）成为年轻女性的时尚。

The novel was written and is set in the decade following World War I, which ended in November 1918. The Roaring Twenties, or the Jazz Age, a term coined by Fitzgerald, was a period of enormous social change in America, especially in the area of women’s rights. Before World War I, American women did not enjoy universal suffrage. In 1920, two years after the end of the war (and after 72 years of organized political agitation), they were finally given the vote. Before the war, standard dress for women included long skirts, tightly laced corsets, high-buttoned shoes, and long hair demurely swept up onto the head. A few years after the war, skirts became shorter (in some cases, much shorter), laced corsets began to disappear (indeed, the most bold and unconventional young women wore few, if any, restraining undergarments), modern footwear frequently replaced high-buttoned shoes, and “bobbed” hair (cut short and worn loosely) became the fashion for young women.

或许最令旧观念的拥护者感到担忧的是，女性的行为开始发生改变。人们开始看到女性吸烟饮酒（尽管当时正值禁酒令时期），而且常常与男性同行，没有监护人陪同。她们也乐于享受夜总会和私人派对上有时喧闹的夜生活。就连当时流行的、在许多人看来狂野且带有明显性暗示的舞蹈，也体现了一种自由表达自我和无拘无束地享受生活的态度。换句话说，正如我们在社会变革时期经常看到的那样，“新女性”在20世纪20年代出现。而且，一如既往，她的出现引发了社会保守派人士（包括男性和女性）的强烈负面反应。他们像以往一样认为，女性对传统角色的任何拒绝都必然会导致家庭的瓦解和整个社会的道德沦丧。

Perhaps most alarming for proponents of the old ways, women’s behavior began to change. Women could now be seen smoking and drinking (despite Prohibition), often in the company of men and without chaperones. They could also be seen enjoying the sometimes raucous nightlife offered at nightclubs and private parties. Even the new dances of the era, which seemed wild and overtly sexual to many, bespoke an attitude of free self-expression and unrestrained enjoyment. In other words, as we often see during times of social change, a “New Woman” emerged in the 1920s. And, again as usual, her appearance on the scene evoked a good deal of negative reaction from conservative members of society, both male and female, who felt, as they generally do at these times, that women’s rejection of any aspect of their traditional role inevitably results in the destruction of the family and the moral decline of society as a whole.

这种将女性视为传统价值观捍卫者的观点，认为她们作为不挣工资的家庭主妇/夫，其存在对于维护社会道德结构至关重要，在工业化的十九世纪，随着家庭不再是全家共同劳作、挣钱养家的地方，男性外出到城镇从事各种职业以维持生计，这种观点成为了占主导地位的父权制意识形态。也就是说，随着女性在家庭中的经济角色消失，一种精神化的家庭角色被赋予了她们，其目的之一就是避免她们在就业市场上与男性竞争。因此，尽管大多数美国人相信美国道德结构的存续，但这种观念却逐渐瓦解。依赖于传统的性别角色，实际上，是国家的经济结构——这种结构赋予男性经济主导地位——依赖于“女人的位置在家里”这一公理。当然，让女性待在家里，衣着朴素，举止安静，另一个好处是它重申了男性对女性性能力和生育能力的掌控。因此，20世纪20年代“新女性”所构成的威胁，对公众意识的许多层面都产生了影响。

This view of women as the standard-bearers of traditional values, whose presence as nonwage-earning supervisors of hearth and home was deemed necessary to maintain the moral structure of society, became the dominant patriarchal ideology of the industrialized nineteenth century as the home ceased to be the place where the family worked together to earn their living and men went off to earn the family bread at various occupations in the towns. That is, as woman’s economic role in the home disappeared, a spiritualized domestic role was created for her in order to keep her, among other things, from competing with men on the job market. Thus, although most Americans believed the survival of America’s moral structure depended on traditional gender roles, it was really the nation’s economic structure, which gave economic dominance to men, that depended upon the axiom “a woman’s place is in the home.” Of course, another advantage of keeping women at home, modestly dressed and quietly behaved, was that it reaffirmed men’s ownership of women’s sexual and reproductive capacities. The threat posed by the New Woman of the 1920s, then, had repercussions on many levels of public consciousness.

文学作品往往反映出其文化中的意识形态冲突，无论作者是否出于本意，因为和我们其他人一样，作家也受到时代意识形态氛围的影响。即使是像F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德这样在20世纪20年代先锋派社交圈中风度翩翩、并娶了一位“新女性”为妻的作家，也难逃他所处时代的意识形态冲突。人们或许会推测，正是他“快节奏生活”的经历，让他对20世纪20年代美国发生的变革产生了一些（有意识或无意识的）疑虑。或者，人们或许会推测，他之所以能够接受“新女性”，仅仅是因为他可以将她们视为心理受创、需要他帮助的对象——这种情况在他的半自传体小说《夜色温柔》（1934）以及他与妻子泽尔达动荡的婚姻生活中都有所体现。然而，我的目的并非探究菲茨杰拉德的生平，而是探究他最经久不衰的作品《了不起的盖茨比》是如何体现了第一次世界大战后文化对新女性的不安情绪的。

Literary works often reflect the ideological conflicts of their culture, whether or not it is their intention to do so, because, like the rest of us, authors are influenced by the ideological tenor of the times. Even a writer like F. Scott Fitzgerald, who cut a dashing figure among the avant-garde social set of the 1920s and who was himself married to a New Woman, was subject to the ideological conflicts that characterized his age. One might speculate that it was precisely his experience of “life in the fast lane” that created some (conscious or unconscious) misgivings about the changes occurring in America during the 1920s. Or one might speculate that he was able to accept the New Woman only as long as he could view her as psychologically troubled and in need of his help, a situation illustrated in his semi-autobiographical novel Tender Is the Night (1934), as well as in his turbulent life with his wife, Zelda. However, it’s not my intention to examine Fitzgerald’s life but to examine the ways in which The Great Gatsby, his most enduring work, embodies its culture’s discomfort with the post-World War I New Woman.

小说对一些次要女性角色的刻画体现了这种不适感，而对主要人物黛西·布坎南、乔丹·贝克和默特尔·威尔逊的塑造则以更为复杂的方式展现了这种不适感。尽管她们之间存在诸多差异，但她们都是“新女性”的化身。我们可以推断，尼克对这些人物的描述反映了小说的意识形态偏见，而不仅仅是他个人的偏见，因为文本对尼克的刻画带有同情色彩，这与对汤姆·布坎南的刻画截然不同。除了作者运用第一人称叙述方式唤起读者对尼克的同情——因为我们通过尼克的视角来看待叙事事件，我们或多或少能够“感同身受”——尼克还以细腻而引人入胜的方式讲述自己的故事，与读者分享他的个人感受：他的欲望、厌恶、恐惧、疑虑和爱慕，从而赢得了我们的同情。最后，作为唯一一个始终关注伦理道德的角色，尼克成为了小说的道德中心。因此，可以合理地得出结论：无论菲茨杰拉德是否打算让卡拉威成为可靠的叙述者，许多读者都会受到尼克的视角的强烈影响。

We see this discomfort in the novel’s representation of its minor female characters, and we see it in more complex ways in the novel’s characterizations of main characters Daisy Buchanan, Jordan Baker, and Myrtle Wilson, who, despite their numerous differences, are all versions of the New Woman. We can assume that Nick’s descriptions of these characters represent the novel’s ideological biases, and not merely his own, because the text portrays Nick sympathetically, unlike Tom Buchanan. In addition to the sympathy Nick evokes by the author’s use of firstperson narration – because we see the narrative events through Nick’s eyes, we are able to more or less “walk in his shoes” – Nick also gains our sympathy because he tells his story in a sensitive and engaging manner, sharing with the reader his personal feelings: his desires, dislikes, fears, doubts, and affections. Finally, as the only character who is consistently aware of ethical considerations, Nick functions as the moral center of the novel. It is therefore reasonable to conclude that, whether or not Fitzgerald intended Carraway as a reliable narrator, many readers will be strongly influenced by Nick’s perspective.

小说中充斥着众多女性配角，她们的穿着打扮和行为举止都体现了“新女性”的形象，但她们却被刻画成单一负面角色的克隆体：肤浅、爱出风头、令人作呕、虚伪狡诈。例如，在盖茨比的派对上，我们看到的是虚伪的、“热情洋溢的聚会，而这些女人甚至连彼此的名字都不知道”（44；第三章），以及众多处于不同程度醉酒歇斯底里的自恋型关注者。我们相遇，因为例如，一个年轻女子为了“壮胆”猛灌一杯鸡尾酒，然后“独自一人在帆布平台上跳舞”（45；第3章）；一个“吵闹的小女孩，稍有挑衅便会止不住地大笑”（51；第3章）；一个醉酒的女人“不仅在唱歌，还在哭泣”，她的脸上布满了“黑色的泪痕”，那是“泪水……沾到她浓密的睫毛上造成的”（55-56；第3章）；一个醉酒的年轻女孩，为了不让她尖叫，她的“头被按在水池里”（113；第6章）；还有两个醉酒的年轻妻子，她们拒绝离开派对，直到她们的丈夫厌倦了她们的言语辱骂，“把她们踢进夜色中”（57；第3章）。此外，还有本尼·麦克莱纳汉的“四个女孩”：

The novel abounds in minor female characters whose dress and activities identify them as incarnations of the New Woman, and they are portrayed as clones of a single, negative character type: shallow, exhibitionist, revolting, and deceitful. For example, at Gatsby’s parties we see insincere, “enthusiastic meetings between women who never knew each other’s names” (44; ch. 3), as well as numerous narcissistic attention-seekers in various stages of drunken hysteria. We meet, for example, a young woman who “dumps” down a cocktail “for courage” and “dances out alone on the canvas platform” (45; ch. 3); “a rowdy little girl who gave way upon the slightest provocation to uncontrollable laughter” (51; ch. 3); a drunken woman who “was not only singing, she was weeping too,” her face lined with “black rivulets” created when her “tears … came into contact with her heavily beaded eyelashes” (55–56; ch. 3); a drunken young girl who has her “head stuck in a pool” (113; ch. 6) to stop her from screaming; and two drunken young wives who refuse to leave the party until their husbands, tired of the women’s verbal abuse, “lifted [them] kicking into the night” (57; ch. 3). Then there are Benny McClenahan’s “four girls”:

她们的容貌虽不完全相同，但彼此之间却又如此相似，以至于人们总觉得她们似曾相识。我忘了她们的名字——我想是杰奎琳，也可能是康苏埃拉、格洛丽亚、朱迪或琼，她们的姓氏要么是悦耳动听的花名或月份名，要么是那些美国大资本家的硬朗姓氏，如果被追问，她们会承认自己是这些资本家的表亲。

They were never quite the same ones in physical person, but they were so identical one with another that it inevitably seemed they had been there before. I have forgotten their names – Jaqueline, I think, or else Consuela, or Gloria or Judy or June, and their last names were either the melodious names of flowers and months or the sterner ones of the great American capitalists whose cousins, if pressed, they would confess themselves to be.

（67；第4章）

(67; ch. 4)

换句话说，所有这些陪同麦克莱纳汉参加盖茨比派对的相貌相似的女子都编造了名字和个人经历，以博得新结识者的好感。因此，当听到尼克说“女人的不诚实，你永远不会真正责怪她”（63；第三章）时，我们也不应该感到太过惊讶。这句话暗示，女人似乎对此无能为力：或许这只是一种天性缺陷，就像许多其他女性弱点一样。

In other words, all of these lookalike women who accompanied McClenahan to Gatsby’s parties invented names and biographies for themselves to impress their new acquaintances. We should not be too surprised, then, to hear Nick say, “Dishonesty in a woman is a thing you never blame deeply” (63; ch. 3), implying that women don’t seem able to help it: perhaps it’s just a natural failing, like so many other feminine weaknesses.

我们得以稍稍了解的仅有的两位次要女性角色，她们都符合“新女性”的刻板印象：一位是麦基太太——她被描述为“尖酸刻薄、懒散、漂亮却可怕”（第34页；第二章）——另一位是默特尔的妹妹凯瑟琳，她完美地契合了上述负面刻板印象。小说对凯瑟琳这个次要角色着墨颇多，或许是因为她被选中来代表这类女性外表上的缺陷，而其他次要女性角色的描述中只是略有提及。

The only minor female characters we get to know a little better, both of whom fit the category of the New Woman, are Mrs. McKee – who is described as “shrill, languid, handsome, and horrible” (34; ch. 2) – and Myrtle’s sister, Catherine, who perfectly fits the negative stereotype outlined above. The novel gives Catherine a good deal of attention for such a minor character, perhaps because she has been chosen to represent the physical unattractiveness of her type, which is only hinted at in the descriptions of the other minor female characters.

那位姐姐……是个三十岁左右、身材苗条、世故圆滑的女子，一头浓密的红色波波头，脸色苍白如雪，扑了一层粉。她的眉毛被拔过，又重新画了一遍，角度更倾斜，但自然恢复原状的努力让她的脸看起来有些模糊。她走动时，手臂上无数的陶制手镯叮当作响，发出不停的咔哒声。她进门时带着一种占有欲极强的急切，环顾四周的家具，眼神里充满了占有欲，以至于我……我当时就在想她是不是住在这里。但当我问她时，她却哈哈大笑，大声重复了我的问题，然后告诉我她和一位女朋友住在酒店里。

The sister … was a slender, worldly girl of about thirty with a solid sticky bob of red hair and a complexion powdered milky white. Her eyebrows had been plucked and then drawn on again at a more rakish angle but the efforts of nature toward the restoration of the old alignment gave a blurred air to her face. When she moved about there was an incessant clicking as innumerable pottery bracelets jingled up and down upon her arms. She came in with such proprietary haste and looked around so possessively at the furniture that I wondered if she lived here. But when I asked her she laughed immoderately, repeated my question aloud, and told me she lived with a girl friend at a hotel.

（34；第2章）

(34; ch. 2)

这段文字描述的是一个令人作呕、聒噪庸俗的年轻女子，她对尼克说的第一句话显然是谎话。凯瑟琳的言行也印证了这种描述，她与尼克谈论默特尔和她的“甜心”（39；第二章）时，言辞粗俗不堪；她还声称自己不喝酒，但默特尔去世当晚，她醉醺醺地出现在乔治·威尔逊的修车厂，我们这才发现她撒了谎。她对和女友在蒙特卡洛的经历的描述，进一步暴露了她的庸俗和愚蠢：

This is the description of a rather revolting, loud, vulgar young woman whose opening words to Nick are an obvious lie. And Catherine fulfills the expectations such a description raises by the vulgar nature of her conversation with Nick concerning Myrtle and her “sweetie” (39; ch. 2) and by her claim that she doesn’t drink, which we learn is a lie when she turns up drunk at George Wilson’s garage the night of Myrtle’s death. Her vulgarity, as well as her foolishness, is further revealed in her description of her and her girlfriend’s experience in Monte Carlo:

我们出发时带了1200多美元，结果在包厢里两天就被骗光了。我跟你说，回去的路真是糟透了。天哪，我恨死那个镇子了！

We had over twelve hundred dollars when we started but we got gypped out of it all in two days in the private rooms. We had an awful time getting back, I can tell you. God, how I hated that town!

（38；第2章）

(38; ch. 2)

有人可能会认为，这部小说的偏见并非性别歧视，而是阶级歧视，因为上述所有女性都属于社会经济地位较低的阶层。然而，小说中也描绘了一些来自同一阶层的男性角色，并对他们抱有同情。例如，乔治·威尔逊被塑造成一个朴实勤劳的男人，尽管他自身存在其他缺陷，却对妻子忠贞不渝。在“灰烬谷”（第27页；第二章）经营咖啡馆的迈克尔斯先生对乔治很友善，并在默特尔去世后尽力照顾他。就连前面提到的那两位爱参加派对的丈夫，尽管他们自己清醒，也以令人钦佩的耐心容忍妻子醉酒后的粗暴行为。因此，真正招致小说谴责的，是这些女性对父权制性别角色的违背，而非她们的社会经济阶层。

One could argue that the novel’s bias here is not sexist, but classist, for all the women described above belong to the lower socioeconomic strata of society. However, there are several male characters from these same strata who are described sympathetically. For example, George Wilson is portrayed as a simple, hardworking man who, despite his other limitations, is devoted to his wife. Mr. Michaelis, who owns a coffee shop in the “valley of ashes” (27; ch.2), is kind to George and tries to take care of him after Myrtle’s death. And even the two party-going husbands mentioned earlier, themselves sober, tolerate their wives’ drunken abuse with admirable patience. Thus it is these women’s violation of patriarchal gender roles, not their socioeconomic class, that elicits the novel’s condemnation.

小说对“新女性”的不安感，在对主要人物黛西·布坎南、乔丹·贝克和默特尔·威尔逊的刻画中，以一种更为复杂的方式显露出来。尽管她们在阶级、职业、婚姻状况、外貌和性格特征上存在显著差异，但这三个人物都是“新女性”的化身。如同那些在外表和社交自由方面体现“新女性”形象的次要女性角色一样，黛西、乔丹和默特尔的言行举止都符合这一形象。她们的发型和穿着非常现代，而且她们不像她们的母亲和祖母那样，认为必须在公共场合举止端庄，避免饮酒、吸烟和跳不雅的舞蹈。此外，这三位女性都展现出相当程度的现代独立性。她们中只有两人已婚，而且她们并不隐瞒婚姻中的不幸，尽管在父权制婚姻中，对这类事情保密是至关重要的规则之一。乔丹拥有自己的事业，而且是在男性主导的职业高尔夫领域。他们都更喜欢夜生活的刺激。她们从事的是更为传统的家庭主妇/主夫职业。她们三人中只有一个孩子，黛西的女儿帕米。帕米虽然受到保姆的悉心照料，也受到母亲的关爱，但黛西的生活并非完全围绕着母亲的角色。最后，这三位女性都违反了父权制下的性禁忌：乔丹发生了婚前性行为，黛西和默特尔则有婚外情。

The novel’s discomfort with the New Woman becomes evident, in a more complex fashion, in the characterizations of main characters Daisy Buchanan, Jordan Baker, and Myrtle Wilson. Despite their striking differences in class, occupation, marital status, personal appearance, and personality traits, these three characters are all versions of the New Woman. Like the minor female characters who embody the New Woman in appearance and social freedom, Daisy, Jordan, and Myrtle look and act the part. Their hair and clothing are very modern, and they don’t feel, as their mothers and grandmothers surely did, that they must behave modestly in public by avoiding hard liquor, cigarettes, and immodest dancing. In addition, all three women display a good deal of modern independence. Only two are married, and they don’t keep their marital unhappiness a secret, although secrecy about such matters is one of the cardinal rules of patriarchal marriage. Jordan has a career of her own and, on top of that, it’s in the maledominated field of professional golf. They all prefer the excitement of nightlife to the more traditional employments of hearth and home. There is only one child among them, Daisy’s daughter, Pammy, and while Pammy is well looked after by her nurse and affectionately treated by her mother, Daisy’s life does not revolve exclusively around her maternal role. Finally, all three women violate patriarchal sexual taboos: Jordan engages in premarital sex, and Daisy and Myrtle are engaged in extramarital affairs.

小说认为女性拥有这种自由是不可接受的，这一点在其对那些行使这种自由的女性的冷漠刻画中显而易见。黛西·布坎南被塑造成一个被宠坏的任性女子和冷血杀手。她习惯了成为众人瞩目的焦点，以至于她眼里只有自己。尽管默特尔的死是意外，黛西却没有停车救助受伤的女子。相反，她加速逃离，让盖茨比背黑锅。（人们不禁会想，至少在过去的几十年里，是否有一些读者曾对自己说：“瞧瞧，让女人开车会造成什么后果？”）一旦她发现盖茨比的出身与自己不同，她便躲在汤姆的财富和权力的庇护之下，任由她的爱人自生自灭。事实上，我们对黛西的谴责很大程度上源于她不配得到盖茨比的爱。尽管她让盖茨比相信她会为了他离开丈夫，但在纽约酒店房间的对峙中，尼克观察到“她的目光落在乔丹和我身上，带着一种恳求的意味，仿佛她……从一开始就从未打算做任何事”（139；第七章）。就连她的说话方式也常常矫揉造作——“我幸福得麻木了”（13；第一章）；“你让我想起一朵——一朵玫瑰，一朵绝世佳人”（19；第一章）；以及“蒙福的宝贝……回到你爱你的亲生母亲身边吧”（123；第七章）——以至于很难认真对待她说的任何话。因此，除了她其他的罪过之外，她还是个伪君子。

That the novel finds this freedom unacceptable in women is evident in its unsympathetic portrayals of those who exercise it. Daisy Buchanan is characterized as a spoiled brat and a remorseless killer. She is so used to being the center of attention that she can think of no one’s needs but her own. Although Myrtle’s death is accidental, Daisy doesn’t stop the car and try to help the injured woman. On the contrary, she speeds off and lets Gatsby take the blame. (One can’t help but wonder if some readers, at least in decades past, have said to themselves, “See what happens when you let a woman get behind the wheel of a car?”) Once she learns that Gatsby doesn’t come from the same social stratum as herself, she retreats behind the protection of Tom’s wealth and power, abandoning her lover to whatever fate awaits him. Indeed, much of our condemnation of Daisy issues from her failure to deserve Gatsby’s devotion. Although she lets Gatsby believe she will leave her husband for him, Nick observes during the confrontation scene in the New York hotel room that “[h]er eyes fell on Jordan and me with a sort of appeal, as though she … had never, all along, intended doing anything at all” (139; ch. 7). Even her way of speaking is frequently so affected – “I’m p-paralyzed with happiness” (13; ch. 1); “You remind me of a – of a rose, an absolute rose” (19; ch. 1); and “Bles-sed precious. … Come to your own mother that loves you” (123; ch. 7) – as to make it difficult to take anything she says seriously. Thus, on top of all her other sins, she’s a phony.

乔丹·贝克被描绘成一个说谎者和骗子。尼克发现她撒谎说把借来的车敞篷停在雨里，而且显然她在一次高尔夫球赛中作弊被抓，尽管她设法逃脱了惩罚，但种种迹象表明她可能使用了贿赂或胁迫手段：“这件事几乎闹成了丑闻——然后就不了了之了。一个球童撤回了他的证词，而另一位证人也承认他可能记错了”（62-63页；第三章）。和黛西一样，乔丹也表现出对他人漠不关心，并拒绝承担责任，正如尼克描述的那样，她开车“离几个工人太近了，以至于我们的挡泥板碰到了一个男人外套上的纽扣”（63页；第三章）。尼克告诫她开车要更小心，或者干脆别开车，她却漫不经心地回应道：“他们会（其他人）会避开我的路……出车祸需要两个人”（63；第三章）。尼克说：“假设你遇到一个和你一样粗心的人”（63；第三章），乔丹的回应暴露了她的操控欲：“我希望永远不会遇到……我讨厌粗心的人。这就是我喜欢你的原因”（63；第三章）。操纵奏效了：“有一瞬间，我以为我爱上了她，”尼克承认道（63；第三章）。当然，乔丹必须作弊才能在高尔夫球赛中取得成功，这也暗示着女性无法仅凭自身能力在男性主导的领域取得成功。而对她外貌的描写则强化了女性闯入男性领域就显得男性化的刻板印象：“她身材纤细，胸部平坦，姿态挺拔，还像个年轻的学员一样，向后仰头，更显姿态”（15；第一章）。用来形容她外貌最常用的词是“轻快”。换句话说，乔丹看起来像个男孩。

Jordan Baker is characterized as a liar and a cheat. Nick catches her lying about having left a borrowed car out in the rain with its top down, and apparently she was caught cheating during a golf tournament, though she managed to get away with it under circumstances that imply the use of bribery or coercion: “The thing approached the proportions of a scandal – then died away. A caddy retracted his statement and the only other witness admitted that he might have been mistaken” (62–63; ch. 3).
