Like Daisy, Jordan exhibits a lack of concern for others that manifests itself in a refusal to take responsibility for herself, as we see when Nick reports that she drove her car “so close to some workmen that our fender flicked a button on one man’s coat” (63; ch. 3). Her response to Nick’s admonition that she should drive more carefully or not drive at all is a careless remark that “They’ll [other people will] keep out of my way. … It takes two to make an accident” (63; ch. 3). When Nick says, “Suppose you met somebody just as careless as yourself” (63; ch. 3), Jordan’s manipulativeness is revealed in her response: “I hope I never will. … I hate careless people. That’s why I like you” (63; ch. 3). And her manipulation works: “for a moment I thought I loved her,” Nick admits (63; ch. 3). Of course, the fact that Jordan must cheat to succeed at golf also implies that women can’t succeed in a man’s field purely on their own ability. And her physical description completes the stereotype that women who invade the male domain are rather masculine: “She was a slender, small-breasted girl with an erect carriage which she accentuated by throwing her body backward at the shoulders like a young cadet” (15; ch. 1). The word most frequently used to describe her appearance is jaunty. In other words, Jordan looks like a boy.

毫无疑问，这三人中最令人反感的莫过于默特尔·威尔逊。她聒噪、令人厌恶、虚伪做作，正如我们在汤姆为他们幽会而租的小公寓里，她“矫揉造作”（35；第二章）的举止所见。她背叛了对她忠贞不渝的乔治——所以她甚至连黛西那种丈夫不忠的借口都没有——而且她还欺凌羞辱乔治。她既没有黛西和乔丹的青春美貌，也没有她们的青春活力：“她三十五六岁，略显丰腴……她的脸上……没有一丝美貌可言”（29-30；第二章）。与其他两位女性不同，她性欲旺盛：“她性感地展现着自己丰腴的身材”（29；第二章），“她身上散发着一种显而易见的活力，仿佛她身体的神经都在持续燃烧”（30；第二章）。此外，她比黛西或乔丹更具性侵略性。当汤姆和尼克意外出现在威尔逊的修车厂时，

Surely, the most unsympathetic characterization of the three is that of Myrtle Wilson. She’s loud, obnoxious, and phony, as we see in her “violently affected” (35; ch. 2) behavior at the party in the small flat Tom keeps for their rendezvous. She cheats on George, who is devoted to her – so she doesn’t even have the excuse Daisy has of an unfaithful husband – and she bullies and humiliates him as well. She has neither the youth nor the beauty of Daisy and Jordan: “She was in the middle thirties, and faintly stout. … Her face … contained no facet or gleam of beauty” (29–30; ch. 2). And unlike the other two women, she is overtly sexual: “[S]he carried her surplus flesh sensuously” (29; ch. 2), and “there was an immediately perceptible vitality about her as if the nerves of her body were continually smouldering” (30; ch. 2). In addition, she’s much more sexually aggressive than Daisy or Jordan. When Tom and Nick show up unexpectedly at Wilson’s Garage,

她缓缓露出笑容，径直穿过丈夫，仿佛他是个幽灵，与汤姆握手，目光灼灼地直视着他。然后她舔了舔嘴唇，头也不回地用低沉沙哑的声音对丈夫说道：

[s]he smiled slowly and, walking through her husband as if he were a ghost, shook hands with Tom, looking him flush in the eye. Then she wet her lips and without turning around spoke to her husband in a soft, coarse voice:

“你们为什么不拿些椅子来，好让别人能坐下呢？”

“Get some chairs, why don’t you, so somebody can sit down.”

“哦，当然，”威尔逊同意道。……白色的灰烬笼罩着他深色的西装和苍白的头发，也笼罩着周围的一切——除了他的妻子，她走到汤姆身边。

“Oh sure,” agreed Wilson. … A white ashen dust veiled his dark suit and his pale hair as it veiled everything in the vicinity – except his wife, who moved close to Tom.

（30；第 2 章）

(30; ch. 2)

事实上，小说中只有默特尔是我们在阅读时“看到”与人发生性关系的女性：尼克买完烟回来后，默特尔和汤姆已经进了卧室，直到其他人陆续到达才出来。此外，默特尔对汤姆的兴趣显然是出于利益。她最初是被他昂贵的衣着所吸引，两人在镇上见面后，她立刻就开始花他的钱，而且她还想让汤姆和黛西离婚，娶她，这样她就可以搬出和乔治合住了十一年的车库公寓。

In fact, Myrtle is the only woman in the novel we “see” having sex: when Nick returns to their flat after his errand to buy cigarettes, she and Tom have disappeared into the bedroom and emerge only as the rest of their company begins to arrive. Furthermore, Myrtle’s interest in Tom is clearly mercenary. She was first attracted to him by the expensive quality of his clothing, she begins spending his money the instant they meet in town, and she wants him to divorce Daisy and marry her so that she can move out of the garage apartment she’s shared with George for the past eleven years.

值得注意的是，除了被负面刻画（几乎没有读者喜欢黛西、乔丹或默特尔）之外，在这三个例子中，这些离经叛道的女性都因故事情节的发展而受到惩罚。黛西的处境尤其令人唏嘘。在故事的那个阶段，乔丹与汤姆的婚姻毫无爱情，似乎是唯一合情合理的结局：她不配拥有更好的归宿，而且考虑到汤姆对婚外情的渴望，我们可以相当肯定，她的惩罚与她的罪行相符。汤姆会继续对她不忠，就像她背叛了他一样，更重要的是，她也背叛了盖茨比。在盖茨比被谋杀前不久的一次电话交谈中，尼克“把她甩了”（186；第九章），乔丹因此受到了惩罚。后来，在尼克告别乔丹的拜访结束时，他说：“她默默地告诉我，她已经和另一个男人订婚了。我怀疑，尽管有很多男人可以嫁给她，但她恐怕不会轻易答应”（185-186；第九章）。乔丹在那次拜访尼克时也对他说：“我现在根本不在乎你，但（被拒绝）对我来说是一种全新的体验，我当时有点晕眩”（186；第9章）。乔丹坚持说她不在乎，这恰恰凸显了她最终“吃了一惊”。

It is important to note that, in addition to being negatively portrayed (few if any readers find Daisy, Jordan, or Myrtle likeable), in all three cases, these transgressive women are punished by the progression of narrative events. That Daisy gets stuck with Tom in a loveless marriage seems, at that point in the narrative, only right and proper: she doesn’t deserve any better, and we can be relatively certain, given Tom’s desire for extramarital affairs, that her punishment will fit her crime. Tom will continue to be unfaithful to her just as she has been unfaithful to him and, more important, unfaithful to Gatsby. Jordan is punished when Nick “throw[s] [her] over” (186; ch. 9) during a telephone conversation just before Gatsby’s murder. Later, at the end of Nick’s farewell visit to Jordan, he says, “[S]he told me without comment that she was engaged to another man. I doubted that though there were several she could have married at a nod of her head” (185–86; ch. 9). Jordan also tells Nick, during that visit, “I don’t give a damn about you now but [being rejected] was a new experience for me and I felt a little dizzy for a while” (186; ch. 9). The way in which Jordan insists she doesn’t care merely underscores the fact that she is finally “brought down a peg or two.”

然而，最严厉的惩罚却加在了对父权制威胁最大的女人身上：默特尔·威尔逊。我说她对父权制威胁最大，是因为她毫不掩饰地违背了父权制下的性别角色，而且，尽管她出身社会底层，处境无力，但她的性活力却被描绘成一种攻击性，一种远胜于黛西或乔丹的个人力量。她的丈夫在她面前几乎完全消失，她“旺盛的活力”（35；第二章）使她成为车库里唯一一个与“水泥色的墙壁”格格不入的存在，而她的丈夫则“立刻融入其中”（30；第二章）。即使尼克和盖茨比开车进城时飞驰经过威尔逊的车库，他也不禁注意到“威尔逊太太气喘吁吁地在加油泵旁用力”（72；第四章）。正如迈克尔斯所观察到的，“威尔逊是他妻子的男人，而不是他自己的男人”（144；第7章）。事实上，迈克尔斯认为“他不够好，配不上他的妻子”（167；第8章）。默特尔甚至敢于反驳汤姆，坚持说她有权“提起黛西的名字”：“‘黛西！黛西！黛西！’威尔逊太太喊道，‘我想什么时候提就什么时候提！’”（41；第2章）。

The most severe punishment, however, is meted out to the woman who threatens patriarchy the most: Myrtle Wilson. I say she threatens patriarchy the most because she violates patriarchal gender roles so unabashedly and because, despite the powerlessness of her situation as a woman from the lower strata of society, her sexual vitality is portrayed as a form of aggressiveness, a personal power much greater than that of Daisy or Jordan. Her husband all but disappears in her presence, and her “intense vitality” (35; ch. 2) makes her the only thing in the garage to stand out from the “cement color of the walls” into which her husband “mingl[es] immediately” (30; ch. 2). Even as Nick speeds past Wilson’s garage on his way to town with Gatsby, he can’t help but notice “Mrs. Wilson straining at the garage pump with panting vitality” (72; ch. 4). As Michaelis observes, “Wilson was his wife’s man and not his own” (144; ch. 7). Indeed, Michaelis believes “there was not enough of him for his wife” (167; ch. 8). Myrtle even stands up to Tom, insisting that she has a right to “mention Daisy’s name”: “‘Daisy! Daisy! Daisy!’ shouted Mrs. Wilson. ‘I’ll say it whenever I want to!’” (41; ch. 2).

她因为喊了黛西的名字而受到的惩罚迅速而无情：“汤姆·布坎南动作利落，用手掌打断了她的鼻子”（41；第二章）。但尼克很快就轻描淡写地化解了这件事，有效地阻止了我们对默特尔产生任何同情。“然后浴室地板上散落着沾满血迹的毛巾，还有女人们的责骂声”（41；第二章），他这样描述道。麦基先生对这件事毫不在意，慢吞吞地走出了门，尼克跟在他身后，留下麦基太太“和凯瑟琳一边责骂一边安慰，跌跌撞撞地在堆满家具的房间里寻找救命的物品”（41-42；第二章）。换句话说，默特尔的鼻子被打断根本算不上什么大事，只不过是女人又要收拾的烂摊子，根本不值得男人操心，而且，默特尔是咎由自取。

Her punishment for saying Daisy’s name is swift and merciless: “Making a short deft movement, Tom Buchanan broke her nose with his open hand” (41; ch. 2). But Nick quickly trivializes the incident, effectively forestalling any sympathy we might feel for Myrtle. “Then there were bloody towels upon the bathroom floor and women’s voices scolding” (41; ch. 2), he reports. Mr. McKee is so unimpressed by the event that he slowly rambles out the door, and Nick follows him, leaving Mrs. McKee “and Catherine scolding and consoling as they stumbled here and there among the crowded furniture with articles of aid” (41–42; ch. 2). In other words, the breaking of Myrtle’s nose is no big deal, just another mess for women to clean up, nothing important enough to concern men, and what’s more, Myrtle had it coming.

当然，汤姆对默特尔的虐待与小说中对她的惩罚相比简直微不足道：当默特尔逃离丈夫并试图拦下一辆汽车时，她她以为情人带着她，结果被车撞死。值得注意的是，她的死状惨烈，包括遭受性虐待——“当他们撕开她汗湿的衬衫时，发现她的左乳像一块布片一样垂了下来”（145；第七章）——这强调了默特尔的性活力，也就是她的攻击性，才是她真正的罪过。事实上，对她死亡的描述以提及她的活力结尾：“她的嘴巴大张着，嘴角撕裂，仿佛她释放了积蓄已久的巨大活力时被噎住了”（145；第七章）。因此，尽管默特尔的罪行远不及黛西或乔丹严重——她不像黛西那样犯下过失杀人罪，然后让情人替她顶罪；她也不像乔丹那样本质上不诚实——但她受到的惩罚却是最严厉的。显然，小说认为攻击性，尤其是性攻击性，是女性最令人厌恶、最不可饶恕的品质。黛西和乔丹或许偶尔会是“坏女孩”，但默特尔的性攻击性让她始终都是个“坏女孩”。

Of course, Tom’s abuse of Myrtle is slight in comparison to the novel’s punishment of her: as Myrtle flees her husband and attempts to flag down the car she believes carries her lover, she is hit by that car and killed. It is important to note that her death includes sexual mutilation – “when they had torn open her shirtwaist still damp with perspiration they saw that her left breast was swinging loose like a flap” (145; ch. 7) – which underscores the notion that Myrtle’s sexual vitality, that is, her aggressiveness, was her real crime. Indeed, the description of her death closes with a reference to her vitality: “The mouth was wide open and ripped at the corners as though she had choked a little in giving up the tremendous vitality she had stored so long” (145; ch. 7). Thus, although Myrtle’s misconduct is much less serious than that of Daisy or Jordan – she doesn’t, like Daisy, commit vehicular homicide and then let her lover take the blame; and she is not, like Jordan, fundamentally dishonest – her punishment is by far the most severe. Obviously, the novel finds aggressiveness, especially sexual aggressiveness, the most unattractive and unforgivable quality a woman can have. Daisy and Jordan may be “bad girls” from time to time, but Myrtle’s sexual aggressiveness makes her a “bad girl” all the time.

《了不起的盖茨比》对一战后“新女性”的不适感——我认为，正是这种不适感导致了影片对现代女性的负面刻画和惩罚性描写——这种不适感至今仍然存在于美国文化中某些父权制意识形态之中。诚然，如今女性不再像以前那样因为留短发、穿短裙、跳狂野的舞蹈或出入喧闹的夜总会而受到谴责（除非她们在这些场合遭受暴力侵害，在这种情况下，她们可能会被指责“咎由自取”）。但是，女性仍然常常因为其他一些违反父权制性别角色的行为而受到异样的眼光，例如选择未婚生育并独自抚养孩子、在性方面表现得过于主动、在工作中“过于”追求成功，或者将事业置于婚姻和家庭之上：所有这些行为都常常被认为对女性而言“过于强势”，并经常被电视和电影行业讽刺。就像默特尔·威尔逊一样，如今的美国女性常常因为被认为具有攻击性而受到惩罚。事实上，一些美国人想把美国针对女性的暴力犯罪案件的增加归咎于女性日益增强的攻击性，或者至少是人们认为的攻击性。然而与此同时，公众却不愿承认女性的性别是导致她们遭受暴力犯罪的一个因素。

The Great Gatsby’s discomfort with the post-World War I New Woman, which, I have argued, is responsible for its negative characterizations and punitive treatment of the modern women it portrays, persists in some of the patriarchal ideology still operating in American culture today. Certainly, women are no longer generally condemned for wearing their hair or their skirts short, for dancing wild dances, or for frequenting raucous nightclubs (unless violence is perpetrated against them under these circumstances, in which case they may be blamed for “bringing it on themselves”). But women are still often looked at askance for other violations of patriarchal gender roles, such as opting to have children out of wedlock and raise them on their own, being sexually assertive, being “too” success-oriented on the job, or putting career before marriage and family: all of these behaviors are frequently considered “too aggressive” for women and are often satirized by the television and movie industries. Like Myrtle Wilson, American women today are often punished for what is perceived as their aggressiveness. Indeed, some Americans want to blame women’s increased aggressiveness, or at least what is perceived as such, for the increase in crimes of violence against women in this country. At the same time, however, the public doesn’t want to admit that women’s gender is a factor in the crimes of violence committed against them.

尽管最终通过了法律来保护女性免受职场性骚扰、免受家庭性虐待和其他形式的家庭暴力，并将强奸定性为暴力犯罪而非默许其为激情犯罪，但公众意识和支持此类虐待受害者的意愿仍然远远落后于立法。例如，人们仍然普遍认为受害者肯定要承担某种责任：“她的裙子领口开得有多低？”“她是不是在被丈夫殴打之前惹恼了他？”这被称为“责怪受害者”：我们倾向于认为，是女性的攻击性或不礼貌导致了这一切。让他们惹上麻烦的并非性别，而是不当或愚蠢的行为。即使是美国联邦调查局（FBI）在其对仇恨犯罪的定义中也忽略了性别因素。该局将仇恨犯罪定义为“全部或部分出于犯罪者对种族、宗教、残疾、民族出身或性取向的偏见而对人身或财产实施的犯罪行为”。

Although, finally, laws have been passed to protect women from sexual harassment on the job, to protect them from sexual abuse and other forms of domestic violence in the home, and to censure rape as a crime of violence rather than tacitly condone it as a crime of passion, public awareness and willingness to support the victims of such mistreatment still lag far behind the legislation. For example, there is the lingering belief that the victim must somehow be responsible: “How low-cut was her dress?” “Did she aggravate her husband before he beat her?” This is called blaming the victim: we want to believe that it is women’s aggressive or inappropriate or foolish behavior, not their gender, that can get them into trouble. Even the United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) overlooks the role of gender in its definition of a hate crime, which the Bureau describes as “a criminal offence against a person or property motivated in whole or in part by an offender’s bias against a race, religion, disability, ethnic origin or sexual orientation.”

然而，几年前加拿大一所大学的女工程系学生被一名男性闯入者押到教室墙边枪杀，这难道不是针对女性的仇恨犯罪吗？此后不久，美国一所大学的女工程系学生开始收到匿名恐吓信，这难道不是针对女性的仇恨犯罪吗？强奸、性骚扰和殴打妻子难道不是针对女性的仇恨犯罪吗？当然是，但它们至今仍未被普遍认可。换句话说，只有当公众和法律都承认父权制意识形态依然存在时，才能有效地解决这种压迫女性的根源。

Yet when the women engineering students were lined up against a classroom wall at a Canadian university several years ago and shot by a male intruder, wasn’t that a hate crime against women? And when, shortly thereafter, women engineering students at an American university began to receive anonymous threatening letters, wasn’t that a hate crime against women? Aren’t rape, sexual harassment, and wifebeating hate crimes against women? Yes, of course they are, but they are still not generally recognized as such. In other words, the patriarchal ideology responsible for the oppression of women can’t be effectively addressed until there is public as well as legal recognition that it still exists.

我非常理解识别父权制意识形态的难度，因为我自己也曾难以识别它，即便我曾是它的受害者。在我成长的白人蓝领家庭里，重点在于经济生存，在于阶级问题而非性别问题。我的父母教导我，政治领袖以及整个社会体系是如何偏袒富人，惩罚中产阶级，尤其是中下层阶级的。虽然他们极力鼓励我上大学，并告诫我不要把婚姻视为必然目标，但他们仍然认为，接受教师培训对我最有利，因为这份工作的时长和性质不会影响我未来作为妻子和母亲的职责（如果我选择结婚的话）。或许正是由于对性别问题的忽视，以及对其他政治议题的过度关注，才使我对父权制的运作视而不见。

I can understand very well the difficulty involved in recognizing patriarchal ideology because I’ve had difficulty learning to recognize it myself, even when I’ve been its victim. In the white, working-class household in which I was raised, the emphasis was on economic survival, on issues of class rather than gender. My parents taught me to see the ways in which political leaders, and our social system as a whole, favored the rich and penalized the middle classes, especially the middlemiddle and lower-middle classes. While I was very strongly encouraged to go to college and not to feel that marriage was an inevitable goal, my parents nevertheless believed that it would be to my best advantage to be trained as a schoolteacher because the hours and the nature of the work would not interfere with my future duties as a wife and mother should I choose to marry. Perhaps the absence of a focus on gender issues, combined with a very strong focus on other political issues, helped blind me to the operations of patriarchy.

然而，我确信，我也被自己逃避痛苦的欲望蒙蔽了双眼：我不想知道自己遭受压迫的种种方式，因为我觉得自己对此无能为力。所以，当我两次拒绝已婚老板的约会后被解雇时，我只是觉得他不再需要我了。当我在面试中把手从我左胸上拿开后，那位男士没有给我提供工作机会时，我只是同情那些最终可能为他工作的可怜女人。当我注意到一位教授每次我靠近他时都显得非常不自在，而且每当我靠近他时，他都会迅速离开正在交谈的人群时，我却从未想到这可能与我当时是哲学研究生项目中唯一的女性，或者与我比他高一个头有关。

I’m sure, however, that I was also blinded by my own desire to avoid pain: I didn’t want to know all the ways in which I was oppressed because I didn’t think there was anything I could do about it. So when I was fired from a job after twice turning down a date with my married boss, I simply thought he had no more use for my services. When I didn’t receive a job offer from the man whose hand I removed from my left breast during the job interview, I simply felt sorry for whatever poor woman might end up working for him. And when I noticed that one of my professors seemed extremely uncomfortable whenever I approached him and would quickly leave whatever group he was talking with when I came near, it didn’t occur to me that it might have something to do with my being the only woman in the graduate program in philosophy at that time or with my being a head taller than he was.

因此，当我二十出头第一次读《了不起的盖茨比》时，发现书中的女性角色——尤其是默特尔——冷酷无情，也就不足为奇了。这部小说既不道德又缺乏同情心，我当时根本没意识到它带有父权制的倾向。我也没有意识到小说中对女性的刻画与我在其他男性作家作品中看到的无数性别歧视的女性形象（尽管我至今仍然珍视这些作品，只是原因有所不同）之间有任何联系，因为我当时并没有意识到这些刻画究竟有多么性别歧视。“睁开双眼”的过程漫长而痛苦，而且至今仍在进行中。通过与许多学生、朋友和同事的交流，我知道很多女性，甚至一些男性，都有过类似的经历。

It should come as no surprise, therefore, that when I first read The Great Gatsby in my early twenties and found the female characters – especially Myrtle – heartless, amoral, and unsympathetic, it didn’t occur to me that the novel had a patriarchal agenda. I didn’t see any connections between the novel’s portrayals of women and the countless sexist portrayals of women I’d seen in the other male-authored works I loved (works I still value highly for different reasons today) because I didn’t see how sexist these portrayals really are. The process of “opening my eyes” has been a long and painful one, and it’s still in progress. I know from talking with numerous students, friends, and colleagues that my experience has been shared by many women and by some men as well.

显然，我们识别父权制意识形态的能力与我们是否愿意承受这种认知可能带来的痛苦之间存在着重要的联系。或许这正是许多女性和男性至今仍对女权主义抱有怀疑态度的原因之一：它不仅映照出我们的公共生活，也映照出我们的私人生活，并要求我们重新审视最私密的经历和最根深蒂固、最习以为常的假设。正因如此，《了不起的盖茨比》这样的作品对女权主义批评的初学者大有裨益。通过帮助我们了解父权制意识形态如何在文学作品中运作，这类作品可以帮助我们引导女权主义的视野，最终将焦点集中在我们自身。

Clearly, there is an important connection between our ability to recognize patriarchal ideology and our willingness to experience the pain such knowledge is liable to cause us. Perhaps this is one reason why feminism is still regarded so suspiciously by many women and men today: it holds a mirror not just to our public lives but to our private lives as well, and it asks us to reassess our most personal experiences and our most entrenched and comfortable assumptions. For this reason, works like The Great Gatsby can be very helpful to new students of feminist criticism. By helping us learn to see how patriarchal ideology operates in literature, such works can prepare us to direct our feminist vision where we must eventually learn to focus it most clearly: on ourselves.

拓展练习题：女性主义视角下的其他文学作品

Questions for further practice: feminist approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用女性主义批评来解读文中提及的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use feminist criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1夏洛特·珀金斯·吉尔曼的《黄色壁纸》（1892 年）是如何批判父权制意识形态的，特别是它在 19 世纪婚姻和医疗实践中的表现形式？

1 How does Charlotte Perkins Gilman’s “The Yellow Wallpaper” (1892) critique patriarchal ideology, specifically as it manifested itself in nineteenth-century marriage and medical practices?

2约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》（1902）是如何通过马洛对女性的评论和态度，以及他对小说中众多次要女性角色（包括他的姑妈、库尔茨的未婚妻、“野蛮”女人、土著洗衣妇和欧洲公司总部身穿黑衣的女人）的性别歧视刻画来反映父权制意识形态的？小说是引导我们接受还是批判马洛的性别歧视？小说本身是否意识到他的性别歧视？

2 How does Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness (1902) reflect patriarchal ideology through Marlow’s comments about and attitude toward women and through his sexist representations of the numerous minor female characters that populate the novel (including his aunt, Kurtz’s intended, the “savage” woman, the native laundress, and the women in black at company headquarters in Europe)? Does the novel invite us to accept or criticize Marlow’s sexism? Is the novel even aware of his sexism?

3托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》 （1987）如何揭示种族与性别交织影响女性经历的方式？这部作品如何强调姐妹情谊和女性社群的重要性？我们如何论证这部小说为我们提供了一个女性写作的范例？

3 How does Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987) reveal the ways in which race intersects with gender in creating women’s experience? How does the work underscore the importance of sisterhood, of women’s community? How might we argue that the novel offers us an example of écriture féminine?

4凯特·肖邦的《暴风雨》创作于1898年，当时人们普遍认为女性有性欲是不自然的。肖邦的故事是如何展现这一现象的呢？这部作品批判了这种父权制观念吗？它还批判了哪些其他父权制意识形态？这部作品对父权制、宗教和社会经济阶层之间的交集有何启示？

4 When Kate Chopin’s “The Storm” was written in 1898, it was generally considered unnatural for women to have sexual desire. How does Chopin’s story critique this patriarchal belief? What other patriarchal ideology does the story critique? What does the story suggest about the intersection of patriarchy, religion, and socioeconomic class?

5威廉·福克纳的《献给艾米丽的玫瑰》（1931）在哪些方面玩味了传统的性别范畴，揭示了传统性别定义的偏见和局限性？

5 In what ways might we say that William Faulkner’s “A Rose for Emily” (1931) plays with traditional gender categories, revealing the biases and limitations of traditional definitions of gender?

5 新批评

5   New Criticism

新批评在本书以及当今文学研究领域都占据着一个特殊的地位。一方面，它是本书所涵盖的唯一一种如今已被文学批评家弃用的理论，因此不能真正称之为当代理论。另一方面，新批评在20世纪40年代至60年代主导了文学研究，并对我们阅读和写作文学作品的方式产生了深远的影响。它关于文本证据的性质和重要性的一些最重要概念——即运用文本本身的具体例证来验证我们的解读——已被当今大多数文学批评家（无论其理论倾向如何）融入到他们解读文学作品的方式之中。事实上，如果你是英语专业的学生，​​你可能理所当然地认为，对文学作品的解读需要详尽的文本支撑，因为这种由新批评家引入美国并被称为“细读”的做法，在过去几十年里一直是高中和大学文学教学的标准方法。从这个意义上讲，新批评在我们中间仍然真实存在，而且在未来一段时间内可能仍将如此。

New Criticism occupies an unusual position, both in this textbook and in the field of literary studies today. On the one hand, it’s the only theory covered in this book that is no longer practiced by literary critics, so it can’t really be called a contemporary theory. On the other hand, New Criticism, which dominated literary studies from the 1940s through the 1960s, has left a lasting imprint on the way we read and write about literature. Some of its most important concepts concerning the nature and importance of textual evidence – the use of concrete, specific examples from the text itself to validate our interpretations – have been incorporated into the way most literary critics today, regardless of their theoretical persuasion, support their readings of literature. In fact, if you’re an English major, you probably take for granted the need for thorough textual support for your literary interpretations because this practice, which the New Critics introduced to America and called “close reading,” has been a standard method of high school and college instruction in literary studies for the past several decades. So in this sense, New Criticism is still a real presence among us and probably will remain so for some time to come.

然而，如今很少有学生了解新批评对文学研究的贡献，也鲜少有人了解它所构建的课堂教学理论框架。因此，我认为我们应该像重视这本教材中的其他理论一样重视新批评。此外，我们需要理解新批评，才能理解那些与之形成对比的理论。正如我们将在后续章节中看到的，读者反应批评反对新批评对文学文本的定义及其阐释方法，而结构主义则反对新批评将单个文学作品孤立地看待，使其脱离其他文学作品和其他文化产物。此外，解构主义的语言理论和新历史主义的客观证据观也与新批评关于语言和客观性的假设截然相反。

Few students today, however, are aware of New Criticism’s contribution to literary studies or of the theoretical framework that underlies the classroom instruction it has fostered. For this reason, I think we should give New Criticism the same kind of attention we give to the other theories in this textbook. In addition, we need to understand New Criticism in order to understand those theories that have developed in reaction against it. As we’ll see in subsequent chapters, reader-response criticism opposes New Criticism’s definition of the literary text and method of interpreting it, and structuralism rejects New Criticism’s focus on the individual literary work in isolation from other literature and from other cultural productions. In addition, deconstruction’s theory of language and new historicism’s view of objective evidence are directly opposed to New Critical assumptions about language and objectivity.

“文本本身”

“The text itself”

要充分理解新批评对当今文学研究的贡献，我们需要记住它所取代的批评形式：传记历史批评。这种批评方法在十九世纪和二十世纪初的文学研究中占据主导地位。当时，人们普遍通过研究作者的生平及其所处的时代背景来解读文学文本，以确定作者的意图，即作者希望文本传达的意义。人们仔细研读作者的信件、日记和散文，以及自传、传记和历史书籍，从中寻找作者意图的证据。在某些人看来，传记历史批评的极端之处在于，它似乎考察的是文本的传记历史背景，而不是文本本身。正如我的一位前教授所描述的那样，学生们去听一场关于华兹华斯《挽歌诗节》（1805）的讲座，他们听到的却是对诗人个人生活和思想生活的描述：他的家庭、朋友、敌人、爱人、习惯、教育、信仰和经历。 “现在你们明白《挽歌诗节》的含义了，”他们会这样被告知，而房间里的任何人，包括讲师本人，都没有翻开书来看过这首诗。或者，学者们也以类似的方式看待文学文本，仅仅将其视为历史的附属品，视为其创作年代“精神”的例证，而不是一件值得单独研究的艺术品。然而，对于新批评家来说，诗歌本身才是最重要的。

To fully appreciate New Criticism’s contribution to literary studies today, we need to remember the form of criticism it replaced: the biographical-historical criticism that dominated literary studies in the nineteenth century and the early decades of the twentieth. At that time, it was common practice to interpret a literary text by studying the author’s life and times to determine authorial intention, that is, the meaning the author intended the text to have. The author’s letters, diaries, and essays were combed for evidence of authorial intention as were autobiographies, biographies, and history books. In its most extreme form, biographical-historical criticism seemed, to some, to examine the text’s biographical-historical context instead of examining the text. As one of my former professors described the situation, students attending a lecture on Wordsworth’s “Elegiac Stanzas” (1805) could expect to hear a description of the poet’s personal and intellectual life: his family, friends, enemies, lovers, habits, education, beliefs, and experiences. “Now you understand the meaning of ‘Elegiac Stanzas,’” they would be told, without anyone in the room, including the lecturer, having opened the book to look at the poem itself. Or, in a similar manner, scholars viewed the literary text merely as an adjunct to history, as an illustration of the “spirit of the age” in which it was written, not as an art object worthy of study for its own sake. For New Critics, however, the poem itself was all that mattered.

“文本本身”成为新批评运动的口号，该运动旨在将我们的注意力集中在文学作品本身，并将其作为解读作品的唯一证据来源。新批评家认为，作者的生平、时代背景以及他/她所处时代的精神固然对文学史学家来说很有价值，但它们并不能为文学批评家提供可用于分析文本本身的信息。首先，他们指出，我们通常无法确切了解作者的意图。我们无法打电话给威廉·莎士比亚，询问他希望我们如何解读哈姆雷特在执行父亲鬼魂指示时犹豫不决的行为，而莎士比亚也没有留下任何关于其意图的书面解释。更重要的是，即使莎士比亚像某些作家一样留下了关于其意图的记录，我们也能从中了解到他想要达成的目标，而不是他实际达成的目标。有时，文学作品并不能完全实现作者的意图。有时，它甚至比作者意识到的更加深刻、丰富和复杂。有时，文本的实际含义与作者想要表达的含义截然不同。因此，了解作者的意图并不能告诉我们文本本身的含义，这就是为什么新批评派创造了“意图谬误”一词，用来指代那种认为作者的意图等同于文本含义的错误观念。

“The text itself” became the battle cry of the New Critical effort to focus our attention on the literary work as the sole source of evidence for interpreting it. The life and times of the author and the spirit of the age in which he or she lived are certainly of interest to the literary historian, New Critics argued, but they do not provide the literary critic with information that can be used to analyze the text itself. In the first place, they pointed out, sure knowledge of the author’s intended meaning is usually unavailable. We can’t telephone William Shakespeare and ask him how he intended us to interpret Hamlet’s hesitation in carrying out the instructions of his father’s ghost, and Shakespeare left no written explanation of his intention. More important, even if Shakespeare had left a record of his intention, as some authors have, all we can know from that record is what he wanted to accomplish, not what he did accomplish. Sometimes a literary text doesn’t live up to the author’s intention. Sometimes it is even more meaningful, rich, and complex than the author realized. And sometimes the text’s meaning is simply different from the meaning the author wanted it to have. Knowing an author’s intention, therefore, tells us nothing about the text itself, which is why New Critics coined the term intentional fallacy to refer to the mistaken belief that the author’s intention is the same as the text’s meaning.

正如我们不能从作者的意图中寻找文学作品的意义一样，我们也不能从读者的个人反应中寻找意义。任何读者都可能对文本本身提供的内容做出反应，也可能不做出反应。读者对文本的感受或看法可能源于过往经验中的某些个人联想，而非文本本身。例如，我对哈姆雷特母亲的感受可能仅仅基于我对自身母亲的感受。然而，我却得出这样的结论：我对文学人物的解读是正确的。这样的结论正是新批评家所说的“情感谬误”的例证。意图谬误混淆了文本与其来源，而情感谬误则混淆了文本与其情感，即文本所引发的情绪。情感谬误导致印象式的解读（如果读者不喜欢某个人物，那么这个人物一定是邪恶的）和相对主义（文本的意义取决于任何读者的理解）。这种做法的最终结果是混乱：我们失去了解读或评价文学的标准，文学因此沦为精神病患者随意投射自身意义的墨迹。

Just as we cannot look to the author’s intention to find the meaning of a literary text, neither can we look to the reader’s personal response to find it. Any given reader may or may not respond to what is actually provided by the text itself. Readers’ feelings or opinions about a text may be produced by some personal association from past experience rather than by the text. I may, for example, respond to Hamlet’s mother based solely on my feelings about my own mother and nevertheless conclude that I have correctly interpreted the literary character. Such a conclusion would be an example of what New Critics called the affective fallacy. While the intentional fallacy confuses the text with its origins, the affective fallacy confuses the text with its affects, that is, with the emotions it produces. The affective fallacy leads to impressionistic responses (if a reader doesn’t like a character, then that character must be evil) and relativism (the text means whatever any reader thinks it means). The final outcome of such a practice is chaos: we have no standards for interpreting or evaluating literature, which is therefore reduced to the status of the ink-blot on which psychiatric patients project their own meanings.

尽管在新批评对文学文本的解读中，作者的意图或读者的反应有时会被提及，但这两者都不是分析的重点。因为我们只有仔细考察，或者说“细读”，才能知道某个作者的意图或某个读者的解读是否真正代表了文本的意义：文本语言本身提供的所有证据——意象、符号、隐喻、韵律、格律、视角、背景、人物刻画、情节等等。这些要素构成或塑造了文学作品，因此被称为其形式要素。但在讨论这种细读方法如何运作之前，我们需要理解新批评家所说的“文本本身”究竟是什么意思，因为他们对文学作品的定义直接关系到他们对如何正确解读作品的看法。

Although the author’s intention or the reader’s response is sometimes mentioned in New Critical readings of literary texts, neither one is the focus of analysis. For the only way we can know if a given author’s intention or a given reader’s interpretation actually represents the text’s meaning is to carefully examine, or “closely read,” all the evidence provided by the language of the text itself: its images, symbols, metaphors, rhyme, meter, point of view, setting, characterization, plot, and so forth, which, because they form, or shape, the literary work are called its formal elements. But before we discuss how this method of close reading operates, we need to understand just what New Critics meant by “the text itself” because their definition of the literary work is directly related to their beliefs concerning the proper way to interpret it.

在新批评中，文学作品是一个永恒的、自主的（自足的）语言对象。读者和解读方式或许会改变，但文学文本本身却保持不变。它的意义如同其在纸上的物理存在一样客观，因为它是由彼此之间存在特定关系的词语构成——特定的词语以特定的顺序排列——而这种独一无二的关系创造了一种意义的复杂性，任何其他词语组合都无法复制。对罗伯特·海登的《中途航程》（1966）进行新批评解读，可以帮助我们理解这首诗，解释其意义的复杂性是如何运作的，但它无法取代这种意义的复杂性：只有《中途航程》才是《中途航程》，而且它永远都是《中途航程》。正因如此，新批评断言，诗歌的意义不能简单地通过释义或将其翻译成日常语言来解释，新批评家将这种做法称为释义的异端邪说。他们认为，改变诗中的一行、一幅图、一个词，你就会得到一首不同的诗。

For New Criticism, a literary work is a timeless, autonomous (self-sufficient) verbal object. Readers and readings may change, but the literary text stays the same. Its meaning is as objective as its physical existence on the page, for it is constructed of words placed in a specific relationship to one another – specific words placed in a specific order – and this one-of-a-kind relationship creates a complex of meaning that cannot be reproduced by any other combination of words. A New Critical reading of Robert Hayden’s “Middle Passage” (1966) can help us appreciate the poem by explaining how the poem’s complex of meaning works, but it cannot replace that complex of meaning: only “Middle Passage” is “Middle Passage,” and it will always be “Middle Passage.” This is why New Criticism asserted that the meaning of a poem could not be explained simply by paraphrasing it, or translating it into everyday language, a practice New Critics referred to as the heresy of paraphrase. Change one line, one image, one word of the poem, they argued, and you will have a different poem.

文学语言与有机统一性

Literary language and organic unity

文学文本形式要素的重要性源于文学语言的本质，而新批评认为，文学语言与科学语言和日常语言截然不同。科学语言以及许多日常语言都与文学文本形式要素相悖。语言依赖于外延，即词语与其所代表的事物或概念之间的一一对应关系。科学语言并不刻意引人注目，也不追求优美或情感上的感染力。它的任务并非指向自身，而是指向它之外的物理世界，并试图描述和解释这个世界。相比之下，文学语言依赖于内涵：依赖于意义及其细微差别的暗示、联想、暗示和唤起。（例如，“父亲”一词指代男性家长，但它也蕴含着权威、保护和责任。）此外，文学语言富有表现力：它传达语气、态度和情感。虽然日常语言也常常具有内涵和表现力，但通常并非刻意或系统地如此，因为它的主要目的是实用。日常语言旨在完成任务。然而，文学语言将语言资源组织成一种特殊的安排，一种复杂的统一体，以创造一种审美体验，一个自成一体的世界。

The importance of the formal elements of a literary text is a product of the nature of literary language, which, for New Criticism, is very different from scientific language and from everyday language. Scientific language, and a good deal of everyday language, depends on denotation, the one-to-one correspondence between words and the objects or ideas they represent. Scientific language doesn’t draw attention to itself, doesn’t try to be beautiful or emotionally evocative. Its job is to point not to itself but to the physical world beyond it, which it attempts to describe and explain. Literary language, in contrast, depends on connotation: on the implication, association, suggestion, and evocation of meanings and of shades of meaning. (For example, while the word father denotes male parent, it connotes authority, protection, and responsibility.) In addition, literary language is expressive: it communicates tone, attitude, and feeling. While everyday language is often connotative and expressive, too, in general it is not deliberately or systematically so, for its chief purpose is practical. Everyday language wants to get things done. Literary language, however, organizes linguistic resources into a special arrangement, a complex unity, to create an aesthetic experience, a world of its own.

因此，与科学语言和日常语言不同，文学语言的形式——即创造审美体验的词语选择和排列——与其内容，即意义，密不可分。更简单地说，文学文本的意义与其内容是不可分割的。因为一部文学作品，至少是一部伟大的文学作品，其形式和意义是共同发展的，如同一个复杂的生命体，其各个部分与整体密不可分。事实上，作品的有机统一性——所有部分协同运作形成一个不可分割的整体——正是新批评家评判文学作品质量的标准。如果一个文本具有有机统一性，那么它的所有形式要素就会共同作用，确立其主题，或者说作品的整体意义。通过这种有机统一性，文本既展现了文学作品必须具备的复杂性（以充分表现人类生活的复杂性），又展现了人类天性所追求的秩序。因此，对于新批评而言，阐释文学意义和评价文学伟大性合二为一，因为当新批评家阐释文本的有机统一性时，他们也同时确立了该文本的伟大之处。让我们仔细考察一下有机统一性所体现的文学价值标准：复杂性和秩序。

Unlike scientific and everyday language, therefore, the form of literary language – the word choice and arrangement that create the aesthetic experience – is inseparable from its content, its meaning. Put more simply, how a literary text means is inseparable from what it means. For the form and meaning of a literary work, at least of a great literary work, develop together, like a complex living organism whose parts cannot be separated from the whole. And indeed, the work’s organic unity – the working together of all the parts to make an inseparable whole – is the criterion by which New Critics judged the quality of a literary work. If a text has an organic unity, then all of its formal elements work together to establish its theme, or the meaning of the work as a whole. Through its organic unity, the text provides both the complexity that a literary work must have, if it is to adequately represent the complexity of human life, and the order that human beings, by nature, seek. For New Criticism, then, the explanation of literary meaning and the evaluation of literary greatness became one and the same act, for when New Critics explained a text’s organic unity they were also establishing its claim to greatness. Let’s take a closer look at each of the criteria of literary value embodied in organic unity: complexity and order.

在新批评中，文本的复杂性源于其中交织的多种且往往相互冲突的意义。而这些意义主要源于四种语言技巧：悖论、反讽、歧义和张力。简而言之，悖论是指看似自相矛盾却又反映事物本质的陈述。例如，圣经中有一个悖论：你必须舍弃生命才能获得生命。表面上看，这句话似乎自相矛盾：如何通过失去来获得它？然而，这句话的真正含义是，通过放弃一种生命——短暂的肉体生命，你将获得另一种更重要的生命：永恒的灵魂生命。同样，日常生活中的悖论也体现在琼尼·米切尔在她歌曲《大黄出租车》中巧妙运用的一句谚语中：“直到失去才懂得珍惜。”这与圣经中的悖论颇为相似。上述古老的谚语告诉我们，你必须先失去（物质上的）某些东西，才能找到（精神上的）它。新批评派指出，生活中许多精神和心理层面的现实本质上都是悖论式的，而悖论正是人类经验及其文学作品复杂性的根源所在。

For New Criticism, the complexity of a text is created by the multiple and often conflicting meanings woven through it. And these meanings are a product primarily of four kinds of linguistic devices: paradox, irony, ambiguity, and tension. Briefly, paradox is a statement that seems self-contradictory but represents the actual way things are. For example, it is a biblical paradox that you must lose your life in order to gain it. On the surface, that phrase seems self-contradictory: how can you gain an object by losing it? However, the phrase means that by giving up one kind of life, the transitory life of the flesh, you gain another, more important kind of life: the eternal life of the soul. Similarly, a paradox of everyday experience can be seen in the old saying Joni Mitchell uses so effectively in her song “Big Yellow Taxi”: “You don’t know what you’ve got ‘till it’s gone.” Not unlike the biblical reference above, this old adage tells us that you have to lose something (physically) before you can find it (spiritually). Many of life’s spiritual and psychological realities are paradoxical in nature, New Critics observed, and paradox is thus responsible for much of the complexity of human experience and of the literature that portrays it.

反讽，简单来说，是指某种陈述或事件因其发生的语境而显得不合时宜。以下摘自伊迪丝·华顿的《欢乐之家》 （1905）中对一位富裕丈夫道德感的描述，就是一个反讽的例子。

Irony, in its simple form, means a statement or event undermined by the context in which it occurs. The following description of a wealthy husband’s sense of moral rectitude, from Edith Wharton’s House of Mirth (1905), is an example of an ironic statement.

冬天的时候，教区长会来吃饭，她的丈夫会恳求她仔细查看名单，确保名单上没有离异妇女，除非她们已经通过再嫁给非常富有的人而表现出悔改之意。

Once in the winter the rector would come to dine, and her husband would beg her to go over the list and see that no divorcées were included, except those who had showed signs of penitence by being remarried to the very wealthy.

（57）

(57)

这段文字的讽刺之处在于，丈夫是个伪君子：他谴责离婚，但前提是离婚后不能获得同等或更大的财富；因此，他真正谴责的，是披着道德外衣的经济衰退。托妮·莫里森的小说《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）中也有类似的讽刺情节：佩科拉终于拥有了她梦寐以求的蓝眼睛。然而，她的愿望之所以“实现”，仅仅是因为她完全脱离了现实，以至于她相信自己棕色的眼睛是蓝色的。

Part of the ironic implication of this passage is that the husband is a hypocrite: he condemns divorce only if it is not followed by the acquisition of equal or greater wealth, so what he really condemns, under the guise of moral principles, is financial decline. An example of an ironic event can be seen in Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) when Pecola finally receives the blue eyes she has wished for so desperately. Her wish has been “fulfilled” only because she has lost touch with reality so completely that she believes her brown eyes are blue.

然而，新批评主要重视广义上的反讽，即文本中包含对同一人物或事件的不同视角。例如，简·奥斯汀的《理智与情感》（1811）就运用了这种反讽手法：我们可以从不同的视角出发，彻底谴责威洛比背叛玛丽安的行为；也可以原谅他，因为他的行为是出于爱情、经济困境以及他自己也感到懊悔的性格缺陷；还可以同情他，因为他的行为给他带来了沉重的惩罚；甚至还可以理解玛丽安的任性愚蠢是如何导致她心碎的。这种多样化的视角之所以被视为一种反讽，是因为每一种视角的合理性都会在一定程度上削弱其他视角的合理性。其结果是意义的复杂性，反映了人类经验的复杂性，并增强了文本的可信度。相反，如果将威洛比描绘成纯粹的恶人，玛丽安就会被理想化为完全无辜的受害者，文本就会容易受到读者质疑，从而产生一种讽刺性的疏离感。因此，文本自身的内在讽刺，或者说对多元视角的把握，使其免受读者质疑带来的外部讽刺。

New Criticism, however, primarily valued irony in a broader sense of the term, to indicate a text’s inclusion of varying perspectives on the same characters or events. We see this kind of irony, for example, when Jane Austen’s Sense and Sensibility (1811) offers us perspectives from which we may utterly condemn Willoughby for his treachery to Marianne; forgive him because his behavior resulted from a combination of love, financial desperation, and a weakness of character which he himself laments; sympathize with him for the severity of the punishment his behavior has brought upon him; and see the ways in which Marianne’s willful foolishness contributed to her own heartbreak. Such a variety of possible viewpoints is considered a form of irony because the credibility of each viewpoint undermines to some extent the credibility of the others. The result is a complexity of meaning that mirrors the complexity of human experience and increases the text’s believability. In contrast, had Willoughby been portrayed as purely and uncomplicatedly evil, Marianne would have been idealized as a completely innocent victim, and the text would have become vulnerable to the reader’s skepticism, which would put the reader at an ironic distance from the text. Thus the text’s own internal irony, or awareness of multiple viewpoints, protects it from the external irony of the reader’s disbelief.

当一个词、图像或事件产生两种或多种不同含义时，就会产生歧义。例如，在托妮·莫里森的小说《宠儿》（1987）中，树的意象就具有歧义性。塞丝背上的疤痕组织所形成的图案，暗示着诸多含义，其中包括苦难（“树”是残酷鞭笞造成的，象征着奴隶制下所经历的一切苦难）、坚韧（树木可以存活数百年，而疤痕组织本身也证明了塞丝非凡的生存能力，能够从最惨痛的经历中幸存下来）以及重生（如同树木在秋季落叶，并在来年春天“重生”，小说结尾，塞丝获得了新生的机会）。在科学或日常语言中，歧义通常被视为缺陷，因为它等同于缺乏清晰度和精确性。然而，在文学语言中，歧义却被视为丰富性、深度和复杂性的来源，能够提升文本的价值。

Ambiguity occurs when a word, image, or event generates two or more different meanings. For example, in Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987), the image of the tree produced by the scar tissue on Sethe’s back implies, among other things, suffering (the “tree” resulted from a brutal whipping, which is emblematic of all the hardships experienced under slavery), endurance (trees can live for hundreds of years, and the scar tissue itself testifies to Sethe’s remarkable ability to survive the most traumatic experiences), and renewal (like the trees that lose their leaves in the fall and are “reborn” every spring, Sethe is offered, at the novel’s close, the chance to make a new life). In scientific or everyday language, ambiguity is usually considered a flaw because it’s equated with a lack of clarity and precision. In literary language, however, ambiguity is considered a source of richness, depth, and complexity that adds to the text’s value.

最后，文学文本的复杂性源于其张力，广义而言，张力指的是对立事物之间的联系。最简单的张力形式是抽象与具象的融合，是将普遍概念融入具体意象之中。例如，在阿瑟·米勒的《推销员之死》（1949）中，威利那间沐浴在蓝光中的小屋，周围环绕着散发着愤怒橙色光芒的巨大公寓楼，这一具体意象体现了弱者、被比自身更强大、数量更多的力量所压迫的普遍概念。同样，琳达·洛曼唱歌哄威利入睡的具体意象体现了贤妻良母、照料者、养育者的普遍概念。这些具体的普遍概念——或者说，既具有具体层面（其意义是字面和具体的）意义，又具有象征层面（其意义是普遍的）意义的意象和虚构人物——被视为一种张力，因为它们以文学语言特有的方式将对立的物质现实和象征现实领域联系在一起。换句话说，洛曼家和琳达·洛曼这个人物既代表了他们自己，也代表了比他们自己更伟大的事物。

Finally, the complexity of a literary text is created by its tension, which, broadly defined, means the linking together of opposites. In its simplest form, tension is created by the integration of the abstract and the concrete, of general ideas embodied in specific images. For example, in Arthur Miller’s Death of a Salesman (1949), the concrete image of Willy’s tiny house, bathed in blue light and surrounded by enormous apartment buildings that emanate an angry orange glow, embodies the general idea of the underdog, the victim of forces larger and more numerous than itself. Similarly, the concrete image of Linda Loman singing Willy to sleep embodies the general idea of the devoted wife, the caretaker, the nurturer. Such concrete universals – or images and fictional characters that are meaningful on both the concrete level, where their meaning is literal and specific, and on the symbolic level, where they have universal significance – are considered a form of tension because they hold together the opposing realms of physical reality and symbolic reality in a way characteristic of literary language. In other words, the Loman home and the character of Linda Loman represent both themselves and something larger than themselves.

文本中对立倾向之间的动态互动也营造了张力，即其悖论、反讽和歧义之间的互动。例如，我们可以说《推销员之死》的情节结构是由现实与幻觉之间的张力构成的：威利·洛曼生活的残酷现实与他不断试图逃避的自我欺骗之间的张力。理想情况下，文本中对立倾向通过相互协作而保持平衡，从而形成稳定而连贯的意义。例如，《推销员之死》中残酷现实与自我欺骗之间的张力通过以下意义保持平衡：威利渴望成为一名成功的推销员和一位好父亲，以至于他面对弱肉强食的世界中普通人不可避免的失败，唯一的防御手段就是自我欺骗，但这种自我欺骗只会加剧他的失败。因此，这部剧向我们展示了残酷现实和自我欺骗如何相互滋养，直至死亡成为唯一的解脱。

Tension is also created by the dynamic interplay among the text’s opposing tendencies, that is, among its paradoxes, ironies, and ambiguities. For example, we might say that the action of Death of a Salesman is structured by the tension between reality and illusion: between the harsh reality of Willy Loman’s life and the self-delusion into which he keeps trying to escape. Ideally, the text’s opposing tendencies are held in equilibrium by working together to make a stable and coherent meaning. For example, the tension between harsh reality and self-delusion in Death of a Salesman is held in equilibrium by the following meaning: so great is Willy’s desire to succeed as a salesman and a father that his only defense against the common man’s inevitable failures in a dog-eat-dog world is self-delusion, but that self-delusion only increases his failure. Thus, the play shows us how harsh reality and self-delusion feed off each other until the only escape is death.

如前所述，文本的复杂性（所有这些语言技巧都促成了这种复杂性）必须与秩序感相辅相成，一部文学作品才能达到伟大境界。因此，所有多重且相互矛盾的含义文本中的悖论、讽刺、歧义和张力所产生的种种问题，必须通过它们对主题的共同贡献来化解或调和。文本的主题，或者说其完整含义，并非等同于其题材。更确切地说，主题是文本如何处理其题材。例如，婚外情是凯特·肖邦的《暴风雨》（1898）和阿尔贝托·莫拉维亚的《追逐》（1967）的题材，但婚外情的意义——其道德和心理内涵——在两篇故事中却截然不同。在肖邦的故事中，一次自发的婚外情似乎改善了两位参与者的情感健康和婚姻关系。我们可以说，《暴风雨》的主题是：决定对错、健康与不健康的，是个人境遇，而非抽象的规则。相比之下，在莫拉维亚的故事中，年轻妻子的婚外情似乎既是她与丈夫情感疏离的结果，也是造成这种疏离的原因。可以说，《追逐》的主题是婚外情是一种情感疏离，因此，它标志着婚姻中情感亲密关系的终结。由此可见，这一主题是对人类经验的一种诠释；如果文本本身是一部伟大的作品，那么这一主题便可作为对人类价值观、人性或人类境况的评述。换言之，伟大的文学作品都蕴含着具有普遍人类意义（道德和/或情感意义）的主题。它们向我们揭示了人性中一些重要的本质。我们或许并不喜欢或认同故事的主题，但我们仍然能够理解其内涵，而对于新批评而言，最重要的是，我们能够判断这一主题是否由文本的形式要素以一种有机统一的方式构建而成。

As noted earlier, the complexity of the text, to which all of these linguistic devices contribute, must be complemented by a sense of order if a literary work is to achieve greatness. Therefore, all of the multiple and conflicting meanings produced by the text’s paradoxes, ironies, ambiguities, and tensions must be resolved, or harmonized, by their shared contribution to the theme. The text’s theme, or complete meaning, is not the same thing as its topic. Rather, the theme is what the text does with its topic. For example, adultery is the topic of both Kate Chopin’s “The Storm” (1898) and Alberto Moravia’s “The Chase” (1967), but the meaning of adultery – its moral and psychological implications – is quite different in each story. In Chopin’s tale, a single, spontaneous act of adultery seems to improve the emotional health and marriages of the two participants. The theme of “The Storm,” we might say, is that individual circumstances, not abstract rules, determine what is right and wrong, healthy and unhealthy. In Moravia’s story, in contrast, the young wife’s extramarital affair seems to both result from and contribute to the emotional distance between her husband and herself. The theme of “The Chase,” it might be argued, is that adultery is a form of emotional distance, and, as such, it signals the end of emotional intimacy in a marriage. Thus, the theme is an interpretation of human experience, and if the text is a great one, the theme serves as a commentary on human values, human nature, or the human condition. In other words, great literary works have themes of universal human (moral and/or emotional) significance.1 They tell us something important about what it means to be human. We may not like or agree with the theme a story offers, but we can still see what that theme is and, most important for New Criticism, we can judge whether or not that theme is established by the text’s formal elements in a way that produces an organic unity.

新批评家正是通过细读，即对文本形式要素与其主题之间复杂关系的严谨考察，来确立文本的有机统一性。由于新批评认为理解文学文本主要在于理解其形式（这也是它有时被称为一种形式主义的原因），因此，清晰理解特定形式要素的定义至关重要。除了上文讨论的形式要素——悖论、反讽、歧义和张力等语言手法——我们还应该花些时间简要定义几种最常用的修辞手法：意象、象征、隐喻和明喻。

Close reading, the scrupulous examination of the complex relationship between a text’s formal elements and its theme, is how the text’s organic unity was established by the New Critic. Because of New Criticism’s belief that the literary text can be understood primarily by understanding its form (which is why you’ll sometimes hear it referred to as a type of formalism), a clear understanding of the definitions of specific formal elements is important. In addition to the formal elements discussed above – the linguistic devices of paradox, irony, ambiguity, and tension – we should also take a moment to briefly define a few of the most frequently used kinds of figurative language: images, symbols, metaphors, and similes.

比喻性语言是指具有超越或不同于字面意义的语言。例如，“下猫下狗”就是一个比喻，用来表示雨下得很大。如果按字面意思理解，这句话的意思当然是真的有猫狗从天上掉下来。广义上讲，意象（正如我们前面使用这个词所说明的）由一个或多个词语构成，这些词语指代感官所感知的物体或感官知觉本身：颜色、形状、光线、声音、味道、气味、质地、温度等等。更狭义的定义，也是在文学文本分析中最常用的定义，意象是视觉的，它由对物体、人物或场景的描述构成，就像眼睛所看到的那样。尽管意象总是具有字面意义，但……含义——对云的描述意味着天气阴天——它们还可以唤起情感氛围：例如，对云的描述可以用来唤起悲伤。

Figurative language is language that has more than, or other than, a strictly literal meaning. For instance, “It’s raining cats and dogs” is a figurative expression used to indicate that it’s raining very heavily. If it were taken literally, then the phrase would mean, of course, that actual cats and dogs were falling from the sky. Broadly defined, an image, as illustrated by our use of the word earlier, consists of a word or words that refer to an object perceived by the senses or to sense perceptions themselves: colors, shapes, lighting, sounds, tastes, smells, textures, temperatures, and so on. More narrowly defined, and most common in the practice of analyzing literary texts, imagery is visual, consisting of descriptions of objects, characters, or settings as they are seen by the eye. Although images always have literal meaning – a description of clouds means that the weather is cloudy – they can evoke an emotional atmosphere as well: for example, a description of clouds can be used to evoke sadness.

如果一个意象在文本中反复出现，它很可能具有象征意义。象征是一种兼具字面意义和象征意义的意象，它代表着具体的普遍概念，例如欧内斯特·海明威的小说《大双心河》（1925）中的沼泽。这片沼泽是字面意义上的沼泽——它潮湿，里面有鱼类和其他水生生物，需要穿靴子和专用工具才能在那里捕鱼——但它也“代表”或“象征”着其他事物：主人公尚未准备好面对的情感问题。公共象征通常很容易识别。例如，春天通常象征着重生或青春；秋天通常象征着死亡或垂死；河流通常象征着生命或旅程。因此，象征具有与其所代表的抽象概念相似的属性。例如，河流可以象征生命，因为河流和生命都是流动且不断向前发展的；两者都有源头和终点。此外，河流确实滋养着生命：有些生命形式生活在其中；有些生命形式饮用其中的河水。

If an image occurs repeatedly in a text, it probably has symbolic significance. A symbol is an image that has both literal and figurative meaning, a concrete universal, such as the swamp in Ernest Hemingway’s “Big, Two-Hearted River” (1925). The swamp is a literal swamp – it’s wet, it contains fish and other forms of aquatic life, one needs boots and special equipment to fish in it – but it also “stands for,” or “figures,” something else: the emotional problems the protagonist does not feel quite ready to face. Public symbols are usually easy to spot. For example, spring is usually a symbol of rebirth or youth; autumn is usually a symbol of death or dying; a river is usually a symbol of life or of a journey. Thus, a symbol has properties similar to those of the abstract idea it stands for. For example, a river can symbolize life because both a river and life are fluid and forward moving; both have a source and an endpoint. In addition, a river literally nurtures life: some life forms live in it; others drink from it.

文本提供的语境也有助于我们理解符号的含义。再次以海明威笔下的沼泽为例，除了沼泽与情感问题之间的相似之处——两者都难以应对，因为它们都包含未知的陷阱，这些陷阱可能危险且充满挑战——主人公对沼泽的态度与他对情感问题的态度如出一辙：他选择逃避。这种相似性暗示了沼泽的象征意义。有时，文本提供的语境是我们唯一的线索，因为有些符号是私密的，或者只对作者有意义，因此更难解读。例如，我们可能会怀疑一顶紫色毡帽的意象在故事中具有象征意义，因为它反复出现，或者扮演着某种似乎与爱、孤独或力量等抽象特质相呼应的角色，但我们需要通过研究这顶帽子在文本整体意义中的作用来理解其象征意义究竟是什么。当然，新批评始终关注文本整体意义的运作方式，因此，我们对文本私密象征意义的分析是否符合作者意图并不重要。重要的是，我们对文本私密象征意义的分析，如同我们对所有形式要素的分析一样，能够支撑我们所主张的文本主题。

The context provided by the text also helps us figure out a symbol’s meaning. To use the example of Hemingway’s swamp again, in addition to the similarities between a swamp and emotional problems – both are difficult to deal with because both involve unknown pitfalls that may be dangerous and are certainly challenging – the protagonist manifests the same attitude toward the swamp that he manifests toward his emotional problems: he avoids them. And this similarity tips us off to the swamp’s symbolic content. Sometimes, the context provided by the text is all we have to go on because some symbols are private, or meaningful only to the author, and therefore more difficult to figure out. We may suspect, for example, that the image of a purple felt hat has symbolic significance in a story because it recurs frequently or plays a role that seems to reverberate with some abstract quality such as love or loneliness or strength, but we’ll have to figure out what that symbolic significance is by studying how the hat operates within the overall meaning of the text. Of course, how something operates within the overall meaning of the text was always the bottom line for New Criticism, so it does not matter whether or not our analysis of the text’s private symbolism matches the author’s intention. What matters is that our analysis of the text’s private symbolism, like our analysis of all its formal elements, supports what we claim is the text’s theme.

与符号的双重维度——既包含字面意义又包含象征意义——不同，隐喻只有象征意义。隐喻是将两个截然不同的事物进行比较，并将其中一个事物的属性赋予另一个事物。例如，“我哥哥是个宝贝”就是一个隐喻。显然，它没有字面意义。如果它有字面意义，那就意味着我母亲生下了一块水晶石头，而她会因此登上所有小报的头条。这个短语的比喻义（也是它唯一的含义）是，我的兄弟与宝石有一些共同的特质：例如，他非常宝贵。因此，“他是个好人”通常用来表示“他是个很棒的人”。从比喻到明喻只需要一步：加上“像”或“如同”。“我的兄弟像宝石一样”或“我的兄弟像宝石一样珍贵”都是明喻，它们与我所引用的比喻做了相同的比较，尽管有人可能会认为明喻更柔和一些，因为“兄弟”和“宝石”之间的联系不那么直接或有力。

In contrast with the double dimension of the symbol – its inclusion of both literal and figurative meaning – a metaphor has only figurative meaning. A metaphor is a comparison of two dissimilar objects in which the properties of one are ascribed to the other. For example, the phrase “my brother is a gem” is a metaphor. Obviously, it has no literal meaning. If it did, it would mean that my mother gave birth to a crystalline stone, for which feat she’d be on the cover of every tabloid in the nation. The figurative meaning of the phrase, which is the only meaning it has, is that my brother shares certain properties with a gem: for example, he is of great worth. Thus, “he’s a gem” is generally used to mean “he’s a great guy.” To get from metaphor to simile requires one small step: add like or as. “My brother is like a gem” or “my brother is as valuable as a gem” are similes that make the same comparison as the metaphor from which I derived them, though one might argue that the simile is softer because the connection between the idea of “brother” and the idea of “gem” is less direct or less forceful.

我认为现在是时候运用这些新批评工具来检验新批评方法的实际应用了。那么，让我们来细读一下露西尔·克利夫顿的《内心深处有个女孩》（1977）。

I think it’s time we put these New Critical tools to work in order to see the New Critical method in action. So let’s do a close reading of Lucille Clifton’s “There Is a Girl Inside” (1977).

对《心中有个女孩》的全新批判性解读

A New Critical reading of “There Is a Girl Inside”

里面有个女孩

There Is a Girl Inside

里面有个女孩。

there is a girl inside.

她像狼一样好色。

she is randy as a wolf.

她不会离开。

she will not walk away

留下这些骨头

and leave these bones

对一位老妇人。

to an old woman.

她是一棵绿树

she is a green tree

在一片燃​​烧的柴火林中。

in a forest of kindling.

她是个绿皮肤的女孩

she is a green girl

一位被用过的诗人。

in a used poet.

她一直在等待

she has waited

像修女一样忍受病痛

patient as a nun

第二次降临，

for the second coming,

当她能克服白发的时候

when she can break through gray hairs

盛开

into blossom

她的情人们将会收获

and her lovers will harvest

蜂蜜和百里香

honey and thyme

而这片树林将保持原始状态。

and the woods will be wild

真是太神奇了。

with the damn wonder of it.

这首诗的标题“心中有个女孩”（There Is a Girl Inside）既是开篇第一句，也是第一节的最后两句，其中提到了“老妇人的骨头”，这立刻暗示着说话者是一位内心依然年轻充满活力的老妇人。这种初步的观察是否有其他文本证据支持呢？嗯，说话者确实提到了“心中有个女孩”。诗歌采用第三人称，以“她”的视角，将自己视为一个比她更年轻、更陌生的人。此外，在第二节结尾，说话者称自己为“一个用过的诗人”，这也暗示了年龄。因此，我们知道这首诗的核心张力很可能是青春与衰老之间的张力，是说话者内心感受与外在形象之间的张力。这种张力通过交替使用青春活力的语言（“女孩”、“好色的”——暗示性吸引或性唤起——“绿树”、“青涩的女孩”和“花朵”）与衰老和衰败的语言（“骨头”、“老妇人”、“引火物”——指用于生火的干枯木柴——“用过的诗人”和“白发”）来构建整首诗的结构。此外，这首诗的叙事维度，或者说它所讲述的“故事”，揭示了一位老妇人梦想着奇迹般的返老还童，梦想着青春的“第二次降临”，她觉得这青春正等待着她内心深处的“少女”，等待着她内心深处的少女，尽管她已“骨瘦如柴”、“白发苍苍”。因此，我们或许可以推测，这首诗的主题可能与永恒青春的悖论有关。（永恒青春之所以是悖论，是因为从生物学的字面意义上讲，时间和青春是互斥的：时间的流逝必然导致衰老。）为了探究这一主题的具体本质，并理解这首诗是如何构建这一主题的，我们需要更仔细地考察这首诗的形式要素。

The poem’s title, “There Is a Girl Inside,” which also serves as the opening line, and the final two lines of the first stanza, which refer to “these bones” of an “old woman,” suggest immediately that the speaker is an old woman who still feels young and vital inside. Is this initial observation supported by any additional textual evidence? Well, there’s the fact that the speaker refers to the “girl inside” in the third person, as “she,” as someone other and younger than herself. In addition, at the end of the second stanza the speaker refers to herself as “a used poet,” which also implies age. So we know that the central tension in the poem is probably the tension between youth and age, between what the speaker feels like on the inside and what she looks like on the outside. This tension structures the poem as a whole through the alternation of the language of youthful vitality (“girl,” “randy” – which suggests sexual attraction or arousal – “green tree,” “green girl,” and “blossom”) with the language of aging and decay (“bones,” “old woman,” “kindling” – which is old, dried-up wood used for starting fires – “used poet,” and “gray hairs”). In addition, the narrative dimension of the poem, or the “story” the poem tells, reveals an old woman dreaming about the miraculous rejuvenation, the “second coming” of youth, that she feels awaits the “girl inside” herself, the girl that she is still, despite her “bones” and “gray hairs.” Thus we might hypothesize, at this point, that the theme of the poem probably involves the paradox of timeless youth. (Timeless youth is a paradox because, on the literal level of biology, time and youth are mutually exclusive: the passage of time inevitably results in aging.) To discover the specific nature of the theme, and to understand how the poem establishes it, we need to closely examine more of the poem’s formal elements.

我们首先会注意到，从整首诗来看，青春与衰老意象的交替出现，在第三节的第四行戛然而止。诗的最后五行，包括最后一节的全部内容，都充满了青春、生育和性欲的意象，唤起了诗人认为能够战胜衰老的青春活力：“花朵”、“恋人”、“收获”、“蜂蜜和百里香”、“树林”、“野性”和“奇迹”。诗中还有其他什么地方强化了这种青春战胜衰老的强调吗？继续从整体上观察这首诗，我们会注意到随着诗歌的推进，标点符号的数量逐渐减少，这实际上是指停顿和停顿次数的减少。前两节共有五个句号（完整的句点），而第三节只有一个逗号（停顿），最后一节则完全没有标点符号，直到诗的结尾句号出现。事实上，从第三节的逗号开始数，这首诗的最后六行没有任何标点符号。这种标点符号，或者说停顿和停顿的急剧减少，暗示着速度的加快、激情的迸发和力量的增强，从而强化了最后一节中对青春胜利的强调。

The first thing we might notice, looking at the poem as a whole, is that the alternation of images of youth with images of age ends with the fourth line of the third stanza. The final five lines of the poem, which include the entire last stanza, consist of images of youth, fertility, and sexuality, and they evoke the youthfulness the speaker believes can overpower age: “blossom,” “lovers,” “harvest,” “honey and thyme,” “woods,” “wild,” and “wonder.” Does anything else in the poem reinforce this emphasis on the triumph of youth over age? Still looking at the poem as a whole, note the decrease in punctuation as the poem progresses, which is literally a decrease in stops and pauses. There are a total of five periods (full stops) in the first two stanzas, but there is only one comma (pause) in the third stanza and no punctuation at all in the final stanza until we get to the period that ends the poem. In fact, counting from the comma in stanza three, there is no punctuation in the final six lines of the poem. This dramatic decrease in punctuation, or decrease in stops and pauses, suggests acceleration, excitement, and power, thus reinforcing the emphasis on the triumph of youth in the final stanza.

既然我们已经开始分析这首诗的标点符号，不妨也看看它使用的词性。例如，我们可以看看动词的运用能告诉我们什么。首先，我们可以注意到说话者使用了强有力的主动语态动词：内心的女孩“不会离开”，她“能够突破”，以及“她的爱人将会收获”。这些强有力的主动动词强化了女孩强大而积极主动的形象，她有足够的力量去获得自己想要的东西。我认为第三节中“has waited”（一直在等待）的使用强化了内心的女孩已经准备好破茧而出的概念。这句诗并没有写成“she is waiting”（她正在等待），因为后者会暗示等待将会持续下去。虽然等待的时间长短不定，但“她一直在等待”，这暗示着她的等待已经结束或即将结束。在此语境下，我们还应该提及“她像狼一样好色”这个比喻，因为狼是一种强大的动物，会为自己想要的东西而战，而且通常都能如愿以偿。（例如，“像兔子一样好色”就肯定没有同样的含义。）

As we are already engaged in examining the poem’s punctuation, let’s take a look at the parts of speech it employs. For example, let’s see what its use of verbs can tell us. First, we might note the speaker’s use of powerful verbs in the active voice: the girl inside “will not walk away,” she “can break through,” and “her lovers will harvest.” These powerful, active verbs reinforce the idea that this girl is powerful and active, strong enough to get what she wants. I think the use of “has waited” in the third stanza reinforces the idea that the girl inside is ready to emerge. The line does not read “she is waiting,” which would imply that the waiting will go on for an indeterminate length of time, but “she has waited,” which suggests that her waiting is over or should be over soon. In this context, we should also mention the simile “she is randy as a wolf,” for a wolf is a powerful animal that fights for what it wants and usually gets what it fights for. (“Randy as a rabbit,” for example, would certainly not carry the same implication.)

还有其他与“绿树”相关的意象吗？如果有，它们是否有助于我们构建主题？“她是一棵绿树”这个比喻很适合我们，因为它让人联想到生长的季节——春夏两季，万物复苏、生机勃勃的季节。而“绿树”作为自然意象，蕴含着复苏的必然性。这棵树整个冬天都像老妇人的“骨头”一样枯萎，如同“引火物”一般死气沉沉，如今却已绽放。冬日里“绿树”的复苏力量，与两行之后“绿树女孩”的复苏力量紧密相连。如果绿树能够“破土而出……/绽放”，那么等待在老妇人体内的女孩也同样可以。

Are there any other images associated with the girl inside, and if so, do they contribute to the theme we’re trying to formulate? The metaphor “she is a green tree” is useful for our purposes because it invokes the growing seasons, spring and summer, the seasons of rebirth and plenitude. And because “green tree” is a nature image, it carries with it the inevitability of rejuvenation. The tree that has been a mere skeleton all winter, like the old woman’s “bones,” and as dead looking as “kindling,” has blossomed. The rejuvenating power of the “green tree” inside the winter tree is thus linked to the rejuvenating power of the “green girl” two lines down. If the green tree can “break through … / into blossom,” then so can the green girl who waits inside the old woman.

当然，“青涩少女”也暗示着这个女孩缺乏经验、天真无邪、不谙世事。而这一意象与下一节第二行的比喻“像修女一样耐心”完美契合。众所周知，大多数修会的修女都放弃了自私享乐的世界，放弃了肉体的世界，例如，罗马天主教修女所发的贞洁、贫穷和服从的誓言。因此，修女的意象在青涩少女和老妇人之间架起了一座桥梁，因为她们三人都以某种方式与肉体的世界隔绝开来。正如修女耐心等待着她的奖赏——基督的再临——老妇人和她内心深处的少女也都在耐心等待着她们的奖赏：青春的再次降临。

Of course, “green girl” also implies that the girl is inexperienced, naive, unused to the world. And this aspect of the image fits nicely with the simile in the second line of the next stanza: “patient as a nun.” As you may know, nuns belonging to most religious orders renounce the world of selfish pleasures, the world of the flesh, as we see, for example, in the vows of chastity, poverty, and obedience taken by Roman Catholic nuns. The image of the nun thus forms a bridge between the inexperienced girl and the old woman, for all three are cut off, in one way or another, from the world of the flesh. And just as a nun waits patiently for her reward – the second coming of Christ – so the old woman and the girl inside have both waited patiently for theirs: the second coming of youth.

诗中还有什么其他元素强化了年迈的叙述者与诗中少女之间的联系？让我们再次审视最后一节的语言，在前一节结尾“绽放”的青春，将在这一节中被“收割”。结尾的诗句总是至关重要的，而这些诗句似乎蕴含着格外丰富的意象。我们之前说过，在这一节中，青春战胜了衰老，的确如此，因为在这一节中，叙述者想象着新生的少女在树林中满足她的性欲。然而，“收割”、“蜂蜜”和“百里香”这几个词本身就具有某种歧义，这也强化了青春与衰老之间的联系。因为除了象征着青春的性活力之外，“收割”、“蜂蜜”和“百里香”还可以指与秋季相关的活动，从而与诗中的老妇人产生关联。

Is there anything else in the poem that reinforces the link between the aging speaker and the young girl inside? Let’s look again at the language of the final stanza, where youth, which has “blossom[ed]” at the end of the previous stanza, will be “harvest[ed].” Closing lines are always very important, and these seem to have especially rich images. We said earlier that this is the stanza where youth triumphs over age, and indeed it does, for this is the stanza in which the speaker imagines the newly emerged girl consummating her sexual desire in the woods. However, the words “harvest,” “honey,” and “thyme” have an ambiguity that also reinforces the bond between youth and age. For in addition to their connotations of youthful sexual vitality, “harvest,” “honey,” and “thyme” can refer to activities associated with autumn and therefore with the old woman.

收获发生在秋季生长季末期，此时植物已完全成熟，而非像“绿姑娘”那样，还“青涩”或幼嫩。蜂蜜和百里香都是需要收获的作物，因此含义相同。蜂蜜是蜜蜂采集花粉后，用花粉酿造的产物；而养蜂人则在蜜蜂酿造完成后，从蜂巢中取出蜂蜜。百里香是一种用于调味的芳香草本植物，主要​​在干燥后使用。因此，从比喻意义上讲，这节诗暗示了青春与衰老的融合。第二节诗中的“kindling”（引火物）一词也具有歧义，这在语境中同样适用。如前所述，“kindling”指的是用来引火的干枯老木。但引火物极易燃烧这一特性，恰恰将其与激情联系起来，因为激情也极易“燃起”。从这个意义上讲，我们可以说，在激情之中，青春与衰老融为一体。

A harvest occurs in the fall at the end of the growing season, when the plants are fully mature, not when they are “green,” or young, like the “green girl” inside. Honey and thyme, in that they are crops that are harvested, carry the same meaning. For honey is the product bees make from flower pollen after the pollen is harvested; beekeepers, in turn, harvest the honey from the hive after it is made. And thyme, a fragrant herb used to season food, is used primarily after it has dried up. Metaphorically, then, the stanza implies a merger of age and youth. The word “kindling” in the second stanza has an ambiguity that is useful in this context, too. As noted earlier, “kindling” refers to old, dried-up wood used to start fires. But the very fact that kindling catches fire so easily associates it with the quality of passion, which also “catches fire” easily. In this sense, we might say that, in passion, youth and age are one.

让我们从这首诗的语调中探寻青春与衰老的关系。我们可以将语调理解为说话者的语气，因为它表达了说话者对所言内容以及对读者的态度。我们知道说话者是一位老妇人。她的语调是忧郁的还是轻松的？是疲惫的还是充满活力的？是正式的还是非正式的？我们该如何描述它呢？首先，她对俚语的运用——例如在诗的第二行用“randy”来表示性欲，以及在最后一节用“damn”——告诉我们，她的语调略带俏皮和不敬，这种语调通常与青春联系在一起。她在第三节中玩的文字游戏也是如此：“修女”所等待的“第二次降临”既可以指基督的第二次降临，也可以指说话者自身的第二次“降临”，或者说，是她生命中第二次体验到性欲、性活力和性高潮的时刻。

Let’s see what we can learn about the relationship between youth and age from the poem’s tone, which it might be helpful to think of as the speaker’s tone of voice, for it expresses the speaker’s attitude toward what he or she is saying and toward the reader. We know that the speaker is an old woman. Is her tone somber or lighthearted? Weary or energetic? Formal or informal? How would we characterize it? Right away, her use of slang – “randy” to indicate sexual hunger in the second line of the poem and “damn” in the final stanza – tells us that the tone is somewhat playful and irreverent, a tone often associated with youth. And so is her play on words in the third stanza: the “second coming” for which the “nun” has waited can refer to both the second coming of Christ and the speaker’s second “coming,” or the second time in her life when she can experience sexual desire, sexual vitality, sexual climax.

说话者运用俚语和幽默营造出的非正式感，因诗歌短小的诗行而更加强烈，仿佛她正以对话的方式与我们交谈。此外，诗歌中缺少大写字母、韵律和格律等传统特征，也强化了这种非正式感。因此，我们可以说，在说话者轻松诙谐、不拘一格的语气中，我们看到了青春与衰老的融合：一个是蔑视礼节的年轻人，一个是超越礼节的老妇人。或者换句话说，我们知道说话者内心深处的少女在她生命中扮演着重要的角色，因为我们能从老妇人的声音中听到她青春的回响。而最后一行的语气无疑融合了少女和老妇人的双重身份，透过这声音，我们仿佛能看到她们举起双手叉腰，感叹“这该死的奇妙”。

The informality created by the speaker’s use of slang and humor is reinforced by the poem’s short lines, which make it seem as if she were speaking to us conversationally, and by the absence of traditional features such as capital letters, rhyme, and meter. We might say, then, that in the playful irreverence and informality of the speaker’s tone, we have the merger of youth and age: the young person who disdains formality and the old woman who has grown beyond it. Or to put it another way, we know that the girl inside the speaker is an important presence in her life because we can hear her youthful voice in the voice of the old woman. And surely the tone of voice in the last line is the voice of both girl and woman, the voice through which we can almost see them raise their hands to their hips as they refer to “the damn wonder of it.”

那么，或许我们可以这样概括这首诗的主题。《心中有个女孩》的主题并非仅仅是对古老格言“希望永存于人心”的重述，而是将其转化为一句同样具有普世意义的新格言：“青春永存于人心”。因为这首诗暗示，年龄本身也带来一种特殊的“收获”，那就是能够欣赏我们内心深处依然存在的青春馈赠，如同种子依然存在于成熟果实之中，从而让我们即使年老也能感受到青春的活力。因此，这首诗的主题将构成其结构的青春与衰老之间的张力融合或化解。我们可以得出结论，这首诗具有有机的统一性，因为正如我们所见，它的主题贯穿于所有形式要素之中；也就是说，它的形式与内容密不可分。此外，尽管这首诗看似简单迷人，却又令人信服，但我们对其有机统一性的分析揭示了其形式要素运作中令人惊讶的复杂性。我们有理由得出这样的结论。因此，作者认为，从新批评的角度来看，《里面有个女孩》是一部精心创作的文学作品，是一个统一、复杂的艺术作品，其主题具有普遍的人类意义。

Perhaps, then, we can formulate our theme in the following manner. The theme of “There Is a Girl Inside” is not merely a restatement of the old adage “Hope springs eternal in the human breast,” but a transformation of that adage into a new one of equally universal importance: youth springs eternal in the human breast. For the poem suggests that age brings with it a special “harvest” of its own, which is the capacity to appreciate the gifts of youth that remain within us as seeds remain within a ripened fruit and, as a result, to feel young even when we are old. Thus the theme of the poem brings together, or resolves, the tension between youth and age that structures it. And we can conclude that the poem has an organic unity because, as we have seen, its theme is carried by all of its formal elements; that is, its form and content are inseparable. Furthermore, although the poem appears to be charmingly, and disarmingly, simple, our analysis of its organic unity reveals a surprising complexity in the operations of its formal elements. We would be justified in arguing, then, that from a New Critical perspective, “There Is a Girl Inside” is a finely wrought literary text, a unified, complex art object the theme of which has universal human significance.

新批评作为一种内在的、客观的批评

New Criticism as intrinsic, objective criticism

正如我希望通过对克利夫顿诗歌的解读所展现的那样，新批评要求我们仔细考察文本的形式要素，以帮助我们发现诗歌的主题，并解释这些形式要素是如何确立主题的。因为新批评家认为这是判断文本价值的唯一途径。通过这种方式深入诗歌本身，新批评家相信他们能够让文学作品本身提供我们解读和评价它的语境。举一个显而易见的例子，在分析克利夫顿的诗歌时，我对“randy”一词的讨论仅限于其俚语含义，因为只有这个含义才能在整首诗的语境中说得通。韦氏新通用词典中该词的其他含义包括“粗俗的”、“庸俗的”、“好争吵的女人”和“威胁性的乞丐”。如果这些含义中的任何一个能够通过为主题增添新的维度来丰富我们对诗歌的解读，我就会将其作为该词歧义的一部分进行分析。但由于这些含义似乎都与诗歌的主题不符，所以我忽略了它们。因此，尽管大多数词语在词典中都有不止一个释义，但词语的歧义并非由词典决定，而是由诗歌的整体语境决定，只有根据诗歌的整体语境才能判断词语的含义。

As I hope the reading of Clifton’s poem illustrates, New Criticism asked us to look closely at the formal elements of the text to help us discover the poem’s theme and to explain the ways in which those formal elements establish it. For New Critics believed that this was the only way to determine the text’s value. By staying within the poem in this manner, New Critics believed they allowed the literary work itself to provide the context within which we interpret and evaluate it. To use an obvious example, in analyzing Clifton’s poem my discussion of the word randy focused only on the slang meaning of the term because only that meaning makes sense in terms of the context of the poem as a whole. Other meanings of the word found in Webster’s New Universal Unabridged Dictionary include “crude” or “vulgar,” “a quarrelsome woman,” and “a threatening beggar.” Had any of these meanings enriched our reading of the poem by bringing another dimension to the theme, I would have analyzed it as part of the word’s ambiguity. But because none of these meanings seemed appropriate in terms of the poem’s theme, I ignored them. Thus, although most words can be found to have more than one dictionary definition, a word’s ambiguity is determined not by the dictionary but by the context of the poem as a whole, in terms of which alone the word’s meaning or meanings must be judged.

同样，我也没有提及克利夫顿是一位非裔美国诗人，而且我的解读中也没有任何迹象表明作者的种族。尽管一位非裔美国批评家很可能会提及这首诗如何融入非裔美国文学传统，但从新批评的视角来看，这些信息虽然具有历史意义，却与我们评价这首诗的内在统一性和普世意义无关。（关于“普世主义”概念的歧视性，请参阅第11章和第12章“非裔美国批评”和“后殖民批评”。）

Similarly, I did not mention that Clifton is an African American poet, and there is nothing in my reading that would indicate the author’s race. Although an African American critic would most probably include some mention of the ways in which the poem participates in the African American literary tradition, from a New Critical perspective such information, while of historical interest, is irrelevant to our evaluation of the poem’s organic unity and universal significance. (See Chapters 11 and 12, “African American criticism” and “Postcolonial criticism,” for a discussion of the discriminatory properties of the concept of “universalism.”)

最后，我并没有尝试分析说话者的心理状态——尽管精神分析的解读可能会分析“狼”、“骨头”、“引火物”、“用过的”、“破碎的”和“野性”这些词语，从而论证诗歌的性意象背后隐藏着对暴力和自我毁灭的恐惧——因为诗歌本身似乎没有任何内容值得进行这样的分析。说话者的心理与诗歌的主题无关，也与我们理解诗歌的主题无关。有时，新批评派确实认为文本值得探讨其心理、社会或哲学元素，因为这些元素显然是作品人物塑造或情节不可或缺的一部分，正如我们所看到的。或许有人会发现，在威廉·福克纳的《献给艾米丽的玫瑰》（1931）或埃德加·爱伦·坡的《泄密的心》（1843）中，心理元素是人物塑造或情节发展不可或缺的一部分。在这些案例中，新批评家们确实探讨了这些元素，但他们的目的是考察这些元素如何运作以确立文本的主题（或者，如果文本存在缺陷，则如何削弱主题）。换句话说，新批评家们并没有忽视文本中显而易见的心理、社会或哲学维度；他们只是将这些维度审美化了。也就是说，他们对待心理、社会和哲学内容的方式与对待文本形式要素的方式相同：探究这些要素如何为作品有机统一所创造的审美体验做出贡献。新批评家们声称，通过这种方式，他们的解读始终保持在文本自身所创造的语境之内。

Finally, I did not try to analyze the speaker’s psychological state – though a psychoanalytic reading might have analyzed “wolf,” “bones,” “kindling,” “used,” “break,” and “wild” in order to argue that a fear of violence and self-destruction lies beneath the poem’s sexual imagery – because there doesn’t seem to be anything in the poem itself to warrant such an analysis. The speaker’s psychology is not involved in the theme of the poem, and it is not relevant to our understanding of the theme of the poem. Sometimes New Critics did believe that the text warranted a discussion of its psychological, sociological, or philosophical elements because those elements were obviously integral to the work’s characterization or plot, as we might find psychological elements integral to characterization or plot in William Faulkner’s “A Rose for Emily” (1931) or Edgar Allan Poe’s “The Tell-Tale Heart” (1843). In such cases, New Critics addressed these elements, but they did so for the purpose of examining how such elements operate to establish the text’s theme (or to undermine it, if the text is flawed). In other words, New Critics didn’t ignore the obvious psychological, sociological, or philosophical dimensions of the text; they aestheticized them. That is, they treated psychological, sociological, and philosophical content the same way they treated the text’s formal elements: to learn what these elements contribute to the aesthetic experience created by the work’s organic unity. In this way, New Critics claimed, their interpretation stayed within the context created by the text itself.

由于新批评派认为他们的阐释完全基于文本所创造的语境和文本提供的语言，他们将自己的批评实践称为内在批评，以表明新批评始终局限于文本本身。与之相对的是，那些运用心理学、社会学或哲学框架的批评形式——换句话说，所有不同于他们自身框架的批评——被他们称为外在批评，因为这些批评需要借助文本之外的工具来进行阐释。新批评派还将他们的方法称为客观批评，因为他们认为，他们关注每个文本自身的结构要素，从而确保了每个文本——每个被阐释的对象——自身将决定它应该如何被阐释。

Because New Critics believed their interpretations were based solely on the context created by the text and the language provided by the text, they called their critical practice intrinsic criticism, to denote that New Criticism stayed within the confines of the text itself. In contrast, forms of criticism that employ psychological, sociological, or philosophical frameworks – in other words, all criticism other than their own – they called extrinsic criticism because it goes outside the literary text for the tools needed to interpret it. New Critics also called their approach objective criticism because their focus on each text’s own formal elements ensured, they claimed, that each text – each object being interpreted – would itself dictate how it would be interpreted.

最佳解释

The single best interpretation

鉴于文本被视为一个拥有自身稳定意义的独立实体，新批评家认为，每部文本都存在一个最佳或最准确的解读，它能够最恰当地展现文本本身：最能解释文本的意义以及意义的产生方式，换言之，最能解释文本的内在统一性。正因如此，在新批评的鼎盛时期，解读文学文本的文章常常以考察其他批评家对同一文本的解读为开篇，旨在表明其他人的解读存在不足——重要的场景或意象被忽略，文本结构中的张力未能得到解决——而这往往是因为对文本主题缺乏正确的理解。换句话说，为了证明你对一部文学作品的解读是最佳的，你必须首先证明所有先前的解读都存在某种缺陷。

Given that the text was thus seen as an independent entity with a stable meaning of its own, New Critics believed that a single best, or most accurate, interpretation of each text could be discovered that best represents the text itself: that best explains what the text means and how the text produces that meaning, in other words, that best explains its organic unity. This is why, during New Criticism’s heyday, essays interpreting a literary text frequently began with a survey of other critics’ interpretations of the same text in order to show that everyone else’s reading fell short – that important scenes or images were unaccounted for, that tensions structuring the text were not resolved – often because a proper understanding of the text’s theme was lacking. In other words, in order to establish that yours was the best reading of a literary work, you would have to begin by establishing that all former readings were in some way inadequate.

鉴于新批评派对文本细节的严谨关注，他们的方法最适用于短诗和短篇小说也就不足为奇了，因为文本越短，其形式要素就越容易被分析。而当分析篇幅较长的作品，例如长诗、小说和戏剧时，新批评的解读通常仅限于对某些方面（或结构）的分析。例如，作品的各个方面，包括意象（或者仅仅是某种意象，例如自然意象）、叙述者或次要角色的角色、时间在作品中的作用、场景营造的光影模式，或其他形式要素。当然，无论分析何种形式要素，都必须证明它在文本主题的推进中发挥了重要作用，从而有助于作品整体的统一性。

In light of the scrupulous attention paid to textual details by the New Critics, it is understandable that their method worked best on short poems and stories because the shorter the text, the more of its formal elements could be analyzed. When longer works were examined, such as long poems, novels, and plays, New Critical readings usually confined themselves to the analysis of some aspect (or aspects) of the work, for example, its imagery (or perhaps just one kind of imagery, such as nature imagery), the role of the narrator or of the minor characters, the function of time in the work, the pattern of light and dark created by settings, or some other formal element. Of course, whatever formal element was analyzed, it had to be shown to play an important role in the text’s advancement of its theme and thus contribute to the unity of the work as a whole.

无论你对本章讨论的新批评原则是否熟悉，你或许都能对新批评对文学研究的持久贡献有所了解。它的一些原则和术语似乎已被人们遗忘。例如，如今很少有文学批评家断言文学文本独立于其产生的历史和文化之外，或者认为它具有单一的、客观的意义。几乎没有人再用“张力”一词来指代符号中具体意象和抽象概念的融合。然而，无论我们采用何种理论视角，新批评在引导我们关注文本的形式要素及其与文本意义的关系方面所取得的成功，在我们今天的文学研究中都显而易见。无论我们运用何种理论框架来解读文本，我们总是会用来自文本的具体证据来支撑我们的解读，这些证据通常包括对形式要素的关注。而且，除了一些解构主义和读者反应理论的解读之外，我们通常会努力构建一种能够传达文本作为一个统一整体的解读。

Through your own familiarity or unfamiliarity with the New Critical principles discussed in this chapter, you can probably form some idea of New Criticism’s lasting contribution to literary studies. Some of its principles and terminology seem to have fallen by the wayside. For example, few literary critics today assert that a literary text is independent of the history and culture that produced it or that it has a single, objective meaning. And almost no one uses the word tension to refer to the symbol’s integration of concrete images and abstract ideas. Nevertheless, New Criticism’s success in focusing our attention on the formal elements of the text and on their relationship to the meaning of the text is evident in the way we study literature today, regardless of our theoretical perspective. For whatever theoretical framework we use to interpret a text, we always support our interpretation with concrete evidence from the text that usually includes attention to formal elements, and, with the notable exception of some deconstructive and reader-response interpretations, we usually try to produce an interpretation that conveys some sense of the text as a unified whole.

颇具讽刺意味的是，新批评对批评理论的贡献——对文本本身的关注——恰恰是其衰落的根源。20世纪60年代末，几乎所有其他批评理论流派都开始关注文学文本的意识形态内容，以及这些内容如何反映和影响社会，而新批评坚持将文本分析为具有单一意义的孤立审美对象，这种做法无法满足这种关注。

It’s rather ironic, then, that New Criticism’s gift to critical theory – its focus on the text itself – was responsible for its downfall. New Criticism was eclipsed in the late 1960s by the growing interest, among almost all other schools of critical theory, in the ideological content of literary texts and the ways in which that content both reflects and influences society, an interest that could not be served by the New Critical insistence on analyzing the text as an isolated aesthetic object with a single meaning.

新批评派对文学文本提出的问题

The question New Critics asked about literary texts

鉴于新批评注重文本的单一意义及其确立该意义的单一方法，我们列出的新批评家对文学文本提出的问题中只有一个复杂的问题，这并不令人惊讶：

Given New Criticism’s focus on the single meaning of the text and its single method of establishing that meaning, it should not be surprising that our list of questions New Critics asked about literary texts should consist of only one complex question:

1对文本的哪一种解读最能体现其内在的统一性？换句话说，文本的形式要素及其所产生的多种含义，是如何共同支撑作品的主题或整体意义的？记住，一部伟大的作品必然具有普世的人类意义。（如果文本篇幅过长，无法涵盖其所有形式要素，将这个问题应用于作品形式的某些方面，例如意象、视角、背景等等。）

1 What single interpretation of the text best establishes its organic unity? In other words, how do the text’s formal elements, and the multiple meanings those elements produce, all work together to support the theme, or overall meaning, of the work? Remember, a great work will have a theme of universal human significance. (If the text is too long to account for all of its formal elements, apply this question to some aspect or aspects of its form, such as imagery, point of view, setting, or the like.)
