无论面对何种文学文本，这都是我们进行新批评解读时需要提出的问题。值得注意的是，尽管新批评家们相信文本具有单一的、客观的意义，但他们对于这一意义究竟是什么，以及文本如何产生这一意义，却鲜有共识。相反，对同一文本的不同解读层出不穷。正如在其他领域一样，即使是新批评领域的专家学者，对于具体作品的意义也存在分歧。我们的目标是运用新批评来丰富我们对文学文本的阅读，帮助我们以全新的视角看待和欣赏其形式要素的复杂运作，以及这些要素如何共同创造意义。

Regardless of the literary text at hand, this is the question we ask in order to produce a New Critical interpretation. It is interesting to note that, despite their belief in the text’s single, objective meaning, New Critics rarely agreed about what that meaning was or how the text worked to produce it. Instead, different interpretations of the same texts abounded. As in every field, even expert New Critical practitioners disagreed about the meaning of specific works. Our goal is to use New Criticism to help enrich our reading of literary texts, to help us see and appreciate in new ways the complex operations of their formal elements and how those elements function to create meaning.

以下对菲茨杰拉德《了不起的盖茨比》的解读，旨在展示新批评解读可能带来的成果。我通过分析文本的意象，发现了我认为小说的主题——人类的渴望。这些意象之美及其情感力量，使其成为小说中最令人难忘、最具启发性的维度。随后，我考察了文本的其他形式要素——特别是人物塑造、场景描写和文体特征——以确定我认为的小说主题：未实现的渴望是人类境况中不可避免的一部分。作为新批评的实践者，我关注小说中描述的历史时空，仅仅因为它们展现了一个超越时空、具有普世意义的主题。

The following interpretation of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a New Critical reading might yield. I discovered what I believe is the novel’s topic – human longing – by analyzing the text’s imagery, the beauty and emotional force of which make it the most memorable and revealing dimension of the novel. Then I examined other formal elements in the text – specifically, characterization, setting, and elements of style – to determine what I claim is the novel’s theme: that unfulfilled longing is an inescapable part of the human condition. As a practitioner of New Criticism, I was interested in the historical time and place described in the novel only as they manifest a theme that transcends historical time and place, a theme that has universal human significance.

渴望的“不朽之歌”：对《了不起的盖茨比》的新批评解读

The “deathless song” of longing: a New Critical reading of The Great Gatsby

几乎所有读过菲茨杰拉德《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）的读者都会注意到书中令人叹为观止的意象之美。的确，小说中萦绕心头、令人回味的意象，让人联想起作者最喜爱的诗人约翰·济慈的忧郁抒情。然而，对于菲茨杰拉德这部极具诗意的小说中，这些意象是如何构建文本整体意义的，却鲜有分析。

Few readers of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925) will fail to notice the breathtaking beauty of its imagery. Indeed, the haunting, wistful quality of the novel’s images evokes the melancholy lyricism of the author’s favorite poet, John Keats. Yet there has been little analysis of how the imagery in Fitzgerald’s powerfully poetic novel structures the meaning of the text as a whole.

有人可能会认为，这种疏忽源于评论界对《了不起的盖茨比》的过度关注，将其视为爵士时代的编年史——对美国历史上特定时期的社会评论——从而将注意力转移到历史问题上，而忽略了文本的形式要素。大多数评论家都认同，菲茨杰拉德的小说对20世纪20年代的美国价值观进行了尖锐的批判，这种价值观的腐败体现在沃尔夫希姆的剥削、黛西的虚伪、汤姆的背叛、乔丹的不诚实、默特尔的粗俗，以及美国民众的肤浅——盖茨比那些寄生虫般的派对宾客便是其化身——他们的道德底线随着岁月的流逝而不断下降。这是一个由汤姆·布坎南和迈耶·沃尔夫希姆这样的人掌控的世界，尽管他们站在法律的对立面，但这两个人物都与法律有着千丝万缕的联系。他们是唯利是图的掠食者，为了达到目的，不惜一切代价，甚至不惜钻任何道德的空子。这是一个空虚的世界，自私、酗酒和粗俗横行，优雅的社交舞蹈变成了“老男人推着年轻女孩在永无止境的笨拙圆圈里往后退”，以及“地位显赫的情侣们扭捏地、时髦地搂着彼此，躲在角落里”（51；第三章）。这是一个充满无常和动荡的世界。布坎南一家永远“不安地四处漂泊，哪里有打马球、哪里有钱人聚集”（10；第一章）。乔丹总是辗转于酒店、俱乐部和别人的家中。就连乔治·威尔逊，尽管家境拮据，也认为只要离开家乡，西迁就能解决问题。匿名和孤立才是常态，肤浅的价值观将追求社会地位和享乐置于一切之上。的确，可以说“灰烬谷”（27；第 2 章）——尼克给乔治和默特尔·威尔逊居住地附近的垃圾场起的名字——是这个世界精神贫瘠的隐喻：

It might be argued that this oversight has resulted from the critical focus on The Great Gatsby as the chronicle of the Jazz Age – as a social commentary on a specific period in America’s past – which has diverted attention onto historical issues and away from the text’s formal elements. Most critics agree that Fitzgerald’s novel offers a scathing critique of American values in the 1920s, the corruption of which is represented by Wolfsheim’s exploitativeness, Daisy’s duplicity, Tom’s treachery, Jordan’s dishonesty, Myrtle’s vulgarity, and the shallowness of an American populace – embodied in Gatsby’s parasitical party guests – whose moral fiber had declined with each passing year. This is a world run by men like Tom Buchanan and Meyer Wolfsheim, and despite their positions on opposite sides of the law, both characters are predators consumed by self-interest, capable of rationalizing their way around any ethical obstacle to get what they want. It’s an empty world where selfishness, drunkenness, and vulgarity abound, where the graceful social art of dancing has become “old men pushing young girls backward in eternal graceless circles” and “superior couples holding each other tortuously, fashionably, and keeping in the corners” (51; ch. 3). And it’s a world of impermanence and instability. The Buchanans are forever “drift[ing] here and there unrestfully wherever people played polo and were rich together” (10; ch.1). Jordan is always on the move among hotels, clubs, and other people’s homes. And even George Wilson, with the scant means he has at his disposal, thinks he can solve his problems by pulling up stakes and moving west. Anonymity and isolation are the rule rather than the exception, and superficial values put the pursuit of social status and good times above every other consideration. Indeed, one could say that the “valley of ashes” (27; ch. 2) – the name Nick gives to the dumping ground near which George and Myrtle Wilson live – is a metaphor for the spiritual poverty of this world:

一个奇特的农场，灰烬像小麦一样生长成垄、山丘和怪诞的花园，灰烬化作房屋、烟囱和升腾的烟雾，最终……化作在粉状空气中模糊移动、已经开始崩塌的人形。

a fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens, where ashes take the forms of houses and chimneys and rising smoke and finally … of men who move dimly and already crumbling through the powdery air.

（27；第 2 章）

(27; ch. 2)

由于杰伊·盖茨比被清晰地描绘成一个颇具神话色彩的浪漫人物，评论界对小说中腐败世界与其主人公之间的叙事张力给予了相当多的关注。对大多数评论家而言，盖茨比的梦想能力以及他对化身为梦想化身的女人全心全意的奉献，包括他对她不值得他如此奉献的真相视而不见，赋予了他一种“纯真”，而这种纯真他“保持”到了最后（Gallo 43）。事实上，评论界普遍认同马里乌斯·贝利的观点，即盖茨比代表了“精神抵抗的力量”以及“对庸俗和低级趣味最终侵蚀的免疫力”（13）。正如汤姆·伯纳姆所说，盖茨比“在周围的腐败环境中幸存下来，保持了健全完整的品格”（105）。2在这些评论家看来，主人公的纯真进一步谴责了摧毁他的社会。

Because Jay Gatsby is clearly portrayed as a romantic figure of rather mythic proportions, a good deal of critical attention has been given to the narrative tension between the corrupt world of the novel and its title character. And for most critics, Gatsby’s capacity to dream and to devote himself to the woman who embodies that dream, including his blindness to the fact that she doesn’t deserve his devotion, give him an “innocence” that he “maintain[s]” to the end (Gallo 43). Indeed, there is considerable critical consensus with Marius Bewley’s opinion that Gatsby represents “the energy of the spirit’s resistance” and “immunity to the final contamination” of “cheapness and vulgarity” (13). As Tom Burnam puts it, Gatsby “survives sound and whole in character, uncorrupted by the corruption which surrounded him” (105).2 For these critics, the protagonist’s innocence serves to indict further the society that destroys him.

然而，这种批判性的关注忽略了小说中一个更为核心的张力，而非盖茨比与他所处世界的张力。因为即便我们想将盖茨比与他所处的社会进行对比，也无法忽视显而易见的文本证据，即他至少在某种程度上也沾染了社会的腐败：例如，他是沃尔夫希姆的门徒，靠贩卖私酒和假债券发家致富。在我看来，文本的核心张力恰恰在于小说中描绘的腐败庸俗的物质主义世界与抒情意象之间的张力——这种令人伤感的优美和强烈的情感力量，使其成为小说中最令人难忘、最能揭示人物本质的维度——它被频繁地用来描绘那个世界。无论我们如何衡量某个特定人物的纯真或堕落，这种张力都构成了叙事结构，并最终通过一个超越小说所处历史时期的、具有普遍人性意义的主题得以解决：未实现的渴望是人类境况的一部分，是所有人的共通之处，也是无法逃避的。正如我们将看到的，无论人物或场景代表的是财富还是贫穷、高雅还是庸俗、堕落还是纯真，未实现的渴望的意象都被用来描述人物和场景。此外，未实现的渴望的意象常常与自然意象联系在一起，这暗示着未实现的渴望如同季节更迭一样，是不可避免的。最后，小说中未实现的渴望的意象往往具有一种静态的、永恒的特质，这既突显了它的普遍性，也突显了它的必然性：未实现的渴望一直是并将永远是人类境况的一部分。

This critical focus, however, overlooks a more central tension in the novel than that between Gatsby and the world in which he lives. For we cannot ignore the obvious textual evidence, even if we want to contrast Gatsby with the society he inhabits, that he shares at least some of its corruption: for example, he was Wolfsheim’s protégé and has made his fortune by selling bootlegged liquor and fake bonds.3 It seems to me that the text’s central tension is, instead, that between the world of corrupt, vulgar materialism portrayed in the novel and the lyric imagery – the wistful beauty and emotional force of which make it the most memorable and revealing dimension of the novel – so frequently used to describe that world. This tension structures the narrative regardless of how we measure the relative innocence or corruption of any particular character, and it is resolved by a theme of universal human significance that transcends the historical period in which the novel is set: the theme that unfulfilled longing is part of the human condition, common to all and inescapable. As we’ll see, the imagery of unfulfilled longing is used to describe characters and settings regardless of the wealth or poverty, refinement or vulgarity, corruption or innocence they represent. In addition, the imagery of unfulfilled longing is often linked with nature imagery, which suggests that unfulfilled longing is as inevitable as, for example, the change of the seasons. Finally, the imagery of unfulfilled longing often has a static, timeless quality in the novel, which underscores both its universality and its inevitability: unfulfilled longing has always been and will always be a part of the human condition.

让我们首先探讨一下，未实现的渴望这一意象是如何贯穿小说中代表不同社会阶层的人物的。为了完成这项任务，我们将从三个方面分析菲茨杰拉德的抒情意象如何影响小说中的人物塑造：（1）对逝去过去的怀念；（2）对未来实现的憧憬；（3）一种模糊不清、没有具体目标的渴望。

Let’s begin by examining how the imagery of unfulfilled longing weaves a common thread through characters who represent very different elements of society. To accomplish this task, we’ll analyze Fitzgerald’s lyric imagery in terms of the three ways in which it informs characterization in the novel: (1) as nostalgia for a lost past; (2) as dreams of future fulfillment; and (3) as vague, undefined longing that has no specific goal.

在对黛西和乔丹在路易斯维尔“美好纯洁的……少女时代”（24；第一章）的田园诗般的描述中，我们看到了对逝去时光的渴望。乔丹在那里“第一次学会了在清爽的早晨漫步于高尔夫球场”（55；第三章）。这是一个充满浪漫气息的过去，乔丹回忆说，她穿着“新买的格子裙……在风中轻轻飘动”，走在“柔软的土地”上，而黛西……

We see the imagery of longing for a lost past in the idyllic description of Daisy and Jordan’s “beautiful white … girlhood” (24; ch. 1) in Louisville, where Jordan “first learned to walk upon golf courses on clean, crisp mornings” (55; ch. 3). This is a romantic past where, Jordan recalls, she walked on “soft ground” in her “new plaid skirt … that blew a little in the wind” and where Daisy

她身着白衣，开着一辆白色小跑车，一整天家里的电话铃声不断，泰勒营地那些兴奋的年轻军官们都要求当晚独占她。“至少就一个小时吧！”

dressed in white and had a little white roadster, and all day long the telephone rang in her house and excited young officers from Camp Taylor demanded the privilege of monopolizing her that night. “Anyways for an hour!”

（79；第4章）

(79; ch. 4)

这是一个充满纯真浪漫的世界：“干净清爽的早晨”、“柔软的土地”、新裙子、白色连衣裙、白色敞篷跑车、铃声响起的电话，以及英俊的年轻军官。就连地上的尘土都散发着神奇的光芒：“一百双金银拖鞋在闪亮的尘土中沙沙作响”（158；第8章，我的斜体字）。

This is a world of virginal romance: “clean, crisp mornings,” “soft ground,” new skirts, white dresses, white roadsters, ringing telephones, and handsome young officers. Even the dust on the ground has a magical glow: “a hundred pairs of golden and silver slippers shuffled the shining dust” (158; ch. 8, my italics).

同样，尼克对童年时期中西部地区的描述也充满了对田园牧歌般过去的怀旧之情。他回忆起自己小时候从寄宿学校和大学乘火车回家的圣诞节情景，说道：

Similarly, Nick’s description of the Midwest of his youth is filled with nostalgic images of an idyllic past. Remembering his Christmas train rides back home from boarding school and college, he says,

当我们驶入冬夜，真正的雪，我们自己的雪，开始在我们身边蔓延，在车窗上闪烁，昏暗的灯光……威斯康星州的小车站掠过，一阵尖锐而狂野的气息突然涌入空气。我们深深地吸了一口气……无比清晰地感受到我们与这片土地的联系。

When we pulled out into the winter night and the real snow, our snow, began to stretch out beside us and twinkle against the windows, and the dim lights of small Wisconsin stations moved by, a sharp wild brace came suddenly into the air. We drew in deep breaths of it … unutterably aware of our identity with this country. …

那是我记忆中的中西部……我年轻时乘坐的激动人心的返程火车，寒冷黑暗中街灯和雪橇铃声，以及灯光照射的窗户在雪地上投下的冬青花环的影子。

That’s my middle-west … the thrilling, returning trains of my youth and the street lamps and sleigh bells in the frosty dark and the shadows of holly wreaths thrown by lighted windows on the snow.

（184；第9章）

(184; ch. 9)

如同黛西和乔丹少女时代“清爽洁净的早晨”、“柔软的地面”和“闪亮的尘土”一样，这段文字中的自然意象唤起了一个清新、纯净、未受世俗侵蚀的过去。诸如“真正的雪，我们自己的雪，开始在我们身边铺展开来，闪闪发光”和“一阵尖锐的狂风突然袭来”之类的句子，描绘出一片片开阔的空间——洁净、洁白、闪亮——不仅令人身心舒畅，更令人精神振奋。“真正的雪”当然指的是美国中西部北部地区冬季持续不断的大量洁白降雪，这与纽约市车轮碾过后变成泥泞的积雪形成了鲜明的对比。但“真正的雪”这个短语也暗示着，尼克童年时期在中西部的生活比他成年后所感受到的那种人为营造的氛围更加真实、更加纯粹。街灯、雪橇铃铛、冬青花环和亮着灯的窗户等温馨画面，进一步强化了这种理念，它们所营造的节日气氛和温馨氛围，唤起了人们对幸福童年安全稳定的感受。

Like the “clean, crisp mornings,” “soft ground,” and “shining dust” of Daisy and Jordan’s girlhood, the nature imagery in this passage evokes a fresh, clean, virginal past, untouched by the corrupt world. Phrases such as “the real snow, our snow, began to stretch out beside us and twinkle” and “a sharp wild brace came suddenly into the air” evoke open spaces – clean, white, and shining – that invigorate not just the body but the spirit as well. “[T]he real snow” refers, of course, to the enormous quantity of clean, white snow that falls in the upper Midwest and lasts all winter, as contrasted with the sooty snow that becomes slush under the wheels of New York City traffic. But the phrase “real snow” also suggests that life in the Midwest of Nick’s youth was more real, more genuine, than the artificial atmosphere he associates with his adult life. This idea is underscored by the homey images of street lamps, sleigh bells, holly wreaths, and lighted windows, whose festive, inviting quality evokes the security and stability of a happy childhood.

在《了不起的盖茨比》中，即使是短暂的对往昔的怀念，也蕴含着强烈的情感力量。例如，年轻的盖茨比在黛西离开后重返路易斯维尔，“绝望地伸出手，仿佛只想抓住一丝空气，留住她为他营造的那片美丽之地的一角”（160；第八章）；汤姆·布坎南“永远漂泊不定，带着一丝怅然，追寻着某场已无法挽回的橄榄球赛的激情”（10；第一章）。这些画面令人难以忘怀，也令人心痛，因为它们诉说着一种永远无法填补的空虚。正如用来描绘黛西、乔丹和尼克青春的意象一样，盖茨比和汤姆的这些画面唤起了一个永远逝去的世界，因为它已成往事。我们永远无法重返青春，而正如盖茨比最终领悟到的，过去的世界终将随着时间的流逝而改变。

In The Great Gatsby, even brief images of longing for the past carry emotional force. For example, the images of the young Gatsby revisiting Louisville after Daisy’s departure, “stretch[ing] out his hand desperately as if to snatch only a wisp of air, to save a fragment of the spot that she had made lovely for him” (160; ch. 8), and of Tom Buchanan, “drift[ing] on forever seeking a little wistfully for the dramatic turbulence of some irrecoverable football game” (10; ch. 1), are haunting and painful because they bespeak an emptiness that can never be filled. Like the imagery used to describe the youth of Daisy, Jordan, and Nick, these images of Gatsby and Tom evoke a world that is forever lost because it is forever past. We can never be young again, and the world of the past, as Gatsby finally learns, inevitably changes with time.

或许，小说结尾处那些最能唤起人们对逝去田园牧歌般往昔美好回忆的画面，最为震撼人心。尼克在返回明尼苏达州的前一天晚上，坐在沙滩上，沉思着……

Perhaps the most powerfully nostalgic images of an idyllic past forever vanished are those that close the novel. As Nick sits on the beach the evening before his return to Minnesota, he muses on

这里曾是荷兰水手们眼中繁花似锦的古老岛屿——新世界鲜嫩翠绿的胸怀。岛上那些消失的树木，那些为盖茨比的豪宅让路的树木，曾低声诉说着人类最终也是最伟大的梦想；在那短暂而迷人的瞬间，人们一定在这片大陆面前屏住了呼吸，被一种唯美的情怀所深深吸引。他既不理解也不渴望沉思，这是历史上最后一次他与足以让他惊叹的事物面对面。

the old island here that flowered once for Dutch sailors’ eyes – a fresh green breast of the new world. Its vanished trees, the trees that had made way for Gatsby’s house, had once pandered in whispers to the last and greatest of all human dreams; for a transitory enchanted moment man must have held his breath in the presence of this continent, compelled into an aesthetic contemplation he neither understood nor desired, face to face for the last time in history with something commensurate to his capacity for wonder.

（189；第9章）

(189; ch. 9)

在这段文字中，尼克的怀旧之情被赋予了全球历史的普遍意义：我们每个人对逝去青春和爱情的渴望——就像美国一样，曾经“盛开过一次”、“清新”、“翠绿”，而我们却“屏息凝神”——都融入并表达了对那片永远消失的原始美洲大陆的“迷人……奇迹”的怀念之中。而与这种失去相关的词语的反复出现——“曾经”、“消失”、“最后一次”、“短暂的”、“历史上最后一次”——则强调了这种失去的彻底、令人心碎的终结性。

In this passage, Nick’s nostalgic longing is universalized in global historical proportions: all of our individual longing for the dreams of lost youth and lost love – which, just like America, “flowered once,” “fresh” and “green,” while we “held [our] breath” – is absorbed in and expressed by a longing for the “enchanted … wonder” of a pristine American continent forever gone. And the repetition of words associated with this loss – “once,” “vanished,” “once,” “last,” “transitory,” and “for the last time in history” – underscore its utter, heartbreaking finality.

未实现的渴望意象也贯穿于人物刻画之中，以对未来实现的梦想的形式呈现。例如，在小说开头，尼克梦想着自己在债券行业取得成功，这体现在他购买的关于银行和投资的书籍中，而对这些书籍的描述紧随其后的是自然意象，两者紧密相连：

The imagery of unfulfilled longing also weaves a common thread through characterization in the form of dreams of future fulfillment. Early in the novel, for example, Nick dreams about his successful future in the bond business, embodied in the books he bought on banking and investments, the description of which is immediately preceded by, and wedded to, nature imagery:

于是，阳光明媚，树木枝繁叶茂……我再次感受到那种熟悉的信念：夏天来了，生活又重新开始了。

And so with the sunshine and the great bursts of leaves growing on the trees … I had that familiar conviction that life was beginning over again with the summer.

首先，要读的书实在太多了，而且，年轻清新的空气中也蕴藏着太多值得汲取的健康养分。我买了十几本关于银行、信贷和投资证券的书籍，它们像新铸的钞票一样，红金相间地摆在我的书架上，仿佛在预示着将揭开只有迈达斯、摩根和梅塞纳斯才知道的闪耀秘密。

There was so much to read, for one thing, and so much fine health to be pulled down out of the young breath-giving air. I bought a dozen volumes on banking and credit and investment securities and they stood on my shelf in red and gold like new money from the mint, promising to unfold the shining secrets that only Midas and Morgan and Maecenas knew.

（8；第1章）

(8; ch. 1)

用来形容这些书的语言——“崭新的”、“即将展开的”和“闪耀的”——将尼克对成功的渴望与春天里被“阳光”、“繁茂的树叶”和“清新的空气”唤醒的新生渴望联系起来。此外，将金融家摩根大通的名字与神话人物迈达斯和梅塞纳斯的名字并列，赋予了这段文字一种神话般的奇幻氛围，强化了尼克的成功并非唾手可得，而是他梦想着、渴望着的那种充满远见的希望，这种希望与春天令人心醉的美丽融为一体，浑然天成。

The language used to describe the books – “new,” “promising to unfold,” and “shining” – links Nick’s longing for success with the longing for new life awakened in the spring by the “sunshine,” “great bursts of leaves,” and “breath-giving air.” Furthermore, the inclusion of financier J. P. Morgan’s name with the names of mythical figures Midas and Maecenas imbues the passage with an ambience of myth, of fantasy, reinforcing the idea that Nick’s success is not guaranteed but dreamed of, longed for with a visionary hopefulness that merges with, and is as natural as, the aching beauty of spring.

尽管规模远不及其他角色，但未实现的渴望这一意象仍然将默特尔和乔治·威尔逊的形象与其他梦想着未来圆满的角色联系起来。尼克和盖茨比前往纽约市赴约吃午饭时，他们驱车穿过了“灰烬谷”：

Though certainly developed on a less grand scale, the imagery of unfulfilled longing nevertheless ties the depictions of Myrtle and George Wilson to those of the other characters who dream of future fulfillment. As Nick and Gatsby head to New York City for their lunch appointment, they drive through the “valley of ashes”:

我们经过罗斯福港，那里隐约可见系着红色腰带的远洋货轮，然后沿着一条鹅卵石铺成的贫民窟疾驰而去，贫民窟两旁是昏暗、无人居住的……褪色的镀金十九世纪的酒吧。然后，灰烬谷在我们两侧展开，我们经过时，我瞥见威尔逊太太气喘吁吁地在加油站的油泵旁使劲加油。

We passed Port Roosevelt, where there was a glimpse of red-belted oceangoing ships, and sped along a cobbled slum lined with the dark, undeserted saloons of the faded gilt nineteen-hundreds. Then the valley of ashes opened out on both sides of us, and I had a glimpse of Mrs. Wilson straining at the garage pump with panting vitality as we went by.

（72；第4章）

(72; ch. 4)

在“灰烬谷”映入眼帘之前，我们先看到了两个街区——都不是富裕的住宅区——它们为我们做好了准备。第一个街区有码头；第二个街区是贫民窟。然而，在这两个地方，我们都看到了未实现的渴望。在罗斯福港，我们看到“系着红色腰带的远洋轮船”，它们象征着未来冒险、享乐、财富，或者至少是改变的可能。在贫民窟，我们看到“褪色的镀金二十世纪初那些依然人迹罕至的酒吧”，它们唤起了昔日的魅力和激情。然后我们看到了默特尔·威尔逊，她此刻“在加油站的油泵旁费力地工作”，她的姿态体现了对未来圆满的渴望，或许是嫁给汤姆·布坎南，他将把她从“灰烬谷”中拯救出来，带她进入一个在她看来是天堂般的幸福世界。她“气喘吁吁，充满活力”，这突显了她与生命、春天、自然的联系，与她所居住的“荒凉的土地”（27；第 2 章）形成鲜明对比，在那里，人和物在“粉状的空气”（27；第 2 章）中都显得“灰蒙蒙的”。

We are prepared for our glimpse of the “valley of ashes” by the two neighborhoods – neither of them wealthy residential areas – that precede it. The first contains wharves; the second is a slum. Yet in both we see images of unfulfilled longing. In Port Roosevelt we see “red-belted ocean-going ships,” which evoke the possibility of future adventure, enjoyment, profit, or at least change. In the slum we see “undeserted saloons of the faded gilt nineteen-hundreds,” which evoke past glamour and excitement. Then we see Myrtle Wilson, whose posture at this moment, “straining at the garage pump,” embodies longing for future fulfillment, presumably in the form of marriage to Tom Buchanan, who will rescue her from the “valley of ashes” and deliver her into a world of, from her perspective, paradisal happiness. That she is “panting with vitality” underscores her connection with life, with springtime, with nature, in direct opposition to the “desolate area of land” (27; ch. 2) in which she lives, where people and objects alike appear “ash-grey” in the “powdery air” (27; ch. 2).

尽管乔治·威尔逊是那种“灰蒙蒙”的人，他的肤色“与车库的水泥色融为一体”（第2章第30页），但他依然充满活力，渴望着未来的实现：当他看到汤姆和尼克把车开进车库时，“他浅蓝色的眼睛里闪过一丝湿润的希望”（第2章第29页）。这是小说中唯一一次用生动的动词来形容乔治，也是唯一一次将这种颜色，或者至少是一种健康的色彩，与他联系起来。值得注意的是，小说中经常将这种颜色与盖茨比的希望联系在一起：他为了靠近黛西而买下的豪宅有“蓝色的花园”（第3章第43页）和“蓝色的草坪”（第9章第189页）；他的树有“蓝色的叶子”（第8章第159页）。当他和黛西重逢时，“一缕湿漉漉的头发像一抹蓝色颜料一样洒在她脸颊上”（90；第五章）。此外，乔治眼中“湿润的希望之光”与月光“浸透”年轻的盖茨比“散落在地板上凌乱的衣物”（105；第六章，斜体为笔者所加）的“湿润光芒”遥相呼应，当时他正夜里躺在床上憧憬着未来。

Although George Wilson is one of those “ash-grey” people, who “mingl[es] … with the cement color” (30; ch. 2) of his garage, even he is energized by longing for future fulfillment: when he sees Tom and Nick pull into his garage, “a damp gleam of hope spr[ings] into his light blue eyes” (29; ch. 2). This is the only time a lively verb is used to describe George, and it’s the only time that color, or at least a healthy color, is associated with him. Notably, it’s the color the novel frequently associates with Gatsby’s hopefulness: the mansion he bought in order to be near Daisy has “blue gardens” (43; ch. 3) and a “blue lawn” (189; ch. 9); his trees have “blue leaves” (159; ch. 8); and when he and Daisy reunite, “a damp streak of hair lay like a dash of blue paint across her cheek” (90; ch. 5). In addition, the “damp gleam of hope” in George’s eyes resonates with the “wet light” with which the moon “soaked” young Gatsby’s “tangled clothes upon the floor” (105; ch. 6, my italics) as he dreamed of the future in his bed at night.

当然，未实现的渴望这一意象，在唤起盖茨比对未来的憧憬时，得到了最富诗意的表达。例如，这位年轻的主人公爱上了黛西·费，渴望拥有她，因此对她的一切都着迷，包括她和家人居住的房子。

Of course, the imagery of unfulfilled longing finds some of its most poetic expression when it evokes Gatsby’s dreams of the future. For example, the young protagonist, in love with Daisy Fay and longing to possess her, is fascinated by everything about her, including the house in which she and her family live.

让[她的房子]弥漫着一种令人窒息的紧张气氛的，正是黛西住在那里。……房子里弥漫着一种浓郁的神秘感，暗示着楼上的卧室比其他卧室更漂亮、更凉爽，走廊里上演着欢快而光彩夺目的活动，以及那些不陈腐、不矫揉造作的浪漫故事。已经飘散着薰衣草的芬芳，但依然清新怡人，散发着今年闪亮的汽车和鲜花尚未凋谢的舞会的气息。

[W]hat gave [her house] an air of breathless intensity was that Daisy lived there. … There was a ripe mystery about it, a hint of bedrooms upstairs more beautiful and cool than other bedrooms, of gay and radiant activities taking place through its corridors, and of romances that were not musty and laid away already in lavender, but fresh and breathing and redolent of this year’s shining motor cars and of dances whose flowers were scarcely withered.

（155-56；第 8 章）

(155–56; ch. 8)

因为在这段文字中，盖茨比梦想着一种他几乎一无所知、遥不可及的生活方式，所以他将其理想化，正如黛西、乔丹、尼克和汤姆理想化他们一去不复返的青春一样。“令人窒息的激情”、“成熟的神秘”和“卧室的气息”这些词句，既营造出一种感官上的愉悦，又让人感觉盖茨比就像个小男孩，脸贴在糖果店的橱窗上，渴望着里面陈列的糖果——从某种意义上说，这正是他正在做的。这里的意象也营造出一种丰饶之感，一种渴望已久的成果即将实现的景象，正如我们从“成熟”、“光彩照人”、“清新芬芳”和“鲜花”这些词语中所感受到的那样。事实上，盖茨比的渴望如此强烈，以至于它能将“汽车”变成自然物：黛西家里发生的浪漫故事都“散发着”——也就是甜美的香气，通常是花香——“今年闪亮的汽车”的气息。因此，这种渴望能够脱离其人类的源头，独立存在也就不足为奇了，就像黛西在纽约酒店房间里，盖茨比与汤姆对峙时，她选择远离盖茨比那样：“只有那死去的梦在午后悄然流逝中挣扎，试图触碰那些不再触手可及的东西，痛苦地、却又不绝望地，朝着房间另一头那消失的声音努力”（142；第七章）。

Because, in this passage, Gatsby dreams of a lifestyle that is largely unknown to him and seems unattainable, he idealizes it just as Daisy, Jordan, Nick, and Tom idealize their irretrievable youth. The phrases “breathless intensity,” “ripe mystery,” and “hint of bedrooms” create simultaneously an air of sensuality and a feeling that Gatsby is a little boy with his face pressed against the window of a candy store, longing for the sweets he sees displayed inside, which is, metaphorically, precisely what he is doing. The imagery here also creates a sense of fecundity, of a fruition so longed for that it seems about to happen, as we see in the words “ripe,” “radiant,” “fresh and breathing and redolent,” and “flowers.” In fact, such is the power of Gatsby’s longing that it can turn “motor cars” into natural objects: the romances that occur in Daisy’s house are “redolent” – that is, sweet-smelling, usually of flowers – of “this year’s shining motor cars.” It should be no surprise, then, that such a longing as this can disconnect itself from its human source and live on its own, as it does when Daisy withdraws from Gatsby during his confrontation with Tom in the New York hotel room: “only the dead dream fought on as the afternoon slipped away, trying to touch what was no longer tangible, struggling unhappily, undespairingly, toward that lost voice across the room” (142; ch. 7).

盖茨比对未来圆满的渴望，最常被提及的意象之一，便是他独自站在长岛豪宅前的沙滩上，在“繁星点点”（第一章第25页）的映照下“颤抖”（第26页），双臂伸向黛西码头尽头“渺小而遥远的绿光”（第一章第26页）。这一意象令人想起之前讨论过的另一个场景：黛西离开后，盖茨比在路易斯维尔伸出手，渴望回到他逝去的过去。但这一次，盖茨比伸出的双臂，将对过去的渴望与对未来的憧憬融为一体，对他而言，这两者已然合二为一：他来到长岛，正是为了实现他对黛西的爱。码头尽头的绿光，如同春日绿意，承载着新生的希望。尽管绿灯看起来“渺小而遥远”，但矛盾的是，盖茨比在地理上和经济上都比失去黛西以来任何时候都更接近她。

One of the more frequently noted images of Gatsby’s longing for future fulfillment is that of the protagonist standing alone on the beach before his Long Island mansion, “trembling” (26; ch. 1) under the “silver pepper of the stars” (25; ch. 1) with his arms outstretched toward the “single green light, minute and far away” (26; ch. 1) at the end of Daisy’s dock. This image recalls one discussed earlier: that of Gatsby in Louisville after Daisy’s departure, his hand outstretched toward his lost past. But this time, the image of Gatsby’s outstretched arms merges longing for the past with longing for the future, which, for him, have become one and the same: the fulfillment of his love for Daisy that he has come to Long Island to gain. The light at the end of her dock is green, carrying with it the hope of new beginnings that the green verdure of spring brings with it. And though the green light seems “minute and far away,” Gatsby is, paradoxically, geographically and financially closer to Daisy than he has been since he lost her.

或许，用来描述盖茨比对未来实现梦想的渴望的最浓烈的意象，是描写这位年轻的主人公与黛西走在路易斯维尔的街道上，梦想着即将到来的伟大成就：

Perhaps the densest imagery used to describe Gatsby’s longing for future fulfillment occurs in the description of the young protagonist walking down a Louisville street with Daisy, dreaming of greatness to come:

这是一个凉爽的夜晚，带着一年中两次更迭时特有的那种神秘的兴奋感。房屋里​​静谧的灯光在黑暗中嗡嗡作响，星空下也涌动着一阵骚动。盖茨比眼角瞥见人行道的石块其实组成了一个梯子，通往树上的一个秘密地方——如果他独自一人爬上去，他就能爬上去，一旦到了那里，他就能吮吸生命的乳汁，吞下无与伦比的奇迹之乳。

Now it was a cool night with that mysterious excitement in it which comes at the two changes of the year. The quiet lights in the houses were humming out into the darkness and there was a stir and bustle among the stars. Out of the corner of his eye Gatsby saw that the blocks of the side-walks really formed a ladder and mounted to a secret place above the trees – he could climb to it, if he climbed alone, and once there he could suck on the pap of life, gulp down the incomparable milk of wonder.

黛西白皙的脸庞靠近他时，他的心跳越来越快。他知道，当他吻上这个女孩，将他那难以言喻的幻想永远与她转瞬即逝的气息交织在一起时，他的思绪将再也无法像神明那样自由驰骋。于是他静静地等待着，聆听着那仿佛来自星辰的音叉声。然后，他吻了她。他的唇瓣触碰着她，她便如花朵般为他绽放，化身圆满完成。

His heart beat faster and faster as Daisy’s white face came up to his own. He knew that when he kissed this girl, and forever wed his unutterable visions to her perishable breath, his mind would never romp again like the mind of God. So he waited, listening for a moment longer to the tuning fork that had been struck upon a star. Then he kissed her. At his lips’ touch she blossomed for him like a flower and the incarnation was complete.

（117；第6章）

(117; ch. 6)

在这段精彩的文字中，未实现的渴望这一意象至少发挥了两个重要的作用。首先，正如我们在尼克对未来成功的渴望中所看到的，这里的意象将人类的梦想与自然界的种种变化联系起来：“群星的涌动”似乎与人物因季节更迭而感受到的“神秘兴奋”相呼应，而这种兴奋又与他们所处的未来门槛相连，盖茨比渴望跨越这道门槛。换句话说，这一意象暗示着人类的渴望如同季节的更迭一样自然而然、不可避免。其次，这一意象将盖茨比渴望的宇宙性——他对未来的“难以言喻的憧憬”，他的思绪在其中“如同上帝的思维般驰骋”，他梦想着“畅饮那无与伦比的奇迹之乳”——与这种渴望的凡人化身：黛西——结合在一起。换句话说，即使人类的渴望与对女人的渴望这样具体而普通的事物联系在一起，它实际上也是比我们更伟大的宇宙力量的化身。

In this remarkable passage, the imagery of unfulfilled longing performs at least two important functions. First, as we saw in the case of Nick’s longing for future success, the imagery here links human dreams to the concerns of nature: the “stir and bustle among the stars” seem in sympathy with the “mysterious excitement” the characters feel because of the change of seasons, which is linked, in turn, to the threshold of the future at which they stand and which Gatsby longs to cross. In other words, the imagery suggests that human longing is as natural and inevitable as the seasons. Second, the imagery weds the cosmic quality of Gatsby’s longing – his “unutterable visions” of the future in which his mind “romp[s] … like the mind of God” and he dreams of “gulp[ing] down the incomparable milk of wonder” – to the mortal “incarnation” of that longing: Daisy. In other words, even when human longing is attached to something as specific and ordinary as the desire for a woman, it is really the incarnation of a cosmic force larger than we are.

换句话说，即便我们以为自己渴望的是某个特定的人、事或物，这种渴望也并非源于我们自身的局限，而是源于人类与生俱来的某种特质。事实上，用来刻画人物未竟之愿的最常见意象，往往是那些模糊不清、不依附于任何具体目标的渴望。例如，尼克从长岛进入纽约市时，他的渴望就体现了这种模糊性：“从皇后区大桥上看到的这座城市，永远是第一次见到的那种感觉，它仿佛第一次展现出世间所有神秘与美丽的奇妙承诺”（73；第四章）。我们并不知道他承诺的是怎样的神秘与美丽，因为尼克自己也无从知晓。他的渴望是模糊的。他只知道自己想要一些新鲜刺激的东西（“第一次见到”），一些令人兴奋的东西（“第一次展现出世间所有神秘与美丽的奇妙承诺”），一些奢华的东西（“世间所有神秘与美丽的奇妙承诺”）。

To put the matter in slightly different terms, even when we think we long for a specific person, event, or object, our longing is fed by something greater than our individual selves, by something inherent in the condition of being human. Indeed, the most frequent images of unfulfilled longing used to depict characters are those in which the longing is vague and undefined, not attached to any specific goal. For example, the vague quality of Nick’s longing is expressed in his comment upon crossing from Long Island into New York City: “The city seen from the Queensboro Bridge is always the city seen for the first time, in its first wild promise of all the mystery and the beauty in the world” (73; ch. 4). We’re not told what kind of mystery and beauty are promised because Nick doesn’t know. His longing is nonspecific. All he knows is that he wants something new and fresh (“seen for the first time”), exciting (“first wild promise”), and extravagant (“all the mystery and the beauty in the world”).

小说中大量描绘人们透过窗户向外眺望的意象，也体现了这种模糊的渴望。例如，尼克经常在傍晚沿着第五大道散步时，他会凝视着窗外……

We see the same kind of vague longing in the novel’s numerous images of people looking through windows. For example, on Nick’s frequent evening walks along Fifth Avenue he gazes in the windows of

出租车呼啸而过，驶向剧院区。……车厢里，人们依偎在一起等候，有人唱歌，有人讲着听不清的笑话，有人在车厢里做出难以辨认的手势，香烟的烟头勾勒出轮廓。

throbbing taxi cabs, bound for the theatre district. … Forms leaned together in the taxis as they waited, and voices sang, and there was laughter from unheard jokes, and lighted cigarettes outlined unintelligible gestures inside.

（62；第3章）

(62; ch. 3)

当然，尼克渴望成为他所看到的一切的一部分，渴望归属感，渴望分享透过出租车车窗看到的兴奋景象。但当他身处车窗内，向外眺望时，他也同样渴望着这一切。当他在汤姆和默特尔的公寓里参加派对时，从窗户向外望去，他不禁沉思：

Of course, Nick longs to be a part of what he sees, to belong, to share in the excitement visible through the cab windows. But he experiences the same kind of longing when he is one of the people inside the window, looking out. As he looks from the window of Tom and Myrtle’s apartment during their party, he muses,

高悬于城市上空的我们那排黄色窗户，想必也为昏暗街道上漫不经心的旁观者增添了几分人间的神秘感，而我，也成了他，抬头仰望，心生疑惑。我既置身其中，又游离于外，同时被这无穷无尽的生活变幻所深深吸引，又感到一丝疏离。

high over the city our line of yellow windows must have contributed their share of human secrecy to the casual watcher in the darkening streets, and I was him too, looking up and wondering. I was within and without, simultaneously enchanted and repelled by the inexhaustible variety of life.

（40；第 2 章）

(40; ch. 2)

我并非暗示在汤姆和默特尔公寓的聚会应该能让尼克感到满足或减轻他的孤独感。正如这段文字所表明的，这反而让他再次感到自己被拒之门外。我的观点很简单，尼克活了三十年，却始终没有遇到能让他产生归属感的人。他的渴望是一种孤独，但他并不清楚自己究竟在渴望什么。他只知道自己就像小说中最令人动容的描写之一中的年轻职员，他们有着一种模糊而未实现的渴望：“可怜的年轻职员，在窗前徘徊，等待着独自一人去餐厅吃晚餐的时间——黄昏时分的年轻职员，浪费着夜晚和生命中最令人心酸的时刻”（62；第三章）。此外，尼克从汤姆和默特尔的公寓窗户向外望去，想象自己是“昏暗街道上漫不经心的旁观者……抬头望着”昏黄的灯光，这一意象使之具有普遍意义。尼克描述的不仅仅是他自己模糊而未实现的渴望，也是“普通人”——“漫不经心的旁观者”——那种模糊而未实现的渴望，从而唤起了我们所有人都会经历的那种模糊而未实现的渴望。

I’m not suggesting that the gathering at Tom and Myrtle’s apartment should satisfy Nick or make him feel less lonely. As this passage indicates, it makes him feel, yet again, that he is on the outside looking in. My point is simply that, in his 30 years of life, Nick has yet to meet people for whom he can sustain the desire to belong. His longing is a form of loneliness, but he doesn’t quite know what it is he’s lonely for. He knows only that he is like the young clerks in one of the novel’s most touching images of vague, unfulfilled longing: “poor young clerks who loitered in front of windows waiting until it was time for a solitary restaurant dinner – young clerks in the dusk, wasting the most poignant moments of night and life” (62; ch. 3). Furthermore, the image of Nick looking out of Tom and Myrtle’s apartment window, imagining that he is “the casual watcher in the darkening streets … looking up” at its yellow light, universalizes the image. Nick is not merely describing his own vague, unfulfilled longing, but the vague, unfulfilled longing of an “Everyman” figure, as well – the “casual watcher” – thus evoking the vague, unfulfilled longing experienced by us all.

值得注意的是，张开双臂的意象，正如我们所见，体现了对过去和未来的渴望，在小说的结尾第三次出现，象征着一种模糊的渴望。

It is interesting to note that the image of outstretched arms, which, as we have seen, embodies the longing for both past and future, occurs a third time as an image of nonspecific longing at the end of the novel.

盖茨比相信那盏绿灯，相信那令人陶醉的未来，它年复一年地在我们眼前消逝。它当时与我们擦肩而过，但这无关紧要——明天我们会跑得更快，伸得更远。……在一个晴朗的早晨——

Gatsby believed in the green light, the orgastic future that year by year recedes before us. It eluded us then, but that’s no matter – to-morrow we will run faster, stretch out our arms farther. … And one fine morning –

于是我们奋力前行，如同逆流而上的船只，却不断被推回过去。

So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.

（189；第9章）

(189; ch. 9)

小说在此强调了盖茨比渴望的普遍性。盖茨比的绿光和伸出的双臂也成为了我们的：未来“在我们面前远去”，“从我们身边溜走”，但“我们会跑得更快”，“把双臂伸得更远”。在成为普遍的渴望的同时，盖茨比的渴望也变得模糊不清：对主人公而言，绿光代表黛西；对我们而言，它可以代表任何事物。但无论它代表什么，我们都会追逐它，即使我们的渴望永远无法实现。尽管我们渴望未来，船头朝前，但实际上，我们就像盖茨比一样，“不断地被拉回过去”。因为在人类渴望的永恒性中，过去与未来融为一体，而我们自身未实现的渴望，就是我们徒劳地“奋力抗争”的“暗流”。因此，尽管《了不起的盖茨比》中很少有人物得到同情的刻画，但他们未实现的渴望——他们彼此之间以及正如最后一段所强调的，与我们共同的经历——却被描绘得十分凄美动人。

Here the novel insists on the universal nature of Gatsby’s longing. Gatsby’s green light and outstretched arms become ours: The future “recedes before us,” “eluded us,” but “we will run faster” and “stretch out our arms farther.” And in becoming universal, Gatsby’s longing also becomes nonspecific: for the protagonist, the green light represents Daisy; for us, it could represent anything. But whatever it represents, we will pursue it despite the fact that our longing will never be fulfilled. Although we’re longing toward the future, with the prow of our boat facing forward, we are, in fact, like Gatsby, “borne back ceaselessly into the past.” For in the timelessness of human longing, past and future are one, and our own unfulfilled longing is the “current” against which we “beat on” in vain. Thus, while few of the characters in The Great Gatsby are sympathetically portrayed, their unfulfilled longing – the experience they have in common with one another and, as this final passage underscores, with us – is portrayed with great poignancy.

未实现的渴望这一意象在小说对场景的描绘中也贯穿始终，并且在这里，它也像一条线索一样，将不同的社会阶层串联起来。第一个显著的例子出现在对盖茨比豪宅的描写中：“无论从哪个角度来看，这都是一座宏伟的建筑——它完全仿照诺曼底的市政厅建造，一侧耸立着一座崭新的塔楼，上面覆盖着一层稀疏的常春藤”（9；第一章）。甚至在我们见到盖茨比之前，他所居住的环境就已经暗示了他生命核心的未实现的渴望。就像盖茨比本人一样，这座豪宅也显得过于宏大，“一座宏伟的建筑”，它试图成为它并非之物，它只能模仿之物——一座诺曼底的市政厅——正如“稀疏的常春藤”让人联想到一个试图成为男人的少年。高耸入云的塔楼也暗示着对眼前之外事物的渴望。此外，宅邸俯瞰海湾，仿佛也在渴望着自身之外的事物。正如我们之前看到的，它正对着黛西码头尽头的绿灯——小说中象征着未竟之愿的标志。

The imagery of unfulfilled longing is also pervasive in the novel’s evocation of setting, and here, too, it weaves a common thread through disparate social strata. The first notable example occurs in the description of Gatsby’s mansion, “a colossal affair by any standard – it was a factual imitation of some Hôtel de Ville in Normandy, with a tower on one side, spanking new under a thin beard of raw ivy” (9; ch. 1). Before we even meet Gatsby, the setting in which he lives suggests the unfulfilled longing that is at the core of his existence. Like Gatsby, the mansion is larger than life, “a colossal affair,” that is trying to be something it’s not, something it can only imitate – a Hôtel de Ville in Normandy – just as the “thin beard of raw ivy” evokes the image of an adolescent boy trying to be a man. The tower, reaching toward the sky, also suggests a yearning for something beyond the immediately available. Furthermore, the mansion looks out over the bay, again as if yearning for something beyond itself, and as we saw earlier, it faces the green light at the end of Daisy’s dock, the novel’s icon of unfulfilled longing.

小说中，更常见的是，通过营造与人物实际生活截然相反的浪漫氛围，来营造一种未实现的渴望感。例如，尼克第一次拜访布坎南家时，家中气氛紧张而充满冲突——汤姆和黛西显然吵过架，默特尔的电话在晚餐时不断打断，乔丹肆无忌惮地试图偷听隔壁房间布坎南夫妇的争吵，汤姆滔滔不绝地发表着他的种族主义言论——此时，作者对场景的描写充满了对田园牧歌式美好生活的向往，尽管这种美好并未实现。

More frequently, an atmosphere of unfulfilled longing is created in the novel by settings that evoke a romantic ambience opposite that experienced by the characters who populate those settings. For example, in the midst of the tension and strife at the Buchanans’ home during Nick’s first visit there – Tom and Daisy have obviously been fighting, insistent phone calls from Myrtle intrude during dinner, Jordan shamelessly tries to overhear the Buchanans’ quarrel in the next room, Tom pontificates about his racist views – the setting is described with keen appreciation for the idyllic fulfillment promised, though not delivered, by the setting.

我们穿过高高的走廊，走进一个明亮粉红的空间，两端的落地窗将这空间与房屋巧妙地连接起来。窗户半开着，洁白的窗框在窗外嫩绿的草坪映衬下闪闪发光，草坪似乎也向屋内蔓延开来。微风吹过房间，将窗帘一端吹进另一端，像淡色的旗帜，卷曲着飘向磨砂的窗外。婚礼蛋糕般的光影飘落在天花板上，然后波光粼粼地洒在酒红色的地毯上，在地毯上投下阴影，就像风在海面上投下阴影一样。

We walked through a high hallway into a bright rosy-colored space, fragilely bound into the house by French windows at either end. The windows were ajar and gleaming white against the fresh grass outside that seemed to grow a little way into the house. A breeze blew through the room, blew curtains in at one end and out the other like pale flags, twisting them up toward the frosted wedding cake of the ceiling, and then rippled over the wine-colored rug, making a shadow on it as wind does on the sea.

（12；第1章）

(12; ch. 1)

这里的一切都暗示着新生、希望和圆满。尼克进入的空间是“玫瑰色的”，这是浪漫圆满的传统氛围。“洁白闪亮”的敞开式窗户、“新鲜的草地”，以及将天花板比作“糖霜婚礼蛋糕”的描述，都唤起了人们对新开始的希望：纯洁、春天、婚礼。此外，对婚礼蛋糕和葡萄酒的提及暗示着庆祝和希望的实现。然而，环境所承诺的圆满与身处其中的人物所感受到的不满之间的反差，最终营造出一种未实现的渴望氛围，正如柯勒律治的《古舟子咏》中，尽管远没有那么浪漫，他在平静的船上写道：“水啊，到处都是水，/却一滴也喝不到”（第121-122行）。

Everything about this setting suggests newness, hopefulness, and fulfillment. The space Nick enters is “rosy-colored,” the traditional ambience of romantic fulfillment. The “gleaming white” open windows, the “fresh grass,” and the description of the ceiling as a “frosted wedding cake” evoke the hopefulness of new beginnings: virginity, springtime, weddings. In addition, the references to wedding cake and wine suggest celebration and the fulfillment of hopes. The net result of the dissonance between the fulfillment promised by the setting and the dissatisfaction experienced by the characters within that setting is an atmosphere of unfulfilled longing, such as Coleridge’s Ancient Mariner describes, though far less romantically, on his becalmed boat: “Water, water every where, / Nor any drop to drink” (ll. 121–22).

书中对场景的描写充满了和谐、优雅和富足的意象，即使是最庸俗的场景也弥漫着一种未实现的渴望，这种渴望指向一种与当下情节形成鲜明对比的天堂般的美丽。例如，汤姆与默特尔幽会的公寓，这对情侣也经常在那里招待默特尔那些喧闹、庸俗、嗜酒如命的朋友们，这间公寓位于“一排长长的白色公寓楼”（32；第二章）中，里面摆满了挂毯家具，上面描绘着“凡尔赛花园里女士们荡秋千的场景”（33；第二章）。当尼克陪同汤姆和默特尔去他们的公寓时，他注意到，夏日的周日下午，第五大道看起来“如此温暖柔和，几乎像田园诗一般，以至于我丝毫不会惊讶地看到一大群白羊转过街角”（32；第二章）。 “长长的白蛋糕”、“荡秋千的女士们”、“花园”、“凡尔赛宫”、“温暖柔和”、“田园风光”、“夏日周日下午”、“一大群白羊”——这是一种田园诗般的语言，一种丰盈、圆满、愉悦与和谐的语言。然而，派对场景中醉酒、暴力和粗俗的景象——客人们跌跌撞撞；默特尔和麦基太太发表反犹太主义、精英主义和淫秽的言论；汤姆和默特尔争吵；汤姆打断了默特尔的鼻子——与上述田园诗般丰盈的描述性语言之间的不协调，营造出一种对理想生活、我们想要的生活、而非现实生活的未竟之渴望的氛围​​。

Settings described with images of harmony, refinement, and plenitude imbue even the most vulgar scenes with a sense of unfulfilled longing that yearns toward a paradisal beauty ironically at odds with the current action. For example, the apartment Tom keeps for his adulterous trysts with Myrtle, where the couple also entertain Myrtle’s noisy, vulgar, hard-drinking friends, is in a “long white cake of apartment houses” (32; ch. 2) and filled with tapestried furniture displaying “scenes of ladies swinging in the gardens of Versailles” (33; ch. 2). When Nick accompanies Tom and Myrtle to their apartment, he notes that Fifth Avenue looks “so warm and soft, almost pastoral, on the summer Sunday afternoon that I wouldn’t have been surprised to see a great flock of white sheep turn the corner” (32; ch. 2). “[L]ong white cake,” “ladies” on swings, “gardens,” “Versailles,” “warm and soft,” “pastoral,” “summer Sunday afternoon,” “great flock of white sheep” – this is an idyllic language, a language of plenitude, fulfillment, pleasure, and harmony. Again, the dissonance between the drunken, violent vulgarity of the party scene – guests stumble about; Myrtle and Mrs. McKee make anti-Semitic, elitist, and obscene remarks; Tom and Myrtle quarrel; Tom breaks Myrtle’s nose – and the pastoral plenitude of the descriptive language noted above creates an ambience of unfulfilled longing for life the way it should be, life the way we want it to be, life the way it isn’t.

粗俗的人物与象征和谐、优雅和富足的环境之间的不协调，营造出一种难以满足的渴望感，这种感觉在对盖茨比派对的描写中尤为引人注目。正如他购买豪宅的钱一样，盖茨比举办奢靡派对的资金也来自与迈耶·沃尔夫希姆相关的犯罪活动，沃尔夫希姆是小说中最阴险、最粗俗的人物之一。正如尼克所指出的，盖茨比的客人们“举止粗俗”，“完全符合……”游乐园里常见的行为”（45；第3章）。几乎每个人都粗鲁无礼。他们肆无忌惮地议论着主人，而主人几乎无人见过，也无人愿意结识。人群本身也处于不同程度的醉酒狂热之中，经常有人上演醉酒闹剧。例如，一位年轻女子“为了壮胆”一口气喝下一杯鸡尾酒，然后“独自一人在帆布平台上跳舞”（45；第3章）；“一个吵闹的小女孩，稍有挑衅便会止不住地大笑”（51；第3章）；一位司机醉得不省人事，当他的车冲进车道旁的沟里，“一个轮子被猛地撞掉”（58；第3章）时，他竟然没有意识到车已经停了下来；还有一个醉醺醺的小女孩，不得不把她的头按进水池里（113；第6章）才能让她停止尖叫。

The sense of unfulfilled longing created by the dissonance between vulgar characters and a setting that bespeaks harmony, refinement, and plenitude is especially interesting in the description of Gatsby’s parties. Like the money with which he bought his mansion, the money that pays for Gatsby’s extravagant parties comes from criminal activities associated with Meyer Wolfsheim, the novel’s most sinister and one of its most vulgar characters. And as Nick points out, Gatsby’s guests “conducted themselves” in extremely vulgar fashion, “according to the rules of behavior associated with amusement parks” (45; ch.3). Almost everyone is rude and obnoxious. They gossip mercilessly about their host, whom few have met or care to meet. And the crowd, itself in varying degrees of drunken hysteria, is frequently treated to a drunken display by one or another of its members. There is, for example, a young woman who “dumps” down a cocktail “for courage” and “dances out alone on the canvas platform” (45; ch. 3); “a rowdy little girl who gave way upon the slightest provocation to uncontrollable laughter” (51; ch. 3); a driver so drunk that, when his car winds up in a ditch beside the driveway, “violently shorn of one wheel” (58; ch. 3), he doesn’t realize it has stopped moving; and a drunken young girl who has to have her “head stuck in a pool” (113; ch. 6) to stop her from screaming.

然而，对场景的描述却充满了浓浓的浪漫情调：“夏夜里，邻居家传来阵阵音乐。在他那蓝色的花园里，男男女女像飞蛾般穿梭于低语、香槟和星光之间”（43；第三章）。“早熟的月亮”无疑是“从餐饮承办人的篮子里变出来的，就像晚餐一样”（47；第三章），就连茶点也仿佛被施了魔法：“一盘鸡尾酒在暮色中向我们飘来”（47；第三章），“自助餐桌上摆满了闪闪发光的开胃小菜，香料烤火腿与五彩缤纷的沙拉、以及被染成深金色的糕点猪和火鸡挤在一起”（44；第三章）。因此，场景被描述为一个宁静的田园风光——“蓝色花园”、“低语”、“星星”——在一个神话般的王国里，月亮以某种神奇的方式“提前”出现；鸡尾酒“漂浮”到想要它们的人面前；食物“被施了魔法”。

The setting is described, however, in an intensely romantic fashion: “There was music from my neighbor’s house through the summer nights. In his blue gardens men and girls came and went like moths among the whisperings and the champagne and the stars” (43; ch. 3). The “premature moon” is “produced like the supper, no doubt, out of a caterer’s basket” (47; ch. 3), and even the refreshments seem enchanted: a “tray of cocktails floated at us through the twilight” (47; ch. 3), and on “buffet tables garnished with glistening hors-d’oeuvre, spiced baked hams crowded against salads of harlequin designs and pastry pigs and turkeys bewitched to a dark gold” (44; ch. 3). The setting is thus described as if it were a quiet pastoral scene – “blue gardens,” “whisperings,” “stars” – in a mythical kingdom where the moon is somehow magically produced “premature[ly]”; where cocktails “floa[t]” toward those who desire them; and where food is “bewitched.”

当然，我们必须记住，尼克是我们的叙述者。我们通过他的视角来看待小说中的场景。因此，我们可以合理地推断，在那些场景与情节不符的段落中，所唤起的未竟之愿正是尼克的。他渴望一个田园牧歌般的美好世界，就像他少年时代在明尼苏达州所熟悉的那个世界一样，但那个世界已经消逝。成年、第一次世界大战以及他自身迷茫的种种因素，共同摧毁了那个世界。然而，奢华却能创造浪漫的可能性。尼克对盖茨比的评价同样适用于他自己：“我深深地意识到，财富囚禁并保存着青春与神秘”（157；第八章）。尼克渴望着他在富人世界中看到的浪漫可能，尽管生活在那个世界里的大多数人似乎对此视而不见，或者习以为常。

Of course, we must remember that Nick is our narrator. We see the settings in the novel through his eyes. Therefore, it would not be unreasonable to conclude that, in those scenes in which setting and action are at odds, the unfulfilled longing evoked is Nick’s. He yearns for a world of pastoral beauty, like the world he knew as a youth in Minnesota, but that world is gone. The combined effects of adulthood, World War I, and his own lack of purpose have wiped it out for him. But opulence creates romantic possibilities. What Nick said of Gatsby is also true of himself: he “was overwhelmingly aware of the youth and mystery that wealth imprisons and preserves” (157; ch. 8). Nick longs for the romantic possibilities he sees in the world of the wealthy although most of the people who inhabit that world seem blind to, or take for granted, its idyllic quality.

正如这些例子所示，《了不起的盖茨比》中令人难以忘怀的意象告诉我们，未实现的渴望是普遍存在的，也是不可避免的。无论我们是谁，拥有什么，我们都无法长久满足：我们必然会渴望其他的东西。我们或许会将这种渴望寄托于某个事物，并相信自己渴望的是某种东西，无论那东西存在于我们的过去还是未来。又或许我们不会将这种渴望寄托于任何事物，在这种情况下，我们会将其体验为一种模糊的躁动，就像梅尔维尔笔下的伊什梅尔“无论何时”都渴望出海的那种躁动一样。他的灵魂深处仿佛笼罩着一层潮湿阴冷的十一月”（21）。但未实现的渴望，无论以何种形式出现，都是无法逃避的。即使在盖茨比终于与黛西重逢的那个下午，他因为得知黛西依然爱着他而“容光焕发”（94；第五章），“也一定有过……黛西未能达到他梦想的时刻——并非出于她的过错，而是因为……再多的热情或新鲜感也无法撼动一个男人内心深处积攒的渴望”（101；第五章）。

As these examples illustrate, The Great Gatsby’s haunting imagery tells us that unfulfilled longing is universal and inevitable. No matter who we are or what we have, we cannot be long content: we will inevitably long for something else. We may attach that longing to an object and believe that we are longing for something, whether that something lies in our past or in our future. Or we may not attach that longing to an object, in which case we will experience it as a vague restlessness, the kind of restlessness that sends Melville’s Ishmael to sea “whenever it is a damp, drizzly November in [his] soul” (21). But unfulfilled longing, in one form or another, is inescapable. Even on that afternoon when Gatsby finally reunites with Daisy and “glow[s]” with “well-being” (94; ch. 5) because he has learned that she still loves him, “there must have been moments … when Daisy tumbled short of his dreams – not through her own fault but because … [n]o amount of fire or freshness can challenge what a man will store up in his ghostly heart” (101; ch. 5).

这种无法逃避的感觉，这种未实现的渴望是人类境况固有的感受，在小说中被其对未实现的渴望的静态意象所强化。我们分析的每一个意象——实际上，小说中的大多数意象——似乎都存在于一个永恒的当下，一幅固定的画面，永远凝固，如同济慈著名颂歌中刻在希腊古瓮上的恋人：“勇敢的爱人，你永远，永远无法亲吻她，/即便胜利在望——也不要悲伤；/她不会消逝，即便你未能拥有幸福，/因为你将永远爱她，而她永远美丽！”（第17-20行）。正如财富永远“囚禁并保存”着“青春与神秘”（第157页；第八章），未实现的渴望也永远囚禁并保存着它所渴望之物。让我们来看两幅未实现的渴望的画面，它们特别清晰地说明了这种永恒的特质。

This sense of inescapability, this feeling that unfulfilled longing is inherent in the human condition, is reinforced in the novel by the static quality of its imagery of unfulfilled longing. Each of the images we’ve analyzed – indeed, most of the imagery in the novel – seems to exist in a timeless present, a fixed tableau, frozen forever like the lovers carved on the Grecian urn in Keats’ famous ode: “Bold Lover, never, never canst thou kiss, / Though winning near the goal – yet, do not grieve; / She cannot fade, though thou hast not thy bliss, / For ever wilt thou love, and she be fair!” (ll. 17–20). For just as wealth “imprisons and preserves” forever “youth and mystery” (157; ch. 8), unfulfilled longing imprisons and preserves forever that for which it longs. Let’s take a look at two images of unfulfilled longing that illustrate this quality of timelessness with particular clarity.

当汤姆和黛西终于参加盖茨比的派对时，黛西在晚宴伊始便被一位“电影明星”的身影所吸引——一位“美艳绝伦、宛若兰花般的女子，端坐在白梅树下”，她的导演“正俯身在她身边”（111；第六章）。晚宴结束时，尼克注意到“电影导演和他的明星”仍然“在白梅树下……他们的脸……几乎贴在一起，只有一缕苍白的月光从他们之间透出”（113；第六章）。他说道：“我突然意识到，他整晚都在缓缓地向她俯身，才得以如此靠近”（113；第六章）。这是一种渴望的意象——字面上，是对渴望对象的一种身体上的倾向——仿佛存在于超越时间的维度，如同凝固在济慈骨灰瓮上的瞬间。整个晚上，人物似乎几乎没有移动，画面的永恒感因超凡脱俗的细节而更加强烈：女人是“一朵几乎不像人的兰花”，视野中唯一的植物是一棵“白梅树”，唯一的光源是“一缕苍白的月光”。

When Tom and Daisy finally attend one of Gatsby’s parties, Daisy is attracted, at the beginning of the evening, by the sight of a “celebrity of the movies,” a “gorgeous, scarcely human orchid of a woman who sat in state under a white plum tree” with her director “bending over her” (111; ch. 6). At the end of the evening, Nick notices that “the moving picture director and his Star” are “still under the white plum tree … their faces … touching except for a pale thin ray of moonlight between” (113; ch. 6). He says, “It occurred to me that he had been very slowly bending toward her all evening to attain this proximity” (113; ch.6). This is an image of longing – literally, a physical leaning toward the object of desire – that seems to exist in a dimension beyond time, like the moment frozen forever on Keats’ urn. The characters seem barely to move over the course of an entire evening, and the timeless quality of the image is increased by the otherworldliness of the pictorial details: the woman is a “scarcely human orchid,” the only vegetation in sight is a “white plum tree,” and the only light is a “pale thin ray of moonlight.”

当汤姆、尼克和盖茨比在布坎南家门外等候，准备开车送黛西和乔丹去纽约市时，他们看到远处有一艘孤零零的帆船，这幅景象也展现了类似的未实现的渴望。

A similar tableau of unfulfilled longing is presented when Tom, Nick, and Gatsby, waiting outside the Buchanans’ house to drive Daisy and Jordan to New York City, see a single sailboat in the distance.

在碧绿的海湾里，酷热难耐，一艘小船缓缓驶向清澈的大海……我们的目光越过玫瑰花丛、炙热的草坪和岸边酷暑难耐的杂草。小船的白色船翼缓缓划过湛蓝清冷的天空。前方是波光粼粼的大海和星罗棋布的岛屿。

On the green Sound, stagnant in the heat, one small sail crawled slowly toward the fresher sea. … Our eyes lifted over the rosebeds and the hot lawn and the weedy refuse of the dog days alongshore. Slowly the white wings of the boat moved against the blue cool limit of the sky. Ahead lay the scalloped ocean and the abounding blessed isles.

（124；第6章）

(124; ch. 6)

这里所描绘的未竟之愿，是对天堂般圆满的渴望，是对逃离现实世界的渴望。这段简短的文字两次强调了船只极其缓慢的移动（“它缓缓爬行”和“船的白色船翼缓缓移动”），船只似乎离陆地很远（从人物站立的位置看，它就像“一面小小的帆”），以及海景的经典色彩（蓝天映衬着白色的船帆），这一切都将画面凝固，如同颜料凝固在画布上一般。这幅画面所唤起的永恒感因其神话般的特质而更加强烈：船只航行的“清新”、“凉爽”的世界与汤姆、尼克和盖茨比所处的现实世界形成了鲜明的对比，现实世界“闷热难耐”、“草坪滚烫”、“岸边杂草丛生”；船帆化作“白色的船翼”；而它的目的地则是某个神话般的永无岛，“富饶的福地”。

The unfulfilled longing represented here is the longing for paradisal fulfillment, the longing to escape the real world. The extremely slow movement of the boat, insisted on twice in this short passage (it “crawled slowly” and “[s]lowly the white wings of the boat moved”), the great distance the boat seems to be from land (from where the characters stand, it looks like “one small sail”), and the classic colors of the seascape (white sails against blue sky) freeze this image as it would be frozen by paint on canvas. The sense of timelessness this image evokes is increased by its mythical quality: the “fres[h],” “cool” world in which the boat sails is contrasted sharply with the real world in which Tom, Nick, and Gatsby stand, with its “stagnant … heat,” “hot lawn,” and “weedy refuse of the dog days alongshore”; the boat’s sail turns into “white wings”; and its destination is some mythical never-never land, “the abounding blessed isles.”

值得注意的是，在小说的核心，时间似乎真的静止了。盖茨比和黛西重逢时，他们的关系体现了一种无法实现的渴望。尼克壁炉架上的钟——盖茨比靠在上面，碰倒了它，又用手接住——已经“失灵”（91；第五章）：时间停止了。随着场景的推进，盖茨比在时间中的存在也停止了：他“像上紧了发条的钟一样倒下”（97；第五章）。当他和黛西静静地坐在暮色渐浓的地方时，他们“远离”（102；第5章）时间流逝的现实世界，他们所居住的永恒维度与外面喧嚣的现实世界形成了鲜明的对比：“外面风很大……西卵的灯都亮了；载着人的电动火车正飞驰回家”（101；第5章）。

It is interesting to note in this context that time seems almost literally to stand still at the very center of the novel, when Gatsby and Daisy, whose relationship embodies unfulfilled longing, reunite. The clock on Nick’s mantlepiece – which Gatsby leans his head against, knocks over, and catches in his hands – is “defunct” (91; ch. 5): time has stopped. As the scene progresses, Gatsby’s existence in time stops, too: he “run[s] down like an overwound clock” (97; ch. 5). And as he and Daisy sit silently together in the gathering dusk, “remot[e]” (102; ch. 5) from the real world in which time passes, the timeless dimension they inhabit is foregrounded by its sharp contrast with the bustle of the real world outside: “Outside the wind was loud and … [a]ll the lights were going on in West Egg now; the electric trains, men-carrying, were plunging home” (101; ch. 5).

正是小说中那份未被满足的渴望这一普世主题，以及小说中恢弘的意象所赋予的强大力量，成就了《了不起的盖茨比》这部经久不衰的杰作。正如出版商查尔斯·斯克里布纳三世在1992年评价这部小说时所说：“时至今日，它在斯克里布纳畅销书排行榜上的地位依然稳固，无人能撼动”（205）。《了不起的盖茨比》之所以拥有如此经久不衰的价值，并非仅仅因为它对爵士时代的社会评论——尽管它的确是一部杰出的社会评论作品。这部小说之所以能在美国文学中占据“神圣地位”（斯克里布纳 205），是因为它触及了人类经验深处的某种东西：那份深藏于人类生存本质的未被满足的渴望。就像黛西的声音一样，“它那忽冷忽热、热情似火的温暖最能打动[盖茨比]，因为它无法被过度幻想”，未实现的渴望的抒情忧郁是一首“不朽的歌”（101；第5章），而菲茨杰拉德的杰出小说捕捉到了这首歌，这是其他任何小说都无法做到的。

It is the universal theme of unfulfilled longing, so powerfully carried by the novel’s magnificent imagery, that has made The Great Gatsby the enduring masterpiece it is. As publisher Charles Scribner III said of the novel in 1992, “to the present day its place at the top of Scribner bestsell[ing paperbacks] has never been challenged” (205). The Great Gatsby doesn’t have this kind of enduring value because of its social commentary on the Jazz Age, though an excellent social commentary it surely is. The novel has maintained its “hallowed place in American literature” (Scribner 205) because it speaks to something deep in the heart of human experience: the unfulfilled longing that is at the core of the human condition. Like Daisy’s voice, which “held [Gatsby] most with its fluctuating, feverish warmth because it couldn’t be over-dreamed,” the lyric melancholy of unfulfilled longing is a “deathless song” (101; ch. 5), and Fitzgerald’s superb novel has captured that song as no other novel has.

拓展练习题：运用新批评方法解读其他文学作品

Questions for further practice: New Critical approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用新批评理论来解读文中提及的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use New Criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1 在凯特·肖邦的《暴风雨》（1898 年）中，自然意象和视角是如何支持“个人境遇，而不是抽象规则，决定对错、健康与不健康”这一主题的呢？

1 In Kate Chopin’s “The Storm” (1898), how do nature imagery and point of view support the theme that individual circumstances, not abstract rules, determine what is right and wrong, healthy and unhealthy?

2在阿尔贝托·莫拉维亚的《追逐》（1967）中，叙述者的性格塑造、故事的开头和结尾场景以及自然意象的运用，是如何支持“通奸是一种情感疏离，标志着婚姻中亲密关系的终结”这一主题的？

2 In Alberto Moravia’s “The Chase” (1967), how does the characterization of the narrator, the story’s opening and closing scenes, and the use of nature imagery support the theme that adultery is a form of emotional distance that signals the end of intimacy in a marriage?

3兰斯顿·休斯的《黑人谈河流》（1926）是如何运用地理、历史和圣经典故以及自然意象来推进他关于黑人种族的主题的？你会如何阐述这个主题？

3 How does Langston Hughes’ “The Negro Speaks of Rivers” (1926) use geographical, historical, and biblical allusion, as well as nature imagery, to forward his theme about the negro race? How would you state that theme?

4在阿瑟·米勒的《推销员之死》（1949）中，场景是如何营造出对威利作为他无法控制的力量的受害者的同情，从而有助于表达个人需求常常被牺牲给社会需求这一主题的？

4 In Arthur Miller’s Death of a Salesman (1949), how does setting work to create sympathy for Willy as the victim of forces beyond his control, thus contributing to the theme that the needs of the individual are often sacrificed to the demands of society?

5在托妮·凯德·班巴拉的《课》（1972）中，故事的叙述视角、叙述者的语气和俚语的使用，以及用来描述玩具店和孩子们反应的意象，是如何暗示“成人礼”这一主题的？你认为通过对这些形式要素的分析，故事暗示了什么主题？这个主题是否得到了故事中对叙述者的刻画的印证？如果是，又是如何印证的？（如果没有，请尝试找到一个能够被所有这些形式要素所支撑的主题。）

5 In Toni Cade Bambara’s “The Lesson” (1972), how is the topic of initiation suggested by the point of view from which the story is told, the narrator’s tone of voice and use of slang, and the imagery used to describe the toy store and the children’s response to it? What theme do you think is implied by your analysis of these formal elements? Is that theme borne out by the story’s characterization of the narrator? How? (If not, try to find a theme that is supported by all of these formal elements.)

笔记

Notes

1如今大多数文学批评家，无论其理论取向如何，都承认新批评的“普遍意义”概念是虚假的，甚至是有害的，因为文本的“普遍性”是由美国白人男性经验决定的，因此常常局限于美国白人男性经验。

1 Most literary critics today, regardless of their theoretical orientation, acknowledge that New Criticism’s concept of “universal significance” was bogus, even harmful, because a text’s “universality” was determined by, and thus too often limited to, white male American experience.

2有关类似论点，请参阅 Cartwright、Chase、Dillon、Gross、Hart、Le Vot、Moore、Nash、Stern 和 Trilling 等人的著作。

2 For similar arguments, see, for example, Cartwright, Chase, Dillon, Gross, Hart, Le Vot, Moore, Nash, Stern, and Trilling.

3布鲁科利、戴森和富塞尔等人认为，盖茨比也受到了他所处世界的腐败影响。

3 The view that Gatsby shares the corruption of his world is held, for example, by Bruccoli, Dyson, and Fussell.

6. 读者反应批评

6   Reader-response criticism

顾名思义，读者反应批评关注的是读者对文学文本的反应。许多批评理论的初学者在学习读者反应批评这一单元时都会感到如释重负，或许是因为他们乐于接受这样的观点：他们的反应足够重要，可以成为文学解读的焦点。又或许他们认为读者反应批评意味着“我不可能出错，因为我对文本的任何解读都是我的反应，所以教授无法否定它。” 但让我先告诉你一个坏消息。根据我们所讨论的读者反应理论的不同，你对文学文本的反应可能会被认为不够充分，或者不如其他人的反应充分。即使某个读者反应理论声称不存在不充分（或不准确或不恰当）的反应，作为该理论的实践者，你的任务也不仅仅是做出反应，而是要分析你自己的反应或他人的反应，而这种分析也可能存在不足之处。

As its name implies, reader-response criticism focuses on readers’ responses to literary texts. Many new students of critical theory are relieved and happy when they get to the unit on reader-response criticism, perhaps because they enjoy the idea that their responses are important enough to become the focus of literary interpretation. Or perhaps they assume that reader-response criticism means “I can’t be wrong because any way I interpret the text is my response, so the professor can’t reject it.” Let me break the bad news to you up front. Depending on the kind of reader-response theory we’re talking about, your response to a literary text can be judged insufficient or less sufficient than others. And even when a given reader-response theory does assert that there is no such thing as an insufficient (or inaccurate or inappropriate) response, your job as a practitioner of that theory isn’t merely to respond but to analyze your response, or the responses of others, and that analysis can be found wanting.

不过，好消息是，读者反应批评是一个广阔、充满活力且不断发展的文学研究领域，它能帮助我们了解自身的阅读过程，以及这些过程与我们所读文本的具体要素、我们的生活经验以及我们所属的知识共同体等因素之间的关联。此外，对于那些计划从事教学工作或已经从事教学工作的人来说，读者反应理论提供的理念可以应用于课堂教学，无论课堂是在小学还是大学校园。

The good news, however, is that reader-response criticism is a broad, exciting, evolving domain of literary studies that can help us learn about our own reading processes and how they relate to, among other things, specific elements in the texts we read, our life experiences, and the intellectual community of which we are members. In addition, for those of you who plan on teaching or are already doing so, reader-response theory offers ideas that can help you in the classroom, whether that classroom is in an elementary school or on a college campus.

如果你觉得读者反应批评涵盖了相当广泛的领域，那么你的感觉是对的。事实上，任何分析阅读行为或读者反应的文章都可以被归类为读者反应批评。例如，精神分析批评在探究对文学文本进行特定解读的心理动机时，也属于读者反应批评。女权主义批评在分析父权制如何教导我们以性别歧视的方式解读文本时，也属于读者反应批评。结构主义批评在考察读者为了理解特定文本而必须有意识或无意识地内化的文学惯例时，也属于读者反应批评。文学文本批评也被视为读者反应批评的一种形式。1而女同性恋和男同性恋批评，当它研究我们的恐同文化如何压制我们理解文学文本中同性恋情欲的能力时，也是一种读者反应批评的形式。

If you’re getting the feeling that reader-response criticism covers a good deal of diverse ground, you’re right. In fact, any time an essay analyzes the act of reading or readers’ responses, one could classify that essay as reader-response criticism. For example, psychoanalytic criticism, when it investigates the psychological motives for certain kinds of interpretations of a literary text, is also a form of reader-response criticism. Feminist criticism, when it analyzes how patriarchy teaches us to interpret texts in a sexist manner, is also a form of reader-response criticism. Structuralist criticism, when it examines the literary conventions a reader must have consciously or unconsciously internalized in order to be able to read a particular literary text, is also considered a form of reader-response criticism.1 And lesbian and gay criticism, when it studies how our homophobic culture suppresses our ability to see homoeroticism in literary texts, is also a form of reader-response criticism.

对阅读过程的关注兴起于20世纪30年代，是对当时日益盛行的否定读者在意义建构中作用的倾向的一种反动。这种倾向后来成为新批评的正式原则，并在20世纪40年代和50年代主导了批评实践。正如我们在第五章中所看到的，新批评家认为文本永恒的意义——即文本的本质——仅存在于文本本身。它的意义并非作者意图的产物，也不会随着读者的反应而改变。你可能还记得，新批评家声称，关注读者的反应会混淆文本的本质和文本的功能。读者反应理论直到20世纪70年代才受到广泛关注，该理论认为文本的本质与其功能密不可分。尽管读者反应理论家们对阅读过程的看法各不相同（我们稍后会对此进行探讨），但他们都认同两个观点：（1）读者在理解文学作品中的作用不可或缺；（2）读者并非被动地接受客观文学文本所呈现的意义，而是主动地在文学作品中创造意义。

Attention to the reading process emerged during the 1930s as a reaction against the growing tendency to reject the reader’s role in creating meaning, a tendency that became a formal principle of the New Criticism that dominated critical practice in the 1940s and 1950s. As we saw in Chapter 5, the New Critics believed that the timeless meaning of the text – what the text is – is contained in the text alone. Its meaning is not a product of the author’s intention and does not change with the reader’s response. As you may remember, New Critics claimed that attention to the reader’s response confuses what the text is with what the text does. Reader-response theory, which didn’t receive much attention until the 1970s, maintains that what a text is cannot be separated from what it does. For despite their divergent views of the reading process, which we’ll examine a little later, reader-response theorists share two beliefs: (1) that the role of the reader cannot be omitted from our understanding of literature, and (2) that readers do not passively consume the meaning presented to them by an objective literary text; rather they actively make the meaning they find in literature.

第二个观点，即读者主动建构意义，当然意味着不同的读者可能会对同一文本产生截然不同的理解。事实上，读者反应理论家认为，即使是同一个读者，在两次不同的阅读场合下阅读同一文本，也可能得出不同的意义，因为诸多变量都会影响我们对文本的体验。例如，我们在第一次和第二次阅读文本之间获得的知识、期间发生的个人经历、两次阅读之间情绪的变化，或者阅读目的的改变，都可能导致我们对同一文本产生不同的理解。

This second belief, that readers actively make meaning, suggests, of course, that different readers may read the same text quite differently. In fact, reader-response theorists believe that even the same reader reading the same text on two different occasions will probably produce different meanings because so many variables contribute to our experience of the text. Knowledge we’ve acquired between our first and second reading of a text, personal experiences that have occurred in the interim, a change in mood between our two encounters with the text, or a change in the purpose for which we’re reading it can all contribute to our production of different meanings for the same text.

为了更清楚地了解读者与文本的互动方式会如何影响文本的意义，我们来看下面的段落。阅读时，请想象自己是一位购房者，圈出你认为在考虑购买文中描述的房子时会比较重要的任何细节，无论是正面的还是负面的。

To get a clear idea of just how much the nature of the reader’s involvement with a text can alter its meaning, let’s look at the following passage. As you read it, imagine that you’re a home buyer and circle any detail, positive or negative, that you think would be important if you were considering buying the house described in the passage.

房屋通道2

The house passage2

两个男孩一路跑到车道边。“看吧，我就说今天适合逃学，”马克说。“妈妈星期四从来不在家，”他补充道。高高的树篱把房子从路上遮挡住了，两人便漫步穿过精心修剪的院子。“我以前都不知道你家这么大，”皮特说。“是啊，不过自从爸爸装了新的石墙板，又加了壁炉之后，比以前漂亮多了。”

The two boys ran until they came to the driveway. “See, I told you today was good for skipping school,” said Mark. “Mom is never home on Thursday,” he added. Tall hedges hid the house from the road so the pair strolled across the finely landscaped yard. “I never knew your place was so big,” said Pete. “Yeah, but it’s nicer now than it used to be since Dad had the new stone siding put on and added the fireplace.”

房子有前门、后门和通往车库的侧门，车库里空空如也，只停着三辆十速自行车。他们从侧门进去，马克解释说，侧门一直开着，以防他的妹妹们比妈妈早回家。

There were front and back doors and a side door which led to the garage, which was empty except for three parked 10-speed bikes. They went in the side door, Mark explaining that it was always open in case his younger sisters got home earlier than their mother.

皮特想看看房子，于是马克先从客厅开始。客厅和楼下其他地方一样，都是新粉刷的。马克打开音响，音响的噪音让皮特有些担心。“别担心，最近的房子也在四分之一英里外，”马克喊道。皮特这才放心起来，因为他看到大院子以外的任何方向都看不到其他房子。

Pete wanted to see the house so Mark started with the living room. It, like the rest of the downstairs, was newly painted. Mark turned on the stereo, the noise of which worried Pete. “Don’t worry, the nearest house is a quarter of a mile away,” Mark shouted. Pete felt more comfortable observing that no houses could be seen in any direction beyond the huge yard.

餐厅里摆满了瓷器、银器和水晶玻璃器皿，根本不适合玩耍，所以孩子们就去了厨房，在那里做了三明治。马克说他们不会去地下室，因为自从安装了新的管道后，那里就一直潮湿发霉。

The dining room, with all the china, silver, and cut glass, was no place to play so the boys moved into the kitchen, where they made sandwiches. Mark said they wouldn’t go to the basement because it had been damp and musty ever since the new plumbing had been installed.

“我爸把他的名画和钱币收藏都放在这里，”马克一边说着，一边往书房里张望。马克得意洋洋地说，他发现他爸在书桌抽屉里藏了不少钱，所以他想什么时候弄点零花钱就什么时候弄。

“This is where my Dad keeps his famous paintings and his coin collection,” Mark said as they peered into the den. Mark bragged that he could get spending money whenever he needed it since he’d discovered that his Dad kept a lot in the desk drawer.

楼上有三间卧室。马克带皮特看了他母亲的衣橱，里面塞满了皮草，还有一个上锁的盒子，装着她的珠宝。他姐姐们的房间没什么特别的，只有一台彩色电视机，马克把它搬到了自己的房间。马克得意洋洋地说，走廊里的浴室是他的，因为后来在他姐姐们的房间里加了一间。不过，他房间里最大的亮点是天花板上的一个漏水点，原来是老屋顶腐烂造成的。

There were three upstairs bedrooms. Mark showed Pete his mother’s closet, which was filled with furs and the locked box which held her jewels. His sisters’ room was uninteresting except for the color TV, which Mark carried to his room. Mark bragged that the bathroom in the hall was his since one had been added to his sisters’ room for their use. The big highlight in his room, though, was a leak in the ceiling where the old roof had finally rotted.

现在请重新阅读这段文字，并划出你认为在踩点行窃时重要的任何细节，无论是正面的还是负面的。许多读者可能会列出类似以下的优缺点清单：

Now reread the passage and underline any detail, positive or negative, that you think would be important if you were casing the house in order to rob it. Many readers probably would produce a list of positive and negative qualities something like the following:

当我们第二次阅读这段文字时，因为我们想到的是入室盗窃，所以我们关注的细节截然不同；即使关注的是相同的细节，它们对我们来说的意义也大相径庭。例如，对许多购房者来说至关重要的隐私，在第二次阅读时却变成了房屋容易被盗的隐患。仅仅改变我们阅读一段文字的目的，就能彻底改变我们对这段文字的理解。当然，一些购房者可能会立刻意识到房屋隐私的负面影响，因为他们的经历让他们对犯罪更加警惕，这印证了读者反应理论的观点：读者会利用自身的经验来构建意义。

During our second reading of this passage, because we’re thinking of robbing the house, we focus on very different details, and even when we focus on the same details, they have a very different meaning for us. For example, the privacy that is an asset for many home buyers becomes a liability in terms of the home’s vulnerability to burglars. Merely changing the purpose for which we read a passage can radically alter the passage we read. Of course, some home-buying readers might immediately see the negative aspect of the home’s privacy because their experience has made them more aware of crime, illustrating reader-response theory’s assertion that readers draw on their personal experiences to create meaning.

正如上述练习所示，书面文本并非一个物体，尽管它具有物理存在，但它是发生在读者内心的一种事件，读者的反应在文本的形成过程中至关重要。然而，理论家们对于我们如何形成这些反应以及文本在其中扮演何种角色（如果有的话）存在分歧。观点不一，有的认为文学文本与读者一样积极地创造意义，有的则认为文本的存在完全取决于读者的创造。

As the above exercise illustrates, a written text is not an object, despite its physical existence, but an event that occurs within the reader, whose response is of primary importance in creating the text. Theorists disagree, however, about how our responses are formed and what role, if any, the text plays in creating them. Opinions range from the belief that the literary text is as active as the reader in creating meaning to the belief that the text doesn’t exist at all except as it is created by readers.

让我们来看一些具有代表性的研究方法，这些方法大致可以归纳为五大类：交互型读者反应理论、情感文体学、主观读者反应理论、心理读者反应理论和社会读者反应理论。需要注意的是，这些分类在某种程度上是人为的：界限往往模糊不清，因为不同学派的实践者会持有某些共同的观点，而同一学派内部的实践者也会在某些方面存在分歧。此外，正如我们之前所看到的，任何对读者反应理论进行分类的尝试都不可避免地会包含一些实践者可能并不自称为读者反应批评家的理论，也会遗漏一些在其他分类体系中会被纳入的理论。然而，正因为读者反应理论本身就由如此众多多元且充满争议的理论交织而成，所以至少在现阶段，某种分类方法才是必要的。我认为我选择的这种方法能够让你对读者反应理论有一个最清晰的认识，并让你为阅读该领域理论家的著作做好准备。

Let’s take a look at a representative sample of this range of approaches, which may be loosely organized under five headings: transactional reader-response theory, affective stylistics, subjective reader-response theory, psychological reader-response theory, and social reader-response theory. It is important to remember that these categories are somewhat artificial: the dividing lines are often fluid and indistinct because practitioners in different schools will hold some ideas in common while practitioners within each school will differ on some points. In addition, as we saw earlier, any attempt to classify reader-response approaches will inevitably include some theories whose practitioners may not call themselves reader-response critics and omit some theories that a different system of classification would include. However, it is precisely because the fabric of reader-response theory is woven of so many diverse and controversial threads that some method of classification is necessary, at least at this stage of the game. The method I’ve chosen is the one I think will give you the clearest sense of the reader-response enterprise in general and prepare you to read the work of theorists in this field.

交互式读者反应理论

Transactional reader-response theory

交互式读者反应理论常与路易丝·罗森布拉特（Louise Rosenblatt）的著作联系在一起，后者提出了该理论的许多前提。该理论分析文本与读者之间的互动。罗森布拉特并非否定文本的重要性而偏袒读者；相反，她认为两者在意义的产生中都不可或缺。她区分了“文本”（指纸上的印刷文字）、“读者”和“诗歌”（指文本与读者共同产生的文学作品）这三个术语。

Often associated with the work of Louise Rosenblatt, who formulated many of its premises, transactional reader-response theory analyzes the transaction between text and reader. Rosenblatt doesn’t reject the importance of the text in favor of the reader; rather she claims that both are necessary in the production of meaning. She differentiates among the terms text, which refers to the printed words on the page; reader; and poem, which refers to the literary work produced by the text and the reader together.

这种互动是如何发生的呢？当我们阅读文本时，文本就像一个刺激物，我们会以各自的方式做出反应。阅读过程中，我们会产生各种感受、联想和记忆，这些反应会影响我们对文本的理解。我们之前接触过的文学作品、我们积累的全部知识，甚至我们当下的身体状况和情绪都会对我们产生影响。然而，在阅读过程中，文本本身也扮演着一个蓝图的角色，当我们意识到自己的解读偏离了文本原文时，我们可以利用这个蓝图来修正自己的理解。这种在阅读过程中修正理解的过程通常会导致我们根据文本中出现的新发展而重新阅读前面的章节。因此，文本在我们阅读的过程中引导着我们的自我修正过程，即使在阅读结束后，如果我们为了发展或完善自己的理解而重新阅读部分或全部文本，文本仍然会继续发挥这种作用。因此，诗歌这种文学作品的创作，是文本与读者互动的结果，而文本与读者在这一过程中都同样重要。

How does this transaction take place? As we read a text, it acts as a stimulus to which we respond in our own personal way. Feelings, associations, and memories occur as we read, and these responses influence the way in which we make sense of the text as we move through it. Literature we’ve encountered prior to this reading, the sum total of our accumulated knowledge, and even our current physical condition and mood will influence us as well. At various points while we read, however, the text acts as a blueprint that we can use to correct our interpretation when we realize it has traveled too far afield of what is written on the page. This process of correcting our interpretation as we move through the text usually results in our going back to reread earlier sections in light of some new development in the text. Thus, the text guides our self-corrective process as we read and will continue to do so after the reading is finished if we go back and reread portions, or the entire text, in order to develop or complete our interpretation. Thus the creation of the poem, the literary work, is a product of the transaction between text and reader, both of which are equally important to the process.

然而，为了使文本与读者之间产生这种互动，我们对待文本的方式，用罗森布拉特的话来说，必须是审美的，而非外在的。当我们以外在的方式阅读时，我们只关注文本中包含的信息，仿佛它是一个事实和思想的宝库，我们可以随身携带。“阿瑟·米勒的《推销员之死》（1949）讲述的是一个旅行推销员为了让儿子获得人寿保险金而自杀的故事”就是一个以外在方式阅读文本的例子。相反，当我们以审美的方式阅读时，我们会与文本建立一种个人化的联系，这种联系会将我们的注意力集中在语言中微妙的情感表达上，并鼓励我们做出判断。“在《推销员之死》中，威利·洛曼的困境通过他沐浴在柔和蓝光中的小屋与周围橙色高楼大厦的对比而得到强烈的展现”就是一个以审美方式阅读文本的例子。如果没有美学方法，文本与读者之间就不可能进行分析。

In order for this transaction between text and reader to occur, however, our approach to the text must be, in Rosenblatt’s words, aesthetic rather than efferent. When we read in the efferent mode, we focus just on the information contained in the text, as if it were a storehouse of facts and ideas that we could carry away with us. “Arthur Miller’s Death of a Salesman (1949) is a play about a traveling salesman who kills himself so that his son will receive his life-insurance money” is an example of an efferent stance toward the text. In contrast, when we read in the aesthetic mode, we experience a personal relationship to the text that focuses our attention on the emotional subtleties of its language and encourages us to make judgments. “In Death of a Salesman, Willy Loman’s plight is powerfully evoked by the contrast between his small house, bathed in soft blue light, and the large, orange-colored apartment buildings that surround it” is an example of an aesthetic stance toward the text. Without the aesthetic approach, there could be no transaction between text and reader to analyze.

沃尔夫冈·伊瑟的追随者或许会用两种意义来解释罗森布拉特所说的文本的蓝图和刺激功能：确定意义和不确定意义。确定意义指的是文本的事实，例如情节中的特定事件或文字清晰呈现的物理描述。与之相反，不确定意义，或称不确定性，指的是文本中的“空白”——例如未明确说明的行为。文本的意义要么清晰明了，要么似乎有多种解释——这允许甚至鼓励读者进行自己的解读。（因此，罗森布拉特的传出意义完全依赖于确定的意义，而她的美学意义则依赖于确定的意义和不确定性的意义。）例如，在《推销员之死》中，我们可以说，文本的确定意义包括威利习惯性地向琳达谎称自己在工作中取得了成功，人缘很好，以及他在公司里扮演着多么重要的角色。而该剧的不确定性则包括琳达对丈夫的职业生涯究竟了解多少真相，她何时意识到真相（如果她最终意识到的话），以及为什么当威利试图告诉她自己的缺点时，她却不肯接受。当然，我们有责任证明某个文本的意义是确定的还是不确定性的。

Followers of Wolfgang Iser3 might explain what Rosenblatt refers to as the blueprint and stimulus functions of the text in terms of two kinds of meaning every text offers: determinate and indeterminate meaning. Determinate meaning refers to what might be called the facts of the text, certain events in the plot or physical descriptions clearly provided by the words on the page. In contrast, indeterminate meaning, or indeterminacy, refers to “gaps” in the text – such as actions that are not clearly explained or that seem to have multiple explanations – which allow or even invite readers to create their own interpretations. (Thus, Rosenblatt’s efferent approach depends entirely on determinate meaning, while her aesthetic approach depends on both determinate and indeterminate meaning.) In Death of a Salesman we might say, for example, that the text’s determinate meaning includes the fact that Willy habitually lies to Linda about his success on the job, about how well liked he is, and about how important his role in the company has been. The play’s indeterminacy includes issues such as how much (or how little) of the truth Linda knows about her husband’s career, at what point she realizes the truth (if she ever does), and why she doesn’t let Willy tell her the truth about his shortcomings when he tries to do so. Of course, the burden is on us to support our claim that a given textual meaning is determinate or indeterminate.

阅读过程中，确定性意义与不确定性意义之间的相互作用，会给读者带来一系列持续的体验：回顾，即回想之前阅读的内容；对接下来情节的期待；期待的实现或落空；对人物和事件理解的修正等等。因为作品中看似确定的意义，在之后往往会变得不确定，因为我们的视角会在不同的视角之间转换，例如叙述者、人物以及情节发展中的事件。因此，伊瑟认为，尽管读者会将意义投射到文本上，但我们构建意义的阅读活动本身是由文本预先构建的，或者说是内置于文本之中的。换句话说，伊瑟认为文本本身引导我们完成诠释（投射意义）的过程。

The interplay between determinate and indeterminate meanings, as we read, results in a number of ongoing experiences for the reader: retrospection, or thinking back to what we’ve read earlier in the text; anticipation of what will come next; fulfillment or disappointment of our anticipation; revision of our understanding of characters and events; and so on. For what at one point in the work appears to be determinate meaning will often, at a later point in the work, appear to be indeterminate, as our point of view shifts among the various perspectives provided by, for example, the narrator, the characters, and the events of an unfolding plot. Thus, for Iser, though the reader projects meaning onto the text, the reading activities through which we construct that meaning are prestructured by, or built into, the text. In other words, Iser believes that the text itself guides us through the processes involved in interpreting (projecting meaning onto) it.

根据交互理论家的观点，不同的读者会得出不同的可接受的解释，因为文本允许一系列可接受的含义，也就是说，文本本身就支持一系列含义。然而，由于这一过程中涉及一个真实的文本，我们必须参考该文本来论证或修正我们的回应，因此并非所有解读都是可接受的，有些解读比其他解读更合理。即使是作者在写作文本时所声明的意图，以及他们之后可能提出的任何解释，也只不过是对文本的另一种解读，必须像所有其他解读一样，提交给作为蓝图的文本进行评估。因此，交互分析在很大程度上依赖于新批评家所坚持的文本权威性，同时也将读者的回应置于聚光灯下。此外，交互分析还能解释即使是新批评家自己也提出了多种成功的解读，尽管他们认为每个文本都只允许一种最佳解读。4

According to transactional theorists, different readers come up with different acceptable interpretations because the text allows for a range of acceptable meanings, that is, a range of meanings for which textual support is available. However, because there is a real text involved in this process to which we must refer to justify or modify our responses, not all readings are acceptable and some are more so than others. Even authors’ stated intentions in writing their texts, as well as any interpretations they may offer afterward, are but additional readings of the text, which must be submitted for evaluation to the text-as-blueprint just as all other readings are. Thus, transactional analysis relies a good deal on the authority of the text, insisted on by the New Critics, while also bringing the reader’s response into the limelight. In addition, transactional analysis accounts for the range of successful readings produced even by the New Critics themselves, despite their belief that every text authorizes a single best reading.4

情感文体学

Affective stylistics

情感文体学源于对文学文本的进一步分析，即文学文本是一个在时间中发生的事件——在阅读过程中产生——而不是一个……文本是存在于空间中的客体。研究者会仔细审视文本，往往逐行甚至逐词地分析，以理解文本在阅读过程中如何（文体学）影响读者（情感）。尽管这种方法非常注重文本本身，以至于一些理论家认为它本质上是交互性的，但许多情感文体学的实践者并不认为文本是一个客观的、自主的实体——它并不具有独立于读者的固定意义——因为文本是由它所产生的结果构成的，而这些结果发生在读者的内心。例如，当斯坦利·菲什描述文本的结构时，他所描述的结构是读者在阅读过程中产生的反应结构，而不是我们读完后拼凑起来的文本结构——就像拼图碎片突然散落在我们面前一样。然而，情感文体学并非对读者印象式反应的描述，而是对文本中特定元素所产生的心理过程的认知分析。事实上，情感文体学最出名的或许就是对文本如何构建读者反应进行“慢动作”式的逐句分析。

Affective stylistics is derived from analyzing further the notion that a literary text is an event that occurs in time – that comes into being as it is read – rather than an object that exists in space. The text is examined closely, often line by line or even word by word, in order to understand how (stylistics) it affects (affective) the reader in the process of reading. Although there is thus a great deal of focus on the text, which is why some theorists consider this approach transactional in nature, many practitioners of affective stylistics do not consider the text an objective, autonomous entity – it does not have a fixed meaning independent of readers – because the text consists of the results it produces, and those results occur within the reader. For example, when Stanley Fish describes how a text is structured, the structure he describes is the structure of the reader’s response as it occurs from moment to moment, not the structure of the text as we might assemble it – like puzzle pieces all spread out at once before us – after we’ve finished reading. Nevertheless, affective stylistics is not a description of the reader’s impressionistic responses but a cognitive analysis of the mental processes produced by specific elements in the text.
