Indeed, it is the “slow-motion,” phrase-by-phrase analysis of how the text structures the reader’s response for which affective stylistics is perhaps best known.

Fish 曾创作过一些运用此方法的最佳范例。为了了解这种方法是如何运作的，让我们来看看他对以下句子的分析。

Some of the finest examples of this procedure have been produced by Fish. To see how this approach works, let’s take a look at his analysis of the following sentence.

关于犹大是否上吊自杀，圣经中并没有确切的记载：虽然有一处似乎肯定了这一点，并且由于一个模棱两可的词语，人们才将其翻译出来；然而在另一处，在更明确的描述中，它又使之变得不太可能，似乎推翻了这一说法。

That Judas perished by hanging himself, there is no certainty in Scripture: though in one place it seems to affirm it, and by a doubtful word hath given occasion to translate it; yet in another place, in a more punctual description, it maketh it improbable, and seems to overthrow it.

（《文学》71）

(“Literature” 71)

菲什认为，“这句话是什么意思？”或“这句话说了什么？”这类问题意义不大，因为这句话本身并没有提供任何事实来回答这个问题。即使我们注意到这句话确实表达了一些内容——它说圣经没有明确指出犹大是否上吊自杀——菲什的观点是，这句话仅仅告诉我们它无法告诉我们任何事情。相比之下，他指出，“这句话对读者有什么影响？”或“读者如何理解这句话的含义？”这类问题则很有帮助。

According to Fish, the question “What does this sentence mean?” or “What does this sentence say?” yields little because the sentence provides us with no facts with which we could answer the question. Even if we notice that the sentence does say something – it says that Scripture gives us no clear indication of whether or not Judas hanged himself – his point is that the sentence tells us only that it is unable to tell us anything. In contrast, he notes, the question “What does the sentence do to the reader?” or “How does the reader of this sentence make meaning?” yields something quite useful.

菲什指出，这段关于犹大的文字的作用在于引导读者从确定性走向不确定性。第一句“犹大上吊身亡”（我们大多数人都知道，这其实是“犹大上吊身亡”这一事实的简略说法），是一个我们默认接受的事实陈述。因此，我们一开始就有一种确定感，这种确定感引导我们在不知不觉中预想到句子可能出现的几种结尾方式，而所有这些结尾方式似乎都能印证我们“犹大上吊身亡”的确定性。菲什列举了第一句引导我们预期的三种结尾方式。

What this passage about Judas does, Fish notes, is move the reader from certainty to uncertainty. The first clause, “that Judas perished by hanging himself” (which, as most of us know, is a kind of shorthand for “the fact that Judas perished by hanging himself”), is an assertion we accept as a statement of fact. We thus begin with a feeling of certainty that leads us, without our being quite conscious of it, to anticipate a number of possible ways the sentence might end, all of which would confirm our certainty that Judas hanged himself. Fish offers these three examples of the kinds of endings the first clause leads us to expect.

1 犹大自缢身亡（这给我们所有人树立了榜样）。

1 That Judas perished by hanging himself is (an example for us all).

2犹大上吊自杀，表明他（对自己的罪行有多么深刻的认识）。

2 That Judas perished by hanging himself shows (how conscious he was of the enormity of his sin).

3犹大上吊自杀身亡这件事应该（让我们深思）。

3 That Judas perished by hanging himself should (give us pause).

（《文学》71）

(“Literature” 71)

这些预期缩小了接下来三个词“没有”的可能含义。此时，读者预期看到的是“毫无疑问”，但却是“没有确定性”。现在，我们理解这句话所依据的犹大上吊自杀的事实变得不确定了。读者现在陷入了一种截然不同的境地。正如菲什所说，“读者不再沿着一条光明的道路追寻论证（毕竟，光明已经熄灭了），而是在寻找新的方向”（《文学》71）。在这种情况下，读者往往会继续阅读，希望能找到答案。但随着我们继续阅读，我们的不确定性只会增加，因为我们会在看似带来清晰解释的词语——“地点”、“肯定”、“地点”、“准时”、“推翻”——和看似否定这种解释的词语——“虽然”、“怀疑的”、“然而”、“不太可能”、“似乎”——之间来回切换。代词“它”的过度使用进一步增加了不确定性，因为随着句子的进行，读者越来越难以弄清楚它指的是什么。

These expectations narrow the possible meanings of the next three words in the passage: “there is no.” At this point, the reader expects to see “there is no doubt,” but is given instead “there is no certainty.” Now the fact of Judas’ hanging himself, upon which our understanding of the sentence has rested, becomes uncertain. Now the reader is involved in a completely different kind of activity. As Fish puts it, “Rather than following an argument along a well-lighted path (a light, after all, has gone out), [the reader] is now looking for one” (“Literature” 71). In such a situation, the reader will tend to read on in hopes of finding clarification. But as we continue to read the passage, our uncertainty only increases as we move back and forth between words that seem to promise clarity – “place,” “affirm,” “place,” “punctual,” “overthrow” – and words that seem to withdraw that promise: “though,” “doubtful,” “yet,” “improbable,” “seems.” Uncertainty is further increased by the excessive use of the pronoun it because, as the sentence progresses, the reader has more and more difficulty figuring out what it refers to.

读者反应批评家进行此类分析，旨在描绘文本在阅读过程中如何构建读者反应的模式。这种反应被用来表明，文本的意义并非在于我们对文本内容的最终结论；相反，文本的意义在于我们在阅读过程中体验到的文本对我们的影响。因为文本是一个发生在时间中的事件：它在我们阅读每一个字、每一个短语时都对我们产生作用。正如我们刚才看到的，菲什的这段文字首先强化了读者可能已经持有的关于犹大的某种信念，然后又否定了这种强化，引导读者继续阅读，希望找到一个永远不会提供的答案。如果这段文字所创造的体验在文本中反复出现，那么读者反应批评家可能会说，文本通过一种期望不断被激发又不断落空的模式，教会我们如何阅读文本，或许也教会我们如何理解世界：我们必须预料到，我们对获得确切知识的期望会被激发，然后又会被辜负。我们渴望确切的知识。我们追求它，并且期望得到它。但这段文字告诉我们，我们无法确定任何事情。换句话说，对于读者反应批评家而言，这段文字主要并非关于犹大或圣经，而是关于阅读体验。

Such analyses are performed by reader-response critics in order to map the pattern by which a text structures the reader’s response while reading. This response is then used to show that the meaning of the text does not consist of the final conclusion we draw about what the text says; rather, the meaning of the text consists of our experience of what the text does to us as we read it. For a text is an event that occurs in time: it acts on us as we read each word and phrase. As we just saw, Fish’s passage first reinforces a belief about Judas the reader probably already holds and then takes that reinforcement away, leading the reader on in hopes of finding an answer that is never provided. If the kind of experience created in this passage is repeated throughout the text from which the passage is taken, then a reader-response critic might say that the text teaches us, through a pattern of raised expectations disappointed, how to read that text and, perhaps, how to read the world: we must expect to have our expectation of acquiring sure knowledge raised and disappointed. We desire sure knowledge. We pursue it, and we expect to get it. But this text teaches us that we cannot be certain of anything. In other words, for a reader-response critic, this text isn’t primarily about Judas or Scripture but about the experience of reading.

除了分析构成读者反应的阅读活动之外，通常还会收集其他类型的证据来进一步支持文本是关于阅读体验的论断。例如，大多数情感文体学的实践者会引用其他读者——其他文学评论家——的反应。例如，批评家可能会引用与自身观点截然相反的评论来支持自己的论点，例如，该文本提供了一种令人不安、去中心化或令人困惑的阅读体验。这并非意味着文本本身存在缺陷，而是说，这种不安感表明，对文本乃至整个世界的解读都是一项充满问题的工作，我们不应期望从中获得确定性。

In addition to an analysis of the reading activities that structure the reader’s response, other kinds of evidence are usually gathered to further support the claim that the text is about the experience of reading. For example, most practitioners of affective stylistics will cite the responses of other readers – of other literary critics, for example – to show that their own analyses of the reading activities provided by a particular text are valid for readers other than just themselves. A critic might even cite an extreme divergence of critical opinion about the text to support, for example, the contention that the text provides an unsettling, decentering, or confusing reading experience. This wouldn’t mean that the text is flawed but that by unsettling the reader it demonstrates, say, the fact that interpretation of written texts, and perhaps of the world, is a problematic endeavor from which we should not expect to achieve certainty.

通常还会提供文本本身的论证证据，以表明文本的主题是阅读体验。例如，读者反应批评家会指出，人物的经历和场景的描写如何反映了读者的阅读体验。如果我要论证约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》（1902）提供了一种令读者感到不安、难以理解情节展开的人物和事件的阅读体验，我会像我们刚才看到的那样，首先分析产生这种不确定性的阅读活动。然后，我会指出读者的不确定性体验反映在马洛的不确定性中——他无法理解库尔茨——以及在对丛林、欧洲公司总部和马洛讲述故事的船甲板的描写中反复出现的黑暗和晦涩（它们是不确定性的隐喻）。我还会寻找文本中描绘的、象征着我所描述的阅读体验的意象。当然，故事中描述的阅读材料或阅读行为尤其能起到这种作用。例如，马洛在丛林中发现的那本破旧不堪、无人能读懂的书，象征着他，也象征着我们，无法解读眼前所见之物。马洛甚至不知道这本书是用什么语言写的：他以为是某种密码语言；后来他才知道，这本书是用俄语写的。

Thematic evidence from the text itself is also usually provided to show that the text is about the experience of reading. For example, the reader-response critic shows how the experiences of characters and descriptions of settings mirror the reader’s experience reading the text. If I were to claim that Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness (1902) provides a reading experience that keeps the reader off balance, unsure of how to interpret the characters and events unfolded by the plot, I would start, as we’ve just seen, by analyzing the reading activities that produce the uncertainty. Then I would show that the reader’s experience of uncertainty is mirrored in Marlow’s uncertainty – his inability to interpret Kurtz – and in the recurring references to darkness and obscurity (which are metaphors for uncertainty) that occur in the descriptions of the jungle, the company headquarters in Europe, and the deck of the ship on which Marlow tells his story. I would also look for images described in the text that serve as emblems of the reading experience I’ve described. Of course, reading materials or acts of reading described in the story work especially well for this purpose. For example, the tattered book that Marlow finds abandoned in the jungle, which he is unable to read, is emblematic of his, and our, inability to decipher what we see before us. Marlow doesn’t even know what language the book is written in: he thinks it’s some form of code language; he later learns that it’s written in Russian.

如上所述，此处的文本证据是主题性的：批评家指出，文本的主题是一种特定的阅读体验，例如阅读的难点、理解文本的过程，或者误读的必然性。尽管许多情感文体学的实践者认为，文本作为一个独立对象，在他们的分析中消失了，变成了读者自身体验的本质，但正如我们刚才看到的，他们对主题证据的运用，恰恰凸显了文本在构建读者体验中所扮演的重要角色。

As noted above, the textual evidence at this point is thematic: the critic shows that the theme of the text is a particular kind of reading experience, such as the difficulties involved in reading, the processes involved in making sense of the text, or the inevitability of misreading. Although many practitioners of affective stylistics believe that the text, as an independent object, disappears in their analysis and becomes what it really is an experience that occurs within the reader their use of thematic evidence, as we’ve just seen, underscores the important role played by the text in establishing what the reader’s experience is.

主观读者反应理论

Subjective reader-response theory

与情感文体学和所有形式的交互式读者反应理论截然不同，主观读者反应理论并不要求分析文本线索。对于以大卫·布莱希认为，读者的反应即是文本本身，这既指不存在超越读者诠释所创造的意义的文学文本，也指批评家分析的文本并非文学作品本身，而是读者的书面反应。让我们更仔细地审视这两种观点。

In stark contrast to affective stylistics and to all forms of transactional reader-response theory, subjective reader-response theory does not call for the analysis of textual cues. For subjective reader-response critics, led by the work of David Bleich, readers’ responses are the text, both in the sense that there is no literary text beyond the meanings created by readers’ interpretations and in the sense that the text the critic analyzes is not the literary work but the written responses of readers. Let’s look at each of these two claims more closely.

要理解为何文学文本本身并无独立于读者诠释而存在的意义，我们需要了解布莱希是如何定义文学文本的。与其他许多读者反应批评家一样，他区分了他所谓的“真实对象”和“象征对象”。真实对象指的是物理实体，例如桌子、椅子、汽车、书籍等等。文学文本的印刷页面就是真实对象。然而，当人们阅读这些印刷页面时所产生的体验，如同语言本身一样，是一种象征对象，因为它并非发生在物理世界，而是发生在概念世界，也就是读者的头脑中。这就是为什么布莱希将阅读——即我们主观地对纸上的文字做出反应时所产生的感受、联想和记忆——称为“象征化”：我们对阅读体验的感知和认同，在我们阅读的过程中，会在头脑中创造一个概念性的或象征性的世界。因此，当我们诠释文本的意义时，我们实际上是在诠释我们自身象征化的意义：我们是在诠释我们因文本而产生的概念体验的意义。因此，他将诠释行为称为重符号化。重符号化发生在我们对文本的体验在我们心中产生解释的渴望之时。我们对文本质量的评价也是一种重符号化行为：我们并非喜欢或厌恶文本本身，而是喜欢或厌恶我们对文本的符号化。因此，我们谈论的文本并非纸面上的文本，而是我们头脑中的文本。

To understand how there is no literary text beyond the meanings created by readers’ interpretations, we need to understand how Bleich defines the literary text. Like many other reader-response critics, he differentiates between what he calls real objects and symbolic objects. Real objects are physical objects, such as tables, chairs, cars, books, and the like. The printed pages of a literary text are real objects. However, the experience created when someone reads those printed pages, like language itself, is a symbolic object because it occurs not in the physical world but in the conceptual world, that is, in the mind of the reader. This is why Bleich calls reading – the feelings, associations, and memories that occur as we react subjectively to the printed words on the page – symbolization: our perception and identification of our reading experience create a conceptual, or symbolic, world in our mind as we read. Therefore, when we interpret the meaning of the text, we are actually interpreting the meaning of our own symbolization: we are interpreting the meaning of the conceptual experience we created in response to the text. He thus calls the act of interpretation resymbolization. Resymbolization occurs when our experience of the text produces in us a desire for explanation. Our evaluation of the text’s quality is also an act of resymbolization: we don’t like or dislike a text; we like or dislike our symbolization of it. Thus, the text we talk about isn’t really the text on the page: it’s the text in our mind.

因为唯一的文本存在于读者的头脑中，所以主观读者反应批评家分析的正是这种文本，在他们看来，文本等同于读者的书面反应。布莱希主要关注教育学，他为我们提供了一种方法，教导学生如何运用他们的反应来学习文学，或者更准确地说，学习文学反应。与大众观点相反，主观批评并非放任自流。它是一种连贯且有目的的方法论，旨在帮助我们的学生和我们自己构建关于阅读体验的知识。

Because the only text is the text in the mind of the reader, this is the text analyzed by subjective reader-response critics, for whom the text is equated with the written responses of readers. Bleich, whose primary interest is pedagogical, offers us a method for teaching students how to use their responses to learn about literature or, more accurately, to learn about literary response. For contrary to popular opinion, subjective criticism isn’t an anything-goes free-for-all. It’s a coherent, purposeful methodology for helping our students and ourselves produce knowledge about the experience of reading.

在探讨该方法论的具体步骤之前，我们需要理解布莱希所说的“知识生产”是什么意思。主观批评以及他所谓的“主观课堂”都基于这样一种信念：所有知识都是主观的，感知到的知识无法与感知者分离。许多科学家、历史学家以及批判理论家至今仍然持有这种观点。所谓“客观”知识，仅仅是指特定群体认为客观为真的内容。例如，西方科学曾经接受“地球是平的，太阳绕着地球转”这一“客观”知识。此后，西方科学又接受了关于地球和太阳的几种不同的“客观”知识版本。最新的科学思想表明，我们所接受的知识……客观知识实际上是由我们提出的问题和我们用来寻找答案的工具所产生的。换句话说，“真理”并非等待被发现的“客观”现实；它是由人们为了满足特定历史、社会和心理情境下产生的特定需求而构建的。

Before we look at the specific steps in that methodology, we need to understand what Bleich means by producing knowledge. Subjective criticism and what he calls the subjective classroom are based on the belief that all knowledge is subjective the perceived can’t be separated from the perceiver which is a belief held today by many scientists and historians as well as by many critical theorists. What is called “objective” knowledge is simply whatever a given community believes to be objectively true. For example, Western science once accepted the “objective” knowledge that the earth is flat and the sun revolves around it. Since that time, Western science has accepted several different versions of “objective” knowledge about the earth and the sun. The most recent scientific thinking suggests that what we take to be objective knowledge is actually produced by the questions we ask and the instruments we use to find the answers. In other words, “truth” isn’t an “objective” reality waiting to be discovered; it’s constructed by communities of people to fulfill specific needs produced by specific historical, sociological, and psychological situations.

布莱希的教学法将课堂视为一个社群，帮助学生了解社群如何产生知识，以及社群中的个体成员如何参与到这一过程中。简而言之，布莱希的教学步骤是：学生需要对一篇文学文本做出回应，先写一篇回应陈述，然后再分析自己的回应陈述。这两项任务都是为了促进全班对阅读体验的知识建构。让我们分别来看一下这两个步骤。

Treating the classroom as a community, Bleich’s method helps students learn how communities produce knowledge and how the individual member of the community can function as a part of that process. To summarize Bleich’s procedure, students are asked to respond to a literary text by writing a response statement and then by writing an analysis of their own response statement, both of which tasks are performed as efforts to contribute to the class’s production of knowledge about reading experiences. Let’s look at each of these two steps individually.

尽管布莱希认为，理论上讲，每条回应陈述在特定读者群体中都是有效的，只要它对该群体有用，那么它就具有意义。但他强调，为了对课堂群体真正有用，回应陈述必须能够转化为关于阅读体验的知识。他的意思是，回应陈述必须有助于群体构建关于阅读特定文学文本体验的知识，而不是关于读者自身或读者之外的现实的知识。以读者为中心的回应陈述用自我对话代替了对阅读体验的探讨。它们大多局限于对读者记忆、兴趣、个人经历等的评论，很少或根本不提及这些评论与文本阅读体验之间的联系。以读者为中心的回应陈述会导致群体讨论个性和个人问题，这些讨论或许在心理咨询中有用，但在布莱希看来，它们无助于群体理解当前的阅读体验。

Although Bleich believes that, hypothetically, every response statement is valid within the context of some group of readers for whose purpose it is useful, he stresses that, in order to be useful to the classroom community, a response statement must be negotiable into knowledge about reading experiences. By this he means that it must contribute to the group’s production of knowledge about the experience of reading a specific literary text, not about the reader or the reality outside the reader. Response statements that are reader oriented substitute talk about oneself for talk about one’s reading experience. They are confined largely to comments about the reader’s memories, interests, personal experiences, and the like, with little or no reference to the relationship between these comments and the experience of reading the text. Reader-oriented response statements lead to group discussions of personalities and personal problems that may be useful in a psychologist’s office but, for Bleich, do not contribute to the group’s understanding of the reading experience at hand.

类似地，以现实为导向的回应陈述用对世界问题的讨论取代了对阅读体验的探讨。它们主要局限于表达个人对政治、宗教、性别问题等方面的观点，很少或根本不提及这些观点与文本阅读体验之间的联系。以现实为导向的回应陈述会引发小组对道德或社会问题的讨论，成员们声称文本正是围绕这些问题展开，但这类回应陈述对小组理解当前的阅读体验并无助益。

Analogously, response statements that are reality oriented substitute talk about issues in the world for talk about one’s reading experience. They are confined largely to the expression of one’s opinions about politics, religion, gender issues, and the like, with little or no reference to the relationship between these opinions and the experience of reading the text. Reality-oriented response statements lead to group discussions of moral or social issues, which members claim the text is about, but such response statements do not contribute to the group’s understanding of the reading experience at hand.

相比之下，布莱希提倡的回应陈述以体验为导向。这类陈述探讨读者对文本的反应，具体描述特定段落如何让读者产生感受、思考或联想。这些回应陈述包括对文本中特定人物、事件、段落甚至词语的评价。贯穿这些评价的个人联想和人际关系记忆，使读者能够了解文本的哪些方面以何种方式、出于何种原因影响了他们。布莱希引用了一位学生的描述。她谈到文本中某些人物和事件如何让她想起自己少女时代的性经历。她的回答在对文本中特定场景的反应和这些场景唤起的青春期具体经历之间来回切换。

In contrast, the response statements Bleich promotes are experience oriented. They discuss the reader’s reactions to the text, describing exactly how specific passages made the reader feel, think, or associate. Such response statements include judgments about specific characters, events, passages, and even words in the text. The personal associations and memories of personal relationships that are woven throughout these judgments allow others to see what aspects of the text affected the reader in what ways and for what reasons. Bleich cites one student’s description of the ways in which particular characters and events in a text reminded her of her sexuality as a young girl. Her response statement moved back and forth between her reactions to specific scenes in the text and the specific experiences they recalled in her adolescence.

由这位学生的主观反应引发的小组讨论可以朝着许多方向发展，其中一些相当传统。例如，小组可能会讨论一个人对这篇特定文本的看法是否取决于其青少年时期遗留的情感。或者，小组可能会讨论这篇文本是作者青少年时期情感的表达，还是作者所处文化中压抑的性道德的体现。即使是后两个例子，学生也需要查找传记和历史资料，但这些问题本身也是由读者的反应以及小组对该反应的回应提出的，因此，与通常情况下学生被布置此类作业的情况相比，他们的个人参与度可能会更高。关键在于，回应陈述是在小组确定的语境中使用。小组根据从经验导向的回应陈述中出现的问题，决定他们想要解答哪些问题以及想要探讨哪些主题。

A group discussion produced by this student’s subjective response could go in any number of directions, some of them quite traditional. For example, the group might discuss whether or not one’s opinion of this particular text depends on feelings one has left over from one’s adolescent experiences. Or the group might discuss whether or not the text is an expression of the author’s adolescent feelings or of the repressive sexual mores of the culture in which the author lived. Even in the case of these last two examples, for which students would have to seek biographical and historical data, the questions themselves would have been raised by a reader’s response and by the group’s reaction to that response, so there probably would be a higher degree of personal engagement than would occur ordinarily for students on whom such an assignment had been imposed. The point is that response statements are used within a context determined by the group. The group decides, based on the issues that emerge from experience-oriented response statements, what questions they want answered and what topics they want to pursue.

此外，读者还需要对体验导向型回应陈述进行回应分析。在此，读者需要：(1) 描述自己对文本整体的感受；(2) 识别文本不同方面引发的各种回应，这些回应最终促成了学生对文本的整体反应；(3) 探究这些回应产生的原因。例如，回应可以被描述为愉悦、不适、着迷、失望、释然或满足，并且可能涉及多种情绪，例如恐惧、喜悦和愤怒。学生的回应分析陈述可能会揭示，某些回应源于对特定角色的认同、某种愿望的替代性满足、内疚感的缓解（或加剧）等等。此处的目的是让学生理解自己的回应，而不仅仅是记录或为其辩解。因此，回应分析陈述是对特定文本要素、特定个人回应以及学生通过个人接触文本而获得的文本意义之间关系的透彻、详细的解释。

In addition, the experience-oriented response statement is analyzed by the reader in a response-analysis statement. Here the reader (1) characterizes his or her response to the text as a whole; (2) identifies the various responses prompted by different aspects of the text, which, of course, ultimately led to the student’s response to the text as a whole; and (3) determines why these responses occurred. Responses may be characterized, for example, as enjoyment, discomfort, fascination, disappointment, relief, or satisfaction, and may involve any number of emotions, such as fear, joy, and anger. A student’s response-analysis statement might reveal that certain responses resulted, for example, from identification with a particular character, from the vicarious fulfillment of a desire, from the relief of (or increase of) a guilty feeling, or the like. The goal here is for students to understand their responses, not merely report them or make excuses for them. Thus, a response-analysis statement is a thorough, detailed explanation of the relationship among specific textual elements, specific personal responses, and the meaning the text has for the student as a result of his or her personal encounter with it.

值得注意的是，正如布莱希所指出的，采用主观方法的学生可能关注的文本要素与他们撰写传统“客观”论文时所关注的要素相同。为了验证这一假设，布莱希让学生们阅读一篇文学作品，但他们并非撰写回应陈述和回应分析陈述，而是撰写意义陈述和回应陈述。意义陈述解释了学生对文本含义的理解，不涉及学生的个人感受。相比之下，回应陈述（如上文所述）记录了学生如何理解文本。文本引发了特定的个人反应，并唤起了人们对人际关系和经历的回忆。布莱希发现，无论学生是否意识到二者之间的联系，他们的回应陈述都清晰地揭示了其意义陈述的个人来源。换句话说，即使我们认为自己是在撰写传统的“客观”文学文本解读，这些解读的来源也在于文本所引发的个人反应。主观解读方法的优点之一在于，它能让学生理解自己为何选择关注某些要素，并让他们为自己的选择负责。

It is interesting to note that, as Bleich points out, students using the subjective approach probably focus on the same elements of the text they would select if they were writing a traditional “objective” essay. To test this hypothesis, Bleich had his students respond to a literary text, not by writing a response statement and a response-analysis statement but by writing a meaning statement and a response statement. The meaning statement explained what the student thought was the meaning of the text, without reference to the student’s personal responses. In contrast, the response statement, just like the one discussed above, recorded how the text produced specific personal reactions and memories of personal relationships and experiences. Bleich found that students’ response statements clearly revealed the personal sources of their meaning statements, whether or not students were aware of the relationship between the two. In other words, even when we think we’re writing traditional “objective” interpretations of literary texts, the sources of those interpretations lie in the personal responses evoked by the text. One of the virtues of the subjective approach is that it allows students to understand why they choose to focus on the elements they do and to take responsibility for their choices.

此外，通过撰写详细的阅读感想，学生常常会发现，他们在阅读过程中所经历的远比自己意识到的要多。有些学生会发现，如果没有认真思考并记录下自己的感受，他们原本会觉得阅读体验枯燥乏味甚至毫无价值，但正是这种努力让他们从中受益匪浅。学生还可以通过将自己的感想与同学的感想进行比较，或者将自己对文本的当前感受与小时候的记忆进行对比，来了解人们感知的多样性和差异性，各种动机如何影响我们的喜好，以及童年阅读经历如何塑造了成年人的阅读偏好。

In addition, by writing detailed response statements, students often learn that more was going on for them during their reading experience than they realized. Some students discover that they benefited from a reading experience that they would have considered unpleasant or worthless had they not put forth the effort to think carefully and write down their responses. Students can also learn, by comparing their response statements to those of classmates or by contrasting their current response to a text with a response they remember having at an earlier age, how diverse and variable people’s perceptions are, how various motives influence our likes and dislikes, and how adult reading preferences are shaped by childhood reading experiences.

通过小组讨论回应陈述以及学生自身的回应分析陈述，他们还可以了解自身和他人的品味是如何运作的。正如布莱希所指出的，仅仅宣称自己喜欢或不喜欢某个文本、人物或段落并不足以阐明品味。相反，学生必须分析文本带给他们的心理收益或代价，并描述这些因素如何塑造他们的喜好。知道自己喜欢什么和理解自己的品味之间存在着巨大的差异，而后者才是布莱希认为课堂教学的恰当目标。事实上，他认为在主观课堂中提倡的系统性品味探究，是学生开始学习语言和文学的理想起点。对自我理解的关注对大多数学生来说极具激励作用，而布莱希的主观教学法培养了一种批判性思维，这种思维方式将使学生终身受益，因为它表明知识是协作创造的，而不仅仅是“传承”的，而且知识的创造是由个人和群体的共同关注所驱动的。

From group discussions of response statements and from their own response-analysis statements, students can also learn how their own tastes and the tastes of others operate. As Bleich notes, one’s announcement that one likes or dislikes a text, character, or passage is not enough to articulate taste. Rather, students must analyze the psychological pay-offs or costs the text creates for them and describe how these factors create their likes and dislikes. There’s a big difference between knowing what you like and understanding your taste, and it is the latter goal that is, for Bleich, the appropriate goal for the classroom. Indeed, he believes that the organized examination of taste promoted in the subjective classroom is a natural place for students to begin their study of language and literature. The focus on self-understanding is extremely motivating for most students, and Bleich’s subjective method fosters a kind of critical thinking that should prove useful to students throughout their lives because it shows that knowledge is created collaboratively, not just “handed down,” and that its creation is motivated by personal and group concerns.

心理读者反应理论

Psychological reader-response theory

精神分析批评家诺曼·霍兰德也认为，读者的动机强烈影响着他们的阅读方式。尽管他声称，至少在他早期的著作中，客观文本是存在的（事实上，他将自己的方法称为交互分析，因为他认为阅读涉及读者与真实文本之间的交互），霍兰德关注的是读者的解读如何揭示他们自身的特质，而非文本本身。鉴于他对读者主观体验的分析，他有时被称为主观读者反应批评家。然而，由于霍兰德运用了精神分析的概念，并着重关注读者的心理反应，许多理论家认为他是一位心理读者反应批评家，这或许也是我们理解他的最佳方式。

Psychoanalytic critic Norman Holland also believes that readers’ motives strongly influence how they read. Despite his claim, at least in his early work, that an objective text exists (indeed, he calls his method transactive analysis because he believes that reading involves a transaction between the reader and a real text), Holland focuses on what readers’ interpretations reveal about themselves, not about the text. Given his analyses of the subjective experiences of readers, he is sometimes referred to as a subjective reader-response critic. However, because Holland employs psychoanalytic concepts and focuses on the psychological responses of readers, many theorists think of him as a psychological reader-response critic, which is probably the most useful way for us to think of him, too.

霍兰德认为，我们对文学作品的反应与我们对日常生活中事件的反应如出一辙。在人际交往中会引发我防御机制的情境，也会在阅读时引发我的防御机制。举个简单的例子，如果我很容易对让我想起酗酒父亲的新朋友产生反感，那么我可能也会很快对任何让我想起他的虚构人物产生反感。或者，如果我最主要的心理特征是控制欲，那么我可能会对那些削弱我控制感的文学作品感到威胁，例如，那些我无法找到可以认同的强大角色，或者无法找到让我感到舒适的那种井然有序、逻辑严密的世界的作品。在这种情况下，我的防御机制可能是讨厌这部作品、误解它，或者干脆停止阅读。鉴于几乎所有文学作品都会以某种方式唤起我的防御机制，触及我潜意识中的恐惧或禁忌的欲望，如果我要阅读它们，就必须找到应对之法。根据霍兰德的理论，这种应对过程就是阐释。

Holland believes that we react to literary texts with the same psychological responses we bring to events in our daily lives. The situations that cause my defenses to emerge in my interpersonal life will cause my defenses to emerge when I read. To use a simple example, if I am quick to dislike new acquaintances who remind me of my alcoholic father, then I probably will be quick to dislike any fictional character who reminds me of him. Or if my overriding psychological trait is my need to control my world, then I probably will be threatened by literary texts that undermine my sense of control, for example, texts in which I can’t find a powerful character with whom I can identify or in which I can’t find the kind of orderly, logical world in which I feel comfortable. My defense in these situations might be to dislike the text, misunderstand it, or stop reading it altogether. Given that virtually all literary texts will in some way arouse my defenses by tapping some unconscious fear or forbidden desire, I must have a way to cope with texts if I am going to read them at all. According to Holland, that coping process is interpretation.

解读的直接目标，如同我们日常生活中的直接心理目标一样，是为了满足我们的心理需求和欲望。当我们感知到文本对我们的心理平衡构成威胁时，我们必须以某种方式解读文本，以恢复这种平衡。例如，设想两位读者，他们都曾在人生的某个阶段感到自己是受害者——或许是被兄弟姐妹欺负、被同龄人排斥，或是被父母忽视——而这些经历并非出于他们所能控制的原因。托妮·莫里森的小说《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）中的佩科拉这个角色很可能会激起这两位读者的防御心理，因为他们会把她视为和自己一样的受害者。换句话说，阅读佩科拉的故事很可能会让他们想起自己痛苦的童年孤独经历。第一位读者可能会通过一种谴责佩科拉而非那些折磨她的角色的方式来解读小说，以此来应对这种文本威胁：例如，佩科拉的被动行为和拒绝反抗，正是她自己造成的伤害。这样一来，读者便会认同施暴者而非受害者，从而暂时缓解自身的心理痛苦。第二类读者，如果书中受害角色可能唤起其痛苦的童年回忆，则可能会通过淡化佩科拉的苦难来应对，转而关注她身上保留的某些积极品质：例如，佩科拉是小说中唯一从未伤害过任何人的角色，她将永远保持孩童般的纯真。这类读者否认佩科拉的心理痛苦，是为了否认自身的痛苦。其他一些读者，如果书中的受害人物会引发其个人的心理创伤，则可能会采取另一种方式来应对。影响者们也必须应对佩科拉，他们会以应对自己生活中受害经历的方式来应对。

The immediate goal of interpretation, like the immediate psychological goal of our daily lives, is to fulfill our psychological needs and desires. When we perceive a textual threat to our psychological equilibrium, we must interpret the text in some way that will restore that equilibrium. Imagine, for example, two readers who, at some point in their lives, have felt victimized – perhaps “picked on” by siblings, rejected by peers, or neglected by a parent – for reasons beyond their control. These readers’ defenses probably would be raised by the character of Pecola in Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) because they would perceive her as a victim as they themselves had been. In other words, reading about Pecola would probably remind them of their own painful childhood isolation. The first reader might cope with this textual threat by interpreting the novel in a way that condemns Pecola instead of the characters who torment her: for example, Pecola instigates her own victimization by behaving in such a passive manner and refusing to stand up for herself. In this way, the reader identifies with the aggressor, rather than with the victim, and temporarily relieves his own psychological pain. The second reader for whom victimized characters threaten to stimulate painful childhood memories might cope with Pecola by minimizing the character’s suffering, focusing instead on some positive quality Pecola retains intact: for example, Pecola is the only character in the novel who never hurts anyone, and she will remain forever in a state of childlike innocence. This reader denies Pecola’s psychological pain in order to deny her own. Other readers upon whom victim figures have a personal psychological impact would have to cope with Pecola, too, and they would do so in the same ways they cope with their relationships to victimization in their own lives.

霍兰德将我们心理冲突和应对策略的模式称为“身份主题”。他认为，在日常生活中，我们会将这种身份主题投射到遇到的每一种情境中，从而透过我们心理经验的视角来感知世界。类似地，当我们阅读文学作品时，我们会将自身的身份主题或其变体投射到文本中。也就是说，我们会以各种方式无意识地在文本中重现我们自身内心世界。因此，我们的解读是我们投射到文本中的恐惧、防御机制、需求和欲望的产物。所以，解读本质上是一个心理过程，而非一个理性过程。文学解读或许能够揭示文本的意义，或许不能，但在有洞察力的人看来，它总是能够揭示读者的心理状态。

Holland calls the pattern of our psychological conflicts and coping strategies our identity theme. He believes that in our daily lives we project that identity theme onto every situation we encounter and thus perceive the world through the lens of our psychological experience. Analogously, when we read literature, we project our identity theme, or variations of it, onto the text. That is, in various ways we unconsciously recreate in the text the world that exists in our own mind. Our interpretations, then, are products of the fears, defenses, needs, and desires we project onto the text. Interpretation is thus primarily a psychological process rather than an intellectual one. A literary interpretation may or may not reveal the meaning of the text, but to a discerning eye it always reveals the psychology of the reader.

我们之所以难以察觉解读背后的心理层面，是因为我们会无意识地将其包裹在审美、理智、社会或道德的抽象概念之中，以此来缓解我们自身投射所引发的焦虑和内疚。例如，假设有两位读者对佩科拉做出上述反应，他们可能会分别将这个角色解读为——如同圣经中的夏娃一般，代表着自我毁灭的人性弱点；或者与之相反，解读为精神纯洁的象征——却并未意识到，他们的解读都源于自身无意识的心理冲突。

The reason why the psychological dimension of our interpretations is not readily apparent to ourselves and others is that we unconsciously couch it in aesthetic, intellectual, social, or moral abstractions to relieve the anxiety and guilt our projections arouse in us. For example, the two hypothetical readers who react to Pecola as described above might interpret the character – respectively, as the representative of self-destructive human frailty, like the biblical Eve, or in contrast as the representative of spiritual innocence – without realizing that their interpretations emerged from their own unconscious psychological conflicts.

因此，霍兰德对诠释的定义可以概括为一个由三个阶段或模式组成的过程，这些阶段或模式在我们阅读时反复出现。首先，在防御模式下，文本会引发我们的心理防御机制（例如，我们觉得佩科拉具有威胁性，因为她让我们想起自己受害的经历）。其次，在幻想模式下，我们会找到一种诠释文本的方式，以安抚这些防御机制，从而满足我们免受心理平衡威胁的愿望（例如，我们通过关注佩科拉永远拥有的孩童般的纯真来淡化她的痛苦）。第三，在转化模式下，我们将前两个步骤转化为一种抽象的诠释，从而获得我们渴望的心理满足，而无需承认那些构成我们对文本评估基础的、引发焦虑的防御机制和引发内疚感的幻想（例如，我们认定佩科拉代表着精神上的纯真）。因此，在转换模式下，我们专注于对文本进行理性的解释，以避免我们自身的情感反应，却忽略了我们的理性解释源于我们的情感反应这一事实。

Holland’s definition of interpretation can thus be summarized as a process consisting of three stages or modes that occur and recur as we read. First, in the defense mode, our psychological defenses are raised by the text (for example, we find Pecola threatening because she reminds us of our own experience of victimization). Second, in the fantasy mode, we find a way to interpret the text that will tranquilize those defenses and thus fulfill our desire to be protected from threats to our psychological equilibrium (for example, we minimize Pecola’s pain by focusing on the childlike innocence that will remain forever hers). Third, in the transformation mode, we transform the first two steps into an abstract interpretation so that we can get the psychological satisfaction we desire without acknowledging to ourselves the anxiety-producing defenses and guilt-producing fantasies that underlie our assessment of the text (for example, we decide that Pecola represents spiritual innocence). Thus, in the transformation mode, we focus on an intellectual interpretation of the text in order to avoid our own emotional response to it, and we ignore the fact that our intellectual interpretation grew out of our emotional response.

当然，霍兰德方法的潜在价值在促进心理治疗中的自我认知方面显而易见。但经过充分的训练，它也可以作为一种传记工具，用于研究作家。霍兰德在对罗伯特·弗罗斯特的简要分析中提供了一个这样的应用实例。霍兰德分析的并非作为作家的弗罗斯特，而是作为读者的弗罗斯特。也就是说，分析的重点是弗罗斯特本人。霍兰德将弗罗斯特视为一个阅读、回应并诠释他所处世界的人。他研究了弗罗斯特的非正式言论、信件、文学品味、性格特征以及他对科学、政治、自身诗歌和自身的态度，以探寻弗罗斯特的身份认同主题。霍兰德认为，弗罗斯特与自身和世界的关系，源于他需要通过“较小的符号：文字或熟悉的物品”来“驾驭”“性与侵略的巨大未知力量”（127）。霍兰德指出，一旦这一身份认同主题确立，便可在弗罗斯特的诗歌中找到踪迹，而诗歌本身也可被视为诗人对其世界的诠释。

Of course, the possible value of Holland’s method seems evident for facilitating therapeutic psychological self-knowledge. But with adequate training, one might also use it as a biographical tool for the study of an author. Holland provides an example of such an application in a brief analysis of Robert Frost. Holland doesn’t analyze Frost the writer, but Frost the reader. That is, the focus of analysis is Frost as a person reading the world in which he lives, reacting to and interpreting it. Holland studied the poet’s informal remarks; his letters; his tastes in literature; his personality traits; and his expressed attitudes toward science, politics, his own poetry, and himself in order to discover Frost’s identity theme. According to Holland, Frost related to himself and to the world in terms of his need to “manage” the “huge unknown forces of sex and aggression” through the means of “smaller symbols: words or familiar objects” (127). Once this identity theme was established, Holland notes, it could be traced as well in Frost’s poetry, which might itself be taken as the poet’s interpretation of his world.

对霍兰德而言，此类分析的目的是与作者建立一种共情融合。无论我们分析的是人还是文学文本，每一次阐释行为都发生在阐释者的身份主题语境之中。正如我们所见，这种身份主题既会引发对这种融合的防御，也会激发对这种融合的渴望。因此，阐释者的任务在于突破将自我与他者分隔开来的心理屏障。霍兰德认为，理解作者的身份主题，能够让我们充分体验到艺术家赋予我们的馈赠——一种“自我与他者的融合”（132）。

For Holland, the purpose of such an analysis is an empathic merger with the author. Whether we’re analyzing a person or a literary text, every act of interpretation takes place within the context of the interpreter’s identity theme, which, as we have seen, sets up defenses against as well as desire for such a merger. It is therefore the interpreter’s task to break through the psychological barriers that separate self from other. Understanding an author’s identity theme, Holland believes, allows us to fully experience, as a “mingling of self and other” (132), the gift the artist offers us.

社会读者反应理论

Social reader-response theory

在主观读者反应理论中，读者对文学文本的主观反应至关重要；然而，在通常与斯坦利·菲什后期著作联系在一起的社会读者反应理论中，并不存在纯粹的个体主观反应。菲什认为，我们自认为的对文学作品的主观反应，实际上是我们所属阐释社群的产物。菲什所说的阐释社群，指的是那些与我们一样，在阅读文本时运用相同阐释策略的人，无论我们是否意识到自己正在使用这些策略，也无论我们是否知道其他人也使用这些策略。这些阐释策略总是源于各种制度化的假设（例如，由主流文化态度和哲学在高中、教堂和大学中确立的假设），这些假设关乎文本的本质——它究竟是文学作品，还是信件、法律文件或教堂布道——以及我们应该从中发现哪些意义。

While the individual reader’s subjective response to the literary text plays the crucial role in subjective reader-response theory, for social reader-response theory, usually associated with the later work of Stanley Fish, there is no purely individual subjective response. According to Fish, what we take to be our individual subjective responses to literature are really products of the interpretive community to which we belong. By interpretive community, Fish means those who share the interpretive strategies we bring to texts when we read, whether or not we realize we’re using interpretive strategies and whether or not we are aware that other people share them. These interpretive strategies always result from various sorts of institutionalized assumptions (assumptions established, for example, in high schools, churches, and colleges by prevailing cultural attitudes and philosophies) about what makes a text a piece of literature – instead of a letter or a legal document or a church sermon – and what meanings we are supposed to find in it.

一个阐释社群可以像某个特定马克思主义批判理论家的追随者所形成的社群那样，既精深复杂又对自身的批判事业有着清醒的认识，也可以像一位高中老师所形成的社群那样，对自身的阐释策略缺乏认识。这位老师教导学生，阅读文学作品时自然而然地会去寻找那些能揭示故事“隐藏含义”的静态符号。当然，阐释社群并非一成不变，它们会随着时间的推移而演变。读者可以同时属于多个社群，无论是有意识的还是无意识的，或者在人生的不同阶段，他们也可能在不同的社群之间转换。

An interpretive community can be as sophisticated and aware of its critical enterprise as the community produced by the followers of a specific Marxist critical theorist. Or an interpretive community can be as unsophisticated and unaware of its interpretive strategies as the community produced by a high school teacher who instructs his students that it is natural to read literature in search of static symbols that tell us the “hidden meaning” of the story. Of course, interpretive communities aren’t static; they evolve over time. And readers can belong, consciously or unconsciously, to more than one community at the same time, or they can change from one community to another at different times in their lives.

无论如何，所有读者在阅读文本之前，都已预先形成某种解读倾向，这种倾向基于他们阅读时所采用的解读策略。因此，尽管布莱希认为他的学生在阅读文本后通过协商构建了共同权威，但​​菲什则认为，基于学生所属的多种解读社群而形成的多种共同权威，从根本上决定了学生最初如何阅读文本。

In any case, all readers come to the text already predisposed to interpret it in a certain way based on whatever interpretive strategies are operating for them at the time they read. Thus, while Bleich believes his students produce communal authority through a negotiation that occurs after they’ve read the text, Fish claims that a multiplicity of communal authorities, based on the multiplicity of interpretive communities to which students already belong, determines how students read the text in the first place.

换句话说，在菲什看来，读者不是在解读诗歌，而是在创作诗歌。他曾连续教授两门大学课程，以此生动地阐释了这一点。第一节课结束时，他在黑板上写下了一份作业，内容是学生们正在学习的语言学家名单。（最后一个名字后面的问号表示菲什不确定其拼写。）

In other words, for Fish, readers do not interpret poems; they create them. He demonstrated this point rather dramatically when he taught two college courses back to back. At the end of his first class he wrote an assignment on the board that consisted of the following list of linguists’ names his students were studying. (The question mark after the final name was to indicate Fish’s uncertainty about the spelling.)

雅各布斯-罗森鲍姆

Jacobs–Rosenbaum

莱文

Levin

索恩

Thorne

海耶斯

Hayes

奥曼（？）

Ohman (?)

（有文本吗？ 323）

(Is There a Text? 323)

当第二班学生走进教室时，他告诉他们黑板上的文字是一首十七世纪的宗教诗歌，就像他们一直在学习的那些诗歌一样，并让他们分析这首诗。

When his second class entered the room, he told them that the writing on the board was a seventeenth-century religious poem like the ones they’d been studying and asked them to analyze it.

在随后的讨论中，他的学生们得出结论：这首诗颂扬了上帝的爱与慈悲，祂为了救赎世人而赐下祂的独生子。他们的解读完美地解释了诗中的每一个字，其中包括以下几点：诗歌的形状像十字架或祭坛；“雅各”暗示着雅各的天梯，象征着基督徒升入天堂；“罗森鲍姆”字面意思是玫瑰树，指的是圣母玛利亚，那朵无刺的玫瑰，她的儿子耶稣是人类通往天堂的途径；“荆棘”指的是耶稣的荆棘冠冕，象征着他为救赎世人所作出的牺牲；诗中出现频率最高的字母是S、O、N（《有文本吗？》322-29页）。

In the discussion that ensued, his students concluded that the poem celebrated God’s love and mercy in giving his only begotten son for our redemption. Their interpretation accounted beautifully for every word in the poem, including, among other evidence, the following points: the poem is in the shape of a cross or an altar; “Jacobs” suggests Jacob’s ladder, a reference to the Christian ascent into heaven; “Rosenbaum” literally means rose tree and refers to the Virgin Mary, the rose without thorns, whose son Jesus is the means by which human beings can climb to heaven; “Thorne” thus refers to Jesus’ crown of thorns, a symbol of the sacrifice he made to redeem us; and the letters that occur most frequently in the poem are S, O, N (Is There a Text? 322–29).

我无需赘述学生的全部论点，你们就能明白菲什的观点：我们做出的每一个文学判断，包括判断某篇作品是否为诗，都源于我们阅读文本时所运用的解读策略。一份语言学家名单，或者任何其他内容，只要读者或读者群体运用了相应的解读策略，都可以成为一首诗。也就是说，构成一首诗的特质并非存在于文本本身，而是存在于我们接触文本之前就已经有意识或无意识地习得的解读策略之中。

I don’t need to recount the students’ argument in its entirety for you to see Fish’s point: every literary judgment we make, including the judgment that a particular piece of writing is a poem, results from the interpretive strategies we bring with us when we read the text. A list of linguists’ names, or anything else, can become a poem if a reader or group of readers uses the interpretive strategies required to make it one. That is, the qualities that make a poem a poem do not reside in the text but in the interpretive strategies we’ve learned, consciously or unconsciously, before we ever encountered the text.

社会读者反应理论并没有为我们提供一种新的文本阅读方式，也没有推广任何现有的文学批评形式。毕竟，它的核心观点是，任何阐释，以及由此而来的任何文学批评形式，都无法声称揭示文本的全部内涵。每一种阐释都只能在其阐释策略的框架内找到其所呈现的内容。然而，这并不意味着我们会陷入不受约束的阐释混乱之中。正如菲什所指出的，阐释始终受到特定历史时期内相对有限的阐释策略的限制。但是，通过理解社会读者反应理论的原理，我们可以更清楚地意识到我们在阐释文本时的行为，以及我们的同伴和学生的行为。这种意识对教师尤其有用，可以帮助他们分析学生的阐释策略，并帮助他们决定是否以及何时尝试用其他策略来替代这些策略。并帮助他们对自己选择教授的策略负责，而不是躲在“某些阅读方式是自然的或本质上正确的，因为它们代表了文本中的内容”这种信念背后。

Social reader-response theory doesn’t offer us a new way to read texts. Nor does it promote any form of literary criticism that already exists. After all, its point is that no interpretation, and therefore no form of literary criticism, can claim to reveal what’s in a text. Each interpretation will simply find whatever its interpretive strategies put there. This doesn’t mean, however, that we are left with the anarchy of unconstrained interpretation. As Fish notes, interpretations will always be controlled by the relatively limited repertoire of interpretive strategies available at any given point in history. By understanding the principles of social reader-response theory, however, we can become more aware of what it is we’re doing when we interpret a text and more aware of what our peers and students are doing as well. Such awareness could be especially useful to teachers by helping them analyze their students’ interpretive strategies; helping them decide if and when to try to replace those strategies with others; and helping them take responsibility for the strategies they choose to teach instead of hiding behind the belief that certain ways of reading are natural or inherently right because they represent what’s in the text.

定义读者

Defining readers

在我们探讨读者反应理论在文学批评中的应用之前，还有一个与上述所有方法都相关的概念需要讨论。你可能已经注意到，一些读者反应理论家使用“读者”一词，而另一些则使用“读者”。例如，当理论家们讨论他们分析的实际读者的反应时，比如诺曼·霍兰德和大卫·布莱希，他们会称这些读者为“读者”或“学生”，或者用其他指代真实人物的名称来称呼他们。然而，许多理论家分析的是一个假想的理想读者阅读特定文本的体验，正如我们在对情感文体学的考察中所看到的。在这种情况下，“读者”实际上指的是批评家根据特定的读者反应原则，分析自己对特定文本的精心记录的阅读体验。由于假想读者的体验可能与实际读者的体验相符，也可能不符，因此一些假想读者被赋予了描述其所代表的阅读活动的名称。因此，在菲什的情感文体学实践中，他提到了“知情读者”：这类读者具备必要的文学素养，能够像菲什本人一样体验文本，充分领略其语言和文学的复杂性，并且会自觉地抑制自身反应中的个人或独特维度。当然，“知情读者”并非千篇一律，因为例如，艾米莉·狄金森诗歌的知情读者未必是理查德·赖特小说的知情读者。其他一些指代类似假想读者的术语还包括“受过教育的读者”、“理想读者”和“最佳读者”。

Before we turn to the uses of reader-response theory in literary criticism, there’s one final concept we need to discuss that relates to all the approaches discussed above. You may have noticed that some reader-response theorists refer to “readers” while others refer to “the reader.” When theorists discuss actual readers whose responses they analyze, as Norman Holland and David Bleich do, for example, they refer to them as “readers” or “students” or call them by some other name that denotes real people. Many theorists, however, analyze the reading experience of a hypothetical ideal reader encountering a specific text, as we saw, for example, in our examination of affective stylistics. In these cases, references to “the reader” are really references to the critic analyzing his or her own carefully documented reading experience of a specific text according to specific reader-response principles. Because the experience of hypothetical readers may or may not correspond to the experience of actual readers, some hypothetical readers have been given names that describe the reading activity they represent. Thus, in Fish’s practice of affective stylistics, he refers to the informed reader: the reader who has attained the literary competency necessary to experience the text as Fish himself does, in the fullness of its linguistic and literary complexity, and who conscientiously tries to suppress the personal or idiosyncratic dimension of his or her response. Of course, there is a variety of informed readers because the informed reader of, say, Emily Dickinson’s poetry may or may not be the informed reader of Richard Wright’s fiction. Other terms you may run across that refer to similar hypothetical readers include the educated reader, the ideal reader, and the optimal reader.

类似地，沃尔夫冈·伊瑟尔（Wolfgang Iser）使用了“隐含读者”一词，他指的是文本似乎在针对的读者，我们可以通过研究文本的写作风格以及叙事对读者的明显“态度”来推断其特征。因此，哈莱昆言情小说的隐含读者与托马斯·曼的《浮士德博士》（1947）这类哲学小说的隐含读者，或托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》（1987）这类心理描写深刻的历史小说的隐含读者截然不同。其他一些指代文本隐含读者的术语包括“预期读者”和“叙述对象”。关键在于，使用假设读者的批评家试图向我们展示特定文本对读者的要求，或者特定文本如何引导读者理解文本。至于读者是否接受这种引导，甚至是否意识到这种引导，则是另一个问题。

Analogously, Wolfgang Iser uses the term implied reader, by which he means the reader that the text seems to be addressing, whose characteristics we can deduce by studying the style in which the text is written and the apparent “attitude” of the narrative toward the reader. Thus, the implied reader of a Harlequin romance is quite different from the implied reader of a philosophical novel like Thomas Mann’s Doctor Faustus (1947) or the implied reader of a psychologically intense, historical novel like Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987). Other terms you may encounter that refer to readers implied by the text include the intended reader and the narratee. The point here is that critics who use hypothetical readers are trying to show us what particular texts require of readers or how particular texts work to position readers in order to guide their interpretations. Whether or not readers accept that guidance or are even aware of it is another matter.

当然，读者反应理论的概念远不止以上讨论的这些。我们在此的目的仅仅是向您介绍一些主要思想和基本原则，以便您能够理解读者反应理论家和文学批评家提出的问题。自然，有些文学作品似乎比其他作品更容易进行读者反应分析，或者至少更容易进行某些类型的读者反应分析。而且，与本书中讨论的许多其他理论不同，文学文本的读者反应分析通常并非分析文本本身，而是分析实际读者的反应。

Of course, there are many more reader-response concepts than the ones discussed above. Our purpose here is merely to introduce you to the main ideas, the general principles you need to know in order to read reader-response theorists and literary critics with some understanding of the issues they raise. Naturally, some literary works will seem to lend themselves more readily than others to reader-response analysis or at least to certain kinds of reader-response analysis. And unlike many other theories addressed in this textbook, a reader-response analysis of a literary text is often an analysis not of the text itself but of the responses of actual readers.

例如，玛丽·洛维-埃文斯分析了她文学课上大学三年级和四年级学生的口头和书面反馈，以了解当今学生如何形成对特定文学文本的态度，以及这些态度如何决定他们对文本的解读。她使用的文本是玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818），并分析了以下因素如何影响学生对这部小说的解读：小说的电影版本（这造成了学生对文本的先入之见）、她自己提出的解读提示（这是谁的故事？这部小说意味着什么？叙述者可靠吗？），以及文本本身的确定性和不确定性含义。洛维-埃文斯的研究结果证实了读者反应理论，即解读是一个持续的过程，随着读者运用不同的解读策略积极地理解文本而不断发展。她还发现，电影版本中怪物的形象与雪莱笔下的怪物截然不同，由此产生的先入之见既促进了某些学生对故事的解读，也阻碍了另一些学生的解读。类似地，某些文本元素，例如故事“序言”的正式风格和叙事的开头书信体形式（故事以叙述者写给他妹妹的一系列信件的形式呈现），与学生们对一个肤浅、有趣的怪物故事的预期相悖。

Mary Lowe-Evans, for example, analyzed the oral and written responses of college juniors and seniors in her literature class in order to learn how students today form attitudes toward a specific literary text and how those attitudes determine their interpretation of it. The text she used was Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818), and she mapped the ways in which the following factors influenced students’ interpretations of the novel: film versions of the novel (which created students’ preconceptions of the text), her own interpretive prompts (whose story is this? what does the novel mean? is the narrator reliable?), and the determinate and indeterminate meanings in the text itself. Among other findings, Lowe-Evans confirmed the reader-response notion that interpretation is an ongoing process that evolves as readers use different interpretive strategies to actively work their way through a text. She also learned that preconceptions created by film versions of the novel, in which the monster is very different from Shelley’s monster, facilitated certain interpretations of the story while frustrating others. Analogously, particular textual elements, such as the formal style of the tale’s “Preface” and the epistolary format that opens the narrative (the story is presented as a series of letters from the narrator to his sister), counteracted the students’ expectations of a superficial, entertaining monster story.

然而，无论采用何种分析方法，读者反应批评的最终目标都是通过以下方式增进我们对阅读过程的理解：调查读者参与的活动以及这些活动对其解读的影响。

Whatever kind of analysis is undertaken, however, the ultimate goal of reader-response criticism is to increase our understanding of the reading process by investigating the activities in which readers engage and the effects of those activities on their interpretations.

读者反应批评家们对文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions reader-response critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在总结文学读者反应理论，或者更准确地说，是文学阅读的读者反应理论。问题1基于交互性读者反应理论。问题2与情感文体学相关。问题3涉及主观读者反应理论。问题4基于心理学读者反应理论。问题5与社会读者反应理论相关。问题6在建立文本主题与读者阅读体验之间的联系时，同时运用了交互性读者反应理论和情感文体学的要素。

The questions that follow are offered to summarize reader-response approaches to literature or, more accurately, to the reading of literature. Question 1 draws on transactional reader-response theory. Question 2 relates to affective stylistics. Question 3 concerns subjective reader-response theory. Question 4 draws on psychological reader-response theory. Question 5 relates to social reader-response theory. Question 6 draws on elements of both transactional reader-response theory and affective stylistics in the course of establishing a parallel between the theme of a given text and the reader’s experience while reading it.

1文本与读者之间的互动如何产生意义？文本的不确定性究竟是如何激发读者进行解读的？（例如，哪些事件被省略或未解释？哪些描述被省略或不完整？哪些意象可能具有多种联想？）文本又是如何引导我们在阅读过程中修正自己的解读的？

1 How does the interaction of text and reader create meaning? How, exactly, does the text’s indeterminacy function as a stimulus to interpretation? (For example, what events are omitted or unexplained? What descriptions are omitted or incomplete? What images might have multiple associations?) And how exactly does the text lead us to correct our interpretation as we read?

2对一篇短篇文学作品或一篇长篇作品的关键部分进行逐句分析，能告诉我们关于文本预设（或内置）的阅读体验的哪些信息？这种对文本对读者作用的分析，与文本“说”或“说”的内容有何不同？换句话说，忽略阅读文本的时间体验，会如何导致对文本意义的理解不完整？

2 What does a phrase-by-phrase analysis of a short literary text, or of key portions of a longer text, tell us about the reading experience prestructured by (built into) that text? How does this analysis of what the text does to the reader differ from what the text “says” or “means”? In other words, how might the omission of the temporal experience of reading this text result in an incomplete idea of the text’s meaning?

3如果你有条件，通过对一群真实的读者（例如你的学生、同学或读书俱乐部成员）进行研究，你能了解到读者的解读策略或预期、特定文本产生的阅读体验，或者其他任何阅读活动方面的哪些信息？例如，你能否设计一项研究来检验布莱希的观点，即学生对文学文本的个人反应是其形式解读的来源？

3 If you have the resources to do it, what can you learn about the role of readers’ interpretive strategies or expectations, about the reading experience produced by a particular text, or about any other reading activity by conducting your own study using a group of real readers (for example, your students, classmates, or fellow book-club members)? For instance, can you devise a study to test Bleich’s belief that students’ personal responses to literary texts are the source of their formal interpretations?

4基于大量详实的传记资料，探究某位作家的身份主题是什么，以及该主题如何在他/她的全部文学作品中体现？或者，通过对一部引起强烈共鸣的文学作品的个人解读，尝试找出你自身的身份主题。

4 Drawing on a broad spectrum of thoroughly documented biographical data, what seems to be a given author’s identity theme, and how does that theme express itself in the sum of his or her literary output? Or, using your own interpretation of a literary work to which you respond strongly, see if you can identify what might be your own identity theme.

5在特定时期内发表的关于某部文学作品的评论文章，反映了评论家们怎样的社会假设？换句话说，这些评论文章反映了评论家们怎样的社会信念——关于道德、关于女性……关于儿童、关于宗教、关于文学的目的和价值——这些似乎影响了当时文学评论家对特定文学文本的反应方式？

5 What does the body of criticism published about a literary text during a given time period suggest about the social assumptions of the critics who interpreted that text? In other words, what social beliefs – about morality, about women, about children, about religion, and about the purpose and value of literature – seem to have influenced the ways in which the literary critics of the time responded to a particular literary text?

6我们如何解读文学文本，才能表明读者的反应与故事的主题相同或相似？换句话说，文本究竟是如何展现读者阅读的，又是如何揭示这一主题的？更进一步来说，某种特定的阅读体验是如何成为文本的重要主题的？当然，我们首先必须确定文本所创造的阅读体验（参见问题1和2），才能证明故事的主题与之相似。然后，我们必须引用文本证据——例如，提及阅读材料、人物阅读文本以及人物解读其他人物或事件——来表明叙事世界中发生的事情反映了读者解读文本时的处境。

6 How might we interpret a literary text to show that the reader’s response is, or is analogous to, the topic of the story? In other words, how is the text really about readers reading, and what exactly does it tell us about this topic? To simplify further, how is a particular kind of reading experience an important theme in the text? Of course, we must first establish what reading experience is created by the text (see Questions 1 and 2) in order to show that the theme of the story is analogous to it. Then we must cite textual evidence – for example, references to reading materials, to characters reading texts, and to characters interpreting other characters or events – to show that what happens in the world of the narrative mirrors the reader’s situation decoding it.

根据具体文学作品，我们可以提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们也可以提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们以富有成效的读者反应视角思考文学作品的一些起点。请记住，即使关注相同的读者反应概念，并非所有读者反应批评家都会以相同的方式解读同一文本，甚至同一读者的反应。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。我们的目标是运用读者反应理论来丰富我们对文学作品的阅读，帮助我们理解作品中蕴含的一些重要思想（这些思想我们可能原本无法如此清晰或深刻地领悟），并帮助我们理解阅读体验的复杂性和多样性。

Depending on the literary work in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us thinking about literature in productive reader-response ways. Keep in mind that not all reader-response critics will interpret the same text, or even the same readers’ responses, in the same way, even if they focus on the same reader-response concepts. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use reader-response theory to help enrich our reading of literary works, to help us see some important ideas they illustrate that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply otherwise, and to help us understand the complexities and varieties of the reading experience.

以下对菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的读者反应分析，旨在展示读者反应解读该小说可能产生的成果。我将运用情感文体学的原则、伊瑟的不确定性概念以及霍兰德的投射概念，探讨小说如何在阅读过程中不断地挑战我们对杰伊·盖茨比不断变化的认知，从而营造出一种不确定性，引导读者将自身的信念和欲望投射到主人公身上。此外，我还会阐述小说的主题内容（即小说“讲述的是什么”）如何反映读者的阅读体验，也就是说，小说的主题在于无法确定意义。

The following reader-response analysis of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a reader-response interpretation of that novel might yield. Using the principles of affective stylistics, Iser’s notion of indeterminacy, and Holland’s notion of projection, I will examine the way the novel continually problematizes our evolving perception of Jay Gatsby as we read, creating an indeterminacy that invites us to project our own beliefs and desires onto the protagonist. In addition, I will show how the novel’s thematic content (what the novel “is about”) mirrors the reader’s experience reading it, that is, how the theme of the novel is the impossibility of establishing determinate meaning.

读者视角：对《了不起的盖茨比》的读者反应分析

Projecting the reader: a reader-response analysis of The Great Gatsby

“有人告诉我，他们认为他曾经杀过人。”

“Somebody told me they thought he killed a man once.”

我们所有人都感到一阵兴奋。三位咕哝先生俯下身子，认真地听着。

A thrill passed over all of us. The three Mr. Mumbles bent forward and listened eagerly.

“我不认为是这样，”露西尔怀疑地反驳道，“更可能是他在战争期间是德国间谍。”

“I don’t think it’s so much that,” argued Lucille skeptically; “it’s more that he was a German spy during the war.”

其中一名男子点头表示同意。

One of the men nodded in confirmation.

“我从一个对他非常了解的人那里听说的，他跟他一起在德国长大，”他肯定地向我们保证。

“I heard that from a man who knew all about him, grew up with him in Germany,” he assured us positively.

“哦，不，”第一个女孩说，“不可能，因为他战争期间在美国军队服役。”我们开始对她产生怀疑，她却兴奋地向前倾身。“你有时会在他以为没人注意的时候偷看他。我敢打赌他杀过人。”

“Oh no,” said the first girl, “it couldn’t be that, because he was in the American army during the war.” As our credulity switched back to her she leaned forward with enthusiasm. “You look at him sometimes when he thinks nobody’s looking at him. I’ll bet he killed a man.”

（48；第3章）

(48; ch. 3)

杰伊·盖茨比在那些热衷八卦、渴望震惊的派对宾客心中激起的种种猜测，在两个重要方面，都预示着他在F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的小说《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）中激起的读者的种种猜测。如同盖茨比的派对宾客一样，随着我们阅读尼克·卡拉威的叙述，我们的轻信程度也在不断地被“转换”；而我们最终的猜测结果——我们对盖茨比的解读，进而对整部小说意义的理解——很大程度上取决于我们自身的信念和欲望，而故事的不确定性恰恰诱使我们将这些信念和欲望投射到自身。换言之，《了不起的盖茨比》生动地展现了读者反应理论中“阅读即意义建构”的概念，小说在故事情节中再现了读者在阅读时的体验。

The speculation Jay Gatsby inspires in his gossip-hungry party guests, who have an obvious desire to be shocked, is, in two important ways, a prototype of the speculation he inspires in the reader of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925). Our credulity, like that of Gatsby’s party guests, is continually “switched” in different directions as we make our way through Nick Carraway’s narration, and the final outcome of our speculation – our interpretation of Gatsby and therefore of the meaning of the novel as a whole – is largely a product of our own beliefs and desires, which the tale’s indeterminacy invites us to project. In other words, The Great Gatsby dramatizes reader-response theory’s concept of reading as the making of meaning, and the novel reproduces within the action of the story the reader’s experience while reading it.

小说中的人物以杰伊·盖茨比为“文本”，构建了一种阅读体验，这种体验可以用以下公式来描述：投射 + 收集的数据 = 投射的验证。换句话说，解读者从环境中收集的数据只有一个主要功能：验证他们已经投射或正在投射的解读。例如，正如我们刚才看到的，盖茨比派对上的宾客在一次对话中就完成了公式的所有三个步骤。尽管他们所依赖的那些离奇谣言并不准确，但谣言是唯一可用的数据，而且它们并不比盖茨比犯罪活动的真相更令人震惊。更重要的是，离奇的谣言满足了他们最初解读盖茨比时对丑闻的渴望：就他们对盖茨比这个“文本”的欣赏而言，他们相信哪个谣言几乎无关紧要，只要谣言足够离谱或能引发更多令人震惊的猜测即可。换句话说，派对宾客们对盖茨比的解读是为了获得震撼，而他们的解读满足了他们的愿望。

With Jay Gatsby as the “text” they decode, the characters in the novel model a reading experience that could be described by the following formula: projection + data gathered = confirmation of projection. In other words, the data that interpreters gather from the environment have one primary function: to validate for them the interpretation they’ve already projected or are in the process of projecting. For example, as we just saw, Gatsby’s party guests perform all three steps of the formula in a single conversation. Although the outlandish rumors they rely on are inaccurate, rumors are the only data available, and they are hardly more shocking than the truth about Gatsby’s criminal activities. More important, outlandish rumors fulfill the desire for scandal that prompts them to interpret Gatsby in the first place: it hardly matters, in terms of their enjoyment of the “text” that is Gatsby, which of the rumors they believe, as long as the rumor is sufficiently outrageous or provokes further shocking speculations. In other words, the party guests interpret Gatsby in order to be shocked, and their interpretations fulfill their desire.

同样，汤姆·布坎南想当然地认为盖茨比是个出身卑微的骗子，于是雇佣私家侦探搜集证据来证明这一点。黛西则想把盖茨比当成她英俊潇洒的白马王子，所以她刻意地对他财富和地位的伪装视而不见，那伪装就像覆盖在他豪宅塔楼上的“稀疏的常春藤胡须”（9；第1章）一样脆弱。沃尔夫希姆则想当然地认为盖茨比是“出身高贵的人”（76；第4章），这样他才能在自己的地下世界里“好好利用他”（179；第9章）。因此，他并不觉得一个出身名门的绅士——“奥格斯福德家族的人”——“穷困潦倒到不得不一直穿着制服，因为他买不起像样的衣服”（179；第九章）有什么矛盾之处。乔治·威尔逊想要相信盖茨比诱奸并杀害了他的妻子，因为这种信念能让他为默特尔的遭遇和死亡复仇，并获得他所需要的情感慰藉。所以，威尔逊轻易地相信了他听到的第一个故事：尽管当天早些时候他亲眼看到汤姆驾驶着那辆“死亡之车”，尽管汤姆不久前还对威尔逊许下过一些未兑现的承诺，但他却对汤姆的解释没有丝毫怀疑，也没有提出任何疑问。最后，盖茨先生想要相信他的儿子“前途无量”：“如果他活下来，他会成为一个伟大的人物。像[铁路大亨]詹姆斯·J·希尔那样的人。他会为国家的建设做出贡献”（176；第九章）。因此，盖茨先生将儿子童年的“日程安排”解释为“吉米注定要出人头地”（182；第9章）的证据，完全相信了盖茨比肯定告诉他的关于其财富来源的任何不切实际的谎言。

Analogously, Tom Buchanan wants to believe that Gatsby is a crook with no respectable family background, and he hires private investigators to provide him with the evidence he needs to prove it. Daisy wants to believe Gatsby is her upper-class knight in shining armor, so she conveniently doesn’t see through his veneer of wealth and status, which is as thin as the “thin beard of raw ivy” (9; ch. 1) covering the tower of his mansion. Wolfsheim wants to believe that Gatsby is “a man of fine breeding” (76; ch. 4) so he can “use him good” (179; ch. 9) in his underworld activities, and therefore he doesn’t see the contradiction in a finely bred man, “an Oggsford,” being “so hard up he had to keep on wearing his uniform because he couldn’t buy some regular clothes” (179; ch. 9). George Wilson wants to believe that Gatsby seduced and murdered his wife because this belief will permit Wilson to avenge Myrtle’s seduction and death and achieve the emotional closure he needs. So Wilson readily believes the first story he hears: he asks no questions and has no doubts about Tom’s explanation despite having seen Tom himself driving the “death” car earlier that day and despite Tom’s unfulfilled promises to Wilson in the recent past. Finally, Mr. Gatz wants to believe that his son “had a big future before him”: “If he’d of lived he’d of been a great man. A man like [railroad tycoon] James J. Hill. He’d of helped build up the country” (176; ch. 9). Mr. Gatz therefore interprets his son’s boyhood “schedule” as proof that “Jimmy was bound to get ahead” (182; ch. 9), having swallowed completely whatever improbable lies Gatsby surely told him about the source of his wealth.

我并非暗示这些人物有能力或机会获取关于盖茨比的更准确信息。我的观点很简单：他们急于接受所获得的信息，并迅速利用这些信息构建他们眼中盖茨比的完整形象，这都取决于这些信息在多大程度上满足了他们自身对盖茨比的幻想。

I’m not suggesting that these characters have the ability or the opportunity to acquire more accurate information about Gatsby. My point is simply that the eagerness with which they embrace the information they acquire and the readiness with which they use it to construct what they choose to regard as the complete picture of Gatsby are products of the degree to which the information fulfills their own desires concerning the man.

或许可以这样认为：这种解读方式造成的诸多不准确之处，旨在引导读者尝试其他方法，小说本身也否定了这些人物所代表的主观、自私的解读。然而，正如我们将看到的，尼克·卡拉威——他以第一人称叙述引领我们穿梭于小说中道德暧昧的世界——同样也是透过自身投射的视角来解读盖茨比。此外，他之所以这样做，是因为在小说这个充满不确定性的世界里，似乎别无他法可以解读盖茨比。随着尼克“时而喜欢盖茨比，时而又不喜欢”的叙述，我们也和他一起，在对主人公截然相反的两种认知之间摇摆不定。尼克对这个人物的开篇评价——他说盖茨比“代表了一切……[尼克]……鄙视的东西”，然而，对于他的长岛朋友们，他却“不受[尼克的]负面反应的影响”（6；第1章）——预示着他将在叙述展开的过程中与我们分享的盖茨比的矛盾经历。

It might be reasonable to conclude that the amount of inaccuracy produced by this sort of interpretation teaches the reader to try another method, that the novel discredits the subjective, self-serving interpretation represented by these characters. However, as we shall see, Nick Carraway – whose first-person narration guides us through the morally ambiguous world of the novel – interprets Gatsby through the lens of his own projections as well. Furthermore, he does so because, in the indeterminate world of the novel, there is no other way to interpret Gatsby. As we follow Nick through his “now-I-like-Gatsby; now-I-don’t” narration, we are thrust, along with him, back and forth between opposing perceptions of the protagonist. Nick’s opening evaluation of the character – in which he says that Gatsby “represents everything … [Nick] … scorn[s]” and yet is “exempt from [Nick’s negative] reaction” (6; ch. 1) to his Long Island friends – announces the paradoxical experience of Gatsby he will share with us as his narrative unfolds.

尼克的叙述构建了一种错综复杂的读者对盖茨比的同情与批判模式，要详细探讨这种模式需要专门撰写一篇论文，但对其轮廓的粗略勾勒足以展现这种模式所带来的不确定性。如上所述，尼克以对盖茨比的矛盾评价来介绍这个人物之后，叙述者将我们带回到故事的开头，或者说是故事开始之前，描述了他自己在明尼苏达州“显赫富裕”（7；第一章）的家庭，以及他决定前往纽约学习债券业务的原因。在第一章的剩余部分，尼克对盖茨比的唯一感受是……他与我们分享的，是他对这个人的好奇心，这体现在他对“盖茨比的豪宅”的描述中。或者更确切地说，由于尼克并不认识盖茨比先生，那只是一座住着一位名叫盖茨比的绅士的豪宅”（第9页；第一章）。换句话说，我们跟随尼克回到过去，体验他亲身经历的事件。第6页出现的“盖茨比”在第9页变成了“盖茨比先生”，因为尼克带我们回到了他尚未遇见这位主人公的那一刻。

Nick’s narrative creates an intricate pattern of reader sympathy for and criticism of Gatsby that would require an essay of its own to trace in detail, but a rough sketch of its contours should demonstrate the sense of indeterminacy this pattern promotes. After the paradoxical evaluation of Gatsby with which Nick introduces us to the character, noted above, the narrator takes us back to the beginning of his tale, or before the beginning, to a description of his own “prominent, well-to-do” (7; ch. 1) family in Minnesota and his decision to go to New York and learn the bond business. Throughout the rest of chapter 1 the only feeling about Gatsby Nick shares with us is his curiosity about the man, which is revealed through his description of “Gatsby’s mansion. Or rather, as [Nick] didn’t know Mr. Gatsby, it was a mansion inhabited by a gentleman of that name” (9; ch. 1). In other words, we travel back in time with Nick and experience events as he experienced them unfolding in time. The “Gatsby” introduced on page 6 has become “Mr. Gatsby” on page 9 because Nick has taken us back to a point in time when he hadn’t yet met the protagonist.

当乔丹提到盖茨比——她在西卵遇到的那个男人——时，我们的好奇心被激发了出来，黛西追问：“盖茨比？……哪个盖茨比？”（15；第一章），但直到第三章中段，叙述者尼克参加了盖茨比举办的派对，他和读者才真正见到盖茨比。尼克从自家小屋的门廊上细致观察盖茨比的派对，既激起了我们的好奇心，也暴露了他自己的好奇。他与邻居的初次相遇，开启了贯穿整部小说的、关于盖茨比的相互矛盾的解读模式，这种模式将贯穿尼克和我们读者的整个阅读体验。盖茨比向尼克做了自我介绍，然后露出微笑，叙述者被他迷住了。尼克说，

Our curiosity is raised when Jordan mentions Gatsby, a man she met at West Egg, and Daisy demands, “Gatsby? … What Gatsby?” (15; ch. 1), but Nick and the reader don’t meet Gatsby until the middle of chapter 3, when the narrator attends one of Gatsby’s parties. Having excited our curiosity, and revealed his own, by his minute observations of what he can see of Gatsby’s parties from the porch of his cottage, Nick’s initial meeting with his neighbor initiates the pattern of conflicting interpretations of Gatsby that will characterize his experience, and ours, throughout the novel. Gatsby introduces himself to Nick, then smiles, and the narrator is charmed. Nick says,

那是一种罕见的微笑，带着一种永恒的安心感……它恰如其分地展现了你最希望传递的那种形象。就在那一刻，微笑消失了——我看到的是一个举止优雅却略显粗犷的年轻汉子……他那矫揉造作的谈吐几乎到了荒谬的地步。

It was one of those rare smiles with a quality of eternal reassurance in it. … [I]t had precisely the impression of you that, at your best, you hoped to convey. Precisely at that point it vanished – and I was looking at an elegant young rough-neck … whose elaborate formality of speech just missed being absurd.

（53；第3章）

(53; ch. 3)

换句话说，尼克对盖茨比的正面印象——他是一位迷人的绅士——紧接着就变成了对盖茨比的负面印象——他是个伪君子。

In other words, Nick’s positive impression that Gatsby is a charming gentleman is immediately followed by a negative impression that Gatsby is a phony.

这种模式一直重复，直到尼克在晚宴结束时离开。叙述者瞥见盖茨比“独自站在大理石台阶上”，说道：“我看不出他有什么不祥之兆”（54；第三章）。但紧接着，尼克又开始怀疑盖茨比天真无邪的外表是否只是假象，因为“盖茨比是唯一一个没喝酒的人……在我看来，随着兄弟间的欢声笑语愈演愈烈，他反而显得更加端庄”（54；第三章）。同样，当尼克向盖茨比道晚安时，他暗示主人并不真诚。盖茨比称呼尼克为“老伙计”，但“那熟悉的表情和轻轻拂过我肩膀的手一样，都透着一丝虚假”（57；第三章）。几秒钟后，盖茨比笑了，尼克又对他有了好感——“突然间，似乎自己是最后离开的人之一这件事有了某种令人愉悦的意义，仿佛他一直都渴望如此”（58；第三章）——盖茨比的“晚安，老伙计……晚安”（58；第三章）听起来温暖而真诚。最后，当尼克从草坪对面回头望向盖茨比，准备回家时，他对这位主人公的描述突显了他自己对盖茨比复杂情感的矛盾感受：“一种突如其来的空虚感似乎从窗户和大门中涌出，使他显得格外孤寂。”站在门廊上的主人举起手，做出正式的告别姿势”（60；第三章，斜体为笔者所加）。这段文字究竟是强调盖茨比的冷漠，从而削弱我们对他的同情，还是强调他的孤独，从而增强我们对他的同情？尼克并没有明确表达自己的态度——或许他自己也不确定——因此，在读者对盖茨比的一系列矛盾反应之后，只能将自身的经历投射到主人公身上。

This pattern is repeated until Nick leaves the party at the end of the evening. The narrator, catching a glimpse of Gatsby “standing alone on the marble steps,” says, “I could see nothing sinister about him” (54; ch. 3). But in the very next sentence Nick wonders if Gatsby’s innocent appearance is an illusion produced by “the fact that [Gatsby] was [the only one] not drinking … for it seemed to me that he grew more correct as the fraternal hilarity increased” (54; ch. 3). Again, as Nick bids Gatsby goodnight he implies that his host is insincere. Gatsby calls Nick “old sport,” but “[t]he familiar expression held no more familiarity than the hand which reassuringly brushed my shoulder” (57; ch. 3). Then a few seconds later Gatsby smiles, and Nick likes him again – “suddenly there seemed to be a pleasant significance in having been among the last to go, as if he had desired it so all the time” (58; ch. 3) – and Gatsby’s “Good night, old sport. … Good night” (58; ch. 3) feels warm and sincere. Finally, as Nick glances back at Gatsby from across the lawn as he heads home, he describes the protagonist in a way that underscores the ambiguity of his own response to him: “A sudden emptiness seemed to flow now from the windows and the great doors, endowing with complete isolation the figure of the host who stood on the porch, his hand up in a formal gesture of farewell” (60; ch. 3, my italics). Does this language emphasize Gatsby’s coldness, which would decrease our sympathy for him, or his loneliness, which would increase it? Nick doesn’t clarify his own attitude – perhaps he’s not sure – so the reader is left, after a series of conflicting responses to Gatsby, to project his or her personal experience onto the protagonist.

我们与盖茨比的下一次交锋发生在第四章开头，当时主人公开车送尼克去纽约。在这一幕中，我们对盖茨比的态度再次在正面和负面之间摇摆不定。尼克首先讲述了他在去纽约之前对盖茨比态度的转变，这是基于他们相识一个月以来，他与这位邻居的六次谈话：

Our next encounter with Gatsby occurs at the beginning of chapter 4, when the protagonist drives Nick to New York. During this scene, our attitude toward Gatsby is again shifted back and forth between positive and negative poles. Nick starts us off with the following account of his change in attitude toward Gatsby prior to their drive to New York, based on the half-dozen conversations he’d had with his neighbor during the month since they’d met:

令我失望的是……他几乎没说什么。因此，我最初对他的印象——一个举足轻重的人物——逐渐消退，他只不过是隔壁一家装潢华丽的路边旅馆的老板而已。

[T]o my disappointment … he had little to say. So my first impression, that he was a person of some undefined consequence, had gradually faded and he had become simply the proprietor of an elaborate road-house next door.

（69；第4章）

(69; ch. 4)

然后，正如尼克所说，“那段令人不安的经历就此展开”（69；第四章）。当盖茨比向尼克讲述他富有的家族故事时，“现在全都去世了”（69；第四章），以及他在牛津大学的求学经历，尼克说道：

Then, as Nick puts it, “came that disconcerting ride” (69; ch. 4). As Gatsby tells Nick the story about his wealthy family, “all dead now” (69; ch. 4), and his Oxford education, Nick says,

他斜眼看了我一眼……然后，他急切地说出了“毕业于牛津”这句话……随着这个疑点，他之前说的一切都显得漏洞百出，我开始怀疑他是不是有点儿阴险狡诈。

He looked at me sideways. … [And] [h]e hurried the phrase “educated at Oxford.”… And with this doubt his whole statement fell to pieces and I wondered if there wasn’t something a little sinister about him after all.

（69；第4章）

(69; ch. 4)

当然，尼克现在对盖茨比关于他收藏珠宝（“主要是红宝石”）、狩猎大型猎物和绘画的任何说法都不相信，他“费了好大劲”才“勉强忍住难以置信的笑声”（70；4）。盖茨比接下来讲述的战争故事听起来和他之前讲的故事一样夸张，尼克感觉自己就像“匆匆翻阅了十几本杂志”（71；4）。然而，盖茨比随后向尼克展示了一枚刻有他名字的战争勋章，“令尼克惊讶的是，这东西看起来很真”（71；4）。当盖茨比拿出他和一群牛津大学同学的合影时，尼克得出结论：“那么，这一切都是真的”（71；4）。

Of course, Nick now believes nothing Gatsby says about his jewel collecting, “chiefly rubies” (70; ch. 4), big-game hunting, and painting, and only “[w]ith an effort” does Nick “manag[e] to restrain [his] incredulous laughter” (70; ch. 4). Gatsby’s war story, which he tells next, sounds just as exaggerated as the rest of his tale, and Nick feels as though he is “skimming hastily through a dozen magazines” (71; ch. 4). However, Gatsby then shows Nick a war medal with his name on it, and “[t]o [Nick’s] astonishment the thing had an authentic look” (71; ch. 4). When Gatsby produces a snapshot of himself with a group of fellow students at Oxford, Nick concludes, “Then it was all true” (71; ch. 4).

然而，当盖茨比说乔丹·贝克要替他向尼克提个要求时，尼克对盖茨比的信任很快就被恼怒所取代：“我确信这个要求肯定荒唐至极，那一刻我真后悔踏入他那杂草丛生的草坪”（72；第四章）。尼克注意到，随着我们接近城市，盖茨比的“一本正经”越来越让他反感。（72；第四章），他似乎再次暗示盖茨比是个伪君子。然而，这一幕以一个事件结尾，似乎再次让尼克以及我们读者的同情心陷入了暧昧之中。盖茨比因超速被警察拦下，他拿出一张纸，不仅让他免于罚单，还让拦下他的警察向他道歉。盖茨比解释说：“我曾经帮过局长一个忙，他每年都给我寄圣诞贺卡”（73；第四章）。虽然这件事无疑凸显了盖茨比的重要性，从而印证了他刚才告诉尼克的故事，但我们该如何看待其中暗示的腐败呢？尼克的回答也无济于事——“即使是盖茨比，在纽约这样的地方也可能发生，没什么好奇怪的”（73；第四章）——所以我们再次陷入了迷茫。

Nick’s belief in Gatsby is quickly submerged under his annoyance, however, when Gatsby says that Jordan Baker is going to make a request of Nick on Gatsby’s behalf: “I was sure the request would be something utterly fantastic and for a moment I was sorry I’d ever set foot upon his overpopulated lawn” (72; ch. 4). When Nick notes that Gatsby’s “correctness grew on him as we neared the city” (72; ch. 4), he seems to be implying again that Gatsby is a phony. Yet the scene ends with an incident that seems to leave Nick’s sympathies, and ours, again mired in ambiguity. When Gatsby is pulled over for speeding, he produces a piece of paper that not only gets him out of a ticket but also causes the officer who pulled him over to apologize. Gatsby explains, “I was able to do the commissioner a favor once, and he sends me a Christmas card every year” (73; ch. 4). While this incident certainly underscores Gatsby’s importance and therefore supports the story he just told Nick, how should we feel about the touch of corruption hinted at here? Nick’s response doesn’t help – “Even Gatsby could happen [in a place like New York] without any particular wonder” (73; ch. 4) – so we’re once more left on our own.

对小说其余部分中塑造读者对盖茨比不断变化的看法的场景进行分析，可以发现类似的相互对立的影响模式，如下文对这些场景的总结所示。

An analysis of the scenes that shape the reader’s evolving view of Gatsby through the rest of the novel reveals a similar pattern of opposing influences, as we see in the following summary of those scenes.

1 尼克、盖茨比和沃尔夫希姆共进午餐（73-79；第 4 章）——由于尼克描述了盖茨比与沃尔夫希姆的密切关系（沃尔夫希姆的形象非常负面），以及尼克对盖茨比的怀疑评论，我们对盖茨比的印象形成了负面的。

1 Nick, Gatsby, and Wolfsheim have lunch (73–79; ch. 4) – Our impression of Gatsby is shaped negatively due to Nick’s description of Gatsby’s close association with Wolfsheim, who is very negatively portrayed, and Nick’s suspicious comments about Gatsby.

2 乔丹告诉尼克盖茨比和黛西的事（79-85；第 4 章）——由于盖茨比对黛西的忠诚奉献、害怕得罪乔丹和尼克，以及尼克对盖茨比困境的同情反应，我们对盖茨比的印象形成了积极的印象。

2 Jordan tells Nick about Gatsby and Daisy (79–85; ch. 4) – Our impression of Gatsby is shaped positively due to Gatsby’s faithful devotion to Daisy, his fear of offending Jordan and Nick, and Nick’s sympathetic response to Gatsby’s plight.

3 尼克和盖茨比安排盖茨比与黛西重逢（86-88；第5章）——由于尼克对盖茨比试图示好的举动始终冷淡，我们对盖茨比的印象变得负面，尤其是在盖茨比“明显且不顾及他人感受”（88；第5章）地提出让他轻松赚钱，以此换取他安排盖茨比与黛西重逢之后。

3 Nick and Gatsby arrange Gatsby’s reunion with Daisy (86–88; ch. 5) – Our impression of Gatsby is shaped negatively due to Nick’s consistently cool responses to Gatsby’s attempts at friendliness, especially after Gatsby “obviously and tactlessly” (88; ch. 5) offers him a chance to make some easy money in exchange for arranging the reunion with Daisy.

4 盖茨比和黛西重逢（88-94；第 5 章）——尼克对盖茨比的描述，让我们对盖茨比产生了积极的同情。盖茨比在与黛西见面之前紧张不安，与黛西初次见面时的极度焦虑，以及当他意识到黛西仍然爱着他时的巨大喜悦，都源于尼克对盖茨比的尴尬和幸福的感同身受。

4 Gatsby and Daisy reunite (88–94; ch. 5) – Our sympathy for Gatsby is shaped positively by Nick’s description of the protagonist’s total emotional investment in Daisy – his nervous apprehension before the meeting, his intense anxiety during the initial awkwardness with Daisy, and his overwhelming joy when he realizes she still loves him – and by Nick’s vicarious experience of the protagonist’s embarrassment and happiness.

5 尼克和盖茨比在尼克的草坪上等黛西（95；第5章）——尼克发现盖茨比在买房子的钱的来源上撒谎，这给我们留下了负面的印象。当尼克问盖茨比是做什么生意时，盖茨比粗鲁而又防备地回答说：“那是我的事情”（95；第5章）。

5 Nick and Gatsby wait for Daisy on Nick’s lawn (95; ch. 5) – Our impression of Gatsby is shaped negatively by Nick’s catching Gatsby in an apparent lie about where he got the money to buy his house and by Gatsby’s rude and defensive reply – “That’s my affair” (95; ch. 5) – when Nick asks him what business he’s in.

6 盖茨比向黛西和尼克展示他的房子（96-102；第 5 章）——我们对盖茨比的反应在正面和负面两极之间摇摆不定，因为尼克对盖茨比对黛西的奉献的同情描述在中间被一个不祥的电话打断，强烈暗示了盖茨比隐藏的犯罪生活。

6 Gatsby shows his house to Daisy and Nick (96–102; ch. 5) – Our response to Gatsby is moved between positive and negative poles as Nick’s sympathetic description of Gatsby’s devotion to Daisy is interrupted in the middle by an ominous phone call that hints strongly at Gatsby’s hidden criminal life.

7 尼克讲述了盖茨比青年时代的真实故事（104-107页；第六章）——我们对盖茨比的感受在正面和负面之间摇摆不定。尼克对盖茨比贫困的童年、少年梦想、辛勤工作和清醒的描述充满同情，但这种同情却两次被尼克的观察所打断：盖茨比的梦想“服务于一种巨大、庸俗而虚伪的美”（104页；第六章），以及它们存在于一个“难以言喻的浮华世界”（105页；第六章）。在这一幕的结尾，尼克说道：“（盖茨比）很久以后才告诉我这一切……那时我对他的一切都深信不疑，却又一无所知”（107页；第六章），这让我们在接下来的很长一段时间里都感到困惑。

7 Nick relates the real story of Gatsby’s youth (104–7; ch. 6) – Our response to Gatsby is moved between positive and negative poles as Nick’s sympathetic description of Gatsby’s impoverished youth, boyhood dreams, hard work, and sobriety is interrupted twice by Nick’s observations that Gatsby’s dreams were in “the service of a vast, vulgar and meretricious beauty” (104; ch. 6) and that they inhabited a “universe of ineffable gaudiness” (105; ch. 6). At the end of the scene Nick says, “[Gatsby] told me all this very much later … when I had reached the point of believing everything and nothing about him” (107; ch. 6), thus reinforcing our uncertainty for some time to come.

8 汤姆和朋友们骑马来到盖茨比家（107-10；第 6 章）——我们对盖茨比的反应在正面和负面两极之间摇摆不定，因为尼克同情地描述了盖茨比面对访客的粗鲁无礼时所表现出的礼貌，但随后他又描述了盖茨比“几乎咄咄逼人”地试图逼迫汤姆说话，以便更多地了解他。

8 Tom and friends on horseback stop at Gatsby’s house (107–10; ch. 6) – Our response to Gatsby is moved between positive and negative poles as Nick’s sympathetic description of Gatsby’s politeness in the face of his visitors’ rudeness is interrupted by his description of Gatsby’s “almost aggressiv[e]” attempts to push Tom into talking in order to learn more about him.

9 尼克、汤姆和黛西参加了盖茨比的派对（110-18；第6章）——尼克对盖茨比关注黛西的同情描述，他对汤姆的暗示对盖茨比的愤怒辩护，以及他对盖茨比讲述与黛西早期生活的极富诗意的描述，都对我们对盖茨比的印象产生了积极的影响，尽管尼克对盖茨比“可怕的多愁善感”（118；第6章）的负面评价在某种程度上削弱了这种积极的影响。

9 Nick, Tom, and Daisy attend Gatsby’s party (110–18; ch. 6) – Our response to Gatsby is shaped positively by Nick’s sympathetic descriptions of Gatsby’s attentions to Daisy, by his angry defense of Gatsby against Tom’s insinuations, and by his extremely poetic rendition of Gatsby’s account of his early days with Daisy, though that rendition is somewhat undercut by Nick’s negative reference to Gatsby’s “appalling sentimentality” (118; ch. 6).

10 尼克得知盖茨比的新仆人（119-20；第 7 章）——尼克对盖茨比与沃尔夫希姆的人交往的描述，以及主人公显然没有注意到他们阴险的特质，都对盖茨比产生了负面的影响。

10 Nick learns about Gatsby’s new servants (119–20; ch. 7) – Our response to Gatsby is negatively shaped by Nick’s description of Gatsby’s association with Wolfsheim’s people and the protagonist’s apparent failure to notice their sinister quality.

11 尼克和盖茨比与布坎南夫妇和乔丹共进午餐（121-128页；第七章）——尼克对盖茨比的描述，让我们对他产生了积极的印象：面对汤姆的咄咄逼人和黛西对情人的公开示爱，盖茨比依然保持着安静和良好的举止。然而，在这一幕的结尾，尼克的负面观察却削弱了这种积极的印象，暗示了主人公的阴暗面：当汤姆隐晦地提及盖茨比的犯罪活动时，“一种难以言喻的表情……掠过盖茨比的脸庞”（127页）。
