11 Nick and Gatsby lunch with the Buchanans and Jordan (121–28; ch. 7) – Our response to Gatsby is shaped positively by Nick’s description of Gatsby’s quiet good manners in the face of Tom’s aggressiveness and Daisy’s open displays of affection for her lover. This response is undercut somewhat at the end of the scene by Nick’s negative observation, which hints at the protagonist’s dark side, that “an undefinable expression … passed over Gatsby’s face” (127) when Tom makes a veiled reference to Gatsby’s criminal activities.

12 汤姆在纽约酒店套房里与盖茨比对峙（133-42；第 7 章）——尼克对盖茨比坦诚讲述他在牛津的经历，以及对盖茨比面对汤姆的冷酷无情和黛西的疏远，绝望而可怜地试图留住黛西的描述，使我们对盖茨比产生了积极的同情。

12 Tom confronts Gatsby in the New York hotel suite (133–42; ch. 7) – Our sympathy for Gatsby is shaped positively by Nick’s description of Gatsby’s honesty about his Oxford experience and his description of Gatsby’s desperate and pathetic attempt to hold Daisy in the face of Tom’s ruthlessness and her withdrawal.

13 在默特尔死后，尼克在布坎南家门外遇到了盖茨比（150-53；第 7 章）——尼克得知肇事逃逸的司机是黛西而不是盖茨比，而盖茨比却替她承担了责任，这让尼克对盖茨比的态度从消极转变为积极。

13 Nick meets Gatsby outside the Buchanans’ house after Myrtle’s death (150–53; ch. 7) – Our response to Gatsby is moved from the negative to the positive by the change in Nick’s behavior toward Gatsby after he learns that Daisy, not Gatsby, drove the hit-and-run car and Gatsby is taking the blame for her.

14 在默特尔去世后的第二天早上，尼克和盖茨比在盖茨比家交谈（154-62；第八章）——我们对盖茨比的反应在正面和负面之间摇摆不定，因为尼克对盖茨比忠于黛西的同情描述被打断了。他声称盖茨比“贪婪地、肆无忌惮地”（156）以虚假借口“占有”了黛西。

14 Nick and Gatsby talk at Gatsby’s house the morning after Myrtle’s death (154–62; ch. 8) – Our response to Gatsby is moved between positive and negative poles as Nick’s sympathetic description of Gatsby’s devotion to Daisy is interrupted by his statement that Gatsby “took” Daisy, “ravenously and unscrupulously” (156), under false pretenses.

15 尼克安排盖茨比的葬礼（171-83；第 9 章）——我们对盖茨比的反应在积极和消极两极之间几度转换，因为尼克与盖茨比“对抗所有人”的“……轻蔑的团结感”（173）不断被主人公的犯罪活动所打断。

15 Nick makes Gatsby’s funeral arrangements (171–83; ch. 9) – Our response to Gatsby is moved several times between positive and negative poles as Nick’s “feeling of … scornful solidarity” with Gatsby “against them all” (173) is repeatedly interrupted by reminders of the protagonist’s criminal activities.

16 尼克在盖茨比返回明尼苏达州的前一天晚上，在盖茨比的海滩上散步（189；第 9 章）——尼克将盖茨比“第一次看到黛西码头尽头的绿光时的惊奇”（189）与处女般的美国大陆所激发的惊奇（“新世界的新鲜绿色胸怀”，189）进行了诗意的比较，这积极地塑造了我们对盖茨比的同情。

16 Nick walks on Gatsby’s beach the night before he heads back to Minnesota (189; ch. 9) – Our sympathy for Gatsby is positively shaped by Nick’s poetic comparison of Gatsby’s “wonder when he first picked out the green light at the end of Daisy’s dock” (189) with the wonder inspired by the virgin American continent, the “fresh, green breast of the new world” (189).

因此，尽管文本在每个场景中都积极地塑造着读者对盖茨比的反应，但随着故事的推进，我们却感受到一种显著的不确定性。因为我们逐渐了解到，文本将支持对盖茨比的两种截然相反的解读：（1）盖茨比是罪犯，为了达到目的不择手段，伤害任何人；（2）盖茨比是浪漫英雄，他摆脱了贫困，将生命奉献给黛西，如同“追寻圣杯”（156；第八章）。换句话说，小说塑造了一个主人公，他为了实现纯粹的目标——赢得黛西并过上美好生活——而使用完全不正当的手段，包括走私私酒和伪造债券——然后让我们来判断，这些手段是否正当。然而，小说并没有提供我们回答这个问题所需的确凿证据。

Thus, while the text actively shapes the reader’s response to Gatsby in each of these scenes, as we move through the tale we experience a significant degree of indeterminacy. For we gradually learn that the text will support two opposing interpretations of Gatsby: (1) Gatsby the criminal, who will hurt anyone and do anything to get what he wants, and (2) Gatsby the romantic hero, who has pulled himself out of poverty and devoted his life to Daisy as “to the following of a grail” (156; ch. 8). In other words, the novel gives us a protagonist who uses wholly corrupt means, including bootlegging and fraudulent bonds, to achieve pure ends – Gatsby’s “incorruptible dream” (162; ch. 8) of winning Daisy and living the good life – and then asks us to decide if the ends justify the means. But the novel doesn’t provide the kind of unequivocal evidence we need to answer the question.

从抽象的道德角度来看，一个简单的“不”——这个显而易见的“正确”答案——并不能充分回应问题的复杂性。盖茨比童年时期的极度贫困，以及小说中尼克称之为“灰烬谷”（27；第二章）的垃圾场，被描绘成富人和名人生活之外的唯一选择，都印证了这一点。小说中，通过交替描写尼克及其圈子的精彩世界，以及威尔逊一家、麦基一家、默特尔的妹妹凯瑟琳，以及盖茨比那些游手好闲、庸俗不堪的派对宾客，还有“在黄昏时分徘徊在窗前……浪费着生命中最美好时光的贫穷年轻职员”（62；第三章），不断强化着我们对贫富对比的感知。

A simple “no,” the obvious “right” answer from an abstract moral perspective, does not adequately respond to the complexities of the question, given the wretched poverty of Gatsby’s childhood and the novel’s portrayal of the dumping ground Nick refers to as the “valley of ashes” (27; ch. 2) as the only alternative to the life lived by the rich and famous. Our perception of the contrast between wealth and poverty is reinforced throughout the novel by alternating descriptions of, on the one hand, the exciting world of Nick and his crowd and, on the other hand, the dreary world of the Wilsons, the McKees, Myrtle’s sister Catherine, and such random characters as Gatsby’s freeloading, vulgar party guests and the “poor young clerks who loitered in front of windows … in the dusk, wasting the most poignant moments of night and life” (62; ch. 3).

盖茨比的手段不能为目的辩护这一简单的结论，对尼克来说也站不住脚。但叙述者也并非简单地认为盖茨比的手段可以为目的辩护。正如我们所见，正是通过尼克，我们才了解到盖茨比阴暗的一面：他的犯罪活动、他对黛西的欺骗、他虚构的身份、他与沃尔夫希姆的交往，以及他对除黛西和他自己之外任何人的福祉都漠不关心。然而，尼克同时也是盖茨比的主要辩护者，例如，他曾多次“重新完全信任盖茨比”（136；第七章）。仅仅因为盖茨比承认他在牛津的经历是第一次世界大战后美国士兵政府安排的，这算是对现实做出了一点让步。而尼克则得出结论，盖茨比“比他那帮人加起来都强”（162页；第八章）。事实上，尼克对主人公热情而频繁的辩护，总体上应该会让我们同情盖茨比，即便他性格中阴暗的一面提醒我们，盖茨比并非正义凛然的白帽英雄。也就是说，尼克并没有回答小说提出的问题，也没有暗示盖茨比的手段可以为他的目的辩护，但他仍然认为盖茨比是他在美国东部遇到的唯一一个“最终还算不错”的人（6页；第一章）。

The simple conclusion that Gatsby’s ends do not justify his means does not work for Nick either. But neither does the narrator simply conclude that Gatsby’s ends do justify his means. As we have seen, it’s through Nick that we learn about Gatsby’s dark side: his criminal activities, his deception of Daisy, his invented identity, his association with Wolfsheim, and his insensitivity to the welfare of anyone but Daisy and himself. Yet it’s Nick who is also Gatsby’s chief defender, who experiences, for example, one of many “renewals of complete faith in him” (136; ch. 7) simply because Gatsby makes a small concession to reality by admitting that his Oxford experience was provided by a government arrangement for American soldiers after World War I. And it’s Nick who concludes that Gatsby is “worth the whole damn bunch [of Nick’s crowd] put together” (162; ch. 8). In fact, Nick’s warm and frequent defense of the protagonist should, on the whole, tend to elicit our sympathy for Gatsby, even while the dark side of his characterization reminds us that Gatsby is not one of the good guys in the white hats. That is, without answering the question the novel poses, without suggesting that Gatsby’s ends justify his means, Nick nevertheless sees Gatsby as the only person he met in the East who “turned out all right at the end” (6; ch. 1).

鉴于尼克对盖茨比的了解，他为何最终会以如此片面的方式解读盖茨比？尼克在《了不起的盖茨比》中频繁地“重拾完全的信念”（136；第七章），这种热情洋溢的语气表明，如同小说中的许多其他人物一样，尼克将自己的渴望投射到了​​盖茨比身上。三十岁的尼克仍在依靠父亲的资助，努力寻找人生的方向，因此，他渴望相信生活依然充满希望，因为他害怕现实并非如此，这并不奇怪。他害怕自己未来所剩无几，正如他所说，“单身男士名单越来越短，热情也越来越少，头发也越来越稀疏”（143；第七章）。在家乡经历了一段失败的恋情，在纽约又经历了一段失败的恋情之后，尼克仍然渴望相信爱情的可能依然存在。在纽约度过的这个夏天——他一系列冒险经历中的最新一次——以灾难告终后，尼克仍然渴望相信盖茨比身上所展现的那种希望能够实现：一个迷茫的年轻人也能像盖茨比那样获得惊人的财富，也能如此深爱一个女人，也能对未来充满如此乐观。事实上，正如我们在小说后半部分所看到的，尼克对盖茨比投入了如此深厚的感情，以至于他毫不犹豫地，尽管自己成长于保守的家庭，却仍然促成了盖茨比与黛西——尼克自己的亲戚——的婚外情。

Why should Nick finally interpret Gatsby in such a one-sided manner, given the knowledge he has of him? The enthusiastic tone of Nick’s frequent “renewals of complete faith” (136; ch. 7) in Gatsby suggests that, like so many other characters in the novel, Nick projects his own desires onto Gatsby. At the age of 30, and still being financed by his father while he tries to figure out what he should do with himself, it is not surprising that Nick wants to believe life still holds promise because he is afraid that it doesn’t. He fears that all he has to look forward to is, as he puts it, “a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair” (143; ch. 7). With one failed romance back home and one in New York, Nick wants to believe that the possibility of romance still exists. With his summer in New York – his latest in a series of adventures – having ended in disaster, he wants to believe in the possibility of fulfilled hope he sees in Gatsby: hope that a young man at loose ends can make the kind of outrageous financial success of himself that Gatsby has made, can fall so completely in love with a woman, and can feel so optimistic about the future. Indeed, as we see throughout the second half of the novel, Nick is so emotionally invested in Gatsby that, without hesitation and despite his own conservative upbringing, he facilitates Gatsby’s adulterous affair with Daisy, Nick’s own relative.

尼克倾向于将自己的欲望投射到他对盖茨比的解读中，这似乎不可避免，也显得顺理成章，因为他和我们对主人公的体验都发生在一个充满未解之谜、矛盾和多种可能解读的背景之中。因此，整部小说的情感冲击力促使我们像尼克一样，将自身的意义投射到小说的世界中，以此来解读它。

Nick’s tendency to project his own desire into his interpretation of Gatsby seems unavoidable and feels natural given that his, and our, experience of the protagonist develops within a setting that is itself full of unanswered questions, contradictions, and multiple possible interpretations. The affective thrust of the novel as a whole thus invites us to project, like Nick, our own meanings onto the world of the novel in order to interpret it at all.

即使列出文本中所有不确定之处的最简短清单，也会包括以下这些未解之谜，我的学生经常对此感到困惑。黛西为什么在收到盖茨比从欧洲寄来的信后就嫁给了汤姆？盖茨比在黛西婚礼后不到三个月就回到了路易斯维尔，他的信里不是已经告诉她他很快就会回来吗？考虑到黛西在婚礼前夜还不想嫁给他，为什么结婚仅仅三个月后，她就“如此恨她的丈夫”（81；第四章）？鉴于汤姆长期以来的不忠，这对夫妇频繁的……汤姆和黛西多次搬迁，而且显然对婚姻不满，是什么让他们的婚姻维系至今？盖茨比和黛西重逢后的关系如何？（菲茨杰拉德写道，他本人“对盖茨比和黛西从重逢到悲剧发生这段时间的情感关系，既无感觉也无所知”[ 《书信集》 341-42页]。）尼克与他留在故乡的年轻女子之间究竟有着怎样的故事？尼克和乔丹对彼此的真实感受是什么？乔丹是怎样一个人？鉴于小说明显否定了汤姆的性别歧视和种族歧视态度，我们又该如何看待尼克那些带有性别歧视和种族歧视色彩的言论呢？文本对此只字未提，似乎在引导我们接受这些言论。 （例如，参见第三章第63页尼克的评论：“女人的不诚实，你永远不会真正责怪她”，以及第四章第73页他把豪华轿车里的三个黑人称为“两块钱加一个妞”，并“看着他们眼珠子傲慢地朝他和盖茨比转过来，哈哈大笑”。）鉴于文本对穷人和富人都有着不讨喜的刻画，这部小说究竟是反精英主义，还是仅仅是厌世？那些“夜里萦绕在盖茨比床上的怪诞而奇特的想法”（第105页；第六章）究竟是什么？（尼克没有告诉我们。）这里以及其他地方所指的“想法”究竟是哪种定义：“概念”、“愿景”、“矫揉造作的风格或言辞”，还是“自恋的观点”？我们应该如何理解 TJ Eckleburg 医生的眼睛呢？它们在小说意象中占据着如此重要的地位，但又可以被解读为代表着许多不同的想法。

Even the briefest list of the text’s indeterminacies would include the following unanswered questions, which my students frequently find disturbing. Why does Daisy marry Tom after receiving Gatsby’s letter from Europe? As Gatsby returned to Louisville within three months of Daisy’s wedding, didn’t his letter tell her that she could expect him soon? Why is Daisy “so mad about her husband” (81; ch. 4) after only three months of marriage, given that she didn’t want to marry him the night before the wedding? Given Tom’s chronic infidelity, the couple’s frequent relocations, and their apparent dissatisfaction with the marriage, what keeps Tom and Daisy together? What is Gatsby and Daisy’s relationship like after their reunion? (Fitzgerald wrote that he, himself, “had no feeling about or knowledge of … the emotional relations between Gatsby and Daisy from the time of their reunion to the catastrophe” [Letters 341–42].) What’s the real story of Nick’s relationship with the young woman he left behind in his hometown? How do Nick and Jordan really feel about each other? What kind of person is Jordan? Given the novel’s obvious rejection of Tom’s sexist and racist attitudes, what are we to make of Nick’s sexist and racist remarks, which the text offers without comment and seems to invite us to accept? (See, for example, Nick’s remark in chapter 3, page 63, that “[d]ishonesty in a woman is a thing you never blame deeply” and his reference in chapter 4, page 73, to three black characters in a limousine as “two bucks and a girl” at whom he “laughed aloud as the yolks of their eyeballs rolled toward [Gatsby and him] in haughty rivalry.”) Given the text’s unflattering portraits of the poor as well as the rich, is the novel anti-elitist or merely misanthropic? What are the “grotesque and fantastic conceits” that “haunted [Gatsby] in his bed at night” (105; ch. 6)? (Nick doesn’t tell us.) And which definition of conceits is operating here and elsewhere: “concepts,” “visions,” “affectations of style or speech,” or “self-flattering opinions”? What are we to make of the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg, which hold such a prominent position in the novel’s imagery but could be taken to represent so many different ideas?

事实上，T·J·埃克尔伯格医生的眼睛只是小说中众多含义模糊的意象之一。小说中充斥着大量含糊不清、引人遐想的描写，鼓励读者在解读这些意象时投射出自己的理解。例如，“淡金色的气味”或“闪闪发光的气味”（第5章，第96页）究竟是什么意思？“一丝希望”是“潮湿的”（第2章，第29页）又意味着什么？我们应该如何理解盖茨比的“蓝色花园”（第3章，第43页）或黛西脸颊上“像一抹蓝色颜料”的头发（第5章，第90页）？黛西的声音“在酷热中挣扎”，是如何“将无意义的话语塑造成某种形态”（第7章，第125页）的？而这些形态又是如何产生的？此外，尼克的描述常常通过频繁使用“无法定义”、“无法沟通”、“难以言说”、“难以形容”和“无法解释”等词语来承认自身无法提供具体细节，这种富有感染力的措辞在诸如“盖茨比脸上再次浮现出那种既陌生又熟悉的神情”（141页；第七章）这样的句子中达到了歧义的极致。如果尼克无法定义、沟通、表达或解释他心中的所思所想，那么读者就必须自行想象他的意思，而文本中的这些空白则引导我们投射自身的经验和欲望，从而构建意义。

The eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg are, in fact, only one of many ambiguous images in a novel dense with vague, evocative descriptions that encourage readers to project their own meanings in interpreting them. For example, what is a “pale gold odor” or a “sparkling odor” (96; ch. 5)? What does it mean that a “gleam of hope” is “damp” (29; ch. 2)? What should we make of Gatsby’s “blue gardens” (43; ch. 3) or the hair that lies across Daisy’s cheek “like a dash of blue paint” (90; ch. 5)? How can Daisy’s voice, “struggl[ing] through the heat,” “moul[d] its senselessness into forms” (125; ch. 7), and what forms are thus produced? In addition, Nick’s descriptions often acknowledge their own inability to provide concrete, specific details by their frequent use of the words indefinable, uncommunicable, unutterable, ineffable, and inexplicable, an evocative diction that reaches the height of its ambiguity in such phrases as “[t]hat unfamiliar yet recognizable look was back again in Gatsby’s face” (141; ch. 7). If Nick can’t define, communicate, utter, or explain what he has in mind, then readers must imagine for themselves what he means, and such gaps in the text invite us to project our own experience and desires in order to make meaning.

《了不起的盖茨比》能够轻易地支撑这本教科书中收录的众多不同理论解读，这恰恰证明了这部小说的不确定性。简而言之，这部小说几乎没有什么确定的意义，以至于如果我们不将自身的信仰和欲望投射到文本上，那么留给我们的唯一解释就只有…… 《了不起的盖茨比》展现了一个道德模糊的世界中意义的不确定性。虽然我认为这是对这部小说的一种有益解读，但包括我在内的大多数读者都渴望得到比这种解读更明确的答案。值得注意的是，在这种背景下，评论界对杰伊·盖茨比的反应呈现出一种趋势。尽管小说对主人公的刻画具有两面性，但相当一部分评论家仍将盖茨比塑造成一位浪漫英雄，如下例所示。马里乌斯·贝利认为，盖茨比“充满抱负和善良”（25）；他是“美国浪漫英雄的化身”（14），代表着“精神抵抗的力量”以及“免受庸俗和低级趣味最终侵蚀”的“免疫力”（13）。杰弗里·哈特认同盖茨比是“美国英雄的代表人物”（34），查尔斯·C·纳什则认为“爱默生的‘私人的无限性’”在杰伊·盖茨比身上得到了“最好的体现，对他而言，一切皆有可能”（23）。安德鲁·狄龙认为盖茨比身上蕴含着一种“神圣的能量”（61），肯特·卡特赖特则说盖茨比的“梦想……使他高尚”（229）。汤姆·伯纳姆认为，盖茨比“在周围的腐败环境中幸存下来，保持了健全完整的品格”（105）。同样，罗斯·艾德琳·加洛也认为盖茨比“至死都保持着纯真”（43），或者正如安德烈·勒沃所说，盖茨比从未失去他“根本的正直，他精神的完整性”（144）。即使主人公的阴暗面被提及，也都被原谅了。正如卡特赖特所言，“盖茨比既可以是罪犯，也可以是浪漫英雄，因为这本书为他塑造了一个超越世俗、充满远见的道德标准，而他的一生也印证了这一点”（232）。或者，正如安德鲁·狄龙总结他所看到的主人公世俗与精神的融合时所说，盖茨比是“一位感性的圣人”（50）。

That The Great Gatsby easily supports the many different theoretical readings contained in this textbook is a testimony to the novel’s indeterminacy. In short, there is so little determinate meaning in the novel that if we don’t project our own beliefs and desires onto the text, the only interpretation left us would be that The Great Gatsby portrays the indeterminacy of meaning in a morally ambiguous world. While I think that’s a useful interpretation of the novel, most readers, including myself, desire more closure than such an interpretation provides. It is interesting to note, in this context, a trend in critical response to Jay Gatsby. Despite the novel’s two-sided characterization of the title character, a significant proportion of critical response casts Gatsby as a romantic hero, as we see in the following examples. According to Marius Bewley, Gatsby is “all aspiration and goodness” (25); he’s “an heroic personification of the American romantic hero” (14) who represents “the energy of the spirit’s resistance” and “immunity to the final contamination” of “cheapness and vulgarity” (13). Jeffrey Hart agrees that Gatsby is “a representative American hero” (34), and Charles C. Nash claims that “Emerson’s ‘Infinitude of the Private Man’” is “best represented by Jay Gatsby, for whom all things are possible” (23). Andrew Dillon believes Gatsby is imbued with a “sacred energy” (61), and Kent Cartwright says that Gatsby’s “dream … ennobles him” (229). For Tom Burnam, Gatsby “survives sound and whole in character, uncorrupted by the corruption which surrounded him” (105). Similarly, Rose Adrienne Gallo believes that Gatsby “maintained his innocence” to the end (43), or, as André Le Vot puts it, Gatsby never loses his “fundamental integrity, his spiritual intactness” (144). Even when the protagonist’s darker side is acknowledged, it is excused. As Cartwright argues, “Gatsby can be both criminal and romantic hero because the book creates for him a visionary moral standard that transcends the conventional and that his life affirms” (232). Or as Andrew Dillon sums up what he sees as the protagonist’s merger of worldliness and spirituality, Gatsby is “a sensual saint” (50).5

当然，尼克对盖茨比的辩护鼓励读者对主人公产生同情。然而，考虑到尼克本人提供的关于盖茨比的负面信息的数量和种类，一些其他因素可能影响了那些只看到盖茨比优点的评论家的反应。换句话说，尽管尼克显然希望我们像他那样，将盖茨比从对盖茨比世界的谴责中排除出去，但叙述者仍然提供了足够的信息，使我们对他所倡导的对主人公的同情判断产生质疑。事实上，关于尼克是否是一个可靠的叙述者的争议，恰恰凸显了小说不确定性的这一层面。6

Of course, Nick’s defense of Gatsby encourages readers to respond sympathetically to the protagonist. However, given the amount and kind of negative data about Gatsby that Nick himself provides, some additional factors probably influenced the response of those critics who see only the good in Gatsby. In other words, although Nick clearly wants us to exempt Gatsby, as he does, from our condemnation of Gatsby’s world, the narrator nevertheless provides us with more than enough data to problematize the sympathetic judgment of the protagonist he promotes. In fact, the critical controversy over whether or not Nick is a reliable narrator underscores this dimension of the novel’s indeterminacy.6

对于这种忽略小说中诸多素材、只关注盖茨比人格塑造中令人钦佩之处的评论趋势，一种可能的解释是，主人公触动了许多读者共同拥有的某种个人信念或渴望，促使他们以完全正面的眼光看待盖茨比。事实上，我发现大多数将盖茨比理想化的评论家，也同样理想化了他们眼中美国未受腐蚀的过去，他们认为盖茨比正是这种过去的化身。在这些读者眼中，盖茨比代表着一个纯洁无瑕的美国，而他们认为，这个美国正是被像迈耶·沃尔夫希姆和汤姆·布坎南这样的人的自私和庸俗所摧毁的。

One possible explanation for a critical trend that ignores so much material in the novel, focusing only on the admirable elements in Gatsby’s characterization, is that the protagonist taps some personal belief or desire that many readers have in common and that encourages them to see Gatsby in a wholly positive light. And indeed, I found that most of the critics who idealize Gatsby also idealize what they see as America’s uncorrupted past, which they believe Gatsby represents. For these readers, Gatsby stands for a pristine America that was destroyed, as they believe he was, by the selfishness and vulgarity of people like Meyer Wolfsheim and Tom Buchanan.

例如，理查德·蔡斯认为盖茨比是“早期田园理想”的一部分，因为他与纳蒂·邦波、哈克·芬和伊什梅尔一样，都秉持着“纯真、逃离和纯粹个人行为准则的理想”（301）。同样，马里乌斯·比尤利认为，像戴维·克罗克特在1836年描述的那种“在黎明中做梦、歌唱着迎接清晨的边疆年轻花花公子”，是“盖茨比的先驱。正是由于这种传统的美国血统，盖茨比的浪漫主义才超越了爵士时代有限的魅力”（128）。因此，盖茨比被视为“美国梦的真正继承人”（比尤利 128），在这个梦想被道德荒漠的影响所腐蚀之前，他依然拥有着这份纯真，而这片荒漠的边界仍在不断向美国社会的核心延伸。的确，有人可能会认为，美国“坚韧不拔的个人主义”意识形态——其变体包括孤独者、不墨守成规者和特立独行者等类型——使许多读者倾向于只看到盖茨比性格中令人钦佩的一面。

Richard Chase, for example, sees Gatsby as part of “an earlier pastoral ideal,” in that he shares, with Natty Bumppo, Huck Finn, and Ishmael, an “ideal of innocence, escape, and the purely personal code of conduct” (301). Similarly, Marius Bewley argues that the “young dandy of the frontier, dreaming in the dawn and singing to the morning,” such as that described by Davy Crockett in 1836, “is a progenitor of Gatsby. It is because of such a traditional American ancestry that Gatsby’s romanticism transcends the limiting glamor of the Jazz Age” (128). Thus, Gatsby is seen as “the true heir of the American dream” (Bewley 128) before that dream was corrupted by the influence of the moral wasteland that continues to extend its borders farther into the core of American society. Indeed, one might argue that the American ideology of the “rugged individual” – variations of which include, among other types, the loner, the nonconformist, and the maverick – predispose many readers to see only the admirable side of Gatsby’s characterization.

大多数不将小说中爵士时代的世界与美国历史上早期一段纯洁时期进行对比的评论家，都以非理想化的视角解读盖茨比。例如，埃德温·福塞尔认为，这部小说体现了菲茨杰拉德对美国梦以及作为美国代表人物的杰伊·盖茨比的刻意而尖锐的批判。马修·布鲁科利和A·E·戴森都没有将盖茨比理想化，他们和福塞尔一样，都认为主人公并没有超越他所处世界的腐败，而是身处其中。换句话说，许多评论家似乎很大程度上是根据他们自身对美国历史的假设来解读盖茨比的。或许正是因为相信美国曾经纯洁无瑕，才使得盖茨比成为那段如今已一去不复返的纯洁过去的代表。总之，那些将盖茨比理想化的批评家们完全忽略或积极地为盖茨比的阴暗面开脱，这表明，至少当文本强烈地引导我们投射自己的信念和欲望时，这种投射的力量比文本提供的解释修正要强大得多。

Most of those critics who do not contrast the Jazz Age world of the novel with an earlier, pristine period of American history interpret Gatsby in nonidealized terms. Edwin Fussell, for example, believes that the novel represents Fitzgerald’s deliberate and scathing criticism of the American dream and of Jay Gatsby, the representative American. Neither Matthew Bruccoli nor A. E. Dyson idealizes Gatsby, and, like Fussell, they recognize that the protagonist does not transcend the corruption of the world he lives in: rather, he shares it. In other words, many critics seem to interpret Gatsby largely according to their own assumptions about America’s past. Perhaps the belief that America was once uncorrupted contributes to the vision of Gatsby as the representative of that pristine past, now gone forever. In any case, the degree to which the critics who idealize Gatsby completely ignore or actively excuse Gatsby’s darker side suggests that the projection of our own beliefs and desires, at least when powerfully invited by the text, is stronger than the correctives to interpretation the text provides.

许多评论家对小说中提供的修正——关于盖茨比的负面信息——的抵触情绪，也体现在文本中大量提及的那些毫无意义的阅读材料上，这些材料要么无人阅读，要么未读完，未能将自身的现实强加于读者。例如，盖茨比书房里的书籍未经裁切，表明它们从未被人翻阅过。乔丹读给汤姆·布坎南听的杂志故事也未完结，“敬请期待下一期”（22；第一章），显然并没有像预期的那样让她感到愉悦，因为她读的时候语气“低沉而平静”（22；第一章）。尼克在等待汤姆和默特尔从公寓卧室出来时读的那本流行小说，对他来说“毫无意义”（34；第二章）。盖茨比从海外写给黛西的信，意在阻止她嫁给汤姆，却彻底失败，在她洗澡时碎裂了。尼克写给沃尔夫希姆的信，恳求他参加盖茨比的葬礼，也同样没有达到目的。尽管盖茨比收集了大量关于布坎南夫妇的剪报，但他“对汤姆却知之甚少”（84页；第四章）。尼克买了一整套关于银行业务的书籍，希望能从中学习债券交易，但这对他毫无用处：他向盖茨比坦白自己赚不到多少钱（87页；第五章），最终在夏末回到明尼苏达州时辞掉了工作。盖茨比童年时在关于霍帕隆·卡西迪（美国西部“好人”的象征）的书后写下的自我提升“计划”，暗示着他将致力于努力工作和过上正直的生活，然而盖茨比长大后却成了罪犯。讽刺的是，唯一真正起到预期作用的文本却毫无作用：汤姆在读《有色帝国的崛起》之前就已经是个种族主义者，所以这本书只不过是强化了他原有的种族主义态度而已。

The resistance of many critics to the correctives provided by the novel – the negative data about Gatsby – is mirrored in the text’s numerous references to reading materials that don’t accomplish anything, that remain unread or unfinished, that fail to impose their reality on their readers. For example, the books in Gatsby’s library are uncut, revealing that no one ever has read them. The magazine story Jordan reads to Tom Buchanan is unfinished, “to be continued in our very next issue” (22; ch. 1), and apparently doesn’t succeed in entertaining her as it is supposed to do, for she reads it in a “murmurous and uninflected” tone (22; ch. 1). The popular novel Nick reads while waiting for Tom and Myrtle to emerge from the bedroom of their apartment “didn’t make any sense” to him (34; ch. 2). Gatsby’s letter to Daisy from overseas, which was intended to prevent her marriage to Tom, fails its mission entirely and crumbles in her bath. Neither does Nick’s letter to Wolfsheim, entreating him to attend Gatsby’s funeral, achieve its purpose. Gatsby has a whole collection of newspaper clippings about the Buchanans despite which “he doesn’t know very much about Tom” (84; ch. 4). Nick has bought a whole set of books on banking to help him learn the bond business, but they do him no good: he admits to Gatsby that he’s not making much money (87; ch. 5), and he winds up quitting his job when he returns to Minnesota at the end of the summer. Gatsby’s boyhood “schedule” for self-improvement, which he wrote at the back of his book on Hopalong Cassidy, a Western icon of the American “good guy,” implies a future dedicated to hard work and clean living, yet Gatsby grew up to be a criminal. And ironically, the only text that does the job for which it is intended doesn’t have any job to do: Tom is a bigot long before he reads The Rise of the Coloured Empires, so the book merely confirms the racist attitude he already has.

正如这些例子所示，小说向我们展示了文本实现其预期目的的力量是多么有限。即使文本本身具有独立于读者的意义，这种意义也往往无法与我们投射的意义相抗衡。在《了不起的盖茨比》这样一部充满不确定性的小说中，读者投射在意义建构中的作用尤为突出，这体现在小说的主题内容以及文本所倡导的积极阅读体验中。因此，菲茨杰拉德的小说阐释了一种“阅读即投射”的理论，因为它同时邀请我们将自身的信念和欲望投射到文本之上。正如许多对这部小说的评论所表明的那样，至少就《了不起的盖茨比》而言，这种阅读理论似乎相当准确。

As these examples illustrate, the novel shows us what little power texts have to achieve their intended purposes. Even if texts do have meaning independent of readers, that meaning often cannot compete with the meanings we project. In a novel with the degree of indeterminacy we experience in The Great Gatsby, the power of readers’ projections in the creation of meaning is especially foregrounded, both in the novel’s thematic content and in the active reading experience the text promotes. Thus, Fitzgerald’s novel illustrates a theory of reading-as-projection as it simultaneously invites us to project our beliefs and desires onto the text. And as a good deal of critical response to the novel suggests, this theory of reading, at least in terms of The Great Gatsby, seems quite accurate.

拓展练习题：读者反应方法在其他文学作品中的应用

Questions for further practice: reader-response approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用读者反应批评方法来解读它们所指的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use reader-response criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1当读者阅读凯特·肖邦的《暴风雨》（1898）的五个章节时，故事的不确定性（例如，没有明确解释或可能有多种含义的动作、人物和意象）会产生怎样的阅读体验？这种阅读体验是如何体现在故事的主题内容中的（例如，人物“解读”或解码其他人物或情境）？

1 As the reader moves through each of the five sections of Kate Chopin’s “The Storm” (1898), what reading experience is produced by the story’s indeterminacy (for example, actions, characters, and images that are not clearly explained or that could have multiple meanings)? How is this reading experience reflected in the story’s thematic content (for example, characters “reading,” or decoding, other characters or situations)?

2对罗伯特·海登的《那些冬日的星期天》（1975 年）或你想要使用的任何其他诗歌进行逐行分析，可以揭示出诗歌是如何将读者的反应构建成一个随时间发生的事件的？

2 What does a line-by-line analysis of Robert Hayden’s “Those Winter Sundays” (1975), or any other poem you would like to use, reveal about the ways in which the poem structures the reader’s response as an event that occurs in time?

3约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》（1902 年）的评论史揭示了分析这部小说的阐释群体的哪些特点？例如，你可以通过确定所使用的解释策略、这些策略所依据的假设以及由此产生的解读，来区分和分析解释社群。

3 What does the history of critical response to Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness (1902) reveal about the interpretive communities that have analyzed the novel? You might, for example, differentiate and analyze interpretive communities by determining the interpretive strategies used, the assumptions on which those strategies were based, and the readings that were thereby produced.

4选择一部着重探讨性别、种族和/或社会经济阶层议题的小说——例如托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）——收集学生（或同学、读书会成员）的一系列简短回应。回应应聚焦于小说中（由你选择）明确突出这些议题的章节。利用这些书面回应以及小组讨论的内容，分析个人的性别、种族和/或社会经济背景与其对小说中性别、种族和/或社会经济背景相关表述的反应之间可能存在的关联。尽管这项练习属于推测性而非科学性，但你能从中得出哪些值得在文学教学中进行实验性实践的推论呢？

4 Using a narrative with a strong focus on issues of gender, race, and/or socioeconomic class – for example, Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) – collect a series of brief response statements from your students (or classmates or bookclub members). Response statements should focus on sections of the narrative (selected by you) in which these issues are clearly foregrounded. Use these written responses and what you learn from group discussions to analyze the possible relationships between one’s own gender, race, and/or socioeconomic background and one’s responses to the narrative’s representations of gender, race, and/or socioeconomic background. Although this exercise is speculative rather than scientific, what inferences can you derive from it that might be worth putting into experimental practice in the teaching of literature?

5选择一本你小时候很喜欢（或很讨厌）但多年未重读的书籍。凭借记忆以及任何可用的日记、信件或其他类似资料，概括你记忆中的故事情节，并从你初次接触这本书的角度出发，写一篇详尽的感想，包括当时帮助你理解这本书的个人经历和人际关系。现在，再次阅读这本书，并写一篇你现在的感想。通过对比你两次阅读这本书的感受，一篇分析性感想揭示了主观因素和解读策略在读者理解文本意义过程中所起的作用。你如何运用所学到的知识来改进文学教学？

5 Select a text you loved (or hated) as a youngster but that you haven’t reread in years. Relying on memory and on any diary entries, letters, or the like that you may have available, summarize the story as you remember it, and write a thorough response statement from the perspective of your initial encounter with the book, including the personal experiences and relationships that helped you relate to the book at the time. Now read the book again, and write a current response statement. What does a response-analysis statement, comparing and contrasting your two encounters with the text, reveal about the role of subjective factors and interpretive strategies in the way readers make meaning? How might you apply what you’ve learned to improve the way literature is taught?

笔记

Notes

1例如，读者反应文集通常会收录乔纳森·库勒的《结构主义诗学：结构主义、语言学与文学研究》中的一篇文章，因为库勒对读者如何运用阐释策略来构建意义很感兴趣。然而，库勒的目标是描绘我们所用阐释策略背后的结构，正如结构语言学试图描绘我们所使用语言背后的结构一样。对库勒而言，潜在的结构而非读者才是最终的分析对象，因此我们将在第七章“结构主义批评”中探讨他的著作。

1 For example, reader-response anthologies often include an essay from Jonathan Culler’s Structuralist Poetics: Structuralism, Linguistics and the Study of Literature because of Culler’s interest in the way readers use interpretive strategies to make meaning. However, Culler’s goal is to map the structures that underlie the interpretive strategies we use, just as structural linguistics seeks to map the structures that underlie the languages we speak. For Culler, underlying structures, not readers, are the ultimate objects of analysis, which is why we’ll examine his work in Chapter 7, “Structuralist criticism.”

2这段文字以及“读者的阅读目的会影响其对文章的理解”这一假设，均出自JA Pichert和RC Anderson进行的一项心理学研究。感谢我在大峡谷州立大学的同事Brian White，是他向我展示了如何利用这段文字来教授读者反应理论。

2 This passage, and the hypothesis that the reader’s purpose in reading it will influence his or her perception of the passage, is taken from a psychological study conducted by J. A. Pichert and R. C. Anderson. My thanks to Brian White, my colleague at Grand Valley State University, for showing me how it can be used to teach reader-response theory.

3尽管伊瑟通常被归类为现象学批评家（研究阅读活动，将其视为作者意识与读者意识之间的互动），但他的作品与罗森布拉特的作品有很多共同之处。

3 Although Iser is generally classified as a phenomenological critic (one who studies the activity of reading as an interaction between the author’s consciousness and the reader’s), his work has a good deal in common with that of Rosenblatt.

4詹姆斯·费兰（James Phelan）恰当地将修辞读者反应批评命名为修辞读者反应批评，它或许可以被视为一种更为细致入微、更注重语言学的交互性读者反应理论。顾名思义，修辞读者反应批评分析作者使用的修辞手法（具体的写作策略），这些手法能够引发读者特定的反应。除了费兰的《叙事即修辞》（Narrative as Rhetoric ）之外，还有许多重要的文献可供参考。文本包括韦恩·布斯的《小说修辞学》和彼得·拉比诺维茨的《阅读之前》。（您也会在其他地方看到这些文本被归类为修辞批评或叙事学的例子。）

4 Rhetorical reader-response criticism, aptly named by James Phelan, might be seen as a more nuanced, linguistically attentive form of transactional reader-response theory. As its name implies, rhetorical reader-response criticism analyzes the rhetorical devices (specific writing strategies) authors use that create particular responses in their readers. In addition to Phelan’s Narrative as Rhetoric, key texts include Wayne Booth’s The Rhetoric of Fiction and Peter Rabinowitz’s Before Reading. (You will also see these texts elsewhere categorized as examples of rhetorical criticism or narratology.)

5有关盖茨比的类似解读，请参阅 Chase、Gross、Moore、Stern 和 Trilling 等人的作品。

5 For similar readings of Gatsby, see, for example, Chase, Gross, Moore, Stern, and Trilling.

6认为尼克的观点值得信赖的评论家包括巴克斯特、狄龙和纳什等。而认为叙述者的感知不可信的评论家则包括卡特赖特、钱伯斯和斯克里姆杰等。

6 Critics who believe Nick’s viewpoint is trustworthy include, for example, Baxter, Dillon, and Nash. Critics who believe the narrator’s perceptions cannot be trusted include, for example, Cartwright, Chambers, and Scrimgeour.

7. 结构主义批评

7   Structuralist criticism

当你开始学习结构主义时，首先要习惯的是，“结构”一词的常用含义并不一定意味着结构主义活动。例如，如果你检查一座建筑的物理结构，以确定其是否物理稳定或美观，那么你并非在进行结构主义活动。然而，如果你检查1850年美国城市中所有建筑的物理结构，以发现支配其构成的基本原则，例如机械构造原则或艺术形式原则，那么你就是在进行结构主义活动。同样，如果你检查一座建筑的结构，以发现其构成如何体现特定结构体系的基本原则，你也是在进行结构主义活动。在第一个结构主义活动中，你是在构建一个结构分类体系；在第二个例子中，你是在证明某个具体事物属于某个特定的结构类别。

The first thing you have to get used to when you begin to study structuralism is that common uses of the word structure do not necessarily imply structuralist activity. For example, you are not engaged in structuralist activity if you examine the physical structure of a building to discover if it is physically stable or aesthetically pleasing. However, you are engaged in structuralist activity if you examine the physical structures of all the buildings built in urban America in 1850 to discover the underlying principles that govern their composition, for example, principles of mechanical construction or of artistic form. You are also engaged in structuralist activity if you examine the structure of a single building to discover how its composition demonstrates the underlying principles of a given structural system. In the first example of structuralist activity, you’re generating a structural system of classification; in the second, you’re demonstrating that an individual item belongs to a particular structural class.

在文学研究中，同样的结构主义活动模式也适用。如果你仅仅描述一篇短篇小说的结构来阐释作品的意义或评价其文学价值，那么你并非在进行结构主义活动。然而，如果你分析大量短篇小说的结构，以发现其构成背后的基本原则，例如叙事推进原则（情节事件发生的顺序）或人物塑造原则（每个人物在整个叙事中所扮演的角色），那么你就是在进行结构主义活动。此外，如果你描述一部文学作品的结构，以探究其构成如何体现特定结构体系的基本原则，那么你也是在进行结构主义活动。

In terms of literary study, the same model of structuralist activity holds true. You are not engaged in structuralist activity if you describe the structure of a short story to interpret what the work means or evaluate whether or not it’s good literature. However, you are engaged in structuralist activity if you examine the structure of a large number of short stories to discover the underlying principles that govern their composition, for example, principles of narrative progression (the order in which plot events occur) or of characterization (the functions each character performs in relation to the narrative as a whole). You are also engaged in structuralist activity if you describe the structure of a single literary work to discover how its composition demonstrates the underlying principles of a given structural system.

换言之，结构主义者对单个建筑或单个文学作品（或任何类型的单个现象）本身并不感兴趣，他们关注的是这些个体事物能够揭示哪些关于构成和组织所有同类事物的基础结构的信息。因为结构主义将自身视为一门人文科学，其目标是系统地理解构成所有人类经验乃至所有人类行为和生产的基础结构。正因如此，结构主义不应被视为一个独立的研究领域，而是一种系统化人类经验的方法，被广泛应用于语言学、人类学、社会学、心理学和文学研究等诸多领域。

In other words, structuralists are not interested in individual buildings or individual literary works (or individual phenomena of any kind) except in terms of what those individual items can tell us about the structures that underlie and organize all items of that kind. For structuralism sees itself as a human science whose effort is to understand, in a systematic way, the fundamental structures that underlie all human experience and, therefore, all human behavior and production. For this reason, structuralism shouldn’t be thought of as a field of study. Rather, it’s a method of systematizing human experience that is used in many different fields of study: for example, linguistics, anthropology, sociology, psychology, and literary studies.

在结构主义看来，我们所知的世界由两个基本层面构成——一个可见层面，一个不可见层面。可见世界由所谓的表面现象构成：我们每天观察、参与和互动的所有无数物体、活动和行为。不可见世界则由支撑和组织所有这些现象的结构构成，使我们能够理解它们。例如，英语包含超过一百万个单词，每个单词都可以由不同的说话者以无数种不同的方式发音，从而产生数百万种不同的单词表达方式。那么，以英语为母语的人是如何掌握如此庞大的语言资源，并在相当小的年纪就达到相当高的沟通水平，并进行有效交流的呢？

For structuralism, the world as we know it consists of two fundamental levels – one visible, the other invisible. The visible world consists of what might be called surface phenomena: all the countless objects, activities, and behaviors we observe, participate in, and interact with every day. The invisible world consists of the structures that underlie and organize all of these phenomena so that we can make sense of them. For example, the English language consists of over a million words, each of which can be pronounced in any number of different ways by different speakers, resulting in millions of different utterances of individual words. How is it possible that native speakers of English master enough of this overwhelming collection of linguistic items to communicate effectively with one another at a rather advanced level of sophistication and at a rather early age?

答案其实很简单：尽管语言表面现象千差万别（包括单词及其各种不同的发音方式），但所有这些词汇背后都隐藏着一个相对简单的结构，而我们掌握的正是这个结构。英语词汇的结构大约由31个音素（母语使用者能够识别并赋予意义的基本语音单位）及其组合规则构成。我们大多数人并不了解这些音素，也无法描述它们的组合规则，但我们运用英语词汇的能力表明，我们已经无意识地内化了这些结构。同样，我们构建简单句的能力也取决于我们对主谓宾语法结构的内化，无论我们是否意识到这一点。如果没有一个结构系统来规范交流，我们就根本无法使用语言。类似地，如果没有那些使我们能够组织和理解自然界的结构原则，我们五官所获取的信息将会是庞杂而毫无意义的。无论我们是否意识到，结构原则使我们能够区分蔬菜（它们生长在土壤中；它们会繁殖；它们可以食用）和石头（它们不会生长；它们不会繁殖；它们不能食用），以及所有其他种类的物质。结构原则也使我们能够区分特定领域内的不同类别，例如，我们可以区分具有药用价值的植物、具有有害价值的植物和具有中性价值的植物。

The answer is fairly simple: while there are millions of individual linguistic surface phenomena (individual words and all the different ways people pronounce them), there is a relatively simple structure underlying all these words, and it is that structure we master. The structure of English vocabulary consists of approximately 31 phonemes (fundamental units of sound recognized as meaningful by native speakers of a language) and the rules of their combination. Most of us are not aware of these phonemes and could not describe the rules of their combination, but our ability to use English vocabulary demonstrates that we have unconsciously internalized these structures. Similarly, our ability to construct simple sentences depends on our internalization, whether or not we are aware of it, of the grammatical structure subject-verb-object. Without a structural system to govern communication, we would have no language at all. Analogously, without the structuring principles that allow us to organize and understand the natural world, the data provided by our five senses would be overwhelming and meaningless. Structuring principles, whether or not we are aware of them, allow us, for example, to differentiate vegetables (they grow in soil; they reproduce; they’re edible) from stones (they don’t grow; they don’t reproduce; they’re not edible) and from all other kinds of physical matter. Structuring principles also allow us to differentiate among groups within a given domain, for example, we might differentiate plant life with medicinal properties from plant life with harmful properties from plant life with neutral properties.

正如这些例子所示，我们所生活的世界由无数的事件和物体构成，也就是无数的表面现象。然而，支撑和组织这些现象的结构却相对较少。如果没有这些结构，我们的世界将会一片混乱。

As these examples illustrate, the world we live in consists of innumerable events and objects, that is, innumerable surface phenomena. However, the structures that underlie and organize these phenomena are relatively few. Without these structures our world would be chaos.

这些结构从何而来？结构主义者认为它们是由人类思维产生的，而人类思维被视为一种结构化机制。这是一个重要且激进的观点，因为它意味着我们所看到的秩序是我们强加于世界的秩序。我们对世界的理解并非源于我们对世界中已存在结构的感知。我们自认为感知到的那些结构，实际上是人类意识中固有的（与生俱来的）结构。我们将这些概念投射到现实世界，以便能够应对现实世界。这并非意味着不存在客观现实；而是事实太多，若没有概念体系来限制和组织它们，我们就无法感知。而这些概念体系源于人类意识。因此，结构主义将自身视为一门研究人类的科学，因为它致力于发现世界表面现象背后的结构——无论我们将这些现象置于数学、生物学、语言学、宗教、心理学还是文学等领域——其目的都在于探索人类意识的内在结构。

Where do these structures come from? Structuralists believe they are generated by the human mind, which is thought of as a structuring mechanism. This is an important and radical idea because it means that the order we see in the world is the order we impose on it. Our understanding of the world does not result from our perception of structures that exist in the world. The structures we think we perceive in the world are actually innate (inborn) structures of human consciousness, which we project onto the world in order to be able to deal with the world. It’s not that there is no factual reality; it’s that there are too many facts to be perceived without conceptual systems to limit and organize them. And those conceptual systems originate within human consciousness. Thus, structuralism sees itself as a science of humankind, for its efforts to discover the structures that underlie the world’s surface phenomena – whether we place those phenomena, for example, in the domain of mathematics, biology, linguistics, religion, psychology, or literature – imply an effort to discover something about the innate structures of human consciousness.

在深入探讨之前，我们应该花点时间思考一下结构主义是如何定义“结构”一词的。首先，正如我们之前提到的，结构并非物理实体；它们是我们用来组织和理解物理实体的概念框架。结构是指任何具有以下三个属性的概念系统：（1）整体性，（2）可转换性，以及（3）自调节性。整体性意味着系统作为一个整体运作；它不仅仅是独立元素的集合。整体不同于部分之和，因为各个部分协同作用会创造出新的事物。以物理例子为例，水是一个整体，它不同于其组成部分（氢和氧）。可转换性意味着系统并非静态的；它是动态的，能够发生变化。系统不仅仅是一个结构（名词）；它还能构建新的事物（动词）。换句话说，新的物质总是在被系统构建。例如，语言作为一个结构系统，能够将其基本组成部分（音素）转化为新的话语（词和句子）。自我调节意味着结构所能进行的转变永远不会超出其自身的结构系统。转变所产生的要素（例如，新的语言表达）始终属于该系统，并遵循其规律。

Before we go any further, we should take a moment to consider how structuralism defines the word structure. First of all, as we noted earlier, structures aren’t physical entities; they’re conceptual frameworks that we use to organize and understand physical entities. A structure is any conceptual system that has the following three properties: (1) wholeness, (2) transformation, and (3) self-regulation. Wholeness simply means that the system functions as a unit; it’s not merely a collection of independent items. The whole is different from the sum of its parts because the parts working together create something new. To use a physical example, water is a whole that is different from its component parts (hydrogen and oxygen). Transformation means that the system is not static; it’s dynamic, capable of change. The system is not merely a structure (a noun); it also structures (a verb). In other words, new material is always being structured by the system. For example, language, a structural system, is capable of transforming its basic components (phonemes) into new utterances (words and sentences). Self-regulation means that the transformations of which a structure is capable never lead beyond its own structural system. The elements engendered by transformations (for example, new linguistic utterances) always belong to the system and obey its laws.

结构主义认为，所有表面现象都属于某种结构系统，无论我们是否意识到该系统是什么。表面现象与结构的关系可以用以下简化的图示来说明。

Structuralism assumes that all surface phenomena belong to some structural system, whether or not we are consciously aware of what that system is. The relationship of surface phenomena to structure might be illustrated by the following simplified diagram.

如果从左到右阅读表层现象的行，你会看到一系列独立的语句，例如“狗快乐地奔跑”和“树看起来是绿色的”。然而，如果从上到下阅读整个图表的列，你会发现这些表层现象（包含15个不同的项目，但实际上可能包含更多）受制于一个结构，在这个例子中，该结构仅由三个词类和两条组合规则构成。因此，“狗快乐地奔跑”（或任何遵循相同语法模式的语句）是一个受以下结构支配的表层现象：

If you read the rows of surface phenomena from left to right, you have a list of individual utterances, such as “dog runs happily” and “tree appears green.” However, if you read the columns of the whole diagram from top to bottom, you can see that the surface phenomena, which consist of 15 different items but could consist of many more, are governed by a structure that consists, in this case, of only three parts of speech and two rules of combination. Thus, the utterance “dog runs happily” (or any utterance that follows the same grammatical pattern) is a surface phenomenon governed by the following structure:

主语（名词）+谓语（动词 + 描述词）

Subject (Noun) + Predicate (Verb + Descriptor)

结构的组成部分（在本例中是词类和组合规则）总是比它们所代表的表面现象的数量少，因为它们的目的是组织、分类和简化。

The components of a structure (in this example, parts of speech and rules of combination) are always fewer in number than the surface phenomena they underlie because their purpose is to organize, classify, and simplify.

到目前为止，我举的例子大多来自语言。这并不奇怪，因为语言被认为是人类最基本的结构，也是其他大多数结构赖以存在的基石。事实上，结构语言学领域正是结构主义大部分术语的来源。那么，现在让我们简要了解一下这个领域。

So far, most of my examples have come from language. This is not surprising because language is considered the most fundamental structure of humankind and the one on which most other structures depend. In fact, the field of structural linguistics is the source of most of structuralism’s terminology. So let’s take a brief look at that field now.

结构语言学

Structural linguistics

结构语言学由费迪南·德·索绪尔于1913年至1915年间发展起来，尽管他的著作直到20世纪50年代末才被翻译成英文并普及开来。在索绪尔之前，语言研究主要关注单个词语随时间推移而发生的变化，即历时性研究，并假定词语在某种程度上模仿了它们所指代的对象。索绪尔意识到，我们需要理解的语言并非一系列具有各自历史的单个词语的集合，而是一个词语在特定时间点（即共时性）使用时所构成的结构性关系系统。这就是结构主义的关注点。结构主义并不探究语言（或任何其他现象）的成因或起源，而是探寻语言运作的规则：它关注的是语言的结构。

Structural linguistics was developed by Ferdinand de Saussure between 1913 and 1915, although his work wasn’t translated into English and popularized until the late 1950s. Before Saussure, language was studied in terms of the history of changes in individual words over time, or diachronically, and it was assumed that words somehow imitated the objects for which they stood. Saussure realized that we need to understand language not as a collection of individual words with individual histories but as a structural system of relationships among words as they are used at a given point in time, or synchronically. This is the structuralist focus. Structuralism doesn’t look for the causes or origins of language (or of any other phenomenon). It looks for the rules that underlie language and govern how it functions: it looks for the structure.

为了区分支配语言的结构和构成语言表层的数百万个个体话语，索绪尔将语言的结构称为“ langue”（法语中“语言”一词），将我们说话时产生的个体话语称为“parole ”（法语中“言语”一词）。当然，对于结构主义者而言，“langue”才是恰当的研究对象；“parole”的意义仅在于它揭示了“langue”。研究文学的结构主义者也使用这些术语：正如我们稍后将看到的，结构主义批评家探寻构成单个文学作品以及构成整个文学体系的“ langue” 。

In order to differentiate between the structure that governs language and the millions of individual utterances that are its surface phenomena, Saussure called the structure of language langue (the French word for language), and he called the individual utterances that occur when we speak parole (the French word for speech). For the structuralist, of course, langue is the proper object of study; parole is of interest only in that it reveals langue. And these terms are used, as well, by structuralists who study literature: as we’ll see later, structuralist critics look for the langue that structures individual literary works and that structures the system of literature as a whole.

正如我们前面所看到的，结构的组成部分并非仅仅是独立元素的集合：它们之所以构成一个运作单元，是因为它们彼此关联，相互作用。正如索绪尔在论述语言结构时所指出的，我们之所以能够感知这些组成部分，正是因为我们感知到了它们彼此之间的差异。差异意味着，我们识别某个实体（例如物体、概念或声音）的能力，是基于我们感知到的它与其他所有实体之间的差异。例如，如果我们认为所有物体都是同一种颜色，我们就根本不需要“红色”（或“蓝色”或“绿色”）这个词。红色之所以是红色，仅仅是因为我们感知到它与蓝色和绿色不同。根据结构主义的观点，人类的思维最容易通过对立概念来感知差异，结构主义者称之为二元对立：两个直接对立的概念，我们通过它们彼此的对立来理解每一个概念。例如，我们理解“上”是“下”的对立面，“女性”是“男性”的对立面，“善”是“恶”的对立面，“黑色”是“白色”的对立面，等等。

As we saw above, the components of a structure are not merely a collection of independent items: they form a working unit because they exist in relation to one another. They interact. And we are able to perceive those components, as Saussure noted in terms of the structure of language, only because we perceive their difference from one another. Difference simply means that our ability to identify an entity (such as an object, a concept, or a sound) is based on the difference we perceive between it and all other entities. For example, if we believed that all objects were the same color, we wouldn’t need the word red (or blue or green) at all. Red is red only because we perceive it to be different from blue and green. According to structuralism, the human mind perceives difference most readily in terms of opposites, which structuralists call binary oppositions: two ideas, directly opposed, each of which we understand by means of its opposition to the other. For example, we understand up as the opposite of down, female as the opposite of male, good as the opposite of evil, black as the opposite of white, and so on.

此外，与他的前辈不同，索绪尔认为词语并非仅仅指称它们所代表的世界中的对象。相反，词语是一种语言符号，如同硬币的两面，由两个不可分割的部分组成：能指和所指。能指是“音像”（语言声音的心理印记）；所指是能指所指称的概念。因此，词语并非仅仅是音像（能指），也并非仅仅是概念（所指）。音像只有与概念相联系才能成为词语。此外，索绪尔指出，能指和所指之间的关系是任意的：一个特定的音像与其所指称的概念之间并无必然联系。没有理由认为“树”的概念必须用音像“tree”来表示，而不能用音像“arbre”；“书”的概念同样可以用音像“livre”来表示。能指与所指之间的关系仅仅是社会习俗的问题：它取决于使用它的社群如何定义它。

Furthermore, unlike his predecessors, Saussure argued that words do not simply refer to objects in the world for which they stand. Instead, a word is a linguistic sign consisting, like the two sides of a coin, of two inseparable parts: signifier + signified. A signifier is a “sound-image” (a mental imprint of a linguistic sound); the signified is the concept to which the signifier refers. Thus, a word is not merely a sound-image (signifier), nor is it merely a concept (signified). A sound-image becomes a word only when it is linked with a concept. Furthermore, the relationship between signifier and signified, Saussure observed, is arbitrary: there is no necessary connection between a given sound-image and the concept to which it refers. There is no reason why the concept of a tree should be represented by the sound-image “tree” instead of by the sound-image “arbre”; the concept of a book is just as well represented by the sound-image “livre” as the sound-image “book.” The relationship between signifier and signified is merely a matter of social convention: it’s whatever the community using it says it is.

结构主义的核心观点是：能指，或者说语言中的声音意象，并非指涉世界上的事物，而是指涉我们头脑中的概念。正如我们之前提到的，结构主义者认为，我们对世界的感知源于人类意识固有的概念框架。我们并非发现世界，而是根据人类思维中固有的结构“创造”世界。鉴于语言是这些结构中最根本的，也是我们信念代代相传的媒介，我们正是通过语言来学习和理解世界。这就是为什么学习一门新语言蕴含着以全新视角看待世界的潜力。

The idea that signifiers, or linguistic sound-images, do not refer to things in the world but to concepts in our mind is crucial for structuralism. As we noted earlier, structuralists believe that our perceptions of the world result from the conceptual framework that is an innate feature of human consciousness. We don’t discover the world; we “create” it according to innate structures within the human mind. Given that language is the most fundamental of these structures, and the one through which our beliefs are passed on from one generation to the next, it makes sense that it is through language that we learn to conceive and perceive the world the way we do. This is why learning a new language carries with it the potential to learn to see the world in new ways.

例如，如果以英语为母语的人学习爱斯基摩语，他们可能会对雪有截然不同的看法，因为他们会了解到，根据雪的大小和质地，爱斯基摩语中有很多不同的词来描述英语中所谓的“雪” 。雪花的形状、降雪的密度、下落的角度、暴风雪的起源方向等等，都会影响人的存在状态。同样地，如果以英语为母语的人学习西班牙语，他们可能会获得一种看待人类存在的新视角，因为他们会发现西班牙语中与英语动词“是” （to be）对应的动词有两个：ser和estar。Ser 的意思是“存在”，指的是一个人永久认同的自我状态。人们用 ser 来表达“我是一个人”、“我是女人”、“我是墨西哥人”等等。人们用 estar 来描述一个人不断变化的存在状态，例如“我在超市”或“我是出租车司机”。而人们既不用ser也不用estar来表达“我饿了”或“我困了”，因为在西班牙语中，这些不被视为存在状态。在西班牙语中，人们会说饥饿或困倦——tengo hambre或tengo sueño——但这并非存在状态。因此，当我们说某种特定的语言时，我们的注意力会被引导到我们经验的某些特定方面，或者更准确地说，是这种语言引发了特定的经验。换句话说，我们的语言调节着我们对世界和自身的体验：它决定了我们环顾四周和审视自身时所看到的东西。

If native speakers of English learn to speak an Eskimo language, for example, they may learn to see snow quite differently, for they will learn that there are many different words for what English calls snow, depending on the size and texture of the flake, the density of the snowfall, the angle at which it falls, the direction from which the storm originates, and so on. Similarly, if native speakers of English learn to speak Spanish, they may learn a new way to view the idea of human existence, for they will learn that Spanish has two different verbs for the English verb to be: ser and estar. Ser means “to be” in the sense of what one permanently considers oneself. One uses ser to say “I am a human being,” “I am a woman,” “I am Mexican,” and the like. One uses estar to make statements about one’s changeable state of being, such as “I am at the supermarket” or “I am a cab driver.” And one uses neither ser nor estar to say “I am hungry” or “I am sleepy,” for in Spanish these are not considered states of being. In Spanish one has hunger or sleepiness – tengo hambre or tengo sueño – but these are not states of being. Thus, when speaking a particular language, our attention is drawn to particular aspects of our experience, or, more precisely, particular experiences are generated by that language. In other words, our language mediates our experience of our world and ourselves: it determines what we see when we look around us and when we look at ourselves.

语言在构建人类经验中占据首要地位的观点，引起了许多研究人类文化的学者的极大兴趣。在探讨结构主义文学方法之前，让我们先简要了解一下结构主义思想在文化研究领域的两个相关分支：结构人类学（对人类文化进行比较研究）和符号学（研究符号系统，尤其关注其在大众文化分析中的应用）。这两个领域中结构主义的实践案例，有助于我们全面理解结构主义理论，并为我们更好地理解其在文学领域的应用做好准备。

The belief in the primacy of language in structuring human experience is of great interest to many students of human culture. Before we examine structuralist approaches to literature, let’s take a brief look at two related areas of cultural study in which structuralist thought plays an important role: structural anthropology, which is the comparative study of human cultures, and semiotics, which is the study of sign systems, especially as they apply to the analysis of popular culture. Examples of structuralist activity in both these areas can help us grasp the structuralist enterprise as a whole and prepare us to better understand its applications to literature.

结构人类学

Structural anthropology

结构人类学由克劳德·列维-斯特劳斯于20世纪50年代末创立，旨在探寻连接所有人类的潜在共同点，即结构，而不论他们所属文化的表面现象有何差异。尽管不同文化表达社群生活重要方面的仪式形式千差万别，但似乎所有人类文化都拥有某种成文的流程，例如择偶、亲属关系和成年礼。虽然考验（例如，在野外独自生存一段时间，不提供食物、衣物或武器）与大学宿舍里的21岁生日派对显然截然不同，但结构人类学家认为，这些差异仅仅存在于表面现象层面，或者如结构语言学家所言，存在于语言层面。因为作为成年礼，这两种文化实践都具有相同的潜在结构，相同的语言。两者都包含某种仪式：从……返回后由社区成员为其沐浴无论是在荒野中庆祝，还是吹灭蜡烛，接受朋友们的祝酒，两者都包含某种特殊的个人装饰：比如在身上绘制特殊的图案，或者戴上派对帽。而且，两者都会在仪式结束时享用某种特殊的食物：或许是某种强大动物的心脏，又或许是生日蛋糕和啤酒。

Structural anthropology, created by Claude Lévi-Strauss in the late 1950s, seeks the underlying common denominators, the structures, that link all human beings regardless of the differences among the surface phenomena of the cultures to which they belong. Despite the very different ritual forms in which different cultures express important aspects of community life, it seems that all human cultures have some codified process of, for example, mate selection, kinship ties, and initiation into adulthood. While trial by ordeal (for example, being expected to survive on one’s own in the wilderness for a specified period of time without the provision of food, clothing, or weapons) certainly appears different from, say, a twenty-first birthday party at a college dormitory, structural anthropologists would argue that the differences are only at the level of surface phenomena or, as structural linguists would put it, at the level of parole. For as rites of initiation, both cultural practices have the same underlying structures, the same langue. Both involve some sort of ritual ceremony: being bathed by members of the community upon one’s return from the wilderness or blowing out candles and being toasted by assembled friends. Both involve some special form of personal decoration: special markings painted on the body or party hats. And both involve eating some sort of special food at the end of the ritual: perhaps the heart of a powerful animal or birthday cake and beer.

列维-斯特劳斯尤其关注不同文化中看似迥异的神话之间存在的结构相似性。他的目标是探究“不同”的神话何时实际上是同一神话的不同版本，从而证明来自截然不同文化的人类共享着共同的意识结构，这种意识结构会投射到结构相似的神话的形成之中。他认为，这些结构相似性揭示了某些人类关注点能够跨越文化边界，其中包括如何界定亲属关系（以确定继承权和乱伦禁忌）等实际问题，以及如何解释人类起源等哲学问题。列维-斯特劳斯对俄狄浦斯神话的分析便是一个例证，他认为该神话体现了我们“由性结合而生”的认知与许多文化中根深蒂固的“由大地而生”的信念之间的冲突，正如俄狄浦斯神话中斯巴达人从泥土中诞生（或者，我们也可以补充一句，正如《圣经》中亚当由泥土塑造而成）。列维-斯特劳斯认为，任何神话都不存在“真实”或“原始”版本。任何神话的每个版本都同样有效，因为每个版本都体现了所有结构试图从原本混乱的世界中寻求意义的努力。

The existence of structural similarities among seemingly different myths of different cultures was one of Lévi-Strauss’ particular areas of interest. His goal was to discover when “different” myths are actually different versions of the same myth in order to show that human beings from very different cultures share structures of consciousness that project themselves in the formation of structurally similar myths. These structural similarities, he claimed, reveal that certain human concerns cross cultural boundaries, and they include such practical questions as how to define kinship ties (in order to determine rights of inheritance and incest taboos) and such philosophical questions as how to account for the origin of the human race. An illustration of the latter question occurs in Lévi-Strauss’ analysis of the Oedipus myth, which he believed embodies the conflict between our knowledge that we are born of sexual union and the persistent belief among many cultures that we are born of the earth, as the Spartoi spring from the soil in the Oedipus myth (or, we might add, as Adam is fashioned from clay in the Bible). Lévi-Strauss argued that there is no “true” or “original” version of any myth. Each version of a given myth is equally valid because each embodies the attempt of all structures to make sense out of an otherwise chaotic world.

从结构主义视角来看，列维-斯特劳斯发现，来自不同文化的浩瀚神话最终可以简化为数量有限的“神话主题”（mytheme），即神话的基本单元。神话主题类似于句子，它代表两个或多个概念之间的关系，通常以主谓关系的形式出现。英雄杀死怪物就是一个神话主题的例子，英雄违反道德法则也是如此。列维-斯特劳斯将神话主题定义为关系的“束”，因为一个神话主题包含了它的所有变体。例如，“英雄杀死怪物”这个神话主题就包含了各种不同类型的英雄（富有的、贫穷的、孤儿、出身名门的）杀死不同类型的怪物（男性、女性、半人半兽、定居的、流动的、陆地上的、海上的、能言善辩的、哑巴的），而他们杀死怪物的原因也各不相同（为了赢得妻子、拯救社群、证明自己）。关键在于，对神话进行结构性研究表明，存在一种相对有限、可知的语言（潜在结构），通过这种语言，我们可以对世界各地产生的数量庞大的不同神话进行排序和理解。

When examined from a structuralist perspective, he found that the enormous number of myths from various cultures reduces itself to a rather limited number of what he called mythemes, the fundamental units of myths. A mytheme is analogous to a sentence in that it represents a relationship between two or more concepts, often in the form of a subject–verb relationship. A hero killing a monster is an example of a mytheme, as is a hero violating a moral law. Lévi-Strauss defines mythemes as “bundles” of relations because a mytheme consists of all its variants. For example, the mytheme “the hero kills a monster” includes a variety of different kinds of heroes (rich, poor, orphaned, of good family) killing different kinds of monsters (male, female, half-human, sedentary, mobile, land-bound, seafaring, articulate, mute) for different reasons (to win a wife, to save a community, to prove himself). The point is that a structural approach to myth shows us that there is a relatively limited, knowable langue (underlying structure) by means of which we can order and understand the otherwise overwhelming number of different myths produced all over the world.

当然，神话是叙事的一种形式，因此神话主题也是叙事结构。所以，对神话进行结构分析，对文学的结构研究显然具有重要意义。事实上，正如我们将在本章后面的“文学体裁的结构”一节中看到的那样，一些文学批评家认为，所有文学作品都是以不同的形式对同一神话进行重述。

Of course, myths are forms of narrative, and mythemes are therefore narrative structures. So the structural analysis of myths has obvious implications for the structural study of literature. Indeed, as we’ll see later in this chapter, in the section entitled “The Structure of Literary Genres,” some literary critics believe that all literature consists of the retelling, in various guises, of the same myths.

符号学

Semiotics

正如结构人类学运用结构主义的洞见对人类文化进行比较研究一样，符号学也运用结构主义的洞见来研究它所谓的符号系统。符号系统是指可以像分析一种专门语言一样分析的语言或非语言对象或行为（或对象或行为的集合）。换句话说，符号学研究语言和非语言对象及行为如何以符号的方式“告诉”我们某些信息。就文学分析而言，符号学关注文学惯例：构成文学结构的规则、文学手法和形式要素。我们将在下一节“结构主义与文学”中详细探讨这一主题。因此，这里我们先集中讨论符号学的非语言应用，我相信你会对此很感兴趣。

Just as structural anthropology applies structuralist insights to the comparative study of human cultures, semiotics applies structuralist insights to the study of what it calls sign systems. A sign system is a linguistic or nonlinguistic object or behavior (or collection of objects or behaviors) that can be analyzed as if it were a specialized language. In other words, semiotics examines the ways linguistic and nonlinguistic objects and behaviors operate symbolically to “tell” us something. In terms of literary analysis, semiotics is interested in literary conventions: the rules, literary devices, and formal elements that constitute literary structures. We’ll examine this topic at some length in the following section, “Structuralism and Literature.” So let’s concentrate here on the nonlinguistic uses of semiotics, which I think you’ll find rather interesting.

例如，某威士忌品牌广告牌上，一位金发美女身着黑色紧身丝绒长裙斜倚而卧，从符号学角度分析，这幅画面“告诉”我们，饮用这款威士忌的人（通常是男性）会吸引像广告牌上这位一样性感迷人的女性。正如这个例子所示，符号学在分析流行文化方面尤为有效。符号学家经常研究的其他流行文化符号系统还包括杂志上的图片广告、流行舞蹈、迪士尼乐园、轮滑德比、芭比娃娃、汽车，以及著名符号学家罗兰·巴特分析过的两个例子：职业摔跤和脱衣舞。

For example, the picture of the reclining blond beauty in the skin-tight, black velvet dress on the billboard advertising a particular brand of whiskey, when examined semiotically, “tells” us that those who drink this whiskey (presumably men) will be attractive to seductive, beautiful women like the one on display. As this example illustrates, semiotics is especially useful in analyzing popular culture. Other examples of the kinds of pop-culture sign systems semioticians often examine might include pictorial ads in magazines, popular dances, Disneyland, roller derby, Barbie dolls, automobiles, and, to use two examples analyzed by the famous semiotician Roland Barthes, professional wrestling and the striptease.

以下是巴特对职业摔跤符号学分析的简要概述。他认为，职业摔跤（参赛者使用诸如“角斗士”或“野蛮人”之类的化名，身着戏服，并事先安排比赛的摔跤类型）可以被视为一种符号系统。它可以被解读为一种具有非常特定目的的语言：为观众提供宣泄式的满足感，让他们看到正义在（与生活不同）善恶分明的情境中最终战胜邪恶。无论参赛者是谁，比赛的结构相似性都揭示了这一目的：例如，（1）每位摔跤手都具有鲜明的类型（例如，衣着整洁的美国英雄、脾气暴躁的邋遢鬼、野蛮的恶棍等等）；（2）每场比赛中的参赛者——无论是通过他们的类型、他们在特定比赛中的行为，还是两者兼而有之——都可以被清晰地识别为“好人”和“坏人”。 （3）每场比赛都以正义战胜邪恶而告终。

Here’s a simplified summary of Barthes’ semiotic analysis of professional wrestling. He argues that professional wrestling (the brand of wrestling in which the contestants use pseudonyms like Gladiator or The Barbarian, dress in costume, and orchestrate the match in advance) can be viewed as a sign system. It can be interpreted as a language with a very specific purpose: to provide the audience with the cathartic satisfaction of watching justice triumph in a situation that (unlike life) makes it very clear who is good and who is evil. This purpose is revealed in the structural similarities of the matches, regardless of who the contestants are: for example, (1) each wrestler is a clear type (clean-cut All-American, mean-tempered slob, barbarous evildoer, and so on); (2) each match contains contestants who – by their type, their behavior during a particular match, or both – can be clearly identified as the “good guy” and the “bad guy”; and (3) each match ends with the triumph of goodness over evil.

巴特斯进一步指出，这场比赛与古希腊戏剧的表演极为相似，摔跤手们通过夸张的手势和表情来演绎他们的痛苦、绝望或胜利。因此，展现苦难、失败和正义正是这场比赛的目的。我们得出这一结论的依据包括参赛者的姓名、体格和服装；他们在擂台上的肢体语言（昂首阔步、畏缩不前、趾高气扬、咄咄逼人、安抚对手等等）；以及他们的面部表情（得意洋洋、义愤填膺、骄傲自满、惊恐万分等等）。胜利、失败等等）。比赛是否被操纵并不重要，因为比赛的目的不是为了确定谁是更优秀的摔跤手，而是为了上演那种几个世纪以来以不同形式为公众提供替代性愤怒、恐惧和沮丧宣泄的表演。

The match, Barthes further observes, greatly resembles the spectacle of ancient Greek theater, as the wrestlers act out their pain, despair, or triumph with exaggerated gestures and grimaces. The exhibition of suffering, defeat, and justice is thus the purpose of the spectacle. The signs we read in order to come to this conclusion include the names, physiques, and costumes of the contestants; their body language in the ring (strutting, cowering, swaggering, menacing, placating, and the like); and their facial expressions (smug, outraged, proud, horrified, triumphant, defeated, and so on). It doesn’t matter that the contest is rigged because its purpose is not to determine who is the better wrestler but to enact the kind of spectacle different versions of which have for centuries provided the public with the vicarious release of anger, fear, and frustration.

现在让我们来看看符号学分析（例如刚才概述的分析）背后的一些理论概念。符号学认为语言是最基本、最重要的符号系统。正如我们在结构语言学的讨论中所看到的，语言符号被定义为能指（声音-图像）和所指（能指所指的概念）的结合。对于符号学来说，符号也等于能指+所指。然而，正如我们刚才看到的，符号学扩展了能指的范围，使其包含物体、手势、活动、声音、图像——简而言之，任何可以通过感官感知的事物。显然，符号学赋予了能指广泛的可能性。然而，在公认的三种符号类型——指示符号、图像符号和象征符号——中，符号学将其研究范围限定于那些作为象征符号的符号。让我们稍作停顿，探讨一下为什么会这样。

Now let’s take a look at some of the theoretical concepts underlying semiotic analyses like the one just summarized. Semiotics recognizes language as the most fundamental and important sign system. As we saw in our discussion of structural linguistics, a linguistic sign is defined as a union of signifier (sound-image) and signified (concept to which the signifier refers). For semiotics, too, sign = signifier + signified. However, as we just saw, semiotics expands the signifier to include objects, gestures, activities, sounds, images – in short, anything that can be perceived by the senses. Clearly, semiotics gives the signifier a wide range of possibilities. However, of the three recognized classes of signs – index, icon, and symbol – semiotics limits its study to signs that function as symbols. Let’s pause briefly to examine why this is the case.

指示符号是指能指与所指之间存在具体因果关系的符号。例如，烟表示火；敲门声表示有人在家。图像符号是指能指在物理上与所指相似。例如，一幅画作如果与它所描绘的对象相似，那么它就是一幅图像符号。一幅肯尼迪总统的写实画像就是一幅图像符号。象征符号是指能指与所指之间的关系既非自然也非必然，而是任意的，也就是说，这种关系是由某个社群的约定俗成或某个群体的共识决定的符号。

An index is a sign in which the signifier has a concrete, causal relationship to the signified. For example, smoke signifies fire; a knock on the door signifies that someone is there. An icon is a sign in which the signifier physically resembles the signified. For example, a painting is an icon to the extent that the picture resembles the subject it represents. A realistic painting of President Kennedy is an icon. A symbol is a sign in which the relationship between signifier and signified is neither natural nor necessary but arbitrary, that is, decided on by the conventions of a community or by the agreement of some group.

正如我们之前所见，语言是符号系统的一个例子。“树”这个音像之所以指代树的概念，仅仅是因为英语使用者约定俗成地这样使用它。虽然烟雾是火的象征，一幅逼真的火焰画作是火的象征，但“火”这个词本身只是火的符号。它并不具备火的固有属性。任何群体认可的其他音像都可以用来代表火。让我们来看另一个例子。客厅窗户上的冰晶是冬天的象征。一张冰封风景的照片是冬天的象征。然而，同样的冰封风景照片，或者故事中对它的文字描述（例如杰克·伦敦的《生火》），对大多数英语专业的学生来说，却是死亡的象征。

As we saw earlier, language is an example of a symbolic sign system. The soundimage “tree” refers to the idea of a tree only because speakers of English have agreed to use it that way. While smoke is an index of fire, and a realistic painting of fire is an icon of fire, the word fire is a symbol of fire. There is no quality of fire inherent in the word fire. Any other sound-image agreed upon by a group could be used to represent fire. Let’s consider a different example. Ice crystals on your living room window are an index of winter. A photograph of a frozen landscape is an icon of winter. However, that same photograph of a frozen landscape or a written description of it in a story (such as Jack London’s “To Build a Fire”) would function for most English majors as a symbol of death.

因此，在三种符号中，只有象征符号的解释权在于人。一群人不会决定火会产生烟雾（指示符号），火产生烟雾是客观存在的。一群人不会决定肯尼迪总统的写实肖像（圣像）必须拥有与这位已故总统相同的发色、瞳色、肤色和其他体貌特征。如果肖像没有这些体貌特征，它就不能称之为圣像。但是，一群人确实需要决定白色象征贞洁，红色象征性欲，角和叉子象征撒旦，十字架象征基督教。

Thus, of the three kinds of signs, only the symbol is a matter of interpretation. A group of people doesn’t decide that fire produces smoke (an index). It is simply the case that fire produces smoke. A group of people doesn’t decide that a realistic portrait of President Kennedy (an icon) will have the same color hair, eyes, skin, and other physical features that the late president had. If the portrait didn’t have these physical features, it wouldn’t be an icon. But a group of people does have to decide that the color white symbolizes virginity, that the color red symbolizes sexuality, that horns and a pitchfork symbolize Satan, and that the cross symbolizes Christianity.

因此，符号学的任务在于分离和分析符号系统的象征功能，尽管被研究的对象或行为通常也具有其他功能。例如，食物和衣物具有显而易见的生物学功能（它们为我们提供营养并保护我们免受自然环境的侵害）和经济功能（食物和衣物价格的波动会影响一个社会的生活水平）。但符号学家对食物和衣物的兴趣仅限于它们作为符号系统的功能，仅限于它们所具有的象征内容。此外，作为一种结构主义的学科，符号学通过共时性地（在特定的时间点）关注一组相似的对象（例如，广告牌、杂志图片广告或餐厅菜单）来分析符号系统。例如，要分析餐厅菜单中食物的符号学表达，人们不会考察同一家餐厅菜单随时间推移的变化（历时性地）。相反，人们会同时（同步地）检查不同餐厅制作的大量菜单，以发现它们的符号代码，即承载某种非语言文化信息的潜在结构组成部分。

It is the business of semiotics, then, to isolate and analyze the symbolic function of sign systems, although the objects or behaviors under investigation will often have other functions as well. For example, food and clothing have obvious biological functions (they keep us nourished and protected from the elements) and economic functions (fluctuations in the price of food and clothing influence a society’s standard of living). But a semiotician will be interested in food and clothing only to the extent to which they function as sign systems, only to the extent to which they have symbolic content. Furthermore, as a structuralist enterprise, semiotics will analyze a sign system by focusing on a group of similar objects (for example, billboards or pictorial magazine ads or restaurant menus) synchronically (at a given moment in time). To analyze the semiotics of food as it is expressed in restaurant menus, for example, one would not examine menus from a single restaurant as they have changed over time (diachronically). Instead, one would examine a large number of menus produced by different restaurants at the same point in time (synchronically) in order to discover their semiotic codes, the underlying structural components that carry a nonverbal cultural message of some sort.

对餐厅菜单进行符号学分析会揭示什么？换句话说，除了菜单上文字所传达的五大类食物的具体信息之外，这些菜单还传递着哪些非语言信息？通过考察菜单的颜色、大小、装饰、印刷类型、页边距、空白区域的数量和分布、价格、菜名（并非像牛排或烤土豆这样的具体词语，而是像“巴黎风味”或“先锋”这样的“标签” ）以及具有象征意义的食物（例如汉堡包或鱼子酱）的出现或缺失等符号，我们或许能够发现一个食品“时尚产业”，在这个产业中，例如，顾客的自我形象信息得以传递。某些菜单的符号学信息会传达这样的信息：“如果您是一位出身良好、受过良好教育、品味高雅且财力雄厚的杰出人士，那么您将身着古驰，坐进宝马，光临本店用餐。”其他菜单则传达这样的信息：“如果你是一个脚踏实地、不做作的人，不想把时间和辛苦赚来的钱浪费在娘娘腔的炫耀上，那就进来吧。”还有一些菜单则传达这样的信息：“如果你是一个爱国的美国人，仍然信仰上帝，仍然喜欢奶奶做的苹果派，那么来这里用餐，你会感受到家庭价值观的传承。”

What might a semiotic analysis of restaurant menus reveal? In other words, besides the concrete data about the five food groups communicated by the words on the menu, what nonlinguistic messages are these menus sending? By examining such signs as the menus’ color, size, decoration, type of print, size of margins, amount and distribution of blank space, prices, names of dishes (not words like steak or baked potato, but “tags” like à la Parisienne or Pioneer’s), and the predominance or absence of foods that carry symbolic value (such as hamburgers or caviar), we would probably be able to discover a “fashion industry” of food in which, for example, messages about patrons’ self-images are communicated. The semiotics of some menus will send the message, “If you’re a well-bred, well-educated person of distinction with an extremely discriminating palate and the wallet to back it up, you will slip into your Guccis, slide into your BMW, and dine with us.” Other menus will send the message, “If you’re a down-to-earth nonphony who doesn’t want to waste time or hard-earned dough on sissified showing off, come on in.” Still other menus will send the message, “If you’re a patriotic American who still believes in God and Grandma’s apple pie, you’ll celebrate your family values by eating here.”

如果你是电影爱好者，或许会有兴趣尝试构建一部音乐喜剧、悬疑片或爱情片的符号学图谱。同样地，你也可能想探索一下日间肥皂剧的符号学。对符号学家而言，任何事物都可以是符号。整个人类文化世界都是一部等待被“解读”的“文本”，而结构主义则为此提供了理论框架。

If you’re a movie fan, you might be interested in trying to map out a semiotics of the musical comedy, the murder mystery, or the love story. Similarly, you might want to see if you can discover a semiotics of daytime drama, or “soap operas.” For semioticians, anything can be a sign. The whole world of human culture is a “text” waiting to be “read,” and structuralism provides the theoretical framework to do it.

结构主义与文学

Structuralism and literature

对于文学专业的学生来说，结构主义具有非常重要的意义。毕竟，文学是一门语言艺术：它由语言构成。因此，它与“大师”的关系……结构和语言都非常直接。此外，结构主义者认为，人类思维的结构机制是我们理解混沌的途径，而文学是人类向自身解释世界（即理解混沌）的基本手段。因此，文学作为一门研究领域与结构主义作为一种分析方法之间似乎存在着相当强烈的相似性。

For students of literature, structuralism has very important implications. After all, literature is a verbal art: it is composed of language. So its relation to the “master” structure, language, is very direct. In addition, structuralists believe that the structuring mechanisms of the human mind are the means by which we make sense out of chaos, and literature is a fundamental means by which human beings explain the world to themselves, that is, make sense out of chaos. So there seems to be a rather powerful parallel between literature as a field of study and structuralism as a method of analysis.

我们将探讨结构主义文学方法，重点关注文学文本的叙事维度，因为结构主义批评主要研究叙事。然而，这种关注点并非乍看之下那么狭隘，如果我们记住叙事涵盖了悠久的历史和广泛的文本类型，从古代口头传统的简单神话和民间故事到后现代小说中复杂的书面形式，都包含在内。此外，大多数戏剧和相当一部分诗歌，虽然不被归类为叙事作品，但它们也具有叙事维度，因为它们讲述的是某种故事。总之，正如我们将看到的，叙事为结构主义批评提供了丰富的素材，因为尽管叙事形式多样，但它们都具有某些共同的结构特征，例如情节、背景和人物。

Our discussion of structuralist approaches to literature will focus on the narrative dimension of literary texts because structuralist criticism deals mainly with narrative. This focus is not as narrow as it may seem at first glance, however, if we remember that narrative includes a long history and broad range of texts, from the simple myths and folk tales of the ancient oral tradition to the complex mélange of written forms found in the postmodern novel. In addition, most drama and a good deal of poetry, though not classified as narrative, nevertheless have a narrative dimension in that they tell a story of some sort. In any event, as we’ll see, narratives provide fertile ground for structuralist criticism because, despite their range of forms, narratives share certain structural features, such as plot, setting, and character.

然而，我们必须记住，结构主义并不试图解释单个文本的意义，甚至也不试图判断某个文本是否是优秀的文学作品。解释和文学质量的问题属于表面现象的范畴，即言辞的范畴。结构主义追求的是文学文本的语言，即文本得以表达意义的结构，它通常被称为语法，因为它支配着识别和组合基本文学要素（例如，英雄、落难少女和反派）的规则（例如，英雄试图从反派手中救出落难少女）。简而言之，结构主义关注的不是文本的意义，而是文本如何表达其意义。因此， 《了不起的盖茨比》中的杰伊·盖茨比、黛西·布坎南和汤姆·布坎南都是表面现象，它们的意义来源于它们与底层结构（分别是英雄、落难少女和反派）之间的关系。

We must keep in mind, however, that structuralism does not attempt to interpret what individual texts mean or even whether or not a given text is good literature. Issues of interpretation and literary quality are in the domain of surface phenomena, the domain of parole. Structuralism seeks instead the langue of literary texts, the structure that allows texts to make meaning, often referred to as a grammar because it governs the rules by which fundamental literary elements are identified (for example, the hero, the damsel in distress, and the villain) and combined (for example, the hero tries to save the damsel in distress from the villain). In short, structuralism isn’t interested in what a text means, but in how a text means what it means. Thus, The Great Gatsby’s Jay Gatsby, Daisy Buchanan, and Tom Buchanan are surface phenomena that draw their meaning from the ways in which they relate to the structures underlying them: respectively, hero, damsel in distress, and villain.

正如你可能在第六章中了解到的，读者反应批评家也关注文本的意义，而非文本本身的意义。事实上，这两个学科之间存在一些重叠之处，因为结构主义者和读者反应批评家都认同文本的潜在结构与读者对文本的反应之间存在关联。毕竟，结构主义认为，我们在文学作品中感知到的结构，如同在其他一切事物中一样，都是人类意识结构的投射。然而，你可能还记得，读者反应批评的最终目标是理解读者的体验，结构主义者称之为表面现象。相比之下，结构主义的最终目标是理解人类体验的潜在结构，这种结构存在于语言层面，无论我们是在考察文学的结构，还是在探讨文学结构与人类结构之间的关系。意识。换句话说，读者反应批评并不寻求一种能够将人类意识的先天结构与所有人类经验、行为和创造联系起来的普世科学。结构主义恰恰追求的就是这一点。

As you may remember from Chapter 6, reader-response critics also focus on how a text means rather than what it means. Indeed, there is some overlap between the two disciplines, for structuralists and reader-response critics would agree that there is a relationship between the underlying structure of the text and the reader’s response to it. After all, structuralism believes that the structures we perceive in literature, as in everything else, are projections of the structures of human consciousness. However, you’ll recall that the final goal of reader-response criticism is to understand the reader’s experience, which structuralists would call a surface phenomenon. In contrast, the final goal of structuralism is to understand the underlying structure of human experience, which exists at the level of langue, whether we are examining the structures of literature or speculating on the relationship between the structures of literature and the structures of human consciousness. In other words, reader-response criticism does not seek a universal science that would link innate structures of human consciousness to all human experience, behavior, and production. Structuralism seeks precisely that.

结构主义文学研究方法通常侧重于文学研究的三个特定领域：文学体裁的分类、叙事手法的描述以及文学阐释的分析。为了便于理解，我们将分别讨论这三个领域。

Structuralist approaches to literature have tended to focus on three specific areas of literary studies: the classification of literary genres, the description of narrative operations, and the analysis of literary interpretation. For the sake of clarity, we’ll discuss these three areas separately.

文学体裁的结构

The structure of literary genres

让我们先从一个最复杂、最全面的例子——诺思罗普·弗莱的“神话理论”——的简要概述开始，探讨结构主义的体裁分析方法。弗莱的“神话”（ mythoi ， mythos的复数形式）理论是一种体裁理论，旨在探寻西方文学传统背后的结构原则。弗莱用这个词来指代他认为构成神话的四种叙事模式。他声称，这些“神话”揭示了各种文学体裁背后的结构原则：具体而言，包括喜剧、浪漫故事、悲剧和反讽/讽刺。

Let’s begin our discussion of structuralist approaches to genre with a simplified summary of one of its most complex and sweeping examples: what Northrop Frye calls his theory of myths, which is a theory of genres that seeks the structural principles underlying the Western literary tradition.1 Mythoi (plural of mythos) is a term Frye uses to refer to the four narrative patterns that, he argues, structure myth. These mythoi, he claims, reveal the structural principles underlying literary genres: specifically, comedy, romance, tragedy, and irony/satire.

弗莱认为，人类的叙事想象主要通过两种方式投射：对理想世界的描绘和对现实世界的描绘。理想世界优于现实世界，是一个充满纯真、富足和圆满的世界。弗莱称之为“夏日神话”，并将其与浪漫小说这一体裁联系起来。这是一个充满冒险的世界，勇敢正直的英雄和美丽的少女克服重重阻碍，最终完成使命。你可能熟悉的浪漫小说包括托马斯·马洛礼爵士的《亚瑟王之死》（1470年）、埃德蒙·斯宾塞的《仙后》（1596年）、约翰·班扬的《天路历程》（1678年）以及《睡美人》。

According to Frye, human beings project their narrative imaginations in two fundamental ways: in representations of an ideal world and in representations of the real world. The ideal world, which is better than the real world, is the world of innocence, plenitude, and fulfillment. Frye calls it the mythos of summer, and he associates it with the genre of romance. This is the world of adventure, of successful quests in which brave, virtuous heroes and beautiful maidens overcome villainous threats to the achievement of their goals. Examples of romance you may be familiar with include the chivalrous adventures in Sir Thomas Malory’s Le Morte d’Arthur (1470), Edmund Spenser’s The Faerie Queene (1596), John Bunyan’s The Pilgrim’s Progress (1678), and “Sleeping Beauty.”

与此相反，现实世界是一个充满经验、不确定性和失败的世界。弗莱称之为“冬日神话”，并将其与反讽/讽刺这两种文体联系起来。反讽是用悲剧的视角审视现实世界，在这个世界里，主人公们被生活错综复杂的谜团所击败。他们或许试图成为英雄，却永远无法达到英雄的高度；他们或许梦想着幸福，却永远无法获得。他们和我们一样，都是凡人，所以他们也会遭受苦难。你可能读过一些反讽作品，例如莎士比亚的《暴风雨》（1611年）、伊迪丝·华顿的《纯真年代》（1920年）、理查德·赖特的《土生子》（1940年）以及约翰·斯坦贝克的《人鼠之间》（1937年）。

In contrast, the real world is the world of experience, uncertainty, and failure. Frye calls it the mythos of winter, and he associates it with the double genre of irony/satire. Irony is the real world seen through a tragic lens, a world in which protagonists are defeated by the puzzling complexities of life. They may try to be heroic, but they never achieve heroic stature. They may dream of happiness, but they never attain it. They’re human, like us, and so they suffer. Examples of ironic texts you may have read include Shakespeare’s The Tempest (1611), Edith Wharton’s The Age of Innocence (1920), Richard Wright’s Native Son (1940), and John Steinbeck’s Of Mice and Men (1937).

类似地，讽刺是用喜剧的视角审视现实世界，展现一个充满人类愚蠢、过度和不协调的世界。在讽刺的世界里，人性的弱点遭到嘲弄，有时甚至以尖刻无情的幽默加以嘲讽。你可能熟悉的讽刺作品包括乔纳森·斯威夫特的《格列佛游记》（1726年）、乔治·奥威尔的《动物庄园》（1946年）以及马克·吐温的《美国内战前夕》中讽刺美国南方各州弊端的章节。马克·吐温的《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》 （1885 年）以及拉尔夫·埃里森的《看不见的人》 （1952 年）中讽刺保守派自满和左派自欺欺人的段落。

Analogously, satire is the real world seen through a comic lens, a world of human folly, excess, and incongruity. In the world of satire, human frailty is mocked, sometimes with biting, merciless humor. Examples of satire you may be acquainted with include Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s Travels (1726), George Orwell’s Animal Farm (1946), the episodes satirizing the abuses of the antebellum American South in Mark Twain’s Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1885), and the passages satirizing conservative complacency and leftist self-delusion in Ralph Ellison’s Invisible Man (1952).

浪漫发生在理想世界，讽刺/反讽发生在现实世界，而其余两种神话则涉及从理想世界到现实世界的转变。悲剧涉及从理想世界到现实世界的转变，从纯真到世故，从夏日神话到冬日神话的转变，因此弗莱称悲剧为秋日神话。在悲剧中，一位拥有超越一切潜能的英雄，如同浪漫英雄一般，从浪漫的巅峰跌落到现实世界——一个充满失落和失败的世界，从此再也无法重返巅峰。著名的悲剧作品包括索福克勒斯的《俄狄浦斯王》 （公元前五世纪）、莎士比亚的《哈姆雷特》（1601年）和《奥赛罗》（1604年），以及玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818年）。

While romance occurs within an ideal world and irony/satire occurs within the real world, the remaining two mythoi involve a movement from one of these worlds to the other.
