Tragedy involves a movement from the ideal world to the real world, from innocence to experience, from the mythos of summer to the mythos of winter, and therefore Frye calls tragedy the mythos of autumn. In tragedy, a hero with the potential to be superior, like a romantic hero, falls from his romantic height into the real world, the world of loss and defeat, from which he can never rise. Well-known examples of tragedy include Sophocles’ Oedipus the King (fifth century BC), Shakespeare’s Hamlet (1601) and Othello (1604), and Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818).

与此相反，喜剧讲述的是从现实世界到理想世界、从经验到纯真、从冬日神话到夏日神话的转变，因此弗莱称喜剧为“春天的神话”。在喜剧中，主人公身陷现实世界的重重困境，却通过情节的曲折变化，最终克服重重阻碍，获得幸福。与阻碍浪漫英雄的反派不同，喜剧中阻碍主人公的角色往往荒诞滑稽。最终，主人公通常会与心爱之人一起，从冷酷无情的现实世界走向更加幸福、友善、温柔的虚构世界。你可能熟悉的喜剧作品包括莎士比亚的《错误的喜剧》（1590）和《仲夏夜之梦》（1595）、威廉·威彻利的《乡村妻子》（1675）以及亨利·菲尔丁的《汤姆·琼斯》（1749）。

In contrast, comedy involves a movement from the real world to the ideal, from experience to innocence, from the mythos of winter to the mythos of summer, and therefore Frye calls comedy the mythos of spring. In comedy, a protagonist caught in a web of threatening, real-world difficulties manages, through various twists in the plot, to overcome the circumstances that have thwarted him and attain happiness. Unlike the villains who obstruct romantic heroes, those who obstruct the protagonists of comedy are absurd and humorous. And in the end, the protagonist moves, usually with his or her beloved, from the cold, troublesome real world to a happier, kinder, gentler fictional space. Examples of comedy you may be familiar with include Shakespeare’s Comedy of Errors (1590) and A Midsummer Night’s Dream (1595), William Wycherley’s The Country Wife (1675), and Henry Fielding’s Tom Jones (1749).

以上对弗莱框架的描述仅仅是他详细分析每种神话体系及其相关类型的一个框架。他认为，每种类型都对应着一套特定的主题、人物类型、氛围、动作类型以及上述情节模式。这四种类型共同构成了一种主线情节，或者说是理解叙事整体的关键。在弗莱看来，这个主线情节就是探寻之旅的结构，而每种神话体系都代表着探寻之旅的一个环节。

This description of Frye’s framework is merely a skeletal map of his detailed analysis of each mythos and the genre to which it is related. He argues that each genre identifies itself with a particular repertoire of themes, character types, moods, kinds of action, and versions of the plot formulas summarized above. Taken together, the four genres form a kind of master plot, or key to understanding narrative as a whole. And for Frye, that master plot is the structure of the quest, of which each mythos represents one leg.

弗莱指出，传统的冒险故事包含四个结构要素：冲突、灾难、混乱和胜利。他观察到，冲突是浪漫故事的基础，浪漫故事由一系列奇幻冒险组成，其中超级英雄们遭遇重重阻碍。灾难是悲剧的基础，悲剧讲述的是英雄的陨落。混乱和困惑是讽刺和反讽的基础，它们要求混乱和无政府状态占据主导地位，有效的行动成为不可能。而胜利是喜剧的基础，在喜剧中，主人公及其爱人成为某种改良社会秩序的核心。因此，浪漫故事、悲剧、讽刺/反讽和喜剧这四种类型——按此顺序——共同构成了弗莱所谓的“整体冒险神话”的结构。因此，对于弗莱认为，所有叙事在结构上都是相互关联的，因为它们都是任务公式的某种形式或某种组成部分。

Frye notes that the traditional quest has four structural components: conflict, catastrophe, disorder and confusion, and triumph. Conflict, he observes, is the basis of romance, which consists of a series of fantastic adventures in which superheroes encounter obstacles. Catastrophe is the basis of tragedy, which consists of the hero’s downfall. Disorder and confusion are the basis of irony and satire, which require that confusion and anarchy reign supreme and that effective action be impossible. And triumph is the basis of comedy, in which the protagonist and his or her beloved become the centerpiece of some sort of improved social order. Taken together, then, the genres of romance, tragedy, irony/satire, and comedy – in that order – spell out the structure of what Frye calls a “total quest-myth.” Thus, for Frye, all narrative is structurally related because it’s all some version of some part of the quest formula.

弗莱将这种分类方法称为原型批评，因为它关注的是西方文学史上某些叙事模式的反复出现。原型一词指的是任何反复出现的意象、人物类型、情节模式或行为模式。因此，原型是一种超类型或模型，其不同版本在人类创作史上反复出现：在我们的神话、文学、梦境、宗教和社会行为仪式中。弗莱的方法旨在探寻西方文学传统背后的结构原则。事实上，原型本身就具有结构性：要成为原型，一个意象、人物类型或其他叙事元素必须作为一种结构模型，能够生成自身的众多不同版本，也就是说，生成具有相同底层结构的众多不同表面现象。因此，尽管特定浪漫故事、悲剧、讽刺/反讽叙事和喜剧的具体内容各不相同——也就是说，它们的表面现象各不相同——但每种体裁的结构却保持不变。

Frye calls this method of classification archetypal criticism because it deals with the recurrence of certain narrative patterns throughout the history of Western literature. The word archetype refers to any recurring image, character type, plot formula, or pattern of action. An archetype, then, is a kind of supertype, or model, different versions of which recur throughout the history of human production: in our myths, literature, dreams, religions, and rituals of social behavior. Frye’s method thus seeks the structural principles that underlie the Western literary tradition. Indeed, archetypes are themselves structural in nature: in order to be an archetype, an image, character type, or other narrative element must serve as a structural model that generates numerous different versions of itself, that is, numerous different surface phenomena with the same underlying structure. So while the specific content of particular romances, tragedies, ironic/satiric narratives, and comedies is different – that is, their surface phenomena are different – the structure of each genre remains the same.2

弗莱探寻西方文学传统中各种体裁结构原则的另一种方法是他称之为“模式理论”的方法。他将小说分为不同的模式，依据是主人公的行动能力，并将其与其他人以及环境（自然和/或社会）的力量进行比较。弗莱的模式划分还取决于主人公是本质上优于他人（例如神或半神，这种能力超越常人），还是仅仅程度上优于他人（拥有所有人都具备的积极特质，但程度更胜一筹）。或许一张图表有助于阐明弗莱的体系。

Another method with which Frye seeks the structural principles that govern genres in the Western literary tradition he calls his theory of modes. His classification of fiction into modes is based on the protagonist’s power to take action as it compares to the power of other men and to the power of their environment (nature and/or society). Frye’s modes are also determined according to whether the protagonist is superior in kind to others (of a type beyond the reach of ordinary people, like gods or demigods) or merely superior in degree (having the same positive attributes that all humans are capable of but having them to a greater degree). Perhaps a chart will help clarify Frye’s system.

弗莱指出，神话虽然是早期叙事形式，但大多不属于通常的文学范畴。因此，也因为将喜剧和现实主义归为同一类似乎有些奇怪，罗伯特·斯科尔斯提出了弗莱模式的另一种版本。他认为，通过剔除非文学的神话模式，并引入一个新的类别来解释喜剧和现实主义之间的差异，这种新版本能够为区分不同体裁提供更清晰、更有用的基础。以下是斯科尔斯分类系统的图表。

Frye notes that, for the most part, myths, though early forms of narrative, fall outside the usual literary categories. For this reason, and because it seems somewhat odd to include comedy and realism under the same heading, Robert Scholes offers a different version of Frye’s modes, one he believes will provide a more clear and useful basis of differentiation among genres by eliminating the nonliterary mode of myth and inserting a new category in order to account for the difference between comedy and realism. Here’s a chart outlining Scholes’ system of classification.

正如这两张图表所示，不同的结构主义者对同一材料可能采用不同的分类方法。而且，关于体裁的结构主义理论远不止本文所列举的这些。这种结构分析是一种持续不断的尝试，旨在通过寻找最有效的方式来呈现支配整个文学的结构体系，从而对文学文本进行分类，进而理解它们之间的关系。

As these two charts indicate, different structuralists can have different ways of categorizing the same material. And there are many more structuralist theories of genre than those outlined here. This kind of structural analysis is an ongoing attempt to classify and thereby understand the relationships among literary texts by finding the most useful way to represent the structural system governing literature as a whole.

叙事结构（结构主义叙事学）

The structure of narrative (structuralist narratology)

叙事结构主义分析细致入微地考察文学文本的内部“运作机制”，旨在发现支配文本叙事运作的基本结构单元（例如叙事进程单元）或功能（例如人物功能）。如今被称为叙事学的大量文学批评与这种结构主义方法有着密切的联系。我们将仅选取三个具有代表性的例子，我认为它们对于您现阶段理解结构主义最为有益：A.J. Greimas、Tzvetan Todorov 和 Gérard Genette 的著作。

Structuralist analyses of narrative examine in minute detail the inner “workings” of literary texts in order to discover the fundamental structural units (such as units of narrative progression) or functions (such as character functions) that govern texts’ narrative operations. A good deal of literary criticism that today goes under the name narratology bears a strong family resemblance to this kind of structuralist approach. We’ll limit ourselves to three examples that are representative of the field in general and that I think you’ll find most useful at this stage in your understanding of structuralism: the work of A. J. Greimas, Tzvetan Todorov, and Gérard Genette.

格雷马斯观察到，人类通过将世界构建成两种对立关系来赋予意义：“A是B的反面”和“-A（A的否定）是-B（B的否定）的反面”。换句话说，我们感知到的每一个事物都具有两个方面：它的对立面（爱的反面是恨）和它的否定（爱的否定是爱的缺失）。他认为，这种由四个组成部分两两组合而成的二元对立的基本结构，塑造了我们的语言、经验以及我们用来表达经验的叙事方式。

Greimas observes that human beings make meaning by structuring the world in terms of two kinds of opposed pairs: “A is the opposite of B” and “−A (the negation of A) is the opposite of −B (the negation of B).” In other words, we perceive every entity as having two aspects: its opposite (the opposite of love is hate) and its negation (the negation of love is the absence of love). He believes that this fundamental structure of binary oppositions, consisting of four components arranged in two pairs, shapes our language, our experience, and the narratives through which we articulate our experience.

在我们的叙事中，这种结构体现为情节模式，例如冲突与解决、斗争与和解、分离与结合。这些情节模式由行动者或角色功能来实现，行动者或角色功能是故事中实际角色（表面现象）所扮演的角色。例如，在《了不起的盖茨比》中，我们可以认为杰伊·盖茨比是寻求真理的英雄，黛西·费·布坎南是英雄寻求真理的对象，尼克·卡拉威是英雄的助手，而汤姆·布坎南是英雄的对手。

In our narratives, this structure is embodied in the form of plot formulas, such as conflict and resolution, struggle and reconciliation, and separation and union. These plot formulas are carried out by means of actants, or character functions, which are slots filled by the actual characters (surface phenomena) in a given story. For example, in The Great Gatsby, we might argue that Jay Gatsby functions as the quester hero, Daisy Fay Buchanan as the object of the hero’s quest, Nick Carraway as the hero’s helper, and Tom Buchanan as the hero’s opponent.

在格雷马斯看来，情节的推进——从冲突到解决、从斗争到和解、从分离到结合等等——涉及某种实体（例如物体或特质）从一个行动者转移到另一个行动者。例如，黛西从汤姆转移到盖茨比，或者更准确地说，是从盖茨比转移到汤姆，再从汤姆转移到盖茨比，最后又回到汤姆。再举一个更微妙的例子，盖茨比的巨大损失——失去黛西、失去幸福梦想、失去生命——以尼克在纽约之行结束时的深刻幻灭的形式转移到了他身上。因此，叙事的基本结构与语言的基本结构相同：主语-谓语-宾语。这种基本的叙事语法通过将格雷马斯认为的六个基本行动者排列成三对对立关系，生成了以下三种情节模式。

For Greimas, the forwarding of the plot – the movement from conflict to resolution, struggle to reconciliation, separation to union, and so forth – involves the transfer of some entity (such as an object or a quality) from one actant to another. For example, Daisy is transferred from Tom to Gatsby or, more precisely, from Gatsby to Tom to Gatsby then back to Tom. And, to consider a more subtle example, Gatsby’s overwhelming loss – of Daisy, of his dream of happiness, of his life – is transferred to Nick in the form of the latter’s profound disillusionment at the end of his sojourn in New York. Thus, the fundamental structure of narrative is the same as the fundamental structure of language: subject-verb-object. This basic narrative grammar generates the following three patterns of plots by aligning what Greimas sees as the six fundamental actants into three pairs of oppositions.

演员

Actants

地块类型

Plot types

主语-宾语

Subject–Object

寻觅/渴望的故事（主人公或英雄寻找某个对象：人、物或存在状态）

Stories of Quest/Desire (a subject, or hero, searches for an object: a person, thing, or state of being)

发送方-接收方

Sender–Receiver

沟通的故事（发送者——人、神或机构——派遣主体去寻找客体，接收者最终收到客体）

Stories of Communication (a sender – a person, god, or institution – sends the subject in search of the object, which the receiver ultimately receives)

帮助者-对手

Helper–Opponent

故事的支线情节：探寻/欲望或交流（帮助者协助主人公完成探寻；对手试图阻挠主人公）

Subplots of Stories of Quest/Desire or Communication (a helper aids the subject in the quest; an opponent tries to hinder the subject)

最后，为了解释各种可能的叙事顺序，格雷马斯提出了以下结构，这些结构是他从对民间故事的研究中得出的。

Finally, in order to account for various possible narrative sequences, Greimas suggests the following structures, which he derived from his study of folk tales.

1 合同结构涉及协议的订立/破坏或禁令的制定/违反，以及随之而来的疏远或和解。

1 Contractual structures involve the making/breaking of agreements or the establishment/violation of prohibitions and the alienation or reconciliation that follows.

2 表演性结构涉及任务的执行、尝试、斗争等等。

2 Performative structures involve the performance of tasks, trials, struggles, and the like.

3 分离结构涉及旅行、移动、到达和离开。

3 Disjunctive structures involve travel, movement, arrivals, and departures.

例如，我们可以探讨《了不起的盖茨比》如何符合格雷马斯关于契约结构的概念，包括已达成和已打破的协议（例如盖茨比和黛西、汤姆和黛西、尼克和乔丹以及默特尔和乔治之间的协议），以及小说中发生的众多违反禁令的行为，这些行为随后导致了疏离。

We might explore, for instance, the ways in which The Great Gatsby conforms to Greimas’ notion of contractual structures, including both agreements made and broken (such as those between Gatsby and Daisy, Tom and Daisy, Nick and Jordan, and Myrtle and George) and the numerous violations of prohibitions occurring in the novel that are followed by alienation.

格雷马斯运用他的体系分析了二十世纪法国作家乔治·贝尔纳诺斯的作品，得出结论：这位小说家创造了一个所有冲突最终都归结为生与死这一根本象征性冲突的世界。此外，格雷马斯认为，这一关键冲突体现在以下结构中（我已对其进行简化），该结构支配着作者的虚构世界。贝尔纳诺斯小说的语法由此构建了一个世界：在这个世界里，我们只有放弃快乐才能避免痛苦，因为快乐与痛苦是紧密相连的：我们感受快乐的能力使我们更容易受到痛苦的侵袭。因此，我们要么必须接受人生是一把双刃剑——快乐与痛苦并存——的真理（尽管我们最初往往会抗拒这一真理），要么就必须拒绝真理，并接受唯一的选择：厌倦和厌恶，这是一种情感上的死亡，我们选择它是为了保护自己免受人生情感风险的侵害。

Greimas uses his system to analyze the works of twentieth-century French author Georges Bernanos, concluding that the novelist creates a world in which all conflicts reduce to the fundamental symbolic conflict between life and death. Furthermore, this key conflict expresses itself, Greimas suggests, in the following structure (which I have simplified) that governs the author’s fictional universe. The grammar of Bernanos’ novels thus structures a world in which we can avoid feeling pain only if we are willing to give up joy as well, for the two are linked: our capacity to feel joy makes us vulnerable to pain. Thus, we must either accept the truth that life is a double-edged sword of joy and pain (though we tend, initially, to revolt against that truth), or we must refuse the truth and resign ourselves to the only alternative: boredom and disgust, which are a kind of emotional death we choose in order to protect ourselves from the emotional risks of life.

托多罗夫以与格雷马斯类似的方式，将叙事的结构单位（如人物刻画和情节的要素）与语言的结构单位（词类及其在句子和段落中的排列）进行了类比。

In a manner similar to that of Greimas, Todorov draws an analogy between the structural units of narrative – such as elements of characterization and plot – and the structural units of language: parts of speech and their arrangement in sentences and paragraphs.

命题由人物与不可简化的动作（例如，“X 杀死 Y”或“X 来到镇上”）或不可简化的属性（例如，“X 是邪恶的”或“X 是女王”）组合而成，即动作或属性的最基本形式。序列是一系列命题，可以独立构成一个故事。最基本的序列结构为：(1) 属性，(2) 动作，(3) 属性：主人公一开始具有某种属性（例如，他不被爱），然后通过一个动作（他寻求爱）使该属性发生转变（他被爱，或者至少在寻求爱的过程中学到了重要的东西）。一个故事必须至少包含一个序列，但也可以包含多个序列。托多罗夫进一步将他的结构体系细分为否定（动作或属性的缺失）、比较（动作或属性的不同程度的存在）和模式（动作或属性的限定，例如当动作或属性是渴望的、害怕的、期望的、不情愿地完成的等等）等类别。

A proposition is formed by combining a character with an irreducible action (for example, “X kills Y” or “X arrives in town”) or irreducible attribute (for example, “X is evil” or “X is queen”), that is, an action or attribute in its most basic form. A sequence is a string of propositions that can stand on its own as a story. The structure of the most basic sequence is (1) attribution, (2) action, (3) attribution: the protagonist starts out with an attribute (for example, he is unloved), and by means of an action (he seeks love) that attribute is transformed (he is loved or, at least, has learned something important as a result of his quest). A story must contain at least one sequence, though it may contain many sequences. Todorov further subdivides his structural system into such categories as negation (the absence of an action or attribute), comparison (the presence of an action or attribute to different degrees), and modes (the qualification of an action or attribute, such as occurs when an action or attribute is desired, feared, expected, done unwillingly, and the like).

这种叙事“语法”使托多罗夫能够根据他所认为的文本基本叙事属性来分析文本。一旦文本的命题被发现——通过将每个角色（名词）与一个动作（动词）或属性（形容词）结合起来——文本中反复出现的动作和属性类型，以及命题类型和命题之间的关系，都可以被分类。例如，在分析薄伽丘的《十日谈》（1350年）中的故事时，托多罗夫发现，所有属性都可以归纳为三类形容词：状态（不稳定的属性，例如快乐和不快乐）、性质 （更稳定的属性，如善与恶），以及条件（最稳定的属性，如性别、宗教或社会地位）。

This “grammar” of narrative allows Todorov to analyze texts in terms of what he sees as their fundamental narrative properties. Once a text’s propositions are discovered – by combining each character (noun) with an action (verb) or attribute (adjective) – the kinds of actions and attributes that recur in a text can be categorized as can the kinds of propositions and the relations between propositions. For example, in his analysis of the stories in Boccaccio’s The Decameron (1350), Todorov finds, among other things, that all attributes can be reduced to three categories of adjectives: states (unstable attributes, such as happiness and unhappiness), qualities (more stable attributes, such as good and evil), and conditions (the most stable attributes, such as one’s sex, religion, or social position).

我认为，他提出的《十日谈》中所有行为都可以归结为三个动词的观点尤为重要：改变、违背和惩罚。这一发现使他观察到故事中一个显著的重复模式：变化不断发生，而罪恶却始终逍遥法外。这一模式以及他对历史的了解，促使托多罗夫推测，薄伽丘故事中体现的价值观与他所处的文化环境之间存在某种联系。托多罗夫认为，无论是《十日谈》还是薄伽丘的世界，一种新的价值体系都在兴起，这种体系推崇与自由企业资本主义体系相关的个人勇气和进取心，而这种体系正逐渐取代旧有的、更为封闭的商业体系。

Especially significant, I think, is his claim that all actions in The Decameron can be reduced to three verbs: to modify, to transgress, and to punish. For this discovery led to his observation of a significant pattern of recurrence in the tales: changes are continually made, and sins continually go unpunished. This pattern, and his knowledge of history, led Todorov to speculate that there is a connection between the values operating in Boccaccio’s stories and those of the culture in which he lived. Todorov suggests that, in both The Decameron and Boccaccio’s world, a new system of values was emerging, one that appreciated the personal daring and initiative associated with the free-enterprise system of capitalism, which was beginning to replace the older, more restrictive system of commerce.

值得注意的是，格雷马斯和托多罗夫都从大量的材料中汲取灵感并运用这些材料构建他们的理论框架——格雷马斯使用了一位作家的全部作品，而托多罗夫则使用了一部由故事集组成的长篇著作——因为他们都希望构建一个有助于理解叙事的结构体系。同样，热奈特也通过对马塞尔·普鲁斯特七卷本巨著《追忆似水年华》（1927）的细致研究来发展他的叙事理论。

It is important to note that both Greimas and Todorov derive their frameworks from and apply them to a large body of materials – Greimas uses all the works of a single author, and Todorov uses a long work that consists of a collection of tales – because they want to produce a structural system useful for understanding narrative in general. Similarly, Genette develops his narrative theory by means of a detailed study of Marcel Proust’s seven-volume work, Remembrance of Things Past (1927).

热奈特首先区分了叙事的三个层次，这三个层次通常都包含在“叙事”一词的范畴之内：故事、叙事和叙述。

Genette begins by differentiating among three levels of narrative that generally have been included under the umbrella of the term narrative: story, narrative, and narration.

故事由一系列被叙述的事件组成。因此，故事的内容按照事件“实际发生”在人物身上的顺序呈现，而这一顺序并不总是与它们在叙述中呈现的顺序一致。

Story consists of the succession of events being narrated. The story thus provides the content of the tale in the order in which events “actually happened” to the characters, an order that does not always coincide with the order in which they are presented in the narrative.

叙事指的是页面上的实际文字，即话语，文本本身，读者从中构建故事和叙述。叙事是由叙述者在叙述行为中产生的。

Narrative refers to the actual words on the page, the discourse, the text itself, from which the reader constructs both story and narration. The narrative is produced by the narrator in the act of narration.

叙述是指将故事讲述给特定受众，从而形成叙事的行为。然而，正如叙述者几乎不可能与作者完全一致一样，受众（被叙述者）也几乎不可能与读者完全一致。

Narration refers to the act of telling the story to some audience and thereby producing the narrative. However, just as the narrator almost never corresponds exactly to the author, the audience (narratee) almost never corresponds exactly to the reader.

例如，在《了不起的盖茨比》中，尼克向一些听众描述了他在纽约的夏天（叙述）。通过这种方式，他呈现了一种口头话语，我们看到的就是纸上的文字（叙述）。而这种话语又代表了尼克作为人物出现的一系列事件（故事）。

For example, in The Great Gatsby, Nick describes his summer in New York to some audience (narration). In doing so, he presents a verbal discourse, which we see as the words on the page (narrative). And that discourse represents the events in which Nick appears as a character (story).

热奈特的著作侧重于叙事，即纸上的文字，但他指出这三个层面是相互关联的。也就是说，为了分析的目的，他将这三个层面区分开来。文本的各个方面并非各自独立运作，但他将它们分开来看，是为了观察它们之间的相互作用。他观察到，故事、叙事和叙述通过三种特质相互作用，他称之为时态、氛围和语调。

Genette’s work focuses on narrative, the words on the page, but he notes that all three levels work together. That is, for the purposes of analysis, he separates aspects of a text that don’t operate separately, but he does so in order to see how they interact. And he observes that story, narrative, and narration interact by means of three qualities, which he calls tense, mood, and voice.

1 时态是指叙事中事件在时间上的排列方式。这种排列方式涉及顺序、持续时间和频率等概念。

1 Tense is the arrangement of events in the narrative with respect to time. That arrangement involves the notions of order, duration, and frequency.

一个 顺序指的是故事的时间顺序（故事中事件在虚构世界中发生的顺序）与叙述的时间顺序（叙述呈现这些事件的顺序）之间的关系。例如，杰伊·盖茨比的故事部分由以下事实构成，其顺序如下：他出生于贫苦的农民家庭，离家出走，为丹·科迪工作，追求黛西，参战，归来，并开始积累财富，最终赢得黛西的芳心。然而，叙述呈现这些事件的顺序却有所不同。例如，直到第六章我们才了解到他的童年经历。

a Order refers to the relationship between the chronology of the story (the order in which the events of the story occur in the fictional world) and the chronology of the narrative (the order in which the narrative presents those events). For example, Jay Gatsby’s story consists, in part, of the following facts in the following order: he was born to poor farmers, ran away from home, worked for Dan Cody, courted Daisy, went to war, returned, and set about acquiring a fortune and reclaiming Daisy. However, the narrative presents these events in a different order. For example, we don’t learn about his boyhood until chapter 6.

b 时长指的是故事中某一事件发生的时间长度与描述该事件所用叙述篇幅之间的关系。例如，一个角色的欧洲之旅在故事中可能持续了五年，但叙述可能只用了五行文字来描述。反之，恋人之间的对话在故事中可能只持续了五分钟，但叙述却可能用了五页篇幅来描述。因此，时长决定了叙事的速度感。

b Duration refers to the relationship between the length of time over which a given event occurs in the story and the number of pages of narrative devoted to describing it. A character’s trip to Europe may last five years in the story, but the narrative may describe it in five lines. Conversely, a conversation between lovers may take five minutes in the story, but the narrative may describe it in five pages. Thus, duration is what produces the sense of narrative speed.

c 频率涉及事件在故事中（同一事件可能多次发生）和叙述中（同一事件可能多次描述）重复出现的方式之间的关系。

c Frequency involves the relationship between the ways in which events may be repeated in the story (the same event may occur more than once) and in the narrative (a single event may be described more than once).

2 氛围是由距离和视角营造出的叙事氛围。

2 Mood is the atmosphere of the narrative created by distance and perspective.

一个 当叙述者本身就是叙事中的一个角色，一个“中间人”，故事通过他的意识被过滤时，距离感便产生了。叙述者的介入程度越高，叙述与故事之间的距离就越大。相反，当我们意识不到叙述者的存在，故事仿佛“自行讲述”时，距离感最小。描述细节的缺失也会造成距离感。细节越少，真实感就越弱，叙述与故事之间的距离感就越强。细节越多，距离感就越小。因此，信息量最大、叙述者存在感最小，才能产生最小的距离感，或者说最接近真实的生活体验。

a Distance is created when the narrator is one of the characters in the narrative, a “go-between” through whose consciousness the story is filtered. The more intrusive the narrator, the greater the distance between narration and story. Conversely, the least distance is created when we are unaware of the narrator’s presence, when a tale seems to “tell itself.” Distance is also created by the absence of descriptive detail. The less detail given, the less the effect of reality is created, and the greater the sense of distance between narration and story. The more detail given, the less distance exists. Thus, the least distance, or the greatest imitation of life, is produced by maximum information and minimum presence of the narrator.

b 视角指的是观点，或者说是我们看待叙事中某一特定部分的视角。虽然叙述者可能正在讲述故事，但视角却可能是其他角色的，而叙述者对故事的感受可能与叙述者的感受不同。

b Perspective refers to point of view, or the eyes through which we see any given part of the narrative. Although the narrator may be speaking, the point of view may be that of one of the other characters, and the feelings of a point-of-view character may be different from those of the narrator telling that character’s story.

3 声音指的是叙述者的声音。我们听到的声音（叙述者的声音）可能与我们透过眼睛看到的景象（视角）不同。分析声音时，我们分析的是叙述者（叙述行为）与所讲述的故事以及叙事方式（故事的讲述方式）之间的关系。声音有助于我们判断叙述者对故事的态度和可靠性。

3 Voice refers to the voice of the narrator. The voice we hear (the narrator’s) may not be the same as the eyes we see through (the perspective). When we analyze voice, we analyze the relationship of the narrator (the act of narration) to the story being told and to the narrative (the way the story is being told). Voice helps us determine the narrator’s attitude toward the story and reliability.

值得注意的是，时态、语气和语态都是动词的方面。因为在热奈特看来，所有虚构作品都像一个扩展的动词：所有叙事最终都归结为行动。尽管他的定义看似“一目了然”，但他构建这些分类体系，很大程度上是为了能够揭示文学文本何时通过“违反”这些分类体系来产生其效果。例如，在对《追忆似水年华》的研究中，热奈特指出普鲁斯特如何通过将最大程度的信息呈现与叙述者最大程度的在场感相结合，营造出一种强烈的即时感，一种叙述与故事之间高度的亲密关系——而这种效果通常是通过将最大程度的信息呈现与最小程度的叙述者在场感相结合来实现的。因此，热奈特强调，分类体系应该帮助我们阐明文学作品的复杂性，而不是通过过度简化来掩盖这种复杂性。

It is interesting to note that tense, mood, and voice are all aspects of verbs. For in Genette’s opinion, all fiction functions like an expanded verb: all narrative reduces to action. Although his definitions may seem “cut and dried,” he generates his categories, in large part, to be able to show when a literary text creates its effects by “violating” those categories. In his study of Remembrance of Things Past, for example, Genette shows how Proust creates an effect of intense immediacy, of great intimacy between narration and story, by combining maximum information with maximum presence of narrator, an effect that is traditionally produced by combining maximum information with minimum presence of narrator. Thus, Genette underscores the notion that systems of classification should be used to help us illuminate the complexity of literary works, not obscure that complexity through oversimplification.

当然，格雷马斯、托多罗夫和热奈特的著作远比这篇概述所暗示的要复杂得多。我们在此的目的仅仅在于理解结构主义叙事学所能进行的分析类型。或许可以将这种方法想象成用显微镜观察叙事，从而识别其最小单元并了解其运作方式。因此，结构主义叙事学为我们提供了一种观察叙事运作细节的方法，以及一套描述这些细节的词汇。

Of course, the work of Greimas, Todorov, and Genette is far more complex than this summary implies. Our purpose here is simply to understand the kinds of analyses made possible by structuralist narratology. It might be helpful to think of this approach as looking at narrative through a microscope in order to identify its smallest units and see how they work. Structuralist narratology thus offers us a way of seeing the details of narrative operations and a vocabulary with which to describe them.

然而，值得注意的是，格雷马斯、托多罗夫和热奈特一旦识别出构成叙事或叙事群的模式，便会运用该模式来探讨关于文学意义及其与人类生活关系的更宏大的问题。也就是说，一旦我们识别出特定叙事或叙事群的模式，我们就必须扪心自问：“这种模式如何揭示叙事的一般模式？这种模式又对人类经验或人类意识的结构有何启示？”换言之，特定的叙事模式如何增进我们对人类数千年来讲述的相对较少的故事的理解（尽管这些故事可能呈现数百种不同的形式，但从结构上看，它们仍然是相同的故事），从而帮助人类应对生活？因为任何形式的结构主义分析的核心都在于理解“人”的意义。

It is important to note, however, that Greimas, Todorov, and Genette, once they identify the formula that structures a narrative or group of narratives, use that formula to address larger questions about literary meaning and its relationship to human life. That is, once we identify the formula of a given narrative or group of narratives, we must then ask ourselves, “How does this formula reveal a pattern in narrative in general, and what does this pattern imply about human experience or the structures of human consciousness?” In other words, what does a given narrative pattern contribute to our knowledge of the relatively small number of stories human beings have been telling themselves for thousands of years (though the stories may take hundreds of different forms, they are still, structurally, the same stories) in order to help themselves cope with life? For at the heart of structuralist analysis of any kind is the desire to understand what it means to be human.

文学阐释的结构

The structure of literary interpretation

根据乔纳森·库勒的说法，支配文学文本写作和阐释的结构体系是规则和规范体系，我们拥有无论是有意识的还是无意识的，这些规则和准则都内化于心，告诉我们阅读文学作品时如何理解其意义。其中一些规则和准则被大众视为理所当然（例如，童话故事是虚构的，不能按字面意思理解），但许多规则和准则是在课堂上学到的（例如，自然意象的运用能够揭示作品的主题）。

According to Jonathan Culler, the structural system that governs both the writing and interpretation of literary texts is the system of rules and codes, which we have consciously or unconsciously internalized, that tell us how to make meaning when we read literature. Some of these rules and codes are taken for granted by the public at large (for example, that a fairy tale is a fictional story not to be taken literally), but many of them are learned in the classroom (for example, that the use of nature imagery reveals a good deal about a work’s theme).

在美国，这套规则和准则体系是西方文学传统的一部分，由我们的大学传承至今，而我们个人的文学素养取决于我们对这套体系的内化程度。关键不在于两位合格的读者对同一作品的解读必然一致，而在于他们的解读都遵循着同一套阐释规则和准则的结构体系。因此，库勒认为，我们所谓的文学结构，实际上是我们赋予作品的阐释体系的结构。他的努力在于揭示这套结构体系，并向我们展示它的运作方式。或许，要让读者熟悉库勒所提出的这套结构体系，最好的方法就是简单地描述它的一些主要组成部分，他将其命名为：距离和非人格化的惯例、自然化、意义规则、隐喻连贯性规则以及主题统一性规则。

In America, this system of rules and codes is part of the Western literary tradition as it has been passed on by our universities, and our individual literary competence is determined by how much of the system we have internalized. The point is not that any two competent readers would necessarily agree in their interpretations of a particular work but that both interpretations would be guided by the same structural system of interpretive rules and codes. Culler thus believes that what we refer to as the structure of literature is really the structure of the system of interpretation we bring to it. His effort is to unearth this structural system and show us how it operates. Perhaps the best way to acquaint you with the structural system Culler has identified is simply to describe some of its major components, which he has named as follows: the convention of distance and impersonality, naturalization, the rule of significance, the rule of metaphorical coherence, and the rule of thematic unity.

一旦我们意识到自己正在阅读一部文学作品，即便这部作品并非文学作品，而是信件（如巴塞尔姆的小说《睡魔》，1972）或日记（如多丽丝·莱辛的《幸存者回忆录》，1974），我们便会默认存在距离感和非人格化的惯例。一旦我们意识到自己阅读的是小说或诗歌，而非信件或日记，我们的阅读方式便会与阅读真实的信件或日记截然不同：我们知道自己正进入一个虚构的世界，这便创造了一种虚构的距离感，这种距离感本身就带有某种非人格化的特质。如果我们知道自己正在阅读的是对某人个人经历的真实记述，这种特质感便不会存在。距离感和非人格化的惯例，正是所有后续规则得以发挥作用的基础。

The convention of distance and impersonality is an assumption we make as soon as we see that we are reading a literary work, even if that work is in the form of nonliterary writing, such as a letter (like Barthelme’s story “The Sandman,” 1972) or a journal (like Doris Lessing’s Memoirs of a Survivor, 1974). As soon as we know we’re reading a piece of fiction or poetry rather than a letter or journal, we read it differently than we would read a real letter or journal: we know we’re entering a fictional world, and this creates a fictional distance, so to speak, that carries with it a kind of impersonality that would not be present if we knew we were reading a factual account of a human being’s personal experience. The convention of distance and impersonality is the code that enables all the following codes to come into play.

自然化是指我们转化文本的过程，使文本中那些我们在日常写作中看不到的文学形式上的奇特之处——例如韵律、格律、分节、幕或章节的划分以及内心独白——在我们所生活的世界中变得有意义。例如，当我们读到“我的爱人是一颗成熟的梨”时，我们不会认为叙述者爱上了一颗水果；我们会认为他是在用比喻的说法。即使我们将文学语言的美感和奇特之处转化为我们能够理解的概念，我们仍然会欣赏它。此外，我们通常会认为自己听到的是叙述者的声音，而不是作者的声音，并且我们会将叙述中的任何不一致或偏见归因于叙述者的视角。我们自然化文本的其他方式还包括识别那些指导我们如何解读诸如人物和符号等文学元素的符号。例如，在现实生活中，我们不会相信……皮肤光滑细腻的人必然拥有光滑纯净的心灵，但我们只能在某些类型的虚构作品中接受这种关联。

Naturalization is the process by which we transform the text so that the strangeness of its literary form, which we don’t see in everyday writing – for example, rhyme; meter; divisions into stanzas, acts, or chapters; and interior monologues – makes sense in terms of the world we live in. When we read, for example, “My darling is a ripening pear,” we don’t think the narrator is in love with a piece of fruit; we assume he is speaking metaphorically. And we appreciate the beauty and strangeness of the literary language even as we translate it into an idea we understand. Furthermore, we generally assume we are hearing the voice of a narrator, rather than that of the author, and it is to the narrator’s point of view that we ascribe any inconsistencies or biases in the narration. Other ways in which we naturalize the text include recognizing the codes that tell us how to interpret such literary elements as characters and symbols. For example, in real life we don’t believe that a person with fine, clear skin necessarily has a fine, clear soul, but we would accept this correlation in certain kinds of fiction.

意义原则假定文学作品表达了对某个重要问题的重要态度，因此我们会格外关注它所传达的信息，而对其他类型的作品则不会如此。如果我们的伴侣留下一张纸条，上面写着“我去古董店找灯了”，我们很可能会按字面意思理解：伴侣想买一盏古董灯。然而，如果把这句话拆分成一首四行诗，“我去”、“找”、“古董”和“灯”这几个词就会突然变得更有意义。例如，我们可能会得出这样的结论：这首诗表达了想要逃离当下某种不尽如人意的处境，回到过去，寻找一种此时此地无法获得的启迪的愿望。

The rule of significance is the assumption that the literary work expresses a significant attitude about some important problem, and so we pay attention to what it says in ways that we wouldn’t do with other kinds of writing. If our spouse left us a note saying “I’ve gone to the antique store in search of a lamp,” we’d probably take the message at face value: our spouse wants to buy an antique lamp. If this same sentence were broken into a four-line poem, however, the words “I’ve gone,” “in search,” “antique,” and “lamp” would suddenly take on greater resonance. We might conclude, for example, that the poem represents the desire to escape some unsatisfactory situation in the present in order to return to the past and find some kind of enlightenment that can’t be found in the here and now.

隐喻连贯性原则要求隐喻的两个组成部分（隐喻的载体或隐喻词，以及隐喻所指的对象或本体）在作品语境中必须保持一致的关系。例如，想象一个故事，讲述的是一位身无分文、年迈的印第安流浪汉的悲惨遭遇，故事结尾，他在冰冷的夜空下长眠不醒。在这种情况下，对苍白冬日落日的描写可以隐喻人物的死亡，甚至可能象征一个时代的终结，但它不太可能象征着美好新生活开始前那段安稳的睡眠。

The rule of metaphorical coherence is the requirement that the two components of a metaphor (the vehicle, or metaphorical term, and the tenor, or subject to which the metaphor is applied) have a consistent relationship within the context of the work. Imagine, for example, a story about the plight of a penniless, aging, Native American drifter who, at the close of the tale, falls asleep forever under a freezing sky. In this context, the description of a pale, winter sunset could be a metaphor for the death of the character and perhaps for the end of an era, but it couldn’t very well be a metaphor for the restful sleep that precedes the hopeful beginning of a bright new life.

主题统一性原则是隐喻连贯性原则存在的主要原因，因为主题统一性原则体现了我们对文学作品具有统一、连贯的主题或中心思想的预期。事实上，正是因为我们预期文学作品具有主题统一性，我们几乎总能在解读文本时找到它，或者更准确地说，是构建它。库勒指出，我们倾向于通过某些程序来构建主题统一性，这些程序包括：（1）主题作为二元对立（善与恶）；（2）主题作为二元对立的解决（善战胜恶）；以及（3）主题作为二元对立被第三个要素所取代（善与恶被包罗万象的自然所吸收，正如我们在惠特曼1855年的《自我之歌》中所见）。

The rule of thematic unity is the chief reason why there is a rule of metaphorical coherence, for the rule of thematic unity is our expectation that the literary work has a unified, coherent theme, or main point. In fact, it is because we expect a literary work to have thematic unity that we almost always manage to find it or, more precisely, construct it when we interpret the text. We tend to create thematic unity, Culler observes, by means of certain procedures, which include, among others, (1) theme as a binary opposition (good versus evil), (2) theme as the resolution of a binary opposition (good conquers evil), and (3) theme as the displacement of a binary opposition by a third term (good-versus-evil is absorbed by an all-encompassing Nature, as we see in Whitman’s “Song of Myself,” 1855).

不难理解库勒的结构主义方法为何会引起读者反应理论家的兴趣。与第六章讨论的斯坦利·菲什的社会读者反应理论类似，库勒的方法也认为，我们对文学的理解基于我们运用到文本中的阐释策略。正如我们之前提到的，结构主义者认为，我们通过将自身的意识结构投射到我们所看到的世界中来“创造”它。将这种信念应用于文学，其结果与读者反应理论的观点相同，即我们在阅读过程中“创造”了文学文本。但库勒的结构主义策略在于他提出的问题：“在我们阐释的表面现象背后，究竟隐藏着怎样的结构？”为了找到答案，他将阐释视为一个结构系统进行考察。与读者反应理论家不同，库勒考察了语言，即西方文学传统中作者写作和读者解读时（有意识或无意识地）运作的规则和代码的结构系统。

It’s not difficult to see why Culler’s structuralist approach is of interest to reader-response theorists. Like the social reader-response theory of Stanley Fish discussed in Chapter 6, Culler’s approach asserts that our understanding of literature is based on the interpretive strategies we bring to the text. As we noted earlier, structuralists believe that we “create” the world we see by projecting onto it our structures of consciousness. Apply this belief to literature, and the result is the same as the reader-response notion that we “create” the literary text as we read it. But the structuralist move Culler makes is his question, “What is the structure that underlies the surface phenomena of our interpretations?” And to find the answer, he examines interpretation as a structural system. Unlike reader-response theorists, Culler examines the langue, the structural system of rules and codes, that operate (consciously or unconsciously) when authors write and readers interpret within the Western literary tradition.

即使这里提供的少量方法也说明了结构主义方法的广泛性，无论是在结构主义者使用的理论框架类型，还是在他们分析的文本类型（文学文本和其他文本）方面。

Even the small sampling of approaches offered here illustrates the wide range of structuralist methodologies, both in terms of the kinds of theoretical frameworks structuralists use and the kinds of texts, literary and otherwise, they analyze.

结构主义批评家对文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions structuralist critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在概括结构主义文学研究方法。需要注意的是，结构主义者并不试图判断一部文学作品是否堪称伟大文学。他们的关注点在于支撑和产生文学意义的结构体系。

The following questions are offered to summarize structuralist approaches to literature. Keep in mind that structuralists don’t try to determine whether or not a literary text constitutes great literature. Their focus is on the structural systems that underlie and generate literary meaning.

1使用特定的结构主义框架（例如我们研究过的弗莱和斯科尔斯的结构主义框架），应该如何根据文本的体裁对其进行分类？

1 Using a specific structuralist framework (such as the ones we examined by Frye and Scholes), how should the text be classified in terms of its genre?

2运用特定的结构主义框架（例如格雷马斯、托多罗夫或热奈特的框架），分析文本的叙事运作方式。你能否推测文本的“语法”与类似文本的“语法”之间的关系？你能否推测文本的语法与文本产生的文化之间的关系？

2 Using a specific structuralist framework (such as that of Greimas, Todorov, or Genette), analyze the text’s narrative operations. Can you speculate about the relationship between the text’s “grammar” and that of similar texts? Can you speculate about the relationship between the text’s grammar and the culture from which the text emerged?

3运用库勒的文学能力理论，为了“理解”文本，必须内化哪些解释规则或准则？根据文本的具体情况，除了库勒提出的准则之外，可能还需要识别其他准则。（换句话说，特定文本对我们理解文学能力有何贡献？）

3 Using Culler’s theory of literary competence, what rules or codes of interpretation must be internalized in order to “make sense” of the text? Depending on the text in question, it might be necessary to identify codes in addition to those specified by Culler. (In other words, what does a given text contribute to our knowledge of literary competence?)

4特定文化现象或“文本”类别的符号学意义是什么？例如，高中橄榄球赛、特定品牌香水（或其他消费品）的电视和/或杂志广告，甚至是媒体对历史事件的报道，如“沙漠风暴行动”、重要法律案件或总统竞选活动。换句话说，分析这些“文本”所传递的非语言信息，以及诸如“沙漠风暴”或“白钻”（一种香水品牌）等语言“标签”的符号学含义。它们传达了什么信息？又是如何传达的？

4 What are the semiotics of a given category of cultural phenomena, or “texts,” such as high school football games, television and/or magazine ads for a particular brand of perfume (or any other consumer product), or even media coverage of a historical event, such as Operation Desert Storm, an important legal case, or a presidential election campaign? In other words, analyze the nonverbal messages sent by the “texts” in question, as well as the semiotic implications of such verbal “tags” as “Desert Storm” or “White Diamonds” (a brand of perfume). What is being communicated, and how exactly is it being communicated?

根据所讨论的文学文本，我们可能会提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们可能会提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们思考如何从结构主义视角有效解读文学的起点。请记住，即使采用相同的方法，结构主义者对同一文本的解读也并非完全相同。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。我们的目标是……运用结构主义，我们可以洞察文学文本结构之间、文学结构与语言结构之间，以及各种文化现象（例如文学、神话、艺术、社会仪式、体育、娱乐形式和广告）结构之间的根本联系。构建一套系统、通用的术语体系来描述文学的基本结构，能够帮助我们进行更清晰、更严谨的比较，从而加深对文学创作和文学史运作机制的理解。

Depending on the literary text or texts in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just starting points to get us thinking about productive ways to approach literature from a structuralist perspective. Remember that not all structuralists will interpret the same texts in the same way, even if they use the same approach. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use structuralism to help us see some fundamental connections among the structures of literary texts, between the structure of literature and that of language, and among the structures of cultural phenomena of every sort, including, for example, literature, mythology, art, social rituals, sports, forms of entertainment, and advertising. The construction of a systematic, universal terminology to describe the fundamental structures of literature offers us the opportunity to make clearer and more rigorous comparisons as we try to increase our understanding of the processes at work in literary production and literary history.

以下对菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的结构主义解读，旨在展示结构主义分析该小说可能带来的成果。借鉴托多罗夫的叙事“语法”概念，我将论证小说中的所有行动都可以简化为三个动词：寻找、发现和失去。我认为，这种语法可以被解读为现代小说对传统“寻找与发现”模式的摒弃。此外，我将指出，《了不起的盖茨比》的“寻找-发现-失去”语法为我们提供了一种有趣的视角，让我们能够运用弗莱的神话理论来分析小说两条主要情节线——杰伊·盖茨比和尼克·卡拉威——之间的关系。

The following structuralist reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a structuralist analysis of that novel might yield. Drawing on Todorov’s notion of narrative “grammar,” I will argue that all of the action in the novel can be reduced to three verbs: to seek, to find, and to lose, which grammar can be interpreted, I think, as the modern novel’s rejection of the traditional seek-and-find quest formula. In addition, I will suggest that The Great Gatsby’s seek-find-lose grammar offers us an interesting way to use Frye’s theory of mythoi to analyze the relationship between the novel’s two principal plot-lines, those concerning Jay Gatsby and Nick Carraway.

“寻找，你必​​寻见”……然后失去：对《了不起的盖茨比》的结构主义解读

“Seek and ye shall find” … and then lose: a structuralist reading of The Great Gatsby

在许多方面，菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）的结构如此精巧，以至于小说的结构本身就引人注目。对文本结构对称性的简要描述便足以说明这一点。故事围绕着杰伊·盖茨比追求、获得并最终失去黛西·费·布坎南展开。正如我们在倒叙中了解到的，这次失败的追求实际上是盖茨比年轻时（小说开篇之前）对同一爱人的追求、获得和失去的重演。两次失败的追求都发生在短短几个月的时间里，而且盖茨比两次都隐瞒了自己的真实身份，因此，虚构的过去和虚构的现在之间存在着一种叙事上的对称性。另一种结构对称性出现在盖茨比与黛西在第五章重逢之时，这一章既是小说九章的物理中心，也是叙事行动的时间中心：当时是七月下旬，正值尼克六月初第一次拜访布坎南夫妇的新家，那时“夏天的历史才真正开始”（10；第一章），以及盖茨比九月初去世的中点。

In many ways, F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925) is so carefully organized that the novel’s structure seems to draw attention to itself. A brief description of the text’s structural symmetry should illustrate this point. The narrative revolves around Jay Gatsby’s pursuit, attainment, and loss of Daisy Fay Buchanan. As we learn in flashback, this failed quest is a replay of the same pursuit, attainment, and loss of the same beloved that occurred in Gatsby’s youth, before the novel opens. Each failed quest occurs during the compressed period of a few months, and in both instances Gatsby disguises his true origins, so there is a kind of narrative symmetry between the structure of fictional past and fictional present. Another kind of structural symmetry is produced when Gatsby is reunited with Daisy in chapter 5, which is at the physical center of the novel’s nine chapters and at the temporal center of the narrative action: it is late July, the midpoint between Nick’s first visit to the Buchanans’ new home in early June, when “the history of the summer really begins” (10; ch. 1), and Gatsby’s death in early September.

此外，叙事以结构相似的三段式模式展开，小说开头和结尾处，叙述者尼克·卡拉威对他所叙述的事件进行了沉思：

In addition, the narrative unfolds in a pattern of similarly structured triads, bounded at the beginning and end of the novel by narrator Nick Carraway’s meditative reflections on the events he recounts:

开篇：叙述者的开篇冥想（第 1 章）

Opening: Narrator’s opening meditation (ch. 1)

我：

I:

财富世界的描述（第一章）

The world of wealth described (ch. 1)

二、

II:

贫困世界的描述（第二章）

The world of poverty described (ch. 2)

第三部分：

III:

第一部分和第二部分的交集——盖茨比的派对上，富人和穷人混杂在一起（第三章）

Intersection of I and II – rich and poor mingle at Gatsby’s party (ch. 3)

I:

尼克听到了盖茨比的过去的故事（第4章）

Nick hears story of Gatsby’s past (ch. 4)

二、

II:

尼克听到了黛西的过去的故事（第4章）

Nick hears story of Daisy’s past (ch. 4)

第三部分：

III:

第一章和第二章的交汇点——盖茨比和黛西在尼克家重逢（第五章）

二、

永恒的三角关系破裂——纽约酒店房间里的对峙场景（第7章）

C.乔治·威尔逊之死（第8章）
