当然，这些叙事模式中的任何一种都可以作为《了不起的盖茨比》结构分析的起点。然而，我想要重点关注的是我认为所有其他结构的基础：小说的叙事“语法”，我认为，茨维坦·托多罗夫的命题模式能够阐明这一语法。正如你所记得的，根据这个框架，我们试图通过重复出现的动作（类似于动词）和与特定人物（类似于名词）相关的属性（类似于形容词）之间的关系模式来发现文本的结构。换句话说，我们试图通过重复相同的语法、相同的公式、相同的“句子”来发现文本的结构。

Of course, any of these narrative patterns could serve as a starting point for a structural analysis of The Great Gatsby. The particular structure I want to focus on, however, is the one I believe is at the foundation of all the others: the novel’s narrative “grammar,” which is illuminated, I think, by the use of Tzvetan Todorov’s schema of propositions. As you’ll recall, according to this framework we try to discover how the text is structured by the pattern of relations among recurring actions (which are analogous to verbs) and attributes (which are analogous to adjectives) associated with particular characters (which are analogous to nouns). In other words, we try to discover how the text is structured by the repetition of the same grammar, the same formula, the same “sentence,” so to speak.

以《了不起的盖茨比》为例，我认为所有情节都可以归结为三个动词：“寻找”、“找到”和“失去”。这三个动词反过来又产生了两种相关的“句子”或叙事模式的重复：（1）“X寻找、找到并最终失去了Y”，或者简单地说（2）“X寻找但没有找到Y”。（X=相关人物；Y=所渴望的人、物、状态或条件。）当然，在这两种情况下，整体叙事模式是相同的：

In the case of The Great Gatsby, I think all the action can be reduced to three verbs: “to seek,” “to find,” and “to lose.” These three verbs produce, in turn, the repetition of two related “sentences,” or narrative patterns: (1) “X seeks, finds, and then loses Y,” or simply (2) “X seeks but doesn’t find Y.” (X = the character in question; Y = a desired person, object, state, or condition.) In both cases, of course, the overall narrative formula is the same:

1

1

属性：X 缺少 Y

Attribute: X lacks Y

2

2

行动：X 寻找 Y

Action: X seeks Y

3

3

属性：X 缺少 Y

Attribute: X lacks Y

（要么是因为 X 没有找到 Y，要么是因为 X 找到了 Y 但随后又弄丢了）

(either because X doesn’t find Y or because X finds but then loses Y)

我想首先分析这部小说，揭示这种叙事模式如何通过构建主要人物的叙事结构来构建整个文本。然后，我会指出“寻找-发现-丢失”的叙事结构可以被视为现代小说对传统寻宝冒险模式的摒弃。最后，我会论证这种叙事方式……语法为我们提供了一个有趣的诺思罗普·弗莱神话理论应用实例。在《了不起的盖茨比》中，这种语法构建了一个叙事，将夏日神话（盖茨比的故事，浪漫小说体裁）嵌入冬日神话（尼克的故事，讽刺体裁）之中。尽管夏日神话最终被冬日神话所取代，但后者的结构仍然“萦绕”着前者的影子。

I’d like to begin my analysis of the novel by revealing how this formula structures the text as a whole by structuring the narratives of the main characters. Then I will suggest that the seek-find-lose grammar can be seen as the modern novel’s rejection of the traditional seek-and-find quest formula. Finally, I will argue that this narrative grammar offers us an interesting application of Northrop Frye’s theory of mythoi. For in The Great Gatsby, this grammar produces a narrative that embeds the mythos of summer (Gatsby’s story, the genre of romance) within the mythos of winter (Nick’s story, the genre of irony). And although the mythos of summer is eventually overridden by the mythos of winter, the latter structure remains “haunted” by the former.

当然，这部小说“寻觅-发现-失去”模式的“主线剧情”是主人公杰伊·盖茨比的故事。正如我们前面提到的，他两次寻觅、找到并失去黛西：一次是在小说开始之前，在他年轻的时候；另一次是在尼克住在西卵他家隔壁的那个夏天。此外，盖茨比追求、获得并失去黛西的故事，与他追求、获得并失去他改名为杰伊·盖茨比后所追求的新生活的故事交织在一起。因此，他的寻觅-发现-失去的故事不仅在两个不同的时间段重复上演，而且围绕着两个不同的目标——爱情和社会地位——展开。当然，随着他的离世，这两样东西都随之消失了。此外，盖茨比的故事为其他人物的故事提供了框架，可以说，其他人物的故事都是通过尼克对盖茨比故事的展开而讲述的。

Of course, the “master plot” of the novel’s seek-find-lose formula is the story of its title character, Jay Gatsby. As we noted above, he seeks, finds, and loses Daisy twice: once in his youth, before the novel begins, and again during the summer that Nick lives next door to him on West Egg. In addition, the narrative of Gatsby’s pursuit, attainment, and loss of Daisy is accompanied by the narrative of his pursuit, attainment, and loss of the new life he sought when he changed his name from James Gatz to Jay Gatsby. His seek-find-lose story is thus repeated not merely in two different time periods but in terms of two different goals: love and social status. Both are lost to him, of course, when he dies. Furthermore, Gatsby’s narrative provides the framework on which the narratives of the other characters are “strung,” so to speak: it is in the unfolding of Gatsby’s story by Nick that the other stories are told.

黛西的故事不仅呼应了盖茨比叙事中“寻觅-获得-失去”的模式，也体现了其重复性。正如我们在闪回中看到的，年轻的黛西·费伊渴望刺激，她从对杰伊·盖茨比中尉的爱情中找到了刺激，却又因战争失去了他。接着，她寻求情感上的安全感，嫁给了汤姆·布坎南，却很快发现他屡次出轨，失去了这份安全感。最后，她渴望得到汤姆无法给予的关注，在盖茨比身上找到了这种关注，却又在盖茨比去世时（或者更准确地说，是在汤姆揭露盖茨比并非黛西以为的那样）失去了这种关注。

Daisy’s story mirrors not only the seek-find-lose pattern of Gatsby’s narrative but its repetitive quality as well. As we learn in flashback, the young Daisy Fay sought excitement, found it in the form of her love for Lieutenant Jay Gatsby, then lost him to the war. Next she sought emotional security, found it in the form of marriage to Tom Buchanan, then lost it when she soon discovered that he was chronically unfaithful to her. Finally, she craves the attention that she isn’t getting from Tom, finds it in Gatsby, and loses it when he dies (or, perhaps more precisely, when Tom reveals that Gatsby isn’t the man Daisy thought he was).

汤姆·布坎南、默特尔·威尔逊和她的丈夫乔治的故事都遵循着类似的“寻找-获得-失去”的模式。年轻时的汤姆追求自我满足，他在大学橄榄球赛场上如鱼得水，成为英雄，毕业后又失去了这一切。婚后，汤姆继续寻求类似的自我满足——被“不如他的人”崇拜——他通过勾引一系列工人阶级女性来满足自己，默特尔·威尔逊就是其中最新的一个。然而，每次这种自我满足都只持续到婚外情结束，汤姆总是不断地回到那个无法满足的追求者的位置。

Similar seek-find-lose grammars structure the narratives of Tom Buchanan, Myrtle Wilson, and her husband George. As a young man, Tom sought ego gratification, found it in his career as a college football hero, then lost it when he graduated from college. As a married man, Tom seeks a similar kind of ego gratification – the adoration of “inferiors” – by seducing a series of working-class women, the latest incarnation of which is Myrtle Wilson. In each case, however, the ego gratification lasts only as long as the affair, so Tom continually returns to the position of the unfulfilled seeker.

同样，默特尔·威尔逊试图逃离婚姻的乏味和经济贫困，她在汤姆·布坎南身上找到了慰藉，却又在一次肇事逃逸事故中丧生，失去了这份慰藉。当然，即便她活了下来，也无法嫁给汤姆。汤姆为了逃避与默特尔的永久关系而撒谎，声称黛西的天主教信仰不允许她与他离婚，这显然表明了他这种逃避的意图。在默特尔“寻找-找到-失去”的故事背后，是乔治·威尔逊的影子。乔治也曾寻求爱情，并在与默特尔的婚姻中找到了它，然而……当她与汤姆出轨时，她就失去了理智（或者更准确地说，当她得知乔治结婚时穿的那套西装并非他自己的）。

Analogously, Myrtle Wilson seeks escape from the boredom and economic poverty of her marriage, finds it in Tom Buchanan, then loses it when she is killed in the hit-and-run accident. Of course, even if she had lived she would not have succeeded in marrying Tom. His intention to avoid a permanent commitment to Myrtle is evident in his lie to her that Daisy’s Catholicism would never permit her to divorce him. Operating as a shadow behind Myrtle’s seek-find-lose narrative is that of George Wilson, who sought love, found it in his marriage to Myrtle, and lost it when she became unfaithful to him with Tom (or, perhaps more precisely, when she learned that George didn’t own the suit in which he was married).

在这些“寻找-发现-失去”的模式背后，隐藏着一个子集：“寻找却未找到”。我们可以在乔治对经济保障的追求中看到这种模式的运作，而​​这终究是一个不可能实现的梦想；在乔丹对社会和经济保障的追求中也能看到这种模式的运作，这些保障似乎总是与她擦肩而过，就像最近她总是差那么一点点就能赢球一样。这种“寻找却未找到”的模式也通过众多次要角色构建了故事背景。麦基先生努力成为一名摄影师，却未能成功。默特尔的妹妹凯瑟琳似乎永远无法满足于现状：她去蒙特卡洛的旅行是一场经济灾难；她那“黏糊糊的红色波波头”、“涂着粉的惨白肤色”以及“不羁”的眉毛，都被拔掉的眉毛“模糊”地画了出来（34；第二章），简直是一场时尚灾难。她对享乐的追求似乎只是将她从一个醉酒的混乱场景带到另一个。就连盖茨比数不胜数的派对宾客也带着不满的游荡者气息，他们从不知名的地方来到他的豪宅，在最新的舞会中寻求新鲜感，在酒精中寻求刺激，或许只是为了逃避内心的不满。

As a backdrop to these seek-find-lose grammars is a subset of seek-find-lose: seek-but-don’t-find. We see this pattern operating in George’s pursuit of financial security, which is an impossible dream, and in Jordan’s pursuit of social and financial security, which seem ever to elude her grasp just as the winning putt remains, of late, just beyond her reach. The grammar of seek-but-don’t-find also structures the setting in the form of the numerous minor characters who populate it. Mr. McKee seeks but doesn’t find success as a photographer. Myrtle’s sister Catherine seems a permanently dissatisfied seeker: her trip to Monte Carlo was a financial disaster; her “solid sticky bob of red hair,” “complexion powdered milky white,” and “rakish” painted eyebrows “blurred” by the plucked hairs growing back (34; ch. 2) are a fashion disaster; and her search for a good time seems merely to take her from one scene of drunken chaos to another. Even Gatsby’s innumerable party guests have the air of dissatisfied wanderers, coming to his mansion from parts unknown, seeking something new in the latest dances, and seeking excitement, or perhaps just escape from their dissatisfaction, at the bottom of a bottle.

小说中最精彩的“寻觅却未果”式叙事无疑是尼克·卡拉威的经历。尼克在纽约的夏天只是他一系列失败尝试中的最新一次。他在第一次世界大战中的经历显然是为了追求刺激，结果却比出发时更加一无所获：“我太享受（第一次世界大战）了，以至于回来后心神不宁。中西部不再是温暖的世界中心，反而成了宇宙的边缘地带——所以我决定去东部学习债券生意”（7；第一章）。正如他的叙述所揭示的那样，他在债券生意以及在东部的冒险也遵循着“寻觅却未果”的模式：抵达纽约几个月后，他就放弃了这两项事业。寻找理想伴侣的旅程也以失败告终。他离开家乡，部分原因是为了逃避一个让他感到被迫结婚的女人。他显然对与他有染的女同事毫不在意，以至于她哥哥“恶狠狠地瞪着[他]”（61；第三章）就把他赶走了。而他和乔丹·贝克的关系也明显是一阵短暂的迷恋：他对她和对布坎南一家一样，很快就厌倦了。

Certainly the most well-developed seek-but-don’t-find narrative in the novel is that of Nick Carraway. Nick’s summer in New York is just the latest in a series of unsuccessful pursuits. His experience in World War I apparently involved the pursuit of excitement from which he returned more empty-handed than when he left: “I enjoyed [World War I] so thoroughly that I came back restless. Instead of being the warm center of the world the Middle West now seemed like the ragged edge of the universe – so I decided to go East and learn the bond business” (7; ch. 1). As his narrative reveals, of course, his venture in the bond business, and in the East in general, also follows the seek-but-don’t-find pattern: he abandons both within a few months of his arrival in New York. Neither is his search for the right woman successful. He leaves his hometown, in part, to escape a woman he was feeling pressured to marry. He apparently cares so little about the woman at work with whom he has an affair that he allows her brother’s “mean looks in [his] direction” (61; ch. 3) to drive him off. And his relationship with Jordan Baker is rather clearly an infatuation with no staying power: he tires of her as soon as he tires of the Buchanans.

然而，尼克最重要的“寻觅却未得”的模式，似乎是他对人生目标的无尽追寻。在他的叙述中，尼克似乎总是“漫无目的”。三十岁的他仍然没有稳定的工作，没有认真的恋爱对象，也没有属于自己的房子。他对此深感匮乏：“三十岁——预示着十年的孤独，单身男性朋友越来越少，热情也越来越少，头发也越来越稀疏”（143；第七章）。事实上，他仍然依靠富有的父亲资助，父亲“同意资助他一年”（7；第一章），让他学习债券业务。难怪他似乎对债券业务如此着迷。盖茨比之所以拥有尼克最缺乏的品质，是因为他拥有尼克竭尽全力也无法获得的品质：目标。

Nick’s most important seek-but-don’t-find pattern, however, seems to be his unfulfilled search for a purpose in life. Throughout his narrative, Nick seems “at loose ends.” At the age of 30 he is still without a stable career, without a serious love interest, and without a home of his own. And he feels their lack acutely: “Thirty – the promise of a decade of loneliness, a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair” (143; ch. 7). In fact, he’s still being supported by his wealthy father, who “agreed to finance [him] for a year” (7; ch. 1) while he learned the bond business. It’s no wonder he seems so fascinated by Gatsby, for Gatsby has, to an extreme degree, the quality Nick lacks most, the quality he is unable to acquire despite his best efforts: purpose.

或许可以将《了不起的盖茨比》中“寻找-发现-失去”的叙事结构视为现代小说对传统探寻模式的摒弃。传统的探寻模式建立在寻找和发现的框架之上。即便主人公在实现探寻目标的过程中或尝试过程中死去，他的努力也会以某种方式改变世界：他发现了某些重要的东西。因此，托多罗夫所揭示的基本情节模式是由一个属性和一个行动转化而成的：（1）属性（例如，主人公未能成功），（2）行动（他寻求成功），（3）属性（他成功了，或者至少通过探寻获得了重要的东西）。因此，传统的探寻模式在某种程度上具有救赎意义。

It might be interesting to think of the seek-find-lose grammar of The Great Gatsby as the modern novel’s rejection of the traditional quest formula. The traditional quest is structured by a seek-and-find grammar. Even if the hero dies achieving the goal of his quest, or attempting to achieve it, the world is transformed in some way by his effort: something important is found. Thus, the basic plot formula Todorov isolated consists of an attribute transformed by an action: (1) attribute (for example, the protagonist is unsuccessful), (2) action (he seeks success), (3) attribute (he is successful or, at least, has learned something important as a result of his quest). The traditional quest is thus redemptive in some way.

正如我们所见，在菲茨杰拉德的小说中，人物的特质既没有因主人公的行为而改变，也没有因他们自身的行为而改变。小说结尾，人物依然拥有着与开篇时相同的特质——同样的缺失，而且显然他们在这个过程中一无所获。盖茨比死了，想必他生前并未意识到黛西已经离他而去，即便意识到了，也未能活到足以从中受益的地步。默特尔和乔治也死了，他们并没有从这段经历中吸取任何教训。我们最后一次见到乔丹时，她依然故我，虚伪地对尼克撒谎，说她对他的疏远毫不在意，而且已经和别人订婚了。最后，汤姆和黛西一如既往地逃离了他们一手造成的混乱，“退回到他们的金钱、他们的漫不经心，或者其他任何维系着他们的东西里”（188；第九章）。

As we have seen, in Fitzgerald’s novel, the characters’ attributes are not transformed by the hero’s action nor by their own actions. At the novel’s end the characters have the same attribute – the same lack – with which they began, and apparently nothing is learned in the process. Gatsby is dead, presumably without having admitted to himself that Daisy has abandoned him and without living long enough to benefit from that insight had it occurred. Myrtle and George are dead, without having learned anything from their experience. The last time we see Jordan, she’s putting up her usual false front, lying to Nick that she is unmoved by his withdrawal from their relationship and is engaged to someone else. Finally, Tom and Daisy, true to form, flee the chaos they helped create, “retreat[ing] back into their money or their vast carelessness or whatever it was that kept them together” (188; ch. 9).

这条规则的唯一例外是尼克，他在纽约的经历彻底改变了他。故事伊始，他非常乐观，觉得“夏天到来，生活又重新开始了”（8；第一章）。他对在纽约的新工作和新生活充满期待。然而到了夏天结束时，他彻底幻灭，放弃了在东部开启新事业和新生活的计划：“去年秋天我从东部回来时，我感觉我希望世界永远井然有序，永远保持某种道德上的严谨；我不想再经历那些喧闹的冒险，也不想再窥探人性的隐秘角落”（6；第一章）。然而，尼克的转变并非救赎。尽管他在那年夏天确实对人性有了重要的认识，但这些认识却在他心中留下了对人生的阴暗印象。小说结尾时，他的态度是绝望的：“所以我们奋力前行，就像逆流而上的船，却不断地被推回过去”（189；第 9 章）。

The only exception to this rule is Nick, who is transformed by his experience in New York. As the narrative opens, he is very optimistic, feeling that “life was beginning over again with the summer” (8; ch. 1). He’s excited by his new job and his new life in New York. By the end of the summer he is utterly disillusioned, abandoning his plans for a new career and a new life in the East: “When I came back from the East last autumn I felt that I wanted the world to be in uniform and at a sort of moral attention forever; I wanted no more riotous excursions with privileged glimpses into the human heart” (6; ch. 1). However, Nick’s transformation is not redemptive. Although he certainly learns something important about human nature over the course of that summer, the lesson produces in him a dark vision of human life. His attitude, as the novel closes, is hopeless and despairing: “So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past” (189; ch. 9).

如果传统的探寻模式——寻找并发现（或寻找并改变）——可以与一种包含救赎可能性的世界观联系起来，那么或许寻找-发现-失去（或寻找却找不到）的模式可以与一种救赎不可能或极不可能的世界观联系起来。这种更为悲观，或者有些人会说是更为现实的人类经验观，正是这种愿景。这种风格与现代主义世界观密切相关，后者从第一次世界大战开始（1914年）到第二次世界大战结束（1945年）主导了英欧文学，《了不起的盖茨比》正是这种世界观的典型代表。我们当然可以在现代小说中找到许多体现这种风格的例子，例如D·H·劳伦斯的《儿子与情人》（1913年）和《恋爱中的女人》（1920年），弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《到灯塔去》 （1927年），以及理查德·赖特的《土生子》（1940年）。想必，这些作品的读者，而非其中的人物，应该经历某种可能的转变，但这些文本并没有提供一种可以称之为救赎的世界观。 （类似地，我们可以将后现代小说的语法描述为“不必费心寻找”。当然，有人可能会认为，像托马斯·品钦的《拍卖第49批》（1966）、琼·迪迪恩的《随心所欲》（1970）、约瑟夫·海勒的《出了事》（1974）和唐·德里罗的《白噪音》（1985）这样的小说，其结构都遵循着这种语法。）

If the traditional quest formula – seek-and-find (or seek-and-be-transformed) – can be associated with a worldview that includes the possibility of redemption, then perhaps the seek-find-lose (or seek-but-don’t-find) grammar can be associated with a worldview in which redemption is impossible or highly unlikely. This more pessimistic, or some would say realistic, vision of human experience is the vision associated with the modernist worldview, which dominated Anglo-European literature from the beginning of World War I (1914) to the end of World War II (1945) and which The Great Gatsby epitomizes. We can certainly find numerous examples of this grammar in modern novels, for example, D. H. Lawrence’s Sons and Lovers (1913) and Women in Love (1920), Virginia Woolf’s To the Lighthouse (1927), and Richard Wright’s Native Son (1940). Presumably, the readers of these works, rather than the characters that populate them, are supposed to undergo whatever transformation is possible, but the texts do not offer a worldview that could be called redemptive. (Analogously, we might characterize the grammar of the postmodern novel as don’t-bother-to-seek. Certainly, it might be argued that novels such as Thomas Pynchon’s The Crying of Lot 49 [1966], Joan Didion’s Play It as It Lays [1970], Joseph Heller’s Something Happened [1974], and Don DeLillo’s White Noise [1985] are structured by such a grammar.)

我推测《了不起的盖茨比》中“寻找-发现-失去”的叙事结构反映了现代小说对传统寻觅模式的摒弃，这与我认为菲茨杰拉德的小说要求我们运用诺思罗普·弗莱的神话理论的方式相吻合。因为根据弗莱的框架，《了不起的盖茨比》将浪漫的结构（盖茨比的叙事、夏日神话、寻觅）嵌入到反讽的结构（尼克的叙事、冬日神话、现实主义）之中，而后者对前者提供了一种持续的评述，最终迫使尼克意识到，浪漫的结构（盖茨比的叙事）在现代世界已不再可行。也就是说，在菲茨杰拉德的小说中，反讽的结构包含并最终凌驾于浪漫的结构之上。

My speculation that The Great Gatsby’s seek-find-lose grammar reflects the modern novel’s rejection of the traditional quest formula is compatible with the way in which I think Fitzgerald’s novel requires us to apply Northrop Frye’s theory of mythoi. For according to Frye’s framework, The Great Gatsby embeds the structure of romance (Gatsby’s narrative, the mythos of summer, the quest) within the structure of irony (Nick’s narrative, the mythos of winter, realism), and the second structure offers a kind of running commentary on the first, which, by the novel’s close, forces Nick to realize that the structure of romance (Gatsby’s narrative) is no longer possible in the modern world. That is, in Fitzgerald’s novel, the structure of irony contains and eventually overrides the structure of romance.

盖茨比当然是浪漫追求的英雄。尽管其他角色也都有各自的“追求”，但只有盖茨比的追求属于浪漫主义范畴。弗莱在《批评的剖析》中指出：“在所有文学形式中，浪漫主义最接近于愿望实现的梦想，因此……在每个时代，统治阶级或知识分子都倾向于以某种浪漫主义的形式来投射他们的理想”（186）。对于20世纪20年代美国追求快速致富的爵士时代而言，杰伊·盖茨比所取得的那种如流星般迅速的财富积累象征着美国梦，而美国梦显然过去是、现在仍然是一个愿望实现的浪漫梦想。盖茨比对昔日黄金时代的执着追寻也体现了浪漫主义的特征，对他来说，那个黄金时代就是他在路易斯维尔与黛西·费伊的恋爱，之后他被派往战场。战后回到美国，他致力于积累财富，并通过报纸关注黛西的社交活动。当他终于能够买下海湾对面的一栋豪宅时，他安排再次与她见面，以便“将一切都恢复到以前的样子”（17；第 1 章），这样他就可以回到黄金时代。

Gatsby is, of course, the hero of the romantic quest. Although all the other characters have “quests” of their own, only Gatsby’s occurs within the mode of romance. In Anatomy of Criticism Frye notes, “[t]he romance is nearest of all literary forms to the wish-fulfillment dream, and for that reason … [i]n every age the ruling social or intellectual class tends to project its ideals in some form of romance” (186). For the get-rich-quick Jazz Age of the American 1920s, the kind of meteoric financial rise Jay Gatsby achieved was emblematic of the American dream, which clearly was and still is a romantic dream of wish fulfillment. Typical of romance, too, is Gatsby’s persistent search for a past Golden Age, which, for him, was his courtship of Daisy Fay in Louisville before he was sent to war. Upon his return to America after the war, he devoted himself to amassing a fortune and following her social activities in the newspapers. When he was able, finally, to buy a mansion across the bay from hers, he arranged to meet her again so that he could “fix everything just the way it was before” (17; ch. 1), so that he could return to the Golden Age.

事实上，盖茨比从遇见丹·科迪到在尼克的小屋与黛西重逢这段时间里的所有活动，构成了浪漫英雄在迎来重大事件之前必须经历的一系列小冒险。一场冒险——他最终将黛西带回自己身边——就此展开。与科迪的冒险经历教会了他人生成功所需的技能，包括浪漫英雄所具备的坚韧和节制。他在军事上的卓越成就使他迅速晋升，从少尉升至少校，并因战场上的英勇表现而荣获多枚勋章。随后，他又以同样的速度在沃尔夫希姆的组织中步步高升，积累了足以与汤姆·布坎南匹敌的财富。

In fact, all of Gatsby’s activities between the time he met Dan Cody to the moment at which he is reunited with Daisy at Nick’s cottage constitute the series of minor adventures the romantic hero must undertake before the major adventure – reclaiming Daisy for his own – occurs. His adventures with Cody taught him the skills he needed to succeed in life, including the perseverance and temperance that mark the romantic hero. His military achievements resulted in his rapid ascendancy through the ranks from lieutenant to major and covered him with medals for his valor on the battlefield. Then with similar rapidity, he ascended the ranks of Wolfsheim’s organization, gaining a fortune to rival that of Tom Buchanan.

盖茨比的主要冒险（他追寻黛西的旅程）也是浪漫爱情故事中典型的求婚之旅。如同传统爱情故事中的英雄，他常常被水阻隔与爱人相伴，盖茨比也与黛西隔着海湾，西卵的豪宅与东卵的家遥遥相望。而且，同样典型的是，他从海湾的这一侧就能看到“应许之地”——布坎南家码头尽头的绿光。此外，他对黛西的追寻也让他与一个读者难以同情的对手对抗。事实上，汤姆扮演着篡位者的角色，黛西必须从他自私的阴谋诡计中被解救出来。

Gatsby’s major adventure (his quest to regain Daisy) is also typical of the romantic quest to obtain a bride. Like the hero of the traditional quest, who is often separated from his love by a barrier of water, Gatsby is separated from Daisy by the bay between his mansion on West Egg and her home on East Egg. And, again typically, he can see the “promised land” – the green light at the end of the Buchanans’ dock – from his side of the gulf that separates them. Furthermore, his quest for Daisy pits Gatsby against an antagonist with whom the reader can have little sympathy. Indeed, Tom fills the role of the usurper, from whose selfish machinations Daisy must be rescued.

对盖茨比而言，英雄与反派之间浪漫冲突的高潮发生在纽约酒店房间里与汤姆的对峙场景中。尽管英雄有时会在这场斗争中丧命，但他为追求目标而牺牲的意愿证明了他是一位英雄。事实上，盖茨比确实死了，既有象征性的死亡——“‘杰伊·盖茨比’在汤姆的恶意攻击下像玻璃一样破碎了”（155；第八章）——也有字面意义上的死亡，汤姆派武装且疯狂的乔治·威尔逊去盖茨比家。实际上，随着叙事走向他的死亡，盖茨比为黛西牺牲的意愿成为了贯穿全书的主题。

The climactic struggle of the romantic conflict between hero and antagonist occurs, for Gatsby, during the confrontation scene with Tom in the New York hotel room. Although the hero sometimes dies as a result of this battle, his willingness to sacrifice himself for his quest proves him a hero. And, indeed, Gatsby does die, both symbolically – “‘Jay Gatsby’ had broken up like glass against Tom’s hard malice” (155; ch. 8) – and literally, when Tom sends George Wilson, armed and crazed, to Gatsby’s house. In fact, Gatsby’s willingness to sacrifice himself for Daisy becomes the dominant motif as the narrative moves toward his death.

盖茨比的寻觅之旅，以一种更为微妙的方式，也与浪漫英雄的另一种化身——拯救王国免遭怪物蹂躏的寻觅者英雄——有着相似之处。正如弗莱所言，“寻觅之旅是丰饶战胜荒芜之地的胜利”（193）：待战胜的怪物是贫瘠堕落的世界，等待着某种救世主的救赎。对于小说背景中体现的现代荒芜之地——既包括“灰烬谷”（27；第二章），也包括游手好闲的富人的空虚享乐——而言，盖茨比象征着生命的复苏和活力。用尼克的话来说，盖茨比“对生活的希望有着高度的敏感”，“拥有非凡的希望天赋，一种浪漫的坦率，这种坦率是我从未在任何人身上发现过的，而且恐怕以后也很难再发现了”（6；第一章）。简而言之，盖茨比拥有现代世界迫切需要的、能够拯救其于自身贫瘠绝望之中的东西。他如同救世主一般，代表着重获的希望。

In a subtler fashion, Gatsby’s quest also resembles that of another incarnation of the romantic hero: the quester-hero who saves the kingdom from the ravages of a monster. As Frye puts it, “the quest-romance is the victory of fertility over the waste land” (193): the monster to be defeated is the sterile, fallen world that waits to be redeemed by some sort of messiah. For the modern wasteland embodied in the novel’s setting – including both the “valley of ashes” (27; ch.2) and the empty pleasures of the idle rich – Gatsby represents the renewal of life and vitality. In Nick’s words, Gatsby has a “heightened sensitivity to the promises of life,” an “extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness such as I have never found in any other person and which it is not likely I shall ever find again” (6; ch. 1). Gatsby has, in short, what the modern world desperately needs to save it from the hopelessness of its own sterility. Like a messiah-figure, he represents renewed hope.

尽管盖茨比在某种程度上似乎是冷漠的现代世界的一部分——他参与犯罪活动，举办的派对最终都演变成醉酒狂欢——但他在象征意义上却与这个世界格格不入。如同拯救危难王国的冒险英雄，他与自己所处的世界隔绝开来。他独居，除了黛西之外，与任何人都不亲近。他不认识派对上的任何人，他举办派对的唯一目的就是希望黛西能在某个夜晚“……漫步而来”（84；第四章）。他最常被描绘成独自一人，置身于一幅象征着他浪漫孤寂的画面之中。例如，一天晚上，尼克看到盖茨比“从[他]豪宅的阴影中走出来”，“向着漆黑的水面伸出双臂”（25；第一章），“颤抖着”望向黛西码头尽头那“微弱而遥远的绿光”（26；第一章）。在默特尔·威尔逊遇害的那晚，他独自一人守在黛西家门外，进行着“神圣的……守夜”（153；第七章），以防汤姆“试图就他们的婚外情骚扰她”（151；第七章）。即使在盖茨比那些喧闹的派对上，他也总是被描绘成浪漫的孤寂：“窗户和大门仿佛突然涌出一股空虚，使站在门廊上、举手告别的主人显得格外孤寂”（60；第3章）。在一个腐败的世界里，盖茨比却不被腐蚀，因为他拥有一个“不朽的梦想”（162；第8章）。

Although Gatsby may seem, on one level, part of the sterile modern world – he engages in criminal activities and throws parties that inevitably turn into drunken revels – he is symbolically separate from it. Like the quester-hero who saves the imperiled kingdom, he is isolated from the world he inhabits. He lives alone and is close to no one but Daisy. He knows none of the people at his parties, which he throws only in the hope that Daisy will “wander i[n] … some night” (84; ch. 4). And he is pictured, most frequently, alone in a tableau that bespeaks his romantic isolation. For example, one evening Nick observes that Gatsby “emerged from the shadow of [his] mansion” and “stretched out his arms toward the dark water” (25; ch. 1), “trembling” toward the “single green light, minute and far away” (26; ch. 1) at the end of Daisy’s dock. The night Myrtle Wilson is killed, he stands guard alone, in a “sacre[d] … vigil” (153; ch. 7) outside Daisy’s house, in case Tom “tries to bother her” (151; ch. 7) about their affair. Even at his riotous parties, Gatsby is pictured in romantic isolation: “A sudden emptiness seemed to flow now from the windows and the great doors, endowing with complete isolation the figure of the host who stood on the porch, his hand up in a formal gesture of farewell” (60; ch. 3). In a world of corruption, Gatsby is incorruptible because he has an “incorruptible dream” (162; ch. 8).

盖茨比的早年生活也符合拯救堕落世界的英雄形象。他的身世成谜，即便在他透露父母是谁之后，我们也得知“他的想象力从未真正接受过他们是他的父母。事实上，杰伊·盖茨比……源于他柏拉图式的自我认知。​​他是上帝之子……[并且]他至死都忠于这种认知”（104；第六章）。盖茨比甚至经历了一种典型的救世主式的洗礼。“那天下午，詹姆斯·盖茨一直在海滩上闲逛”（104；第六章），但当他划船来到停泊在苏必利尔湖岸边的科迪的游艇旁时，“从水中出来接受科迪管家工作的却是……杰伊·盖茨比”（104；第六章）。正如弗莱告诉我们的，太阳神“被描绘成乘船航行在我们世界的表面”（192），盖茨比也曾与科迪一起航行了五年。的确，正如探险英雄通常是“第三个儿子，或是第三个踏上征程的人，或是第三次尝试才成功的人”（弗莱 187），盖茨比的航海之旅也让他“环游了欧洲大陆三次”（106；第六章），最终才“登陆”现代世界。

Gatsby’s early life, too, fits that of the quester-hero who saves the fallen world. His origins are mysterious, and even when he reveals who his parents are we learn that “his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all. The truth was that Jay Gatsby … sprang from his Platonic conception of himself. He was a son of God. … [A]nd to this conception he was faithful to the end” (104; ch. 6). Gatsby even goes through a kind of baptism by water, typical of the messiah figure. “It was James Gatz who had been loafing along the beach that afternoon” (104; ch. 6), but by the time he rowed out to Cody’s yacht anchored off the shore of Lake Superior, “it was … Jay Gatsby” (104; ch. 6) who emerged from the water to accept a job as Cody’s steward. And like the sun god who, Frye tells us, “is represented as sailing in a boat on the surface of our world” (192), Gatsby sailed with Cody for five years. Indeed, just as the quester-hero is often “a third son, or the third to undertake the quest, or successful on his third attempt” (Frye 187), Gatsby’s travels by boat took him “three times around the Continent” (106; ch. 6) before he “landed” in the modern world.

盖茨比的浪漫追求故事嵌入在另一种截然不同的叙事之中：尼克在纽约的夏天。我们之所以了解盖茨比，是因为尼克与他之间的关系构成了叙述者自身经历的重要组成部分。然而，尼克的叙事结构却采用了与浪漫截然相反的体裁：反讽。弗莱指出，反讽“与内容的完全现实主义相一致”（224）。弗莱认为，反讽源于冬日神话。与浪漫的理想化世界形成对比，弗莱观察到，冬日神话“试图赋予非理想化存在中变幻莫测的暧昧性和复杂性以形式”（223）。这种“非理想化的存在”并非英雄的世界，而是充满日常缺陷的普通人的世界。在这个世界里，人类的苦难并非源于命运或某种宇宙干预，而是源于社会和心理因素。换句话说，这就是真实的世界，优缺点并存。

The narrative of Gatsby’s romantic quest is embedded within a very different kind of narrative: that of Nick’s summer in New York. We learn about Gatsby because Nick’s relationship with him forms a large part of the narrator’s own experience. However, Nick’s narrative is structured by a genre that is the polar opposite of romance: the genre of irony, which, Frye says, “is consistent … with complete realism of content” (224). Irony, Frye argues, derives from the mythos of winter. In contrast to the idealized world of romance, Frye observes, the mythos of winter “attempts to give form to the shifting ambiguities and complexities of unidealized existence” (223). This “unidealized existence” is not a world of heroes but of everyday, flawed human beings. It’s a world in which human misery is the result not of fate or of some kind of cosmic intervention but of sociological and psychological causes. In other words, this is the real world, warts and all.

在尼克和其他所有非英雄角色所生活的现实世界中，积累财富或找到真爱并非易事。有时甚至根本无法实现。在这个世界里，人们不像尼克那样容易找到一份满意的工作，也不像乔治·威尔逊那样容易维持生计。在这个世界里，人们不会像盖茨比那样，穿着“粉色破烂西装”（162；第八章）“光彩照人”，也不会举办奢华派对，期盼着失散多年的爱人出现。相反，他们像盖茨比的客人们一样，去参加派对只是为了蹭吃蹭喝，从素未谋面的主人那里捞好处，然后醉得不省人事。他们的衣服“紧紧地贴在……略显宽阔的臀部上”（31；第二章），就像默特尔的衣服一样；他们也像默特尔的妹妹凯瑟琳那样，留着“黏糊糊的红色波波头”（34；第二章）。在现实世界里，“灰白瘦弱的意大利孩子”（30；第二章）生活在像“灰烬谷”那样的地方，人们喜欢站在事故现场，观看人类的苦难。

In the real world, in which Nick and all the other nonheroic characters live, it isn’t easy to amass a fortune or find your one true love. Sometimes it isn’t even easy to find a satisfying career, as Nick knows, or survive financially, as George Wilson knows. In this world, people don’t look “gorgeous” in their “pink rag of a suit” (162; ch. 8) or throw lavish parties in the hope that their lost love will appear, as Gatsby does. Instead, like Gatsby’s guests, they go to parties to sponge off a host they’ve never met and get obnoxiously drunk on his liquor. Their clothing “stretch[es] tight over … rather wide hips” (31; ch. 2), like Myrtle’s, and they have “sticky bob[s] of red hair” (34; ch. 2), as Myrtle’s sister Catherine has. In the real world, “grey, scrawny Italian child[ren]” (30; ch. 2) live in places like the “valley of ashes,” and people enjoy standing around the scene of an accident to watch human misery.

此外，在现实世界中，女人并非总能等到白马王子出现，即便她知道他是谁。有时，她会嫁给汤姆·布坎南。即便她获得了第二次幸福的机会，因为她的白马王子对她忠贞不渝，但通往真爱的道路上哪怕出现一丝小小的波折，都可能让她匆匆回家，就像黛西匆匆回到她自私、粗暴、不忠的丈夫身边一样。而当她的白马王子为了保护她免于肇事逃逸的杀人指控而牺牲时，她甚至可能在牧师前来主持葬礼之前就离开小镇。

In the real world, furthermore, a woman doesn’t always wait for her knight in shining armor, even when she knows who he is. Sometimes she marries Tom Buchanan instead. Even when she has a second chance at happiness, because her knight is faithful to her to the end, a small bend in the road to true love might send her scurrying home, as Daisy scurries back to her selfish, brutish, unfaithful husband. And when her knight dies protecting her from a charge of hit-and-run homicide, she might leave town before the minister arrives for the funeral.

在现实世界中，男人并非总能忠于自己的妻子，即便已婚。有时，他会像汤姆和默特尔那样，频繁地与情人出轨，甚至在公共场合炫耀；有时，他还会打断情妇的鼻子。在这里，像汤姆·布坎南和迈耶·沃尔夫希姆这样的“坏人”才是幕后主使。像乔治·威尔逊这样单纯诚实的男人，被妻子欺骗，又被她的情人操纵，最终杀害了一个无辜的人。而像乔丹·贝克这样“伟大的运动健将”，盖茨比认为她“绝不会做任何不妥的事”（76；第四章），却在打高尔夫球时作弊，谎称损坏了借来的车，并且“耍尽各种诡计……只为了保持她那冷艳傲慢的笑容，同时又能满足她那强健而轻佻的身体的需求”（63；第三章）。

In the real world, a man doesn’t always remain faithful to his woman, even when he’s married to her. Sometimes he has frequent extramarital affairs and parades them in public places, as Tom does with Myrtle, and sometimes he breaks his mistress’s nose. Here, “bad guys” like Tom Buchanan and Meyer Wolfsheim call the shots. A simple, honest man like George Wilson is deceived by his wife and manipulated by her lover into killing an innocent man. And a “great sportswom[an]” like Jordan Baker, who Gatsby believes would “never do anything that wasn’t all right” (76; ch. 4), cheats at golf, lies about damaging a borrowed car, and “deal[s] in subterfuges … in order to keep that cool, insolent smile turned to the world and yet satisfy the demands of her hard, jaunty body” (63; ch. 3).

或许最重要的是，在现实世界中，浪漫英雄的死亡并非拯救人类的殉道，而是人类无可救药、毫无希望的标志。一旦这个标志出现，尼克便明白自己别无选择，只能回家：放弃对未来的憧憬，抛弃乐观，及时止损，离开。如此一来，尼克的叙事建立在反讽的结构之上，可以说，它为浪漫故事——也就是浪漫的结构——关上了大门。换句话说，在《了不起的盖茨比》中，现代小说特有的反讽结构凌驾于浪漫结构之上，仿佛在宣告浪漫已成绝响。

Perhaps most important, in the real world the death of a romantic hero is not a martyrdom that saves humanity. It’s a sign that humanity is beyond saving, beyond hope. And once that sign is given, Nick knows there is nothing to do but go back home: forget his plans for the future, give up his optimism, cut his losses, and get out. In this way, Nick’s narrative, grounded in the structure of irony, closes the door, so to speak, on the romantic tale it tells, that is, on the structure of romance. In other words, in The Great Gatsby, the ironic structure associated with the modern novel overrides the structure of romance as if to say that romance is no longer possible.

这一过程在盖茨比和汤姆在纽约酒店的对峙场景中得到了象征性的体现。按照浪漫爱情故事的套路，男主角通常会在这里赢得新娘的芳心，并揭示自己的真实出身——要么是皇室成员，要么是拥有某种显赫的血统。然而，盖茨比却在汤姆的帮助下，揭露了自己的真实出身远逊于心爱之人，结果……那就是她抛弃了他。因此，从弗莱的神话理论的角度来看，浪漫的公式“脱轨”了，不再起作用，而叙事中唯一剩下的结构——反讽——填补了这一空白。

This process finds its symbolic expression in the confrontation scene between Gatsby and Tom in the New York hotel. According to the romantic formula, it is here that the hero wins his bride and reveals his true origins, which are royal or associated with some kind of important parentage. Instead, Gatsby reveals, with Tom’s help, that his true origins are far beneath those of his beloved, and the result is that she abandons him. Thus, from the perspective of Frye’s theory of mythoi, the romantic formula “jumps the track,” ceases to function, and the void is filled by the only structure left in the narrative: that of irony.

然而，反讽的结构并不能根除浪漫的结构。相反，反讽的结构反而被它所凌驾的结构所“萦绕”。或许正是因为尼克明白浪漫已成过往，他的叙述中才充满了对逝去过去的强烈怀念，对盖茨比所代表的那个逝去的浪漫世界的怀念。我们可以在他对纯洁田园般过去的抒情描写中看到这种渴望：他对黛西和乔丹在路易斯维尔“美丽的白色……少女时代”（24；第一章）的描写，以及对他青年时代在中西部度过的圣诞节的描绘，那里“寒冷的夜里，街灯和雪橇铃声交相辉映，冬青花环的影子从亮着灯的窗户投射在雪地上”（184；第九章）。

The structure of irony does not succeed, however, in eradicating the structure of romance. Instead, the structure of irony is “haunted” by the very structure it overrides. Perhaps because he knows that romance is no longer possible, Nick’s narrative is marked by an intense nostalgia for a lost past, for the lost world of romance that Gatsby represents. We see this longing in his lyric descriptions of a virginal, idyllic past: descriptions of Daisy and Jordan’s “beautiful white … girlhood” (24; ch. 1) in Louisville and of Christmas in the Midwest of his youth, with its “street lamps and sleigh bells in the frosty dark and the shadows of holly wreaths thrown by lighted windows on the snow” (184; ch. 9).

这种对逝去的纯真、对逝去的乐园、对夏日神话、对浪漫爱情的怀念，在尼克对一个永远消失的、名副其实的天堂的结尾描述中达到了顶峰。在返回明尼苏达州的前一天晚上，尼克坐在沙滩上，沉思着……

This nostalgia for a lost innocence, a lost paradise, for the mythos of summer, the genre of romance, reaches its climax in Nick’s closing description of a literal paradise forever gone. As Nick sits on the beach the evening before his return to Minnesota, he muses on

这里曾是荷兰水手们眼中繁花似锦的古老岛屿——新世界清新翠绿的胸怀。如今消失的树木，那些为盖茨比的豪宅让路的树木，曾低声诉说着人类最后也是最伟大的梦想；在那短暂而迷人的瞬间，人类一定屏息凝神，面对着这片大陆，被迫陷入一种既不理解也不渴望的审美沉思，在历史上最后一次与某种足以匹配其惊叹能力的事物面对面。

the old island here that flowered once for Dutch sailors’ eyes – a fresh, green breast of the new world. Its vanished trees, the trees that had made way for Gatsby’s house, had once pandered in whispers to the last and greatest of all human dreams; for a transitory enchanted moment man must have held his breath in the presence of this continent, compelled into an aesthetic contemplation he neither understood nor desired, face to face for the last time in history with something commensurate to his capacity for wonder.

（189；第9章）

(189; ch. 9)

这段文字象征着小说中发生的结构性变化：夏季的神话（浪漫、成功的冒险）被冬季的神话（讽刺、现实的复杂性）所取代，而冬季的神话则始终萦绕着它所克服的结构的丧失。

This passage is emblematic of the structural process that occurs over the course of the novel: the mythos of summer (romance, the successful quest) is overridden by the mythos of winter (irony, the complexities of reality), which remains haunted by the loss of the structure it has overcome.

因此，在《了不起的盖茨比》中，我们看到了一种相当复杂的结构运作。我们看到一种叙事语法，它由“寻找-发现-失去”及其子集“寻找却未找到”构成。我认为，这种语法反映了一种与现代主义时期相关的世界观，以及现代小说对传统“寻找与发现”式叙事的摒弃。类似地，文本的结构体现在两种截然不同的文学体裁之间的主导权争夺：浪漫（夏日神话，盖茨比的叙事属于这一体裁）和反讽（冬日神话，尼克的叙事属于这一体裁）。我认为，在小说中，浪漫体裁最终被反讽体裁所取代，尽管在整部文本中，前者以叙述者对逝去的过去、对浪漫而天堂般的青春的抒情描述的形式“萦绕”着后者。

In The Great Gatsby, then, we see the operations of quite a complex structure. We see a narrative grammar consisting of seek-find-lose and its subset, seek-but-don’t-find. This grammar, I have suggested, reflects a worldview associated with the modernist period and with the modern novel’s rejection of the traditional seek-and-find quest. Analogously, the text is structured by a struggle for dominance between two very different literary genres: romance (the mythos of summer and the genre to which Gatsby’s narrative belongs) and irony (the mythos of winter and the genre to which Nick’s narrative belongs). I have argued that the genre of romance is overcome by that of irony in the novel, although, throughout the text, the former “haunts” the latter in the form of the narrator’s lyric descriptions of a lost past, a romantic, paradisal youth.

因此，本文试图阐明结构主义的两个看似矛盾的方面：一是它对公式化描述的依赖，这种依赖源于其对数学式客观性的坚持；二是它作为一门人文科学的哲学基础，这要求我们思考我们所描述的结构公式与我们所生活的世界之间的关系。尽管在结构主义批评的实践中，第二个方面常常被忽略，但正是结构主义的这种双重性，对我们许多人来说，才使其如此引人入胜。

This analysis has thus attempted to illustrate two aspects of structuralism that sometimes seem in conflict: its reliance on formulaic description, which derives from its commitment to the kind of objectivity associated with mathematics, and its philosophical grounding as a science of humanity, which requires us to speculate on the relationship between the structural formulas we describe and the world in which we live. Although this second aspect is often forgotten in the practice of structuralist criticism, it is the dual nature of structuralism that, for many of us, makes it exciting.

拓展练习题：结构主义方法在文学作品中的应用

Questions for further practice: structuralist approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用结构主义批评来解读它们所指的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use structuralist criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1如何运用弗莱的神话理论来分析约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》（1902）？库尔茨是怎样的英雄？你会如何给马洛分类？这部小说在什么意义上可以被称为悲剧？它在什么意义上属于反讽体裁？我们在对这部作品进行分类时遇到的困难（或分歧）可能揭示了康拉德的小说或我们的分类体系的哪些问题？

1 How might you use Frye’s theory of mythoi to analyze Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness (1902)? What kind of hero is Kurtz? How would you classify Marlow? In what sense might the novel be called a tragedy? In what sense does it belong to the genre of irony? What might our difficulties (or disagreements) in classifying this text suggest about Conrad’s novel or about our system of classification?

2托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》（1987）由多条叙事线索交织而成，每条线索都讲述一个特定人物的故事。这些叙事线索包括与塞丝、丹佛、宠儿、贝比·萨格斯、保罗·D和斯塔姆·帕伊德相关的叙事。请找出小说中出现的所有叙事线索，并从结构上分析它们，如同分析一系列故事（某种意义上，它们确实是故事集）。是否存在一种贯穿所有“故事”的叙事语法？或者结构分析是否揭示了它们属于不同的结构类别？你的分析对莫里森的小说以及类似文本的意义建构方式有何启示？

2 Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987) is structured by the interweaving of several narratives, each the story of a particular character. There are, among others, narratives associated with Sethe, Denver, Beloved, Baby Suggs, Paul D, and Stamp Paid. Identify all the narratives present in the novel and analyze them structurally, as if they were a collection of stories (which, in a sense, they are). Is there a narrative grammar that informs all the “stories,” or does a structural analysis reveal that they belong to different structural groups? What does your analysis suggest about the way in which Morrison’s novel and similar texts make meaning?

3威廉·福克纳的小说《献给艾米丽的玫瑰》（1931）结构复杂，非常适合运用热奈特的理论框架进行分析。请运用热奈特的分类方法，分析故事、叙事和叙述之间的关系。务必讨论时态（顺序、持续时间和频率）、语气（距离和视角）以及声音的功能。你的分析如何帮助你理解福克纳在这篇小说中达到的叙事效果？你的发现是否适用于福克纳的其他作品？

3 William Faulkner’s story “A Rose for Emily” (1931) has a complex structure that lends itself well to Genette’s theoretical framework. Using Genette’s categories, analyze the text in terms of the relationship among story, narrative, and narration. Be sure to discuss the functions of tense (order, duration, and frequency), mood (distance and perspective), and voice. How does your analysis help you understand the narrative effects Faulkner achieves in this story? Do your findings apply to other Faulkner works?

4尽管内容截然不同，凯瑟琳·安妮·波特的《格拉尼·韦瑟罗尔的遗弃》（1930）和蒂莉·奥尔森的《我站在这里熨衣服》（1956）这两篇短篇小说在结构上却有诸多相似之处。例如，两篇小说都主要由内心独白构成；都由故事中的人物以非常有限且主观的视角进行叙述；并且都采用了……的结构。一系列倒叙。你还能发现哪些其他结构上的相似之处？请参考你认为最有助于理解这两部作品的结构叙事学家的著作。结构上的相似之处（或不同之处）是否与主题上的相似之处（或不同之处）相关？

4 Although their content is quite different, Katherine Anne Porter’s “The Jilting of Granny Weatherall” (1930) and Tillie Olsen’s “I Stand Here Ironing” (1956) are short stories with a number of structural similarities. For example, both consist largely of interior monologues; both are narrated by a character within the story who has a very limited, subjective point of view; and both are structured by a series of flashbacks. What other structural similarities can you find? Draw on the structural narratologist(s) whose work you find most helpful in illuminating these two pieces. Are structural similarities (or dissimilarities) related to similarities (or dissimilarities) in theme?

5约翰·斯坦贝克的政治小说《愤怒的葡萄》（1939）被好莱坞改编成电影。电影在很大程度上忠实于原著的结构、人物塑造和主题（逃离尘暴区、前往加州务工的佃农遭受资本家的剥削）。然而，电影的结局却充满乐观主义的胜利，与小说的结局截然相反。请运用弗莱的神话理论、模式理论和斯科尔斯的模式理论分析小说的体裁。然​​后，分析电影的结局如何促使你修正对小说的分类。你的研究结果对政治小说（自然主义体裁属于哪一类）与好莱坞“大团圆结局”的传统之间存在怎样的冲突有何启示？

5 John Steinbeck’s political novel The Grapes of Wrath (1939) was produced as a Hollywood film. For the most part, the film is very faithful to the novel’s structure, characterization, and theme (the capitalist exploitation of tenant farmers who fled the Dust Bowl to become migrant laborers in California). However, the film’s ending is triumphantly optimistic, in direct contrast to the ending of the novel. Analyze the novel’s genre using Frye’s theory of myths, Frye’s theory of modes, and Scholes’ theory of modes. Then analyze the ways in which the film’s ending calls for a modification of your classification of the novel. What do your findings suggest about the conflict between political novels (to which category the genre of naturalism belongs) and the Hollywood tradition of “the happy ending”?

笔记

Notes

1弗莱的《批评的解剖：四篇论文》试图从四个不同的角度系统化文学。他将这些方法称为：（1）模式理论，或历史批评（悲剧、喜剧和主题）；（2）符号理论，或伦理批评（字面/描述、形式、神话和寓意）；（3）神话理论，或原型批评（喜剧、浪漫故事、悲剧、反讽/讽刺）；以及（4）体裁理论，或修辞批评（史诗、散文、戏剧、抒情诗）。尽管关于弗莱的著作是否属于结构主义范畴存在一些争议，但《批评的解剖》中提出的这四种方法显然都是结构主义的体裁理论，因为它们都旨在探寻西方文学传统中各种体裁的结构原则，例如情节模式和人物功能。

1 Frye’s Anatomy of Criticism: Four Essays attempts to systematize literature in four different ways. He calls these approaches his (1) theory of modes, or historical criticism (tragic, comic, and thematic); (2) theory of symbols, or ethical criticism (literal/descriptive, formal, mythical, and anagogic); (3) theory of myths, or archetypal criticism (comedy, romance, tragedy, irony/satire); and (4) theory of genres, or rhetorical criticism (epos, prose, drama, lyric). Although there has been some debate concerning whether or not Frye’s work falls within the category of structuralism, it seems rather clear that all four of the approaches offered in Anatomy of Criticism are structuralist theories of genre because all seek the structural principles – such as plot formulas and character functions – that underlie genres in the Western literary tradition.

2并非所有原型批评都将文学作品中的神话主题与文学体裁联系起来。许多原型批评家，或称神话批评家——其中大多数受到卡尔·荣格的影响——分析文学作品是为了识别其所借鉴的具体神话。例如，参见博德金、坎贝尔和荣格的著作。

2 Not all archetypal criticism relates the mythic motifs found in literature to literary genres. Many archetypal critics, or myth critics – most of whom have been influenced by the work of Carl G. Jung – analyze literary works in order to identify the specific myths on which they draw. See, for example, Bodkin, Campbell, and Jung.

8. 解构主义批评

8   Deconstructive criticism

对于我们这些自诩为文学爱好者的人来说，“能指的随机游戏”和“超越的所指”之类的词句，唤起的恐惧和憎恶，恐怕就像当年十字军得知异教徒攻占圣城时所感受到的那样。尽管解构主义在学术界已不再是新鲜事物——这一理论由雅克·德里达于20世纪60年代末开创，并在70年代末对文学研究产生了重大影响——但许多学生和教师仍然误解解构主义，认为它只是对文字游戏的肤浅分析，会破坏我们对文学的鉴赏能力和对文学作品进行有意义的解读。解构主义经常被误解的原因之一可能是，该领域一些最杰出人物——雅克·德里达、露西·伊里加雷、杰弗里·哈特曼——的著作，以及那些试图总结这些思想家作品的人所提供的解释，经常使用非常规的语言和组织原则，以至于它们似乎难以被我们理解和接受。

For many of us who consider ourselves lovers of literature, phrases such as “the random play of signifiers” and “the transcendental signified” evoke the kind of fear and loathing the Crusaders must have felt when they learned that the infidels had taken the Holy City. Although deconstruction is no longer a new phenomenon on the academic scene – the theory was inaugurated by Jacques Derrida in the late 1960s and became a major influence on literary studies during the late 1970s – many students and faculty alike continue to misperceive deconstruction as a superficial analysis of wordplay that destroys our appreciation of literature and our ability to interpret it meaningfully. Perhaps one reason deconstruction is frequently misunderstood is that the writing by some of the biggest names in the field – Jacques Derrida, Luce Irigaray, Geoffrey Hartman – as well as the explanations offered by those who attempt to summarize the work of these thinkers, frequently employ such unusual language and organizational principles that they seem to defy our understanding and acceptance.

然而，解构主义确实能给我们带来诸多益处：它可以提升我们的批判性思维能力，让我们更容易地洞察自身经验如何被我们意识不到的意识形态所左右，因为这些意识形态“内嵌”于我们的语言之中。正因为解构主义具备这些优势，它才能成为马克思主义、女权主义以及其他旨在让我们意识到意识形态在生活中所扮演的压迫性角色的理论的有力工具。为了理解解构主义如何揭示意识形态在我们日常自我体验和世界体验中的隐蔽作用，我们首先必须理解解构主义对语言的看法。因为根据德里达的观点，语言并非我们所认为的那种可靠的沟通工具，而是一个流动、模糊的复杂经验领域，意识形态在这个领域中潜移默化地影响着我们，而我们却浑然不觉。

Nevertheless, deconstruction has a good deal to offer us: it can improve our ability to think critically and to see more readily the ways in which our experience is determined by ideologies of which we are unaware because they are “built into” our language. And because deconstruction offers these advantages, it can be a very useful tool for Marxism, feminism, and other theories that attempt to make us aware of the oppressive role ideology can play in our lives. In order to understand how deconstruction reveals the hidden work of ideology in our daily experience of ourselves and our world, we must first understand deconstruction’s view of language because, according to Derrida, language is not the reliable tool of communication we believe it to be, but rather a fluid, ambiguous domain of complex experience in which ideologies program us without our being aware of them.

解构语言

Deconstructing language

在日常生活中，我们大多数人都把语言视为理所当然，认为它能传达我们想要表达的意思；如果它没有传达，我们就认为是语言本身的问题。我们自身，而非语言本身。诸如“玛丽，请把书递给约翰”这样的短语通常会促成预期的行为，即便没有，我们也会认为问题不在于语言，而在于玛丽或约翰未能理解请求或拒绝执行。因为我们如此习惯于语言似乎总是按照我们想要的方式运作的日常模式和仪式，所以我们理所当然地认为语言本质上是一种稳定可靠的沟通思想、情感和愿望的工具。与此相反，解构主义的语言理论则基于这样一种信念：语言远比我们意识到的更加难以捉摸和模棱两可。

In our daily lives, most of us take language for granted, assuming that it communicates what we want it to, and if it doesn’t, we assume that the fault is in ourselves, not in language. A phrase such as “Mary, please hand John the book” usually results in the desired action, and even when it doesn’t we assume that the fault lies not in language but in Mary’s or John’s failure to understand the request or refusal to act on it. Because we are so used to the everyday patterns and rituals in which language seems to work the way we want it to, we assume that it is by nature a stable and reliable means of communicating our thoughts, feelings, and wishes. Deconstruction’s theory of language, in contrast, is based on the belief that language is much more slippery and ambiguous than we realize.

例如，请看这句话：“时光飞逝如箭”。我们大多数人都熟悉这句古老的谚语，也知道它的意思是时间过得很快：

Consider, for example, the following sentence: Time flies like an arrow. Most of us are familiar with this old saying, and we know it means that time passes quickly:

如果我请你提出其他含义，你可能会说这句话也可以理解为时间朝着一个方向，或者说笔直向前流动，因为箭就是这么飞的。但如果我们把句子的第一个词理解为祈使句——告诉我们去做某事——而把第二个词理解为某种昆虫，会怎么样呢？那么这句话就变成了一个命令：

If I asked you to suggest additional meanings, you might say that the sentence could also mean that time moves in one direction, or straight ahead, because that’s how arrows fly. But what would happen if we thought of the first word of the sentence as a verb in the imperative mode – telling us to do something – and the second word as if it represented a kind of insect? Then the sentence would be giving us an order:

如果我们把句子的前两个词——“时光飞逝”（想想果蝇）——看作是一种昆虫，把第三个词看作是动词“喜欢”的一种形式，会发生什么呢？那么，这句话就能告诉我们某种昆虫的情感生活了：

And what would happen if we thought of the first two words of the sentence as if they represented a kind of insect – time flies (think of fruit flies) – and the third word as if it were a form of the verb to like? Then the sentence would tell us something about the emotional life of a certain kind of insect:

这个练习表明，即使不改变一个词，一个句子也可以有多种含义。

This exercise shows how, without changing a word, a single sentence can have several meanings.

语气和重音的变化可以进一步揭示语言的微妙之处。例如，想象一下，一位新闻播音员要读这样一句话：“里根总统说，海军陆战队不必去萨尔瓦多。”

Changes in tone of voice and emphasis can further reveal the slippery quality of language. Imagine, for example, that a newscaster were given the following line to read: President Reagan says the Marines do not have to go to El Salvador.

现在请注意，根据强调的词语不同，句子的意思会发生多么巨大的变化：

Now note how the meaning of the sentence changes dramatically, depending on which word is emphasized:

1里根总统说海军陆战队不必去萨尔瓦多（暗示他在撒谎）。

1 President Reagan says the Marines do not have to go to El Salvador (implying that he’s lying).

2里根总统说海军陆战队不必去萨尔瓦多（暗示他是在纠正一个不实的谣言）。

2 President Reagan says the Marines do not have to go to El Salvador (implying that he’s correcting a false rumor).

3里根总统说海军陆战队不必去萨尔瓦多（言下之意是其他部队必须去）。

3 President Reagan says the Marines do not have to go to El Salvador (implying that some other group has to go).

4 里根总统说海军陆战队不必去萨尔瓦多（暗示另一位重要人物曾说过海军陆战队必须去萨尔瓦多）。

4 President Reagan says the Marines do not have to go to El Salvador (implying that another important person had said that the marines have to go to El Salvador).

5里根总统说，海军陆战队不必去萨尔瓦多（言下之意是，如果他们愿意，他们可以去）。

5 President Reagan says the Marines do not have to go to El Salvador (implying that they can go if they want to).

6里根总统说海军陆战队不必去萨尔瓦多（言下之意是他们必须去其他地方）。

6 President Reagan says the Marines do not have to go to El Salvador (implying that they have to go somewhere else).

这两个练习应该能帮助你开始意识到，语言并不像我们通常认为的那样稳定可靠。让我们进一步探讨这个观点。正如我们在第七章中看到的，结构主义者和符号学家用“符号”一词来指代交流的基本要素，他们用以下公式来定义符号。

These two exercises should help you begin to see that language isn’t as stable and reliable as we generally assume it is. Let’s examine this idea further. As we saw in Chapter 7, structuralists and semioticians use the word sign to denote a basic element of communication, and they define sign by the following formula.

词语是一种语言符号。例如，如果符号是单词“rose”（玫瑰），那么能指就是作为一个整体书写或发音的字母组合（“rose”），所指就是你脑海中浮现的玫瑰。如果能指（或者，在本例中，是一对能指）是“red rose”（红玫瑰），那么所指就是你脑海中浮现的红玫瑰。当然，不同的人听到能指“rose”时，可能会想到不同种类的玫瑰。而对于某些人来说，上述两个能指——“rose”和“red rose”——都会产生相同的所指，因为这些人总是把玫瑰想象成红玫瑰，除非被引导去想象其他的玫瑰。

A word is a linguistic sign. For example, if the sign is the word rose, then the signifier is the group of letters written or pronounced as a unit (“rose”), and the signified is the rose you picture in your mind. If the signifier (or, in this case, pair of signifiers) is “red rose,” then the signified is the red rose you picture in your mind. Of course, in response to the signifier “rose,” different people will probably picture different kinds of roses. And for some people, both of the above signifiers – “rose” and “red rose” – will produce the same signified because these people always picture roses as red roses unless prompted to do otherwise.

为了避免这种模糊不清和歧义，我们来看一个非常简单、具体的短语，它出现在一个非常具体的语境中，以至于其中的能指应该能产生一个非常清晰明确的所指。想象一下，一个人站在开阔的田野里，指着视野中唯一的一棵树。在这个语境中，由能指“这棵树很大”构成的短语似乎暗示着一个单一而清晰的所指：这里只提到了一棵树，而且我们知道是在描述它的大小。然而，解构主义要求我们审视句子中的歧义，即便乍看之下，这个句子似乎像这句话一样清晰明确。当说话者说“这棵树很大”时，她是在将这棵树与自己比较吗？还是与另一棵树比较？是哪棵树？她是否对树的大小感到惊讶？或者她仅仅是在告诉我们这棵树很大？她是为了让我们了解这棵树，还是为了让我们理解“大”这个词的含义？如果她认为我们需要这样的信息，她会怎么看待我们？她认为我们只是在学习英语吗？或者她是在讽刺我们？如果是，为什么？这一连串的问题或许显得有些牵强，但它确实表明，人类的表达很少（如果有的话）像结构主义公式“能指+所指”所暗示的那样清晰简单。正如我们所见，任何一个能指在任何特定时刻都可以指代任意数量的所指。虽然语境通常有助于我们缩小某些能指的可能指代范围，但同时也会扩大另一些能指的可能指代范围。正因如此，沟通才如此复杂且充满不确定性。

To avoid this kind of vagueness and ambiguity, let’s look at a very simple, concrete phrase uttered in a context so specific that the signifiers should produce a very clear and unambiguous signified. Picture a person standing in an open field pointing to the only tree in sight. In this context, a phrase consisting of the signifiers “This tree is big” seems to imply a single, clear signified: there is only one tree in question, and we know that a claim is being made about its size. Deconstruction, however, asks us to look at the sentence’s ambiguities, even when the sentence seems, at first glance, as clear and specific as this one does. When the speaker says, “This tree is big,” is she comparing the tree to herself? To another tree? What other tree? Is she surprised by the size of the tree? Or is she merely informing us that the tree is big? Is she informing us so that we will know something about the tree or so that we will understand something about the word big? What must she think of us if she believes we need such information? Does she think we are just learning to speak English? Or is she being sarcastic? If so, why? This string of questions may seem to push the point a bit far, but it does illustrate that human utterances are rarely, if ever, as clear and simple as the structuralist formula signifier + signified seems to imply. As we have seen, any given signifier can refer to any number of signifieds at any given moment. And although context often helps us to limit the range of possible signifieds for some signifiers, it simultaneously increases the range of possible signifieds for others. This is why communication is such a complicated and uncertain thing.

如果我们就此止步，可以将结构主义公式改写为：符号 = 能指 + 所指…… + 所指。也就是说，我们可以尝试将交流解释为所指的滑动累积。但是，“所指”究竟是什么意思呢？如果能指是“树”，那么所指必然是我们想象中能够描绘出的那棵树。但是，我们通过这棵想象中的树来理解什么呢？我们的概念又是由什么构成的呢？我们对树的概念是由我们一生中与它联系起来的所有能指链构成的，例如，就我个人而言，这些能指链包括“树荫”、“野餐”、“攀爬”、“锁骨骨折”、“徒步旅行”、“俄亥俄州霍金山”、“眩晕”、“秋叶”、“耙地”、“种植花旗松”、“松针鳞片虫”、“石灰硫磺”等等。结构主义所谓的所指，实际上始终是一系列能指的集合。

If we stopped at this point, we could rewrite the structuralist formula as sign = signifier + signified … + signified. That is, we could try to explain communication as a sliding accumulation of signifieds. But what does the term signified mean? If the signifier is “tree,” then the signified must be the tree in our imagination that we can picture. But what do we understand by this imagined tree? Of what does our concept consist? Our concept of the tree consists of all the chains of signifiers we have come to associate with it over the course of our lives, in my own case, for example, “shade,” “picnics,” “climbing,” “broken collarbone,” “hiking,” “Hocking Hills, Ohio,” “vertigo,” “autumn leaves,” “raking,” “planting Douglas firs,” “pine-needle scale,” “lime sulfur,” and so on. What structuralism calls the signified is really always a chain of signifiers.

因此，根据解构主义的观点，语言这棵树永远不会指向某个概念，即所指。我所说的能指指向我头脑中的能指链，并在听者心中唤起一系列能指链。而这些链中的每一个能指本身又由另一条能指链构成，如此往复。所以，在解构主义看来，语言并非能指与所指的结合，而仅仅是能指链本身。正如我们在第七章中所看到的，结构主义认为语言是非指涉性的，因为它不指涉世界上的事物，而仅仅指涉我们对世界上事物的概念。解构主义更进一步，声称语言是非指涉性的，因为它既不指涉世界上的事物，也不指涉我们对事物的概念，而仅仅指涉构成语言本身的能指的相互作用。

According to deconstruction, then, the word tree never reaches the point when it refers to a concept, a signified. The signifier I utter refers to chains of signifiers in my mind and evokes chains of signifiers in the mind of the person who hears my utterance. And each signifier in those chains is itself constituted by another chain of signifiers, and so on. So for deconstruction, language does not consist of the union of signifiers and signifieds; it consists only of chains of signifiers. As we saw in Chapter 7, structuralism says that language is nonreferential because it doesn’t refer to things in the world but only to our concepts of things in the world. Deconstruction takes that idea a big step further by claiming that language is nonreferential because it refers neither to things in the world nor to our concepts of things but only to the play of signifiers of which language itself consists.

因此，解构主义为我们提供了一种关于思维活动的全新视角。我们的精神生活并非由概念构成——并非由坚实、稳定的意义构成——而是由转瞬即逝、不断变化的能指游戏构成。这些能指看似稳定的概念——当我们听到它们被说出或看到它们时，它们看起来确实很稳定。写下来！——但它们在我们脑海中却无法稳定运作。正如我们之前所见，每一个能指都包含并产生更多的能指，从而形成一种永无止境的意义延宕或推迟：我们寻求坚实稳定的意义，但我们永远无法真正找到它，因为我们永远无法超越语言中能指的游戏。用德里达的话来说，我们所认为的意义实际上只是能指游戏留下的心理痕迹。而这种痕迹正是我们定义一个词时所依据的差异。让我来解释一下。

Deconstruction thus offers us a radical vision of the activity of thinking. Our mental life consists not of concepts – not of solid, stable meanings – but of a fleeting, continually changing play of signifiers. These signifiers may seem to be stable concepts – they look stable enough when we hear them spoken or see them written down! – but they don’t operate in a stable manner in our mind. As we saw earlier, every signifier consists of and produces more signifiers in a never-ending deferral, or postponement, of meaning: we seek meaning that is solid and stable, but we can never really find it because we can never get beyond the play of signifiers that is language. In Derrida’s words, what we take to be meaning is really only the mental trace left behind by the play of signifiers. And that trace consists of the differences by which we define a word. Let me explain.

意义似乎只有在我们区分词语（或事物）与其他词语（或事物）的差异时才存在于词语（或事物）之中。例如，如果我们认为所有物体都是同一种颜色，我们就根本不需要“红色”（或“蓝色”或“绿色”）这个词。红色之所以是红色，仅仅是因为我们认为它不同于蓝色和绿色（也因为我们认为颜色不同于形状）。因此，“红色”这个词本身就带有所有它所不代表的能指的痕迹（因为我们正是通过与其他能指的对比来定义它）。

Meaning seems to reside in words (or in things) only when we distinguish their difference from other words (or things). For example, if we believed that all objects were the same color, we wouldn’t need the word red (or blue or green) at all. Red is red only because we believe it to be different from blue and green (and because we believe color to be different from shape). So the word red carries with it the trace of all the signifiers it is not (for it is in contrast to other signifiers that we define it).

总而言之，德里达认为语言有两个重要特征：(1) 其能指的运作不断地延缓或推迟意义的产生；(2) 语言表面所呈现的意义，实际上是我们区分不同能指的差异的结果。在法语中， “ différer ”一词既可以表示“延缓”，也可以表示“不同”。因此，德里达创造了一个词，意在同时表达延缓和不同这两个含义：différance，这是他用来指代语言唯一“意义”的词汇。¹至此，你或许会疑惑，既然语言似乎指向一种并不存在的稳定意义，那么我们为何还要使用语言呢？德里达解释说，我们必须使用语言，因为如果我们没有其他工具，就必须使用我们所掌握的工具。但即便我们在使用这个工具时，我们也能意识到它并不像我们假设的那样坚固稳定，因此我们可以对其进行即兴发挥，拓展它以适应新的思维模式（这种活动被称为拼贴）。德里达正是通过这种拓展活动，将一个词置于他所谓的“擦除”之下，即先写下这个词，然后用一个大大的“X”将其划掉（例如，就像我在这里对这个词所做的那样，以表明他以一种新的方式使用了一个旧词）。

To sum up, Derrida argues that language has two important characteristics: (1) its play of signifiers continually defers, or postpones, meaning, and (2) the meaning it seems to have is the result of the differences by which we distinguish one signifier from another. In French, the word différer means either “to defer” or “to differ.” So Derrida coined a word intended to suggest both meanings – to defer and to differ – at the same time: différance, which is his name for the only “meaning” language can have.1 At this point, you may wonder, why use language at all if it seems to refer to a kind of stable meaning that doesn’t really exist? We must use language, Derrida explains, because we must use the tool at our disposal if we don’t have another. But even while we use this tool, we can be aware that it doesn’t have the solidity and stability we have assumed it has, and we can therefore improvise with it, stretch it to fit new modes of thinking (an activity called bricolage). Derrida does this stretching activity when he puts a word under erasure, as he calls it, by writing it and then crossing it out with a large X (for example, as I’m doing here with the word to indicate that he’s using an old word in a new way.

鉴于解构主义认为语言塑造了我们，且我们无法超越它，因此，以新的方式拓展语言显得尤为重要。我们无法超越语言，无法超越能指的运作，因为我们的存在——我们的思考、感知和感受——都根植于我们与生俱来的语言之中。我们如何感知和理解自身以及世界，都受制于我们被教导用来感知它们的语言。也就是说，语言调解了我们对自身和世界的体验。对于解构主义而言，语言完全是意识形态的：它完全由在特定文化中特定时期运作的众多相互冲突、动态变化的意识形态——或者说信仰和价值体系——构成。例如，我们用“荡妇”（slut）一词来指代与多名男性发生性关系的女性，用“种马” （stud）一词来指代与多名女性发生性关系的男性，这揭示并延续了一种文化观念，即与多名伴侣发生性关系对女性而言是耻辱，对男性而言则是骄傲。

It seems rather important that we stretch language in new ways, given deconstruction’s belief that language is what forms us and there is no way to get beyond it. There is no getting beyond language, beyond the play of signifiers, because we exist – we think, we perceive, we feel – within the language into which we were born. How we perceive and understand ourselves and the world is thus governed by the language with which we are taught to perceive them. That is, language mediates our experience of ourselves and the world. And for deconstruction, language is wholly ideological: it consists entirely of the numerous conflicting, dynamic ideologies – or systems of beliefs and values – operating at any given point in time in any given culture. For example, our use of the word slut for a woman who sleeps with many men and the word stud for a man who sleeps with many women reveals and perpetuates the cultural belief that sexual relations with multiple partners should be a source of shame for women and a source of pride for men.

为了更详细地说明语言的意识形态特性，我想分享一个我高中生物老师讲过的故事：多年前，在一个技术欠发达的国家，人们尝试推广安全期避孕法。参与该项目的每位女性都拿到一个类似算盘的装置，上面排列着红白相间的珠子，代表着她们的生育周期。每颗珠子代表一天，如果某天的珠子是红色的，就意味着当天不能进行性生活；白色的珠子则表示当天可以安全进行性生活。几个月后，统计数据显示，参与该项目的女性怀孕率没有任何变化，社工们百思不得其解。最终，他们发现，那些想在红珠日进行性生活的女性会简单地拨动珠子，直到出现白色的珠子：她们认为这些珠子具有某种魔力。因此，该项目最初失败的原因在于，无论是服务对象还是社工，都只能从自身的文化或意识形态视角来看待这个项目。客户和社会工作者以为他们理解对方的语言，但实际上他们并没有，因为他们不了解对方语言背后的意识形态。

To cite an extended example of the ideological quality of language, let me pass on a story my high school biology teacher told us about the attempt to introduce the rhythm method of birth control in a technologically underdeveloped country many years ago. Each woman in the program was given an abacus-like device, consisting of red and white beads arranged to represent her fertility cycle. Each bead represented one day and, if a given day’s bead was red, she was not to have sexual intercourse; a white bead meant that sex on that day was safe. After several months passed, statistics showed that the pregnancy rate among women in the program had not changed at all, and social workers were at a loss to understand the problem. They finally discovered that women who wanted to have sex on red-bead days would simply push the beads over until a white one appeared: they assumed the beads were a kind of magic. Thus the program initially failed because both clients and social workers were able to view the project only in terms of their own cultural, or ideological, perspectives. Clients and social workers thought they understood each other’s language, but they didn’t because they didn’t understand the ideologies of which each other’s language was composed.

为了探究语言如何具体地决定我们的经验，德里达借鉴并改造了结构主义的观点，即我们倾向于用对立的两极来概念化我们的经验——我们通过它们彼此之间的对立来理解它们——这种对立被称为二元对立。例如，根据结构主义，我们通过与“恶”的对比来理解“善”这个词。类似地，我们理解理性是情感的对立面，男性是女性的对立面，文明是原始的对立面，等等。然而，德里达指出，这些二元对立也是一种微小的等级制度。也就是说，一对概念中总有一个概念处于优先地位，或者被认为优于另一个概念。 （在上述二元对立中，每一对中的第一个词在西方文化中都是享有特权的词。）因此，通过在文化作品（例如小说、电影、对话、课堂或法庭审判）中发现二元对立，并确定对立中的哪个成员享有特权，人们可以发现该作品所宣扬的意识形态。

To explore the specific ways in which our language determines our experience, Derrida borrowed and transformed structuralism’s idea that we tend to conceptualize our experience in terms of polar opposites – each of which we understand by means of its opposition to the other – called binary oppositions. For example, according to structuralism, we understand the word good by contrasting it with the word evil. Similarly, we understand reason as the opposite of emotion, masculine as the opposite of feminine, civilized as the opposite of primitive, and so on. However, Derrida noted that these binary oppositions are also little hierarchies. That is, one term in the pair is always privileged, or considered superior to the other. (In the binary oppositions listed above, the first term in each pair is, in Western culture, the privileged term.) Therefore, by finding the binary oppositions at work in a cultural production (such as a novel, a film, a conversation, a classroom, or a courtroom trial), and by identifying which member of the opposition is privileged, one can discover something about the ideology promoted by that production.

德里达指出，为了发现已揭示的意识形态的局限性，必须考察对立双方并非完全对立的方式，以及它们之间的重叠或共同之处。例如，考虑美国文化中“客观”和“主观”这两个词的二元对立。我们倾向于将客观等同于非人格化的、理性的（这意味着智慧）以及人类经验的科学维度，因此认为客观性是可靠性的必要标准。与之形成鲜明对比的是，我们倾向于将主观等同于人格化的、情感化的（这意味着非智慧）甚至是人类经验的非理性维度，因此认为主观性是不可靠的。我们可以从我们文化对……的推崇中看到这种对客观的偏爱。客观的新闻报道，体现在其对客观历史数据的接受，以及对客观科学实验的依赖。对我们而言，客观是知识的来源；主观仅仅是观点的来源。

In order to discover the limitations of the ideology one thus has uncovered, Derrida observed, one must examine the ways in which the two members of the opposition are not completely opposite, the ways in which they overlap or share some things in common. For example, consider the binary opposition in American culture between the words objective and subjective. We tend to identify the objective with the impersonal, the rational (which implies the intelligent), and the scientific dimensions of human experience and therefore consider objectivity a necessary criterion of reliability. In sharp contrast, we tend to identify the subjective with the personal, the emotional (which implies the unintelligent), and even the irrational dimensions of human experience and therefore consider it unreliable. We can see this privileging of the objective over the subjective in our culture’s praise of “objective” news reporting, in its acceptance of “objective” historical data, and in its reliance on “objective” scientific experimentation. For us, the objective is the source of knowledge; the subjective is merely the source of opinion.

为了解构这种二元对立，并了解其所支持的意识形态的局限性，让我们思考一下客观与主观并非真正对立的种种方式。例如，当记者、历史学家和科学家收集“客观”数据时，他们究竟基于什么来决定使用哪些数据、舍弃哪些数据？即便他们遵循特定的数据收集准则，我们又如何确定这些准则本身就是“客观的”？无论如何，我们又如何确定这些准则能够被“客观地”解读并应用于每一条收集或舍弃的数据？也就是说，记者、历史学家和科学家难道不是拥有主观需求、恐惧和欲望（包括职业动机）的普通人吗？这些因素会在他们的认知或认知之外影响他们。一个人真的能够完全摆脱自身的观点、感受和偏见吗？声称自己做到了这一点，无疑是在自欺欺人。那么，客观性难道不正是我们为了掩盖自身的主观性而对自己和他人撒的一个谎吗？那么，客观性难道不是伪装的主观性吗？

To deconstruct this binary opposition and learn something about the limitations of the ideology it supports, let’s consider the ways in which the objective and the subjective are not really opposites. For example, when reporters, historians, and scientists gather “objective” data, on what basis do they decide which data to use and which to discard? Even if they are following specific guidelines for data collection, how can we be sure those guidelines are “objective,” and, in any case, how can we be sure that the guidelines are “objectively” interpreted and applied to each piece of data collected or discarded? That is, aren’t reporters, historians, and scientists human beings with subjective needs, fears, and desires (including career motivations) that might influence them with or without their knowledge? Can one totally escape one’s own viewpoints, feelings, and biases? Surely, to claim that one has done so is to claim the impossible. Isn’t objectivity, then, really a lie we tell ourselves and others about our subjectivity? Isn’t objectivity, therefore, subjectivity in disguise?

换个角度来看，对客观的推崇难道不是对理性的推崇胜过情感的产物吗？毕竟，主观性之所以被否定，是因为它被情感“污染”了，我们认为情感会蒙蔽我们的思维，削弱我们客观（也就是理性）的能力。然而，将所有情感都归为非理性真的合理吗？某些情感难道不是对特定情境最“理性”的反应吗？难道不是能产生最准确、最有用、最可靠的洞见的反应吗？而对理性的执着，难道不是源于对自身情感的恐惧吗？关键在于，语言——词义，我们用来组织经验的语言范畴——并非像我们想象的那样井然有序。语言中充满了各种含义、联想和矛盾，而这些恰恰反映了构成语言的意识形态的含义、联想和矛盾。

Looked at from a different perspective, isn’t the privileging of the objective over the subjective a product of the privileging of reason over emotion? After all, subjectivity is discredited because it is “contaminated” by emotion, which we believe clouds our thinking and undermines our ability to be objective, that is, to be rational. However, is it really rational to lump all emotions in the category of the irrational? Aren’t some emotions sometimes the most “rational” response one can have to a given situation, that is, the response that produces the most accurate, useful, and reliable insights? And isn’t the insistence on the rational sometimes an emotional response produced by fear of one’s own feelings? The point here is that language – the meanings of words, the linguistic categories by which we organize our experience – doesn’t operate in the tidy fashion we like to think it does. Language is constantly overflowing with implications, associations, and contradictions that reflect the implications, associations, and contradictions of the ideologies of which it is formed.

解构我们的世界

Deconstructing our world

因为文化的意识形态是通过语言传承的，所以说我们正是通过语言来构想和感知我们的世界和我们自身，这并非不合理。用哲学术语来说，对于解构主义而言，语言是我们的“存在基础”，或者说是我们经验和世界知识的生成根基。但是，正如我们将看到的，从解构主义的视角来看，语言作为一种存在基础，与通常与传统西方哲学相关的那些存在基础截然不同。

Because it is through language that a culture’s ideologies are passed on, it is not unreasonable to say that it is through language that we come to conceive and perceive our world and ourselves. To put the matter in philosophical terms, for deconstruction, language is our “ground of being,” or the foundation from which our experience and knowledge of the world are generated. But, as we shall see, language, from a deconstructive perspective, is a very different ground of being from those generally associated with traditional Western philosophies.

自柏拉图以来，西方思想史上的每一个哲学体系都有其存在的基础。也就是说，所有西方哲学体系都源于并围绕着一个基本原则构建，我们相信可以从中探寻存在的意义。对一些思想家而言，存在的基础是某种宇宙秩序或和谐的原则，例如柏拉图关于完美理念的思想，它存在于一个抽象的、永恒的思维维度中。对另一些思想家而言，这一基本原则是理性思维在自我反思中的体现，例如笛卡尔的名言“我思故我在”（Cogito ergo sum）。还有一些思想家则认为，存在的基础是人类与生俱来的（先天且永恒的）特质，例如结构主义认为人类语言和经验是由人类意识的内在结构所生成的。

In the history of Western thought since Plato, every philosophical system has had its ground of being. That is, all systems of Western philosophy derive from and are organized around one grounding principle from which we believe we can figure out the meaning of existence. For some thinkers, the ground of being is some cosmic principle of order or harmony, as illustrated, for example, by Plato’s idea of perfect Forms that exist in an abstract, timeless dimension of thought. For others, that grounding principle is rational thought engaged in the act of self-reflection, as illustrated by Descartes’ famous statement, “I think, therefore I am” (Cogito ergo sum). For others still, the grounding principle is some innate (inborn and permanent) quality in human beings as illustrated by structuralism’s belief that human language and experience are generated by innate structures of human consciousness.

这些基础概念虽然构建了我们对周围动态演化的世界——以及我们自身动态演化——的理解，但概念本身却保持稳定。与它们所解释的一切事物不同，它们本身并不动态演化。正如德里达所说，它们“置身事外”。德里达将这种哲学——简而言之，即所有西方哲学——称为逻各斯中心主义，因为它将一个概念（逻各斯）置于其世界理解的核心（中心） ，这个概念为我们组织和解释世界，却又置身于它所组织和解释的世界之外。但在德里达看来，这正是西方哲学最大的错觉。既然每一个基础概念——柏拉图的理念论、笛卡尔的“我思故我在”、结构主义的人类意识固有结构等等——本身都是人类概念，因而也是人类语言的产物，那么它又怎能超越语言的歧义呢？也就是说，任何概念又怎能超越产生它的语言的动态演化和充满意识形态的运作呢？

While these grounding concepts produce our understanding of the dynamic, evolving world around us – and of our dynamic, evolving selves as well – the concepts themselves remain stable. Unlike everything they explain, they are not dynamic and evolving. They are “out of play,” as Derrida would put it. This type of philosophy – in short, all Western philosophy – Derrida calls logocentric because it places at the center (centric) of its understanding of the world a concept (logos) that organizes and explains the world for us while remaining outside of the world it organizes and explains. But for Derrida, this is Western philosophy’s greatest illusion. Given that each grounding concept – Plato’s Forms, Descartes’ cogito, structuralism’s innate structures of human consciousness, and so on – is itself a human concept and therefore a product of human language, how can it be outside the ambiguities of language? That is, how can any concept be outside the dynamic, evolving, ideologically saturated operations of the language that produced it?

对德里达而言，答案在于任何概念都无法超越语言的动态不稳定性。语言如同花朵随风播撒种子一般，每一次书面或口头表达都传播着无数种可能的意义。因此，对于解构主义而言，语言是存在的基础，但这个基础并非无关紧要：它本身与它所产生的世界观一样，都是动态的、不断演进的、充满问题的，并且饱含意识形态。正因如此，我们对存在的理解并不存在一个中心。相反，存在着无数个观察存在的视角，而每个视角都有其自身的语言，解构主义称之为“话语”。例如，有现代物理学的话语、基督教原教旨主义的话语、二十一世纪初几十年博雅教育的话语、十九世纪英国医学的话语等等。换句话说，德里达颠覆了西方哲学的中心地位，正如哥白尼在 17 世纪颠覆了地球的中心地位一样，他断言宇宙并非围绕地球运转。

For Derrida, the answer is that no concept is beyond the dynamic instability of language, which disseminates (as a flower scatters its seeds on the wind) an infinite number of possible meanings with each written or spoken utterance. For deconstruction, then, language is the ground of being, but that ground is not out of play: it is itself as dynamic, evolving, problematical, and ideologically saturated as the worldviews it produces. For this reason, there is no center to our understanding of existence. There are, instead, an innumerable number of vantage points from which to view it, and each of these vantage points has a language of its own, which deconstruction calls its discourse. For example, there is the discourse of modern physics, the discourse of Christian fundamentalism, the discourse of liberal arts education in the opening decades of the twenty-first century, the discourse of nineteenth-century British medicine, and so on. In other words, Derrida decentered Western philosophy just as Copernicus decentered the earth in the 1600s by asserting that the universe does not revolve around it.

认为我们对世界的认知是由语言构建的这一理论，在西方哲学去中心化的过程中扮演着关键角色，因为语言不再被视为我们经验的产物（首先我们看到的是地上的一个巨大的洞；然后……）。我们称之为大峡谷，但更确切地说，它是一种构建我们体验的概念框架。例如，当早期的西班牙探险家第一次看到如今非美洲原住民所称的大峡谷时，他们的认知体系——或者说他们的语言——中没有任何内容能够让他们准确地感知峡谷的尺寸。例如，他们认为峡谷底部的科罗拉多河只有几百英尺远。结果，他们命令全副武装的步兵侦察该地区——跑下去四处看看——令他们的同胞惊讶的是，这些士兵再也没有回来。这个例子说明了概念（我们的想法）如何先于感知（我们通过感官体验到的东西），以及我们的期望、信念和价值观——所有这些都由语言承载——如何决定我们体验世界的方式。虽然结构主义者是最早提出我们对世界的看法是由我们所说的语言构建的，但他们认为语言是由人类意识中稳定、固有的结​​构产生的。因此，解构主义被称为后结构主义理论，不仅因为它是在结构主义流行之后出现的，而且还因为它对结构主义关于语言和人类经验的有序观点做出了反动。

The theory that our view of the world is constructed by language performs a key role in the decentering of Western philosophy because language is no longer seen as a product of our experience (first we see an enormous hole in the ground; then we call it the Grand Canyon) but rather as the conceptual framework that creates our experience. For example, when the early Spanish explorers first saw what non-Native Americans now call the Grand Canyon, there was nothing in their conceptual repertoire – in their language – to enable them to perceive its dimensions accurately. For instance, they thought the Colorado River, at the bottom of the canyon, was only a few hundred feet away. As a result, foot soldiers in full armor were ordered to reconnoiter the area – to run down and have a look around – and to the surprise of their countrymen, they never returned. This example illustrates how conception (what we think) precedes perception (what we experience through our senses) and how our expectations, beliefs, and values – all of which are carried by language – determine the way we experience our world. While structuralists were among the first to argue that our view of the world is constructed by the language we speak, they believe that language is generated by stable, innate structures of human consciousness. Thus, deconstruction is called a poststructuralist theory, not only because it emerged in the wake of structuralism’s popularity but also because it constitutes a reaction against structuralism’s orderly vision of language and human experience.

解构人类身份

Deconstructing human identity

在解构主义看来，如果语言是存在的基础，那么世界就是无限的文本，即永远处于运作状态的无限能指链。因为人类是由语言构成的，所以他们本身也是文本。换言之，解构主义的语言理论对主体性，即对“人”的意义，具有深远的影响。

For deconstruction, if language is the ground of being, then the world is infinite text, that is, infinite chains of signifiers always in play. Because human beings are constituted by language, they, too, are texts. In other words, deconstruction’s theory of language has implications for subjectivity, for what it means to be a human being.

正如我们所见，解构主义断言，我们对自身和世界的体验是由我们所说的语言所建构的。由于所有语言都是一个不稳定、模糊的、相互竞争的意识形态场，因此我们自身也是不稳定、模糊的、相互竞争的意识形态场。我们许多人所拥有的稳定身份的自我形象，实际上只是一种令人感到安慰的自我欺骗，这种欺骗是我们与文化共同炮制出来的。因为文化也希望将自身视为稳定和连贯的，而实际上它极不稳定且支离破碎。我们并不真正拥有一个身份，因为“身份”一词暗示我们由一个单一的自我构成，但事实上我们是多元且分裂的，在任何时刻都包含着无数相互冲突的信念、欲望、恐惧、焦虑和意图。然而，随着我们长大，我们通过语言内化了我们文化中的意识形态冲突和矛盾，每个人都找到了一种“融入”的方式，通过否认我们生活在其中的支离破碎、含糊不清的语言所产生的自身支离破碎的体验，来达到目的。

As we have seen, deconstruction asserts that our experience of ourselves and our world is produced by the language we speak, and because all language is an unstable, ambiguous force-field of competing ideologies, we are, ourselves, unstable and ambiguous force-fields of competing ideologies. The self-image of a stable identity that many of us have is really just a comforting self-delusion, which we produce in collusion with our culture, for culture, too, wants to see itself as stable and coherent when in reality it is highly unstable and fragmented. We don’t really have an identity because the word identity implies that we consist of one, singular self, but in fact we are multiple and fragmented, consisting at any moment of any number of conflicting beliefs, desires, fears, anxieties, and intentions. However, as we grow up, we internalize through language the ideological conflicts and contradictions of our culture, each finding a way to “fit in” by finding a way to deny, both to ourselves and others, the fragmented experience of ourselves produced by the fragmented, ambiguous language within which we live.

这一切听起来是不是相当糟糕，甚至令人困惑？别急着放弃。让我们先来看看解构人类经验为我们带来的一些有趣的视角。首先，难道……自我碎片化是否能解释我们日常生活中许多不同的体验？我们大多数人在工作、购物、约会或独自看电视时，难道不是截然不同的两个人吗？即使我们只关注工作中的自我体验，例如，随着我们遇到不同的人，或者随着各种想法、记忆和情绪的涌现，这种体验难道不会每天、有时甚至每时每刻都在变化吗？换句话说，我们每个人难道不都是一个万花筒般的自我吗？事实上，我们难道不会有时感觉自己并不真正了解自己吗？尤其是在我们与那些（因为我们从外部观察）自我形象似乎始终如一的人进行比较时？同样地，如果我们创造了自己的“身份”，那么我们也可以重塑它。这不正是许多人加入匿名戒酒互助会或因心理咨询或宗教皈依而“幡然悔悟”时所做的吗？最后，语言的歧义性和意识形态性难道不能解释我们在与他人沟通时遇到的许多困难吗？尤其是在与背景与我们不同的人沟通时？或许，理解解构主义的语言理论可以帮助我们了解这种意识形态差异何时以及如何发挥作用。

Does all this sound rather grim, if not completely confusing? Well, don’t jump ship yet. Let’s consider first some of the interesting vantage points on human experience deconstruction opens up for us. First of all, doesn’t the idea of a fragmented self explain a good deal of our day-to-day experience? Aren’t most of us very different people on the job, at the store, on a date, or alone in front of the television set? And even if we confine our investigation to our experience of ourselves on the job, for example, doesn’t that experience change from day to day, sometimes from hour to hour or minute to minute, as we encounter different people or as various thoughts, memories, and emotions occur? In other words, isn’t each of us really a kaleidoscope of selves? In fact, don’t we sometimes have the feeling that we don’t know who we really are, especially when we contrast ourselves to other people who (because we view them from the outside) seem so consistent in their self-image? Similarly, if we’ve invented our “identity,” then we can reinvent it. Isn’t that exactly what many people do when they join Alcoholics Anonymous or have a “change of heart” as a result of psychological counseling or religious conversion? Finally, doesn’t the ambiguous, ideological nature of language explain many of the difficulties we encounter in communicating with others, especially with others from backgrounds different from our own? Perhaps an understanding of deconstruction’s theory of language can help us see when and how such ideological differences are operating.

解构文学

Deconstructing literature

现在让我们花点时间总结一下本章目前为止讨论的三个要点。对于解构主义而言，（1）语言是动态的、模糊的、不稳定的，它不断地传播着各种可能的意义；（2）存在没有中心，没有稳定的意义，也没有固定的根基；（3）人类是相互竞争的意识形态的碎片化战场，而我们唯一的“身份”是我们自己创造并选择相信的。正如你可能已经注意到的，这里的关键词是“不稳定”。因此，对于解构主义而言，文学也像构成它的语言一样，具有动态性、模糊性和不稳定性，这一点也就不足为奇了。

Now let’s take a moment to summarize the three main points we’ve discussed so far in this chapter. For deconstruction, (1) language is dynamic, ambiguous, and unstable, continually disseminating possible meanings; (2) existence has no center, no stable meaning, no fixed ground; and (3) human beings are fragmented battlefields for competing ideologies whose only “identities” are the ones we invent and choose to believe. As you may have noticed, the key word here is unstable. It should come as no surprise, then, to learn that, for deconstruction, literature is as dynamic, ambiguous, and unstable as the language of which it is composed.

意义并非文本中一个稳定存在的元素，供我们去发现或被动地接受。意义是由读者在阅读过程中创造的。更准确地说，意义是通过读者这一媒介，由语言的运作而产生的，尽管我们通常将这一过程称为“读者”。此外，所创造的意义并非一个能够得出最终结论的稳定元素；也就是说，没有任何一种解释能够最终定论。相反，文学文本，如同所有文本一样，由多种相互重叠、相互冲突的意义构成，这些意义彼此之间以及与我们之间都存在着动态的、流动的关系。那些被认为是“显而易见”或“符合常理”的文本解读，实际上是意识形态解读——由某种文化的价值观和信仰所产生的解读——我们对此习以为常，以至于认为它们是“自然而然的”。简而言之，我们创造了我们在文本中“发现”的意义和价值。正如作者在创作文本时不可避免地会受到其文化环境假设的影响一样，读者也无法避免地会受到其文化环境的影响。他们构建解读时所基于的假设。因此，文学文本和批评文本都可以被解构。

Meaning is not a stable element residing in the text for us to uncover or passively consume. Meaning is created by the reader in the act of reading. Or, more precisely, meaning is produced by the play of language through the vehicle of the reader, though we generally refer to this process as “the reader.” Furthermore, the meaning that is created is not a stable element capable of producing closure; that is, no interpretation has the final word. Rather, literary texts, like all texts, consist of a multiplicity of overlapping, conflicting meanings in dynamic, fluid relation to one another and to us.
