What have been considered the “obvious” or “common-sense” interpretations of a given text are really ideological readings – interpretations produced by a culture’s values and beliefs – with which we are so familiar that we consider them “natural.” In short, we create the meaning and value we “find” in the text. Just as authors can’t help but draw on the assumptions of their cultural milieux when they construct their texts, readers can’t help but draw on the assumptions of theirs when they construct their readings. Therefore, both literary and critical texts can be deconstructed.

文学文本的解构通常有两个主要目的，在任何一次解构解读中，我们都可能看到其中之一或两者同时发挥作用：（1）揭示文本的不可判定性；（2）揭示文本所构建的意识形态的复杂运作及其局限性。就你目前对解构的理解而言，我认为你会发现第二种方法更有意义、更有用，因此我将仅简要概述第一种方法，然后更详细地描述第二种方法。

There are generally two main purposes in deconstructing a literary text, and we may see either or both at work in any given deconstructive reading: (1) to reveal the text’s undecidability and/or (2) to reveal the complex operations and limitations of the ideologies of which the text is constructed. At this stage in your relationship to deconstruction, I think you’ll find the second procedure more meaningful and useful, so I’ll provide only a brief summary of the first approach and then describe the second more fully.

揭示文本的不可判定性，意味着表明文本的“意义”实际上是一系列不确定、不可判定、多元且相互冲突的可能意义，因此，就传统意义上而言，文本本身根本没有意义。以下简要概述了一种实现这一目标的方法。提供此概述并非期望您按照此方法进行文本分析，而是为了帮助您更深入地理解文本最终不可判定性的含义。

To reveal a text’s undecidability is to show that the “meaning” of the text is really an indefinite, undecidable, plural, conflicting array of possible meanings and that the text, therefore, has no meaning, in the traditional sense of the word, at all. One way to pursue this goal is outlined, in brief, below. This outline is offered, not in the expectation that you will perform a textual analysis along these lines, but to help increase your sense of what it means to say that texts are, ultimately, undecidable.

1认真努力地去发现文本所提供的各种解释的例子——对文本整体的解释，以及对特定人物、情节事件、图像等等的解释。

1 Work conscientiously to discover as many examples as you can of the various interpretations – interpretations of the text as a whole as well as interpretations of particular characters, plot events, images, and so on – the text seems to offer.

2尽可能多地找出这些解释的具体方面相互冲突的例子。

2 Find as many examples as you can of the ways in which specific aspects of these interpretations conflict with one another.

3解释这些冲突是如何不可调和的——它们无法共同作用，产生对文本的单一、有意义的解释——或者解释通过进一步解释来解决这些冲突的尝试是如何揭示文本中其他相互冲突的含义的。

3 Explain how these conflicts are either irreconcilable – they can’t operate together to produce a single, meaningful interpretation of the text – or how attempts to resolve these conflicts through additional interpretation uncover additional conflicting meanings in the text.

4使用步骤 1、2 和 3 来论证文本的不可判定性。

4 Use steps 1, 2, and 3 to argue for the text’s undecidability.

不可判定性并非意味着读者无法在各种可能的解读中做出选择，也并非意味着文本无法“决定”它想要表达的内容。相反，不可判定性意味着读者和文本都与语言意义的传播密不可分。也就是说，读者和文本如同交织在语言这台永不停歇的织机上的丝线。具体的意义仅仅是意义的“瞬间”，它们必然会为更多意义的出现让位于意义本身。因此，文学文本被用来阐释构成所有文本（无论文学与否）的不确定、多元且相互冲突的意义，因为所有文本都由语言构成。这是一项有益且有趣的探索，因为此类解读能够有效地提醒我们，语言及其所有产物（包括我们自身）都是丰富、激动人心、有时令人警醒但始终引人入胜的意义的繁衍。

Undecidability does not mean that the reader is unable to choose among possible interpretations. And it does not mean that the text cannot “make up its mind” as to what it wants to say. Rather, undecidability means that reader and text alike are inextricably bound within language’s dissemination of meanings. That is, reader and text are interwoven threads in the perpetually working loom of language. Specific meanings are just “moments” of meaning that give way, inevitably, to more meanings. Thus, the literary text is used to illustrate the indefinite, plural, conflicting possible meanings that constitute all texts, literary and otherwise, because all texts are made of language. This is a useful and interesting endeavor because such readings serve as helpful reminders that language and all of its products, including ourselves, are rich, exciting, sometimes alarming but always interesting, proliferations of meanings.

解构文学文本的另一个目的（我们将在后文详细讨论）是探究文本能够揭示其构建过程中所蕴含的意识形态。这种探索通常会让我们了解……意识形态也影响着我们对世界的认知。因此，我认为无论你的理论偏好如何，这都是一项极其有益的练习。为了理解这种解构方法是如何运作的，让我们将其与第五章讨论的新批评方法进行对比，因为新批评的诸多原则至今仍在课堂上教授，使我们大多数人对这种方法都相当熟悉，而且新批评的阅读方法通常可以作为文本解构的第一步。

The other purpose in deconstructing a literary text, which we’ll discuss at greater length, is to see what the text can show us about the ideologies of which it is constructed. This endeavor usually shows us something about the ways in which ideologies operate in our own view of the world as well. For these reasons, I think it is an extremely useful exercise whatever your theoretical preferences are. To understand how this kind of deconstruction works, let’s contrast it with the New Critical approach discussed in Chapter 5 because enough New Critical principles are still taught in the classroom to make that approach fairly familiar to most of us and because a New Critical reading often can serve as the first step in the deconstruction of a text.

正如你可能记得的，新批评旨在揭示文本作为一个统一整体的运作方式，通过展示文本的形式或风格要素——例如意象、象征、语调、韵律、节奏、情节、人物塑造、场景、视角等等——如何构建其主题、整体意义或信息。首先，新批评家会识别文本中存在的核心张力，例如善恶之争、主人公从天真到成熟的转变、科学与宗教的冲突，或其他具有情感或道德意义的张力。然后，新批评家会展示这种张力如何在文本推进其主题的过程中得到化解——例如，善恶存在于我们每个人心中；从天真到成熟的转变虽然必要，但也可能代价高昂，同时也充满回报；科学一旦演变成宗教就会变得危险；或其他具有人文意义的主题——而文本中的所有形式要素都为之做出贡献。新批评派尤其欣赏文学文本中的张力、反讽、歧义和悖论，但所有这些特质都必须服务于一个统一的目的，即支撑文本的主题。文本中任何看似冲突的含义都必须被证明服务于主题，从而使整部文本能够流畅、自然、完整地实现其艺术目的。

As you may recall, New Criticism seeks to reveal how the text works as a unified whole by showing how its main theme, or overall meaning or message, is established by the text’s formal, or stylistic, elements: imagery, symbolism, tone, rhyme, meter, plot, characterization, setting, point of view, and so forth. First, the New Critic identifies the central tension operating in the text, for example, the struggle between good and evil, the protagonist’s evolution from innocence to experience, the conflict between science and religion, or some other tension that is emotionally or morally compelling. Then the New Critic shows how that tension is resolved in the text’s advancement of its main theme – for example, that good and evil exist in all of us; that the evolution from innocence to experience, though necessary, can be costly as well as rewarding; that science becomes dangerous when it becomes a religion; or some other theme that has human significance – to which all the formal elements in the text contribute. While New Critics especially appreciate tension, irony, ambiguity, and paradox in a literary text, all of these qualities must serve the unifying purpose of supporting the text’s main theme. Any conflicting meanings that seem to appear in the text must be shown to serve some function for the main theme so that the whole text can be seen to achieve its artistic purpose smoothly, seamlessly, and completely.

对于解构主义而言，这意味着新批评家与文本串通一气，掩盖那些揭示其意识形态框架局限性的自相矛盾之处。为了找到这个意识形态框架并理解其局限性，解构主义批评家会寻找文本中与主题相冲突的意义，着重关注文本似乎并未意识到的自相矛盾。掌握这一方法的最佳途径就是亲身实践。让我们以罗伯特·弗罗斯特的精彩诗作《修墙》（1914）为例来探讨。

For deconstruction, this means that the New Critic is in collusion with the text to hide the self-contradictions that reveal the limitations of its ideological framework. To find that ideological framework and understand its limitations, a deconstructive critic looks for meanings in the text that conflict with its main theme, focusing on self-contradictions of which the text seems unaware. The best way to grasp this procedure is to try it. Let’s do so with Robert Frost’s wonderful poem “Mending Wall” (1914).

对罗伯特·弗罗斯特的《修墙》进行解构性解读

A deconstructive reading of Robert Frost’s “Mending Wall”

修墙

Mending Wall

有些东西不喜欢墙，

Something there is that doesn’t love a wall,

这会导致其下方的冻土隆起。

That sends the frozen-ground-swell under it,

并将上方的巨石倾倒在阳光下，

And spills the upper boulders in the sun,

甚至能拉出两人并排通过的缝隙。

And makes gaps even two can pass abreast.

猎人的工作则是另一回事：

The work of hunters is another thing:

我随后进行了修复。

I have come after them and made repair

他们把石头上连一块石头都没留下。

Where they have left not one stone on a stone,

但他们会把兔子从藏身之处赶出来。

But they would have the rabbit out of hiding,

为了安抚那些吠叫的狗。我指的是缝隙。

To please the yelping dogs. The gaps I mean,

没有人见过它们被制作出来，也没有人听说过它们被制作出来。

No one has seen them made or heard them made,

但到了春季缝补衣物的时候，我们却在那里发现了它们。

But at spring mending-time we find them there.

我把这件事告诉了山那边的邻居；

I let my neighbor know beyond the hill;

有一天，我们相约走这条线。

And on a day we meet to walk the line

再次在我们之间筑起高墙。

And set the wall between us once again.

我们一路保持着彼此之间的距离。

We keep the wall between us as we go.

每个人都得到了落到自己身上的巨石。

To each the boulders that have fallen to each.

有些像面包，有些几乎像球。

And some are loaves and some so nearly balls

我们需要施个魔法才能让它们达到平衡：

We have to use a spell to make them balance:

“在我们转身之前，都待在原地别动！”

“Stay where you are until our backs are turned!”

我们经常摆弄它们，手指都磨粗糙了。

We wear our fingers rough with handling them.

哦，不过是另一种户外游戏而已。

Oh, just another kind of outdoor game,

一边。仅此而已：

One on a side. It comes to little more:

在那里，我们不需要这堵墙：

There where it is we do not need the wall:

他浑身都是松树，而我浑身都是苹果园。

He is all pine and I am apple orchard.

我的苹果树永远也到不了那边去。

My apple trees will never get across

我告诉他，去吃他家松树下的松果。

And eat the cones under his pines, I tell him.

他只说：“好篱笆造就好邻居。”

He only says, “Good fences make good neighbors.”

春天是我内心的恶作剧，我好奇

Spring is the mischief in me, and I wonder

如果我能把一个想法灌输到他脑子里：

If I could put a notion in his head:

“为什么他们会成为好邻居？难道不是吗？”

“Why do they make good neighbors? Isn’t it

哪里有牛？可是这里没有牛。

Where there are cows? But here there are no cows.

在砌墙之前，我会先问问自己。

Before I built a wall I’d ask to know

我当时用墙围起来或用墙围起来的东西，

What I was walling in or walling out,

我本想冒犯谁。

And to whom I was like to give offense.

有些东西不喜欢墙，

Something there is that doesn’t love a wall,

他想把它拆掉。”我可以对他说“精灵”，

That wants it down.” I could say “Elves” to him,

但它们并不完全是精灵，我更喜欢……

But it’s not elves exactly, and I’d rather

他说的都是他自己说的。我看到他在那里了。

He said it for himself. I see him there,

用手紧紧抓住石头的顶端

Bringing a stone grasped firmly by the top

每只手里都拿着，像一个武装起来的古老石像野人。

In each hand, like an old-stone savage armed.

在我看来，他似乎在黑暗中行动。

He moves in darkness as it seems to me,

不仅限于树林和树荫。

Not of woods only and the shade of trees.

他不会违背他父亲的话。

He will not go behind his father’s saying,

他很喜欢自己能想到这个主意。

And he likes having thought of it so well

他再次说道：“好篱笆造就好邻居。”

He says again, “Good fences make good neighbors.”

对文本进行新批评式的解读——即这首诗的核心张力是什么？它又是如何通过诗歌对主题的统一推进而得到解决的？——通常是解构文学作品的有效第一步，因为这类解读几乎总是建立在二元对立的基础上，其中一方凌驾于另一方之上。文本所支持的一方——二元对立的“一方”——通常揭示了文本所秉持的意识形态（或至少是其中一种意识形态）。一旦形成新批评式的解读，就可以解构它所依赖的二元对立：也就是说，可以对其进行考察，找出文本中对立元素相互重叠或并非真正对立的方式。而这正是我们了解文本（有意或无意地）所宣扬的意识形态局限性的方法。

A New Critical reading of the text – What is the central tension at work in this poem, and how is it resolved in the poem’s unified advancement of its main theme? – is often a useful first step in deconstructing a literary work because such readings can almost always be found to rest on a binary opposition in which one member of the pair is privileged over the other. The member of the pair – the “side” of the binary opposition – the text supports usually reveals the ideology (or at least one of the ideologies) the text embraces. Once a New Critical reading is formulated, the binary opposition on which it rests can be deconstructed: that is, it can be examined to find the ways in which the opposing elements in the text overlap or aren’t really opposed. And this is how we can learn something about the limitations of the ideology the text (consciously or unconsciously) promotes.

以《修墙》为例，文本中二元对立的结构显然体现在说话者与其邻居之间的分歧上。说话者主张，当人们所遵循的传统不再适应自身所处的境况时，就应该打破常规。而邻居则不假思索地主张墨守成规，墨守成规。因此，这首诗的二元对立便是“不墨守成规”与“墨守成规”之间的对立。由于我们是从说话者的视角来看待这一情境，因而同情他，所以可以说“不墨守成规”是这首诗的核心概念。从新批评的视角来看——或者用解构主义的术语来说，这首诗的显性意识形态意图——其主题可以概括为：它批判了盲目地墨守过时的传统，而“墙”正是这种传统的隐喻。

In the case of “Mending Wall,” it seems rather clear that the binary opposition structuring the text can be found in the disagreement between the speaker and his neighbor. The speaker advocates nonconformity when the tradition one has followed no longer fits the circumstances in which one finds oneself. The neighbor, without even thinking about what he is doing, advocates conformity to the way things have always been done in the past. Thus the binary opposition structuring the poem is that between nonconformity and conformity. Because we see the situation from the speaker’s point of view and our sympathies therefore lie with him, it is safe to say that nonconformity is the privileged term. The main theme, from a New Critical perspective – or, in deconstructive terms, the poem’s overt ideological project – might be stated as follows: the poem criticizes mindless conformity to obsolete traditions for which the wall is a metaphor.

为了确保我们识别出这首诗的意识形态意图，而不是仅仅设定一个容易被攻击的目标，我们必须以新批评的方式，找出诗歌中所有支持我们所识别主题的证据。例如，我们接受诗人对邻居和过时传统的负面看法，因为他清楚地表明这堵墙已经失去了存在的意义——“我的苹果树永远也过不去/吃不到他松树下的松果”（第25-26行）——而且因为诗人将自己与自然联系起来（“春天[一种自然现象]是我心中的恶魔”：第28行），而自然通常被认为是美好的。事实上，我们对自然智慧的信仰促使我们最初接受诗人在诗歌开头四行中的观点，这四行将自然与墙对立起来：正是自然“使冻土隆起”，将“上方的巨石”倾泻到阳光下（第2-3行）。

To be sure that we have identified the poem’s ideological project and not just set up an easy target that we can then proceed to shoot down, we must find, in New Critical fashion, all the evidence the poem offers in support of the theme we’ve identified. For example, we accept the speaker’s negative views of his neighbor and of obsolete traditions because he clearly shows that the wall has outlived its purpose – “My apple trees will never get across / And eat the cones under his pines” (ll. 25–26) – and because the speaker associates himself with nature (“Spring [a natural event] is the mischief in me”: l. 28), which is generally presumed good. Indeed, our faith in nature’s wisdom promotes our initial acceptance of the speaker’s viewpoint in the poem’s opening four lines, which put nature in opposition to the wall: it is nature that “sends the frozen-ground-swell” to spill “the upper boulders in the sun” (ll. 2–3).

当男人们“不得不施咒”才能让那些不听话的巨石（天然物体）保持原位时（第18-19行），以及暗示巨石会在男人们一转身就掉落时（第19行），这一主题得到了强化。自然的“孩子”——第5-7行中的猎人和第36行中的精灵——也支持了说话者对这堵墙的态度。此外，我们常常将“墙”这个词与沟通或情感交流的障碍联系起来，而这种功能也被强调了。第13-15行再次强调了这一点，从而强化了我们对这堵墙以及维系这堵墙的过时传统的摒弃：“总有一天我们会相遇……/再次在我们之间筑起这堵墙。/我们一路走来，始终保持着这堵墙”（我的斜体字）。最后，邻居被比作一个“古石野蛮人”，他“在黑暗中行走……/不仅在树林和树荫下”（第40-42行），也就是说，他未开化。因此，邻居与开明的说话者形成了鲜明的对比，后者明白应该摒弃过时的传统。

This theme is reinforced when the men “have to use a spell” to make the unwilling boulders, natural objects, stay in place (ll. 18–19) and when it is implied that the boulders will fall as soon as the men turn their backs (l. 19). Nature’s “children” – the hunters in lines 5–7 and the elves in line 36 – also support the speaker’s attitude toward the wall. In addition, we often associate the word wall with barriers to communication or emotional exchange, and this function is insisted upon in lines 13–15, thereby reinforcing our rejection of the wall and of the obsolete tradition that keeps it in place: “And on a day we meet … / And set the wall between us once again. / We keep the wall between us as we go” (my italics). Finally, the neighbor is compared to an “old-stone savage” who “moves in darkness … / Not of woods only and the shade of trees” (ll. 40–42), that is, who is unenlightened. Thus, the neighbor is contrasted sharply with the enlightened speaker, who knows that obsolete traditions should be abandoned.

到目前为止，我们已经找到了构成这首诗主题结构的二元对立：不墨守成规/墨守成规。我们也确定了诗中哪一方占据主导地位：不墨守成规。下一步是解构这种对立，找出诗中所有与这种等级制度相冲突或削弱它的内容。也就是说，我们必须找到与我们刚刚收集到的支持新批评理论对诗歌主题解读的证据相矛盾的文本证据。这种矛盾的证据往往容易被忽视，尤其是在像新批评家那样，人们试图在文学文本中寻找统一的意义时。我们现在的目标是表明，一旦我们开始关注诗歌内部的矛盾而非其统一性，诗歌就会揭示出，支撑主题的二元对立中，任何一方都不能凌驾于另一方之上。换句话说，尽管大多数读者没有接受过这方面的训练，但我们将展示这首诗是如何自我解构的。

So far we’ve located the binary opposition that thematically structures the poem: nonconformity/conformity. And we’ve determined which member of the opposition is privileged in the poem: nonconformity. The next step is to deconstruct this opposition by finding everything in the poem that conflicts with or undermines this hierarchy. That is, we must find textual evidence that contradicts the evidence we have just gathered in support of our New Critical reading of the poem’s main theme. This contradictory evidence is the kind that tends to be overlooked when one is searching for a unified meaning in a literary text, as the New Critics did. Our goal now is to show that, once we begin to focus on the poem’s internal contradictions instead of its unity, the poem reveals that neither side of the binary opposition supporting the main theme can be privileged over the other. In other words, though most readers have not been trained to see it, we will show how the poem deconstructs itself.

首先，诗歌中诸多冲突围绕着诗人对邻居盲目顺从的强调展开，这种反差体现在他们对分隔两地的围墙的态度上。自然站在诗人一边——反对传统（即反对顺从）——希望拆掉围墙，但猎人们也同样如此，他们不仅象征着自然，也象征着传统。由于他们狩猎是为了娱乐（他们想要“把兔子从藏身之处赶出来”，未必是为了果腹，而是为了“取悦吠叫的猎犬”：第8-9行），猎人们唤起了一种源于英国乡绅传统狩猎的体育传统。类似地，魔法，以精灵的形式，希望拆掉围墙（第36行），而魔法，以第18-19行的魔法“咒语”的形式，又被用来维持围墙的存在。此外，由于精灵是顽皮的生物，传说中它们喜欢给人类制造麻烦，因此它们想要拆掉这堵墙的愿望，与其说是促进工程，不如说是削弱了我们对这项工程的信任。事实上，说话者使用“精灵”这样含义模糊的词语，以及他难以找到合适的词语（“严格来说，不是精灵”：第37行），都暗示了他自己对这堵墙及其所代表的传统抱有无意识的矛盾心理。说话者过去曾独自修缮过这堵墙，如今又请邻居帮忙，这更加强化了他的矛盾心理。这些行为似乎与他对这堵墙的非传统态度自相矛盾。

In the first place, a number of conflicts revolve around the poem’s privileging of the speaker’s nonconformity over the unthinking conformity of his neighbor, a difference represented by their attitudes toward the wall that separates their property. Siding with the speaker, nature – against tradition (that is, against conformity) – wants the wall down, but so do the hunters, who function not only as emblems of nature but of tradition as well. Because they hunt for sport (they want “the rabbit out of hiding,” not necessarily for food, but to “please the yelping dogs”:ll.8–9), the hunters evoke a sporting tradition that has its roots in the traditional hunt of the British landed gentry. Analogously, while magic, in the form of elves, wants the wall down (l. 36), magic, in the form of the magic “spell” in lines 18–19, is invoked to keep the wall up. Furthermore, because elves are mischievous creatures who, according to legend, delight in making trouble for human beings, their desire to have the wall down can just as easily undermine our trust in the project rather than promote it. In fact, the speaker’s use of such an ambiguous term as elves, and his difficulty in finding the right word (“it’s not elves exactly”: l. 37), imply his own unconscious ambivalence toward the wall and toward the tradition it represents. This ambivalence is reinforced by the speaker’s having repaired the wall on his own in the past and by his having called on his neighbor to do so now. These behaviors certainly seem to contradict his nonconformist attitude toward the wall.

最后，这首诗批判的主要观点——“好篱笆造就好邻居”——实际上在诗歌的行动中是成立的：那就是修墙的行为。正是这项工作将两人聚集在一起，想必激发了这首诗的创作灵感，也让他们通过共同劳动这一纽带成为了邻居。显然，这是两人唯一一次见面。如果我们把“ mending” （修补）理解为形容词而非动词，那么诗的标题也暗示了这一点：“Mending Wall”（修补墙）就变成了一堵修补墙（例如，修补人际关系），而不是一堵被修补的墙。

Finally, the main idea the poem criticizes – good fences make good neighbors – is actually valid within the action of the poem: it is the activity of mending the wall that brings the men together, presumably inspiring the poem’s creation, and lets them be neighbors through the bonding activity of shared work. Evidently, this is the only time the two men meet at all. Even the poem’s title suggests this idea if we read mending as an adjective rather than a verb: “Mending Wall” then becomes a wall that mends (for example, that mends relationships) rather than a wall that is mended.

既然我们已经展示了这首诗是如何悄然瓦解支撑其主题的二元对立，那么我们解构的最后一步就是思考这种瓦解的意义。例如，顺从的意义、重要性和力量与不顺从的意义、重要性和力量，似乎并不像《修墙》最初暗示的那样泾渭分明。这首诗呼吁理性地摒弃看似空洞的传统，这种态度很容易让人联想到1914年诗歌发表前五十年间发生的科学技术进步。然而，这种传统的价值，以及试图摒弃它的可疑性，却构成了对这种呼吁的有力反制。或许，文本中的这种冲突表明，传统的强大力量很大程度上在于它能够在我们不知不觉中影响我们的态度。

Now that we’ve shown how the poem quietly collapses the binary opposition supporting its own main theme, the final step of our deconstruction is to consider the implications of this collapse. It would seem, for example, that the meaning, importance, and power of conformity and the meaning, importance, and power of nonconformity are not as easily placed in opposition as “Mending Wall” initially appears to suggest. The poem calls for a rational abandonment of a seemingly empty tradition, an attitude easily associated with the scientific and technological progress that occurred during the five decades preceding the poem’s publication in 1914. Yet the value of that tradition, and the dubious nature of the attempt to abandon it, form a powerful counterweight against that call. Perhaps this conflict in the text suggests that much of the power of tradition lies in its ability to influence our attitudes without our being aware of its presence.

诗中不墨守成规与墨守成规之间无法调和的冲突之所以存在，原因之一在于，用来唤起二者差异的某些词语——尤其是“自然”和“原始”这两个词——本身就在我们的文化中引发了复杂的情感。例如，我们把自然与美好联系在一起——天真、纯洁、简朴、健康、直觉智慧——然而，自然往往阻碍着我们高度重视的科学技术进步。为了修建道路，我们炸毁山脉；为了发展商业，我们砍伐森林；为了促进工业发展，我们污染空气、土壤和水源。同样，西方文化将原始与自然的美好联系在一起，但同时也将其与无知、未知和邪恶联系在一起，这种联系会引发恐惧和蔑视。正如我们所见，“魔法”、“精灵”和“猎人”这些词语也引发了相互矛盾的联想。那么，或许我们对《修墙》的解构应该让我们重新思考影响我们文化的其他二元对立，例如男性/女性、个人/群体和客观/主观。

One reason the unresolvable conflict between nonconformity and conformity occurs in the poem is that some of the terms used to evoke their difference – especially the terms nature and primitive – themselves evoke mixed feelings in our culture. For example, we associate nature with goodness – innocence, purity, simplicity, health, intuitive wisdom – yet nature usually stands in the way of the scientific and technological progress we value so highly. Mountains are blown up to build our roads; forests are destroyed to foster our business enterprises; and air, soil, and water are polluted to promote our industries. Similarly, Western culture associates the primitive with the goodness of nature, yet it also associates the primitive with ignorance, the unknown, and the sinister, and this association evokes fear and contempt. And as we have seen, conflicting associations are also evoked by the words magic, elves, and hunters. Perhaps, then, our deconstruction of “Mending Wall” should make us reconsider other binary oppositions that inform our culture, such as masculine/feminine, individual/group, and objective/subjective.

正如对《修墙》的解读所示，解构主义并非试图将文学文本中的主题张力消解为某种稳定统一的解释，而是力图维持这些张力，以便从中汲取养分。文学作品中存在相互冲突的意识形态，且这些意识形态并未被纳入某种统摄性的目的或主题之中，这并非如新批评所认为的那样是一种缺陷，而是语言固有的不稳定性与意识形态冲突的必然产物，并且这种产物能够丰富我们对文本的体验。这是一种将艺术视为意义沸腾、不断变化之熔炉的视角。作为一种与孕育它的文化和诠释它的文化都紧密相连的动态实体，艺术成为我们理解自身文化、历史、语言以及我们自身的载体。

As this reading of “Mending Wall” illustrates, deconstruction does not try to resolve the thematic tensions in literary texts into some stable, unified interpretation, but rather tries to sustain those tensions in order to learn from them. That a literary work has conflicting ideological projects that are not absorbed in some overarching purpose or theme is not considered a flaw, as it was for New Criticism, but a necessary product of the instability and ideological conflict inherent in language, and it is a product that can enrich our experience of the text. This is a vision of art as a seething cauldron of meanings in flux. As a dynamic entity tied to both the culture that produced it and the culture that interprets it, art becomes a vehicle for understanding our culture, our history, our language, and ourselves.

我们必须记住，所有写作（或者更广义地说，所有交流），包括我们对文学文本的解构，都在不断地自我解构，不断地传播意义。换句话说，严格来说，我们并非解构文本本身，而是展现文本如何自我解构。因此，刚才概述的过程有助于我们观察《修墙》是如何自我解构的，并利用我们的观察来了解语言的意识形态运作。但我们必须记住，我们从诗歌分析中得出的意义仅仅是文本意义传播过程中的一个“瞬间”，只要这首诗被阅读，它就会继续传播意义。

It is important to remember that all writing (or, more broadly, all communication), including our deconstruction of a literary text, continually deconstructs itself, continually disseminates meanings. In other words, strictly speaking, we do not deconstruct a text; we show how the text deconstructs itself. The process just outlined, then, helps us to observe how “Mending Wall” deconstructs itself and to use our observations to learn about the ideological operations of language. But we must remember that the meanings we derived from our analysis of the poem constitute only a “moment” in the text’s dissemination of meanings, which it will continue to disseminate as long as the poem is read.

解构主义批评家对文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions deconstructive critics ask about literary texts

以下两个问题总结了上面讨论的两种解构方法。

The following two questions summarize the two deconstructive approaches discussed above.

1我们如何利用文本产生的各种相互矛盾的解读（“意义的游戏”），或者找出文本未能回答其看似回答的问题的各种方式，来论证语言的不稳定性以及意义的不可判定性？（请记住，解构主义对“不可判定性”一词的使用方式很特殊。）

1 How can we use the various conflicting interpretations a text produces (the “play of meanings”) or find the various ways in which the text doesn’t answer the questions it seems to answer, to demonstrate the instability of language and the undecidability of meaning? (Remember that deconstruction uses the word undecidability in a special way.)

2文本似乎宣扬何种意识形态？也就是说，文本公开的意识形态意图（其主题、整体意义或信息）是什么？文本中相互矛盾的证据又如何揭示了这种意识形态的局限性？我们通常可以通过寻找构成文本主题的二元对立来发现文本公开的意识形态意图。

2 What ideology does the text seem to promote? That is, what is the text’s overt ideological project (its main theme, or overall meaning or message)? And how does conflicting evidence in the text show the limitations of that ideology? We can usually discover a text’s overt ideological project by finding the binary opposition that structures the text’s main theme.

根据所讨论的文学文本，我们可能会提出上述一个或两个问题。或者，我们可能会找到一种此处未列出的、有效的文本解构方法。这只是两个起点，旨在引导我们以富有成效的解构方式思考文学文本。请记住，即使解构批评家关注的是文本中相同的意识形态，他们也不会以相同的方式解读同一作品。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。我们的目标是运用解构来丰富我们对文学文本的阅读，帮助我们看到文本所阐述的一些重要思想——如果没有解构，我们可能无法如此清晰或深刻地理解这些思想——并帮助我们认识到语言是如何蒙蔽我们对它所蕴含的意识形态的认知的。

Depending on the literary text in question, we might ask one or both of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful way of deconstructing the text not listed here. These are just two starting points to get us thinking about literary texts in productive deconstructive ways. Keep in mind that not all deconstructive critics will interpret the same work in the same way, even if they focus on the same ideological projects in the text. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use deconstruction to help enrich our reading of literary texts, to help us see some important ideas they illustrate that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply without deconstruction, and to help us see the ways in which language blinds us to the ideologies it embodies.

以下对F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的解构式解读，旨在展示对该小说进行解构可能产生的结果。值得注意的是，在关于马克思主义批评的章节中，我们已经对该小说进行了一次简要的解构式解读。您或许还记得，对《了不起的盖茨比》的马克思主义解读包含两个方面。首先，它揭示了……文本首先对资本主义意识形态进行了强有力的批判；然后，它揭示了文本自身对所批判的资本主义世界的迷恋是如何削弱了这种批判的。这种解读的第二个组成部分是对第一个组成部分的解构，因为它借鉴了小说中的一些元素，揭示了文本自身反资本主义意识形态的局限性。因此，正如我们之前提到的，由于解构有助于我们理解意识形态的隐蔽运作，它对于任何有兴趣考察意识形态在我们生活中可能扮演的压迫性角色的批评家来说，都是一个有用的工具。事实上，马克思主义和女性主义批评家在解构原则被发展成为语言理论的一部分并被称为“解构”之前，就经常在文学和文化分析中运用解构原则，而且他们至今仍在运用这些原则。

The following deconstructive reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a deconstruction of that novel might yield. It is important to note that a brief deconstructive reading of the novel has already been presented in the chapter on Marxist criticism. The Marxist reading of The Great Gatsby, you may recall, had two components. First, it showed the ways in which the text offers a powerful critique of capitalist ideology; then it showed the ways in which that critique is undermined by the text’s own fascination with the capitalist world it condemns. The second component of this reading is a deconstruction of the first because it draws on elements in the novel to show the limitations of the text’s own anticapitalist ideology. Thus, as we noted earlier, because deconstruction helps us understand the hidden operations of ideology, it can be a useful tool for any critic interested in examining the oppressive role ideology can play in our lives. In fact, Marxist and feminist critics had often used deconstructive principles in their analyses of literature and culture before those principles were developed as part of a theory of language and called deconstruction, and they still use them today.

在接下来的《了不起的盖茨比》解构中，我将论证，小说公开的意识形态计划——对20世纪20年代美国颓废风气的批判，认为它永远地取代了过去纯真年代的美好——被文本自身对支撑这一意识形态计划的二元对立（过去/现在、纯真/颓废、西方/东方）的矛盾态度所削弱。这种矛盾态度在杰伊·盖茨比的人物塑造中体现得最为淋漓尽致，他是小说对它所批判的现代世界隐秘迷恋的浪漫化身。尽管这种对小说的解构解读比上文所述的马克思主义解构更为宽泛，但它们对美国颓废风气的共同关注，正如我们将看到的，使它们具有一些共同之处。

In the deconstruction of The Great Gatsby that follows, I will argue that the novel’s overt ideological project – the condemnation of American decadence in the 1920s, which replaced forever the wholesome innocence of a simpler time – is undermined by the text’s own ambivalence toward the binary oppositions on which that ideological project rests: past/present, innocence/decadence, and West/East. This ambivalence finds its most conflicted expression in the characterization of Jay Gatsby, the romantic embodiment of the novel’s covert fascination with the modern world it condemns. Although this deconstructive reading of the novel is much broader than the Marxist deconstruction described above, their shared focus on American decadence gives them, as we shall see, some elements in common.

“……我青春岁月里那些激动人心的返程列车……”：对《了不起的盖茨比》的解构式解读

“ … the thrilling, returning trains of my youth … ”: a deconstructive reading of The Great Gatsby

在菲茨杰拉德的小说《了不起的盖茨比》（1925年）接近尾声时，叙述者尼克·卡拉威对他在东部的经历彻底失望，开始回忆他在明尼苏达州的青年时代：

Toward the end of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925), narrator Nick Carraway, thoroughly disillusioned by his experience in the East, reminisces about his youth in Minnesota:

我最深刻的记忆之一，就是圣诞节期间从预科学校和大学回到西部的情景。那些去了比芝加哥更远的地方的人，会在十二月的一个傍晚六点聚集在昏暗的老旧的联合车站……

One of my most vivid memories is of coming back west from prep school and later from college at Christmas time. Those who went farther than Chicago would gather in the old dim Union Station at six o’clock of a December evening …

当我们驶入冬夜，真正的雪，我们自己的雪，开始在我们身旁铺展开来，在车窗上闪烁，威斯康星州小车站昏暗的灯光掠过，空气中突然涌起一股强劲而狂野的气息。我们深深地吸了一口气……无比清晰地感受到我们与这片土地的联系……

When we pulled out into the winter night and the real snow, our snow, began to stretch out beside us and twinkle against the windows, and the dim lights of small Wisconsin stations moved by, a sharp wild brace came suddenly into the air. We drew in deep breaths of it … unutterably aware of our identity with this country …

那是我记忆中的中西部……我年轻时乘坐的激动人心的返程火车，寒冷夜色中闪烁的街灯和雪橇铃声，以及灯光照耀下的冬青花环在雪地上投下的阴影。我也是其中的一部分，对漫长的冬季略感忧郁，对成长中的些许安逸。在卡拉威家，这座城市里的住宅几十年来仍然沿用着家族的姓氏。

That’s my middle-west … the thrilling, returning trains of my youth and the street lamps and sleigh bells in the frosty dark and the shadows of holly wreaths thrown by lighted windows on the snow. I am part of that, a little solemn with the feel of those long winters, a little complacent from growing up in the Carraway house in a city where dwellings are still called through decades by a family’s name.

（184；第9章）

(184; ch. 9)

这种对过去的怀旧之情在小说中以各种方式涌现，并赋予其情感力量，而这正是我认为文本中最普遍、最直白的意识形态建构：对20世纪20年代美国颓废风气的批判，这种颓废风气永远地取代了过去纯真美好的时光。对现代世界的怪诞刻画，两位满怀希望的年轻人——尼克·卡拉威和杰伊·盖茨比——在被卷入残酷的现实后痛苦的幻灭，以及对理想化过去的怀旧描绘，共同构成了一部深切哀悼美国在第一次世界大战结束后十年间纯真逝去的哀悼之作。然而，正如我们将看到的，在《了不起的盖茨比》中，这种对被当下颓废所腐蚀的理想化过去的信念，本身就是一个不稳定的意识形态建构。因为它本身对支撑这一计划的二元对立——过去/现在、纯真/颓废、西方/东方——抱有矛盾态度，这种矛盾态度在杰伊·盖茨比的刻画中得到了最矛盾的体现，他是这部小说对它所谴责的现代世界隐秘迷恋的浪漫化身。

Such nostalgia for the past emerges in various ways throughout the novel and lends emotional force to what I will argue is the text’s most pervasive and overt ideological project: the condemnation of American decadence in the 1920s, which replaced forever the wholesome innocence of a simpler time. The grotesque portrayal of the modern world, the painful disillusionment of two hopeful young men – Nick Carraway and Jay Gatsby – as they are initiated into the harsh realities of that world, and the nostalgic representations of an idealized past create a novel that deeply mourns the passing of America’s innocence during the decade following the end of World War I. As we shall see, however, this belief in an idealized past corrupted by the decadence of the present is, in The Great Gatsby, an unstable ideological project. For it is deconstructed by the text’s own ambivalence toward the binary oppositions on which that project rests – past/present, innocence/decadence, and West/East – an ambivalence that finds its most conflicted expression in the characterization of Jay Gatsby, the romantic embodiment of the novel’s covert fascination with the modern world it condemns.

《了不起的盖茨比》所描绘的现代世界几乎毫无可取之处。这是一个由汤姆·布坎南和迈耶·沃尔夫希姆这样的人掌控的世界，尽管他们站在法律的对立面，但这两个人物都是被私利吞噬的掠食者，为了达到目的，他们能够为自己的所作所为找到各种理由，绕过任何道德障碍。这是一个空虚的世界，自私、酗酒和粗俗充斥其中，优雅的社交舞蹈变成了“老男人推着年轻女孩在永无止境的笨拙圆圈里往后退”，以及“地位显赫的情侣们扭捏地、时髦地搂着彼此，躲在角落里”（51；第三章）。与尼克年轻时在明尼苏达州的生活不同，这里没有丝毫的恒久感和稳定性。布坎南一家永远“不安分地四处漂泊，哪里有打马球、哪里有钱人聚在一起”（10；第一章）。乔丹也总是在酒店、俱乐部和别人的家中辗转。即使是乔治·威尔逊，凭借着他所拥有的微薄积蓄，也认为他可以通过离开家乡，搬到西部来解决他的问题。匿名和孤立是常态而非例外。书中没有一个人物拥有亲密而持久的友谊，而人性的疏离似乎在尼克在纽约街头看到的那些“可怜的年轻职员”身上得到了体现，“他们徘徊在窗前，等待着独自一人去餐厅吃晚餐的时间——黄昏时分的年轻职员，浪费着夜晚和生命中最令人心酸的时刻”（62；第三章）。

There is little to redeem the modern world portrayed in The Great Gatsby. It’s a world run by men like Tom Buchanan and Meyer Wolfsheim, and despite their positions on opposite sides of the law, both characters are predators consumed by self-interest, capable of rationalizing their way around any ethical obstacle to get what they want. It’s an empty world where selfishness, drunkenness, and vulgarity abound, where the graceful social art of dancing has become “old men pushing young girls backward in eternal graceless circles” and “superior couples holding each other tortuously, fashionably, and keeping in the corners” (51; ch. 3). Unlike life in the Minnesota of Nick’s youth, there is no sense of permanence or stability. The Buchanans are forever “drift[ing] here and there unrestfully wherever people played polo and were rich together” (10; ch. 1). Jordan is always on the move among hotels, clubs, and other people’s homes. And even George Wilson, with the scant means he has at his disposal, thinks he can solve his problems by pulling up stakes and moving to the West. Anonymity and isolation are the rule rather than the exception. None of the characters has close, lasting friendships, and the alienation of humanity seems to be summed up in the “poor young clerks” Nick sees on the streets of New York City, “who loitered in front of windows waiting until it was time for a solitary restaurant dinner – young clerks in the dusk, wasting the most poignant moments of night and life” (62; ch. 3).

此外，小说中描绘的每个群体，无论其成员的阶级、性别或种族如何，都存在着将追求社会地位和享乐置于一切之上的肤浅价值观。中产阶级而像麦基一家、默特尔·威尔逊、默特尔的妹妹凯瑟琳以及盖茨比形形色色的派对宾客这样的工人阶级人物，与富有的布坎南家族一样，同样在意社会地位，同样渴望寻欢作乐。参加盖茨比晚宴的女性角色，即便不是比男性宾客更甚，也同样肤浅、自私、酗酒。尼克某天在去纽约的路上遇到的黑人角色，也和白人角色一样肤浅、注重身份地位：他们坐在专车后座上，带着“傲慢的竞争”的目光（73；第四章）朝载着盖茨比和尼克的豪华轿车翻白眼。书中唯一没有表现出这些行为的人物是乔治·威尔逊和迈克尔斯，后者是威尔逊车库隔壁餐馆的老板。他们显然太忙或太穷，无暇顾及这些：他们的精力都投入到在“灰烬谷”（27；第二章）的绝望贫困中挣扎求生，而这个地方本身就是对孕育它的文化的一种控诉。事实上，可以说“灰烬谷”是现代世界精神贫瘠的隐喻：

Furthermore, the superficial values that put the pursuit of social status and good times above every other consideration are found among every group portrayed in the novel, regardless of the class, gender, or race of its members. The middle-class and working-class characters – such as the McKees, Myrtle Wilson, Myrtle’s sister Catherine, and Gatsby’s menagerie of party guests – are as concerned with social status and as hungry for amusement as the wealthy Buchanans. The female characters who attend Gatsby’s soirées are as shallow, selfish, and drunken as the male partygoers, if not more so. And the black characters Nick sees one day on his way to New York are as superficial and status-conscious as the white characters: from the back seat of their chauffeured limousine, they roll their eyes “in haughty rivalry” (73; ch. 4) toward the luxury car carrying Gatsby and Nick. The only characters who don’t seem to exhibit these behaviors, George Wilson and Michaelis, the man who owns the restaurant next to Wilson’s garage, are apparently too busy or too poor for such concerns: their energy is devoted to surviving the hopeless poverty of the “valley of ashes” (27; ch. 2), a location that is itself an indictment of the culture that produced it. Indeed, one could say that the “valley of ashes” is a metaphor for the spiritual poverty of the modern world:

一个奇特的农场，灰烬像小麦一样生长成垄、山丘和怪诞的花园；灰烬化作房屋、烟囱和升腾的烟雾，最终……化作在粉状空气中模糊移动、已经开始崩塌的人形。

a fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens; where ashes take the forms of houses and chimneys and rising smoke and finally … of men who move dimly and already crumbling through the powdery air.

（27；第 2 章）

(27; ch. 2)

小说的叙述者兼表面上的道德中心尼克·卡拉威，带着青春活力和乐观所带来的天真无知，踏入了这个腐败的世界。起初，他对这个世界不可避免的“污浊尘埃”（第6页；第1章）和“夭折的悲伤”（第7页；第1章）浑然不觉。在尼克成长的世界里，父亲会教导儿子“基本的礼仪”（第6页；第1章）；儿子们像他们的父辈一样从耶鲁大学毕业；如果年轻男子与同一位年轻女子频繁出入，就会被认为已经订婚；而且，没有人能够想象“一个人”就能像迈耶·沃尔夫希姆那样操纵世界大赛，“就像窃贼撬开保险箱一样一心一意”（第78页；第4章）。 1922年初夏，尼克来到他在西卵租住的小屋，准备开始新的事业和生活。从他对新社区的描述中，我们能感受到他的热情：“树木枝繁叶茂……空气清新，充满活力”（8；第1章）。即使是尼克做债券推销员的纽约市，在他充满渴望的眼中也显得年轻而纯洁：“从皇后区大桥上看到的城市，永远是第一次见到的那种城市，它最初充满野性，蕴藏着世间所有的神秘和美丽”（73；第4章，斜体为原文所有）。

Nick Carraway, the narrator and apparent moral center of the novel, enters this corrupt world with all the innocent blindness that youthful vitality and optimism can create, oblivious, at first, to the “foul dust” (6; ch. 1) and “abortive sorrows” (7; ch. 1) that are the inevitable products of such a world. In the world in which Nick grew up, fathers gave sons advice about “the fundamental decencies” (6; ch. 1); sons graduated from Yale just as their fathers had before them; young men were considered engaged to be married if they had been seen in the company of the same young woman too often; and no one could have imagined that “one man” could fix the World Series, as Meyer Wolfsheim did, “with the single-mindedness of a burglar blowing a safe” (78; ch. 4). It is early summer in 1922 as Nick arrives at his rented cottage in West Egg to begin a new career and a new life, and we see his enthusiasm in his description of his new neighborhood, with its “great bursts of leaves growing on the trees … and so much fine health to be pulled down out of the young breath-giving air” (8; ch. 1). Even New York City, where Nick works as a bond salesman, seems young and virginal to his eager eyes: “The city seen from the Queensboro Bridge is always the city seen for the first time, in its first wild promise of all the mystery and beauty in the world” (73; ch. 4, my italics).

然而，到了夏末，尼克已经30岁了，他觉得除了“十年的孤独、越来越少的单身男性朋友、越来越少的热情、越来越稀疏的头发”（143；第七章）之外，自己没有什么值得期待的了。他有他发现布坎南一家和他们那帮人“都是些烂人”（162），他“受够了他们所有人”（150；第七章）。因此，在东部度过一个夏天后，小说结尾，尼克准备再次返回中西部，他渴望回到那里熟悉的秩序和可预测的生活，厌倦了现代世界精神的空虚。正如他在小说开头，以回顾性的序言告诉我们的那样：“去年秋天我从东部回来时，我希望世界永远保持统一，并处于某种道德规范之中；我不想再经历那些喧闹的冒险，也不想再窥探人心的特权”（6；第一章）。为了完整展现尼克从年轻时的乐观到幻灭的转变，小说以同年秋天结束，“当枯叶的蓝色烟雾弥漫在空中，风吹得晾衣绳上湿漉漉的衣服僵硬起来”（185；第9章）：一年中自然界的衰败凸显了尼克在东方逗留所造成的精神疲惫。

By the end of the summer, however, Nick has turned 30 and feels he has nothing to look forward to but “a decade of loneliness, a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair” (143; ch. 7). He has discovered that the Buchanans and their lot are “a rotten crowd” (162), and he has “had enough of all of them” (150; ch. 7). Thus, after spending a single summer in the East, Nick prepares, as the novel closes, to return once again to the Midwest, longing for the order and predictability of the life he knew there, sick of the spiritual bankruptcy of life in the modern world. As he tells us at the beginning of the novel, in a retrospective prologue to his narrative, “When I came back from the East last autumn I felt that I wanted the world to be in uniform and at a sort of moral attention forever; I wanted no more riotous excursions with privileged glimpses into the human heart” (6; ch. 1). And to complete the progression from Nick’s youthful optimism to disillusionment, the novel ends in the autumn of that same year, “when the blue smoke of brittle leaves was in the air and the wind blew the wet laundry stiff on the line” (185; ch. 9): the time of year when nature’s decay underscores the spiritual exhaustion that results from Nick’s sojourn in the East.

当然，盖茨比也是尼克东迁后所进入的那个腐败世界的一部分，但“盖茨比……却不受尼克的影响”，正如叙述者所观察到的，“盖茨比最终安然无恙；真正令尼克“不屑一顾”的是那些侵蚀盖茨比的东西，是那些在他梦想之后飘散的污浊尘埃”（第6页；第1章）。正是盖茨比身上那种浪漫梦想家的特质——他对“生活承诺的敏锐感知”和他“浪漫的准备”（第6页；第1章）——使他免受他所生活的腐败世界的侵蚀，也因此免受尼克的谴责。的确，盖茨比具备了美国式浪漫英雄的所有特质。他白手起家的成功，唤起了美国浪漫主义中白手起家的理想形象，甚至他写在《霍帕隆·卡西迪》一书背面的童年“日程表”，也让人联想起美国浪漫主义偶像本杰明·富兰克林的自我提升格言。盖茨比作为战争英雄的身份，以及他为了赢得梦中情人而实现的惊人财富，都提升了他作为浪漫象征的价值。他俊朗的外表、温文尔雅的举止和一丝不苟的仪容，都凸显了他的青春和纯真。最后，他对黛西的绝对忠诚，体现在年轻恋人“伸出双臂”（25；第一章）望向黛西家码头尽头的绿光，“颤抖着”（26；第一章）的理想化画面中，最终成就了这位浪漫人物的完美化身。

Of course, Gatsby is part of the corrupt world Nick enters when he moves East, but “Gatsby … was exempt from [Nick’s] reaction” because, as the narrator observes, “Gatsby turned out all right at the end; it is what preyed on Gatsby, what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams” that elicits Nick’s “unaffected scorn” (6; ch. 1). It is Gatsby’s quality as a romantic dreamer – his “heightened sensitivity to the promises of life” and his “romantic readiness” (6; ch. 1) – that insulates him from the corrupt world in which he lives and, therefore, from Nick’s censure. Indeed, Gatsby has all the makings of a romantic hero, American style. His rags-to-riches success evokes the American romantic ideal of the self-made man, and even his boyhood “schedule” at the back of his Hopalong Cassidy book recalls the self-improvement maxims of Benjamin Franklin, an icon of America’s romantic past. Gatsby’s status as a war hero increases his value as a romantic symbol as does the fact that his meteoric financial rise was accomplished to win the woman of his dreams. His boyish good looks, his quiet, gentlemanly manners, and his flawless grooming accentuate his youth and innocence. Finally, his absolute devotion to Daisy, epitomized in the idealized image of the young lover “stretch[ing] out his arms” (25; ch. 1) toward the green light at the end of Daisy’s dock, “trembling” (26; ch. 1), completes the romantic incarnation.

不幸的是，盖茨比独特的浪漫特质，如同昔日骑士精神的回响，却与他所处的时代肤浅庸俗格格不入。事实上，正是汤姆和黛西·布坎南所体现的现代世界的空洞价值观，最终击垮了盖茨比：当黛西在纽约的酒店里，在他与汤姆对峙时离他而去，“越来越封闭自己”（142；第七章），盖茨比“像玻璃一样在汤姆的恶意中破碎”（155；第八章）。他的死，正是由于他骑士精神地承担了黛西撞死默特尔的罪责，现代世界永远失去了盖茨比带给它的礼物：“一种非凡的希望……是尼克从未在任何人身上找到的，而且他以后也不太可能再找到的”（6；第 1 章）。事实上，盖茨比的“浪漫情怀”和“对希望的渴望”在小说所描绘的现代世界中无法生存，这是该文本对那个世界最严厉的控诉之一。

Unfortunately, Gatsby’s unique romantic qualities, which echo the chivalry of ages past, ill suit him to survive the shallow vulgarity of the time in which he lives. Indeed, it is the empty values of the modern world, embodied in Tom and Daisy Buchanan, that crush Gatsby: when Daisy abandons him during his confrontation with Tom at the hotel in New York, “drawing further and further into herself” (142; ch. 7), Gatsby “br[eaks] like glass against Tom’s hard malice” (155; ch. 8). With his death, which is the direct result of his chivalrously taking the blame for Daisy’s hit-and-run killing of Myrtle, the modern world loses forever the gift that Gatsby had brought to it: “an extraordinary gift for hope … such as [Nick] ha[s] never found in any other person and which it is not likely [he] shall find again” (6; ch. 1). Indeed, that Gatsby’s “romantic readiness” and “gift for hope” can’t survive in the modern world depicted in the novel is one of the text’s severest indictments of that world.

与20世纪20年代美国快节奏、肤浅的颓废形成鲜明对比的是，一些段落唤起了人们对田园牧歌般过去的怀念，这些段落提醒我们美国失去了什么。其中最令人印象深刻的段落之一，便是本文开头引用的那段，尼克在其中回忆了他在明尼苏达州的青年时代。诸如“真正的雪，我们那里的雪，开始在我们身边铺展开来，闪闪发光”以及“一阵猛烈的风突然吹了起来”（184页；第九章）之类的词句，描绘出一片片开阔的空间——洁净、洁白、闪耀——不仅令人身心舒畅，也令人精神振奋。“真正的雪”当然指的是美国中西部北部地区大量降下的洁白积雪，这种积雪会持续整个冬季，与纽约车水马龙、车轮碾过后变成泥泞的积雪形成鲜明对比。但这句话也强化了这样一个观念：尼克童年时期在中西部的生活比他成年后在东部感受到的那种虚假氛围更加真实、更加真切。当然，尼克童年时期在明尼苏达州的生活也更加稳定和安全。正如这段文字所指出的，“几十年来，房屋仍然沿用着家族的姓氏”（184；第九章），这表明当地居民之间存在着一种在东部无法寻觅的归属感和人与人之间的紧密联系。

Juxtaposed against the fast-paced, shallow decadence of the American 1920s are passages that evoke an idyllic past, passages that serve to remind us of what it is America has lost. One of the most effective is the passage quoted at the opening of this essay, the passage in which Nick reminisces about his youth in Minnesota. Phrases such as “the real snow, our snow, began to stretch out beside us and twinkle” and “a sharp wild brace came suddenly into the air” (184; ch. 9) evoke open spaces – clean, white, and shining – that invigorate not just the body but the spirit as well. “[T]he real snow” refers, of course, to the enormous quantity of clean, white snow that falls in the upper Midwest and lasts all winter, as contrasted with the sooty snow that becomes slush under the wheels of New York traffic. But the phrase also reinforces the notion that life in the Midwest of Nick’s youth was more real, more genuine, than the artificial atmosphere he associates with his adult life in the East. Certainly, life in the Minnesota of Nick’s youth was more stable and secure as well. For as this same passage indicates, “dwellings are still called through decades by a family’s name” (184; ch. 9), which suggests a sense of permanence and personal connection among residents of the community that Nick doesn’t find in the East.

叙述者对东方的梦境描述，紧接着他对明尼苏达州冬季的回忆，从而更加凸显了过去与现在、纯真与颓废、西方与东方之间的对比：

This contrast between past and present, between innocence and decadence, between West and East, is heightened by the narrator’s description of his dreams about the East, which immediately follows his recollection of Minnesota winters:

即使在我最向往东方的时候……它对我来说也始终带着一种扭曲的特质。尤其是西卵，至今仍是我那些奇幻梦境中的常客。我把它想象成埃尔·格列柯的一幅夜景画：一百栋房子，既循规蹈矩又怪诞，蜷缩在阴沉的天空和黯淡无光的月亮下。前景中，四个身着正装、神情严肃的男人抬着一副担架，上面躺着一个醉醺醺的、身穿白色晚礼服的女人。她垂在担架边的手，闪烁着冰冷的珠宝光芒。男人们神情肃穆地走进一栋房子——却走错了。但没有人知道女人的名字，也没有人关心。

Even when the East excited me most … it had always for me a quality of distortion. West Egg especially still figures in my more fantastic dreams. I see it as a night scene by El Greco: a hundred houses, at once conventional and grotesque, crouching under a sullen, overhanging sky and a lustreless moon. In the foreground four solemn men in dress suits are walking along the sidewalk with a stretcher on which lies a drunken woman in a white evening dress. Her hand, which dangles over the side, sparkles cold with jewels. Gravely the men turn in at a house – the wrong house. But no one knows the woman’s name, and no one cares.

（184-85；第9章）

(184–85; ch. 9)

这里描绘的人类疏离的意象——一百座怪诞的房子、醉酒的女人、把她送到错误房子的男人（因为他们不知道她的名字，也不在乎知道）——与疏离、疲惫的自然景象形成鲜明对比，这与尼克对他年轻时中西部的描述截然不同：与明尼苏达州干净、令人振奋的天空不同，东方的天空是“阴沉的”和“压抑的”，甚至女人冰冷的珠宝都比“黯淡无光”的东方月亮更有“光彩”。

The images of human alienation here – the hundred grotesque houses, the drunken woman, the men who deliver her to the wrong house because they don’t know her name and don’t care to know it – are reinforced by images of an alienated, exhausted nature that contrast sharply with Nick’s description of the Midwest of his youth: unlike the clean, bracing, Minnesota sky, the Eastern sky is “sullen” and “overhanging,” and even the woman’s cold jewels have more “sparkle” than the “lustreless” Eastern moon.

其他关于田园诗般过去的描述围绕着黛西和乔丹在路易斯维尔美好的“白人少女时代”（24；第一章）。尼克想象着，乔丹“第一次学会了在清爽的早晨漫步于高尔夫球场”（55；第三章）。这是一个充满浪漫气息的过去，乔丹回忆说，她穿着“新买的格子裙……在风中轻轻飘动”（79；第四章），走在“柔软的土地”上，而黛西也在那里。

Other references to an idyllic past revolve around Daisy and Jordan’s beautiful “white girlhood” (24; ch. 1) in Louisville, where, Nick imagines, Jordan “first learned to walk upon golf courses on clean, crisp mornings” (55; ch. 3). This is a romantic past where, Jordan recalls, she walked on “soft ground” in her “new plaid skirt … that blew a little in the wind” (79; ch. 4) and where Daisy was

她无疑是所有年轻女孩中最受欢迎的……她身着白衣，开着一辆白色敞篷跑车，一整天她家的电话铃声不断，泰勒营地那些兴奋的年轻军官们都要求当晚独占她。“哪怕只有一小时也好！”

by far the most popular of all the young girls. … She dressed in white and had a little white roadster, and all day long the telephone rang in her house and excited young officers from Camp Taylor demanded the privilege of monopolizing her that night. “Anyways for an hour!”

（79；第4章）

(79; ch. 4)

这是一个年轻女孩为红十字会制作绷带的世界，一位名叫杰伊·盖茨比的英俊年轻军官“用一种每个年轻女孩都渴望被注视的眼神看着黛西”（80；第四章）。这是一个充满纯真浪漫的世界：“清爽洁净的早晨”、“柔软的土地”、崭新的裙子、白色连衣裙、白色敞篷跑车、铃声响起的电话，以及英俊的年轻军官。而年轻的杰伊·盖茨比也无法抵挡它的魅力：

This is a world in which young girls made bandages for the Red Cross and a handsome young officer named Jay Gatsby “looked at Daisy … in a way that every young girl wants to be looked at sometime” (80; ch. 4). This is a world of virginal romance: “clean, crisp mornings,” “soft ground,” new skirts, white dresses, white roadsters, ringing telephones, and handsome young officers. And the young Jay Gatsby was not immune to its charms:

黛西的房子里弥漫着一种浓郁的神秘感，暗示着楼上的卧室比其他卧室更漂亮、更凉爽，走廊里上演着欢快而光彩夺目的活动，以及那些并非陈腐过时、被薰衣草掩盖的浪漫故事，而是新鲜而充满活力，散发着今年闪亮的汽车和鲜花尚未凋谢的舞会的气息。

There was a ripe mystery about [Daisy’s house], a hint of bedrooms upstairs more beautiful and cool than other bedrooms, of gay and radiant activities taking place through its corridors, and of romances that were not musty and laid away already in lavender, but fresh and breathing and redolent of this year’s shining motor cars and of dances whose flowers were scarcely withered.

（156；第 8 章）

(156; ch. 8)

只有这样田园诗般的过去才能孕育出与其浪漫氛围相称的壮举：盖茨比将自己托付给黛西，就像“追寻圣杯”一样（156；第 8 章）。

Only such an idyllic past could produce the deed worthy of its romantic ambience: Gatsby’s committing himself to Daisy as “to the following of a grail” (156; ch. 8).

或许，最能唤起人们对一去不复返的田园牧歌般往昔的感慨的段落，就是小说结尾的那段。尼克在返回明尼苏达州的前一天晚上，坐在沙滩上，沉思着……

Perhaps the most powerful passage that evokes an idyllic past forever vanished is the one that closes the novel. As Nick sits on the beach the evening before his return to Minnesota, he muses on

这里曾是荷兰水手们眼中繁花似锦的古老岛屿——新世界清新翠绿的胸怀。如今消失的树木，那些为盖茨比的豪宅让路的树木，曾低声诉说着人类最后也是最伟大的梦想；在那短暂而迷人的瞬间，人类一定屏息凝神，面对着这片大陆，被迫陷入一种既不理解也不渴望的审美沉思，在历史上最后一次与某种足以匹配其惊叹能力的事物面对面。

the old island here that flowered once for Dutch sailors’ eyes – a fresh, green breast of the new world. Its vanished trees, the trees that had made way for Gatsby’s house, had once pandered in whispers to the last and greatest of all human dreams; for a transitory enchanted moment man must have held his breath in the presence of this continent, compelled into an aesthetic contemplation he neither understood nor desired, face to face for the last time in history with something commensurate to his capacity for wonder.

（189；第9章）

(189; ch. 9)

在这段文字中，小说中所展现的所有损失——现代美国价值观的丧失、一个国家纯真和活力的丧失、盖茨比梦想的破灭——都与一个具有全球历史意义的损失联系在一起：原始的美洲大陆最初被欧洲对更多殖民地和更大财富的贪婪所剥削、污染和摧毁。

In this passage, all the losses represented in the novel – the loss of values in modern America, the loss of a nation’s innocence and vitality, the loss of Gatsby’s dream – are associated with a loss of global historical magnitude: the original loss of a pristine American continent that was exploited, polluted, and destroyed by Europe’s lust for more colonies and greater wealth.

显然，《了不起的盖茨比》描绘了20世纪20年代美国阴郁的景象。然而，小说对这种文化颓废的刻画，却因其自身对构成这种刻画基础的二元对立的矛盾态度而显得苍白无力。正如我们所见，小说将美国昔日的纯真（如今已然消逝）与过去的青春活力联系起来，尤其体现在对西部地区的描写中。与之形成对比的是，美国的颓废则与小说的当代背景——20世纪20年代的现代世界——以及东部地区联系在一起。在东部，尼克第一次体验到了标志着国家价值观衰落的自私和肤浅。如果我们审视这些对立——过去/现在、纯真/颓废、西部/东部——的不稳定性，就能明白小说是如何解构其自身的意识形态的。

Clearly, The Great Gatsby paints a grim picture of America in the 1920s. However, the novel’s representation of this culture’s decadence is undermined by the text’s own ambivalence toward the binary oppositions on which this representation rests. As we have seen, the novel associates America’s innocence, now vanished, with the youthful vitality of the past, especially as it is invoked by the text’s descriptions of the West. In contrast, America’s decadence is associated with the present-day setting of the novel – the modern world of the 1920s – and with the East, where Nick gets his first taste of the selfishness and superficiality that mark the decline in national values. If we examine the instability of these oppositions – past/present, innocence/decadence, and West/East – we will be able to see how the novel deconstructs its own ideological project.

小说通过描绘田园牧歌般的过去，来凸显现代美国精神的空虚，这种做法在过去与现在之间制造了一种不稳定的对立，因为它削弱了文本自身对过去并非人人都能拥有的田园牧歌式生活的认知。杰伊·盖茨比的过去当然并非如此。“他的父母是游手好闲、一事无成的农民”（104页；第六章），他的父亲曾对尼克说：“他告诉我，我曾经吃得像猪一样，我为此揍了他一顿”（182页；第九章）。事实上，盖茨比无法接受自己的过去，于是他重塑了它：他离家出走，将自己的名字从吉米·盖茨改为杰伊·盖茨比，“塑造了一个十七岁男孩可能会塑造的那种杰伊·盖茨比，并且他至死都忠于这个形象”（104页；第六章）。作为一个身无分文的年轻中尉，“他让黛西相信他和她出身相仿”（156；第八章），他告诉尼克：“我的家人都去世了，我继承了一大笔钱……之后，我像个年轻的拉贾一样在欧洲各大城市游历……收集珠宝……狩猎大型猎物，也画画”（70；第四章）。在这种背景下，盖茨比“重温过去”（116；第六章）的执着，实际上也是他想要逃离过去的决心。因为他想要重温的，是他和黛西最初的恋情，而这段恋情建立在一个虚构的过去之上。因此，对于这个体现小说浪漫过去概念的人物而言，浪漫的过去，实际上是由谎言编织而成的。

The novel’s evocation of an idyllic past in order to underscore, by contrast, the spiritual emptiness of modern America creates an unstable opposition between past and present because it undermines the text’s own awareness that the past was not idyllic for everyone. Certainly, Jay Gatsby’s past was not so. “His parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people” (104; ch. 6), and his father tells Nick, “He told me I et like a hog once and I beat him for it” (182; ch. 9). In fact, Gatsby found his past so unacceptable that he reinvented it: he left home, changed his name from Jimmy Gatz, and “invented just the sort of Jay Gatsby that a seventeen-year-old boy would be likely to invent, and to this conception he was faithful to the end” (104; ch. 6). As a penniless young lieutenant “he let [Daisy] believe that he was a person from much the same strata as herself” (156; ch. 8), and he tells Nick, “My family all died and I came into a good deal of money. … After that I lived like a young rajah in all the capitals of Europe … collecting jewels … hunting big game, painting a little” (70; ch. 4). In this context, even Gatsby’s singular determination to “repeat the past” (116; ch. 6) is really a determination to escape the past. For the past he wants to repeat is his initial liaison with Daisy, which was built on an invented past. Thus, for the character who embodies the novel’s notion of the romantic past, the romantic past is, in reality, a tissue of lies.

《了不起的盖茨比》中过去与现在的对立还存在另一个问题，那就是它与小说中纯真与颓废的对立紧密相连，而这种对立本身就不稳定。例如，尽管尼克是小说中反对时代颓废的主要代言人，但他却深深地被颓废所吸引。尼克说：

Another problem with the opposition between past and present in The Great Gatsby is its link to the novel’s opposition of innocence and decadence, which is itself an unstable opposition. For example, although Nick is the novel’s chief spokesperson against the decadence of the age, he is very much attracted by it. Nick says,

我开始喜欢上纽约，喜欢它夜晚那种充满活力和冒险的氛围，以及熙熙攘攘的人群和机器带来的满足感。那双不安分的眼睛。我喜欢沿着第五大道漫步，从人群中挑选那些浪漫的女子，幻想几分钟后我就会走进她们的生活，而且不会有人知道，也不会有人反对。有时，在我的想象中，我会一路跟随她们来到隐蔽街角的公寓，她们转身对我微笑，然后消失在温暖的黑暗中。

I began to like New York, the racy adventurous feel of it at night and the satisfaction that the constant flicker of men and women and machines gives to the restless eye. I liked to walk up Fifth Avenue and pick out romantic women from the crowd and imagine that in a few minutes I was going to enter into their lives, and no one would ever know or disapprove. Sometimes, in my mind, I followed them to their apartments on the corners of hidden streets, and they turned and smiled back at me before they faded through a door into warm darkness.

（61；第3章，斜体为原文所有）

(61; ch. 3, my italics)

虽然尼克没有把话说完，但这段斜体字部分清楚地表明，他想象自己跟随这些女人走进“温暖的黑暗”；她们的笑容充满诱惑。换句话说，对他而言，这座城市“充满刺激和冒险的氛围”源于它所提供的无穷无尽的禁忌性爱机会。这并非尼克年轻时居住的明尼苏达州，那里“没完没了的审讯只放过孩子和老人”（185；第九章），他非常庆幸这里不是他记忆中的那个地方。

Although Nick doesn’t complete the thought, the italicized portion of the passage makes it clear that he imagines himself following these women into the “warm darkness”; their smiles are smiles of invitation. In other words, the “racy adventurous feel” of the city is produced, for him, by the infinity of illicit sexual possibilities it offers. This is not the Minnesota of Nick’s youth, with its “interminable inquisitions which spared only the children and the very old” (185; ch. 9), and he’s very glad it isn’t.

小说所谴责的颓废，在叙述者对乔丹·贝克的迷恋中也有所体现。她并非盖茨比所认为的“伟大的女运动员”，不会“做任何不妥的事”（76；第四章）。她是个骗子，是个说谎者，尼克心知肚明。尽管他轻描淡写地将她的不诚实行为当作无关紧要的缺点——“女人的不诚实，你永远不会真正责怪她”（63；第三章）——但正是她的不诚实，实际上吸引了他，因为他认为这掩盖了他渴望体验的秘密而禁忌的性欲：“我想她从小就开始耍花招，这样才能保持那副冷艳傲慢的笑容，同时又能满足她那健壮而轻佻的身体的需求”（63；第三章）。

A similar attraction to the decadence the novel condemns is revealed in the narrator’s attraction to Jordan Baker. For she is not the “great sportswoman” who would “never do anything that wasn’t all right” (76; ch. 4), as Gatsby believes. She’s a cheat and a liar, and Nick knows it. Although he dismisses her dishonest behavior as if it were not a serious flaw – “Dishonesty in a woman is a thing you never blame deeply” (63; ch. 3) – it’s her dishonesty that, in fact, attracts him because he believes it serves to mask a secret, illicit sexuality that he wants to experience: “I suppose she had begun dealing in subterfuges when she was very young in order to keep that cool, insolent smile turned to the world and yet satisfy the demands of her hard, jaunty body” (63; ch. 3).

值得注意的是，尼克似乎很难离开那些体现他所谴责的肤浅价值观的场景。例如，在盖茨比家参加的两场派对上，他都是最后离开的人之一。更令人费解的是，他似乎无法从汤姆和默特尔公寓里的醉酒狂欢中脱身：

It’s interesting to note in this context that Nick seems to have great difficulty leaving the scenes that epitomize the superficial values he condemns. For example, he’s among the very last to leave both of the parties he attends at Gatsby’s house. Even more puzzling, he doesn’t seem to be able to extract himself from the drunken revel at Tom and Myrtle’s apartment:

我想出去，在柔和的暮色中向东走到公园去，但每次我尝试离开时，都会被卷入一些激烈的争论中，这些争论就像绳子一样把我拉回椅子里。

I wanted to get out and walk eastward toward the park through the soft twilight, but each time I tried to go I became entangled in some wild strident argument which pulled me back, as if with ropes, into my chair.

（40；第 2 章）

(40; ch. 2)

尼克说，是“无穷无尽的生活多样性”让他“既着迷又厌恶”（40；第二章），但似乎正是现代世界无穷无尽的庸俗，在他表面上的厌恶之下，深深地吸引着他。因此，在小说的结尾，我们看到他再次成为最后一个离开的人，在汤姆、黛西、乔丹和盖茨比都离开很久之后，他仍然在西卵海滩上徘徊。

Nick says that it’s the “inexhaustible variety of life” that “simultaneously enchant[s] and repel[s]” him (40; ch. 2), but it seems to be the inexhaustible vulgarity of the modern world that, beneath his overt revulsion, fascinates him. And so we see him at the novel’s close, once again the last to leave, lingering on the beach at West Egg long after Tom, Daisy, Jordan, and Gatsby are gone.

《了不起的盖茨比》中天真与颓废的对立，其另一个问题在于天真本身的概念。正如前文对尼克的讨论所暗示的那样，他之所以对颓废着迷，是因为他天真无邪——也就是缺乏经验——因此渴望了解这个世界。同样地，尼克也曾一度沦为他所谴责的颓废的牺牲品，因为他天真无知——也就是懵懂无知——不了解自己所面临的道德危险。换句话说，天真无邪的概念，因为它包含了缺乏经验和无知的概念，可以说，它本身就蕴含着一种对颓废的脆弱性，几乎必然会导致堕落。因此，说天真无邪会导致颓废并非毫无道理；事实上，它甚至在原本不存在颓废的地方创造了颓废。

Another problem with The Great Gatsby’s opposition of innocence and decadence is the concept of innocence itself. As the above discussion of Nick implies, he is fascinated by decadence because he is innocent – that is, inexperienced – and therefore hungry for knowledge of the world. Analogously, Nick falls prey, at least for a time, to the decadence he condemns because he is innocent – that is, ignorant – and doesn’t understand the kind of moral danger that is confronting him. In other words, the concept of innocence, because it includes the concepts of inexperience and ignorance, has built into it, so to speak, a vulnerability to decadence that is almost sure to result in a fall. Thus, it is not unreasonable to say that innocence leads to decadence; in fact, it creates decadence where before there was none.

小说中天真与颓废的对立，在乔治·威尔逊这个人物的塑造上体现得尤为明显。在许多方面，他是故事中唯一真正天真的角色。他不伤害任何人，信任所有人，天真得近乎孩童。与尼克初次接触颓废时感到着迷不同，乔治第一次体验到颓废——以妻子不忠的形式——却让他感到恶心：“他发现默特尔在另一个世界里过着与他截然不同的生活，这种冲击让他生理上感到不适”（130；第七章）。然而，乔治的天真并非被描绘成一种积极的品质，而是被描绘成一种没有任何品质的状态。威尔逊几乎没有任何个性。正如迈克尔斯所观察到的，“乔治不工作的时候，就坐在门口的椅子上，盯着路上来来往往的人群和车辆。有人跟他说话，他总是发出一种令人愉悦却又毫无生气的笑声”（144页；第七章）。迈克尔斯毫不意外地发现，他甚至连个朋友都没有：他甚至“连妻子都配不上他”（167页；第八章）。因此，在这部哀悼纯真逝去的小说中，纯真被描绘成无知，被描绘成缺乏品质，被描绘成一种虚无。尽管小说叙述者和其中对颓废人物的冷漠刻画都公开谴责颓废，但文本似乎认为颓废远比纯真有趣得多。纯真令人乏味；颓废则不然。

A particularly revealing problem with the novel’s opposition of innocence and decadence is seen in the characterization of George Wilson. In many ways, he is the only truly innocent character in the story. He harms no one, he trusts everyone, and he is rather childlike in his simplicity. Unlike Nick, who is fascinated by his first encounter with decadence, George’s first experience of it – in the form of his wife’s infidelity – literally makes him ill: “He had discovered that Myrtle had some sort of life apart from him in another world, and the shock had made him physically sick” (130; ch. 7). Yet George’s innocence is portrayed not as a positive quality in its own right but as an absence of qualities of any kind. Wilson has almost no personality at all. As Michaelis notices, “when [George] wasn’t working, he sat on a chair in the doorway and stared at the people and the cars that passed along the road. When anyone spoke to him he invariably laughed in an agreeable, colorless way” (144; ch. 7). He didn’t even have a friend, Michaelis learns without surprise: there wasn’t even “enough of him for his wife” (167; ch. 8). Thus, in a novel that mourns the loss of innocence, innocence is portrayed as ignorance, as the absence of qualities, as a kind of nothingness. And although decadence is overtly condemned by the narrator and by the novel’s unsympathetic portrayals of decadent characters, the text seems to find decadence infinitely more interesting than innocence. Innocence is boring; decadence is not.

过去/现在和纯真/颓废的二元对立所支撑的主题结构，与东西方的地理对立紧密相连。正如我们所见，过去的纯真与尼克的明尼苏达州以及黛西和乔丹成长的路易斯维尔紧密相连。尽管盖茨比在北达科他州和明尼苏达州的青年时期并不快乐，但小说仍然将西部与17岁的吉米·盖茨的纯真梦想联系起来。在遇到丹·科迪或听说迈耶·沃尔夫希姆之前，吉米“穿着破旧的绿色运动衫和帆布裤，在苏必利尔湖的沙滩上闲逛”（104；第六章）。与之相反，当下的颓废则与东部，特别是20世纪20年代的纽约联系在一起。然而，《了不起的盖茨比》中东西方的对立并非完全是地理上的。例如，芝加哥和底特律都位于中西部，但小说暗示它们也和纽约一样颓废。东西方之间的对立也并非完全等同于乡村与城市之间的对立，因为尼克纯真的童年，以及黛西和乔丹的少女时代，都是在中西部城市度过的。

The thematic structure supported by the binary oppositions past/present and innocence/decadence is tied to a geographic structure that opposes West and East. As we have seen, the innocence of the past is associated with Nick’s Minnesota and the Louisville in which Daisy and Jordan grew up. And though Gatsby’s youth in North Dakota and Minnesota was an unhappy time in his life, the novel nevertheless associates the West with the innocent dreams of 17-year-old Jimmy Gatz, who “loaf[ed] along the beach [of Lake Superior] … in a torn green jersey and a pair of canvas pants” (104; ch. 6) before he ever met Dan Cody or heard of Meyer Wolfsheim. In contrast, the decadence of the present is associated with the East, specifically with New York in the 1920s. However, the opposition between West and East in The Great Gatsby isn’t entirely a matter of geography. For example, Chicago and Detroit are in the Midwest, yet the novel indicates that they share the decadence of New York. Neither is the opposition between West and East entirely that between countryside and city, for Nick’s innocent youth, as well as the girlhoods of Daisy and Jordan, were passed in Midwestern cities.

小说中东西方的真正区别在于原始自然——尼克明尼苏达州的“真雪”和“曾为荷兰水手绽放的古老岛屿”——与文明腐蚀作用之间的区别。也就是说，无论地理位置如何，“西方”一词对美国人来说都意味着未受破坏、未受污染的自然。“东方”则与之相反，它与古老、腐败的社会联系在一起。因此，尼克提到的“古老岛屿”，尽管指的是纽约的长岛，却与“西方”一词联系在一起，不仅因为它位于殖民它的欧洲文明以西，还因为当荷兰水手最初抵达那里时，它还是一片原始净土。

The real distinction between West and East in the novel is the distinction between pristine nature – the “real snow” of Nick’s Minnesota and the “old island that flowered once for Dutch sailors” – and the corrupting effects of civilization. That is, regardless of the geography involved, the word West invokes, for Americans, untouched, uncorrupted nature. The word East, in contrast, is associated with old, corrupt societies. Therefore, the “old island” Nick refers to, though it is New York’s Long Island, is associated with the word West not only because it is west of the European civilization that colonized it, but because when the Dutch sailors first arrived there, it was pristine.

然而，在《了不起的盖茨比》中，即便在最年轻、最有活力、最神奇的时刻，自然也与现代美国腐败的文明密不可分，而这种二者之间的联系进一步消解了东西方之间的对立。例如，尼克在开篇对西卵初夏的描述中，就将自然与文明联系起来。他将“树上蓬勃生长的树叶”比作“快节奏电影中事物的生长方式”（8；第一章）。紧接着，在他描述“从清新的空气中汲取的健康”之后，他又以同样的崇高语气谈到，他将从自己购买的“十二卷关于银行、信贷和投资证券的书籍”中学到发财致富的“闪亮秘诀”，这些书“像新铸的钞票一样，红金相间地摆放在[他的]书架上”（8；第一章）。同样，文本也无法将自然的美丽和活力与拥有自然的富人的腐败权力分开，正如我们在以下对布坎南家的描述中所看到的那样：

In The Great Gatsby, however, nature, even at its most youthful, energetic, and magical, is inextricably bound to the corrupt civilization of modern America, and this tie between the two further deconstructs the opposition between West and East. Nick associates nature with civilization, for example, in his opening description of early summer in West Egg. He compares the “great bursts of leaves growing on the trees” to the way “things grow in fast movies” (8; ch. 1). And in the very next sentence after he describes the “fine health to be pulled down out of the young breath-giving air,” he speaks, in the same exalted tone, of the “shining secrets” he will learn about making his fortune from the “dozen volumes on banking and credit and investment securities” he bought, which “stood on [his] shelf in red and gold like new money from the mint” (8; ch. 1). Similarly, the text can’t separate the beauty and vitality of nature from the corrupt power of the wealthy who “own” it, as we see in the following description of the Buchanans’ home:

草坪从海滩开始，向前延伸了四分之一英里，越过日晷、砖砌小路和燃烧的花园——最后到达房子时，明亮的藤蔓沿着房子的侧面向上蔓延，仿佛是奔跑的惯性使它向上生长。

The lawn started at the beach and ran toward the front door for a quarter of a mile, jumping over sun-dials and brick walks and burning gardens – finally when it reached the house drifting up the side in bright vines as though from the momentum of its run.

（11；第1章）

(11; ch. 1)

尽管庄园位于海边，毗邻地球上最强大的自然力量之一——大海，但在本段文字中，自然却被彻底驯化了。原本生长在海边的野生草丛被草坪取代，草坪像训练有素的狗一样“跃过”障碍物，藤蔓则像珠宝般装饰着房屋。然而，对布坎南家住宅的冗长描写（本段文字只是其中的一小部分）所展现的感官之美，暗示着作者并未意识到，诸如“屋外的嫩草……似乎长进了屋里”（12；第一章）之类的意象，是如何利用自然的纯净来为它所装饰的颓废文明辩护的。的确，自然之美常常被描述得仿佛是文明的产物，例如尼克在参加盖茨比的派对时说道：“那轮早熟的月亮，无疑就像晚餐一样，是从餐饮承办人的篮子里变出来的”（47；第3章）。而当文明的产物被描述得如同自然的产物时，自然与文明的融合就达到了极致，例如，我们被告知布坎南家二楼的“两扇窗户”在“葡萄藤间绽放着光芒”（149；第7章，斜体为原文所有）。

Although the estate is on the edge of the sea, one of the most powerful natural forces on earth, nature, in this passage, is utterly domesticated. The wild grasses that normally border the ocean have been replaced by a lawn that “jump[s] over” objects like a trained dog, while vines adorn the house like jewelry. Yet the sensuous beauty of the lengthy description of the Buchanans’ home, of which this passage is but a small part, suggests that the text is unaware of how images such as “the fresh grass outside … seemed to grow a little way into the house” (12; ch. 1) use the purity of nature to validate the decadent civilization it decorates. Indeed, the beauties of nature are often referred to as if they were manufactured by civilization, as when Nick, attending one of Gatsby’s parties, says that “the premature moon [was] produced like the supper, no doubt, out of a caterer’s basket” (47; ch. 3). And the blending of nature and civilization is complete when the products of civilization are described as if they were products of nature, as when we’re told that “two windows” on the second floor of the Buchanans’ house “bloomed with light among the vines” (149; ch. 7, my italics).

我们从丹·科迪身上看到了过去/现在、纯真/颓废、西方/东方这三个对立面的不稳定性。“他是内华达银矿、育空地区以及自1975年以来每一次淘金热潮的产物”（105；第六章），“他面色红润，却面容冷峻空洞——这位拓荒时代的放荡不羁之徒，曾在美国生活的某个阶段，将边境妓院和酒吧的野蛮暴力带回了东海岸”（106）。从丹·科迪以及他所代表的历史时期来看，我们看到的是过去而非现在与颓废联系在一起，我们看到的是西方对东方的腐蚀。

We see the instability of all three oppositions – past/present, innocence/decadence, and West/East – in the person of Dan Cody, “a product of the Nevada silver fields, of the Yukon, of every rush for metal since Seventy-five” (105; ch. 6), a “florid man with a hard empty face – the pioneer debauchee who during one phase of American life brought back to the eastern seaboard the savage violence of the frontier brothel and saloon” (106). In the person of Dan Cody, and the historical period he represents, we see the past, not the present, associated with decadence, and we see the West corrupting the East.

然而，这部小说对其自身意识形态抱持矛盾态度的最根本原因在于它对杰伊·盖茨比的刻画。正如我们所见，盖茨比被描绘成一个浪漫的英雄：一个叛逆的少年，一个雄心勃勃的年轻粗犷汉子，一个理想主义的梦想家，一个忠诚的情人，一个勇敢的士兵，一个慷慨的主人。对他的外貌描写也营造出一种纯真、活力和美丽的氛围：“他身上有一种令人惊艳的气质”（第6页；第1章），他那件“华丽的粉红色破烂西装”（第162页；第8章），“他晒黑的皮肤……紧绷地贴在他的脸上，显得格外迷人”（第54页；第3章），以及他“罕见的微笑……带着一种永恒的安心感”（第52页；第3章）。他就像一位来自远古时代的浪漫骑士，不知何故迷失在历史长河中，带着他“不朽的梦想”（162；第八章），身处一个肤浅到无法欣赏他的时代。然而，他同时也是这部小说所批判的现代世界的浪漫化身。也就是说，通过对盖茨比的浪漫化，小说也美化了造就他的腐败，以及他心甘情愿且成功地参与其中的腐败。

The most pervasive source of the novel’s ambivalence toward its own ideological project, however, is its characterization of Jay Gatsby. As we have seen, Gatsby is portrayed as a romantic hero: a rebellious boy, an ambitious young roughneck, an idealistic dreamer, a devoted lover, a brave soldier, a lavish host. The physical descriptions of his person also generate an ambience of innocence, vitality, and beauty: “[T]here was something gorgeous about him” (6; ch. 1), with his “gorgeous pink rag of a suit” (162; ch. 8), “his tanned skin … drawn attractively tight on his face” (54; ch. 3), and his “rare smil[e] … with a quality of eternal reassurance in it” (52; ch. 3). He is like a romantic knight of ages past somehow displaced in history, lost, with his “incorruptible dream” (162; ch. 8), in a time too superficial to appreciate him. Yet he is also the romantic embodiment of the modern world the novel condemns. That is, by romanticizing Gatsby, the novel also romanticizes the corruption that produced him, the corruption in which he willingly and successfully participates.

“我把他从一无所有，从街头巷尾捧了出来”（179；第九章），梅耶·沃尔夫希姆说道。他操纵了1919年世界大赛，是小说中犯罪世界最阴险的代表。盖茨比通过走私酒水和伪造债券，在极短的时间内积累了惊人的财富。就像小说中谴责的那些人物一样，盖茨比在一个弱肉强食的世界里获得了成功。他非法的、因此往往品质低劣的酒水被公开出售给任何有钱人，而他的伪造债券则在小镇上流传给毫不知情的投资者。一些购买他酒水的人可能会生病，有些人甚至会因此丧命。所有购买伪造债券的小投资者都会损失他们可能根本无法承受的损失。当不可避免的错误发生，法律介入时，总会有人成为牺牲品，就像盖茨比牺牲沃尔特·蔡斯那样。

“I raised him up out of nothing, right out of the gutter” (179; ch. 9), says Meyer Wolfsheim, the man who fixed the 1919 World Series and the most sinister representative of the criminal world the novel offers. And through bootlegged liquor and fraudulent bonds, Gatsby made his extraordinary fortune in record time. Like the characters the novel condemns, Gatsby succeeds in a world of predators and prey. His illegal, and thus often imperfect, liquor is sold over the counter to anyone with the money to pay for it, and his false bonds are passed in small towns to unsuspecting investors. Some of the people who buy the liquor may become ill from it; some may die. All of the small investors who buy the fraudulent bonds will lose money that they probably can’t afford to lose. And when the inevitable mistakes are made and the law steps in, someone will have to be sacrificed, as Gatsby does when he sacrifices Walter Chase.

即使是主人公对黛西的渴望——这在许多读者心中塑造了他最浪漫的形象——也未能摆脱他阴暗的人生观：当盖茨比第一次在路易斯维尔黛西父母家中追求她时，“他贪婪而肆无忌惮地攫取一切——最终他得到了黛西”（156；第八章）。盖茨比不仅仅是与黛西发生了性关系；他“贪婪而肆无忌惮地”占有了她。这种措辞强烈地反映了他在遇到黛西之前与丹·科迪的暧昧关系，以及他们在最初交往之后他的犯罪活动。因此，盖茨比“不朽的梦想”（162；第八章）深陷于他为了实现梦想而参与的腐败之中。

Even the protagonist’s desire for Daisy – which creates, for many readers, the most romantic image of him – is not free from the taint of his underworld view of life: when Gatsby first courted Daisy at her parents’ home in Louisville, “[h]e took what he could get, ravenously and unscrupulously – eventually he took Daisy” (156; ch. 8). Gatsby did not just make love to Daisy; he “took” her “ravenously and unscrupulously.” This language resonates strongly with his dubious association with Dan Cody before meeting Daisy and with his criminal activities subsequent to their initial affair. Gatsby’s “incorruptible dream” (162; ch. 8) is thus mired in the corruption he participated in to fulfill it.

小说对盖茨比所代表的对立世界的混淆，很大程度上导致了我们之前讨论过的结尾段落的问题。让我们再来看一遍。当尼克最后一次站在西卵海滩上时，他告诉我们，

The novel’s confusion of the opposing worlds Gatsby represents is largely responsible for the problematic nature of the closing passage we discussed earlier. Let’s look at it again. As Nick stands on the beach at West Egg for the last time, he tells us that he

这里曾是荷兰水手们眼中繁花似锦的古老岛屿——新世界清新翠绿的胸怀。如今，岛上的树木已然消失，盖茨比的豪宅也因此而毁于一旦。这些树木曾低语着，满足着人类最伟大、最崇高的梦想；在短暂而迷人的瞬间，人类一定屏息凝神，面对着这片大陆，被迫陷入一种既不理解也不渴望的审美沉思，在历史上最后一次与足以匹配人类惊叹能力的事物面对面。

became aware of the old island here that flowered once for Dutch sailors’ eyes – a fresh, green breast of the new world. Its vanished trees, the trees that had made way for Gatsby’s house, had once pandered in whispers to the last and greatest of all human dreams; for a transitory enchanted moment man must have held his breath in the presence of this continent, compelled into an aesthetic contemplation he neither understood nor desired, face to face for the last time in history with something commensurate to his capacity for wonder.

（189；第9章）

(189; ch. 9)

尽管尼克提醒我们，“新世界清新翠绿的胸怀”，那“与我们惊叹的能力相称”的景象，“消失了”，为“盖茨比的房子让路”——也就是说，被文明摧毁了——但尼克也将荷兰水手们的这种“迷人的”梦想与盖茨比的梦想联系起来，盖茨比试图通过他身处的腐败文明的犯罪手段来实现这个梦想。因为尼克说：“当我坐在那里沉思着那个古老而未知的世界时，我想起了盖茨比第一次看到黛西码头尽头的绿光时的惊奇”（189；第九章）。换言之，文本将“新世界清新翠绿的胸怀”与“黛西码头尽头的绿光”联系起来，从而将原始自然的浪漫崇高与取代它的腐败文明——以盖茨比为代表——紧密相连，使得二者在情感上（即便在逻辑上并非如此）几乎无法分离。此外，“消失的树木”，即原始的过去，“在耳语中被迎合”（我的斜体字）。 “迎合”一词与“拉皮条”等词语强烈呼应，即引诱或迎合他人不道德的欲望。因此，在这段文字中，原始的自然，纯真的过去，与剥削它的文明密不可分，正如杰伊·盖茨比与剥削他、也被他剥削的腐败世界密不可分一样。

Although Nick reminds us that the “fresh, green breast of the new world,” that setting “commensurate to [our] capacity for wonder,” “vanished” to make “way for Gatsby’s house” – that is, was obliterated by civilization – Nick also associates this “enchanted” dream of the Dutch sailors with Gatsby’s dream, which Gatsby attempted to fulfill through the criminal means of the corrupt civilization of which he was a part. For Nick says, “[A]s I sat there brooding on the old, unknown world, I thought of Gatsby’s wonder when he first picked out the green light at the end of Daisy’s dock” (189; ch. 9). In other words, the text associates the “fresh, green breast of the new world” with the “green light at the end of Daisy’s dock,” thus tying the romantic sublime of pristine nature to the corrupt civilization that replaced it – in the form of Gatsby – in a way that makes the two, emotionally if not logically, almost impossible to untangle. Furthermore, the “vanished trees,” the pristine past, “pandered in whispers” (my italics). To pander resonates strongly with words like to pimp, that is, with soliciting or accommodating the indulgence of another’s immoral desires. Thus, pristine nature, the innocent past, cannot be separated in this passage from the civilization that exploits it, just as Jay Gatsby cannot be separated from the corrupt world that exploits and is exploited by him.

《了不起的盖茨比》谴责了现代的颓废，小说暗示，这种颓废取代了过去纯真无邪的美国，一个与未受破坏的西部紧密相连的美国。然而，这种意识形态的构建却因文本本身过去与现在、纯真与颓废、西方与东方的不可分割性而受到削弱。尽管如此，小说对逝去的过去、纯真无邪的过去、更美好的过去的怀念，至少根据近几百年来西方文学的记载，是各个时代人们共同的情感。虽然我们对《了不起的盖茨比》的解构式解读肯定无法消除这种由来已久的情感投入，但它可以帮助我们理解这种投入的意识形态局限性。此外，我们对菲茨杰拉德小说的分析也印证了解构主义对小说观点的有效性。根据解构主义的观点，小说由于由语言构成，因此体现了产生它的文化的意识形态。因此，小说可以向我们展示各种意识形态如何运作，从而塑造我们对世界的认知。换句话说，正如我们对《了不起的盖茨比》的解构性解读所表明的那样，小说并不反映世界的真实面貌，而是反映我们感知到的世界。而对于解构主义而言，我们感知到的世界就是我们所知的唯一世界。

The Great Gatsby condemns the modern decadence that, the novel suggests, replaced the innocent America of the past, an America associated with the unspoiled West. But this ideological project is undermined by the inseparability in the text itself of past and present, innocence and decadence, and West and East. Nevertheless, the novel’s nostalgia for a lost past, an innocent past, a happier past, is a nostalgia shared, at least according to Western literature of the last several hundred years, by people from every age. Although our deconstructive reading of The Great Gatsby surely will not eliminate an emotional investment of such long standing, it can help us understand the ideological limitations of that investment. In addition, our analysis of Fitzgerald’s novel illustrates the validity of deconstruction’s view of fiction. According to deconstruction, fiction, because it is made of language, embodies the ideologies of the culture that produces it. Fiction can therefore show us the various ways in which our ideologies operate to create our perceptions of the world. In other words, as our deconstructive reading of The Great Gatsby demonstrates, fiction doesn’t represent the world as it really is; it represents the world as we perceive it to be. And for deconstruction, the world as we perceive it to be is the only world we know.

拓展练习题：对其他文学作品的解构分析

Questions for further practice: deconstructive approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用解构主义批评方法来解读它们所指的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use deconstructive criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1路易斯·瓦尔德斯（Luis Valdez）的独幕剧《被贩卖的人》（Los Vendidos，1967）的公开意识形态意图似乎在于嘲讽强加于墨西哥裔美国人身上的种族刻板印象。首先，请阐述这部独幕剧是如何实现这一意识形态意图的。其次，请阐述该剧是如何在结尾处无意间重新确立了它原本试图瓦解的某些刻板印象，从而解构了自身的意识形态意图。这种意识形态冲突揭示了在试图避免刻板印象的过程中所面临的种种困难，或者任何受压迫群体在面对偏见时，在确立自身身份认同方面所面临的种种困境？

1 The overt ideological project of Luis Valdez’s “Los Vendidos” (1967) seems to be to ridicule the ethnic stereotypes that have been imposed on Mexican Americans. First, show how this one-act play accomplishes this ideological project. Then, show how the text deconstructs its own project by inadvertently reasserting, at the end of the play, some of the same stereotypes it has worked to undermine. What does this ideological conflict suggest about the difficulties involved in the attempt to avoid stereotypes or about the difficulty any oppressed group might have asserting its own identity in the face of prejudice?

2凯特·肖邦的《暴风雨》（1898）是如何推进其关于女性性满足重要性的主题的？这似乎是故事显而易见的意识形态意图。文本中对自然意象的运用以及标准的童话式大团圆结局，是如何既促进又削弱这一主题的？这种意识形态冲突对于故事试图超越其所代表的十九世纪社会价值观又意味着什么？

2 How does Kate Chopin’s “The Storm” (1898) forward its theme of the importance of sexual fulfillment for women, which seems to be the story’s overt ideological project? How does the text’s use of nature imagery and the standard fairy-tale happy ending both promote and undermine this project? What does this ideological conflict imply about the story’s attempt to transcend the nineteenth-century social values of the culture it represents?

3罗伯特·弗罗斯特的《未选择的路》（1916）已成为美国不墨守成规价值观的象征：“我选择了人迹更少的路，/而那条路……”这改变了一切。” 解构这个假定的意识形态计划，找出诗中所有看似削弱“不墨守成规”价值的证据，例如，两条路殊途同归，以及诗中说话者自身在某些地方表现出的明显顺从。你可能会发现，事实上，诗中并没有像你预期的那样为“不墨守成规”的意识形态提供多少支持。我们该如何解释美国公众为何未能理解这首诗的这种截然不同的解读呢？

3 Robert Frost’s “The Road Not Taken” (1916) has become an American icon of the value of nonconformity: “I took the one less traveled by, / And that has made all the difference.” Deconstruct this assumed ideological project by finding all the evidence in the poem that seems to undermine the value of nonconformity, for example, the ways in which the two roads are the same and the speaker’s own apparent conformity at various points in the poem. You may find that there is, in fact, not as much support in the poem as you expected for the ideology of nonconformity. How might we account for the apparent failure of the American public to recognize this very different reading of the poem?

4玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818）创作于英国浪漫主义时期，作者与当时一些主要的浪漫主义诗人交往密切。这部作品经常将自然描绘成浪漫崇高的象征：对自然令人敬畏的壮丽景象——巍峨的高山、汹涌的海浪、被闪电击碎的参天大树等等——的沉思，能够激发人类崇高而高尚的思想和情感，使他们超越世俗经验的局限。请找出文本中的证据来支持这一论点。然后，分析小说如何解构这一意识形态，找出自然不符合这一定义之处。并探讨这种意识形态冲突在文本中存在的原因。

4 Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818), which was produced during England’s romantic period by an author who associated with some of the leading romantic poets of her day, frequently represents nature as romantic sublime: the contemplation of nature’s awesome grandeur – great mountains, storms at sea, huge trees blasted by lightning, and the like – can produce in human beings lofty, noble thoughts and feelings that take them beyond the finite boundaries of mundane experience. Find textual evidence to support this claim. Then show how the novel deconstructs this ideological project by finding, in the text, the ways in which nature does not live up to this definition. Speculate on the reasons why this ideological conflict is present in this text.

5威廉·布莱克的《小黑孩》（1789）如何体现解构主义的“不可判定性”概念？具体而言，这首诗是如何展现种族平等、白人优于黑人以及黑人优于白人这三个看似矛盾的主题的？这种明显的意识形态冲突又意味着什么？

5 How might William Blake’s “The Little Black Boy” (1789) provide an example of deconstruction’s notion of undecidability? Specifically, how does the poem seem to promote the mutually exclusive themes of racial equality, the superiority of white people to black people, and the superiority of black people to white people? What are the implications of this apparent ideological conflict?

9. 新历史与文化批评
