9   New historical and cultural criticism

正如我们在前几章中所看到的，批判理论在许多方面可以相互重叠。马克思主义者可以借鉴精神分析的概念来分析资本主义造成的心理创伤。女权主义者可以借鉴马克思主义的概念来审视女性所遭受的社会经济压迫。分析美国文学阐释惯例的文章既可以收录于结构主义文集，也可以收录于读者反应文学文集。诸如此类。

As we’ve seen in previous chapters, critical theories can overlap with one another in a number of ways. Marxists can draw on psychoanalytic concepts to help them analyze the debilitating psychological effects of capitalism. Feminists can draw on Marxist concepts to examine the socioeconomic oppression of women. Essays analyzing the conventions of American literary interpretation can be included both in structuralist anthologies and in reader-response anthologies. And so forth.

尽管存在这种重叠，但大多数批判理论在目的上仍然彼此不同。例如，让我们来看看刚才提到的几种批判理论截然不同的目标。马克思主义试图揭示我们的社会经济体系如何成为我们经验的最终来源。女权主义试图揭示父权制性别角色如何成为我们经验的最终来源。精神分析试图揭示被压抑的心理冲突如何成为我们经验的最终来源。结构主义试图揭示使我们能够理解这个原本混乱的世界的简单结构系统。而读者反应理论则试图揭示读者如何构建他们所阅读的文本。

Despite such overlap, however, most critical theories remain distinct from one another in terms of their purpose. Let’s look, for example, at the very different goals of the critical theories just mentioned. Marxism attempts to reveal the ways in which our socioeconomic system is the ultimate source of our experience. Feminism attempts to reveal the ways in which patriarchal gender roles are the ultimate source of our experience. Psychoanalysis attempts to reveal the ways in which repressed psychological conflicts are the ultimate source of our experience. Structuralism attempts to reveal the simple structural systems that make possible our understanding of an otherwise chaotic world. And reader-response theory attempts to reveal the operations whereby readers create the texts they read.

然而，有时批判理论的重叠之处如此之多，以至于很难确定它们之间的差异，尤其当实践者对这些差异的理解存在分歧时更是如此。新历史主义和文化批评就是如此。正如我们将看到的，这两个领域拥有如此多的共同理论基础，以至于它们在文学阐释方面的方法往往非常相似。但是，为了清晰起见，也为了充分理解新历史主义和文化批评之间确实存在的差异，我们将首先分别讨论这两个领域。由于新历史主义者比文化批评家更透彻地阐述了他们的理论前提，我们将从新历史主义入手。一旦你对新历史主义有了较为清晰的认识，就更容易看出文化批评与它的异同之处。

Sometimes critical theories overlap so much, however, that it is difficult to determine the ways in which they are different, especially when practitioners disagree about what those differences are. Such is the case with new historicism and cultural criticism. As we’ll see, these two fields share so much common theoretical ground that their approaches to literary interpretation are often quite similar. For the sake of clarity, however, and in order to fully appreciate the differences that do exist between new historicism and cultural criticism, we will begin by discussing the two fields separately. And because new historicists have articulated their theoretical premises more thoroughly than have cultural critics, we’ll start with new historicism. Once you have a fairly clear idea of the new historical enterprise, it will be easier to see the ways in which cultural criticism compares and contrasts with it.

新历史主义

New historicism

我们大多数从小接受传统历史观念教育的人，都会读到一位美国历史学家在1944年撰写的关于美国独立战争一场战役的记述。如果我们真的要问什么问题的话，那就是“这个记载准确吗？”或者“这场战役揭示了它所处的时代精神的哪些方面？”相比之下，一位新历史主义者在阅读同样的战役记载时会问：“这个记载揭示了1944年产生和阅读它的文化的政治议程和意识形态冲突的哪些方面？”对这场战役本身的新历史兴趣会引发诸如此类的问题：“在战役发生的时期，美国殖民地或英国（或欧洲国家）是如何描述这场战役的（通过报纸、杂志、小册子、政府文件、故事、演讲、绘画和照片）？这些描述又揭示了美国革命是如何塑造并被塑造它的文化的哪些方面？”

Most of us raised to think about history in the traditional way would read an account of a Revolutionary War battle written by an American historian in 1944 and ask, if we asked anything at all, “Is this account accurate?” or “What does this battle tell us about the ‘spirit of the age’ in which it was fought?” In contrast, a new historicist would read the same account of that battle and ask, “What does this account tell us about the political agendas and ideological conflicts of the culture that produced and read the account in 1944?” New historical interest in the battle itself would produce such questions as, “At the time in which it was fought, how was this battle represented (in newspapers, magazines, tracts, government documents, stories, speeches, drawings, and photographs) by the American colonies or by Britain (or by European countries), and what do these representations tell us about how the American Revolution shaped and was shaped by the cultures that represented it?”

正如你所见，传统历史学家和新历史学家提出的问题截然不同，这是因为这两种历史研究方法基于对历史本质和认知方式的截然不同的观点。传统历史学家会问：“发生了什么？”以及“这一事件告诉我们特定时期和地点的历史状况是什么？”相比之下，新历史学家则会问：“这一事件是如何被解读的？”以及“这些解读揭示了解读者背后的意识形态力量是什么？”

As you can see, the questions asked by traditional historians and by new historicists are quite different, and that’s because these two approaches to history are based on very different views of what history is and how we can know it. Traditional historians ask, “What happened?” and “What does the event tell us about a particular time and place in history?” In contrast, new historicists ask, “How has the event been interpreted?” and “What do the interpretations tell us about the ideological forces in play for the interpreters?”

对大多数传统历史学家而言，历史是一系列具有线性因果关系的事件：事件A导致事件B，事件B导致事件C，以此类推。此外，他们认为，通过客观分析，我们完全有能力揭示历史事件的真相，而这些真相有时能够揭示时代的精神，即这些真相所指涉的文化所秉持的世界观。事实上，一些最流行的传统历史叙述提出了一个关键概念来解释特定历史群体的世界观，例如文艺复兴时期的“存在之链”——宇宙创造的等级制度，上帝位于顶端，人类位于中间，最卑微的生物位于底端。这一概念被用来论证伊丽莎白时代文化的指导精神是对人类生活各个领域秩序重要性的信仰。1.在历史课上，我们可以看到传统研究方法的这一方面，例如，历史课会根据时代精神来研究过去的事件，比如理性时代或启蒙时代；在文学课上，我们也能看出传统研究方法的这一方面，例如，文学课会根据历史时期来研究文学作品，比如新古典主义时期、浪漫主义时期或现代主义时期。最后，传统历史学家普遍认为历史是进步的，人类物种随着时间的推移不断进步，在道德、文化和技术成就方面不断提升。

For most traditional historians, history is a series of events that have a linear, causal relationship: event A caused event B, event B caused event C, and so on. Furthermore, they believe we are perfectly capable, through objective analysis, of uncovering the facts about historical events, and those facts can sometimes reveal the spirit of the age, that is, the worldview held by the culture to which those facts refer. Indeed, some of the most popular traditional historical accounts have offered a key concept that would explain the worldview of a given historical population, such as the Renaissance notion of the Great Chain of Being the cosmic hierarchy of creation, with God at the top of the ladder, human beings at the middle, and the lowliest creatures at the bottom which has been used to argue that the guiding spirit of Elizabethan culture was a belief in the importance of order in all domains of human life.1 You can see this aspect of the traditional approach in history classes that study past events in terms of the spirit of an age, such as the Age of Reason or the Age of Enlightenment, and you can see it in literature classes that study literary works in terms of historical periods, such as the neoclassical, romantic, or modernist periods. Finally, traditional historians generally believe that history is progressive, that the human species is improving over the course of time, advancing in its moral, cultural, and technological accomplishments.

与此相反，新历史主义者认为，我们只能清晰地了解最基本的历史事实。例如，我们知道乔治·华盛顿是美国第一任总统，拿破仑在滑铁卢战役中战败。但是，对于新历史主义者而言，我们对这些事实意义的理解，以及它们如何融入当时当地错综复杂的意识形态、社会、政治和文化议程，则完全取决于我们自身的认知。关键在于诠释，而非事实。即便传统历史学家自认为坚持事实，他们如何解读这些事实（包括哪些事实被认为足够重要而值得报道，哪些事实被忽略）也决定了这些事实最终讲述的故事。从这个角度来看，根本不存在所谓的事实呈现，只有诠释。此外，新历史主义者认为，由于种种原因，可靠的诠释难以产生。

New historicists, in contrast, don’t believe we have clear access to any but the most basic facts of history. We can know, for example, that George Washington was the first American president and that Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo. But our understanding of what such facts mean, of how they fit within the complex web of competing ideologies and conflicting social, political, and cultural agendas of the time and place in which they occurred is, for new historicists, strictly a matter of interpretation, not fact. Even when traditional historians believe they are sticking to the facts, the way they contextualize those facts (including which facts are deemed important enough to report and which are left out) determines what story those facts will tell. From this perspective, there is no such thing as a presentation of facts; there is only interpretation. Furthermore, new historicists argue that reliable interpretations are, for a number of reasons, difficult to produce.

新历史主义者认为，造成这种困难的首要原因在于客观分析的不可能性。如同所有人类一样，历史学家生活在特定的时空之中，他们对过去和现在事件的看法会受到自身文化经历的无数有意识或无意识的影响。历史学家或许自认为客观，但他们自身对是非对错、文明与野蛮、重要与不重要等问题的看法，会强烈影响他们对事件的解读。例如，历史是进步的传统观点，正是基于许多盎格鲁-欧洲历史学家过去持有的信念，即土著民族的“原始”文化不如“文明”的盎格鲁-欧洲文化发展程度高，因而也逊于后者。因此，拥有高度发达的艺术形式、道德准则和精神哲学的古代文化，如美洲原住民、非洲人和澳大利亚原住民的部落文化，经常被误解为无法无天、迷信和野蛮的。

The first and most important reason for this difficulty, new historicists believe, is the impossibility of objective analysis. Like all human beings, historians live in a particular time and place, and their views of both current and past events are influenced in innumerable conscious and unconscious ways by their own experience within their own culture. Historians may believe they’re being objective, but their own views of what is right and wrong, what is civilized and uncivilized, what is important and unimportant, and the like, will strongly influence the ways in which they interpret events. For example, the traditional view that history is progressive is based on the belief, held in the past by many Anglo-European historians, that the “primitive” cultures of native peoples are less evolved than, and therefore inferior to, the “civilized” Anglo-European cultures. As a result, ancient cultures with highly developed art forms, ethical codes, and spiritual philosophies, such as the tribal cultures of Native Americans, Africans, and Aboriginal Australians were often misrepresented as lawless, superstitious, and savage.

历史难以做出可靠解读的另一个原因是其复杂性。对于新历史主义者而言，历史不能简单地理解为一系列事件的线性发展。在历史上的任何特定时刻，任何特定文化都可能在某些方面取得进步，而在另一些方面则出现倒退。而且，任何两位历史学家都可能对何为进步、何为非进步持有不同意见，因为这些术语本身就涉及定义。也就是说，历史并非如许多传统历史学家所认为的那样，是一场有序的、迈向不断进步未来的游行。它更像是一场即兴舞蹈，由无数种舞步组成，在任何时刻都可能沿着任何新的路线行进，并且没有特定的目标或终点。个人和群体或许有目标，但人类历史本身却没有。

Another reason for the difficulty in producing reliable interpretations of history is its complexity. For new historicists, history cannot be understood simply as a linear progression of events. At any given point in history, any given culture may be progressing in some areas and regressing in others. And any two historians may disagree about what constitutes progress and what doesn’t, for these terms are matters of definition. That is, history isn’t an orderly parade into a continually improving future, as many traditional historians have believed. It’s more like an improvised dance consisting of an infinite variety of steps, following any new route at any given moment, and having no particular goal or destination. Individuals and groups of people may have goals, but human history does not.

同样，虽然事件的发生肯定有其原因，但新历史主义者认为，这些原因通常是多元的、复杂的，而且难以分析。人们无法确定地做出简单的因果陈述。此外，因果关系并非单向的。任何特定事件——无论是政治选举还是儿童动画片——都是其文化的产物，但反过来也会影响该文化。换言之，所有事件——从艺术作品的创作到电视直播的谋杀案审判，再到贫困状况的持续或改变——都受到其所处文化的影响，同时也塑造着该文化。

Similarly, while events certainly have causes, new historicists argue that those causes are usually multiple, complex, and difficult to analyze. One cannot make simple causal statements with any certainty. In addition, causality is not a one-way street from cause to effect. Any given event – whether it be a political election or a children’s cartoon show – is a product of its culture, but it also affects that culture in return. In other words, all events – including everything from the creation of an art work, to a televised murder trial, to the persistence of or change in the condition of the poor – are shaped by and shape the culture in which they emerge.

同样，我们的主体性或自我意识，既受我们出生的文化塑造，也反过来塑造这种文化。对大多数新历史主义者而言，我们的个人身份不仅仅是社会的产物，也不仅仅是我们自身经历的产物。个人意志和欲望并非独立存在。相反，个人身份与其文化环境相互依存、相互映照、相互定义。二者关系相互构成（彼此创造），且动态不稳定。因此，关于决定论与自由意志的旧争论无法解决，因为它基于一个错误的问题：“人类身份是由社会决定的，还是人类是自由行动者？”对于新历史主义而言，这个问题无法回答，因为它涉及在两个并非完全分离的实体之间做出选择。更恰当的问题是：“个人身份与社会形态——例如政治、教育、法律和宗教制度及意识形态——是如何相互创造、促进或改变的？”因为每个社会都会在文化限制的网络内约束个人的思想和行动，同时又赋予个人思考和行动的能力。因此，我们的主体性是一个终生的过程，在这个过程中，我们自觉或不自觉地在特定时刻所处社会提供的限制和自由之间进行协商。

In a similar manner, our subjectivity, or selfhood, is shaped by and shapes the culture into which we were born. For most new historicists, our individual identity is not merely a product of society. Neither is it merely a product of our own individual will and desire. Instead, individual identity and its cultural milieu inhabit, reflect, and define each other. Their relationship is mutually constitutive (they create each other) and dynamically unstable. Thus, the old argument between determinism and free will can’t be settled because it rests on the wrong question: “Is human identity socially determined or are human beings free agents?” For new historicism, this question cannot be answered because it involves a choice between two entities that are not wholly separate. Rather, the proper question is, “What are the processes by which individual identity and social formations – such as political, educational, legal, and religious institutions and ideologies – create, promote, or change each other?” For every society constrains individual thought and action within a network of cultural limitations while it simultaneously enables individuals to think and act. Our subjectivity, then, is a lifelong process of negotiating our way, consciously and unconsciously, among the constraints and freedoms offered at any given moment in time by the society in which we live.

因此，根据新历史主义者的观点，权力并非仅仅源自政治和社会经济结构的顶层。法国哲学家和历史学家米歇尔·福柯（1926-1984）的思想对新历史主义的发展产生了深远的影响，他认为权力在各个层面、各个时间都以各种方式流通。而权力流通的载体是永无止境的交换：（1）通过买卖、物物交换、赌博、税收、慈善以及各种形式的盗窃等行为进行物质交换；（2）通过婚姻、收养、绑架和奴隶制等制度进行人口交换；（3）通过一种文化所产生的各种话语进行思想交流。

Thus, according to new historicists, power does not emanate only from the top of the political and socioeconomic structure. According to French philosopher and historian Michel Foucault (1926–84), whose ideas have strongly influenced the development of new historicism, power circulates in all directions, to and from all social levels, at all times. And the vehicle by which power circulates is a never-ending proliferation of exchange: (1) the exchange of material goods through such practices as buying and selling, bartering, gambling, taxation, charity, and various forms of theft; (2) the exchange of people through such institutions as marriage, adoption, kidnapping, and slavery; and (3) the exchange of ideas through the various discourses a culture produces.

话语是指在特定时空下，由特定文化条件所创造的社会语言，它表达了一种特定的理解人类经验的方式。例如，你可能熟悉现代科学话语、自由人文主义话语、白人至上主义话语、生态意识话语、基督教原教旨主义话语等等。而当你阅读这本教材的章节时，你也将熟悉精神分析批评话语、马克思主义批评话语、女性主义批评话语等等。尽管“话语”一词与“意识形态”一词含义大致相同，且这两个词经常被互换使用，但“话语”一词强调了语言作为意识形态载体的作用。

A discourse is a social language created by particular cultural conditions at a particular time and place, and it expresses a particular way of understanding human experience. For example, you may be familiar with the discourse of modern science, the discourse of liberal humanism, the discourse of white supremacy, the discourse of ecological awareness, the discourse of Christian fundamentalism, and the like. And as you read the chapters of this textbook, you will become familiar with the discourses of psychoanalytic criticism, Marxist criticism, feminist criticism, and so on. Although the word discourse has roughly the same meaning as the word ideology, and the two terms are often used interchangeably, the word discourse draws attention to the role of language as the vehicle of ideology.

从新的历史视角来看，任何单一的话语都无法充分解释社会权力复杂的文化动态。因为不存在一个时代铁板一块的（单一的、统一的、普世的）精神，也不存在一个能够全面解释历史的解释（一个能够为特定文化的所有方面提供单一钥匙的解释）。相反，各种话语之间存在着一种动态的、不稳定的相互作用：它们始终处于变化之中，以各种方式相互重叠、相互竞争（或者，用新的历史术语来说，就是在进行权力的博弈）。在任何特定时间点，话语都不是一成不变的。话语赋予掌权者权力，但同时也激发了对这种权力的反抗。这正是新历史主义者认为个体身份与社会关系相互构成的原因之一：总体而言，人类绝非仅仅是压迫性社会的受害者，因为他们可以在个人生​​活和公共生活中找到各种方式来反抗权威。

From a new historical perspective, no discourse by itself can adequately explain the complex cultural dynamics of social power. For there is no monolithic (single, unified, universal) spirit of an age, and there is no adequate totalizing explanation of history (an explanation that provides a single key to all aspects of a given culture). There is, instead, a dynamic, unstable interplay among discourses: they are always in a state of flux, overlapping and competing with one another (or, to use new historical terminology, negotiating exchanges of power) in any number of ways at any given point in time. Furthermore, no discourse is permanent. Discourses wield power for those in charge, but they also stimulate opposition to that power. This is one reason why new historicists believe that the relationship between individual identity and society is mutually constitutive: on the whole, human beings are never merely victims of an oppressive society, for they can find various ways to oppose authority in their personal and public lives.

在新历史主义看来，即使是小国的独裁者也无法独自掌握绝对权力。为了维持统治，他的权力必须渗透到众多话语体系中，例如，宗教话语（可以宣扬君权神授或上帝对等级社会的眷顾），科学话语（可以用达尔文“适者生存”的理论来支持统治精英），时尚话语（可以通过推广模仿服饰来提升领导人的声望，正如我们看到的尼赫鲁夹克风靡一时以及时尚界争相效仿第一夫人杰奎琳·肯尼迪的风格），法律话语（可以将反对统治者决定的行为定为叛国罪），等等。

For new historicism, even the dictator of a small country doesn’t wield absolute power on his own. To maintain dominance, his power must circulate in numerous discourses, for example, in the discourse of religion (which can promote belief in the “divine right” of kings or in God’s love of hierarchical society), in the discourse of science (which can support the reigning elite in terms of a theory of Darwinian “survival of the fittest”), in the discourse of fashion (which can promote the popularity of leaders by promoting copycat attire, as we saw when Nehru jackets were popular and when the fashion world copied the style of First Lady Jacqueline Kennedy), in the discourse of the law (which can make it a treasonous offense to disagree with a ruler’s decisions), and so on.

正如这些例子所示，“正确”、“自然”和“正常”的定义因人而异。因此，在不同的文化和历史时期，同性恋曾被视为异常、正常、犯罪或值得称赞。乱伦、食人以及女性对政治平等的渴望也是如此。事实上，米歇尔·福柯指出，所有关于“精神错乱”、“犯罪”和性“变态”的定义都是社会建构，统治权力正是利用这些建构来维持其控制。我们之所以接受这些定义是“自然的”，仅仅是因为它们已经深深植根于我们的文化之中。

As these examples suggest, what is “right,” “natural,” and “normal” are matters of definition. Thus, in different cultures at different points in history, homosexuality has been deemed abnormal, normal, criminal, or admirable. The same can be said of incest, cannibalism, and women’s desire for political equality. In fact, Michel Foucault has suggested that all definitions of “insanity,” “crime,” and sexual “perversion” are social constructs by means of which ruling powers maintain their control. We accept these definitions as “natural” only because they are so ingrained in our culture.

正如对社会行为和反社会行为的定义会助长某些个人和群体的权力一样，对历史事件的特定解读也会起到同样的作用。例如，对卡斯特将军臭名昭著的针对美洲原住民的军事行动进行粉饰，无疑迎合了当时美国白人权力结构消灭美洲原住民、以便政府能够夺取其土地的愿望。这种粉饰在卡斯特之后的几十年里仍然继续为美国白人权力结构服务，因为即使是那些了解卡斯特罪行的人，也认为将美国历史上的丑闻公之于众是不明智的，即便是在美国人面前。类似地，如果纳粹赢得了第二次世界大战，我们今天在美国历史书中读到的关于这场战争以及数百万犹太人遭种族灭绝的记载，将会与现在截然不同。因此，新历史主义将历史叙述视为叙事，视为故事，而这些叙事不可避免地会受到撰写者（无论是有意识的还是无意识的）观点的影响。历史学家越是不了解自己的偏见——也就是说，他们越认为自己“客观”——这些偏见就越能控制他们的叙述。

Just as definitions of social and antisocial behavior promote the power of certain individuals and groups, so do particular versions of historical events. Certainly, the whitewashing of General Custer’s now-infamous military campaigns against Native Americans served the desire of the white American power structure of his day to obliterate Native American peoples so that the government could seize their lands. And that same whitewashing continued to serve the white American power structure for many a decade beyond Custer’s time, for even those who had knowledge of Custer’s misdeeds deemed it unwise to air America’s dirty historical laundry, even in front of Americans. Analogously, had the Nazis won World War II, we would all be reading a very different account of the war, and of the genocide of millions of Jews, than the accounts we read in American history books today. Thus, new historicism views historical accounts as narratives, as stories, that are inevitably biased according to the point of view, conscious or unconscious, of those who write them. The more unaware historians are of their biases – that is, the more “objective” they think they are – the more those biases are able to control their narratives.

到目前为止，我们已经看到了新历史主义关于历史分析局限性的论断。历史分析（1）无法做到客观，（2）无法充分论证认为某种特定的时代精神或世界观可以解释任何特定文化的复杂性，并且（3）无法充分证明历史是线性的、因果的或进步的。我们无法脱离历史事件、物品或人物所处的语境来理解它们，因为我们无法脱离它们在当时所承载的意义来理解它们。我们越是孤立地看待它们，就越倾向于用我们自身所处的时代和地域的意义来解读它们，或许还会受到我们自身对人类随着时间推移而进步的渴望的影响。

So far, we’ve seen new historicism’s claims about what historical analysis cannot do. Historical analysis (1) cannot be objective, (2) cannot adequately demonstrate that a particular spirit of the times or worldview accounts for the complexities of any given culture, and (3) cannot adequately demonstrate that history is linear, causal, or progressive. We can’t understand a historical event, object, or person in isolation from the web of discourses in which it was represented because we can’t understand it in isolation from the meanings it carried at that time. The more we isolate it, the more we will tend to view it through the meanings of our own time and place and, perhaps, our own desire to believe that the human race is improving with the passage of time.

鉴于这些局限性，历史分析究竟能取得什么成就？我们可以发展出哪些历史理解方法？而对我们而言最重要的是，新历史文学批评家可以尝试哪些类型的分析？如果您已经阅读过第八章“解构批评”，那么您就能很好地理解这些问题的答案，因为许多新历史实践都融入了关于人类语言和经验的解构主义见解。例如，我们可以说，新历史主义解构了历史（传统上被认为是事实性的）与文学（传统上被认为是虚构的）之间的传统对立。因为新历史主义将历史视为一种文本，其解读方式与文学批评家解读文学文本的方式相同；反之，它将文学文本视为文化产物，能够揭示在这些文本创作的时代和地点中，各种话语的相互作用以及社会意义网络是如何运作的。让我们仔细审视一下这些主张，首先讨论新历史实践的关键要素，然后讨论新历史主义对文学批评的影响。

Given these limitations, what can historical analysis accomplish? What approaches to historical understanding can be developed, and, most important for our purposes, what kinds of analyses can new historical literary critics attempt? If you’ve read Chapter 8, “Deconstructive Criticism,” you’re in a good position to understand the answer to these questions because a good deal of new historical practice incorporates deconstructive insights about human language and experience. For example, we might say that new historicism deconstructs the traditional opposition between history (traditionally thought of as factual) and literature (traditionally thought of as fictional). For new historicism considers history a text that can be interpreted the same way literary critics interpret literary texts, and conversely, it considers literary texts cultural artifacts that can tell us something about the interplay of discourses, the web of social meanings, operating in the time and place in which those texts were written. Let’s take a closer look at each of these claims by discussing, first, the key elements of new historical practice and, then, the implications of new historicism for literary criticism.

总的来说，我们对历史的了解主要来自文本形式，即记录特定时空下态度、政策、程序和事件的文件、统计数据、法律条文、日记、信件、演讲、论文、新闻报道等等。也就是说，即使历史学家的研究成果基于上述“一手资料”，而非其他历史学家的解读（二手资料），这些一手资料几乎也总是以某种文字形式存在。因此，它们需要像文学批评家分析文学文本那样进行分析。例如，我们可以研究历史文献的修辞策略（文本为达到其目的而运用的文体手法）；我们可以解构历史文献，揭示其自身意识形态假设的局限性；我们还可以通过分析历史文献，揭示其显性和隐性的父权制、种族主义和恐同倾向。此外，历史记载——即在相关时期或之后撰写的二手资料——也可以用同样的方法进行分析。

By and large, we know history only in its textual form, that is, in the form of the documents, written statistics, legal codes, diaries, letters, speeches, tracts, news articles, and the like in which are recorded the attitudes, policies, procedures, and events that occurred in a given time and place. That is, even when historians base their findings on the kinds of “primary sources” listed above, rather than on the interpretations of other historians (secondary sources), those primary sources are almost always in the form of some sort of writing. As such, they require the same kinds of analyses literary critics perform on literary texts. For example, historical documents can be studied in terms of their rhetorical strategies (the stylistic devices by which texts try to achieve their purposes); they can be deconstructed to reveal the limitations of their own ideological assumptions; and they can be examined for the purpose of revealing their explicit and implicit patriarchal, racist, and homophobic agendas. In addition, historical accounts – secondary sources, written during the period in question or at a later date – can be analyzed in the same manner.

换句话说，新历史主义者认为历史信息的第一手资料和第二手资料都是叙事形式。两者都在讲述某种故事，因此这些故事都可以运用文学批评的工具进行分析。事实上，我们可以说，新历史主义将边缘群体（如妇女、有色人种、穷人、工人阶级、男同性恋和女同性恋、囚犯、精神病院居民等）被压制的历史叙事推到前台，从而解构了白人、男性、盎格鲁-欧洲的历史叙事，揭示了其令人不安的隐藏潜台词：那些被其压迫的人民的经历，而这种压迫是为了维持其控制大多数美国人对历史的认知的统治地位。

In other words, new historicists consider both primary and secondary sources of historical information forms of narrative. Both tell some kind of story, and therefore those stories can be analyzed using the tools of literary criticism. Indeed, we might say that in bringing to the foreground the suppressed historical narratives of marginalized groups – such as women, people of color, the poor, the working class, gay men and lesbians, prisoners, the inhabitants of mental institutions, and so on – new historicism has deconstructed the white, male, Anglo-European historical narrative to reveal its disturbing, hidden subtext: the experiences of those peoples it has oppressed in order to maintain the dominance that allowed it to control what most Americans know about history.

事实上，关注边缘化群体的历史叙事一直是新历史主义的重要特征，以至于一些理论家质疑，新历史主义者为何能够比接受父权制盎格鲁-欧洲权力结构的叙事更容易地接受来自受压迫群体的叙事。对此，一种解释是，多元的声音，包括所有群体历史叙事的平等呈现，有助于确保一种主导叙事——一种从单一文化视角出发，却自诩为唯一准确历史版本的叙事——不再主导我们对历史的理解。目前，我们仍然未能实现所有群体历史叙事的平等呈现。即便某些群体的历史叙事，例如女性和有色人种的叙事，数量日益增多，但在我们大多数人学习历史的课堂上，这些叙事通常无法获得与父权制盎格鲁-欧洲叙事同等的关注。因此，新历史主义试图促进边缘化民族历史的发展，并使其受到关注。

In fact, a focus on the historical narratives of marginalized peoples has been such an important feature of new historicism that some theorists have asked how new historicists can accept narratives from oppressed peoples any more readily than they have accepted narratives from the patriarchal Anglo-European power structure. One answer to this question is that a plurality of voices, including an equal representation of historical narratives from all groups, helps ensure that a master narrative – a narrative told from a single cultural point of view that, nevertheless, presumes to offer the only accurate version of history – will no longer control our historical understanding. At this point in time, we still do not have an equal representation of historical narratives from all groups. And even as the historical narratives of some groups are becoming more and more numerous, such as those of women and of people of color, those narratives generally do not receive the same kind of attention as patriarchal Anglo-European narratives do in the classroom, where most of us learn about history. Therefore, new historicism tries to promote the development of and gain attention for the histories of marginalized peoples.

多元的历史视角也往往会提出一些新历史主义认为重要的问题，例如意识形态如何在个人和群体身份的形成中发挥作用，一种文化对自身的认知（例如，美国人认为自己是坚韧不拔的个人主义者）如何影响其政治、法律和社会政策和习俗，以及权力如何在特定文化中流通。如果我们设想以下几门关于美国革命的大学课程之间的差异，就能理解多元的历史视角为何会提出这类问题：（1）一门研究美国传统战争叙述的课程；（2）一门将美国传统战争叙述与英国、法国、荷兰和西班牙传统战争叙述进行对比的课程，这些国家认为美国革命只是其争夺殖民霸权（主要在加勒比地区）斗争中的一个插曲；（3）一门将上述叙述与受战争影响的部落口述历史中记录的美洲原住民战争叙述进行对比的课程。

A plurality of historical voices also tends to raise issues that new historicism considers important, such as how ideology operates in the formation of personal and group identity, how a culture’s perception of itself (for example, Americans’ belief that they are rugged individualists) influences its political, legal, and social policies and customs, and how power circulates in a given culture. We can see how a plurality of historical voices tends to raise these kinds of issues if we imagine the differences among the following hypothetical college courses on the American Revolution: (1) a course that studies traditional American accounts of the war; (2) a course that contrasts traditional American accounts of the war with traditional British, French, Dutch, and Spanish accounts of the war, countries for whom the American Revolution was but a moment in their struggle for colonial power, primarily in the Caribbean; (3) and a course that contrasts the above accounts with Native American accounts of the war recorded from the oral histories of tribes that were affected by it.

当我们的想象力从第一道菜式过渡到第二道菜式，再到第三道菜式时，我们的关注点逐渐从历史叙述和前景的“事实”内容转移到历史作为一种文本如何被不同文化解读以适应其自身权力结构的意识形态需求上，这成为了一种新的历史学关注点。在此背景下，新历史主义或许可以发挥作用。可以将其定义为文化讲述自身故事的历史。或者，作为对某些传统历史叙述的修正，新历史主义可以定义为文化讲述自身谎言的历史。因此，并不存在传统意义上的历史，存在的只是对历史的各种表述。

As we move, in our imagination, from the first course to the second and then to the third, our focus moves farther away from the “factual” content of historical accounts and foregrounds, instead, the ways in which history is a text that is interpreted by different cultures to fit the ideological needs of their own power structures, which is a new historical concern. In this context, new historicism might be defined as the history of stories cultures tell themselves about themselves. Or, as a corrective to some traditional historical accounts, new historicism might be defined as the history of lies cultures tell themselves. Thus, there is no history, in the traditional sense of the term. There are only representations of history.

除了关注被边缘化的历史叙事之外，新历史分析还涉及一种被称为“深度描述”的方法，这个术语借鉴自人类学。深度描述通过对特定文化产物——例如生育习俗、仪式、游戏、刑法、艺术作品、版权法等等——进行细致入微的考察，试图发现这些文化产物对于其所在社群的意义，并揭示赋予这些意义的社会习俗、文化规范和世界观。因此，深度描述并非探寻事实，而是探寻意义。正如上文列举的文化产物案例所示，深度描述关注历史的个人层面——家庭动态史、休闲活动史、性行为史、育儿习俗史——其重要性丝毫不亚于甚至超过军事战役和法律制定等传统历史主题。事实上，由于传统历史主义倾向于忽视或边缘化私人生活，认为它是主观的、无关紧要的，因此新历史主义试图通过将与私人生活相关的问题置于历史研究的前沿来弥补这一疏漏。

In addition to its focus on marginalized historical narratives, new historical analysis involves what is called thick description, a term borrowed from anthropology. Thick description attempts, through close, detailed examination of a given cultural production – such as birthing practices, ritual ceremonies, games, penal codes, works of art, copyright laws, and the like – to discover the meanings that particular cultural production had for the people in whose community it occurred and to reveal the social conventions, cultural codes, and ways of seeing the world that gave that production those meanings. Thus, thick description is not a search for facts but a search for meanings, and as the examples of cultural productions listed above illustrate, thick description focuses on the personal side of history – the history of family dynamics, of leisure activities, of sexual practices, of childrearing customs – as much as or more than on such traditional historical topics as military campaigns and the passage of laws. Indeed, because traditional historicism tended to ignore or marginalize private life as subjective and irrelevant, new historicism tries to compensate for this omission by bringing issues concerned with private life into the foreground of historical inquiry.

让我总结一下人类学家克利福德·格尔茨在《文化的解释》一书中提出的“深度描述”的例子。想象一下，一个年轻人在拥挤的房间里向对面的人眨眼。如果用“浅显描述”来描述这件事，只会说右眼皮快速收缩了一下——仅此而已。而“深度描述”则会试图探究眨眼在特定语境下的含义。首先，这究竟是眨眼——一种旨在传递信息的公开手势——还是仅仅是无意识的眼皮抽搐？如果是眨眼，那么它是否像通常那样传递着某种阴谋信号？或者，它是否是一个虚假的眨眼，意在让别人误以为存在某种阴谋，而实际上并非如此？在这种情况下，眨眼就不意味着阴谋，而意味着欺骗。又或者，它是否是对刚才描述的虚假眨眼的一种模仿，意在讽刺那个为了欺骗而眨眼的人？在这种情况下，眨眼既不代表阴谋，也不代表欺骗，而是嘲讽。现在假设，在最后一个例子中，这位想成为讽刺作家的人对自己的能力没有把握：他不想被误认为只是在抽搐或眨眼；他想让朋友们知道他是在嘲讽某人。所以为了确保自己能做得恰到好处，他对着镜子练习讽刺性的眨眼。在这种情况下，眨眼的含义就变得复杂了：它变成了对朋友假装眨眼以欺骗他人，让他们以为正在进行阴谋的拙劣模仿。虽然这个深度描述的例子可能有些夸张，但它说明了一个新的历史观，即历史是诠释而非事实的产物，而且诠释总是发生在社会习俗的框架之内。

Let me summarize an example of thick description offered by anthropologist Clifford Geertz in The Interpretation of Cultures. Imagine a young man winking at someone across a crowded room. A “thin description” of the event would describe it as a rapid contraction of the right eyelid – period. A thick description would attempt to find out what the wink meant in the context in which it occurred. First, was it a wink – that is, a public gesture intended to communicate a message – or just an involuntary twitch? If it was a wink, was it a wink performing its usual activity of imparting a conspiratorial signal? Or was it a fake wink, intended to make others believe a conspiracy was underway when, in fact, it was not? In this case, the wink would not mean conspiracy but deception. Or was it a parody of the fake wink just described, intended to satirize the person who winked in order to deceive? In this case, the wink would mean neither conspiracy nor deception, but ridicule. Now suppose that, in this last example, the would-be satirist is unsure of his ability: he doesn’t want to be mistaken for someone merely twitching or winking; he wants his friends to know that he’s mocking someone. So to be sure he can do it properly, he practices his satirical wink in front of a mirror. In this case, the wink would have a complicated meaning: it would be the rehearsal of a parody of a friend faking a wink to deceive others that a conspiracy is underway. Although this example of thick description may push the point a bit far, it illustrates the new historical notion that history is a matter of interpretations, not facts, and that interpretations always occur within a framework of social conventions.

最后，新历史主义认为历史分析不可避免地带有主观性，但这并非意在为一种放纵自私、“百无禁忌”的历史写作态度辩护。相反，个人偏见的必然性使得新历史主义者必须尽可能地意识到并坦诚地阐述自身在分析材料方面的心理和意识形态立场，以便读者能够了解他们看待历史问题的视角。这种做法被称为自我定位。

Finally, new historicism’s claim that historical analysis is unavoidably subjective is not an attempt to legitimize a self-indulgent, “anything goes” attitude toward the writing of history. Rather, the inevitability of personal bias makes it imperative that new historicists be as aware of and as forthright as possible about their own psychological and ideological positions relative to the material they analyze so that their readers can have some idea of the human “lens” through which they are viewing the historical issues at hand. This practice is called self-positioning.

例如，在路易斯·蒙特罗斯的新历史论文《宣扬文艺复兴：文化的诗学与政治》的结尾部分，他坦诚地表达了自己的观点，其中就包括他作为文艺复兴学者和教授的身份所带来的影响。他告诉我们，他个人对某些文本中展现的文艺复兴形象有着特殊的偏爱，例如莎士比亚和斯宾塞的作品。此外，他还承认，在分析这些文本时，他探讨的是与当今社会息息相关的问题，因为他不仅希望参与到对伊丽莎白时代文化的重新思考中，也希望参与到对我们自身文化的重新思考中。最后，蒙特罗斯承认，尽管他的写作旨在破坏传统的文学研究历史方法——例如传统上将文艺复兴时期划分为一个有限的时期，并赋予其特定的文化特质——但作为一名教授和文艺复兴学者，他“在维护和再生产他想要质疑其运作的那些机构方面有着复杂而实质性的利益”（30）。

For example, near the end of Louis Montrose’s new historical essay, “Professing the Renaissance: The Poetics and Politics of Culture,” he announces his own biases, which include those produced by his role as a Renaissance scholar and professor. He tells us that he has a personal investment in those representations of the Renaissance in texts for which he feels a particular affinity, such as those of Shakespeare and Spenser. Furthermore, he acknowledges that, in analyzing these texts, he writes about issues that are socially relevant today because he wants to participate not only in the current rethinking of Elizabethan culture but in the current rethinking of our own culture. Finally, Montrose admits that although his writing works to undermine traditional historical approaches to literary scholarship – such as the traditional demarcation of a finite period called the Renaissance to which specific cultural qualities are attributed – he has, as a professor and Renaissance scholar, “a complex and substantial stake in sustaining and reproducing the very institutions whose operations [he] wish[es] to call into question” (30).

在讨论新历史主义对文学批评的影响之前，让我们先停下来回顾一下它的关键概念。

Before we discuss the implications of new historicism for literary criticism, let’s pause for a moment to review its key concepts.

1历史写作关乎诠释，而非事实。因此，所有历史记述都是叙事，可以运用文学批评家分析叙事作品的诸多方法进行分析。

1 The writing of history is a matter of interpretations, not facts. Thus, all historical accounts are narratives and can be analyzed using many of the tools used by literary critics to analyze narrative.

2历史既不是线性的（它不会从原因 A 到结果 B，再从原因 B 到结果 C 整齐地发展），也不是进步的（人类物种不会随着时间的推移而稳步进步）。

2 History is neither linear (it does not proceed neatly from cause A to effect B and from cause B to effect C) nor progressive (the human species is not steadily improving over the course of time).

3权力从来不会完全局限于某个人或某个社会阶层。相反，权力在文化中通过物质商品的交换、人口的交换，以及——正如我们将在下文看到的，对文学批评家而言最为重要的——通过文化所产生的各种话语进行的思想交流而流通。

3 Power is never wholly confined to a single person or a single level of society. Rather, power circulates in a culture through exchanges of material goods, exchanges of human beings, and, most important for literary critics as we’ll see below, exchanges of ideas through the various discourses a culture produces.

4时代精神并非铁板一块，也不存在能够全面解释历史的单一、统一、普世的模式（即能够为理解特定文化的方方面面提供单一钥匙的解释）。存在的只是各种话语之间动态且不稳定的相互作用，历史学家可以尝试分析这些话语的意义，但这种分析永远是不完整的，只能展现历史图景的一部分。

4 There is no monolithic (single, unified, universal) spirit of an age, and there is no adequate totalizing explanation of history (an explanation that provides a single key to all aspects of a given culture). There is only a dynamic, unstable interplay among discourses, the meanings of which the historian can try to analyze, though that analysis will always be incomplete, accounting for only a part of the historical picture.

5个人身份——如同历史事件、文本和文物一样——既受其所处的文化塑造，也反过来塑造其所处的文化。因此，诸如“正常”之类的文化范畴也同样重要。而正常、不正常和不正常，都取决于定义。换句话说，我们的个人身份由我们讲述的关于自身的叙事构成，而我们构建这些叙事的素材则来源于构成我们文化的各种话语的流通。

5 Personal identity – like historical events, texts, and artifacts – is shaped by and shapes the culture in which it emerges. Thus, cultural categories such as normal and abnormal, sane and insane, are matters of definition. Put another way, our individual identity consists of the narratives we tell ourselves about ourselves, and we draw the material for our narratives from the circulation of discourses that constitutes our culture.

6所有历史分析都不可避免地带有主观性。因此，历史学家必须揭示他们如何意识到自身的文化经验会影响他们对历史的解读。

6 All historical analysis is unavoidably subjective. Historians must therefore reveal the ways in which they know they have been positioned, by their own cultural experience, to interpret history.

新历史主义与文学

New historicism and literature

具体而言，新的历史概念如何在文学批评领域发挥作用？尽管新历史文学批评将我们对文学文本的研究融入历史研究之中，但正如我们刚才所见，历史研究已今非昔比。因此，新历史批评与传统历史批评鲜有共同之处。后者在十九世纪和二十世纪初的文学研究中占据主导地位，其研究主要局限于作者的生平，以探寻其创作意图；或局限于作品创作的历史时期，以揭示文本所体现的时代精神。对于传统文学史家而言，文学存在于一个纯粹的主观领域，而历史则由客观可辨识的事实构成。因此，文学的解读永远不能超越历史的既定范畴。

How, specifically, do new historical concepts operate in the domain of literary criticism? Although new historical literary criticism embeds our study of literary texts in the study of history, the study of history, as we’ve just seen, isn’t what it used to be. Therefore, new historical criticism has little in common with traditional historical criticism. The latter, which dominated literary studies in the nineteenth century and the early decades of the twentieth, confined itself largely to studies of the author’s life, in order to discover his or her intentions in writing the work, or to studies of the historical period in which the work was written, in order to reveal the spirit of the age, which the text was then shown to embody. For traditional literary historians, literature existed in a purely subjective realm, unlike history, which consisted of objectively discernible facts. Therefore, literature could never be interpreted to mean anything that history didn’t authorize it to mean.

正如您在第五章中所了解到的，“新批评”推翻了传统的历史批评，并在20世纪40年代至60年代主导了文学研究，它摒弃了传统历史主义的文学研究方法。在新批评家看来，文学史家唯一能提供的只是关于文学作品的有趣背景资料。然而，新批评家认为，对文本意义的理解与历史毫无关系，因为伟大的文学作品是超越历史的、独立的（自足的）艺术对象。由于新批评的主导地位，文学史研究逐渐退居幕后，只能满足于新批评认为其应尽的职责：例如，提供关于作家生平和时代的背景资料——但这些资料并不用于解读他们的作品——以及通过提供经典作品的准确版本来保存文学经典。

As you may recall from Chapter 5, “New Criticism,” which dethroned traditional historical criticism and controlled literary studies from the 1940s to the 1960s, rejected traditional historicism’s approach to literature. For the New Critics, the only thing literary historians could offer was interesting background material about literary works. The understanding of a text’s meaning, however, has nothing whatsoever to do with history, the New Critics argued, because great literary works are timeless, autonomous (self-sufficient) art objects that exist in a realm beyond history. As a result of New Critical dominance, the historical study of literature faded into the background and tried to content itself with the tasks New Criticism deemed its proper work: for example, providing background material on authors’ lives and times – which would not, however, be used to interpret their works – and preserving, through the provision of accurate editions of revered works, the canon of great literature.

新历史主义兴起于20世纪70年代末的学术界，它既反对传统历史主义对文学的边缘化，也反对新批评将文学文本置于超越历史的永恒维度之中。对于新历史批评家而言，文学文本并不像传统文学史学家所断言的那样，体现作者的意图或展现其所处时代的精神。文学文本也不是超越其所处时空、自足的艺术品。正如新批评派所认为的那样，文学文本并非是被写成的。相反，文学文本是文化产物，能够揭示话语的互动以及社会意义网络在文本创作的时代和地点中的运作方式。它们之所以能够做到这一点，是因为文学文本本身就是话语互动的一部分，是动态社会意义网络中的一条线索。对于新历史主义而言，文学文本及其产生的历史情境同等重要，因为文本（文学作品）和语境（产生它的历史条件）相互构成：它们彼此塑造。如同个体身份与社会之间动态的互动一样，文学文本塑造着其历史语境，同时也被其历史语境所塑造。

New historicism, which emerged in academia in the late 1970s, rejects both traditional historicism’s marginalization of literature and New Criticism’s enshrinement of the literary text in a timeless dimension beyond history. For new historical critics, a literary text doesn’t embody the author’s intention or illustrate the spirit of the age that produced it, as traditional literary historians asserted. Nor are literary texts self-sufficient art objects that transcend the time and place in which they were written, as New Critics believed. Rather, literary texts are cultural artifacts that can tell us something about the interplay of discourses, the web of social meanings, operating in the time and place in which the text was written. And they can do so because the literary text is itself part of the interplay of discourses, a thread in the dynamic web of social meaning. For new historicism, the literary text and the historical situation from which it emerged are equally important because text (the literary work) and context (the historical conditions that produced it) are mutually constitutive: they create each other. Like the dynamic interplay between individual identity and society, literary texts shape and are shaped by their historical contexts.

或许，我们可以通过比较新历史主义对特定文学作品的解读与传统历史主义对这些作品的解读方式，来更好地理解新历史主义批评家与传统历史主义批评家的区别。我们将考察两部著名作品：约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》（1902）和托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》（1987）。值得注意的是，在第一个例子中，作者描写的是他自身社会所造成的、他亲身经历过的情境——欧洲对非洲的商业剥削。而在第二个例子中，作者描写的是一群生活在小说出版一百多年前的群体——一群在内战前俄亥俄州挣扎求生的前奴隶，他们既要面对过往的记忆，又要面对残酷的现实。然而，康拉德对题材的亲身经历，以及莫里森与她所处时代的距离，都并不意味着哪一种叙述就一定比另一种更“准确”。对于传统历史批评而言，两部作品的历史准确性必须通过与书中描绘的人群的历史记载进行比较来判断。而对于新历史主义而言，历史“准确性”从来都不是绝对的：《黑暗之心》和《宠儿》呈现的是作者对他们所描绘人群的诠释，这些诠释或许能为我们理解所描绘的历史经验提供新的视角，也或许不能，但它们无疑能让我们深入了解康拉德和莫里森创作这些小说时所处的语境。

Perhaps we can best see how new historical critics differ from their traditional counterparts by noting some of the ways in which new historical readings of specific literary works might contrast with traditional historical readings of those same works. We’ll look at two well-known texts: Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness (1902) and Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987). It’s interesting to note that, in our first example, the author wrote about a situation – Europe’s commercial exploitation of Africa – produced by his own society and one that he’d experienced firsthand. In our second example, the author wrote about a population – former slaves struggling to survive both their own memories of the past and the harsh realities of daily life in antebellum Ohio – that had lived over 100 years before the publication of her novel. However, neither Conrad’s firsthand experience with his subject matter nor Morrison’s temporal distance from hers means that either narrative is necessarily more “accurate” than the other. For traditional historical criticism, the historical accuracy of both texts must be judged by comparisons with historical accounts of the populations represented. And for new historicism, historical “accuracy” is never a certainty: Heart of Darkness and Beloved offer us the authors’ interpretations of the populations they depict, which may or may not provide us with new ways to view the historical experience portrayed but which will certainly give us insight into the circulation of discourses within which Conrad and Morrison wrote these novels.

对《黑暗之心》的传统历史解读可能会基于十九世纪欧洲在刚果的活动史料，分析这部小说在多大程度上忠实地反映了欧洲为获取象牙而对人力和自然资源进行剥削的历史现实。对人类生命的肆意践踏是否真如康拉德所描绘的那样骇人听闻？欧洲列强瓜分非洲领土以及对这些领土的管理背后，究竟隐藏着怎样的政治博弈？或者，传统的文学史学家可能会考察传记资料，以确定小说中哪些部分取材于康拉德本人作为比利时公司轮船船长沿刚果河航行的真实经历。马洛的经历在多大程度上是康拉德的真实经历？小说在多大程度上描绘了康拉德亲眼所见或亲耳所闻的事件。关于他自己？最后，一位传统的历史批评家可能会分析传记资料，以了解康拉德的创作想象力。他对十九世纪伟大探险家的早期兴趣如何影响了他的写作？他是否详细记录了自己作为水手的经历，还是主要依靠记忆写作？他在刚果的经历，包括由此造成的永久性健康损害，如何影响了他的艺术创作？

A traditional historical reading of Heart of Darkness might analyze, based on historical accounts of European activities in the Congo during the nineteenth century, how faithful the novel is to the historical realities of European exploitation of human and natural resources in its quest for ivory. Was the waste of human life as flagrant as Conrad portrays it? What were the politics involved in the division of African territories among various European powers and in the administration of those territories? Or a traditional literary historian might examine biographical materials in order to determine what parts of the novel are drawn from Conrad’s actual experience during his own trip up the Congo River as a steamship captain for a Belgian company. To what extent are Marlow’s experiences actually those of Conrad? To what extent does the novel depict events that Conrad saw or heard about himself? Finally, a traditional historical critic might analyze biographical materials in order to learn about Conrad’s creative imagination. What was the influence on Conrad’s writing of his early interest in the great explorers of the nineteenth century? Did he keep extensive journals of his experiences as a sailor, or did he write largely from memory? How did his experience in the Congo, including the permanent impairment of his health that resulted therefrom, affect his artistic production?

同样，对《宠儿》进行传统的历史解读，可能会基于十九世纪美国奴隶、奴隶主和前奴隶的历史记载，分析莫里森对美国这一历史层面的描绘是否忠实于历史现实。她笔下的加纳一家、他们的邻居、女教师以及博德温一家，是否准确地反映了当时奴隶主和废奴主义者所持有的各种价值观？莫里森是否捕捉到了那个动荡时代精神中相互冲突的观点？或者，传统的历史解读也可能探究小说的创作背景，以寻找其人物、场景和情节的历史渊源。例如，塞丝的故事在多大程度上是以逃亡奴隶玛格丽特·加纳的经历为原型？玛格丽特·加纳和塞丝一样，为了不让自己的女儿被送回主人的种植园而杀死了她。小说中还有哪些人物和事件是基于真实的历史人物和事件创作的？莫里森具体参考了哪些历史资料——报纸报道、奴隶叙述、法律文件、中段航程记录、历史书籍等等？最后，传统的历史批评家可能会分析作者的阅读习惯，以寻找其他文学作品对其艺术技巧的影响。她读过哪些非裔美国文学、历史小说或南方小说？这些作品的影响能否在小说的情节、人物塑造或风格中体现出来？

Similarly, a traditional historical reading of Beloved might analyze – based on historical accounts of nineteenth-century American slaves, slaveholders, and former slaves – whether or not Morrison’s depiction of this aspect of American experience is faithful to historical reality. Do her portraits of the Garners, their neighbors, Schoolteacher, and the Bodwins accurately represent the range of values held by slave owners and abolitionists at that time? Did Morrison capture the conflicting viewpoints that delineate the spirit of that troubled age? Or a traditional historical reading might investigate the circumstances of the novel’s composition in order to find the historical sources of her characters, setting, and plot. For example, to what extent was Sethe’s story modeled on that of runaway slave Margaret Garner, who, like Sethe, killed her baby daughter to save her from being returned to her master’s plantation? What other characters and events in the novel are based on actual historical figures and events? What specific historical sources – newspaper accounts, slave narratives, legal documents, records of the Middle Passage, history books, and the like – did Morrison draw on? Finally, a traditional historical critic might analyze the author’s reading habits in order to find evidence of the influence of other literary works on her own artistic technique. What African American literature, historical fiction, or Southern fiction did she read, and can their influence be perceived in the novel’s plot, characterization, or style?

与这些传统的史学关注点不同，对《黑暗之心》进行新的历史分析或许可以考察康拉德的叙事如何体现了他自身文化中两种相互冲突的话语：反殖民主义和欧洲中心主义。小说的反殖民主义主题似乎是其核心，体现在其对欧洲奴役和剥削非洲人民的罪恶的描绘中。然而，正如奇努阿·阿切贝所观察到的，小说仍然（表面上无意识地）从欧洲中心主义的视角出发：马洛对欧洲人性格的深刻洞察在于，他意识到欧洲人在文明的外衣之下，与他们意图征服的非洲人民一样“野蛮”，这意味着非洲部落文化被认为是“野蛮”的化身。或者，尽管小说带有欧洲中心主义的偏见，一位新的历史批评家或许可以将这部作品视为一种原型，或者说是新历史分析的早期体现。正如布鲁克·托马斯所指出的，康拉德的小说驳斥了传统的历史主义观点，即历史是进步的，人类会随着时间的推移而进步；其叙事结构也用一层朦胧的面纱掩盖了情节事件。主观描述意味着我们无法获得对过去清晰、客观的视角。最后，对《黑暗之心》进行新的历史分析，或许可以考察这部小说在评论界和读者群体中的接受史，从而探究这部小说如何塑造并被其诞生地（即小说创作和出版的时代和地点）以及随着时间的推移而不断演变的各种话语所塑造，包括对其与未来潜在读者关系的推测。例如，这部小说的接受史如何揭示了对文本的解读如何塑造并被历史进步主义、社会达尔文主义、白人至上主义、非洲中心主义、多元文化主义、新历史主义等等话语所塑造？

In contrast to these traditional historical concerns, a new historical analysis of Heart of Darkness might examine the ways in which Conrad’s narrative embodies two conflicting discourses present in his own culture: anticolonialism and Eurocentrism. The novel’s anticolonialist theme, which seems to be a primary focus of the text, can be seen in its representation of the evils of Europe’s subordination and exploitation of African peoples. However, as Chinua Achebe observes, the novel nevertheless speaks from an (apparently unconscious) Eurocentric perspective: Marlow’s harrowing insight into the European character consists of his realization that Europeans are, beneath their veneer of civilization, as “savage” as the African peoples they intend to subdue, which means that African tribal culture is held to epitomize “savagery.” Or, despite the novel’s Eurocentric bias, a new historical critic might analyze the text as a kind of prototype, or early embodiment, of new historical analysis. As Brook Thomas points out, Conrad’s novel debunks the traditional historicist belief that history is progressive, that the human species improves over time; and its narrative structure, which obscures plot events behind a hazy veil of subjective description, implies that we do not have access to a clear, unbiased view of the past. Finally, a new historical analysis of Heart of Darkness might examine the history of the novel’s reception by critics and the reading public to discover how the novel shaped and was shaped by discourses circulating at its point of origin (the time and place in which the book was written and published) and over the passage of time, including speculations about its relationship to possible future audiences. For example, how might the novel’s reception over time reveal the ways in which interpretations of the text shaped and have been shaped by the discourses of historical progressivism, social Darwinism, white supremacy, Afrocentrism, multiculturalism, new historicism, and so on?

同样，对《宠儿》进行新的历史分析，可以考察小说如何偏离其所依据的历史记载，从而构成对这些历史记载的修正，即对小说所呈现的历史的一种诠释。例如，丹佛和保罗·D在理解塞丝的经历过程中发生的转变，在多大程度上能够指导我们理解塞丝的历史处境？或者，一位新的历史批评家可以考察《宠儿》是如何受到现代关于奴隶制的两种相互矛盾的观点的影响，以及反过来又如何影响了这两种观点的争论：(1) 奴隶在很大程度上被贬低为像孩子一样依赖主人；(2) 奴隶们比传统白人历史学家所记载的更加彻底和一致地构建了一个连贯的抵抗体系，他们通过创造自己的编码交流方式、建立自己的社群联系，以及策略性地运用各种角色（例如“快乐的奴隶”或“愚笨的奴隶”）来掩盖他们的观点、意图和颠覆活动。最后，一种新的历史解读或许可以考察十九世纪中期话语的传播，以及这些话语如何与小说情节中的特定元素相互作用。例如，小说中描绘的塞丝的各种形象——例如教师、加纳太太、艾米·丹佛、博德温先生、斯坦普·佩德、艾拉、贝洛维德和保罗·D——是如何强化或削弱十九世纪中期关于白人至上主义、废奴主义、男性至上主义和母爱的论述的？

Similarly, a new historical analysis of Beloved might examine how the novel’s departures from the historical accounts on which it is based constitute a revision of those accounts, that is, an interpretation of the history it represents. For example, to what extent do the transformations of Denver and Paul D, as they come to understand Sethe’s experience, function as a guide for our own understanding of Sethe’s historical situation? Or a new historical critic might examine how Beloved was shaped by and has shaped the modern debate between two conflicting views of slavery: (1) that slaves were, for the most part, reduced to a childlike dependency on their masters, and (2) that slaves managed, much more thoroughly and consistently than has been reported by traditional white historians, to build a coherent system of resistance through the creation of their own coded forms of communication, the establishment of their own communal ties, and the strategic use of personae (such as the “happy slave” or the “dim-witted slave”) as camouflage for their opinions, intentions, and subversive activities. Finally, a new historical reading might investigate the circulation of mid-nineteenth-century discourses with which specific elements of the plot interact. For example, how do the various views of Sethe depicted in the novel – such as those of Schoolteacher, Mrs. Garner, Amy Denver, Mr. Bodwin, Stamp Paid, Ella, Beloved, and Paul D – reinforce or undermine the mid-nineteenth-century discourses of white supremacy, abolitionism, male supremacy, and motherly love?

正如你可能已经注意到的，在上述所有传统历史批评的例子中，历史——文本所呈现的历史情境、所描绘的人群、作者的生平及其所处的时代——被视为一种客观现实，可以被认知，并以此来解读或衡量主观的文学作品。与之相反，在新历史主义的例子中，重点在于文学文本本身如何作为一种历史话语与其他历史话语互动：这些历史话语可能在文本设定的时代和地点流传，也可能在文本接受史的后期阶段出现。因为新历史主义关注的并非作为事件的历史事件本身，而是事件的解读方式、历史话语、看待世界的方式以及意义的模式。的确，正如我们之前所看到的，历史事件是通过……来看待的。新历史主义者不再将历史视为需要记录的事实，而是将其视为需要“解读”的“文本”，以帮助我们推测人类文化在不同的历史“时刻”如何理解自身及其所处的世界。我们无法确切地知道历史上任何特定时刻究竟发生了什么，但我们可以了解当时的人们是如何看待这件事的——我们可以从他们的叙述中了解他们如何诠释自己的经历——并且我们可以解读这些诠释。

As you may have noticed, in all of the above examples of traditional historical criticism, history – the historical situation represented in the text, the population portrayed, the author’s life and times – is an objective reality that can be known and against which the subjective literary work is interpreted or measured. In contrast, in the new historical examples, the focus is on how the literary text itself functions as a historical discourse interacting with other historical discourses: those circulating at the time and place in which the text is set, at the time the text was published, or at later points in the history of the text’s reception. For new historicism is concerned not with historical events as events, but with the ways in which events are interpreted, with historical discourses, with ways of seeing the world and modes of meaning. Indeed, as we saw earlier, historical events are viewed by new historicists not as facts to be documented but as “texts” to be “read” in order to help us speculate about how human cultures, at various historical “moments,” have made sense of themselves and their world. We can’t really know exactly what happened at any given point in history, but we can know what the people involved believed happened – we can know from their own accounts the various ways in which they interpreted their experience – and we can interpret those interpretations.

因此，对于新历史文学批评家而言，文学文本通过其对特定时空下人类经验的再现，成为对历史的一种诠释。由此，文学文本既反映了其创作时期盛行的各种话语，本身也是这些话语之一。也就是说，文学文本塑造了其所处文化中盛行的各种话语，同时也被这些话语所塑造。同样，我们对文学的诠释也塑造了我们所处的文化，同时也被我们所处的文化所塑造。

For new historical literary critics, then, the literary text, through its representation of human experience at a given time and place, is an interpretation of history. As such, the literary text maps the discourses circulating at the time it was written and is itself one of those discourses. That is, the literary text shaped and was shaped by the discourses circulating in the culture in which it was produced. Likewise, our interpretations of literature shape and are shaped by the culture in which we live.

文化批评

Cultural criticism

如果你刚刚读过关于新历史主义的章节，那么你已经熟悉了文化批评的许多理论前提，因为这两个领域在理论基础上有很多共通之处。事实上，它们之间的相似之处远多于差异。例如，文化批评与新历史主义都认为，人类历史和文化构成了一个充满动态力量的复杂场域，我们只能构建出一幅片面的、主观的图景。这两个领域都相信，个体的主体性（自我）是在与文化环境的互动关系中发展起来的：虽然我们受到文化设定的限制，但我们也可以反抗这些限制，甚至改变它们。而且，这两个领域都是跨学科的，或者更准确地说，是反学科的，因为它们都认为，作为人类历史和文化基础的人类经验，无法通过那些将人类经验人为划分成社会学、心理学、文学等类别的学科来充分理解。事实上，文化批评和新历史主义都大量借鉴了相同的哲学来源，特别是法国哲学家和历史学家米歇尔·福柯的著作，而且在实践中，文化批评并不总是能轻易与新历史主义区分开来。

If you’ve just read the sections on new historicism, you’re already acquainted with many of the theoretical premises of cultural criticism, for the two fields share a good deal of the same theoretical ground. In fact, there are more similarities between them than there are differences. For example, cultural criticism shares with new historicism the view that human history and culture constitute a complex arena of dynamic forces of which we can construct only a partial, subjective picture. Both fields share the belief that individual human subjectivity (selfhood) develops in a give-and-take relationship with its cultural milieu: while we are constrained within the limits set for us by our culture, we may struggle against those limits or transform them. And both fields are interdisciplinary or, perhaps more accurately, antidisciplinary, for both argue that human experience, which is the stuff of human history and culture, cannot be adequately understood by means of academic disciplines that carve it up into such artificially separated categories as sociology, psychology, literature, and so forth. Indeed, both cultural criticism and new historicism draw heavily on the same philosophical sources, in particular the work of French philosopher and historian Michel Foucault, and in practice, cultural criticism is not always readily distinguishable from new historicism.

除了与新历史主义的相似之处外，文化批评对初学者来说可能是一个初始难题，因为该术语经常被广义地使用，指代对文化任何方面的任何分析。例如，本教材中关于马克思主义批评、女性主义批评、女同性恋/男同性恋/酷儿批评、非裔美国人批评以及后殖民主义批评的章节中对《了不起的盖茨比》的解读，都可以被视为广义上的文化批评，因为所有这些解读都运用这部小说来探讨某些问题。这是美国文化的一个方面。即使是我对菲茨杰拉德小说的精神分析解读——即认为故事展现了功能失调的爱情心理——也可以被修正为一种文化批判，如果我转而论证《了不起的盖茨比》中所描绘的那种功能失调的爱情，是20世纪20年代美国文化价值观所造成的一种文化弊病。而这正是文化批评与新历史主义之间的一个重要区别。文化批评常常借鉴上述政治理论，因为它比新历史主义更具政治导向性。

In addition to its similarity to new historicism, cultural criticism can pose an initial problem for beginners in the way the term is often used, in its broadest sense, to refer to any kind of analysis of any aspect of culture. For example, the readings of The Great Gatsby offered in this textbook in the chapters on Marxist criticism, feminist criticism, lesbian/gay/queer criticism, and African American criticism, and postcolonial criticism could all be considered examples of cultural criticism, in its broadest sense, because all of these interpretations use the novel to explore some aspect of American culture. Even my psychoanalytic reading of Fitzgerald’s novel – which suggests that the story illustrates the psychology of dysfunctional love – could be revised to function as a cultural critique if I were to argue that the kind of dysfunctional love illustrated in The Great Gatsby is a form of cultural malaise produced by the cultural values that came to the fore during the American 1920s. And herein lies one important difference between cultural criticism and new historicism. Cultural criticism often draws on such political theories as those listed above because it tends to be much more politically oriented than new historicism.

文化批评最初源于马克思主义批评，后于20世纪60年代中期发展成为一种独立的分析方法。狭义的文化批评认为，工人阶级文化一直被误解和低估。统治阶级决定哪些艺术形式应被视为“高雅”（优质）文化，例如芭蕾舞、歌剧和其他“美术”。而大众文化形式——例如电视情景喜剧、流行音乐和通俗小说——则被降格为“低俗”（劣等）文化。然而，对于文化批评家而言，“高雅”和“低俗”文化之间并无实质性的界限。因为所有文化产品都可以通过分析来揭示其所发挥的文化功能——即它们如何通过传播或转化意识形态来塑造我们的经验——这当然也意味着文化产品在权力流通中所扮演的角色。

Originally an outgrowth of Marxist criticism, then organized as an analytical approach in its own right during the mid 1960s, cultural criticism, in the narrower definition of the term, argues that working-class culture has been misunderstood and undervalued. The dominant class dictates what forms of art are to be considered “high” (superior) culture, such as the ballet, the opera, and the other “fine” arts. Forms of popular culture, on the other hand – such as television situation comedies, popular music, and pulp fiction – have been relegated to the status of “low” (inferior) culture. For cultural critics, however, there is no meaningful distinction between “high” and “low” forms of culture. For all cultural productions can be analyzed to reveal the cultural work they perform – that is, the ways in which they shape our experience by transmitting or transforming ideologies – which means, of course, the role of cultural productions in the circulation of power.

事实上，文化批评家认为，统治阶级通过定义“高雅”和“低俗”文化来强化自身的优越感，从而巩固自身的权力。然而，文化批评家也指出，被压迫群体所创造的艺术形式不仅改变了他们自身的体验，也影响着整个文化。艾滋病纪念被便可被视为此类文化产物的例证。显然，许多文化批评家在进行分析时会借鉴马克思主义、女权主义或其他政治理论，因为这些分析往往带有政治目的，例如分析（并推崇）受压迫群体的文化作品，或探究在将特定艺术形式归类为“高雅”或“低俗”文化的过程中，权力关系是如何运作的。正如我们之前所见，许多新历史学家则认为，任何单一的批判理论，无论是否具有政治性，都过于狭隘，无法充分考察人类文化的复杂运作。

Indeed, cultural critics believe that the dominant class defines “high” and “low” culture in order to reinforce its own image of superiority and thus its own power. Nevertheless, cultural critics argue, subordinate populations produce forms of art that not only transform their own experience but affect the whole culture as well. The AIDS quilt might be considered an example of such a cultural production. Clearly, many cultural critics draw on Marxist, feminist, or other political theories in performing their analyses because those analyses often have political agendas, such as analyzing (and valorizing) the cultural productions of an oppressed group or exploring the power relations at work in the categorization of specific art forms as examples of “high” or “low” culture. As we saw earlier, many new historians, in contrast, believe that any single critical theory, political or otherwise, is too narrowly focused to adequately examine the complex operations of human culture.

到目前为止，我一直在使用“文化”这个词，但并没有真正定义文化批评中“文化”一词的含义。对文化批评家而言，文化是一个过程，而非产物；它是一种鲜活的体验，而非固定的定义。更确切地说，文化是由多种互动文化组成的集合体，每一种文化都在发展变化，在任何特定时刻，它都由性别、种族、民族、性取向、社会经济阶层、职业以及其他类似因素交织而成，这些因素共同塑造了其成员的体验。

So far, I’ve used the word culture without actually defining what cultural criticism means by the term. For cultural critics, culture is a process, not a product; it is a lived experience, not a fixed definition. More precisely, a culture is a collection of interactive cultures, each of which is growing and changing, each of which is constituted at any given moment in time by the intersection of gender, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic class, occupation, and similar factors that contribute to the experience of its members.

综上所述，文化批评与新历史主义的理论前提基本相同，但以下三点除外：

To sum up, then, cultural criticism shares new historicism’s theoretical premises except in the following three instances:

1 文化批评在支持受压迫群体方面往往更具公开的政治性。

1 Cultural criticism tends to be more overtly political in its support of oppressed groups.

2由于其政治倾向，文化批评在进行分析时经常借鉴马克思主义、女权主义和其他政治理论。

2 Because of its political orientation, cultural criticism often draws on Marxist, feminist, and other political theories in performing its analyses.

3狭义上的文化批评尤其关注流行文化。

3 Cultural criticism, in the narrower sense of the term, is especially interested in popular culture.

然而，必须记住的是，即使文化批评分析压迫的运作方式，它也不会将被压迫的人民视为无助的受害者。相反，与新历史主义一样，文化批评认为被压迫的人民既是统治权力结构的受害者，也有能力反抗或改造这种权力结构。

It is important to remember, however, that even when cultural criticism analyzes the operations of oppression, it does not view oppressed peoples as helpless victims. Rather, like new historicism, cultural criticism views oppressed peoples as both victimized by the dominant power structure and as capable of resisting or transforming that power structure.

文化批评与文学

Cultural criticism and literature

对于文化批评家而言，文学文本或任何其他类型的文化产品，其文化功能取决于它对读者文化体验的塑造程度，也就是说，取决于它对我们作为文化群体成员的体验的塑造程度。斯蒂芬·格林布拉特（Stephen Greenblatt）的著作对20世纪80年代新历史主义和文化批评的发展起到了至关重要的作用。他认为，以下问题可以帮助我们开始考察文学文本所发挥的文化功能：

For cultural critics, a literary text, or any other kind of cultural production, performs cultural work to the extent to which it shapes the cultural experience of those who encounter it, that is, to the extent to which it shapes our experience as members of a cultural group. According to Stephen Greenblatt, whose work is primarily responsible for the development of new historicism and cultural criticism during the 1980s, the following questions can help us begin to examine the kinds of cultural work performed by a literary text:

1这项工作似乎在推崇哪些行为模式和实践模式？

1 What kinds of behavior, what models of practice, does this work seem to enforce?

2为什么特定时间和地点的读者会觉得这部作品引人入胜？

2 Why might readers at a particular time and place find this work compelling?

3我的价值观与我正在阅读的作品中隐含的价值观是否存在差异？

3 Are there differences between my values and the values implicit in the work I am reading?

4这项工作依赖于哪些社会认知？

4 Upon what social understandings does the work depend?

5这部作品可能会以某种方式（无论是隐性的还是显性的）限制哪些人的思想或行动自由？

5 Whose freedom of thought or movement might be constrained implicitly or explicitly by this work?

6这些特定的赞扬或谴责行为（即文本表面上的伦理倾向）可能与哪些更大的社会结构相关联？（226）

6 What are the larger social structures with which these particular acts of praise or blame (that is, the text’s apparent ethical orientation) might be connected? (226)

用格林布拉特的话来说，文化分析似乎“服务于文学研究，但在广义的博雅教育中，文学研究才是服务于文化理解的”（227）。因此，以上所有问题都要求我们建立文学文本、其产生的文化以及其被解读的文化之间的联系。

In Greenblatt’s words, it might “appear that the analysis of culture is the servant of literary study, but in a liberal education broadly conceived it is literary study that is the servant of cultural understanding” (227). Thus, all of the above questions ask us to make connections between the literary text, the culture in which it emerged, and the cultures in which it is interpreted.

或许此时探讨文化批评在文学作品中的一些具体应用会有所帮助。我们先来描述一下什么是文化批评家。或许可以借鉴约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》和托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》这两部作品，我们之前曾用它们来阐释传统历史文学研究方法和新历史文学研究方法之间的差异。正如我之前提到的，许多新历史文学解读都可以被视为广义上的文化批评。因此，之前讨论的所有对康拉德和莫里森小说的新历史文学解读，只要它们考察了文学文本所发挥的文化功能，都可以被视为文化批评的范例。

Perhaps it would help at this point to consider some specific applications of cultural criticism to literary works. Let’s start by describing what a cultural critic might do with Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness and Toni Morrison’s Beloved, the two texts we used earlier to illustrate the differences between traditional and new historical approaches to literature. As I mentioned before, many new historical readings could be considered forms of cultural criticism, broadly conceived. So all of the examples of new historical interpretations of Conrad’s and Morrison’s novels discussed earlier could be considered examples of cultural criticism to the extent that these interpretations examine the kind of cultural work performed by the literary text.

然而，让我们来看看，究竟哪些解读方式能够将对《黑暗之心》和《宠儿》的文化批判与对这些作品的新历史诠释区分开来。鉴于这两部小说都已被奉为“高雅”文化经典，狭义上的文化批评家或许会选择分析这些小说的流行版本，而不仅仅是小说本身。例如，文化批评家可能会研究弗朗西斯·福特·科波拉执导的《现代启示录》（1978），众所周知，这部电影改编自康拉德的小说；或者研究由约翰·马尔科维奇主演的电视电影版《黑暗之心》（1993）。同样，文化批评家也可能会考察由奥普拉·温弗瑞主演的电影版《宠儿》（1998），或者未来可能根据莫里森的小说改编的电视迷你剧。

Let’s look, however, at what kinds of readings might distinguish cultural critiques of Heart of Darkness and Beloved from new historical interpretations of these works. Given that both novels have been canonized as works of “high” culture, a cultural critic, in the narrower sense of the term, might choose to analyze popular representations of these novels, rather than just the novels themselves. For example, a cultural critic might study Francis Ford Coppola’s Apocalypse Now (1978), which, as most film fans know, is based on Conrad’s novel, or the made-for-television version of Heart of Darkness starring John Malkovich (1993). Similarly, a cultural critic might examine the film version of Beloved starring Oprah Winfrey (1998) or a television miniseries that might someday be produced based on Morrison’s novel.

在分析这些经典作品的流行版本时，文化批评家可能会试图探究流行版本是如何传递和/或转化原著的意识形态内容的。例如，电影版本是否比小说展现了更为阴暗的人性？或者，电影是否提供了小说所没有的更为乐观的人性视角？电影对种族、阶级、性别、性取向或其他文化现象的呈现，与小说中的呈现有何异同？电影版本如何处理叙事上的歧义，例如《黑暗之心》中马洛的可靠性，或是《宠儿》中婴儿鬼魂的意义？最重要的是，电影版本与小说之间的差异（如果有的话）揭示了大众想象的哪些方面——即观众的心理欲望和意识形态假设——或者娱乐产业对观众的认知？这种对比又揭示了电影的目标受众与小说的目标受众在意识形态上的哪些差异？

In analyzing these popular forms of canonized works, a cultural critic might try to determine the ways in which the popular versions transmit and/or transform the ideological content of the novels. For example, does the film version seem to have a darker vision of human nature than the novel? Or, in contrast, does the film provide a more optimistic view of the human condition that the novel does not offer? How does the film’s representation of race, class, gender, sexual orientation, or any other cultural phenomenon resemble or differ from the novel’s representation thereof? How does the film version handle narrative ambiguities, such as Marlow’s reliability in Heart of Darkness or the meaning of the baby ghost in Beloved? Most important, what do the differences, if any, between the film version and the novel suggest about the popular imagination – that is, about the psychological desires and ideological assumptions of the viewing public – or about the entertainment industry’s conception of the viewing public? And what does this contrast suggest about the ideological differences between the public for whom the film was produced and the public for whom the novel was written?

文化批评家通常对那些在“高雅”文化中找不到对应版本的流行文化作品感兴趣：例如，前文提到的电视情景喜剧、流行音乐和通俗小说，以及其他流行文化作品，例如印刷品、广播和电视广告；玩具和游戏；印刷品和电视动画片；职业体育赛事；都市传说和童话故事；以及选美比赛。因为文化作品的形式可能并非字面意义上的文本，但在文化批评家看来，它总是蕴含着某种意识形态的“故事”。

Cultural critics are often interested in productions of popular culture for which there are no corresponding versions in “high” culture: for example, the television situation comedies, popular music, and pulp fiction mentioned earlier, as well as such productions of pop culture as, for instance, print, radio, and television advertisements; toys and games; print and television cartoons; professional sports; urban legends and fairy tales; and beauty contests. For a cultural production may or may not take the form of a literal text, but for a cultural critic it always has some sort of ideological “story” to tell.

为了吸引尽可能多的批判理论爱好者，我们不妨以电子游戏为例。在许多游戏中，玩家都试图通过尽可能多地消灭屏幕上出现的敌人来积累财富或社会地位。以下问题或许有助于我们探究这类游戏所发挥的文化作用——即它们所传播或转化的意识形态。为什么积累巨额财富和获得高社会地位会成为如此强大的激励？为什么与其他玩家的竞争往往是游戏的重要组成部分？敌人的外貌如何？他们的体貌特征或服饰是否让他们看起来不像人类？玩家需要具备哪些传统的男性和/或女性特质才能成功通关？在游戏创造的世界中，哪些传统的男性和/或女性特质似乎受到推崇？哪些个人特质被贬低或显得无关紧要？游戏中是否存在女性角色？她们的外貌如何？她们的穿着打扮又是怎样的？他们表现出哪些行为？男性和女性形象与异性形象之间有何关系？他们与同性形象之间又有何关系？

To appeal to the greatest possible number of critical-theory enthusiasts, let’s take for our example video games. In one format common to many games, players try to accumulate some form of wealth or social rank by destroying as many as possible of the enemy figures that appear on the screen. Questions like the following might help us discover the cultural work being done – that is, the ideologies being transmitted or transformed – by such games. Why are the accumulation of great wealth and the acquisition of high social rank such motivating rewards? Why is competition against other players often an important part of the game? What do the enemy figures look like? Do their physical features or apparel make them look less than or other than human? What traditional masculine and/or feminine qualities does a player need in order to play the game successfully? What traditional masculine and/or feminine qualities seem to be valued in the world created by the game? What personal qualities are devalued or seem to be irrelevant? Are female figures present in the game? What do they look like, and how are they dressed? What kinds of behavior do they exhibit? How do male and female figures relate to figures of the opposite sex? How do they relate to figures of the same sex?

对文化批评不感兴趣的人可能会这样回答这些问题：“将敌人非人化、渴望积累巨额财富和获得高社会地位、享受竞争，这些都是人之常情。”或者“在某种形式的格斗游戏中，推崇传统的男性特质是很自然的。”然而，如果你对文化批评感兴趣，你就会想要探究一款电子游戏所构建的世界观价值观，与支撑这款游戏的文化价值观之间可能存在的联系。例如，游戏中对财富和地位竞争的高度重视是如何强化资本主义意识形态的？这款游戏中男性气质和/或女性气质是如何定义的？这些定义与游戏创作和游玩文化中普遍存在的性别定义（尤其是掌握权力的性别定义）是否一致？问题的关键不在于我们是否玩某种特定类型的电子游戏，也不在于我们是否赞成或反对某种特定类型的电子游戏。而在于我们是否有能力注意到并解读我们每天从电子游戏以及其他各种流行娱乐和信息渠道接收到的信息。这些渠道已经成为我们文化中不可或缺的一部分，以至于我们可能根本不会去深思熟虑。

People who are not interested in cultural criticism probably would respond to these questions by saying, “It’s human nature to dehumanize our enemies, to be strongly motivated by the prospect of accumulating great wealth and acquiring high social rank, and to enjoy competition” or “It’s natural for traditional masculine traits to be valorized in a game that is, in one form or another, a game of physical combat.” If you are interested in cultural criticism, however, you will want to examine what connections might exist between the values governing the world created in a given video game and the values supporting the culture that creates and plays that game. For example, how does the high value placed on competition for the acquisition of some form of wealth and status reinforce capitalist ideologies? How are masculinity and/or femininity defined in this game, and how are those definitions in keeping or not in keeping with the gender definitions in circulation – and, especially, in power – in the culture that creates and plays that game? The issue here isn’t whether or not we play any particular kind of video game or whether we approve or disapprove of any particular kind of video game. Rather, the issue here is our ability to notice and interpret the messages we receive every day from video games and from all the other modes of popular entertainment and information that are so much a part of our culture that we may not give them a second thought.2

文化批评家也倾向于考虑文化作品的感知或使用方式可能与创作者的预期不符的情况。例如，正如约翰·菲斯克所观察到的：

A cultural critic would also be inclined to take into account the ways in which a cultural production might not be perceived or used the way those who produced it intended it to be perceived or used. For example, as John Fiske observes,

无家可归的美国原住民……选择在收容所里用录像机观看老西部片，但他们只看了前半部分，然后就关掉了录像机。在电影中，当篷车队遭到成功袭击、堡垒被攻克时，原住民选择不去关注白人帝国的复兴。在澳大利亚观看《第一滴血》系列电影的原住民，选择忽略自由的西方与共产主义的东方之间的冲突，而是将注意力集中在兰博（他们通过一些外貌和行为特征，将他视为与他们一样的第三世界成员）与系统性地、错误地低估他能力的白人军官阶层之间的冲突上。

[h]omeless Native Americans … chose to watch old westerns on the VCR in their shelter, but they selected only the first half of them, and switched off the movie at the point when the wagon train had been successfully attacked, the fort captured – they chose not to watch the reassertion of white empire. Aboriginal people watching the Rambo movies in Australia chose to ignore the conflict between the free west and the communist east and focused instead on the conflict between Rambo, whom they saw, by a selection of physical and behavioral characteristics, as a member of the third world like them, and the white officer class that systematically and mistakenly underestimated his abilities.

（327）

(327)

因此，无论是研究流行文化、“高雅”文化，还是两者兼而有之，文化批评家都试图描绘出特定文化产品在受众手中所发挥的不断变化的意识形态功能。

So whether examining popular culture, “high” culture, or both, cultural critics try to map the changing ideological functions that a given cultural production performs at the hands of those who respond to it.

新历史文化批评家们就文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions new historical and cultural critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在概括新历史主义者和文化批评家所采用的文学分析方法。用文化批评的术语来说，这些问题为我们提供了考察文学文本所发挥的文化作用的途径。在阅读这些问题并设想新历史主义者或文化批评家可能如何回应它们时，请记住，对于这类批评家而言，任何历史事件、文物或意识形态都无法脱离其所处的无数历史事件、文物和意识形态而得到完全理解，而我们自身的文化经验也必然会影响我们的认知，从而使真正的客观性成为不可能。因为只有当我们清楚地认识到我们的分析永远是不完整的、片面的，我们的视角永远是主观的，我们才能恰当地运用新历史主义和新文化批评。我们无法置身于自身文化之外，以客观的视角分析文本。我们只能在自身所处的历史语境中进行写作。

The following questions are intended to summarize approaches to literary analysis employed by new historicists and cultural critics. In the terminology of cultural criticism, these questions offer us ways to examine the cultural work performed by literary texts. As you read these questions and imagine the ways in which a new historical or cultural critic might address them, keep in mind that, for such critics, no historical event, artifact, or ideology can be completely understood in isolation from the innumerable historical events, artifacts, and ideologies among which it circulates, and our own cultural experience inevitably influences our perceptions, making true objectivity impossible. For we can use new historical and cultural criticism properly only if we keep clearly in mind that our analysis is always incomplete, partial, and our perspective is always subjective. We can’t stand outside our own culture and analyze texts from an objective vantage point. We can write only from within our own historical moment.

1文学文本如何与同一时期的其他历史文化文本（例如刑法典、生育习俗、教育重点、法律对儿童的待遇、其他艺术形式（包括大众艺术形式）、性观念等）构成一个连续体？也就是说，作为对特定历史时期特定文化的“深度描述”的一部分，这部文学作品对我们理解特定时空下的人类经验有何贡献？这其中又包含哪些关于个人身份如何塑造文化制度以及如何被文化制度塑造的内容？

1 How does the literary text function as part of a continuum with other historical and cultural texts from the same period, for example, penal codes, birthing practices, educational priorities, the treatment of children under the law, other art forms (including popular art forms), attitudes toward sexuality, and the like? That is, taken as part of a “thick description” of a given culture at a given point in history, what does this literary work add to our tentative understanding of human experience in that particular time and place, including the ways in which individual identity shapes and is shaped by cultural institutions?

2我们如何利用一部文学作品来“描绘”该作品诞生的文化背景下，传统话语与颠覆性话语之间相互作用的图景？以及/或者作品被解读的文化？换句话说，文本是如何宣扬那些支持和/或削弱其创作和/或解读时期当地盛行的权力结构的意识形态的？

2 How can we use a literary work to “map” the interplay of both traditional and subversive discourses circulating in the culture in which that work emerged and/or the cultures in which the work has been interpreted? Put another way, how does the text promote ideologies that support and/or undermine the prevailing power structures of the time and place in which it was written and/or interpreted?

3运用修辞分析（分析文本的目的以及它试图实现该目的的风格手段），文学文本对我们理解文学和非文学话语（如政治、科学、经济和教育理论）在特定历史时期相互影响、重叠和竞争的方式有何贡献？

3 Using rhetorical analysis (analysis of a text’s purpose and the stylistic means by which it tries to achieve that purpose), what does the literary text add to our understanding of the ways in which literary and nonliterary discourses (such as political, scientific, economic, and educational theories) have influenced, overlapped with, and competed with one another at specific historical moments?

4这部文学作品对那些被传统历史忽视、代表性不足或歪曲的群体（例如，劳工、囚犯、妇女、有色人种、女同性恋和男同性恋、儿童、精神病患者等等）的经历有何启示？需要注意的是，新历史和文化批评通常会关注文学作品与其产生文化和/或解读文化中盛行的非文学话语的交汇点，并常常聚焦于权力流通以及个人和群体身份的动态变化等问题。

4 What does the literary work suggest about the experience of groups of people who have been ignored, underrepresented, or misrepresented by traditional history (for example, laborers, prisoners, women, people of color, lesbians and gay men, children, the insane, and so on)? Keep in mind that new historical and cultural criticism usually include attention to the intersection of the literary work with nonliterary discourses prevalent in the culture in which the work emerged and/or in the cultures in which it has been interpreted and often focus on such issues as the circulation of power and the dynamics of personal and group identity.

5这部作品在文学评论界和读者群体中的接受情况（包括其诞生地的接受情况、随着时间的推移对作品的不同反应以及它与读者未来可能的关系）是如何受到接受该作品的文化环境的影响，以及反过来又是如何塑造接受该作品的文化环境的？

5 How has the work’s reception by literary critics and the reading public – including the reception at its point of origin, changing responses to the work over time, and its possible future relationship with its audience – been shaped by and shaped the culture in which that reception occurred?

根据所讨论的文学文本，我们可以提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们可能会提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们像新历史主义和新文化批评家那样思考文学文本的一些起点。请记住，即使关注相同的理论概念并拥有相同的目的，并非所有新历史主义或新文化批评家都会以相同的方式解读同一作品。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。我们的目标是运用新历史主义和文化批评来丰富我们对文学的阅读，帮助我们理解文学文本如何参与话语的流通，如何塑造并受其产生和被解读的文化的影响；帮助我们理解话语的流通如何成为政治/社会/知识/经济权力的流通；以及帮助我​​们理解我们自身的文化定位如何影响我们对文学和非文学文本的解读。

Depending on the literary text in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us thinking about literary texts as new historical and cultural critics do. Keep in mind that not all new historical or cultural critics will interpret the same work in the same way even if they focus on the same theoretical concepts and have the same purpose. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use new historicism and cultural criticism to help enrich our reading of literature by helping us see how literary texts participate in the circulation of discourses, shaping and shaped by the culture in which they emerge and by the cultures in which they are interpreted; by helping us see the ways in which the circulation of discourses is the circulation of political/social/intellectual/economic power; and by helping us see the ways in which our own cultural positioning influences our interpretations of literary and nonliterary texts.

以下对菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的解读，旨在展示一种新的历史解读方式可能带来的成果。用文化批评的术语来说，它分析了这部小说所发挥的文化作用。然而，我之所以称我对菲茨杰拉德小说的解读为一种新的历史解读，是因为它并不像通常与历史解读相关的那种公开的政治议程。文化批评，以及我大量运用新历史主义相关术语，都使我的解读更具文化性。然而，这两个领域之间存在诸多重叠之处，因此我的解读完全可以称得上是一种文化分析，尤其因为我的论证并未区分菲茨杰拉德被奉为经典的“作品”与受同一意识形态影响的各种流行文化形式。
