The following reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a new historical interpretation of that novel might yield. In the terminology of cultural criticism, it analyzes the cultural work performed by the novel. I call my interpretation of Fitzgerald’s novel a new historical reading, however, because it doesn’t have the kind of overt political agenda often associated with cultural criticism and because I rely rather heavily on terminology associated with new historicism. However, the overlap between the two fields is such that my interpretation could also be called, quite legitimately, a cultural analysis, especially because my argument makes no distinction between Fitzgerald’s canonized “classic” and various forms of popular culture informed by the same ideology.

具体而言，我认为这部小说传播了其创作时期的一种主流话语：白手起家论。这种话语认为，任何一个美国贫苦男孩，只要具备合适的个人素质，就能跻身金融界的顶峰。此外，我还探讨了《了不起的盖茨比》如何体现了白手起家论的核心矛盾之一：尽管这种话语声称向所有拥有“成就一番事业”所需的雄心壮志和毅力的人敞开了美国历史的大门，但其内部却充斥着一种“逃避”历史、超越时间、地点和人类局限的历史现实的渴望。

Specifically, I argue that the novel circulates one of the dominant discourses of the period in which it was written: the discourse of the self-made man, which held that any poor boy in America, if he had the right personal qualities, could rise to the top of the financial world. In addition, I examine the ways in which The Great Gatsby embodies one of the central contradictions of the discourse of the self-made man: although this discourse claims to open the annals of American history to all those who have the ambition and perseverance required to “make their mark,” the discourse is permeated by the desire to “escape” history, to transcend the historical realities of time, place, and human limitation.

白手起家者的论述：对《了不起的盖茨比》的全新历史解读

The discourse of the self-made man: a new historical reading of The Great Gatsby

F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）出版于美国经济史上最辉煌的时期之一。从1865年内战结束到1929年股市崩盘，随着美国疆域扩张和工业发展，无数人积累了巨额财富。约翰·D·洛克菲勒、杰伊·古尔德、吉姆·菲斯克、安德鲁·卡内基、J·P·摩根、菲利普·阿莫尔和詹姆斯·J·希尔等百万富翁的成功故事，几乎人尽皆知。就连盖茨比的父亲——一个不识字、生活拮据的农民——也对这些故事耳熟能详。他谈到儿子时说：“如果他活下来，他一定会成为一个伟大的人。像詹姆斯·J·希尔那样的人。他会为国家的建设做出贡献。”（176页；第九章）除了出身富裕银行家家庭的摩根大通之外，所有这些百万富翁都是白手起家：他们从极其卑微的出身一路攀升至金融界的顶峰。当时人们普遍认为，任何一个具备相应个人素质的美国穷小子都能做到这一点。

F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925) was published during one of America’s greatest periods of economic growth. As the nation expanded its borders and developed its industries between the end of the Civil War in 1865 and the stockmarket crash in 1929, many private fortunes were made. Everyone in America knew the success stories of millionaires like John D. Rockefeller, Jay Gould, Jim Fisk, Andrew Carnegie, J. P. Morgan, Philip Armour, and James J. Hill. Even Gatsby’s father, an uneducated and unsuccessful farmer, is aware of these stories. He says of his son, “If he’d of lived he’d of been a great man. A man like James J. Hill. He’d of helped build up the country” (176; ch. 9). With the exception of J. P. Morgan, the son of a wealthy banker, all of these millionaires were self-made men: from very humble beginnings they rose to their position at the top of the financial world. And popular belief held that any poor boy in America with the right personal qualities could do the same.

因此，当时的主流话语是白手起家者的话语，这种话语在当时的“成功手册”、白手起家的百万富翁撰写的自我提升演讲和文章、霍雷肖·阿尔杰的小说、在全国范围内用于教幼儿阅读的麦格菲读本以及著名白手起家者的传记中都有所体现。我认为，菲茨杰拉德的小说至少在两个重要方面参与了这种话语的传播。它反映了这种话语的主要信条，而且我认为，它体现了这种话语的一个核心矛盾：白手起家者的话语一方面声称要向所有拥有“留下印记”所需的雄心壮志和毅力的人敞开美国历史的大门，另一方面却又……充满了“逃离”历史、超越时间、地点和人类局限性的历史现实的渴望。

Thus, a dominant discourse of the period was the discourse of the self-made man, which circulated in the “success manuals” of the period; in the self-improvement speeches and essays composed by the self-made millionaires of that era; in the Horatio Alger novels; in the McGuffey Readers, which were used throughout the nation to teach young children to read; and in the biographies of famous self-made men. Fitzgerald’s novel participates in the circulation of this discourse, I think, in at least two significant ways. It reflects the major tenets of the discourse and, I would argue, it embodies one of its central contradictions: the discourse of the self-made man, while it claims to open the annals of American history to all those who have the ambition and perseverance required to “make their mark,” is permeated by the desire to “escape” history and to transcend the historical realities of time, place, and human limitation.

让我们首先探讨《了不起的盖茨比》如何体现了白手起家论的主要原则。读者们常常会注意到盖茨比童年时期的“日程安排”——他将一天的时间用于体育锻炼、学习电学、工作、运动、练习演讲和仪态举止，以及研究必要的发明——与美国白手起家的先驱本杰明·富兰克林自传中的自我提升理念有着相似之处。显然，盖茨比希望，甚至计划，过上与当时那些白手起家的百万富翁们一样的“白手起家”的生活。然而，盖茨比这个人物形象对自我提升传统的借鉴程度，可能比一些今天的读者所意识到的要深远得多。

Let’s begin by examining the ways in which The Great Gatsby reflects the major tenets of the discourse of the self-made man. Of course, readers frequently notice the similarities between Gatsby’s boyhood “schedule” – in which the young man divided his day among physical exercise, the study of electricity, work, sports, the practice of elocution and poise, and the study of needed inventions – and the self-improvement ideology found in the autobiography of Benjamin Franklin, America’s original self-made man. Obviously, Gatsby hoped, indeed planned, to live the “rags-to-riches” life associated with the self-made millionaires of his day. However, the characterization of Gatsby draws on the self-improvement tradition more thoroughly than some readers today may realize.

在盖茨比生活的年代（1890-1922年）——大致与小说诞生的历史时期相同，因为菲茨杰拉德生于1896年，《了不起的盖茨比》出版于1925年——盛行着一类讲述穷小子如何致富的书籍，被称为“成功指南”。奥斯汀·比尔鲍尔的《如何成功》（1900年）是此类书籍的代表作，书中给未来的白手起家者提出了以下建议：努力工作，目标明确，抓住机遇，切勿拖延，坚持不懈，保持良好的身体状态，远离酒精。比尔鲍尔指出，穷小子比富家子弟更有优势，因为他们从小就接触到艰苦的工作，并且受到经济需求的驱使而努力奋斗。与此相反，作者指出，许多富裕的年轻人却逃避辛勤工作，转而追求诸如时尚和礼仪等无关紧要的目标，结果有时甚至无法增加或保住他们继承的财富。类似出版物中推崇的美德还包括储蓄的重要性，以及避免吸烟、说俚语、结交损友等懒惰行为。简而言之，这些出版物建议年轻男性避免任何浪费时间、浪费金钱或损害健康或名誉的行为。

During the period in which Gatsby lived (1890–1922) – roughly the same historical period from which the novel emerged, for Fitzgerald was born in 1896 and The Great Gatsby was published in 1925 – books that explained how poor boys could rise to heights of great wealth, called “success manuals,” flourished. In Austin Bierbower’s How to Succeed (1900), a representative example of the genre, the following advice is given to the prospective self-made man: work hard, have a clear purpose, be prepared for opportunity, don’t procrastinate, persevere, keep in good physical condition, and avoid drink. Poor boys have an advantage over rich boys, Bierbower notes, because they are introduced to hard work at a young age and motivated by financial need to apply themselves. In contrast, many wealthy youth, the author points out, avoid hard work and focus instead on insubstantial goals like fashion and etiquette, thereby sometimes failing to increase or even maintain the fortunes they inherited. The virtues extolled in similar publications include, in addition, the importance of saving money and of avoiding such slothful behaviors as smoking, using slang, and keeping bad company. In short, rising young men were advised to avoid any behavior that wasted time, cost money, or was injurious to health or reputation.

帮助父母也被认为是培养男孩勤奋和主动等品质的好方法，这些品质对他日后的人生大有裨益。出于类似的原因，人们普遍认为，在农村，最好是在农场长大，比在城市里度过童年要好得多。3

Making himself useful to his parents was also considered a good way for a young boy to develop the traits of industry and initiative, which would serve him well later in life. And for similar reasons, it was generally accepted that a rural upbringing, preferably on a farm, was superior to a boyhood spent in the city.3

杰伊·盖茨比在很多方面都符合这种形象。他出生于贫困的“农户家庭”（104；第6章），并在明尼苏达州的乡村度过了他的青少年时期。在他那本《霍帕隆·卡西迪》中，紧挨着他那份颇具富兰克林风格的每日活动安排表的童年“总体目标清单”，读起来就像一本迷你成功指南：

Jay Gatsby fits this profile in a number of ways. He was born to poor “farm people” (104; ch. 6) and spent his youth in rural Minnesota. His boyhood list of “General Resolves,” found in his copy of Hopalong Cassidy just below his Franklinesque daily schedule of activities, reads like a mini-success manual:

不要在沙夫特斯或[一个无法辨认的名字]浪费时间

No wasting time at Shafters or [a name, indecipherable]

不再吸烟或嚼烟

No more smokeing or chewing

隔天洗澡

Bath every other day

每周阅读一本提升自我的书籍或杂志

Read one improving book or magazine per week

每周节省 5.00 美元 [已划掉] 3.00 美元

Save $5.00 [crossed out] $3.00 per week

对父母好一点

Be better to parents

（181-82；第9章）

(181–82; ch. 9)

盖茨比的体魄强健，这是书中经常提及的自我提升美德，尼克对他的描述便可见一斑：“他身手敏捷地在汽车仪表盘上保持平衡，这种身手极具美国特色——带着……我们那种神经质、零散的游戏般的无形优雅”（68；第四章）。盖茨比“精心雕琢的正式言辞”，让尼克觉得他“斟酌字句”（53；第三章），这体现了避免使用俚语的自我提升美德。此外，盖茨比严格戒酒，即使在自己的派对上也不例外，这也体现了成功学手册中推荐的另一项行为。

Gatsby’s physical fitness, a frequently mentioned self-improvement virtue, is evident in Nick’s description of his “balancing himself on the dashboard of his car with that resourcefulness of movement that is so peculiarly American – that comes … with the formless grace of our nervous, sporadic games” (68; ch. 4). Gatsby’s “elaborate formality of speech,” which gives Nick the impression that he is “picking his words with care” (53; ch. 3), illustrates the self-improvement virtue of avoiding slang, and we see another behavior recommended by success manuals in Gatsby’s strict avoidance of alcohol, even at his own parties.

与汤姆·布坎南和尼克·卡拉威不同，盖茨比的奋斗动力源于经济上的需要：他在沃尔夫希姆公司的前三年就积累了巨额财富。盖茨比卓越的战功也使他被视为一个注定要在世上出人头地的年轻人，而尼克的军旅生涯却显得平淡无奇，至于汤姆的经历，我们则完全没有听到任何提及。事实上，汤姆和尼克的性格塑造恰恰印证了自我提升传统中的一条格言：继承的财富反而会成为自我提升的绊脚石。汤姆终其一生都在挥霍继承的财富，而尼克虽然已经30岁，却仍然依靠父亲的资助学习债券业务，他感到自己的人生没有明确的方向。最后，乔治·威尔逊未能养活自己和妻子的悲惨境遇，也隐晦地警示着那些不像盖茨比那样拥有“白手起家”的毅力和动力的穷人，他们的命运将会如何。

Unlike Tom Buchanan and Nick Carraway, Gatsby was motivated by the financial need to apply himself: he made his fortune during his first three years with Wolfsheim. Even Gatsby’s outstanding war record marked him as a young man certain to get ahead in the world, while Nick’s military experience seems singularly undistinguished, and we hear no mention of Tom’s at all. Indeed, the characterization of Tom and Nick exemplify the dictum of the self-improvement tradition that inherited wealth is a handicap to self-improvement: Tom does nothing with his life but find more and more extravagant ways to spend his inherited fortune, while Nick, 30 years old and still being supported by his father while he learns the bond business, feels he has no clear direction in life. Finally, George Wilson’s rather pathetic failure to adequately support himself and his wife serves as an implicit warning about the fate of poor men who, unlike Gatsby, lack the fortitude and drive to “pull themselves up by their bootstraps.”

在许多白手起家的百万富翁的演讲和文章中，我们都能看到类似的成功理念，安德鲁·卡内基就经常在文章中揭示他们的成功秘诀。例如，在《通往商业成功之路》（1885年）中，卡内基告诫那些渴望白手起家的人要志存高远、勤俭节约、远离酒精。卡内基指出，要想在商界出人头地，年轻人必须能够独立思考：“历史上没有哪个伟大的人物不曾打破常规，为自己制定新的规则”（8）。在《如何赢得财富》（1890年）中，卡内基认为，鉴于商界的竞争本质，对于那些渴望白手起家的人来说，即使能够通过某种方式完成学业，浪费宝贵的时间接受大学教育也是不明智的，因为在大学里花费的时间会让他落后于那些很早就拜师学艺的年轻人。卡内基说，“大学教育似乎对白手起家者的成功几乎是致命的”（91）。

We see the same kind of success ideology at work in the speeches and essays in which many self-made millionaires revealed the secrets of their success, as Andrew Carnegie often did. In “The Road to Business Success” (1885), for example, Carnegie tells the would-be self-made man to aim high, save his money, and avoid liquor. To rise in the business world, Carnegie notes, a young man must be able to think for himself: “There never was a great character who did not sometimes smash the routine regulations and make new ones for himself” (8). In “How to Win Fortune” (1890), Carnegie argues that, given the competitive nature of the business world, it is unwise for the prospective self-made man to waste precious time acquiring a college education, even if he were able to somehow work his way through, because the time he spends in college will put him behind the young man who apprentices himself to a captain of industry at an early age. A “college education,” Carnegie says, “seems almost fatal to [the] success” (91) of the self-made man.

正如我们前面所看到的，盖茨比即使在青少年时期就相信储蓄的重要性，并且“他很早就养成了远离酒精的习惯”（107；第6章）。生活亦是如此。与都毕业于耶鲁大学的汤姆和尼克不同，盖茨比拒绝浪费时间上大学：出于“对未来荣耀的本能”，他在“圣奥拉夫学院这所小型路德教会学院”待了两周后便退学了（105；第六章）。然而，卡内基的建议与盖茨比的行为之间最有趣的相似之处或许在于，盖茨比始终追求卓越，并“打破常规”，以便“为自己制定新的规则”（卡内基，《路》8）。盖茨比迅速赢得了丹·科迪的赏识，科迪“越来越信任他”（106；第六章），正如他在第一次世界大战期间迅速晋升为陆军少校一样，也正如他在迈耶·沃尔夫希姆公司迅速晋升一样。我们初次见到盖茨比时，他显然已身居要职，要么在沃尔夫希姆的组织中，要么在他自己的组织里：他随时都会接到来自全国各地的电话，在电话里他做出决策，并向下属下达命令。虽然卡内基肯定不希望他的建议被如此解读，但盖茨比对常规规章制度的漠视在他选择犯罪生涯中显而易见：他靠经营私酒生意和出售假债券发家致富。

As we saw above, Gatsby believed, even as a teenager, in the importance of saving money, and “he formed the habit of letting liquor alone” (107; ch. 6) early in life as well. In contrast to Tom and Nick, who both graduated from Yale, Gatsby refused to waste time attending college: led by an “instinct toward his future glory,” he quit after two weeks at “the small Lutheran college of St. Olaf” (105; ch. 6). Perhaps the most interesting similarity between Carnegie’s advice and Gatsby’s behavior, however, is seen in Gatsby’s consistent tendency to aim high and “smash the routine regulations” in order to “make new ones for himself” (Carnegie, “The Road” 8). Gatsby rose quickly in the esteem of Dan Cody, who “repos[ed] more and more trust in [him]” (106; ch. 6), just as he rose quickly to the rank of army major during World War I, just as he rose quickly in the organization of Meyer Wolfsheim. By the time we meet him, Gatsby clearly occupies an executive position, either in Wolfsheim’s organization or in one of his own: he receives phone calls, at all hours and from various parts of the country, during which he makes decisions and gives orders to his underlings. And though Carnegie certainly didn’t intend his advice to be taken in quite this way, Gatsby’s disregard for routine regulations is obvious, of course, in his choice of a criminal career: he made his fortune in the management of bootlegging operations and the sale of fraudulent bonds.

其他传播白手起家理念的文本还包括霍雷肖·阿尔杰的小说，这些小说在十九世纪末和二十世纪初风靡一时。在这些故事中，主人公总是出身贫寒的少年，他们勤劳、诚实、整洁、自立、坚韧、谦逊、善良、慷慨，而且运气极佳。在阿尔杰看来，运气意味着能够抓住机遇，这既需要想象力，也需要勇气。在阿尔杰的所有小说中，主人公都要克服重重障碍，包括一个会以某种方式欺骗他的反派；故事中还有一个地位较低的英雄人物会以某种方式帮助他；此外，还有一位或多位成功且仁慈的商人，扮演着父亲般的角色。主人公的杰出品质最终总能为他带来某种程度的经济成功，因此，这些故事颂扬的正是我们在成功学手册中看到的白手起家者的美德。

Other texts that circulated the discourse of the self-made man were the novels of Horatio Alger, which were immensely popular during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. In these tales, the hero is always a poor young boy who is hardworking, honest, neat, self-reliant, persevering, modest, kind, generous, and lucky. Luck, for Alger, included being ready to seize an opportunity when it occurs, which requires both imagination and nerve. In all of Alger’s novels, the hero has obstacles to overcome, including a villain who cheats him in some way; there is a lesser hero in the story who helps him in some way; and there are one or more father figures in the form of successful, benevolent businessmen. The hero’s out-standing qualities always end up bringing him some sort of financial success, and the stories thus extol the same virtues of the self-made man we see in the success manuals.

《了不起的盖茨比》与霍雷肖·阿尔杰式的经典小说有很多共同之处。杰伊·盖茨比衣着考究、举止温和友善，这一点尼克曾多次提及，这使他与阿尔杰笔下的主人公颇为相似，即便他并不认同后者的道德准则。然而，更引人注目的是菲茨杰拉德的小说与阿尔杰小说在结构上的相似性。与阿尔杰笔下的主人公一样，盖茨比出身卑微，渴望在社会上闯出一片天地，并且当机会以丹·科迪的形式意外降临时，他拥有足够的想象力和勇气去把握它。

The Great Gatsby shares many important features with the Horatio Alger formula novel. Jay Gatsby’s well-groomed appearance and quiet amiability, which is noted several times by Nick, give him much of the same appeal as the Alger hero, even if he doesn’t share the latter’s ethics. More striking, however, is the similarity in structure between Fitzgerald’s novel and those of Alger. Like the Alger hero, Gatsby is of humble origins, willing to work hard to make his way in the world, and had more than enough imagination and nerve at his disposal when opportunity unexpectedly knocked in the form of Dan Cody:

那天下午，詹姆斯·盖茨一直在海滩上闲逛……但杰伊·盖茨比已经借了一条划艇，划到图奥洛米河边，并告诉科迪，半小时后可能会被风吹走，把他折断。

It was James Gatz who had been loafing along the beach that afternoon … but it was already Jay Gatsby who borrowed a row-boat, pulled out to the Tuolomee, and informed Cody that a wind might catch him and break him up in half an hour.

（104；第6章）

(104; ch. 6)

在为科迪工作五年并了解了世事之后，盖茨比再次像阿尔杰笔下的主人公一样，失去了他应得的报酬：科迪遗嘱中承诺留给23岁的盖茨比的“两万五千美元遗产”（107；第六章），却通过某种“针对他的法律手段”（107；第六章），落入了科迪的情妇艾拉·凯手中。从某种意义上说，盖茨比也失去了黛西·费伊，因为在第一次世界大战结束后，盖茨比仍在海外时，汤姆娶了她。然而，菲茨杰拉德笔下的主人公坚持不懈地追求财富和黛西，最终在小说结尾实现了这两个目标。最后，帮助阿尔杰英雄的次要英雄角色由尼克·卡拉威扮演，而商人父亲形象的角色则由丹·科迪扮演（正如我们上面看到的），以及迈耶·沃尔夫希姆扮演，后者在盖茨比从战争中身无分文地回来时“将他从一无所有中提拔出来”（179；第9章）。

After working for Cody for five years and learning the ways of the world, Gatsby is cheated, again like the Alger hero, of his rightful reward: “a legacy of twenty-five thousand dollars” (107; ch. 6), promised to the 23-year-old Gatsby in Cody’s will, went instead, through some “legal device that was used against him” (107; ch. 6), to Cody’s companion, Ella Kaye. Gatsby is also, in a sense, cheated out of Daisy Fay when Tom marries her while Gatsby is still overseas after World War I. Fitzgerald’s hero perseveres, however, in his pursuit both of fortune and of Daisy, and before the novel closes he attains both goals. Finally, the role of the lesser hero who helps the Alger hero in some way is played by Nick Carraway, and the role of the businessman-father figure is played by Dan Cody, as we saw above, and by Meyer Wolfsheim, who “raised him up out of nothing” (179; ch. 9) when Gatsby returned penniless from the war.

或许，传播“白手起家”理念最广泛的载体当属《麦格菲读本》（McGuffey Readers）。这是一套小学阅读教材，从19世纪中期到20世纪20年代初，它在美国教育界占据着主导地位。这套读本中的故事和诗歌颂扬的美德，与当时的成功手册所倡导的如出一辙：诚实、勤奋、善良，以及远离酒精和不良朋友。此外，与成功手册、霍雷肖·阿尔杰小说以及其他传播“白手起家”理念的文本一样，《麦格菲读本》也阐明了“成功源于良好品格”的信念。例如，一个穷小子因为好心帮助一位老人过马路而获得了一份工作，而这位老人恰好是一位企业主。又或者，一个孤儿因为抵制住了偷窃富人金表的诱惑而被富人收养。

Perhaps the most pervasive vehicles for the ideology of the self-made man were the McGuffey Readers, a series of elementary school books used to teach reading, which were a dominant force in American education from the mid-nineteenth century to the early 1920s. The stories and poems contained in the Readers extol the same virtues promoted by the success manuals of the period: honesty, hard work, kindness, and the avoidance of alcohol and bad company. In addition, like the success manuals, Horatio Alger novels, and other texts that circulated the discourse of the self-made man, the Readers illustrated the belief that success is a product of good character. For example, a poor boy receives a job because the old man he has kindly helped cross the street turns out to own his own business. Or an orphan boy is adopted by a wealthy man because he has resisted the temptation to steal the man’s gold watch.

正如我们所见，盖茨比与白手起家的英雄有很多共同之处，而麦格菲笔下的主人公们只不过是这种英雄的另一种版本。盖茨比从丹·科迪那里得到的工作，让他得以进入他一直渴望的金融成功世界，而这份工作正是他划船到科迪的游艇上警告他即将发生风暴的善举的成果，正如麦格菲笔下那些男孩的成功源于他们的良好品格一样。

As we have seen, Gatsby has many traits in common with the self-made hero, of which McGuffey’s protagonists are just another version. And the job Gatsby receives from Dan Cody, which serves as his introduction to the world of financial success to which he has always aspired, is the product of the good deed he performed in rowing out to Cody’s yacht to warn him of an impending storm, just as the success of McGuffey’s boys is a product of their good character.

最后，盖茨比的早年生活与美国最著名的白手起家百万富翁的成长岁月有着惊人的相似之处，而这些富豪的故事也正是“白手起家”这一概念广为流传的另一种方式。在《强盗大亨》（1934）一书中，马修·约瑟夫森详细描述了19世纪末期杰伊·古尔德、吉姆·菲斯克、菲利普·阿莫尔、安德鲁·卡内基、詹姆斯·希尔、约翰·洛克菲勒和杰伊·库克等白手起家百万富翁的诸多共同经历。尽管约瑟夫森对文学分析并不感兴趣，也没有将本书与《了不起的盖茨比》进行比较，但他所叙述的人物故事与杰伊·盖茨比的传记之间的相似之处实在太过显著，令人无法忽视。

Finally, there is a startling resemblance between Gatsby’s early life and the formative years of America’s most famous self-made millionaires, the oft-told stories of which were another way in which the discourse of the self-made man circulated. In The Robber Barons (1934), Matthew Josephson details many of the common experiences shared by such self-made millionaires of the late nineteenth century as Jay Gould, Jim Fisk, Philip Armour, Andrew Carnegie, James Hill, John Rockefeller, and Jay Cooke. Although Josephson is not interested in literary analysis and makes no comparisons with The Great Gatsby, the similarities between the life stories Josephson narrates and the biography of Jay Gatsby are too striking to be ignored.

约瑟夫森指出，这些年轻人大多出身贫寒，“他们很早就离开了父亲的庇护，独自流浪，自谋生路……他们展现出……”他们在少年时期就展现出狡猾和自立的迹象”（33）。尽管他们的同伴常常酗酒赌博，但这些年轻人却不沉迷其中。他们临危不惧，“暴力也无法动摇他们”（35）。事实上，他们常常在淘金热潮中或对自然资源、铁路或股票的垄断中发家致富，而这些追求不仅在经济上充满风险，在人身安全上也同样危险：财富来得快去得也快，在边疆的同伴，甚至是在华尔街被自己欺骗过的股东，都可能变成愤怒的、充满复仇之心的暴民。约瑟夫森观察到，“在物质进步的激动人心、变幻莫测的戏剧性事件中，围绕着新铁路或金矿的开发，其核心是个人财富和地位的改变”（37）。

Born into poverty, “most of these young men,” Josephson notes, “left the paternal shelter early in youth, to wander alone and make their own way. … [T]hey showed promising signs of shiftiness and self-reliance in boyhood” (33). Although their companions often drank and gambled, these young men did not. Cool under pressure, “violence [did] not shake [them]” (35). Indeed, they often made their fortunes in the rush for gold or for the monopoly of natural resources, railroad lines, or stocks, all of which pursuits were not merely financially dangerous but physically dangerous as well: as fortunes were quickly made and lost, one’s companions on the frontier, or even a group of stockholders one had defrauded on Wall Street, could turn into an angry, vengeful mob. And “[a]t the center of the stirring, shifting drama of material progress toward new railroads or gold fields,” Josephson observes, “was the notion of individual fortune and change of station” (37).

换句话说，约瑟夫森笔下的那些白手起家的人，就像杰伊·盖茨比一样，都渴望致富，摆脱出身阶级的束缚。盖茨比也像这些白手起家的人一样，十几岁就离开了家，独自闯荡，开创了自己的道路。和他们一样，他没有沾染同伴们那些有害的恶习，而是遵循着一个充满暴力的亚文化圈子的危险规则，最终获得了财富。

In other words, much like Jay Gatsby, the self-made men of whom Josephson writes were driven by a desire to become rich and rise up out of the class into which they were born. And much like these self-made men, Gatsby left his parents’ home as a teenager, wandered alone, and made his own way. Like them, he did not adopt the debilitating personal habits of his companions, and he made his fortune according to the dangerous rules of a violent subculture.

显然，《了不起的盖茨比》反映了在十九世纪末二十世纪初众多塑造美国文化并受其影响的文本中流传的“白手起家”的论述。因为意识形态并不区分“高雅”文化和“大众”文化：在诸如成功指南、儿童读物和说教式小说等实用而平凡的文本中流传的论述，也能渗透到那个时代最精妙的艺术作品之一的字里行间。

Clearly, The Great Gatsby reflects the discourse of the self-made man circulating in so many of the texts that both shaped and were shaped by American culture during the final decades of the nineteenth century and the early decades of the twentieth. For ideology does not observe boundaries between “high” and “popular” culture: a discourse circulating in such practical and mundane texts as success manuals, children’s readers, and didactic formula-novels can also saturate the pages of one of the era’s most sophisticated artistic productions.

然而，这部小说也对“白手起家”的论述进行了评述，因为它揭示了这一论述的核心矛盾之一，即它与历史的关系。尽管“白手起家”的论述声称，只要有雄心壮志和坚韧毅力，就能在美国历史上留下自己的印记，但这种论述本身却充斥着逃避历史、超越时间、地点和人类局限等历史现实的渴望。

However, the novel also serves as a comment on the discourse of the self-made man to the extent that it reveals one of its central contradictions, which concerns the relationship of that discourse to history. Although the discourse of the self-made man claims to open the annals of American history to all those who have the ambition and perseverance required to “make their mark” on its pages, the discourse is permeated by the desire to escape history, to transcend the historical realities of time, place, and human limitation.

这种矛盾出现在上述许多白手起家百万富翁的自传故事中。尽管这些白手起家的人经常谈及他们童年时期经历的残酷现实，尤其是贫困，但他们这样做仅仅是为了庆祝自己取得的成就。我认为，这种庆祝方式实际上是对历史现实的否定，因为它将他们青年时期的苦难重新定义为通往成功的序曲。回首往事，他们将童年的自己视为“未来百万富翁的训练生”，在“逆境”的磨砺中淬炼，在贫困的熔炉中淬炼。这种观念使他们看不到自己摆脱的贫困对那些未能摆脱贫困的人造成的毁灭性影响。

This contradiction appears in many of the autobiographical stories of the self-made millionaires mentioned above. Although self-made men often spoke of the harsh historical realities they experienced as children, particularly of their poverty, they did so only to celebrate how far they had come. And the form that celebration took, I would argue, constitutes a denial of historical reality because it was a way of reinventing the suffering self-made men saw in their youth as nothing but a prelude to their success. Looking back on their lives, they saw their boyhood selves as “future millionaires in training,” so to speak, being honed in the workshop of “hard knocks” and fired in the kiln of poverty. Such an ideology didn’t permit them to see the debilitating effects of the poverty they escaped on those who didn’t manage to do the same.

在美国贫困人口中，每一代人中成为百万富翁的人都相对较少。根据白手起家论调，那些未能跻身顶峰的人只能怪自己，这当然意味着贫困和贫民窟生活的恶劣影响（更不用说女性和有色人种在商业机会方面几乎无法逾越的障碍）不能成为在商界失败的借口。这种失败被定义为纯粹的品格缺陷。这就是为什么许多白手起家的百万富翁拒绝向慈善机构捐款，而将他们的慈善活动限制在捐赠图书馆、博物馆和大学上。他们认为，这些机构只能帮助那些愿意自助的人，而不会助长他们认为慈善会助长的懒惰行为。

Among the general population of America’s impoverished, relatively few, in any generation, have become millionaires. According to the discourse of the self-made man, those who didn’t rise to the top had only themselves to blame, which implies, of course, that poverty and the degrading influence of tenement life (not to mention the almost insurmountable obstacles raised against business opportunities for women and people of color) are no excuse for the failure to rise in the business world. Such failure was defined as a failure of one’s character, pure and simple. This is why many self-made millionaires refused to give money to charity, confining their philanthropy to endowing libraries, museums, and universities, which could, they reasoned, help only those who were willing to help themselves and not encourage the slothful behavior that charity would, they believed, encourage.4

例如，安德鲁·卡内基在他的自传中描述了他作为贫困移民家庭的孩子所拥有的幸福家庭生活。他提到，除了家庭的经济困境之外，他的亲戚们积极参与政治活动，他的父母非常重视教育，他的家庭环境也培养了他参与时事辩论的能力。事实上，卡内基认为，他童年时期遭受的经济贫困，被他在一个强大的家庭中获得的教育和支持所弥补。然而，他显然没有意识到，他所在社区的许多其他贫困青年——例如，那些父母不理解教育价值的孩子，或者那些父母酗酒、虐待他们的孩子——并没有他所拥有的那些优势，因此不能指望他们像他一样轻易地出人头地。也就是说，卡内基一心想强调自己如何超越历史现实，却忽略了那些无法轻易克服的历史层面。

For example, in his autobiography, Andrew Carnegie describes the happy family life he enjoyed as a child of poor immigrant parents. He notes, in addition to his family’s economic hardship, how politically active his relatives were, how education was valued by his parents, and how he was trained by his home environment to engage in rigorous debate on the issues of the day. Indeed, Carnegie observes that the economic poverty he suffered in childhood was richly compensated by the training and support he received in the bosom of a strong family. Yet he was apparently unable to realize that many other poor youngsters in his own neighborhood – for example, the sons of parents who did not understand the value of education or the sons of drunken, abusive parents – did not have the same advantages he had and therefore could not be expected to raise themselves up as readily as he did. That is, in Carnegie’s desire to focus on his own transcendence of historical reality, he ignores those aspects of history that cannot be overcome so readily.

《了不起的盖茨比》反映了盖茨比试图超越历史的渴望，他竭力否认自己的真实出身。盖茨比的“父母是游手好闲、一事无成的农民”，但“他的想象力从未真正接受过他们是自己的父母”（104页；第六章）。相反，盖茨比虚构了一个家庭、牛津大学的教育经历和一笔遗产，以此来说服自己和他人，他生来就拥有财富和社会地位。也就是说，盖茨比想要否认他一生所受制于的社会经济阶级的历史现实。正如尼克所说，“杰伊·盖茨比……源于他对自身的柏拉图式构想”（104页；第六章）。柏拉图式构想的定义是超越历史的：它存在于一个不受物质世界日常事件影响的永恒维度中。而这正是盖茨比想要生活的维度。

The Great Gatsby reflects this same desire to transcend history in Gatsby’s efforts to deny his true origins. Gatsby’s “parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people,” but “his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all” (104; ch. 6). Instead, Gatsby invented a family, an Oxford education, and an inheritance in order to convince himself and others that he was born to wealth and social position. That is, Gatsby wants to deny the historical realities of socioeconomic class to which he had been subjected all his life. As Nick puts it, “Jay Gatsby … sprang from his Platonic conception of himself” (104; ch. 6). A Platonic conception is one that, by definition, is outside history: it exists in a timeless dimension untouched by daily occurrences in the material world. And this is the dimension in which Gatsby wants to live.

盖茨比声称黛西对汤姆的爱“只是个人之爱”（160；第八章），这句话令尼克和许多读者感到困惑，但在这个语境下却合情合理。在盖茨比眼中，黛西对汤姆的爱存在于历史之中，属于个人的范畴，因此无法与她和盖茨比之间的爱情相提并论，后者存在于超越历史的永恒维度。同样，盖茨比对我们力量的信念也体现在……只有当他将自己的生活置于历史现实之外时，他对过去的种种思考才有意义。他坚信，黛西与汤姆结婚的三年时光可以通过她告诉汤姆她从未爱过他而被“抹去”，他们可以“回到路易斯维尔，在她家重新结婚——就像五年前一样”（116；第六章），从而“重蹈覆辙”。这种信念只能存在于历史之外，存在于一个过去可以被重现的地方，因为它被永恒地保存下来，永远触手可及。

Gatsby’s claim that Daisy’s love for Tom “was just personal” (160; ch. 8), a statement that confuses Nick as well as many readers, makes sense in this context. In Gatsby’s eyes, Daisy’s love for Tom exists within history, within the domain of the personal, and is thus no competition for the love she and Gatsby share, which exists in a timeless dimension beyond history. Similarly, Gatsby’s belief in our power over the past makes sense only if he conceives of his own life outside the bounds of historical reality. His conviction that the three years Daisy has spent married to Tom can be “obliterated” by her telling Tom that she never loved him, and that they can “repeat the past” by “go[ing] back to Louisville and be[ing] married from her house – just as if it were five years ago” (116; ch. 6) is a conviction one can hold only from a place outside history, a place where the past is repeatable because it is timelessly preserved, forever accessible.

白手起家论也“抹杀了历史”，它选择忽略或淡化许多著名白手起家者身上巨大的性格缺陷，同时将白手起家的成功定义为个人品格而非环境的产物。这一时期的成功指南几乎没有提供任何关于商业事务的实用建议。相反，它们的所有建议都集中在品格特质上——从职场上的诚实正直到家庭中的节俭自律——因为人们相信成功源于内心。因此，品格而非教育或商业才能被认为是白手起家者的基石。然而，一些白手起家的百万富翁身上的道德缺陷，恰恰是他们能够登上顶峰的关键因素，使他们能够冷酷无情、往往不择手段地摧毁商业对手。当然，在大量赞扬白手起家者的美德的文本中，历史现实的这一方面是缺失的；或者，在大众的想象中，它被重新塑造为一种资本主义美德：竞争力、侵略性、坚韧。

The discourse of the self-made man also “erases history” in choosing to ignore or marginalize the enormous character flaws of many famous self-made men while simultaneously defining self-made success as a product of one’s character rather than of one’s environment. The success manuals from this period offered very little, if any, practical advice about business matters. All of their advice focused, instead, on attributes of character – from honesty and integrity in the workplace to frugality and sobriety in the home – because it was believed that success comes from within the man. Therefore, character, rather than education or business acumen, was considered the foundation of the self-made man. Yet some of the moral failings of self-made millionaires were the very factors that enabled them to rise to the top by enabling them to ruthlessly and often unethically destroy their business rivals. Of course, this aspect of historical reality was absent from the proliferation of texts that extolled the virtues of the self-made man, or it was recast, in the popular imagination, as a capitalist virtue: competitiveness, aggressiveness, toughness.

在此背景下，值得注意的是，自《了不起的盖茨比》出版以来，大多数评论家对小说主人公盖茨比的评价都带有浪漫化的色彩，正如美国文化对白手起家者的浪漫化一样，他们理想化地描绘了盖茨比的成功愿望，却忽略或边缘化了他实现这一愿望的手段。一位早期评论家在1925年对盖茨比的评价，在小说的整个接受过程中，一直代表着许多读者的感受：盖茨比“充满活力……这种活力源于他拥有一个不朽的梦想，即便为了实现这个梦想，他经历了非凡的物质堕落”（EK 426）。1945年，威廉·特洛伊将盖茨比描述为“一个种族意识”的“愿望实现的投射”（21）。汤姆·伯纳姆在1952年指出，盖茨比“在周围的腐败环境中幸存下来，保持了健全完整的品格”（105）。 1954年，马里乌斯·贝利写道，盖茨比“充满抱负和善良”（25）：“他是美国浪漫英雄的化身”（14），代表着“精神抵抗的力量”和“免受庸俗和低劣最终玷污”的“免疫力”（13）。1963年，巴里·爱德华·格罗斯指出，“盖茨比的梦想本质上是‘不可腐蚀的’”，因为它“本质上是非物质的”，这也是为什么“他最终‘安然无恙’”（57）。同样，1978年，罗斯·阿德里安娜·加洛认为，盖茨比“始终保持着他的纯真”（43），或者正如安德烈·勒沃在1983年所说，盖茨比从未失去他的“根本正直，他的”“精神上的完整性”（144）。即使主人公的阴暗面被承认，也得到了宽恕。正如肯特·卡特赖特在1984年所论述的，“盖茨比既可以是罪犯，也可以是浪漫英雄，因为这本书为他创造了一个超越世俗的、具有远见的道德标准，而他的一生也印证了这一点”（232）。或者正如安德鲁·狄龙在1988年总结的那样，他认为主人公将世俗与精神融合在一起，盖茨比是“一个感性的圣人”（50）。5

It is interesting to note in this context that since the publication of The Great Gatsby, the majority of critical response to the novel’s title character has romanticized him much as American culture has romanticized the self-made man, by idealizing his desire to succeed and ignoring or marginalizing the means by which he fulfilled that desire. What an early reviewer said of Gatsby in 1925 has continued to represent the feeling of a good many readers over the course of the novel’s reception: Gatsby’s “is a vitality … the inner fire [of] which comes from living with an incorruptible dream, even if extraordinary material corruption has been practised in its realization” (E. K. 426). In 1945, William Troy describes Gatsby as the “projected wish fulfillment” of the “consciousness of a race” (21). And Tom Burnam argues in 1952 that Gatsby “survives sound and whole in character, uncorrupted by the corruption which surrounded him” (105). In 1954, Marius Bewley writes that Gatsby is “all aspiration and goodness” (25): “an heroic personification of the American romantic hero” (14), who represents “the energy of the spirit’s resistance” and “immunity to the final contamination” of “cheapness and vulgarity” (13). And Barry Edward Gross suggests in 1963 that “Gatsby’s dream is essentially ‘incorruptible’” because it “is essentially immaterial,” which is why “he turns ‘out all right at the end’” (57). Similarly, in 1978 Rose Adrienne Gallo argues that Gatsby “maintained his innocence” to the end (43), or as André Le Vot puts it in 1983, Gatsby never loses his “fundamental integrity, his spiritual intactness” (144). Even when the protagonist’s darker side is acknowledged, it is excused. As Kent Cartwright argues in 1984, “Gatsby can be both criminal and romantic hero because the book creates for him a visionary moral standard that transcends the conventional and that his life affirms” (232). Or as Andrew Dillon sums up, in 1988, what he sees as the protagonist’s merger of worldliness and spirituality, Gatsby is “a sensual saint” (50).5

最后，我们可以在《麦格菲读本》中看到白手起家论与超越历史的渴望之间的联系。在《读本》的大部分内容中，自我提升的论述明显缺乏对历史现实的参照。即使在内战结束后的时期，关于战争的诗歌和歌曲层出不穷，其中唯一一篇“历史性”的作品也并非真正意义上的历史作品：这是一首名为《蓝与灰》（1867）的感伤诗，诗中对交战双方士兵的歌颂，其描述之精妙，几乎可以适用于任何历史时期任何战争中的士兵。换句话说，这首诗创造了一个不受历史事件影响的永恒世界。正如亨利·斯蒂尔·康马杰所说，

Finally, the connection between the discourse of the self-made man and the desire to transcend history can be seen in the McGuffey Readers. In the self-improvement discourse that informs the bulk of the material in the Readers there is a striking absence of reference to historical reality. Even during the period directly after the Civil War, when poems and songs about the war abounded, the only “historical” piece included isn’t historical at all: it’s a sentimental poem called “The Blue and the Gray” (1867) in which soldiers from both sides are glorified in terms such that they could be soldiers from almost any war fought during almost any historical period. In other words, the poem creates a timeless world that remains untouched by historical events. As Henry Steele Commager puts it,

尽管《读者手册》的初版出版于人们对独立战争和1812年战争记忆犹新的年代——麦格菲本人就亲历了那场战争，而且在俄亥俄边境地区，书中也没有对英国的强烈敌意，没有对乔治三世的谴责，也没有关于印第安人暴行的记载。尽管在美墨战争、昭昭天命论和青年美国运动时期，新的《读者手册》和旧版的修订版层出不穷，但这些内容却丝毫没有反映出来：就连俄勒冈小径和加利福尼亚淘金热也未能撼动其宁静的篇章。更令人惊讶的是，后来修订《读者手册》的人……竟然成功地避开了南北战争！除了弗朗西斯·芬奇的《蓝与灰》（一部公正无私的杰作）之外，就《读者手册》而言，这场战争或许从未发生过。

[t]hough the original volumes of the Readers appeared when men could still remember the Revolutionary War and the War of 1812 – McGuffey himself lived through that war, and on the Ohio frontier, too there is no ardent hostility to Britain, no execration of George III, no atrocity story about the Indians. And though new Readers, and revisions of old Readers, poured from the presses all through the era of the Mexican War, of Manifest Destiny, and of Young America, the Readers reflect none of this: even the Oregon Trail and the gold rush to California were not allowed to ruffle the serenity of their pages. Even more startling is the fact that those who later revised the Readers … managed to avoid the Civil War! Aside from Francis Finch’s “The Blue and the Gray” – a masterpiece of impartiality – the war might never have happened, as far as the Readers are concerned.

（十三）

(xiii)

在《麦格菲读本》中，历史也因对经验的感伤化而被超越。读本中充满了对受伤动物的感伤描写，对因无私奉献而获得意外之财的善良孩童的描写，对天使般孩童安详离世的描写，以及对英雄事迹的描写。当经验以感伤的语言描绘时，它便变得普遍而非具体，如同童话故事一般“超越现实”：它们存在于某种超越日常人类事件、超越历史的永恒维度。正如斯坦利·W·林德伯格在评论麦格菲的一首战争诗时所指出的那样，它是“安全的感伤”（320），他的意思当然是指它游离于当时的政治和社会纷争之外，也就是说，它游离于历史之外。

History is also transcended in the McGuffey Readers through the sentimentalization of experience. The Readers are full of sentimental descriptions of injured animals, of virtuous children rewarded for their unselfishness by some monetary windfall, of the peaceful deaths of angelic children, and of heroic deeds. When experience is depicted in sentimental terms, that experience becomes general rather than specific, “larger than life” in the same way that fairy tales are larger than life: they exist in some timeless dimension beyond the daily course of human events, beyond history. As Stanley W. Lindberg observes about one of McGuffey’s war poems, it is “safely sentimental” (320), by which he means, of course, outside the fray of the political and social issues of the day, that is, outside history.

《麦格菲读本》中过分渲染的感伤主义与盖茨比向尼克讲述的自传体故事中“令人震惊的感伤主义”（118；第六章）有着惊人的相似之处，这种感伤主义使盖茨比的生活脱离了历史的现实，正如它使《麦格菲读本》脱离了历史的现实一样。盖茨比告诉尼克，

There is a striking similarity between the overblown sentimentality of the McGuffey Readers and the “appalling sentimentality” (118; ch. 6) of the autobiographical narrative Gatsby offers Nick, a sentimentality that removes Gatsby’s life, just as it removed the McGuffey Readers, from the realities of history. Gatsby tells Nick,

我的家人都去世了，我继承了一大笔钱。……之后，我像个年轻的王公一样在欧洲各大城市游历……收集珠宝，主要是红宝石，狩猎大型猎物，画画……并试图忘记很久以前发生在我身上的一件非常悲伤的事情。

My family all died and I came into a good deal of money. … After that I lived like a young rajah in all the capitals of Europe … collecting jewels, chiefly rubies, hunting big game, painting a little … and trying to forget something very sad that had happened to me long ago.

（70；第4章）

(70; ch. 4)

盖茨比的自传式叙述与其说是真实人生的叙述，不如说更像是维多利亚时代舞台剧的剧本大纲。正如尼克所说，“那些词句陈旧不堪，除了一个头戴头巾、浑身散发着锯末气息的‘人物’形象外，再也唤不起任何画面”（70；第四章）。然而，正是这种感伤的“人生演绎”——尼克说，他用一种“庄严”的语气讲述着，“仿佛那段记忆……仍然萦绕着他”（70）——使得盖茨比得以逃离历史现实，遁入一个“超乎寻常”的童话世界。

Gatsby’s autobiographical sketch sounds more like an outline for a staged Victorian melodrama than a narrative about an actual life. As Nick puts it, “The very phrases were worn so threadbare that they evoked no image except that of a turbaned ‘character’ leaking sawdust at every pore” (70; ch. 4). But it is this sentimental “translation” of his life – which he offers, Nick says, in a “solemn” voice, “as if the memory … still haunted him” (70) – that allows Gatsby to escape historical reality into a “larger-than-life” fairy tale.

当然，“白手起家”的说法在今天仍然具有很强的影响力。例如，在美剧《马特洛克》的一集中，一位儿子试图通过强调父亲是“白手起家”来挽回被谋杀的父亲作为冷酷无情、不择手段的商业高管的名声。因此，这句话仍然具有强大的力量，暗示着那些能够取得如此重要且受人尊敬的成就的人，不应该因为他们冷酷无情、不道德的行为而受到过于严厉的评判，因为“白手起家”需要“坚韧不拔”的品质。同样，电视系列节目《美国城堡》也大量运用了“白手起家”的说法。该节目带领观众参观美国宏伟的庄园，并讲述建造这些庄园的人们的生平故事。节目甚至不加批判地引用了19世纪和20世纪初一些白手起家的百万富翁关于自身努力和正直的自我吹嘘之词。

Of course, the discourse of the self-made man retains much of its vitality today. On an episode of the American television series Matlock, for example, a son attempts to recuperate his murdered father’s reputation as a ruthless, unethical business executive by saying that his father was a self-made man. Thus, the phrase still has the power to suggest that men capable of achieving such an important and respected goal should not be judged too harshly for their ruthless, unethical behavior because it requires “toughness” to make it as a self-made man. Similarly, the television series America’s Castles, which offers guided tours of America’s great mansions and of the lives of the men who built them, relies heavily on the discourse of the self-made man, even quoting uncritically the self-serving statements of nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century self-made millionaires concerning their own hard work and integrity.

此外，杰伊·盖茨比仍然是美国人浪漫化白手起家者的象征。罗伯特·雷德福和莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥这两位以俊朗外表著称、常被选为浪漫英雄的演员，分别在菲茨杰拉德小说改编的电影版（1974年和2013年上映）中饰演盖茨比，这揭示了西方大众对盖茨比的浪漫想象根深蒂固。事实上，在《美国城堡》的一集中，当讨论白手起家的俄克拉荷马州石油大亨E·W·马兰德时，旁白提到菲茨杰拉德认为英雄的故事总是悲剧，而此时，《了不起的盖茨比》的著名封面却被叠加在马兰德的豪宅照片上。换句话说，这部电视传记试图通过将马兰德与杰伊·盖茨比联系起来，来浪漫化马兰德。

Furthermore, Jay Gatsby remains the icon of America’s romanticization of the self-made man. That actors Robert Redford and Leonardo DiCaprio, both known for their boyish good looks and often cast as romantic heroes, were chosen to play Gatsby in the movie versions of Fitzgerald’s novel (released, respectively, in 1974 and 2013), reveals the persistence of a romantic view of Gatsby in the Western popular imagination. Indeed, during a discussion of self-made, Oklahoma oil millionaire E. W. Marland on an episode of America’s Castles, the narrator notes Fitzgerald’s belief that the story of a hero is always a tragic story while the well-known cover art of The Great Gatsby is superimposed over a photo of Marland’s mansion. In other words this television biography attempts to romanticize Marland by associating him with Jay Gatsby.

显然，《了不起的盖茨比》对白手起家者话语的复杂性和矛盾性的体现，揭示了菲茨杰拉德时代的美国人对追求财富成功的态度中所蕴含的复杂性和矛盾性。如果没有白手起家者的话语，菲茨杰拉德这部最著名的小说就不可能存在。因为杰伊·盖茨比这个人物就只不过是他所担心的那种“卑鄙的骗子”（159；第八章）——又一个罪犯而已。正是这种话语，以及他对黛西的忠贞和他孩子般的乐观，使得盖茨比成为如今我们所熟知的浪漫人物。

Clearly, The Great Gatsby’s embodiment of the complexities and contradictions of the discourse of the self-made man reveals the complexities and contradictions that informed the attitude of Fitzgerald’s America toward the achievement of financial success. Without the discourse of the self-made man, Fitzgerald’s best-known novel would not be possible. For the character of Jay Gatsby would simply be the “cheap sharper” (159; ch. 8) – just another criminal – he fears people will see in him. It is this discourse, as much as his devotion to Daisy and his boyish optimism, that makes it possible for Gatsby to remain the romantic figure he is today.

菲茨杰拉德的小说也向我们展示了话语的传播如何对我们每个人都有着非常切身的意义。因为它阐明了文化话语如何成为我们塑造个人身份的原材料。尼克·卡拉威或许认为盖茨比“源于他柏拉图式的”非历史性的“自我认知”（104；第六章），盖茨比显然也持有这种观点，但盖茨比的个人身份并非如此产生。正如我们所见，詹姆斯·盖茨塑造的杰伊·盖茨比深受“白手起家”话语的影响，而这正是他所处文化中盛行的主流话语之一。就像杰伊·盖茨比一样，我们每个人都在做着同样的事情。我们每个人都可能借鉴不同的话语，也可能以不同的方式借鉴它们，但正是通过在我们文化中传播的话语，我们的个人身份得以形成，彼此相连，并与塑造我们、同时也被我们塑造的文化紧密相连。

Fitzgerald’s novel also shows us how the circulation of discourses has very personal implications for all of us. For it illustrates the ways in which cultural discourses are the raw materials from which we fashion our individual identities. Nick Carraway may think that Gatsby “sprang from his Platonic” ahistorical “conception of himself” (104; ch. 6), a belief Gatsby clearly shares, but Gatsby’s personal identity did not so originate. As we have seen, James Gatz’s creation of Jay Gatsby drew heavily on the discourse of the self-made man, one of the dominant discourses circulating in the culture in which he lived. And like Jay Gatsby, all of us do the same. We each may draw on different discourses, and we each may draw on them in different ways, but it is through the discourses circulating in our culture that our individual identities are formed, are linked to one another, and are linked to the culture that both shapes and is shaped by each of us.

拓展练习题：对其他文学作品进行新的历史和文化批评

Questions for further practice: new historical and cultural criticism of other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用新历史文化批评来解读文中提及的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。你回答这些问题的目的、你论文的侧重点以及你自身认同的批评取向，将决定你的论文是否被视为新历史文化批评的范例。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use new historical and cultural criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or to other texts of your choice. Your purpose in addressing these questions, the way in which you focus your essay, and your own self-identified critical orientation will determine whether your essay is considered an example of new historical or cultural criticism.

1霍桑在《红字》 （1850）中对海丝特·白兰在思想和行为上违背清教徒压抑价值观的描写，与十九世纪的废奴运动和妇女运动等革命性活动之间有何关联？换句话说，海丝特·白兰（一位殖民地清教徒）的故事是如何体现和/或批判十九世纪在小册子、通俗故事、政治活动和其他文化文本中传播的这些意识形态的？

1 What is the relationship between Hawthorne’s depiction of Hester Prynne’s transgression, in thought and deed, of repressive Puritan values in The Scarlet Letter (1850) and such revolutionary nineteenth-century activities as the abolitionist movement and the women’s movement? In other words, how does the story of Hester Prynne (a colonial Puritan) embody and/or criticize these nineteenth-century ideologies as they were circulated in pamphlets, popular stories, political activities, and other cultural texts?

2托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）出版于美国保守主义意识形态（包括种族、阶级、性别和社会正义等议题）几乎在美国人生活的各个领域都受到质疑的时期。从这部小说的接受史来看，自小说出版至今，保守派和自由派就这些紧迫的社会问题展开的论述发生了怎样的变化？

2 Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) was published at a time when conservative American ideologies concerning race, class, gender, and social justice were being called into question in almost every domain of American life. What does the history of this novel’s reception suggest about the circulation of conservative and liberal discourses addressing these pressing social issues since the time of the novel’s publication to the present?

3约翰·斯坦贝克的《愤怒的葡萄》（1939）是如何受到当时关于工人权利和责任的辩论影响的，又是如何反过来影响这些辩论的？例如，关于美国企业、政府机构、工会和公民个人之间适当关系的辩论？换句话说，这部小说在出版时发挥了哪些文化作用？

3 How was John Steinbeck’s The Grapes of Wrath (1939) shaped by, and how did it shape, debates about the rights and responsibilities of workers circulating at the time the novel was published, for example, debates concerning the appropriate relationship among American business, government agencies, labor unions, and the individual citizen? In other words, what kinds of cultural work did the novel perform at the time of its publication?

4凯特·肖邦的《觉醒》 （1899 年）在哪些方面与小说创作时期流行的关于女性权利和责任的辩论（例如，关于女性选举权、经济独立、婚姻和母性的辩论）进行了互动（再现、评论、质疑）？

4 In what ways does Kate Chopin’s The Awakening (1899) interact with (reproduce, comment on, question) debates about women’s rights and responsibilities circulating at the time the novel was written, for example, debates concerning women’s suffrage, economic independence, marriage, and motherhood?

5威廉·布莱克的《小黑孩》（1789 年）与十八世纪下半叶在英国流传的关于种族、奴隶制以及居住在大英帝国任何地区的黑皮肤民族的论述之间有何关系？

5 What is the relationship between William Blake’s “The Little Black Boy” (1789) and discourses circulating in England during the second half of the eighteenth century concerning race, slavery, and the dark-skinned peoples inhabiting any part of the British Empire?

10 女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评

10 Lesbian, gay, and queer criticism

在我教授的批判理论概论课上，我有时会在讲解女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评单元时，先向学生朗读一份经常被收入选集的英美作家名单：例如，奥斯卡·王尔德、田纳西·威廉姆斯、薇拉·凯瑟、詹姆斯·鲍德温、阿德里安娜·里奇、沃尔特·惠特曼、弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫、伊丽莎白·毕肖普、兰斯顿·休斯、爱德华·阿尔比、格特鲁德·斯坦、艾伦·金斯伯格、W·H·奥登、威廉·莎士比亚、卡森·麦卡勒斯、萨默塞特·毛姆、T·S·艾略特、詹姆斯·梅里尔、H·D·、莎拉·奥恩·朱厄特、哈特·克莱恩、威廉·S·巴勒斯和艾米·洛厄尔。然后我会问学生是否知道这些作家是同性恋、女同性恋或双性恋。有时，学生们一开始会有些犹豫，难以回答这个问题，而我们在讨论其他理论时却很少遇到这种情况。

In the critical-theory survey course I teach, I sometimes open the unit on lesbian, gay, and queer criticism by reading the class a list of frequently anthologized British and American writers: for example, Oscar Wilde, Tennessee Williams, Willa Cather, James Baldwin, Adrienne Rich, Walt Whitman, Virginia Woolf, Elizabeth Bishop, Langston Hughes, Edward Albee, Gertrude Stein, Allen Ginsberg, W. H. Auden, William Shakespeare, Carson McCullers, Somerset Maugham, T. S. Eliot, James Merrill, H.D., Sarah Orne Jewett, Hart Crane, William S. Burroughs, and Amy Lowell. Then I ask my students if they are aware that these writers are gay, lesbian, or bisexual. Sometimes that question is met by an initial reticence to respond, a difficulty not encountered in our opening discussions of other theories.

当然，我知道，不幸的是，在当今的美国，人们对同性恋的偏见依然根深蒂固，一些学生可能在看到其他同学的反应之前，不愿就此话题发表任何意见。正如一位学生告诉我的，她为了给我的课写论文，从大学图书馆借阅了几本关于同性恋理论的书籍。她当时觉得，或许在借阅台接待她的同学对她的性取向感到好奇，这让她非常尴尬，她甚至想大喊：“等等，我不是女同性恋！”

Of course, I know that, unfortunately, the stigma attached to being thought gay or lesbian is still quite strong in America today, and some students may be unwilling to express anything on the subject until they see how the rest of the group responds. As one student told me, after signing out a number of books on lesbian and gay theory from the university library for a paper she was writing for my class, she thought perhaps the student who waited on her at the circulation desk wondered about her sexual orientation, and to her embarrassment she found herself wanting to shout, “Hey, wait a minute; I’m not a lesbian!”

然而，学生遇到困难的另一个原因是他们缺乏相关知识。同性恋作家的作品是文学经典的重要组成部分，因此大多数文学课程都会涵盖这些作品，但许多本科生却想当然地认为这些作家都是异性恋。而且，他们的这种假设并非总是得到纠正。当然，我们的英美文学选集通常会包含收录作家的传记介绍，教授们也经常会提供关于作家个人生活的补充信息。例如，我们可能会了解到，夏洛特·珀金斯·吉尔曼在生下唯一的孩子后患上了严重的抑郁症；兰斯顿·休斯年轻时与父亲的紧张关系几乎让他走上了自杀的道路；或者罗伯特·弗罗斯特临终前的妻子拒绝让他进入自己的房间。但是，我们往往很少能了解到作家的同性恋或双性恋倾向，更不用说了解他们的性取向了。有关这种性取向如何影响他或她的生活和文学创作的信息。

Another reason for my students’ difficulty, however, is their lack of knowledge. The work of gay and lesbian writers forms a major part of the literary canon and is therefore included in most literature courses, but many undergraduate students assume that these writers are heterosexual. And their assumptions are not always corrected. Of course, our anthologies of English and American literature usually include biographical introductions to the writers whose works they contain, and professors frequently offer additional information about authors’ personal lives. We may be told, for example, that Charlotte Perkins Gilman suffered a deep depression after the birth of her only child; that, as a young man, Langston Hughes’ difficult relationship with his father almost drove him to suicide; or that Robert Frost’s dying wife refused to admit him to her room. But often we are given little biographical information about a writer’s lesbian or gay sexual orientation, let alone information concerning how that orientation affected her or his life and literary production.

如果作家异性恋生活的个人信息与我们理解他们的作品息息相关，那么为什么作家LGBTQ（女同性恋、男同性恋、双性恋、跨性别者和酷儿）生活的个人信息却常常被排除在相关的历史资料之外？如果性别和/或种族歧视的经历是作家生活中的重要因素，那么为什么了解LGBTQ作家所遭受的压迫就不重要呢？显然，在当今许多大学课堂上，LGBTQ性取向仍然被视为一个令人尴尬的话题。一些文学教授甚至在非LGBTQ作家研究的本科课程中，干脆避谈LGBTQ议题。在许多大学，尽管LGBTQ作家研究课程可以作为“专题”课程开设，但即便自20世纪70年代以来同性恋研究项目取得了长足进步，以及女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿理论在20世纪90年代初成为学术界的重要力量，这些课程也并非总是作为本科英语系的常规课程开设。

If personal information about writers’ heterosexual lives is relevant to our appreciation of their work, why is personal information about writers’ LGBTQ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer)1 lives often excluded from the realm of pertinent historical data? If the experience of gender and/or racial discrimination is an important factor in writers’ lives, then why isn’t it important to know about the oppression suffered by LGBTQ writers? Clearly, in many of our college classrooms today, LGBTQ sexuality is still considered an uncomfortable topic of discussion. Some literature professors simply avoid addressing LGBTQ issues in undergraduate courses not specifically devoted to LGBTQ writers. And at many colleges, although courses on LGBTQ writers can be offered as “special topics” courses, they do not always occur as regular course offerings in undergraduate English departments, despite the progress made by gay studies programs since the 1970s and the emergence of lesbian, gay, and queer theory as an important force in academia in the early 1990s.

换句话说，我的学生对他们所读作家的性取向感到困惑，这反映了部分教授对此问题的沉默，包括一些编纂选集的教授的沉默。此外，我认为，一些英语系教师对LGBTQ作家问题的沉默，反过来又反映了许多文学批评家长期以来对LGBTQ作家的性身份问题保持沉默，他们淡化或忽视了LGBTQ作家的身份，并歪曲或忽略了文学作品中LGBTQ人物的形象。

In other words, my students’ uncertainty concerning the sexual orientation of the writers they read reflects the silence of some of their professors on that subject, including the silence of some professors who compile anthologies. Furthermore, I would argue that the silence of some English faculty on the subject of LGBTQ writers reflects, in turn, the longstanding silence of many literary critics who have minimized or ignored the sexual identities of LGBTQ writers and distorted or overlooked the representations of LGBTQ characters in literary works.

LGBTQ人群的边缘化

The marginalization of LGBTQ people

例如，莉莲·法德曼分析了亨利·詹姆斯的小说《波士顿人》（1885）的评论界反响。正如法德曼所解释的，詹姆斯在小说中描绘了一种“波士顿婚姻”，这个词在19世纪末的新英格兰地区用来指代两位单身女性之间长期的一夫一妻制关系。她们通常经济独立，并且往往在文化、女权主义议题、社会进步和职业发展等方面有着共同的兴趣。这种关系并不罕见，虽然我们无法得知其中有多少包含性关系，但可以肯定的是，这些女性之间存在着强烈的情感纽带，她们将时间、精力和注意力都投入到彼此以及她们的女性朋友身上。

Consider, for example, the critical response, analyzed by Lillian Faderman, to Henry James’ The Bostonians (1885). As Faderman explains, James’ novel, by his own testimony, describes a “Boston marriage,” a term used in late-nineteenth-century New England to refer to a monogamous relationship of long standing between two single women who lived together; who were usually financially independent; and who often shared interests in culture, feminist issues, the betterment of society, and professional careers. Such relationships were not that uncommon, and although it’s impossible to know how many of them included sexual relations, it is clear that the women involved shared a strong emotional tie and focused their time, attention, and energy on each other and on their women friends.

在詹姆斯的小说中，奥利弗和维蕾娜之间存在着这样的关系，她们都是当时妇女运动的积极参与者。她们的关系被巴兹尔破坏了，巴兹尔凭借着强大的意志力，最终几乎是凭借一己之力说服维蕾娜抛弃奥利弗，嫁给了他。尽管如此，正如法德曼所指出的，詹姆斯并没有把奥利弗塑造成英雄，实际上，他对她进行了讽刺。从她身边的女性同伴来看，作者显然对巴兹尔也毫无同情心，他被描绘成一个自私、粗暴、好胜的操纵者，对妇女运动感到愤怒，并且注定会让维蕾娜过上不幸的生活。相比之下，维蕾娜与奥利芙的生活幸福美满。然而，正如法德曼所指出的，一些评论家认为，巴兹尔将维蕾娜从他们眼中与奥利芙不自然的关系中解救出来，让她重新拥有了他们认为女人只能在“真正”男人的怀抱中找到的真爱。

In James’ novel, such a relationship exists between Olive and Verena, who are active in the women’s movement of their day. Their relationship is broken up by Basil, whose overpowering determination finally convinces Verena, almost by the sheer force of his will, to abandon Olive and marry him. Although, as Faderman points out, James does not portray Olive heroically, and indeed satirizes her and her women companions, it is obvious the author has no sympathy for Basil either, whom he depicts as a selfish, brutish, competitive manipulator who is infuriated by the women’s movement and sure to give Verena an unhappy life. In contrast, Verena’s life with Olive is happy and productive. Yet, Faderman observes, critics have argued that Basil rescues Verena from what they see as her unnatural relationship with Olive and restores her to what they assume is the true love a woman can find only in the arms of a “real” man.

这些批评家怎能忽视维蕾娜与奥利芙之间关系中诸多积极的方面，并完全歪曲詹姆斯对巴兹尔的刻画？显然，他们的解读基于一种观念，并将这种观念强加于小说之上：异性恋是唯一正常、健康的爱情。任何其他形式的爱情都被认为是异常的、不健康的，应该避免。因此，这些批评家无法认识到巴兹尔显而易见的严重性格缺陷。因为他是异性恋，并且从奥利芙身边夺走了维蕾娜，所以他常常被赋予非常正面，甚至是英雄般的形象。

How can these critics ignore the very positive aspects of Verena’s relationship with Olive and completely distort James’ portrayal of Basil? Clearly, their interpretation rests on, and imposes on the novel, a view of heterosexual love as the only kind of normal, healthy love there is. Any other kind of love is presumed abnormal, unhealthy, and to be avoided. As a result, these critics are unable to recognize Basil’s obvious and serious character flaws. Because he is heterosexual and takes Verena away from Olive, he is often viewed in a very positive, even heroic, light.

这种解读方式体现了恐同情绪，即基于对同性恋的恐惧和厌恶而进行的解读。因此，它是恐同情绪长期占据主导地位的更大文化背景的一部分。尽管LGBTQ群体不再被送进精神病院接受“治疗”（这些治疗有时包括厌恶疗法、电击疗法甚至脑叶切除术），但直到1974年，同性恋才从美国精神病学会的心理疾病列表中移除，此类做法才正式终止。此外，直到1990年，1952年限制同性恋者移民美国的移民政策才被废除。尽管自1969年同性恋解放运动兴起以来，LGBTQ群体在社会和政治领域取得了巨大的进步，但恐同症仍然以多种形式存在于当今社会。1969年，格林威治村石墙酒吧的LGBTQ顾客终于对警察的暴行进行了反击，两千多人连续两晚参与了骚乱。这一具有重大象征意义的事件被称为“石墙事件”，因为它标志着LGBTQ群体不再将自己视为受害者，而是团结起来争取作为美国公民的权利。

This kind of interpretation is an example of a homophobic reading, that is, a reading informed by the fear and loathing of homosexuality. Thus, it is part of a larger cultural context in which homophobia has long played a major role. Although LGBTQ individuals are no longer placed in mental institutions for “treatment” which sometimes included aversion therapy, electric shock treatment, and even lobotomies – it wasn’t until 1974 that such practices officially ended, when the category of homosexuality was removed from the American Psychiatric Association’s list of psychological disorders. Moreover, it wasn’t until 1990 that the 1952 immigration policy restricting homosexual immigration into the United States was lifted. And homophobia is evident in many forms of discrimination against the LGBTQ community still practiced today, despite the enormous social and political gains achieved by activist groups since the Gay Liberation Movement began in 1969, after the LGBTQ patrons of Greenwich Village’s Stonewall Inn bar finally responded to police brutality by fighting back, two thousand strong, during two nights of rioting. This momentous event, referred to as Stonewall, has great symbolic significance because it marks the turning point when LGBTQ people renounced their victim status and stood up collectively for their rights as American citizens.

如今，尽管美国LGBTQ群体在军队中争取平等待遇方面取得了显著进展，但他们在就业和住房方面仍然面临歧视；在使用酒店、酒吧等公共设施时；在家庭法领域，例如结婚权、子女监护权、收养权或寄养权方面；作为警察骚扰和暴力仇恨犯罪的受害者；以及在与艾滋病相关的歧视方面，他们仍然遭受歧视。2毫无疑问，针对LGBTQ群体最令人震惊、最具破坏性的歧视形式是对LGBTQ青少年和年轻人的欺凌，这种欺凌在校内外持续发生，却往往得不到应有的重视。这种欺凌包括身体和情感上的暴力。针对不符合传统性别或性取向规范的青少年的犯罪行为，极大地提高了这些青少年的辍学率和自杀率。³最后，在美国，LGBTQ群体中的少数族裔成员面临着复杂的歧视体系。除了在白人异性恋文化中遭受的压迫外，LGBTQ非裔美国人、亚裔美国人、墨西哥裔美国人和拉丁裔美国人有时还会在他们自己的社区中遭受严重的污名化。

Today, although LGBTQ people in America have achieved significant gains toward equal treatment in the military, they still face discrimination in obtaining jobs and housing; in using public facilities, such as hotels and taverns; in areas of family law such as the right to marry, retain custody of their children, adopt children, or provide foster care; as victims of police harassment and violent hate crimes; and in AIDS-related discrimination.2 Certainly the most alarming, and damaging, form of discrimination against LGBTQ individuals is the bullying of LGBTQ adolescents and young adults that continues to occur in and out of school and that remains too often under-addressed. The physical and emotional violence committed against young people who do not conform to conventional gender or sexual norms has greatly increased the school drop-out and suicide rates among these teens.3 Finally, LGBTQ individuals who are members of racial minorities in America face a complex system of discrimination. In addition to the oppression they suffer in white heterosexist culture, LGBTQ African Americans, Asian Americans, Chicanos/as, and Latinos/as are sometimes heavily stigmatized in their own communities.

针对LGBTQ人群的歧视中，不可或缺的一部分是那些曾经被普遍接受、如今仍然具有一定影响力的负面迷思。这些迷思包括：LGBTQ人群是病态的、邪恶的，或者两者兼具；因此，他们“天生”就是贪得无厌的性侵犯者，会猥亵儿童，并通过“招募”青少年成为LGBTQ群体来腐蚀他们。另一个迷思则将LGBTQ群体描绘成一个极小的“异类”群体，而事实上，据估计，LGBTQ人群至少占美国人口的10%。其他常见的误解还包括：认为由LGBTQ人群抚养的孩子长大后也会成为LGBTQ人群；认为放任LGBTQ行为下去会导致人类灭绝；以及认为LGBTQ人群应对美国外交实力的下降负责。

Part and parcel of the discrimination practiced against LGBTQ people are the negative myths that used to be generally accepted as truth and that still exert some influence today. These include the myth that LGBTQ people are sick, evil, or both and that it is therefore in their “nature” to be insatiable sexual predators, to molest children, and to corrupt youths by “recruiting” them to become LGBTQ. Another myth portrays the LGBTQ community as a very small population of deviants, when, in fact, it is estimated that LGBTQ people comprise at least 10 percent of the US population. Other common misconceptions include the belief that children raised by LGBTQ people will grow up to be LGBTQ, that unchecked LGBTQ behavior will result in the extinction of the human race, and that LGBTQ people are responsible for declines in US foreign power.

这里或许是个停下来解释一些术语的好地方，其中许多术语都与针对LGBTQ人群的歧视有关。这些术语在你阅读女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿文学批评时可能会遇到。虽然“恐同症”一词通常用来指个人对同性之爱的病态恐惧，但我上面使用这个词指的是针对LGBTQ人群的制度化歧视（即根植于文化法律和习俗中的歧视），因为我认为，我们很难否认这种歧视是基于父权制所助长的集体性（有时甚至是无意识的）恐同症，或者许多LGBTQ理论家所说的异性恋父权制。 （ “异性恋父权制”一词提醒我们，父权制由于偏向于传统的性别角色，因此总是偏向于异性恋。）内化恐同症指的是一些 LGBTQ 人群所经历的自我厌恶，因为在他们从青春期到成年的成长过程中，他们内化了异性恋美国强加给他们的恐同症。

This might be a good place to pause and define some terms, many of which are related to discrimination against LGBTQ people. These are terms that you may encounter when you read lesbian, gay, and queer literary criticism. While the word homophobia is generally used to refer to an individual’s pathological dread of samesex love, I used the term above to refer to institutionalized discrimination (discrimination that is built into a culture’s laws and customs) against LGBTQ people because I think we would be hard pressed to argue that such discrimination is based on anything other than the collective, if sometimes unconscious, homophobia promoted by patriarchy, or what many LGBTQ theorists call heteropatriarchy. (The word heteropatriarchy draws our attention to the fact that patriarchy, because it is biased in favor of traditional gender roles, is always biased in favor of hetero-sexuality.) Internalized homophobia refers to the self-hatred some LGBTQ people experience because, in their growth through adolescence to adulthood, they’ve internalized the homophobia pressed on them by heterosexual America.

用来指代针对LGBTQ人群的制度性歧视以及随之而来的异性恋特权的常用词是“异性恋主义”（heterosexism）。例如，异性恋主义文化会强制推行异性恋，这个词由艾德丽安·里奇（Adrienne Rich）等人提出，用来描述年轻人所承受的巨大压力，这种压力来自家庭、学校、教会、医疗行业以及各种媒体，迫使他们成为异性恋。如今， “异性恋规范” （heterornormative）是更常用的术语，用来指代那些迫使每个人都必须符合传统定义的性“正常”的社会态度和假设。

The word more commonly used to refer to institutionalized discrimination against LGBTQ people, and the privileging of heterosexuality that accompanies it, is heterosexism. For example, a heterosexist culture enforces compulsory heterosexuality, a term used by Adrienne Rich, among others, to describe the enormous pressure to be heterosexual placed on young people by their families, schools, the church, the medical professions, and all forms of the media. Today, heteronormative is the more commonly used term for the social attitudes and assumptions that pressure everyone to be what is conventionally defined as sexually “normal.”

异性恋中心主义是一种更为隐蔽的针对LGBTQ群体的偏见，它指的是一种（通常是无意识的）假设，即异性恋是普遍存在的，例如：除非有人特意说明，否则房间里的每个人——除非有人明确表示并非如此——都是异性恋。异性恋中心主义理所当然地认为，所有人的经历都可以用异性恋的框架来理解。因此，异性恋中心主义使LGBTQ人群的经历隐形化，例如，在过去的几十年里，沃尔特·惠特曼的粉丝们可能意识不到他诗歌中蕴含的同性恋情愫。

Heterocentrism, a more subtle form of prejudice against LGBTQ individuals, is the assumption, often unconscious, that heterosexuality is universal, for instance that everyone in the room – unless someone makes a point of being otherwise – is heterosexual. Heterocentrism takes it for granted that everyone’s experience can be understood within a heterosexual framework. Heterocentrism thus renders the experience of LGBTQ people invisible, making it possible in decades past, for example, for fans of Walt Whitman to be unaware of the homoerotic dimension of his poetry.

如果“恐同症”、“异性恋霸权主义”和“异性恋中心主义”这几个词听起来有点重叠，因而让人困惑，现在不必过于担心。事实上，你有时会听到它们被交替使用，这或许是因为这三个词都假定了异性恋者天生优越。如果你仔细想想，你可能会意识到这三种偏见——恐同症、异性恋霸权主义和异性恋中心主义——都是异性恋规范化的：它们都是强制性异性恋的形式。这三个词之间的区别显然在于程度：恐同症暗示着最强烈的反LGBTQ情绪，异性恋中心主义则暗示着最轻微的反LGBTQ情绪，当然，这三个词都指的是极具破坏性的偏见形式。

Don’t be too concerned, right now, if the words homophobia, heterosexism, and heterocentrism seem a bit overlapping and, therefore, a bit confusing. Indeed, you’ll sometimes hear them used interchangeably, perhaps because all three terms assume the inborn superiority of heterosexuals. And if you think about it for a minute, you’ll probably realize that all three biases – homophobia, heterosexism, and heterocentrism – are heteronormative: they are all forms of compulsory heterosexuality. The difference among the three terms is apparently one of degree: homophobia suggests the most virulent anti-LGBTQ sentiment, heterocentrism the least virulent, though all three, of course, refer to extremely damaging forms of prejudice.

将我们的注意力集中在LGBTQ群体作为受压迫群体上，恐同症、异性恋霸权、异性恋中心主义和异性恋规范等词汇​​往往凸显了LGBTQ群体在政治上构成少数群体的现状。作为少数群体，他们当然理应享有与美国种族、民族和宗教少数群体同等的法律保护。另一个强调LGBTQ群体少数群体地位的概念是生物本质主义，即认为人口中固定的一部分人天生就是LGBTQ，正如其余人口天生就是异性恋一样。相反，一些理论家认为，尽管LGBTQ群体在美国构成受压迫的政治少数群体，但所有人都有可能产生同性欲望或进行不符合异性恋框架的性行为。根据这种被称为社会建构主义的观点，LGBTQ的性取向和异性恋是社会力量而非生物力量的产物。关注LGBTQ群体少数群体地位的理解方式被称为少数群体化观点。那些将所有人身上都存在的同性恋倾向视为理解LGBTQ群体经历的方式，被称为普遍化观点。4

By focusing our attention on the LGBTQ community as an oppressed group, the words homophobia, heterosexism, heterocentrism, and heteronormative tend to spotlight the ways in which LGBTQ people constitute a political minority. As a minority they deserve, of course, the same protection under the law afforded to racial, ethnic, and religious minorities in America. Another concept that emphasizes the minority status of LGBTQ people is biological essentialism, the idea that a fixed segment of the population is naturally LGBTQ, just as the rest of the population is naturally heterosexual. Conversely, some theorists argue that, although LGBTQ people constitute an oppressed political minority in America, all human beings have the potential for same-sex desire or for sexual activity that does not fit a heterosexual framework. According to this view, which is called social constructionism, LGBTQ sexuality and heterosexuality are products of social, not biological, forces. Ways of understanding LGBTQ experience that focus on their minority status are called minoritizing views. Ways of understanding LGBTQ experience that focus on the homosexual potential in all people are called universalizing views.4

有趣的是，本质主义（少数化）和建构主义（普遍化）观点都曾被用来攻击LGBTQ群体：例如，（1）LGBTQ群体天生有病（或邪恶）；（2）LGBTQ群体是病态（或邪恶）环境的产物。同样，本质主义和建构主义观点也曾被用来捍卫或赞扬LGBTQ群体：例如，（1）有些人天生具有LGBTQ特质，无论他们出生在何种环境中，因此他们应该被视为自然而然；（2）LGBTQ性取向是对特定环境因素的正常反应，因此LGBTQ群体应该被视为正常人。

Interestingly, both essentialist (minoritizing) and constructionist (universalizing) views have been used to attack LGBTQ individuals: for example, (1) LGBTQ people are born sick (or evil); (2) LGBTQ people are sick (or evil) products of a sick (or evil) environment. By the same token, both essentialist and constructionist views have been used to defend or celebrate the LGBTQ community: for example, (1) it is biologically natural for some people to be LGBTQ, no matter what environment they’re born into, and therefore they should be accepted as natural; (2) LGBTQ orientation is a normal response to particular environmental factors, and therefore LGBTQ people should be accepted as normal.

最后，还有两个常用来指代同性关系的词：同性恋情欲（homoerotic），我之前曾用它来形容惠特曼的诗歌；以及同性社交（homosocial）。“同性社交”指的是带有情色意味（但不一定直白地表达性欲）的描写，暗示同性之间的吸引，或可能对同性读者产生性吸引力，例如，对女性互相帮助脱衣或裸男在池塘中沐浴的感官描写。这类描写可以出现在任何媒介中，例如电影、绘画、雕塑、摄影，当然也包括文学作品。“同性社交”指的是类似于男女之间友谊的同性友谊。例如，托妮·莫里森的小说《最蓝的眼睛》 （1970）中三位妓女——中国、波兰和玛丽小姐——之间的关系，马克·吐温的小说《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》（1885 ）中哈克和吉姆之间的关系，以及凯特·肖邦的小说《觉醒》 （1899）中埃德娜·庞特利耶和阿黛尔·拉蒂尼奥尔之间的关系，都属于同性社交关系。此外，在对艾德娜对阿黛尔丰满美貌的感官反应的描述中，这两个人物之间的关系也是同性恋的。

Finally, two oft-used words that refer to same-sex relationships are homoerotic, which I used earlier to describe Whitman’s poetry, and homosocial. Homoerotic denotes erotic (though not necessarily overtly sexual) depictions that imply same-sex attraction or that might appeal sexually to a same-sex reader, for example, a sensually evocative description of women in the process of helping each other undress or of nude men bathing in a pond. Such depictions can occur in any medium, such as film, painting, sculpture, photography, and, of course, literature. The word homosocial denotes same-sex friendship of the kind seen in female- or male-bonding activities. For example, the relationship among the three prostitutes – China, Poland, and Miss Marie – in Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) is homosocial, as is the relationship between Huck and Jim in Mark Twain’s Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1885) and between Edna Pontellier and Adèle Ratignolle in Kate Chopin’s The Awakening (1899). Furthermore, in the descriptions of Edna’s sensual response to Adèle’s voluptuous beauty, the relationship between these two characters is homoerotic as well.

既然同性社交活动并非LGBTQ人群独有，为何还要在此提及“同性社交”一词呢？例如，“女生之夜”和“男生之夜”长期以来都是许多异性恋文化的重要组成部分。我认为至少有两个理由可以解释为何本章需要提及“同性社交”。首先，同性社交在异性恋和LGBTQ文化中都扮演着重要角色，这让我们有机会去理解LGBTQ人群和异性恋人群共同拥有的重要社交和情感体验。其次，尽管同性社交通常被认为对儿童的情感成长和成年人的情感健康至关重要（无论其性取向如何），但许多人由于自身的恐同心理或害怕遭到他人的恐同反应，对某些形式的同性社交感到不安。例如，一位异性恋女性在周六晚上与一位女性朋友去一家“高档餐厅”吃饭时，是否会犹豫不决？会吗？不会吗？那么两位异性恋男性朋友呢？两位LGBTQ同性朋友呢？异性恋父母在什么情况下会对子女自然的同性社交活动过度担忧？简而言之，与同性社交关系相关的复杂问题，深刻揭示了恐同症对每个人福祉的破坏性影响之普遍性。

Why include the term homosocial here when homosocial activity is not unique to LGBTQ people? For example, “girls’ night out” and “boys’ night out” have long been an important part of many heterosexual cultures. I think we could argue that there are at least two reasons to include the term in this chapter. First, the very fact that homosocial bonding plays an important role in both heterosexual and LGBTQ cultures offers us an opportunity to appreciate a significant area of social and emotional experience shared by LGBTQ and straight people alike. Second, although homosocial bonding is generally considered vital to the emotional growth of children and the emotional health of adults, regardless of their sexual orientation, many individuals are apprehensive about some forms of same-sex bonding due to their own homophobia or for fear of a homophobic response from others. For instance, might a straight woman think twice before going to a “wine-and-white-tablecloth” restaurant for dinner with a female friend on a Saturday night? Yes? No? What about two straight male friends? What about two same-sex LGBTQ friends? When might a heterosexual parent become unduly concerned about the natural homosocial activities of a son or daughter? In short, the complex issues often associated with homosocial bonding sheds a strong light on the pervasiveness of homophobia’s destructive impact on everyone’s well being.

到目前为止，我一直将LGBTQ群体视为一个整体进行讨论。事实上，即使将同性恋、女同性恋和酷儿批评纳入同一章节，也暗示着他们构成某种同质化的群体。诚然，作为性少数群体成员，他们共同遭受着政治、经济、社会和心理上的压迫。对许多思想家而言，这种共同经历的巨大影响，以及LGBTQ群体作为一个群体行动时所蕴含的潜在政治力量，足以支持我们应该从这个角度来审视他们的观点。

So far, I have discussed LGBTQ people as a group. Indeed, even the inclusion of gay, lesbian, and queer criticism in the same chapter implies that they constitute some sort of homogenous collectivity. Certainly, they share in common the political, economic, social, and psychological oppression they suffer as members of a sexual minority. And for many thinkers, the enormity of this shared experience, and the potential for political power generated when LGBTQ people act as a group, is sufficient to support the claim that they should be considered in this light.

然而，许多女同性恋者和男同性恋者认为，压迫是他们为数不多的共同经历之一，甚至可能是唯一共同经历；在其他大多数方面，男同性恋者和女同性恋者截然相反。例如，许多男同性恋者和女同性恋者最重要的社会、政治和个人经历，甚至可以说全部经历，都发生在同性群体中。此外，许多女同性恋者只认同女性身份，而许多男同性恋者只认同男性身份。而且，女同性恋者即使“隐瞒”（伪装成异性恋），也经历了所有女性，无论性取向如何，都经历过的性别压迫，而隐瞒性取向的男同性恋者却有机会享受父权制赋予异性恋男性的特权。无论是否隐瞒性取向，男同性恋作家在文学史上的代表性都远超女同性恋作家（或异性恋女性作家），因为直到最近，男性作家的作品比女性作家的作品更容易被奉为经典。

Many lesbians and gay men, however, argue that oppression is one of the few experiences, if not the only one, they have in common and that, in most other ways, gay men and lesbians are polar opposites. For example, many gay men and lesbians have their most significant social, political, and personal experiences, if not all of their experiences, in same-sex groups. In addition, many lesbians identify exclusively with women, while many gay men identify exclusively with men. Furthermore, lesbians, even if “closeted” (posing as heterosexuals), have experienced the gender oppression that all women, straight or gay, have experienced, while closeted gay men have had the opportunity to enjoy the patriarchal privileges extended to straight men. And whether closeted or not, gay male writers have enjoyed an incomparably greater representation in literary history than lesbians (or heterosexual women) because, until recently, works by male authors were much more readily canonized than works by female authors.

为了更好地理解女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评的独特之处，我们将分章节进行讨论。正如你将看到的，酷儿批评作为一个相对新兴的研究领域，其理论基础是解构主义，它既与异性恋身份认同问题相关，也与LGBTQ性身份认同问题相关。

In order to appreciate the distinctive features of lesbian, gay, and queer criticism, we’ll discuss them under separate headings. As you’ll see, queer criticism relatively speaking, a newer field of inquiry – is based on the insights of deconstruction and is relevant to issues of heterosexual identity as well as to issues of LGBTQ sexual identity.

女同性恋批评

Lesbian criticism

或许是因为女同性恋批评和女性主义批评都源于同一土壤——都是对父权压迫的回应——而且女同性恋批评家通常也是女性主义者，所以女同性恋批评关注的个人身份和政治问题与女性主义者分析的问题类似（见第四章）。然而，女性主义关注的是与性别歧视相关的问题，以及如何在性别歧视意识形态的影响之外，为个人身份和政治行动开辟空间；而女同性恋批评则同时关注性别歧视和异性恋霸权。换言之，女同性恋批评家必须应对由父权制男性特权和异性恋特权共同造成的心理、社会、经济和政治压迫。而正是这第二种特权，常常使异性恋女性主义者和女同性恋女性主义者之间产生分歧。

Perhaps because lesbian criticism and feminist criticism grew from the same soil – as responses to patriarchal oppression – and because lesbian critics are generally feminists, lesbian criticism is concerned with issues of personal identity and politics analogous to those analyzed by feminists (see Chapter 4). However, while feminism addresses issues related to sexism and the difficulties involved in carving out a space for personal identity and political action beyond the influence of sexist ideologies, lesbian critics address issues related to both sexism and heterosexism. In other words, lesbian critics must deal with the psychological, social, economic, and political oppression fostered not only by patriarchal male privilege, but by heterosexual privilege as well. And this second form of privilege has often put heterosexual and lesbian feminists at odds with each other.

事实上，女权主义在不同时期都曾被指责为异性恋中心主义，因为它倾向于关注异性恋女性所受的压迫，而非所有女性（包括女同性恋者）所受的压迫；也曾被指责为异性恋霸权主义，因为它最引人注目的领导层成员的异性恋倾向，以及它对被美国恐同的父权制权力结构“贴上”女同性恋运动的标签的担忧（这种担忧是合理的，因为恐同症是一种如此普遍且具有破坏性的力量）。类似地，有色人种女同性恋者和工人阶级女同性恋者在女同性恋女权主义运动中也长期遭受边缘化，甚至被排斥。女同性恋女权主义运动和女权主义运动一样，主要起源于白人中产阶级，因此，直到最近，它一直受到白人中产阶级视角和目标的限制。

Indeed, feminism has been, at various times, vulnerable to charges of hetero-centrism in its tendency to focus on the oppression of heterosexual women rather than on the oppression of all women, including lesbians, and of heterosexism in the heterosexual orientation of its most visible leadership and in its legitimate fear of being “branded” a lesbian movement by the homophobic patriarchal power structure in America (legitimate because homophobia is such a pervasive and disarming force). Analogously, lesbians of color and working-class lesbians have suffered a history of marginalization, if not exclusion, within the lesbian-feminist movement, which, like the feminist movement, emerged largely from the white middle class and, therefore, has been limited – until relatively recently – by white middle-class perspectives and goals.

我之所以一开始就提及这些问题，是因为尤其自20世纪80年代中期以来，女同性恋者一直拒绝被异性恋女权主义者边缘化；而且女同性恋者有色人种和工人阶级女同性恋者拒绝被白人中产阶级女同性恋者边缘化。因此，女同性恋批评已成为理论探究和政治活动中最为丰富和激动人心的领域之一。长期以来，女同性恋批评的核心问题——例如“什么是女同性恋？”和“女同性恋文学文本的构成要素是什么？”——在女同性恋批评家们既考虑到自身阶级出身和种族对其观点造成的局限性，又考虑到种族、阶级、性别和性取向在我们日常生活中密不可分地交织在一起，赋予我们所有人的复杂遗产的美丽和重要性时，便以极具启发性的方式呈现出来。

I mention these problems up front because, especially since the mid 1980s, lesbians have refused to be marginalized by heterosexual feminists; and lesbians of color and working-class lesbians have refused to be marginalized by white middle-class lesbians. As a result, lesbian criticism has become one of the richest and most exciting domains of theoretical inquiry and political activity. Questions that have long been central to lesbian critical inquiry – such as “What is a lesbian?” and “What constitutes a lesbian literary text?” – are problematized in very productive ways when lesbian critics take into account both the limitations imposed on their viewpoints by their class origins and race, and the beauty and importance of the complex heritage bestowed on all of us by the ultimate inseparability of race, class, gender, and sexual orientation in our daily lives.

除了引出女同性恋研究的基本问题之外，“什么是女同性恋？”和“女同性恋文学文本的构成要素是什么？”这两个问题本身也属于一种自我质疑的理论活动，而这种活动形式通常并非同性恋批评的范畴。因此，让我们更深入地探讨这两个问题。

In addition to generating fundamental issues of lesbian inquiry, the questions “What is a lesbian?” and “What constitutes a lesbian literary text?” belong to a self-questioning form of theoretical activity not generally performed by gay criticism. So let’s take a closer look at these two questions.

女同性恋能否定义为与另一位女性发生性关系的女性？性行为的具体含义是什么？（必须有生殖器接触吗？）如果将这样的定义应用于异性恋，又该如何解释？想必这意味着，那些自认为是异性恋的处女，除非与男性发生过生殖器性行为，否则就无权自称为异性恋。因此，一个人的性取向似乎必须根据其性欲来定义。

Can a lesbian be defined as a woman who has sex with another woman? What activity constitutes sex? (Must there be genital contact?) How would such a definition work if we applied it to heterosexuality? Presumably, it would mean that virgins who thought of themselves as heterosexuals would have no right to call themselves heterosexuals unless and until they had genital sex with men. So one’s sexuality must be defined, it seems, in terms of one’s sexual desire.

或许，定义女同性恋者更好的方式是说，她是指性欲指向女性的女性。这种定义的优势在于，它使我们能够在异性婚姻的框架内承认女同性恋者的存在。纵观历史，女性往往不得不结婚，无论她们是否愿意，要么是为了经济生存，要么是因为她们所处的僵化社会制度没有给她们提供其他社会或心理选择。而有些女性，尽管她们可能爱着并尊重自己的丈夫，却对女性而非男性有着强烈的吸引力。弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫就是一个典型的例子，她已婚，却与维塔·萨克维尔-韦斯特保持着一段激情而长久的婚外情。

Perhaps a better way to define a lesbian, then, is to say that she is a woman whose sexual desire is directed toward women. The advantage of a definition of this sort is that it allows us to recognize lesbian existence even within the confines of heterosexual marriage. For throughout history, women often have had to marry, whether they wanted to or not, in order to survive economically or because the rigid social system in which they lived offered them no other social or psychological option. And some of these women, though they may have loved and respected their husbands, were passionately attracted to women rather than to men. Virginia Woolf, who was married but who had a passionate, long-standing affair with Vita Sackville-West, is a case in point.

然而，如果存在两名女性之间存在炽热情谊的证据——例如，她们之间有过多次书信往来，字里行间流露出浓烈的爱意——但由于这段关系发生在与我们所处历史时期不同的时期，我们便无法确切地确定她们当时表达的究竟是什么呢？例如，我们该如何解读十九世纪英国和美国女性之间所谓的“浪漫友谊”——其中一个例子就是前文讨论过的“波士顿婚姻”——在这种关系中，她们或许表达了最温柔的爱意或炽热的情感，但却没有任何确凿的证据表明存在性行为或性欲？

What if, however, there is evidence of a passionate attachment between two women – such as a long exchange of letters in which passionate love is expressed – but because the relationship occurred in a different historical period from our own, we can’t be certain exactly what it was that was being expressed? For example, how do we interpret the “romantic friendships,” as they are called, between women in nineteenth-century Britain and America – one embodiment of which was the “Boston marriage” discussed earlier – in which the most tender love or passionate attachment may have been expressed, but for which there is no concrete evidence of sexual activity or sexual desire?

这一时期以过分夸张的感伤主义和过分夸张的语言表达而闻名，父权制接受甚至鼓励女性之间流露出的身体亲昵，认为这是女性“过度情绪化的天性”的迷人表现。因此，我们不能断定女性之间充满热情洋溢的信件往来——例如“亲爱的，我爱你，这份爱远超我的言语所能表达，远超我自身的认知” ⁵——就一定代表着性欲，更遑论性行为。另一方面，许多此类关系可能包含着某种性层面，而十九世纪的父权制对此却视而不见。事实上，鉴于十九世纪对女性性欲和性意识的限制，许多女性可能对其他女性怀有强烈的性欲，却从未意识到这一点。

The period is known for its overblown sentimentality and excesses of verbal expression, and effusions of physical affection between women were accepted, even encouraged, by patriarchy as charming displays of women’s “overemotional nature.” So we can’t assume with any certainty that women’s exchanges of letters filled with exuberant expressions of passion – such as “I love you my darling, more than I can express, more than I am conscious of myself”5 – are indicative of sexual desire, let alone sexual activity. On the other hand, many such relationships might have involved a sexual dimension to which nineteenth-century patriarchy would have been utterly blind. Indeed, given the nineteenth century’s restriction of women’s sexuality and sexual awareness, many women might have had enormous sexual desire for other women without ever recognizing it as such.

因此，如果仅仅关注我们今天所定义的性行为或性欲，就有可能抹杀女性生活中一个重要的维度，而这个维度或许只有通过女同性恋的视角才能得到充分理解。为了避免这种抹杀，并促进所有女性之间的团结，一些女同性恋理论家提出，女同性恋者是认同自己为女性的女性。认同自己为女性并非仅限于性领域，而是意味着将大部分的注意力和情感能量投入到其他女性身上，并将其他女性作为自己情感滋养和心理支持的主要来源。<sup> 6</sup>

Thus, a strict focus on what we would define today as sexual activity or sexual desire runs the risk of erasing an important dimension of women’s lives that very well might be understood fully only through a lesbian lens. In order to avoid this kind of erasure, and to promote solidarity among all women, some lesbian theorists have suggested that a lesbian is a woman-identified woman. Being a woman-identified woman is not restricted to the sexual domain but consists of directing the bulk of one’s attention and emotional energy to other women and having other women as one’s primary source of emotional sustenance and psychological support.6
