艾德丽安·里奇（Adrienne Rich）运用了这一理念，论证了她所谓的“女同性恋连续体”的存在。里奇解释说，女同性恋连续体“涵盖了女性一生以及整个历史中一系列与女性身份认同相关的体验，而不仅仅是女性是否曾与另一位女性有过或有意识地渴望过性交体验”（239）。与女性身份认同相关的体验包括，例如通过共同工作或娱乐建立的情感纽带、给予或接受心理支持，以及任何形式的共同快乐体验。女性身份认同并不排除对另一位女性的性欲或性行为，但也不要求必须如此。因此，女性可以在一生中进出女同性恋连续体，也可以始终处于其中。从这个角度来看，19世纪女性之间的浪漫友谊，无论是否涉及性行为或性欲，都确实是女同性恋分析的恰当对象。

Adrienne Rich makes use of this idea when she argues for the existence of what she calls a lesbian continuum. A lesbian continuum, Rich explains, “include[s] a range – through each woman’s life and throughout history – of woman-identified experience, not simply the fact that a woman has had or consciously desired genital sexual experience with another woman” (239). Woman-identified experience includes, for example, emotional bonding through shared work or play, the giving or receiving of psychological support, and the shared experience of joy in any form. Woman-identification does not preclude sexual desire for or sexual activity with another woman, but neither does it require them. A woman can thus move in and out of the lesbian continuum throughout her life or remain within it entirely. From this perspective, women’s romantic friendships during the nineteenth century, whether or not they involved sexual activity or desire, are indeed an appropriate subject for lesbian analysis.

当然，一些理论家认为，轻视女同性恋体验中的性维度，就等于轻视了女同性恋生活中最独特、最解放的方面。女同性恋者通过性结合，拒绝男性触碰她们的身体，从而剥夺了父权制最强大的工具之一：异性恋。因为异性恋并非“正常”女性的“自然”性取向，而是一种政治制度，它将女性置于父权制之下，因为女性对男性的顺从被构建在异性恋对女性性欲的定义之中。换言之，从这个角度来看，父权制和异性恋密不可分。要反抗前者，就必须反抗后者。

Of course, to underplay the sexual dimension of lesbian experience is to underplay, some theorists argue, that which is most unique and liberating in lesbian life. In bonding with one another sexually and denying men access to their bodies, lesbians deny patriarchy one of its most powerful tools: heterosexuality. For heterosexuality is not a “natural” sexual orientation for “normal” women but a political institution that subordinates women to patriarchy in that women’s subservience to men is built into heterosexual definitions of feminine sexuality. In other words, from this point of view, patriarchy and heterosexuality are inseparable. To resist the former, one must resist the latter.

因此，一些女同性恋者是分离主义者。她们尽可能地与所有男性（包括男同性恋者）以及异性恋女性保持距离。她们也可能与那些不认同她们性取向的女同性恋者保持距离。观点。鉴于上世纪70年代以男性为主导的同性恋解放运动中的性别歧视，以及我们前文提到的女权主义的异性恋中心主义倾向，女同性恋分离主义者认为，只有女同性恋组织才会优先考虑女同性恋问题。对于分离主义者而言，正如对于大多数非分离主义者的女同性恋女权主义者而言一样，女同性恋是一种政治立场，而不仅仅是个人性取向的问题。

For this reason, some lesbians are separatists. They disassociate themselves as much as possible from all men, including gay men, and from heterosexual women as well. They may also disassociate themselves from lesbians who don’t share their views. Recalling the sexism of the male-dominated Gay Liberation Movement of the 1970s and, as we noted above, the heterosexist tendencies of feminism, lesbian separatists believe that only lesbian organizations will give priority to lesbian issues. For separatists, just as for the majority of lesbian feminists who are not separatists, lesbianism is a political stance, not merely an issue of personal sexuality.

然而，正如玛丽莲·弗莱所论证的那样，尽管分离主义是一种蓄意的、系统性的政治策略，但这并非女性脱离父权统治的唯一形式。事实上，女性脱离父权统治的程度因一系列旨在增强女性权力的制度性实践而异，例如为受虐妇女提供庇护所、离婚、增加日托服务、女性研究项目、女性酒吧以及堕胎合法化。甚至一些看似个人化的行为，如结束一段亲密关系、将某人拒之门外或排除在公司之外、停止支持、撤回忠诚、拒绝观看带有性别歧视的电视节目或收听带有性别歧视的音乐以及拒绝与令人厌恶的人交往，也都是女性脱离男性或男性主导的机构的形式，这些都能增强女性的权力。正如弗莱所言，“进入权是权力的一种体现……主人永远有权进入奴隶的茅屋。奴隶若决定将主人拒之门外，便是在宣告自己不再是奴隶”（95-96）。因此，尽管大多数女性并不选择分离主义政治，但她们既不应认为这种政治与自身经历完全格格不入，也不应冷漠对待那些选择分离主义政治的女性。

Nevertheless, as Marilyn Frye argues, while separatism is a deliberate, systematic political policy, it is not the only form in which women’s separation from patriarchal domination occurs. In fact, separation is enacted to varying degrees across a range of institutional practices that increase women’s power, including, for example, the provision of shelters for battered women, divorce, the increased availability of day care, women’s studies programs, women’s bars, and the legalization of abortion. Even such apparently personal behaviors as breaking up a close relationship, excluding someone from one’s house or one’s company, withholding one’s support, withdrawing one’s loyalty, refusing to watch sexist television programs or listen to sexist music, and rejecting obnoxious individuals are all forms of separation from males or from male-dominated institutions that can increase women’s power. As Frye puts it, “Access is one of the faces of Power. … It is always the privilege of the master to enter the slave’s hut. The slave who decides to exclude the master from her hut is declaring herself not a slave” (95–96). Thus, although most women do not choose separatist politics, neither should they find them completely alien to their own experience nor be unsympathetic to women who do choose them.

显然，试图定义“女同性恋”一词，甚至阐明各种形式的女性分离所蕴含的全部政治意义，既令人兴奋又充满挑战。同样困难且意义非凡的是，试图回答“何为女同性恋文学作品？”这个问题。鉴于我们无法总是确定某位作家是否是女同性恋者（尤其考虑到我们刚才讨论的关于该术语定义的种种困难），即使我们知道作者的性取向，也不能以此来判断我们正在阅读的是否是女同性恋作品。当然，批评家如何定义“女同性恋”将决定他或她对女同性恋作家和女同性恋作品的定义。

Clearly, attempts to define the word lesbian, or even to articulate the full political implications of various forms of women’s separation, are as problematic as they are exciting. Equally difficult and equally rewarding are efforts to answer the question “What constitutes a lesbian literary text?” As we can’t always be sure whether or not a particular writer was a lesbian, especially given the difficulties we’ve just discussed concerning the definition of that term, we can’t depend on an author’s sexual orientation, even if we know it, to tell us whether or not we are reading a lesbian text. Of course, how the critic defines lesbian will determine her or his definition of both lesbian writers and lesbian texts.

例如，一位女同性恋评论家可能会认为，像薇拉·凯瑟这样一位性生活活跃的女同性恋作家，之所以在看似异性恋的叙事中隐喻女同性恋的含义，是因为她知道自己无法公开描写女同性恋的欲望，至少如果她希望作品能够出版，并避免公众谴责甚至刑事诉讼的话。朱迪思·费特利在解读凯瑟的《我的安东尼娅》（1918）时就提出了这一论点。费特利认为，叙述者吉姆·伯登的性格经常自相矛盾，许多评论家都难以解读，但如果我们把他视为凯瑟自身女同性恋欲望的化身，就能理解他。费特利指出，尽管吉姆多次承认自己爱着安东尼娅，并渴望她成为自己的爱人或妻子，但出于某种无法解释的原因，他却始终没有真正爱上她。他得不到她。此外，他的行为举止也带有传统的女性特征。他大部分时间都待在厨房里，待在女性的空间里。我们从未见过他参与男性的狩猎和捕鱼活动。他不认同镇上的男人，并且对他们滥用的父权特权充满敌意。当吉姆代替安东妮娅去威克·卡特家时——卡特是一个性骚扰者，他的怪异行为令安东妮娅感到恐惧——吉姆并没有为了保护自己心爱的女人而殴打他。相反，他显然代替安东妮娅遭到了强奸，因为他跑回家找祖母，对卡特令人作呕的行为感到厌恶和羞愧，并恳求祖母不要告诉任何人，甚至不要告诉医生。最后，吉姆表现出对男性性欲的厌恶，例如，他对阳具状男性气质的反感，这在他对“第一卷中那条极其阳具状的蛇”（费特利 152）的描述中显而易见：

For example, a lesbian critic might argue that a writer known to have been a sexually active lesbian, such as Willa Cather, coded lesbian meaning in an apparently heterosexual narrative because she knew that she couldn’t write about lesbian desire openly, at least not if she hoped to have her work published and to avoid public censure if not criminal prosecution. Judith Fetterly makes this argument in her interpretation of Cather’s My Ántonia (1918). Among other codings, Fetterly argues that narrator Jim Burden, whose characterization is frequently contradictory and whom many critics have difficulty interpreting, can be understood if we see him as the embodiment of Cather’s own lesbian desire. Fetterly notes, among other evidence, that despite Jim’s frequent admissions of love for Ántonia and of his desire to have her as his sweetheart or his wife, for some unexplained reason he can’t have her. Furthermore, he behaves in ways that are traditionally female. He spends most of his time in the kitchen, in women’s space. We never see him participating in the male world of hunting and fishing. He doesn’t identify with the men of his town and is hostile to the patriarchal privilege they abuse. And when Jim takes Ántonia’s place in the home of Wick Cutter, her sexually predatory employer whose strange behavior is frightening her, Jim doesn’t defend the woman he loves by beating up Wick. Instead, he is apparently raped in her place, for he runs home to his grandmother, repulsed and shamed by what he calls Cutter’s disgusting behavior, and he begs his grandmother to tell no one, not even the doctor. Finally, Jim reveals a loathing of male sexuality, for example in his revulsion toward phallic masculinity evident in his description of “the extraordinarily phallic snake of Book I” (Fetterly 152):

他那令人作呕的男性气质，他那令人厌恶的流畅动作，不知怎的让我感到恶心。他像我的腿一样粗壮，看起来好像用磨盘都碾不碎他身上那令人作呕的生命力……他就像古老而最古老的邪恶化身。

His abominable masculinity, his loathsome, fluid motion, somehow made me sick. He was as thick as my leg, and looked as if millstones couldn’t crush the disgusting vitality out of him. … He seemed like the ancient, eldest Evil.

（Cather 45–47；引自 Fetterly 152）

(Cather 45–47; quoted in Fetterly 152)

费特利认为，当我们意识到吉姆是凯瑟的化身时，这些叙事问题就迎刃而解了；而当我们得知这个故事是自传体小说时，这一点就更有意义了。

These narrative problems are resolved, Fetterly argues, when we realize that Jim is a stand-in for Cather, which makes even more sense when we learn that the tale is autobiographical.

女同性恋批评家可能执行的另一项任务是论证，即使现有的传记资料仅表明作家与另一位女性之间存在一种充满激情的情感纽带，一种“浪漫的友谊”，其文学作品也足以确立作家的女同性恋身份。例如，宝拉·贝内特令人信服地论证了艾米莉·狄金森的诗歌策略揭示了其诗歌中同性恋的维度，贝内特指出，这与她“一生中与女性的关系”所获得的“巨大的情感和性方面的慰藉”有关（109）。例如，狄金森的诗歌策略之一是将阳具意象与恐惧和厌恶联系起来。正如我们在《我早早出发——带上了我的狗》（第520首诗）中所见，被大海追逐的“珍珠”（其“溢出”显然是男性化的，也显然是性方面的）使人惊恐逃窜，因为她害怕大海会将她吞噬。同样地，在《冬天在我的房间里》（第 1670 首诗）中，说话者被一条“虫子——/粉红色，瘦长而温暖”的存在所困扰，当它变成“一条蛇……周身环绕着力量”时，这让她感到恐惧和厌恶。

Another task a lesbian critic might perform is to argue that a writer’s literary output establishes her lesbian status even when available biographical material posits only a passionate emotional bond, a “romantic friendship,” with another woman. For example, Paula Bennett argues persuasively that Emily Dickinson’s poetic strategies reveal a homoerotic dimension of the author’s poetry that is related, Bennett points out, to the “enormous amount of comfort, both emotional and sexual,” she drew from her “relationships with women throughout her life” (109). For example, among other poetic strategies, Dickinson associates phallic imagery with fear and revulsion. As we see in “I started Early – Took my Dog” (poem #520), the speaker, pursued by the sea (whose “overflow” of “Pearl” is obviously male and obviously sexual), flees in terror because she fears it will consume her. Similarly, in “In Winter in My Room” (poem #1670), the speaker is disturbed by the presence of a “Worm—/Pink, lank and warm” that terrifies and repels her when it transforms itself into “A snake … ringed with power.”

相反，贝内特观察到，狄金森将女性性意象——特别是与阴蒂和阴唇相关的意象——与“伊甸园般的欢愉”（111）联系起来，这些欢愉“通常是口交的”，并以“开放、渴望、丰盈”（110）的方式描述。例如，《我能写的所有信》（第334首诗）呼唤一位爱人（以蜂鸟的迷你形态出现，其性别被含糊地用“它”指代）“演奏它……/……只是啜饮”她的“红宝石般的深渊，未曾枯竭，我为你藏匿，唇。”同样，《我为你照料我的花朵》（第339首诗）也包含诸如“我的倒挂金钟珊瑚般的缝隙/撕裂——播种者——沉睡”和“我的仙人掌——裂开胡须/露出喉咙”等女性性意象。无论这些诗歌中的叙述者是否采用男性视角，狄金森的“关注点显然在于女性性欲本身”（111），并且“表明诗人对自身性别的强烈生理吸引力”（110）。值得注意的是，狄金森去世后，她的家人要求对诗人的信件进行编辑，以掩盖狄金森对她终生挚友苏珊·吉尔伯特炽热的爱恋的证据。

Conversely, Bennett observes, Dickinson links female sexual imagery – specifically, images associated with the clitoris and vaginal lips – with “Edenic pleasures” (111) that are “typically oral” and described in a manner that is “open, eager, and lush” (110). For example, “All the letters I can write” (poem #334) calls upon a lover (who is represented by the diminutive form of a hummingbird and whose gender is referred to, ambiguously, as “it”) to “Play it … / … just sipped” her “Depths of Ruby, undrained, I Hid, Lip, for Thee.” Similarly, “I tend my flowers for thee” (poem #339) includes such female sexual images as “My Fuchsia’s Coral Seams / Rip – while the Sower – dreams” and “My Cactus – splits her Beard / To show her throat.” Whether or not the speaker in such poems adopts a male point of view, Dickinson’s “focus is obviously on female sexuality itself” (111) and “bespeaks the poet’s overwhelming physical attraction to her own sex” (110). Significantly, after Dickinson’s death, family members requested that publication of the poet’s letters be edited to suppress evidence of Dickinson’s passionate love for Susan Gilbert, her lifelong friend.

女同性恋批评家可能承担的另一项任务是，揭示一部意图明显为异性恋的文本如何蕴含重要的女同性恋维度。芭芭拉·史密斯运用一种不要求同性欲望的女同性恋定义——例如，认同女性的女性——来论证托妮·莫里森的小说《苏拉》（1973）中蕴含的这一维度。小说讲述了两个年轻的黑人女孩为了在种族主义和性别歧视的重压下生存而结盟的故事。除了史密斯所指出的莫里森“一贯批判异性恋的男女关系、婚姻和家庭制度”（165页）之外，这位批评家还有力地论证了小说中唯一深刻而持久的爱存在于两个女性之间：主人公内尔和苏拉。她们彼此认同，彼此给予情感支持，没有任何男人，包括内尔的丈夫，在她们的生活中比彼此更重要或更有影响力。事实上，这两个女人与男性的关系都令人不满。最后，苏拉的非传统行为——她拒绝结婚生子，对与她发生一夜情的已婚男人不屑一顾等等——代表了一种越轨的性行为，一种对父权制规范的违背，这与女同性恋对父权制的反抗有着强烈的共鸣。事实上，苏拉与男人上床，并非为了体验与他们之间的情感交流（这种交流并没有发生），而是为了了解她内在的力量，体验她内心的和谐。

Another task a lesbian critic might perform is to show the ways in which a text that is clearly heterosexual in its intention nevertheless has an important lesbian dimension. Using a definition of lesbian that does not require same-sex desire – for example, the woman-identified woman – Barbara Smith make this case for Toni Morrison’s Sula (1973), in which two young black girls bond together to survive the racism and sexism that constrict their lives. In addition to what Smith notes as Morrison’s “consistently critical stance toward the heterosexual institutions of male/female relationships, marriage, and the family” (165), this critic argues forcefully that the only deep and sustained love experienced in the novel is between two women: the main characters Nel and Sula. Their primary identification is with each other, their primary emotional sustenance comes from each other, and no man, including Nel’s husband, is more influential or important in their lives than each other. In fact, both women’s relationships with men are unsatisfactory. Finally, Sula’s unconventional behavior – her refusal to marry and have children, her dismissive attitude toward the married men with whom she has one-night stands, and the like – represents a transgressive sexuality, a violation of patriarchal norms, that resonates strongly with lesbian violations of patriarchy. Indeed, Sula goes to bed with men, not in order to experience communion with them, which doesn’t occur, but in order to learn about her own internal power and experience her own inner harmony.

当然，女同性恋文学批评家还承担着许多其他任务。其中一项任务是，她们试图界定女同性恋文学传统的构成要素，以及哪些作家和作品属于这一传统。她们试图确定女同性恋诗学的构成要素，即一种独特的女同性恋写作方式。她们分析女同性恋作家的性取向/情感取向如何影响其文学表达；种族与性取向/情感取向的交织如何影响有色人种女同性恋的文学表达；以及阶级、种族与性取向/情感取向的交织如何影响出身工人阶级的女同性恋的文学表达。女同性恋批评家还会分析特定文本的性政治，例如，考察女同性恋角色或“男性化”女性在女同性恋文学作品中或关于女同性恋的文学作品中的形象塑造。她们也会研究经典的异性恋文本，以了解这些文本明确体现了哪些对女同性恋的态度。或者隐含地。他们还会识别并纠正那些未能认识到或欣赏特定文学作品中女同性恋维度的异性恋中心主义文学解读。

Of course, lesbian literary critics perform a number of other tasks. Among other things, they try to decide what constitutes a lesbian literary tradition and what writers and works belong to it. They attempt to determine what might constitute a lesbian poetics, that is, a uniquely lesbian way of writing. They analyze how the sexual/emotional orientation of lesbian writers has affected their literary expression; how the intersection of race and sexual/emotional orientation has affected the literary expression of lesbians of color; and how the intersection of class, race, and sexual/emotional orientation has affected the literary expression of lesbians of working-class origins. Lesbian critics also analyze the sexual politics of specific texts by examining, for example, how lesbian characters or “masculine” women are portrayed in literature by and about lesbians. They study canonized heterosexual texts, too, in order to learn what attitudes toward lesbians they embody explicitly or implicitly. And they identify and correct heterosexist interpretations of literature that fail to recognize or appreciate the lesbian dimensions of specific literary works.

显然，这些研究并未涵盖整个领域，它们仅仅是一些代表性的例子。只有亲自阅读女同性恋批评家的作品，才能真正了解她们研究的广度和深度，而她们的研究也在逐年扩展和发展。

Clearly, these tasks do not exhaust the field. They are intended merely as a representative sample. Only your own reading of the work done by lesbian critics will acquaint you with the breadth and depth of their enterprise, which continues to expand and evolve with each passing year.

此外，如果您还没有读过当代女同性恋作家的文学作品，不妨去了解一下，她们的作品广受好评。这些作家包括珍妮特·温特森、格洛丽亚·安扎尔杜亚、莱斯利·费恩伯格、明妮·布鲁斯·普拉特、丽塔·梅·布朗、保拉·冈恩·艾伦、多萝西·艾莉森、安·艾伦·肖克利、莫妮克·维蒂格、朱厄尔·戈麦斯、琼·阿诺德、瓦莱丽·米纳、贝基·伯莎、简·鲁尔、伯莎·哈里斯、莎拉·舒尔曼、妮可·布罗萨德、凯蒂·崔，当然还有奥德丽·洛德和艾德丽安·里奇。

In addition, you might want to acquaint yourself, if you haven’t already done so, with literary works by contemporary lesbian writers, who are receiving much critical acclaim. These writers include, among others, Jeanette Winterson, Gloria Anzaldúa, Leslie Feinberg, Minnie Bruce Pratt, Rita Mae Brown, Paula Gunn Allen, Dorothy Allison, Ann Allen Shockley, Monique Wittig, Jewelle Gomez, June Arnold, Valerie Miner, Becky Birtha, Jane Rule, Bertha Harris, Sarah Shulman, Nicole Brossard, Kitty Tsui, and, of course, Audre Lorde and Adrienne Rich.

同性恋批评

Gay criticism

正如我们前面提到的，与女同性恋批评不同，男同性恋批评往往并不着重于定义同性恋。在当今美国白人中产阶级社会，男性之间的性关系，甚至仅仅是男性对男性的性欲，通常被认为是同性恋的普遍标准。然而，并非所有文化都认同这种定义。例如，在一些拉丁美洲文化中，仅仅与男性发生性行为或对男性产生性欲，并不意味着该男性就是同性恋。只要他表现得像传统的男性那样——强壮、强势、果断——并且始终扮演男性性行为中的插入者角色（从不接受口交或肛交），他仍然是一个“男子汉”，一个“真正的”男人。作为“男子汉”，他可以与男性和女性发生性关系，而不会被视为北美人所说的同性恋。在二十世纪初，美国白人工人阶级文化中也使用了同样的同性恋定义：只有那些在性行为中允许被男性插入，并且表现得像传统女性一样——顺从、娇羞、调情、“温柔”——的男性才被认为是同性恋。

As we noted above, unlike lesbian criticism, gay criticism doesn’t tend to focus on efforts to define homosexuality. Sexual relations between men, or even just the sexual desire of one man for another, is the generally accepted criterion of gayness in white middle-class America today. Nevertheless, not all cultures share this definition. For example, in some Latin American cultures, the mere fact of sexual activity with or desire for another male does not indicate that a man is homosexual. As long as he behaves in a traditionally masculine manner – strong, dominant, decisive – and consistently assumes the male sexual role as penetrator (never allowing himself to be penetrated, orally or anally), a man remains a macho, a “real” man. As a macho, a man can have sex with both men and women and not be considered what North Americans call homosexual. The same definition of homosexuality was used in white American working-class culture around the turn of the twentieth century: only men who allowed themselves to be penetrated by a man during sex and behaved in a traditionally feminine manner – submissive, coy, flirtatious, “soft” – were considered homosexual.

古雅典也对当代白人中产阶级关于同性恋的固有观念提出了类似的质疑。在古雅典，同性恋和异性恋行为之间并不存在泾渭分明的对立关系。性伴侣的选择并非基于生理性别，而是遵循种姓制度。在雅典，男性统治精英阶层的成员只能与社会地位低于自己的人发生合法的性关系，这些人包括任何年龄、任何阶级的女性、已过青春期但尚未达到公民年龄的自由民男孩、奴隶以及外国人。

A similar problem for contemporary white middle-class assumptions about homosexuality is offered by ancient Athens, where there was no polar opposition between homosexual and heterosexual behavior. Sexual partners were chosen along caste lines, not according to their biological sex. In Athens, a member of the elite male ruling class could have legitimate sexual relations only with his social inferiors: women of any age and from any class, free-born boys past the age of puberty but not old enough for citizenship, slaves, and foreigners.

事实上，直到19世纪，同性恋身份的概念，甚至“同性恋”这个词，才被盎格鲁-欧洲人所接受。美国文化。在此之前，某些性行为——通常指所有非生育性行为——被教会或国家禁止，但并不被视为特定性取向的证据。同性恋的概念出现，与医学界宣扬的“同性恋是一种病态”的观点密切相关。这就是为什么如今许多男同性恋者更愿意称自己为“男同性恋”：对许多人来说， “同性恋”一词与“同性恋是一种医学或心理疾病”的观念联系在一起。

In fact, it wasn’t until the nineteenth century that the notion of homosexual identity and even the word homosexual were adopted in Anglo-European and American culture. Before that time, certain sexual acts – generally speaking, all forms of nonprocreative sex – were forbidden by church or state, but they weren’t viewed as evidence of a specific sexual identity. The idea that one could be a homosexual came along with the idea, promoted by the medical professions, that such an identity was a form of pathology. This is why many gay men today prefer to refer to themselves as gay: the word homosexual is associated, for many, with the belief that homosexuality is a medical or psychological disorder.

同样，“手淫者”在十九世纪也成为了一种病态的性身份。如今医学界认为这是一种正常、健康的性宣泄方式，但在十九世纪却被认为极其危险，以至于患有这种“疾病”的儿童会被绑在床上，以防止他们触摸自己。此外，还有一些医生为了“治疗”小女孩而烧灼她们生殖器的案例。

Similarly, “the masturbator” also became a pathological sexual identity in the nineteenth century. An act that the medical professions today consider a normal, healthy outlet was considered so dangerous in the nineteenth century that children “suffering” from the “affliction” were tied to their beds at night to prevent their touching themselves, and there are several case histories of doctors’ burning the genitals of little girls in order to “cure” them.

关键在于，人们对同性恋的态度，如同人们对性取向的总体态度一样，因地域和历史时期而异。20世纪50年代初在美国兴起并持续至今的强烈反同性恋情绪，并不代表某种普遍存在的对同性恋的态度，甚至不能代表对同性恋的普遍定义。

The point here is that attitudes toward homosexuality, like attitudes toward sexuality in general, differ widely from one place to another and from one historical period to another. The intense antigay sentiment that emerged in an especially concentrated and virulent form in America during the early 1950s and that lingers today does not represent some kind of universally held attitude toward, or even definition of, homosexuality.

那些往往能引起同性恋评论家关注的分析，通常都归于“同性恋情怀”这一范畴。身为同性恋者，会如何影响一个人看待世界、看待自己和他人、创作和欣赏艺术音乐、创作和解读文学作品，以及体验和表达情感的方式？在像我们身处的二十一世纪初的美国这样以异性恋为主导的文化中，“同性恋情怀”包含着一种意识，即至少在某些方面，自己与主流文化成员存在差异，以及由此产生的由持续存在的隐性社会压迫所导致的复杂情感。换句话说，作为一名同性恋男性，看待世界的方式也包括如何应对作为同性恋男性所遭受的压迫。其中，同性恋情怀的三个重要领域——都与对异性恋压迫的回应有关——分别是变装、坎普艺术以及对艾滋病问题的应对。

The kinds of analyses that tend to engage the attention of gay critics often fall under the heading of gay sensibility. How does being gay influence the way one sees the world, sees oneself and others, creates and responds to art and music, creates and interprets literature, or experiences and expresses emotion? In a heterosexist culture such as the one we inhabit in the early decades of the twenty-first century in America, gay sensibility includes an awareness of being different, at least in certain ways, from the members of the mainstream, dominant culture, and the complex feelings that result from an implicit, ongoing social oppression. In other words, part of seeing the world as a gay man includes the ways in which one deals with being oppressed as a gay man. Among others, three important domains of gay sensibility, all of which involve responses to heterosexist oppression, are drag, camp, and dealing with the issue of AIDS.

变装是指穿着女性服装的行为。变装皇后是经常或以变装为职业的男同性恋者。然而，并非所有男同性恋者都会异装，并非所有异装者都是男同性恋者，也并非所有男同性恋者都认可变装。但对某些人来说，变装是一种自我表达和娱乐的方式，也可以是对传统性别角色的一种政治宣言。变装并不一定（或许也从不）包含扮演女性的幻想。相反，它是男性表达其女性特质、标新立异或不墨守成规的一种方式。对另一些男同性恋者来说，变装是一种政治行动主义形式，用于引起人们对同性恋问题的关注，批评恐同的政府和宗教政策，以及筹集资金抗击艾滋病。无论出于何种目的，变装都是一种拒绝被束缚的方式。受异性恋性别界限的束缚，以及通过挑战性别角色来让我们所有人思考自身性取向的方式。

Drag is the practice of dressing in women’s clothing. Drag queens are gay men who dress in drag on a regular basis or who do it professionally. However, not all gay people cross-dress, not all cross-dressers are gay, and not all gay people approve of drag. But for some, it’s a source of self-expression and entertainment that can also be a political statement against traditional gender roles. Drag doesn’t necessarily involve (and perhaps never involves) the fantasy that one is a woman. Rather it is a way for a man to express his feminine side or his sense of the outrageous or his nonconformity. For other gay men, drag is a form of political activism used to draw attention to gay issues, criticize homophobic government and religious policies, and raise funds to fight AIDS. Whatever the purpose, drag is a way of refusing to be intimidated by heterosexist gender boundaries and a way of getting all of us to think about our own sexuality by challenging gender roles.

女同性恋者有时也会穿异性服装。事实上，有一些变装皇后，比如埃尔维斯·赫塞尔维斯（Elvis Herselvis），她讽刺猫王模仿者，并在表演中探讨猫王的毒瘾和性取向。然而，对于女同性恋者来说，异装似乎不像对男同性恋者那样是一个重要议题。原因之一可能是，至少自20世纪60年代末以来，女性穿着男性化的服装和打扮并不被认为是离经叛道的，甚至也不被认为是不时尚的。此外，总的来说，女同性恋群体穿着男性化的服装和打扮（例如，男性化的装扮）或穿着中性化的服装和打扮（例如，20世纪70年代的女同性恋女权主义装扮）往往是一种个人自我表达和/或低调的政治宣言，并不像男同性恋的异装那样具有戏剧性。因此，尽管女同性恋者经常遭到殴打和强奸，尤其是在 20 世纪 50 年代这样的压迫时期，但她们的异装行为从未像男同性恋变装那样引起全国的关注。

Lesbians sometimes cross-dress, too. In fact, there are some drag kings, such as Elvis Herselvis, who satirizes Elvis impersonators and includes in her act a discussion of Elvis’ drug problem and sexual proclivities. However, drag doesn’t seem to be for lesbians the major issue it is for gay men. One reason may be that, at least since the late 1960s, women’s adoption of masculine attire and grooming is not considered outrageous or even unfashionable. Also, in general, the lesbian community’s adoption of male clothing and grooming (for example, butch attire) or of androgenous clothing and grooming (for example, lesbian-feminist attire of the 1970s) has tended to be a matter of personal self-expression and/or quiet political statement that hasn’t had the theatrical quality of gay drag. Therefore, although butch lesbians frequently have been beaten and raped, especially during such repressive periods as the 1950s, their cross-dressing never drew the national attention focused on gay drag.

“坎普”（Camp）一词指的是一种奔放的自我表达方式，其特点是离经叛道、矫揉造作、夸张和戏剧化。坎普风格充满讽刺、诙谐和幽默，常常模糊或跨越性别界限。事实上，当变装表演以一种浮夸、戏剧化的方式呈现时，通常被认为是坎普风格。例如，想想约翰·沃特斯1988年的经典电影《发胶星梦》（Hairspra​​y ）中，由才华横溢的演员兼变装皇后迪瓦恩（Divine）饰演的艾德娜·特恩布拉德（Edna Turnblad）一角。实际上，整部电影——以及它所启发的热门百老汇音乐剧和2007年的翻拍版——都因其坎普特质而备受赞誉。此外，坎普风格具有颠覆性，它通过以离经叛道的方式模仿权威和传统行为准则，通常是通过夸张的手势、姿势和声音，来嘲讽它们。除了《发胶星梦》 （Hairspra​​y）之外，坎普风格的经典例子还包括著名的蒙提·派森小品《约克郡谢菲尔德镇妇女协会重演珍珠港事件》（Reenactment of the Battle of Pearl Harbor by the Towns-women's Guild of Sheffield in Yorkshire）。在这个小品中，六名男子身着20世纪50年代中年妇女的裙装和帽子，跑到田野中央，用手提包互相殴打。（你可以在YouTube上找到这段视频，我想你会喜欢的。）另一个例子是长寿动画剧集《辛普森一家》第十四季第十七集《公寓里的三个同性恋》（Three Gays of the Condo ）。在这一集中，荷马·辛普森和妻子吵架后，搬去和两个同性恋男子同住。埃尔顿·约翰爵士和Lady Gaga都是坎普风格的代表人物。20世纪60年代的流行/摇滚明星达斯蒂·斯普林菲尔德也是如此，原因之一是她标志性的蓬松发型和浓妆艳抹，常常让她在舞台上呈现出一位美丽的变装皇后的形象。一个人不必是LGBTQ群体成员才能表现出某种被认为是“坎普”的行为。坎普的本质很大程度上取决于旁观者的视角，而非旁观者的意图。因此，朱迪·嘉兰和雪儿的华丽戏剧性，以及贝蒂·米德勒和麦当娜的张扬不羁，都因其坎普特质而受到许多同性恋粉丝的喜爱。就像变装一样，坎普也是一种肯定自我的方式。它体现了个人与异性恋文化的差异。这是一种化解异性恋霸权、通过笑声疗愈自我的方式。因此，它也是一种将受害者心态转化为力量的方式。

The word camp refers to a kind of exuberant self-expression characterized by irreverence, artifice, exaggeration, and theatricality. Camp is ironic, witty, and humorous and often involves a blurring or crossing of gender lines. Indeed, when drag is practiced in a flamboyant, theatrical manner, it is generally considered camp. Think, for instance, of the role of Edna Turnblad, played by gifted actor and drag queen Divine, in John Waters’ 1988 film classic Hairspray. In fact, the entire film – as well as the hit Broadway musical and 2007 remake it inspired – are generally appreciated for their camp qualities. Moreover, camp is subversive in that it mocks authority and traditional standards of behavior by imitating them in outrageous ways, often through the use of exaggerated gestures, postures, and voice. In addition to Hairspray, time-honored examples of camp include the well-known Monty Python skit entitled “Reenactment of the Battle of Pearl Harbor by the Towns-women’s Guild of Sheffield in Yorkshire,” in which six men, attired in the dresses and hats of middle-aged women from the 1950s, run into the middle of a field and beat one another with their handbags. (You can find the video on YouTube. I think you’ll enjoy it.) Another example is “Three Gays of the Condo” – season 14, episode 17 of the long-lived animated television series The Simpsons – in which Homer Simpson has a fight with his wife and moves in with two gay men. Sir Elton John and Lady Gaga are camp icons. So is Dusty Springfield, pop/rock star of the 1960s, because, among other reasons, her signature bouffant hairstyles and extremely heavy makeup often gave her the onstage appearance of a beautiful drag queen. One doesn’t have to be LGBTQ to behave in a manner that might be considered camp. Camp is as much, or more, in the eye of the beholder as in the intention of the beheld. Thus, the flamboyant theatricality of Judy Garland and Cher – and the flamboyant irreverence of Bette Midler and Madonna – are appreciated for their camp qualities by many gay fans. As in the case of drag, camp is a way of affirming one’s difference from heterosexual culture. It’s a way of disarming heterosexism and healing oneself through laughter. And thus it’s a way of transforming victimhood into power.

当然，在20世纪80年代，与艾滋病现实共存，包括与艾滋病相关的歧视，已成为同性恋群体生活的一部分。他们不得不面对这样的现实：联邦政府直到艾滋病也威胁到异性恋公民的生命时才开始资助艾滋病研究；一些医务人员仍然不愿治疗艾滋病患者或给予他们应有的尊重；在职场中遭遇针对艾滋病患者或HIV阳性者（他们虽然尚未患上艾滋病，但很可能在未来某个时候会发展成艾滋病）的歧视；以及每天承担着照顾因艾滋病去世的朋友和亲人的身心重担。这些都必然会影响同性恋男性看待世界的方式。

Of course, living with the reality of AIDS, which includes AIDS-related discrimination, became part of gay sensibility during the 1980s. It can’t help but affect the way gay men see the world to know that the federal government was reticent to fund AIDS research until the disease became a threat for heterosexual citizens as well, to be aware of the lingering reluctance of some medical professionals to treat AIDS patients or to treat them with respect, to encounter discrimination in the workplace against people who have AIDS or who are HIV positive (who do not have AIDS but who will presumably develop the disease at some future point), and to put forth the daily physical and emotional labor of caring for friends and loved ones dying of AIDS.

艾滋病于1981年首次被发现，到80年代末，一代男性已因此丧生。同性恋群体对这场全国性的公共卫生危机做出了极其积极和乐观的回应。他们组建了诸如“艾滋病解放力量联盟”（ACT UP）之类的政治组织，通过公开示威和抗议活动宣传并争取公众支持，力图促使制药公司、保险公司、政府机构和医疗官僚机构对这场疫情做出适当的应对。与此同时，女同性恋者也积极声援男同性恋者，加入他们的抗议活动，并在照顾病患和临终者方面发挥了重要作用，这两个群体之间由此诞生了一种新的团结精神。正如玛格丽特·克鲁克香克所说，“那些曾被贴上‘异类’和‘非美国式变态’标签的人，发起了一场典型的美国式自助运动，这或许是美国历史上规模最大的志愿者行动之一”（182-83页）。

AIDS was first identified in 1981, and by the end of the decade a generation of men had died from it. The gay community’s response to this national health emergency has been extremely active and positive. They have formed political organizations, such as the AIDS Coalition to Unleash Power (ACT UP), to publicize and gain support for their cause through public demonstrations and protests in an effort to get drug companies, insurance companies, government agencies, and the medical bureaucracy to respond appropriately to this epidemic. And as lesbians rallied to the support of gay men, joining their protests and playing a significant role in caring for the sick and dying, a new spirit of solidarity emerged between these two communities. As Margaret Cruikshank puts it, “those who had been labeled misfits and un-American perverts launched a typically American self-help movement which was probably one of the largest volunteer efforts in the nation’s history” (182–83).

尽管同性恋批评家和女同性恋批评家关注的理论问题不同，但他们在解读文学文本的方式上却有很多相似之处。例如，与女同性恋批评家一样，同性恋批评家也试图确定何为同性恋诗学，或一种独特的同性恋写作方式；建立同性恋文学传统；并确定哪些作家和作品属于这一传统。同性恋批评家还考察同性恋情感如何影响文学表达，并研究异性恋文本如何展现同性恋情欲维度。他们试图重新发现过去那些作品被低估、歪曲或压制的同性恋作家，包括那些被认为是异性恋的同性恋作家。他们试图确定特定文本的性政治，例如，分析同性恋角色或“女性化”男性在同性恋和异性恋文本中的形象塑造。最后，同性恋批评家会识别并纠正那些未能认识到或欣赏特定文学作品中蕴含的同性恋情感的异性恋中心主义文学解读。为了了解这些方法能够对文学产生哪些类型的洞见，让我们简要地看一下三个具体的例子：对沃尔特·惠特曼诗歌风格的分析、对……的研究当代小说家埃德蒙·怀特的作品中对同性恋身份的刻画，以及对田纳西·威廉姆斯戏剧中同性恋情感的辩护。

Despite their focus on different theoretical issues, there is a good deal of similarity in the way gay and lesbian critics approach literary texts. For example, like lesbian critics, gay critics attempt to determine what might constitute a gay poetics, or a way of writing that is uniquely gay; to establish a gay literary tradition; and to decide what writers and works belong to that tradition. Gay critics also examine how gay sensibility affects literary expression and study the ways in which heterosexual texts can have a homoerotic dimension. They try to rediscover gay writers from the past whose work was underappreciated, distorted, or suppressed, including gay writers who have been presumed heterosexual. They try to determine the sexual politics of specific texts, analyzing, for example, how gay characters or “feminine” men are portrayed in both gay and heterosexual texts. Finally, gay critics identify and correct heterosexist interpretations of literature that fail to recognize or appreciate the gay sensibility informing specific literary works. To get an idea of the kinds of insights into literature these approaches can produce, let’s take a brief look at three specific examples: an analysis of Walt Whitman’s poetic voice, a study of the representation of gay identity in the work of contemporary novelist Edmund White, and a defense of the gay sensibility in Tennessee Williams’ plays.

在《沃尔特·惠特曼的“露营”》一文中，卡尔·凯勒通过对惠特曼诗歌自我呈现方式的精彩分析，拓展了我们对惠特曼诗歌创作的理解，揭示了惠特曼的诗歌创作如何体现出一种“坎普”风格。凯勒指出：“我们可以在惠特曼诗歌中常见的叙述者身上看到这一点，例如，在《自我之歌》（1855）中，他经常使用夸张的姿态、矫揉造作的语调、歌剧般的嗓音、夸张的角色扮演以及语言的延展性”（115）。凯勒还说：“那些哀叹惠特曼声称他的诗歌……充分展现了他的个性，却又缺乏自传性细节的人，只是没有深入探究……惠特曼诗歌语言的运作机制”（115）。凯勒断言， “诗人是在表演”（115），他表演中那种略带夸张的特质，揭示了他声音和姿态中那诱人的“挑逗”（116），这种挑逗以一种幽默的方式将他与自然和他人建立联系的超验主义理想赋予了性意味。凯勒观察到，惠特曼“并非在嘲讽他所谈论的事物，而是在从中汲取乐趣”，以此“加深他对周围世界的享受”（118）。凯勒将这位诗人比作“美国文学界的梅·韦斯特”，并认为惠特曼向读者展现自我的方式并非“向我们袒露他的全部”，而是“展现他个性的各种可能性”（115）。

In “Walt Whitman Camping,” Karl Keller extends our understanding of Whitman’s poetic project through his interesting analysis of the ways in which Whitman’s poetic self-presentation is a form of camp. “We see this,” Keller argues, “in the flamboyant gestures, the exaggerated tone, the operatic voice, the inflated role-playing, the dilation of language” (115) that frequently characterize Whitman’s speaker, for example, the speaker in “Song of Myself” (1855). Keller says, “Those who have bemoaned the contradiction between Whitman’s claim that his poetry … revealed his personality well and the paucity of autobiographical detail in the poems have only failed to look … at the workings of Whitman’s voice” (115). “The poet is performing” (115), Keller asserts, and the camp quality of his performance reveals the seductive “come-on” (116) in his voice and in his pose that humorously sexualizes his transcendentalist ideals of bonding with nature and with other human beings. Whitman “is not making fun of the things he talks about but making fun out of them,” Keller observes, in order to “intensif[y] his enjoyment of the world around him” (118). Referring to the poet as “the Mae West of American literature,” Keller argues that Whitman reveals himself to the reader, not by “flashing his entire person at us,” but by “showing the range of possibilities of his personality” (115).

尼古拉斯·F·拉德尔（Nicholas F. Radel）的论文《作为他者的自我：埃德蒙·怀特作品中的身份政治》是同性恋文学批评的又一代表性范例。拉德尔指出，“同性恋身份是怀特许多作品的明确主题”，而他笔下的许多同性恋角色“未能形成连贯的自我意识”，这种失败“可以归因于性与性别差异的政治性”（175）。换言之，怀特审视了恐同的美国文化对成长于其中的男同性恋者和男孩的伤害，而这种伤害最为严重的便是他笔下同性恋角色内化的恐同症，即习得的自我憎恨。事实上，拉德尔指出，怀特的同性恋角色在他们内心深处经历了一种明显的分裂：一方面是他们所认为的“本质自我”，另一方面是“他们自己认为与自身分离的同性恋他者自我”（176）。这种与自我疏离的体验既削弱了同性恋身份，也削弱了同性恋社群。如果一个男人与自己的同性恋身份疏离，他又如何能感受到自己属于同性恋群体呢？此外，拉德尔认为，怀特作品中的自我疏离并非源于个体心理问题，而是异性恋霸权政治压迫的直接结果。因此，“我们可以将怀特的小说视为历史机制的一部分，它揭示了同性恋主体（自我）如何回应来自整个文化的政治压力”（176）。

Another representative example of gay literary criticism is Nicholas F. Radel’s thoughtful essay “Self as Other: The Politics of Identity in the Works of Edmund White.” “Gay identity,” Radel observes, “is the explicit subject of many of White’s works,” and many of his gay characters “fail to achieve a coherent sense of self,” a failure that “can be attributed to the politics of sexual and gender difference” (175). In other words, White examines the damaging effects of homophobic American culture on the gay men and boys who grow up within it, and its most damaging effect is the internalized homophobia, the learned self-hatred, of his gay characters. Indeed, Radel points out that White’s gay characters experience a distinct split within themselves between what they consider their “essential selves” and “a homosexual self as Other that they themselves conceive as being separate” from them (176). This experience of being alienated from oneself undermines both gay identity and gay community. How can a man feel he belongs to a gay community if he is alienated from his own gayness? Furthermore, Radel argues, self-alienation in White’s work is not due to individual psychological problems but is the direct result of the politics of heterosexist oppression. Therefore, “we might view White’s novels as part of the historical apparatus for revealing a gay subject [selfhood] as it responds to political pressure from the culture at large” (176).

最后，在《坎普与同性恋情怀》一文中，杰克·巴布西奥认为，同性恋情怀对每个人都有借鉴意义：它的洞见并非如某些批评家所认为的那样，仅限于同性恋群体。巴布西奥举例指出，批评家们未能充分理解坎普对人类生活的深刻洞见。田纳西·威廉姆斯笔下的女主角——其中最著名的或许是《欲望号街车》（1947）中的布兰奇·杜波依斯——之所以如此重要，是因为这些角色代表了威廉姆斯作为一名同性恋者的自身情感。换句话说，威廉姆斯笔下的女主角可以说是他本人的化身，表达了他作为同性恋者的焦虑：例如，他肉体欲望与精神追求之间的挣扎，他渴望放荡不羁却又想保持尊严，以及在以年轻人为主导的同性恋亚文化中，他对衰老的恐惧。巴布西奥指出，因此，评论家们得出结论，威廉姆斯的作品与主流异性恋文化无关。简而言之，他们认为同性恋的情感只与同性恋男性产生共鸣。

Finally, in “Camp and the Gay Sensibility,” Jack Babuscio argues that gay sensibility has something to offer everyone: the relevance of its insights is not limited, as some critics believe, to the gay community. As a case in point, Babuscio observes that critics have failed to fully appreciate the insights into human life offered by Tennessee Williams’ heroines – the most famous of whom is probably Blanche Dubois in A Streetcar Named Desire (1947) – because these characters represent Williams’ own emotions as a gay man. In other words, Williams’ heroines are Williams himself in drag, so to speak, expressing his own anxieties about being gay: for example, his battle between the demands of the flesh and those of the spirit, his desire to be promiscuous and yet still keep his pride, and his fear of aging in a youth-oriented homosexual subculture. Critics have concluded therefore, Babuscio notes, that Williams’ work is not relevant to mainstream heterosexual culture. In short, they believe that gay sensibility speaks only to gay men.

与此相反，巴布西奥断言，威廉姆斯在美国主流社会边缘的经历，使他成为“恐惧、怀疑，甚至仇恨”的对象（34），这赋予了他一种独特的视角，使他能够理解人类生活的冲突——这种独特的视角也适用于其他族裔群体——因为他不得不以一种尤为强烈的形式去面对这些冲突。此外，巴布西奥指出，对于所有优秀的作家而言，文学创作都包含着将自身经历转化为文学形式的过程。因此，当马克辛·福克在《鬣蜥之夜》（1962）中说，我们每个人迟早都会走到人生的某个阶段，不得不接受某种适合自己的生活方式时，她不仅是在对同性恋群体说话，也是在对整个人类社会说话。

In contrast, Babuscio asserts that Williams’ experience on the margins of mainstream America, as an object of “fear, suspicion, and, even, hatred” (34), gave him a privileged position from which to understand the conflicts of human life – the same privileged position occupied, for example, by members of racial minorities – because he had to deal with those conflicts in a particularly intense form. Furthermore, Babuscio notes, the act of literary creation involves, for all good writers, the transformation of their own experience into literary form. So when Maxine Faulk, in The Night of the Iguana (1962), says that we all reach a point in our lives, sooner or later, where we must settle for something that works for us, she is speaking not just to the gay community but to the entire human community.

当然，正如我们之前讨论女同性恋文学批评时一样，这里提供的男同性恋批评案例并非涵盖所有领域，而仅仅是男同性恋批评家所做工作的代表性样本。您自己阅读男同性恋批评作品将有助于您更深入地理解这一日益丰富的领域。

Of course, just as in the case of our discussion of lesbian literary criticism, the examples of gay criticism provided here do not exhaust the field but are intended only as a representative sample of the kind of work done by gay critics. Your own reading of gay criticism will expand your understanding of this growing body of work.

此外，如果您尚未了解当代同性恋作家的文学作品，不妨去看看，他们的作品广受好评。这些作家包括：大卫·费恩伯格、托尼·库什纳、大卫·利维特、埃德蒙·怀特、阿米斯特德·莫平、保罗·莫内特、马克·多蒂、兰迪·希尔茨、丹尼斯·库珀、尼尔·巴特利特、艾伦·古尔加努斯、大卫·塞达里斯、安德鲁·霍勒兰、塞缪尔·R·德兰尼、戴尔·佩克、约翰·雷奇、保罗·罗素、马修·施塔德勒和彼得·韦尔特纳等。

In addition, you might want to acquaint yourself, if you haven’t already done so, with literary works by contemporary gay writers, who are receiving much critical acclaim. These writers include, among others, David Feinberg, Tony Kushner, David Leavitt, Edmund White, Armistead Maupin, Paul Monette, Mark Doty, Randy Shilts, Dennis Cooper, Neil Bartlett, Allan Gurganus, David Sedaris, Andrew Holleran, Samuel R. Delany, Dale Peck, John Rechy, Paul Russell, Matthew Stadler, and Peter Weltner.

酷儿批评

Queer criticism

对于初涉同性恋批评领域的学生来说，他们最先提出的问题之一就是：为什么同性恋者会选择带有恐同色彩的“酷儿” （queer）一词来指代他们自身学科中的一种研究方法？我认为这个问题有多种答案，而这些答案也将有助于我们了解酷儿理论的一些基本前提。

One of the first questions asked by students new to the study of gay and lesbian criticism is why gay men and women have chosen the homophobic word queer to designate an approach within their own discipline. I think there are several answers to that question, and they will serve as an introduction to some of the basic premises of queer theory.

首先，使用“酷儿”（queer）一词可以被视为一种尝试，旨在将该词从其恐同的用法中重新定义，以表明不应允许异性恋主义者来定义LGBTQ群体的经历。定义行为本身也是一种尝试。自我指称是一种强有力的举动，它传达的信息包括：“我们不怕被看见！”；“你无法定义我们是谁——我们自己定义自己！”；以及“我们为与众不同而自豪！”或者，正如一句流行的酷儿口号所概括的那样：“我们就在这里，我们是酷儿——习惯就好！”正如许多LGBTQ群体成员所认识到的，“酷儿”一词既是压迫的工具，也是变革的工具。

First, the use of the term queer can be seen as an attempt to reappropriate the word from what has been its homophobic usage in order to demonstrate that heterosexists shouldn’t be allowed to define LGBTQ experience. The act of defining the terms of one’s own self-reference is a powerful move that says, among other things, “We’re not afraid to be seen!”; “You don’t tell us who we are – we tell us who we are!”; and “We’re proud to be different!” Or, as the popular queer slogan sums it up, “We’re here, we’re queer – get used to it!” As many members of the LGBTQ community have learned, the word queer is a tool of oppression, but it’s also a tool of change.

此外，一些LGBTQ群体采用“酷儿”（queer）一词作为包容性范畴，指代女同性恋、男同性恋、双性恋、跨性别者以及所有出于各种原因不认为自己是异性恋的人所共有的政治或文化立场。如此使用，“酷儿”一词试图弥合此前因白人中产阶级背景而分裂的阵营。这些分裂部分源于20世纪70年代初同性恋解放运动和女同性恋女权主义运动的白人中产阶级根基。作为白人中产阶级的产物，这些运动未能意识到自身所享有的白人中产阶级特权。因此，在整个70年代乃至80年代，有色人种同性恋者以及工人阶级出身的男同性恋和女同性恋者的经历普遍被忽视，因为这些群体几乎没有机会在同性恋权力结构中担任显赫的领导职位。此外，某些同性恋性表达形式被排斥或边缘化，例如在20世纪50年代和60年代女同性恋文化中扮演重要角色的“女汉子-女阴柔”型女同性恋伴侣。这类伴侣在穿着、仪容和个人风格方面与异性恋伴侣相似​​。尽管他们在情感或性关系上未必与异性恋伴侣相同，但人们通常认为他们如此，因此他们被批评为复制了异性恋关系中普遍存在的权力失衡。“酷儿”（queer）一词作为一个包容性术语，旨在通过提供一个所有LGBTQ群体都能归属的集体身份来弥合这些分歧。

Furthermore, some LGBTQ people have adopted the word queer as an inclusive category for referring to a common political or cultural ground shared by lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and all people who, for whatever reasons, do not consider themselves heterosexual. Used in this way, the term queer tries to reunite the heretofore divided camps that resulted, in part, from the white middle-class roots of the gay liberation and lesbian feminist movements of the early 1970s. As products of the white middle class, these movements were unable to perceive their own white middle-class privilege. As a result, through the 1970s and into the 1980s, the experiences of gay people of color and of working-class gay men and lesbians were generally ignored, for these groups had little or no opportunity to assume visible leadership positions within the gay power structure. In addition, certain forms of gay sexual expression were excluded or marginalized, such as the butch–femme lesbian couples who played such an important role in lesbian culture during the 1950s and 1960s. Butch–femme couples resemble heterosexual couples in terms of clothing, grooming, and personal style. Although they did not necessarily resemble heterosexual couples in terms of emotional or sexual relatedness, it was usually assumed that they did, and they were therefore criticized for reproducing the same power imbalance generally found in heterosexual relationships. The word queer, then, as an inclusive term, seeks to heal these divisions by offering a collective identity to which all LGBTQ people can belong.

然而，在大多数情况下，“酷儿”一词被用来指代一种特定的理论视角。从理论角度来看，“男同性恋”和“女同性恋”这两个词暗示着一个可定义的范畴——同性恋——它显然与另一个可定义的范畴——异性恋——相对立。然而，对于酷儿理论而言，性取向的范畴不能用同性恋/异性恋这种简单的对立来定义。酷儿理论借鉴了解构主义对人类主体性（自我）的洞见，认为它是一个流动、碎片化、动态的、由各种可能的“自我”构成的集合体，并将个体性取向定义为一个流动、碎片化、动态的、由各种可能的性取向构成的集合体。我们的性取向在人生的不同阶段，甚至在一周的不同时间点都可能有所不同，因为性取向是一个动态的欲望范围。对我们所有人来说，男同性恋、女同性恋、双性恋和异性恋都是性取向可能性连续体上的各种可能性。这些类别对不同个体而言的意义，也会受到他们如何看待自身种族和阶级身份的影响。因此，性取向并非完全由我们的生理性别（男性或女性）或文化对生理性别的诠释所决定。性被纳入性别角色（男性或女性）的范畴。性超越了这些定义，它拥有自身的意志、创造力和表达需求。

For the most part, however, the word queer is used to indicate a specific theoretical perspective. From a theoretical point of view, the words gay and lesbian imply a definable category – homosexuality – that is clearly opposite to another definable category: heterosexuality. However, for queer theory, categories of sexuality cannot be defined by such simple oppositions as homosexual/heterosexual. Building on deconstruction’s insights into human subjectivity (selfhood) as a fluid, fragmented, dynamic collectivity of possible “selves,” queer theory defines individual sexuality as a fluid, fragmented, dynamic collectivity of possible sexualities. Our sexuality may be different at different times over the course of our lives or even at different times over the course of a week because sexuality is a dynamic range of desire. Gay sexuality, lesbian sexuality, bisexuality, and heterosexuality are, for all of us, possibilities along a continuum of sexual possibilities. And what these categories mean to different individuals will be influenced by how they conceive their own racial and class identities as well. Thus, sexuality is completely controlled neither by our biological sex (male or female) nor by the way our culture translates biological sex into gender roles (masculine or feminine). Sexuality exceeds these definitions and has a will, a creativity, an expressive need of its own.

此外，异性恋并非定义同性恋的参照标准，因为人类性取向的复杂性无法用同性恋和异性恋这样狭隘的概念来完全理解。首先，这些概念将性取向简化为伴侣的生理性别，或者用心理学术语来说，简化为性对象的选择。然而，构成人类性欲的因素远不止于此。正如伊芙·科索夫斯基·塞奇威克所论证的那样，除了同性或异性对象选择之外，任何其他成对的对立关系都能更好地理解人类性取向的复杂性。例如，对性取向的定义可以基于对年长者或年幼者的偏好，对人或动物的偏好，对单一伴侣或群体活动的偏好，对自我满足（如自慰）或对各种不同伴侣的偏好。性取向的其他维度甚至与性对象的选择无关。例如，塞奇威克指出，对性取向的定义可能基于诸如“有性高潮/无性高潮、非商业性/商业性、仅使用身体/使用人造物品、私下/公开、自发/预先安排”之类的对立概念（57）。或者，对性取向的定义可能基于对特定行为、感觉或身体类型的偏好。

Moreover, heterosexuality is not a norm against which homosexuality can be defined because the range of human sexuality cannot be completely understood in terms of such limited concepts as homosexual and heterosexual. For one thing, these concepts reduce sexuality to the biological sex of one’s partner, or, in psychological terms, one’s object choice. There are a host of other factors that make up human sexual desire. As Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick argues, the intricacies of human sexuality could be understood just as well, or better, in terms of any number of paired opposites other than same-sex or different-sex object choice. For example, the definition of one’s sexuality might be based on one’s preference for someone older or younger, for a human or an animal, for a single partner or a group activity, for oneself alone (as in masturbation) or for a variety of different partners. Other dimensions of sexuality don’t even involve object choice. For example, Sedgwick notes, the definition of one’s sexuality might be based on such oppositions as “orgasmic/nonorgasmic, noncommercial/commercial, using bodies only/using manufactured objects, in private/in public, spontaneous/scripted” (57). Or the definition of one’s sexuality might be based on one’s preference for particular acts, sensations, or physical types.

因此，对于酷儿理论而言，我们的性取向在很大程度上是社会建构的，因为它基于我们所处文化对性取向的定义方式。我们之前在讨论古雅典时已经看到了性取向社会建构的例子，当时的性别分类基于一种不区分男女的等级制度；此外，在一些拉丁美洲文化、20世纪初的美国工人阶级以及当今的美国白人中产阶级中，对同性恋的定义也截然不同。简而言之，我们的性取向或许是与生俱来的，但对恰当性别行为的定义却是社会建构的。正是基于这种性取向是社会建构的信念，我们才努力在解读古代文学作品时，不仅要从我们自身的性取向定义出发，还要从该文学作品诞生的文化背景下的性取向定义出发。

For queer theory, then, our sexuality is socially constructed to the extent that it is based on the ways in which sexuality is defined by the culture in which we live. We saw examples of the social construction of sexuality earlier, when we discussed ancient Athens, where sexual categories were based on a caste system that didn’t differentiate between male and female, and the very different definitions of homosexuality operating in some Latin American cultures, in early-twentieth-century working-class America, and in white middle-class America today. In short, our sexual orientation may indeed be inborn, but definitions of appropriate gender behavior are socially constructed. The belief that sexuality is, in this way, socially constructed is behind efforts to read literature from the past not just in terms of our own definitions of sexuality, but in terms of those definitions operating in the culture from which that literature emerged.

显然， “酷儿”（queer）一词在当今文学研究中具有多种含义。作为一个包容性术语，它可以指任何从LGBTQ视角解读文本的文学批评。因此，前文讨论的任何同性恋批评案例都可以被纳入酷儿论文集。然而，如果我们仅限于其更为狭义的理论含义——即其解构维度——酷儿批评解读文本旨在揭示其对性取向范畴的表述中存在的问题，换言之，旨在展现同性恋和异性恋这两个范畴如何瓦解、重叠，或者无法充分体现人类性取向的动态多样性。这类解读可能相当复杂。以下是一些简化的例子。

Clearly, the word queer has a range of meanings in literary studies today. As an inclusive term, it can refer to any piece of literary criticism that interprets a text from an LGBTQ perspective. Therefore, any of the examples of gay and lesbian criticism discussed earlier could be included in a collection of queer essays. However, if we restrict ourselves to its narrower theoretical meaning – its deconstructive dimension – queer criticism reads texts to reveal the problematic quality of their representations of sexual categories, in other words, to show the various ways in which the categories homosexual and heterosexual break down, overlap, or do not adequately represent the dynamic range of human sexuality. These kinds of readings can be rather complex. Here are a few simplified examples.

对威廉·福克纳的《献给艾米丽的玫瑰》（1931）进行酷儿解读，或许可以探讨传统的性别认同定义（男性与女性）以及性取向（同性恋或异性恋）无法解释或概括艾米莉·格里尔森的性格。她的性别并非固定不变，而是在男性和女性特质之间游走。她既是身着白衣、纤细苗条、受父亲管束的处女，又是桀骜不驯、不顾阶级规范和道德准则，从霍默·巴伦手中夺取一切（包括他的生命）的叛逆个体。她既是教授瓷器彩绘这门女性艺术的孩童般的隐士，又是拥有铁灰色头发、如同精力充沛的男性般强势的存在，她将自己的意志强加于男性主导的权力结构之上，包括邮局、税务局、教会，以及药剂师所代表的医疗行业。

A queer reading of William Faulkner’s “A Rose for Emily” (1931) might examine how traditional definitions of gender identity (masculine versus feminine) and sexuality (homosexual versus heterosexual) fail to explain or contain the character of Emily Greirson. Her gender categorization is not fixed but crosses back and forth between the masculine and the feminine. She’s both the slender virgin in white dominated by her father and the defiant individualist who violates class norms and moral law to take what she wants from Homer Barron, including his life. She’s both the childlike recluse who teaches the feminine art of china painting and the dominant presence with iron-gray hair, like that of a vigorous man, who imposes her will on the male power structure, including the post office, the tax collectors, the church, and, in the person of the pharmacist, the medical profession.

更重要的是，对艾米丽的刻画超越了同性恋与异性恋的二元对立。就生理性别而言，荷马和艾米丽是一对异性恋伴侣：他是男人，她是女人。然而，正如我们刚才所见，文本将艾米丽的性别建构为在女性特质和男性特质之间摇摆不定的状态。事实上，许多传统上与男性相关的强烈反叛行为，在艾米丽与荷马的关系中都被赋予了她。因此，就性别行为而言，我们可以认为，荷马和艾米丽至少在象征意义上是一对酷儿伴侣：他们的性别都被赋予了男性特征。因此，《献给艾米丽的玫瑰》这部表面上讲述异性恋激情与越轨的作品，同时也是（或者更确切地说）一部酷儿作品，它揭示了传统性别和性取向定义的局限性。

More tellingly, the characterization of Emily exceeds the opposition between homosexual and heterosexual. In terms of their biological sex, Homer and Emily are a heterosexual couple: he’s a man; she’s a woman. However, as we’ve just seen, the text constructs Emily’s gender as a vacillation between the feminine and the masculine. Indeed, much of the powerfully defiant behavior traditionally associated with men is ascribed to Emily during her relationship with Homer. In terms of gender behavior, then, one might argue that Homer and Emily, symbolically at least, are a queer couple: they are both gendered as men. Thus, “A Rose for Emily,” ostensibly a text about heterosexual passion and transgression, is also (or more so) a queer text that reveals the limits of traditional definitions of gender and sexuality.

同样，从酷儿视角解读沃尔特·惠特曼的《自我之歌》或许会探讨这首诗的情色维度如何要求我们拓展对性的理解。惠特曼这首杰出诗作的标志之一是其对生活的热情回应：诗中的叙述者（自称为惠特曼）沉醉于自然之美，体验着与来自各行各业的美国人的精神联结，并歌颂着生命本身的纯粹喜悦。正如我们之前所见，评论家卡尔·凯勒分析了惠特曼的坎普风格如何揭示出一种诱人的语调和姿态，这种语调和姿态以一种幽默的方式将诗人与自然和他人建立联结的超验主义理想性化。然而，如果我们以酷儿视角解读这首诗，我们或许会以凯勒未曾关注的方式，聚焦于惠特曼对体验的情色化，因为它超越了当代白人中产阶级对同性恋的定义。有人可能会认为，《自我之歌》中所展现的性欲过于流动，无法被局限于男性同性欲望的范畴之内。

Similarly, a queer reading of Walt Whitman’s “Song of Myself” might examine how the poem’s erotic dimension requires us to expand our understanding of the sexual. One of the hallmarks of Whitman’s remarkable poem is its exuberant response to life: the speaker, who identifies himself as Whitman, revels in the beauty of nature, experiences spiritual union with fellow Americans from all walks of life, and celebrates the pure joy of just being alive. As we saw earlier, critic Karl Keller examines how Whitman’s camp style reveals, among other things, a seductive tone of voice and pose that humorously sexualizes the poet’s transcendentalist ideals of bonding with nature and with other human beings. Reading the poem through a queer lens, however, we might focus, in ways that Keller does not, on Whitman’s eroticization of experience as it exceeds the contemporary white middle-class definition of homosexuality. For one might argue that the sexuality represented in “Song of Myself” is too fluid to be contained within the boundaries of male same-sex desire.

事实上，这首诗对性的隐含定义包含了情欲体验的诸多维度，正如我们之前所见，伊芙·科索夫斯基·塞奇威克认为，这些维度在以同性恋/异性恋对立为框架的性定义中被忽略了。在惠特曼的视角下，几乎所有体验都具有强烈的情欲特质：他不仅对在河中沐浴的年轻男子（传统的同性恋情欲意象）进行了情欲化的描写，也对远处注视他们的年轻女子以及自然环境本身进行了情欲化的描绘，后者既私密（与世隔绝），又公开（暴露在外）。同样，惠特曼的视角不仅赋予了……情欲化，而且……诗人不仅描绘了男女在各种工作中展现的健康体魄，也描绘了他们工作的场所：雄伟的山脉、肥沃的平原、繁忙的港口和繁华的城市。此外，诗人还对受人尊敬的老人、动物的力量与宁静、大海以及他自身身体的每一个部位都赋予了情色意味。因此，对《自我之歌》的一种另类解读或许会认为，惠特曼的诗歌并非同性恋情色，而是宇宙情色；或者更准确地说，只有超越基于生物性别或基于选择对象本身的性取向定义，才能充分理解惠特曼的同性恋情色。

Indeed, the poem’s implicit definition of sexuality includes many of those dimensions of erotic experience that, as we saw earlier, Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick argues have been neglected in sexual definitions structured by the homosexual/heterosexual opposition. Under Whitman’s gaze, almost all experience has an intensely erotic quality: he offers erotic descriptions not just of young men bathing in a river (a traditional homoerotic image), but of the young woman watching them from a distance, and of the natural setting itself, which is simultaneously private (isolated) and public (out in the open). Similarly, Whitman’s gaze eroticizes not only the healthy bodies of men and women at their various modes of employment, but the modes of employment as well, and the places in which they perform them: the magnificent mountains, the fertile plains, the busy harbors, and the thriving cities. In addition, the poet eroticizes – among other persons, places, things, and activities – venerable old men and women, the strength and serenity of animals, the sea, and every conceivable zone of his own body. A queer reading of “Song of Myself” might argue, therefore, that Whitman’s poem is not homoerotic but cosmically erotic or, perhaps more accurately, that Whitman’s homoeroticism can be fully comprehended only by transcending definitions of human sexuality that rest on the biological sex of one’s object choice or on object choice at all.

最后，对托妮·莫里森的《宠儿》 （1987）进行酷儿解读，或许可以探究这部小说丰富的情感内涵和多层次的意义，部分依赖于它对同性之爱与异性之爱、以及“自然”与“非自然”之间传统界限的跨越、转化或摒弃。例如，宠儿模仿她在树林中看到的交配乌龟（即模仿自然），与保罗·D发生性关系，并因此怀孕（小说结尾处她隆起的腹部以及前来营救塞丝的女性提及她怀孕，便可知晓）。然而，更深层次的解读是，宠儿“孕育”的是她自己：她试图孕育一个全新的自我，一个能够融入塞丝和丹佛所处的自然世界的新自我，从而永远地从不断威胁着要吞噬她的幽灵般的超自然黑暗中挣脱出来。而这种“孕育”没有父亲。更确切地说，这部作品有两个母亲：贝拉维德和塞丝。贝拉维德如同一个贪婪的情人，吞噬着塞丝的生命，孕育着自己的生命。我们亲眼目睹了这一过程：塞丝日渐消瘦，而贝拉维德则日渐丰腴。这条叙事线索的背景是同性之爱——丹佛、贝拉维德和塞丝之间融合了亲情与浪漫的奉献——这种爱远比贝拉维德与保罗·D之间如同行尸走肉般的性爱更加强烈，并且至少在一段时间内，它战胜了保罗·D和塞丝的异性恋关系。事实上，贝拉维德对塞丝的炽热依恋，如同丹佛对贝拉维德的依恋一样，都以浪漫甚至带有性暗示的语言来描写，蕴含着小说中最强烈的情感力量。因此， 《宠儿》充满了酷儿特质——拒绝将自己局限于传统的性观念和自然观念——这在很大程度上促成了小说的叙事发展、主题内容和情感力量。

Finally, a queer reading of Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987) might explore the ways in which the novel’s evocative richness and multilayered meanings depend in part on its crossing or transforming or abandoning traditional demarcations between samesex and opposite-sex love and between the “natural” and the “unnatural.” For example, imitating the mating turtles she sees in the woods (that is, imitating the natural), Beloved has sex with Paul D and presumably becomes pregnant as a result (witness her swollen belly near the novel’s close and the reference to her pregnancy by the women who come to rescue Sethe). In a more meaningful sense, however, Beloved is “pregnant” with herself: she’s trying to give birth to herself, to a new self able to take its place in the natural world inhabited by Sethe and Denver, and thereby emerge permanently from the ghostly, supernatural darkness that continually threatens to swallow her up. And this “pregnancy” has no father. Rather, it has two mothers: Beloved and Sethe. For Beloved, like a predatory lover, consumes Sethe’s life in order to give birth to her own, which we see quite literally as Sethe grows thinner while Beloved grows larger. And this strand of the narrative occurs against a backdrop of same-sex love – a blend of familial and romantic devotion among Denver, Beloved, and Sethe – that is much more powerful than Beloved’s zombielike sex with Paul D and that triumphs, at least temporarily, over the heterosexual coupling of Paul D and Sethe. Indeed, Beloved’s passionate attachment to Sethe, like Denver’s to Beloved, is described in romantic, even sexual, language that carries some of the most intense emotional charge of the novel. Beloved is thus infused with a queerness – with a refusal to limit itself to traditional notions of sexuality and of the natural – that is responsible for a good deal of the novel’s narrative progression, thematic content, and emotional force.

如果这些酷儿批评的例子看起来比前面提到的女同性恋和男同性恋批评的例子更加难以捉摸、更加模糊和复杂，请记住，酷儿批评的解构性项目正是试图强调人类性行为的这种难以捉摸、模糊和复杂的特质。作为女同性恋和男同性恋文学研究中最新、最具哲学性的趋势，酷儿批评预示着一个令人兴奋的理论探索和实验的未来。

If these examples of queer criticism seem more slippery, more indefinite, and more complicated than the examples of lesbian and gay criticism cited earlier, keep in mind that it is the slippery, indefinite, and complicated quality of human sexuality that queer criticism’s deconstructive project tries to underscore. As the most recent and most philosophical trend in lesbian and gay literary studies, queer criticism promises us an exciting future of theoretical exploration and experimentation.7

女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评的一些共同特征

Some shared features of lesbian, gay, and queer criticism

尽管我们刚才探讨了女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评之间的差异，但这三个领域在文学阐释的方法上存在诸多重叠之处。例如，请注意前文讨论过的女同性恋和男同性恋批评家所承担任务的相似之处。此外，许多男同性恋和女同性恋批评家将酷儿理论的一些解构性见解与更传统的女同性恋和男同性恋批评中涉及的社会和政治关切结合起来。事实上，许多酷儿理论的拥护者仍然自称为男同性恋或女同性恋批评家。

Regardless of the differences we’ve just seen among lesbian, gay, and queer criticism, there is a good deal of overlap in the ways all three domains approach literary interpretation. Note, for example, the similarities in the tasks performed by lesbian and gay critics discussed earlier. In addition, many gay and lesbian critics combine some of the deconstructive insights offered by queer theory with the social and political concerns associated with more traditional forms of lesbian and gay criticism. Indeed, many devotees of queer theory still refer to themselves as gay or lesbian critics.

此外，来自这三个领域的评论家都对LGBTQ文学中反复出现的主题产生了浓厚的兴趣，这些主题构成了不断演变的文学传统的一部分。这些主题包括：入会仪式，例如发现自己的LGBTQ性取向、作为LGBTQ人士的第一次性经历以及在LGBTQ亚文化中“摸索前行”；向家人和朋友出柜；在职场出柜；应对恐同症和异性恋歧视；同性恋者的自我厌恶心理；克服自我厌恶；坎普和变装在同性恋生活中的作用；应对孤独和疏离；寻找爱情；与LGBTQ伴侣共建生活；追求构建女同性恋乌托邦；石墙事件前后的生活；艾滋病前后的生活（包括个人生活和LGBTQ群体的集体生活）；照顾患有艾滋病的亲人；悼念艾滋病逝者；以及LGBTQ团结的重要性。当然，随着LGBTQ作家的社会和政治处境的变化，LGBTQ写作的主题也会随之改变。在当代作品中公开出现的主题，在早期文学作品中可能只以伪装的形式出现（正如我们在讨论薇拉·凯瑟的作品时所看到的），或者以戏谑的形式出现（例如，考虑奥斯卡·王尔德1894年出版的《不可儿戏》中文字游戏的双重含义）。

Furthermore, critics from all three domains have taken an interest in recurring themes that appear throughout LGBTQ literature and that constitute part of an evolving literary tradition. These themes include the following: initiation, including discovering one’s LGBTQ sexual orientation, experiencing one’s first sexual encounters as an LGBTQ person, and “learning the ropes” in the LGBTQ subculture; coming out to family and friends; coming out at the workplace; dealing with homophobia and with heterosexist discrimination; the psychology of gay self-hatred; overcoming gay self-hatred; the role of camp and drag in gay life; dealing with loneliness and alienation; finding love; building a life with an LGBTQ partner; the quest to build a lesbian utopia; life before and after Stonewall; life before and after AIDS (in terms of both one’s personal life and the collective life of the LGBTQ community); caring for loved ones with AIDS; mourning the death of AIDS victims; and the importance of LGBTQ solidarity. Of course, the themes in LGBTQ writing change over time as the social and political situation of LGBTQ writers changes. And themes that occur openly in contemporary works may appear, in literature from earlier periods, only in disguised forms (as we saw in our discussion of the work of Willa Cather) or in playful forms (consider, for example, the double meanings of the wordplay in Oscar Wilde’s The Importance of Being Earnest, 1894).

最后，女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评通常依赖于类似的文本证据。例如，除了更明显的文本线索——例如同性恋情色意象和同性角色之间的情色互动——还有一些相当微妙的文本线索，即使在看似异性恋的文本中也能营造出同性恋情色的氛围，正如我们之前在女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评的例子中看到的那样。任何单一的文本线索都不能单独作为文本中存在同性恋情色氛围的证据。少量此类线索也不能支持女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿的解读。但是，大量的此类线索，尤其是在与其他类型的文本或传记证据相结合时，可以强化对看似异性恋文本的女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿解读。让我们仔细看看这些微妙线索中最常见的几个例子。

Finally, lesbian, gay, and queer criticism often rely on similar kinds of textual evidence. For example, in addition to the more obvious forms of textual cues – such as homoerotic imagery and erotic encounters between same-sex characters – there are rather subtle textual cues that can create a homoerotic atmosphere even in an otherwise heterosexual text, as we saw in the examples of lesbian, gay, and queer criticism provided earlier. No single textual cue can stand on its own as evidence of a homoerotic atmosphere in a text. Nor can a small number of such cues support a lesbian, gay, or queer reading. But a preponderance of these cues, especially if coupled with other kinds of textual or biographical evidence, can strengthen a lesbian, gay, or queer interpretation even of an apparently heterosexual text. Let’s take a closer look at a few of the most common examples of these subtle cues.

同性社交纽带——对同性角色之间强烈情感联系的描绘可以营造出一种同性社交氛围，这种氛围可能是微妙的，也可能是公开的。无论是否带有同性恋色彩，对同性社交关系的描绘都凸显了同性情感纽带在人类身份认同和社群发展中的深远意义。这种人类潜能常常因异性恋文化中恐同的焦虑而被贬低、边缘化或轻视。凯特·肖邦的小说《觉醒》（1899）中的埃德娜·庞特利耶和阿黛尔·拉蒂尼奥尔之间存在着同性社交关系，小说中埃德娜和赖兹小姐也是如此。其他文学作品中人物之间同性社交关系的例子包括赫尔曼·梅尔维尔的《白鲸》 （1851）中伊什梅尔和奎奎格之间的关系，马克·吐温的《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》 （1885）中哈克·费恩和吉姆之间的关系，以及托妮·莫里森的小说《苏拉》 （1973）中内尔和苏拉之间的关系。

Homosocial bonding – The depiction of strong emotional ties between same-sex characters can create a homosocial atmosphere that may be subtly or overtly homoerotic. Whether homoerotic or not, however, the depiction of homosocial bonding foregrounds the profound importance of same-sex emotional ties in the development of human identity and community, which is a human potential often devalued, marginalized, or trivialized by the homophobic anxiety of heterosexist culture. Edna Pontellier and Adèle Ratignolle, in Kate Chopin’s The Awakening (1899), share a homosocial bond, as do, in the same novella, Edna and Mademoiselle Reisz. Other examples of homosocial bonds among literary characters include those between Ishmael and Queequeg in Herman Melville’s Moby Dick (1851), between Huck Finn and Jim in Mark Twain’s The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn (1885), and between Nel and Sula in Toni Morrison’s Sula (1973).

同性恋或女同性恋的“符号” ——同性恋或女同性恋的符号分为两类。第一类是异性恋文化刻板印象中与LGBTQ人群相关的特征，例如，在“女性化”的男性角色或“男性化”的女性角色的外表和行为中可能体现出来。第二类是同性恋或女同性恋亚文化自身创造的编码符号。例如，在20世纪初格特鲁德·斯坦的著作中使用的“ gay ”一词，很可能是一种“内部群体”的编码符号，当时的异性恋文化无法识别。当然，前面讨论过的艾米莉·狄金森诗歌中的女同性恋意象，也是一种编码符号，通常不被异性恋读者所识别。解读这两种符号都可能很棘手，因为LGBTQ亚文化创造的符号和异性恋文化形成的刻板印象都会随着时间而改变。因此，我们必须谨慎地使用这类证据，并结合其他形式的证据。有些作者可能刻意在文学作品中加入同性恋符号，因为他们认为在异性恋主导的文化中，这是表达自身LGBTQ经历或与LGBTQ读者对话的唯一安全方式。而另一些作者则可能出于各种有意或无意的原因加入这些符号，并非有意将其作为同性恋符号。无论我们是否考虑作者的意图，我们的目标都是分析这些符号在文本中的作用，从而探讨其是否具有酷儿解读的可能性。

Gay or lesbian “signs” – Gay or lesbian signs are of two types. The first type consists of characteristics that heterosexist culture stereotypically associates with LGBTQ people, such as might be evident, for example, in the appearance and behavior of “feminine” male character or “masculine” female characters. The second type are coded signs created by the gay or lesbian subculture itself. For example, the word gay, as used in the writing of Gertrude Stein in the early decades of the twentieth century, may well have been an “in-group” coded sign that heterosexual culture of the period would not have recognized. And certainly the lesbian images in Emily Dickinson’s poetry, discussed earlier, operate as coded signs generally not recognized by heterosexual readers. Interpreting both kinds of signs can be tricky because both the signs created by LGBTQ subcultures and the stereotypes created by heterosexist culture change over time. So we must use this kind of evidence cautiously and in conjunction with other forms of evidence. Some authors may have deliberately included gay or lesbian signs in their literary works because they felt it was the only safe way, in heterosexist culture, to express their own LGBTQ experience or to speak to an LGBTQ readership. Other authors may have included these signs for any number of conscious or unconscious reasons and may not have intended them as gay or lesbian signs. Whether or not we take into account an author’s intention, our goal is to analyze how these signs function in the text to create the potential for a queer interpretation.

同性“镜像”——一种更为微妙、略带抽象的同性恋符号形式，指的是外貌相似、行为举止相近或经历相似的同性角色。由于同性恋性行为强调性方面的相似性，因此，彼此互为“镜像”的同性角色也可以作为同性恋符号。同性镜像之间可能存在同性情欲纽带、同性社交纽带，也可能彼此素不相识。例如，凯特·肖邦的小说《觉醒》 （1899）中的埃德娜·庞特利耶和阿黛尔·拉蒂尼奥尔，以及同一部小说中的罗伯特·勒布伦和阿尔塞·阿罗宾；F ·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的小说《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）中的黛西·布坎南和乔丹·贝克；威廉·福克纳的小说《爱丽丝梦游仙境》中的昆汀·康普森和道尔顿·艾姆斯。《喧哗与骚动》 （1929 年）；以及托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》 （1970 年）中的中国小姐和波兰小姐。

Same-sex “doubles” – A more subtle, somewhat abstract, form of gay and lesbian signs consists of same-sex characters who look alike, act alike, or have parallel experiences. Because gay and lesbian sexuality foregrounds sexual similarity, same-sex characters who function as some sort of “mirror image” of each other can also function as gay or lesbian signs. Same-sex doubles may share a homoerotic bond, a homosocial bond, or they may not know each other at all. Examples of same-sex doubles might include Edna Pontellier and Adèle Ratignolle in Kate Chopin’s The Awakening (1899), as well as Robert Lebrun and Alcée Arobin in the same novella; Daisy Buchanan and Jordan Baker in F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925); Quentin Compson and Dalton Ames in William Faulkner’s The Sound and the Fury (1929); and Miss China and Miss Poland in Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970).

越轨性行为——文本对越轨性行为（包括越轨异性恋，例如婚外情）的关注，质疑了传统异性恋的规则，从而为各种越轨性行为的想象打开了大门。当然，大量文学作品都涉及异性恋越轨行为——但未必带有酷儿潜台词。然而，某些对异性恋越轨行为的描写——例如，涉及多个角色、过着双重生活、在酒精和狂欢派对中放松禁忌——营造了一种性实验的氛围，可以说为酷儿解读奠定了基础。虽然一个既定的框架本身不足以构成酷儿解读的充分条件，但它可以提供一个引人入胜的背景，以补充更具体的文本证据。

Transgressive sexuality – A text’s focus on transgressive sexuality, including transgressive heterosexuality (such as extramarital romance), throws into question the rules of traditional heterosexuality and thus opens the door of imagination to transgressive sexualities of all kinds. Of course, a great deal of literature deals with heterosexual transgression – without necessarily having a queer subtext. But some representations of heterosexual transgression – for example, those that involve several characters, the leading of double lives, the relaxing of inhibitions associated with alcohol and riotous parties – create an atmosphere of sexual experimentation that sets the stage, so to speak, for a queer interpretation. While a set stage is not sufficient by itself for a queer reading, it can provide an evocative backdrop to complement more concrete textual evidence.

显然，女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评之间的界限仍然有些模糊。你运用上述文本证据的目的，以及你自身认同的批评取向，将决定你对文学作品的解读是女同性恋、男同性恋还是酷儿解读。

Clearly, the boundaries among lesbian, gay, and queer criticism remain somewhat fluid. Your purpose in using the kinds of textual evidence just described, as well as your own self-identified critical orientation, will determine whether your interpretation of a literary work is a lesbian, gay, or queer reading.

女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿评论家们对文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions lesbian, gay, and queer critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在概括女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿群体对文学的解读方式。问题7——因为它基于一种解构主义的性观念——是唯一符合酷儿批评这一较为狭义的理论定义的问题。其余问题均可从这三种视角中的任何一种来回答。

The following questions are offered to summarize lesbian, gay, or queer approaches to literature. Question 7 – because it rests on a deconstructive view of sexuality – is the only question that falls within the narrower theoretical definition of queer criticism. The remaining questions can be answered from any one of the three perspectives.

1具体的同性恋、女同性恋或酷儿作品的政治（意识形态议程）是什么？这些政治是如何在作品的主题内容或人物刻画中体现出来的？

1 What are the politics (ideological agendas) of specific gay, lesbian, or queer works, and how are those politics revealed in, for example, the work’s thematic content or portrayals of its characters?

2一部特定的女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿作品的诗学（文学手法和策略）是什么？这部作品对目前正在进行的、旨在定义独特的女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿诗学、文学传统或经典的尝试做出了哪些贡献？

2 What are the poetics (literary devices and strategies) of a specific lesbian, gay, or queer work? What does the work contribute to the ongoing attempt to define a uniquely lesbian, gay, or queer poetics, literary tradition, or canon?

3这部作品对我们了解酷儿、男同性恋或女同性恋的经历和历史（包括文学史）有何贡献？

3 What does the work contribute to our knowledge of queer, gay, or lesbian experience and history, including literary history?

4在表面上看似异性恋的文本中，酷儿、同性恋或女同性恋的经历是如何被编码的？（这种分析通常针对那些生活在公开的酷儿、同性恋或女同性恋文本会被认为不可接受的时代的作家的作品，或者用于帮助重新定义先前被认为是异性恋的作家的性取向。）

4 How is queer, gay, or lesbian experience coded in texts that are apparently heterosexual? (This analysis is usually done for works by writers who lived at a time when openly queer, gay, or lesbian texts would have been considered unacceptable, or it is done in order to help reformulate the sexual orientation of a writer formerly presumed heterosexual.)

5 如何重新解读异性恋作家的作品，以揭示其中未言明或无意识的女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿元素？也就是说，作品中是否存在某种被掩盖（或被异性恋读者掩盖）的无意识的女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿欲望或冲突？

5 How might the works of heterosexual writers be reread to reveal an unspoken or unconscious lesbian, gay, or queer presence? That is, does the work have an unconscious lesbian, gay, or queer desire or conflict that it submerges (or that heterosexual readers have submerged)?

6这部作品揭示了异性恋霸权主义在社会、政治和心理层面上的运作方式吗？这部作品（有意或无意地）带有恐同倾向吗？这部作品是在批判、颂扬还是盲目接受异性恋霸权主义价值观？

6 What does the work reveal about the operations (socially, politically, psychologically) of heterosexism? Is the work (consciously or unconsciously) homophobic? Does the work critique, celebrate, or blindly accept heterosexist values?

7文学文本是如何阐明性取向和性“身份”的问题的，也就是说，人类的性取向并不能简单地归入同性恋和异性恋这两个不同的类别？

7 How does the literary text illustrate the problematics of sexuality and sexual “identity,” that is, the ways in which human sexuality does not fall neatly into the separate categories defined by the words homosexual and heterosexual?

根据所讨论的文学文本，我们可能会提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们可能会提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们从女同性恋、男同性恋或酷儿视角审视文学作品的一些切入点。请记住，即使使用相同的理论概念，不同的批评家对同一作品的解读方式也各不相同。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。我们的目标是运用女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评来丰富我们对文学作品的阅读，帮助我们理解作品中一些重要的思想——如果没有这些批评形式，我们可能无法如此清晰或深刻地领悟这些思想——并帮助我们更好地欣赏LGBTQ群体的历史和文学创作。

Depending on the literary text in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us to look at literature through a lesbian, gay, or queer lens. Remember, not all these critics will interpret the same work in the same way, even if they use the same theoretical concepts. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal is to use lesbian, gay, and queer criticism to help enrich our reading of literary works, to help us see some important ideas they illustrate that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply without these forms of criticism, and to help us appreciate the history and literary production of LGBTQ people.

以下对《了不起的盖茨比》的解读旨在展现酷儿视角下对菲茨杰拉德小说的诠释可能带来的成果。我之所以称之为酷儿解读，既包含其包容性的含义——我的讨论不会局限于单一性别或单一性取向的角色——也包含其解构性的含义：我的解读旨在探究小说中性取向表述的变幻莫测和不稳定之处。具体而言，我将论证《了不起的盖茨比》是一部性取向模糊的小说：它提出了许多关于人物性取向的问题，但并未给出答案。我认为，这种模糊性源于小说通过隐瞒性取向的同性恋叙述者尼克·卡拉威的视角来讲述一个异性恋的故事。最后，我将指出，小说的性取向模糊反映了菲茨杰拉德自身在性取向问题上的矛盾冲突。

The following reading of The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a queer interpretation of Fitzgerald’s novel might yield. I call my reading queer in both the inclusive sense of the term – my discussion will not be limited to characters of a single sex or a single sexuality – and in its deconstructive sense: my reading explores the vagaries and instabilities of the novel’s representation of sexuality. Specifically, I will argue that The Great Gatsby is a sexually ambiguous novel: it raises a number of questions about the sexuality of its characters, but it does not answer them. And I will argue that this ambiguity results from the delivery of a heterosexual plot through the medium of a closeted gay sensibility, that of narrator Nick Carraway. Finally, I will suggest that the novel’s sexual ambiguity is a reflection of Fitzgerald’s apparent conflicts concerning his own sexuality.

真正的尼克·卡拉威会现身吗？——对《了不起的盖茨比》的酷儿解读

Will the real Nick Carraway please come out? A queer reading of The Great Gatsby

当然，我们很难找到比F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）更直白的异性恋情节了。小说的叙事发展由杰伊·盖茨比对黛西·费·布坎南的悲剧爱情以及三个交织的异性恋三角关系所驱动：盖茨比-黛西-汤姆、汤姆-默特尔-乔治和默特尔-汤姆-黛西。然而，这种异性恋叙事中却笼罩着一层同性恋的潜台词，虽然它在异性恋情节的跌宕起伏中显得不那么显眼，但它在小说中却无处不在。

Certainly, we couldn’t ask for a more overtly heterosexual plot than that of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925). The novel’s narrative progression is driven by Jay Gatsby’s tragic love for Daisy Fay Buchanan and by three overlapping heterosexual romantic triangles: Gatsby-Daisy-Tom, Tom-Myrtle-George, and Myrtle-Tom-Daisy. This heterosexual narrative is shadowed, however, by a homoerotic subtext, which, though it remains closeted, so to speak, by the spectacular twists and turns of the heterosexual plot, is a pervasive presence in the novel.

具体而言，我将论证小说对性越轨的处理方式以及其中大量出现的同性恋符号共同构建了一种同性恋情愫，这种情愫扰乱并动摇了异性恋叙事，从而造就了一部性取向模糊的小说。正如我们将看到的，这种同性恋情愫在叙述者尼克·卡拉威的刻画中得到了最完整的体现，我认为他并未意识到自己的同性恋倾向。换言之，《了不起的盖茨比》的性取向模糊性源于通过隐秘的同性恋视角来呈现异性恋情节。此外，我还将指出，小说的性取向模糊性反映了菲茨杰拉德本人在性取向问题上所经历的挣扎。

Specifically, I will argue that the novel’s treatment of sexual transgression and its proliferation of gay and lesbian signs work together to create a homoerotic subtext that disrupts and destabilizes the heterosexual narrative, creating, in the process, a sexually ambiguous novel. And as we shall see, this homoerotic subtext finds its most complete embodiment in the characterization of narrator Nick Carraway, who is, I believe, unaware of his gay orientation. Put another way, The Great Gatsby’s sexual ambiguity results from the delivery of a heterosexual plot through the medium of a closeted gay sensibility. In addition, I will suggest that the novel’s sexual ambiguity mirrors the conflicts Fitzgerald apparently experienced concerning his own sexuality.

尽管对越轨异性恋的描绘本身并不能在一部异性恋小说中构建出酷儿潜文本，但《了不起的盖茨比》对性越轨行为的明显痴迷——正如我们将看到的，其中包含着对同性恋性行为的暗示——为酷儿解读奠定了基础。首先，构成小说大部分情节的三段三角恋情都涉及婚外情：黛西、汤姆和默特尔都违背了他们的婚姻誓言。黛西与盖茨比的非法重逢是由尼克安排的，尼克是她的男性亲戚，按传统来说，他应该保护黛西的贞洁，但他却反而促成了黛西的堕落。此外，盖茨比在与黛西初次交往时就与她发生了婚前性行为，“在一个静谧的十月夜晚，他占有了她，贪婪而肆无忌惮地占有了她……因为他根本没有权利触碰她的手”（156；第八章）。尼克和乔丹显然也有婚前性关系，而且两人都不是第一次了。事实上，尼克认为乔丹性生活混乱：他推测她“无可救药地不诚实”，因为她想“保持那副冷漠傲慢的笑容面对世人，同时又想满足她那强健、活泼的身体的需求”（63；第3章）。

Although the depiction of transgressive heterosexuality cannot by itself create a queer subtext in a heterosexual novel, The Great Gatsby’s apparent obsession with sexual transgression, which as we shall see includes intimations of gay and lesbian sexuality, sets the stage for a queer interpretation. For one thing, the three romantic triangles that generate most of the novel’s action are all adulterous: Daisy, Tom, and Myrtle are all breaking their marital vows. And Daisy’s illicit reunion with Gatsby is arranged by Nick, a male relative who, traditionally, should protect her virtue but, instead, facilitates her losing it. Furthermore, Gatsby had premarital sex with Daisy during their initial courtship, when “he took [her] one still October night, took her … ravenously and unscrupulously … because he had no real right to touch her hand” (156; ch. 8). And Nick and Jordan, too, are apparently engaged in a premarital affair, neither of them for the first time. Indeed, Nick believes that Jordan is sexually promiscuous: he speculates that she is “incurably dishonest” because she wants to “keep that cool, insolent smile turned to the world and yet satisfy the demands of her hard, jaunty body” (63; ch. 3).

当然，书中描绘的喧闹派对，无论是在汤姆和默特尔的公寓里，还是在盖茨比的草坪上，也营造了一种性越轨的氛围。例如，汤姆和默特尔的派对是他们婚外情的产物，他们和宾客们对此都毫不避讳。而对盖茨比派对的描写则充斥着性越轨的意象，例如汤姆试图勾搭一位“平凡但漂亮”的年轻女子（112页；第六章）；盖茨比和黛西偷偷溜出派对，到尼克的别墅独处，尼克则在一旁守卫，以免被人打扰；一位身份不明的男子“用一种奇怪的热情与一位年轻女演员交谈”，而他的妻子则“在他耳边低声说‘你答应过我！’”（56页；第三章）；“白鲸的女孩们”（66页；第四章），这个短语暗示她们是他的性对象。还有像“休伯特·奥尔巴赫和克里斯蒂先生的妻子”（66；第4章）以及“克劳迪娅·希普小姐和一位据说是她司机的男子”（67；第4章）这样隐晦地带有禁忌色彩的情侣。尼克对纽约市的描述也同样适用于弥漫在整部小说中的性氛围：这是一个“任何事情都可能发生……任何事情都可能发生”（73；第4章）的地方。

Of course, the riotous parties depicted, both in Tom and Myrtle’s apartment and on Gatsby’s lawn, also contribute an ambience of sexual transgression. For example, Tom and Myrtle’s party is an outgrowth of their illicit affair, about which they and their guests talk openly. And the descriptions of Gatsby’s parties are peppered with sexually transgressive images, such as Tom’s attempting to pick up a “common but pretty” young woman (112; ch. 6); Gatsby and Daisy’s sneaking away from the party to be alone at Nick’s cottage while Nick stands guard lest they be intruded upon; the unidentified man “talking with curious intensity to a young actress” while his wife “hisse[s] ‘You promised!’ into his ear” (56; ch. 3); “Beluga’s girls” (66; ch. 4), with the implication that phrase carries of their being his sexual objects; and such implicitly transgressive couples as “Hubert Auerbach and Mr. Chrystie’s wife” (66; ch. 4) and “Miss Claudia Hip with a man reputed to be her chauffeur” (67; ch. 4). What Nick says of New York City is thus true of the sexual atmosphere that pervades the novel: this is a place where “[a]nything can happen … anything at all” (73; ch. 4).

事实上，正是在这些派对上，我们看到了引人注目的同性恋“符号”，它们开启了小说中同性恋隐喻的展开。例如，在尼克第一次遇见盖茨比的派对上，他看到“两个穿着黄色连衣裙的女孩停在台阶下，齐声喊道：‘你好！’”（47；第三章）。这两个年轻女子是典型的同性“替身”，她们扮演着女同性恋符号的角色：她们外貌相似，谈吐相像，穿着打扮也一样，形影不离，而且她们原来是一对“舞台‘双胞胎’”，在派对上“穿着戏服表演婴儿节目”（51；第三章）。实际上，在1974年的电影版中，对这两个角色的刻画是该片唯一一次暗示故事中可能存在同性恋维度：在电影中，她们共舞的场景充满了显而易见的性暗示。

Indeed, it is at these parties where we see the striking examples of gay and lesbian “signs” that initiate the development of the novel’s homoerotic subtext. For example, at the party where Nick first meets Gatsby, he sees “two girls in twin yellow dresses who stopped at the foot of the steps. ‘Hello!’ they cried together” (47; ch. 3). These two young women are a striking example of same-sex “doubles” that function as lesbian signs: they look alike, talk alike, are dressed alike, are apparently inseparable, and turn out to be a “pair of stage ‘twins’” who do “a baby act in costume” (51; ch. 3) at the party. In fact, the depiction of these two characters in the 1974 film version of the novel is that film’s only concession to the possibility of a queer dimension in the story: in the film, the women are portrayed dancing together in a manner the sexual meaning of which cannot be missed.

在汤姆和默特尔的公寓里举行的聚会上，尼克与麦基先生的相遇展现了一系列同性恋的迹象。麦基先生“面色苍白，举止阴柔”（34；第二章），他和妻子住在隔壁公寓。相遇始于麦基在椅子上睡着。尼克告诉我们：“我拿出手帕，擦去他脸颊上残留的干涸泡沫，那泡沫让我整个下午都心神不宁”（41；第二章）。麦基醒来离开聚会时，留下了他的妻子，尼克形容她“尖声尖气，懒散慵懒，英俊却可怕”（34；第二章）。尼克“跟着”（42；第二章）麦基走了出去，麦基邀请他共进午餐。尼克答应了。

At the party in Tom and Myrtle’s apartment, we see a series of gay signs during the encounter between Nick and Mr. McKee, “a pale, feminine man” (34; ch. 2), who lives with his wife in a neighboring apartment. The encounter begins when McKee falls asleep in his chair. Nick tells us, “Taking out my handkerchief I wiped from his cheek the remains of the spot of dried lather that had worried me all the afternoon” (41; ch. 2). When McKee wakes up and leaves the party, he leaves his wife whom Nick describes as “shrill, languid, handsome and horrible” (34; ch. 2) behind. Nick “follow[s]” (42; ch. 2) McKee out, and the latter invites him to lunch one day. Nick agrees.

“好的，”我同意道，“我很乐意。”

“All right,” I agreed, “I’ll be glad to.”

我当时站在他的床边，他坐在被子中间，只穿着内裤，手里拿着一个厚厚的文件夹。

… I was standing beside his bed and he was sitting up between the sheets, clad in his underwear, with a great portfolio in his hands.

“美女与野兽……孤独……老杂货店马……布鲁克桥……”

“Beauty and the Beast … Loneliness … Old Grocery Horse … Brook’n Bridge. …”
