然后，我半睡半醒地躺在宾夕法尼亚车站冰冷的底层，盯着早晨的《论坛报》，等待着四点钟的火车。

Then I was lying half asleep in the cold lower level of the Pennsylvania Station, staring at the morning Tribune and waiting for the four o’clock train.

（菲茨杰拉德的省略号，42；第2章）

(Fitzgerald’s ellipses, 42; ch. 2)

显然，两人都喝得酩酊大醉，这一幕很容易被解读为他们醉酒状态的真实写照。从这个角度来看，省略号指的是醉酒状态下常见的记忆缺失。尼克实际上是在说：“我当时就是醉成这样”，仅此而已。

Obviously, both men are very drunk, and the scene easily can be interpreted as nothing more than a representation of their drunkenness. From this perspective, the ellipses refer to the memory lapses that commonly occur in such a state of inebriation. Nick is saying, in effect, “That’s how drunk I was,” and that’s all he’s saying.

然而，从酷儿视角来看，这一幕却引出了另一种解读。这里充斥着大量的同性恋暗示，它们出现的顺序暗示​​着两个男人之间同性情愫的逐渐发展，甚至也暗示着麦基卧室里可能发生了性行为。这些暗示包括麦基的女性化外表、他妻子的男性化（强势、霸道、“英俊”）特质，以及尼克对麦基脸上泡沫的关注（换句话说，尼克的……）尼克对麦基仪容的细致关注、他“跟着”麦基走出房间、午餐邀请、尼克跟着麦基进入卧室、麦基只穿着内裤坐在床上，以及尼克直到凌晨四点在火车站的地板上醒来才想起其他事情（因此，这期间发生的一切都成了被压抑的记忆）。这些迹象单独来看或许并不重要。但当它们以这种方式聚集在一起时，却暗示了一种同性恋的潜台词，任何酷儿评论家都不会错过。

Through a queer lens, however, the scene suggests another reading. The gay signs here are numerous, and the order in which they appear implies the progression of a homoerotic attraction between the two men, if not the equally likely possibility of a sexual encounter in McKee’s bedroom. These signs include McKee’s feminine appearance, the masculine (aggressive, overbearing, “handsome”) quality of his wife, Nick’s attention to the spot of lather on McKee’s face (in other words, Nick’s fastidious attention to McKee’s grooming), Nick’s “following” him out of the room, the lunch invitation, Nick’s following McKee into his bedroom, McKee’s sitting in bed attired only in his underwear, and Nick’s remembering nothing else until he wakes up at four o’clock in the morning on the floor of the train station (so whatever occurred in the interim has the status of a repressed memory). None of these signs would carry much weight by itself. But when clustered in this fashion they suggest a homoerotic subtext that no queer critic would miss.

然而，或许与杰伊·盖茨比和乔丹·贝克相关的同性恋迹象最为多。盖茨比一丝不苟的仪容、华丽的服饰和其他物品都有效地象征着他的同性恋身份。“他的短发看起来好像每天都修剪过”（54；第三章），他无可挑剔的衣橱里以各种深浅不一的薰衣草色和粉色为主，这两种颜色长期以来都与同性恋联系在一起。书中提到，盖茨比拥有数十件“条纹、卷轴纹和格子图案的衬衫，颜色有珊瑚色、苹果绿、薰衣草色和淡橙色，上面还绣着印度蓝色的字母组合”（97-98；第五章），他的粉色西装至少被提及三次。

Perhaps the most numerous gay and lesbian signs are associated, however, with Jay Gatsby and Jordan Baker. Gatsby’s fastidious grooming and flamboyant clothing and other possessions function effectively as gay signs. “[H]is short hair looked as though it were trimmed every day” (54; ch. 3), and his impeccable wardrobe features various shades of lavender and pink, two colors that have been long associated with gayness. We are told that Gatsby owns dozens of “shirts with stripes and scrolls and plaids in coral and apple green and lavender and faint orange with monograms of Indian blue” (97–98; ch. 5), and his pink suit is mentioned at least three times.

事实上，盖茨比那套粉色西装的描述方式凸显了它作为同性恋象征的功能。尼克两次提及这套粉色西装，措辞都颇为浪漫，仿佛在描述一位迷人女性的衣着：“我满脑子想的都是月光下他那套粉色西装的光芒”（150；第七章），以及“他那套华丽的粉色破烂西装在白色台阶上显得格外醒目”（162；第八章）。而汤姆对这套西装的提及则更加突出了它作为同性恋象征的功能，因为显然是恐同的汤姆如此看待它的。让我们进一步探讨最后一点。

In fact, the manner in which Gatsby’s pink suit is mentioned underscores its function as a gay sign. Nick’s two references to the pink suit are phrased quite romantically, as if the clothing of a desirable woman were being described: “I could think of nothing but the luminosity of his pink suit under the moon” (150; ch. 7) and “[H]is gorgeous pink rag of a suit made a bright spot of color against the white steps” (162; ch. 8). And Tom’s reference to the suit foregrounds its function as a gay sign because that seems to be precisely how Tom, who is clearly homophobic, sees it. Let’s consider this last point a bit further.

汤姆与众多工人阶级女性的婚外情，以及他公开炫耀这些女性的行为（28；第二章），都表明他需要通过这些行为来确认自己的异性恋倾向。他在小说中不断、咄咄逼人地展现自己的男子气概，也印证了这一点。正如尼克所说，

Tom’s numerous extramarital affairs with working-class women, whom he parades in public (28; ch. 2) and whose socioeconomic vulnerability gives him a great deal of power over them, suggests a need to reassure himself of his heterosexuality, as does his constant, aggressive assertion of his manhood, which we see throughout the novel. As Nick puts it,

他的语气中带着一丝父亲般的轻蔑，即使是对他喜欢的人也是如此……

There was a touch of paternal contempt in [his voice], even toward people he liked ….

“不过，别以为我对这些问题的看法就是最终的，”他似乎在说，“仅仅因为我比你更强壮、更有男子气概。”

“Now, don’t think my opinion on these matters is final,” he seemed to say, “just because I’m stronger and more of a man than you are.”

（11；第1章）

(11; ch. 1)

这种大男子主义的过度补偿与恐同症直接相关：汤姆需要证明自己的男子气概，这导致他攻击任何他认为是他人同性恋迹象的事物。因此，当汤姆对盖茨比的蔑视体现在对后者粉色西装的贬损性评价上时，就突显了这套西装作为同性恋标志的功能：“牛津人！……他才不是！他居然穿粉色西装！”（129；第七章）。

This kind of macho overcompensation is directly related to homophobia: Tom’s need to prove his own manhood leads him to attack anything he perceives as an indication of homosexuality in others. So when Tom’s contempt for Gatsby expresses itself in a derogatory reference to the latter’s pink suit, it underscores the suit’s function as a gay sign: “An Oxford man! … Like hell he is! He wears a pink suit” (129; ch. 7).

盖茨比的其他物品也带有同性恋的象征意义。他家里的许多装饰都极尽奢华，充满女性气息：“玛丽·安托瓦内特式的音乐室和复辟时期的沙龙……[以及]铺着玫瑰色和薰衣草色丝绸、摆满鲜花的古典卧室”（96；第五章）。正如汤姆所说，盖茨比的汽车也像“马戏团的篷车”一样张扬（128；第七章）：“它是浓郁的奶油色，”尼克说，“闪着镍的光泽，在它那庞大的车身里，到处都塞满了夸张的帽盒、餐盒和工具箱，层层叠叠的挡风玻璃如同迷宫一般，映照着十几个太阳”（68；第四章）。事实上，盖茨比为自己创造的生活充满了矫揉造作和戏剧性，带有一种滑稽的特质，这种特质甚至在虚构的“自传”中也有所体现，盖茨比在自传中将自己描述为“年轻的拉贾……收集珠宝，主要是红宝石，狩猎大型猎物[和]绘画”（70；第4章）。

Gatsby’s other possessions also function as gay signs. Much of the decor of his house is extravagantly feminine: “Marie Antoinette music rooms and Restoration salons … [and] period bedrooms swathed in rose and lavender silk and vivid with new flowers” (96; ch. 5). And Gatsby’s car has the flamboyance, as Tom puts it, of a “circus wagon” (128; ch. 7): “It was a rich cream color,” Nick says, “bright with nickel, swollen here and there in its monstrous length with triumphant hatboxes and supper-boxes and tool-boxes, and terraced with a labyrinth of windshields that mirrored a dozen suns” (68; ch. 4). In fact, the artifice and theatricality of the life Gatsby has created for himself has a camp quality about it, a quality evident even in the fictional “autobiography” in which Gatsby describes himself as a “young rajah … collecting jewels, chiefly rubies, hunting big game, [and] painting” (70; ch. 4).

同样，乔丹·贝克（Jordan Baker）这个名字男女皆宜，却与许多女同性恋的象征联系在一起。她以职业高尔夫为生，而当时的高尔夫领域几乎是男性的天下。正如盖茨比经常被赋予女性化的描述一样，乔丹也经常被赋予男性化的描述。尼克第一次见到她时说：“我喜欢看她。她身材苗条，胸部不大，仪态端庄，她会像个年轻的军校学员一样，向后仰头，更显姿态”（15；第一章），也就是说，像个军校里的男孩。即使穿着最女性化的服装，她也被赋予了相当男性化的描述：“她穿着晚礼服，所有的裙子，都像运动服——她的举止轻快活泼，仿佛她第一次学会走路就是在清爽的早晨的高尔夫球场上”（55；第三章）。事实上，尼克对乔丹的外貌和行为的频繁描述几乎总是唤起相当男性化的形象：她有着“健壮而轻快的身躯”（63；第3章）；“她的身体以一种不安的动作展现出来”（22；第1章）；“她棕色的手轻快地挥舞着，像是在敬礼”（57；第3章）；她有一张“苍白而轻蔑的嘴”（85；第4章）；“她的脸色和她膝盖上的露指手套一样呈棕色”（185；第9章）；她“似乎掌握了一种坚韧的怀疑精神”（20；第1章）；她是一个“干净、坚韧、局限的人”（84；第4章）；等等。

Analogously, Jordan Baker, whose name could belong to a man or a woman, is associated with numerous lesbian signs. She makes her living in the, then, male domain of professional golf. And just as Gatsby is frequently described in feminine terms, Jordan is frequently described in masculine terms. Upon first meeting her, Nick says, “I enjoyed looking at her. She was a slender, small-breasted girl with an erect carriage which she accentuated by throwing her body backward at the shoulders like a young cadet” (15; ch. 1), that is, like a young boy at military school. Even when dressed in her most feminine attire, she is described in rather masculine terms: “she wore her evening dress, all her dresses, like sports clothes – there was a jauntiness about her movements as if she had first learned to walk upon golf courses on clean, crisp mornings” (55; ch 3). Indeed, Nick’s frequent descriptions of Jordan’s appearance and behavior almost always evoke rather masculine images: she has a “hard, jaunty body” (63; ch. 3); “[h]er body asserted itself with a restless movement” (22; ch. 1); “her brown hand waved a jaunty salute” (57; ch. 3); she has a “wan, scornful mouth” (85; ch. 4); “her face [had] the same brown tint as the fingerless glove on her knee” (185; ch. 9); she “seemed to have mastered a certain hardy skepticism” (20; ch. 1); she’s a “clean, hard, limited person” (84; ch. 4); and the like.

乔丹的性格中可能存在的同性恋倾向，在她与男性的关系中得到了进一步的强化。正如尼克所观察到的，乔丹“本能地避开那些精明狡猾的男人……因为她觉得在一个任何偏离既定规则的行为都被认为不可能发生的圈子里，她会更安全”（63；第三章）。换句话说，乔丹不想被人看穿。她不想被认为拥有与既定规则“相悖”的私生活，所以她会和那些可以被她操控的男人交往，比如陪她参加盖茨比派对的那个明显不成熟的男伴，“一个爱说些粗俗话的纠缠不休的大学生”（49；第三章），又比如尼克，他“受宠若惊”，能和“一位高尔夫冠军”在一起（62；第三章），而她只要说一句“我喜欢你”，就能把他玩弄于股掌之间（63；第三章）。在这种情况下，尽管她与尼克有性关系，但乔丹通过“耍花招”来“满足她那强健、轻快的身体的需求”（63；第 3 章），这暗示了女同性恋的欲望。

The possibility of a lesbian subtext in Jordan’s characterization is reinforced by her relationships with men. As Nick observes, Jordan “instinctively avoided clever shrewd men … because she felt safer on a plane where any divergence from a code would be thought impossible” (63; ch. 3). In other words, Jordan doesn’t want to be seen through. She doesn’t want to be thought to have a private life that “diverges” from the code, so she dates men she can manipulate, like the obviously immature escort who accompanies her to one of Gatsby’s parties, “a persistent undergraduate given to violent innuendo” (49; ch. 3), or like Nick, who is “flattered” to be seen with “a golf champion” (62; ch. 3) and whom she can wrap around her little finger simply by saying “I like you” (63; ch. 3). In this context, and despite her sexual relationship with Nick, the “demands of her hard, jaunty body” that Jordan “satisf[ies]” by “dealing in subterfuges” (63; ch. 3) imply lesbian desire.

鉴于盖茨比和乔丹作为同性恋符号的载体，从酷儿视角来看，尼克最关注的两个人物意义非凡。尼克对盖茨比的迷恋带有同性恋色彩，这体现在他对盖茨比女性特质的关注上，这与他对麦基的关注如出一辙；他对盖茨比“英俊潇洒”的外表和“浪漫的准备”（6；第一章）的强烈赞赏；他频繁、热情且往往盲目地为盖茨比辩护，认为他是他人自私和堕落的受害者；以及在盖茨比死后，当对他的爱“安全”起来时，尼克与盖茨比之间建立起的深厚情谊。同样，尼克对乔丹的依恋似乎也源于同性恋情愫，而非异性恋情愫，因为他主要把她当作一个年轻男孩看待。

Given their function as repositories of gay signs, it is meaningful, from a queer perspective, that Gatsby and Jordan are the two characters in whom Nick takes the most personal interest. That Nick’s attraction to Gatsby is homoerotic is suggested by his focus on Gatsby’s feminine qualities, which mirrors his focus on McKee; his intense appreciation of Gatsby’s “gorgeous” appearance and “romantic readiness” (6; ch. 1); his frequent, passionate, and often blind defense of Gatsby as the victim of others’ selfishness and corruption; and the deep bond he feels with Gatsby after the latter’s death, when it is “safe” to feel love for him. Similarly, Nick’s attachment to Jordan seems as much the product of homoerotic as heterosexual attraction because he sees her primarily as a young boy.

在这种情况下，尼克成功帮助盖茨比与毫不知情的黛西重燃旧情，也带有同性恋的隐喻。由于尼克对盖茨比抱有同性恋情愫，他很可能对盖茨比的性取向感到好奇，并想方设法介入他的私生活。“为盖茨比拉皮条”（正如盖茨比提出付钱给他所暗示的那样，尼克“安排”黛西的行为本质上就是拉皮条）或许能让尼克感受到与盖茨比的性亲近。（当然，也可以提出类似的论点，认为乔丹促成黛西与盖茨比的恋情，源于乔丹对黛西的性吸引和好奇。）此外，通过帮助黛西和盖茨比在自己家中重聚，尼克或许还能通过与黛西的互动，体验到一种替代性的性快感。他似乎正是这么做的，他斥责盖茨比对黛西的感受漠不关心：“‘黛西也很尴尬……你像个小男孩一样，’我不耐烦地吼道，‘不仅如此，你还很粗鲁。黛西一个人坐在那里。’”（93；第五章）。在随后的盖茨比豪宅参观中，尼克的处境与黛西相似，因为他也是第一次窥见盖茨比的私人领地。

In this context, Nick’s successful effort to help Gatsby rekindle his affair with the unsuspecting Daisy also has a homoerotic subtext. Because of Nick’s homoerotic attraction to Gatsby, he is likely to be curious about Gatsby’s sexuality and to want to be involved in his personal life in any way he can. “Pimping” for Gatsby (which is what Nick’s “procurement” of Daisy amounts to, as Gatsby’s offer to pay him for the service suggests) may let Nick feel sexually close to him. (An analogous argument can be made, of course, that Jordan’s interest in promoting Daisy’s affair with Gatsby springs from Jordan’s sexual attraction to and curiosity about Daisy.) In addition, by helping Daisy and Gatsby reunite in his own home, Nick may also experience a vicarious sexual thrill by identifying with Daisy during this episode. This is just what he seems to do as he chastises Gatsby for being insensitive to Daisy’s feelings: “‘Daisy’s embarrassed too. … You’re acting like a little boy,’ I broke out impatiently. ‘Not only that, but you’re rude. Daisy’s sitting in there all alone’” (93; ch. 5). And during the subsequent tour of Gatsby’s mansion, Nick’s position is parallel to that of Daisy, as he, too, is getting a glimpse of Gatsby’s private domain for the first time.

的确，尼克身上处处体现着同性恋的特质，这更加凸显了他角色塑造中的同性恋情愫。他即将年满30岁，从未结婚或订婚，尽管有过异性恋情，但他从未让与女性的恋爱关系发展到认真的程度。事实上，尼克的形象与一战期间成千上万发现自己同性恋倾向的年轻男性如出一辙。正如乔治·昌西在其纽约市同性恋史著作中所观察到的那样，

Indeed, Nick is a repository of gay signs, a fact that underscores the homoerotic dimension of his characterization. He is just turning 30, has never married or been engaged, and, his heterosexual affairs notwithstanding, he doesn’t let his romantic relationships with women get serious. In fact, Nick fits the profile of thousands of young men who discovered their gay orientation during World War I. As George Chauncey observes in his gay history of New York City,

第一次世界大战期间的军事动员，将男性从家庭和小镇社区的监护下带走，并将他们置于单一性别的环境中，增加了他们遇到自认为是同性恋的男性并探索自身同性恋倾向的机会。战后，海军官员立即对驻扎在罗德岛州纽波特海军训练站的男性进行了一项广泛的同性恋调查，结果显示，许多水兵在战争期间结识了其他自认为是同性恋的水兵后，开始形成自己的同性恋身份。还有很多不认为自己是同性恋的男性，却也熟悉同性恋圈子，有过同性恋经历。这些人中许多认为，如果回到家乡，他们只能小心翼翼地继续同性恋生活，这既是因为需要向父母隐瞒自己的性取向，也是因为大多数小城镇的同性恋生活十分有限。

[M]ilitary mobilization [during World War I], by removing men from the supervision of their families and small-town neighborhoods and placing them in a single-sex environment, increased the chances that they would encounter self-identified gay men and explore their homosexual interests. An extensive investigation of homosexuality among the men stationed at the Naval Training Station in Newport, Rhode Island, conducted by naval officials immediately following the war revealed that numerous sailors there had begun to forge [gay] identities … after meeting other gay-identified sailors during the war, and that a much larger number of men who did not consider themselves homosexual had nonetheless become familiar with the gay world and had homosexual experiences. Many of these men believed they could continue their homosexual lives only with great difficulty and circumspection if they returned to their home-towns, both because of the need to hide their homosexuality from their parents and because of the limited gay life available in most small towns.

军事动员也让许多新兵有机会见识到大城市，尤其是纽约（美国军队前往欧洲的主要港口）的同性恋生活……我们无法确定战后有多少同性恋士兵留在了纽约，但 20 世纪 20 年代纽约同性恋机构的日益增多……表明他们中的许多人确实留了下来——在见识过纽约的同性恋生活之后，确实很难让他们留在农场。

Military mobilization also gave many recruits the chance to see the sort of gay life that large cities, especially New York [the major port from which American troops embarked for Europe], had to offer … It is impossible to determine how many gay soldiers stayed in New York after the war, but the growing visibility of gay institutions in the city in the 1920s … suggests that many of them did so – that it was, indeed, hard to keep them down on the farm after they’d seen gay New York.

（145）

(145)

尼克是中西部人，和上面提到的那些士兵一样，他从战场归来后无法重新适应家乡的生活。尼克说：

Nick is a Midwesterner, and like the soldiers described above, he returned from the war unable to readjust to life in his hometown. Nick says,

我参与了那场姗姗来迟的日耳曼人迁徙，也就是所谓的第一次世界大战。我如此享受反击战，以至于回来后感到不安。中西部不再是温暖的世界中心，如今却像是宇宙的荒芜边缘——于是我决定向东进发。

I participated in that delayed Teutonic migration known as the Great War. I enjoyed the counter-raid so thoroughly that I came back restless. Instead of being the warm center of the world, the middle-west now seemed like the ragged edge of the universe – so I decided to go east. …

（7；第 1 章）

(7; ch. 1)

他去了东方的哪里？他去了纽约市，他和乔丹都认为纽约市与越轨的性观念有关。尼克谈到纽约时说：“我开始喜欢……它夜晚那种刺激、冒险的感觉”（61；第3章），乔丹则观察到：“它有一种非常感性的气息——过熟的，仿佛各种奇奇怪怪的水果都要落到你手里”（132；第7章）。

And where in the East does he go? He goes to New York City, which both he and Jordan associate with transgressive sexuality. Nick says of New York, “I began to like … the racy, adventurous feel of it at night” (61; ch. 3), and Jordan observes, “There’s something very sensuous about it – overripe, as if all sorts of funny fruits were going to fall into your hands” (132; ch. 7).

更确切地说，尼克在纽约市工作，晚上也大多待在那里，住在西卵——他称之为“百老汇在一个长岛渔村孕育出的前所未有的‘地方’”（113-114；第六章），“一个自成一体的世界，拥有自己的标准和伟人”（110；第六章），一个“原始的活力在旧有的委婉语下显得格格不入”的世界（114；第六章）。换句话说，尼克暗示他身处一个离经叛道的亚文化圈。尼克认为百老汇是这种亚文化的根源，这一点值得注意，不仅因为当时的百老汇是纽约市的同性恋聚集地（Chauncey 146），还因为无论这种联系是否准确，戏剧行业一直以来都与性宽容和性实验联系在一起。

More precisely, Nick works in New York City, where he also spends most of his evenings, and lives at West Egg, “this unprecedented ‘place,’” as he puts it, “that Broadway had begotten upon a Long Island fishing village” (113–14; ch. 6), “a world complete in itself, with its own standards and its own great figures” (110; ch. 6), a world with a “raw vigor that chafed under the old euphemisms” (114; ch. 6). In other words, Nick is implying that he inhabits a transgressive subculture. And Nick’s observation that Broadway is responsible for this subculture is noteworthy both because Broadway was a gay cruising area in New York City at this time (Chauncey 146) and because the theatrical profession has always been associated, whether accurately so or not, with sexual tolerance and experimentation.

当然，当我们分析尼克时，我们实际上是在分析小说的叙述者。因此，正是尼克的视角产生了小说中存在的性暧昧之处。让我们来看……现在是时候总结一下这些暧昧之处了。正如我们所见，《了不起的盖茨比》这部小说似乎痴迷于性越轨，但这种越轨的本质并非总是清晰明了。尼克与女性发生关系，但他似乎对麦基，以及更深层次的盖茨比，都抱有性吸引力。尼克对乔丹的迷恋似乎带有同性恋色彩，因为他执着于她男孩般的外表。乔丹与尼克有染，而且“只要她点点头”（186；第九章），她本可以嫁给“好几个”男人，这本身就是女同性恋的象征。盖茨比，小说中最重要的异性恋浪漫人物，却是男同性恋的象征。最后，盖茨比和黛西——异性恋浪漫情侣的典范——最终由尼克和乔丹——小说中隐秘的同性恋欲望的化身——联系在一起。

Of course, when we analyze Nick, we’re analyzing the novel’s narrator. So it is Nick’s point of view that produces the novel’s sexual ambiguities. Let’s take a moment to sum up those ambiguities. As we have seen, The Great Gatsby is a novel that seems obsessed with sexual transgression, but the nature of that transgression is not always clear. Nick sleeps with women but seems to be sexually attracted to McKee and, more profoundly, to Gatsby. Nick’s attraction to Jordan seems to have a homoerotic dimension because of his fixation on her boyish appearance. Jordan, who is having an affair with Nick and could have married “several” men “at a nod of her head” (186; ch. 9), is a repository of lesbian signs. Gatsby, the novel’s most important heterosexual romantic figure, is a repository of gay signs. Finally, Gatsby and Daisy, the heterosexual icon of the romantic couple, are brought together by Nick and Jordan, the novel’s embodiment of closeted gay and lesbian desire.

因此，这部小说提出了许多关于人物性取向的问题，但并未给出答案。尼克是异性恋、同性恋还是双性恋？如果他的性取向中有同性恋的成分，他自己是否意识到这一点，又是否付诸行动？乔丹的性取向是什么？她自己是否知情？鉴于盖茨比对黛西的浪漫情愫，我们应该如何理解他身上那些女性化甚至略带矫揉造作的特质？小说中弥漫的性自由乃至性放纵的氛围是否仅限于异性恋领域，还是也涵盖了同性恋群体？如果涵盖，又是如何体现的？

The novel thus raises a number of questions about the sexuality of its characters, but it does not answer them. Is Nick heterosexual, gay, or bisexual? If there is a gay dimension to his sexuality, does he know it, and has he acted on it? What is Jordan’s sexual orientation? Is she aware of it? What should we make of Gatsby’s feminine, even camp, characteristics, given his romantic devotion to Daisy? Is the atmosphere of sexual freedom, even sexual license, that pervades the novel limited to the heterosexual domain, or does it include the gay world, and if so, in what ways?

我认为，最能解释小说中大部分性取向模糊性的解释是：尼克的性取向是同性恋，而他的同性恋情结影响了他对所叙述事件的感知。因此，盖茨比和乔丹成为了同性恋符号的载体，因为我们是通过尼克的视角来看待他们的，而这正是他看待他们的方式。他的感知可能源于他自身的投射（他有同性恋倾向，所以他会在别人身上看到这种倾向），也可能是因为他自身也具有同性恋倾向，所以对盖茨比和乔丹性取向中的同性恋元素格外敏感，或者两者兼而有之。但我认为，尼克之所以将叙事中的同性恋维度隐藏起来，使其成为异性恋爱情故事的潜台词，是因为他隐藏了自己的同性恋倾向。换句话说，小说的性取向模糊性源于一个异性恋情节，而这个情节却通过一种不仅对他人隐瞒，甚至对自身也隐瞒的同性恋情结来呈现。

The explanation that, I think, best accounts for most of the novel’s sexual ambiguity is that Nick’s sexual orientation is gay, and his gay sensibility influences his perception of the events he narrates. Thus, Gatsby and Jordan are repositories of gay and lesbian signs because we see them through Nick’s eyes, and this is how he sees them. His perceptions may result from his own projection (he has gay desire, so he sees signs of it in others), or he may be sensitive to the queer aspects of Gatsby’s and Jordan’s sexuality because he shares them, or both. But Nick has closeted the queer dimension of his narrative and made it a subtext of the heterosexual love story because, I would argue, he has closeted his own gay desire. In other words, the novel’s sexual ambiguity is the result of a heterosexual plot delivered by means of a gay sensibility that is hidden not only from others but from itself as well.

尼克否认自己是同性恋，这不仅体现在他与女性的性关系上（否认自己是同性恋的男性常常如此），也体现在他的自我呈现上——他似乎竭力想让我们（也包括他自己）相信他是个循规蹈矩的人。例如，在感情方面，尼克把自己塑造成小说中保守的、近乎清教徒式的形象。当他得知汤姆与“纽约的某个女人”有染时（19；第一章），他说：“我的第一反应是立刻打电话报警”（20；第一章），“我觉得黛西应该抱着孩子冲出家门，但她显然没有这种想法”（25；第一章）。同样，在允许自己与乔丹发展恋爱关系之前，尼克觉得他必须正式结束与家乡一位年轻女子的关系，因为正如他所说，“我……内心充满了各种规则，这些规则就像刹车一样抑制着我的欲望”（63-64页；第三章）。事实上，尼克对这种道德观念感到如此反感。纽约的松懈让他回到中西部后，盖茨比死后，他告诉我们：“我希望世界永远保持统一，并处于某种道德关注状态”（6；第 1 章）。

That Nick is denying his gay orientation is suggested not merely by his sexual affairs with women, which gay men in denial often have, but by his self-presentation, which seems to try too hard to convince us, and himself, of his conventionality. For example, concerning romantic matters, Nick represents himself as the conservative, almost puritanical, consciousness of the novel. When he learns that Tom is having an affair with “some woman in New York” (19; ch. 1), he says, “[M]y own instinct was to telephone immediately for the police” (20; ch. 1) and “It seemed to me that the thing for Daisy to do was to rush out of the house, child in arms but apparently there were no such intentions in her head” (25; ch. 1). Similarly, before he allows himself to become romantically involved with Jordan, Nick feels that he must officially end his relationship with a young woman he’d been seeing back home because, as he puts it, “I am … full of interior rules that act as brakes on my desires” (63–64; ch. 3). In fact, so repelled is Nick by the moral laxity of New York that when he returns to the Midwest after Gatsby’s death, he tells us, “I wanted the world to be in uniform and at a sort of moral attention forever” (6; ch. 1).

然而，与此同时，尼克似乎刻意让我们把他视为一个积极的异性恋者。例如，他告诉我们，他“和公司会计部门的一个女孩有过一段短暂的恋情”（61；第三章）。他为什么要提供这条看似无关紧要的信息呢？难道不是为了确保我们知道他是异性恋吗？他之前告诉我们，他在家乡交往的那个年轻女子——大家都认为他会娶她——只是“一个老朋友”（24；第一章），他想让我们相信，他有能力和女性发展出超越朋友的关系。同样，当他描述自己在纽约的夜晚，和其他年轻男子一起“在窗前闲逛”（62；第三章）时，尼克通过详细描述自己跟踪“浪漫的女人……到她们位于隐蔽街角的公寓”（61；第三章）的幻想，消解了这一场景中可能存在的同性恋情愫。

At the same time, however, Nick seems to go out of his way to be sure we see him as an active heterosexual. For example, he tells us he “had a short affair with a girl who … worked in the accounting department” (61; ch. 3) at his place of employment. Why does he give us this apparently irrelevant bit of information except to make sure we know he’s heterosexual? Having told us that the young woman he’d been seeing back home, whom everyone expected him to marry, was just “an old friend” (24; ch. 1), he wants to reassure us that he’s capable of being more than just friends with a woman. Similarly, when he describes his evenings in New York City, “loiter[ing] in front of windows” (62; ch. 3) with other young men like himself, Nick deflates the homoerotic potential of the scene by relating in detail his fantasies about following “romantic women … to their apartments on the corners of hidden streets” (61; ch. 3).

最后，当尼克谈到与乔丹·贝克的约会时，正如我们之前看到的，他暗示乔丹性生活放荡。为了确保我们知道尼克接受了乔丹的性服务，第四章结尾描写了他在中央公园乘坐马车浪漫游览时与乔丹接吻的场景——“我把[乔丹]拉到我身边，紧紧地搂住她……[她]笑了，于是我又把她拉近，这次更近了，脸贴着我的脸”（85；第四章）——第五章开头就告诉我们尼克回家有多晚：“那天晚上我回到西卵的时候……已经是凌晨两点了”（86；第五章）。换句话说，尼克想让我们知道，那个吻仅仅是他与乔丹浪漫邂逅的开始。

Finally, when Nick talks about dating Jordan Baker he implies, as we saw earlier, that she is sexually promiscuous. And to make sure we know that Nick is a recipient of her sexual favors, chapter 4 ends with a description of his kissing Jordan during a romantic carriage ride through Central Park – “I drew up [Jordan] beside me, tightening my arms. … [She] smiled and so I drew her up again, closer, this time to my face” (85; ch. 4) – and chapter 5 opens by telling us how late Nick got home: “When I came home to West Egg that night. … [it was] [t]wo o’clock” (86; ch. 5) in the morning. In other words, Nick wants us to know that the kiss was just the beginning of his romantic encounter with Jordan.

的确，尼克似乎过于强调自己的“正常”和诚实。小说开篇，尼克就将自己与大学里那些“狂野不羁、身份不明的男人”作对比，这些人想向他倾诉“秘密的悲伤”，因为他们知道他“倾向于保留所有判断”（5；第1章）。他说：“不正常的人很容易发现并依附于正常人身上的这种特质”（5；第1章）。也就是说，尼克身边或许围绕着一群对他咄咄逼人的“不正常”男人，但他自己却是“正常”的。后来，他又告诉我们：“我认识的人当中，诚实的人寥寥无几”（64；第3章）。而且，我们恐怕要忘记了，他在最后一章提醒我们：“我已经三十岁了……我比自欺欺人、称之为荣誉的年纪大了五年”（186；第9章）。然而，乔丹最终看穿了尼克的自欺欺人。她告诉他，

Indeed, it seems that Nick insists on his “normality” and honesty rather too much. On the very first page of the novel Nick contrasts himself to the “wild, unknown men” at his college who wanted to reveal their “secret griefs” to him because they knew he was “inclined to reserve all judgments” (5; ch. 1). He says, “The abnormal mind is quick to detect and attach itself to this quality when it appears in a normal person” (5; ch. 1). That is, Nick may be surrounded by “abnormal” men who press themselves upon him, but he himself is “normal.” Later, he tells us, “I am one of the few honest people that I have ever known” (64; ch. 3). And lest we forget, he reminds us in the very last chapter, “I’m thirty. … I’m five years too old to lie to myself and call it honor” (186; ch. 9). Jordan, however, finally sees through Nick’s self-deception. She tells him,

你说一个驾驶技术差的人只有在遇到另一个驾驶技术差的人之前才是安全的？好吧，我确实遇到了另一个驾驶技术差的人，不是吗？我的意思是，我做出如此错误的判断确实很草率。我一直以为你是一个相当诚实坦率的人。我以为这是你内心深处的骄傲。

You said a bad driver was only safe until she met another bad driver? Well I met another bad driver, didn’t I? I mean it was careless of me to make such a wrong guess. I thought you were rather an honest, straightforward person. I thought it was your secret pride.

（186；第9章）

(186; ch. 9)

换句话说，乔丹开始认为尼克（和她一样）是个越轨者，而且对自己的越轨行为不诚实。从酷儿视角来看，到了故事的这个阶段，乔丹的观察就显得颇有分量：尼克坚持自己的“正常”和诚实，这种说法已经显得苍白无力了。

In other words, Jordan has come to believe that Nick is (as is she) transgressive and dishonest about his transgression. Through a queer lens, by this point in the narrative Jordan’s observation carries some weight: Nick’s insistence on his “normality” and honesty has worn rather thin.

值得注意的是，尼克在第一次意识到自己想和乔丹发展关系的那段话中，似乎无意间对自己的性取向表达得有些含糊不清。他说：

It’s interesting to note that Nick, apparently without intending it, is somewhat ambiguous about his sexuality in the passage in which he first realizes he wants to become involved with Jordan. He says,

我知道，首先我必须彻底摆脱家里的那团乱麻。我每周都给她写信，署名“爱你的，尼克”，但我满脑子想的都是，那个女孩打网球时，上唇会渗出淡淡的汗珠。尽管如此，我还是得委婉地打破这种模糊的默契，才能真正获得自由。

I knew that first I had to get myself definitely out of that tangle back home. I’d been writing letters once a week and signing them “Love, Nick,” and all I could think of was how, when that certain girl played tennis, a faint mustache of perspiration appeared on her upper lip. Nevertheless there was a vague understanding that had to be tactfully broken off before I was free.

（64；第3章）

(64; ch. 3)

在这段文字中，尼克一如既往地强调了他的诚实和异性恋倾向。但他对那“淡淡​​的汗珠”（男性特征的象征）的反应描述却并不十分清晰。如果我们仔细分析这段文字的措辞，就会发现尼克内心感到愧疚，因为他每周都会给家乡的一位年轻女子写信，署名“爱你的尼克”，而实际上，他想和新的人约会。尼克提到的“家乡的纠葛”与他提到的“那个女孩”形成了对比。“那个女孩”这个词组，至少在过去，通常用来形容年轻男子对某个特别的年轻女子（在本例中指的是乔丹）的爱慕之情。然而，他提到的唯一爱慕迹象仅仅是“淡淡的汗珠”，而且他没有指明“那个女孩”的名字，这使得究竟是哪个年轻女子起了汗珠，以及尼克对此有何感受，都变得扑朔迷离。当然，女性脸上的汗珠并非传统意义上异性恋男性的性吸引力特征。的确，就尼克这个人物的解读而言，这的确是一个奇怪的信号，所以我认为他之所以把它藏在一个不如其他叙述清晰明了的段落里，也就不足为奇了。因此，当我听到一些读者说，他们第一次读这部小说时，以为尼克是在说家乡的那个女孩打网球时总是汗流浃背，而尼克不喜欢这样时，我并不感到惊讶。

In this passage Nick is, characteristically, emphasizing both his honesty and his heterosexuality. But his description of his response to that “faint mustache of perspiration” – an emblem of masculinity – is not particularly clear. If we look closely at the wording of the passage, we can see that Nick feels guilty writing weekly letters signed “Love, Nick” to a young woman back home when, in fact, he wants to date someone new. Nick’s reference to the “tangle back home” is thus contrasted with his reference to “that certain girl,” a phrase used, at least in the past, to describe a young man’s attraction to a special young woman, in this case to Jordan. Yet the facts that the single sign of attraction he mentions is a “faint mustache of perspiration” and that he doesn’t name “that certain girl” create a degree of ambiguity concerning which young woman develops a mustache of perspiration and how Nick feels about it. Certainly, a mustache of perspiration on a woman is not a classical male heterosexual turn-on. Indeed, in context of the interpretation of Nick being developed here it’s a queer sign, which is why I would argue that he couches it in a passage that is not as clearly written as most of the rest of his narrative. I’m not surprised, then, when I hear some readers say that, on their first reading of the novel, they thought Nick was saying that the girl back home was the one who tended to develop a mustache of perspiration during tennis and that Nick didn’t like it.

当然，我们无法确定尼克是否意识到自己性取向中的同性恋倾向。但我认为，如果他意识到了，就不会如此反复强调自己的异性恋身份、自己的“正常”以及自己的诚实。也就是说，他的否认似乎不仅仅是出于策略性地向其他角色或异性恋中心主义读者隐瞒自己的同性恋倾向。他对自身循规蹈矩的辩解构成了一种心理否认的修辞，暗示着他甚至在对自己隐瞒自己的同性恋倾向。基于这种否认的心理，我认为尼克的……正是由于他对自身性取向的无知，才使得他的同性恋情怀能够如此彻底地投射到他的叙事中，为小说增添了多重含义，并注入了多种解读的可能性。从酷儿视角来看，这极大地丰富了小说的阅读体验。

Of course, we can’t be sure whether or not Nick is aware of the gay dimension of his sexuality. But I think if he were aware of it, he wouldn’t insist so repeatedly on his heterosexuality, on his “normality,” on his honesty. That is, his denial seems to go beyond the strategic need to hide his gay orientation from other characters or from heterosexist readers. His protestations of his own conventionality constitute a rhetoric of psychological denial that suggests he is hiding his gay orientation from himself as well. In keeping with the psychology of denial, I think Nick’s blindness to his sexual orientation is precisely what gives his gay sensibility the power it has to project itself into his narrative so thoroughly, layering the novel with multiple meanings and infusing it with interpretive possibilities that, from a queer perspective, greatly enrich the reading experience it offers.

有趣的是，小说中尼克同性恋倾向所造成的性取向模糊性，以及他对自身性取向的明显否认，都与菲茨杰拉德本人在性取向问题上经历的冲突不谋而合。虽然我们不必用作者自身的性取向来解释他们对性的描写，但在菲茨杰拉德的例子中，他的生活经历与作品之间的关联实在太过显著，不容忽视。

Interestingly, the sexual ambiguity Nick’s gay sensibility creates in the novel as well as his apparent denial of his gay orientation mirror the conflicts Fitzgerald seemed to have experienced concerning his own sexuality. While we are not required to explain authors’ representations of sexuality in terms of their own sexual orientations, in Fitzgerald’s case, the correlations between his life and his work are too striking to be overlooked.

就像《了不起的盖茨比》中的人物一样，菲茨杰拉德本人似乎也对离经叛道的性行为着迷。“多年来，菲茨杰拉德总是问朋友和新认识的人，婚前是否和妻子发生过性关系，这让他很恼火”（布鲁科利 114）。他有时似乎会被那些除了性之外几乎不谈论其他话题的人所吸引。据他的妻子泽尔达说，“菲茨杰拉德和他的朋友们谈论的都是性——普通的、复杂的、混合的、花哨的性”（梅菲尔德 138）。然而，菲茨杰拉德似乎对同性恋情格外着迷，他一生中对同性恋的态度也曾经历过从玩世不恭到恐同的转变。

Much like The Great Gatsby, Fitzgerald himself seemed obsessed with transgressive sexuality. “For years Fitzgerald would annoy friends and new acquaintances by asking whether they had slept with their wives before they were married” (Bruccoli 114). And he sometimes seemed drawn to people who liked to talk of little else. According to his wife, Zelda, “all [Fitzgerald and his friends] talk[ed] about [wa]s sex – sex plain, striped, mixed, and fancy” (Mayfield 138). Fitzgerald seemed especially fascinated, however, by gay sexuality, toward which his attitude ranged, at different times during his life, from playful to homophobic.

在普林斯顿大学读本科时，菲茨杰拉德曾装扮成歌舞女郎拍摄了一张宣传照，为该校一场全部由男生组成的戏剧演出做宣传。

As a Princeton undergraduate, Fitzgerald posed for a publicity photo, dressed as a showgirl, to advertise one of the university’s all-male theatrical productions. The photo

他的事迹出现在包括《纽约时报》在内的几家报纸上，并为他带来了粉丝来信，这些粉丝希望见到他，还有一位经纪人提出安排他以女性模仿者的身份参加杂耍巡演。

appeared in several newspapers, including The New York Times, and brought him fan letters from men who wanted to meet him and from an agent who offered to book him for a vaudeville tour as a female impersonator.

（布鲁科利 62）

(Bruccoli 62)

尽管普林斯顿大学所有女性角色都由男大学生扮演，但菲茨杰拉德对反串的尝试并未止步于此。他曾女扮男装参加明尼苏达大学的兄弟会舞会，并在那里“用一句挑逗的台词震惊了（以为他是年轻女子的）男舞伴们”（布鲁科利 65）。他还保留着自己身着歌舞女郎装扮的照片，并喜欢拿给朋友们看（梅菲尔德 134）。

Although all the female roles at Princeton were played by male college students, Fitzgerald’s experimentation with drag didn’t stop there. He dressed as a woman and attended a fraternity dance at the University of Minnesota, where he “shocked his [male] dancing partners [who thought he was a young woman] with a racy line” (Bruccoli 65). And he kept the photos of himself dressed as a showgirl and liked to show them to friends (Mayfield 134).

菲茨杰拉德也喜欢拿自己开玩笑，仿佛他是同性恋。“他在军队服役期间，曾给埃德蒙·威尔逊（他的朋友兼文学评论家）寄了两张自己的照片，说是让威尔逊把这两张照片送给某个可怜的、没有母亲的……没有梦想的仙女”（梅菲尔德 134）。后来，他告诉威尔逊，他的一个愿望是“和一个风流成性的年轻男子去海边度过一个有偿的浪漫周末。他补充说，这是深渊与深渊的呼唤”（梅菲尔德 134）。当然，菲茨杰拉德本意是想用这些话来“开一些关于自己的低俗玩笑”（梅菲尔德 134），但它们也揭示了他对同性恋生活的好奇，以及他性幻想中同性恋的一面。

Fitzgerald also liked to banter about himself as if he were gay. “While he was in the army, he sent Edmund Wilson [his friend and literary critic] two photographs of himself in a letter, saying that he enclosed the two pictures for Wilson to give to some poor, motherless … fairy who had no dream” (Mayfield 134). Later, he told Wilson that one of his longings was “to go with a young man affectueux [affectionate] for a paid amorous weekend on the coast. It was, he added, deep calling to deep” (Mayfield 134). Certainly, Fitzgerald intended these remarks as “off-color jokes about himself” (Mayfield 134), but they reveal his curiosity about gay life as well as the gay dimension of his sexual imagination.

在其他情况下，菲茨杰拉德对同性恋的兴趣显然带有恐同色彩：“他一直公开鄙视‘娘娘腔’”（布鲁科利 278），他和欧内斯特·海明威喜欢拿“恋童癖、肛交和其他变态行为”开玩笑（梅菲尔德 133）。事实上，正是“娘娘腔”让菲茨杰拉德将他与海明威的亲密友谊“破坏”归咎于此（梅菲尔德 142）。菲茨杰拉德大概指的是关于他和海明威是同性恋的传闻，这让他非常恼火（布鲁科利 278）。然而，菲茨杰拉德自己也“不介意”暗示海明威是同性恋，“称他为‘嗜血症患者，流血男孩’”（梅菲尔德 136）。

At other times, Fitzgerald’s interest in homosexuality was clearly homophobic: “He had always been outspokenly contemptuous of ‘fairies’” (Bruccoli 278), and he and Ernest Hemingway liked to joke “about pederasty, anal eroticism, and other forms of perversion” (Mayfield 133). Indeed, it was “the fairies” whom Fitzgerald blamed for “spoil[ing]” his close friendship with Hemingway (Mayfield 142). Presumably, Fitzgerald was referring to the rumors that he and Hemingway were gay, which upset Fitzgerald greatly (Bruccoli 278). Yet Fitzgerald was “not averse” to implying, himself, that Hemingway was gay, “referring to him as ‘Hemophile, the Bleeding Boy’” (Mayfield 136).

同性恋倾向也是菲茨杰拉德婚姻中一个令人担忧的问题。泽尔达认为她的丈夫“与海明威有染”（布鲁科利 278），而且“为了证明自己的男子气概，菲茨杰拉德决定尝试与妓女发生性关系，并购买了避孕套；泽尔达发现了这些避孕套，两人因此爆发了激烈的争吵”（布鲁科利 279）。泽尔达还认为自己“有潜在的同性恋倾向”，而且“当巴黎臭名昭著的‘亚马逊女战士’多莉·王尔德对泽尔达示好时，菲茨杰拉德勃然大怒”（布鲁科利 279）。

Gay sexuality was also an issue of concern in Fitzgerald’s marriage. Zelda believed that her husband “was involved in a homosexual liaison with Hemingway” (Bruccoli 278), and “to verify his masculinity, Fitzgerald decided to try sleeping with a whore and purchased condoms; Zelda found them, and a bitter argument ensued” (Bruccoli 279). Zelda also believed that she, herself, “was a latent lesbian,” and “Fitzgerald was furious when Dolly Wilde, a notorious Paris ‘amazon,’ made a pass at Zelda” (Bruccoli 279).

尽管我们无法就菲茨杰拉德的性取向得出任何可靠的结论——关于他的性行为没有任何确凿的数据，而且有关他性欲的证据往往被相互矛盾的传闻所掩盖——但我们可以非常肯定地说，性，尤其是同性恋性取向，对他来说是一个重要的问题。显然，他对同性恋生活既充满好奇，又内心充满矛盾，因为他既被同性恋所提供的性可能性所吸引，又感到厌恶。他对同性恋世界的恐同反应，即便没有揭示其他任何信息，也至少表明菲茨杰拉德不愿承认自己在性取向方面所经历的冲突。

Although it’s impossible to draw any reliable conclusions about Fitzgerald’s sexual orientation – there is no concrete data about his sexual activity, and evidence of his sexual desire is often marred by contradictory hearsay – we can very safely say that sexuality, especially gay sexuality, was an important issue for him. It is clear that he was intensely curious about gay life and intensely conflicted about it as well, for he was both drawn to and repulsed by the sexual possibilities it offered. And his homophobic response to the gay world reveals, if it reveals nothing else, that Fitzgerald did not want to admit the conflicts he experienced concerning his sexuality.

鉴于菲茨杰拉德在其小说创作中一贯依赖自身经历，因此， 《了不起的盖茨比》对越轨性行为的关注必然包含酷儿维度，无论作者是否出于本意，都不足为奇。正如我们所见，菲茨杰拉德对越轨性行为的迷恋绝不仅限于异性恋领域。如果正如作者自身经历所暗示的那样，杰伊·盖茨比体现了菲茨杰拉德致力于追求异性恋理想的能力，那么尼克·卡拉威无疑体现了他否认自身矛盾性取向中同性恋维度的能力。因此，透过酷儿视角，真实的尼克·卡拉威得以展现——或者至少得以清晰呈现——我们看到，他隐秘的同性恋倾向如何将美国最著名的异性恋爱情故事之一转化为酷儿解读。

Given Fitzgerald’s consistent reliance on his own personal experience for the material he used in his novels, it should not be surprising that The Great Gatsby’s focus on transgressive sexuality should include a queer dimension, whether the author intended it so or not. For as we have seen, Fitzgerald’s fascination with transgressive sexuality was in no way limited to the heterosexual domain. And if, as the author’s own life suggests, Jay Gatsby embodies Fitzgerald’s capacity to devote himself to the pursuit of a heterosexual ideal, then surely Nick Carraway embodies his capacity to deny the gay dimension of his conflicted sexuality. Through a queer lens, then, the real Nick Carraway does come out – or at least comes into focus – as we see the ways in which his closeted gay sensibility opens one of America’s best-known heterosexual love stories to queer interpretations.

拓展练习题：女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿视角下的其他文学作品

Questions for further practice: lesbian, gay, and queer approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评来解读它们所指的文学作品或其他文本。你可以根据自己的选择来回答这些问题。你回答这些问题的目的、你文章的重点方向以及你自身认同的批判取向，将决定你的文章是被视为女同性恋、男同性恋还是酷儿批评的范例。但请注意，问题2中提到的对传统同性恋和异性恋定义的否定，正是酷儿理论的核心原则。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use lesbian, gay, and queer criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice. Your purpose in addressing these questions, the way in which you focus your essay, and your own self-identified critical orientation will determine whether your essay is considered an example of lesbian, gay, or queer criticism. Note, however, that the rejection of traditional definitions of homosexuality and heterosexuality referred to in question 2 is the primary tenet of queer theory.

1薇拉·凯瑟的《保罗的遭遇》（1905）是如何展现同性恋者在异性恋主导的世界中成长过程中所面临的社会和心理冲突的？这部小说又在哪些方面体现了强制异性恋的运作机制？

1 How does Willa Cather’s “Paul’s Case” (1905) represent, among other things, the social and psychological conflicts of gay identity coming of age in a heterosexist world? In what ways might the story be said to illustrate the operations of compulsory heterosexuality?

2托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）中对性的描写是如何超越传统同性恋和异性恋定义的？例如，妓女们与男人、性以及彼此之间的关系；杰拉尔丁与丈夫和猫的关系；乔利与猎人达琳、波琳和佩科拉的关系；佩科拉与玛丽·简糖果的关系；索普黑德·丘奇与维尔玛和小女孩们的关系；亨利先生与妓女和麦克蒂尔家女孩们的关系；等等。换句话说，这部小说是如何揭示“异性恋”和“同性恋”这两个范畴不足以解释我们人类性行为的？

2 How do representations of sexuality in Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) exceed traditional definitions of homosexuality and heterosexuality? Consider, for example, the prostitutes’ relationship to men, to sex, and to one another; Geraldine’s relationship to her husband and to the cat; Cholly’s relationship to the hunters, Darlene, Pauline, and Pecola; Pecola’s relationship to the Mary Jane candies; Soaphead Church’s relationship to Velma and to little girls; Mr. Henry’s relationship to the prostitutes and to the MacTeer girls; and so forth. In other words, how does the novel reveal the inadequacy of the categories “heterosexual” and “homosexual” for our understanding of human sexuality?

3尽管亨利·詹姆斯显然过着独身生活，但许多学者认为他的作品属于同性恋文学经典，因为作品中流露出同性恋的情感，而且作者与他指导的年轻男性保持着长期的关系，并给他们写信表达爱意和奉献。师徒关系也是詹姆斯小说中反复出现的主题。请探讨作者在《螺丝在拧紧》（1898）中对师徒关系的描写。昆特与迈尔斯的关系是否代表了师徒关系中潜在的阴暗面？而女家庭教师（是否是詹姆斯的化身？）是否体现了这种关系中自我牺牲的奉献？从这个角度来看，我们该如何理解迈尔斯的死？（值得注意的是，一位杰出男学生的突然离世是詹姆斯小说中反复出现的主题。）

3 Although Henry James apparently led a celibate life, many scholars claim his work for the gay canon because of its gay sensibility and because of the author’s long-term relationships with the younger men whom he mentored and to whom he wrote letters expressing his love and devotion. The master–pupil relationship is also a recurring theme in James’ fiction. Explore the author’s representation of the master–pupil relationship in The Turn of the Screw (1898). Might Quint’s relationship to Miles represent the dark potential of the master–pupil bond, while the governess (a stand-in for James?) illustrates its self-sacrificing devotion? From this perspective, what do we make of Miles’ death? (It is interesting to note that the sudden, mysterious death of an exceptional male pupil is a recurring theme in James’ fiction.)

4分析珍妮特·温特森的小说《橘子不是唯一的水果》（1985）中的性政治。这部作品希望读者理解女同性恋性行为与异性恋家庭、教会等社会/心理/政治力量之间的关系。小说中描绘的压抑性宗教团体的态度如何体现了社会对女同性恋的普遍压迫？

4 Analyze the sexual politics of Jeanette Winterson’s Oranges Are Not the Only Fruit (1985). What does the text want its readers to understand about the relationships among lesbian sexuality and such social/psychological/political forces as the heterosexual family and the church? How might the attitude of the repressive religious sect represented in the novel illustrate the oppression of lesbianism by society in general?

5探讨玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818）中（看似无意识的）同性恋隐喻。我们如何论证维克多的真爱是克莱瓦尔（她无私地照顾维克多度过了漫长的病痛），而不是伊丽莎白？沃尔顿对维克多的浪漫仰慕与这种同性情谊有何相似之处？伊丽莎白与克莱瓦尔之间又存在哪些相似之处？与维克多和克莱瓦尔的关系，以及玛丽·雪莱与她的丈夫珀西，以及他们共同的朋友和伴侣拜伦勋爵的关系？

5 Examine the (apparently unconscious) homoerotic subtext of Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818). How might we argue that Victor’s true love is Clerval (whose self-sacrificing care nurses the protagonist through a long illness) rather than Elizabeth? How is this same-sex bond paralleled in Walton’s romantic admiration of Victor? What similarities might we find between Elizabeth’s relationship to Victor and Clerval, and Mary Shelley’s relationship to her husband, Percy, and to their mutual friend and companion Lord Byron?

笔记

Notes

1跨性别者的性别认同（男性或女性）与其生理性别（男性或女性）不符。例如，一位跨性别男性拥有男性的生理构造，但他内心深处认为自己是女性：他的生理性别是男性，但他的性别认同是女性。此外，他的跨性别身份并不代表他的性取向。最后，一位接受过变性手术的跨性别者不再是跨性别者（因为生理性别和性别认同现在一致），而是变性人。

1 A transgender person’s gender (masculine or feminine) doesn’t match his or her biological sex (male or female). For example, a transgender man has the anatomy of a male but knows that, inside, he is a woman: his biological sex is male, but his gender is feminine. Furthermore, his transgender status doesn’t indicate his sexual orientation. Finally, a transgender individual who has undergone the process of sex change is no longer transgender (for sex and gender now match) but transsexual.

正如你将在本章“酷儿批评”部分看到的那样，“酷儿” （queer）一词可以有多种不同的含义。例如，酷儿理论指的是一种理解人类性行为的视角，这种视角并非基于性吸引对象的生理性别。此外，“酷儿”一词也经常被用作一个积极的、包容性的术语，指代LGBT（或GLBT）群体以及任何非严格意义上的异性恋者。因此，包容性的缩写是LGBTQ（或GLBTQ）。虽然你可能更常听到LGBT（或GLBT）这个词，但为了本章的目的，我们将使用包容性的缩写LGBTQ。（ LGBTQ中的Q也可以指代“质疑”（questioning），即指代那些对自己的性别或性取向感到不确定的人，或者同时指代“酷儿”和“质疑”这两个概念。）

The word queer, as you’ll see in the “Queer criticism” section of this chapter, can have several different meanings. For example, queer theory refers to a perspective for understanding human sexuality that is not based on the biological sex of the people to whom one is sexually attracted. The word queer is also frequently used as a positive, inclusive term referring to LGBT (or GLBT) individuals and to anyone who is, in whatever way, not strictly heterosexual. The inclusive acronym, therefore, is LGBTQ (or GLBTQ). Although you may hear the term LGBT (or GLBT) used more frequently, for our purposes in this chapter we’ll use the inclusive acronym LGBTQ. (The Q in LGBTQ can also refer to the word questioning that is, to refer to people who are uncertain about their gender or their sexual orientation or to refer to both queer and questioning.)

2有关对女同性恋者和男同性恋者的歧视的完整讨论，请参阅 Cruikshank。

11 非裔美国人批评

11 African American criticism

每个学期，我都会震惊地发现，在我的批判理论课上，竟然有那么多学生——包括各个种族的高年级英语专业学生——对非裔美国人历史上的一些里程碑事件，例如“中段航程”、“地下铁路”、“大迁徙”、“哈莱姆文艺复兴”、“民权运动”、“黑人权力运动”和“黑人艺术运动”——知之甚少或一无所知。尽管美国高中越来越重视多元文化教育，大学也开设了越来越多的非裔美国人经历、历史和文学课程，但这些领域的教育努力仍然不足以满足我们这样一个多元文化社会中学生的需求，尤其考虑到他们未来将作为世界公民，在一个日益紧密联系的全球社会中扮演重要角色。

Each semester I’m always alarmed to learn how many students in my critical theory course – including senior English majors of all races – are unacquainted or minimally acquainted with such milestones of African American history as the Middle Passage, the Underground Railroad, the Great Migration, the Harlem Renaissance, the Civil Rights Movement, the Black Power Movement, and the Black Arts Movement. Despite the increased focus on multicultural education in America’s high schools and the increased provision of college courses in African American experience, history, and literature, educational efforts in these areas remain inadequate to the needs of students in a multicultural society such as ours, especially in light of their future role as world citizens of a rapidly shrinking globe.

由于非裔美国人在美国人口中占比巨大，并且他们对艺术做出了卓越贡献——包括数量庞大、享誉国际的文学作品——我应该可以假定我的高年级英语专业学生对非裔美国人的历史和文学有一定的了解，我可以以此为基础展开教学。但我的工作很大一部分是提供背景知识，姑且这么说吧。鉴于时间有限，我常常需要概述我认为学生应该了解的内容，并希望能够激发他们学习的欲望，从而让他们对这个领域产生足够的兴趣，并自主探索更多知识。从某种意义上说，这正是我在这里要做的事情：让你们了解影响非裔美国文学史的种族问题，介绍当今非裔美国种族理论家关注的基本问题，阐述当代非裔美国文学批评家的研究兴趣，并希望你们能够对这个令人兴奋的文学研究领域产生足够的兴趣，并自主探索。

Because African Americans constitute such a large part of the US population, and because they have contributed so much to the arts – including an enormous, internationally acclaimed literary output – I should be able to assume that my senior English majors have a certain amount of knowledge about African American history and literature on which I can build. But much of my job consists of providing background knowledge, for lack of a better term. And given the constraints of time, I often find myself outlining what I think students should know and, hopefully, promoting their desire to know it, so that they’ll become interested enough in the field to pursue more knowledge on their own. In a sense, that’s what I’ll be trying to do here: acquaint you with the racial issues that have informed African American literary history, introduce you to the fundamental concerns of African American race theorists today, describe the range of interests of contemporary African American literary critics, and hope that you’ll become interested enough to pursue this exciting field of literary study on your own.

种族问题与非裔美国人文学史

Racial issues and African American literary history

美国教育中几乎完全排除了非裔美国人历史和文化，直到20世纪60年代末才开始有人关注这个问题，这反映了……在此之前，非裔美国人的历史和文化一直被排除在美国官方历史版本之外。直到近几十年，美国历史教科书才开始收录那些曾被压制以维护白人美国文化霸权或统治地位的非裔美国人信息。例如，用于教授美国历史（更准确地说，应该称之为白人美国历史）的教科书，对骇人听闻的“中段航程”（将非洲奴隶运过大西洋）期间的奴隶起义、种植园中无数次的奴隶叛乱，以及奴隶们在奴隶主眼皮底下建立的沟通和反抗网络，几乎只字未提。此外，20世纪20年代哈莱姆区涌现出的巨大创造力——包括黑人文学、音乐、绘画、雕塑、哲学和政治辩论——被称为“哈莱姆文艺复兴”，也未得到应有的关注。

The virtual exclusion of African American history and culture from American education, which began to be addressed only in the late 1960s, reflects the virtual exclusion of African American history and culture from official versions of American history before that time. Only over the past few decades have American history books begun to include information about black Americans that had been repressed in order to maintain the cultural hegemony, or dominance, of white America. For example, textbooks that were used to teach American history (which, more accurately, should have been called white American history) said little or nothing about the slave uprisings during the horrific Middle Passage (the transportation of African captives across the Atlantic Ocean), the numerous slave rebellions on the plantations, and the network of communication and resistance developed by slaves right under the noses of the slavemasters. And such accomplishments as the tremendous outpouring of creative enterprises – including, for example, black literature, music, painting, sculpture, philosophy, and political debate – associated with Harlem during the 1920s and known as the Harlem Renaissance were not given the attention they deserved.

我之所以选择奴隶反抗和哈莱姆文艺复兴这两个例子，是因为我认为它们最清晰地揭示了将非裔美国人排除在美国历史之外的政治动机。一部认真研究奴隶反抗的历史，会彻底打破那种认为奴隶安于现状、愚钝无知，并对白人主人的父辈式指导感恩戴德的种族主义刻板印象——仿佛没有主人，奴隶要么会沦为迷途的孩子，要么会成为危险的野蛮人。而一部认真研究非裔美国文学天才的历史，也会彻底打破非裔美国人低人一等的神话——正是这种神话支撑着许多种族主义政策和实践。

I choose these two examples – slave resistance and the Harlem Renaissance – because I think they illustrate most clearly the political motives that lay behind the exclusion of African Americans from American history. A conscientious history of slave resistance would have blasted the racist stereotype of the contented, dimwitted slave who was grateful for the paternal guidance of the white master, without whom the slave would have been either a lost child or a dangerous savage. And a conscientious history of African American literary genius would have blasted the myth of African American inferiority on which so many racist policies and practices rested.

鉴于如此多的非裔美国文学作品都涉及种族主义——作为非裔美国人经历的文学记录，这又怎能不涉及呢？——我们不妨花点时间来定义一些关于种族主义的关键概念，因为许多人对这个概念仍然存在误解。“种族主义”一词在日常对话中并不常见，它指的是基于这样一种信念而产生的种族优越性、劣等性和纯洁性：道德和智力特征，如同生理特征一样，是区分不同种族的生物学属性。种族主义指的是一个种族对另一个种族的社会政治统治所导致的不平等权力关系，这种关系最终导致了系统性的歧视行为（例如，种族隔离、统治和迫害）。因此，虽然任何人都有可能成为种族主义者，但要成为种族主义者——要能够系统性地进行种族隔离、统治或迫害——一个人必须身居政治统治地位，成为政治统治群体的一员，而在美国，这通常意味着这个人必须是白人。换句话说，系统性的种族主义行为（例如，剥夺有色人种的就业、住房、教育或其他任何他们应享有的权利）只有在实施者普遍能够逍遥法外的情况下才会经常发生。而当实施者所属的群体控制着政治、司法和执法系统中的大部分权力职位时，他们就能够逍遥法外。

Given that so much African American literature deals with racism – as a literary record of African American experience, how could it not? – let’s take a moment to define some key concepts concerning that issue about which many people still have misconceptions. Racialism, a word we don’t often hear in everyday speech, refers to the belief in racial superiority, inferiority, and purity based on the conviction that moral and intellectual characteristics, just like physical characteristics, are biological properties that differentiate the races. Racism refers to the unequal power relations that grow from the sociopolitical domination of one race by another and that result in systematic discriminatory practices (for example, segregation, domination, and persecution). Therefore, although anyone can be a racialist, in order to be a racist – in order to be in a position to systematically segregate, dominate, or persecute – one has to be in a position of power as a member of the politically dominant group, which in America usually means that one has to be white. In other words, the systematic practice of racism (for example, denying qualified persons of color employment, housing, education, or anything else to which they’re entitled) can occur on a regular basis only when those who do it can expect, by and large, to get away with it. And those who do it can expect to get away with it when the group to which they belong controls most of the positions of power in the political, judicial, and law-enforcement systems.1

换句话说，只有当种族主义制度化时，系统性的种族歧视才会发生。制度化的种族主义指的是将种族主义政策和做法纳入社会运作的各个机构中，例如：教育；联邦、州和地方政府；法律，包括法律条文以及法院和警察的执行方式；医疗保健，从科研经费的分配到医院选址，再到对患者的治疗，医疗保健的各个方面都可能存在种族偏见；以及企业界，尽管企业官方声称奉行机会均等政策，但其在招聘和晋升方面往往存在种族歧视。

To put the matter another way, the systematic practice of racial discrimination can occur only when racism has become institutionalized. Institutionalized racism refers to the incorporation of racist policies and practices in the institutions by which a society operates: for example, education; federal, state, and local governments; the law, both in terms of what is written on the books and how it is implemented by the courts and by police officials; health care, which can be racially biased in everything from the allocation of research dollars to the location of hospitals to the treatment of individual patients; and the corporate world, which often practices racial discrimination in its hiring and promotion despite whatever equal-opportunity policies it officially claims to have.

制度性种族主义在歧视非裔美国人方面发挥了极其有效的作用，其中之一便是美国文学经典。正如许多人可能了解的那样，西方（英国、欧洲和美国）文学经典一直被一种以欧洲为中心的普世主义定义所主导：文学作品被定义为伟大的艺术，被定义为“普世的”——与所有人的经验相关——并且只有当它们反映欧洲经验并符合欧洲文学传统的风格和主题时，才能被纳入经典，也就是说，只有当它们与那些已被认定为“伟大”的欧洲作品相似时，才能被纳入经典。因为欧洲中心主义的核心在于认为欧洲文化远胜于其他所有文化。尽管非裔美国人拥有可以追溯到十八世纪的悠久而辉煌的文学历史，但白人美国文学史学家即便考虑黑人作家，也只是将他们视为支流或分支，而非美国文学史不可分割的一部分。因此，直到最近，包括用于高中和大学课程教学的选集在内，美国文学选集基本上都只收录白人男性作家的作品。因此，文学经典被用来维护白人文化霸权。

One area in which institutionalized racism has been very effective in discriminating against African Americans is the American literary canon. As many of you probably know, the Western (British, European, and American) literary canon has been dominated by a Eurocentric definition of universalism: literary works have been defined as great art, as “universal” – relevant to the experience of all people – and included in the canon only when they reflect European experience and conform to the style and subject matter of the European literary tradition, that is, only when they resemble those European works already deemed “great.” For Eurocentrism is the belief that European culture is vastly superior to all others. Although African Americans can boast a long and impressive literary history dating back to the eighteenth century, white American literary historians considered black writers, when they considered them at all, as a tributary or an offshoot rather than part and parcel of American literary history. Therefore, until recently, anthologies of American literature, including those used to teach high school and college courses, were confined largely to the work of white male writers. The literary canon has thus been used to maintain white cultural hegemony.

当然，这种情况已经开始改变，但改变的速度相当缓慢。尽管当代美国黑人作家如今确实享有盛誉——例如，托妮·莫里森（1993年诺贝尔文学奖得主）、爱丽丝·沃克、约翰·埃德加·威德曼、玛雅·安杰卢、格洛丽亚·内勒、伊什梅尔·里德、尼基·乔瓦尼、查尔斯·约翰逊、丽塔·多夫、雪莉·安妮·威廉姆斯、奥古斯特·威尔逊、琼·乔丹、托妮·凯德·班巴拉和欧内斯特·J·盖恩斯等都是最受赞誉的美国作家——但无论是过去还是现在，黑人作家的作品在美国文学课程的教学大纲中仍然常常被忽视。

This situation has begun to change, of course, but that change is coming rather slowly. Although contemporary black American authors certainly hold top honors today – with, for example, Toni Morrison (who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1993), Alice Walker, John Edgar Wideman, Maya Angelou, Gloria Naylor, Ishmael Reed, Nikki Giovanni, Charles Johnson, Rita Dove, Sherley Anne Williams, August Wilson, June Jordan, Toni Cade Bambara, and Ernest J. Gaines among the most widely acclaimed American authors – works by black writers, past and present, are still too often underrepresented on course syllabi in American literature courses.

制度化的种族主义助长了种族歧视，这往往体现在社会中根深蒂固的种族主义刻板印象以及对狭隘的盎格鲁-撒克逊式审美标准的坚持上。在20世纪60年代末“黑即美！”和“大声说出来：我是黑人，我为此自豪！”的口号响起，呼吁非裔美国人彻底改变自我定义和自我认知之前，许多非裔美国人饱受内化种族主义的折磨。尽管黑人自豪运动取得了成功，但许多人仍然……时至今日，有色人种仍然饱受种族主义之苦。内化种族主义源于种族主义社会对有色人种的心理操控，使他们相信白人至上。内化种族主义的受害者通常觉得自己不如白人，缺乏吸引力、价值感和能力，并且常常希望自己看起来更像白人，例如拥有更浅的肤色或更直的头发。托妮·莫里森在《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）中为我们呈现了一幅令人不寒而栗的内化种族主义画像。小说中的黑人女孩佩科拉·布里德洛夫看不到自己的美丽，她认为如果自己拥有一双蓝眼睛，就会变得漂亮、快乐，并被人爱戴。

The promotion of racial discrimination by institutionalized racism is often mirrored in a society’s racist stereotypes and in its adherence to a narrow standard of Anglo-Saxon beauty. Before “Black is beautiful!” and “Say it loud: I’m black and I’m proud!” sounded the call for a radical change in African American self-definition and self-perception in the late 1960s, many African Americans suffered from internalized racism. And despite the success of black-pride advocates, many people of color continue to suffer from it today. Internalized racism results from the psychological programming by which a racist society indoctrinates people of color to believe in white superiority. Victims of internalized racism generally feel inferior to whites, less attractive, less worthwhile, less capable, and often wish they looked more white, for example had lighter skin or straighter hair. Toni Morrison provides us with one of the most chilling portraits of internalized racism in The Bluest Eye (1970), in which Pecola Breedlove, a young black girl who can’t see her own beauty, believes she would be pretty, happy, and loved if only she had blue eyes.

内化种族主义往往会导致种族内部歧视，指的是黑人社区内部对肤色较深、非洲特征更明显的人的歧视。电影《最蓝的眼睛》就展现了这种现象：佩科拉因为肤色较深而遭到其他黑人孩子的欺负，而肤色较浅的莫琳·皮尔却被同样的黑人孩子视为高人一等。电影导演斯派克·李在《校园风云》（1988）中也描绘了种族内部歧视，片中一所传统黑人学院的学生根据外貌的“白”或“黑”程度分成了两个敌对的群体。制度性种族主义造成的经济困境和社会边缘化已是众所周知，但内化种族主义和种族内部歧视也揭示了由此带来的毁灭性心理创伤。

Internalized racism often results in intra-racial racism, which refers to discrimination within the black community against those with darker skin and more African features. We see this phenomenon illustrated in The Bluest Eye when Pecola is picked on by other black children for having dark skin, while another black child, the light-skinned Maureen Peal, is treated by the same black youngsters as if she were superior to them. Filmmaker Spike Lee also portrays intra-racial racism in School Daze (1988), in which students at a historically black college form two rival groups based on the relative “whiteness” or “blackness” of their physical appearance.2 While the economic hardship and social marginalization caused by institutionalized racism are common knowledge, internalized racism and intra-racial racism illustrate the devastating psychological experiences that also result.

鉴于非裔美国人不得不面对多种形式的种族主义，许多非裔美国人经历着W.E.B.杜波依斯在其著作《黑人的灵魂》（1903年）中首次描述的“双重意识”或“双重视野”也就不足为奇了。这种双重意识指的是他们意识到自己属于两种相互冲突的文化：一种是源于非洲根源并在美国土地上经历了独特历史演变的非洲文化；另一种是白人强加于美国的欧洲文化。对许多非裔美国人来说，这意味着在家中拥有一种文化身份，而在白人主导的公共空间，例如工作场所和学校，则拥有另一种文化身份。双重意识有时还体现在他们会说两种语言上。在家中，非裔美国人有时会使用非裔美国人白话英语（AAVE，也称为黑人英语或黑人方言），这种语言符合所有真正语言的语法标准，但许多白人和一些非裔美国人仍然将其视为不合格或不正确的英语，而不是将其视为一种独立的语言。

Given the multiple forms of racism with which African Americans have had to contend, it should come as no surprise that many African Americans experience what W. E. B. DuBois first described in The Souls of Black Folk (1903) as double consciousness or double vision, the awareness of belonging to two conflicting cultures: the African culture, which grew from African roots and was transformed by its own unique history on American soil, and the European culture imposed by white America. For many black Americans this means having one cultural self at home and another cultural self in white-dominated public space, such as the workplace and the school. And double consciousness sometimes involves speaking two languages. Black culture lived at home sometimes includes the use of African American Vernacular English (AAVE, also called Ebonics or Black Vernacular English), which fulfills all the grammatical criteria of a genuine language but is still dismissed by many white and some black Americans as substandard or incorrect English rather than recognized as a language in its own right.

对于黑人作家而言，“双重意识”意味着他们必须决定主要面向黑人读者、白人读者还是两者兼顾。这一决定反过来又影响到作家所使用的语言类型。例如，哈莱姆文艺复兴时期的诗人康蒂·卡伦选择使用高度精炼的标准白人英语，以及符合欧洲文学传统的古典典故风格。这种风格在他的十四行诗《我仍惊叹》（1925）的以下几行中就体现得淋漓尽致，其中引用了希腊神话。演讲者质疑上帝为何要“把诗人变成黑人，并让他歌唱”，并说，如果“祂屈尊挑剔”，那么上帝就无法……

For black writers, double consciousness has meant having to decide whether to write primarily for a black audience, a white audience, or both. This decision involves, in turn, the kind of language the writer uses. For example, Harlem Renaissance poet Countee Cullen chose to use highly polished, standard white English and a classically allusive style that conforms to the best of the European literary tradition. This style is evident, for example, in the Greek mythological allusions in the following lines from his sonnet “Yet Do I Marvel” (1925). The speaker, questioning why God would “make a poet black, and bid him sing,” says that, if “He stoop[ed] to quibble,” God could

坦塔罗斯遭受折磨的原因必须明确说明。

Make plain the reason tortured Tantalus

被变幻莫测的果实所诱惑，他宣称

Is baited by the fickle fruit, declare

如果仅仅是蛮横的任性注定了西西弗斯的命运

If merely brute caprice dooms Sisyphus

艰难地攀登永无止境的阶梯。

To struggle up a never-ending stair.

尽管库伦的大部分诗歌都包含与种族相关的政治主题，但他认为黑人作家应该像白人作家一样，拥有创作自由，可以根据自身的艺术灵感进行创作，而不必考虑本族群的政治需求。当然，这位诗人对正式英语和希腊神话的运用引发了人们对其艺术灵感合法性的质疑，因为这些灵感源自几个世纪以来压迫非洲人民的种族主义文化。但库伦古典风格的诗歌仍然表明，非裔美国作家完全有能力以他们喜欢的任何风格进行写作，从而有力地驳斥了非洲人低人一等的种族主义假设。

Although most of Cullen’s poetry contains political themes relating to race, he believed black authors should be as free as white authors to create according to the dictates of their own artistic inspiration without being obliged to consider the political needs of their people. Of course, this poet’s use of formal English and Greek mythology raised questions about the validity of his artistic inspiration because it derived from the racist culture that had oppressed African peoples for centuries. But Cullen’s classically crafted verse nevertheless demonstrated that African American writers were more than capable of writing in whatever style they preferred and thus provided a powerful argument against the racist assumption of African inferiority.

与之形成鲜明对比的是，另一位在哈莱姆文艺复兴时期涌现的作家兰斯顿·休斯的大部分作品都运用了带有黑人语言节奏和布鲁斯音乐韵律的白话英语。他笔下充满力量、感人至深的文字——白人读者也能从中欣赏，并从中了解黑人文化的创造力——讲述着非裔美国人的故事，歌颂着他们丰富的文化遗产，并呼吁为黑人公民争取平等的机会。例如，我们可以在《早安》（1951）的以下诗句中看到这种风格，诗中运用了具体的意象，并展现了作者街头智慧和白话化的语言风格。诗中的叙述者哀叹着那些渴望美好生活的有色人种的希望破灭，他们“肤色黝黑/茫然/睁大双眼/怀揣梦想/走出纽约的宾夕法尼亚车站”：

In contrast, much of the work of Langston Hughes, another writer who emerged during the Harlem Renaissance, uses vernacular English resonant with the rhythms of black speech patterns and blues music. His powerfully moving writing – which white readers, too, can appreciate and from which they can learn about the creativity of black culture – speaks of and for African Americans, celebrating their rich cultural heritage and calling for equal opportunity for black citizens. We see this style, for example, in the concrete imagery and the streetwise, vernacular quality of the voice in the following lines from “Good Morning” (1951). The speaker laments the dashed hopes of people of color, in search of a better life, who’ve “come dark / wondering / wide-eyed / dreaming / out of Penn Station” in New York:

大门打开了——

The gates open –

但那里有酒吧

but there’re bars

每个大门处。

at each gate.

会发生什么

What happens

梦想被搁置了吗？

to a dream deferred?

爸爸，你没听说吗？

Daddy, ain’t you heard?

尽管我们对文学语言和风格的讨论实际上是对诗学——即文学手法和策略——的探讨，但它显然也是对政治——即政治、社会和经济权力的现实——的探讨。正如卡伦和休斯的例子所表明的那样，黑人作家选择的文学风格与其对作家作为社会成员角色的政治观点密不可分。受压迫群体。事实上，黑人文学界最古老的问题之一就是黑人作家在种族主义社会中的社会角色。

Although our discussion of literary language and style is a discussion of poetics – that is, of literary devices and strategies – it is clearly also a discussion of politics, that is, of the realities of political, social, and economic power. For as the Cullen and Hughes examples demonstrate, the literary style black writers choose cannot be separated from their political views on the writer’s role as a member of an oppressed group. Indeed, one of the oldest issues in the black literary community concerns the social role of the black writer in a racist society.

毕竟，非裔美国人的写作始于十八世纪，很大程度上是非洲奴隶为向白人证明自身人性而做出的努力。奴隶主们为了维护奴隶制的合法性，声称非洲人并非真正的人，因为他们不会写诗！（当然，奴隶主们刻意忽略了他们曾禁止奴隶学习阅读的事实。）事实上，菲利斯·惠特利的奴隶主鼓励她写诗，以驳斥这种种族主义论调。奴隶们也撰写自传体叙事作品，以警醒北方白人，让他们了解自己的困境。哈丽雅特·雅各布斯的《一个女奴的生平轶事》（1861年）便是其中之一。然而，即使在北方，人们普遍认为非洲奴隶没有写作能力，更遑论文学创作，以至于许多叙事作品都附有白人赞助人的序言，以证明作者的身份和叙事的真实性。事实上，如何吸引白人读者阅读他们原本可能抗拒的作品，一直是许多黑人作家面临的一项挑战。

After all, African American writing began during the eighteenth century largely as the effort of African slaves to prove their humanity to whites. For slaveholders, as one of their many attempts to justify slavery, claimed that Africans weren’t fully human because they couldn’t write poetry! (Of course, slaveholders conveniently neglected to consider that they had made it illegal for slaves to learn even to read.) In fact, Phillis Wheatley’s owners encouraged her to write poetry to prove this racist argument wrong. Slaves also wrote autobiographical narratives to alert white Northerners to their plight. Harriet Jacobs’ Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl (1861) is one such text. Yet so widespread was the belief, even in the North, that African slaves were incapable of writing, let alone of literary production, that many narratives were prefaced by the statements of white patrons, testifying to the identity of the writer and the authenticity of the narrative. Indeed, finding ways to pull white readers into texts they otherwise might have resisted has remained a task that many black writers still face.

早期非裔美国作家的反种族主义政治思想，在非裔美国人漫长的争取正义的斗争历史中，始终与他们的诉求息息相关。因此，对于许多非裔美国人来说，写作作为一种纯粹的个人表达形式，在当时众多族人遭受压迫的情况下，被视为一种他们难以负担的奢侈品，也就不足为奇了。

The antiracist politics of early African American writers have remained relevant to the needs of black Americans over the long history of their struggle for justice. It is not surprising, therefore, that writing as a form of purely individual expression has been viewed by many African Americans as a luxury the race could not afford while so many of its members were oppressed.

在20世纪60年代的黑人艺术运动中，黑人作家的社会角色始终是一个重要议题。这场运动是黑人权力运动的文学艺术分支。一些运动中最积极的代言人，例如诗人阿米里·巴拉卡，认为黑人作家有义务通过文学手段帮助黑人，例如描绘种族主义的罪恶、塑造非裔美国人的正面形象，以及为黑人社区面临的社会问题提供可能的解决方案。同样，黑人艺术运动也影响了非裔美国文学批评家的角色，强调了他们作为文化批评家的职责。也就是说，黑人批评家被要求从文学作品对非裔美国人政治和经济状况的呈现及其与非裔美国人政治和经济状况的关系的角度来解读文学作品，这项工作类似于马克思主义批评家的工作，但其重点当然是种族问题。例如，非裔美国批评家分析了文学文本如何削弱或强化那些使非裔美国人在政治上遭受压迫、在经济上处于劣势的种族主义意识形态。这种方法至今仍然是非裔美国批评的重要组成部分。

The social role of the black writer remained an important issue during the Black Arts Movement of the 1960s, the literary and artistic offshoot of the Black Power Movement. Some of the most vocal spokespersons for the movement, such as the poet Amiri Baraka, believed that black writers have an obligation to help the race through such literary means as depicting the evils of racism, providing positive images of African Americans, and offering possible solutions to social problems confronting the black community. Similarly, the Black Arts Movement affected the role of African American literary critics by emphasizing their job as cultural critics. That is, black critics were called on to interpret literature in terms of its representation of and relationship to the political and economic situation of African Americans, a task analogous to that performed by Marxist critics but with the focus, of course, on race. For example, Afro-American critics analyzed the ways in which literary texts undermine or reinforce the racist ideologies that have kept black Americans politically oppressed and economically disadvantaged. This approach remains an important part of African American criticism today.

黑人艺术运动也质疑了白人批评理论是否适用于解读黑人文学。毕竟，正是以欧洲中心主义视角对“伟大”文学的定义，将黑人作家边缘化于美国文学史之外，实际上将他们排除在美国文学经典之外。而大多数当代主流批评理论，包括本文讨论的所有理论，都未能充分体现这一点。本书其他章节都源于欧洲。鉴于一些批评家对解构主义理论对各种文学批评形式的广泛影响持保留态度，白人理论是否适用于解读黑人文本的问题在今天仍然具有现实意义。正如芭芭拉·克里斯蒂安所观察到的，解构主义的抽象话语认为“中心”和“边缘”等概念是虚幻的，并允许少数精通解构主义的人“掌控批评界”，而这种话语的出现“恰逢有色人种文学……开始向‘中心’靠拢”（459）。此外，解构主义批判了稳定且具有内在意义的文化身份的概念。相反，正如你可能在第八章中读到的，解构主义将“自我”定义为众多“自我”的碎片化集合，除了我们赋予它的意义和价值之外，它本身没有任何稳定的意义或价值。正如亨利·路易斯·盖茨二世所指出的那样，“在批判我们的文化身份之前，剥夺[非裔美国人]探索和重新获得我们[文化身份]的过程是不公平的”（《大师之作》32）。

The Black Arts Movement also called into question the appropriateness of white critical theories for the interpretation of black literature. After all, it was a Eurocentric definition of “great” literature that marginalized black authors in American literary history and virtually excluded them from the American canon. And most contemporary mainstream critical theories, including all the theories discussed in the other chapters of this textbook, have European roots. The question of the appropriateness of white theories for the interpretation of black texts remains pertinent today in light of the reservations some critics have about the widespread influence of deconstructive theory on all forms of literary criticism. As Barbara Christian observes, the abstract discourse of deconstruction, which argues that such concepts as “center” and “periphery” are illusory and which allows those few who are especially fluent in deconstruction “to control the critical scene,” emerged “just when the literature of peoples of color … began to move to ‘the centre’” (459). In addition, deconstruction critiques the concept of a stable, inherently meaningful cultural identity. Rather, as you may recall from Chapter 8, deconstruction defines the “self” as a fragmented collection of numerous “selves” that has no stable meaning or value except those we assign to it. And as Henry Louis Gates Jr. points out, it isn’t fair “to deny [African Americans] the process of exploring and reclaiming our [cultural identity] before we critique it” (“The Master’s Pieces” 32).

另一方面，许多非裔美国批评家认为，包括解构主义在内的众多当代批评理论中的要素都可以被非裔美国批评所借鉴。尽管不加批判地将欧美理论应用于非裔美国文学存在诸多风险，但许多批评家认为，将白人批评理论完全排除在黑人批评体系之外，不仅会剥夺黑人批评家一些潜在的有用批评工具，还会阻碍非裔美国批评家与其同行之间的交流。正如亨利·路易斯·盖茨（Henry Louis Gates Jr.）所言，“任何能够帮助批评家解释文本语言复杂运作机制的工具都是合适的工具。因为正是语言，尤其是黑人文本的黑人语言，表达了我们文学传统的独特品质”（《黑人形象》第21页）。正如我们在其他章节中所看到的，大多数批评理论都可以用来解释语言的运作方式，例如，它们可以让我们注意到语言承载意识形态内容的各种方式，而这些内容会在我们不知不觉中影响我们。

On the other hand, many African American critics believe that elements from any number of contemporary critical theories, including deconstruction, can be adapted for use by African American criticism. For despite the dangers involved in the uncritical application of European American theories to African American literature, many critics feel that the wholesale exclusion of white critical theory from the black critical repertoire would deny black critics some potentially useful critical tools and, in addition, would close off avenues of communication between African American critics and their colleagues. As Henry Louis Gates Jr. argues, “any tool that enables the critic to explain the complex workings of the language of a text is an appropriate tool. For it is language, the black language of black texts, that expresses the distinctive quality of our literary tradition” (Figures in Black xxi). And as we have seen in other chapters, most critical theories can be used to explain the operations of language, for example by calling our attention to the various ways in which language carries ideological content that can affect us without our even being aware of it.

盖茨所指的黑人文学独特性，是黑人艺术运动期间探讨的另一个重要议题，至今仍影响着我们。与所有“伟大”文学都具有“普遍性”的观点相反，黑人艺术运动中的许多作家认为，非裔美国文学拥有其独特的品质、政治和诗学，这些都无法完全被欧洲裔美国文学的宏大框架所解释或涵盖。一些理论家认为，这种独特性源于非裔美国人的口头叙事传统，包括故事讲述、民间传说和口述历史，这些传统根植于非洲文化，并且一些评论家认为，它与一种本质的、与生俱来的“黑人性”相关，这种“黑人性”是一种所有非洲裔民族共有的思维、情感和创造方式。另一些人则认为，并不存在所谓的本质黑人性，非裔美国文学作品的共同特质源于其他文化背景。作者的历史和文化。一些评论家认为，非裔美国文学的独特品质源于其对非洲和欧洲裔美国人文化传统的独特融合。

The idea of the distinctiveness of black literature to which Gates refers was another important issue explored during the Black Arts Movement that remains with us today. In opposition to the notion of the “universality” of all “great” literature, many writers in the Black Arts Movement argued that African American literature has its own unique qualities, its own politics and poetics, that cannot be fully explained by or contained within the larger framework of European American literature. Some theorists believe that this uniqueness derives from the African American oral tradition of storytelling, folklore, and oral history, which has its roots in African culture and, according to some critics, relates to an essential, or inborn, “blackness,” a way of thinking, feeling, and creating shared by all peoples of African descent. Others argue that there is no such thing as an essential blackness, that the qualities African American texts have in common result from the shared history and culture of their authors. For some of these critics, the distinctive quality of African American literature follows from its unique blending of both African and European American cultural traditions.

无论哪种情况，我们在解读非裔美国文本时，都绝不能忽视其非洲中心性——即它们与非洲历史和文化的首要关系——否则就有可能在重要方面扭曲非裔美国文学。例如，正如约翰·W·罗伯茨所观察到的，奴隶制时期出现的非裔美国骗子故事，例如关于布雷尔兔的故事，“与非洲口头传统中的骗子故事有着密切的联系”（97）。然而，以欧洲为中心的美国民俗学家却假定奴隶制已经切断了非裔美国人与非洲的文化联系，并认为这些故事源于欧洲裔美国人的传统。或者他们断言，故事的起源并不重要，因为奴隶们改变了它们，以适应一种非常具体的心理需求：通过认同一个反抗道德秩序的弱小动物来弥补他们在奴隶制下的无力感，这个弱小动物通过狡猾和欺骗来愚弄体型更大、更强大的动物，惩罚它们，夺取它们的食物等等。

In either case, the Afrocentricity of African American texts – that is, the primacy of their relationship to African history and culture – must not be overlooked when we interpret them or we risk deforming African American literature in very important ways. For example, as John W. Roberts observes, the African American trickster tales that emerged during slavery, such as those about Br’er Rabbit, “exhibi[t] a close kinship to trickster tales in African oral tradition” (97). However, Eurocentric American folklorists, assuming that enslavement had abolished African Americans’ cultural ties to Africa, argued that these tales derived from the European American tradition. Or they asserted that it didn’t matter where the tales originated because slaves transformed them to fit a very specific psychological need: the need to compensate for their powerlessness under slavery by identifying with a small, disadvantaged animal who rebels against the moral order and, through cunning and deceit, fools the larger, more powerful animals, punishes them, takes their food, and so forth.

罗伯茨指出，非洲中心主义民俗学家纠正了这种误解，他们指出，非洲和非裔美国人的骗子故事“都围绕着旨在弥补物质必需品长期匮乏以及在等级森严的社会环境中生存困境的行为展开”（107）。简而言之，非洲和非裔美国人骗子故事的相似之处在于，尽管原因截然不同，但这两个群体都必须学会如何在食物供应不稳定且常常不足的情况下生存。而这两类故事的差异则源于非洲文化严格的社会秩序——在这种秩序中，社群的福祉始终优先于个人利益；以及美国种植园文化严格的社会秩序——在这种秩序中，奴隶主的个人利益始终优先于为其工作的奴隶群体的福祉。因此，从非洲中心主义视角解读骗子故事，既能解释故事的延续性，又能解释其演变，同时又不会将非裔美国人文化与其非洲根源割裂开来。

Afrocentric folklorists have corrected this misinterpretation, Roberts observes, by showing, among other things, that both African and African American trickster tales “revolv[e] around behaviors designed to compensate for chronic shortages of material necessities and existence in a rigid social hierarchy” (107). In short, the similarities between African and African American trickster tales derived from the fact that both populations, though for very different reasons, had to learn how to survive with an uncertain and often inadequate food supply. And the differences between the two groups of tales resulted from the differences between the strict social order of African culture, in which the welfare of the community always took precedence over individual gain, and the strict social order of American plantation culture, in which the individual gain of the slaveholder always took precedence over the welfare of the community of slaves that worked for him. An Afrocentric reading of the trickster tales thus accounts for both the continuity and the transformation of the tales without severing African American culture from its African roots.

最新进展：批判种族理论

Recent developments: critical race theory

当然，过去几十年间，时代在很多方面都发生了变化。针对非裔美国人的极端暴力行为——例如私刑、暗杀黑人领袖、炸毁黑人教堂、暴徒袭击“离”白人社区“太近”的黑人住宅，以及残酷对待民权抗议者——在美国似乎已成为历史。此外，对非裔美国人的种族歧视现在是非法的：根据法律，人们有色人种可以自由选择居住、工作、购物、外出就餐等场所。因此，许多美国人——至少是许多白人——认为，除了像三K党这样的白人至上主义团体之外，种族主义已经成为过去。的确，我们不再像上世纪五六十年代民权运动鼎盛时期那样，在晚间新闻中看到种族抗议、静坐或骚乱的报道，也不再在日报上读到相关内容。事实上，五六十年代的民权运动已经结束，那么认为它不再必要难道不合情理吗？的确，非裔美国作家、法学家、科学家、哲学家、政治家、音乐家、画家、舞蹈家、演员、导演、运动员以及其他体现当代非裔美国思想和非裔美国文化传统的人士，在国内外都享有盛名。而且，美国现在拥有庞大的非裔美国人中产阶级。那么，我们为什么还要关注种族问题，更不用说研究批判种族理论了？

Of course, times have changed in many ways over the past few decades. Extreme forms of overt violence against African Americans – such as lynching, the assassination of black leaders, the bombing of black churches, mob attacks on black homes “too near” white neighborhoods, and the brutal treatment of civil rights protestors – seem to be a thing of the past in the United States. In addition, racial discrimination against African Americans is now illegal: according to the law, people of color may live, work, shop, dine out, and so forth where they please. Therefore, many Americans – at least many white Americans – believe that racism, with the exception of white supremacist groups like the Ku Klux Klan, is a thing of the past. Certainly, we don’t see reports of racial protests, sit-ins, or riots on the nightly news or read about them in the daily newspaper as we did during the 1950s and 1960s when the Civil Rights Movement was in its heyday. In fact, the Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s and 1960s is over, so isn’t it logical to believe that it’s no longer needed? Indeed, black American writers, jurists, scientists, philosophers, politicians, musicians, painters, dancers, actors, directors, athletes, and others who embody contemporary African American thought and the African American cultural tradition are famous both nationally and internationally. And the United States now has a large African American middle class. So why do we still need to concern ourselves with race at all, let alone study something called critical race theory?

然而，正如许多不同肤色的美国人所知，种族主义并未消失，只是转入了“地下”。也就是说，美国的种族不公正仍然是一个重大且紧迫的问题；它只是变得不像以前那样显而易见了。种族不公正可以说是在暗中进行的，以逃避法律制裁，并且在许多情况下，只有受害者才真正了解其运作方式。例如，正如理查德·德尔加多和吉恩·斯特凡西克所指出的，非裔美国人和拉丁裔美国人获得工作、住房和贷款的机会仍然比拥有类似资历的白人少（10）。此外，

As many Americans of all colors know, however, racism has not disappeared: it’s just gone “underground.” That is, racial injustice in the United States is still a major and pressing problem; it’s simply become less visible than it used to be. Racial injustice is practiced on the sly, so to speak, to avoid legal prosecution, and it has flourished in ways that, in many cases, only its victims really know well. For example, as Richard Delgado and Jean Stefancic point out, African Americans and Latinos/as still have fewer chances of acquiring jobs, housing, and loans than whites with similar qualifications (10). In addition,

监狱人口以黑人和棕色人种为主；企业首席执行官、外科医生和大学校长几乎都是白人。……黑人家庭的平均资产只有白人家庭的十分之一左右。他们购买许多产品和服务（包括汽车）的价格更高。有色人种的预期寿命更短，获得的医疗保健更差，受教育年限更短，从事的低级工作也更多。联合国最近的一份报告显示，如果将美国非裔美国人视为一个独立的国家，那么他们的社会福祉在全球排名第27位。拉丁裔美国人则排名第33位。

The prison population is largely black and brown; chief executive officers [of corporations], surgeons, and university presidents are almost all white. … [B]lack families have, on the average, about one-tenth of the assets of their white counterparts. They pay more for many products and services, including cars. People of color lead shorter lives, receive worse medical care, complete fewer years of school, and occupy more menial jobs than do whites. A recent United Nations report showed that African Americans in the United States [if thought of as comprising a nation of their own] would make up the twentyseventh ranked nation in the world … [in terms of] social well-being. Latinos would rank thirty-third.

（Delgado 和 Stefancic 10–11）

(Delgado and Stefancic 10–11)

我认为刚才引述的段落中列出的第一个事实值得进一步探讨，因为美国有色人种囚犯人数不成比例地高，助长了（如果不是造成的话）许多白人美国人的一种误解，即非裔美国人犯罪的比例过高，换句话说，犯罪是非裔美国人的特质。为了说明这种想法的缺陷，我举一个引人注目的例子来说明为什么非裔美国人犯罪的比例更高。在我国，非裔美国人的监禁率远高于白人。持有28克霹雳可卡因（主要由非裔美国人使用）将自动触发五年强制监禁。然而，持有500克粉状可卡因（主要由白人美国人使用）才会触发同样的五年强制监禁。³诸如此类的歧视性法律使人们关注贫困黑人社区的毒品使用情况，导致这些地区警方加强了监控，而白人社区的毒品使用情况却大多被忽视。事实上，在美国，大多数吸毒者（各种类型的吸毒者）都是白人。然而，因毒品犯罪而被监禁的囚犯中，绝大多数是黑人。正如这个典型例子所示，我们法律体系的种族偏见，而非非裔美国人“天生”的犯罪倾向，才是导致许多黑人身陷囹圄的原因，而如果他们是白人，就不会面临这样的后果。

I think the first fact listed in the passage just cited deserves further comment because the disproportionate number of prisoners of color in this country has encouraged, if not created, the misconception held by many white Americans that a disproportionate number of African Americans are criminals, in other words, that criminality is an African American trait. In order to show the flaws in this kind of thinking, let me offer just one striking example of why there is a larger proportion of African Americans than whites incarcerated in our country. The possession of 28 grams of crack cocaine (used predominantly by black Americans) automatically triggers a five-year mandatory prison sentence. However, it takes 500 grams of powder cocaine (used predominantly by white Americans) to trigger that same five-year mandatory prison sentence.3 Discriminatory laws like these draw attention to the use of drugs in poor black neighborhoods, a situation that has resulted in increased police surveillance in these areas, while drug use in white neighborhoods is largely ignored. In fact, in the United States the majority of drug users (of all kinds) are white. Yet the majority of prisoners incarcerated for drug-related offenses are black. As this representative example illustrates, the racial bias of our legal system, not the “natural” criminality of African Americans, has put many black Americans behind bars who wouldn’t be there if they were white.

显然，尽管有旨在保障公民权利的民权法，许多非裔美国人仍然经常被剥夺这些权利。因此，或许可以将批判种族理论视为一种新的民权研究方法。批判种族理论由德里克·A·贝尔等人于20世纪70年代发起，当时20世纪50年代和60年代的民权运动已不再具有政治或社会影响力。虽然批判种族理论最初是对宪法——即以宪法为基础、各州法律不得违反的联邦法律——的批判，但它已扩展到其他学科，包括人文学科。正如我们将看到的，批判种族理论关注所有与种族相关的议题。除了调查上述引文中描述的那种显而易见的压迫问题外，批判种族理论还研究了我们日常生活中的细节与种族之间的关联方式（尽管我们可能没有意识到这一点），并研究了看似简单、常见的种族假设背后复杂的信念，以揭示种族主义在何处以及如何以“隐蔽”的方式继续存在。
