Clearly, many African Americans are still routinely deprived of their civil rights despite the civil rights laws intended to guarantee these rights. Perhaps, then, one useful way to think of critical race theory is as a new approach to civil rights. Initiated by the work of Derrick A. Bell Jr. and others in the 1970s, critical race theory began at a time when the Civil Rights Movement of the 1950s and 1960s ceased to be a political or social force. And though critical race theory started out as a critique of constitutional law – that is, federal law, which is based on the Constitution and which the laws of individual states are not supposed to violate – it has spread to other disciplines, including those in the humanities. As we’ll see, critical race theory concerns itself with every topic that is relevant to race. In addition to investigating such obvious issues as the kind of oppression described in the passage quoted above, critical race theory examines the ways in which details of our everyday lives are related to race, though we may not realize it, and studies the complex beliefs that underlie what seem to be simple, commonplace assumptions about race in order to show where and how racism still thrives in its “undercover” existence.

我们先来看看德尔加多和斯特凡西克提出的批判种族理论的基本原则。我在这里列出来——别指望现在就能理解所有的术语——然后我们会逐一仔细研究。

Let’s start by examining what Delgado and Stefancic identify as the basic tenets of critical race theory. I’ll list them for you here – don’t expect to understand all of the vocabulary yet – and then we’ll take a closer look at each one.

基本原则

Basic tenets

1 在美国，种族歧视是少数族裔普遍面临的日常问题。

1 Everyday racism is a common, ordinary experience for people of color in the United States.

2种族主义在很大程度上是利益趋同的结果，有时被称为物质决定论。

2 Racism is largely the result of interest convergence, sometimes referred to as material determinism.

3种族是社会建构的产物。

3 Race is socially constructed.

4种族主义常常表现为种族差异化。

4 Racism often takes the form of differential racialization.

5每个人的身份都是多种因素交叉作用的产物。

5 Everyone’s identity is a product of intersectionality.

6 少数族裔的经历赋予了他们一种独特的有色人种之声。

6 The experiences of racial minorities have given them what might be called a unique voice of color.

（6-9）

(6–9)

批判种族理论家们对这些原则的看法并不完全一致，但理解这六点将有助于你了解这门新兴学科。我们还将探讨一些其他主题，作为批判种族理论家关注的不同问题的代表性例子。

Critical race theorists don’t all hold the same opinion regarding these tenets, but an understanding of these six points will be a very helpful means of introducing you to this growing discipline. We’ll also take a look at a few additional topics as representative examples of the different kinds of issues that are of interest to critical race theorists.

1 日常种族主义——许多美国白人仍然认为，“种族主义”一词仅适用于非常明显的种族主义形式，例如针对有色人种的肢体或言语攻击；白人至上主义团体的活动；蓄意且公开地将少数族裔排除在特定住房、餐馆和面向公众开放的社交组织之外等等。然而，在许多方面，最令人情绪崩溃、压力最大的种族主义形式恰恰是那些每天都发生在有色人种身上的种族主义，而且这些种族主义形式才是常态，而非例外。例如，白人店员或保安人员经常会观察甚至跟踪进店的非裔美国人。少数族裔成员也经常会遇到白人同胞缺乏基本礼貌的情况——他们被忽视，他们看到白人皱眉或翻白眼，他们听到针对他们的讽刺挖苦——即使在最平凡的场景中也是如此：在超市或药店排队时，在加油站付款时，在银行咨询信息时等等。白人日常生活中常见的其他种族主义行为包括“居高临下、轻视他人、假定他人缺乏自信、雇用象征性的黑人……或偏袒白人……[以及]回避接触[与有色人种保持物理距离或避免身体接触]”（Essed 205）。一种特别有害的日常种族主义形式是不断低估少数族裔的能力，例如，立即假定“他们写作中的拼写错误……[是由于]语言能力不足”（Essed 206）。这种行为在课堂上尤其具有破坏性，因为中小学教师和大学教授常常无意识地假定有色人种学生在某些方面低人一等：“智力较低……缺乏……文化素养……职业道德或社交技能”（Essed 207）。这些毫无根据的假设会导致教师评分不公、隐瞒奖学金信息、忽视或缺乏对黑人学生成就的热情，以及未能充分让黑人学生参与课堂讨论（Essed 207）。当然，我们大多数人也都熟悉这样一个持续存在的问题：儿童和青少年接触到的课程材料种族构成严重失衡，而这种失衡往往基于……（有时甚至完全）基于白人经验，以及白人教师对待黑人学生的方式，仿佛这些学生“代表”或“代表”了整个种族，这是一个持续存在的问题。

1 Everyday racism – Many white Americans still think that the word racism applies only to very visible forms of racism, for example, physical or verbal attacks against people of color; the activities of white supremacist groups; the deliberate and overt exclusion of racial minorities from particular housing, restaurants, and social organizations open to the public; and the like. However, in many ways the most emotionally draining, stress-provoking forms of racism are the kinds that happen to people of color every day, and these forms of racism are the rule, not the exception. For instance, white store clerks or security personnel often watch, or even follow, African Americans who come into their stores. And members of minority groups frequently encounter a lack of common civility from their white fellow Americans – they’re ignored, they see white people grimace or roll their eyes, they overhear sarcastic comments made at their expense – in the most mundane situations: while waiting in line at the supermarket or pharmacy, while paying for gas at the gas station, while asking for information at the bank, and so forth. Other common examples of everyday racist behavior exhibited by white people include “being patronizing, talking down, assuming lack of confidence, hiring token blacks … or favoring whites. … [and] contact avoidance [keeping a physical distance from a person of color or avoiding touch]” (Essed 205). A particularly damaging form of everyday racism consists of constantly underestimating the ability of minority persons, for example, immediately assuming that “typos in their writing are … [due to] language deficiency” (Essed 206). This kind of behavior is especially destructive when it occurs in the classroom, when schoolteachers and college professors assume, often unconsciously, that students of color are in some way inferior: “less intelligent … lack[ing] … cultural sophistication … work ethic, or social skills” (Essed 207). These kinds of unfounded assumptions can result in the teacher’s grading unfairly, withholding information about scholarships, ignoring or lacking enthusiasm for the achievements of black students, and neglecting to include black students adequately in class discussions (Essed 207). Of course, most of us are also familiar with the continuing problem of exposing children and young people to racially unbalanced curriculum materials based too much (and sometimes exclusively) on white experience as well as the continuing problem of white teachers who respond to black students as if those students “spoke for,” or represented, their entire race.

陶尼亚·洛弗尔·班克斯是一位黑人女法学教授，她提供了一个特别能揭示日常种族歧视的例子。一个星期六下午，班克斯教授和她的四位同事——她们都是三十多岁到四十多岁的非裔美国女性，衣着得体——去拜访一位住在费城中心城区豪华公寓的同事。她们走进一部宽敞的电梯准备离开。“几层楼后，电梯门开了，一位五十多岁的白人女性探头进来，发出了一声压抑的惊呼，然后退后一步，让电梯门关上，没有进去。又过了几层楼……另一位中年白人女性……也决定不进去”（331）。吓到这两位白人女性的，不可能是黑人女性的衣着、年龄、性别或所处地点。一定是她们的肤色。然而，仅仅是肤色就足以掩盖电梯里这些女性对任何人不构成威胁的所有其他外在特征。事实上，我们完全可以合理地假设，这两位白人女性根本没有注意到电梯里其他乘客的衣着、年龄或性别，也没有考虑到她们所处的豪华公寓安保严密：受白人社会的影响，她们往往对肤色反应强烈，肤色很可能是她们唯一关注的因素。这无疑是她们唯一做出反应的因素。

One particularly revealing example of everyday racism is offered by Taunya Lovell Banks, a black woman law professor. One Saturday afternoon, Professor Banks and four of her fellow law professors, all African American women in their thirties and forties and all well dressed, had been visiting a colleague living in a luxury condominium in downtown Philadelphia. They got on a spacious elevator to leave. “A few floors later, the door opened and a white woman in her late fifties peered in, let out a muffled cry of surprise, stepped back and let the door close without getting on. Several floors later … another white middle-aged woman … also decided not to get on” (331). It couldn’t have been the black women’s clothing, age, sex, or locale that frightened the two white women. It had to have been nothing but their skin color alone. Yet their skin color alone was enough to overcome every other physical indication that the women on the elevator were not a threat to anyone. In fact, it’s not unreasonable to assume that the two white women didn’t even see the clothing, age, or sex of the elevator passengers or think about the well-protected nature of the luxury condominium in which they were all gathered: programmed by white society to react strongly to skin color, skin color was probably all they saw. It was certainly the only factor to which they reacted.

或许，日常生活中最令人痛心的种族主义形式之一，就是白人否认种族主义的存在，或者否认种族主义在特定情境中发生过。有色人种被指责对“歧视、……种族玩笑、当众嘲笑、居高临下的态度[以及]粗鲁无礼”过于敏感（Essed 207）。换句话说，他们被指责在根本不存在种族主义的地方看到了种族主义，而事实上，种族主义确实存在，只是那些表现出或目睹种族主义行为的白人无法或不愿将其视为种族主义。正如班克斯所观察到的，当你的同事告诉你他不认为你是黑人时，你知道他是在试图表达一些积极的意思，他想告诉你，对他来说，你的人性比你的种族更重要。然而，这种说法的潜在前提是，身为黑人就意味着低人一等（236）。当然，还有一种困扰：你总是会怀疑，那个对你恶语相向或出言不逊的白人究竟是出于种族歧视，还是只是心情不好。面对日常生活中遭受的种族歧视，人们承受着巨大的精神压力，这会损害有色人种的身心健康，因为日常种族歧视的影响是累积性的：“一次事件会触发对其他类似事件的记忆”（Essed 207）。与此同时，日常种族歧视的施害者和目击者可能根本意识不到它的存在。正如菲洛梅娜·埃塞德所指出的，尽管大多数人认为种族歧视不应该存在，“但国际社会在教育儿童、普及相关知识方面投入不足”。向成年人提供相关信息，并向公民提供有关如何识别种族主义、种族主义的传播方式、种族主义的体验方式以及如何应对种族主义的相关信息”（204）。

Perhaps one of the most distressing forms of everyday racism is white people’s denial that racism exists or has occurred in a particular instance. Persons of color are accused of being oversensitive “about discrimination, … ethnic jokes, ridicule in front of others, patronizing, [and] rudeness” (Essed 207). In other words, they’re accused of seeing racism where it doesn’t exist when, in fact, it does exist, but the white people exhibiting or witnessing it aren’t able or don’t choose to see it as racism. As Banks observes, when you are told by your coworker that he doesn’t think of you as black, you know that he is trying to say something positive, that he intends to tell you that your humanity matters to him, not your race. The underlying premise of such a statement, however, is that to be black is to be less than human (236). Then, of course, there’s the difficulty of always wondering if the white person who gave you a mean look or said something rude to you was being racist or was just having a bad day. The emotional stress of trying to cope with being the target of everyday racism can damage the psychological and physical health of people of color because the effects of everyday racism are cumulative: “[o]ne event triggers memories of other, similar incidents” (Essed 207). Meanwhile, white perpetrators and witnesses of everyday racism might not even know that it’s occurring. As Philomena Essed points out, though most people believe that racism should not exist, “there is insufficient inter/national commitment to educate children, inform adults, and provide citizens with relevant information about how to identify racism, how it is communicated, how it is experienced, and how it can be countered” (204).

2 利益趋同——德里克·贝尔用这个术语来解释种族主义在我国的普遍存在，是因为它常常与白人个人或群体的利益——即某种需求或欲望——趋同或重叠（布朗诉教育委员会案，第20-29页）。例如，种族主义符合上层白人的经济利益，他们通过支付比白人更低的工资来剥削黑人劳工；它也符合工人阶级白人的心理利益，他们自身被富裕白人低薪剥削的经历使他们需要感觉自己优于他人。换句话说，种族主义对白人有很多好处。这就是为什么利益趋同有时被称为物质决定论（德尔加多和斯特凡西克，第7页）。在物质世界中提升自我的欲望——例如，我们刚才看到的，渴望在经济上提升自我或在心理上感觉更好——决定了主流社会实施种族主义的方式。

2 Interest convergence – Derrick Bell uses this term to explain that racism is common in our country because it often converges, or overlaps, with the interest – with something needed or desired – of a white individual or group (Brown v. Board of Education 20–29). For example, racism is in the financial interest of upper-class whites who exploit black laborers by paying them less than their white counterparts, and it’s in the psychological interest of workingclass whites whose own experience of being underpaid and exploited by wealthy whites makes them need to feel superior to someone else. In other words, racism has many pay-offs for whites. This is why interest convergence is sometimes referred to as material determinism (Delgado and Stefancic 7). The desire to advance oneself in the material world – as we just saw, for example, the desire to advance oneself financially or to feel better about oneself psychologically – determines the ways in which the dominant society practices racism.

即使在民权领域取得的成功也“与……白人的自身利益不谋而合”（Delgado 和 Stefancic 18）。例如，正如玛丽·L·杜齐亚克 (Mary L. Dudziak) 1988 年对美国政府冷战档案的调查所揭示的那样，最高法院 1954 年在布朗诉教育委员会案 (Brown v. Board of Education )中作出的合法取消公立学校种族隔离的裁决，正如德里克·贝尔 (Derrick Bell) 几年前在激烈的争议中指出的那样（布朗诉教育委员会案20-29），并非伦理问题，而是政治问题。促使最高法院最终在学校种族隔离案中支持全国有色人种协进会 (NAACP) 的，并非出于利他主义，这在历史上尚属首次。相反，“大量秘密电报”、“美国驻外大使来信”以及“外国媒体报道”（Delgado和Stefancic 19）都表明，如果美国想要在与共产主义国家争夺尚未结盟的第三世界国家（其中许多国家居住着非白人）的支持方面取得成功，就迫切需要改变其种族主义的世界形象（Delgado和Stefancic 18-20）。因此，许多批判种族理论家认为利益趋同是种族主义的主要原因之一，甚至可能是主要原因，这并不令人惊讶。

Even successes in the area of civil rights “coincide with … white self-interest” (Delgado and Stefancic 18). For example, as Mary L. Dudziak’s 1988 investigation of the US government’s Cold War archives reveals, the Supreme Court’s 1954 decision, Brown v. Board of Education, to legally desegregate our public school system was, as Derrick Bell had argued amid much controversy several years earlier (Brown v. Board of Education 20–29), not an issue of ethics but of politics. It wasn’t altruism that led the Supreme Court finally to side with the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in a school desegregation case for the first time in history. Rather, “a flood of secret cables” and “letters from US ambassadors abroad” as well as “foreign press reports” (Delgado and Stefancic 19) all indicated that the United States desperately needed to change its racist world image if it wanted to compete successfully with communist countries for the allegiance of uncommitted Third World nations, many of which were peopled by nonwhite inhabitants (Delgado and Stefancic 18–20). It should not be surprising that many critical race theorists consider interest convergence one of the primary causes, if not the primary cause, of racism.

3 种族的社会建构——我们如何能将种族定义为生理特征的问题呢？举例来说，浅肤色黑人和深肤色白人之间的生理差异远小于我们经常在各自群体成员之间看到的生理差异。（Delgado 和 Stefancic 75）。然而，早在1790年，美国国会就将入籍（获得美国公民身份）限制在白人男性，这一种族标准仅略作修改，一直沿用至1952年。因此，在长达162年的种族限制时期，美国司法系统经常需要在诸多方面做出抉择，其中包括……许多公民申请者，哪些是白人，哪些不是？阿拉伯人是白人吗？印度人呢？如果一个国家既有肤色较浅的人，也有肤色较深的人，又该如何界定？更复杂的是，在历史长河中，一些群体可以说“变成了”白人。例如，在建国初期，意大利人、犹太人和爱尔兰人被认为是非白人，也就是说，他们与非裔美国人处于同一地位（Delgado 和 Stefancic 76-77）。

3 The social construction of race – How can we define race as a matter of physical features when the physical differences between light-skinned blacks and darkskinned whites, to cite just one example, are much fewer than the physical differences we often see among members of each group? (Delgado and Stefancic 75). Yet in 1790, the US Congress restricted naturalization (the acquisition of US citizenship) to white men, and this racial criterion, with only slight modifications, remained in effect until 1952. So over the course of those 162 years of racial restrictions the US judicial system frequently had to decide, among its many applicants for citizenship, which men were white and which weren’t. Are Arabs white? What about people from India? What if a given country contains both light- and dark-skinned people? To complicate matters, over the course of our history some groups have “become” white, so to speak. For instance, during our nation’s early years, Italian, Jewish, and Irish people were considered nonwhite, that is, of the same status as African Americans (Delgado and Stefancic 76–77).

考察美国人口普查局在1790年至1920年间使用的种族分类（每十年进行一次人口普查），我们可以清楚地看到，种族分类并非反映生物学事实，而是反映了不同时期官方对种族的看法。例如，从1790年到1810年，人口普查局将以下人群划分为不同的种族：（1）自由白人，（2）除未纳税的印第安人以外的所有其他自由人，以及（3）奴隶。从1820年到1840年，种族分类如下：（1）自由白人，（2）未入籍的外国人（非美国公民），（3）自由有色人种，以及（4）奴隶。在1850年和1860年，种族分类则变为：（1）白人，（2）黑人，（3）混血儿（一半白人血统，一半黑人血统），（4）混血奴隶，以及（5）黑人奴隶。从1870年到1920年，我们有（1）白人，（2）黑人，（3）混血儿，（4）四分之一黑人血统的 ...

A look at the racial categories used by the US Census Bureau between 1790 and 1920 (the census is taken every ten years) should show us rather clearly that racial categorization doesn’t reflect biological reality but rather the official beliefs about race at different times. For example, from 1790 to 1810, the Census Bureau designated the following populations as different races: (1) free whites, (2) all other free persons except Indians not taxed, and (3) slaves. From 1820 to 1840 racial categories were as follows: (1) free whites, (2) unnaturalized foreigners (foreigners who were not US citizens), (3) free colored, and (4) slaves. In 1850 and 1860 we had (1) whites, (2) blacks, (3) mulattos (half-white, half-black), (4) mulatto slaves, and (5) black slaves. From 1870 to 1920 we had (1) whites, (2) blacks, (3) mulattos, (4) quadroons (one-quarter black), (5) octoroons (oneeighth black), (6) Chinese, (7) Japanese, and (8) Indians. In short, our definitions of race change as economic and social pressures change (Ferrante and Brown, “Introduction to Part 2” 115–16). The dominant culture claims that “races” are fixed categories, but our history shows us that race in this country has always been a matter of definition. And if you find these facts rather intriguing, consider that “[i]n parts of the Caribbean class has shaped racial classification so that the richer one is, the whiter one is perceived to be” (Harding 219).

此外，纵观历史，许多美国人属于多个种族。然而，直到2000年人口普查，人口普查局才允许美国人在种族选项中勾选多个方框。自19世纪以来，种族一直分为四个类别——白种人、非洲人、亚洲人和美洲原住民——几十年前，又增加了一个“第五类：西班牙裔，可以是任何种族”（Sollors 102）。事实上，“西班牙裔”根本不是一个种族名称，尽管有些人误以为它是。它指的是来自不同国家的讲西班牙语的移民的族裔名称，虽然这个名称涵盖所有种族，但大多数西班牙裔都认为自己是白人（Muir 95）。

Throughout our history, moreover, many Americans have belonged to more than one race. However, until the 2000 census the Census Bureau did not allow Americans to check more than one box designating race, which since the nineteenth century has consisted of various forms of four racial categories – Caucasians, Africans, Asians, and Native Americans – to which it added, some decades back, “a fifth, Hispanics, who can be of any race” (Sollors 102). In fact, Hispanic is not a racial designation at all, though some people think it is. It’s an ethnic designation for Spanish-speaking immigrants from a number of different countries, and though the designation includes all races, most Hispanics identify themselves as white (Muir 95).

鉴于许多美国人属于多个种族类别，政府两百多年来坚持每个人只能被归入一个种族类别，这再次表明种族是社会建构而非生物建构的。也就是说，“每个人似乎（现在仍然似乎）都符合单一种族类别，这实际上是美国种族分类制度的结果”（Ferrante 和 Brown，“导论” 2）。例如，Naomi Zack 观察到，黑人和白人被归类的方式……在美国，对白种人的定义“排除了混血（黑白混血）的可能性，因为混血儿，即拥有黑人和白人祖先的人，会被自动归类为黑人”，而且只要“追溯到任何一代之前，只要有一位黑人祖先”，就可以将一个人定义为黑人（引自 Sollors，第 101-102 页）。此外，对于非白人混血儿（例如，亚裔和黑人父母的子女，或黑人和美洲原住民父母的子女），人口普查有时根据母亲的种族进行分类，有时则根据父亲的种族进行分类（Ferrante 和 Brown，“第二部分导论”，第 114-115 页）。

Given that so many Americans belong to more than one racial category, the government’s insistence, for more than two hundred years, on a single racial category for each person provides another illustration of how race is socially rather than biologically produced. That is, “the fact that everyone seemed (and still seems) to fit into a single racial category is really the result of the system of racial classification used in the United States” (Ferrante and Brown, “Introduction” 2). As a case in point, Naomi Zack observes that the way the black and white races are defined in America “precludes the possibility of mixed [black and white] race because cases of mixed race, in which individuals have both black and white forebears, are automatically designated as cases of black race,” and it takes only “one black forebear, any number of generations back” to define an individual as black (cited in Sollors 101–2). Moreover, in the case of mixed race nonwhite children (for example, the offspring of an Asian and a black parent or the offspring of a black and a Native American parent), during some years the census classified the children according to the race of the mother, other years according to the race of the father (Ferrante and Brown, “Introduction to Part 2” 114–15).

具有讽刺意味的是，尽管人口普查局几个世纪以来为了按种族对美国人进行分类而进行了大量的统计调整，但没有任何生物学或科学证据支持人类属于不同种族或存在“种族”这种概念的观点。正如小普林斯·布朗所解释的那样，

Ironically, given the centuries of statistical contortions performed by the Census Bureau to classify Americans according to race, there is no biological or scientific evidence to support the idea that human beings belong to different races or that there is any such thing as “race.” As Prince Brown Jr. explains,

当今世界所有人，无论其外貌特征如何，在繁衍后代时都会进行基因交换。我们彼此观察时所看到的人类特征差异，是解剖学和生理学上对特定环境的适应。没有任何一组特定的特征被某个群体或“种族”所垄断。例如，虽然灰眼睛通常与浅肤色联系在一起，但深色肤色的人也可能拥有灰眼睛——棕色眼睛和黑色眼睛也是如此。同样，卷发通常与深色皮肤联系在一起，但我们也都知道，肤色浅的人也拥有卷发。没有任何一组特定的特征会聚集在一起形成一个群体或“种族”。相反，有些人拥有相似的特征，是因为他们生活在社会隔离中，这限制了潜在配偶的选择。也就是说，他们所在社会的社会规则（习俗、法律）禁止他们与外貌特征不同的人通婚。

[A]ll of the people in the world today … regardless of their physical features readily exchange genes when they produce offspring. The variations in human traits … evident when we look at each other are anatomical and physiological adaptations … [to a] particular environment. … No particular set of traits is limited to any one group or “race.” … For example, while grey eyes are associated with a light complexion, they do occur among dark complexioned people – as do brown eyes and black eyes. In the same vein, curly hair is associated with dark skin but we all know light complexioned people who also have curly hair. … [N]o particular set of traits cluster together to form one group or “race.” … [Rather] [s]ome people share similar traits … because they live in social isolation, which limits the availability of potential mates. … [That is,] [t]he social rules (customs, laws) of their society … prohibit them from mating with people whose features are different.

（144–45）

(144–45)

换句话说，如果一个社会的法律或习俗强迫所有拥有白皙皮肤、红色卷发和蓝色眼睛的人居住在单独的社区，并禁止他们与除拥有白皙皮肤、红色卷发和蓝色眼睛的人以外的任何人通婚，那么可能在几代人之内，肯定在几百年之内，我们就会拥有一个相当庞大的拥有白皙皮肤、红色卷发和蓝色眼睛的人口群体。我们会说这些人属于一个独立的种族吗？我认为不会。

In other words, if a society’s laws or customs forced all people with fair white skin, curly red hair, and blue eyes to live in separate communities and prohibited their marrying anyone other than people with fair white skin, curly red hair, and blue eyes, we would have, probably within a few generations and certainly within a few hundred years, a rather large population of people with fair white skin, curly red hair, and blue eyes. Would we say that these people belonged to a separate race? I don’t think so.

严格从遗传学的角度来看，

From a strictly genetic perspective,

如果人类可以被绝对地划分为“种族”类别……就会出现一些群体无法与其他任何群体生育后代的情况……同一群体中的人之间不会有任何差异。相反，我们发现，75%的基因是相同的……无论个体被归入哪个社会群体。剩下的25%是存在多种形式的基因……例如……存在于四种不同的血型（A、B、O、AB）中。也就是说，并不存在决定“种族”的基因。

[I]f humans could be grouped into absolute “racial” categories … [w]e would have groups of people unable to have children with any other groups … [and] [t]here would not be any differences between people in the same group. Instead what we find is that 75 percent of genes are identical … in all individuals regardless of the population to which they are socially assigned. The remaining 25 percent are genes which appear in more than one form. … for example … in the four (A, B, O, AB) different types of blood. That is, there is no gene for “race.”

（布朗 145–46）

(Brown 145–46)

事实上，种族概念最初在自然史领域引入，仅仅是为了方便指代不同地理位置的人类群体，而非意在将人类划分为生理上不同的群体。然而，到了19世纪，科学家们开始将这些群体固定下来，并声称生理差异对应着基于生物学的文化等级：他们断言，人类属于不同的种族，某些种族——尤其是白种人——优于其他种族。美国公民正苦苦思索种族和种族优越论问题，而当时大多数白人美国人认为黑人存在某种程度的种族劣等性，这种观点在他们看来足以证明种族隔离乃至奴隶制的合理性（Muir 98），这绝非巧合。自然科学领域的专业人士之所以从他们的学科中剔除种族作为生物学范畴的概念，正是因为它缺乏科学依据。然而，无论是自然科学家还是其他任何人，都没有“有组织地努力让学校、政府、公众，甚至相关学科注意到这种拒绝”（Muir 102）。

Indeed, the concept of race was originally introduced in the field of natural history merely as a convenient way to refer to groups of human beings in different geographic locations, not with the intention of separating human beings into physiologically distinct groups. However, by the nineteenth century, scientists were fixing these groups in permanent categories and claiming that physical differences corresponded to a cultural hierarchy based on biology: human beings, they asserted, belong to different races, and some races – in particular, the white race – are superior to others. It hardly seems a mere coincidence that members of the scientific community adopted this viewpoint at a time when US citizens were struggling with issues of race and racial superiority, at a time when most white Americans believed in a degree of black racial inferiority that justified, in their minds, racial segregation if not slavery (Muir 98).4 Professionals in the natural sciences have eliminated from their discipline the concept of race as a biological category precisely because it is not a scientifically supportable concept. However, neither natural scientists nor anyone else has made any “organized effor[t] to bring this rejection to the attention of schools, government, general public, or even related disciplines” (Muir 102).

4 种族化差异——种族化差异指的是“主流社会在不同时期，根据自身不断变化的需求，以不同的方式对不同的少数族裔群体进行种族化（定义其种族特征）”（Delgado 和 Stefancic 8）。例如，在南北战争前，为了迎合白人种植园主的需求，他们将非洲人描绘成头脑简单、需要白人监管以免回归“异教徒”生活方式、并且乐于为白人服务的形象。种植园主认为，这种虚构的刻板印象有助于为他们奴役非洲人的行为辩护。后来，尤其是在人们认为非洲人与白人存在工作竞争时，非裔美国人就被刻板地描绘成具有威胁性、易受暴力侵害，并且常常同时被贴上懒惰的标签。这种逻辑至少可以说相当片面（一个人如果懒惰，又怎么可能具有威胁性和暴力倾向呢？），但刻板印象往往是不合逻辑的，因为它们源于偏见而非现实。

4 Differential racialization – Differential racialization refers to the fact that “the dominant society racializes [defines the racial characteristics of] different minority groups [in different ways] at different times, in response to [its] shifting needs” (Delgado and Stefancic 8). For example, it suited the needs of white plantation owners before the Civil War to depict Africans as simple-minded, in need of white supervision lest they revert to their “heathen” ways, and as happy to serve white people. This mythical stereotype helped justify, the plantation owners believed, their enslavement of Africans. Later, especially whenever they were thought to be in competition with whites for jobs, African Americans were stereotyped as threatening, prone to violence, and, often at the same time, lazy. The logic of this one seems rather skewed, to say the least (how can one be threatening and violent if one is lazy?), but stereotypes are often illogical because they grow from prejudice rather than from reality.

出于类似的原因，我们看到其他少数族裔群体也存在同样的种族化差异。这取决于历史时期和白人的需求。在白人社会中，美洲原住民有时被认为是友善高尚的，有时被认为是懒惰的酒鬼，有时被认为是偷窃成性的异教徒，有时又被认为是嗜血的野蛮人。同样，奇卡诺人也被刻板印象地描绘成虔诚的宗教信徒、极其重视家庭的人、迷信易受骗的人，或者懒惰无能的寄生虫，这取决于白人社会对他们的看法。华裔美国男性被刻板印象地描绘成睿智慈祥的长者，引导各个种族的年轻人；华裔美国女性被刻板印象地描绘成顺从男性；而华裔美国男女都被刻板印象地描绘成狡猾奸诈。尽管日裔美国人通常被认为勤劳可靠，但在二战期间，他们却被视为危险的潜在叛徒，并被关押在集中营直至战争结束。德裔和意裔美国人并没有受到这种种族歧视，尽管当时美国也与德国和意大利交战。日裔美国人是否因为被定义为非白人而更容易受到伤害呢？日裔美国人之所以更容易受到伤害，是否是因为他们在西海岸经济上取得了成功，拥有大量房产和其他金融资产，而所有这些——包括他们的银行账户和家中的家具——都被政府没收，并且永远无法归还，即使在战争结束后，日裔美国人从集中营获释之后也是如此？无论日裔美国人被拘禁的真正动机是什么，关键在于，像所有少数族裔群体一样，他们被种族化，而这种种族化方式服务于主流白人美国社会所认为的需求。

We see the same kind of differential racialization of other minority groups for analogous reasons. Depending on the historical moment and the needs of white society, Native Americans have been considered friendly and noble, lazy drunkards, thieving heathens, or bloodthirsty savages. Similarly, Chicanos/as have been stereotyped as devoutly religious and extremely family oriented, superstitious and gullible, or lazy, good-for-nothing freeloaders, depending on white society’s need to see them one way or the other. Chinese American men have been stereotyped as wise, fatherly guides for youngsters of all races; Chinese American women have been stereotyped as submissive to men; and Chinese American men and women have both been stereotyped as sneaky and treacherous. And although Japanese Americans are generally considered hardworking and trustworthy, during World War II they were seen as dangerous potential traitors and put in internment camps for the duration of the war. German and Italian Americans were not racialized in this manner, though the United States was also at war with Germany and Italy. Could it be that Japanese Americans were more vulnerable because they were defined as nonwhite? Could it be that Japanese Americans were more vulnerable because they had been financially successful on the West Coast and owned considerable property and other financial assets, all of which – including their bank accounts and the furniture in their homes – were seized by the government never to be returned, not even after the war was over and Japanese Americans were released from the camps? Whatever the real motivation for Japanese American internment, the point is that, like all minority groups, they were racialized in a manner that served the perceived needs of mainstream white America.

5 交叉性——没有人能仅凭种族就拥有简单、纯粹的身份认同。种族与阶级、性别、性取向、政治倾向和个人经历交织在一起，共同塑造了每个人复杂的身份认同。“每个人都可能拥有相互冲突、重叠的身份、忠诚和效忠对象”（Delgado 和 Stefancic，第 9 页）。例如，一个人可能是黑人、就业不足的工人阶级男性，也可能是墨西哥裔美国女同性恋者。这些人会遭受来自多个方面的压迫，并且往往难以确定自己在特定情况下遭遇歧视的原因（Delgado 和 Stefancic，第 51-52 页）。我在工作中是否因为种族、阶级或过往工作经历而受到不公平对待？我是否因为性别、民族或性取向而被解雇？如果我想提起诉讼，而我又无法确定自己遭遇歧视的具体原因，我应该以什么为依据？

5 Intersectionality – No one has a simple, uncomplicated identity based on race alone. Race intersects with class, sex, sexual orientation, political orientation, and personal history in forming each person’s complex identity. “Everyone has potentially conflicting, overlapping identities, loyalties, and allegiances” (Delgado and Stefancic 9). For example, an individual may be a black, underemployed, working-class male or a Mexican American lesbian. Such persons will suffer oppression from more than one source and often have difficulty knowing the reason they are encountering discrimination in any given instance (Delgado and Stefancic 51–52). Am I being treated unfairly at work because of my race, class, or past employment? Have I been fired because of my sex, ethnicity, or sexual orientation? If I want to sue, on which basis do I do so if I can’t be sure on which basis I encountered discrimination?

金伯莉·威廉姆斯·克伦肖举了一个例子，说明一个人的多重身份如何轻易地导致其被政府官僚机构忽视，以及这种情况发生时对生命和人身安全造成的危险。具体来说，她考察了有色人种的移民工人阶级女性遭受家庭暴力时会发生什么。1990年，“国会修订了《移民和国籍法》中关于婚姻欺诈的条款，以保护遭受虐待或处于极端危险境地的移民妇女。”她们来到美国是为了结婚，却遭受了美国公民或永久居民的虐待”（358-59）。此前，“移民到美国与美国公民或永久居民结婚的人，必须先‘合法’结婚两年，才能申请永久居民身份”（359），届时夫妻双方都必须申请妻子的永久身份。为了制止这些女性遭受剥削——她们宁愿忍受配偶虐待也不愿失去获得美国永久居留权的机会——国会投票通过了一项法案，允许在家庭暴力案件中豁免两年婚姻期限的要求。然而，克伦肖发现，“在社会、文化或经济上享有特权的移民女性更有可能……满足豁免要求”（360），例如，这些要求包括来自社会服务机构、警察、医疗保健提供者、心理学家或学校官员的报告（359）。“那些最无力利用这项豁免的女性——女性社会或经济地位最边缘化的人群——最有可能是有色人种女性”（360）。这些女性除了丈夫之外，在美国没有任何其他关系，因此丈夫是她们与外界联系的唯一纽带。她们不知道该向谁寻求帮助，甚至可能根本不知道有这样的帮助。由于1990年旨在保护移民女性免受家庭暴力侵害的豁免条款忽略了性别、种族和阶级的交叉性，使得这项法律安全网对最需要它的人来说反而最难获得。

Kimberlé Williams Crenshaw offers an example that illustrates how easily one’s intersectionality can result in one’s falling through the cracks of government bureaucracy and how dangerous it can be to life and limb when this situation occurs. Specifically, she examined what can happen when immigrant working-class women of color are victims of domestic violence. In 1990 “Congress amended the marriage fraud provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act to protect immigrant women who were battered or exposed to extreme cruelty by the US citizens or permanent residents” (358–59) they had come to the United States to marry. Formerly, “a person who immigrated to the United States to marry a US citizen or permanent resident had to remain ‘properly’ married for two years before even applying for permanent resident status” (359) at which time both husband and wife had to apply for the wife’s permanent status. To put a stop to the exploitation of these women, who accepted spousal abuse rather than lose their chance at permanent US residency, Congress voted to allow for a waiver of the two-year requirement in cases of domestic violence. However, Crenshaw found that “[i]mmigrant women who are socially, culturally, or economically privileged are more likely to be able to … satisfy the waiver requirements” (360), which consist, for example, of reports from social service agencies, police, healthcare providers, psychologists, or school officials (359). “Those women who are least able to take advantage of this waiver – women who are socially or economically the most marginal – are the ones most likely to be women of color” (360). These are women who don’t have connections in the United States besides their husbands, so their husbands are their only link to the outside world. They’re women who don’t know where to go for help and who might not even know that help is available. Because the 1990 waiver to protect immigrant women from domestic violence neglects to consider the intersectionality of sex with race and class, it renders this legal safety net the least accessible to those who need it the most.

6 有色人种之声——许多批判种族理论家认为，少数族裔作家和思想家通常比白人作家和思想家更有优势去书写和谈论种族和种族主义问题，因为他们直接经历过种族主义。这种立场被称为“有色人种之声”。的确，“黑人、印度裔、亚裔和拉丁裔作家和思想家或许能够向他们的白人同行传达一些白人不太可能了解的事情”（Delgado 和 Stefancic 9）。有人可能会认为，这种观点的逻辑如此强大，以至于“白人不太可能了解的事情”这句话完全可以替换为“大多数白人几乎肯定不知道的事情”。白人能够也确实了解许多种压迫——例如，因阶级、性别、性取向、种族、宗教等等而遭受的压迫——所有形式的压迫都是可怕的。但是，认为种族压迫在无数重要方面并非独一无二，就忽略了美国三百多年来关于种族的历史。

6 Voice of color – Many critical race theorists believe that minority writers and thinkers are generally in a better position than white writers and thinkers to write and speak about race and racism because they experience racism directly. This positionality is called the voice of color. Indeed, “black, Indian, Asian, and Latino/a writers and thinkers may be able to communicate to their white counterparts matters that the whites are unlikely to know” (Delgado and Stefancic 9). One might argue that the logic of this idea seems so strong that the phrase matters that the whites are unlikely to know could be accurately replaced with matters that most whites almost certainly don’t know. White people can and do know about many kinds of oppression – for instance, oppression due to class, sex, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, and so forth – and all forms of oppression are horrific. But to think that racial oppression isn’t unique in myriad important ways is to ignore over three hundred years of American history regarding race.

值得注意的是，德尔加多和斯特凡西奇认为“有色人种之声”理论“与反本质主义之间存在着某种不安的张力”（9）。也就是说，批判种族理论所秉持的反本质主义认为，不存在与我们所定义的种族相关的本质的或先天的遗传特征，因此，断言存在“有色人种之声”似乎自相矛盾。因为“有色人种之声”一词，如果脱离语境，就意味着……因为有些人天生肤色黝黑或棕色，所以他们天生就对种族压迫的运作方式有着某种天然的洞察力。然而，有人可能会认为这里并不存在自相矛盾之处，因为德尔加多和斯特凡西克并非认为有色人种的声音是一种本质性的——即与生俱来的或基因决定的——特质。相反，它是通过种族压迫的经历而习得的。换句话说，有色人种的声音——即由于种族压迫的经历而增强的谈论和书写种族和种族主义的能力——是社会习得的，而非生物习得的。因此，我们可以合理地认为，有色人种的声音论并非本质主义的例证，因此并不与批判种族理论的反本质主义哲学相矛盾。

It is interesting to note that Delgado and Stefancic believe the voice-of-color thesis “[c]oexist[s] in somewhat uneasy tension with anti-essentialism” (9). That is, because antiessentialism, which critical race theory embraces, holds that there are no essential, or inborn, genetic character traits associated with what we define as race, it may seem self-contradictory to assert that there is such a thing as a voice of color. For the term voice of color, taken out of context, implies that because some people are born with black or brown skin, they are born with some kind of natural racial insight into the operations of oppression. One might argue, however, that there is no self-contradiction here because Delgado and Stefancic are not positing that the voice of color is an essential – that is, an inborn, or genetic – quality. Rather, it is learned through the experience of racial oppression. In other words, the voice of color – the enhanced ability to speak and write about race and racism due to the experience of racial oppression – is socially, not biologically, acquired. So it is reasonable to argue that the voice-ofcolor thesis is not an example of essentialism and thus does not contradict critical race theory’s antiessentialist philosophy.

当然，我们必须记住，即使是同一少数族裔群体成员，他们所经历的压迫类型和程度也未必相同，而且每个人处理自身经历的方式也各不相同。因此，否认自己曾遭受种族压迫，或否认种族压迫在当今社会依然存在的少数族裔成员，显然不能作为“有色人种之声”理论的有效例证。但是，那些希望利用“有色人种之声”向他人讲述自身经历的种族不公的人们，正被鼓励去讲述他们的故事。“‘法律叙事’运动敦促黑人和棕色人种作家讲述他们与种族主义和法律体系的斗争经历，并运用他们独特的视角来审视法律的主流叙事”（Delgado 和 Stefancic 9），也就是说，审视法律在哪些方面并非其声称的那样，是无视种族差异、中立的公正工具。站在这场运动前沿的人物包括 Derrick Bell、Patricia Williams 和 Richard Delgado 等人。例如，德尔加多曾撰文指出，“白领犯罪和企业/工业犯罪——主要由白人实施——造成的伤亡和财产损失比所有街头犯罪加起来还要多”（引自德尔加多和斯特凡西克，第43页）。然而，如今监狱里关押的却是黑人，他们犯下的罪行相对较轻，而白人大型企业犯罪分子却很少受到法律的制裁。

Of course, we must remember that even members of the same minority group will not necessarily experience the same kind or amount of oppression and that individuals will handle their experiences differently. For this reason, members of a minority group who deny the racial oppression they’ve encountered, or who deny that racial oppression is still a problem today, obviously would not be useful examples of the voice-of-color thesis. But those who seek to use the voice of color to inform others of the racial injustice they’ve experienced are being encouraged to tell their stories. “The ‘legal storytelling’ movement urges black and brown writers to recount their experiences with racism and the legal system and to apply their own unique perspectives to assess law’s master narratives” (Delgado and Stefancic 9), that is, to assess the ways in which the law is not the colorblind, neutral instrument of justice it claims to be. In the frontline of this movement are, among others, Derrick Bell, Patricia Williams, and Richard Delgado. Delgado, for example, wrote an article “pointing out that white-collar and corporate/industrial crime – perpetrated mostly by whites – causes more personal injury, death, and property loss than all street crime combined” (cited in Delgado and Stefancic 43). Yet it’s the black, relatively small-time lawbreakers that are filling our prisons today, while white big-time corporate criminals are rarely pursued by our legal system.

我希望这六条原则能让您对批判种族理论的总体视角和目标有一个较为清晰的了解。为了加深理解，让我们简要探讨几个具有代表性的例子，这些例子反映了许多批判种族理论家持续关注的问题。具体来说，我们将考察白人特权、自由主义的问题以及种族现实主义。

I hope these six tenets have given you a fairly clear idea of the general perspective and goals of critical race theory. To expand on that understanding, let’s take a brief look at a few representative examples of the kinds of issues that continue to engage many critical race theorists. Specifically, we’ll examine the issues of white privilege, the problem with liberalism, and racial realism.

白人特权可以定义为“作为主流种族成员所享有的无数社会优势、福利和礼遇”（Delgado 和 Stefancic 78）。佩吉·麦金托什（Peggy McIntosh）的著名清单经常被批判种族理论家引用，她“列出了作为白人她所享有的46项优势，而她的非裔美国同事、朋友和熟人却无法享有这些优势”（Wildman 18）。例如，这些优势包括被告知她的非裔美国人不会像白人那样对待她。种族被认为是美国历史遗产的缔造者（想想我们都读过的那些历史书，它们声称要全面展现美国的过去，但实际上却只关注白人的成就）；为了保护孩子，不必向他们解释白人种族主义的种种表现形式；从未被要求代表自己的种族发言（引自Wildman 18）；知道自己的成就不会被视为与自己肤色相同的人的例外；认为自己偶尔犯的错误不会被视为种族低人一等的标志；并且期望在日常生活中，遇到的公众人物会以礼相待，而不是恐惧、怀疑或不适（引自Delgado和Stefancic 78）。McIntosh指出，白人特权也使白人期望他们的孩子能够从非正式的白人邻居网络或邻居的朋友和熟人那里找到某种暑期工作；他们相当确信自己的孩子会得到白人老师的帮助，哪怕只是获得一份额外的加分作业来提高勉强及格的成绩；他们还依赖于一个隐秘的裙带关系网络——一种“俱乐部”——来帮助一位勉强及格的白人候选人获得重要的晋升机会（引自Delgado和Stefancic，第78-79页）。“考虑到尽管取得了一些象征性的进步，但大多数企业权力职位仍然由白人把持，最后这个例子就显得尤为耐人寻味了”（Delgado和Stefancic，第78页）。

White privilege can be defined as “the myriad of social advantages, benefits, and courtesies that come with being a member of the dominant race” (Delgado and Stefancic 78). Peggy McIntosh, whose famous list is frequently mentioned by critical race theorists, “identified forty-six advantages available to her as a white person that her African American coworkers, friends, and acquaintances could not count on” (Wildman 18). They include, for example, being told that people of her race were responsible for America’s heritage (just think back to the history books we’ve all read that purported to give a balanced picture of America’s past but in reality focused on white American accomplishment); not having to explain to her children, for their own protection, the many modes of white racism; never being asked to speak for her race (cited in Wildman 18); knowing that her achievements will not be considered exceptions to the rule for people of her color; assuming that her occasional errors will not be viewed as signs of her racial inferiority; and expecting that she will be treated with common courtesy – rather than with fear, suspicion, or discomfort – by the individuals she encounters in public places over the course of her day (cited in Delgado and Stefancic 78). White privilege, McIntosh observes, also allows whites to expect that their children will be able to find summer employment of some sort from their unofficial network of white neighbors or from the friends and acquaintances of those neighbors; to feel reasonably confident that their children will get help from a white teacher, if only in the form of an extra-credit assignment to raise a borderline grade; and to rely on a quiet network of favoritism – a kind of “club” – that would help a borderline white candidate receive an important promotion (cited in Delgado and Stefancic 78–79). “This [last] example becomes especially telling when one considers that most corporate positions of power, despite token inroads, are still held by whites” (Delgado and Stefancic 78).

白人特权是一种日常种族主义，因为特权的整个概念都建立在劣势之上。也就是说，一个人只有在与不享有特权的人形成对比时，才能获得特权。因此，如果白人仅仅因为肤色而享有日常特权，那就意味着黑人仅仅因为肤色而被剥夺了这些特权。这当然是一种种族主义。通常情况下，白人特权是无意识的，因为拥有这种特权的人将其视为理所当然，视之为日常生活的一部分（Essed 205）。正是由于白人特权的无意识性，才使得白人难以察觉它，更遑论去解决它。

White privilege is a form of everyday racism because the whole notion of privilege rests on the concept of disadvantage. That is, one can be privileged only in contrast with someone else who is not privileged. So if whites enjoy a system of everyday privileges because they are white, this means that blacks are deprived of these privileges because they are black. And this is, of course, a form of racism. More often than not, white privilege is unconscious because it is taken for granted, seen as a natural part of daily life, by those who have it (Essed 205). The unconscious nature of white privilege is often what makes it so difficult for whites to spot, let alone to address.

例如，在我自己的课堂上，小组讨论种族和种族主义问题时，经常会有心地善良、出发点良好的白人学生对全班同学说：“我不太注意别人的种族；大多数时候我甚至都不会想到种族问题。” 我毫不怀疑这些学生的感受是真诚的，而且他们说的肯定是实话。但他们却没抓住重点。所以我总是反问他们：“如果你是黑人，你觉得你会注意到别人的种族，并且经常思考种族问题吗？” 到目前为止，这个问题从未让我失望。学生们的回答总是“会”。是的，如果他们是黑人，他们就会注意到别人的种族，而且种族问题会经常萦绕在他们的脑海中。我看到他们恍然大悟，意识到不必注意到或思考种族问题是多么奢侈。不必注意到他人的种族或思考种族问题是一种白人特权。黑人，除非身处全是黑人的环境中，否则就必须……注意他人的种族，并思考他们日常经历中的种族含义，因为他们总是“无论[他们的]声望或地位如何……都离因种族原因而遭受的排斥、限制或冒犯只有几步之遥”（贝尔，《种族现实主义》306）。

During group discussions of race and racism in my own classroom, for example, it is not uncommon for a good-hearted, well-intentioned white student to tell the class, “I don’t really notice people’s race; I don’t even think about race most of the time.” I have no doubt that such students are sincere in their feelings and are most certainly telling the truth. But they’re missing the point. So I always reply to them by asking, “Do you think you would notice people’s race and think about race a good deal of the time if you were black?” So far, this question has never failed to achieve its goal. Students invariably answer, “Yes.” Yes, if they were black they would notice people’s race, and race would often be on their mind. And I see a light bulb go on over their heads as they realize what a luxury it is for them to not have to notice or think about race. Not having to notice others’ race or think about race is a white privilege. Black people, unless they’re in an all-black environment, have to notice the race of others and think about the racial implications of their daily experiences because they’re always, “no matter [their] prestige or position … no more than a few steps away from a racially motivated exclusion, restriction, or affront” (Bell, “Racial Realism” 306).

我们不妨补充一点，在任何时刻，非裔美国人都可能随时面临种族歧视的威胁，而施害者（白人）甚至可能并未意识到自己正在发出这种侮辱。比如，在白人社区里，一个为学校卖糖果的黑人孩子，却常常被拒之门外；一个黑人少女在高中作文课上，小组讨论中，白人女生突然变得异常安静，因为她们意识到自己热烈讨论的发型并不适用于她“与众不同”的发型，而这种发型在她们看来似乎不够美观；一个黑人大学生在文学课上，他的白人同学正在解释，如果理解了黑色象征邪恶、白色象征善良，他们刚刚读完的故事就说得通了；还有这些有色人种年轻人的父母，他们必须努力帮助孩子应对种族歧视带来的伤害，就像他们自己也必须面对这些伤害一样——这些只是许多黑人每天都必须面对的几个例子。相比之下，白人却享有不必考虑这些问题的特权。换句话说，白人享有不必考虑——甚至不必了解——日常种族主义的特权。

We might add that black Americans are, at any given moment, little more than one step away from a racially motivated insult that the white perpetrator may not even be conscious of communicating. The black youngster selling candy for his school for whom too many doors remain closed in the white neighborhood; the black teenager in her high school composition class whose white female discussiongroup members suddenly become uncomfortably quiet because they realize that their animated talk about hairstyles does not apply to her “different” hair, which is assumed to be somehow less attractive; the black college student in his literature class whose white classmate is in the process of explaining how the story they’ve just read makes sense if you realize that black symbolizes evil and white symbolizes good; and the parents of these young people of color, who must try to help their children deal with hurtful racial experiences just as they must deal with their own hurtful racial experiences – these are just a few examples of the incidents that many black people must anticipate on a daily basis. White people, in contrast, have the privilege of not having to think about it. In other words, white people have the privilege of not having to think about – or even know about – everyday racism.

具有讽刺意味的是，正如斯蒂芬妮·M·怀尔德曼所指出的，我们这些拥有特权的人常常“如此真心实意地想要避免歧视，以至于我们因为未能批判性地审视自己的行为而赋予了这种特权。缺乏这种审视，特权体系就会被复制，排斥的循环也会继续下去”（179）。那么，拥有白人特权的人该如何应对呢？“‘放弃特权’似乎既显而易见又不可能”（怀尔德曼 180），因为白人特权已经渗透到美国文化的方方面面，只要大多数白人仍然普遍没有意识到白人特权的存在，那么所有白人都会从中受益，无论他们是否愿意。

Ironically, as Stephanie M. Wildman points out, often “those of us with privilege so earnestly want not to discriminate that we privilege our conduct by failing to examine it critically. Without this examination, the systems of privilege are replicated and the cycle of exclusion continues” (179). So what can those who have white privilege do about it? “‘Just give up the privilege’ seems both obvious and impossible” (Wildman 180) because white privilege is built into every aspect of American culture, and as long as most white people remain by and large unaware of white privilege, all white people will benefit from it whether they want to or not.

但要摆脱白人特权，一个小小的办法就是停止假装种族无关紧要，即便我们仍然希望它不应该重要。如果我们不再假装种族没有渗透到我们的日常生活、课堂和政府事务中，或许我们就能更清楚地看到白人特权的运作方式……我们需要……在各个角落展开讨论：在课堂、工作场所和会议中……[这样我们才能]迈出第一步，去瓦解这个无形的……特权世界。

But one small way to give up white privilege is to stop pretending that race does not matter, even though our aspiration continues to be that it should not matter. If we stop pretending that race does not permeate our daily lives, our classrooms, and the affairs of government, perhaps we will start to see the operation of white privilege … more clearly. … We need … the discussion to take place everywhere: in classrooms, workplaces, and meetings … [so that we can] take our first steps toward dismantling this world of invisible … privilege.

（Wildman 180）

(Wildman 180)

许多批判种族理论家认为，自由主义在种族正义方面采取的措施太少、太慢，是其问题的一部分。尽管保守主义政治绝非更可取，但考虑到保守主义的局限性，它仍然是自由主义的一大弊端。这种观点通常反对那些只会让受压迫者受益的变革，自由主义在种族问题上往往过于温和、过于妥协、过于谨慎。试图通过小步推进变革是行不通的，因为在这个国家实现种族正义所需的变革无法通过小步推进来实现：“体制只会吞噬微小的进步……一切依旧如故”（Delgado 和 Stefancic 57）。

Taking steps toward racial justice, but taking too few and taking them too slowly, is seen by many critical race theorists as part of the problem with liberalism. Although conservative politics is by no means preferable, given that the conservative viewpoint generally opposes change that would benefit only oppressed people, liberalism has tended to be too moderate, too conciliatory, too cautious when it comes to racial issues. Attempting to accomplish change in small increments doesn’t work because the kinds of changes needed for racial justice in this country cannot be contained in small increments: “the system merely swallows up the small improvement … and everything remains the same” (Delgado and Stefancic 57).

例如，1954年的布朗诉教育委员会案看似是一项重大进步，因为正如我们之前看到的，最高法院宣布公立学校的种族隔离违法。这项裁决对全国产生了巨大影响：许多美国人为此欢呼雀跃，而另一些人则为此感到悲痛。然而，最高法院的这项裁决并没有改变公立学校仍然存在种族隔离的现状，而这种隔离并非源于法律，而是源于贫困。生活在贫困城区的儿童大多是非裔美国人和拉丁裔。生活在富裕郊区的儿童大多是白人。由于儿童在居住地所在的学区就读，我们仍然会看到一些公立学校几乎全是白人或全是非白人学生。当然，鉴于学校经费来源于地方税收，贫困地区的非白人学校的经费严重不足。

Brown v. Board of Education (1954), for example, seemed like a big improvement because, as we saw earlier, the Supreme Court declared the racial segregation of public schools illegal. That decision hit the nation with enormous impact: many Americans celebrated the decision; others mourned it. However, this Supreme Court decision did nothing to remedy the fact that public schools are still largely segregated, not by law but by poverty. Most children living in poor urban locations are African American and Latino/a. Most children living in wealthy suburban neighborhoods are white. Because children go to school in the school district in which they live, we still have public schools that are largely all white or all nonwhite. Of course, given that school funding derives from local taxes, the nonwhite schools in the poor districts are woefully underfunded.

从这个角度来看，布朗诉教育委员会案不仅是一小步，而且还是一个误导性的举措。许多自由派人士认为它解决了问题，于是他们转而关注其他国家问题（Delgado 和 Stefancic 24）。如此看来，这种所谓的“解决方案”就好比医学界的庸医。庸医不仅开出无效的药，而且还通过让病人相信问题已经解决，从而阻止病人获得真正有效的医疗救助。

From this perspective, Brown v. Board of Education was not only a small step, but it was also a misleading step. Many liberals thought it solved the problem, and they went about addressing other national concerns (Delgado and Stefancic 24). In this way, such “solutions” can be compared to quackery in the medical profession. The “quack” doctor not only prescribes medicine that doesn’t work but, by convincing the patient that the problem has been addressed, prevents the sufferer from receiving medical aid that might really help.

批判种族理论也反对那种认为宪法“不分种族”或对种族保持中立的自由主义观点。尽管我们现在确实有法律保障人人享有平等机会，但这些法律并没有采取任何措施来支持确保人人都能真正获得这些机会的项目。众所周知，尽管住房和就业领域的种族歧视是违法的，但它仍然屡见不鲜（Delgado 和 Stefancic 21-23）。白人房东只需礼貌地告诉有色人种的求职者，没有空房，或者房子刚刚出租或出售。白人雇主只需告诉有色人种的求职者，工作已经有人了，但可以留下电话号码，以防有其他机会。有时这些伎俩确实能让人信服，但大多数时候并非如此。但对于有色人种申请人而言，要想获得公正待遇，他们需要花费时间和金钱聘请律师并出庭，而如果律师无法证明房东或雇主存在种族歧视的意图，案件就可能败诉。有多少求职者或住房需求者能够在经济上或心理上承受得起这一步呢？正如德尔加多和斯特凡西克所言，“只有积极主动、关注种族问题的努力才能真正改善现状。”苦难”(22)。他们指出，他们的一位同事提出了一种策略，“即社会在评判新法律时应该‘向下看’。如果[新法律]不能减轻最贫困群体的苦难——或者更糟的是，如果它们加剧了苦难——我们就应该拒绝它们”(22)。

Critical race theory also opposes the kind of liberalism that believes constitutional law is “color-blind,” or neutral in terms of race. For although we do have laws now that guarantee equal opportunities for all, these laws do nothing to support programs to ensure that such opportunities actually are available to all. As most of us know, although racial discrimination in housing and employment is illegal, it still occurs regularly (Delgado and Stefancic 21–23). The white landlord need only tell the applicant of color, politely of course, that there are no vacancies or that the dwelling has just been rented or sold. The white employer need only tell the applicant of color that the job has just been taken but the applicant can leave his or her phone number in case something else comes up. Sometimes these ploys are convincing. Most often they’re not. But for the applicant of color to get justice, he or she would need the time and money it takes to hire a lawyer and go to court, where the case may be lost if the lawyer can’t prove that there was an intention to discriminate racially on the part of the landlord or employer. How many individuals seeking a job or in need of housing are in a position, financially or psychologically, to take this step? As Delgado and Stefancic argue, “[o]nly aggressive, color-conscious efforts to change the way things are will do much to ameliorate misery” (22). They point to a strategy suggested by one of their colleagues “that society ‘look to the bottom’ in judging new laws. If [new laws] would not relieve the distress of the poorest group – or, worse, if they compound it – we should reject them” (22).

尽管传统的、谨慎的自由主义仍然是许多批判种族理论家所希望看到的有意义的种族进步的一个问题，但当今种族正义面临的更大障碍是……

Although classic, cautious liberalism remains a problem for the kind of meaningful racial progress many critical race theorists want to see, the larger obstacle to racial justice today is the

这种猖獗的、咄咄逼人的保守主义，挪用了马丁·路德·金的言论，对福利、平权行动或其他对穷人和少数族裔至关重要的项目漠不关心，甚至想要将边境军事化，并强制所有人说英语——而企业却急需具备外语能力的员工。因此，一些批判种族理论家不再关注自由主义及其弊病，而是开始关注这股保守主义浪潮。

rampant, in-your-face conservatism that co-opts Martin Luther King, Jr.’s language, has little use for welfare, affirmative action, or other programs vital to the poor and minorities, and wants to militarize the border and make everyone speak English when businesses are crying for workers with foreign-language proficiency. Some critical race theorists, accordingly, have stopped focusing on liberalism and its ills and begun to address the conservative tide.

（Delgado 和 Stefancic 24–25）

(Delgado and Stefancic 24–25)

在我们迄今为止对批判种族理论的讨论中，许多问题、议题和概念都隐含着一种种族理想主义的信念：即通过教育、校园反种族主义言论规范、媒体对少数族裔的正面报道（Delgado 和 Stefancic，第 20 页）以及法律手段（Bell，“种族现实主义”，第 308 页），改变人们（通常是无意识的）种族主义态度，就能实现种族平等。简而言之，如果我们对种族的态度是由社会建构的，那么社会也可以重塑这种态度。这种种族问题的观点被大多数美国人所接受，无论黑人还是白人，他们都希望看到种族平等成为现实。与此截然相反的是，种族现实主义认为，种族平等在美国永远无法实现，因此非裔美国人应该停止抱有这种幻想。我相信，对于许多读者来说，这种观点乍一看可能会令人震惊，过于悲观，甚至显得不合逻辑且自相矛盾。但我希望你在听取更多论点后再做决定。

Many of the problems, issues, and concepts we’ve encountered so far in our discussion of critical race theory have implied a belief in racial idealism: the conviction that racial equality can be achieved by changing people’s (often unconscious) racist attitudes through such means as education, campus codes against racist speech, positive media representations of minority groups (Delgado and Stefancic 20), and the use of the law (Bell, “Racial Realism” 308). In short, if our attitudes toward race are constructed by society, then society can reconstruct them. This perspective on racial issues is embraced by the majority of Americans, black and white alike, who want to see racial equality become a reality. Racial realism, in sharp contrast, is the conviction that racial equality will never be achieved in the United States and that African Americans should, therefore, stop believing that it will. I’m sure that, for many readers, this position initially might seem shocking, overly pessimistic, even illogical and self-defeating. But I hope you’ll wait until you hear more of the argument before you make up your mind.

种族现实主义，这一哲学思想在一篇题为《种族现实主义》的文章中得到了恰当的阐述，它源于纽约大学法学教授德里克·A·贝尔（Derrick A. Bell Jr.）的长期经验和不懈努力。贝尔曾是一位杰出的民权律师，正如我们之前提到的，他也是批判种族理论运动的创始人之一。贝尔指出：“我的预测——黑人不会被平等对待——并不令人意外，因为我们作为一个群体已经与平等地位失之交臂三百多年了。大多数黑人目前的处境也印证了这一点”（306）。非裔美国人的死亡率、失业率、贫困率、就业歧视率等等都远高于白人，这一点已被权威机构多次证实。然而，这些“令人震惊的差距……对政策制定者或整个社会几乎没有影响”（306）。或者在过去。贝尔指出，历史本身就应该“促使民权倡导者质疑平等理论的有效性。毕竟，宪法的制定者最初选择通过第五修正案来保护财产，包括被奴役的非洲人，这是一个不争的事实”（307）。而且，“那些致力于种族平等的人也不得不忽视内战修正案背后的政治动机——这种自私的动机几乎注定了，当政治需要发生变化时，对前奴隶的保护将无法得到执行”（307）。

Racial realism, a philosophy described in an essay aptly entitled “Racial Realism,” grew out of the long experience and committed work of New York University law professor Derrick A. Bell Jr., formerly a distinguished civil rights attorney and, as we noted earlier, one of the founders of the critical race theory movement. As Bell points out, “There is little reason to be shocked at my prediction that blacks will not be accepted as equals, a status that has eluded us as a group for more than three hundred years. The current condition of most blacks provides support for this position” (306). The appallingly higher rate of mortality, unemployment, poverty, job discrimination, and the like for African Americans than for white Americans has been documented by reputable sources many times over. Yet these “shocking disparities … have little effect on policymakers or the society in general” (306) now or in the past. Indeed, Bell notes, history itself should “trigger civil rights advocates to question the efficacy of equality theory. After all, it is an undeniable fact that the Constitution’s Framers initially opted to protect property, including enslaved Africans in that category, through the Fifth Amendment” (307). And “[t]hose committed to racial equality also had to overlook the political motivations for the Civil War amendments – self-interested motivations almost guaranteeing that when political needs changed, the protection provided the former slaves would not be enforced” (307).

贝尔在此指的是内战期间及战后通过的各项宪法修正案，这些修正案的主要目的在于惩罚南方，并确保黑人支持北方政治候选人。例如，1863年，也就是内战结束前两年，奴隶被宣布解放，但仅限于那些没有脱离联邦的州；黑人被赋予投票权，人们相信他们会投票给北方候选人；等等。在内战结束后长达十年的重建时期，北方政治官员和军队驻扎在南方，这在一定程度上保护了获释奴隶免受南方白人的侵害。然而，一旦北方白人总统候选人需要南方白人在国会的政治支持，情况就发生了变化。

Here Bell is referring to the various amendments to the Constitution passed during and after the Civil War largely for the purpose of punishing the South and ensuring black support for Northern political candidates. For example, the slaves were declared free in 1863, two years before the war ended, only in those states that did not secede from the Union; black men were given the vote in the belief that they would vote for Northern candidates; and so forth. The presence of Northern political administrators and troops stationed in the South during the decade-long Reconstruction period that followed the Civil War was the means by which, among other things, freed slaves were protected from Southern whites. However, as soon as the political support of Southern whites in Congress was needed by a white Northern presidential candidate, things changed.

为了确保共和党候选人拉瑟福德·B·海斯在充满争议的总统选举中获胜，北方欣然接受了一项对黑人极为不利的妥协方案。其中一项内容是[1877年的海斯-蒂尔登妥协方案]，该方案承诺……将剩余的联邦军队撤出南方各州，并保证不再干预这些州的“政治事务”。

With an eye toward ensuring the victory of the Republican Rutherford B. Hayes in a disputed presidential election, the North was more than ready to agree to a compromise that ill served blacks. Among other things, [the Hayes-Tilden Compromise of 1877] promised … both removal of remaining federal troops from the southern states and freedom from intervention in “political affairs” in those states.

（贝尔，《种族现实主义》312，注28）

(Bell, “Racial Realism” 312, n. 28)

联邦政策的这一转变意味着，获得自由的南方黑人只能任由憎恨和恐惧他们的白人摆布。我们许多人都了解随之而来的私刑、剥夺黑人选举权、屈辱的种族隔离法以及令人贫困的种族歧视。

This change in federal policy meant that freed Southern blacks were left at the mercy of a white population who hated and feared them. Many of us are aware of the holocaust of lynching, black disenfranchisement (being deprived of the vote), humiliating racial segregation laws, and impoverishing racial discrimination that followed.

当然，旨在帮助非裔美国人的法律最终屈从于白人权力结构需求的问题并非仅限于过去。贝尔认为，这个问题是系统性的，源于法律的形式主义，即法律使用抽象语言，并以此假定自身能够为所有公民提供中立（公正）的保护。问题在于，法律的抽象语言使其极易受到执行者的解读，而法官们往往利用法律的抽象语言来掩盖其“中立”判决背后的个人价值判断，而这些判决几乎总是有利于白人权力结构。

Of course, the problem of laws officially intended to aid black Americans giving way to the needs of the white power structure is not confined to the past. Bell sees the problem as systemic and due to the formalistic nature of the law, that is, due to the use of abstract language by which the law assumes it provides neutral (unbiased) protection to all citizens. The problem is that the law’s abstract language leaves it particularly open to the interpretation of the judges who administer it, and judges have tended to use the law’s abstract language to hide the personal value judgments behind their “neutral” decisions, decisions that almost always favor the white power structure.

贝尔以加州大学董事会诉巴克案（1978年）为例。巴克是一名白人，申请加州大学医学院。他起诉该大学，理由是其旨在确保合格的少数族裔候选人被录取的平权行动政策因其白人身份而歧视他。法院以抽象的平等概念为幌子，“无视究竟哪个种族拥有权力和优势，哪个种族几个世纪以来一直被拒之于学术界之外的社会问题，裁定平权行动政策不得以种族为由剥夺白人候选人的入学资格”（304）。因此，法院做出了一项具有里程碑意义的判决，该判决依赖于抽象的平等概念，从而回避了平权行动政策旨在维护的真正平等问题。事实上，贝尔指出，“在巴克案判决中显而易见的对白人种族特权的保护，已成为民权判决中的常见主题，尤其是在日益保守的最高法院所作出的许多判决中”（304）。贝尔还指出，任命克拉伦斯·托马斯法官进入最高法院“尤其令人不齿，因为选择像克拉伦斯·托马斯这样的黑人，重现了奴隶主提拔那些愿意模仿主人观点、执行命令的奴隶的做法，这些奴隶的存在为他们所协助和认可的压迫提供了一种扭曲的合法性”（304）。

As a representative example, Bell cites the case of Regents of the University of California v. Bakke (1978). Bakke, a white applicant to the University of California’s School of Medicine, sued the university on the grounds that its affirmative action policy, intended to help ensure that qualified minority candidates were accepted to the university, discriminated against him because he was white. Hiding behind an abstract application of the notion of equality and “ignoring social questions about which race in fact has power and advantages and which race has been denied entry for centuries into academia, the court held that an affirmative action policy may not unseat white candidates on the basis of their race” (304). The court thus made a landmark decision that relied on an abstract notion of equality in order to sidestep the real issues of equality that affirmative-action policies were designed to defend. In fact, Bell observes, “[t]he protection of whites’ race-based privilege, so evident in the Bakke decision, has become a common theme in civil-rights decisions, particularly in many of those decided by an increasingly conservative Supreme Court” (304). Indeed, Bell notes, the appointment of Judge Clarence Thomas to the Supreme Court “is particularly unkind because the choice of a black like Clarence Thomas replicates the slave-masters’ practice of elevating those slaves willing to mimic the masters’ views, carry out orders, and by their presence provide a perverse legitimacy to the oppression they aided and approved” (304).

基于以上种种原因，贝尔敦促非裔美国人“将法律——以及由此延伸出的法院——视为维护现状的工具，而只是偶尔且不可预测地成为受压迫者的避难所”，以便非裔美国人能够“挑战……种族平等的原则……并让他们的声音和愤怒被听到”（302）。贝尔写道：

For all of these reasons, Bell urges black Americans to “vie[w] the law – and, by extension, the courts – as instruments for preserving the status quo and only periodically and unpredictably serving as a refuge of oppressed people” so that blacks can “challenge … the principle of racial equality … and have their voice and outrage heard” (302). Bell writes,

我深信，在美国，黑人的确拥有某种真实的东西。然而，这并非对种族融合的浪漫憧憬；也绝非我们长期以来追求的法律面前人人平等的目标，尽管我们必须坚持反抗种族主义，否则黑人权利的丧失只会比现在更加严重。我们必须追求的种族现实主义，是对种族主义的本质以及我们在其中所扮演的从属角色的清醒认识。我们必须像我们的奴隶先辈那样认识到，争取自由的斗争，归根结底，是我们人性的体现，这种人性会在反抗压迫的过程中得以生存并变得更加强大，即便这种压迫永远无法被彻底消除。

I am convinced that there is something real out there in America for black people. It is not, however, the romantic love of integration; it is surely not the long-sought goal of equality under law, though we must maintain the struggle against racism, else the erosion of black rights will become even worse than it is now. The Racial Realism that we must seek is simply a hard-eyed view of racism as it is and our subordinate role in it. We must realize, as our slave forebears did, that the struggle for freedom is, at bottom, a manifestation of our humanity which survives and grows stronger through resistance to oppression, even if that oppression is never overcome.

（308）

(308)

因此，对贝尔而言，“紧盯目标”并非指种族平等。因为持续期待一个自己已经赢得却永远无法得到的奖赏，只会导致“沮丧和挫败”（308）。具有讽刺意味的是，对种族平等的信念——因为它现在不存在，过去不存在，将来也不会实现——实际上反而会造成一种冷漠或道德麻木。那些需要继续斗争的人们。贝尔心中所想的奖赏在于，面对种族主义的现实并继续与之斗争，从而增强人性，取得道德上的“胜利”（309），同时不抱任何白人权力结构终将被瓦解的幻想。

For Bell, then, keeping one’s “eyes on the prize” does not refer to the prize of racial equality. For the continued expectation of a prize that one has earned but will never receive leads only to “discouragement and defeat” (308). Ironically, then, the belief in racial equality – because it is not now, never has been, and never will be forthcoming – actually can tend to create a kind of apathy or moral paralysis in people who need to keep fighting. The prize Bell has in mind consists of the strengthened humanity and moral “triumph” (309) of facing the realities of and continuing to struggle against racism in all its forms without the illusion that the white power structure will ever be dismantled.

尽管我认为我们在了解批判种族理论的过程中已经触及了许多重要领域，但在很多方面，我们仍然只是浅尝辄止。关于我们讨论过的每一个问题，都还有很多值得深入研究的资料，还有许多其他问题我们仍然可以学习，例如黑人民族主义与同化、美国非黑即白的种族二元论、修正主义历史在批判种族理论中的作用、无意识种族主义等等。虽然批判种族理论并非直接针对文学研究，但它对我们解读文学作品有着重要的意义，因为正如我们所见，它为我们提供了许多理解种族的新视角，从而也帮助我们理解人际关系。而对人际关系的探索，可以说正是大多数作家写作的原因，也是大多数读者阅读的原因。

Although I think we’ve covered a good deal of important ground in our attempt to become acquainted with critical race theory, in many ways we’ve only scratched the surface. There is so much more to read about each of the issues we’ve discussed, and there are so many more issues about which we can still learn, issues such as black nationalism versus assimilation, America’s black-and-white binary vision regarding race, the role of revisionist history in critical race theory, unconscious racism, and many more. While critical race theory doesn’t address itself directly to literary studies, it has significant implications for our interpretation of literature because, as we have seen, it offers us a number of new perspectives from which to understand race and, therefore, from which to understand human relations. And the quest to understand human relations, one might argue, is the reason why most authors write as well as the reason why most readers read.

非裔美国批评与文学

African American criticism and literature

无论非裔美国文学批评家是通过引用非洲本土资源还是非洲和欧洲裔美国人的共同资源来阐释非裔美国文学的独特品质，他们都投入了大量精力来勾勒出被认定为非裔美国文学传统的鲜明特征。总的来说，批评家们一致认为，非裔美国文学聚焦于一系列反复出现的历史和社会主题，所有这些主题都反映了非裔美国人的政治经历——政治、社会和经济权力的现实。这些主题包括：重拾非洲历史；从“中段航程”的恐怖中幸存；从奴隶制的苦难中幸存；寻求摆脱奴隶制和其他形式压迫的自由；追求识字；非裔美国人在内战和重建时期的经历；在种族隔离的南方生存；混血儿在种族主义社会中的困境和冲突；以及经济生存的艰难。北迁及其相关的城市化、疏离感和寻求调和双重意识等主题；宗教在个人和集体生存中的作用；文化遗产的重要性；家庭和社区的重要性；以及如何在种族主义、阶级歧视和性别歧视的双重压迫下生存。然而，直到20世纪中期，黑人作家往往小心翼翼地处理种族主义这一主题，或者将其隐晦地隐藏在作品中，以便被白人编辑出版，并被白人读者阅读。也就是说，黑人作家常常通过微妙的暗示间接地展现种族主义的罪恶，这些暗示只有黑人读者和同情他们的白人读者才能领会，而不同情他们的白人读者则难以察觉。这一点显而易见。例如，查尔斯·瓦德尔·切斯纳特的短篇小说《波·桑迪》（1899）就清晰地展现了这种策略，他运用“夸张故事”的体裁，以一种较为含蓄的方式描绘了奴隶制的恐怖。事实上，当切斯纳特开始公开描写种族主义时，他的作品就找不到出版社愿意出版了。

Whether African American literary critics have sought to explain the unique quality of African American literature by citing its African sources or its African and European American sources, much effort has been expended in delineating the distinguishing features of what has been identified as the African American literary tradition. Generally speaking, critics agree that African American literature has focused on a number of recurring historical and sociological themes, all of which reflect the politics – the realities of political, social, and economic power – of black American experience. Among these themes are the following: reclaiming the African past; surviving the horrors of the Middle Passage; surviving the ordeal of slavery; the quest for freedom from slavery and from other forms of oppression; the quest for literacy; the experience of African Americans during the Civil War and Reconstruction; surviving life in the South under segregation; the problems and conflicts of mulattoes in a racist society; the difficulties of economic survival; the migration North and the related themes of urbanization, alienation, and the quest to reconcile double consciousness; the role of religion in personal and collective survival; the importance of cultural heritage; the importance of family and community; and surviving the combined oppression of racism, classism, and sexism. Until the mid twentieth century, however, black writers often treated the subject of racism carefully or encoded it in their writing in order to be published by white editors and read by white audiences. That is, black writers often represented the evils of racism indirectly through subtle references that black readers and sympathetic white readers would catch but that unsympathetic white readers wouldn’t readily notice. We see this strategy quite clearly in, for example, Charles Waddell Chesnutt’s story “Po Sandy” (1899), in which the “tall tale” genre is used to convey a rather guarded portrait of the horrors of slavery. Indeed, when Chesnutt became overt in his portrayals of racism, he was unable to find a press to publish his work.

正如这些主题所示，非裔美国文学的政治内涵包括：纠正对非裔美国人的刻板印象；纠正美国历史中对非裔美国人的错误描述和忽视；颂扬非裔美国人的文化、经历和成就；以及揭示种族主义的社会和心理运作机制。你还会注意到，许多此类主题都涉及如何克服人生中的负面经历并追求积极向上。因为精神上的生存和充分发挥非裔美国人的潜能是非裔美国文学中经常颂扬的价值观。

As these themes suggest, the political content of African American literature includes correcting stereotypes of African Americans; correcting the misrepresentation of African Americans in American history and the omission of African Americans from American history; celebrating African American culture, experience, and achievement; and uncovering the social and psychological operations of racism. You’ll notice, too, that many of these themes involve surviving life’s negative experiences and questing for the positive. For spiritual survival and the realization of African Americans’ full human potential are values frequently celebrated in African American writing.

就其诗学或风格要素而言，非裔美国文学传统以其诸多特征而著称，其中最显著的两个特征是：口语性和民间意象。口语性，即语言的口语特质，赋予文学作品一种即时感和人性化的存在感，使读者仿佛置身于真人的声音之中。在非裔美国文学中，口语性通常是通过使用黑人白话英语和模仿黑人语言的节奏来实现的，例如重复重要的短语和交替使用不同的声音，这些手法常见于教堂布道以及蓝调、爵士乐和说唱音乐中。正如我们之前所看到的，兰斯顿·休斯的作品以其口语性而闻名，索尼娅·桑切斯和尼基·乔瓦尼的诗歌也是如此。托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970 年）也为我们提供了一个引人注目的例子，展现了黑人声音的多样性，其中最“可听见”的声音包括麦克蒂尔夫人、宝琳·布里德洛夫和玛丽小姐的声音。

In terms of its poetics, or stylistic elements, the African American literary tradition is distinguished by, among other characteristics, two prominent features: orality and folk motifs. Orality, or the spoken quality of its language, gives a literary work a sense of immediacy, of human presence, by giving readers the feeling they are hearing a human voice. In African American literature, orality is usually achieved by using Black Vernacular English and by copying the rhythms of black speech, including, for example, the repetition of important phrases and alternating voices, devices associated with church sermons and with blues, jazz, and rap music. As we saw earlier, the work of Langston Hughes is noted for its orality, and so is the poetry of Sonia Sanchez and Nikki Giovanni. Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970), too, offers us a striking example of orality in the range of black voices it represents, the most “audible” of which include those of Mrs. MacTeer, Pauline Breedlove, and Miss Marie.

民间题材的运用涵盖了广泛的人物类型和民间习俗，营造出一种与非洲和非裔美国人历史的延续感。这些人物类型包括：当地的治疗师、巫师、女族长、当地的说书人、骗子、宗教领袖和民间英雄。民间习俗包括：吟唱劳动歌、赞美诗和蓝调；参与民间和宗教仪式，以此维系社群并与过去保持联系；通过讲故事来讲述个人和群体历史，传承传统智慧；传承民间工艺和技能，例如绗缝、家具制作和传统食物的烹饪；以及强调命名的重要性，包括爱称、昵称，以及被辱骂（被取下侮辱性的称呼）。

The use of folk motifs includes a wide range of character types and folk practices and creates a sense of continuity with the African and African American past. These character types include, for example, the local healer, the conjurer, the matriarch, the local storyteller, the trickster, the religious leader, and the folk hero. Folk practices include, for example, singing worksongs, hymns, and the blues; engaging in folk and religious rituals as a way of maintaining community and continuity with the past; storytelling as a way of relating personal and group history and passing down traditional wisdom; passing down folk crafts and skills, such as quilting, furniture making, and the preparation of traditional foods; and emphasizing the importance of naming, including pet names, nicknames, and being called out of one’s name (being called a derogatory name).

在众多分析非裔美国文学传统的著作中，最著名的包括亨利·路易斯·盖茨的《能指之猴》（The Signifying Monkey）和休斯顿·A·贝克的《布鲁斯、意识形态与非裔美国文学》（Blues, Ideology, and Afro-American Literature）。盖茨试图将非裔美国文学史描绘成一部文学文本间关系史。他认为……黑人文本之间“谈论”彼此——例如，通过复制、改变或戏仿彼此的文学手法——就像黑人在进行被称为“指称”的非裔美国民间实践时彼此谈论一样。

Among the best-known attempts to analyze the African American literary tradition are The Signifying Monkey, by Henry Louis Gates Jr., and Houston A. Baker Jr.’s Blues, Ideology, and Afro-American Literature. Gates attempts to chart African American literary history as a history of relationships among literary texts. He argues that black texts “talk” about one another – for example, by copying, altering, or parodying one another’s literary devices – the same way that black people talk about one another when they engage in the African American folk practice called signifying.

“Signifyin(g)”一词，盖茨特意这样拼写是为了强调其通俗发音，并与其他定义区分开来。它指的是用各种间接、巧妙、讽刺或玩笑的方式表达你对他人的看法——例如，侮辱某人、揭穿某人的虚伪或赞美某人——而无需直接说出你的意思。举个最简单的例子，如果你想告诉你的室友别霸占所有冰淇淋，你可以在室友面前对第三方说：“这冰箱肯定有问题，因为我每次放半加仑巧克力薄荷冰淇淋进去，一夜之间就变成一品脱了。”当你的室友回答说“我又没吃光所有冰淇淋”时，你可以说：“我刚才提到你的名字了吗？我根本就没在跟你说话！你肯定良心不安吧！” 这就叫做对你的室友进行“Signifyin(g)”式的暗示。盖茨选择用来体现这种间接沟通过程的形象是“能指猴”，即非裔美国民间故事中的骗术大师。让我们简要地看一下盖茨理论在文学作品中的应用。

Signifyin(g), which Gates spells in this manner to emphasize the folk pronunciation of the word and to distinguish it from other definitions of the term, refers to various indirect, clever, ironic, and playful ways of giving your opinion about another person – for example, insulting someone, deflating someone’s pretentiousness, or paying someone a compliment – without saying explicitly what you mean. To cite the simplest example, if you want to tell your roommate to quit hogging all the ice cream, you can say to a third party, in your roommate’s presence, “Something must be wrong with this freezer because every time I put a half-gallon of chocolate-chip-mint in here it turns into a pint overnight.” When your roommate responds with “I don’t eat all the ice cream,” you can then say, “Did I mention your name? I wasn’t even talking to you! You must have a guilty conscience!” This would be called signifying on your roommate. The figure Gates chooses to embody this process of indirect communication is the Signifying Monkey, the master trickster of African American folk tales. Let’s look briefly at a literary application of Gates’ theory.

理查德·赖特和拉尔夫·埃里森是两位在20世纪40年代和50年代涌现的杰出的非裔美国作家，他们对如何在文学中展现黑人经历持有不同的看法。赖特是一位自然主义者：他认为，种族压迫的残酷现实应该用直白、朴实的语言来呈现，以便尽可能有力地传达种族主义的罪恶和黑人所遭受的苦难。赖特在《土生子》（1940）和《黑孩子》（1945）等作品中正是如此。与此相反，拉尔夫·埃里森是一位现代主义者：他认为，人类经验的复杂性、模糊性和不确定性最好用含蓄的隐喻语言和具有多层次意义的复杂叙事来表现。在《看不见的人》（1952）中，埃里森“通过重复和差异来戏仿赖特的文学结构，从而对赖特进行意义上的反讽”（盖茨，《意义猴子》 ， 106页）。也就是说，《看不见的人》通过以一种颠倒的方式呼应赖特作品中的某些关键元素，间接而巧妙地揭示了埃里森对赖特文学观点的不满。

Richard Wright and Ralph Ellison, two great African American writers who emerged during the 1940s and 1950s, disagreed about how black experience should be rendered in literature. Wright was a naturalist: he believed that the harsh, inescapable realities of racist oppression should be represented in straightforward, stark language in order to convey as powerfully as possible the evils of racism and the depth of black suffering. This is exactly what Wright did in works like Native Son (1940) and Black Boy (1945). Ralph Ellison, in contrast, was a modernist: he believed that the complexities, ambiguities, and uncertainties of human experience could best be represented by ambiguous, metaphorical language and a complex narrative with multiple layers of meaning. In Invisible Man (1952), Ellison “signifies upon Wright by parodying Wright’s literary structures through repetition and difference” (Gates, Signifying Monkey 106). That is, Invisible Man indirectly and cleverly reveals Ellison’s disagreement with Wright’s literary vision by echoing certain key elements in Wright’s texts in a manner that reverses them.

例如，盖茨解释说，赖特的小说标题《土生子》和《黑孩子》暗示了一种具体、可见的种族存在。埃里森通过将其小说命名为《看不见的人》来阐释这些标题。虽然“人”这个词“暗示着比‘儿子’或‘男孩’更成熟、更强大的地位”（《能指猴子》 106页），但埃里森笔下的“人”是“看不见的”，是一种缺席而非存在，这正是历史上美国白人对待黑人的方式：仿佛他们隐形一般。埃里森还通过赖特的主人公比格·托马斯来阐释这一点。比格是“无声的”：他从不为自己发声，事实上，他很少说话。与其说他主动行动，不如说他对周围环境做出了反应。他。埃里森的回应是塑造了一个“仅仅是声音”的主人公：我们从未被告知他的名字，但“正是他塑造、编辑和叙述了自己的故事”（《能指的猴子》 106页）。简而言之，

For example, Gates explains, Wright’s titles, Native Son and Black Boy, suggest a concrete, visible, racial presence. Ellison signifies on these titles by calling his novel Invisible Man. While man “suggests a more mature and stronger status than either son or boy” (Signifying Monkey 106), Ellison’s man is “invisible,” an absence rather than a presence, which is how black people historically have been treated by white America: as if they were invisible. Ellison also signifies on Wright’s protagonist, Bigger Thomas. Bigger is “voiceless”: he never speaks up for himself and, indeed, rarely speaks at all. He doesn’t act so much as react to the circumstances around him. Ellison responds with a protagonist who “is nothing but voice”: we are never told his name, but “it is he who shapes, edits, and narrates his own tale” (Signifying Monkey 106). In short,

尽管小说标题中存在“存在”的隐喻，但比格的无声和无力行动（而非反应）却象征着一种缺席；《看不见的人》则恰恰相反，隐形所暗示的缺席被叙述者作为自己文本的作者的存在所削弱。

Bigger’s voicelessness and powerlessness to act (as opposed to react) signify an absence, despite the metaphor of presence found in the novel’s title; the reverse obtains in Invisible Man, where the absence implied by invisibility is undermined by the presence of the narrator as the author of his own text.

（象征猴子106）

(Signifying Monkey 106)

盖茨指出，埃里森的作品在诸多方面都对赖特的作品有所影响，埃里森试图借此表明，自然主义无情的阴郁并不能充分展现黑人经验。事实上，关于如何最好地展现黑人经验的争论，构成了盖茨分析所有文学符号行为（包括拉尔夫·埃里森、理查德·赖特、佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿、让·图默、保罗·劳伦斯·邓巴、伊什梅尔·里德、爱丽丝·沃克等人的作品）的争议基础。

Gates points out numerous other ways in which the works of Ellison signify upon those of Wright in Ellison’s attempt to show that naturalism’s unrelenting gloom does not adequately represent black experience. In fact, disagreements over the best way to represent black experience form the contested ground on which Gates maps all the acts of literary signifyin(g) he analyzes, including, in addition to Ralph Ellison’s, those of Richard Wright, Zora Neale Hurston, Jean Toomer, Paul Laurence Dunbar, Ishmael Reed, Alice Walker, and others.

休斯顿·贝克还试图将非裔美国文学传统与一种非裔美国民间艺术——布鲁斯——联系起来。贝克认为，布鲁斯是一种非裔美国文化自我表达的形式，它既影响着其他所有非裔美国表达文化形式，又受其影响；它既影响着其他非裔美国表达文化形式，又反映着其他非裔美国表达文化形式。布鲁斯是一个“母体”——“一个子宫，一个网络……一个永不停歇的输入输出点”（3）——因此，它也是整个非裔美国文化的隐喻。简而言之，布鲁斯是一种语言，一种文化密码，它被许多不同的非裔美国艺术形式以多种不同的方式“表达”出来，包括文学。因此，布鲁斯为研究非裔美国文学史提供了一种独特的非裔美国视角。让我们简要地看一下贝克提出的众多关于布鲁斯与非裔美国文学之间复杂关系的例子之一。

Houston Baker also attempts to relate the African American literary tradition to an African American folk art: the blues. Baker argues that the blues are a form of African American cultural self-expression that both influences and is influenced by, that both affects and reflects, all other forms of African American expressive culture. The blues are a “matrix” – “a womb, a network … a point of ceaseless input and output” (3) – and as such, they are also a metaphor for African American culture as a whole. In short, the blues are a language, a cultural code that gets “spoken” in many different ways by many different African American art forms, including literature. Thus, the blues offer a specifically African American approach to African American literary history. Let’s take a brief look at one of Baker’s many different examples of the complex relationship between the blues and African American literature.

贝克观察到，纵观非裔美国文学史，我们发现许多文本的主题结构与布鲁斯音乐颇为相似。他指出，布鲁斯歌曲通常具有双重主题：一个是精神主题，通常关乎失落与渴望；另一个是物质主题，通常关乎经济困境。贝克在非裔美国文学作品中也看到了同样的双重性，其中物质主题是驱动作品显性精神主题的潜台词。例如，《奥劳达·埃奎亚诺的生平，或称古斯塔夫·瓦萨，非洲人。自述》（1789）、弗雷德里克·道格拉斯的《弗雷德里克·道格拉斯自述：一个美国奴隶的生平》（1845）以及哈丽雅特·雅各布斯的《一个奴隶女孩的生平轶事》（1861）都具有一个共同的精神主题：通往精神觉醒、寻找自我的旅程，这是他们通往自由之旅的重要维度。它们的共同潜台词隐藏在……之下。贯穿全书的，是与精神主题并存，却又暗流涌动的经济现实，主人公们的精神追求正是建立在经济基础之上。埃奎亚诺、道格拉斯以及雅各布斯的琳达·布伦特都必须想方设法获得所需的资金，才能实现他们的自由——而自由正是他们精神目标得以实现的土壤。

Throughout African American literary history, Baker observes, we find texts with a thematic structure akin to that of the blues. Blues songs, he notes, generally have a double theme: a spiritual theme, usually about loss and desire, and a material theme, usually about the exigencies of economic necessity. Baker sees this same doubleness in African American literary texts, in which the material theme is the subtext that drives the work’s overt spiritual theme. For example, The Life of Olaudah Equiano, or Gustavus Vassa, the African. Written by Himself (1789), Frederick Douglass’ Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, An American Slave (1845), and Harriet Jacobs’ Incidents in the Life of a Slave Girl (1861) share a common spiritual theme: the journey to spiritual awakening, to finding oneself, which is an important dimension of their journey to freedom. Their common subtext, which lies below the spiritual theme and quietly competes with it, is the economic reality on which the protagonists’ spiritual quests depend. Equiano, Douglass, and Jacobs’ Linda Brent must all find ways to get the money they need in order to achieve their freedom, which is the soil in which their spiritual goals are planted.

当然，所有非裔美国文学作品的经济隐喻并非都体现在逃离或赎身所需的经济需求上。但贝克仍然将非裔美国文学的“经济基础”（39）称为“奴隶制的经济”（13），因为非裔美国人所遭受的经济压迫是奴隶制的遗毒，而经济压迫本身就是一种奴役。因此，贝克的研究旨在描绘非裔美国文学史上那些以某种形式展现“布鲁斯”的时刻：“当人物、主人公、自传体叙述者或文学评论家成功地应对顽固的‘奴隶制的经济’，并最终获得一种富有感染力、即兴发挥的表达尊严时”（13）。在当代文学中，我们可能会说，这样的时刻发生在《宠儿》中，贝比·萨格斯抚慰了前奴隶们的情感创伤，用即兴布鲁斯的方式鼓励他们同时欢笑和哭泣。

Of course, the economic subtext of all African American texts does not lie in the financial requirements of escaping from or buying oneself out of slavery. But Baker nevertheless refers to the “economic grounding” (39) of African American literature as the “economics of slavery” (13) because the economic oppression of black Americans is slavery’s legacy, and economic oppression is itself a form of bondage. Baker’s project, then, is to chart those moments in African American literary history when the blues, in one form or another, are being played: “when personae, protagonists, autobiographical narrators, or literary critics successfully negotiate an obdurate ‘economics of slavery’ and achieve a resonant, improvisational expressive dignity” (13).
