In contemporary literature, we might say that such a moment occurs, for example, when Beloved’s Baby Suggs, who administers to the emotional deprivations of the former slaves, urges them, in improvisational blues fashion, to laugh and cry at the same time.

人们也做了大量工作来界定非裔美国女性写作特有的文学传统轮廓。非裔美国女性作家被排除在非裔美国文学经典之外，或被边缘化，而这种文学经典既由黑人男性作家定义，也由白人文学界定义。此外，在白人作家和黑人男性作家的文学作品中，非裔美国女性的形象通常仅限于次要角色或刻板印象。因此，在整个文学创作历程中，黑人女性作家一直致力于将黑人女性描绘成真实存在的人，展现她们所拥有的复杂性和深度。正如玛丽·海伦·华盛顿所说：“黑人女性作家的主要关注点之一就是黑人女性本身——她们的抱负、她们的冲突、她们与伴侣和孩子的关系、她们的创造力”（《黑眼苏珊》第十页）。

There has also been a good deal of work done to define the contours of a literary tradition specific to the writing of African American women, who were excluded from or marginalized by the African American literary canon as defined both by black male writers and by the white literary establishment. Furthermore, in literary works by white authors and black male authors alike, the representations of African American women generally were restricted to minor or stereotyped characters. As a result, black women writers have been concerned, throughout their literary history, to portray black women as real people with all the complexity and depth that black women have. As Mary Helen Washington puts it, “[O]ne of the main preoccupations of the Black woman writer has been the Black woman herself – her aspirations, her conflicts, her relationship to her men and her children, her creativity” (Black-Eyed Susans x).

在华盛顿的声明中， “关系”一词至关重要。正如我们在第四章“女性主义批评”中所看到的，黑人女性必须权衡她们与整个黑人社群之间相互冲突的关系——她们既要与黑人男性团结一致，反对种族压迫，又要与所有种族的女性建立关系，以抵抗性别歧视的压迫。尤其值得注意的是，黑人男性对种族团结的要求与白人女性主义者对性别团结的要求之间的冲突，迫使许多从事文学批评的非裔美国女性在探讨黑人女性写作中的性别议题时，不得不避而不谈女性主义。（关于此问题的进一步讨论，请参见第四章。）

Relationship is a key word in Washington’s statement. For as we saw in Chapter 4, “Feminist criticism,” black women must negotiate the conflicting requirements of their relationship to the black community as a whole – their solidarity with black men against racist oppression – and their relationship to women of all races in an effort to resist sexist oppression. In particular, the dilemma created by the conflicting requirements of black men’s demands for racial solidarity and white feminists’ demands for gender solidarity has forced many African American women engaged in literary criticism to address gender issues in black women’s writing without mentioning feminism. (See Chapter 4 for further discussion of this issue.)

非裔美国女性作家对黑人女性身份的关注体现在许多反复出现的主题中。其中包括：黑人女性作为低薪劳动者被迫从事最底层的工作，遭受歧视和迫害。作为暴力和性剥削的受害者；作为被压制的艺术家，黑人女性；黑人女性社群对她们心理（有时甚至是生理和经济）生存的重要性，这其中也包括祖母、母亲和女儿之间的关系；年轻黑人女孩如何被启蒙，直面种族主义和性别歧视的残酷现实；肤色、发质和白人审美标准在黑人女性自我认知和社群地位中的作用；黑人女性与男性之间关系的重要性；以及与黑人男性作家或白人作家的作品相比，黑人女性作品中对种族主义、性别歧视和阶级歧视的综合压迫的持续关注。在早期黑人女性的文学作品中，我们也能看到“冒充白人”的主题。而在过去二十年的文学作品中，女同性恋关系的主题也逐渐出现。此外，黛博拉·E·麦克道尔观察到，“很大程度上是因为黑人女性的贬损形象在历史上一直存在，无论是在文学作品中还是在文学作品之外，黑人女小说家（我们还可以补充，诗人、剧作家也是如此）在其传统中一直承担着修正主义的使命，旨在用现实取代刻板印象”（94-95）。

The focus on black women’s identity in writing by African American women is embodied in a number of recurring themes. Among them are the following: the victimization of black women as underpaid workers forced into the lowliest jobs and as victims of violence and sexual exploitation; the black woman as suppressed artist; the importance of black women’s community for psychological (and sometimes physical and economic) survival, which includes relationships among grandmothers, mothers, and daughters; the initiation of young black girls into the harsh realities of racism and sexism; the role of skin color, hair texture, and white standards of beauty in the black woman’s self-perception and status within the community; the importance of the relationships between black women and men; and a more sustained focus on the combined oppression of racism, sexism, and classism than we find in the work of black male writers or white writers. In earlier literary works by black women we also see the theme of passing for white. And in literature written over the past two decades the theme of lesbian relationships has emerged. In addition, “[l]argely because degraded images of black women have persisted throughout history, both in and out of literature,” Deborah E. McDowell observes, “Black women novelists [and, we might add, poets and playwrights as well] have assumed throughout their tradition a revisionist mission aimed at substituting reality for stereotype” (94–95).

这种修正主义使命包括塑造更贴近现实的女性角色类型。在《教导黑眼苏珊》一书中，玛丽·海伦·华盛顿借鉴了爱丽丝·沃克的洞见，描述了三种显著的女性角色类型，这些类型经常被黑人女作家用来代表不同历史时期的黑人女性。第一种是“悬置的女性”，她们是男性和整个社会的受害者，几乎没有选择，之所以“悬置”，是因为她对自身处境无能为力。这种类型常见于以十九世纪和二十世纪初为背景的作品中。例如，佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿的《他们的眼睛望着上帝》（1937）中的南妮和托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）中的宝琳·布里德洛夫。第二种是“同化的女性”，她们没有遭受身体暴力，对自己的生活拥有更大的掌控权，但却遭受了心理暴力，因为她们渴望被白人社会接纳，从而与自己的非裔美国人根源割裂开来。这种类型的人物常见于以20世纪40年代和50年代为背景的作品中。例如，《他们的眼睛望着上帝》中的特纳夫人和《最蓝的眼睛》中的杰拉尔丁。最后，第三种人物类型是“觉醒女性”，她们逐渐意识到自身在心理和政治上所受到的压迫，并开始有能力为自己创造新的生活和新的选择，通常是通过一段艰难的成人礼经历，使她们做好改变的准备。这种类型的人物常见于以20世纪60年代为背景的作品中。例如，爱丽丝·沃克的小说《子午线》（1976）中的子午线和《他们的眼睛望着上帝》中的简妮。正如简妮的例子所示，这些人物类型并不局限于它们通常被赋予的历史背景。

This revisionist mission has included the provision of realistic female character types. In “Teaching Black-Eyed Susans,” Mary Helen Washington draws on the insights of Alice Walker to describe three salient types, which frequently have been used by black women writers to represent black women from different historical periods. The first is the “suspended woman,” the victim of men and of society as a whole, with few or no options, “suspended” because she can’t do anything about her situation. This type is often found in works set in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Examples include Nannie in Zora Neale Hurston’s Their Eyes Were Watching God (1937) and Pauline Breedlove in Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970). The second type is the “assimilated woman,” who is not victimized by physical violence and has much more control of her life, but who is victimized by psychological violence in that she is cut off from her African American roots by her desire to be accepted by white society. This type is often found in works set in the 1940s and 1950s. Examples include Mrs. Turner in Their Eyes Were Watching God and Geraldine in The Bluest Eye. Finally, the third character type is the “emergent woman,” who is coming to an awareness of her own psychological and political oppression and becoming capable of creating a new life and new choices for herself, usually through a harsh experience of initiation that makes her ready for the change. This type is often found in works set in the 1960s. Examples include Meridian in Alice Walker’s Meridian (1976) and Janie in Their Eyes Were Watching God. As the example of Janie illustrates, these character types are not confined to the historical settings with which they are generally associated.

我认为，一些批评家可能会认为，我们应该在这个有用的列表中添加第四种人物类型：即“解放女性”，她们发现了自己的能力，知道自己需要什么，并努力去获得它。简而言之，我们可以说……“解放女性”已经找到了自我，并且对自己的现状感到满意。虽然我们可能会认为这种人物类型最常出现在以20世纪70年代及以后为背景的黑人女性作品中，或者说最引人注目，但我认为在更早时期的作品中也能找到她的身影。例如，爱丽丝·沃克的小说《紫色》（ 1982）中的舒格·艾弗里和托妮·莫里森的小说《所罗门之歌》（1977）中的彼拉多，都是“解放女性”的典型代表，这两部作品的背景都设定在20世纪上半叶。

Some critics might argue, I think, that we should add a fourth character type to this useful list: that of the “liberated woman,” who has discovered her abilities, knows what she needs, and goes about getting it. We might say, in short, that the “liberated woman” has already found herself and likes what she has found. Although we might expect that this character type would appear most often, or most visibly, in black women’s writing set in the 1970s and later, I think she can be found in works set in earlier periods as well. Examples of the “liberated woman” include Shug Avery in Alice Walker’s The Color Purple (1982) and Pilate in Toni Morrison’s Song of Solomon (1977), both of which are set in the decades of the first half of the twentieth century.

最后，非裔美国女性的诗歌创作传统上包含一些反复出现的文学策略。例如，黑人女作家经常在小说或短篇小说中以黑人女性角色作为叙述者，或在诗歌或戏剧独白中以黑人女性角色作为说话者，以此赋予黑人女性讲述自身故事的权威。当采用第三人称叙述时，视角人物（即我们通过其视角来观看故事的角色）通常是黑人女性或女孩。为了强调黑人女性之间关系的重要性，有时叙事框架会设定为两位黑人女性或女孩之间的对话（可以是真实的对话、主人公想象的对话，也可以是通过书信进行的对话）。

Finally, African American women’s poetics traditionally include a number of recurring literary strategies. For example, black women writers frequently use a black female character as the narrator in a novel or work of short fiction or as the speaker in a poem or dramatic monologue in order to give black women authority as the tellers of their own stories. When third-person narration is used, the point-of-view character (the character through whose eyes we see the story) is usually a black woman or girl. To emphasize the importance of relationships between black women, sometimes the narrative is framed as a conversation (a real conversation, one imagined by the protagonist, or one that takes place through letters) between two black women or girls.

为了营造一个与黑人女性经历产生共鸣的世界，运用与黑人女性家庭空间和活动相关的意象也是一种常用的文学策略：例如，与厨房以及家中其他场所相关的意象，这些场所是进行诸如缝制被子、罐装食品、园艺和农活以及将家族和文化遗产传承给子女等传统技艺的场所。或者，也可以通过与黑人女性外貌相关的意象来展现黑人女性的世界，例如服饰、发型、肤色、化妆品等等。

In order to evoke a world that resonates with black women’s experience, the use of imagery associated with black women’s domestic space and activity is also a frequently employed literary strategy: for example, imagery associated with the kitchen and other locations within the home where such traditional skills as quilting, canning, the performance of garden and farm chores, and the passing down of family and cultural heritage to children occur. Or the world of black women may be evoked by imagery associated with black women’s physical appearance, such as clothing, hairstyles, skin color, cosmetics, and the like.

总的来说，我们讨论过的所有文学手法都强调了黑人女性为确立自身身份而进行的斗争。这种身份认同可能表现为为了家庭、社区或种族的利益而牺牲自我，正如许多早期作品中所展现的那样；也可能表现为探索自身的能力、需求和欲望，正如许多当代文学作品中所展现的那样。但无论采取何种形式，黑人女性自我认同过程中复杂的心理、社会和经济动态都在她们的写作中占据着重要的地位。

Generally speaking, all the literary devices we’ve discussed emphasize the struggle of black women to assert their own identity. That identity may take the form of sacrificing oneself for the good of the family, the community, or the race, as it does in many earlier works. Or it may take the form of exploring one’s own abilities, needs, and desires, as it does in many contemporary literary texts. But whatever form it takes, the complex psychological, social, and economic dynamics of black women’s self-definition occupy an important place in their writing.

当然，非裔美国批评的独特视角也能让我们更深入地理解美国白人作家的文学作品。在《黑暗中嬉戏：白人身份与文学想象》一书中，托妮·莫里森为我们提供了一种极具启发性的方法，让我们从非裔美国人的视角解读白人主流文学，揭示了白人文本如何出于自身目的，构建她所谓的“非洲主义在美国历史中的存在”。莫里森使用“非洲主义”一词，指的是“非洲人民所代表的字面意义和引申意义上的‘黑色’，以及伴随欧洲中心主义对这些人民的认知而产生的各种观点、假设、解读和误读”。（6-7）简而言之，莫里森意义上的非洲主义，是白人对非洲人和非裔美国人的一种观念（或者更准确地说，是误解），白人作家将他们自己的恐惧、需求、欲望和冲突投射到这种观念上。

Of course, the unique perspectives of African American criticism can also offer us insights into literary works by white American writers. In Playing in the Dark: Whiteness and the Literary Imagination, Toni Morrison offers us a very productive approach to reading white mainstream literature from an African American perspective that reveals the ways in which white texts construct, for their own purposes, what she calls the Africanist presence in American history. Morrison uses the word Africanist as “a term for the denotative and connotative blackness that African peoples have come to signify as well as the entire range of views, assumptions, readings, and misreadings that accompany Eurocentric learning about these people” (6–7). In short, Africanism, in Morrison’s sense of the word, is a white conception (or, more accurately, misconception) of African and African American people on which white authors have projected their own fears, needs, desires, and conflicts.

在白人主流文学中，非洲主义的存在可以表现为黑人角色、关于黑人的故事、对黑人语言的描绘，以及与非洲或黑人身份相关的意象。莫里森呼吁人们探究这些手法在白人作家作品中的运作方式，但她并非建议我们分析文学中的种族主义——此类分析早已开展，并且仍在进行——也并非建议我们根据作品中对非白人角色的刻画来评判其质量。相反，她鼓励我们审视……

In white mainstream literature, an Africanist presence can take the form of black characters, stories about black people, representations of black speech, and images associated with Africa or with blackness. In calling for investigations of how these devices function in the work of white writers, Morrison is not suggesting that we analyze racism in literature – such analyses have been and are being conducted – nor that we judge the quality of a work based on its representation of nonwhite characters. Rather, she encourages us to examine the ways in which

我们国家（白人）文学的主要和被推崇的特征——个人主义、男性气质、社会参与与历史孤立；尖锐而模糊的道德问题；天真无邪的主题以及对死亡和地狱意象的痴迷——都是……对黑暗、持久的……非洲主义存在的回应。

the major and championed characteristics of our national [white] literature – individualism, masculinity, social engagement versus historical isolation; acute and ambiguous moral problematics; the thematics of innocence coupled with an obsession with figurations of death and hell – are … responses to a dark, abiding … Africanist presence.

（5）

(5)

也就是说，莫里森想要分析的是，经典化的美国白人文学如何通过与虚构的非洲身份形成对比，来定义一种积极的“典型的美国身份”（44）。这种虚构的非洲身份“原始而野蛮……束缚而不自由，反叛却有用”（45），白人正是以此来定义自身的文明美德。“在我看来，”莫里森指出，“这些主题使美国文学成为一个更加复杂且富有价值的知识体系”（53）。

That is, Morrison wants to analyze the ways in which canonized white American literature has defined a positive “quintessential American identity” (44) by contrast with an invented Africanist identity, “raw and savage … bound and unfree, rebellious but serviceable” (45), against which whites have been able to define their own civilized virtues. “These topics,” Morrison observes, “seem to me to render the nation’s literature a much more complex and rewarding body of knowledge” (53).

莫里森指出，白人作家运用非洲裔形象的方式多种多样，其中之一是将黑人角色作为一种象征和“载体”，用来表达“非法性行为、对疯狂的恐惧、被驱逐和自我厌恶”等主题（52），以及“定义白人角色的目标并强化其特质”（52-53）。例如，莫里森认为，欧内斯特·海明威的《拥有与失去》（1937）除了其他对非洲裔角色的策略性运用外，还安排了一位渔船上的黑人船员来“博取我们对船长——主人公哈里·摩根——的钦佩”（80），哈里·摩根是一位远洋渔民。“哈里·摩根，”莫里森指出，

Among the many ways in which white writers have employed the Africanist presence, Morrison notes, is the use of black characters as a sign of and “vehicle for,” among other things, “illegal sexuality, fear of madness, expulsion, [and] selfloathing” (52) as well as “to define the goals and enhance the qualities of white characters” (52–53). For example, Morrison argues that Ernest Hemingway’s To Have and Have Not (1937), among other strategic uses of Africanist characters, employs a black crewman on a fishing boat to “solicit our admiration” (80) for the boat’s white captain, protagonist Harry Morgan, a deep-sea fisherman. “Harry Morgan,” Morrison notes,

他似乎代表了典型的美国英雄：一个孤胆英雄，与试图限制其自由和个性的政府抗争。他浪漫而……尊重他赖以谋生的自然……能力出众……充满活力、自由、勇敢且道德高尚。

seems to represent the classic American hero: a solitary man battling a government that would limit his freedom and his individuality. He is romantically … respectful of the nature he destroys for a living … competent … virile, free, brave, and moral.

（70）

(70)

海明威是如何向读者展现哈里具备这些品质的呢？他主要是通过将主人公与他船员中的一个“黑鬼”进行对比来实现的，这个“黑鬼”……在第一部分中，他始终没有名字”（70）。在第二部分，当海明威从哈利的第一人称叙述切换到第三人称叙述时，这个黑人角色以两种不同的方式被“命名”：“哈利在与黑人直接对话时称他为‘韦斯利’；海明威作为叙述者提到他时则用‘黑鬼’”（71）。然而， “人”这个词却只用来指代哈利。

How does Hemingway show the reader that Harry has these qualities? He does so largely by contrasting the protagonist with a “‘nigger’ in his crew, a man who, throughout all of part one, has no name” (70). In part two, when Hemingway switches from Harry’s first-person narration to a third-person narrator, the black character is “named” in two different ways: “Harry says ‘Wesley’ when speaking to the black man in direct dialogue; Hemingway writes ‘nigger’ when as narrator he refers to him” (71). The word man, however, is reserved for Harry.

此外，“这个黑人角色要么不说话（作为‘黑鬼’，他保持沉默），要么说话方式经过精心安排和操控（作为‘韦斯利’，他的言辞服务于哈利的需要）”（71）。即使黑人是第一个发现船上所有人翘首以盼的飞鱼的人，海明威也没有让他“看到飞鱼时惊呼出声”（73），而这本是他自然而然会做的事。相反，作者让哈利用一种略显笨拙的句式写道：“我看了一眼，发现他看到了一群飞鱼”（海明威 13），因为“叙事中种族歧视的逻辑”决定了必须是哈利——“有权有势的人，有权威的人”——才​​能看到飞鱼，即使这需要一种不够“优美”的句法才能达到这个目的（73）。

Furthermore, “[t]his black character either does not speak (as a ‘nigger’ he is silent) or speaks in very legislated and manipulated ways (as a ‘Wesley’ his speech serves Harry’s needs)” (71). Even when the black man is the first to spot the flying fish for which everyone on board has been waiting, Hemingway does not let him “cry out at the sighting” (73), which would be the natural thing for him to do. Instead, the author gives Harry the awkwardly constructed phrase, “I looked and saw he had seen a patch of flying fish” (Hemingway 13) because “the logic of the narrative’s [racial] discrimination” dictates that it must be Harry, “the powerful one, the authoritative one, who sees,” even if it requires a less “graceful” syntax to achieve this goal (73).

最后，当那位黑人船员在他们的船遭到炮火袭击后终于开始开口说话时，这显然是为了突出哈里的勇敢。莫里森指出：

Finally, when the black crewman finally does begin to speak a good deal, after their boat has been fired upon, it serves the clear purpose of foregrounding Harry’s bravery. Morrison points out that

在得知哈里也中枪，而且伤势比韦斯利严重得多之前，我们听了整整三页韦斯利因枪伤而发出的呻吟、低吼和虚弱之声。相比之下，哈里不仅没有提及自己的痛苦，反而以同情的目光忍受着韦斯利的哀嚎，并以迅速而坚忍的男子气概完成了艰难的驾驶和将违禁品（船上运输的非法货物）抛入海中的工作。

[w]e hear the grumbles, the groans, the weakness as Wesley’s responses to his gunshot wounds for three pages before we learn that Harry is also shot, and much worse than Wesley is. By contrast, Harry has not only not mentioned his own pain, he has taken Wesley’s whining with compassion and done the difficult work of steering and tossing the contraband [the illegal goods the boat is transporting] overboard in swift, stoic gestures of manliness.

（74-75）

(74–75)

因此，我们之所以更加钦佩哈利，正是因为我们不钦佩韦斯利——他被描绘成哈利的对立面。可以说，哈利的叙事力量——他的权威、力量和勇气——因黑人角色的沉默、软弱和怯懦而更加凸显。这只是非洲裔角色在白人主流文学中发挥重要作用的众多方式之一，而这种作用值得进一步研究。正如莫里森所言，“当批评过于礼貌或过于胆怯而对眼前的黑暗视而不见时，我们所有人，无论是读者还是作家，都会感到失落”（90-91）。

Thus, we admire Harry the more because we don’t admire Wesley, who is depicted as his opposite. Harry’s narrative power, so to speak – his authority, strength, and bravery – are enhanced by the black character’s silence, weakness, and cowardice. This is just one of the many ways in which an Africanist presence performs a major function in white mainstream literature, a function that merits further study. As Morrison puts it, “All of us, readers and writers, are bereft when criticism remains too polite or too fearful to notice a disrupting darkness before its eyes” (90–91).

在结束本节之前，我想先回答学生们经常问的一个问题：为什么我们只研究非裔美国文学批评，而不研究其他族裔文学批评？当然，非裔美国人并非唯一创作出杰出文学作品的美国少数族裔。其他族裔，如美洲原住民、亚裔美国人、奇卡诺人/墨西哥裔美国人和拉丁裔美国人，也为美国的文学创作做出了巨大贡献。然而，自……以来，非裔美国文学在美国历史上一直扮演着举足轻重的角色。自十八世纪以来，黑人研究一直是美国学术界的重要领域，尤其是在20世纪60年代之后。相比之下，其他优秀文学作品的理论导向型批评体系才刚刚起步。因此，在当下，将我们的注意力集中于非裔美国人文学批评似乎是合乎逻辑的。这既能让你们了解这一激动人心的领域正在开展的工作，也能鼓励你们去研究其他美国少数族裔的文学和批评。而对非裔美国人文学批评的深入理解，既可以作为有益的范例，也可以作为与其他美国文学进行比较和对比的出发点。

Before we draw this section to a close, let me pause here to answer a question frequently asked by students: why are we studying African American criticism and not the criticism of other ethnic literatures as well? Certainly, African Americans aren’t the only American ethnic minority to produce a body of exquisite literature. Among others, Native Americans, Asian Americans, Chicanos/as, and Latinos/as have contributed a great deal to the literary output of the United States. African American literature, however, has played a significant role in American history since the eighteenth century, and Black Studies has been an important field in American academia since the 1960s. In contrast, theoretically oriented bodies of criticism of these other wonderful literatures are just beginning to emerge. So it seems logical at this point in time to focus our attention on African American criticism, both to acquaint you with the work being done in this exciting field and to encourage you to investigate the literature and criticism of other American ethnic minorities, an endeavor for which a thorough grounding in African American criticism can serve as both a useful model and as a point of departure for comparison and contrast with other American literatures.

非裔美国评论家就文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions African American critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在概括非裔美国人文学研究方法。需要注意的是，与女权主义批评、女同性恋/男同性恋/酷儿批评、后殖民主义批评，以及任何分析特定历史受压迫群体作品的批评一样，非裔美国人批评既是一个研究对象——即对特定边缘化群体所创作的文学作品的研究——也是一个理论框架。作为研究对象，任何对非裔美国人文学作品的分析，无论采用何种理论框架，都可以被称为非裔美国人批评，即便并未关注文本中特有的非裔美国人元素。然而，作为理论框架——这也是我们在此主要关注的——非裔美国人批评将种族（种族认同、非裔美国人文化传统、心理、政治等等）置于分析的核心地位，因为在美国，种族深刻地影响着我们的个人和文化心理，进而影响着我们的文学创作。因此，作为一种理论框架，非裔美国人批评可以用来分析任何涉及非裔美国人问题的文学文本，无论其作者的种族如何，尽管非裔美国作家的作品是主要关注点。

The following questions are offered to summarize African American approaches to literature. Keep in mind that, like feminist, lesbian/gay/queer, postcolonial, or any criticism that analyzes the writing of a specific group of historically oppressed people, African American criticism is both a subject matter – the study of a body of literature written by a specific group of marginalized people – and a theoretical framework. As a subject matter, any analysis of a literary work written by an African American, regardless of the theoretical framework used, might be called African American criticism, even if no attention is paid to elements in the text that are specifically African American. However, as a theoretical framework – and this is our primary concern here – African American criticism foregrounds race (racial identity, African American cultural traditions, psychology, politics, and so forth) as the object of analysis because race, in America, informs our individual and cultural psychology, and therefore our literature, in profound ways. As a theoretical framework, then, African American criticism can be used to analyze any literary text that speaks to African American issues, regardless of the race of its author, although the work of African American writers is the primary focus.

1这部作品能教会我们哪些关于非洲传统、非裔美国人文化和经历，以及/或者非裔美国人历史（包括但不限于边缘化历史）的具体知识？

1 What can the work teach us about the specifics of African heritage, African American culture and experience, and/or African American history (including but not limited to the history of marginalization)?

2特定非裔美国人作品的种族政治（与种族压迫或解放相关的意识形态议程）是什么？例如，这些作品是否纠正了对非裔美国人的刻板印象；纠正了历史上对非裔美国人的错误描述；颂扬了非裔美国人的文化、经历和成就；或者探讨了种族问题，包括种族主义的经济、社会或心理影响？或者，正如许多白人作家的文学作品所展现的那样，这些作品是否强化了种族主义意识形态？

2 What are the racial politics (ideological agendas related to racial oppression or liberation) of specific African American works? For example, does the work correct stereotypes of African Americans; correct historical misrepresentations of African Americans; celebrate African American culture, experience, and achievement; or explore racial issues, including, among others, the economic, social, or psychological effects of racism? Or as can be seen in the literary production of many white authors, does the work reinforce racist ideologies?

3 特定非裔美国文学作品的诗学（文学手法和策略）是什么？例如，作品使用的是黑人方言还是标准白人英语？作品是否借鉴了非洲神话、非裔美国民间故事或民间主题？作品中的意象是否与非裔美国女性的家庭空间、非裔美国文化习俗、历史或传统产生共鸣？这些文学手法产生了哪些效果？它们与作品的主题或意义有何关联？

3 What are the poetics (literary devices and strategies) of specific African American works? For example, does the work use Black Vernacular or standard white English? Does the work draw on African myths or African American folk tales or folk motifs? Does the work provide imagery that resonates with African American women’s domestic space, African American cultural practices, history, or heritage? What are the effects of these literary devices and how do they relate to the theme, or meaning, of the work?

4这部作品如何融入非裔美国文学传统？就其政治和诗学而言，我们应该将其归入哪一类非裔美国文学作品？它与这些作品有何相似之处？它又如何突破这些作品，或许是通过尝试新的形式来重新定义文学美学？简而言之，它在非裔美国文学史或非裔美国女性文学史中占据着怎样的地位？

4 How does the work participate in the African American literary tradition? To what group of African American texts might we say it belongs in terms of its politics and poetics? How does it conform to those texts? How does it break with them, perhaps seeking to redefine literary aesthetics by experimenting with new forms? In short, what place does it occupy in African American literary history or in African American women’s literary history?

5这部作品如何体现利益趋同、种族的社会建构、白人特权或批判种族理论中的其他概念？理解这些概念如何加深我们对这部作品的解读？

5 How does the work illustrate interest convergence, the social construction of race, white privilege, or any other concept from critical race theory? How can an understanding of these concepts deepen our interpretation of the work?

6白人作家的作品中是如何运用非洲元素（黑人角色、关于黑人的故事、黑人语言的表达、与非洲或黑人相关的形象）来构建白人角色的正面形象的？

6 How is an Africanist presence – black characters, stories about black people, representations of black speech, images associated with Africa or with blackness – used in works by white writers to construct positive portrayals of white characters?

根据所讨论的文学作品，我们可以提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们也可以提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们从非裔美国人的视角出发，对文学文本进行富有成效的思考的一些起点。请记住，即使运用相同的理论概念，并非所有非裔美国批评家都会以相同的方式解读同一部作品。一如既往，即使是专家学者也会持有不同意见。我们运用非裔美国批评的目标是，学习看到文学中一些重要的方面——如果没有这种理论视角，我们可能无法如此清晰或深刻地理解这些方面——并理解生活在一个种族多元化的社会中所面临的挑战、责任和机遇。

Depending on the literary work in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us thinking productively about literary texts from an African American perspective. Remember, not all African American critics will interpret the same work in the same way, even if they employ the same theoretical concepts. As always, even expert practitioners disagree. Our goal in using African American criticism is to learn to see some important aspects of literature that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply without this theoretical perspective and to understand the challenges, responsibilities, and opportunities of living in an ethnically diverse society.

以下对菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的解读，旨在展现非裔美国人对该作品的诠释可能带来的结果。本文将着重探讨小说对其自身背景的种族主义回应。小说刻意忽略了爵士时代赖以存在的地点——哈莱姆区——以及非裔美国人群体，而这正是小说所要展现的时代。因此，《了不起的盖茨比》呈现给我们的，是一幅在历史上不完整，甚至可以说是不准确的20世纪20年代初纽约景象。鉴于菲茨杰拉德以其对文化细节的严谨刻画而闻名，这种“疏忽”引发了人们对作者自身种族政治立场的质疑。

The following reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what an African American interpretation of that work might yield. It focuses on what I will argue is the novel’s racist response to its own setting. By omitting the place – Harlem – and the people – African Americans – responsible for the Jazz Age the novel purports to represent, The Great Gatsby gives us a historically inadequate, even inaccurate, portrait of New York City in the early 1920s. Because Fitzgerald is known for his scrupulous attention to the cultural details of setting, this “oversight” raises questions about the author’s own racial politics.

我认为，非裔美国批评最重要的成果之一，在于它有可能将边缘化的美国作家的作品带入大众视野。我希望，通过对菲茨杰拉德小说的解读，并着重探讨色彩运用，从而达到反种族主义的目的。这种解读不仅体现在对种族主义刻板印象或主题的运用上，也体现在对场景的操控上。后一种手法往往更为微妙，有时也更难言表，因此通常对学术界的反种族主义努力构成更大的挑战。

While I believe that one of the most important products of African American criticism is its potential to bring the works of marginalized American writers of color to the fore, I hope that my interpretation of Fitzgerald’s novel serves an antiracist purpose by illustrating some of the ways in which racism can inform a literary work, not just in its use of racist stereotypes or themes, but in its manipulation of setting as well. For this latter technique is often more subtle, sometimes more difficult to articulate, and therefore usually more of a challenge to antiracist efforts in the academic community.

但哈莱姆在哪里？非裔美国人解读《了不起的盖茨比》

But where’s Harlem? An African American reading of The Great Gatsby

F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德作品的一大特色在于其对地域感的强烈描绘。作者一丝不苟地刻画了特定时代和地域的文化细节，使读者能够身临其境地感受历史的某个特定时刻。马修·J·布鲁科利指出：“伟大的小说就是伟大的社会史；菲茨杰拉德的作品已然与美国的一个十年——咆哮的二十年代——紧密相连。”（《序言》ix）。或者正如马尔科姆·布拉德伯里所说：“在二十世纪二十年代的作家中，最能清晰感受到现代美国经验的强烈情感及其所有具体而不断演变的细节的，莫过于斯科特·菲茨杰拉德。”（141）。事实上，布拉德伯里指出，

One of the hallmarks of the writing of F. Scott Fitzgerald is its strong evocation of sense of place. Through the author’s scrupulous representation of cultural details very specific to the time and locale in which he places his characters, his novels and stories offer readers the opportunity to feel that they are experiencing a particular moment in history. “Great fiction,” says Matthew J. Bruccoli, “is great social history; Fitzgerald’s work has become automatically identified with an American decade: … The Roaring Twenties” (“Preface” ix). Or as Malcolm Bradbury puts it, “The writer of the nineteen twenties who most obviously feels the intensity of modern American experience in all its specified and evolving detail is Scott Fitzgerald” (141). Indeed, Bradbury notes,

他作品的伟大之处在于，年仅二十多岁的他就能将他所处的时代人性化、内化，把握其发展脉络，捕捉到当年的流行旋律、时尚风尚和时代语调。……他以对社会细节的敏锐洞察力，追溯了时代的精神历程，以及那场盛大浮华狂欢的历史。

The great fact of his work is that he was able, as a young man in his twenties, to humanize and internalize his times, to follow out their running sequences, catching the right tunes for the year and the right fashions and tones of voice. … [W]ith a tigh[t] [attention to] social detail, he follows out the psychic history of the times, the history of the great gaudy spree.

（144）

(144)

由于菲茨杰拉德的写作具有这种标志性特点，许多人称他为“他那个时代的编年史家”（布拉德伯里 141）。

Because of this signature aspect of his writing, Fitzgerald has been dubbed by many the “chronicler … of his times” (Bradbury 141).

这种说法似乎尤其适用于他最著名的小说《了不起的盖茨比》（1925），这部小说长期以来被认为是爵士时代的代表作，而“爵士时代”一词正是菲茨杰拉德用来描述20世纪20年代的。正如我们将看到的，《了不起的盖茨比》的故事发生在1922年夏天的纽约市曼哈顿区及其附近的长岛，它对那个时代和地点的描绘如此细致入微，以至于可以说，这部小说成为了他最令人难忘的作品。然而，《了不起的盖茨比》却完全没有提及，更不用说描述哈莱姆区了。哈莱姆区位于曼哈顿，是爵士时代的主要发源地之一。当时，哈莱姆文艺复兴——这场非裔美国文学、音乐、绘画、雕塑、哲学和政治辩论等诸多创意领域的伟大运动——正在这里蓬勃发展。这里曾因夜总会吸引大批白人蜂拥而至而闻名——尤其是像《了不起的盖茨比》中的汤姆和黛西·布坎南、杰伊·盖茨比、乔丹·贝克以及叙述者尼克·卡拉威那样有钱的白人——在那里，他们可以聆听最新的爵士乐曲，结识上流人士，并畅饮私酒。在哈莱姆区，私酒的流通量与禁酒令时期美国其他繁华都市的私酒一样畅通无阻。因此，如果说菲茨杰拉德是时代的记录者，他通过对社会细节的细致刻画，唤起了人们对那个时代非凡地域感的感受，那么我们也有理由提出这样的问题：“哈莱姆究竟在哪里？”正如本文将要论证的那样， 《了不起的盖茨比》完全忽略了 20 世纪 20 年代的哈莱姆区——实际上，它几乎抹去了当时曼哈顿的非裔美国人人口——因此未能达到其设定的背景要求，尤其是菲茨杰拉德所构想的背景，这引发了人们对作者对非裔美国人态度的质疑。

This claim seems especially descriptive of his best-known novel, The Great Gatsby (1925), which long has been considered the representative American novel of the Jazz Age, a term Fitzgerald coined to describe the 1920s. For as we shall see, The Great Gatsby, which is set in the borough of Manhattan in New York City and on nearby Long Island during the summer of 1922, paints a portrait of that time and place so rich in detail that, arguably, it renders this novel his most memorable work. Yet The Great Gatsby omits all reference to, let alone description of, Harlem, which is located in Manhattan and is one of the primary places responsible for the Jazz Age. It’s the place where, at that very time, the Harlem Renaissance – that great outpouring of African American literature, music, painting, sculpture, philosophy, and political debate, among other creative enterprises – was in progress. And it’s the place that was famous for attracting white folks to its nightclubs in droves – especially white folks with money like The Great Gatsby’s Tom and Daisy Buchanan, Jay Gatsby, Jordan Baker, and narrator Nick Carraway – where they would hear the latest jazz tunes, see and be seen by the in-crowd, and drink the bootlegged liquor that flowed as freely in Harlem as it flowed in every sophisticated metropolis of Prohibition America. So if it’s reasonable to consider Fitzgerald the chronicler of his times, the writer who evoked an unusually strong sense of place through his meticulous attention to social detail, then it’s also reasonable to ask, “But where is Harlem?” As this essay will argue, in its total omission of the Harlem of the 1920s – indeed, in its virtual erasure of the African American population of Manhattan at that time – The Great Gatsby falls short of the requirements of its setting, especially as Fitzgerald conceived of setting, in a way that raises questions about the author’s attitude toward African Americans.

这部小说充满了菲茨杰拉德标志性的当代文化细节，这一点对于任何一位带着文化史视角去阅读它的人来说都显而易见。《了不起的盖茨比》通过对20世纪20年代初期重大事件和人物的提及，以及对当时日常生活的种种描绘，向我们展现了那个时代的风貌：20年代初期的时尚、流行歌曲、舞蹈、消费热潮和阅读材料；以及对20年代纽约特定地点的描写。虽然我们将用几个段落来阐述这部小说强烈的地域感——希望各位读者能够耐心读完——但请记住，我们仅仅触及了菲茨杰拉德描绘那个特定时空的无数种方式的冰山一角。

That the novel is bursting with the kind of contemporary cultural detail for which Fitzgerald is known is obvious to anyone who reads it with an eye to cultural history. Among other things, The Great Gatsby shows us the early 1920s through its references to the significant events and people of the period as well as through the glimpses it provides of the everyday world at that time: the fashions of the early twenties, references to the period’s popular songs, dances, consumer crazes, and reading materials; and descriptions of specific places in 1920s New York. Although we’ll devote several paragraphs to establishing the novel’s strong sense of place – and I hope you’ll bear with me in this effort – do keep in mind that we’ll be only scratching the surface of the innumerable ways in which Fitzgerald evokes this specific place and time.

20世纪20年代初期最明显、最普遍的时代标志或许就是禁酒令。这项1919年通过的联邦法律禁止生产和消费酒精，但当时的时尚人士却对此嗤之以鼻。事实上，违反这项法律反而成了时髦之举。禁酒令在整部小说中都随处可见。例如，小说中描绘的每场派对上都充斥着豪饮，几乎随处可见酒精；汤姆在主人公们驱车前往纽约的那个注定以默特尔·威尔逊之死告终的日子里，随身携带了一瓶“用毛巾包着”的威士忌（127页；第七章）；汤姆还透露，盖茨比和迈耶·沃尔夫希姆“在纽约和芝加哥买下了许多街边药店，直接出售谷物酒精”（141页；第七章），这在禁酒令时期是一种常见的做法。甚至在尼克提到的“通往加拿大的‘地下管道’”中，也出现了“当代传说”（103；第 6 章），即酒类以某种方式从加拿大“输送”到美国。

Perhaps the most obvious and pervasive sign of the times in the early 1920s was Prohibition, the passing of the 1919 federal law that made the production and consumption of alcohol illegal but that was treated by the fashionable set as a scoff law. Indeed, breaking this law became the fashionable thing to do. And Prohibition makes its presence known throughout the novel. We see it, for example, in the heavy drinking that occurs at every party depicted in the novel and in the availability of alcohol almost everywhere else; in the bottle of whiskey “wrapp[ed] … in a towel” (127; ch. 7) that Tom brings along when the main characters drive into New York on the fateful day that will end with Myrtle Wilson’s death; in Tom’s revelation that Gatsby and Meyer Wolfsheim “bought up a lot of side-street drug stores here and in Chicago and sold grain alcohol over the counter” (141; ch. 7), a common practice during Prohibition; and even in Nick’s mention of “the ‘underground pipe-line to Canada,’” the “[c]ontemporary legend” (103; ch. 6) that liquor was somehow being “piped in” to the United States from Canada.

20世纪20年代禁酒令时期有组织犯罪的扩张在《了不起的盖茨比》中体现得最为明显，最明显的是迈耶·沃尔夫希姆这个角色，他是臭名昭著的赌徒和敲诈勒索者阿诺德·罗斯坦的化身。当时许多人，包括盖茨比（78；第四章），都曾贿赂芝加哥白袜队故意输掉1919年世界大赛（布鲁科利，“注释”211-12页）。有组织犯罪的兴起也体现在盖茨比这个人物身上，正如我们前面提到的，他从事私酒活动；他与沃尔夫希姆这样的黑帮分子有着长期的犯罪联系（179；第九章）；以及他自己参与的出售假债券的行动（174；第九章），这在当时是一种流行的非法敛财手段，与20世纪20年代人们渴望快速致富的愿望产生了强烈的共鸣，小说中提到的石油大亨约翰·D·洛克菲勒（31；第二章）和铁路大亨詹姆斯·J·希尔（176；第九章）也反映了这种渴望。当然，有组织犯罪与暴力以及警察腐败有关，沃尔夫希姆回忆起赌徒罗西·罗森塔尔在街头意外被枪杀的事件，从中我们可以窥见这个世界的一角。这起枪击案导致四名黑帮分子被处决，或者正如沃尔夫希姆指出的那样，“五人，包括贝克尔”（75；第4章），一名腐败的纽约警察中尉，据称他下令谋杀，大概是因为罗森塔尔曾向报纸抱怨警察腐败（“查尔斯·贝克尔”）。

The expansion of organized crime that accompanied Prohibition in the 1920s is present in The Great Gatsby most obviously in the character of Meyer Wolfsheim, a stand-in for Arnold Rothstein, the notorious gambler and racketeer credited by many people at that time, as well as by Gatsby (78; ch. 4), with bribing the Chicago White Sox to throw the 1919 World Series (Bruccoli, “Explanatory Notes” 211–12). The rise of organized crime is also present in the character of Gatsby himself, through his bootlegging activities, as we saw above; in his longtime criminal connection with a gangster like Wolfsheim (179; ch. 9); and in his own operation involving the sale of fake bonds (174; ch. 9), a popular illegal moneymaker at that time and one that resonates strongly with the get-rich-quick aspirations of the 1920s, aspirations that are also recalled by the novel’s mentions of oil magnate John D. Rockefeller (31; ch. 2) and railroad tycoon James J. Hill (176; ch. 9). Organized crime, of course, is associated with violence as well as with police corruption, and we get a hint of this world in Wolfsheim’s reminiscence about the unexpected street shooting of gambler Rosy Rosenthal, for which four gangsters were executed or, as Wolfsheim points out, “Five, with Becker” (75; ch. 4), a corrupt New York police lieutenant who allegedly ordered the murder presumably because Rosenthal had complained to the newspapers about police corruption (“Charles Becker”).

同样，小说也有效地展现了第一次世界大战对20世纪20年代美国的影响。这场战争结束的时间距离《了不起的盖茨比》故事发生的1922年夏天仅仅不到四年。小说通过盖茨比的战争经历——他获得的荣誉和参与的著名战役——以及他与战争相关的经历（包括战后在英国牛津大学的短暂学习）来体现这一点（136页；第七章）。尼克在盖茨比的派对上看到的“许多年轻的英国人”也体现了这场当时被称为“大战”的战争的影响，“他们看起来都有些饥肠辘辘，都用低沉而认真的声音与那些富裕稳重的美国人交谈……他们都在兜售某种东西……他们痛苦地意识到附近唾手可得的钱，并坚信只要说几句得体的话，就能得到它”（46页；第三章）。这段文字提醒我们，英国和欧洲在战争期间遭受了巨大的经济破坏，盖茨比购买的“一座哥特式风格的图书馆，镶着雕刻精美的英国橡木，很可能是从海外某个废墟中完整运来的”（49；第三章）也印证了这一点。在20世纪20年代，富有的美国人利用战后海外的经济形势购买原本无法出售的传家宝，这并非罕见之举。最后，盖茨比的熟人对他财富来源的猜测也表明，1922年夏天，人们仍然对第一次世界大战念念不忘：例如，一位熟人认为“他是德皇威廉二世的侄子或堂兄弟”（37；第二章），威廉二世是第一次世界大战期间的德国君主。另一个说法是他是“战争期间德国最高级别军官冯·兴登堡的侄子”（65；第 4 章）；还有一个说法认为“他是战争期间的德国间谍”（48；第 3 章）。

Similarly, the effects on 1920s America of World War I, which ended less than four short years before The Great Gatsby’s summer of 1922, are effectively evoked in the novel by means of both Gatsby’s war record – the honors he accrued and the famous battles in which he fought – and his war-related experiences, including his brief attendance at England’s Oxford University after the war (136; ch. 7). The effects of the Great War, as it was then called, are also seen in the “number of young Englishmen” Nick sees at Gatsby’s parties, “all looking a little hungry and all talking in low earnest voices to solid and prosperous Americans. … They were all selling something … agonizingly aware of the easy money in the vicinity and convinced that it was theirs for a few words in the right key” (46; ch. 3). This reference reminds us of the economic devastation suffered by Great Britain and Europe during the war, as does Gatsby’s purchase of “a high Gothic library, panelled with carved English oak, and probably transported complete from some ruin overseas” (49; ch. 3). It was not an uncommon practice for wealthy Americans in the 1920s to take advantage of postwar economic conditions abroad in order to purchase heirlooms that would otherwise not have been for sale. Finally, that people are still thinking a good deal about the Great War in the summer of 1922 is also evident in the speculations of Gatsby’s acquaintances concerning the origin of his wealth: for instance, one acquaintance believes that “he’s a nephew or cousin of Kaiser Wilhelm’s” (37; ch. 2), Germany’s monarch during the Great War; another suggests that he’s “nephew to von Hindenburg” (65; ch. 4), the highest-ranking German officer during the war; and yet another thinks “he was a German spy during the war” (48; ch. 3).

虽然当下的时尚潮流在某些方面不如著名的历史事件及其背后的人物重要，但它们仍然具有重要的意义。通过展现那个时代的集体自我认知和生活态度，我们可以了解文化史的一个方面。例如，第一次世界大战后，尤其是在20世纪20年代，时髦的女性纷纷将长发剪成齐下巴、蓬松垂落的“波波头”，黛西和乔丹肯定都留着这种发型，我们在对默特尔·威尔逊的妹妹凯瑟琳的描述中也能看到，她留着“黏糊糊的红色波波头”（第2章，第34页）。在盖茨比的派对上，女人们也“以奇特的新奇方式剪了头发”（第3章，第44页）。同样，化妆在20世纪20年代也开始流行，例如，凯瑟琳使用眉笔和粉底（第2章，第34页），以及盖茨比一位醉酒的派对客人“浓密的睫毛”（第3章，第56页）上涂着睫毛膏。与往昔不同，如今的女性服饰“色彩艳丽”，设计现代，例如盖茨比派对上出现的“煤蓝色”连衣裙“缀以薰衣草色珠子”，以及“美得令人窒息的卡斯蒂利亚披肩”（44；第三章）。当然，在第一次世界大战之前，女性不会像黛西和乔丹那样佩戴“金属布料制成的小巧紧身帽”，也不会像她们那样“披在手臂上的轻薄斗篷”（127；第七章）。即使在炎热的夏夜，她们也可能需要这些，因为她们的现代服饰轻薄简洁。

Current fashions, though in some ways less important than famous historical events and the people who made them happen, nevertheless render an important aspect of cultural history by giving us a sense of the era’s collective self-perception and attitude toward life. For example, after World War I and especially with the advent of the 1920s, fashionable women cut their long hair into chin-length, loosely hanging “bobs,” which Daisy and Jordan surely wear and which we see specifically in the description of Myrtle Wilson’s sister Catherine with her “sticky bob of red hair” (34; ch. 2). At Gatsby’s parties, too, the women have “hair shorn in strange new ways” (44; ch. 3). Similarly, makeup became popular during the 1920s, and we see it, for example, in Catherine’s use of eyebrow pencil and face powder (34; ch. 2) as well as in the mascara on the “heavily beaded eyelashes” (56; ch. 3) of one of Gatsby’s inebriated party guests. Women’s clothing, unlike that of yesteryear, is “gaudy with primary colors” and modern designs, such as the “gas blue” dress “with lavender beads” and the “shawls beyond the dreams of Castile” we see at Gatsby’s parties (44; ch. 3). And certainly, before World War I women didn’t wear the “small tight hats of metallic cloth” sported by Daisy and Jordan nor the “light capes [draped] over their arms” (127; ch. 7), which they might need even on this hot summer night because their modern attire is so thin and spare.

同样，20世纪20年代初，年轻男士在需要展现“休闲优雅”的场合，夏季的时尚着装是轻薄的白色西装，被称为“白法兰绒”。尼克（第3章，第46页）和盖茨比（第5章，第89页）都穿着这种西装，他们也都戴着当时流行的草帽（第7章，第121页）。此外，盖茨比的短发（第3章，第54页）也符合一战后美国男士的新时尚。整部小说中，都没有出现战后时尚男士不再留的那种胡须——例如，浓密的络腮胡和“羊排胡”。

Analogously, the fashionable summer attire for young men on occasions requiring “casual elegance” in the early 1920s was a lightweight white suit referred to as “white flannels,” which we see on both Nick (46; ch. 3) and Gatsby (89; ch. 5), who also sport the straw hats popular during this period (121; ch. 7). In addition, Gatsby’s short hair (54; ch. 3) is in keeping with the new fashion for men in post-World War I America, and there is an accurate absence, throughout the novel, of the kinds of facial hair – for example, full beards and “mutton chops” – that were no longer worn by fashionable men after the war.

小说中提到的流行歌曲、舞蹈和消费热潮也有助于营造作品强烈的地域感，因为它们让我们感受到20世纪20年代初休闲世界的声色景象。除了小说中多次提及爵士乐（当时的流行音乐）之外，我们还能找到一些当时流行的歌曲，这些歌曲都创作于1920年至1922年间，例如《阿拉伯酋长》（第83页；第4章）、《爱巢》（第100页；第5章）、《我们玩得不开心吗？》（第101-102页；第5章）和《凌晨三点》（第115页；第6章）。盖茨比的派对上也出现了各种即兴舞蹈（45，51；第3章）——这同样是那个时代的典型特征——我们还看到盖茨比和黛西跳狐步舞（112；第6章），这是当时流行的一种舞厅舞蹈。此外，书中还提到了当时纽约流行的娱乐活动：例如，百老汇“齐格菲歌舞团”的首席舞者吉尔达·格雷（45；第3章）；著名喜剧演员兼舞蹈家乔·弗里斯科（45；第3章）；以及以逼真布景著称的百老汇制作人大卫·贝拉斯科（50；第3章）（布鲁科利，“注释”209）。

The popular songs, dances, and consumer crazes referred to in the novel also help create the work’s strong sense of place because they give us a sense of the sounds and sights of the leisure world of the early 1920s. In addition to the novel’s several references to jazz, which was the music of the decade, we find mention of specific popular songs of the period, all written in the years from 1920 to 1922: “The Sheik of Araby” (83; ch. 4), “The Love Nest” (100; ch. 5), “Ain’t We Got Fun?” (101–2; ch. 5), and “It’s Three o’clock in the Morning” (115: ch. 6). There are also various improvisational dances that occur at Gatsby’s parties (45, 51; ch. 3) – again, typical of the period – and we see Gatsby and Daisy dancing the foxtrot (112; ch. 6), a popular ballroom dance of the time. Moreover, there are references to the period’s popular New York entertainments: for example, Gilda Gray (45; ch. 3), the lead dancer at Broadway’s “Ziegfeld Follies”; Joe Frisco (45; ch. 3), a well-known comedian and dancer; and David Belasco (50; ch. 3), a Broadway producer known for his realistic sets (Bruccoli, “Explanatory Notes” 209).

小说中对时髦消费品的提及，体现了那个时代对机械化、电气化或“新式改良”事物的迷恋。他买得起这些东西：例如盖茨比的摩托艇（第3章第43页）、水上飞机（第3章第52页）、水上滑翔机（第3章第43页）以及电动榨汁机（第3章第43-44页），后者当然不如他的其他财产那样光鲜亮丽，但仍然体现了20世纪20年代的现代科技。然而，20世纪20年代初期最引人注目的消费热潮或许是汽车。

We see the period’s fascination with all things mechanized, electrified, or “new and improved” in the novel’s references to trendy consumer items, for those who could afford them: for instance, Gatsby’s motor boats (43; ch. 3), his hydroplane (52; ch. 3), his aquaplane (43; ch. 3), and his electric juicer (43–44; ch. 3), the latter of which is certainly not as glamorous as his other possessions but nevertheless indicative of the modern gadgetry of the 1920s. Perhaps the most significant consumer craze of the early 1920s, however, was the automobile.

到了20世纪20年代初，汽车已成为人人都梦寐以求的新机器。与15年前汽车还是稀罕物时的美国景象截然不同，1920年汽车随处可见，交通拥堵在美国城市也屡见不鲜（O'Meara 53）。在《了不起的盖茨比》中，除了主人公们拥有的汽车外，每当他们驾车驶入曼哈顿时，路上的汽车都会被反复提及。此外，尼克至少两次提到了交通拥堵：他写道，某个星期六晚上，盖茨比家车道上“排了五排车”（44；第三章），派对结束后，这些车堵在了路上（58；第三章）；尼克还告诉我们，他喜欢晚上八点钟沿着第五大道散步，那时“四十街昏暗的小巷里挤满了五排疾驰而去的出租车，都开往剧院区”（62；第三章）。事实上，在前往曼哈顿的途中，载着盖茨比、黛西、汤姆、尼克和乔丹的两辆车甚至都无法并排停下进行短暂的交谈，因为“后面（卡车）传来一声咒骂的口哨声”（132；第七章）。毫无疑问，现代社会已经到来。

By the early 1920s, the automobile had become the new machine that everyone wanted. Unlike the American landscape of just 15 years earlier, in which cars were an oddity, in 1920 cars could be seen everywhere, and traffic jams were not uncommon in American cities (O’Meara 53). In The Great Gatsby, in addition to the autos owned by the main characters, cars on the road are routinely mentioned whenever the characters drive into Manhattan. Moreover, Nick mentions traffic jams at least twice: he reports that the cars “parked five deep” (44: ch. 3) in Gatsby’s driveway one Saturday evening become tied up in a traffic jam when the party is over (58; ch. 3), and Nick tells us that he likes to walk up 5th Avenue at eight o’clock in the evening when “the dark lanes of the Forties [are] five deep with throbbing taxi cabs, bound for the theatre district” (62; ch. 3). Indeed, on their way to Manhattan, the two cars carrying Gatsby, Daisy, Tom, Nick, and Jordan can’t even pull up side by side for a brief exchange of words without “a cursing whistle [from a truck] behind [them]” (132; ch. 7). No doubt, modern times have arrived.

尽管《了不起的盖茨比》中提到的阅读材料并不多，但它们对小说营造地域氛围至关重要，因为它们让我们得以窥见当时许多美国人普遍持有的观念。例如，汤姆提及戈达德的《有色帝国的崛起》 ，这与西奥多·洛思罗普·斯托达德的《有色浪潮》（1920）中的观点遥相呼应，反映了20世纪20年代一种广为流传的观点，即“占主导地位的‘北欧’种族正受到与‘劣等’种族通婚的威胁”（吉德利 173）。事实上，小说中也提到了《星期六晚邮报》 （第22页；第1章），它是当时美国最受欢迎的杂志。该杂志从1920年开始推荐麦迪逊·格兰特1916年出版的一本类似种族主义书籍《伟大种族的消亡》（吉德利，173页）。实际上，北欧主义——即认为美国是由“北欧人种”建立和发展起来的，而这种“优越”种族与其他种族的“杂交”会导致“北欧人种”的消失（德克尔，122页）——在20世纪20年代初非常流行，以至于1924年通过了一项限制性移民法案，并得到了柯立芝总统的支持。柯立芝总统声称“美国必须保持美国特色”（引自德克尔，123页）。

Although the reading materials mentioned in The Great Gatsby are not numerous, they are significant in terms of their contribution to the novel’s sense of place, for they offer us a glimpse of the beliefs that were prevalent among many Americans at that time. For example, Tom’s reference to The Rise of the Coloured Empires by Goddard, which echoes the sentiments of The Rising Tide of Color (1920) by Theodore Lothrop Stoddard, bespeaks an opinion widely held in the 1920s that “the dominant ‘Nordic’ race was being threatened by the intermarriage … with persons of ‘inferior’ races” (Gidley 173). Indeed, The Saturday Evening Post, which is also mentioned in the novel (22; ch. 1) and which was the most popular magazine in the United States at that time, began in 1920 to recommend the ideas of a similarly racist book Madison Grant published in 1916 entitled The Passing of the Great Race (Gidley 173). In fact, the popularity of Nordicism – the belief that the United States was founded and developed by the “Nordic race” and that the “crossbreeding” of this “superior” race with other races would result in the disappearance of the “Nordic race” (Decker 122) – was so widespread in the early 1920s that a restrictive Immigration Bill was passed in 1924 and supported by President Coolidge, who said that “America must be kept American” (cited in Decker 123).

文中提及了当时颇受欢迎的纽约报纸，如《论坛报》（第42页；第2章）——据推测是指《纽约论坛报》或《纽约先驱论坛报》（后者于1922年被后者收购，参见“纽约先驱论坛报”）——以及《日报》（第89页；第5章），据推测是指《纽约美国日报》，此外还有《城镇闲谈》等类似报纸。“百老汇丑闻杂志”（31；第二章）也为小说营造地域氛围做出了贡献：这些报纸和杂志在纽约出版，专门刊登纽约人可能感兴趣的新闻。小说对罗伯特·基布尔的《西蒙，又名彼得》（1921）的引用也具有类似的意义，这部小说在当时非常流行。它的情节讲述的是“一位军队牧师卷入了一系列激情事件”（布鲁科利，“注释”209），这个主题显然与20世纪20年代人们追求纸醉金迷、打破一切旧规则的生活方式不谋而合。

Mention of the popular New York newspapers of the day, the Tribune (42; ch. 2) – presumably the New York Tribune or the New York Herald Tribune, which absorbed the former in 1922 (see “New York Herald Tribune”) – and the Journal (89; ch. 5), presumably the New York Journal American, as well as Town Tattle and similar “scandal magazines of Broadway” (31; ch. 2), also contribute to the novel’s evocation of place: these are newspapers and magazines published in New York with an eye to news likely to be of interest to New Yorkers. An analogous claim can be made for the novel’s reference to Robert Keable’s Simon Called Peter (1921), a popular novel of the day. Its plot concerns “an army chaplain who becomes involved in passionate episodes” (Bruccoli, “Explanatory Notes” 209), a subject that clearly resonates with the 1920s reputation for living life in the fast lane and breaking all the old rules.

最后，小说中提到的地点往往位置非常具体，至少在1922年，我们只需一本《了不起的盖茨比》就能找到它们。举几个例子来说，小说中提到广场酒店正对着“中央公园南侧”（第7章，132页），电影明星——当时纽约拍了很多电影——住在“西五十街的高层公寓里”（第4章，83页），我们可以去“五十街附近”的“大型”电影院看电影（第7章，132页），老默里山酒店位于麦迪逊大道，步行即可到达曼哈顿下城的金融区，宾夕法尼亚车站则位于西三十三街（第3章，61页）。如果我们能找到一位会员做我们的担保人，我们就可以去耶鲁俱乐部参观，尼克通常在那里吃晚饭，还可以去看看它的图书馆，图书馆仍然位于二楼，尼克晚饭后会在那里“研究投资和证券”（61；第三章）。我们还会了解到，我们可以从长岛的大颈（西卵）或曼哈塞特颈（东卵）穿过皇后区大桥到达曼哈顿（73；第四章）。我们也会认出尼克从桥上看到的城市景色——建筑物“像白色的小山和糖块一样拔地而起”（73；第四章）——因为这些建筑物确实有“白色和浅色的……装饰”（奥米拉 58）。事实上，在我们从长岛前往皇后区大桥的途中，我们甚至做好了经过科罗纳垃圾场的准备，那里景象令人作呕，气味难闻。小说中称之为“灰烬谷”（27；第二章），那里“宛如一片沼泽……堆满了灰烬、垃圾和粪便”（布鲁科利，“注释” 208）。正如我之前提到的，这里提到的文化细节仅仅是《了不起的盖茨比》对20世纪20年代曼哈顿的描绘中的一小部分，而小说的主人公们对这座城市可谓十分熟悉。

Finally, places mentioned in the novel are often so specifically located that we could probably find our way to them, in 1922 at least, with just a copy of The Great Gatsby as our guide. To cite just a few of the novel’s many examples, we learn that the Plaza Hotel fronts “the south side of Central Park” (132; ch. 7), that movie stars – many movies were made in New York in those days – lived in “tall apartments … in the West Fifties” (83; ch. 4), that we can go to a movie in one of the “big” movie theaters “around Fiftieth Street” (132; ch. 7), that the old Murray Hill Hotel is located on Madison Avenue within walking distance from the financial district in lower Manhattan, and that Pennsylvania Station is on West Thirty-third Street (61; ch. 3). And if we can get a member to sponsor us, we can visit the Yale Club, where Nick usually eats dinner, and see its library, which is still located on the second floor, where Nick “studied investments and securities” after his evening meal (61; ch. 3). We also learn that we can get from Great Neck (West Egg) or Manhasset Neck (East Egg), Long Island, to Manhattan by crossing the Queensboro Bridge (73; ch. 4). And we’d recognize the view of the city, as Nick describes it from that bridge – buildings “rising up … in white heaps and sugar lumps” (73; ch. 4) – because the buildings actually had “[w]hite and light … finishes” (O’Meara 58). Indeed, on our way from Long Island to the Queensboro Bridge, we’re even prepared to pass by the unpleasant sights and smells of the Corona dump, known in the novel as the “valley of ashes” (27; ch. 2), which was “a swamp … being filled with ashes, garbage, and manure” (Bruccoli, “Explanatory Notes” 208). As I mentioned earlier, the cultural details noted here are but a small sampling of The Great Gatsby’s evocation of 1920s Manhattan, a city with which the novel’s main characters are well acquainted.

事实上，曼哈顿只是纽约市五个行政区之一（其他四个分别是皇后区、布朗克斯区、布鲁克林区和斯塔滕岛），但《了不起的盖茨比》中的人物像我们今天一样，称曼哈顿为纽约市、纽约、这座城市，甚至只是“镇”。他们知道，曼哈顿既是娱乐休闲的好去处，也是经商的理想之地。早在第15页（第一章），当乔丹抱怨自己一下午都躺在沙发上时，黛西回应道：“别看我……我一下午都在想办法带你去纽约。”尼克当然在纽约工作，但他的大部分休闲时间也都花在那里，下班后在耶鲁俱乐部用餐，晚餐后在曼哈顿下城漫步（第61页；第三章），以及“小跑”。书中写道：“和乔丹一起四处游玩”（107；第6章）。我们甚至看到这对情侣乘坐马车穿过曼哈顿中央公园（83；第4章），这种马车类似于如今情侣们在公园里乘坐的马车。住在皇后区的默特尔经常去纽约探望姐姐，她正是在去纽约的火车上第一次遇到了汤姆（40；第2章）。汤姆在曼哈顿西158街租了一间公寓，用来与默特尔幽会（32；第2章），这意味着他们的出租车必须经过哈莱姆区，甚至穿过哈莱姆区才能到达目的地。此外，书中还提到，他经常带情妇去城里的“热门餐厅”，这让他的“熟人”看到他们时非常恼火（28；第2章）。显然，汤姆在曼哈顿待的时间很长。尼克和盖茨比甚至在……他们相约在位于四十二街的一家餐厅共进午餐，尼克正是在那里结识了迈耶·沃尔夫希姆（73页；第四章）。盖茨比也确实为了与沃尔夫希姆会面而前往纽约。此外，小说中的关键事件之一——汤姆与盖茨比的对峙——就发生在曼哈顿的广场酒店（132页；第七章）。甚至盖茨比的大部分宴会宾客（44页；第三章），以及用来装饰开胃菜和饮品的“成箱的橘子和柠檬”（43页；第三章），也都来自纽约。

Although in point of fact, Manhattan is just one of five boroughs of New York City (the others are Queens, the Bronx, Brooklyn, and Staten Island), The Great Gatsby’s characters refer to Manhattan, just as we do today, as New York City, New York, the city, or even just town. And they know that it’s the place to go for fun as well as to conduct business. As early as page 15 (ch. 1), Daisy responds to Jordan’s complaint about lying on the sofa all afternoon by saying, “Don’t look at me. … I’ve been trying to get you to New York all afternoon.” Nick works in New York, of course, but he also spends much of his leisure time there, dining at the Yale Club after work, walking around lower Manhattan after dinner (61; ch. 3), and “trotting around with Jordan” (107; ch. 6). We even see the couple driving through Manhattan’s Central Park in a horse-drawn Victoria (83; ch. 4), a vehicle similar to the horsedrawn hansom cabs in which twosomes tour the park today. Myrtle, who lives in the borough of Queens, often visits her sister in New York, and it was on the train to New York that she first met Tom (40; ch. 2). West 158th Street in Manhattan is the location of the apartment Tom keeps for his trysts with Myrtle (32; ch. 2), which means that their taxi has to pass right by Harlem, if not pass through it, to get to their destination. Moreover, we’re told that he frequently takes his mistress to “popular restaurants” in the city, to the chagrin of his “acquaintances” who see them there (28; ch. 2). Clearly, Tom spends a good deal of time in Manhattan. Nick and Gatsby even run into him in the Forty-second Street restaurant where they meet for lunch and where Nick is introduced to Meyer Wolfsheim (73; ch. 4). And certainly Gatsby visits New York City to meet with Wolfsheim. In addition, the confrontation scene between Tom and Gatsby, one of the novel’s pivotal events, occurs in the Plaza Hotel in Manhattan (132; ch. 7). Even most of Gatsby’s party guests (44; ch. 3), as well as the “crates of oranges and lemons” (43; ch. 3) that garnish their hors d’oeuvres and drinks, come from New York.

那么，叙述者尼克·卡拉威和他的朋友们怎么会错过哈莱姆区呢？哈莱姆区的夜总会曾云集了尤比·布雷克、法茨·沃勒、路易斯·阿姆斯特朗、贝西·史密斯、杜克·艾灵顿和卡布·卡洛威等爵士乐巨匠（刘易斯 91、120、183、210），吸引了来自纽约市内外的白人。像巴伦小萨沃伊夜总会、道格拉斯俱乐部（刘易斯 28）、康妮客栈（斯托瓦尔 29）和专属俱乐部（斯托瓦尔 44）等夜总会，其顾客中不乏“白人名媛、社交名流、政客和表演者”（斯托瓦尔 29）。哈莱姆区的剧院也曾汇聚了保罗·罗伯逊、埃塞尔·沃特斯和比尔·“博扬格尔斯”·罗宾逊等老牌演员（刘易斯 120）。正如杰维斯·安德森所说，“哈莱姆区是曼哈顿的欢乐和娱乐中心……整个纽约市没有比这里更热闹的地方了，尤其是在夜幕降临之后。每晚，成千上万的白人游客——大部分来自市中心，一些来自美国其他地区，还有一些来自国外城市——涌向哈莱姆区”（139）。据大卫·莱弗林·刘易斯报道，在熙熙攘攘的普通民众和富裕白人中，不乏一些名人，包括当时的知名人士，例如约翰和埃塞尔·巴里摩尔夫妇、查理·卓别林（105-106）、著名作曲家莫里斯·拉威尔（173）、乔治·格什温（183）、吉米·杜兰特、琼·克劳馥、本尼·古德曼、乐队指挥汤米和吉米·多尔西兄弟、未来的纽约市长菲奥雷洛·拉瓜迪亚、梅·韦斯特、塔卢拉·班克黑德和艾米莉·范德比尔特（209）。

How, then, can narrator Nick Carraway and his friends have missed Harlem? Harlem’s nightclubs, which offered such jazz greats as Eubie Blake, Fats Waller, Louis Armstrong, Bessie Smith, Duke Ellington, and Cab Calloway (Lewis 91, 120, 183, 210), attracted white people from all over the city and beyond. Nightspots like Barron’s Little Savoy, the Douglass Club (Lewis 28), Connie’s Inn (Stovall 29), and the Exclusive Club (Stovall 44), among others, could boast among their clientele “white debutantes, socialites, politicians, [and] performers” (Stovall 29). And Harlem’s theaters offered the talents of such time-honored actors as Paul Robeson, Ethel Waters, and Bill “Bojangles” Robinson (Lewis 120). As Jervis Anderson puts it, “Harlem was Manhattan’s capital of gaiety and amusement. … [T]here was no livelier place in all of New York City, especially after dark. Nightly, thousands of white visitors – most from downtown, some from other parts of the country, a few from cities abroad – made their way to Harlem” (139). Among the throngs of ordinary folk and wealthy whites who visited Harlem’s nightspots, David Levering Lewis reports, were the very famous, including such notables of the period as John and Ethel Barrymore, Charlie Chaplin (105–6), the famous composer Maurice Ravel (173), George Gershwin (183), Jimmy Durante, Joan Crawford, Benny Goodman, bandleaders Tommy and Jimmy Dorsey, future mayor of New York Fiorello LaGuardia, Mae West, Tallulah Bankhead, and Emily Vanderbilt (209).

事实上，当非裔美国人音乐喜剧《Shuffle Along》首演时，它席卷了整个纽约市。这部剧完全由黑人创作、制作和演出，在长期闲置的六十三街剧院上演，对于百老汇的观众来说，这个剧院的位置相当偏北。然而，“短短几周内，《Shuffle Along》就风靡了六十三街剧院。”该剧院是城里最著名的剧院之一，以至于交通部门不得不将第六十三街改为单行道来疏导交通（Johnson 188）。这部音乐喜剧于1921年夏天首演，连续上演两年后开始巡演。这意味着它在1922年夏天仍在上演，而尼克·卡拉威当时住在长岛，大部分时间都待在纽约。尽管这是一场“打破纪录、划时代”的演出，超越了当时纽约所有其他戏剧——事实上，“它的一些曲调……传遍了世界”（Johnson 186）——但在《了不起的盖茨比》中却只字未提。

In fact, when the African American musical comedy Shuffle Along opened, it took all of New York City by storm. Written, produced, and performed exclusively by black people, the show appeared in the long unused Sixty-third Street Theatre, which was considered rather far uptown for Broadway audiences to attend. Nevertheless, “[w]ithin a few weeks Shuffle Along made the Sixty-third Street Theatre one of the best-known houses in town and made it necessary for the Traffic Department to declare Sixty-third Street a one-way thoroughfare” to handle the traffic (Johnson 188). The musical comedy opened in the summer of 1921 and ran for two years before going on the road. This means that it was running in the summer of 1922, when Nick Carraway was living on Long Island and spending most of his time in New York. Although it was a “record-breaking, epoch-making” show that eclipsed all other New York theatricals at that time – in fact, “some of its tunes … went round the world” (Johnson 186) – there is no mention of it in The Great Gatsby.

纽约的白人居民无需依赖口口相传就能了解哈莱姆区正在发生的事情，尽管口口相传的传播也十分活跃。他们可以从《每日新闻》、《纽约世界报》、《纽约时报》和《综艺》等主流报纸上了解相关信息（Lewis 22, 61, 73）。白人文学界，包括白人出版商，对哈莱姆区的文学创作表现出浓厚的兴趣。鼓励哈莱姆区黑人文人的著名白人作家包括赛珍珠、多萝西·帕克、辛克莱·刘易斯、舍伍德·安德森、哈特·克莱恩和尤金·奥尼尔（Lewis 98–99）。在当时被称为“新黑人运动”的哈莱姆文艺复兴时期，涌现出许多吸引白人关注的伟大作家，例如克劳德·麦凯、让·图默、兰斯顿·休斯、康蒂·卡伦、杰西·福塞特、詹姆斯·韦尔登·约翰逊、阿纳·邦坦普斯和佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿。事实上，当菲茨杰拉德在 1923 年开始计划和创作《了不起的盖茨比》时，让·图默的小说《甘蔗》出版后获得了“杰出的”评论界反响，包括著名白人评论家艾伦·泰特和剧作家尤金·奥尼尔的高度赞扬（刘易斯 70），康蒂·卡伦还接受了纽约首屈一指的主流报纸《纽约时报》的采访（刘易斯 77）。

The white population of New York didn’t have to depend on word of mouth to know what was transpiring in Harlem, though word of mouth was certainly active. They could read about it in such mainstream newspapers as the Daily News, The New York World, The New York Times, and Variety (Lewis 22, 61, 73). And the white literary world, including white publishers, took great interest in the literary creations of Harlem. Among the noteworthy white writers who encouraged the black literati of Harlem were Pearl Buck, Dorothy Parker, Sinclair Lewis, Sherwood Anderson, Hart Crane, and Eugene O’Neill (Lewis 98–99). Among the great writers of the Harlem Renaissance – referred to at the time as the New Negro Movement – who attracted white attention were Claude McKay, Jean Toomer, Langston Hughes, Countee Cullen, Jesse Fauset, James Weldon Johnson, Arna Bontemps, and Zora Neale Hurston. In fact, while Fitzgerald was in the initial stages of planning and writing The Great Gatsby in 1923, Jean Toomer’s novel Cane was released to “outstanding” critical response, including high praise by renowned white critic Allen Tate and playwright Eugene O’Neill (Lewis 70), and Countee Cullen was interviewed in New York’s premier mainstream newspaper The New York Times (Lewis 77).

尽管哈莱姆区在曼哈顿面积相对较小，但它实际上是一座城中之城，和其他城市一样，它也存在就业不足的贫困人口，尤其是在人口增长之后（Anderson 139）。20世纪20年代初，哈莱姆区面积“不足两平方英里”，却居住着“超过20万”的黑人人口（Johnson 147）。然而，哈莱姆区位于中央公园北端，“地处曼哈顿中心”，20世纪20年代的哈莱姆区“并非边缘地带，……也并非贫民窟，更不是由破旧公寓楼组成的‘街区’。它拥有……公寓楼和漂亮的住宅，街道铺设良好、照明充足、维护得当，与城市其他任何地方一样”（Johnson 146）。在哈莱姆区，无论白天黑夜，都能看到来自文学、戏剧和学术界的著名人物，无论黑人还是白人，在街头漫步或发表公开演讲，例如约翰·杜威在哈莱姆基督教青年会发表的演讲（Lewis 104）。

Although Harlem was a relatively small section of Manhattan, it was really a city within a city, and like any other city it had its underemployed poor, especially as its population increased (Anderson 139). “[L]ess than two square miles” in size during the early 1920s, it was home to a black population that numbered “more than two hundred thousand” (Johnson 147). However, situated at the north end of Central Park, “in the heart of Manhattan,” 1920s Harlem was “not a fringe, … not a slum, nor [was] it a ‘quarter’ consisting of dilapidated tenements. It [was] a section of … apartment houses and handsome dwellings, with streets as well paved, as well lighted, and as well kept as in any other part of the city” (Johnson 146). Celebrated people, black and white, from the world of literature, theater, and academia could be seen at any time of the day or night strolling the streets of Harlem or giving public lectures, such as that given by John Dewey at the Harlem YMCA (Lewis 104).

哈莱姆区甚至拥有自己的报纸和杂志，包括《危机》（Crisis）、《火！》（Fire!）、《信使》（Messenger）（道格拉斯 312-13）和《机遇》（ Opportunity）（刘易斯 120）。哈莱姆区也涌现出许多著名的黑人艺术家、作家、音乐家和演员，其中包括画家罗玛尔·哈莱姆。比尔登、亚伦·道格拉斯和劳拉·惠勒·沃林，以及雕塑家萨金特·约翰逊、伊丽莎白·普罗菲特和奥古斯塔·萨维奇。为了让您了解哈莱姆文艺复兴时期艺术家们的创作力，即使就画家和雕塑家而言（这一群体往往不如作家和表演艺术家那样受到关注），到20世纪80年代末，已有超过一百位哈莱姆画家和雕塑家参加年度比赛和展览（Lewis 261–62）。

Harlem even had its own newspapers and magazines, including Crisis, Fire!, Messenger (Douglas 312–13), and Opportunity (Lewis 120). And Harlem boasted famous black artists as well as writers, musicians, and actors, including painters Romare Bearden, Aaron Douglas, and Laura Wheeler Waring and sculptors Sargent Johnson, Elizabeth Prophet, and Augusta Savage. Just to give you an idea of how productive the Harlem Renaissance was, even in terms of its painters and sculptors (a category that has tended to receive less attention than that of writers and performing artists), by the end of the decade over one hundred Harlem painters and sculptors were entering their works in annual contests and exhibitions (Lewis 261–62).

正如我们所见，哈莱姆文艺复兴的艺术成就早已为纽约白人乃至整个西方世界所熟知。那么，像尼克·卡拉威这样一位耶鲁大学毕业生——受过良好教育、敏感、好奇，而且正如他自己所说“颇具文学气质”（8；第一章）——怎么可能对哈莱姆的存在一无所知呢？即便尼克真的忽略了哈莱姆“高雅”文化的辉煌成就——包括文学、哲学和政治著作、绘画、雕塑等等——他也不可能在纽约工作和生活却对哈莱姆的夜生活一无所知。从历史角度来看，这种疏忽几乎是不可能的。如果菲茨杰拉德在描述文化现实时保持一贯的风格，尼克和他的朋友们肯定会去过哈莱姆的夜总会，或者至少会提到去过。他肯定会在他们众多的纽约约会中带乔丹去那里。汤姆和黛西自诩为时髦现代的潮人，他们不可能错过哈莱姆区。事实上，尼克告诉我们，布坎南夫妇“总是心不在焉地四处游荡，哪里有打马球、哪里有钱人聚在一起就去哪里”（10；第一章）。如果汤姆和黛西像当时其他富裕的白人一样，去那些“富人聚集地”消遣，那么他们应该经常光顾哈莱姆区的夜总会。他们至少会去那些最昂贵、最高档的夜总会，比如巴伦小萨沃伊酒吧和康妮旅馆，这些地方专门服务于白人顾客（刘易斯 106）。正如泰勒·斯托瓦尔所说，“在（20世纪20年代），富裕显赫的纽约白人习惯在哈莱姆区众多地下酒吧之一听爵士乐，以此结束一天的夜生活”（29）。5

The creative output of the Harlem Renaissance was, as we have seen, well known to white New Yorkers and to the Western world at large. So how can a Yale graduate like Nick Carraway – well-educated, sensitive, curious, and, as he tells us, “rather literary” (8; ch. 1) – be completely oblivious to the existence of Harlem? Even if Nick somehow overlooks the celebrated outpouring of Harlem’s “high” culture – its literature, philosophical and political writing, painting, sculpture, and the like – he certainly can’t work and play in New York City without knowing about Harlem’s nightlife. From a historical perspective, such an oversight is virtually impossible. Had Fitzgerald remained true to form in his description of cultural reality, Nick and his friends would have visited, or at least mentioned having visited, a Harlem nightclub. Surely, he would have taken Jordan there on one of their numerous New York dates. And there’s no way that Tom and Daisy, who consider themselves so fashionably modern, would have missed Harlem. Indeed, Nick tells us that the Buchanans “drifted here and there unrestfully wherever people played polo and were rich together” (10; ch. 1). If Tom and Daisy go where other wealthy whites of the period go to be “rich together,” they would have visited Harlem nightspots on a fairly regular basis. They at least would have gone to the most expensive and exclusive nightspots, like Barron’s Little Savoy and Connie’s Inn, which catered to a segregated white clientele (Lewis 106). As Tyler Stovall puts it, “During [the 1920s] it became the custom for wealthy and prominent white New Yorkers to finish up an evening on the town listening to jazz in one of Harlem’s many speakeasies” (29).5

此外，20世纪20年代居住在哈莱姆区的庞大非裔美国人群体并非仅限于该街区。事实上，来自哈莱姆区以及纽约其他地区的非裔美国人在曼哈顿各地工作、娱乐和购物。然而，小说中唯一对非裔美国人的生动描写出现在盖茨比和尼克驱车前往纽约市吃午饭的途中。尼克看到“三个时髦的黑人”坐在“一辆由白人司机驾驶的豪华轿车”里（73页；第四章）。他形容他们是“两个美元加一个姑娘”，并说道：“我大笑起来，因为他们的眼珠子带着傲慢的竞争朝我们滚过来”（73页；第四章）。6当然，尼克对这些人物的反应中，他毫不掩饰的种族主义显而易见：黑人是“buck”——动物而不是人——对他们睁大眼睛、翻白眼的描述，强烈地呼应了将非裔美国人描绘成愚蠢、幼稚、过分戏剧化、滑稽人物的种族主义刻板印象。

The enormous population of African Americans inhabiting Harlem in the 1920s, moreover, was not confined to that neighborhood. In fact, African Americans from Harlem and from elsewhere in New York worked, played, and shopped all over Manhattan. Yet the only vivid representation of African Americans in the novel occurs when Gatsby and Nick are driving into New York City to have lunch. Nick sees “three modish [fashionable] Negroes” in “a limousine … driven by a white chauffeur” (73; ch. 4). He describes them as “two bucks and a girl” and says, “I laughed aloud as the yolks of their eyeballs rolled toward us in haughty rivalry” (73; ch. 4).6 Of course, Nick’s unselfconscious racism is obvious in his reaction to these characters: the black men are “bucks” – animals rather than men – and the description of their wide-stretched, rolling eyes resonates strongly with racist stereotypes that portrayed African Americans as foolish, childish, overly dramatic, comic characters.

此外，尼克对这些人物的描述，也体现了托妮·莫里森在其对美国白人文学中非洲裔形象的分析中所阐述的那种叙事功能。这些黑人人物——衣着时髦，乘坐豪华轿车，非常在意自己在他人眼中的社会地位——是盖茨比的镜像和影子。他们之间唯一明显的区别在于，盖茨比可以隐藏自己的出身，而他们却无法做到，因为他们无法掩盖自己的肤色。在尼克看来，尽管盖茨比“言辞繁复，几乎到了荒谬的地步”（第3章，第53页），他荒谬地捏造了富有的“祖先”（第4章，第69页），他那辆被汤姆称为“马戏团篷车”（第7章，第128页）的汽车，以及他所有其他滑稽的做作，他仍然是成功的浪漫化身。然而，这些黑人人物却是对这种成功的讽刺。尼克仅用寥寥数语，仅凭对黑人角色的一笔带过，便将他（或许也包括读者）对盖茨比的一切鄙夷都投射到了他们身上。在他眼中，他们荒诞不经，而非盖茨比。因此，尼克对这些角色的种族主义态度，使他们沦为替罪羊，成为尼克乃至整部小说重塑盖茨比形象的牺牲品。换言之，这部小说抹杀了真实的非裔美国人——他们在20世纪20年代的纽约市曾是举足轻重的存在，而小说的大部分情节也正是发生在那里——取而代之的是一种强化白人优越感的滑稽刻板印象。考虑到20世纪20年代纽约市的真实历史，这绝非小事。

In addition, Nick’s description of these characters fulfills the kind of narrative function Toni Morrison describes in her analysis of the Africanist presence in white American literature. These black characters – fashionably dressed, riding in a chauffeured limousine, very conscious of their social status in the eyes of others – are the mirror and shadow of Gatsby. The only obvious difference between them is that Gatsby can hide his origins, which he does, whereas they can’t because they can’t hide their color. From Nick’s point of view, despite Gatsby’s “elaborate formality of speech [that] just missed being absurd” (53; ch. 3), his ridiculous fabrication of wealthy “ancestors” (69; ch. 4), his “circus wagon” (128; ch. 7) of a car, as Tom calls it, and all his other ludicrous affectations, he is the romantic embodiment of success. The black characters, however, are its parody. In barely more than one sentence, in the single image with which Nick describes the black characters, he projects onto them everything about Gatsby that he, and perhaps the reader, hold in contempt. They are preposterous, not Gatsby. Thus, Nick’s racist attitude toward these characters facilitates their function as scapegoats sacrificed to Nick’s, and the text’s, recuperation of Gatsby. To put the matter another way, the novel erases real African Americans, who were a very visible and important presence in New York City during the 1920s where, as we have seen, much of the novel is set, and substitutes in their place a comic stereotype that reinforces white superiority. This is no small move, given the historical reality of New York City during the 1920s.

显然，菲茨杰拉德不仅决定将非裔美国人从他对爵士时代的描绘中抹去，而且还决定将爵士乐从发明它的非裔美国人手中夺走。因为小说象征性地将爵士乐的功劳归于白人。我们看到的唯一演奏爵士乐的乐手是盖茨比派对上的白人乐手。尼克告诉我们，他们“可不是那种五人小乐队，而是一个庞大的乐队，里面有双簧管、长号、萨克斯管、维奥尔琴、短号、短笛以及各种高低音鼓”（44；第三章）。换句话说，爵士乐被“提升”到了管弦乐队这种高雅文化的层面，而高雅文化属于白人，而不是黑人。值得注意的是，管弦乐队重点演奏了一首曾在卡内基音乐厅演出过的曲目，指挥告诉我们，这首曲子是《弗拉基米尔·托斯托夫的世界爵士乐史》（54；第三章）。菲茨杰拉德还能找到比弗拉基米尔·托斯托夫更显眼的欧洲——也就是白人——名字吗？读者绝不会把他误认为是非裔美国人。在这部小说的世界里，爵士乐至少在象征意义上是欧洲人的发明。因此，汤姆警告说：“我们这些占主导地位的种族必须小心，否则其他种族就会掌控一切”（17；第一章），尽管尼克嘲笑他，小说中对汤姆的刻画也颇具讽刺意味，但小说本身却无意识地持有这种态度。

Apparently, Fitzgerald decided not only to remove African Americans from his representation of the Jazz Age, but he also decided to remove jazz from the hands of the African Americans who invented it. For the novel gives the credit for jazz symbolically to whites. The only musicians we see playing jazz are the white musicians at Gatsby’s party. And they are “no thin five-piece affair,” Nick tells us, “but a whole pit full of oboes and trombones and saxophones and viols and cornets and piccolos and low and high drums” (44; ch. 3). In other words, jazz has been “elevated” to the status of high culture in the form of an orchestra, and high culture belongs to white, not black, Americans. Significantly, the orchestra spotlights its performance of a piece that, the conductor informs us, was played at Carnegie Hall: “Vladimir Tostoff’s Jazz History of the World” (54; ch. 3). Could Fitzgerald have found a more conspicuously European – that is, white – name than Vladimir Tostoff? There’s no way a reader could mistake him for an African American. In the world of this novel, jazz is, symbolically at least, a European invention. Thus, Tom’s warning that “[i]t’s up to us who are the dominant race to watch out or these other races will have control of things” (17; ch. 1), though mocked by Nick and by the novel’s unflattering characterization of Tom, is an attitude the novel unconsciously shares.

一位以精准描绘场景而闻名的作家，为何会犯下如此明显的疏漏？诚然，正如劳拉莉·奥米拉所指出的，菲茨杰拉德本人对曼哈顿及其所有“非凡之处”都非常熟悉。多样性”（34）。斯科特·菲茨杰拉德和泽尔达·菲茨杰拉德于1920年4月在纽约市结婚，婚后第一个月住在纽约市的比尔特莫尔酒店和科莫多尔酒店。虽然接下来的几个月他们住在康涅狄格州的韦斯特波特，但曼哈顿距离他们只有50英里，他们经常去那里玩乐。1920年10月，他们搬回纽约市，住在西五十九街的一间公寓里，直到1921年夏天前往欧洲。但到了1922年，他们又回到了曼哈顿。虽然这对夫妇从1922年10月到1924年4月住在长岛的大颈，但他们经常去纽约市参加聚会（奥米拉 33-34）。事实上，从他们在长岛的家到纽约太近、太有吸引力了，这就是为什么他们在1924年4月再次前往法国的原因（奥米拉 50）。

What could be responsible for such a glaring omission on the part of an author known for his accurate renditions of setting? Certainly, as Lauraleigh O’Meara notes, Fitzgerald was personally familiar with Manhattan in all its “remarkabl[e] divers[ity]” (34). Scott and Zelda Fitzgerald were married in New York City in April 1920 and spent the first month of their married life at the Biltmore and Commodore hotels in New York City. Although they spent the next several months in Westport, Connecticut, Manhattan was a mere 50 miles away, and they frequently went to the city for fun. Moving back to New York City in October 1920, they remained there, in an apartment on West Fifty-ninth Street, until they left for Europe for the summer of 1921, but by 1922 they had returned to Manhattan. Although the couple lived in Great Neck, Long Island, from October 1922 to April 1924, they often partied in New York City (O’Meara 33–34). Indeed, from their home on Long Island, New York was too nearby and too inviting, which is why they again left for France in April 1924 (O’Meara 50).

菲茨杰拉德对纽约市的了解也包括他对哈莱姆区的了解，这得益于他与白人作家、评论家兼摄影师卡尔·范·维克滕的友谊。范·维克滕对哈莱姆区着迷，并在那里颇有名气。到20世纪20年代中期，范·维克滕已成为“哈莱姆区最热情、最活跃的北欧人”（Lewis 182）。菲茨杰拉德经常参加范·维克滕在纽约西区家中举办的派对，派对上既有白人也有黑人宾客，当然也包括范·维克滕在哈莱姆区的朋友和熟人（Lewis 182-84）。事实上，菲茨杰拉德在 1922 年的小说《美丽与毁灭》中专门提到了纽约市（包括哈莱姆区）的多样性，而且众所周知，菲茨杰拉德像他的许多其他作品一样，以他的个人经历为基础创作了这部小说（O'Meara 34）。

Fitzgerald’s personal acquaintance with New York City included a personal acquaintance with Harlem as well through his friendship with white writer, critic, and photographer Carl Van Vechten. Van Vechten was fascinated by Harlem and was very well known there. By the mid 1920s, Van Vechten had become “Harlem’s most enthusiastic and ubiquitous Nordic” (Lewis 182). Fitzgerald attended Van Vechten’s parties, which were given in his own home on New York’s west side for both white and black guests, including, of course, Van Vechten’s friends and acquaintances from Harlem (Lewis 182–84). In fact, Fitzgerald refers specifically to the diversity of New York City, including Harlem, in his 1922 novel The Beautiful and Damned, and Fitzgerald is known to have based that novel, like so much of his other work, on his personal experience (O’Meara 34).

菲茨杰拉德在巴黎的时光也加深了他对哈莱姆区的了解，正如泰勒·斯托瓦尔所指出的，许多来自哈莱姆的非裔美国人在巴黎建立了一个艺术家聚居地——由非裔美国爵士乐手、作家、画家、雕塑家和运动员组成——正如菲茨杰拉德、海明威、斯坦因和其他“迷惘的一代”成员在那里建立了一个作家聚居地一样（26）。事实上，斯托瓦尔声称，“在20世纪20年代巴黎数以万计的杰出流亡者中，很少有人能比得上那些选择在巴黎定居的数百名非裔美国人对这座城市的影响”（25-26）。“在20世纪20年代的巴黎，黑人文化风靡一时”，因为“巴黎的知识分子认真对待黑人文化，认为它代表了时代的精神”（斯托瓦尔 32）。菲茨杰拉德本人想在他的小说中体现时代精神，他不可能没有注意到，1921 年的龚古尔文学奖（“法国最负盛名的文学奖”）颁给了“勒内·马兰的小说《巴图阿拉》 ……勒内·马兰是一位出生于马提尼克的法国黑人作家” (Stovall 32)。

Even the time Fitzgerald spent in Paris contributed to his awareness of Harlem because, as Tyler Stovall points out, African Americans, many of whom were from Harlem, established an expatriate artists’ colony in Paris – consisting of African American jazz musicians, writers, painters, sculptors, and athletes – just as Fitzgerald, Hemingway, Stein, and other members of the “Lost Generation” established a writers’ colony there (26). Stovall claims, in fact, that “few of the tens of thousands of illustrious exiles in Paris during the 1920s had a greater impact on the city than the hundreds of African Americans who chose to call it home in those years” (25–26). “[B]lackness became the rage in Paris during the 1920s,” for “Parisian intellectuals took black culture seriously, considering it to represent the spirit of the age” (Stovall 32). Fitzgerald, who himself wanted to represent the spirit of the age in his novels, could not have failed to notice that the 1921 Prix Goncourt for literature, “the most prestigious literary award in France” went “to the novel Batouala by René Maran … a black Frenchman … [b]orn in Martinique” (Stovall 32).

菲茨杰拉德与巴黎哈莱姆区居民的私人交往源于他频繁光顾蒙马特区的爵士俱乐部。蒙马特区位于巴黎北部，是20世纪20年代巴黎大多数非裔美国人的居住地（Stovall 39）。从某种意义上说，蒙马特区通过复制哈莱姆区的爵士俱乐部类型和使用许多相同的爵士乐手，再现了哈莱姆区的夜生活。哈莱姆区有很多音乐家。“白人美国侨民经常光顾蒙马特的夜总会”（Stovall 78），菲茨杰拉德尤其喜欢那里一位名叫布里克托普的著名非裔美国爵士歌手，她因其红头发而得名，她在美国时也曾在哈莱姆区的俱乐部演唱（Stovall 78-79）。

Fitzgerald’s personal acquaintance with Harlemites in Paris resulted from his frequent visits to jazz clubs in Montmartre, a section in the northern part of the city where most African Americans in Paris lived during the 1920s (Stovall 39). In a very real sense, Montmartre reproduced the nightlife available in Harlem by reproducing the same kind of jazz clubs and by employing many of the same jazz musicians available in Harlem. “White American expatriates frequently visited Montmartre’s nightclubs” (Stovall 78), and Fitzgerald was particularly fond of a famous African American jazz singer there called Bricktop, so named for her red hair, who also sang in Harlem clubs when she was in the United States (Stovall 78–79).

那么，一个显而易见的问题就摆在了眼前：菲茨杰拉德的爵士时代巨著《了不起的盖茨比》为何完全忽略了哈莱姆区，暗示爵士乐是白人文化的产物，并且对20世纪20年代纽约的非裔美国人的刻画也仅限于负面的“喜剧”刻板印象？换句话说，菲茨杰拉德在创作这部最著名的小说时，对非裔美国人的态度究竟如何？尽管罗伯特·福雷和艾伦·马戈利斯等人都认为，菲茨杰拉德在晚年“表现出”逐渐“摆脱”种族主义态度的迹象（福雷，296页），但显而易见的是，《了不起的盖茨比》写于菲茨杰拉德二十多岁时，在他创作生涯的早期阶段，尚未能受益于他后来观点的转变。确实有大量证据表明，《了不起的盖茨比》存在上述的遗漏和歪曲，是因为其作者有意或无意地想要从小说创作的视野中抹去那些在真实的纽约——这个在小说地域感中扮演着重要角色的城市——中如此显眼的非裔美国人。正如我们将看到的，菲茨杰拉德认为非裔美国人远逊于白人。虽然作者种族主义的心理动机并非本文的重点，但或许在他坚信自身种族优越性的背后，隐藏着一种根深蒂固的不安全感，这种不安全感源于他对非裔美国人在艺术和文学领域所取得的杰出成就的担忧，而这些成就他既在巴黎也在纽约亲眼目睹。无论原因如何，显而易见的是，菲茨杰拉德一生中的大部分时间里，他对非裔美国人的态度都带有明显的种族主义色彩。

A rather obvious question, then, seems to present itself: Why does The Great Gatsby, Fitzgerald’s great novel of the Jazz Age, omit entirely any reference to Harlem, imply that jazz was a product of white culture, and limit its only vivid representation of African Americans in 1920s New York City to a negative “comic” stereotype? In other words, what was Fitzgerald’s attitude toward African Americans while he was writing his most famous novel? Although Robert Forrey and Alan Margolies, for example, agree that Fitzgerald “show[ed] signs,” toward the end of his life, of “outgrowing” his racist attitude (Forrey 296), it seems evident that The Great Gatsby, written when the author was in his twenties, arrived too early in Fitzgerald’s career to benefit from his later change in perspective. There is, indeed, a good deal of evidence to suggest that The Great Gatsby suffers from the omissions and misrepresentations noted above because its author, consciously or unconsciously, wanted to erase from his novelistic field of vision the African Americans who so visibly populated the real New York, the New York that plays such an important role in his novel’s sense of place. As we shall see, Fitzgerald believed that African Americans were woefully inferior to whites. And although the psychological motives for the author’s racism are not the issue here, it is possible that beneath his belief in the superiority of his race lay a deep-seated insecurity about his own literary value in face of the outstanding achievements of African Americans in arts and letters, which he was witnessing in Paris as well as in New York. Whatever the reason, it is evident that Fitzgerald’s attitude toward African Americans, for the greater part of his life, was decidedly racist.

正如罗伯特·福雷所观察到的，菲茨杰拉德众多短篇小说中的黑人角色“几乎总是卑微卑微的人物，他们被贬称为‘黑鬼’、‘黑鬼’、‘小黑孩’或‘桑博’。他们的作用通常是为了制造喜剧效果”（293）。泰勒·斯托瓦尔对此表示赞同，他指出菲茨杰拉德的《夜色温柔》 ——“描写美国侨民生活的伟大长篇小说之一”——包含“臭名昭著的种族主义段落”（80）。福雷补充道，“在现实生活中，正如在小说中一样，黑人的出现通常是菲茨杰拉德开始恶作剧的信号”（294）。福雷引用安德鲁·特恩布尔1962年出版的斯科特·菲茨杰拉德传记，指出菲茨杰拉德曾有一次“把一位毫无戒心的黑人牧师介绍为来自非洲的贵宾，这位牧师当时正在为当地一家孤儿院募捐。牧师虽然礼貌，但惊慌失措，逃离了现场”（294页）。还有一次，菲茨杰拉德让他的非裔美国司机（他有口吃）一遍又一遍地重复一句他发音不准的句子（特恩布尔，引自福雷，294页）。当然，菲茨杰拉德对待非裔美国人布里克托普的态度也值得关注。正如我们前面提到的，他非常钦佩这位歌手，这很有启发性：虽然他是她作品的忠实粉丝，经常光顾她唱歌的俱乐部，但“她来到[他]家时，是以受雇音乐家的身份，而不是以朋友和平等者的身份”（Stovall 80）。

As Robert Forrey observes, the black characters in Fitzgerald’s numerous short stories “are almost always menial characters who are referred to disparagingly – sometimes by the author himself in the third person – as ‘coons,’ ‘niggers,’ ‘pickaninnies,’ or ‘Samboes.’ Their function is usually to create a comic effect” (293). Tyler Stovall concurs, observing that Fitzgerald’s Tender Is the Night, “one of the great novels of American expatriate life,” contains “notoriously racist passages about blacks” (80). And “[i]n real life, as in fiction,” Forrey adds, “the appearance of a Negro was usually the signal for Fitzgerald to promote a prank” (294). Citing Andrew Turnbull’s 1962 biography Scott Fitzgerald, Forrey notes that, on one occasion, Fitzgerald “introduced an unsuspecting Negro clergyman, soliciting funds for a local orphanage, as a distinguished visitor from Africa. Polite but panic-stricken, the clergyman fled the premises” (294). Another time, Fitzgerald made his African American chauffeur, who had a speech impediment, repeat over and over again a sentence filled with words he was unable to pronounce correctly (Turnbull, cited in Forrey 294). And certainly Fitzgerald’s attitude toward Bricktop, the African American singer whom, as we noted earlier, he greatly admired, is revealing: although he was a great fan of her work and frequented the club where she sang, “she came to [his] hom[e] as a hired musician, not as a friend and equal” (Stovall 80).

M·吉德利借鉴安德鲁·特恩布尔1963年出版的《F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德书信集》，着重分析了菲茨杰拉德写给他朋友埃德蒙·威尔逊的一封信中一段关于作者种族哲学的重要段落：

Drawing on Andrew Turnbull’s 1963 The Letters of F. Scott Fitzgerald, M. Gidley underscores a telltale passage in a letter from Fitzgerald to his friend Edmund Wilson concerning the author’s racial philosophy:

上帝诅咒欧洲大陆……黑人血统正向北蔓延，玷污北欧人种。意大利人身上已经沾染了黑人的灵魂。提高（美国的）移民门槛，只允许斯堪的纳维亚人、日耳曼人、盎格鲁-撒克逊人和凯尔特人入境。

God damn the continent of Europe. … The Negroid streak creeps northward to defile the Nordic race. Already the Italians have souls of blackamoors [black or dark-skinned people]. Raise the bars of immigration [in the United States] and permit only Scandinavians, Teutons [people of Germanic or Celtic origin], Anglo-Saxons and Celts [British, Scottish, or Irish people] to enter.

（178）

(178)

在给埃德蒙·威尔逊的另一封信中，菲茨杰拉德写道：“我们[盎格鲁-撒克逊人、凯尔特人等等]比现代法国人高出一大截，就像他比黑人高出一大截一样。即使在艺术方面也是如此！”（特恩布尔，《书信集》，引自吉德利 178）。

In another letter to Edmund Wilson, Fitzgerald wrote, “We [Anglo-Saxons, Celts, and the like] are as far above the modern French man as he is above the Negro. Even in art!” (Turnbull, Letters, cited in Gidley 178).

我认为，菲茨杰拉德对非裔美国人的态度，同样可以从他对朋友卡尔·范·维克滕所著书籍的反应中看出。正如我们之前所见，范·维克滕在哈莱姆区待了很长时间，并且对那里充满热情。1926年，范·维克滕出版了一部关于哈莱姆区的小说，名为《黑鬼天堂》（Nigger Heaven）。单是书名就足以说明问题，W.E.B.杜波依斯写道，这本书“简直是当头一棒……是对黑人（他们曾热情地接纳范·维克滕进入他们的社区）的热情好客以及白人智商的侮辱……我认为这部小说既不真实也不艺术……它简直就是一幅漫画”（引自安德森，第219页）。大卫·莱弗林·刘易斯认为，“情节纯粹是通俗剧”，而且“90%的黑人……都像杜波依斯那样看待这本书”（第181页）。

Equally revealing of Fitzgerald’s attitude toward African Americans, I think, is his response to a book written by his friend Carl Van Vechten. As we saw earlier, Van Vechten spent a good deal of time in and had a great deal of enthusiasm for Harlem. In 1926 Van Vechten came out with a novel about Harlem entitled Nigger Heaven. The title alone is revealing, and W. E. B.
