DuBois wrote that the book “is a blow in the face … an affront to the hospitality of black folk [who had welcomed Van Vechten into their community] and to the intelligence of white[s]. … I find the novel neither truthful nor artistic. … It is a caricature” (cited in Anderson 219). According to David Levering Lewis, “[t]he plot is sheer melodrama,” and “90 percent of the [black] race … saw the book as DuBois did” (181).

然而，许多白人读者和文学评论家对此持不同意见，菲茨杰拉德便是其中之一。他称《黑鬼天堂》为“一件艺术品”（安德森 217），并赞扬其对“北方黑鬼，或者更确切地说，是纽约黑鬼”的刻画（特恩布尔，《书信集》，引自吉德利 181）。据刘易斯所述，菲茨杰拉德“喜爱这部小说，因为对他而言，它印证了文明所造成的非裔美国人的怪诞形象，以及……‘未受污染的黑人’的持久性”（188）。换言之，菲茨杰拉德认为非裔美国人无法真正内化白人文化——他们仍然保持原始状态，或者说“未受污染”——因此，哈莱姆区只不过是他们模仿白人文化的尝试。菲茨杰拉德认为，“哈莱姆[正在]模仿……白人的方式，仿佛白人文化是从其语境中挖出来的，并被放置在一个偶然的、不相关的背景中”（卡尔·范·维克滕收藏，纽约公共图书馆，引自刘易斯 188）。

Many white readers and literary critics disagreed, however, and Fitzgerald was among them. He called Nigger Heaven “a work of art” (Anderson 217) and praised it for its representation of “the northern nigger or, rather the nigger in New York” (Turnbull, Letters, cited in Gidley 181). According to Lewis, Fitzgerald “adored the novel because, for [him] it confirmed the Afro-American grotesqueries produced by civilization and the durability of … the ‘unspoiled Negro’” (188). In other words, Fitzgerald believed that African Americans were unable to truly internalize white culture – they remained primitive, or “unspoiled” – and therefore Harlem was merely their attempt to copy white culture. For Fitzgerald, “Harlem [was] aping … white ways, as if white culture had been dug out of its context and set down against an accidental and unrelated background” (Carl Van Vechten Collection, N.Y. Public Library, cited in Lewis 188).

在我看来，最后这句话既发人深省又令人震惊。非裔美国人发明了爵士乐，这很难说是抄袭白人音乐。哈莱姆文艺复兴时期涌现出兰斯顿·休斯、佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿和克劳德·麦凯等作家，他们拓展了非裔美国人的文学传统，而这绝非是对白人文学文化的简单复制。相反，美国以外的白人社会往往认可非裔美国人文化的独创性。例如，正如我们之前所见，爵士时代的巴黎就对非裔美国人文化的独特品质赞赏有加。然而，菲茨杰拉德却无法或不愿正视哈莱姆的独特之处。显然，他仍然固守着白人对非裔美国人的刻板印象，认为他们野蛮无知。如果他在哈莱姆看到了任何与这种刻板印象不同的事物，正如我们前面提到的，他都会将其归咎于非裔美国人“模仿”白人——在这个语境下，这种用词也暴露了菲茨杰拉德的种族主义视角。

This last statement is as revealing, it seems to me, as it is startling. African Americans invented jazz, which can hardly be said to be a copy of white music. The Harlem Renaissance produced writers like Langston Hughes, Zora Neale Hurston, and Claude McKay, who expanded on an African American literary tradition that was by no means a copy of white literary culture. On the contrary, white societies outside the United States often recognized the originality of African American culture. As we saw earlier, for example, Jazz Age Paris greatly admired the unique quality of African American culture. Yet Fitzgerald was unable or unwilling to see Harlem in its own right. Clearly, he wanted to continue believing the white stereotype of African Americans as uncivilized and uncultured. If he saw anything in Harlem other than this stereotype, he chalked it up, as we noted above, to African Americans’ “aping” whites, a word choice that, in this context, also reveals Fitzgerald’s racist perspective.

因此，颇具讽刺意味的是，“《了不起的盖茨比》已成为美国社会史的国际文献，并被解读为特定时空下美国生活的记录”（布鲁科利，《了不起的盖茨比的文本》，193页）。如果真是如此，那么世人所拥有的关于爵士时代美国生活的记录，却忽略了小说所探讨的那个时代背后的重要地点和人物。M·吉德利说道：“菲茨杰拉德，这位被誉为‘爵士时代的桂冠诗人’的作家——爵士时代的许多特质都源于哈莱姆区的夜生活——如今在我们看来，却像是一个被偏见束缚的囚徒，但他却能超越自身的枷锁”（181页）。菲茨杰拉德或许确实是偏见的囚徒，但至少从《了不起的盖茨比》的文本证据来看，很明显，他不愿意或无法超越他种族偏见所设定的狭隘界限。

It is ironic, then, to say the least, that “The Great Gatsby has become an international source for American social history and is read as a record of American life at an actual time and place” (Bruccoli, “The Text of The Great Gatsby” 193). For if this is the case, then the world has a record of American life during the Jazz Age that omits the place and the people largely responsible for creating the era that the novel examines. M. Gidley says, “Fitzgerald, who was known … as the ‘laureate of The Jazz Age,’ so much of the quality of which era emanated originally from the night life of Harlem, strikes us now, I would suggest, as a prisoner of prejudice who yet sees beyond his own chains” (181). Fitzgerald may indeed have been a prisoner of prejudice, but at least in terms of the textual evidence offered in The Great Gatsby, it is evident that he was unwilling or unable to see beyond the narrow boundaries set by his racial biases.

拓展练习题：非裔美国人对其他文学作品的解读

Questions for further practice: African American approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用非裔美国文学批评来解读文中提及的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use African American criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1托妮·莫里森的《最蓝的眼睛》（1970）在哪些方面参与了非裔美国文学传统？例如，你可以分析这部小说的反种族主义政治立场。（莫里森以其对内化种族主义心理的深刻洞察而闻名。）或者，你可以分析它的诗学，例如它的口头性、民间主题，以及小说中这些手法的运用如何与作品的意义相关联。或者，你也可以论证莫里森的小说更具体地参与了非裔美国女性写作的传统。

1 In what ways does Toni Morrison’s The Bluest Eye (1970) participate in the African American literary tradition? For example, you might analyze the novel’s antiracist politics. (Morrison is known for her insights into the psychology of internalized racism.) Or you might analyze its poetics, for example, its orality, its folk motifs, and the ways in which the novel’s use of these devices relates to the meaning of the work. Or you might want to argue that Morrison’s novel participates more specifically in the tradition of African American women’s writing.

2在奥古斯特·威尔逊的戏剧《钢琴课》（1990）中，他设置了两个反复出现的非裔美国人主题之间的冲突：文化遗产的重要性以及经济生存的困境。分析该剧如何展现并维系这种冲突，而不让我们偏袒任何一方。（或者，如果您认为该剧确实解决了冲突，请论证这种解读。）您如何将威尔逊对这些主题的运用与休斯顿·贝克关于非裔美国文学中精神追求及其经济潜文本之间关系的观察联系起来？如果您认为该剧并不完全符合这种文本与潜文本的特定模式，请像贝克所说的那样，即兴构建您自己的模式，并解释您的模式与贝克的模式有何不同。

2 In his play The Piano Lesson (1990), August Wilson sets up a conflict between two recurring African American themes: the importance of cultural heritage and the difficulties of economic survival. Analyze how the play represents and sustains this conflict without letting us resolve it in favor of one side or the other. (Or if you think the play does resolve the conflict, argue for that interpretation instead.) How might you relate Wilson’s use of these themes to Houston Baker’s observations about the relationship between the spiritual quest and its economic subtext in African American literature? If you don’t think the play quite fits this particular schema of text and subtext, improvise, as Baker would say, a schema of your own, explaining how yours differs from Baker’s.

3运用玛丽·海伦·华盛顿对非裔美国女性写作中反复出现的人物类型——“悬置的女性”、“同化的女性”和“觉醒的女性”——的描述，分析爱丽丝·沃克的《紫色》（1982）、佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿的《他们的眼睛望着上帝》（1937）或其他任何适合此类研究的非裔美国作品中的女性人物。这些类型中哪些出现在文本中？它们与作品的整体意义有何关联？也就是说，这些类型在文本中如何发挥作用，传达某种道德、教训或主题？

3 Use Mary Helen Washington’s description of recurring character types in African American women’s writing – the “suspended woman,” the “assimilated woman,” and the “emergent woman” – to analyze the female characters in Alice Walker’s The Color Purple (1982), Zora Neale Hurston’s Their Eyes Were Watching God (1937), or any other African American work that will lend itself to such a study. Which of these types appear in the text, and how do they relate to the meaning of the work as a whole? That is, how do these types function in the text to convey some sort of moral or lesson or theme?

4运用批判种族理论中的概念，例如交叉性、白人特权、种族的社会建构，或者任何你认为有用的概念，来分析查尔斯·约翰逊的《中途航程》（1990）、凯特·肖邦的《觉醒》（1899）或弗兰纳里·奥康纳的《审判日》（1965）中黑人和/或白人角色的经历。这些概念如何帮助我们阐明人物塑造的某些方面？

4 Use such concepts from critical race theory as intersectionality, white privilege, the social construction of race, or any others you find helpful, to analyze the experience of black and/or white characters in Charles Johnson’s Middle Passage (1990), Kate Chopin’s The Awakening (1899), or Flannery O’Connor’s “Judgment Day” (1965). How do these concepts help clarify certain aspects of characterization?

5运用托妮·莫里森关于美国主流白人文学中非洲主义存在的理论（黑人角色、黑人故事、黑人语言的呈现方式，以及与非洲或黑人相关的意象的功能），分析一位美国白人作家的文学作品中的非洲主义存在。F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德的《离岸海盗》（1920）、《风中的家庭》（1932）或《夜色温柔》（1934）或许是不错的选择。

5 Using Toni Morrison’s theory of the Africanist presence in white mainstream American literature (the function of black characters, of stories about black people, of representations of black speech, or of images associated with Africa or with blackness), analyze the Africanist presence in a literary text by a white American author. F. Scott Fitzgerald’s “The Off-shore Pirate” (1920), “Family in the Wind” (1932), or Tender Is the Night (1934) might work well for this purpose.

笔记

Notes

1当然，在日常用语中，大多数人使用“种族主义者”一词既指种族优越论，也指任何种族对其他种族的不公平的种族歧视态度和行为。在区分种族主义和种族歧视时，我的目的是强调两者之间的巨大差异，例如，白人种族主义态度和行为受到制度化权力结构的支持，而非裔美国人的“种族主义”态度和行为则缺乏制度支持。

1 In our everyday speech, of course, most people use the word racist to refer both to the belief in racial superiority and to the unfair race-based attitudes and practices of any race against any other. In differentiating between racism and racialism, my effort is to foreground the enormous difference between, for example, white racist attitudes and behaviors, which are backed up by the institutionalized power structure, and African American “racist” attitudes and behaviors, which are not institutionally supported.

2学生们经常问，白人内部是否存在某种类似于本文讨论的非裔美国人内部种族歧视的肤色偏见。事实上，白人内部确实存在这种偏见，它被称为北欧主义。虽然我们现在很少听到这个词了，北欧主义在大多数（如果不是全部）白人文化中仍然扮演着重要的角色。从北欧主义的视角来看，高加索人种不仅在基因上优于其他所有种族，而且北欧人——即北欧的日耳曼民族——更是基因最优越的高加索人种：他们天生拥有超凡的智慧、强健的体魄和出众的容貌。就外貌而言，“北欧人”通常与身材高挑、脸型修长而非圆润、肤色白皙、金发或棕发以及浅色眼睛的人联系在一起。关于北欧主义的更深入探讨，请参阅本书第十二章“殖民主义意识形态与后殖民身份认同”。

2 Students often have asked whether or not white people have some form of color prejudice within the white race comparable to the intra-racial racism of African Americans discussed here. Indeed, they have, and it’s called Nordicism. Although we no longer frequently hear the word today, Nordicism still plays a powerful role in most if not all white cultures. From a Nordicist perspective, not only is the Caucasian race genetically superior to all other races, but Nordics – Germanic peoples of Northern Europe – are the most genetically superior Caucasians: they are born with superior intelligence, physical strength, and beauty. In terms of physical appearance, the word Nordic is associated with persons of tall stature, long rather than round facial structure, fair skin, blond or brown hair, and light-colored eyes. For a more thorough discussion of Nordicism, see “Colonialist ideology and postcolonial identity” in Chapter 12 of this book.

3关于持有可卡因的强制性量刑的完整讨论，可在量刑项目网站上找到，网址为 http://sentencingproject/CRACKREFORM/。

3 A full discussion of mandatory sentencing for the possession of cocaine is available online at The Sentencing Project, http://sentencingproject/CRACKREFORM/.

4值得注意的是，缪尔在这里特指十九世纪美国科学界的官方种族主义信条。我相信许多读者都会记得，他所描述的这种种族主义思想自美国殖民地时期以来就以各种形式存在于美国白人公众之中。

4 It is interesting to observe that Muir here refers specifically to the official racial tenets of the American scientific community in the nineteenth century. Many readers will recall, I’m sure, that the racist ideology he describes had been present in various forms among the white American public since the days of the American colonies.

520世纪20年代，哈莱姆区的一些夜总会由黑人经营，一些由白人经营，但几乎所有夜总会都存在顾客种族隔离。通常情况下，在夜总会工作的乐手和其他人员都是非裔美国人，而顾客则是白人。因此，像布坎南一家这样的富人去哈莱姆区的夜总会，并非为了与不同种族的人群交往、拓展社交圈，而是为了结识其他富有或有影响力的白人，并被他们看到。

5 During the 1920s, some Harlem nightclubs had black owners, some had white, but almost all were segregated in terms of their clientele. Typically, the musicians and others who worked in the clubs were African American; the customers were white. Therefore, wealthy people like the Buchanans would have gone to Harlem nightclubs, not to mix with an interracial crowd and broaden their social experience, but to see and be seen by other wealthy or important whites.

6正如我的学生们提醒我的那样，在默特尔·威尔逊被撞身亡的那场戏中，出现了一个“肤色苍白、衣着体面的黑人走到”一名警官身边，讲述他目睹的经过。而警官也急于采纳此人的信息（147；第七章）。虽然这段简短的描写赋予了这位黑人角色一定的权威性，但小说中弥漫的种族氛围表明，如果他肤色不够白皙、衣着不够体面，他的证词就不会被认真对待。事实上，有人可能会认为，菲茨杰拉德这样描写他是为了让警官和（白人）读者有理由相信他的证词。

6 As my students have reminded me, the scene of Myrtle Wilson’s hit-and-run death includes “[a] pale, well dressed Negro [who] step[s] near” a police officer in order to tell what he witnessed. And the officer is eager to take this character’s information (147; ch. 7). While this brief passage confers some authority on the black character, the racial atmosphere pervading the novel suggests that he wouldn’t have been taken seriously had he not had light skin and worn good clothing. Indeed, one could argue that Fitzgerald portrayed him in this manner so that the officer, and the (white) reader, would have reason to believe his testimony.

12 后殖民批评

12 Postcolonial criticism

批判理论培养的最重要的能力之一，或许就是发现我们原本未曾意识到的关联：例如，我们个人的心理冲突与我们对诗歌的解读之间的关联，我们内化的意识形态与我们认为具有审美价值的文学作品之间的关联，一个国家的政治氛围与其知识分子眼中的“伟大”文学作品之间的关联，等等。我们迄今为止学习的大多数批判理论都鼓励我们沿着这些思路中的一个或多个方向建立联系。后殖民批评尤其擅长帮助我们看到自身经验各个领域——心理、意识形态、社会、政治、知识和审美——之间的联系，并向我们展示这些范畴在我们对自身和世界的体验中是如何密不可分的。事实上，正因如此，后殖民批评要求我们从其所谓的“文化差异”的角度来思考自身和他人：种族、阶级、性别、性取向、宗教、文化信仰和习俗如何共同塑造个体身份。此外，后殖民理论为我们提供了一个框架，让我们能够审视所有处理人类压迫的批判理论之间的相似之处，例如马克思主义、女权主义、同性恋、女同性恋和酷儿理论以及非裔美国人理论。

Perhaps one of the most important abilities critical theory develops in us is the ability to see connections where we didn’t know they existed: for example, connections between our personal psychological conflicts and the way we interpret a poem, between the ideologies we’ve internalized and the literary works we find aesthetically pleasing, between a nation’s political climate and what its intellectuals consider “great” literature, and so forth. Most of the critical theories we’ve studied so far have encouraged us to make connections along one or more of these lines. Postcolonial criticism is particularly effective at helping us see connections among all the domains of our experience – the psychological, ideological, social, political, intellectual, and aesthetic – in ways that show us just how inseparable these categories are in our lived experience of ourselves and our world. Indeed, that’s why postcolonial criticism asks us to think of ourselves and others in terms of what it calls cultural difference: the ways in which race, class, sex, gender, sexual orientation, religion, cultural beliefs, and customs combine to form individual identity. In addition, postcolonial theory offers us a framework for examining the similarities among all critical theories that deal with human oppression, such as Marxism; feminism; gay, lesbian, and queer theories; and African American theory.

事实上，由于后殖民批评将曾经被殖民的人民定义为任何曾遭受另一民族政治和经济统治的群体，因此我们可能会看到后殖民批评家从非裔美国人的文学作品中汲取例证，例如澳大利亚原住民的文学作品或印度前殖民地人民的文学作品。然而，后殖民批评倾向于关注全球性问题，关注不同民族之间的比较和对比，这意味着特定群体的成员有责任发展出一套关于自身文学历史、传统和诠释的批评体系。当然，这正是非裔美国批评家长期以来一直在做的事情，早在20世纪90年代初后殖民批评成为文学研究领域的一股强大力量之前，他们就已经开始这样做了。

In fact, because postcolonial criticism defines formerly colonized peoples as any population that has been subjected to the political and economic domination of another population, you may see postcolonial critics draw examples from the literary works of African Americans as well as from, for example, the literature of Aboriginal Australians or the formerly colonized population of India. However, the tendency of postcolonial criticism to focus on global issues, on comparisons and contrasts among various peoples, means that it is up to the individual members of specific populations to develop their own body of criticism on the history, traditions, and interpretation of their own literature. Of course, this is precisely what African American critics have been doing for some time, long before postcolonial criticism emerged as a powerful force in literary studies in the early 1990s.

然而，为了将后殖民批评置于其自身的历史语境中，让我们花点时间回想一下高中历史课的内容。正如我们大多数人所能理解的那样，根据我们高中所学，欧洲对新世界的统治始于十五世纪末。西班牙、法国、英国、葡萄牙和荷兰是掠夺自然资源和人力资源的主要竞争者，在接下来的几个世纪里，欧洲帝国的版图扩张至全球。十九世纪，英国崛起为最大的帝国主义强国，到二十世纪初，大英帝国统治着地球四分之一的面积，包括印度、澳大利亚、新西兰、加拿大、爱尔兰，以及在非洲、西印度群岛、南美洲、中东和东南亚的重要领土。英国的殖民统治一直持续到第二次世界大战结束，印度于1947年获得独立，其他殖民地也陆续效仿。到1980年，英国几乎失去了所有殖民地。

To place postcolonial criticism in a historical context of its own, however, let’s take a minute and think back to our high school history classes. As most of us can recall from our high school education, European domination of the New World began in the late fifteenth century. Spain, France, England, Portugal, and the Netherlands were the main contenders for the plunder of natural and human resources, and over the next few centuries European empires extended themselves around the globe. During the nineteenth century Britain emerged as the largest imperial1 power, and by the turn of the twentieth century the British Empire ruled one quarter of the earth’s surface, including India, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Ireland, and significant holdings in Africa, the West Indies, South America, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia. British colonial domination continued until the end of World War II, when India gained independence in 1947, and other colonies gradually followed suit. By 1980 Britain had lost all but a few of its colonial holdings.

尽管后殖民批评直到20世纪90年代初才成为文学研究领域的一股重要力量，但它所借鉴的殖民主义文化分析在世界各地的反殖民政治运动中都发挥了重要作用，并在二战后殖民政权开始瓦解时确立了其作为学术研究领域的地位。作为文学研究的一个分支，后殖民批评既是一个研究对象，也是一个理论框架。作为研究对象，后殖民批评分析的是从殖民接触之初到今天，在殖民统治下发展起来的各种文化所创作的文学作品。 （你可能还记得，在20世纪80年代之前，后殖民文学曾被归类为“英联邦文学”。）这些文学作品中有些是由殖民者创作的，而更多的是由被殖民者和前被殖民者创作的，并且至今仍在创作。作为研究对象，任何对后殖民文学作品的分析，无论采用何种理论框架，都可以被称为后殖民批评。当然，对于英语专业的学生来说，后殖民批评侧重于对英国殖民统治做出回应而发展起来的文化文学，因为英语系主要研究的是用英语写成的文学作品。

Although postcolonial criticism didn’t become a major force in literary studies until the early 1990s, the cultural analysis of colonialism on which it draws has played an important role in anticolonial political movements everywhere and took its place as a field of intellectual inquiry when colonial regimes began to topple after World War II. As a domain within literary studies, postcolonial criticism is both a subject matter and a theoretical framework. As a subject matter, postcolonial criticism analyzes literature produced by cultures that developed in response to colonial domination, from the first point of colonial contact to the present.2 (You may recall reading postcolonial literature under the heading of “Commonwealth literature,” which it was called until the 1980s.) Some of this literature was written by the colonizers. Much more of it was written, and is being written, by colonized and formerly colonized peoples. As a subject matter, any analysis of a postcolonial literary work, regardless of the theoretical framework used, might be called postcolonial criticism. For English majors, of course, postcolonial criticism focuses on the literature of cultures that developed in response to British colonial domination because English departments study, for the most part, literatures written in English.

然而，作为一种理论框架（这也是我们在此主要关注的），后殖民批评旨在理解殖民主义和反殖民主义意识形态在政治、社会、文化和心理层面的运作。例如，大量的后殖民批评分析了两种意识形态力量：一方面，它们迫使被殖民者内化殖民者的价值观；另一方面，它们又推动被殖民人民反抗压迫者，而这种反抗与殖民主义本身一样古老。正如我们将看到的，由于殖民主义和反殖民主义意识形态可以存在于任何文学文本中，因此，一部作品不必被归类为后殖民作品，我们也可以运用后殖民批评对其进行分析。

However, as a theoretical framework, and this is our primary concern here, postcolonial criticism seeks to understand the operations – politically, socially, culturally, and psychologically – of colonialist and anticolonialist ideologies. For example, a good deal of postcolonial criticism analyzes the ideological forces that, on the one hand, pressed the colonized to internalize the colonizers’ values and, on the other hand, promoted the resistance of colonized peoples against their oppressors, a resistance that is as old as colonialism itself. And as we’ll see, because colonialist and anticolonialist ideologies can be present in any literary text, a work doesn’t have to be categorized as postcolonial for us to be able to use postcolonial criticism to analyze it.

殖民主义意识形态与后殖民身份认同

Colonialist ideology and postcolonial identity

许多曾被英国殖民的民族讲英语、用英语写作、在学校和大学中使用英语，并用英语处理政府事务。英语，以及他们在家可能使用的当地语言，都表明了殖民统治对其文化的残留影响。事实上，前殖民地居民所认同的本土、土著、前殖民文化与强加于他们的英国文化之间动态的心理和社会互动，构成了后殖民批评研究领域的重要组成部分。因为后殖民文化既包含被殖民文化与殖民文化之间的融合，也包含二者之间的对抗。在当今时代，由于英国对殖民地人民的政府、教育、文化价值观和日常生活的渗透如此彻底，这两种文化很难被明确区分。

That so many peoples formerly colonized by Britain speak English, write in English, use English in their schools and universities, and conduct government business in English, in addition to the local languages they may use at home, is an indication of the residual effect of colonial domination on their cultures. In fact, the dynamic psychological and social interplay between what ex-colonial populations consider their native, indigenous, precolonial cultures and the British culture that was imposed on them constitutes a large portion of the field of study for postcolonial critics. For postcolonial cultures include both a merger of and antagonism between the culture of the colonized and that of the colonizer, which, at this point in time, are difficult to identify and separate into discrete entities, so complete was the British intrusion into the government, education, cultural values, and daily lives of its colonial subjects.

简而言之，尽管殖民者撤退并将他们侵略的土地交还给了被殖民者，但非殖民化往往仅限于英国军队和政府官员的撤离。留下的却是根深蒂固的文化殖民：英国的政府和教育体系、英国文化以及英国价值观的灌输，这些都贬低了曾经被征服民族的文化、道德乃至外貌。因此，前殖民者往往背负着一种心理上的“遗产”——负面的自我形象以及与自身本土文化的疏离。由于长期以来这些文化被禁止或贬低，许多前殖民时期的文化已经失传。

In short, although the colonizers retreated and left the lands they had invaded in the hands of those they had colonized, decolonization often has been confined largely to the removal of British military forces and government officials. What has been left behind is a deeply embedded cultural colonization: the inculcation of a British system of government and education, British culture, and British values that denigrate the culture, morals, and even physical appearance of formerly subjugated peoples. Thus, ex-colonials often were left with a psychological “inheritance” of a negative self-image and alienation from their own indigenous cultures, which had been forbidden or devalued for so long that much precolonial culture has been lost.

鉴于大量后殖民批评探讨了后殖民文学中呈现的文化认同问题，让我们更深入地考察一下后殖民认同这一议题。然而，要做到这一点，我们首先必须理解殖民主义意识形态，因为对这种意识形态的各种反应在很大程度上构成了个人和社群后殖民认同的起源。但是，当我们开始使用以下概念时，必须记住，我们是在对殖民统治之前、期间和之后在历史和经历方面存在巨大差异的人群进行概括。因此，诸如“无家感”和“模仿”之类的后殖民术语（我们稍后会讨论）仅仅是“一种有用的简略说法，因为它们没有考虑到不同殖民情境之间的差异，也没有考虑到阶级、性别、地理位置、种族、种姓或意识形态等因素在那些生活被殖民统治重塑的人们身上所发挥的作用”（Loomba 19）。

Given that a good deal of postcolonial criticism addresses the problem of cultural identity as it is represented in postcolonial literature, let’s take a closer look at the issue of postcolonial identity. In order to do so, however, we must first understand colonialist ideology, the various reactions to which, in large part, constitute the origins of postcolonial identity for individual human beings as well as for communities. As we begin to use the following concepts, however, we must remember that we are applying generalizations to groups of people that differ greatly in terms of their history and experience before, during, and after colonial rule. Thus, such postcolonial terms as unhomeliness and mimicry, which we’ll discuss shortly, are only “a helpful shorthand, because they do not allow for the differences between distinct kinds of colonial situations, or the workings of class, gender, [geographical] location, race, caste or ideology among people whose lives have been restructured by colonial rule” (Loomba 19).

殖民主义意识形态，通常被称为殖民主义话语，以凸显其与表达殖民主义思想的语言之间的关联，其基础是殖民者自认为优越，并将其与被征服土地上的原住民（土著居民）的所谓劣等性进行对比。殖民者认为，只有他们自己的盎格鲁-欧洲文化才是文明的、先进的，或者如后殖民主义批评家所言，是“都市的”。因此，原住民被定义为野蛮的、落后的和不发达的。由于他们的技术更为先进，殖民者认为他们的整个文化也更为先进，因此他们忽视或摒弃了被征服民族的宗教、习俗和行为准则。因此，殖民者认为……殖民者将自己置于世界中心；被殖民者则被边缘化。殖民者视自己为人类应有的化身，是完美的“自我”；而土著居民则被视为“他者”，与他们不同，因此低人一等，甚至不具备完整的人性。

Colonialist ideology, often referred to as colonialist discourse to mark its relationship to the language in which colonialist thinking was expressed, was based on the colonizers’ assumption of their own superiority, which they contrasted with the alleged inferiority of native (indigenous) peoples, the original inhabitants of the lands they invaded. The colonizers believed that only their own Anglo-European culture was civilized, sophisticated, or, as postcolonial critics put it, metropolitan. Therefore, native peoples were defined as savage, backward, and undeveloped. Because their technology was more highly advanced, the colonizers believed that their whole culture was more highly advanced, and they ignored or swept aside the religions, customs, and codes of behavior of the peoples they subjugated. So the colonizers saw themselves at the center of the world; the colonized were at the margins. The colonizers saw themselves as the embodiment of what a human being should be, the proper “self”; native peoples were considered “other,” different, and therefore inferior to the point of being less than fully human.

这种将所有与自己不同的人视为低人一等的做法被称为“他者化”，它将世界划分为“我们”（“文明人”）和“他们”（“他者”、“野蛮人”）。例如，当欧洲人最初抵达“新大陆”时，未被基督徒占据的土地被视为“空地”，因此任其掠夺。换句话说，这些土地上的原住民被殖民者如此彻底地“他者化”，以至于他们在法律意义上不被承认。原住民的确存在——事实上，欧洲征服者经常将他们当作奴隶，欧洲传教士也曾来到​​这里试图使他们皈依基督教——但作为非基督教的“野蛮人”，他们被排除在外。“野蛮人”通常被认为是邪恶的（恶魔般的他者）和低劣的。但有时，“野蛮人”也被认为拥有源于与自然亲近的“原始”之美或高贵气质（异域风情的他者）。但无论哪种情况，“野蛮人”仍然是异类，因此并非完全是人类。

This practice of judging all who are different as less than fully human is called othering, and it divides the world between “us” (the “civilized”) and “them” (the “others,” the “savages”). When Europeans first arrived in the “New World,” for example, land that wasn’t occupied by Christians was considered “empty land” and, therefore, theirs for the taking. In other words, native inhabitants of these lands were so othered by the colonizers that they didn’t officially exist. Native inhabitants were certainly physically present – indeed, European conquerors often used them as slaves, and European missionaries arrived to Christianize them – but as non-Christian “savages,” they didn’t count. The “savage” was usually considered evil (the demonic other) as well as inferior. But sometimes the “savage” was perceived as possessing a “primitive” beauty or nobility born of a closeness to nature (the exotic other). In either case, however, the “savage” remained other and, therefore, not fully human.

如今，这种以欧洲文化为标准，并将其他所有文化进行负面对比的态度被称为欧洲中心主义。文学研究中一个常见的欧洲中心主义例子是长期存在的所谓“普遍主义”哲学。英国、欧洲以及后来的美国文化权威人士都以“普遍性”来评判所有文学作品：一部文学作品要想被视为伟大作品，就必须具备“普遍”的人物和主题。然而，一部作品的人物和主题是否被认为是“普遍的”，取决于它们是否与欧洲文学中的人物和主题相似。因此，这种假设认为欧洲的思想、理想和经验是普遍的，是全人类的标准。

Today, this attitude – the use of European culture as the standard to which all other cultures are negatively contrasted – is called Eurocentrism. A common example of Eurocentrism in literary studies is the longstanding philosophy of so-called universalism. British, European, and, later, American cultural standard-bearers judged all literature in terms of its “universality”: to be considered a great work, a literary text had to have “universal” characters and themes. However, whether or not a text’s characters and themes were considered “universal” depended on whether or not they resembled those from European literature. Thus, the assumption was that European ideas, ideals, and experience were universal, that is, the standard for all humankind.

我之前用过的“新世界”一词就是一个欧洲中心主义语言的例子，它用来指代美洲这片古老的土地，而这片土地对欧洲人来说只是“新的”。类似的欧洲中心主义语言例子还可以从“第一世界”、“第二世界”、“第三世界”和“第四世界”这些术语中看出，它们分别指代：（1）英国、欧洲和美国；（2）加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰和南部非洲的白人人口（一些理论家认为还包括前苏联集团）；（3）技术发展中国家，例如印度以及非洲、中南美洲和东南亚的国家；（4）各大洲的土著居民，他们曾被白人殖民者征服，如今又被周围的主流文化边缘化，例如美洲原住民和澳大利亚原住民（一些理论家认为还包括在第一世界国家中被视为少数族裔的非土著居民，例如非裔美国人）。尽管如今人们通常称这四个“世界”为“世界”，而且我们也会在本章中使用这些术语，但我们仍应意识到它们的含义。这种说法带有欧洲中心主义色彩。只有当历史以欧洲为起点，并以欧洲殖民征服为框架时，这种说法才成立。它忽略了更早时期世界的存在——例如希腊、埃及、非洲、中东、中国和美洲——并将欧洲军事征服视为组织世界历史的主要手段。

An example of Eurocentric language can be seen in the term I used earlier – New World – to denote the very old worlds of the Americas, a land which was “new” only to the Europeans. Similar examples of Eurocentric language can be seen in the terms First World, Second World, Third World, and Fourth World to refer to, respectively, (1) Britain, Europe, and the United States; (2) the white populations of Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and southern Africa (and, for some theorists, the former Soviet bloc); (3) the technologically developing nations, such as India and those of Africa, Central and South America, and Southeast Asia; and (4) the indigenous populations on every continent who were subjugated by white settlers and are marginalized today by the majority culture that surrounds them, such as Native Americans and Aboriginal Australians (and, for some theorists, nonindigenous populations who have the status of racial minorities in First World countries, such as African Americans). Although these four “worlds” are commonly referred to today, and we’ll use these terms in this chapter, we should remain aware of their Eurocentric implications. Such language makes sense only if history begins with Europe and is organized in terms of European colonial conquest. It ignores the existence of earlier worlds – such as those of Greece, Egypt, Africa, the Middle East, China, and the Americas – and it privileges European military conquest as the primary means of organizing world history.

Orientalism is an example of Eurocentric othering, analyzed by Edward Said (pronounced sah-eed), which has been practiced in Europe, Britain, and America. Its purpose is to produce a positive national self-definition for Western nations by contrast with Eastern nations on which the West projects all the negative characteristics it doesn't want to believe exist among its own people. Thus the Chinese or the Arabs, or whatever Asian or Middle Eastern population is politically convenient, are defined as cruel, sneaky, evil, cunning, dishonest, given to sexual promiscuity and perversion, and the like. (Think of the cruel, deceitful Arab merchant in Mary Shelley's Frankenstein , published in 1818, who is saved from prison by the young DeLacey, a European, whom the Arab subsequently betrays.) Citizens of the West then define themselves, in contrast to the imaginary “oriental” they've created, as kind, straightforward, good, upright, honest, and moral. 简而言之，“东方”是西方的发明，通过与西方的对比，西方得以正面定义自己，并为任何它认为有利的军事或经济侵略行为辩护。

Orientalism is an example of Eurocentric othering, analyzed by Edward Said (pronounced sah-eed), which has been practiced in Europe, Britain, and America. Its purpose is to produce a positive national self-definition for Western nations by contrast with Eastern nations on which the West projects all the negative characteristics it doesn’t want to believe exist among its own people. Thus the Chinese or the Arabs, or whatever Asian or Middle Eastern population is politically convenient, are defined as cruel, sneaky, evil, cunning, dishonest, given to sexual promiscuity and perversion, and the like. (Think of the cruel, deceitful Arab merchant in Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein, published in 1818, who is saved from prison by the young DeLacey, a European, whom the Arab subsequently betrays.) Citizens of the West then define themselves, in contrast to the imaginary “oriental” they’ve created, as kind, straightforward, good, upright, honest, and moral. In short, the “oriental” is an invention of the West, by contrast to whom it has been able to define itself positively and justify any acts of military or economic aggression it has found advantageous.

最后，北欧主义或许可以被视为以欧洲为中心的“他者化”推向极端的一个例子。虽然许多学生从未听说过“北欧主义”这个词，但它在大多数（如果不是全部）白人文化中都扮演着重要的角色。从北欧主义的视角来看，高加索人种不仅在基因上优于其他所有种族，而且北欧人——北欧的日耳曼民族——更是基因最优越的高加索人种：他们天生拥有超凡的智力、体魄和美貌。尽管北欧主义者有时对哪些国家应该被视为北欧国家存在分歧，但大多数人认同挪威、瑞典、丹麦和冰岛属于这一群体。然而，我们的国籍并非决定我们是否属于这个“优等种族”的关键因素。人类长期以来一直在全球范围内迁徙，因此我们的出生地，甚至我们曾曾祖父母的出生地，都不能可靠地反映我们的种族血统。唯一能够揭示我们种族构成的因素是我们的外貌。具体来说， “北欧”一词通常与身材高挑、脸型修长而非圆润、肤色白皙、金发或棕发、浅色眼睛的人联系在一起。如果我们拥有这些体貌特征，人们就会认为我们拥有北欧血统，因此在基因上优于其他所有人。1924年的美国移民法案就是一个众所周知的例子，该法案给予来自北欧的移民优惠待遇，同时限制来自南欧和东欧的移民，这正是20世纪20年代席卷美国的北欧主义的典型体现。另一个北欧主义的例子是希特勒的雅利安主义，或者说是优等种族论。这种理论在20世纪30年代末和40年代初助长了纳粹对犹太人的屠杀。如今，北欧主义在世界各地的许多新纳粹、白人民族主义和白人至上主义团体中仍然盛行。我认为，即使是无意识的，它仍然在我们的日常生活中扮演着一定的角色，例如，人们对“金发男孩”和“金发女孩”的理想化，以及金发碧眼芭比娃娃经久不衰的魅力。

Finally, Nordicism is an ideology that might be seen as an example of Eurocentric othering taken to its logical extreme. While many students have never heard the term Nordicism, it plays a powerful role in most if not all white cultures. From a Nordicist perspective, not only is the Caucasian race genetically superior to all other races, but Nordics – Germanic peoples of Northern Europe – are the most genetically superior Caucasians: they are born with superior intelligence, physical strength, and beauty. Although Nordicists sometimes disagree on which countries should be considered Nordic, most agree that Norway, Sweden, Denmark, and Iceland belong to this group. Our nationality, however, is not important in determining our membership in this “superior race.” Human beings have been migrating around the globe so much for so long that our place of birth, or even our great-great-great grandparents’ place of birth, is not a reliable indicator of our racial heritage. The only factor that can be counted on to reveal our racial makeup is our physical appearance. Specifically, the word Nordic is associated with persons of tall stature, long rather than round facial structure, fair skin, blond or brown hair, and lightcolored eyes. If we have this combination of physical features, it is assumed that we are of Nordic ancestry and, therefore, genetically superior to all others. The US Immigration Act of 1924, which gave immigrants from Northern Europe favored status while restricting the immigration of peoples from Southern and Eastern Europe, is a well-known example of the Nordicism that pervaded the United States during the 1920s. Another example of Nordicism is Hitler’s Aryanism, or master-race theory, which fueled the Holocaust during the late 1930s and early 1940s. Nordicism is still alive and well throughout the world today in many neo-Nazi, white nationalist, and white supremacist groups. And I think it’s reasonable to argue that it still plays a role, even if it’s an unconscious role, in our everyday lives, for instance in the idealization of “fair-haired boys” and “golden girls” and in the staying power of blond, blue-eyed Barbie dolls.

殖民主义意识形态本质上是欧洲中心主义的，它在英国殖民地建立的学校中根深蒂固，旨在向当地土著居民灌输英国文化和价值观，从而阻止反抗。一个人很难反抗一个被灌输了数代人思想的制度或民族，即认为其优越于自己。这一计划非常成功，造就了殖民地臣民——这些被殖民者之所以不反抗殖民统治，是因为他们被教导相信英国的优越性，因而也相信自身的低劣。许多人在穿着、言谈、行为和生活方式上都尽可能地模仿殖民者。后殖民主义批评家将这种现象称为模仿，它既反映了被殖民者渴望被殖民文化接纳的愿望，也反映了他们对自身文化的羞耻感——他们被灌输了文化优越性的观念。后殖民理论家经常将殖民地人民描述为具有双重意识或双重视角，换句话说，他们的意识或世界观分裂于两种对立的文化之间：殖民者的文化和土著社区的文化。3

Colonialist ideology, which is inherently Eurocentric, was a pervasive force in the British schools established in the colonies to inculcate British culture and values in the indigenous peoples and thereby forestall rebellion. It’s difficult to rebel against a system or a people one has been programmed, over several generations, to consider superior. The plan was extremely successful and resulted in the creation of colonial subjects, colonized persons who did not resist colonial subjugation because they were taught to believe in British superiority and, therefore, in their own inferiority. Many of these individuals tried to imitate their colonizers, as much as possible, in dress, speech, behavior, and lifestyle. Postcolonial critics refer to this phenomenon as mimicry, and it reflects both the desire of colonized individuals to be accepted by the colonizing culture and the shame experienced by colonized individuals concerning their own culture, which they were programmed to see as inferior. Postcolonial theorists often describe the colonial subject as having a double consciousness or double vision, in other words, a consciousness or a way of perceiving the world that is divided between two antagonistic cultures: that of the colonizer and that of the indigenous community.3

双重意识常常导致自我意识不稳定，而殖民主义造成的强制迁徙，例如为了寻找工作而从农村或乡村涌入城市，则加剧了这种不稳定。（强制迁徙，无论是为了谋生（包括契约劳工）还是奴役，都将大量人口分散到世界各地，而他们的后代中也有相当一部分人留在了海外，或与故土分离。）这种游离于两种文化之间的感觉，既不属于任何一种文化，也不属于任何一种文化，这种感觉源于一种心理上的困境，这种困境并非仅仅源于某种个体的心理障碍，而是源于自身所处的文化流离失所带来的创伤。霍米·巴巴等人将这种感觉称为“无家感”。“无家感”并不等同于无家可归。“无家感”是指即使在自己的家中也感到不自在，因为你内心深处并不认同自己：可以说，你的文化认同危机使你成为了一个心理上的难民。

Double consciousness often produced an unstable sense of self, which was heightened by the forced migration colonialism frequently caused, for example, from the rural farm or village to the city in search of employment. (Forced migration, either as a quest for employment, including indentured servitude, or as the result of enslavement, scattered large numbers of peoples around the globe, and large populations of their descendants have remained in the diaspora, or separated from their original homeland.) This feeling of being caught between cultures, of belonging to neither rather than to both, of finding oneself arrested in a psychological limbo that results not merely from some individual psychological disorder but from the trauma of the cultural displacement within which one lives, is referred to by Homi Bhabha and others as unhomeliness. Being “unhomed” is not the same as being homeless. To be unhomed is to feel not at home even in your own home because you are not at home in yourself: your cultural identity crisis has made you a psychological refugee, so to speak.

双重意识和无家感在当今的非殖民化国家依然存在。前殖民地人民面临的任务之一是摒弃将他们定义为低人一等的殖民主义意识形态，并重新认识他们前殖民时代的过去。这两项任务都涉及许多复杂的议题，而这些议题正是后殖民主义批评家所关注的。例如，为了摒弃殖民主义意识形态并拥抱他们前殖民时代的过去，在一些文化背景下，一些本土作家，例如肯尼亚作家恩古吉·瓦·提昂戈，会用自己的母语写作。然而，这样做会让他们面临在出版业生存的困境，无论是在本国还是在国际上，出版业都要求使用英语。使用母语写作往往意味着本土作家需要付出双重努力：既要用母语写作，又要将作品翻译成英语，或者请人翻译。

Double consciousness and unhomeliness persist in decolonized nations today. Among the tasks formerly colonized peoples face is the rejection of colonialist ideology, which defined them as inferior, and the reclamation of their precolonial past. Both tasks involve many complex problems of interest to postcolonial critics. For example, in order to reject colonialist ideology and embrace their precolonial cultures, some native authors, such as Kenyan writer Ngugi wa Thiong’o, write in their own local languages. When they do so, however, they face the difficulty of surviving in a publishing industry, both in their own countries and internationally, that requires the use of English. The use of native languages often requires native writers to put forth the double effort of writing in their indigenous languages and then translating their work into English or having it translated.

另一方面，许多来自前英国殖民地的本土作家更倾向于用英语写作，因为这是他们最初学习写作的语言。正如尼日利亚作家奇努阿·阿切贝所言：“对我而言别无选择。我被赋予了这种语言，我注定要使用它”（《创世之晨》第62页）。一些人还认为，英语为第三世界和第四世界国家中讲着各种不同地方语言的各族人民提供了一种通用语言，使他们能够彼此交流。他们指出，英语作为一种世界语言，促进了这些国家融入全球政治和经济体系。

On the other hand, many indigenous writers from former British colonies prefer to write in English because that is the language in which they first learned to write. As Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe observes, “[F]or me there is no other choice. I have been given the language and I intend to use it” (Morning Yet on Creation Day 62). Some also argue that English provides a common language for the various indigenous peoples within Third and Fourth World nations, who speak a number of different local languages, to communicate with one another. And they point out that English, as a world language, facilitates the emergence of those nations into global politics and economics.

另一个阻碍人们重拾前殖民时代历史的难题在于，发现这段历史并非易事。正如我们前文所述，许多前殖民文化在漫长的殖民统治下已经消逝。此外，许多后殖民理论家认为，即便没有殖民，古代文化如今也早已发生变化：没有一种文化能够停滞不前，凝固于时间之中。而且，大多数文化都会因跨文化交流而发生改变，而这种交流往往伴随着军事入侵。例如，古凯尔特文化就因罗马军团占领不列颠群岛而改变。盎格鲁-撒克逊文化也因诺曼人于11世纪征服该地区后，法国长达数代的统治而改变。同样，被殖民民族的前殖民文化也影响了欧洲文化。例如，毕加索的艺术深受他对非洲面具的研究的影响。因此，许多后殖民理论家认为，后殖民身份必然是本土文化与殖民文化动态融合、不断演进的产物。此外，他们认为，这种混合性（有时也称作文化融合）并非两种敌对文化之间的僵局，而是一种富有成效、令人振奋的积极力量，在一个日益全球化、文化融合程度不断加深的世界中发挥着重要作用。这种观点鼓励前殖民地居民拥抱自身文化中多元且往往相互冲突的方面，因为这是他们文化不可磨灭的历史事实。

Another problem that complicates the desire to reclaim a precolonial past is that it is not always easy to discover that past. As we noted earlier, much precolonial culture has been lost over many generations of colonial domination. In addition, many postcolonial theorists argue that, even had there been no colonization, the ancient culture would have changed by now: no culture stands still, frozen in time. Furthermore, most cultures are changed by cross-cultural contact, often through military invasion. For example, ancient Celtic culture was changed by the Roman legions who occupied the British Isles. And Anglo-Saxon culture was changed by the many generations of French rule that followed the Norman conquest of that same territory in the eleventh century. By the same token, the precolonial cultures of colonized peoples influenced European culture. For example, Picasso’s art was greatly influenced by his study of African masks. Therefore, many postcolonial theorists argue that postcolonial identity is necessarily a dynamic, constantly evolving hybrid of native and colonial cultures. Moreover, they assert that this hybridity, or syncretism as it’s sometimes called, does not consist of a stalemate between two warring cultures but is rather a productive, exciting, positive force in a shrinking world that is itself becoming more and more culturally hybrid. This view encourages ex-colonials to embrace the multiple and often conflicting aspects of the blended culture that is theirs and that is an indelible fact of history.

然而，值得注意的是，这些论点忽略了前殖民地人民重新发现并肯定其前殖民文明的必要性，而这背后的原因恰恰在于殖民者曾告诉他们，他们根本不存在任何前殖民文明。殖民者声称，在殖民之前，土著居民过着野蛮的生活，没有任何政府体系、宗教或理性的习俗。或者，即使殖民者承认土著文化的存在，他们也声称，面对“更优越”的文明，这种文化不值得保留。欧洲人提供的文明，使得许多前殖民地居民感到必须捍卫本土文化，既是为了避免被根深蒂固于其土地上的西方文化所淹没，也是为了在自己和他人眼中重塑民族形象。这种对本土文化的强调，尤其是在试图消除西方影响的同时，被称为本土主义或民族主义。从本土主义的视角来看，文化随时间推移而发生改变与一个民族与其文化彻底割裂之间有着巨大的区别。

It is important to note, however, that these arguments don’t take into account the need of formerly colonized peoples to rediscover and affirm their precolonial civilizations for the very good reason that the colonizers told them they didn’t have any precolonial civilizations. Before colonization, the colonizers claimed, native peoples lived barbarically, without any systems of government, religion, or rational customs. Or if colonizers acknowledged that a native culture existed, they claimed that such cultures were not worth sustaining in the face of the “superior” civilization offered by the Europeans. Many ex-colonials therefore feel they must assert a native culture both to avoid being swamped by the Western culture so firmly planted on their soil and to recuperate their national image in their own eyes and in the eyes of others. This emphasis on indigenous culture, especially when accompanied by the attempt to eliminate Western influences, is called nativism or nationalism. From a nativist perspective, there is a big difference between a culture changing over time and a people being cut off from their culture.

如果你读过第四章“女性主义批评”，你可能已经注意到，正如许多后殖民批评家所发现的那样，女性主义批评家和后殖民批评家所关注的理论问题存在诸多相似之处。例如，父权制对女性的压迫类似于殖民主义对土著居民的压迫。由此导致的女性和被殖民人民的贬低，在实现独立的个人和群体身份认同、获得政治权力和经济机会，以及寻找不受压迫者意识形态支配的思考、表达和创造方式等方面，都给这两个群体带来了非常相似的问题。

If you’ve read Chapter 4, “Feminist criticism,” you’ve probably noticed by now, as many postcolonial critics have, a number of similarities in the theoretical issues that concern feminist and postcolonial critics. For example, patriarchal subjugation of women is analogous to colonial subjugation of indigenous populations. And the resultant devaluation of women and colonized peoples poses very similar problems for both groups in terms of achieving an independent personal and group identity; gaining access to political power and economic opportunities; and finding ways to think, speak, and create that are not dominated by the ideology of the oppressor.

女权主义和后殖民主义关注点之间的这些相似之处凸显了后殖民女性所遭受的双重压迫，这通常被称为“双重殖民”。她们既是殖民主义意识形态的受害者，这种意识形态因其种族和文化背景而贬低她们；又是父权制意识形态的受害者，这种意识形态因其性别而贬低她们。令人遗憾的是，后殖民女性不仅遭受殖民者的压迫，也遭受自身父权制文化的压迫。性别不平等在农村社区尤为明显，女性不仅要承担大部分甚至全部的农业劳动，还要承担大量的家庭照料工作，却无法获得与男性同等的家庭权威、社区领导角色或经济机会。

These parallels between feminist and postcolonial concerns underscore the double oppression suffered by postcolonial women, often referred to as double colonization. For they are the victims of both colonialist ideology, which devalues them because of their race and cultural ancestry, and patriarchal ideology, which devalues them because of their sex. Sadly, postcolonial women have suffered patriarchal oppression not only at the hands of colonialists, but within their own patriarchal cultures as well. Gender inequities are often particularly visible in rural communities where women are expected to do most or all of the agricultural work, in addition to the considerable work associated with taking care of homes and families, without compensation comparable to the familial authority, community leadership roles, or economic opportunities afforded their male counterparts.

然而，显而易见的是，后殖民时代的女性在条件允许的情况下完全有能力发挥有效的领导作用。例如，第三世界许多反对破坏当地环境的基层抵抗运动都是由乡村妇女发起的，而且如今也主要由乡村妇女组成。以印度的奇普科运动为例，该运动源于1973年当地妇女自发发起的抗议活动，反对为商业目的而持续过度砍伐当地树木。奇普科运动运用非暴力抵抗策略，阻止对农村环境及其居民生存至关重要的大片森林遭到砍伐。此外，由旺加里·马塔伊于1977年在肯尼亚发起的“绿带运动”旨在通过一棵棵幼苗恢复那些已经遭受森林砍伐严重影响的地区，该运动已遍及肯尼亚全国，并获得了国际影响力。然而，在分配金融机会方面，对技术发展中国家的国际援助往往会强化父权制观念，即女性天生不如男性，因为援助中提供的资金、机器和资源都来自女性。即使在非洲，女性农民生产了65%至80%的农产品，却不拥有自己耕种的土地，而且总是被援助项目和“发展”项目所忽略（McClintock 298），培训仍然只针对男性。因此，对女性的双重殖民仍在继续。正如安妮·麦克林托克所观察到的，“在一个女性承担了世界三分之二的工作，却只赚取了世界10%的收入，拥有的世界财产却不到1%的世界里，‘后殖民主义’的承诺”——即殖民者离开后所有人将过上更好生活的承诺——“一直是希望被一再推迟的历史”（298）。

It is clear, nevertheless, that postcolonial women are very capable of effective leadership when circumstances offer the opportunity. For example, much of the grassroots resistance to the destruction of local environments in the Third World was started by village women and consists today mostly of village women. The Chipko Movement in India, for instance – which grew from a spontaneous protest by local women in 1973 against the continued and excessive felling of local trees for commercial purposes – employs the strategies of nonviolent resistance to prevent the deforestation of large wooded regions critical to the survival of the rural environment and of the Indian people who inhabit it. And the Green Belt Movement – begun in Kenya in 1977 by Wangari Maathai to restore, seedling by seedling, those areas already suffering the dreadful effects of deforestation – has spread throughout her country and gained international influence.4 When it comes, however, to the distribution of financial opportunities, international aid to technologically developing countries has tended to reinforce the patriarchal belief that women are naturally less capable than men by giving the money, the machinery, and the training to men alone, even in Africa, where “women farmers produce 65–80 percent of all agricultural produce, yet do not own the land they work, and are consistently by-passed by aid programs and ‘development’ projects” (McClintock 298). So the double colonization of women continues. As Anne McClintock observes, “In a world where women do two-thirds of the world’s work, earn 10 percent of the world’s income, and own less than 1 percent of the world’s property, the promise of ‘post-colonialism’” – that is, the promise of a better life for all once the colonizers were gone – “has been a history of hopes postponed” (298).

后殖民主义基础性辩论

Foundational postcolonial debates

或许您已经注意到，我们目前讨论的许多内容都涉及一些尚存争议的问题。例如，后殖民时代的人们寻找其前殖民时期遗失的证据究竟有多重要？他们究竟能获取多少前殖民时期的历史？后殖民时代的作家应该用英语写作，还是用他们的母语写作，抑或两者兼而有之？一位以英语为母语的后殖民时代作家应该如何写作？后殖民理论家所定义的“混杂性”对于那些感到无所归属的后殖民时代个体来说，是否是一种现实的选择？等等。

Perhaps you have noticed that a good deal of the material we’ve discussed so far involves issues that seem to be under debate. For example, how important is it that postcolonial peoples seek lost evidence of their precolonial past? How much of their precolonial past is really available to them? Should postcolonial authors write in English, in their native languages, or in both? What should a postcolonial writer do who was raised with English as his or her first language? Is hybridity, as postcolonial theorists define the term, a realistic alternative for postcolonial individuals who feel unhomed? And so forth.

许多后殖民议题，如同我们在其他章节讨论过的许多理论议题一样，在后殖民研究领域内部存在一些分歧。但在我们深入探讨后殖民研究中一些相对较新的议题之前，让我们先简要回顾一下三个从一开始就对后殖民理论领域形成起到重要作用的辩论：哪些民族——以及哪些文学作品——应该被视为后殖民作品？后殖民理论是否有可能边缘化后殖民民族的真正诉求？最后，后殖民批评是否有可能边缘化后殖民作家的作品？

Many postcolonial issues, like many of the theoretical issues we’ve discussed in other chapters, are matters of some disagreement among those who study the field. But before we move on to issues that are of somewhat more recent origin in postcolonial studies, let’s take a brief look at three of the important debates that have helped form the field of postcolonial theory from the beginning: Which peoples – and, therefore, which literary works – should be considered postcolonial? Is postcolonial theory in danger of marginalizing the real concerns of postcolonial peoples? Finally, is postcolonial criticism in danger of marginalizing the work of postcolonial writers?

正如您可能已经注意到的，本章目前为止主要关注的是对土著民族的政治、社会、文化和心理殖民化，这使得我们的讨论仅限于入侵殖民地——即英国武力在非白人民族中建立的殖民地，例如在印度、非洲、西印度群岛、南美洲、中东和东南亚建立的殖民地——因为没有人质疑将这些文化的文学纳入后殖民文学研究的范畴。此外，人们普遍认为美国和爱尔兰并非后殖民国家，前者是因为它独立已久，并且自身也曾殖民过其他国家；后者是因为它长期以来一直是英国文化不可分割的一部分（尽管一些爱尔兰人，尤其是在北爱尔兰，肯定会反对这种说法，许多后殖民批评家也引用爱尔兰诗人叶芝的作品作为反殖民主义民族主义的象征）。然而，后殖民批评家们对于这些文学作品是否属于后殖民文学范畴一直存在诸多争论。白人定居殖民地——特别是那些在加拿大、澳大利亚、新西兰和南部非洲建立的殖民地——应该纳入后殖民文学的研究范围。

As you may have noticed, our focus in this chapter, so far, on the political, social, cultural, and psychological colonization of indigenous peoples has limited our discussion to invader colonies – colonies established among nonwhite peoples through the force of British arms, such as those established in India, Africa, the West Indies, South America, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia – for no one debates the inclusion of literature from these cultures in postcolonial literary studies. There is also a general consensus that the United States and Ireland are not postcolonial nations, the first because it has been independent for so long and has itself colonized others, the second because it has long been an integral part of British culture (though some Irish people, especially in Northern Ireland, would surely disagree with this assessment, and many postcolonial critics cite the work of Irish poet B. Yeats as emblematic of anticolonialist nationalism). However, there has been much debate among postcolonial critics concerning whether or not the literature of white settler colonies – specifically, those established in Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and southern Africa – should be included in the study of postcolonial literature.

那些认为“后殖民”一词应仅用于第三世界和第四世界作家的观点指出，白人殖民文化与英国有着诸多共同之处，包括种族、语言和文化。这些殖民地视英国为“母国”，而非帝国侵略者，并且它们所受到的待遇与英国控制的非白人殖民地截然不同。例如，白人殖民殖民地被赋予了相当大的自治权，并被授予自治领地位（在英联邦内享有政治自治权），而无需诉诸武力。事实上，正是白人殖民者，如同英国在其他地方所做的那样，征服了非白人土著居民，掠夺了他们的土地和自然资源。换言之，这些理论家认为，将白人殖民文化纳入“后殖民”范畴，忽略了种族在殖民历史中扮演的巨大角色，以及种族在当今种族主义态度中持续发挥的作用，而这种种族主义态度正是第三世界和第四世界人民遭受经济压迫的根源。

Those who argue that the term postcolonial should be reserved for Third and Fourth World writers observe that white settler cultures share a tremendous common ground with Britain, including race, language, and culture. These colonies viewed Britain as the “mother country,” not as an imperial invader, and they were treated very differently from the nonwhite colonies Britain controlled. For example, white settler colonies were permitted a good deal of self-government and were granted Dominion status (political autonomy within the British Commonwealth) without having to take up arms to achieve it. Indeed, it was white settlers who, as Britain did elsewhere, subjugated nonwhite indigenous peoples and took their land and natural resources. In other words, these theorists argue, the inclusion of white settler cultures under the postcolonial rubric ignores the enormous difference race has played in the history of colonization and continues to play today in the racist attitudes that keep Third and Fourth World peoples economically oppressed.

另一方面，一些理论家认为，白人殖民文化也应被纳入后殖民范畴。他们认为，后殖民批评的基础概念是反殖民抵抗，而白人殖民文化的文学作品能够很好地帮助我们理解反殖民抵抗的复杂性。这是因为他们自身对英国文化压倒性影响的文化消亡的抵抗，并非建立在殖民者和被殖民者之间清晰的界限之上——而这种界限对于非白人入侵殖民地而言却是毋庸置疑的。换言之，白人殖民者以一种更为微妙、界限更为模糊的形式，体验着与非白人殖民者相同的双重意识。由此可见，我们不能简单地忽视第二世界国家产生的反殖民主义文学，却不加批判地假定所有非白人后殖民民族的文学作品都必然是抵抗文学。

On the other hand, theorists who believe white settler cultures should be included under the rubric postcolonial argue that the foundational concept of postcolonial criticism is anticolonial resistance, and the literatures of white settler cultures have a good deal to teach us about the complexities of anticolonial resistance because their own resistance to cultural obliteration by an overwhelming British cultural presence has occurred without the help of a clear distinction between colonized and colonizer, a distinction that nonwhite invader colonies have been able to count on. In other words, white colonial subjects experience – in a subtler, less clearly demarcated form – the same double consciousness experienced by nonwhite colonial subjects. From this perspective, we can’t simply ignore the anticolonialist literature produced by the Second World while we uncritically assume that all the literature produced by nonwhite postcolonial peoples is necessarily a literature of resistance.

另一个引起后殖民理论家关注的争论是，后殖民理论本身是否面临着边缘化其希望关注群体声音的危险。一方面，大多数后殖民理论家——包括那些出生于前殖民地国家、其中许多人曾在欧洲大学接受教育并生活在国外的人——都属于知识精英阶层，一个学术统治阶级，他们似乎与底层民众，也就是他们所关注的大多数贫困、受剥削的前殖民地人民，几乎没有任何共同之处。

Another debate that has engaged the attention of postcolonial theorists involves the concern that postcolonial theory is itself in danger of marginalizing the voices of those it wishes to bring into the spotlight. For one thing, most postcolonial theorists – including those born in formerly colonized nations, many of whom were educated at European universities and live abroad – belong to an intellectual elite, an academic ruling class that has, it would seem, little in common with subalterns, or people of inferior status, that is, with the majority of poor, exploited ex-colonial peoples who are the object of their concern.

此外，后殖民批评对文化认同问题的分析——特别是其对文化认同的流动性、动态性和混合性的关注——很大程度上是第一世界后结构主义解构理论的产物。正如你可能在第八章中了解到的，解构主义将自我定义为……无数“自我”碎片拼凑而成，存在于一个没有稳定意义、价值也完全由我们赋予的世界之中。这种理论对于理解我们如何利用文化提供的意识形态素材构建自身身份的幻象极为有益。解构主义已被有效地用于揭示西方哲学和文学强加于世界其他地区的欧洲中心主义。然而，可以理解的是，那些正努力定义自身文化身份的国家可能并不觉得这种颠覆性的理论很有吸引力，并且由于长期遭受西方统治，它们可能普遍对西方理论抱有不信任感。

Furthermore, postcolonial criticism’s analysis of the problem of cultural identity – specifically, its focus on the fluid, dynamic, hybrid forms of cultural identity – is largely a product of the poststructuralist, deconstructive theory of the First World. As you may recall from Chapter 8, deconstruction defines the self as a fragmented pastiche of numerous “selves” within a world that has no stable meaning and no value beyond that which we assign it. Such a theory is extremely helpful in allowing us to understand how we construct the illusion of our own identity out of the ideological materials provided by our culture. And deconstruction has been used effectively to reveal the Eurocentrism of the Western philosophy and literature that have been imposed on the rest of the world. However, it is understandable that nations struggling to define their cultural identity might not find this destabilizing theory very attractive and might mistrust Western theories in general, having suffered Western domination for so long.

最后，由于后殖民批评可以用来解读西方文学经典，一些理论家长期以来一直担心，它将变成解读我们多年来一直在阅读的第一世界作家的另一种方式，而不是一种突出后殖民作家作品的方法。令人欣慰的是，鉴于奇努阿·阿切贝（尼日利亚）、萨尔曼·拉什迪（印度）、牙买加·金凯德（西印度群岛安提瓜）、贝西·海德（南非）、巴拉蒂·穆克吉（印度）、齐齐·丹加伦巴（津巴布韦）、莱斯利·马蒙·西尔科（美国拉古纳普韦布洛部落）、弗洛拉·恩瓦帕（尼日利亚）、扎克斯·姆达（南非）、爱德华·卡毛·布雷思韦特（巴巴多斯）、阿伦达蒂·罗伊（印度）、琳达·霍根（美国奇克索族）和恩古吉·瓦·提昂戈（肯尼亚）等后殖民作家在国际上取得的成功，这种担忧似乎不太可能成为现实。

Finally, because postcolonial criticism can be used to interpret literature in the Western literary canon, some theorists have been long concerned that it will become just one more way to read the same First World authors we’ve been reading for years, rather than a method that brings to the fore the works of postcolonial writers. Happily, it seems unlikely that this fear will be realized, given the international success of such postcolonial authors as, to name but a few, Chinua Achebe (Nigeria), Salman Rushdie (India), Jamaica Kincaid (Antigua, West Indies), Bessie Head (South Africa), Bharati Mukherjee (India), Tsitsi Dangarembga (Zimbabwe), Leslie Marmon Silko (Laguna Pueblo tribe, United States), Flora Nwapa (Nigeria), Zakes Mda (South Africa), Edward Kamau Brathwaite (Barbados), Arundhati Roy (India), Linda Hogan (Chickasaw Nation, United States), and Ngugi wa Thiong’o (Kenya).

事实上，1986年，沃莱·索因卡（尼日利亚）荣获诺贝尔文学奖；1991年，纳丁·戈迪默（南非）获奖；1992年，德里克·沃尔科特（西印度群岛圣卢西亚）获奖；1993年，托妮·莫里森（美国）获奖；2001年，V·S·奈保尔（特立尼达）获奖；2003年，J·M·库切（南非）获奖。此外，开设后殖民文学课程的院校数量也大幅增长，该领域已成为国际主流学科。

Indeed, the Nobel Prize for literature was won by Wole Soyinka (Nigeria) in 1986, by Nadine Gordimer (South Africa) in 1991, by Derek Walcott (St. Lucia, West Indies) in 1992, by Toni Morrison (United States) in 1993,5 by V. S. Naipaul (Trinidad) in 2001, and by J. M. Coetzee (South Africa) in 2003. And there has been such a great increase in the number of colleges offering courses in postcolonial literature that the field has become an international staple.

然而，担心后殖民文学会被“殖民化”，即按照欧洲的规范和标准来解读，并非毫无道理。因为文化上的欧洲中心主义仍然主导着世界各地的文学教育和文学批评。

Nevertheless, it’s not unreasonable to be apprehensive that postcolonial literature will be “colonized,” that is, interpreted according to European norms and standards. For cultural Eurocentrism still dominates literary education and literary criticism the world over.

在思考所有这些问题时，请记住，“基础性辩论”与“以往的辩论”含义不同。许多构成后殖民思想基础的论点在今天仍然至关重要。C·迈克尔·霍尔和黑兹尔·塔克指出，“核心问题——何为后殖民文本——仍然是一个争论不休的问题”(1)，这一观点也适用于后殖民理论的大部分基础哲学。这种将自身领域的核心要素视为问题而非前提或“既定事实”的意愿，无疑是众多后殖民理论家和文学批评家能够以如此深刻的洞察力和个人参与来回应我们这个快速变化的世界的原因之一。

As you think about all of these issues, keep in mind that the phrase foundational debates does not have the same meaning as the phrase former debates. Many of the arguments that helped form the foundation of postcolonial thinking are still vital issues today. C. Michael Hall and Hazel Tucker’s observation that “the central question – what constitutes a postcolonial text – remains a contentious issue” (1) can be said of much of postcolonial theory’s foundational philosophy. This willingness to see the core elements of one’s field as questions rather than as premises, or “givens,” is surely one of the reasons why so many postcolonial theorists and literary critics continue to respond to our rapidly changing world with such insight and personal engagement.

全球化与后殖民理论的“终结”

Globalization and the “end” of postcolonial theory

或许，当今后殖民批评家们最关注的发展之一，是包括一些经济学家在内的学者认为后殖民理论整体上已经过时。他们认为，殖民主义在很大程度上在二战后不久就结束了。而曾经被殖民的人民为建立自己的政府、传承自己的文化遗产等等所做的努力，已经被国际文化和全球经济的全球传播所掩盖——或者更准确地说，是被其所吸收。这些传播影响了所有民族，无论他们是否属于后殖民国家。正如你可能已经注意到的，文化产品——例如音乐、电影、文学作品、时尚以及各种消费品——已经全球化，这主要归功于互联网和其他电子信息通信方式在全球范围内的不断普及。事实上，如今分隔世界各国的地理边界在许多方面都变得不如连接世界各国人民的互联网能力重要。

Perhaps one of the most interesting developments engaging the attention of postcolonial critics today is what some economists, among others, consider the outdated quality of the field of postcolonial theory as a whole. Colonialism, the argument goes, ended, by and large, shortly after World War II. And the efforts of formerly colonized peoples to create their own governments, establish their own cultural heritage, and the like, have been overshadowed by – or perhaps more accurately, absorbed within – the worldwide spread of international culture and global economics that have affected all peoples, whether postcolonial or not. As you’ve probably noticed, cultural production – for example, music, movies, literary works, fashion, and a variety of consumer products – has gone global due largely to the continually increasing global access to the Internet and other forms of electronic information and communication. Indeed, the geographic borders that separate the nations of the world today are becoming, in many ways, less important than the Internet capabilities that connect the peoples of the world.

此外，这种文化全球化——或者说技术、产品和理念的全球传播——很大程度上归功于经济全球化，而经济全球化可以定义为资本主义在各国政府干预极少的情况下在全球范围内的传播。那么，经济全球化是如何实现的呢？它是由通用电气、埃克森美孚、英国石油和丰田等跨国公司的成功所促成的。<sup> 6 </sup> 这些跨国公司，尤其是总部位于美国的跨国公司，在以前从未涉足这些行业的国家开发技术和生产产品，进而将产品销售到以前从未有过市场的国家。正如它们的发言人所指出的那样，跨国公司通过在当地建设工厂和其他类型的工作场所、创造当地就业机会以及培训当地工人，为发展中国家的经济发展做出了贡献。因此，他们得出结论：如果我们想探讨当今世界文化转型和个人身份认同的发展——无论我们认为这些变化是好是坏——我们都必须认识到，后殖民时代早已过去，后殖民理论也随之失去了意义。简而言之，他们的论点是，在全球化时代，我们需要一套全球化理论，或许可以借鉴国际关系理论，但我们不再需要后殖民理论。

Furthermore, this kind of cultural globalization – or worldwide spread of technologies, products, and ideas – is due largely to the globalization of economics, which can be defined as the worldwide spread of capitalism with minimal interference from national governments. And how did the globalization of economics come about? It was created by the success of multinational corporations such as General Electric, ExxonMobil, British Petroleum, and Toyota.6 For multinational corporations, with those based in the United States leading the way, develop technology and manufacture products in countries that never before housed these industries and, in turn, sell products in countries that never before had markets for them. As their spokespersons point out, multinational corporations contribute to the economies of developing nations by building local factories and other kinds of workplaces, by creating local jobs, and by training local workers. So, they conclude, if we want to talk about the transformation of culture and the development of individual identity in the world today – whether we believe these changes are for good or ill – we need to realize that the postcolonial world is long gone, and with it has gone the usefulness of postcolonial theory. In short, the argument goes, in an age of globalization we need a theory of globalization, perhaps along the lines of international relations theory, but we don’t need postcolonial theory.

然而，我们必须提出这样一个问题：为什么全球化意味着后殖民理论不再适用？这个结论准确吗？诚然，殖民主义不再像15世纪末到20世纪中叶那样，由殖民国的总督和教育者直接、公开地进行统治。然而，如今，同样的政治、经济和文化上的征服依然在脆弱地区上演，只不过手段有所不同，而施暴者正是那些成就全球化的跨国公司。这使得后殖民批评的相关性受到质疑。这些手段包括后殖民批评家所称的文化帝国主义和新殖民主义。

The question must be raised, however: Why does globalization mean that postcolonial theory is no longer relevant? Is this conclusion an accurate one? It’s true that colonialism is no longer practiced as it was between the late fifteenth and midtwentieth centuries, through the direct, overt administration of governors and educators from the colonizing country. Today, nevertheless, the same kind of political, economic, and cultural subjugation of vulnerable regions occurs, through different means, at the hands of the very multinational corporations whose success has called into question the relevance of postcolonial criticism. These means include what postcolonial critics call cultural imperialism and neocolonialism.

你可能已经听说过一些文化帝国主义的例子，有时也被称为文化殖民，尽管你可能以前没听过这两个词。文化帝国主义通常是跨国公司经常实施的经济统治的结果。它指的是一种文化被另一种文化“接管”：经济上占主导地位的文化的食物、服装、习俗、娱乐和价值观逐渐取代经济上处于弱势地位的文化，直到后者看起来像是前者的某种模仿者。美国文化帝国主义是这种现象最普遍的形式之一，我们看到美国的时尚、电影、音乐、体育、快餐、消费品以及对个人美和成功的定义正在世界各地挤压区域和民族的文化传统。最近，我听到一些学生开玩笑说，大家不必担心某个国家“统治世界”，因为可口可乐和耐克已经做到了。我想他们并没有意识到，他们谈论的正是文化帝国主义的迹象。

You’re probably already aware of some examples of cultural imperialism, sometimes called cultural colonization, although you might not have heard these two terms before. Cultural imperialism is often a result of the kind of economic domination frequently imposed by multinational corporations. It consists of the “takeover” of one culture by another: the food, clothing, customs, recreation, and values of the economically dominant culture increasingly replace those of the economically vulnerable culture until the latter appears to be a kind of imitation of the former. American cultural imperialism has been one of the most pervasive forms of this phenomenon, as we see American fashions, movies, music, sports, fast food, consumer products, and definitions of personal beauty and success squeeze out regional and national cultural traditions all over the world. Recently, I heard some of my students joking that no one need worry about a single country “taking over the world” because Coca Cola and Nike have already done it. I don’t think they realized it, but they were talking about signs of cultural imperialism.

或许对我们许多人来说，企业全球化常常以新殖民主义的形式运作这一事实并不那么显而易见，但其影响却更为广泛。新殖民主义，即对发展中国家廉价劳动力的剥削，往往以牺​​牲这些国家自身举步维艰的企业、文化传统和生态福祉为代价。跨国公司可能会与它们想要扩张的国家的政府建立合作关系，或者获得少数相对富裕的个人的支持，这些人将从跨国公司的存在中获利。但该国的大多数弱势群体却未必能从中受益。事实上，即使跨国公司与一国政府合作，也并不意味着该国的弱势群体或自然资源就能得到保护。例如，一家公司为了获取土地或修建巨型水坝发电，可能迫使整个社区甚至几个社区离开家园、农场和渔场，最终沦为大城市贫民窟的居民。虽然就业机会往往由此产生，但童工现象却屡见不鲜。无论工人是儿童还是成人，他们通常都收入微薄、工时过长，且工作环境恶劣。有时，木材、石油、矿产和贵金属等自然资源本身就成了被“收割”和掠夺的目标。有时，土壤、水、空气、动物和植被等自然资源也会因工业活动造成的污染、土壤侵蚀和动物栖息地减少而受到威胁或破坏。为了让您了解问题的严重性，我们不妨简要看一下三个具有代表性的例子——实际上还有数百个例子——来说明跨国公司在第三世界不受监管或监管不力的活动常常造成的破坏。各国。我们的第一个例子来自全球石油工业，第二个例子来自全球服装工业，第三个例子来自全球农业综合企业，后者包括大规模、高科技的农作物和机械的商业化生产和分销。

Perhaps less obvious to many of us, but certainly more wide-ranging in its worldwide effects, is the fact that corporate globalization frequently operates as a form of neocolonialism. Neo – that is, new – colonialism consists of the exploitation of the cheap labor available in developing countries, often at the expense of those countries’ own struggling businesses, cultural traditions, and ecological well-being. Multinational corporations may form partnerships with the governments of the nations into which they want to expand, or they may gain the support of the relatively wealthy, and relatively few, individuals who will benefit financially from their corporate presence. But the subaltern majority of the country’s inhabitants do not necessarily derive any benefit. Indeed, even when a multinational corporation partners with a national government, it doesn’t mean that the nation’s subaltern inhabitants or natural resources are protected. For example, an entire community, or several communities, may be driven from their homes, farms, and fisheries – driven away only to add to the population of slum dwellers in the big cities – by a corporation’s need for land or for new mega-dams to create waterpower. And while jobs are frequently created, child labor is often used, and whether the workers are children or adults, they usually receive low pay, work long hours, and endure unsafe working conditions. Sometimes natural resources – in the form of timber, oil, minerals, and precious metals – are themselves the desired commodities to be “harvested” and taken away. Sometimes natural resources – in the form of soil, water, air, animals, and vegetation – are imperiled or destroyed by the pollution, soil erosion, and reduction of animal habitat that result from industrial operations. To give you an idea of the scope of this problem, let’s take a brief look at three representative examples – there are hundreds more – of the damage often done by unregulated or under-regulated multinational corporate activity in Third World nations. Our first example comes from the global oil industry, our second from the global garment industry, and our third from global agribusiness, which consists of the wide-scale, high-tech, commercial production and distribution of agricultural crops and machinery.

在尼日利亚尼日尔三角洲地区，英荷石油公司皇家荷兰壳牌公司肆意倾倒石油废料，因管道腐蚀频繁发生石油泄漏，以及石油开采产生的天然气排放，破坏了农民的土地、森林和鱼类资源。当地居民并未从石油工业的存在中获得任何好处，反而承受着由此带来的种种后果：空气不再适宜呼吸，大部分土地无法耕种，当地鱼类几乎消失殆尽，饮用水也已无法饮用。正如国际特赦组织所指出的，这种自20世纪50年代以来持续不断的污染和环境破坏，已经造成了人权侵犯，甚至包括当地居民获得食物和水的权利。7.另一种持续不断的灾难正在孟加拉国发生。当地工人在不安全的建筑物中，在危险的工作环境下，为沃尔玛、西尔斯和盖璞等美国品牌，邦玛奇和普里马克等英国品牌，以及芒果、C&A和贝纳通等欧洲品牌生产服装，这些工人大多是十几岁或二十出头的年轻人，工资微薄。2012年11月24日，臭名昭著的塔兹林服装厂发生火灾，至少112名工人因无法逃离燃烧的工厂而丧生。2013年4月24日，位于孟加拉国的拉纳广场大楼倒塌，造成1000多名工人死亡，这座八层楼的建筑结构简陋，内设五家服装厂。这仅仅是孟加拉国服装业一系列灾难中的两起。8最后，瑞士跨国食品饮料公司雀巢数十年来一直在哥伦比亚、斯里兰卡和菲律宾等国摧毁本土乳制品产业，其手段是用大量分销雀巢加工的、通常是进口的牛奶和奶制品来取代当地生产的乳制品。当地鲜奶奶场因此消失，雀巢奶制品的价格也随之上涨。在挤压当地奶农的同时，该公司还开展了欺诈性的营销活动，诱使第三世界国家的母亲们用雀巢婴儿配方奶粉喂养婴儿，而不是母乳。这场营销活动的成功导致数十万婴儿死于传染病，这些传染病是由于必须将配方奶粉与当地水混合，以及缺乏母乳所能提供的免疫力造成的。雀巢的不道德行为导致其产品在全球范围内长期遭到抵制，但该公司对此的回应仍然远远不够。9

In the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, Royal Dutch Shell, an Anglo-Dutch oil company, has destroyed farmers’ lands, forestland, and fish populations through the unchecked dumping of petroleum waste, frequent oil spills due to corroded pipelines, and natural gas emissions that result from oil extraction. Local residents receive no benefit whatsoever from the presence of the oil industry on their land, but they are the ones who suffer the consequences of that presence: their air is no longer fit to breathe, much of their land will no longer produce agricultural crops, the local fish population has all but disappeared, and their water is no longer drinkable. As Amnesty International points out, this kind of pollution and environmental damage, which has been ongoing since the 1950s, has resulted in human rights violations, including the violation even of the local residents’ right to their own food and water.7 A different kind of ongoing devastation has been occurring in Bangladesh, where garments are manufactured in unsafe buildings under dangerous working conditions by underpaid local workers, many in their teens and early twenties, for such American brands as Wal-Mart, Sears, and the Gap; such British brands as Bonmarché and Primark; and such European brands as Mango, C&A, and Benetton. At least 112 workers, unable to escape their burning factory, were killed in the infamous Tazreen factory fire on November 24, 2012, and on April 24, 2013, over 1,000 workers were killed when the poorly constructed, eight-story Rana Plaza, which housed five garment factories, collapsed. These are just two in a long series of disasters related to the garment industry in Bangladesh.8 Finally, Nestlé, the multinational Swiss food and beverage company, has a decades-long history of destroying indigenous dairy industries in such countries as Colombia, Sri Lanka, and the Philippines by replacing locally made dairy products with the mass distribution of Nestlé’s processed, often imported, milk and milk substitutes. When local fresh-milk dairy farms are thereby eliminated, the prices of Nestlé’s milk products go up. In tandem with the squeezing out of local dairy farmers is the company’s fraudulent marketing campaign to convince Third World mothers to feed their babies Nestlé’s infant formula instead of breast milk. The success of this campaign has resulted in hundreds of thousands of infant deaths from infectious diseases caused by the necessity of mixing the formula with local water and by the absence of the immunities that would have been provided by breast milk. Nestlé’s unethical practices have resulted in a longstanding global boycott of their products, but the company’s response to this outcry remains grossly inadequate.9

正如这些例子所示，新殖民主义跨国公司唯一真正关心的，是企业利润的增值，而不是当地人民或当地环境的福祉。事实上，当需要时，新殖民主义跨国公司企业靠贿赂（必要时，企业会收买各级政府官员以维护自身利益）和公开或秘密的武装干预来维持运转（有时是资助地方警察和军队以保护企业的政治利益，有时是向与企业利益最为密切的西方强权寻求军事援助）。尽管数十年来，基层民众一直在有组织地抵抗新殖民主义企业造成的破坏，但这场博弈中蕴藏着巨大的利益，而主要参与者势力过于强大，根本不受任何公平竞争规则的约束。

As these examples illustrate, the well-being of corporate profits, not of the local peoples or the local environment, is the only real concern of neocolonialist multinational corporations. Indeed, when the need arises, neocolonialist corporate enterprise is supported by bribery (officials at every level of government, if necessary, paid by a corporation to support its interests) and by overt or covert armed intervention (sometimes in the form of financing local police and military troops to protect corporate political interests, sometimes in the form of enlisting military aid from the Western power most closely aligned with the corporation’s concerns). Although there is a decades-long history of organized grassroots local resistance to the destruction wreaked by neocolonialist corporate enterprise,10 there is big money to be made in this game, and the major players are too powerful to be bound by any rules of fair play.

简而言之，许多跨国公司及其合作伙伴政府所称的“发展”项目——即通过现代化手段“发展”贫困地区——对生活在这些地区的贫困人口而言，却并非如此。显然，殖民剥削和后殖民抵抗的政治、经济和文化现实已经呈现出新的形式，但它们依然存在。放弃后殖民理论提供的洞见所带来的危险在于，我们将越来越难以认识这些现实，因而也越来越难以应对。

In short, what many multinational corporations, and the governments with which they partner, refer to as their “development” projects – they are “developing” poor regions by modernizing them – are anything but for the poor people who inhabit those regions. Clearly, the political, economic, and cultural realities of colonialist exploitation and postcolonial resistance have taken new forms, but they are still with us. The danger in abandoning the insights offered by postcolonial theory is that it will become increasingly difficult to recognize, and therefore to respond to, these realities.

后殖民理论与全球旅游

Postcolonial theory and global tourism

当你阅读上一节并思考跨国公司时，你是否想到了迪士尼、地中海俱乐部或维京河轮之类的名字？可能没有。我们通常不会将“跨国公司”这个听起来颇为吓人、严肃的词组与湛蓝的天空、波光粼粼的白色沙滩、一尘不染的高尔夫球场，或是身着运动服、笑容满面的人们在美丽度假胜地尽情享受的景象联系起来。然而，旅游业已经发展成为一个产业，而且这个产业已经走向全球，但它并非总是“阳光下的乐趣”——至少对所有参与者而言并非如此。想想看，在任何特定情况下，一个旅游度假村的开发究竟会惠及谁，又会损害谁的利益？

As you were reading the previous section and thinking about multinational corporations, did names like Disney or Club Med or Viking River Cruises occur to you? Probably not. We don’t tend to associate the rather intimidating, stern-sounding phrase multinational corporation with images of clear blue skies, sparkling white beaches, spotless putting greens, or smiling people in sports clothes enjoying themselves at a beautiful vacation spot. Nevertheless tourism has become an industry, that industry has gone global, and it isn’t always just “fun in the sun” – at least not for everyone involved. Think about it. In any given instance, who benefits from and who is hurt by the development of a tourist resort?

当然，很多时候旅游业带来的益处远不止于此，很少有人受到伤害，甚至无人受到伤害。例如，一些由当地管理的旅游景点，如风景优美的湖滨、森林公园、历史遗迹、露营地等等，都对公众开放且价格合理。在这种情况下，当地企业得到扶持，当地经济得到支持或改善，当地居民也从中受益。例如，当地居民可以在当地休闲娱乐，可以从事旅游业创造的工作，或者可以创办自己的小型旅游相关企业。

Well, surely there are many times when few or none are hurt while many people benefit from tourism, for example in the case of locally controlled tourist attractions – such as lovely lakefronts, forested parks, interesting historical sites, campgrounds, and the like – all open to and affordable by the general public. In such cases, local businesses receive a boost, local economies are supported or improved, and local inhabitants are benefitted. For example, local residents can themselves spend leisure time locally, can take jobs created by local tourism, or can start their own small tourist-related businesses.

相比之下，许多面向国际旅游市场、通常由外国投资者与当地银行家、房地产公司或其他精英金融家联手支持的全球旅游景点，既超出了普通当地居民的掌控范围，也超出了他们的经济承受能力。“精英们发展中国家从旅游业发展中获益往往远超普通民众，例如，地价飙升以及在吸引外国投资方面享有特权（M. Smith，引自 Jaakson，170）。因此，尽管“一个国家的整体收入可能增加……但贫富差距可能保持不变，甚至扩大”（Jaakson，170）。许多类型的全球旅游都符合这一模式，从宣传自然奇观的壮丽或风景优美的地区，到宣传可供游客用相机或枪支拍摄的各种大型野生动物，再到宣传当地居民及其文化的“异域风情”。当然，全球旅游的形式多种多样，每一种都与各国政府和当地民众有着冲突、妥协和合作的历史。这些民众的家园——无论好坏——都已成为大众旅游目的地或富裕精英的高端度假胜地。

In contrast, many global tourist attractions – geared to an international tourist market and often supported by foreign investors in conjunction with local bankers, local real-estate companies, or other elite local financiers – are beyond both the influence and the pocketbooks of the general local population. “[E]lites in developing countries consistently gain disproportionately more [than the general population] from tourism development, as for example through soaring land values and from favouritism in the participation in investments from abroad” (M. Smith, cited in Jaakson, 170). Thus, while “[i]ncome may increase overall in a country … the wealth gap may remain the same or may even widen” (Jaakson, 170). Many kinds of global tourism fit this model, from those that market the grandeur of natural wonders or the beauty of scenic locales, to those that market the range of large wildlife available for shooting with camera or gun, to those that market the perceived “exotic” quality of the local inhabitants and their cultures. Of course, there are many varieties of global tourism,11 and each has its history of conflicts, compromises, and partnerships with national governments and with the local peoples whose homelands – for good or ill – have become either mass-market tourist destinations or upscale vacation locations for the wealthy elite.

不幸的是，当地居民常常被剥夺了进入祖传森林、丛林和牧场的权利，以便为付费游客腾出空间；许多农村居民甚至被迫离开家园，放弃传统的生计，只为建造旅游住宿设施，这些设施通常包括建在旅游景点附近甚至内部的豪华酒店和公寓。当然，经济拮据使发展中国家更容易受到这种剥削，而其技术落后、生物多样性丰富的土地也使其对那些企图从中牟利的人更具吸引力。因此，受全球旅游业负面影响最大的国家是那些殖民剥削历史遗留下的经济劣势严重的第三世界国家，这些国家的政府甚至主动寻求投资者来“开发”和推广其潜在的全球旅游景点。因为全球旅游业被视为这些国家提升其在全球市场经济地位的唯一途径，尽管这种提升往往是以牺牲本国农村居民的利益为代价的。在此背景下，全球旅游业引起了后殖民理论的极大兴趣：如今，旅游业在脆弱的后殖民国家的存在，常常会产生与几个世纪前盎格鲁-欧洲殖民势力存在时类似的负面影响。

Unfortunately, it is often the case that local peoples are denied access to their ancestral forests, jungles, and pasturelands to make way for paying tourists, and many rural peoples have been simply evicted from their homes and their traditional livelihoods to make way for tourist accommodations, which often include luxury hotels and condominiums built near, if not within, tourist attractions. Of course, a struggling economy makes a developing nation vulnerable to such exploitation, and its technologically undeveloped, biologically diverse lands make it attractive to those who would profit by that vulnerability. So the nations that incur the most negative effects of global tourism are those of the Third World whose history of colonial exploitation has left them so economically disadvantaged that their governments embrace, even seek, investors to “develop” and market their potential global tourist attractions. For global tourism is seen as perhaps the only means by which such countries can improve their economic standing in the global marketplace, albeit too often at the expense of their own rural inhabitants. In this context, the global tourism industry is of great interest to postcolonial theory: too often, the industry’s presence in vulnerable postcolonial nations today has much the same negative impact as the presence of Anglo-European colonial forces had in centuries past.

以菲律宾哈辛达洛克（Hacienda Looc，发音为“洛克” ）居民的处境为例。<sup> 12</sup>这个位于南海沿岸、马尼拉西南约60英里的乡村社区由四个村庄组成，约有10,000名居民，占据着8,650公顷（1公顷=2.47英亩）的祖传沿海农田。当地居民世世代代都在这片土地上成功且可持续地耕作和捕鱼。1991年至1993年间，菲律宾土地改革部向村民颁发了哈辛达洛克5,000公顷土地的土地所有权证书。同时，政府还将哈辛达洛克全部8,650公顷土地以“无限量合同”的形式出售给了两家房地产开发商：Fil-Estate和马尼拉南海岸开发公司。现在，请听我说完。这份合同，可以被视为一份……由于投机性购买，开发商获得了在哈辛达洛克（Hacienda Looc）3650公顷未受农民土地所有权证书保护的土地上建造旅游景点和住宿设施的权利，而开发商也确实这样做了。合同还赋予他们开发农民保护土地中任何他们能够证明不适宜耕种的部分的权利。1996年，菲尔地产公司（Fil-Estate）和马尼拉南海岸开发公司（Manila Southcoast Development Corporation）联合提起诉讼，最终胜诉，得以开发哈辛达洛克此前受农民土地所有权证书保护的1219公顷土地。这些地块的所有权证书被取消，理由是这些土地平均坡度超过18%，且未用于农业耕作。当地居民管理的、种植着各种果树的林地，为他们提供重要的主食，也属于可以改造成旅游景点的土地之列。简而言之，开发商从当地居民手中夺走了维护良好、物产丰饶的沿海土地，这些居民依靠这些土地谋生，并世代守护着它们。事实上，正是这片土地和沿海水域的优良条件，才使得该地区最初对开发商具有吸引力。

As a case in point, consider the situation of the people of Hacienda Looc (pronounced low-ahk) in the Philippines.12 This rural community, located on the South China Sea about 60 miles southwest of Manila, consists of four villages inhabited by roughly 10,000 people and occupying 8,650 hectares (1 hectare = 2.47 acres) of ancestral coastal farmland, which the inhabitants have successfully and sustainably farmed and fished for many generations. Between 1991 and 1993, the Philippine Department of Agrarian Reform issued the villagers Certificates of Land Ownership Awards for 5,000 hectares of Hacienda Looc. The government also sold what is called an Indefinite Quantity Contract for all 8,650 hectares of Hacienda Looc to two real-estate developers, Fil-Estate and Manila Southcoast Development Corporation. Now, stay with me here. This contract, which might be thought of as a purchase made on speculation, gave developers the right to proceed with the building of tourist attractions and accommodations on the 3,650 hectares of Hacienda Looc not protected by the farmers’ certificates of land ownership, which is what developers proceeded to do. The contract also gave them the right to develop whatever portions of the farmers’ protected land that they could show were not suitable for farming, and in 1996 Fil-Estate and Manila Southcoast Development Corporation won their joint suit to develop 1,219 hectares of Hacienda Looc that had been thus far protected by farmers’ certificates of ownership. The certificates for these parcels were cancelled because, it was argued, the land therein had an average slope of 18 percent or more and had not been used for agricultural crops.
