Wooded land containing a variety of fruit trees, managed by the inhabitants and providing important staples in their diet, was among the land that could be converted into tourism sites. In short, developers took well-maintained, productive coastal lands away from the people who have inhabited them, gained their livelihoods from them, and preserved them for generations. Indeed, it was the excellent condition of the land and the coastal waters that made the area attractive to developers in the first place.

当卢克庄园的居民拒绝离开，继续耕作和捕鱼，并开始上诉要求收回土地时，他们并不知道等待着他们的将是怎样的麻烦。国家警察、菲律宾军方人员以及开发商雇佣的保安被派往庄园“维持秩序”。随后，农民和渔民遭到这些全副武装的执法人员的骚扰：他们受到武装警卫的言语威胁；他们的房屋遭到非法搜查；许多房屋被毁；许多渔民被禁止捕鱼；至少有七名居民在未得到调查的事件中丧生，他们都曾公开反对土地被征用。一些居民因不堪恐吓而搬离了庄园。一些居民被迫搬离家园，因为他们的土地上建起了一座海滨度假村。这座度假村包括九栋六七层高的豪华公寓楼、一家设有乡村俱乐部和水疗中心的豪华酒店，以及由高尔夫冠军哈尔·欧文和弗雷德·卡波斯设计的两座高尔夫球场，占据了大片曾经的农田和森林。由于耕作和捕鱼技能不再有用，一些居民只能前往马尼拉寻找低薪工作，如今生活在城市的贫困地区。留在哈辛达洛克的居民则饱受推土机砍伐森林造成的土壤侵蚀、洪水和山体滑坡之苦，以及每年在高尔夫球场喷洒两吨除草剂和杀虫剂造成的水污染和空气污染。农民权益组织——在地方、国家和国际层面——仍在为哈辛达洛克的居民寻求正义。然而，当地居民所处的冲突状态依然悬而未决。

When inhabitants of Hacienda Looc refused to leave, kept working their farms and fisheries, and began to file appeals to regain their land, they could not know what trouble awaited them. National police officers, members of the Philippine military, and security guards hired by the developers were sent in to “keep the peace.” Subsequently, farmers and fisherfolk have been harassed by these heavily armed deputies: they’ve been verbally threatened by armed guards; their homes have been subject to illegal searches; many of their dwellings have been destroyed; many of the fisherfolk have been prevented from fishing; and at least seven inhabitants, all of whom spoke out against the seizure of their land, have been killed in incidents that were not investigated. Some inhabitants have moved away as a result of this intimidation. Some have moved away because a residential beach resort has been built on their homeland, a resort which includes nine six- and seven-story buildings housing luxury residential condominiums, a luxury hotel with country club and spa, and two golf courses, designed by champion golfers Hale Irwin and Fred Couples, that occupy large tracts of former farmland and forest. With their farming and fishing skills no longer of any use to them, some inhabitants have taken what low-paying jobs they could find in Manila and now live in the city’s impoverished areas. Those who remain in Hacienda Looc are subject to soil erosion, floods, and landslides, caused by the bulldozing of forests, and to the water and air pollution caused by the two tons of weed-killers and insecticides sprayed on the golf courses annually. Peasants’ rights organizations – at the local, national, and international level – continue to seek justice for the people of Hacienda Looc. The state of conflict in which the locals live, however, remains unsettled.

令人痛心的是，哈辛达洛克（Hacienda Looc）人民所遭受的土地掠夺，在菲律宾农村乃至世界各地都在发生。印度、西藏……东南亚、非洲、中南美洲、加勒比海地区等国家和地区都曾经历过或正在经历此类变革。即使是生态旅游——尽管其初衷是作为一种可持续、环保的旅游形式，尊重自然美景并向全球游客开放——也常常既不可持续也不环保。例如，第三世界网络（TWN）在致联合国的一封信中指出，在泰国，“生态旅游需求的激增导致农村和自然地区出现建设热潮，以便为游客提供住宿和基础设施（例如道路、电力和下水道）”（引自Higham 11）。13此外，第三世界国家未受破坏的农村土地的国际市场也在不断增长。例如，豪华“度假产权”的吸引力正在上升：一个规模相对较小但极其富裕的客户群体正在提升经济欠发达、气候温暖国家的乡村土地的市场价值，这些土地被用于开发诸如“高尔夫休闲社区”、“海滨住宅度假村”和“爱好或休闲农场”等豪华项目。正如我们在菲律宾哈米洛海岸的Pico de Loro豪华海滨度假村的在线广告中所看到的，客户可以在“令人叹为观止的自然环境中享受度假胜地的所有现代化舒适和奢华体验”。<sup> 14</sup>哈米洛海岸以前被称为帕帕亚，是洛克庄园的四个村庄之一。<sup> 15</sup>

Sadly, the land-grabbing from which the people of Hacienda Looc are suffering is occurring throughout the rural Philippines and throughout the world. India, Tibet, and the nations of Southeast Asia, Africa, Central and South America, the Caribbean, and more, have had and still have regions undergoing these kinds of changes. Even ecotourism – although intended as a sustainable, eco-friendly form of tourism respectful of the natural beauty opened to global visitors – is too often neither sustainable nor eco-friendly. For example, in a letter to the United Nations, Third World Network (TWN) reported that in Thailand an “upsurge of ecotourism demand had resulted in a construction frenzy in rural and natural areas to provide accommodation and infrastructure [such as roads, electricity, and sewers] for visitors” (cited in Higham 11).13 And the international market for unspoiled rural land in Third World countries is growing. For instance, the appeal of luxury “vacation ownership” is on the rise: a relatively small but very wealthy population of clients is increasing the marketability of, among other things, rural lands in economically underdeveloped, warm-climate countries for the creation of such luxury developments as “golf leisure communities,” “residential beach resorts,” and “hobby” or “leisure farms.” As we see in the online ad for Pico de Loro’s luxury beach resort at Hamilo Coast in the Philippines, clients can have the “complete modern comforts and luxuries of a vacation destination in a breathtaking natural setting.”14 Hamilo Coast used to be called Papaya, one of the four villages of Hacienda Looc.15

正如我们所见，在经济脆弱的后殖民国家，推动全球旅游业发展的动机至少有三方面：后殖民政府希望改善本国经济；精英投资者希望赚取巨额利润；以及数量相对较少但非常富有的国际客户群体希望购买属于自己的、未受破坏的热带天堂。此外，这种发展的动力还来自国界之外的政治力量。仅举一例，不妨看看美国国际开发署（USAID）对洛克庄园的立场。美国国际开发署成立于1961年，旨在为陷入困境的国家提供技术援助和培训、资源管理咨询以及财政援助。正如1999年纪录片《海湾战争》的旁白所说，美国国际开发署在1991年发布的一份报告中得出结论：“洛克庄园地区适合发展旅游业和土地用途转换”，也就是说，将农田和林地改造成旅游景点和住宿设施。

As we have seen, the incentive for a good deal of global tourism development in economically vulnerable postcolonial nations is, at least, threefold: postcolonial governments want to improve poor national economies; elite individual investors want to make large amounts of money; and a very wealthy though relatively small international clientele want to buy their own private, unspoiled tropical paradises. In addition, the impetus for such development comes from political forces beyond national borders. To cite just one example, consider the position on Hacienda Looc taken by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). USAID was formed in 1961 to provide technical assistance and training, resource-management advice, and financial aid to struggling nations. As the narrator of the 1999 documentary film The Golf War tells us, in 1991 USAID released a report concluding that “the Hacienda Looc area is right for tourism and land conversion,” that is, the conversion of farmland and woodland into tourist attractions and accommodations.

然而，从后殖民理论的角度来看，第三世界各地的农村地区——那些正面临或已经经历着与哈辛达洛克（Hacienda Looc）类似命运的地区——只有在我们透过殖民主义意识形态的视角来看待世界时，才被认为是“适合发展旅游业和土地用途的”。在这种视角下，世界各地的农村贫困人口要么因为全球旅游业的发展而受益，要么被视为进步进程中的附带损害，要么根本不值得关注。听起来是不是很耳熟？的确如此。如果我们用“文明”一词来代替“全球旅游业的发展和进步”，我们就会发现，如今这种看待第三世界农村贫困人口的观点与早期盎格鲁-欧洲殖民者的观点非常相似。殖民者将“新世界”视为“空地”——即无人居住的土地，任由他们为所欲为——因为实际上，他们认为当地居民并非盎格鲁-欧洲人，因此不完全是人。正如霍尔和塔克精辟地指出，“当代国际旅游的实践表明，先前基于殖民主义的经济结构、文化表征和剥削关系远未结束”（185）。<sup> 16</sup>

From the perspective of postcolonial theory, however, rural areas throughout the Third World – areas threatened by or already undergoing fates similar to that of Hacienda Looc – are “right for tourism and land conversion” only if we see the world through the lens of colonialist ideology, a lens through which the worldwide rural poor are considered better off as a result of global tourism development, or collateral damage from the forward march of progress, or not important enough to be considered at all. Sound familiar? It should. If we substitute the word civilization for global tourism development and progress, we will see that this perspective on the Third World rural poor today is much like that of the first Anglo-European colonizers who viewed the “New World” as “empty land” – that is, uninhabited land available to them for any purposes they desired – because, in effect, the native inhabitants were not Anglo-European and, therefore, not fully human. As Hall and Tucker aptly put the matter, “the practice of contemporary international tourism indicates that the economic structures, cultural representations and exploitative relationships that were previously based in colonialism are far from over” (185).16

后殖民理论与全球保护

Postcolonial theory and global conservation

诚然，当我们试图应对全球环境破坏的灾难时，后殖民理论的持续意义便显而易见。正如许多后殖民批评家所指出的，被殖民人民遭受的损失包括他们赖以生存的自然环境的枯竭或破坏，以及由此导致的家园乃至生命的丧失。正如我们在本章前面所看到的，这个问题至今依然存在：跨国公司的发展和全球旅游业的扩张持续消耗或破坏第三世界“欠发达”地区的资源，从而危及这些地区世世代代赖以生存的人类生命。事实上，自然保护主义和后殖民主义或许可以被视为两个伦理关注领域，它们在思想上本就密不可分，因为在现实中也从未分离：自然保护与人类生命的保护。

Certainly, the continued relevance of postcolonial theory can be seen today as we attempt to address the global catastrophe of environmental destruction. For as many postcolonial critics point out, the losses endured by colonized peoples included the depletion or destruction of the natural environments they inhabited and the consequent loss of their homelands and often their lives. And as we saw earlier in this chapter, the problem persists today: the growth of multinational corporations and the expansion of the global tourism industry continue to deplete or destroy “undeveloped” regions of the Third World, thereby jeopardizing the human life those regions had sustained for countless generations. Indeed, conservationism17 and postcolonialism might be seen as areas of ethical concern that never should have been separated in thought because they never have been separated in reality: the conservation of nature and the preservation of human life.

为什么自然保护主义和后殖民批评一直被视为，甚至被许多人视为两个独立甚至对立的研究领域？造成这种分歧的原因有很多，其中之一源于欧洲和英美两国根深蒂固的观念，即“自然”和“人”代表着截然相反的概念。例如，在环境问题上，后殖民批评倾向于强调人的因素：例如，土著社群在工业化和商业化全球扩张侵蚀的自然环境中挣扎求生。相比之下，源于拉尔夫·沃尔多·爱默生和亨利·戴维·梭罗等美国作家哲学思想的自然保护主义，则倾向于关注自然环境本身：渴望“原始荒野和保护‘未受破坏’的最后一片净土”，在那里人们可以追求“与自然永恒而宁静的交流时刻”（尼克松 236）。全球18个自然保护组织也同样渴望保护原始自然。他们效仿美国国家公园体系，几乎完全致力于保护荒野地区。然而，几乎每次都会发生这样的情况：自前殖民时代以来，原住民一直守护和保护着那些环保主义者认为正因人类活动而受到威胁的土地，结果往往是一场争夺地盘的战争，而原住民通常以失败告终。

Why have conservationism and postcolonial criticism been considered, and continue to be considered by many people, separate and even adversarial areas of enquiry? A number of reasons for the divide grew from the European and Anglo-American belief that the words nature and human represent diametrically opposed concepts. In terms of the environment, for example, postcolonial criticism tends to emphasize the human element: for instance, the struggle of native communities to survive in natural environments invaded by the global spread of industrialization and commercialization. In contrast, conservationism, which grew from the philosophies of such American writers as Ralph Waldo Emerson and Henry David Thoreau, tends to focus on the natural environment itself: the desire for “virgin wilderness and the preservation of ‘uncorrupted’ last great places” where one can pursue “timeless, solitary moments of communion with nature” (Nixon 236).18 Global conservation organizations share this desire for the protection of pristine nature. Modeled upon the American national park system, they focus their efforts almost exclusively on the preservation of wilderness areas. And when, as almost always happens, indigenous19 inhabitants have stewarded and preserved, since precolonial times, the very lands that conservationists believe are endangered by human presence, the result usually has been a turf war that indigenous inhabitants generally have lost.

事实上，许多后殖民主义思想家认为，大多数自然保护主义者对“荒野”一词的定义，是造成以下目标之间对立的主要原因：全球自然保护组织和后殖民主义对人权的关注。根据1964年《荒野法案》（美国公法88-577）C部分（该法案是当今大多数美国和全球自然保护组织所采用定义的来源），

Indeed, many postcolonial thinkers see the word wilderness, as it is defined by most conservationists, as a major cause of the antagonism between the goals of global conservation organizations and postcolonialist concerns about human rights. According to Part C of The Wilderness Act of 1964 (US Public Law 88–577), which is the source of the definition used today by most American and global conservation organizations,

与人类及其活动主导景观的地区不同，荒野在此被认定为地球及其生物群落不受人类干扰的区域，人类本身只是过客，不会在此久留。本法案进一步将荒野定义为未开发的联邦土地，保留其原始特征和影响，没有永久性设施或人类居住，并受到保护和管理以维护其自然条件，且符合以下条件：(1) 通常主要受自然力量影响，人类活动的痕迹几乎无法察觉；(2) 提供绝佳的独处机会或原始、自由的休闲方式；(3) 面积至少五千英亩，或足以使其在不受损害的状态下得到切实的保护和利用；(4) 也可能包含具有科学、教育、景观或历史价值的生态、地质或其他特征。

wilderness, in contrast with those areas where man and his works dominate the landscape, is hereby recognized as an area where the earth and its community of life are untrammeled by man, where man himself is a visitor who does not remain. An area of wilderness is further defined to mean in this Act an area of undeveloped Federal land retaining its primeval character and influence, without permanent improvements or human habitation, which is protected and managed so as to preserve its natural conditions and which (1) generally appears to have been affected primarily by the forces of nature, with the imprint of man’s work substantially unnoticeable; (2) has outstanding opportunities for solitude or a primitive and unconfined type of recreation; (3) has at least five thousand acres of land or is of sufficient size as to make practicable its preservation and use in an unimpaired condition; and (4) may also contain ecological, geological, or other features of scientific, educational, scenic, or historical value.

简而言之，荒野是指尚未被殖民者侵占的广袤美丽、未受破坏的土地，这些土地可​​能属于定居或商业开发的范围。原住民的传统住所并非“永久性”建筑，因此不予考虑。

In short, a wilderness is a large, beautiful tract of unspoiled land that the colonizing forces of homesteading or business development have not yet acquired. The traditional dwellings of native peoples are not “permanent” structures and, therefore, are not taken into consideration.

那些坚持保护无人居住的荒野的自然保护主义者，要么不了解，要么不在乎在此过程中被驱逐的原住民。例如，优胜美地国家公园所在区域最初无人居住的说法，很大程度上要归功于著名摄影师安塞尔·亚当斯等人拍摄的令人叹为观止的该地区照片。

Conservationists who insist on preserving a wilderness free of human habitation either don’t know or don’t care about the native dwellers evicted in the process. For example, the myth that the region now covered by Yosemite National Park was originally uninhabited by humans was successfully fostered by the breathtaking images of the region created by celebrated photographer Ansel Adams, among others, who

在优胜美地山谷工作期间，他刻意避免拍摄任何当地的米沃克人，尽管他们几乎总是在他的视线范围内。他拍摄了数千张没有人类的底片，这些底片记录了米沃克人至少四千年来耕耘的土地。他也知道，米沃克人是被强行驱逐出优胜美地山谷的，就像后来其他原住民被驱逐出尚未建立的国家公园一样，这一切都是为了……（所谓的）……保护自然免受人类干扰。

assiduously avoided photographing any of the local Miwok who were rarely out of his sight as he worked Yosemite Valley. He filled thousands of human-free negatives with land he knew the Miwok had tended for at least four thousand years. And he knew that the Miwok had been forcibly evicted from Yosemite Valley, as other natives would later be from national parks yet to be created, all in the … [supposed] … interest of protecting nature from human disturbance.

（道伊 16）

(Dowey 16)

尽管原住民世世代代在这片土地上可持续地生活，并守护着这里的野生动植物、森林和水域，但公园保护主义者认为，原住民的继续存在将会破坏这片土地。破坏自然环境。当然，他们的继续存在意味着优胜美地就不能被称作真正的荒野——一个没有人居住的荒野——而真正的荒野正是人们所渴望的。目睹了国家如此多的自然资源被城市化、工业化和商业化破坏，美国自然主义者希望将剩余的自然环境尽可能多地保存下来，作为国家遗产，以便美国人（更准确地说，是白人美国人）可以永远参观、学习，并从大自然的奇观中获得精神上的慰藉。因此，游客可以参观这座新公园，甚至可以长期停留，但那些将这里视为家园的人们却不得不离开。

Despite the fact that native peoples had lived sustainably on this land and had stewarded its wildlife, its forests, and its waters from time out of mind, park preservationists believed that the indigenous inhabitants’ continued presence would harm the natural setting. Certainly, their continued presence would have meant that Yosemite could not have been described as a true wilderness – a wilderness without human inhabitants – and a true wilderness is what was wanted. Having seen so much of the nation’s natural resources destroyed by urbanization, industrialization, and commercialization, American naturalists wanted to preserve, as a national heritage, as much as possible of the remaining natural environment so that Americans (or, more precisely, white Americans) could forever visit, learn from, and be morally refreshed by the wonders of nature.20 Thus, tourists could visit the new park, even for extended stays, but the people for whom it was homeland had to leave.

殖民主义对待优胜美地国家公园原住民的态度，一直是世界各地自然保护组织为保护荒野而划定的土地上原住民的普遍态度。为了获得所需的土地，自然保护组织可能会偿还贫困国家的部分外债，或提供其他经济激励，以换取所需的土地面积。<sup> 21</sup>有时，土地的获取过程会被粉饰，例如使用“自愿搬迁”之类的措辞，或者将其掩盖在所谓的共同管理项目之下，政府在其中施加严格的生计限制（例如，禁止狩猎、捕鱼、采集某些植物、从事农业活动）”（Dowie，第 xxii-xxiii 页），直到原住民因饥饿而被迫离开。其结果是，数百万原住民持续被迫离开祖先的土地，生活在如今公园边界之外的贫困之中；在公园里做服务员、搬运工或临时工等低薪工作；或者在城市里陷入贫困。

The colonialist attitude toward the original inhabitants of Yosemite National Park has remained the dominant attitude toward native inhabitants of lands set aside for wilderness preservation by conservation organizations throughout the world. To obtain the land it wants, a conservation organization might, for example, pay off a portion of a poor country’s foreign debt, or provide some other economic incentive, in exchange for the desired acreage.21 Sometimes land is obtained by sanitizing the process with “terms such as voluntary relocation, or [by] veil[ing] it behind a so-called co-management project where a government imposes strict livelihood restrictions (e.g., no hunting, fishing, gathering of certain plants, agricultural practices)” (Dowie, xxii–xxiii) until native inhabitants are driven away by starvation. The result has been the continuing worldwide eviction of millions of native peoples from their ancestral lands to live in poverty just outside the confines of what is now the park; to take low-paying jobs as waiters, porters, or day laborers within the park; or to drift into poverty in the cities.

然而，由于缺乏原住民的守护，许多面积过大、难以有效巡逻的保护区遭到了曾经守护这些土地的被驱逐者的侵占。例如，一些走投无路的被驱逐者以商业偷猎者的身份重新进入了他们曾经的狩猎场。

Without the presence of indigenous peoples to safeguard areas designated as wilderness, however, many tracts of preserved land too big to patrol effectively have fallen victim to invasion by the very evictees who used to steward them. For instance, some desperate evictees reenter, as commercial poachers, areas that used to be their own hunting grounds. Others

他们偷偷溜回森林，采集药用植物和柴火，冒着被自然保护机构雇佣的生态卫士合法击毙的风险。而更不受欢迎的群体——殖民者、非法伐木者、异域动物猎人、经济作物种植者和牧场主——正涌入世界各地无人巡逻的保护区。由于他们往往与相关国家的统治阶级有着共同的族裔背景，这些新来的定居者在与原住民的领土冲突中通常更受优待……而原住民却因为做着同样的事情而被逮捕或驱逐。

sneak back into the forest to harvest medicinal plants and firewood at the risk of being legally killed by eco-guards hired and paid by conservation agencies. And much less desirable groups – colonists, renegade loggers, exotic animal hunters, cash-crop farmers, and cattle ranchers – are moving into unpatrolled protected areas the world over. As they often share ethnicity with the ruling class of the nation involved, the new settlers are generally favored in territorial conflicts with … aboriginals who are arrested or expelled for doing the same things.

（Dowie xxvii）

(Dowie xxvii)

这些地区最终的悲剧结果是生态环境迅速衰退，而原本当地居民和自然保护主义者之间本可以建立合作关系。这将使原住民土地的生态保护得以继续，并由原住民掌控。事实上，正如马克·道伊所观察到的，原住民领袖们“二十五年来”一直在世界各地奔走，向各地的自然保护组织传递这样的信息：“我们已经证明自己是优秀的土地管理者，否则你们就不会选择我们的土地进行保护。让我们留在祖先长眠之地，我们将帮助你们保护我们共同珍视的生物多样性”（第十六至十七页）。正如澳大利亚原住民哲学家比尔·内杰所解释的那样，他的族人珍视土地，因为“大地就像你的父亲、兄弟或母亲……你的骨骼，你的血液”（引自普拉姆伍德，第226页）。

The tragic result for these areas is rapid ecological decline where there could be, instead, a cooperative relationship between native inhabitants and conservationists that would allow the ecological preservation of indigenous lands, in indigenous hands, to continue. Indeed, indigenous leaders have been traveling the globe for “a quarter of a century,” Mark Dowie observes, to bring the message to conservation organizations everywhere: “We have proven ourselves good stewards, otherwise you wouldn’t have selected our land for conservation. Let us stay where our ancestors are buried and we will help you preserve the biological diversity we all treasure” (xvi–xvii). As Australian Aboriginal philosopher Bill Neidjie explains, his people care for the land because “Earth [is] like your father or brother or mother … your bone, your blood” (cited in Plumwood 226).

许多国际机构——包括世界五大自然保护组织：国际自然保护协会（CI）、大自然保护协会（TNC）、世界自然基金会（WWF）、非洲野生动物基金会（AWF）和野生动物保护协会（WCS）——都已正式宣布支持土著人民的领土权利。此外，自20世纪80年代初以来一直备受争议的《联合国土著人民权利宣言》最终于2007年获得联合国大会批准。然而，所有这些文件均不具有法律约束力。因此，

Many international agencies – including the world’s five biggest conservation organizations: Conservation International (CI), The Nature Conservancy (TNC), the Worldwide Fund for Nature (WWF), the African Wildlife Foundation (AWF), and the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) – have made formal announcements supporting the territorial rights of indigenous peoples. In addition, the United Nations Declaration of the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, an issue under debate since the early 1980s, was finally approved by the UN General Assembly in 2007. None of these documents, however, is legally binding. Therefore,

部落人民的思考和计划往往以世代而非周、月、年为单位，他们耐心地等待着这些深思熟虑的宣言和声明中所承诺的重视。与此同时，人权界和全球自然保护界在流离失所问题（即把土著居民从他们的家园带走）上仍然存在严重分歧，双方都指责对方造成了他们所认为的特定危机。

[t]ribal people, who tend to think and plan in generations rather than weeks, months, and years, patiently await the consideration promised in these thoughtful declarations and pronouncements. Meanwhile, the human rights and global conservation communities remain at serious odds over the question of displacement [the removal of indigenous people from their homeland], each side blaming the other for the particular crisis they perceive.

（Dowie xxv）

(Dowie xxv)

具有讽刺意味的是，荒野保护与环境保护并非同一概念，尽管两者常常被混淆。单靠荒野保护既无法保护全球环境，也无法弥补其已遭受的破坏。事实上，正如拉马钱德拉·古哈所观察到的，对荒野保护的片面关注转移了人们对两个更为危险且“全球面临的根本性生态问题”的注意力：一是“工业化国家和第三世界城市精英日益增长的过度消费”，二是“日益严重的军事化，无论是在短期内（例如，持续不断的区域战争），还是在长期内（例如，军备竞赛和核毁灭的前景）”（《激进的美国环境主义》95页）。让我们思考一下这两点。首先，工业化的全球扩张是由消费主义的全球扩张所推动的，反过来，工业化的全球扩张又反过来推动了消费主义的全球扩张，或者说，消费主义是一种为了购买而购买的行为。简而言之，那些有能力的人正在迅速消耗地球资源，以追求越来越奢侈的“美好生活”。这种失控的全球浪费——除了减少粮食供应外，为世界贫困人口提供水源和住所——加剧了土壤、水和空气污染，并破坏了其他自然资源。其次，核武器的持续制造和扩散正使地球面临灾难性的生态危机。即使是非核战争中相对小规模战争所使用的武器——除了造成人员伤亡和财产损失外——还会向全球大气排放大量污染物。保护荒野地区与上述两个紧迫的环境问题都无关，甚至毫无关联。

Ironically, wilderness preservation is not the same thing as environmental protection, though the two are often confused. Wilderness preservation alone can neither protect the global environment nor remedy the damage it has already suffered. In fact, as Ramachandra Guha observes, the single-minded focus on wilderness preservation has deflected attention from two much more dangerous and “fundamental ecological problems facing the globe”: increasing “overconsumption by the industrialized world and by urban elites in the Third World” and “growing militarization, both in a short-term sense (i.e., ongoing regional wars) and in a long-term sense (i.e., the arms race and the prospect of nuclear annihilation)” (“Radical American Environmentalism” 95). Let’s think about these two points for a minute. First, the global spread of industrialization is fueled by, and in turn fuels, the global spread of rampant consumerism, or what might be called purchase for the sake of purchase. In short, those who can afford it are rapidly using up the planet to get for themselves ever more extravagant versions of “the good life.” Such runaway global wastefulness – in addition to decreasing the availability of food, water, and shelter for the world’s poor – increases the pollution of soil, water, and air as well as the destruction of other natural resources. Second, the continued creation and dissemination of nuclear weapons is putting the planet in catastrophic ecological jeopardy. And even the weapons used in non-nuclear, relatively small-scale wars – in addition to destroying human life and property – fill the global atmosphere with large quantities of pollutants. Neither of these pressing environmental issues is addressed by, or even related to, the preservation of wilderness areas.

主流媒体鲜少关注原住民因保护自然而被不公正、不明智地驱逐出家园的困境，这无疑加剧了问题的严重性。罗布·尼克松认为，“在媒体崇尚壮观场面的时代”，“坠落的尸体、燃烧的摩天大楼、爆炸的头颅、雪崩、火山和海啸具有……引人注目、令人欲罢不能的力量”，而他所谓的“缓慢暴力”则无法与之匹敌（3）。尼克松解释说，缓慢暴力是“一种逐渐发生且不易察觉的暴力，一种延迟的破坏性暴力，它分散在时间和空间之中”，这种暴力会造成死亡，但“通常根本不被视为暴力”（2）。他在这里指的是第三世界生态环境的破坏——例如，由监管不力的外国工业化造成的破坏——以及生活在那里的穷人所遭受的环境后果。但他对长期生态破坏“隐蔽性”的分析同样适用于全球数百万原住民被驱逐出家园的“隐蔽性”。环保组织并没有动用大规模杀伤性武器将划为荒野保护区的土地上的原住民驱逐出去。如果他们真的这么做了，我们肯定会在晚间新闻中听到相关报道。然而，正如我们所见，环保组织已经成功地将这些原住民驱逐出去，尽管这会造成人道主义灾难，甚至在保护区面积过大而无法有效巡逻的情况下，还会造成环境后果。因此，虽然我们很多人都感激地意识到全球数百万平方英里的“荒野”已被划为保护区，但很少有人知道这些“荒野”是如何形成的，或者在失去原住民守护者之后，它们会变成什么样子。

It hasn’t helped matters that mainstream news media have done little to increase public awareness of the plight of native peoples unjustly and unwisely evicted from their homelands in the name of conservation. “In an age when media venerate the spectacular” event, Rob Nixon argues, “[f]alling bodies, burning towers, exploding heads, avalanches, volcanoes and tsunamis have a[n] … eye-catching and page-turning power” that cannot be matched by what he calls “slow violence” (3). Slow violence, Nixon explains, is “a violence that occurs gradually and out of sight, a violence of delayed destruction that is dispersed across time and space,” a violence that kills, but “that is typically not viewed as violence at all” (2). He’s talking here about the ecological devastation of the Third World – caused by, for example, under-regulated foreign industrialism – and the environmental consequences suffered by the poor who live there. But his analysis of the “invisibility” of long-term ecological destruction also applies to the “invisibility” of the millions of aboriginal peoples who have been and are being evicted from their lands all over the world. Conservation organizations have not used military weapons of mass destruction to rid lands earmarked for wilderness preservation of their native human inhabitants. If they had, we surely would have heard about it on the nightly news. As we have seen, however, conservation organizations have succeeded, slowly and methodically, in getting those inhabitants evicted, despite the human or even – in cases where preserves are too big to be adequately patrolled – the environmental consequences. Thus, while many of us are gratefully aware of the millions of square miles of “wilderness” worldwide that have been set aside for preservation, very few of us know how that “wilderness” was created or what has become of it without its native stewards.

自20世纪60年代以来，原住民维权人士一直在为争取本族人民的权益而不懈努力。他们的努力已发展成为一场国际原住民运动：一个不断壮大的全球原住民交流网络，旨在统一各国境内外原住民的利益。该运动的主要目标之一是用一种合作模式取代自优胜美地国家公园建立以来占据主导地位的殖民主义荒野保护模式，这种合作模式既能保障原住民对其土地的控制权，又能满足国际自然保护组织的关切。由澳大利亚原住民提出的“原住民保护区”（IPA）概念便是这种合作模式的例证。根据IPA的价值观，保护区应……这些地区不被视为“荒野”，而是被视为“土地” ——这个术语既包括陆地也包括其毗邻的海洋——由已居住于此的原住民或已重新安置在其祖先家园的被驱逐原住民共同照料。在澳大利亚，原住民保护区（IPA）由原住民社区自愿设立，他们指定在其祖先土地内或毗邻的区域进行保护。他们绘制拟议区域的地图；制定并负责执行的运作规则；并向澳大利亚政府提交生物多样性保护管理计划。尽管这些原住民尚未获得土地所有权，但澳大利亚家园运动（Australian Homelands Movement）已在原住民祖先土地上安置原住民超过30年，并持续致力于恢复所有原住民的监护权。世界各地已经设立了各种版本的原住民保护区，并且还在不断设立（Dowie 237–39）。

Indigenous activists have been making a concerted effort to get justice for their peoples since the 1960s. Their efforts have grown into an international indigenous movement: a steadily growing, worldwide web of communication among indigenous peoples in an attempt to unify indigenous interests within and across national borders. One of the movement’s major goals is to replace the colonial model of wilderness conservation, dominant since the creation of Yosemite National Park, with a cooperative model that would both keep indigenous people in control of their lands and satisfy the concerns of international conservation organizations. The Indigenous Protected Area (IPA) concept, invented by Australian Aboriginals, is one example of the cooperative model. According to IPA values, conservation reserves are not thought of as “wilderness” areas but as country – a term including both land and the sea it borders – that is cared for by the native peoples who already inhabit it or by indigenous evictees who have been resettled in their ancestral homelands. IPAs in Australia are created voluntarily by Aboriginal communities who designate an area they want to protect within or bordering their ancestral lands. They map the proposed area; draw up rules of operation, which they will be responsible for enforcing; and submit a management plan to the Australian government for the conservation of biodiversity.22 Although land titles have not been granted to these original owners, the Australian Homelands Movement, which has been resettling indigenous peoples on their ancestral lands for over 30 years, continues working toward the restoration of all Aboriginal custodial rights. Various versions of Australia’s IPAs have been created and are being created around the world (Dowie 237–39).

尽管这些进展相对较小，但仍然令人鼓舞。然而，考虑到争夺自然环境控制权的强大势力包括政府机构、目标狭窄的保护组织，以及本章前面讨论过的跨国公司和全球旅游公司，全球范围内相当数量的原住民社区能够继续或重新管理其土地的可能性似乎微乎其微。尽管如此，马克·道伊并未放弃希望：“原住民的存在……或许能为保护区提供最佳的保护。国际自然保护主义者已经开始考虑这种可能性”（第27页）。从后殖民主义的视角来看，这种可能性越早考虑越好。23

Such gains as these, while relatively small, are encouraging. Yet when we consider that the powerful groups vying for control of the natural environment include government agencies, narrowly focused conservation organizations, and the multinational corporations and global tourism companies discussed earlier in this chapter, the chances that a globally significant number of native communities will be allowed to continue, or return to, stewarding their own lands seem slim indeed. Still, Mark Dowie hasn’t lost hope: “[i]ndigenous peoples’ presence … may offer the best protection that protected areas can ever receive. That’s a possibility that international conservationists have begun to consider” (xxvii). From a postcolonial perspective, that possibility can’t be considered soon enough.23

后殖民批评与文学

Postcolonial criticism and literature

无论后殖民批评家们在讨论我们一直在探讨的后殖民议题中如何定位自己，他们大多都会从一些相互重叠的主题来解读后殖民文学。这些主题包括以下几个常见主题，它们体现了后殖民批评对心理学与意识形态之间，或者更具体地说，对个体身份与文化信仰之间密切关系的认识：

Wherever postcolonial critics place themselves in terms of the postcolonial issues we’ve been discussing, most interpret postcolonial literature in terms of a number of overlapping topics. These include, among others, the following common topics, which illustrate postcolonial criticism’s recognition of the close relationship between psychology and ideology or, more specifically, between individual identity and cultural beliefs:

1土著居民与殖民者的最初接触以及土著文化的破坏；

1 the native people’s initial encounter with the colonizers and the disruption of indigenous culture;

2一位欧洲游客在当地向导的带领下，穿越陌生荒野的旅程；

2 the journey of the European outsider through an unfamiliar wilderness with a native guide;

3殖民者将土著文化成员视为非人（即视他们为不够完整的人）以及各种形式的殖民压迫；

3 othering (the colonizers’ treatment of members of the indigenous culture as less than fully human) and colonial oppression in all its forms;

4模仿（被殖民者试图通过模仿殖民者的穿着、行为、言语和生活方式来感受到自己的归属感——感受到自己并不低人一等）；

4 mimicry (the attempt of the colonized to feel that they belong – to feel that they are not inferior – by imitating the dress, behavior, speech, and lifestyle of the colonizers);

5 流放（在自己的国家里成为“局外人”或在欧洲成为外国流浪者的经历）；

5 exile (the experience of being an “outsider” in one’s own land or a foreign wanderer in Europe);

6独立后的热情之后是幻灭；

6 post-independence exuberance followed by disillusionment;

7文化差异（种族、阶级、性别、性取向、宗教、文化信仰和习俗等因素结合起来形成个人身份的方式）；

7 cultural difference (the ways in which race, class, sex, gender, sexual orientation, religion, cultural beliefs, and customs combine to form individual identity);

8对个人和集体文化认同的斗争，以及与之相关的疏离感、无家可归感（感觉自己没有文化“家”，或没有文化归属感）、双重意识（感觉自己在两种对立文化的社会和心理需求之间摇摆不定）和混合性（体验到自己的文化认同是两种或多种文化的混合体，这种感觉通常被认为是无家可归感的一种积极替代）等主题；

8 the struggle for individual and collective cultural identity and the related themes of alienation, unhomeliness (feeling that one has no cultural “home,” or sense of cultural belonging), double consciousness (feeling torn between the social and psychological demands of two antagonistic cultures), and hybridity (experiencing one’s cultural identity as a hybrid of two or more cultures, which feeling is generally considered a positive alternative to unhomeliness);

9双重殖民，或后殖民时代女性在殖民主义和父权制意识形态的双重压迫下所经历的苦难；

9 double colonization, or the experience of postcolonial women under the dual subjugation of colonialist and patriarchal ideologies;

10自然环境的作用及其丧失在后殖民时代人民的文化和经验中的作用；

10 the role of the natural environment, and the loss thereof, in the culture and experience of postcolonial peoples;

11既需要与前殖民时代的过去保持延续性，又需要对政治未来进行自我定义；

11 the need for continuity with a precolonial past and self-definition of the political future;

12文学文本本身体现殖民主义或反殖民主义的方式。

12 the ways in which a literary text is itself colonialist or anticolonialist.

我们清单上的最后一点需要讨论。对于大多数后殖民批评家而言，无论他们关注的主题是什么，他们都会分析文学文本的殖民主义或反殖民主义倾向，也就是说，文本如何强化或抵制殖民主义的压迫性意识形态。例如，简而言之，文本可以通过正面描绘殖民者、负面描绘被殖民者，或者不加批判地呈现殖民主义给被殖民者带来的益处来强化殖民主义意识形态。类似地，文本可以通过描绘殖民者的罪行、被殖民者的苦难，或者殖民主义对被殖民者的有害影响来抵制殖民主义意识形态。

This last item on our list requires discussion. For most postcolonial critics, whatever the topic or topics on which they focus, also analyze the ways in which a literary text is colonialist or anticolonialist, that is, the ways in which the text reinforces or resists colonialism’s oppressive ideology. For example, in the simplest terms, a text can reinforce colonialist ideology through positive portrayals of the colonizers, negative portrayals of the colonized, or the uncritical representation of the benefits of colonialism for the colonized. Analogously, texts can resist colonialist ideology by depicting the misdeeds of the colonizers, the suffering of the colonized, or the detrimental effects of colonialism on the colonized.

然而，这种分析并非总是像这个简单的概述所暗示的那样直截了当。因为文学文本的意识形态内容很少能被如此清晰的类别所束缚。例如，约瑟夫·康拉德的《黑暗之心》（1902）对殖民主义的负面刻画就极具反殖民主义色彩：在刚果进行象牙贸易的欧洲人被描绘成冷酷无情、贪婪成性的窃贼，他们实际上奴役了当地居民，帮助他们收集和运输“战利品”，欧洲人的存在对当地居民造成的负面影响也被生动地展现出来。然而，正如奇努阿·阿切贝所指出的，这部小说对欧洲人的谴责是基于对非洲人野蛮人的定义：小说告诉我们，在文明的外表下，欧洲人与非洲人一样野蛮。阿切贝指出，这部小说确实将非洲人描绘成一群史前疯狂、嚎叫、难以理解的野蛮人：“非洲[是一个]背景，它消除了非洲人作为人类的因素。非洲是一个象征性的战场，那里没有任何可辨识的人性，游荡的欧洲人若踏入其中，必将身陷险境”（《非洲的形象》12）。换言之，尽管《黑暗之心》的反殖民主义倾向显而易见，但小说却将殖民地人民视为野蛮的标杆，以此来与欧洲人进行比较。由此，阿切贝揭示了小说中隐藏的殖民主义潜台词，而文本本身似乎并未意识到这一点。

Such analysis is not always as straightforward as this simple outline might lead you to expect, however. For the ideological content of literary texts is rarely able to confine itself to such tidy categories. Joseph Conrad’s Heart of Darkness (1902), for example, is extremely anticolonialist in its negative representation of the colonial enterprise: the Europeans conducting the ivory trade in the Congo are portrayed as heartless, greedy thieves who virtually enslave the indigenous population to help collect and transport the Europeans’ “loot,” and the negative effects of the European presence on the native peoples are graphically depicted. However, as Chinua Achebe observes, the novel’s condemnation of Europeans is based on a definition of Africans as savages: beneath their veneer of civilization, the Europeans are, the novel tells us, as barbaric as the Africans. And indeed, Achebe notes, the novel portrays Africans as a prehistoric mass of frenzied, howling, incomprehensible barbarians: “Africa [is a] setting and backdrop which eliminates the African as human factor. Africa [is] a [symbolic] battlefield devoid of all recognizable humanity, into which the wandering European enters at his peril” (“An Image of Africa” 12). In other words, despite Heart of Darkness’s obvious anticolonialist agenda, the novel points to the colonized population as the standard of savagery to which Europeans are compared. Thus, Achebe uncovers the novel’s colonialist subtext, of which the text does not seem to be aware.

让我们再来看几个后殖民主​​义文学文本解读的简短例子。霍米·巴巴为我们提供了一个绝佳的例子，展现了许多后殖民主义批评的全球视野。他提出了一种分析世界文学的新方法，不再像以往那样从民族传统的角度出发，而是从跨越国界的后殖民主义议题入手。例如，巴巴认为，我们可以从不同文化经历历史创伤的方式来研究世界文学，这些创伤可能包括奴隶制、革命、内战、政治屠杀、压迫性的军事政权、文化认同的丧失等等。或者，我们可以将世界文学视为研究不同文化如何通过“他者化”或贬低某些群体来积极定义自身的一种方式。此外，我们还可以通过考察跨越文化边界而非文化内部的人物和事件的表征来分析世界文学，例如对移民、政治难民和被殖民人民的表征。巴巴说：“这类研究的核心既不是民族文化的‘主权’，也不是人类文化的普遍性，而是关注……那些萦绕在历史当下、未被言说、未被呈现的过去”（12）。也就是说，我们可以研究世界文学如何讲述那些被历史遗忘的人们——被剥夺权利者、被边缘化者、无家可归者——的个人经历，例如南非作家纳丁·戈迪默和非裔美国作家托妮·莫里森的作品中所描绘的那些人。

Let’s look at a few more brief examples of postcolonial interpretations of literary texts. Homi Bhabha gives us a wonderful example of the global orientation of much postcolonial criticism when he offers a new way to analyze world literature, not in terms of national traditions, which is how it generally has been studied, but in terms of postcolonial topics that cut across national boundaries. For example, Bhabha suggests that world literature might be studied in terms of the different ways cultures have experienced historical trauma, perhaps such traumas as slavery, revolution, civil war, political mass murder, oppressive military regimes, the loss of cultural identity, and the like. Or world literature might be seen as the study of the ways in which cultures define themselves positively by “othering” groups whom they demonize or otherwise devalue for that purpose. Or we might analyze world literature by examining the representations of people and events that occur across cultural boundaries, rather than within them, such as representations of migrants, political refugees, and colonized peoples. “The center of such a study,” Bhabha says, “would neither be the ‘sovereignty’ of national cultures, nor the universalism of human culture, but a focus on … the unspoken, unrepresented pasts that haunt the historical present” (12). That is, we might study what world literature tells us about the personal experience of people whom history has ignored – the disenfranchised, the marginalized, the unhomed – such as are found in the work of South African writer Nadine Gordimer and African American writer Toni Morrison.

例如，巴巴认为戈迪默的《我儿子的故事》（1990）和莫里森的《宠儿》（1987）都是“无家可归”的小说，小说中的两位女主人公——艾拉和塞丝——分别生活在不同文化之间的边缘地带。艾拉无家可归是因为她为了反抗南非种族主义政府，利用自己的房子掩护走私军火而被捕入狱；塞丝无家可归则是因为她为了保护自己的女儿免受残暴奴隶主的虐待而亲手杀死了她。因此，巴巴指出，这两个人物都处于双重边缘化：首先，她们是有色人种女性，生活在种族主义社会中；其次，她们的行为使她们被排除在各自的社群之外。这两部小说通过展现人物在道德抉择中所面临的心理和历史复杂性，揭示了历史现实并非仅仅发生在战场或政府办公室。相反，历史现实会走进我们的家庭，以最深刻的方式影响我们的个人生活。被边缘化的人群可能更清楚这个事实，因为他们遭受暴力和压迫，但这对每个人来说都是如此。

For example, Bhabha argues that Gordimer’s My Son’s Story (1990) and Morrison’s Beloved (1987) are unhomely novels in which the female protagonists – Aila and Sethe, respectively – live in the hinterland between cultures. Aila is unhomed because she is imprisoned for using her house as a cover for gun-running in an effort to resist South Africa’s racist government; Sethe, because she has killed her baby daughter in order to save the child from the abuses of a cruel slavemaster. Thus, Bhabha observes, these two characters are doubly marginalized: first as women of color living in racist societies, second as women whose actions have placed them outside the circle of their own communities. In representing the psychological and historical complexities of these characters’ ethical choices, both novels reveal the ways in which historical reality is not something that happens just on the battlefield or in the government office. Rather, historical reality comes into our homes and affects our personal lives in the deepest possible ways. Marginalized people may be more aware of this fact because it is pressed on them by violence and oppression, but it is true for everyone.

海伦·蒂芬也试图在后殖民文学中寻找共同点。她认为，“后殖民文本特有的颠覆性[反殖民主义]策略”并非在于“构建或重建”民族文化认同，而在于“重读和改写欧洲的历史和虚构记录”（95）。蒂芬指出，由于不可能完全摆脱殖民历史的影响，重现前殖民时代或构建新的文化认同，大多数后殖民文学转而“探究欧洲如何强加并维持对世界其他大部分地区的殖民统治”（95）。蒂芬认为，后殖民文学完成这项任务的众多方法之一，是通过使用她所谓的“经典反话语”，这是一种策略，即“后殖民作家选取英国经典文本中的一个或几个角色，或基本假设，并揭示其（殖民主义的）假设，为了后殖民目的而颠覆文本”（97）。

Another attempt to find a common denominator in postcolonial literature is made by Helen Tiffin, who claims that the “subversive [anticolonialist] manoeuvr[e] … characteristic of post-colonial texts” does not lie in “the construction or reconstruction” of national cultural identity, but rather in “the rereading and rewriting of the European historical and fictional record” (95). Tiffin argues that, as it is impossible to retrieve a precolonial past or construct a new cultural identity completely free of the colonial past, most postcolonial literature has attempted, instead, “to investigate the means by which Europe imposed and maintained … colonial domination of so much of the rest of the world” (95). One of the many ways postcolonial literature accomplishes this task, Tiffin maintains, is through the use of what she calls “canonical counter-discourse,” a strategy whereby “a post-colonial writer takes up a character or characters, or the basic assumptions of a British canonical text, and unveils [its colonialist] assumptions, subverting the text for post-colonial purposes” (97).

蒂芬认为，牙买加裔作家简·里斯的《藻海无边》（1966）就是这种“文学革命”（97）。里斯的小说是对夏洛蒂·勃朗特的《简·爱》（1847）的后殖民主义回应，它“回击”（98）勃朗特的小说，其方式之一是重新诠释了罗切斯特的西印度裔妻子伯莎·梅森。勃朗特的小说将伯莎描绘成一个精神错乱、酗酒、暴力且淫荡的女人，她欺骗罗切斯特与她结婚，而她的丈夫为了保护她自己和其他人，不得不将她锁在阁楼里。相比之下，里斯的小说则将伯莎描绘成，用盖亚特里·斯皮瓦克的话来说，她是一个“帝国主义的批判者”（斯皮瓦克 271），一个理智的女人，却因罗切斯特的帝国主义压迫而走向暴力。里斯的叙述由此揭露了勃朗特叙事中蕴含的殖民主义意识形态。我们不妨补充一点， 《简·爱》的部分殖民主义意识形态体现在小说将伯莎与殖民主义欧洲眼中的非白人土著居民联系起来：伯莎的脸是“黑红相间的面容”（勃朗特，第93页；第二卷第27章），她居住的房间是“野兽的巢穴”（勃朗特，第92页；第二卷第27章）。换言之，根据《简·爱》所处的殖民主义话语体系，精神错乱、酗酒、暴力和淫荡等同于非白人身份。

Tiffin sees this kind of “literary revolution” (97) in, for example, Wide Sargasso Sea (1966) by Jamaican-born writer Jean Rhys. Rhys’ novel, a postcolonial response to Charlotte Brontë’s Jane Eyre (1847), “writes back” (98) to Brontë’s novel by, among other things, reinterpreting Bertha Mason, Rochester’s West Indian wife. Brontë’s novel portrays Bertha, the descendent of white colonial settlers, as an insane, drunken, violent, and lascivious woman who tricked Rochester into marriage and whom her husband must keep locked in the attic for her own and everyone else’s protection. In contrast, Rhys’ novel depicts Bertha, in Gayatri Spivak’s words, as a “critic of imperialism” (Spivak 271), a sane woman driven to violent behavior by Rochester’s imperialist oppression. Rhys’ narrative thereby unmasks the colonialist ideology informing Brontë’s narrative. And part of Jane Eyre’s colonialist ideology, we might add, is revealed when the novel associates Bertha with the nonwhite native population as seen through the eyes of colonialist Europe: Bertha’s face is a “black and scarlet visage” (Brontë 93; ch. 27, vol. II), and the room she inhabits is “a wild beast’s den” (Brontë 92; ch. 27, vol. II). In other words, according to the colonialist discourse in which Jane Eyre participates, to be insane, drunken, violent, and lascivious is the equivalent of being nonwhite.

蒂芬指出，类似的经典反话语也出现在南非作家J·M·库切的小说《福》 （1988）中。这部小说揭示了丹尼尔·笛福的《鲁滨逊漂流记》（1719）中的殖民主义意识形态，这种意识形态体现在鲁滨逊对他遭遇海难的土地以及他“殖民”并命名为“星期五”的黑人的殖民主义态度上。当然，经典反话语也出现在莎士比亚的《暴风雨》（1611）在加勒比海和南美洲的众多现代演出中，这些演出揭示了原剧中普洛斯彼罗对卡利班的殖民统治背后的政治和心理运作。正如蒂芬所观察到的，经典反话语并非仅仅揭露……它所回应的文学作品，以及这些作品所参与的整个殖民主义话语体系。

Tiffin notes that similar canonical counter-discourse can be found, for example, in Foe (1988), by South African writer J. M. Coetzee, in the way the novel reveals the colonialist ideology of Daniel Defoe’s Robinson Crusoe (1719), an ideology manifest in Crusoe’s colonialist attitude toward the land on which he’s shipwrecked and toward the black man he “colonizes” and names Friday. And of course, canonical counter-discourse occurs in the numerous modern Caribbean and South American performances of Shakespeare’s The Tempest (1611), which reveal the political and psychological operations of Prospero’s colonialist subjugation of Caliban in the original play. As Tiffin observes, canonical counter-discourse doesn’t unmask merely the literary works to which it responds, but the whole fabric of colonialist discourse in which those works participate.

最后，爱德华·萨义德阐明了后殖民主义批评如何将经典文学作品的“边缘”（例如，次要人物和次要地理位置）推至我们关注的中心。他在分析简·奥斯汀的《曼斯菲尔德庄园》（1814）时正是如此。整部小说以十九世纪初的英国为背景，大部分情节发生在富有的托马斯·伯特伦爵士庞大的庄园里。伯特伦爵士是传统英国绅士的正面形象的典范：他出身良好、理性、正直、道德高尚，是家庭和海外农业企业（为家庭提供经济支持）的称职家长。

Finally, Edward Said demonstrates how postcolonial criticism of a canonized literary work often involves moving the “margins” of the work (for example, minor characters and peripheral geographical locations) to the center of our attention. This is what he does in his analysis of Jane Austen’s Mansfield Park (1814). The entire novel is set in England around the turn of the nineteenth century, most of it on the sizable estate of the wealthy Sir Thomas Bertram, who epitomizes the positive image of the traditional English gentleman of property: he is well bred, rational, honorable, and highly moral, and is the proper patriarchal head of his home and of the overseas agricultural enterprise that financially sustains that home.

这项事业位于加勒比海的英国​​殖民地安提瓜岛，依靠奴隶劳动维持运转。但安提瓜岛的情况并不乐观，托马斯爵士必须亲自前往掌控局面。他确实做到了，而且显然像管理自己的家一样高效。正如萨义德所说，托马斯爵士在整理好他的“殖民地花园”（《文化与帝国主义》 86页）后，回到家中迅速整顿家务。由于失去了他的管教，家里的秩序已经失控：成年的子女们互相争斗，秘密交往，总之，家里一片混乱。因此，萨义德指出，这部小说在“国内权威与国际权威”（《文化与帝国主义》 97页）之间建立了一种强烈的平行关系。因为英国庄园的经济繁荣取决于殖民事业的成功，而两者的有序运作都依赖于英国族长的指导。

This enterprise is in Antigua, in the Caribbean British colonies, and it is maintained by slave labor. But things are not going well in Antigua, and Sir Thomas must travel there to take control personally. And take control he does, apparently with the same efficiency with which he rules his home. For having set his “colonial garden” (Culture and Imperialism 86) in order, as Said puts it, Sir Thomas returns home to quickly set to rights his household, which, without his paternal guidance, has gotten out of order: his grown children have fought among themselves, engaged in clandestine courtships, and generally created a domestic uproar. Thus, among other things, Said notes that the novel draws a strong parallel between “domestic [and] international authority” (Culture and Imperialism 97). For the financial wellbeing of the British estate depends on the success of the colonial enterprise, and the orderly operation of both depends on the guidance of the British patriarch.

尽管托马斯爵士的安提瓜之旅在叙事中只是边缘性的——只是被顺带提及，我们也没有看到在那里发生的任何事情——但它“对情节发展至关重要”（《文化与帝国主义》 89页）。用萨义德的话来说，

Although Sir Thomas’ trip to Antigua is peripheral to the narration – it is mentioned only in passing and we see nothing that goes on there – it is “absolutely crucial to the action” (Culture and Imperialism 89). In Said’s words,

《曼斯菲尔德庄园》是英国不断扩张的帝国主义事业的一部分。……我们可以感受到，关于依附种族和领土的观念不仅存在于外交部官员、殖民地官僚和军事战略家之中，也存在于那些自学道德评价、文学平衡和文体修辞技巧等精髓的优秀小说读者之中。

Mansfield Park [is] part of the structure of [Britain’s] expanding imperialist venture. … [And] we can sense how ideas about dependent races and territories were held [not only] by foreign-office executives, colonial bureaucrats, and military strategists [but also] by intelligent novel-readers educating themselves in the fine points of moral evaluation, literary balance, and stylistic finish.

（文化与帝国主义95）

(Culture and Imperialism 95)

换句话说，文学作品中所包含的殖民主义意识形态是由作家注入其中的，并被读者吸收，而读者未必意识到这一点。

In other words, the colonialist ideology contained in literature is deposited there by writers and absorbed by readers without their necessarily realizing it.

后殖民批评家对文学文本提出的一些问题

Some questions postcolonial critics ask about literary texts

以下问题旨在概括后殖民主义文学研究方法。请记住，大多数后殖民主义分析，无论其关注的问题是什么，都旨在探讨后殖民主义文学研究方法。他们关注的重点将包括对文本是殖民主义的、反殖民主义的，还是两者的某种结合（即意识形态上的冲突）的关注。

The questions that follow are offered to summarize postcolonial approaches to literature. Keep in mind that most postcolonial analyses, regardless of the issues on which they focus, will include some attention to whether the text is colonialist, anticolonialist, or some combination of the two, that is, ideologically conflicted.

1文学文本是如何以明确或隐喻的方式表现殖民压迫的各个方面的？人们常常特别关注政治压迫和文化压迫相互交织的领域，例如殖民者对被殖民国家的语言、交流和知识的控制。

1 How does the literary text, explicitly or allegorically, represent various aspects of colonial oppression? Special attention is often given to those areas where political and cultural oppression overlap, as it does, for example, in the colonizers’ control of language, communication, and knowledge in colonized countries.

2文本揭示了后殖民身份认同的哪些问题，包括个人身份与文化身份之间的关系，以及双重意识和混合性等问题？

2 What does the text reveal about the problematics of postcolonial identity, including the relationship between personal and cultural identity and such issues as double consciousness and hybridity?

3这段文字揭示了反殖民主义抵抗运动的政治和/或心理层面的哪些方面？例如，这段文字暗示了哪些意识形态、政治、社会、经济或心理因素促进或抑制了抵抗运动？这段文字又是如何阐述个人或群体如何实现并维持抵抗运动的？

3 What does the text reveal about the politics and/or psychology of anticolonialist resistance? For example, what does the text suggest about the ideological, political, social, economic, or psychological forces that promote or inhibit resistance? How does the text suggest that resistance can be achieved and sustained by an individual or a group?

4这段文字揭示了文化差异的运作机制——种族、宗教、阶级、性别、性取向、文化信仰和习俗如何共同塑造个人身份——如何影响我们对自身、他人以及我们所处世界的认知？“他者化”或许是其中的一个分析方向。

4 What does the text reveal about the operations of cultural difference – the ways in which race, religion, class, gender, sexual orientation, cultural beliefs, and customs combine to form individual identity – in shaping our perceptions of ourselves, others, and the world in which we live? Othering might be one area of analysis here.

5文本如何回应或评论一部经典（殖民主义）作品中的人物、主题或假设？借鉴海伦·蒂芬的观点，探讨后殖民文本如何重塑我们先前对经典文本的解读。

5 How does the text respond to or comment on the characters, topics, or assumptions of a canonized (colonialist) work? Following Helen Tiffin’s lead, examine how the postcolonial text reshapes our previous interpretations of a canonical text.

6不同后殖民时期族群的文学作品之间是否存在有意义的相似之处？例如，我们可以比较被殖民者侵占土地的不同国家原住民的文学作品、不同国家白人定居者殖民地的文学作品，或者非洲散居群体中不同族群的文学作品。或者，我们也可以比较这三类文学作品，以探究殖民经历是否塑造了一些超越种族和国籍差异的共同文化认同元素。

6 Are there meaningful similarities among the literatures of different postcolonial populations? One might compare, for example, the literatures of native peoples from different countries whose land was invaded by colonizers, the literatures of white settler colonies in different countries, or the literatures of different populations in the African diaspora. Or one might compare literary works from all three of these categories in order to investigate, for example, if the experience of colonization creates some common elements of cultural identity that outweigh differences in race and nationality.

7文本如何展现其所描绘的人物（例如，文化上的主导人物、弱势群体和文化局外人）与他们所居住的土地之间的关系？自然环境是否随时间发生变化？如果发生变化，原因是什么？叙述者或任何人物对自然环境的态度是否随时间发生变化？文本似乎在宣扬人与自然之间怎样的关系？诸如此类的问题可以帮助你从后殖民批评的环境视角来思考文本。24

7 How does the text represent relationships between the characters it portrays – for example, culturally dominant characters, subalterns, and cultural outsiders – and the land these characters inhabit? Does the natural setting change over time and, if so, what is the cause? Does the narrator’s attitude toward the natural setting, or the attitude of any character toward the natural setting, change over time? What kinds of relationships between human beings and nature does the text seem to promote? Questions like these can help you think about a text in terms of postcolonial criticism’s environmental concerns.24

8西方经典文学作品如何通过其对殖民化的描写和/或其不恰当的表达来强化或削弱殖民主义意识形态。对被殖民人民保持沉默？文本是否通过对我们讨论过的任何后殖民概念的阐释，向我们揭示了殖民主义或反殖民主义意识形态的本质？（文本并不一定要涉及殖民主义主题才能做到这一点。）

8 How does a literary text in the Western canon reinforce or undermine colonialist ideology through its representation of colonization and/or its inappropriate silence about colonized peoples? Does the text teach us anything about colonialist or anticolonialist ideology through its illustration of any of the postcolonial concepts we’ve discussed? (A text does not have to treat the subject of colonization in order to do this.)

根据具体文学作品，我们可以提出以下一个或多个问题。或者，我们也可以提出一些此处未列出的有用问题。这些只是引导我们从后殖民视角进行富有成效的文学思考的一些起点。请记住，即使关注相同的后殖民概念，并非所有后殖民批评家都会以相同的方式解读同一文本。正如在任何领域一样，即使是专家也会有分歧。

Depending on the literary work in question, we might ask one or any combination of these questions. Or we might come up with a useful question not listed here. These are just some starting points to get us thinking productively about literature from a postcolonial perspective. Keep in mind that not all postcolonial critics will interpret the same text in the same way, even if they focus on the same postcolonial concepts. As in every field, even expert practitioners disagree.

无论我们选择以何种方式运用后殖民批评，我们运用这种方法的目标都是：学会看到文学中一些重要的方面，如果没有这种理论视角，我们可能不会如此清晰或深刻地看到这些方面；欣赏生活在文化多元世界中的机遇和责任；并理解文化不仅仅是凝固在时间中的固定的器物和习俗的集合，而是一种与自身和世界建立联系的方式，一种心理和社会参照框架，它必然会随着跨文化交流而改变，无论这些交流发生在我们的社区还是文学文本的字里行间。

Whatever ways we may choose to apply postcolonial criticism, our goal in using this approach is to learn to see some important aspects of literature that we might not have seen so clearly or so deeply without this theoretical perspective; to appreciate the opportunities and the responsibilities of living in a culturally diverse world; and to understand that culture is not just a fixed collection of artifacts and customs frozen in time but a way of relating to oneself and to the world, a psychological and social frame of reference that necessarily alters in response to crosscultural encounters, whether those encounters occur in our community or on the pages of a literary text.

以下对菲茨杰拉德的《了不起的盖茨比》的解读，旨在展示后殖民主义视角下对这部小说的诠释可能带来的成果。你会注意到，我的后殖民主义解读大量运用了心理分析，并且在某些方面与我在第三章“马克思主义批评”中对这部小说的探讨相似。此外，我的后殖民主义解读还包括对小说中三个次要黑人角色的分析，以及对小说抹杀爵士时代纽约非裔美国人存在的批判——你也会在第十一章中看到我对这部小说的非裔美国人视角解读。这种理论上的“重叠”在后殖民主义解读中相当常见，因为后殖民主义批评在分析殖民主义和反殖民主义意识形态的各个方面时，会借鉴这三种理论以及其他理论。简而言之，我对菲茨杰拉德小说的后殖民主义解读，着重探讨其作品中蕴含的殖民主义意识形态。这种意识形态既能奴役一国境内的少数族裔，也能奴役世界其他地区的被殖民者。事实上，正如我将要论证的，这部小说揭示了殖民主义意识形态如何成为一种心理状态——它不仅是一种思维方式，更是一种存在方式——这种状态对压迫者和被压迫者都同样有害。

The following reading of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby is offered as an example of what a postcolonial interpretation of that novel might yield. You’ll notice that my postcolonial reading relies a good deal on psychological analysis and is similar, in some ways, to my discussion of the novel in Chapter 3, “Marxist criticism.” In addition, my postcolonial interpretation includes both an analysis of the novel’s three minor black characters and its erasure of the African American presence in Jazz Age New York City, an analysis you will also find as part of my African American reading of the novel in Chapter 11. This kind of theoretical “overlap” is quite common for a postcolonial interpretation because postcolonial criticism draws on these three theories, among others, in its attempt to analyze all aspects of colonialist and anticolonialist ideologies. In short, my postcolonial interpretation of Fitzgerald’s novel focuses on what I will argue is the work’s colonialist ideology, an ideology that can subjugate minority populations within a nation’s borders as well as colonized populations elsewhere on the globe. Indeed, as I will argue, the novel illustrates some of the ways in which colonialist ideology is also a psychological state – not just a way of thinking but a way of being – that is detrimental to those who oppress others as well as to those who are oppressed.

尽管我认为后殖民批评最伟大的成果之一在于它能够将来自前殖民地社会的作家，特别是边缘化的后殖民作家的作品推向聚光灯下，但我希望我对《了不起的盖茨比》的解读能够通过阐明这一点，为反殖民主义的知识分子努力做出贡献。殖民主义意识形态本质上是种族主义、阶级主义和性别歧视的，并且是潜藏在美国文化认同核心的根本要素。正如许多后殖民批评家所言，后殖民批评的核心在于抵制一切形式的殖民主义意识形态，而只有当我们了解其隐藏之处，才能真正抵制这种意识形态。

Although I believe that one of the greatest products of postcolonial criticism is its potential to bring the work of writers from formerly colonized societies, especially the work of marginalized postcolonial writers, to the fore, I hope that my reading of The Great Gatsby serves anticolonialist intellectual efforts by illustrating the ways in which colonialist ideology is inherently racist, classist, and sexist and is a fundamental element lurking at the core of American cultural identity. As many postcolonial critics attest, the key concern of postcolonial criticism is resistance to colonialist ideology in all its forms, and we can’t resist an ideology until we know where it’s hiding.

殖民地之内：对《了不起的盖茨比》的后殖民解读

The colony within: a postcolonial reading of The Great Gatsby

正如马克思主义、女权主义、女同性恋/男同性恋/酷儿理论以及非裔美国人批评等批判框架所揭示的那样，任何意识形态都与其所产生的心理密不可分。意识形态离不开与之相适应的心理，离不开支撑它的心理。因此，诸如阶级主义、性别歧视、异性恋霸权主义和种族主义之类的意识形态不仅仅是信仰体系，它们也是人们与自身和他人建立联系的方式，因此，它们涉及复杂的心理状态。

As such critical frameworks as Marxism, feminism, lesbian/gay/queer theory, and African American criticism have taught us, no ideology is really separate from the psychology it produces. Ideology cannot exist without the psychology appropriate to it, without the psychology that sustains it. Thus, such ideologies as classism, sexism, heterosexism, and racism are not merely belief systems. They are also ways of relating to oneself and others and, as such, involve complex psychological modes of being.

或许，意识形态与心理学之间的密切联系在后殖民批评中体现得最为淋漓尽致。后殖民理论最重要的目标之一，便是通过理解殖民主义意识形态如何塑造殖民者和被殖民者的身份认同——即心理——来与之抗争。作为西方文明中一股无处不在的力量，殖民主义意识形态的运作无处不在，有时隐而不显，但几乎总是卓有成效，甚至在我们意想不到的文化实践和作品中也能找到它的踪迹。例如，在看似与殖民主义毫不相干的美国小说《了不起的盖茨比》（1925）中，就可见其身影。从后殖民主义的视角来看，菲茨杰拉德这部描写美国爵士时代的著名小说，正是“他者化”这一概念的典型代表。“他者化”是一种心理运作，殖民主义意识形态正是依赖于此，而这正是其无可辩驳的标志。

Perhaps nowhere is the intimate connection between ideology and psychology demonstrated more clearly than in postcolonial criticism. For one of postcolonial theory’s most definitive goals is to combat colonialist ideology by understanding the ways in which it operates to form the identity – the psychology – of both the colonizer and the colonized. And as a pervasive force in Western civilization, colonialist ideology can be found operating, sometimes invisibly but almost always effectively, even in those cultural practices and productions in which we would not expect to find it, for example in an American novel that doesn’t seem concerned with colonialism at all: F. Scott Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby (1925). When looked at through a postcolonial lens, Fitzgerald’s famous novel about the American Jazz Age is the quintessential text about othering, a psychological operation on which colonialist ideology depends and that is its unmistakable hallmark.

西方文明史反复表明，为了征服一个“异族”，一个国家必须说服自己，这些人是“不同的”，而“不同”必然意味着低人一等，甚至不完全是人。用后殖民主义的术语来说，被征服的人民必须被“他者化”。例如，在我们自己的国家，对一些美洲原住民部落进行种族灭绝，并通过强制殖民主义教育同化其他部落的理由，就是美洲原住民是“野蛮人”，实际上是非人。同样，奴役非洲人并向他们灌输白人​​至上主义的殖民主义意识形态，其理由是官方将非洲人定义为只有五分之三的人。由此可见，正如我们自身的国家历史所揭示的，殖民主义并不需要被殖民人口位于一个国家的地理边界之外。被殖民人口也可以存在于殖民国家的地理边界之内。

As the history of Western civilization has shown repeatedly, in order to subjugate an “alien” people, a nation must convince itself that those people are “different,” and “different” must mean inferior to the point of being less than fully human. In postcolonial terminology, the subjugated people must be othered. In our own country, for example, the justification for exterminating some Native American nations and assimilating others through compulsory colonialist education was that Native Americans were “savages,” literally inhuman. Similarly, the enslavement of Africans and their indoctrination in the colonialist ideology of white superiority was justified by officially defining Africans as only three-fifths human. As our own national history reveals, then, colonialism doesn’t require a colonized population beyond a nation’s geographical borders. Colonized populations can exist within the geographical borders of the colonizing nation.

正如《了不起的盖茨比》所展现的那样，殖民主义也以另一种方式存在于“内部”：它存在于个人的心灵深处，影响着我们的个人行为。身份认同以及我们对他人的认知。具体而言，我将论证菲茨杰拉德的小说通过揭示潜藏在美国文化身份核心的殖民主义心理，揭示了隐藏在美国文化核心的殖民主义意识形态。

As The Great Gatsby illustrates, colonialism exists “within” in another sense of the term as well: it exists within the individual psyche, where it influences our personal identity and our perceptions of others. Specifically, I will argue that Fitzgerald’s novel reveals the colonialist ideology hiding at the heart of American culture by revealing the colonialist psychology that lurks at the core of American cultural identity.

正如人们所预料的那样，殖民主义心理学包含诸多方面，其中包括文化特权群体将文化弱势群体“他者化”的（通常是无意识的）态度和行为，即文化特权群体在情感上与他们想要控制或维持控制的群体保持距离。这种“他者化”行为背后有着诸多政治和经济动机，但其主要的心理动机似乎在于渴望获得权力、掌控感和优越感。因此，殖民主义心理学在缺乏安全感的个体身上找到了滋生的沃土。正如我们将看到的，殖民主义心理学具有自我延续性：它助长了个人不安全感，从而促进了自身的运作。由于“他者化”既是其动力来源，也是其表现形式，因此殖民主义心理学严重依赖于种族主义和阶级歧视——这两种非常有效的“他者化”手段。当然，性别歧视常常与种族主义重叠，并且正如我们将在下文看到的，也与阶级歧视重叠，从而使来自文化弱势群体的女性遭受多种形式的复杂“他者化”。事实上，正是多种形式的“他者化”实践构成了殖民主义心理学的特征。

As might be expected, colonialist psychology consists of, among other things, those (often unconscious) attitudes and behaviors by which a culturally privileged group others a culturally subordinate group, that is, by which the culturally privileged distance themselves emotionally from populations over whom they want to gain or maintain control. There are many political and economic motives for othering, but the primary psychological motive seems to be the need to feel powerful, in control, and superior. Thus, colonialist psychology finds in the insecure individual fertile ground on which to establish itself. And as we shall see, colonialist psychology is self-perpetuating: it encourages the personal insecurity that facilitates its operations. Because othering is the activity that both fuels and expresses it, colonialist psychology depends heavily on racism and classism, two very successful forms of othering. Of course, sexism often overlaps with racism and, as we shall see below, with classism, thus subjecting women from culturally subordinate groups to complex forms of multiple othering. Indeed, it is the practice of multiple forms of othering that distinguishes colonialist psychology.

在《了不起的盖茨比》中，殖民主义心理并非仅仅体现在小说本身批判的人物刻画上，例如汤姆·布坎南。相反，殖民主义心理贯穿整个叙事，因为它是叙述者尼克·卡拉威这一人物塑造的核心。此外，小说还帮助我们从殖民地臣民的视角理解殖民主义心理。无论是否获得经济上的成功，这些臣民始终处于文化边缘，他们渴望的仅仅是被文化精英所接纳，杰伊·盖茨比正是这种心态的典型代表。最后，通过汤姆·布坎南这个人物，《了不起的盖茨比》揭示了殖民主义心理的负面影响，即使是对那些看似受益于殖民主义心理的文化特权阶层也同样如此。

In The Great Gatsby, colonialist psychology is not confined to the depiction of characters the novel itself discredits, such as Tom Buchanan. Rather, colonialist psychology is a pervasive presence in the narrative as a whole because that psychology is central to the characterization of the narrator, Nick Carraway. In addition, the novel helps us understand colonialist psychology from the viewpoint of the colonial subject, who, remaining a cultural outsider whether or not he achieves financial success, wants only to be accepted by the cultural elite, a position epitomized by the character of Jay Gatsby. Finally, in the character of Tom Buchanan, The Great Gatsby reveals the detrimental effects of colonialist psychology even on the culturally privileged who seem to be its beneficiaries.

尼克·卡拉威给许多读者留下的印象，正如他自己所希望的那样，是一个非常宽容的人。正如他所说，他“倾向于保留所有判断”，因此，当他还是耶鲁大学本科生时，他“知晓熟人们的秘密悲伤”（5；第一章）。小说中，我们再次见到他时，他已年近三十，依然如此。几乎所有主要人物都向尼克倾诉心事。黛西向他倾诉婚姻烦恼；汤姆和他谈起默特尔；盖茨比向他坦白了自己的过去以及与黛西的初次恋情；甚至默特尔也向他描述了初遇汤姆以及第一次婚外情时的兴奋之情。虽然尼克是这部小说的道德中心——他是唯一一个关心他人、真正关心他人喜怒哀乐、并对他们显而易见的自私行为表达强烈道德保留意见的角色——但他对他们的个人选择却极其宽容。在他们的私生活中，尼克虽然觉得必须先断绝与家乡一位年轻女子的联系才能和乔丹约会，但他似乎完全适应了在长岛结识的这群人截然不同的生活方式。事实上，尼克同意安排盖茨比和黛西重逢，并在盖茨比举办的派对上，在两人于他的别墅见面时负责守卫。

Nick Carraway strikes many readers, as indeed he wants to strike them, as a very tolerant person. Because, as he says, he is “inclined to reserve all judgments,” he “was privy to the secret griefs” (5; ch. 1) of his acquaintances when he was a Yale undergraduate. And so is he still when we meet him in the novel as a man just turning 30. Almost all the main characters confide in Nick. Daisy tells him about her marital troubles; Tom talks to him about Myrtle; Gatsby tells him the truth about his past life and his initial relationship with Daisy; and even Myrtle describes to him her excitement at meeting Tom and having an extra-marital affair for the first time. And though Nick functions as the novel’s moral center – he’s the only character who cares about others, who takes a genuine personal interest in their happiness and their sorrows, and who expresses strong ethical reservations about their obvious selfishness – he is extremely tolerant of the personal choices they make in their private lives. While he feels he must break off his correspondence with a young woman he knew back home before he can date Jordan, he seems perfectly comfortable with the very different lifestyle of the group he has fallen in with on Long Island. Indeed, Nick agrees to arrange Gatsby’s reunion with Daisy and to stand guard while the two meet at his cottage during one of Gatsby’s parties.

因此，尼克在某个领域不断地对他人的评判显得尤为重要，尽管他似乎并未意识到这一点：他多次提及众多次要人物，这些人与他所属的那个特权文化群体——白人、上层阶级、盎格鲁-撒克逊新教徒，其家族在美国已繁荣数代——在某种程度上是异类或疏离的。每当尼克提及来自不同文化背景的人时，他都会强调他们的种族，仿佛那是他们最主要甚至唯一的特征，从而凸显了他们的“异类”特质。例如，他雇佣来照看房子、做早餐的女人，他每天都能见到，被他提及六次，而且每次都用“我的芬兰人”（第88页；第五章）和“那个芬兰人”（第89页；第五章）这样的称呼。她的语言是“对着电炉喃喃自语芬兰智慧”（8；第 1 章），甚至她的走路方式——“芬兰人的步伐”（89；第 5 章）——也被描述成突出了她的民族差异。

So it seems especially significant that there is one area in which Nick continually makes judgments about others with no apparent consciousness of doing so: in his numerous references to the plethora of minor characters who are in some way foreign, in some way alien, to the privileged cultural group of his day, of which he is a member: white, upper-class, Anglo-Saxon Protestants, born of families who had prospered in America for several generations. Whenever Nick has cause to mention people from a different culture, he emphasizes their ethnicity as if that were their primary or only feature and thus foregrounds their “alien” quality. For example, the woman he has hired to keep his house and cook his breakfast, whom he sees every day, is referred to six different times and always by such appellations as “my Finn” (88; ch. 5) and “the Finn” (89; ch. 5). Her language consists of “mutter[ing] Finnish wisdom to herself over the electric stove” (8; ch. 1), and even her walk – “the Finnish tread” (89; ch. 5) – is described in a way that foregrounds her ethnic difference.

同样，沃尔夫希姆的秘书是“一位可爱的犹太女子”（178页；第9章）；在默特尔死亡现场与警察交谈的证人是“那个黑人”（148页；第7章）；在“灰烬谷”（27页；第2章）玩烟花的小孩是“一个灰白瘦弱的意大利孩子”（30页；第2章）；尼克有一天在去纽约的路上看到的送葬队伍里的人“有着东南欧人特有的悲怆眼神和短小的上唇”（73页；第4章）。虽然尼克的用词确实生动形象，但他对爵士时代美国主流文化之外人物种族的执着关注，暗示了他对“外国人”态度中令人不安的一面，而这种不安在他谈到迈耶·沃尔夫希姆时变得尤为明显。

Similarly, Wolfsheim’s secretary is “a lovely Jewess” (178; ch. 9); the witness talking to the police officer at the scene of Myrtle’s death is “the Negro” (148; ch. 7); the youngster playing with fireworks in the “valley of ashes” (27; ch. 2) is “a gray, scrawny Italian child” (30; ch. 2); and the people in the funeral procession Nick sees one day on his way to New York City have “the tragic eyes and short upper lips of south-eastern Europe” (73; ch. 4). While Nick’s choice of words is certainly effective as colorful description, its relentless focus on the ethnicity of characters outside the dominant culture of Jazz Age America hints at a disquieting dimension of his attitude toward “foreigners,” a dimension that becomes clear when he speaks of Meyer Wolfsheim.

尼克向我们介绍沃尔夫希姆时，称他为“一个矮小扁鼻子的犹太人”（75；第四章），除了鼻子之外，我们对他的外貌几乎一无所知。但他的鼻子被反复提及，描述得如此细致，以至于沃尔夫希姆的外貌特征几乎被简化为尼克认为最丑陋、也最能代表其种族特征的那一个——正如刚才引述的句子所表明的那样。例如，尼克写道，沃尔夫希姆抬起“头，用两根细细的鼻毛看着我，这两根鼻毛在两个鼻孔里蓬松生长”（73-74；第四章），“他松开我的手，用他那富有表现力的鼻子盖住了盖茨比”（74；第四章）。在尼克看来，沃尔夫希姆的所有表情似乎都集中在他的鼻子上。当尼克想告诉我们沃尔夫希姆生气时，他说：“沃尔夫希姆先生的鼻子愤愤地朝我瞥了一眼”（75；第四章）。当沃尔夫希姆对尼克说的话感兴趣时，尼克描述道：“他的鼻孔饶有兴趣地转向了我”。（75；第 4 章）。当沃尔夫希姆情绪激动时，尼克会这样描述这一事实：“他那悲惨的鼻子在颤抖”（77；第 4 章）或“他鼻孔里的毛发微微颤动”（180；第 9 章）。

Nick introduces Wolfsheim to us as a “small flat-nosed Jew” (75; ch. 4), and we are told very little else about his appearance except for his nose. But his nose is mentioned so frequently and in such descriptive detail that Wolfsheim is reduced to the single physical feature that, as the statement just cited indicates, Nick finds the most unattractive and associates the most strongly with Wolfsheim’s ethnicity. For example, Nick says, Wolfsheim raised his “head and regarded me with two fine growths of hair which luxuriated in either nostril” (73–74; ch. 4), and “dropp[ing] my hand [he] covered Gatsby with his expressive nose” (74; ch. 4). Apparently, all of Wolfsheim’s expressiveness, in Nick’s opinion, resides in his nose, for when Nick wants to tell us that Wolfsheim has become angry, he says, “Mr. Wolfsheim’s nose flashed at me indignantly” (75; ch. 4). When Wolfsheim is interested in something Nick has said, Nick reports, “His nostrils turned to me in an interested way” (75; ch. 4). When Wolfsheim is emotionally moved, Nick communicates this fact by saying, “[H]is tragic nose was trembling” (77; ch. 4) or “The hair in his nostrils quivered slightly” (180; ch. 9).

尼克显然是在将沃尔夫希姆视为“他者”，就像他几乎将他所见到的所有少数族裔角色都视为“他者”一样。这样做，他便将他们非人化了。“他者化”之所以会使人非人化，是因为它允许人们将自己视为“人类”，而将与自己不同的人视为“异类”。因此，“他者化”助长了我们对那些被我们定义为与我们不同的人的妖魔化，正如我们在尼克对沃尔夫希姆的描述中所看到的，他将这个角色变成了“犹太人怪物”的某种版本，这种“他者化”的形式在纳粹德国时期被希特勒充分利用。尼克似乎毫无意识地达到了这种效果，他笔下对沃尔夫希姆的描述中，除了他的鼻子之外，几乎没有其他特征：用尼克的话来说，沃尔夫希姆“头很大”（73页；第四章），“眼睛很小”（74页；第四章），“手指粗大”（179页；第九章），最后，他的“袖扣”是用“人类臼齿”制成的（77页；第四章）。当然，尼克妖魔化沃尔夫希姆是因为这个角色是个罪大恶极的罪犯。但尼克对沃尔夫希姆的犹太身份着墨过多，以至于沃尔夫希姆的犯罪行为也与他的种族身份紧密相连。

Nick is clearly othering Wolfsheim, as he others almost all the ethnic characters he sees. And in doing so he dehumanizes them. Othering dehumanizes because it permits one to identify oneself as “the human being” and people who are different as something “other” than human. Othering thus facilitates the demonization of people we define as different from us, as we see when Nick’s description of Wolfsheim turns that character into a version of “the Jew as monster,” a form of othering that served Hitler well in Nazi Germany. Nick achieves this effect, apparently with no consciousness of doing anything amiss, with the only descriptions we get of Wolfsheim that do not include his nose: in Nick’s words, Wolfsheim has a “large head” (73; ch. 4), “tiny eyes” (74; ch. 4), “bulbous fingers” (179; ch. 9), and finally, “cuff buttons” made of “human molars” (77; ch. 4). Of course, Nick is demonizing Wolfsheim because this character is a criminal of rather vast proportions. But Nick foregrounds Wolfsheim’s Jewishness to such a degree that even Wolfsheim’s criminal status becomes associated with his ethnicity.

尼克对少数族裔人物进行“他者化”的另一个显著例子发生在盖茨比开着他那辆巨大的豪华轿车送他去纽约的时候。尼克看到“三个时髦的黑人”坐在“一辆由白人司机驾驶的豪华轿车”里（73；第四章）。他把他们描述为“两个花瓶和一个姑娘”，并说：“我大笑起来，因为他们的眼珠子像牛角一样朝我们翻过来，带着傲慢的竞争姿态”（73；第四章）。当然，尼克毫不掩饰的种族主义在他对这些人物的“他者化”中显而易见：这些黑人被称作“花瓶”——动物而非人——而对他们瞪大眼睛、翻白眼的描述强烈地呼应了将非裔美国人描绘成愚蠢、幼稚、过分戏剧化、滑稽可笑的种族主义刻板印象。25

Another significant example of Nick’s othering of ethnic characters occurs when Gatsby is driving him to New York City in his enormous luxury car. Nick sees “three modish [fashionable] Negroes” in “a limousine … driven by a white chauffeur” (73; ch. 4). He describes them as “two bucks and a girl” and says, “I laughed aloud as the yolks of their eyeballs rolled toward us in haughty rivalry” (73; ch. 4). Of course, Nick’s unselfconscious racism is obvious in his othering of these characters: the black men are “bucks” – animals rather than men – and the description of their wide-stretched, rolling eyes resonates strongly with racist stereotypes that portrayed African Americans as foolish, childish, overly dramatic, comic characters.25

此外，尼克对这些人物的描述，也体现了托妮·莫里森在其对美国白人文学中非洲裔形象的分析中所阐述的那种叙事功能。这些黑人人物——衣着时髦，乘坐豪华轿车，非常在意自己在他人眼中的社会地位——是盖茨比的镜像和影子。他们之间唯一明显的区别在于，盖茨比可以隐藏自己的出身，而他们却无法做到，因为他们无法掩盖自己的肤色。在尼克看来，尽管盖茨比“言辞繁复，几乎到了荒谬的地步”（第3章，第53页），他荒谬地捏造了富有的“祖先”（第4章，第69页），他那辆被汤姆称为“马戏团篷车”（第7章，第128页）的汽车，以及他所有其他滑稽的做作，他仍然是成功的浪漫化身。然而，这些黑人人物却是对这种成功的讽刺。尼克仅用一句话，用一个意象来描述黑人角色，就将他（或许也包括读者）对盖茨比的一切鄙夷都投射到了他们身上。他们荒诞不经，而非盖茨比。因此，尼克将这些黑人角色视为异类。这些角色成为了替罪羊，为尼克和文本中对盖茨比的重新塑造做出了牺牲。

In addition, Nick’s description of these characters fulfills the kind of narrative function Toni Morrison describes in her analysis of the Africanist presence in white American literature. These black characters – fashionably dressed, riding in a chauffeured limousine, very conscious of their social status in the eyes of others – are the mirror and shadow of Gatsby. The only obvious difference between them is that Gatsby can hide his origins, which he does, whereas they can’t because they can’t hide their color. From Nick’s point of view, despite Gatsby’s “elaborate formality of speech [that] just missed being absurd” (53; ch. 3), his ridiculous fabrication of wealthy “ancestors” (69; ch. 4), his “circus wagon” (128; ch. 7) of a car, as Tom calls it, and all his other ludicrous affectations, he is the romantic embodiment of success. The black characters, however, are its parody. In barely more than one sentence, in the single image with which Nick describes the black characters, he projects onto them everything about Gatsby that he, and perhaps the reader, hold in contempt. They are preposterous, not Gatsby. Thus, Nick’s othering of these characters facilitates their function as scapegoats sacrificed to Nick’s, and the text’s, recuperation of Gatsby.

换句话说，这部小说抹杀了真实的非裔美国人，而他们在20世纪20年代的纽约市——小说的大部分情节都发生在那里——却是一股非常活跃且重要的力量。小说用一种滑稽的刻板印象——殖民主义的“他者”——取而代之，强化了白人至上主义。考虑到20世纪20年代纽约市的历史背景，这种做法绝非小事。当时的纽约市是哈莱姆文艺复兴的中心，也是像棉花俱乐部这样的黑人文化创作场所的所在地，非裔美国爵士乐大师们在那里吸引了大批富有的白人顾客。事实上，鉴于菲茨杰拉德一贯擅长通过描绘具体的文化细节来营造强烈的地域感，我们可以合理地认为，这部小说未能充分展现其所处时代的特征，因为小说中没有让任何一位主要人物光顾哈莱姆夜总会，或者至少没有提及此事。毕竟，像布坎南一家、尼克和乔丹这样时髦的年轻白人肯定会去那里。考虑到《了不起的盖茨比》被认为是爵士时代的代表作——“爵士时代”一词正是菲茨杰拉德创造的——小说中对非裔美国人的抹杀就显得更具讽刺意味了。然而，发明了爵士乐并成为其最著名音乐家的非裔美国人，却在文本中明显缺席。

To put the matter another way, the novel erases real African Americans, who were a very visible and important presence in New York City during the 1920s, where much of the novel is set, and substitutes in their place a comic stereotype – a colonialist other – that reinforces white superiority. This is no small move, given the historical reality of New York City during the 1920s, which was home to the Harlem Renaissance as well as to sites of black cultural production like The Cotton Club, where African American jazz greats attracted wealthy white patrons in droves. In fact, given Fitzgerald’s penchant for creating a strong sense of place through the evocation of specific cultural details, it wouldn’t be unreasonable to argue that the text falls short of the demands of its setting by not having one of the main characters visit a Harlem nightclub, or at least refer to a visit there, for that is surely what fashionable young white people such as the Buchanans, Nick, and Jordan would have done. The novel’s erasure of African Americans becomes even more ironic when we consider that The Great Gatsby is credited with representing the Jazz Age, a term coined by Fitzgerald. Yet black Americans, who invented jazz and who were its most famous musicians, are conspicuously absent from the text.

事实上，小说对当地“被殖民”人口的抹杀正是殖民主义意识形态的一个特征，这种意识形态常常伴随着“他者化”。被殖民的“他者”被忽视，在殖民者的眼中变得隐形，殖民者不仅攫取被殖民者劳动的成果，还将这些成果据为己有。因此，小说象征性地将爵士乐的功劳归于白人也就不足为奇了。我们看到的唯一演奏爵士乐的乐手是盖茨比派对上的白人乐手。尼克告诉我们，他们“可不是那种五人小乐队，而是一个庞大的乐队，里面有双簧管、长号、萨克斯管、维奥尔琴、短号、短笛以及各种高低音鼓”（44；第三章）。换句话说，爵士乐以管弦乐队的形式被“提升”到高级文化的地位，而高级文化属于白人，而不是黑人。

Indeed, the novel’s erasure of this local, “colonized” population is a feature of colonialist ideology that often accompanies othering. The colonized other doesn’t count, becomes invisible to the eyes of the colonizer, who not only takes the fruits of colonized labor but also takes credit for those fruits. It should be no surprise, then, that the novel gives the credit for jazz symbolically to whites. The only musicians we see playing jazz are the white musicians at Gatsby’s party. And they are “no thin five-piece affair,” Nick tells us, “but a whole pit full of oboes and trombones and saxophones and viols and cornets and piccolos and low and high drums” (44; ch. 3). In other words, jazz has been “elevated” to the status of high culture in the form of an orchestra, and high culture belongs to white, not black, Americans.

值得注意的是，乐团着重演奏了一首曾在卡内基音乐厅演出过的曲目，指挥告诉我们，这首曲子是《弗拉基米尔·托斯托夫的世界爵士乐史》（54；第三章）。菲茨杰拉德还能找到比弗拉基米尔·托斯托夫更显眼的欧洲——也就是白人——名字吗？读者绝不会把他误认为是非裔美国人。在这部小说的世界里，爵士乐至少在象征意义上是欧洲人的发明。因此，汤姆警告说：“我们这些占主导地位的种族必须小心，否则其他种族就会掌控一切”（17；第一章），尽管尼克嘲笑他，小说中对汤姆的刻画也对他不加掩饰，但小说似乎在无意识中也持有这种态度。

Significantly, the orchestra spotlights its performance of a piece that, the conductor informs us, was played at Carnegie Hall: “Vladimir Tostoff’s Jazz History of the World” (54; ch. 3). Could Fitzgerald have found a more conspicuously European – that is, white – name than Vladimir Tostoff? There’s no way a reader could mistake him for an African American. In the world of this novel, jazz is, symbolically at least, a European invention. Thus, Tom’s warning that “[i]t’s up to us who are the dominant race to watch out or these other races will have control of things” (17; ch. 1), though mocked by Nick and by the novel’s unflattering characterization of Tom, is an attitude the novel seems, unconsciously, to share.

即使是书中描绘得颇具同情心的“年轻的希腊人迈克尔斯，他在乔治·威尔逊的车库旁边经营着一家咖啡馆”（143；第7章），也并非完全不受……的影响。尼克对少数族裔角色的刻画带有明显的“他者化”色彩。在默特尔遇害后，迈克尔斯整夜陪伴在乔治·威尔逊身边，试图帮助和安慰他。他为自己、乔治以及“前夜的守夜人之一”（168；第八章）做了早餐，这位守夜人第二天早上又回来帮忙。小说还赋予迈克尔斯一定的权威性，让他成为关于默特尔死因的“主要证人”（143；第七章）。然而，迈克尔斯仍然保留着移民“他者”的身份。首先，他体现了所有希腊裔美国人都经营餐馆的刻板印象，这凸显了他的族裔身份。此外，尽管事实上， 20世纪20年代希腊裔美国人经营的餐馆数量急剧增加（Moskos 123），但小说却将迈克尔斯的小餐馆注定要在灰烬谷默默无闻地倒闭，这凸显了他的经济失败。最后，考虑到小说的时代背景和地域条件，迈克尔斯的养育特质可以被视为女性特质，这凸显了他与“真正的”美国男性之间的差异。事实上，从小说设定的20世纪20年代的视角来看，迈克尔斯之所以被接受为调查默特尔之死的“主要证人”（143页；第七章），是因为默特尔作为灰烬谷的一名女性居民，不配得到更好的待遇。

Even the sympathetically portrayed “young Greek, Michaelis, who ran the coffee joint” (143; ch. 7) next to George Wilson’s garage, is not entirely immune from Nick’s othering of ethnic characters. Michaelis spends the whole night sitting up with George Wilson, trying to help and comfort him, after Myrtle is killed. He cooks breakfast for himself, George, and “one of the watchers of the night before” (168; ch. 8) who returns the next morning to help out. And the text gives Michaelis some authority by making him “the principal witness at the inquest” (143; ch. 7) concerning Myrtle’s death. Nevertheless, Michaelis retains the status of the immigrant other. First, he embodies the assumption that all Greek Americans run restaurants, which foregrounds his ethnicity. Moreover, while in point of fact the number of successful Greek American restaurants rose sharply during the 1920s (Moskos 123), the novel dooms Michaelis’ small eatery to economic obscurity in the Valley of Ashes, which foregrounds his economic failure. Finally, given the time and place in which the novel is set, Michaelis’ nurturing qualities can be seen as feminine qualities, which foregrounds his difference from “real” American men. Indeed, from the perspective of the novel’s 1920s setting, Michaelis is accepted as the “principal witness at the inquest” (143; ch. 7) into Myrtle’s death because Myrtle, as a female resident of the Valley of Ashes, doesn’t deserve better.

尼克为何会参与这种种族上的“他者化”？当然，一个重要的原因是，作为主流文化群体的一员，他从小就被灌输了这种观念。然而，尼克自身也存在一些不安全感，这让他需要掌控一切，需要在某种程度上凌驾于他人之上，因此，他特别容易受到殖民主义心理的影响。30岁的尼克仍然依靠父亲的资助，同时他也在努力寻找自己的人生方向。他在纽约度过的这个夏天，只是他一系列失败经历中的最新一次，这些经历既没有带来有前途的事业，也没有带来长久的爱情。尼克担心，他未来唯一可以期待的，正如他自己所说，“单身男士名单越来越短，热情也越来越少，头发也越来越稀疏”（143；第七章）。此外，尽管尼克出身于“体面”的家庭和“体面”的背景，但他显然并不指望能继承一大笔遗产。他需要找到一份职业，但在寻找期间，家里的资助仅够他租一间简陋的小屋，支付日常开销。这当然并非易事，尤其尼克还要花大价钱追求乔丹。但考虑到他成长的文化环境，他无疑有很多朋友来自比他富裕得多的家庭。作为文化精英的一员，尼克深知社会等级的重要性，因此也必然意识到，与同龄人相比，他的经济拮据使他处于社会劣势。因此，尼克至少有两个重要的理由感到需要彰显自己的优越感，从而巩固自己的地位。而将少数族裔边缘化，恰恰能让他产生这种感觉。

Why does Nick engage in this kind of ethnic othering? Of course, one important reason is that, as a member of the dominant cultural group, he was programmed to do so. However, Nick also has some personal insecurity that makes him need to feel he is in control, that makes him need to feel superior to others in some way, and therefore that makes him especially vulnerable to colonialist psychology. At the age of 30, Nick is still being financed by his father while he tries to figure out what he should do with himself. His summer in New York is just the latest in a series of experiences failing to produce either a promising career or a lasting romance. Nick fears that all he has to look forward to is, as he puts it, “a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair” (143; ch. 7). In addition, though Nick comes from the “right” family and the “right” background, apparently he doesn’t expect a large inheritance. He needs to find a profession and, while he searches, his family funding goes only so far as to provide a modest cottage and pay his expenses. Certainly, this is no small feat, especially as Nick’s expenses include courting Jordan. But given the cultural milieu in which he was raised, he doubtless has had many friends who come from families immensely more wealthy than his. As a member of the cultural elite, Nick knows the importance of gradations in social rank and must therefore be aware that his lack of fortune, relative to his peers, puts him at a social disadvantage. Thus, Nick has at least two important reasons to feel the need to assert his superiority and thereby assert his control. And the othering of ethnic subalterns offers him precisely this feeling.
