这部小说也帮助我们从殖民地臣民的视角理解殖民主义心理，这个文化局外人只想被文化精英接纳。尽管盖茨比有两个重要特征，从地理位置上来说，他已经跻身于文本中的文化精英之列——他是白人，而且足够富有。在长岛海峡买一栋豪宅——他与殖民地臣民的共同点远比他多。盖茨比所向往的文化，黛西·费·布坎南所属的文化，并非他自己的文化。那种微妙的社会规则和等级制度对他来说既陌生又难以理解。例如，他完全没有意识到上流社会的东卵居民和他自己居住的“不太时髦”（9；第一章）的西卵居民之间存在着重要的社会差异，正如他对参加他派对的汤姆口中的“形形色色”（114，第六章）的宾客之间的阶级差异也浑然不觉一样。盖茨比似乎根本没意识到，像尼克这样出身的人——耶鲁大学毕业生，出身名门望族，与黛西有亲戚关系——可能对贩卖假债券不感兴趣。盖茨比提出让尼克参与这项犯罪活动，以此换取尼克安排他与黛西重聚。

The novel also helps us understand colonialist psychology from the viewpoint of the colonial subject, the cultural outsider who wants only to be accepted by the cultural elite. Although Gatsby has two important characteristics that place him, geographically, among the cultural elite in the text – he’s white and wealthy enough to buy a mansion on Long Island Sound – he has far more in common with the colonial subject. For the culture to which Gatsby aspires, the culture to which Daisy Fay Buchanan belongs, is not his own. Its subtle social codes and gradations of social status are unfamiliar to him, and he can’t quite get the hang of them. He is oblivious, for example, to the important social distinction between the uppercrust East Eggers and those who live at “the less fashionable” (9; ch. 1) West Egg, where he resides, just as he is oblivious to the gradations of class among the “menagerie” (114, ch. 6), as Tom calls them, who attend his parties. And it doesn’t even seem to occur to Gatsby that a person of Nick’s background – a Yale graduate from a socially established family, related to Daisy – might not be interested in selling fake bonds, a criminal enterprise in which Gatsby offers to include him in return for Nick’s arranging Gatsby’s reunion with Daisy.

简而言之，盖茨比缺乏黛西圈子所需的血统、阶级出身、教养和教育。无论是在初次追求黛西，还是在重逢之后，他都靠谎言和欺骗才得以进入她的生活。因此，盖茨比无家可归：他感到自己无处可归，因为他被夹在两种截然相反的文化之间——他出生的文化和他渴望融入的文化。事实上，他的性格深受一种永无止境的挣扎所支配，他试图摆脱自己的出身，摆脱自己作为北达科他州一个“游手好闲、一事无成的农民”（104；第六章）家庭出身的穷小子的身份。当他告诉尼克他的“家人都去世了”（70；第四章）时，这个谎言承载着他潜意识里的一种心理渴望：盖茨比想要抹去他社会出身的所有痕迹。

In short, Gatsby lacks the proper bloodline, class origin, upbringing, and education for Daisy’s set. He has lied and faked his way into her life, both during their initial courtship and again after their reunion. And as a result, Gatsby is unhomed: he feels he belongs nowhere because he is caught between two antagonist cultures, that into which he was born and that to which he aspires. Indeed, his personality is dominated by an endless struggle to rid himself of his own roots, his own identity as a poor boy from a family of “shiftless and unsuccessful farm people” (104; ch. 6) in North Dakota. When he tells Nick that his “family all died” (70; ch. 4), the lie carries with it the weight of unconscious psychological desire: Gatsby would like to eradicate all trace of his social origins.

我们可以从盖茨比过度模仿的程度中看出这种欲望的强烈程度，他煞费苦心地模仿文化特权阶层的穿着、言谈、举止和生活方式。例如，盖茨比虚构了一个上流社会家庭，编造了一段包括牛津大学教育、狩猎大型猎物、在欧洲各大城市“像年轻的拉贾一样生活”、收藏珠宝（主要是红宝石）以及“画画，只为自己而画”（70；第四章）在内的过往经历。他给自己取了一个听起来更时髦的新名字。他模仿上流社会的言谈举止和“正确”的礼仪，包括称呼每个人为“老伙计”，以及“向宴会上的客人依次鞠躬致谢”（53；第三章）。他还购置了一座巨大的豪宅和许多极其昂贵的物品，而这些物品仅仅是为了炫耀。即使是盖茨比对自私肤浅的黛西的盲目迷恋，也可以用她在盖茨比眼中的象征意义来解释——她是一位“高踞于白色宫殿的公主，国王的女儿，金光闪闪的女孩”（127；第七章）。如果盖茨比能赢得黛西的芳心，就证明他属于她所代表的文化精英阶层，证明他不再是汤姆口中的那个“无名小卒”（137；第七章）。显然，盖茨比努力摆脱吉米·盖茨的身份，就像他努力成为杰伊·盖茨比一样。正如他的人物刻画所展现的那样，模仿不仅意味着费尽心力地融入与自身出生文化截然不同的文化，更意味着……同时，模仿者还会试图摆脱一切被自己视为与该文化不同的事物。因此，模仿包含着自我他者化的过程。

We can see the force of this desire in the excessive quality of Gatsby’s mimicry, his elaborate attempt to imitate the dress, speech, behavior, and lifestyle of the culturally privileged. For example, Gatsby fabricated an upper-class family and invented a past that includes an Oxford education; big-game hunting; living “like a young rajah in all the capitals of Europe”; jewel collecting, “chiefly rubies”; and “painting a little, things for myself only” (70; ch. 4). He created a new, more fashionable-sounding name for himself. He adopted numerous affectations of upperclass speech and “correct” manners, including calling everyone “old sport” and “excus[ing] himself” from his party guests “with a small bow that included each of us in turn” (53; ch. 3). And he purchased an enormous mansion and many very expensive possessions that he uses for display only. Even Gatsby’s blind devotion to the selfish and shallow Daisy can best be explained by her symbolic quality, in Gatsby’s eyes, as a princess “[h]igh in a white palace[,] the king’s daughter, the golden girl” (127; ch. 7). If Gatsby can win Daisy, then he has proof that he belongs to the cultural elite she represents for him, that he is no longer a poor farm boy, a “Mr. Nobody from Nowhere” (137; ch. 7), as Tom calls him. Clearly, Gatsby is trying to stop being Jimmy Gatz as much as he is trying to become Jay Gatsby. For as his characterization illustrates, mimicry involves not only the laborious attempt to be accepted by a culture different from the one into which one was born but a simultaneous attempt to rid oneself of everything one has identified as other than that culture. Mimicry thus involves the othering of oneself.

盖茨比的形象也表明，模仿与无家可归密不可分，因为如果一个人没有无家可归的感觉，就不会进行模仿。模仿是一种心理上的寻求归属感的尝试，即通过寻找一种能够让自己感到归属的文化。然而，促使人们进行模仿的，正是对自身自卑的信念，这也要求人们在一种自己认为优于自身的文化中寻找归属感。因此，正如盖茨比的形象所展现的那样，模仿是一种注定失败的归属尝试，因为即使一个人成功地融入了“优越”的文化，其自卑感也会确保他永远无法真正融入其中。事实上，盖茨比虽然成功地获得了他梦寐以求的家——那座“无论从哪个角度来看都堪称宏伟的建筑……一侧耸立着一座塔楼……还有一个大理石游泳池，以及超过四十英亩的草坪和花园”（9；第一章）——但他实际上并没有真正住在那里。

Gatsby’s characterization also suggests that mimicry is inseparable from unhomeliness, for one wouldn’t engage in mimicry if one didn’t feel unhomed. Mimicry is an attempt to find a home, psychologically, by finding a culture to which one can feel one belongs. But the conviction of one’s own inferiority that produces mimicry also requires one to seek that home in a culture one deems superior to oneself. Therefore, as the portrayal of Gatsby illustrates, mimicry is an attempt to belong that is doomed to failure because, even if one succeeds in adopting the “superior” culture, one’s feelings of inferiority will ensure that one is never at home in it. Indeed, Gatsby, who actually succeeds in acquiring the literal home he seeks, the mansion – the “colossal affair by any standard … with a tower on one side … and a marble swimming pool and more than forty acres of lawn and garden” (9; ch. 1) – does not really occupy his home.

例如，在所有“玛丽·安托瓦内特风格的音乐室和复辟时期风格的沙龙……[以及]铺着玫瑰色和淡紫色丝绸的古典卧室……[以及]更衣室、台球室和带下沉式浴缸的浴室”（96；第五章）中，唯一能看出盖茨比居住痕迹的地方，只有一间小小的“公寓，一间卧室、一间浴室和一间亚当风格的书房”（96；第五章）。此外，盖茨比似乎没有注意到，一方面，在他解雇的训练有素的仆人的照料下，他的家井然有序、一尘不染；另一方面，在沃尔夫希姆提供给他的非专业人员的管理下，他的家却变得杂乱不堪：“到处都是莫名其妙的灰尘，”尼克观察到，“房间里弥漫着霉味，好像好几天没通风了”（154-155；第八章）。事实上，“杂货店小弟说厨房看起来像个猪圈”（120；第七章）。盖茨比似乎也丝毫不在意克利普斯普林格先生的长期逗留，这位显然无处可去的客人擅自住进了主人的一间空卧室。盖茨比对家中这些相当大的变化毫无反应，因为在情感上，他早已不在人世。他无法在自己的家中感到自在，因为那并非他的家：那只是一种模仿。而模仿过于外在，无法为人的内心世界提供任何空间。

For example, among all the “Marie Antoinette music rooms and Restoration salons … [and] period bedrooms swathed in rose and lavender silk … [and] dressing rooms and poolrooms, and bathrooms with sunken baths” (96; ch. 5), the only area that shows any signs of Gatsby’s occupancy is a small “apartment, a bedroom and a bath and an Adam study” (96; ch. 5). Furthermore, Gatsby doesn’t seem to notice the difference between, on the one hand, the well-ordered cleanliness of his home under the care of the trained servants he fires and, on the other hand, the disarray into which it falls at the hands of the nonprofessional crew supplied him by Wolfsheim: “There was an inexplicable amount of dust everywhere,” Nick observes, “and the rooms were musty as though they hadn’t been aired for many days” (154–55; ch. 8). In fact, “[t]he grocery boy reported that the kitchen looked like a pigsty” (120; ch. 7). Neither does Gatsby seem at all perturbed by the prolonged presence of Mr. Klipspringer, evidently a party guest with no place else to go who took it upon himself to stay in one of his host’s empty bedrooms. Gatsby doesn’t respond to these rather radical alterations in his home because, emotionally, he’s not really there. He can’t be at home in his home because it’s not his home: it’s a form of mimicry. And mimicry is too outer-directed to provide any space for one’s inner life.

最后，《了不起的盖茨比》通过汤姆·布坎南这个人物揭示了殖民主义心理的危害，即使是对那些表面上受益于殖民主义的文化特权阶层也造成了损害。汤姆显然是小说中最具文化特权的人物。尽管他缺乏个人修养，行为举止也“不绅士”，但他却拥有种族、民族、社会经济阶层、性别、家庭和教育所带来的所有文化优势。此外，他继承的巨额财富无需他费心维护。“例如，”尼克写道，“汤姆从森林湖运来了一队马球马。我很难相信，和我同龄的人竟然有钱到可以这样做……即使在大学里，他挥霍无度的生活方式也令人不齿”（10；第一章）。

Finally, The Great Gatsby reveals, in the character of Tom Buchanan, the detrimental effects of colonialist psychology even on the culturally privileged who are its apparent beneficiaries. Tom is clearly the most culturally privileged character in the novel. Despite his lack of personal refinement and his “ungentlemanly” behavior, he has all the cultural advantages afforded by race, ethnicity, socioeconomic class, gender, family, and education. In addition, his inherited wealth, which he need not lift a finger to maintain, is enormous. “[F]or instance,” Nick reports, Tom “brought down a string of polo ponies from Lake Forest. It was hard to realize that a man in my own generation was wealthy enough to do that. … [E]ven in college his freedom with money was a matter for reproach” (10; ch. 1).

汤姆也是剧中表现最明显地体现殖民主义心理态度和行为的角色。首先，正如我们之前看到的，他狂热地信奉白人至上主义，这是一种将非白人视为“他者”的殖民主义意识形态，以此为借口压迫他们。事实上，汤姆在情感上深深地认同一种名为“北欧主义”的白人至上主义意识形态。这种意识形态不仅认为白人在基因上优于其他所有种族，而且还认为北欧人——身材高挑、皮肤白皙、头发和眼睛颜色较浅、脸型修长而非圆润——是基因上最优越的高加索人种：他们天生拥有超凡的智慧、体魄和美貌。汤姆引用戈达德的种族主义著作《有色帝国的崛起》 （虚构作品，影射斯托达德的《有色浪潮》）（布鲁科利 208），告诉尼克：“我们是北欧人……我们创造了所有构成文明的东西——哦，科学、艺术等等”（18；第 1 章），但是“如果我们不注意，白种人将会……被”其他种族“彻底淹没”（17；第 1 章）。

Tom is also the character who most overtly exhibits the attitudes and behaviors associated with colonialist psychology. For one thing, as we saw earlier, he fervently believes in white supremacy, a colonialist ideology that others nonwhite people in order to justify subordinating them. Indeed, Tom has emotionally invested in a very specific form of white supremacist ideology called Nordicism, which refers to the belief not only that whites are genetically superior to all other races, but that Nordics – tall people with fair skin, light-colored hair and eyes, and long, rather than round, facial structure – are the most genetically superior Caucasians: they are born with superior intelligence, physical strength, and beauty. Paraphrasing the racist The Rise of the Coloured Empires by Goddard, a fictional stand-in for The Rising Tide of Color by Stoddard (Bruccoli 208), Tom tells Nick, “[W]e’re Nordics … and we’ve produced all the things that go to make civilization – oh, science and art and all that” (18; ch. 1), but “if we don’t look out the white race will be … utterly submerged” by “these other races” (17; ch. 1).

此外，汤姆是个阶级主义者，而对上层阶级固有优越性的信念正是殖民主义为统治被殖民人民辩护的一种方式。事实上，汤姆鄙视所有社会阶层低于他的人，包括他口中的“这些暴发户”，即那些白手起家的人。他说“他们中的很多人不过是走私酒的大贩”（114；第六章）。虽然20世纪20年代确实有不少人通过走私酒发了财，但这里的言外之意是，那些不像汤姆那样继承了财富的人不可信。事实上，汤姆对盖茨比的不信任——他关于暴发户的评论正是针对盖茨比——正是这种阶级主义的产物。而且，这种不信任早在汤姆得知盖茨比是他追求黛西的情敌之前就已经存在了，而他得知盖茨比正是他追求黛西的竞争对手，这让他大吃一惊。

In addition, Tom is a classist, and the belief in the inherent superiority of the upper class is one way in which colonialism justifies the domination of colonized peoples. Indeed, Tom holds everyone in contempt who is beneath him in social class, including “these newly rich people,” as he calls those who have acquired their own wealth. He says that “[a] lot of [them] are just big bootleggers” (114; ch. 6). While it is true that a number of people acquired a fortune through bootlegging in the 1920s, the implication here is that people who have not inherited their wealth as Tom has done are not to be trusted. In fact, Tom’s mistrust of Gatsby, to whom Tom’s comment about the newly rich specifically refers, is the product of his classism. And that mistrust occurs long before Tom learns, to his enormous surprise, that Gatsby is his rival for Daisy’s affections.

汤姆知道盖茨比是西卵镇人，并非他自己圈子里的人。这种社会阶层的差异对读者来说显而易见，但盖茨比显然并不在意。一天下午，汤姆和两个朋友骑马去盖茨比家小酌，三人对盖茨比都表现出轻蔑的态度。汤姆的朋友斯隆先生甚至都没跟盖茨比说话，只是“傲慢地靠在椅子上”（108-109页；第六章）。后来，斯隆先生的女伴喝得有点醉了，邀请盖茨比一起吃晚饭，斯隆先生却催促她出去，盖茨比则去拿外套。三个骑马的人在盖茨比还没来得及上前之前就离开了。汤姆对盖茨比没有意识到自己不受欢迎感到愤怒：“‘我的天哪，我相信那家伙来了，’汤姆说，‘难道他不知道她不想要他吗？’”（109；第六章）。汤姆无法想象黛西究竟是从哪里（110；第一章）遇到盖茨比的，他把这归咎于“如今的女人到处乱跑”，因此会遇到“各种各样的疯子”（110；第六章）。汤姆站在盖茨比占地40英亩、装饰奢华的巨大豪宅里，但他很清楚，而且他完全正确，盖茨比的社会地位比他低。事实上，盖茨比对汤姆如此重视的社会等级观念一无所知，而正是这些等级观念在很大程度上导致了……汤姆对盖茨比的派对、财产以及可能的社会出身都冷嘲热讽。因为汤姆需要让所有人都清楚地知道，他在哪些方面凌驾于他们之上。

Tom knows that Gatsby is a West Egger and not a member of his own set, a social distinction made painfully clear to the reader, though apparently not to Gatsby, when Tom and two friends, all on horseback, drop by Gatsby’s house one afternoon for something to drink. All three treat Gatsby disdainfully. Tom’s friend, Mr. Sloane, doesn’t even speak to Gatsby but just “lounge[s] back haughtily in his chair” (108–9; ch. 6). When Sloane’s ladyfriend becomes tipsy and invites Gatsby to join them for dinner, Mr. Sloane hurries her outside while Gatsby goes to get his coat, and the three riders depart before Gatsby is able to join them. Tom is outraged that Gatsby doesn’t realize he’s unwelcome: “‘My God, I believe the man’s coming,’ said Tom. ‘Doesn’t he know she doesn’t want him?’” (109; ch. 6). Tom can’t imagine “where in the devil” (110; ch. 1) Daisy could have met Gatsby and writes it off to “women run[ning] around too much these days” and therefore meeting “all kinds of crazy fish” (110; ch. 6). Tom is standing in Gatsby’s enormous, lavishly furnished mansion set on a 40-acre estate, and yet he knows, and quite correctly, that Gatsby is his social inferior. Indeed, Gatsby is unaware of the social distinctions so important to Tom, distinctions that are largely responsible for the mocking references Tom makes to Gatsby’s parties, possessions, and probable social origins. For Tom needs everyone to know exactly in what manner he outranks them.

阶级歧视，如同种族歧视一样，是一种将人视为“他者”的意识形态，汤姆在谈到盖茨比时所使用的语言，尤其清晰地体现了这一点。正如我们所见，汤姆称盖茨比的派对为“动物园”（114；第六章），意指动物的聚集地。他称盖茨比的汽车为“马戏团的篷车”（128；第七章），换句话说，就是用来运送动物或人类“怪胎”的交通工具。他还称盖茨比为“疯鱼”（110；第六章）。在汤姆眼中，盖茨比无法拥有完整的人格，因为他没有这种身份所要求的社会地位。当然，汤姆对盖茨比的阶级歧视也是他能够毫不犹豫地除掉盖茨比的原因之一。他明知威尔逊意图谋杀盖茨比，却不采取任何行动阻止他，而是派了全副武装、精神错乱的威尔逊去盖茨比的住所。

Classism, like racism, is an ideology that others people, a fact illustrated with particular clarity in the language Tom uses when referring to Gatsby. As we have seen, Tom calls Gatsby’s parties “menagerie[s]” (114; ch. 6), that is, collections of animals. He refers to Gatsby’s car as a “circus wagon” (128; ch. 7), in other words, something used to transport animals or human “freaks.” And he refers to Gatsby as a “crazy fish” (110; ch. 6). Gatsby cannot have fully human status in Tom’s eyes because he doesn’t have the social rank such a status requires. Surely, Tom’s classist othering of Gatsby is also one of the reasons Tom is able to dispose of him without a moment’s hesitation when he sends Wilson, armed and crazed, to Gatsby’s house, knowing that Wilson intends to murder Gatsby yet taking no action to prevent it.

阶级主义与殖民主义心理之间的联系在汤姆的风流韵事中体现得尤为明显。他并非挑选自己文化背景的女性，而是只勾引工人阶级女性：例如，汤姆和黛西蜜月归来后下榻的圣巴巴拉酒店的“一名女佣”（82页；第四章）；默特尔·威尔逊；以及汤姆在盖茨比的派对上试图搭讪的“出身平凡却很漂亮”（112页；第六章）的年轻女子。这些女性最吸引汤姆的地方似乎在于她们的无力感，这反而增强了他的权力。他可以随心所欲地摆布她们。他公然欺骗默特尔，让她对他言听计从，甚至可以打断她的鼻子而逍遥法外。他打断默特尔的鼻子——仅仅因为她胆敢说出黛西的名字，也就是说，因为她自认为和黛西一样优秀——这表明汤姆把工人阶级女性视为“坏女孩”，视为性对象，仅此而已，她们与他的妻子和乔丹·贝克这样的“好女孩”完全不同。因为他的情妇们在社会地位上低于他，所以他认为她们不配享有上层阶级女性所拥有的尊重。换句话说，汤姆的阶级歧视和性别歧视交织在一起，他的拈花惹草是一种阶级歧视式的“他者化”。因为在汤姆所处的特权文化环境中，工人阶级女性是文化上的局外人。也就是说，汤姆对工人阶级女性的阶级歧视式迫害，类似于白人殖民官员对被殖民土著女性的种族主义迫害：两者都将猎物定义为“坏女孩”，从而将她们视为“他者”，进而允许自己对受害者进行性剥削，同时又免除了自己作为人应尽的一切责任。

The connection between classism and colonialist psychology is especially evident in the nature of Tom’s womanizing. He doesn’t pick on women from his own cultural milieu. He seduces only working-class women: for example, “one of the chambermaids in the Santa Barbara Hotel” (82; ch. 4), where Tom and Daisy stayed upon returning from their honeymoon; Myrtle Wilson; and the “common but pretty” (112; ch. 6) young woman Tom tries to pick up at Gatsby’s party. What seems to attract Tom most to these women is their powerlessness, which augments his own power. He can do what he wants with them. He flagrantly lies to Myrtle. He keeps her at his beck and call. He can even break her nose and get away with it. And the reason he breaks Myrtle’s nose – because she dares to say Daisy’s name, that is, because she thinks she’s as good as Daisy – suggests that Tom sees working-class women as “bad girls,” as sexual objects and nothing more, who are in a separate category altogether from “good girls” like his wife and Jordan Baker. Because his mistresses are his social inferiors, he feels they don’t deserve the respect reserved for upper-class women. In other words, Tom’s classism and sexism are merged, and his womanizing is a form of classist othering. For in terms of Tom’s privileged cultural milieu, working-class women are cultural outsiders. That is, Tom’s classist victimization of working-class women resembles the white colonial official’s racist victimization of women from the indigenous colonized population: both define their prey as “bad girls” and are thereby able to other them, thus allowing themselves to sexually exploit their victims while relieving themselves of all responsibility toward these women as human beings.

没错，默特尔的行为举止确实像个殖民地臣民。她似乎已经内化了汤姆那种殖民主义心理。但由于她处于社会等级的最底层，这种心理反而让她感到无力，也让她更容易受到汤姆的影响：她把汤姆的社会优越感视为一种宝贵的财富，以至于她会不惜一切代价留住他。在汤姆用来幽会的那间三居室小公寓里举行的派对上，我们最清楚地看到了默特尔的殖民地臣民形象，她也以自己的方式模仿着汤姆。

Certainly, Myrtle behaves like a colonial subject. She seems to have internalized the same colonialist psychology Tom has. But because she’s on the bottom rung of the social hierarchy, that psychology disempowers her and makes her especially vulnerable to Tom: she considers his social superiority such a valuable asset that she will do anything to keep him. We see Myrtle as the colonial subject most clearly during the party at the small, three-room apartment Tom keeps for their trysts, where she engages in her own form of mimicry.

威尔逊夫人……现在穿着一件精致的米色雪纺下午礼服……受这件礼服的影响，她的性格也发生了变化……她的笑声、手势、言语都变得越来越剧烈。

Mrs. Wilson … was now attired in an elaborate afternoon dress of creamcolored chiffon … With the influence of the dress her personality had also undergone a change … Her laughter, her gestures, her assertions became more violently affected moment by moment.

（35；第2章）

(35; ch. 2)

默特尔按照她想象中富人的样子行事，抱怨电梯男孩，仿佛他是她的仆人一般，“她绝望地扬起眉毛，对底层人民的懒散感到不满。‘这些人！你得时刻盯着他们，’”她说（36；第二章）。然后她“径直走进厨房，仿佛那里有十几个厨师等着她吩咐”（36；第二章）。显然，默特尔表现得如此虚伪，是因为她觉得自己“真实的自我”不够好，因为她觉得自己不如汤姆和他的社交圈。

Behaving as she imagines the very wealthy behave, Myrtle complains about the elevator boy as if he were her servant, “rais[ing] her eyebrows in despair at the shiftlessness of the lower orders. ‘These people! You have to keep after them all the time,’” she says (36; ch. 2). Then she “swept into the kitchen, implying that a dozen chefs awaited her orders there” (36; ch. 2). Clearly, Myrtle behaves in such an artificial manner because she believes that her “real self” isn’t good enough, because she feels inferior to Tom and his social set.

然而，殖民主义心理学赋予汤姆的自由和权力，无论多么巨大，都是有代价的。除了殖民主义心理学通过助长和合理化不道德行为，对文化特权阶层造成的显而易见的精神或道德伤害之外，它还会造成痛苦的内心世界。汤姆·布坎南的遭遇正是如此。

However much freedom and power colonialist psychology affords Tom, though, it comes at a cost. Besides the obvious spiritual or moral damage colonialist psychology does to the culturally privileged by facilitating and providing a rationale for unethical behavior, it also can produce a tormented inner life. This is precisely what it does to Tom Buchanan.

如果没有与之形成对比的文化劣势，文化优越感也就无从谈起。而没有人比汤姆更彻底地内化了这种观念。他的行为仿佛表明，他的社会地位取决于将所有“不如”他的人视为异类，然后通过某种形式的攻击来展现自己的“优越感”。他不仅怀有种族主义、阶级主义和性别歧视的态度；正如我们所见，他不断地、咄咄逼人地展现这些态度。正是这些反复出现且琐碎的行为，暗示着背后存在着强烈的心理动机。

There could be no cultural superiority if there were no cultural inferiority to contrast with it. And no one internalizes this idea more thoroughly than Tom. He behaves as if his social status depended on othering everyone “beneath” him and then showing his “superiority” through some form of aggression. He doesn’t merely harbor racist, classist, and sexist attitudes; as we have seen, he continually and aggressively displays them. And it’s the recurrent and petty nature of these displays that suggests the existence of a strong psychological motive.

例如，汤姆残忍地利用乔治·威尔逊的贫穷，不仅抢走了他的妻子，还就乔治想从他那里买的那辆车不断折磨他。乔治认为自己可以把车转手卖掉赚一笔，而他急需用钱，汤姆却反复戏弄他，让他不知是否愿意把车卖给他，甚至提出把盖茨比的豪华轿车卖给他，好让乔治承认自己买不起。事实上，汤姆甚至连从一个穷老头那里买只小狗都要羞辱他，以此来证明老头并没有在狗的价值上欺骗他：“给你钱，”汤姆一边说着一边递给老头十美元，“去用这些钱再买十条狗吧！”（32；第二章）。汤姆对社会地位低于他的人表现出毫无必要且公开的敌意的例子还有很多，但关键在于，如果他真的对自己的社会地位感到自信，他就无需如此咄咄逼人地炫耀自己的优越感了。

For example, Tom takes cruel advantage of George Wilson’s poverty, not only by stealing his wife but also by tormenting George about the car George would like to buy from Tom. George thinks he can resell the car at a profit, which he badly needs, and Tom toys with him repeatedly concerning whether or not he will let George have the vehicle, even offering to sell him Gatsby’s enormous luxury car so that George will have to admit he can’t afford it. Indeed, Tom can’t even buy a puppy from a poor old man without insulting him to show that the man has not fooled Tom about the value of the dog: “Here’s your money,” Tom snaps as he gives the man ten dollars; “[g]o and buy ten more dogs with it” (32; ch. 2). There are many more examples of Tom’s unnecessary and open hostility toward his social inferiors, but the point is that he wouldn’t need to display his social superiority so aggressively if he were secure in it.

汤姆缺乏安全感的一个解释是，他来自中西部，因此他永远无法拥有那种文化地位——在那个年代，只有那些自祖辈很久以前就居住在东部的富裕古老贵族家族才能享有这种地位。他曾就读于耶鲁大学，而且他肯定知道，正如菲茨杰拉德所说……身为普林斯顿大学的中西部人，汤姆痛苦地意识到，无论他拥有多少财富，生活多么奢华，他永远无法拥有这种文化上的优越感。在这一点上，汤姆本身就是个异类，这在他最近搬到东部之后，无疑让他格外不安。我认为，正是这种认知——无论是有意识的还是无意识的——让他感到极度缺乏安全感，以至于他需要抓住一切机会来证明自己的社会优越性。

One explanation for Tom’s insecurity is that he is from the Midwest, and therefore he can never have the cultural status that, in his day, belonged only to the wealthy old blueblood families who had lived in the East since their forebears arrived in America so long ago. He attended Yale and must know, as Fitzgerald painfully knew as a Midwesterner at Princeton, that this is the one kind of cultural superiority he can never have, no matter how many millions he has or how lavishly he lives. In this one way, Tom himself is other, a fact that must be especially disconcerting since his recent move east. And I think it is this knowledge, whether it is conscious or unconscious, that makes him feel insecure enough to need to prove his social superiority at every conceivable opportunity.

尼克察觉到了问题所在，他指的是汤姆对《有色帝国的崛起》的评论：“他专注的样子有些可悲，仿佛他的自满……已经无法满足他了”（18；第一章）。尼克补充道：“某种东西让他反复琢磨那些陈旧的想法，仿佛他那坚韧的肉体上的自负已经无法滋养他那专横跋扈的心”（25；第一章）。尼克无法解释汤姆的问题，但我们可以：赋予汤姆力量的殖民主义心理同时也削弱了他的自信，因为它一方面告诉他“如果你不是顶峰，你就什么都不是”，另一方面又让他更加在意自己可能“不在顶峰”的任何方面。

Nick senses the problem when he says, referring to Tom’s comments about The Rise of the Coloured Empires, “There was something pathetic in his concentration as if his complacency [self-satisfaction] … was not enough to him any more” (18; ch. 1). “Something,” Nick adds, “was making him nibble at the edge of stale ideas as if his sturdy physical egotism no longer nourished his peremptory [dictatorial] heart” (25; ch. 1). Nick can’t explain Tom’s problem, but we can: the colonialist psychology that empowers Tom also undermines his confidence because it simultaneously tells him, “If you’re not on top, you’re nobody” and heightens his awareness of any way in which he might not be “on top.”

我希望通过对《了不起的盖茨比》的解读能够阐明这一点：我并非暗示菲茨杰拉德的小说可以被解读为殖民主义寓言，也并非暗示其人物可以被解读为殖民主义典型人物的象征性代表，就像霍桑的《年轻的古德曼·布朗》（1835）或《牧师的黑面纱》（1836）中的人物象征着善恶等抽象道德概念一样。相反，我认为《了不起的盖茨比》揭示了殖民主义心理（殖民主义意识形态赖以存在的心理）如何在本土运作，以维持自美国建国以来就存在的文化权力失衡。因为尽管这个国家的缔造者在制定美国宪法时与盎格鲁-欧洲政治哲学决裂，但他们仍然继承了盎格鲁-欧洲文化哲学的许多方面。

As I hope this reading of The Great Gatsby makes clear, I’m not suggesting that Fitzgerald’s novel can be read as a colonialist allegory, that its characters can be interpreted as symbolic stand-ins for colonialist types the way that characters in, for example, Hawthorne’s “Young Goodman Brown” (1835) or “The Minister’s Black Veil” (1836) are symbolic stand-ins for abstract moral concepts like good and evil. Rather, I’m suggesting that The Great Gatsby reveals the ways in which colonialist psychology, on which colonialist ideology depends, operates on the home front to sustain the imbalances of cultural power that have characterized America since its inception. For although the founders of this nation broke with Anglo-European political philosophy when they framed the American Constitution, they nevertheless inherited many aspects of Anglo-European cultural philosophy.

最显著的是，他们继承了这样一种信念：白种人是上帝的选民，是世界的天然统治者。也就是说，他们继承了盎格鲁-欧洲殖民主义意识形态。这种意识形态使得少数几个小国——英国、法国、西班牙、葡萄牙和荷兰——从18世纪中期到20世纪中期统治了全球大部分地区，并反过来使美国白人得以统治我们今天称之为美利坚合众国的印第安人土地，并将非洲人奴役为奴。如此成功的意识形态难以根除。正如《了不起的盖茨比》所揭示的那样，殖民主义意识形态如此成功的原因之一在于，它背后有着复杂的心理机制支撑，这种机制深刻地影响着我们看待自己和他人的方式。

Most conspicuously, they inherited the belief that members of the white race are God’s chosen people and the natural rulers of the world. That is, they inherited Anglo-European colonialist ideology, which permitted a small group of small nations – England, France, Spain, Portugal, and the Netherlands – to dominate most of the globe from the mid eighteenth to the mid twentieth century and which permitted white Americans, in turn, to dominate the Native American lands we now call the United States of America and to hold African captives as slaves. An ideology this successful dies hard. And as The Great Gatsby illustrates, one reason colonialist ideology is so successful is that it is supported by a complex psychology that strongly influences the way we perceive ourselves and others.

殖民主义心理在当今美国是否像《了不起的盖茨比》所暗示的那样，在20世纪20年代根深蒂固？当然，将美国公民视为“他者”的做法已不再受法律支持，这与20世纪60年代民权运动之前那种压迫所有非白人美国人以及许多白人移民的法律歧视截然不同。而且，尊重文化差异也得到了我们社会的倡导。政府、媒体和教育体系都发生了前所未有的变化。毫无疑问，这些变化构成了一项重大进步。

Is colonialist psychology as pervasive a presence in America today as The Great Gatsby suggests it was during the 1920s? Certainly, the othering of American citizens is no longer supported by law, as it was in the legal discrimination that subjugated all nonwhite Americans, and many white immigrants, before the Civil Rights Movement of the 1960s. And respect for cultural difference is promoted by our government, our media, and our educational system as it has never been before. Surely, these changes constitute a significant improvement.

然而，白人至上主义的反弹，例如种族主义仇恨团体的激增；隐性种族歧视的持续存在，例如在住房、就业和教育领域；将无家可归者边缘化，甚至将其从美国人的意识和良知中抹去；以及当今美国仍然盛行的各种形式的“他者化”，都清楚地表明，美国在全球推行的新殖民主义行径，在未来很长一段时间内，都将伴随着国内类似形式的延续。正如《了不起的盖茨比》所揭示的那样，殖民主义心理及其所支持的歧视性意识形态，已成为我们历史和文化遗产的一部分。而每一代美国人都必须重新面对这一现实。

Yet white supremacist backlash, for example as witnessed in the proliferation of racist hate groups; the persistence of covert racial discrimination, for example in housing, employment, and education; the othering of the homeless, indeed their virtual erasure from American consciousness and conscience; and all the forms of othering that still flourish in this country today make it clear that America’s neocolonialist enterprises around the globe will be accompanied by versions thereof at home for a long time to come. For colonialist psychology and the discriminatory ideologies it supports are part of our historical and cultural legacy, as The Great Gatsby illustrates. And this is a reality that will have to be confronted anew by each generation of Americans.

拓展练习题：后殖民主义视角下的其他文学作品

Questions for further practice: postcolonial approaches to other literary works

以下问题旨在作为范例。它们可以帮助你运用后殖民批评来解读文中提及的文学作品或你选择的其他文本。

The following questions are intended as models. They can help you use postcolonial criticism to interpret the literary works to which they refer or other texts of your choice.

1分析奇努阿·阿切贝的小说《瓦解》（1958）中的反殖民主义倾向。为了完成这项任务，请考察小说对非洲前殖民时期部落生活的描写。殖民接触导致了哪些损失？殖民者采用了哪些策略来向当地居民灌输他们的思想？为什么殖民者如此成功？

1 Analyze the anticolonialist agenda of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart (1958). In order to accomplish this task, examine the novel’s representation of precolonial tribal life in Africa. What is lost as a result of colonial contact? What are the colonizers’ strategies in indoctrinating the native population to their way of thinking? Why are the colonizers so successful?

2牙买加·金凯德的《我母亲的自传》（1996）揭示了殖民主义对殖民者（菲利普和莫伊拉）以及被殖民者（主要是被殖民者）的社会和心理影响。例如，分析书中通过叙述者苏埃拉、她的父亲和继母、她的情人罗兰以及拉巴特夫妇的人物刻画，揭示的腐败、阶级分化和殖民教育等问题。苏埃拉是如何在心理上生存下来，并获得个人独立和自信的？

2 What does Jamaica Kincaid’s The Autobiography of My Mother (1996) suggest about the social and psychological effects of colonialism on the colonizers (Philip and Moira) and, primarily, on the colonized? Analyze, for example, the problems of corruption, class division, and colonial education as they are revealed in the characterizations of Xuela, the narrator; her father and stepmother; her lover, Roland; and Monsieur and Madame LaBatte. How does Xuela manage to survive psychologically and achieve personal independence and self-confidence?

3分析V.S.奈保尔的小说《模仿者》（1967）中“无家可归”和“模仿”这两个主题。我们如何理解殖民主义剥夺了叙述者稳定的（或任何）自我认同感？他如何试图寻找身份认同？他最终成功了吗？为什么？叙述者的语言（用词、语气、意象）如何揭示了他与自身经历的情感距离？这又如何加深了我们对小说的理解？

3 Analyze the themes of unhomeliness and mimicry as they apply to V. S. Naipaul’s The Mimic Men (1967). How might we say that colonialism has robbed the narrator of a stable (or of any) sense of himself? How does he try to find an identity? Does he ever succeed? Why or why not? How does the narrator’s language (word choice, tone, imagery) reveal his emotional distance from his own experience, and what does this add to our understanding of the novel?

4玛丽·雪莱的《弗兰肯斯坦》（1818）揭示了“他者化”的意识形态和心理运作机制的哪些方面？例如，雪莱对欧洲乡绅阶层的刻画，以阿尔方斯·弗兰肯斯坦为代表，以及她对其他阶层的刻画，是如何体现“他者化”的？他的家人代表着正当的“自我”，与异己的“他者”形成对比，例如阿拉伯商人（尤其要注意阿拉伯商人与他信奉基督教的妻子之间的对比）、抚养伊丽莎白的农民、维克多在研究女怪物期间居住的农民，以及克莱瓦尔死后他遇到的农民。萨菲在哪些方面可以被视为在反抗某种殖民统治？又在哪些方面可以被视为在寻求这种统治？我们应该如何解读这个怪物？他是否可以被视为小说中的后殖民主义批评家，一个不愿接受殖民统治的异乡“他者”？他又在哪些方面不符合这一角色？

4 What does Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein (1818) reveal about the ideological and psychological operations of “othering”? For example, how does Shelley’s portrayal of the European landed gentry, embodied in Alphonse Frankenstein and his family, represent the rightful “self” in contrast with an alien “other” embodied in, for example, the Arab merchant (among other things, note the contrast between the Arab and his Christian wife), the peasants who raised Elizabeth, the peasants among whom Victor lived while he worked on the female monster, and the peasants he met after the death of Clerval? In what ways might Safie be viewed as resisting a kind of colonial subjugation? In what ways might she be viewed as seeking it? How should we interpret the monster in this context? Might he be seen as the novel’s postcolonial critic, the unhomely “other” who will not accept colonialist domination? In what ways does he not fit this role?

5扎克斯·姆达的《红色之心》（2000）对文化信仰、经济得失以及土地所有权和使用权之间的关系提出了怎样的见解？例如，我们该如何解释当地居民与土地开发商之间的冲突，以及当地居民内部的冲突？这部小说似乎在宣扬人与自然之间怎样的关系？对环境，尤其是自然环境的描写，在我们对小说这一方面的理解中扮演着怎样的角色？

5 What does Zakes Mda’s The Heart of Redness (2000) suggest about the relationship among cultural beliefs, economic loss and gain, and the ownership and use of land? For example, how might we account for, on the one hand, the conflict between the local people and the land-developers and, on the other hand, the conflict among the local people themselves? What kinds of relationships between human beings and nature does the novel seem to promote? What role do descriptions of setting, especially of the natural setting, play in our response to this aspect of the novel?

笔记

Notes

1如今， “帝国主义”和“殖民主义”这两个词经常被混用。然而，在二战之前，当英国仍拥有大片殖民地时，这两个术语之间的区别相当清晰。严格来说，帝国主义是指通过军事征服、控制自然资源、控制世界市场和殖民等手段，建立和维持帝国（由单一统治者控制的一系列领土）的体系。殖民主义（通过建立殖民地来扩大领土控制）仅仅是帝国主义的一种形式。然而，在二战后的几十年里，诸如新殖民主义、文化帝国主义和文化殖民化等概念——所有这些概念都涉及一个社会对另一个社会的经济和文化统治，而无需扩大领土控制——模糊了帝国主义和殖民主义之间的界限。

1 Today, the words imperialism and colonialism are often used interchangeably. Before World War II, however, when Britain still had extensive colonial holdings, the distinction between the two terms was fairly clear. Strictly speaking, imperialism is the system of forming and maintaining an empire (a collection of territories under the control of a single ruler) through such means as military conquest, the control of natural resources, the control of world markets, and colonization. Colonialism (the extension of territorial control through the establishment of colonies) is merely one form of imperialism. In the decades since World War II, however, such concepts as neocolonialism, cultural imperialism, and cultural colonization – all of which involve the economic and cultural domination of one society by another without the extension of territorial control – have blurred the distinction between the terms imperialism and colonialism.

2作为历史术语，“后殖民”（带连字符）通常指一个国家摆脱另一个国家的殖民统治。然而，对于文学批评和其他形式的文化研究而言，“后殖民”一词却存在争议。正如本章所述，殖民统治的结束——即殖民者撤离其军事和政府力量，使被殖民国家获得解放——并不意味着被解放国家就此停止遭受技术更发达的国家在文化、社会或经济上的剥削。如果一个国家仍然遭受剥削，例如，跨国公司利用其廉价劳动力和缺乏环境保护法律进行不公平的剥削，那么就很难说这个国家真正实现了后殖民统治。因此，我们在此使用“后殖民”（不带连字符）一词来指代一种用于分析文学和其他文化产品的理论框架，并非仅仅局限于殖民者撤离后创作的文本。相反，我们感兴趣的是分析殖民化时期产生的文学作品，这意味着我们对一个国家与殖民压迫者首次接触后任何时期创作的文学作品都感兴趣。

2 As a historical term, the word post-colonial (hyphenated) generally refers to the cessation of colonialist domination of one country by another. For literary criticism and other forms of cultural studies, however, post-colonial is a problematic term. For as this chapter explains, the cessation of colonialist domination – the liberation of a colonized nation by the removal of the colonizers’ military and governmental forces – does not automatically result in the cessation of the cultural, social, or economic exploitation of the liberated nation by more technologically developed countries. And it is difficult to say that a nation is truly post-colonial if it continues to be exploited by, for example, multinational corporations taking unfair advantage of its cheap labor and its lack of environmental protection laws. By employing the term postcolonial (without the hyphen), as we do here, to name a theoretical framework used to analyze literature and other cultural productions, we are not limiting ourselves to texts written after the removal of the colonizers’ military and governmental forces. Rather, we’re interested in analyzing writing produced as a result of colonization, which means we’re interested in literature written at any time following a nation’s initial contact with a colonialist oppressor.

3值得注意的是，双重意识的概念最早是由非裔美国作家W.E.B.杜波依斯于1903年在《黑人的灵魂》一书中提出的。

17与下文讨论的所有术语一样， “保护主义”一词在不同的时期和不同的地域有着不同的含义。如今，尤其是在美国， “保护主义”通常指的是促进可持续发展的努力：对空气、水、土壤、木材、可再生和不可再生能源以及金属和其他矿石等自然资源进行负责任的利用和管理，以确保子孙后代能够继续利用这些资源。然而，从美国和世界各地保护组织的角度来看， “保护主义”指的是将大片未受破坏的土地划为保护区，以保护其所支持的所有植物和非人类动物生命形式——即保护生物多样性——这既是为了保护生物多样性本身，也是为了地球的环境福祉。这是我们在此使用的该词的第二个含义。相关且经常重叠的术语包括生态学、环境主义和生态批评。

17 Like all of the terminology discussed below, the word conservationism has had different meanings at different times and in different places. Today, especially in the United States, conservationism often refers to efforts to promote sustainability: the conscientious use and management of such natural resources as air, water, soil, timber, renewable and nonrenewable energy sources, and metal and other mineral ores so that they will continue to be available for use by future generations. However, from the perspective of conservation organizations in the US and around the world, conservationism means the setting aside of large tracts of unspoiled land as protected areas for the preservation of all the forms of plant and nonhuman animal life it supports – that is, for the preservation of its biodiversity – both for its own sake and for the environmental well-being of the planet. It is the second meaning of the word we are using here. Related, and often overlapping, terms include ecology, environmentalism, and ecocriticism.

生态学是一门研究生物（例如动物、人类、昆虫、植物和微生物）与其所处特定环境（包括生物环境和非生物环境）之间复杂关系的科学。生态学领域还包括研究人类管理不善对自然环境造成的有害影响，以及如何保护或恢复自然环境。

Ecology is the scientific study of the complex web of relationships among living things (for example, among animals, human animals, insects, plants, and microorganisms) and the specific environments – living and non-living – they inhabit. The field of ecology includes the study of the harmful effects of human mismanagement on the natural environment and how the natural environment might be preserved or recuperated.

环境保护主义通常指的是有组织地倡导保护自然——即自然环境，它包括所有非人类生命形式——免受污染和其他人为破坏的侵害。环保人士游说政府官员，组织抗议活动，并筹集资金来支持他们的工作，其中包括保护和恢复本土动植物。

Environmentalism generally refers to organized advocacy for the protection of nature – the natural environment, which consists of all nonhuman forms of life – from the destructive forces of pollution and other human damage. Environmental activists lobby government officials, organize protests, and raise funds to support their work, which includes the preservation and restoration of native plant and nonhuman animal life.

生态批评兴起于20世纪90年代的文学研究领域，它关注文学作品中对环境的描绘，以及这些描绘所揭示的文学作品对自然的态度。生态批评家们坚信保护自然环境的重要性，并认为人类文化应当尊重自然，与自然和谐共处。正如谢丽尔·格洛特费尔蒂所言，生态批评是“一种以地球为中心的文学研究方法”（第十八页）。其奠基性著作包括劳伦斯·布埃尔的《环境想象：梭罗、自然写作与美国文化的形成》（1995）以及谢丽尔·格洛特费尔蒂和哈罗德·弗罗姆合著的《生态批评读本：文学生态学的里程碑》（1996）。

Ecocriticism, which emerged in literary studies during the 1990s, focuses on literary representations of the environment and what those representations suggest about the literary work’s attitude toward nature. Ecocritics believe strongly in the preservation of the natural world and in the proposition that human culture should respect and harmonize with nature. Ecocriticism is, as Cheryll Glotfelty puts it, “an earth-centered approach to literary studies” (xviii). Foundational texts include Lawrence Buell’s The Environmental Imagination: Thoreau, Nature Writing, and the Formation of American Culture (1995) and Cheryll Glotfelty and Harold Fromm’s The Ecocriticism Reader: Landmarks in Literary Ecology (1996).

18有关后殖民主义和保护主义对环境的关注之间的分歧的深入讨论，请参阅尼克松（233-62）。

18 For a thorough discussion of the divide between postcolonial and conservationist concerns about the environment, see Nixon (233–62).

19根据联合国土著问题常设论坛的说法，“据估计，全球70个国家有超过3.7亿土著人民。他们秉持独特的传统，保留着与他们所居住的主流社会截然不同的社会、文化、经济和政治特征。他们遍布世界各地，从北极到南太平洋，根据普遍定义，他们是居住在某一国家或地区的人的后裔，当时不同文化或种族的人迁徙至此。后来，新来者通过征服、占领、定居或其他手段成为主导者”（第五届会议，2006年5月）。土著人民——也被称为原住民、第一民族、第一民族和部落民族——包括美洲的土著人民（例如，美国的拉科塔人、危地马拉的玛雅人和玻利维亚的艾马拉人）；北极圈的因纽特人；北欧的萨米人；肯尼亚和坦桑尼亚的马赛人；菲律宾南部的 Katawhang Lumad；印度、孟加拉国和尼泊尔的檀香；澳大利亚中部的阿伦特；和新西兰的毛利人。

19 According to the United Nations Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues, “It is estimated that there are more than 370 million indigenous people spread across 70 countries worldwide. Practicing unique traditions, they retain social, cultural, economic and political characteristics that are distinct from those of the dominant societies in which they live. Spread across the world from the Arctic to the South Pacific, they are the descendants – according to common definition – of those who inhabited a country or a geographical region at the time when people of different cultures or ethnic origins arrived. The new arrivals later became dominant through conquest, occupation, settlement or other means” (Fifth Session, May 2006). Indigenous peoples – also referred to as native peoples, first peoples, first nations, and tribal peoples – include, for example, those of the Americas (for instance, the Lakota in the United States, the Maya in Guatemala, and the Aymara in Bolivia); the Inuit of the Arctic circle; the Saami of northern Europe; the Maasai of Kenya and Tanzania; the Katawhang Lumad of the southern Philippines; the Santal of India, Bangladesh, and Nepal; the Arrernte of central Australia; and the Maori of New Zealand.

19世纪50年代， 20位白人美国人出于旅游目的对优胜美地地区产生了兴趣。1864年，该地区的一部分被划为公园，由加利福尼亚州管理。1890年，优胜美地国家公园正式成立，如今占地1169平方英里。1916年，负责管理美国国家公园的国家公园管理局成立。亚当斯拍摄的该地区著名照片于1927年出版。

20 White Americans became interested in the Yosemite region for tourist purposes during the 1850s. In 1864, a portion of the area was set aside as a park under the management of the state of California. In 1890 Yosemite National Park – today comprising 1,169 square miles – was created. In 1916, the National Park Service, which oversees the management of America’s national parks, was established. Adams’ famous photographs of the area were published in 1927.

21首次“债务换自然”发生在1987年，当时国际自然保护协会（CI）偿还了玻利维亚部分外债，以换取该国同意投资保护玻利维亚北部及其周边地区（即现在的贝尼生物圈保护区）的土地。自那时以来，全球范围内已投入超过10亿美元用于“债务换自然”项目。如需了解国际自然保护协会对这一做法的看法，请访问www.conservation.org/global/gcf/…/GCF_debtfor-nature_overview.pdf。如需了解对这一做法的批判性观点，包括其对土著居民的负面影响，请参阅Knicley的著作。

21 The first “debt-for-nature swap” occurred in 1987 when Conservation International (CI) paid a portion of Bolivia’s foreign debt in exchange for that country’s agreement to invest in the protection of lands in northern Bolivia in and adjacent to what is now called the Beni Biosphere Reserve. Since then, over a billion dollars have been spent in debt-for-nature swaps worldwide. For CI’s view of this practice, go online to www.conservation.org/global/gcf/…/GCF_debtfor-nature_overview.pdf. For a critical view of this practice, including its negative effects on indigenous peoples, see Knicley.

Coetzee’s The Lives of Animals (1999), Arundhati Roy’s The God of Small Things (1997), Derek Walcott’s Collected Poems 1948–1984 (1986), Ah Cheng’s “The King of Trees” (1985), Ngugi wa Thiong’o’s Petals of Blood (1977), Flora Nwapa’s Efuru (1966), and Alejo Carpentier’s The Lost Steps (1953).

25正如我的学生提醒我的那样，默特尔·威尔逊被撞身亡的场景中出现了一位“肤色苍白、衣着体面的黑人”，他并没有被区别对待。这位黑人“走到”一位警官身边，讲述他所目睹的一切，而警官也急于听取他的证词（147；第七章）。这段简短的描写赋予了这位黑人角色一定的权威性。然而，小说中弥漫的种族氛围表明，如果他肤色不够白皙、衣着不够体面，他的证词就不会被认真对待。事实上，有人可能会认为，菲茨杰拉德这样描写他是为了让警官和（白人）读者有理由相信他的证词。

25 As my students have reminded me, the scene of Myrtle Wilson’s hit-and-run death includes “[a] pale, well dressed Negro” who is not othered. This character “step[s] near” a police officer in order to tell what he witnessed, and the officer is eager to take the man’s information (147; ch. 7). This brief passage thus confers some authority on the black character. Nevertheless, the racial atmosphere pervading the novel suggests that he wouldn’t have been taken seriously had he not had light skin and worn good clothing. Indeed, one could argue that Fitzgerald portrayed him in this manner so that the officer, and the (white) reader, would have reason to believe his testimony.

13 概览

13 Gaining an overview

如果您已经阅读了前面的几章，您可能会感到信息量过大，以及各种批评理论之间相互交织的复杂方式让您有些不知所措。以下问题并非旨在总结我们讨论过的各种批评流派，而是帮助您整理思路，反思所学内容，并决定您想要进一步研究哪些理论。当然，前面的章节提供了“批评家对文学文本提出的一些问题”和“拓展练习题”（作为应用相关批评理论的具体指导），它们比下面列出的简短问题更加详尽。然而，接下来的问题可以为您提供一个关于我们所学理论的概览，从而让您有机会更全面地了解各种批评理论之间的异同。

If you’ve read several of the preceding chapters, you may be feeling a bit overwhelmed both by the amount of information you’ve consumed and by the various ways in which many critical theories overlap with one another. The following questions are offered, not as a summary of the schools of criticism we’ve discussed but as ways to organize your thoughts as you reflect on what you’ve learned and decide which theories you’d like to pursue further. Certainly, “Some Questions Critics Ask about Literary Texts” and “Questions for Further Practice” (which preceding chapters provide as specific guidelines for applying the critical theories they describe) are more thorough than the brief questions listed below. However, the questions that follow offer you a kind of bird’s-eye overview of the theories we’ve studied and, therefore, an opportunity to see more generally the ways in which critical theories both resemble and differ from one another.

精神分析批评——文本是如何通过（有意或无意地）表现其人物（或作者）的心理欲望、需求和冲突而形成的？

Psychoanalytic Criticism – How is the text shaped by its (intentional or unintentional) representation of the psychological desires, needs, and conflicts of its characters (or the psychological desires, needs, and conflicts of its author)?

马克思主义批评——文本是如何受到其（有意或无意的）对资本主义和/或阶级主义的表述的影响的？这种表述是支持还是削弱了这些压迫性的社会经济意识形态？

Marxist Criticism – How is the text shaped by its (intentional or unintentional) representation of capitalism and/or classism? Does this representation support or undermine these oppressive socioeconomic ideologies?

女性主义批评——文本是如何（有意或无意地）受到父权制规范和价值观的影响的？这种呈现方式是支持还是削弱了这些压迫性的规范和价值观？

Feminist Criticism – How is the text shaped by its (intentional or unintentional) representation of patriarchal norms and values? Does this representation support or undermine these oppressive norms and values?

新批评——这部作品是一部伟大的文学作品吗？也就是说，它是否既具有内在的统一性，又具有普遍意义的主题？

New Criticism – Is the text a great work of literature? That is, does it have both organic unity and a theme of universal significance?

读者反应批评——读者在阅读文本时如何理解文本的意义，以及他们所理解的意义与文本之间有何关系？

Reader-Response Criticism – How do readers make meaning as they read the text, and what is the relationship between the meaning they make and the text?

结构主义批评——我们理解文本所依据的潜在结构系统（例如，原型系统、模态系统或叙事系统）是什么？结构主义批评家通常将文本的潜在结构称为其语法，它可以被表达为一种“数学公式”，代表了人物及其行为的功能。

Structuralist Criticism – What is the underlying structural system (for example, archetypal, modal, or narratological) by which we make sense of the text? Structuralist critics often refer to a text’s underlying structure as its grammar, which might be expressed as a kind of “mathematical formula” that represents the functions of characters and their actions.

解构批评——我们通过分析文本的自相矛盾，而不是试图将这些矛盾归结为某种总体主题，来了解文本中运作的意识形态（或多种意识形态）是什么？

Deconstructive Criticism – What do we learn about the ideology (or ideologies) operating in the text by analyzing the text’s self-contradictions rather than by trying to resolve those contradictions into some overarching theme?

新历史主义——文本如何参与历史的诠释？具体而言，文本在作品产生的文化和/或作品被诠释的文化中盛行的话语（与特定意识形态相关的语言使用方式，例如自由人文主义、基督教原教旨主义或白人至上主义的话语）的传播中扮演着什么角色？

New Historicism – How does the text participate in the interpretation of history? Specifically, what role does the text play in the circulation of discourses (ways of using language that are associated with particular ideologies, such as the discourses of liberal humanism, Christian fundamentalism, or white supremacy) prevalent in the culture from which the work emerged and/or prevalent in the culture(s) in which the work is interpreted?

文化批评——尤其是在工人阶级文化产品（如通俗小说和电影）以及工人阶级产品与“高雅”文化产品（如经典文学）的比较中，文本发挥了怎样的文化作用？也就是说，文本是如何传递和转变在文本创作时期和/或接受过程中支持和/或削弱社会政治权力结构的意识形态的？

Cultural Criticism – Especially in regard to working-class cultural productions (such as popular fiction and movies) and to comparisons of working-class productions with the productions of “high” culture (such as canonized literature), what cultural work does the text perform? That is, how does the text transmit and transform the ideologies that support and/or undermine the sociopolitical power structure at the time the text was produced and/or over the course of its reception?

女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评——文本如何受到其（有意或无意的）LGBTQ性取向表征的影响？这种表征是支持还是削弱了异性恋霸权？具体到酷儿理论而言，文本如何揭示我们传统性取向思维方式的不足？

Lesbian, Gay, and Queer Criticism – How is the text shaped by its (intentional or unintentional) representation of LGBTQ sexuality? Does this representation support or undermine heterosexism? For queer theory, specifically, how does the text illustrate the inadequacy of our traditional way of thinking about sexuality and sexual orientation?

非裔美国人批评——文本如何受到其（有意或无意的）种族和种族差异表征的影响？这种表征是支持还是削弱了种族主义意识形态？

African American Criticism – How is the text shaped by its (intentional or unintentional) representation of race and racial difference? Does this representation support or undermine racist ideologies?

后殖民批评——文本如何受到其（有意或无意的）文化差异表征的影响（种族、阶级、性别、性取向、宗教、文化信仰和习俗如何结合起来形成个人身份）？这种表征是支持还是削弱了殖民主义意识形态？

Postcolonial Criticism – How is the text shaped by its (intentional or unintentional) representation of cultural difference (the ways in which race, class, sex, gender, sexual orientation, religion, cultural beliefs, and customs combine to form individual identity)? Does this representation support or undermine colonialist ideologies?

尽管这些问题侧重于文学文本的解读，但我相信此时各位已经充分意识到，每一种理论视角都会改变我们感知自身和世界的方式。举例来说，从广义上讲，非裔美国人批评要求我们探究种族（例如，对种族差异的认知、美国种族历史以及种族主义）如何影响我们的个人和集体身份认同、人际关系、历史以及文化产出（包括但不限于文学），从而从中汲取哪些经验。因此，总而言之，批评理论不仅拓展了我们对文学作品的理解（尽管这本身就是一个有价值的目标），也拓展了我们对人类经验的理解。

Although these questions focus on the interpretation of literary texts, I trust that by this point you are fully aware that each theoretical lens alters the way we perceive ourselves and our world as well. To cite just one example, African American criticism, considered in its broadest context, asks us to see what we can learn by examining the ways in which race (for example, perceptions of racial difference, the history of race in America, and racism) informs our individual and collective identity; our interpersonal relationships; our history; and our cultural productions, including but not limited to literature. Thus, taken together, critical theories enlarge our understanding not only of literary works, though that is a worthwhile end in itself, but also of human experience in general.

我相信你已经注意到，上面列举的一些批评流派带有明显的政治色彩：它们的目标是以某种方式改善社会。其他有些理论自诩“非政治化”，脱离了塑造历史和政治的各种力量。新批评就是这类理论的一个显著例子。它在20世纪40年代末和50年代主导了文学研究领域，并自认为占据着纯粹的美学领域。然而，如今大多数批判理论家都认识到，所有批判理论都源于历史现实，并具有政治意义，无论其拥护者是否意识到这些现实和意义。

I’m sure you’ve noticed that some of the schools of criticism listed above are overtly political: their goal is to change society for the better in some way. Other theories see themselves as “apolitical,” as removed from the forces that shape history and politics. A striking example of this kind of theory is New Criticism, which was the dominant force in literary studies in the late 1940s and 1950s and which saw itself as occupying a purely aesthetic realm. However, most critical theorists today recognize that all critical theories are produced by historical realities and have political implications whether or not their advocates are aware of those realities and implications.

例如，许多政治倾向的理论家认为，构建一个纯粹的文学分析美学领域本身就是一种政治举动，反映了一种逃避历史的渴望，一种想要开辟一个“安全”空间，使人免受世事无常、往往令人恐惧的现实侵害的愿望。然而，一种忽视政治现实的批评实践并不能使其脱离政治。它只是无意中保护了现有的权力结构，因为它将我们的注意力从权力结构上转移开来。从这个角度来看，新批评在二战后兴起，结构主义出现也就不足为奇了。当时，人们对核战争的恐惧达到了顶峰，因此，相信存在一个超越人类事件影响的永恒思想领域显得尤为吸引人。事实上，“非政治性”理论总是服务于保守的权力结构。

For example, many politically oriented theorists believe that the creation of a purely aesthetic realm of literary analysis is itself a political move that reflects a desire to escape history, a desire to carve out a “safe” space where one can feel protected from the unpredictable and often frightening realities of the world. However, a critical practice that ignores political reality does not thereby remove itself from politics. It merely protects, however inadvertently, whatever power structure is in place by drawing our attention away from that power structure. From this perspective, it is not surprising that New Criticism rose to prominence and that structuralism emerged in the years following World War II, when the fear of nuclear holocaust was at its height and, therefore, the belief in a permanent realm of ideas beyond the reach of human events was especially appealing. Indeed, “apolitical” theories always serve conservative power structures.

人们可以用类似的方法分析任何批判理论的历史根源和政治内涵。当然，有些批判理论的历史根源和政治内涵比其他理论更为显而易见。例如，女权主义批评、非裔美国人批评以及女同性恋、男同性恋和酷儿批评都直接源于政治运动：分别是20世纪60年代末的妇女解放运动、黑人权力运动以及同性恋解放运动。尽管这三个批评流派的知识根源与争取平等的斗争一样古老，无论性别、种族或性取向如何。同样，马克思主义批评是对社会不公的回应，后殖民主义批评、新历史批评和文化批评在很大程度上也是如此。

One could analyze, in a similar fashion, the historical roots and political implications of any critical theory. Of course, the historical roots and political implications of some critical theories are more obvious than those of others. For example, feminist criticism, African American criticism, and lesbian, gay, and queer criticism grew directly out of political movements: respectively, the women’s liberation, Black Power, and gay and lesbian liberation movements of the late 1960s, although the intellectual roots of all three schools of criticism are as old as the struggle for equality regardless of sex, race, or sexual orientation. Similarly, Marxist criticism is a response to social injustice, as are, in large part, postcolonial, new historical, and cultural criticism.

另一方面，精神分析批评、读者反应批评和解构批评的政治性或“非政治性”倾向完全取决于批评者个人及其运用理论的目的。例如，第二章对《了不起的盖茨比》的精神分析解读是“非政治性的”（也就是说，它忽略了政治，因此对政治现状没有任何改变），因为它将功能失调的爱情视为一种个体或家庭的疾病。如果我转而将小说中对功能失调的爱情的刻画视为现代美国文化的产物——或许是资本主义、父权制和其他意识形态力量交织的产物——那么我就会得出一种公开的政治性精神分析解读（或者，取决于我文章的侧重点，一种精神分析导向的马克思主义或女权主义解读）。

On the other hand, the political or “apolitical” orientation of psychoanalytic, reader-response, and deconstructive criticism depends entirely on the individual critic and the purpose for which the theory is used. For example, the psychoanalytic reading of The Great Gatsby offered in Chapter 2 is “apolitical” (that is, it ignores politics and thus does nothing to alter the political status quo) because it focuses on dysfunctional love as an individual, or familial, disorder. Had I, instead, examined the novel’s representation of dysfunctional love as a product of modern American culture – perhaps as a product of the intersection of capitalism, patriarchy, and other ideological forces – I would have produced an overtly political psychoanalytic reading (or, depending on how I focused the essay, a psychoanalytically oriented Marxist or feminist reading).

同样，读者反应批评也可以“非政治化”，例如，当它考察文本如何引发特定的阅读体验时，正如我们在该章节中所看到的。第六章讨论了情感文体学。或者说，当读者反应批评考察影响几代批评家解读某些文学作品的意识形态动机时，它也可以发挥政治功能。解构主义也一样，当它被用来表明文本的意义是不可确定的时，它也是“非政治性的”：文本的意义无法被确定，因此，文本在传统意义上没有意义。当然，如果一个文本没有意义，它也就没有政治性。然而，在其他实践者的手中，当解构主义被用来揭示文本中存在的意识形态矛盾——隐藏的政治——时，它就可以成为一种强有力的政治工具，正如我们在第八章对《了不起的盖茨比》的解构解读中所看到的那样。

Similarly, reader-response criticism can function “apolitically” when, for example, it examines how texts elicit particular reading experiences, as we saw in the section on affective stylistics in Chapter 6. Or reader-response criticism can have a political function when, for example, it examines the ideological motives informing the way certain literary works have been read by whole generations of critics. Deconstruction, too, is “apolitical” when it is used to show that the meaning of a text is undecidable: the text’s meaning can’t be pinned down and, therefore, the text has no meaning in the traditional sense of the word. Certainly, if a text has no meaning, it has no politics. In the hands of other practitioners, however, deconstruction can be a powerful political tool when it is used to reveal the ideological contradictions – the hidden politics – operating in a text, as we saw in the deconstructive reading of The Great Gatsby offered in Chapter 8.

简而言之，每一种批评理论的意义和力量很大程度上取决于你。批评理论只是你手中的工具，仅此而已。你可以选择一种理论，并仅以此视角解读文学作品；也可以熟练运用两种、三种甚至更多理论，甚至将它们提供的洞见结合起来，共同解读一部文学作品。例如，你可以运用马克思主义、精神分析和女性主义的概念，从非裔美国人的角度解读一部文学作品中种族差异的呈现。或者，你可以运用后殖民主义和读者反应理论，从女性主义的角度分析一部文学作品中你认为反复出现的误读，例如，这部作品的作者是一位西印度群岛的女性。事实上，为了真正熟练地运用某些批评理论，你必须熟悉这些理论所借鉴的理论本身，这种说法并非毫无道理。许多马克思主义、女权主义、后殖民主义、非裔美国人以及女同性恋/男同性恋/酷儿批评家会借鉴彼此的理论框架，以及精神分析、解构主义、读者反应理论和符号学等理论，以分析压迫的各种形式和过程以及对压迫的抵抗。

In short, the meaning and power of every critical theory depend largely on you. Critical theories are tools in your hands, no more, no less. You can choose one theory and interpret literature through that lens alone, or you can become adept at using two, three, or more theories, even combining the insights they offer as you interpret a single literary work. You might produce, for example, an African American reading that draws on Marxist, psychoanalytic, and feminist concepts in order to interpret the representation of racial difference in a literary work. Or you might produce a feminist reading that draws on postcolonial and reader-response concepts in order to analyze what you consider a recurrent misreading of a literary work written, for example, by a West Indian woman. In fact, it is not unreasonable to argue that, in order to be really proficient at applying some critical theories, it is necessary that you familiarize yourself with the theories on which they draw. For many Marxist, feminist, postcolonial, African American, and lesbian/gay/queer critics draw on one another’s theoretical frameworks as well as on such theories as psychoanalysis, deconstruction, reader-response theory, and semiotics in order to analyze the myriad forms and processes of oppression and the resistance to oppression.

然而，你选择运用哪些理论来解读特定文本，主要取决于两个因素：(1) 你运用该理论的能力，以及 (2) 你计划应用该理论的文学文本。因为为了进行有效的解读，你需要确保你与所选理论以及所选理论与文学文本之间都高度契合。并非所有文学文本都同样适用于所有理论。因此，你的技能之一在于能够识别何时应用哪种理论。任何值得掌握的技能都需要练习。不要被最初遇到的困难所吓倒。就像你的小提琴在学会演奏莫扎特之前，也需要发出很多吱吱声一样。

The theory or theories you choose to use for a particular reading, however, should depend mainly on two factors: (1) your own ability to use the theory, and (2) the literary text to which you plan to apply it. For in order to produce a useful reading you need a good fit, both between yourself and the theory you choose and between the theory you choose and the literary text. Not all literary texts lend themselves equally well to all theories. So part of your skill must involve recognizing when to apply which theory. Like any skill worth acquiring, it takes practice. Don’t be discouraged by initial difficulties you may encounter. Your violin has to squeak quite a bit before you learn to play Mozart.

如果允许我再提一点警告，不要因为发现某个理论存在一些缺陷就将其全盘否定。批评理论很容易被挑毛病，因为它们都存在缺陷。这正是理论而非事实的本质所在。例如，正如新批评所声称的那样，文学作品如何能成为其自身的语境呢？这难道不是一个逻辑上的荒谬，是对语境定义的违背吗？或者，精神分析如何能忽略或边缘化心理形成过程中的社会因素呢？家庭（精神分析认为家庭对心理的形成负有责任）本身也是一个社会实体吗？

And if I may offer one more warning, don’t dismiss a theory because you find it has some flaws. It’s easy to find fault with critical theories. They all have flaws. That’s part of what it means to be a theory rather than a fact. For example, how can a literary work be its own context, as New Criticism claims it is? Isn’t that a logical absurdity, a violation of the definition of context? Or how can psychoanalysis omit or marginalize sociological factors in the creation of the psyche, when the family (which psychoanalysis holds responsible for the formation of the psyche) is itself a sociological entity?

然而，指出理论中的缺陷并不必然降低该理论对文学阐释的价值。如果我们在学习过程中过早地进行挑剔，就会忽略许多理论的巨大价值，因为我们对它们的排斥倾向会日益增强——在我看来，这种倾向源于我们想要减少对批判理论畏惧的心理。这种逻辑看似诱人，实则适得其反：如果一个批判理论存在缺陷，那么我就不必精通它，也不必担心自己在使用过程中遇到的困难。因此，我强烈建议你暂时搁置“批判模式”，至少在你通过运用各种理论阐释文学作品而充分熟悉它们之前，不要急于进入这个阶段。

Finding faults in a theory, however, does not necessarily render that theory less helpful for literary interpretation. And if we practice faultfinding too soon in our learning process, we can overlook the enormous usefulness of many theories as our tendency to dismiss them grows, a tendency that is fed, it seems to me, by our understandable desire to feel less intimidated by critical theory. The logic is inviting but very self-defeating: if a critical theory is flawed, then it’s not so important that I become proficient at it, and I don’t have to worry about my difficulties with it. So I urge you very strongly to postpone the “critique mode” for a while, at least until you have thoroughly familiarized yourself with a range of theories by using them to interpret literature.

不过，在你开始独自阅读之前，我想先分享一下我最近的经历，我认为它既体现了批评理论和文学阐释的个人性，也体现了其政治性。我向一位对文学很感兴趣但对批评理论一窍不通的朋友简要介绍了我对《了不起的盖茨比》的女性主义、后殖民主义和酷儿理论解读。他立刻问道：“你教科书里用的那些理论，有哪一套和小说本身相符吗？” “都相符，”我赶紧向他保证。“如果某种理论会扭曲作品，我就不会用它，”我解释道。“不，”他说，“我的意思是，所有理论都觉得小说有什么问题吗？”

Before I send you off on your own to do those readings, however, I’d like to share with you a recent experience that I think reflects both the personal and the political nature of critical theory and literary interpretation. I briefly described my feminist, postcolonial, and queer readings of The Great Gatsby to an interested friend who loves to read literature but who knows nothing about critical theory. He immediately asked, “Are any of the theories you use in your textbook in harmony with the novel?” “They all are,” I hastened to assure him. “I wouldn’t apply a theory to a literary work if it distorted the work,” I explained. “No,” he said, “I mean, do all the theories find something wrong with the novel?”

我突然明白了。他说得对！我之前用过的几乎所有理论都让我得出这样的结论：这部小说在意识形态上存在某种缺陷。如果我把所有这些缺陷放在一起，我会得出这样的结论：“《了不起的盖茨比》是一部阶级歧视、性别歧视、恐同、种族歧视、殖民主义的小说，它美化了资本主义的罪恶，歌颂了不健康的爱情，而且，似乎这还不够，它还营造了一种不确定的阅读体验，诱使我们把自身的信仰和欲望投射到文本之上。”然而，《了不起的盖茨比》同时也是我读过的最感人、文笔最精湛的文学作品之一。这怎么可能呢？

Then it hit me. He’s right! Almost all the theories I used have led me to conclude, in effect, that the novel is ideologically flawed in some way. If I put all these flaws together, I come up with a statement something like this: “The Great Gatsby is a classist, sexist, homophobic, racist, colonialist novel that romanticizes the evils of capitalism, glorifies dysfunctional love, and, as if that weren’t enough, creates an indeterminate reading experience that invites us to project our own beliefs and desires onto the text.” Yet The Great Gatsby is also one of the most moving and exquisitely written literary works it’s ever been my pleasure to read. How can that be?

或许更恰当的问题是：这怎么可能不是事实呢？几乎没有评论家会否认菲茨杰拉德拥有美国作家中最敏锐的语言天赋之一，或者《了不起的盖茨比》是史上最具诗意、最精湛技艺的作品之一。与此同时，这部小说写于1924年，作者是一位年轻的白人，他渴望被上流社会接纳，渴望获得文学上的认可，而这一切在他生前都未能实现。如果他的传记作者所言属实，包括那些欣赏他的作品并理解他人生坎坷的传记作者，那么菲茨杰拉德是一位典型的时代人物，他拥有那个时代人物所能拥有的所有意识形态偏见。这些因素怎能不体现在他认为自己最伟大的成就，并倾注了全部心血的作品中呢？事实上，即便菲茨杰拉德没有那些影响他小说创作的意识形态偏见，这些偏见也依然会……某种程度上，社会偏见在《了不起的盖茨比》中有所体现，因为这部作品意在记录20世纪20年代，记录作者自己那一代人的生活——或者至少是作者所熟悉的白人精英阶层的生活——而菲茨杰拉德对人性的观察极其敏锐。简而言之，即便作者本人没有偏见，那个时代在意识形态上也存在缺陷。

Perhaps the better question is, How can that not be? Few critics would deny that Fitzgerald had one of the best ears for language ever bestowed on an American writer or that The Great Gatsby is one of the most lyrically beautiful, masterfully crafted works ever produced. At the same time, the novel was written in 1924 by a young white man struggling for acceptance by the upper class and for literary recognition that he did not achieve during his lifetime. And if his biographers are to be believed, including those biographers who admire his work and appreciate the difficulties he suffered in life, Fitzgerald was a man of his time who had all the ideological biases that a man of his time could possibly possess. How could these elements not appear in the work that he believed would be his greatest achievement and into which he poured himself so completely? In fact, even had Fitzgerald not shared all the ideological biases that inform his novel, those biases would have appeared in the work in some form because The Great Gatsby was intended as a chronicle of the 1920s, of the author’s own generation – or at least of the elite white population with whom the author was acquainted – and Fitzgerald was an extremely accurate observer of human behavior. In short, the times were ideologically flawed even if the author hadn’t been.

然而，正如我的朋友所说，我并没有真正把这些缺陷看作是“小说本身的问题”。我当时兴奋不已，因为我的理论帮助我揭示了那些令人震惊的意识形态，以至于我忘记了对它们感到震惊。是的，这部小说在意识形态上令人震惊，这是我们不应忘记的事实。但同时，这部小说也美得令人窒息。我试图在欣赏《了不起的盖茨比》无与伦比的艺术性的同时，也欣赏那些向我揭示其令人不安的潜台词的理论，从而保持这种矛盾。我相信，在菲茨杰拉德的小说以及我阅读的所有文学作品中保持这种矛盾，是运用理论视角进行阅读所带来的最大乐趣之一。这或许是一种需要慢慢品味的体验。如果是这样，我非常希望你手中的这本书能帮助你获得这种体验。

Yet I didn’t really see these flaws as “something wrong with the novel,” as my friend put it. I was so excited by my ability to see the appalling ideologies my theories were helping me uncover that I forgot to be appalled by them. Yes, the novel is ideologically appalling, a fact we mustn’t forget. And the novel is intensely beautiful as well. This is the contradiction I try to sustain as I continue to appreciate both the incomparable artistry of The Great Gatsby and the theories that show me the multiple layers of its disquieting subtext. Sustaining that contradiction in Fitzgerald’s novel and in all the literature I read is, I believe, one of the greatest pleasures that reading through a theoretical lens offers us. It may be an acquired taste. If so, I would be very happy if the book you hold in your hands helped you acquire it.
